items.title: [Feat] PD: Add opt-in first-chunk decode KV allocation
items.author: sufubao
items.summary: Adds opt-in `first_chunk` KV allocation policy for disaggregated LLM serving, allowing decode to reserve KV destination after first prefill chunk instead of waiting for full prefill completion.
items.body:
## Problem and behavior

In disaggregated serving, `early` can reserve decode destination KV before prefill produces any KV. `prefill_complete` waits until the final prefill result is accepted. This PR adds an opt-in intermediate policy:

```bash
--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy first_chunk
```

Set the same policy on both roles. After accepting the first chunk result, prefill signals that decode may allocate the complete request destination. Once destination admission and the existing pointer handshake finish, chunk transfers can overlap subsequent prefill computation. This is a single full-prompt reservation triggered by the first chunk, not incremental allocation per chunk. Decode still waits for the complete handoff before generating tokens. The default remains `early`.

## Implementation and scope

- Reuse the deferred bootstrap, lifecycle ownership, and error propagation from #40703. No new wire message or scheduler is introduced.
- Keep first-chunk allocation readiness separate from final-result acceptance through two sender methods sharing an idempotent notification implementation. Single-chunk requests signal readiness only after accepting the final token, logprobs, and speculative sidecars.
- For intermediate chunks, publish readiness after existing result-copy, abort, and yield checks. Continue optimistic prefill while waiting for decode admission, retaining the existing timeout and retry paths.
- Preserve whole-transfer, final-token, and cleanup barriers. An intermediate chunk does not constitute transfer success.
- Inherit the current `prefill_complete` restrictions: Mooncake, Python bootstrap, and attention TP1/CP1/PP1. This PR does not enable staging, decode radix/HiCache, hybrid recurrent/Mamba state pools, or other previously excluded configurations.
- Reject mismatched P/D allocation policies. Pending requests retain KV on prefill, so destination pressure can become prefill pressure.

This is related to the follow-up discussion in #40703 about notifying decode when the final chunk is scheduled. This PR instead uses **acceptance of the first chunk result** to enable transfer overlap with subsequent chunks. It preserves the existing final-result notification boundary for `prefill_complete`.

## Validation

**193 CPU regression tests passed.** Ruff 0.15.1 checks/formatting, isort 7.0.0, and `git diff --check` also passed. Coverage includes CLI defaults, both deferred policies, overlap/non-overlap result handling, cancellation, timeouts, duplicate readiness, recomputation, fake warmup, bootstrap registration, and role switching.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99 PYTHONPATH=python exp -m "Validate first-chunk allocation CPU lifecycle" \
  python -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete_integration.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_abort_result_cleanup.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_deferred_bootstrap.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_register_to_bootstrap.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_admission_abort_not_enqueued.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_fake_kv_sender.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_dsv4_retract_rebootstrap.py
```

The run produced seven warnings: CPU platform fallbacks, dependency deprecations, and the existing bootstrap thread fault-injection test's expected thread exception. There were no test failures.

The existing two-GPU lifecycle and forced optimistic-retry tests now also cover `first_chunk`, but **GPU tests have not been executed locally**. The PR is ready for review so upstream checks can proceed; GPU/upstream CI validation remains outstanding. There are no SGLang performance measurements yet, and LightLLM results are not presented as SGLang gains. Qwen3.8-27B validation is being prepared separately; the current commit still rejects its recurrent state pool.

CPU validation used an isolated environment with Python 3.12.9, Transformers 5.19.0, and Tokenizers 0.23.2, while reusing local Torch 2.9.1 rather than the repository's 2.14.1 pin. Full dependency-lock parity is unverified. `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99` hides all physical GPUs while accommodating the upstream test utility's inability to handle an empty value. No import shims or weakened assertions were used.

AI assistance was used for implementation and test preparation.

items.title: [Perf] [Intel] gemma4: Use exact softcap comparison ranks for greedy verification
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Optimizes greedy-logit verification on Intel XPU by precomputing exact FP32 softcap comparison ranks into a 256 KB table, avoiding per-vocab-element softcap recomputation.
items.body:
Stacked on #44884; this PR contains only the exact comparison-rank lookup follow-up.

## Motivation

The fused greedy-verification logits reduction still computes FP32 softcap for every vocabulary element. BF16 has only 65,536 bit patterns, so build exact comparison ranks through the existing native FP32 softcap once and reduce those ranks instead. This preserves transformed equality classes, including softcap saturation, signed zero, and NaNs. Weights, BF16 logits, and the head GEMM remain unchanged.

## Modifications

- Extend the XPU reduction with an optional immutable 256 KB comparison table and unsigned-rank/first-index reductions.
- Keep the table in a nonpersistent LogitsProcessor buffer, keyed by generation device and softcap. Construct it during eager warmup; unmatched first capture or compile keeps the existing tanh reduction.
- Carry the immutable table reference with deferred logits through graph replay. Slice token rows without slicing the table. Current-request eligibility and the ordinary-logits fallback remain unchanged.

The table records exact FP32 output ordering and equality for the actual native softcap operation; it does not approximate or change model precision. Scope remains no-gather Gemma4 BF16 FrozenKV target verification, validated at TP1.

## Accuracy Tests

- Exhaustive native FP32 softcap order/equality proof across all 65,536 BF16 bit patterns for softcap None, zero, and 30; device lookup checked for every pattern.
- Six XPU kernel tests passed, including signed zero, saturation ties, first NaN/global index, chunk boundaries, public lazy dispatch, Meta shapes, and graph replay with changed inputs.
- Two real LogitsProcessor lifetime/capture tests passed, covering separate owners, cap changes, nonpersistent state, immutable captured references, and no table construction inside first capture.
- 75 CPU namespace/policy tests and 15 subtests passed. Rank-aware Meta smoke and pre-commit passed.
- Fifteen controlled same-GPU serving cases matched the parent exactly, including returned token logprobs and repetition-penalty/bias/min-new-token fallbacks.
- Official GSM8K200, temperature 0, seed 42, eight threads: parent 159/200 (79.5%), candidate 164/200 (82.0%), zero errors and two truncations each. Earlier parent serving scored 165/200; these are compatibility results, with no quality-improvement claim.
- Candidate official GSM8K200 temperature 1: 165/200 (82.5%), zero errors, two truncations. This uses the ordinary-logits fallback, not the changed greedy reduction.

Exact operator and controlled-serving parity do not establish arbitrary batch-independent model bitwise equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same-GPU ABBA versus parent 7aba: Gemma4 E2B BF16, TP1, MTP steps 3/top-k 1/draft tokens 4, full graph backend; actual target-verify capture sizes end at 48, overlap disabled, page size 64, max running 64, max total tokens 32768, context 8192, static memory fraction 0.70. Each server switch warmed 128 requests at c32 with 256 output tokens. Timing uses seed 42 and 256 outputs, 64 requests at c1 and 128 at c8/c32. All 12 runs completed without errors, with identical input/output token counts.

Mean TPOT, ms, control/candidate/candidate/control:

| Concurrency | Control A | Candidate A | Candidate B | Control B | Lower time vs mean controls | Lower time vs final control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 |4.129629|4.120205|4.115793|4.093881|-0.152%|-0.589%|
| 8 |6.017597|5.979372|5.986314|5.960932|0.107%|-0.368%|
| 32 |10.882142|10.804637|10.778815|10.925135|1.026%|1.221%|

C1/c8 are near flat and slightly slower versus final controls. At c32, both candidate repeats beat both controls; final control was 0.395% slower than initial, and candidate mean was 0.831% lower than initial control. On 55/128 requests with identical texts across all four c32 runs, mean streaming-time improvement was 1.014%. Controls differed on 38/128 texts; candidates differed on 48/128. This subset does not remove between-run drift.

Additional bounded c64 ABBA uses 256 requests/run with 256 output tokens, a deterministic repeated copy of the 200 canonical prompts, and 256-request c64 warmup per server switch:

| Concurrency | Control A | Candidate A | Candidate B | Control B | Lower time vs mean controls | Lower time vs final control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 |20.931916|20.349956|20.459503|20.564288|1.655%|0.776%|

Control improved 1.756% between repeats, so the final-control comparison is conservative. Both candidate repeats beat final control. The 109/256 identical-text subset improved 1.753% in mean streaming time; controls differed on 92/256 texts and candidates on 107/256. These figures retain between-run drift limitations.

C64 is mixed eager/captured execution: startup logs resolve target-verify capture sizes through 48, every logged above 48-request decode batch used eager execution, and smaller decode batches also used captured execution. All four runs succeeded without errors and had identical input/output token counts.

A real c32 serving trace contains 16 rank partial/final reductions, confirming actual dispatch. Profile timing alone is not an end-to-end gain measurement.

Bounded eager head-plus-finalization microbenchmark, four rotating original BF16 weight banks (3.2 GB), compared to the parent tanh reduction:

| Rows | Parent us | Rank-table us | Lower time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 1371.28 | 1370.04 | 0.09% |
| 32 | 1524.96 | 1500.50 | 1.60% |
| 128 | 1971.09 | 1822.13 | 7.56% |
| 256 | 2576.16 | 2217.53 | 13.92% |

These are microbenchmarks, not serving gains. Fixed 4096 chunks use 16 B shared memory and report zero spill bytes; the table adds 256 KB model-owned GPU storage and indexed read traffic. An 8192-chunk candidate offered no consistent improvement. No achieved-occupancy claim is inferred from compiler resource reports.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add kernel and runtime lifetime tests.
- [x] Document exact semantics, state ownership, capture fallback, and scope.
- [x] Finish and archive paired serving benchmarks and official quality results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

items.title: fix(moe): report reason for CUTLASS FP8 backend rejection
items.author: Gitcoder12
items.summary: Routes CUTLASS FP8 MoE backend rejections through the existing _make_log_unsupported helper to surface the specific reason and list supported alternative backends.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62135. 

Currently, requesting `moe_backend="cutlass"` with online FP8 raises a bare `ValueError` without stating the reason or alternatives. This PR updates `select_fp8_moe_backend` to use `_make_log_unsupported` for the CUTLASS branch and explicitly list the supported alternative backends.

## Claims

- Fixes the error message for CUTLASS FP8 MoE backend rejections to include the specific reason and list of supported alternatives.
- Aligns the CUTLASS error reporting with sibling backends (like HUMMING).

## Validation

- Validated locally by triggering the error path with an unsupported configuration. The error now correctly prints the supported alternatives.
- Test command run: `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/test_fp8.py`

## Details

The root cause is a hardcoded `raise ValueError` at `oracle/fp8.py:468` that bypassed the `_make_log_unsupported` helper used by other backends in the same function. The change simply routes the CUTLASS rejection through the existing reporting helper to improve startup UX.

items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fix macOS build: read inherited listener family from its address
items.author: khluu
items.summary: Fixes vllm-rs macOS arm64 build failure by replacing Linux-only socket2::Socket::domain with cross-platform SockAddr::domain to determine inherited listener address family.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes the macOS arm64 CPU wheel build, which fails on main (release-v2 #8588) and on `releases/v0.32.0` (release-v2 #8575):

```
error[E0599]: no method named `domain` found for struct `socket2::Socket` in the current scope
 --> src/engine-core-client/src/transport.rs:408:25
408 |     let domain = socket.domain()?;
```

#54113 uses `socket2::Socket::domain()` (`SO_DOMAIN`) in `adopt_listener` to tell inherited TCP and Unix listeners apart. socket2 only provides that method on Linux, Android, FreeBSD and Fuchsia, so `vllm-rs` doesn't compile on macOS. The macOS wheel is in the "additional wheels" group, which only runs when unblocked, so nothing caught this when it landed.

## Change

Read the family from the listener's bound address instead: `socket.local_addr()?.domain()`. `SockAddr::domain` works on every platform. The TCP/Unix branching after it is unchanged.

Also adds `inherited_unix_listener_is_adopted_without_rebinding`, a Unix-socket counterpart to the existing inherited TCP listener test. Before this, the Unix branch had no test.

## Test Plan

On macOS (arm64, rustc 1.95):
- `cargo check -p vllm-engine-core-client`: failed with the error above before the change, passes after.

items.title: [Feat] PD: Support KV-only hybrid decode radix cache with linear EAGLE
items.author: Jzz1943
items.summary: Enables KV-only prefix reuse in the hybrid decode radix cache without requiring recurrent-state checkpoints, supporting linear EAGLE/MTP speculation.
items.body:
## Motivation

Hybrid PD decode receives the recurrent state for the full prompt from the prefill worker. Requiring a cached Mamba/KDA checkpoint to reuse a KV prefix unnecessarily couples these two resources; a prefix checkpoint also cannot replace the freshly transferred full-prompt state.

Enable KV-only prefix reuse in the built-in hybrid decode radix cache, including linear EAGLE/MTP, while keeping recurrent state request-local.

## Modifications

- Let KV prefix matching proceed without a recurrent checkpoint. Do not restore, donate, or insert request-local Mamba state into the tree; reuse the existing request-release path.
- Enable EAGLE bigram keys for this mode so diverging prefixes cannot share the wrong shifted draft KV at a page boundary.
- Budget persistent and speculative state for both running and PD transfer requests, matching the decode pool's eager tracking-slot allocation. Ordinary checkpoint-cache budgeting is unchanged.
- Keep this mode on the Python TreeCore. Guard unsupported cache/session combinations; speculative hybrid use currently requires EAGLE with top-k 1, NIXL, and no sliding-window attention.

Uses the existing `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` option. With overlap and extra tracking buffers, for example, 124 running requests plus 6 transfer slots require `(124 + 6) × 3 = 390` Mamba state slots.

## Accuracy Tests

Existing GLM-5.3-Flash integration validation on 8 × H200 (P TP4/EP4, D TP4/EP4):

- Without MTP: eight cold/shared-prefix/isolated/concurrent requests returned the expected answers. D-side shared-prefix hits reached 3,840 tokens, while isolated controls had zero hits; differing suffixes retained their own state.
- With MTP516 and BF16 recurrent state: GSM8K, 1,314 examples × 2 rounds, **95.4% / 95.9%**. The BF16 integration configuration also includes the independent KDA tracking dtype fix in #44886.

These full-model results predate the rebase onto the current main. On the rebased branch, seven existing cache/validation test files pass: **104 tests and 80 subtests**. The four focused regressions cover KV-only matching/state isolation, release, shifted draft-KV boundary keys, and state budgeting. Existing sizing fixtures were adjusted without adding more test cases. All changed files pass pre-commit checks.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The existing MTP516 configuration completed a C132 benchmark (64K/1K, 99.9% shared prefix, 2,048 requests per round) with all requests successful in both rounds. The higher-throughput round reached **9,254.07 output tok/s**, with mean TTFT **1,594.00 ms** and TPOT **12.39 ms**. This is integration evidence, not an isolated speedup attributable to this PR.

items.title: [Fix] diffusion: pipeline and model-helper bug fixes
items.author: OnePunchMonk
items.summary: Fixes multiple diffusion pipeline and model-helper bugs including Plucker ray precision, texture dimension swaps, output tensor layout, and argument ordering.
items.body:
Part of #43875 (items 25-33). Split out of #43585 so it can be reviewed on its own. It does not depend on the other two PRs (#43585, #44887).

**Note: behavior change in item 25. LingBot-World camera poses and intrinsics are now built in float32, and the Plucker rays are computed in float32 before the final cast. Plucker values will differ slightly from before. The effect on generated video was not checked, so a maintainer with a GPU may want to compare LingBot-World output.**

CPU check (16 frames at 832x480, synthetic forward-walk with yaw sweep, float64 as ground truth): the old bf16 path differs from truth in 74% of the conditioning values (mean error 0.0045, max 0.032); the new path matches the float64 result exactly after the final bf16 cast.

## Summary
Fixes in pipelines and the model helpers they use, one commit per item. Item numbers match #43875.

25. Plucker rays were built in bf16 when poses were bf16, so pixel columns above 256 shared a ray. They are computed in float32 now (LingBot-World poses too).
26. The blank default texture and the bake buffers used `(width, height)` where `(height, width)` is needed, which breaks non-square textures.
27. `ImageProcessorV2.load_image` raised `UnboundLocalError` for an ndarray or tensor. ndarrays work and other types raise a `TypeError`.
28. `DiffusersPipeline` output layout: NumPy videos were permuted twice, PIL lists were read as a batch, and several images from an image pipeline were stacked as video frames.
29. `DiffusersPipeline.add_stage` took its arguments in the reverse order of the base class.
30. SANA-Video always encoded the negative prompt at 300 tokens. It uses `max_sequence_length` now.
31. ErnieImage treated a `[null, null]` `pe` entry as a real prompt-enhancement model. It is treated as absent.
32. HunyuanImage3 ignored `--revision` when downloading weights.
33. Hunyuan3D picked an arbitrary checkpoint when several matched the fallback glob. It picks the first by name now.

## Tests
- New `test_pipeline_regressions.py` (CPU): 11 pass.
- With the source changes reverted, 9 fail. The 2 that still pass are the ErnieImage cases for a real `pe` entry and a missing one, which guard that the fix does not over-reject.
- No tests for 29, 32 and 33 (signature order, a passed-through kwarg, and a sort).
- No GPU run, see the note on item 25.

items.title: [Fix] diffusion: runtime utils bug fixes
items.author: OnePunchMonk
items.summary: Fixes multiple bugs in multimodal_gen/runtime/utils including video download cleanup, base64 parsing, Hub cache fallbacks, path matching, and dtype restoration.
items.body:
Part of #43875 (items 8-24). Split out of #43585 so it can be reviewed on its own. It touches only `runtime/utils` and its tests, and does not depend on the other two PRs (#43585, #44888).

## Summary
Bug fixes in `multimodal_gen/runtime/utils`, one commit per item. Item numbers match #43875.

Downloads and inputs
8. `load_video` never deleted the video it downloaded from a URL, so `/tmp` filled up over time. It now cleans up (also on failure) and the download has a timeout.
9. Line-wrapped base64 images were silently cut at the first line. The data URL regex now matches across newlines.

Hub, cache and config loading
10. An unreachable Hub was treated as "this repo has no model_index.json", so the cache fallback never ran. It now falls back to the cached copy.
11. The same condition sent `maybe_download_model_index` down the single-model path with a misleading "-Diffusers" error. It now reports the download failure.
12. A local cache dir of `ltx-2.3-distilled` matched the `ltx-2.3` overlay by substring. Cache dirs are now matched by path component.
13. An overlay repo resolved by Hub id downloaded only its manifest, so `model_index.json` was missing on a fresh cache. It now downloads the full overlay metadata.
14. `scheduler` anywhere in a component's path made every component read `scheduler_config.json`. Only the component dir name counts now.
15. Normalizing a ModelOpt `config.json` wrote through the HF cache symlink and changed the shared blob. The file is now replaced instead.
16. The ModelScope LoRA path raised a `TypeError` when no weights were found. It now raises a `FileNotFoundError` that says so.
17. Corrected a comment claiming CI validation failures after download are retried (they are not).

Precision, logging and misc
18. `temporary_module_dtype` restored the whole module to the first parameter's dtype, undoing mixed precision (bf16 weights with fp32 norms). Each tensor keeps its own dtype now.
19. All `RequestMetrics` instances compared equal. They compare by identity now.
20. `log_request_summary` ignored its `tag` argument. It is honored now, with the previously written value as the default, so existing callers see no change.
21. `get_git_commit_hash` ran `git rev-parse` in the current directory. It now runs in the sglang install dir.
22. The "log on every rank at DEBUG" rule read the log level when the logger was created, before `configure_logger`. It reads it at log time now.
23. Enabling the NVTX hooks between a module's pre- and post-hook popped a range that was never pushed. Push and pop stay balanced across toggles.
24. `get_bool_env_var` warned once per bad value instead of once per variable. It is keyed by name now.

## Tests
- New unit tests for each item except 16, 17 and 21 (error message, comment, and cwd-only changes).
- `test_runtime_utils_regressions.py`, `test_hf_diffusers_utils.py`, `test_model_overlay.py`, `test_logging_utils.py`, `test_nvtx_pytorch_hooks.py`, `test_performance_metrics.py`, `test_precision_consistency.py` on CPU: 127 pass, 1 fails. The failure, `test_autocast_and_dtype_alignment`, fails the same way on main in this environment.
- With the source changes reverted, all 15 new test cases fail.
- No GPU run: these are CPU-testable utility fixes.

items.title: [Fix] kda: Align graph tracking branch dtype with the recurrent state pool
items.author: Jzz1943
items.summary: Fixes Triton compilation error when BF16 recurrent state pool and FP32 snapshot branches mismatch by casting snapshot dtype before merging.
items.body:
## Motivation

KDA graph tracking can read an FP32 chunk-boundary snapshot or a recurrent-state pool entry. With a BF16 state pool, these branches produce different Triton types, causing compilation to fail before the final store cast.

Observed during GLM-5.3-Flash prefill BCG initialization with BF16 recurrent state:

```text
CompilationError: at 19:4:
    if mode == 1:
    ^
AssertionError("Mismatched type for val between then block (<['1024'], bf16>) and else block (<['1024'], fp32>)")
Fail when using backend: breakable for prefill runner.
```

A cast after the `if/else` cannot resolve this error: Triton requires matching types for `val` when merging the branches, before compiling the subsequent cast.

## Modifications

Cast the snapshot to the state-pool element type before the branches merge. The stored dtype is unchanged, and FP32 state pools retain their existing behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated in GLM-5.3-Flash PD serving on 8 × H200 with BF16 recurrent state and MTP516: GSM8K, 1,314 examples × 2 rounds, scored **95.4% / 95.9%**. These results are from the existing integration configuration containing this fix and the separate Decode RadixCache changes, not a new full-model run on this rebased PR branch.

Pre-commit checks passed. This is a correctness fix; no inference speed improvement is claimed.

items.title: [Core] Bound prefix-cache reuse for target-token prefill scoring
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: Binds prefix-cache KV reuse at prompt_logprob_start during target-token prefill scoring to guarantee complete score returns with ~3.7× speedup.
items.body:
## Overview

When a target-token scoring request opts into prefix-cache reads, a cache hit can skip rows whose scores are required. This PR bounds reuse at `prompt_logprob_start` so every requested score is returned. Implements the bounded-KV step of #60366 and M1 of #62175.

Related work on prefix-cache reuse for prompt scoring: #60960. This PR resolves unsupported configurations before connector admission, checks the worker-resolved KV format, and adds complete-score regressions.

## Claims

- With `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False`, scoring requests reuse KV before the first scored row and return the complete score matrix.
- Defaults and ordinary generation are unchanged. Unsupported configurations, and requests that also ask for ordinary prompt logprobs, recompute the full prompt and log a one-time warning.
- With Qwen3-32B at TP=4, teacher scoring is 3.7x to 3.8x faster for long shared documents and about 1.1x faster for short prompts.

## Validation

| Setup | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single GPU | Cache and scheduler suites | 447 passed (2 multi-GPU cases excluded) |
| Qwen3-0.6B, TP=1 | Eager and CUDA-graph scoring with async scheduling; incomplete-buffer rejection | 2 GPU tests and 1 CPU test passed |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8, TP=1 | 7 cache-boundary cases with FP8 weights and 16-bit KV | Passed |
| 2×A40 and 4×A40, Qwen3-0.6B | 32-response replay, cache boundaries, forced prefill preemption at TP=2 and TP=4 | Complete outputs, exact match with uncached scoring in batch-invariant mode |

### Teacher-stage performance

Qwen3-32B, 4×A100 80GB with NVLink, TP=4, BF16, FlashAttention 2, compilation and CUDA graphs, synchronous scheduling. Batch-invariant mode is off. Each prompt group has four responses and starts with an empty cache. Each case alternates six repetitions per path after warmup.

The table uses grouped arrivals. Each row covers 16 responses across four groups; times sum the four group medians. The token budget is `max_num_batched_tokens`.

| Token budget | Workload | Uncached | Bounded reuse | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 512 | Short math prompts | 1.88 s | 1.66 s | 1.13x |
| 512 | Long documents | 6.13 s | 1.60 s | 3.84x |
| 2048 | Short math prompts | 1.61 s | 1.42 s | 1.14x |
| 2048 | Long documents | 5.16 s | 1.39 s | 3.71x |

Short prompts have 142 to 209 context tokens and 437 to 1024 response tokens. Documents have 2933 to 3944 context tokens and 13 to 58 response tokens. Staggered arrivals, targeting 20 ms gaps with admission at engine-step boundaries, gave similar results: 1.11x to 1.13x for short prompts and 3.71x to 3.83x for documents. Across all six repetitions, aggregate speedups ranged from 1.11x to 1.14x for short prompts and 3.66x to 3.87x for documents. These are offline scoring times, including the existing one-token generation step; model loading, compilation and warmup are excluded.

BF16 scores vary with execution shape. The largest absolute logprob difference from uncached scoring on the 32B runs was 0.50, compared with 0.37 between single and batched uncached scoring. A separate Qwen3-0.6B synthetic probe reached 0.14 for actual tokens and 1.17 for extra candidates. Batch-invariant Qwen3-0.6B checks matched exactly across uncached, bounded and preempted paths. Training loss and gradient validation is part of the VIME integration.

Scripts, raw results and pinned source/model versions: [reproduction materials in my fork](https://github.com/LinzeShi/vllm/blob/db215c5db9eec0decd891b802b2928f90fe16d46/benchmarks/opd_prefix_reuse_tp4/README.md).

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

The scoring command below uses `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn`. A40 GPU checks also passed with `error`.

```bash
# Local single-GPU validation. Omit the filter on a multi-GPU host.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q \
  -k 'not test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders and not test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait'
# Scoring checks.
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -q \
  -k 'bounded_prefix_reuse or reject_incomplete_prefill'
```

</details>

## Details

KV holds attention state, not the logits for skipped rows. The cache hit is capped at `min(prompt_logprob_start or 0, num_tokens - 1)` with the usual block alignment, and the cap applies again after preemption. Admission decides the fallback before connector hooks run, on a copy of the caller's sampling params.

The first version uses MRV2 and supports text token inputs, one causal full-attention KV group, unquantized KV, `max_tokens=1`, and single-GPU or tensor-parallel execution. It adds no response fields and no score storage. Connector, adapter and other configuration exclusions are documented in `docs/training/prompt_token_id_logprobs.md`.

---

<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the cache coordinator and existing scoring worker.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Single-GPU and TP=2/4 replay, complete-score regressions, and teacher-stage measurements.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Existing suites extended, documentation updated, checks passed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Motivation, related work, evidence and limitations included.

</details>

items.title: [Roadmap] Q4 2026 OPD Teacher Serving in vLLM
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: Roadmap for efficient teacher model serving in vLLM for on-policy distillation, covering prefix-cache reuse, VIME integration, AuxOutput score delivery, and tensor-parallel candidate support across six milestones.
items.body:
Part of the [Q4 2026 vLLM × RL roadmap #58990](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58990) (Learn Faster, inference to training).

## Motivation

In on-policy distillation (OPD), the student generates responses and a teacher model scores every response token. The [per-position token scoring RFC #56860](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56860) and its implementations for [fixed-token prefill scoring #54335](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54335) and [per-row candidates #56984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56984) let the teacher return scores for caller-specified tokens at each position.

This roadmap covers the next steps on the teacher side: avoid repeated work across scoring requests, deliver scores to the trainer efficiently, and validate the path in training frameworks.

## Roadmap

| Milestone | Work | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | Bounded prefix-cache reuse for scoring requests | @LinzeShi |
| M2 | VIME integration and teacher workload baseline | @LinzeShi |
| M3 | Score reuse through AuxOutput | @LinzeShi |
| M4 | Teacher-score delivery integration | @LinzeShi |
| M5 | Requested-candidate integration under tensor parallelism | @LinzeShi |
| M6 | Multi-turn and verl validation | @LinzeShi |

### M1. Bounded prefix-cache reuse

Scoring requests currently skip prefix-cache reads, because cached KV does not include the logits needed for scoring.

- [ ] Implement the [bounded prefix reuse RFC #60366](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60366): with `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False`, reuse cached blocks before `prompt_logprob_start` and compute every requested score. Preserve the no-read default.
- [ ] Cover cache boundaries, candidate order and padding, chunked prefill and preemption. Measure teacher scoring latency against uncached execution.

Implementation and validation: [bounded prefix reuse PR #62176](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62176).

The first version uses MRV2 and supports text token inputs, one causal full-attention KV group, unquantized KV, `max_tokens=1`, and single-GPU or tensor-parallel execution. Unsupported configurations recompute the full prompt. With Qwen3-32B at TP=4 on 4×A100, teacher scoring is 3.7x to 3.8x faster for long shared documents and about 1.1x faster for short math prompts.

### M2. VIME integration

- [ ] Extend [VIME's per-position OPD teacher scoring #467](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/467) with a bounded-reuse option tied to engine versions that implement M1. Older engines accept `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False` but can return no scores after a cache hit.
- [ ] Establish a teacher-serving baseline with a 32B-class dense teacher. Set numerical tolerances and compare score lengths, masks, loss and gradients with uncached scoring in a short training run before enabling reuse in training. Record queueing, scoring time, transfer, cache hits and trainer wait time.

### M3. Score reuse through AuxOutput

M3 has two parts, using the [AuxOutput Connector RFC #45221](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45221) and the [structured AuxOutput response RFC #61291](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61291):

- [ ] **M3a: Score format and publication.** Publish newly computed scores with their causal prefix, row positions, candidate IDs/order, padding, scoring mode, model/adapter identity and weight version. Row `i` predicts token `i + 1`. Preserve cache namespace isolation. Extend the shared score-only configuration from [prompt and generation logprob AuxOutput support #60789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60789) and [logprob AuxOutput support #61953](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61953) to per-position candidates.
- [ ] **M3b: Cached-score execution.** Acquire both KV and the required score artifacts before skipping computation. Missing or evicted scores use the M1 boundary. Add connector admission support: M1 currently recomputes the full prompt when AuxOutput is enabled.

Start with fixed teacher weights and bounded score storage. Cache reset invalidates the associated scores. Cover candidate mismatches, eviction races, cancellation and preemption. The related AuxOutput interfaces are still evolving; M1 and M2 can ship independently.

### M4. Teacher-score delivery integration

- [ ] Integrate structured AuxOutput responses and transports such as the [Mooncake AuxOutput backend #57968](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57968) for large score matrices. Keep the current inline Base64 format for small results.
- [ ] Implement result retrieval, release and cancellation, keeping decoder buffers alive until the trainer finishes using them. Measure copy, serialization, transfer and time until the tensor is usable.

M4 uses the M3a format for newly computed scores and can proceed before M3b. AuxOutput requests retain full recomputation until cache/connector compatibility is validated in M3b.

### M5. Requested-candidate integration under tensor parallelism

Each TP rank computes normalization statistics over its vocabulary shard and exchanges only requested candidate logits and normalization statistics, instead of gathering full-vocabulary logits. Exact probabilities still require full-vocabulary normalization.

- [ ] Extend a compatible shared projection/reduction interface from [fused vocabulary-parallel projection #53267](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53267) or [distributed prompt logprobs #54575](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54575) to per-position candidates.
- [ ] Validate candidate order, padding and scoring offsets at TP=1/2/4. Measure communication, peak memory and scoring latency, retaining the gathered path as fallback.

### M6. Multi-turn and verl validation

- [ ] Add a verl integration for student/teacher pairs sharing token-ID semantics, starting with the actual-token objective in its [teacher manager](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/18cfb74852a053a27dcf301d3318a093be81b628/verl/experimental/teacher_loop/teacher_manager.py). Keep teacher-selected top-k objectives separate from caller-supplied candidate scoring.
- [ ] Validate supported combinations on multi-turn trajectories, including tool observations, response masks and repeated scoring. Record teacher utilization and queueing to guide deployment work.

## Dependencies

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M1["M1: Bounded prefix reuse"] --> M2["M2: VIME integration"]
    M1 --> M3b["M3b: Cached-score execution"]
    M3a["M3a: Score format and publication"] --> M3b
    M3a --> M4["M4: Score delivery integration"]
    M2 --> M6["M6: Multi-turn and verl validation"]
    M5["M5: TP candidate integration"]
```

Arrows show code/interface prerequisites. M3a and M3b are parts of M3. M3a can start independently of M1; M4 needs its format and publisher, not M3b's cache path. M5 is independent of score storage and transport. M2 supplies evaluation workloads for M3, M4 and M5. M6 starts after M2 and adds coverage as those milestones land, including supported combinations.

## Related work

- Scoring-only requests (`max_tokens=0`), proposed in the [per-position token scoring RFC #56860](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56860).
- The [prompt-scoring cache-boundary PR #60960](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60960) explores related prefix-cache reuse.
- [Multi-teacher GPU sharing in verl #7307](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7307) and the [engine sleep/wake/drain lifecycle RFC #48311](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48311).
- The [RL weight-update roadmap #58906](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58906) covers moving or self-distilled teachers. Stored scores are not reused across weight updates.

cc @aoshen02

items.title: [Perf] Fuse GLM-5.x MoE finalize into the next RMSNorm's all-reduce
items.author: haosdent
items.summary: Fuses GLM-5.x MoE finalize into the next RMSNorm all-reduce via a FlashInfer kernel, reducing three per-layer kernels to one and improving decode throughput.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

GLM-5.x (the `DeepseekV32` NVIDIA path) now leaves each decode MoE layer's top-k reduction open. The next RMSNorm's
fused all-reduce then finalizes it in one FlashInfer kernel (`trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion`). This uses
the existing deferred-finalize contract (`MoEOutput`, `defer_moe_finalize`) that DeepSeek-V4.1 and Kimi-K3 already
use.

**Needs flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630 (deadlock fix) and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631 (speed); draft until a
FlashInfer release with both is pinned.** Without the first the kernel can hang under back-to-back launches; without the
second, deferring is slower than the unfused path.

## Claims

With the FlashInfer fixes, on GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3, B300:

- Target verify forward (`vllm bench forward`, spread < 0.1%): -1.2% to -1.3% at 1 request, -1.5% at 3, -0.8% at 7.
  Serving decode at batch 1: -1.2% ms/token.
- Per MoE layer, the GEMM2 tail is one kernel instead of three: finalize, shared + routed add, all-reduce +
  residual + RMSNorm.
- Accuracy: GSM8K unchanged within run-to-run noise (see below). The fused kernel accumulates in FP32.

## Validation

- New `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_allreduce_rms_norm.py`: a `MoEOutput` holding an `UnfinalizedMoEOutput`
  through `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` must match finalize, shared add, then `RMSNorm(all_reduce(.))`. It runs on TP
  1, 2 and 4, with 1, 4 and 64 tokens, hidden 2048 and 6144, on both the fused kernel (checking it was called) and
  the fallback. Result on B300 with the FlashInfer fixes: 30 passed, 6 skipped (TP=1 has no fused path).
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103), GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3, `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, on top of the other GLM-5 decode changes
  (#62170, #62171, #62172). "fix only" is FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, "fix + perf" adds
  flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631.

  Target verify forward, `vllm bench forward` (dummy weights, exact shapes, CUDA graph), us:

  | shape (requests x 4 tokens @ KV) | no deferral | deferral, fix only | deferral, fix + perf |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8570.1 | 8618.4 (+0.56%) | 8464.4 (-1.23%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12075.2 | 12128.4 (+0.44%) | 11891.7 (-1.52%) |
  | 5x4 @25K | 15470.2 | 15784.6 (+2.03%) | 15357.2 (-0.73%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17472.5 | 17849.5 (+2.16%) | 17337.3 (-0.77%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8639.5 | 8676.0 (+0.42%) | 8528.0 (-1.29%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12267.1 | 12318.9 (+0.42%) | 12081.3 (-1.51%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 17785.9 | 18160.8 (+2.11%) | 17644.7 (-0.79%) |

  Serving decode ms/token (synthetic acceptance length 3.0, median of 9), batch 1: 3.131 -> 3.094 at 25K and
  3.169 -> 3.131 at 94K (-1.2%) with fix + perf; 3.158 / 3.182 (slower) with fix only.

  nsys node-level trace, batch-1 verify graph per step: `finalizeKernel` (297 us) and most of the
  shared + routed add (elementwise 217 -> 70 us) are gone; finalize + all-reduce + norm 1438 -> 1265 us.

  GSM8K (lm_eval, 5-shot, 1319 questions, real MTP verification, concurrency 32), flexible / strict:

  | | run 1 | run 2 |
  |---|---|---|
  | main | 0.9439 / 0.9424 | 0.9439 / 0.9424 |
  | this PR (with all the changes above) | 0.9401 / 0.9401 | 0.9447 / 0.9424 |

  (stderr 0.0063). Greedy outputs differ from main: the finalize now rounds once instead of after each step.

## Details

- `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` accepts a `MoEOutput`. If the routed part is unfinalized, and TP > 1 with the TRT-LLM
  workspace in use, it calls `trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion`, which does the top-k sum, routed scaling,
  shared add, all-reduce, residual add and RMSNorm. Otherwise it finalizes in torch and takes the normal path.
- `moe_finalize_allreduce_max_num_tokens` bounds deferral by the kernel's one-shot limit (128 tokens) and by the
  size up to which vLLM already picks the one-shot all-reduce. Above that, or when the backend isn't `trtllm`, the
  layer finalizes as before.
- A decoder layer defers only when its experts are TRT-LLM-Gen (NVFP4 or BF16 monolithic/modular, the ones that
  can stop after GEMM2), it isn't sequence parallel, and the router doesn't fold `routed_scaling_factor` in. Each
  local layer defers except the last one on a non-last PP rank, since its output leaves as `IntermediateTensors`.
  Layers that feed an aux hidden state (EAGLE-3) don't defer. The MTP block defers into its final norm.
- `_forward_impl` and `_unpack` are used directly, as in `deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py`, because the runner's
  custom op returns tensors only.

items.title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Capture every small decode request count by default
items.author: haosdent
items.summary: Changes speculative decoding to capture CUDA graphs for every small decode batch size (1–8) by default, eliminating power-of-two padding overhead and improving per-request throughput.
items.body:
## Overview

With speculative decoding, the default CUDA graph sizes now include every decode batch of 1 to 8 requests. Small
batches stop padding to the next power of two, which runs 1 + K extra tokens per padded request through every
layer.

## Claims

- With MTP K=3, 3, 5 and 7 running requests replay 12-, 20- and 28-token graphs instead of 16, 24 and 32. GLM-5.2-
  NVFP4, TP4, B300: decode -6% to -7% at 3 requests, -2.5% to -3.4% at 5, -2.2% to -2.4% at 7, unchanged at 1.
- Three extra decode graphs (and their piecewise twins) for K=3: capture 6 s -> 7 s, graph memory 0.61 -> 0.65 GiB per GPU.
- Without speculation, and for explicit `cudagraph_capture_sizes`, nothing changes.

## Validation

- `tests/compile/test_config.py -k keep_all_sizes_bounded` (expected request grid updated) and
  `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py` pass. On B300, `tests/compile/test_config.py -k cudagraph` has 12
  failures, the same 12 as on main on that machine (`unchanged_without_speculation`, `respects_platform_ceiling`,
  `still_clamped_by_token_budget`, `test_use_cudagraphs`), so unrelated to this change.
- End to end: B300 x4 (SM103), GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP K=3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count),
  `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, default CUDA graph sizes. Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of
  (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts:

  | context | requests | before | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.094 | 3.097 |
  | 25K | 3 | 4.300 | 3.991 (-7.2%) |
  | 25K | 5 | 5.134 | 5.007 (-2.5%) |
  | 25K | 7 | 5.662 | 5.540 (-2.2%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.131 | 3.119 |
  | 94K | 3 | 4.370 | 4.097 (-6.2%) |
  | 94K | 5 | 5.265 | 5.087 (-3.4%) |
  | 94K | 7 | 5.788 | 5.647 (-2.4%) |

  (Measured on top of other GLM-5 decode changes; this PR touches only the capture sizes.) On GB200 with an
  explicit list of every request count up to 32, 3 requests went from 4.145 to 3.944 ms/token at 40K and AgentX
  c=8 throughput rose 1.7%.

## Details

For speculative decoding, `_set_cudagraph_sizes` appends a request-count grid times `decode_query_len` (1 + K).
That grid started 1, 2, 4, 8, copied from the one-token grid, where padding 3 requests to 4 costs one token. A
decode request is 1 + K tokens, so the same padding costs 1 + K tokens. Padded tokens still go through the
attention, the GEMMs and the MoE (routed like real tokens), and at small batches decode is bound by those layers.
The token grid's 8-token stride already yields even request counts at K=3, so this adds 3, 5 and 7 requests there.

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Let cooperative_topk read the BF16 indexer logits
items.author: haosdent
items.summary: Allows cooperative_topk to read BF16 logits directly on SM100, eliminating an FP32 upcast kernel and halving memory reads during paged MQA decode.
items.body:
## Overview

Stacked on #62171 (row-length single pass); only the last commit is new.

`cooperative_topk` now also reads BF16 logits. On SM100 the DSA indexer then keeps the paged MQA logits in BF16
instead of upcasting them to FP32 before the decode top-k. This extends what main already does for
`deep_select`.

## Claims

- One fewer kernel per indexer decode call on SM100/SM103 (the FP32 upcast `as_fp32_logits`), and the top-k reads
  half the bytes.
- The selected top-k values are the same as from the FP32 upcast: BF16 widens to FP32 exactly. Among exactly
  equal logits, which index wins was already unspecified.
- DCP, top-k backends that take only FP32, and BF16 rows that are not 16-byte aligned still upcast as before.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` on B300 (SM103): 285 passed, 37 skipped.
  - `test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride` now runs FP32 and BF16 logits through every cluster size and
    both paths. It compares the selected values with `torch.topk` and checks that no index repeats.
  - `test_sparse_indexer_topk_backend_resolution` checks when BF16 logits skip the upcast: `auto` or `cooperative`
    within the row limit, with a 16-byte-aligned stride. `persistent` and over-limit batches still upcast.
- Kernel time on B300 is the same for BF16 and FP32 input (10.3 us at 4 rows x 40K, 11.1 us at 16 rows), so the
  saving is the upcast kernel and its extra pass over the logits.
- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300, on top of #62170 and #62171:

  | shape | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8630.6 | 8589.8 (-0.47%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12136.9 | 12090.4 (-0.38%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17547.7 | 17497.8 (-0.28%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8702.3 | 8654.3 (-0.55%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12361.1 | 12284.4 (-0.62%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 17940.9 | 17806.9 (-0.75%) |

  In an nsys node-level trace of the batch-1 verify graph, `_upcast_logits_kernel` (36 us per step) is gone.

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%), on top of #62170 and #62171:

  | context | B | before | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.145 | 3.132 (-0.4%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.190 | 3.167 (-0.7%) |
  | 94K | 7 | 5.814 | 5.740 (-1.3%) |

## Details

- `CooperativeTopKParams`, the TMA staging buffers and the histogram loads are templated on the input type.
- TMA units are 16 bytes (8 BF16 or 4 FP32 elements), so the stride and per-block alignment follow the element
  size.
- Scores are widened to FP32 when binned, so both input types use the same radix keys.
- The extension dispatches on `logits.scalar_type()`.
- `SparseIndexerTopk.takes_bf16_logits` reports whether the resolved backend reads BF16 directly: `cooperative`
  (also as `auto`'s choice) when its constraints hold, and `deep_select`. The indexer upcasts only when it doesn't
  or when DCP is on. This replaces main's `topk_backend != "deep_select"` check with the same rule extended to
  `cooperative`.
- Candidate-block selection (DeepSeek-V4.1) already handles BF16 logits under `deep_select`. With `cooperative` it
  now gets them too. I could not run that model here.

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Size cooperative_topk's single pass by row length, not stride
items.author: haosdent
items.summary: Optimizes cooperative_topk kernel to select single-pass path by row length instead of stride, reducing TMA streaming overhead and improving decode throughput up to 8% on B300.
items.body:
## Overview

`cooperative_topk` now chooses between its single-pass and two-pass paths from each row's length instead of the
logits row stride. Rows that fit the single-pass staging no longer stream through TMA twice just because the
buffer is wide (`max_model_len`).

## Claims

- On B300, the decode top-k for rows that fit the single-pass staging is up to 8% faster when the logits stride is
  larger than the per-block staging, for example `max_model_len` 1M at 1-8 rows, or about 200K at 9-64 rows.
- Selection is unchanged: both paths compute the same exact radix top-k.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k cooperative` on B300 (SM103): 73 passed, 6 skipped.
- The new `test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride` covers every cluster size (1, 4, 8, 33 and 64 rows) with
  strides of 64K and 1M. Its rows are 300 to 300K tokens long, so one launch mixes trivial, register, single-pass
  and streaming rows. It compares the selected values with `torch.topk`.
- Microbenchmark: `cooperative_topk`, k=2048, rows = batch x 4 (MTP), CUDA graph replay, B300:

  | rows | context | stride | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 4 | 40K | 1M | 10.99 | 10.27 |
  | 4 | 40K | 64K | 10.25 | 10.16 |
  | 4 | 150K | 1M | 12.98 | 12.11 |
  | 4 | 150K | 160K | 12.21 | 12.10 |
  | 16 | 40K | 1M | 12.18 | 11.24 |
  | 16 | 40K | 256K | 12.10 | 11.18 |
  | 16 | 40K | 64K | 11.27 | 11.09 |

- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300, on top of #62170:

  | shape | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8696.4 | 8630.6 (-0.76%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12231.4 | 12136.9 (-0.77%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17649.7 | 17547.7 (-0.58%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8799.6 | 8702.3 (-1.11%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12532.0 | 12361.1 (-1.36%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 18116.0 | 17940.9 (-0.97%) |

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%), on top of #62170:

  | context | B | before | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.171 | 3.145 (-0.8%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.207 | 3.190 (-0.5%) |

## Details

The DSA indexer allocates its decode logits with `max_model_len` columns, and `cooperative_topk` gets that as
`stride`. The kernel sized `per_block` (elements per CTA of the cluster) from the stride. But `large_topk` splits
the row by its actual length (`seq_len`, in 16-byte units across the cluster ranks). With a long `max_model_len`,
every row took the two-pass streaming path even when its context fit the all-stages-resident single pass. For
example, 16 rows use 4-CTA clusters, and a 256K stride gives 64K elements per block, above the 48K single-pass
staging, while a 40K-token row needs only 10K per block.

`per_block` now uses the same split `large_topk` uses, so each row picks its path from its own length. Rows in one
launch can take different paths. Each row is its own cluster, and the barrier setup already follows the chosen
path.

items.title: [Perf] Emit the DSA indexer weights in BF16 on SM100
items.author: haosdent
items.summary: On SM100, now writes the DSA indexer weights directly in BF16, the dtype DeepGEMM's MQA logits kernels take. This removes the FP32 to BF16 copy launched on every indexer call.
items.body:
## Overview

On SM100, `fused_q` now writes the DSA indexer weights directly in BF16, the dtype DeepGEMM's MQA logits kernels
take. This removes the FP32 to BF16 copy `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` launched on every indexer call.

## Claims

- One fewer kernel per indexer call (prefill chunks and decode) on SM100/SM103 for DSA models using `fused_q`
  (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x). The logits are bit-identical: the weights are still computed in FP32 and rounded to
  BF16 once, just inside `fused_q` instead of in a separate copy.
- Other platforms are unchanged (FP32 weights).

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py` on B300 (SM103): 214 passed, 8 skipped. The weight
  assertions now check BF16 output on SM100 and FP32 elsewhere.
- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300:

  | shape | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8724.8 | 8696.4 (-0.33%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12264.2 | 12231.4 (-0.27%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17688.4 | 17649.7 (-0.22%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8829.5 | 8799.6 (-0.34%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12561.0 | 12532.0 (-0.23%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 18148.9 | 18116.0 (-0.18%) |

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%):

  | context | B | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.182 | 3.171 (-0.3%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.227 | 3.207 (-0.6%) |

  Batches of 3-7 move within the measurement noise (about ±1.5%).

## Details

`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()` already decides that the SM100 logits kernels take BF16 weights, and
`mqa_logits_mx_inputs` returned `weights.to(torch.bfloat16)`. That was a real copy kernel for every indexer call,
since `fused_q` (Triton and CuTeDSL) always wrote FP32. `fused_q` now allocates its weights output in the dtype the
logits kernels take, and both kernels cast on store. `.to(torch.bfloat16)` then returns the tensor as-is.

The CuTeDSL kernel's compile key gains the output dtype.

items.title: [Feature] kv-shard: Pass Q instead of KV for short prefills with long cached prefixes
items.author: Shunkangz
items.summary: Today, extend batches are zigzag-split across all ranks, and every request’s prefix KV is all-gathered to every rank one layer ahead. For agentic and multi-turn workloads, a short prefill often extends a long cached prefix, so prefix KV dominates communication…
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Background

With `--enable-kv-cache-sharding`, each CP rank stores \(1/N\) of every cached prefix. Today, extend batches are zigzag-split across all ranks, and every request’s prefix KV is all-gathered to every rank one layer ahead.

For agentic and multi-turn workloads, a short prefill often extends a long cached prefix, so prefix KV dominates communication. DCP avoids this for decode by passing Q instead of KV, but directly applying it to prefill would replicate new-token computation across ranks.

## Overall Design

Use **per-request placement**: each request has one home CP rank that computes all its new tokens. Choose the communication policy per request based on \(P/T\):

- Pass-KV for short prefixes: the home fetches only its requests’ prefix stripes via all-to-all.
- Pass-Q for long prefixes: all-gather Q, attend over each rank’s local prefix stripes, and return partial outputs and LSE to the home for merging with its causal new-token attention.

Overlap both pass-Q collectives with the home’s local attention and use copy-engine transfers for large messages. In the 8× B200 per-layer harness, exposed communication is 0.1–1.2% of layer time at 128K–256K prefixes; choosing pass-Q when \(P/T > 128\) is within 1.9% of the best measured split on average.

## PR Stack

The following PRs will be released soon.

### 1/5 — Enable FA4 for GQA KV Sharding and Fix Sharded KV Writes

- Enable FA4 for GQA KV sharding on Blackwell.
- Fix a silent wrong-logits bug where fused RoPE + KV writes bypass the sharded pool on short extends, affecting both FA3 and FA4.
- Validation: sharded and unsharded outputs are bit-exact at CP4.

### 2/5 — Add Symmetric-Memory Transports for Pass-Q Attention

- Add `PassQCommunicator` with variable-size Q all-gather, partial O + LSE all-to-all, and LSE merging.
- Support Triton SM-push and copy-engine transports using Torch symmetric memory.
- Add multi-GPU tests.

### 3/5 — Add Per-Request CP Placement for Prefill

- Assign whole requests to CP ranks when the batch can be balanced, using one FA call per rank.
- Fetch only each rank’s own requests’ prefix stripes via all-to-all instead of all-gathering every prefix.
- Validation: sharded and unsharded outputs are bit-exact at CP4 with B=4.
- Reduce latency versus zigzag placement by 8 ms unsharded and 5 ms sharded at 32K/64K.

### 4/5 — Pass Q Instead of KV for Long-Prefix Requests

- Add `--kv-shard-pass-q-ratio` for per-request P/T policy selection.
- Add pass-Q-aware placement, including B < N, and pool stripe tables.
- Implement Q all-gather, local prefix-stripe attention, partial O + LSE all-to-all, and merging.
- Start with a serial schedule.

### 5/5 — Overlap Pass-Q Communication with Local Attention

- Run communication on a side stream.
- Split the home rank’s local attention across both collectives to **overlap** communication and computation.
- Select the transport by message size.
- Run end-to-end A/B validation at CP8.

### Related resources

_No response_

items.title: [Perf] [Intel] gemma4: Fuse greedy verification logits finalization
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Fuses greedy verification logits finalization in Gemma4 MTP on Intel XPU, eliminating FP32 logits materialization via a new BF16 softcap_argmax kernel.
items.body:
Stacked on #44869; the performance comparison uses that parent branch as its control.

## Motivation

Gemma4 MTP verification on Intel XPU converts BF16 vocabulary logits to FP32, softcaps them, and reduces them to greedy token IDs. Fuse this finalization into two reductions over the existing BF16 head output for eligible greedy verification batches. Model weights and the head GEMM remain unchanged.

## Modifications

- Add an XPU BF16 `sampling.softcap_argmax` kernel with Meta support. Preserve FP32 softcap ordering, saturation ties, first-index tie breaking, and nonfinite handling.
- Let Gemma4 defer FP32 conversion and softcap for local no-gather FrozenKV target verification. Preserve and slice deferred output through graph replay, then check the current sampling requirements after replay.
- Use compact token IDs only for eligible greedy requests. Restore ordinary logits through the original softcap helper for logprobs, sampling, penalties, bias, grammar, watermarking, diagnostics, and other unsupported processing.

The optimization requires no logits or hidden-state gather; serving validation below uses TP1. It eliminates FP32 logits materialization on the eligible path; existing graph buffers remain allocated. No new flag is required.

## Accuracy Tests

- 15 same-GPU control/candidate serving cases matched exactly: greedy output, returned token logprobs, and repetition-penalty/logit-bias/min-new-token fallbacks.
- Official GSM8K, 200 questions, temperature 0, seed 42: control **163/200 (81.5%)**, candidate **165/200 (82.5%)**, zero errors. Truncations: one control, two candidate. These requests exercise the fused greedy path. This small difference is not a quality-improvement claim.
- Official GSM8K candidate temperature 1 compatibility run: **165/200 (82.5%)**, zero errors, one truncation. This run exercises materialized-logits fallback and does not validate the fused greedy path.
- Four XPU kernel tests passed, including softcap saturation, NaNs/infinities, signed zero, chunk-boundary ties, strides, Meta validation, lazy-dispatch lifecycle, and graph replay with changed inputs.
- Three dedicated CPU policy/fallback tests passed; broader CPU dispatch/policy checks passed 110 tests and 15 subtests. Pre-commit passed.

Changing batch schedules can change generated texts: the c32 control repetitions differed on 44/128 texts, and candidate repetitions differed on 46/128. Exact kernel and controlled serving parity do not establish arbitrary batch-independent model equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same Intel XPU, pinned Gemma4 E2B BF16 checkpoint, TP1, MTP draft steps 3 / top-k 1 / draft tokens 4, full graph capture, overlap disabled, page size 64, max running requests 64, context 8192, static memory fraction 0.70. Compare this commit against its parent norm/RoPE branch. Each server switch received a 128-request c32 warmup with 256 output tokens. Measurements use control/candidate/candidate/control order; c1 has 64 requests per run, c8/c32 have 128, all with 256 output tokens and seed 42. All 12 runs completed without request errors and had identical input/output token counts.

Mean TPOT, milliseconds:

| Concurrency | Control A | Candidate A | Candidate B | Control B | Improvement vs final control | Improvement vs mean controls |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.1377 | 4.1205 | 4.1080 | 4.1200 | 0.139% | 0.354% |
| 8 | 6.0779 | 6.0207 | 6.0189 | 6.0312 | 0.189% | 0.574% |
| 32 | 11.4920 | 11.0764 | 10.9266 | 11.2300 | **2.035%** | **3.164%** |

At c32, control A to control B improved by **2.28%**, so final-control comparison is conservative. Both candidate repetitions beat final control. C1/c8 are effectively flat at this resolution. On the 56/128 c32 requests with identical texts across all four runs, mean streaming-time improvement was 2.799%; this subset does not remove between-run drift.

A real c32 serving profile records 16 fused partial/final reduction kernels (2.429 ms total), confirming serving dispatch. Head-plus-finalization microbenchmarks show larger gains but do not represent end-to-end serving gains.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add CPU and registered XPU kernel tests.
- [x] Document scope/fallback behavior in code and this description; no new configuration.
- [x] Provide accuracy, serving benchmark, and profiling results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

items.title: [Feat][NPU] enable device-side multimodal feature transport via torch_npu IPC
items.author: sanqiannianyiqian
items.summary: currently requires NVIDIA CUDA: the feature pool, proxy lifecycle, and device primitives are hardcoded against and CUDA IPC handles. On Ascend NPU, multimodal features produced by the tokenizer process must therefore detour through host memory (CPU transport) …
items.body:
Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Single-node device-side feature transport — provide an NPU-capable alternative to CUDA IPC for transferring multimodal feature tensors between local processes*).

## Motivation

`--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` currently requires NVIDIA CUDA: the feature pool, proxy lifecycle, and device primitives are hardcoded against `torch.cuda.*` and CUDA IPC handles. On Ascend NPU, multimodal features produced by the tokenizer process must therefore detour through host memory (CPU transport) even when both processes sit on the same node and the features already live in device HBM.

This PR makes the existing `cuda_ipc` transport NPU-capable with **zero behavior change on CUDA**. CUDA keeps the bounded pool + lease/ACK design unchanged; NPU follows the official torch_npu IPC recipe (`docs/memory_sharing_ipc.md`, method two): `torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor` → `rebuild_npu_tensor`, using public APIs only (no undocumented ACL calls).

## Design

- **No new CLI option**: NPU reuses the existing `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` entry, gated per platform.
- **Features never leave NPU HBM**: the producer packs `(rebuild_func, args)` via the public `reduce_tensor` and pickles it into `proxy_state["ipc_extra"]["npu_ipc_payload"]` — a ~377 B descriptor regardless of feature size. The consumer rebuilds the tensor on its own device by redirecting the storage device index (`args[6]`), guarded by a layout/type check so an upstream layout change degrades with a warning instead of silently corrupting an unrelated argument.
- **No pool on NPU**: zero HBM reservation, no lease/ACK bookkeeping; the KV-cache budget is no longer deducted for a pool that does not exist.
- **Platform branches stay in one place**: the new `srt/multimodal/transport/npu_ipc_bridge.py` hosts `IS_NPU` detection, the torch_npu `reductions` patch import (single side-effect point), device primitives (`make_device` / `current_device` / `device_guard` / `is_device_tensor`), and the pack/rebuild pair. All other touched files stay host-agnostic.

## Roadmap item coverage

| Roadmap requirement | How it is covered |
|---|---|
| Bounded memory use | No pool on NPU → zero HBM reservation; `kv_cache_configurator` skips the pool deduction on NPU, recovering ~2–3 GB of usable KV |
| Tensor lifetime | torch_npu ref-counter keeps the shared block alive while consumers exist; rebuilt tensors verified bitwise-identical even after the producer drops its source tensor |
| Cancellation | `cancel_proxy` handles NPU proxies on the processor rollback path |
| Pool exhaustion | Not applicable — NPU has no pool; the failure mode is `reduce_tensor` raising, which falls back to the CPU transport |
| Fallback to CPU path | `wrap_tensor` returns `None` on any pack failure → CPU transport; A/B runs show 0 fallbacks |
| Transfer cost & TTFT comparison | Benchmarks below |

## Modifications

- **NEW** `srt/multimodal/transport/npu_ipc_bridge.py` (112 lines): platform detection + patch import, device primitives, `npu_ipc_pack_tensor` / `npu_ipc_rebuild_tensor` with `args[6]` redirect + layout guard
- `srt/multimodal/transport/cuda_ipc.py`: NPU branches on the shared transport — producer pack + proxy shell, `cancel_proxy`, `_restore_npu_ipc_proxy_state`, consumer rebuild in `reconstruct_on_target_device` (cached, returns before the CUDA-pool fields), borrow/lease paths report unsupported so the scheduler falls back to reconstruct
- `srt/utils/msgpack_utils.py`: call `_restore_npu_ipc_proxy_state` after msgpack decode
- `srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py`: gate device-IPC wrapping on `is_device_tensor`; skip CUDA-pool reservation logs on NPU
- `srt/models/qwen3_vl.py`: resolve the visual-tower device via the bridge; treat `cuda`/`npu` alike in the on-device check
- `srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`: skip the pool KV deduction on NPU
- `srt/arg_groups/serving_hook.py`: platform check relaxation + per-platform pool-reservation logs

On CUDA, every modified call site either executes identical code or is unreachable — behavior is unchanged.

## Benchmarks (Ascend 910, CANN 9.1.0, torch_npu 2.10.0, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking)

Transfer-level, two processes, 16 producer threads, in-flight depth 8, 800 frames per group:

| Feature size | CPU ms/frame | NPU IPC ms/frame | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5 MiB | 0.98 | 0.52 | 46.8% |
| 18.4 MiB | 13.07 | 0.54 | 95.9% |
| 47.6 MiB | 56.30 | 0.52 | 99.1% |

IPC cost is constant (~0.52 ms/frame — only the 377 B descriptor crosses processes) while CPU transfer is strictly linear in feature size.

End-to-end (4×1024² images per request, 16 concurrency, 90 s): 0 errors and 0 fallbacks on both arms; p50 delta −13.5% is within the noise band (p99 +11.1%, single round, transfer explains ~0.4% of end-to-end latency at this scale) and is not claimed as a win.

Accuracy: MMBench EN DEV v1.1, 1292 questions, CircularEval, greedy decoding, `cuda_ipc` vs `cpu` on the same node with a position-swap control over 3 rounds — no transport-induced accuracy delta (observed ±0.7 pp shifts do not follow the transport arm and flip sign after swapping dies).

## Test plan

- [x] `py_compile` on all touched files
- [x] Functional smoke on Ascend: real image request end-to-end, `NPU IPC rebuild success` in scheduler log, 0 CPU fallbacks / 0 tracebacks
- [x] Cross-process bitwise consistency of rebuilt tensors
- [x] 16-concurrency A/B (`cuda_ipc` vs `cpu`): 0 errors, 0 fallbacks on both arms
- [x] MMBench accuracy A/B as above

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Chunk sparse indexer decode logits by request
items.author: booth-algo
items.summary: Chunks sparse indexer decode logits by request to bound per-chunk memory usage, freeing GPU memory for KV cache without accuracy loss.
items.body:
## Overview

> **Draft, not ready for review.** The submitter's line-by-line review is still pending. I will mark this ready once that is done.

The CUDA sparse-indexer decode path scores the whole batch into one fp32 `[batch * next_n, max_model_len]` logits tensor. Full CUDA graphs keep that tensor in their pool, while the profiling run reserves only `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` for it. This PR scores whole requests in chunks bounded by that budget, as the prefill path already does. At long context with many sequences, this frees several GiB per GPU for KV cache.

## Claims

- Decode logits never exceed `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` (default 512 MiB) per chunk on SM90/SM120. At least one whole request goes into each chunk.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8x RTX PRO 6000, TP8, 1M context, 1,024 sequences: the CUDA graph pool drops from 12.45 to 3.09 GiB per GPU, and KV cache capacity grows 2.12x (6.31M to 13.39M tokens).
- Accuracy is unchanged (GSM8K 0.901 before, 0.904 after, with 1,024 concurrent requests so the chunked path runs).
- Nothing changes when the batch fits in one chunk. Varlen decode (SM100), DCP and XPU keep the single full-batch call.

## Validation

**End to end.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition (SM120). Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`; the files under test are identical to current `main`. Both arms add #60762 on top, because without it V4.1 cannot boot on SM120 (#59203). This PR does not depend on #60762.

`vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}' --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`

| Arm | CUDA graph pool / GPU (actual) | Available KV memory / GPU | GPU KV cache size | GSM8K accuracy, 3 runs (mean) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main + #60762 | 12.45 GiB | 13.10 GiB | 6,306,185 tokens (6.01x of 1M) | 0.901 / 0.904 / 0.901 (0.902) |
| main + #60762 + this PR | 3.09 GiB | 27.82 GiB | 13,392,984 tokens (12.77x of 1M) | 0.895 / 0.900 / 0.917 (0.904) |

GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 1024`.

- Every run had 0 client errors and at most 0.001 invalid responses.
- Running requests peaked at 1,024 (sampled from `/metrics`), so the patched runs took the chunked path.
- The spread within each arm comes from batch-order nondeterminism at temperature 0.
- The memory figures are identical across the two boots of each arm.

**Unit tests.** All on SM120 in the same image:

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py`: 25 passed, 18 of them new.
- The new test compares chunked against full-batch top-k through the real `sparse_attn_indexer` entry point. It covers `next_n` 1/2, top-k 128/512/2048, and candidate blocks off/write/read. It also covers a zero-length request and an incomplete last chunk.
- Every chunk's allocation must stay within a 1 MiB budget.
- A captured CUDA graph is replayed after context lengths and weights change.
- Negative control: the new test fails 18/18 against unpatched `main`, with one unchunked allocation of 2,359,296 or 4,718,592 bytes.
- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py`: 174 passed, 12 skipped. The result is the same with and without this PR.
- `pre-commit` passes.

**Not covered:**

- SM90 was not run locally. The new test runs in CI in the "(H100) DeepGEMM Kernels" step.
- SM100 is not exercised. Its varlen path is unchanged, and the new test skips there.
- The FP4 indexer cache and XPU are not tested on hardware.

## Details

**Root cause.** The decode branch calls `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` once for the whole batch. For V4.1 at 1M context, each row has 262,144 compressed columns (1 MiB of fp32). During FULL-graph capture, that allocation is made at the captured batch size and stays in the graph pool. The profiling run's dummy allocation reserves only `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, and prefill is already chunked to that budget, but decode was not. The measured pool shrinks by 9.36 GiB per GPU. That is more than one 1 GiB logits tensor; I have not broken it down per captured size.

**Change.**

- `chunk_size = max(1, budget // (next_n * max_model_len * 4))` requests.
- Each chunk slices Q, Q scales, weights, block-table rows, candidate rows and top-k rows.
- Each chunk rebuilds its DeepGEMM schedule metadata from its own context lengths. It uses `get_num_sms()`, DeepGEMM's current SM count, which dual-batch overlap lowers. That is the count the kernel checks the metadata against (the full-batch case of this is #60732).
- Each chunk's logits are freed before the next chunk is allocated.
- The chunk size depends only on shapes, so it adds no host sync, and graph capture stays deterministic. The test captures the chunked path in a graph.
- The extra cost is one small metadata kernel per chunk per indexer layer, paid only when the batch is larger than one chunk.
- GSM8K throughput was the same in both arms: 2,339–2,541 output tok/s patched, against 2,313–2,556 unpatched, over 3 runs each. This is not a performance claim.

**Scope.**

- SM100 decode is varlen (`indices`, with bf16 logits). Chunking it would need varlen-aware schedule metadata that I cannot test, so that path keeps one call.
- DCP keeps one call, because `_merge_dcp_topk_global` runs over the full rows.

**Not a duplicate.**

- #58068 fixes the prefill logits width (#55569), not decode.
- #56686 and #42856 size decode logits by `max_seq_len` for eager steps. Under graph capture, `max_seq_len` is `max_model_len`, so captured graphs keep the full width.
- Searches for open PRs on decode-logits chunking, `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` and `sparse_attn_indexer` decode memory found nothing else.
- #58536 (TP-sharded decode rows) and #60732 touch the same decode branch but solve different problems. I will rebase onto whichever lands first.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The tests and evaluations above were run as described. The submitter's line-by-line review is pending, and this PR stays a draft until it is done.
