items.title: [Feat] mem_cache: defer prefill for pending external linker lookups
items.author: feichai0017
items.summary: External linker lookups cannot currently report pending separately from a completed miss. This lets an asynchronous lookup fall through to recomputation unless a backend blocks or patches private admission internals.
items.body:
## Motivation

External linker lookups cannot currently report pending separately from a completed miss. This lets an asynchronous lookup fall through to recomputation unless a backend blocks or patches private admission internals.

Refs https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44872.

## Modifications

- Accept `None` for pending lookup and propagate `cache_lookup_pending` through the actual match result and request. Skip pending requests before PrefillAdder capacity checks, budgets, locks and loads; ready siblings remain eligible.
- Reuse slot zero of the existing sparse-boundary MIN mask for readiness. Every rank participates before deciding pending versus a terminal result; no additional collective. Cancel a miss only after all ranks are ready.
- Add a default no-op lookup-only cancellation callback for synchronous backends. Retire superseded queries/markers at native abort, session/disabled bypass, full HBM and unusable tails. Cancellation errors still preserve the existing queued/started-load cleanup responsibility.
- Update the native Scheduler LoRA set only for actually appended requests. A deferred adapter cannot block a ready sibling when max_loras_per_batch=1; an admitted adapter still occupies its slot.
- Require stable terminal results and an original finite deadline across rematches. Keep timeout/input validation and stale callback fencing in the async backend. No new payload-transfer lifecycle or default backend change.

## Accuracy Tests

165 CPU tests and 66 subtests pass; 16 CUDA-fixture cases explicitly skip. This covers actual candidate-source matching, native prefill and abort methods with local backend/allreduce collaborators, including pending/miss/hit rank combinations, changed keys, repeated polls, HBM/session bypass, force-miss and cancellation errors. Baseline controls detect pending and premature-admission gaps. All 3,722 pre-existing installed SGLang Python files remain unchanged; CUDA stays uninitialized.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python"
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=999999
export FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE=/tmp/sglang-pending-admission-cache
python -B -m pytest -q --no-showlocals --tb=short \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_cache_linker.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_prefill_memory_budget.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_force_miss.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_policy.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_policy_dfs_weight.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_hicache_transfer_lifecycle.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_held_row_admission.py
```

Source base: `bce7b27aa6aabda681351f8f4c20776981b5d5d4`. Genuine dependencies: Python 3.11.10, PyTorch 2.13.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, FlashInfer 0.6.18, NumPy 2.2.6, pytest 9.1.1. The checkout supplies SGLang modules via PYTHONPATH; the borrowed environment's installed distribution metadata is 0.5.20. Scheduler capacity/preemption checks retain their existing order before rematching; the no-budget/lock/load mutation guarantee is local to PrefillAdder. The real caller/LoRA-manager CPU control passes on this candidate and fails the old parent for the deferred-request case, while its admitted-request capacity control passes. This is source CPU testing, not installed 0.5.21 or GPU qualification. No runtime-module replacements are used. GPU/model output, physical multi-rank collectives/failures, live DMA cancellation/page reuse and released adoption remain untested; keeping this draft for contract discussion and those gates.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance claim, kernel change or inference benchmark. The existing reduction gains a readiness bit without adding a collective.

- [x] Changed files pass pinned isort 7.0.0 and Ruff 0.15.1.
- [x] Extend existing registered CPU suites.
- [x] Document pending/cancellation ownership in the public interface.
- [ ] GPU/model and physical multi-rank validation.

items.title: [Feature] Support pending external linker lookup at native prefill admission
items.author: feichai0017
items.summary: currently returns a list of restorable boundaries. It cannot distinguish a query that is still pending from a completed miss.
items.body:
### Motivation

`UnifiedCacheLinker.lookup(rid, transfers)` currently returns a list of restorable boundaries. It cannot distinguish a query that is still pending from a completed miss. An asynchronous external cache must block the scheduler or add a private prefill-admission Hook to avoid immediately recomputing a pending hit.

Could the native linker contract represent pending and carry that state through prefix matching to prefill admission? Ready requests should continue while a pending request remains queued. Rank-local readiness should use the same reduction as sparse hit boundaries, so a ready rank cannot admit while a peer still waits.

### Proposed scope

- Allow `None` for pending and keep `[]` as a completed miss.
- Carry the current match state into `PrefillAdder.add_one_req` before budgets, locks or destination loads.
- Expose lookup-only cancellation for abort and superseded/session/HBM matches; retain existing accepted-load ownership and drain.
- Count only actually admitted requests in the native LoRA batch set, so a deferred lookup cannot occupy an adapter slot.
- Keep synchronous backends unchanged. Async backends own bounded waiting, input validation and stale-completion retirement.

A candidate implementation passes actual source CPU admission/linker/lifecycle tests. GPU, real rank collectives, cancellation during DMA and released-engine adoption still need separate validation. This proposal is independent of worker pre-graph preparation in #44856.

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1: on ROCm, encoder SWA bounded replay rewrites the cached KV of the replayed tokens on every prefix hit
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: The new values are recomputed with a sliding window truncated at the replay start. Later requests that hit the same prefix read the rewritten entries instead of what the original prefill wrote.
items.body:
## Describe the bug

With `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` on ROCm, each prefix hit overwrites the cached main KV, compressed KV, and index keys of the replayed tokens (the last up to 128 cached tokens). The new values are recomputed with a sliding window truncated at the replay start. Later requests that hit the same prefix read the rewritten entries instead of what the original prefill wrote.

Found by reading the code at `ef26f6ad49`; not run on ROCm hardware.

- On ROCm, `create_dsv4_backend` selects `DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py:189-198`). It keeps `folds_encoder_swa_replay = False` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/base_attn_backend.py:66`), so `run_encoder_swa_replay` runs the replay as a separate forward (`python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py:627-632`).
- That forward's `out_cache_loc` is the replayed tokens' cached slots (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/encoder_swa_replay.py:151-153`).
- Its prefill metadata hands that `out_cache_loc` to the compressors with compression on (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py:2201-2206`). The c1/c2 and index-K stores therefore write every replayed row over its cached entry.

The CUDA backend had the same effect on its folded path. #44857 fixed it by giving the replayed rows the padding slot (`raw_out_loc` 0) as their compressor write location, which the c1/c2/index-K stores skip. On GB300, the fix was checked by comparing the replayed tokens' cached c1/c2 bytes before and after each replay prefill. Before the fix, 3,308-3,712 of 3,712 checked rows changed per prefill; after it, none changed.

Possible fix: do the same in the replay forward. When `forward_batch.encoder_swa_replay` is set, build the compressors' write locations as all zeros. The SWA write is not affected: it takes the request-window layout, not `out_cache_loc` (`deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py:3042-3048`). This needs a check that the ROCm compressor stores, including the split index-K store, skip slot 0.

## Reproduction

Not run. To check on gfx950: start DeepSeek-V4.1 with `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` and send the same long prompt twice. Copy the c1 KV bytes at the replayed tokens' slots before the second request's replay forward, and compare them after it.

## Environment

sglang main at `ef26f6ad49`; ROCm (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1.
discussion: Retracting this: the analysis stopped at the metadata and missed that the separate replay forward skips the compressors. `forward_low_ratio_sources` sets `run_compressor = False` when `forward_batch.encoder_swa_replay` is set (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:3031-3032`), and `DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend` reuses that method (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py:883`). On ROCm the replayed rows' c1/c2 KV and index keys are therefore not written. Closing.

items.title: [Perf] [Intel] gemma4: Fuse QKV normalization and RoPE
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Fuses QKV normalization and RoPE into a single XPU kernel launch for Gemma4, reducing per-layer kernel dispatch overhead while preserving BF16/FP16 rounding behavior.
items.body:
Stack (6/6), merge in order: [#44851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44851) → [#44852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44852) → [#44853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44853) → [#44854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44854) → [#44863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44863) → [#44869](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44869)

## Motivation

Gemma4 on XPU launches normalization and RoPE separately for every attention layer. Shared-KV layers additionally allocate a dummy key tensor just to rotate Q. Fuse these operations while preserving the BF16/FP16 normalization rounding boundary and the existing checkpoint weights.

## Modifications

- Extend the existing Gemma QKV norm/RoPE operator to XPU and query-only shared-KV calls.
- Dispatch eligible XPU Gemma4 layers through the fused operator, including unweighted V normalization for nonshared layers.
- Match native XPU rotary contraction order. Explicitly materialize the FP16 intermediate encoding before rotation to preserve its rounding, including subnormal and nonfinite values.

## Accuracy Tests

Intel Arc Pro B70, `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, BF16, TP1:

- Official `sgl-eval` GSM8K-200: 163/200 (81.5%), zero errors, two truncated responses. Temperature 1, top_p 0.95, seed 42, max_tokens 2048, concurrency 8, thinking disabled.
- Six greedy model parity cases matched, including 1,016- and 1,814-token prompts.
- All 64 sampled native XPU kernel comparisons matched exactly across BF16/FP16, shared/nonshared KV, geometries, and batch sizes. Graph replay, packed-stride guards, FP16 cancellation, and 8,204 FP16 rounding edge/random inputs passed.
- 123 CPU namespace/dispatch tests passed.
- All four serving capture tests passed (three-step and single-step MTP), in 88.754 seconds.

Expanded 256-token serving comparisons also expose output variation within control repeats. Of three differing prompts replayed on the same GPU/configuration with cache flushed before each repeat, two matched across all four control/candidate runs; one varied in every run. These measurements do not establish bitwise model equivalence on arbitrary prompts. CUDA execution was not available locally; its existing contraction path is preserved.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same B70, same serving configuration and unchanged BF16 weights; current stack tip as control. Captured three-step MTP, max_running_requests=32, context_length=8192, max_total_tokens=32768, page_size=64, overlap disabled. Control/candidate/candidate/control sequence, 256 output tokens, 64 requests at c1 and 128 at c8/c32. Each server switch discarded a full 128-request c32 warmup before measurement.

| Concurrency | Control mean TPOT (ms) | Candidate mean TPOT (ms) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.155 | 4.116 | 0.95% |
| 8 | 6.118 | 6.049 | 1.14% |
| 32 | 11.334 | 11.102 | 2.04% |

Both candidate repeats were faster than both control repeats at every measured concurrency. The subset with identical generated text in all four runs showed streaming-interval TPOT reductions of 1.03%, 1.15%, and 1.94%, respectively. These are results on this device/workload, not a claim for all XPU hardware or batch sizes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add kernel tests with CI registration.
- [x] Document the extended operator contract in its docstring.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed measurements.
- [x] Follow the existing kernel organization and code style.

items.title: fix: validate ngram_gpu compatibility with disabled compilation
items.author: kyadav09
items.summary: Fixes #62134 by adding early configuration validation for speculative decoding when compilation is explicitly disabled. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62134 by adding early configuration validation for `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding when compilation is explicitly disabled.

## Claims

*   **Bug Fix:** Prevents a fatal engine initialization crash when `speculative_config.method="ngram_gpu"` is paired with `compilation_config.mode="NONE"`.
*   **UX Improvement:** Intercepts the invalid configuration early in `create_engine_config()` and provides an actionable `ValueError` directing the user to either enable compilation or use the CPU `ngram` proposer.

## Validation

*   Verified against the reproduction script provided in #62134.
*   Initializing an `LLM` with the conflicting configs now cleanly raises the target `ValueError` during configuration setup, rather than crashing with an obscure `ValueError: No compilation mode is set` deeply inside `GPUModelRunnerV1.__init__`.

## Details

**Root Cause:** The `ngram_gpu` kernel unconditionally wraps itself in `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper`, which requires an active compilation backend. If `mode="NONE"`, this wrapper fails during EngineCore initialization, resulting in a cryptic error disconnected from the user's explicit configuration choices.

**Fix:** Added a direct compatibility check in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:create_engine_config()` immediately after `speculative_config` and `compilation_config` are instantiated. This cleanly rejects the combination before the engine attempts to initialize devices.

---

items.title: [Fix] deterministic: Disable the hybrid SWA memory pool with the radix cache
items.author: aarnetalman
items.summary: Deterministic inference promises the same output for a request whatever else the server has served, but on hybrid sliding-window models (for example gpt-oss) the radix cache breaks that. The hybrid SWA memory pool keeps only the sliding window of KV for the sl…
items.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference promises the same output for a request whatever else the server has served, but on hybrid sliding-window models (for example gpt-oss) the radix cache breaks that. The hybrid SWA memory pool keeps only the sliding window of KV for the sliding-window layers and evicts the rest. A cached prefix can then be reused only as far as its sliding-window KV is still there, so how much of a prompt is served from the cache, and so how it is prefilled, depends on which earlier requests evicted what. The result of the same request changes with the server's history.

With gpt-oss-20b in deterministic mode on MI350X, `test_deterministic --test-mode prefix` (the same prompts sent repeatedly, sharing prefixes) gave up to 8 different outputs for one prompt. It passes with `--disable-radix-cache`, and it passes with `--disable-hybrid-swa-memory` with the radix cache on.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/attention_hook.py` (`handle_deterministic_inference`): in deterministic mode with the radix cache on, hybrid SWA models get `disable_hybrid_swa_memory=True` with a warning, as deterministic mode already does for `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`. The sliding-window layers then keep the full KV like the other layers.
- DeepSeek V4 (which keeps its sliding-window KV in its own pool) and Inkling (which requires the hybrid SWA pool) are left unchanged.
- `test_model_overrides.py`: deterministic mode resolves `disable_hybrid_swa_memory` to `True` for gpt-oss; it stays `False` with `--disable-radix-cache`, without deterministic mode, and for a model without sliding-window layers.
- Unchanged: deterministic mode off; deterministic mode with `--disable-radix-cache`; models that already disable the pool (Gemma 2/3, EXAONE 4, OLMo 2).

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, gpt-oss-20b, TP1 and TP2, Triton attention, deterministic inference, radix cache on. The MoE layer runs AITER's deterministic MXFP4 MoE (ROCm/aiter#6583) through a local integration in SGLang that is not part of this PR (without it, the MoE itself is not batch-invariant), with the open fixes #43788 and #34543 applied (deterministic mode on MI350X needs them).

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path openai/gpt-oss-20b --tp {1,2} \
  --attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference
```

`python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode prefix --n-trials 50` (4 prompts with prefix lengths 1, 511, 2,048 and 4,097, about 300 samples each), run 3-4 times in a row on one server; numbers are distinct outputs per prompt:

| | TP1 | TP2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 4 of 8 runs differ: 1 1 1 1, 1 1 3 3, 1 1 3 4, 1 1 1 1, 1 1 1 1, 1 2 4 5, 1 1 1 2, 1 1 1 1 | 5 of 5 runs differ: 1 2 2 3, 1 4 1 8, 1 2 1 2, 1 4 1 3, 1 3 3 3 |
| before, `--disable-radix-cache` | 1 1 1 1 in 4 of 4 runs | 1 1 1 1 in 3 of 3 runs |
| after (server logs "Disable the hybrid SWA memory pool because deterministic inference is enabled with the radix cache.") | 1 1 1 1 in 8 of 8 runs | 1 1 1 1 in 4 of 4 runs |

After, on the same servers: `single` 1 output; `prefix --return-logprob` identical logprobs; `radix_cache` pass; a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses; token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response) 1,275 / 1,275, at TP1 and TP2. The same set also passes for gpt-oss-20b at TP4 and TP8 and for gpt-oss-120b at TP1, TP2, TP4 and TP8.

GSM8K (sgl-eval 0.1.2, `--temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048`, TP1): gpt-oss-20b 94.77% before and after; gpt-oss-120b 95.98% after.

Unit tests, `python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py -k "deterministic or hybrid_swa or gpt_oss or step3p"` (same image): before, the new test fails (1 failed, 10 passed); after, 11 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change without deterministic mode, with `--disable-radix-cache`, or for models without sliding-window layers. For hybrid SWA models in deterministic mode, the sliding-window layers now keep the full KV, so the KV cache holds fewer tokens. gpt-oss-20b TP1, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, 3 rounds each, medians, same session (output tok/s):

| | 1,024 in / 1,024 out, 256 prompts, concurrency 256 | 8,192 in / 1,024 out, 256 prompts, concurrency 128 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| deterministic, before (pool on) | 5,087 | 1,726 |
| deterministic, after (pool off) | 5,062 (-0.5%) | 1,719 (-0.4%) |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

items.title: [Bug]: sharded_state can't round-trip models with attention/KV-cache scale params (Missing keys ...attn.q_scale, k_scale, v_scale, prob_scale)
items.author: yibol9768-alt
items.summary: registers placeholder parameters,, and (initialized to -1.0). copies their values into the / /...
items.body:
### Your current environment

- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` (digest `c1c9f6fd5c10…`), torch 2.13.0+cu130
- 2x NVIDIA H20 (SM90), TP=2
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` (block-FP8)
- The relevant code is unchanged on main (`08a65e2`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Saving a `sharded_state` checkpoint and loading it back with **identical** settings fails for any model whose attention layers use `BaseKVCacheMethod` (FP8 checkpoints and the like):

```
ValueError: Missing keys ('language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.q_scale',
 'language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.k_scale', 'language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.v_scale',
 'language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.prob_scale', ...) in loaded state!
```

**Repro**

```bash
python examples/features/sharded_state/save_sharded_state_offline.py \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enforce-eager --output /tmp/q38_sharded
vllm serve /tmp/q38_sharded --load-format sharded_state --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192
```

**Cause**

1. `BaseKVCacheMethod.create_weights` registers placeholder parameters `q_scale`, `k_scale`, `v_scale` and `prob_scale` (initialized to -1.0).
2. `process_weights_after_loading` copies their values into the `_q_scale` / `_k_scale` / ... buffers and then `del`s the placeholders.
3. `save_sharded_state` runs on the fully loaded engine, so the shards contain only `attn._k_scale`, `_v_scale`, `_q_scale` and `_prob_scale`. I checked the saved files: each rank has the 4 `_*_scale` buffers for each of the 16 full-attention layers (64 keys), and no `k_scale`.
4. `ShardedStateLoader.load_weights` iterates over a freshly created model, which still has the placeholders. They are never loaded, so it raises `Missing keys`.

The existing round-trip test only uses `Llama-3.2-1B` in BF16, which has no such placeholders. That is why this hasn't shown up.

**Patching the keys in is not a real fix.** Adding the keys with -1.0 makes it load. But then `process_weights_after_loading` runs a second time on already-processed weights (`base_loader.load_model` always calls it). It sees `k_scale = -1` and overwrites the loaded `_k_scale` with 1.0, so a checkpoint with calibrated KV scales would silently lose them. For this checkpoint (no calibrated scales) the patched round trip did give correct output.

**Suggested fix**

A `sharded_state` checkpoint holds post-processed weights, the same as the weight-cache IPC loader from #54921 ("Fast Start"). That PR already added `weights_already_processed()` / `supports_pre_processed_weights`. Under that mode, `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading` drops the placeholders and rebuilds `_*_scale_float` / `_*_scale_cpu` from the loaded buffers.

So I think `ShardedStateLoader` should:

- load and post-process under `weights_already_processed()`;
- not require keys that only exist as pre-processing placeholders.

One trade-off: quant methods that don't declare `supports_pre_processed_weights` would then raise in `process_weights_after_loading` instead of being processed twice. That seems more correct, but it changes behavior for methods that happen to tolerate double processing today.

Would maintainers prefer that approach, or something narrower? I'm happy to send the PR.

Related: #62155 (`ShardedStateLoader` silently partially loads shape-mismatched tensors; root cause of #61681), found during the same investigation.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bugfix] Reject shape mismatches in ShardedStateLoader instead of partially loading (fixes #61681 mechanism)
items.author: yibol9768-alt
items.summary: Fixes silent wrong outputs when loading sharded checkpoints with a different tensor-parallel layout by raising ValueError on shape mismatches instead of partially loading weights.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes the silent wrong-output mechanism behind #61681.

`ShardedStateLoader.load_weights` loads a saved tensor that is smaller than its parameter into a narrowed view of the parameter, and only logs a warning. The code comment says this is for LoRA padding. The rest of the parameter keeps whatever was in memory, and nothing raises.

That happens whenever a `sharded_state` checkpoint is loaded with a different parallel layout than it was saved with. One concrete case is `--mm-encoder-tp-mode`. With `weights` (the default), the vision tower is TP-sharded. With `data`, every rank holds the full tower. A checkpoint saved from a `weights`-mode engine and served with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` therefore gets a vision tower that is half real weights and half uninitialized memory. Requests succeed, the text side is fine, and image answers are wrong. That matches #61681.

This PR makes the loader raise a `ValueError` on any shape mismatch, naming the tensor, both shapes, and the likely cause. Tensors larger than the parameter already failed in `copy_`. They now fail with the same clear message.

**Why dropping the narrowing is safe:** LoRA no longer pads parameters (there is no `lora_vocab_padding_size` on main; vocab padding is `DEFAULT_VOCAB_PADDING_SIZE` with or without LoRA). I also checked it directly. Saving a sharded checkpoint without LoRA and loading it with `enable_lora=True` takes zero narrowing paths, and greedy output is identical to `--load-format auto`. That is the same scenario as `test_sharded_state_loader[enable_lora=True]`, run on Qwen3-0.6B at TP=2, v0.31.0.

## Reproduction (before this PR)

Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (Qwen3-VL vision path, which supports `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`), TP=2, 2x H20, `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`.

1. Save with `examples/features/sharded_state/save_sharded_state_offline.py --tensor-parallel-size 2 --mm-encoder-tp-mode weights`.
2. Serve the result with `--load-format sharded_state` and run the color-quadrant script from #61681.

| load with | `loading tensor of shape ...` warnings | result |
|---|---|---|
| `--mm-encoder-tp-mode weights` | 0 | 4/4 correct |
| `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` | 330, e.g. `loading tensor of shape torch.Size([1728, 1152]) into parameter 'visual.blocks.0.attn.qkv.weight' of shape torch.Size([3456, 1152])` | garbage tokens for a single image; HTTP 500 for 48 images |

With this patch applied to the same build, the `data`-mode server fails at startup instead:

```
ValueError: Shape mismatch for 'visual.blocks.0.attn.proj.weight': the checkpoint has (1152, 576), the model expects (1152, 1152). A sharded_state checkpoint must be loaded with the parallel layout it was saved with (tensor/pipeline parallel size, --mm-encoder-tp-mode, ...). Re-save it with the current configuration or load the original checkpoint with --load-format auto.
```

(For this FP8 checkpoint I had to add the attention `q/k/v/prob_scale` keys to the shards to load it at all, with identical settings. That is a separate round-trip bug, which I'll report in its own issue. It is unrelated to this change.)

## Test Plan

New CPU unit tests in `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_sharded_state_loader.py`:

- `test_load_weights_rejects_smaller_shard`: a `(2, 4)` shard for a `(4, 4)` parameter must raise.

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Count retracted output tokens as uncached HRRN work
items.author: luicarus
items.summary: sizes a waiting request by its uncached tokens, and divides by that value when it builds the response ratio. The helper returns: is missing from the minuend, but is produced against: builds and matches that, and caps the result with.
items.body:
## Motivation

`SchedulePolicy._uncached_len` sizes a waiting request by its uncached tokens, and `_sort_by_hrrn` divides by that value when it builds the response ratio (`ratio_delta = waited_tokens / uncached`). The helper returns:

```python
return max(0, len(r.origin_input_ids) - r.num_matched_prefix_tokens)
```

`r.output_ids` is missing from the minuend, but `num_matched_prefix_tokens` is produced against `origin_input_ids + output_ids`: `_compute_prefix_matches` builds `prefix_ids = r.origin_input_ids + r.output_ids` and matches that, and `match_kv_cache` caps the result with `_compute_max_prefix_len(len(token_ids))`. The two sides of the subtraction therefore measure spans of different length.

For a fresh request `output_ids` is empty and the expression is correct, which is why this only shows up for requests that already generated tokens. It matters when such a request is retracted back into the waiting queue: `reset_for_retract` clears the matched prefix but keeps `output_ids` — it discards them only when `input_embeds is not None` — so those tokens have to be prefilled again. HRRN then underestimates the remaining work by `len(output_ids)`, which makes the response ratio too large and admits the request earlier than its real cost warrants.

The sibling helper `_shortest_prefill_work` in the same file already counts both spans:

```python
return max(1, len(r.origin_input_ids) + len(r.output_ids) - r.num_matched_prefix_tokens)
```

When the underestimation is large enough the clamped result reaches 0, and `_sort_by_hrrn` treats `uncached <= 0` as having no prefill work left (`return (-float("inf"), rid)`), so the request is ordered ahead of the queue.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_policy.py`: `_uncached_len` now measures by `r.seqlen`, which is defined as `len(origin_input_ids) + len(output_ids)`. One line changed; no new helper, no signature change, and no difference for requests whose `output_ids` is empty.

- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_policy.py`: one regression test added to the existing `TestSchedulePolicyHRRN` class. It puts a retracted request (90 output tokens, 90 matched) and a fresh request (same origin length, same matched count) through `_sort_by_hrrn`; the retracted one has more work left and must sort second.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only affects the order in which waiting requests are admitted. It does not touch model forward, KV cache contents, sampling, or logits.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this is a denominator in an integer sort key. It adds no work to the scheduling path.

items.title: [Spec Decode] Fix adaptive verification startup on FA2 GPUs
items.author: waynehacking8
items.summary: With and no, the selector picks FLASHATTN on GPUs where it runs FA2 (SM8x, SM12x), and the worker then rejects it after the weights load, because FA2's decode cudagraphs cannot replay variable per-request query lengths. Automatic selection now skips such back…
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62094. With `enable_adaptive_verification` and no `--attention-backend`, the selector picks FLASH_ATTN on GPUs where it runs FA2 (SM8x, SM12x), and the worker then rejects it after the weights load, because FA2's decode cudagraphs cannot replay variable per-request query lengths. Automatic selection now skips such backends for verifier layers, as it already skips backends that plan from CPU query lengths.

## Claims

1. The issue's command starts and serves: verifier layers on TRITON_ATTN, the EAGLE-3 drafter stays on FLASH_ATTN, and selection logs `Adaptive verification precluded higher-priority attention backend(s) FLASH_ATTN, FLASHINFER. Using TRITON_ATTN instead.`
2. An explicit `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` on FA2 is rejected at backend selection, before the weights load, instead of after.
3. Nothing changes with adaptive verification off, or where FLASH_ATTN runs FA3 or FA4 (their builders declare `ALWAYS` since #60908).

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), torch 2.14.0+cu130, this branch on main `153a17166e` (the touched files are identical at the branch base). Qwen/Qwen3-4B with AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3, 4 speculative tokens, BF16 KV:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the issue's command | `ValueError: Adaptive verification replays decode cudagraphs whose per-request query lengths vary up to 5, but FlashAttentionBackend allows none` after loading | starts; verifier on TRITON_ATTN, drafter on FLASH_ATTN |
| `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` | the same error after loading | `Selected backend ... FLASH_ATTN is not valid for this configuration`, before loading |
| adaptive verification off | FLASH_ATTN | FLASH_ATTN |

Serving against main with `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, the configuration that works today (MT-Bench prompts, greedy, 256 output tokens, two runs per cell): mean TPOT 4.041 against 4.005 ms at c=1 and 5.83 against 5.90 ms at c=32 (ranges overlap), mean acceptance length 2.00 against 2.01, chat GSM8K (250) 0.936 against 0.940.

Tests on SM120: the new selector cases fail on main (the verifier FA2 case selects FLASH_ATTN; the others need the new field) and pass here; `test_attention_selector.py` and `test_adaptive_verification.py`: 107 passed on main, 113 with this PR (22 skipped each).

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --max-model-len 4096 --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3", "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "enable_adaptive_verification": true}'
```

## Details

FA2's metadata builder declares `UNIFORM_BATCH`, which the worker's `get_varlen_cudagraph_unsupported_backend` rejects for target layers, but the selector's only adaptive-verification check was `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch()`, which FA2 passes. A backend hook `supports_varlen_decode_cudagraphs()` (default True; FlashAttention answers from its builder's declared support, so both checks read the same declaration) is now checked in `validate_configuration()`.

It applies to verifier layers only, through `AttentionSelectorConfig.use_varlen_decode_cudagraphs`, set like `use_adaptive_verification` but off under the `eagle_head` tag, following the tag check from #47808's review: drafters built under that tag replay FULL graphs only for untrimmed batches of uniform length, so they can keep FA2. It is a field because selections are cached per config. The worker check stays as the per-layer backstop. Drafters built under other tags (`draft_model`, `dflash_head`, `extract_hidden_states`) keep the requirement, and other backends that declare `UNIFORM_BATCH` without a varlen bound (TRITON_MLA, FLASHMLA, ROCM_AITER_FA) still fail at the worker as on main; both can follow the same pattern if wanted. The check lives in the selector rather than `_validate_adaptive_verification` because backends are resolved per layer during model construction.

This change was prepared with AI assistance.

items.title: [Feat] speculative: Online acceptance estimator for DSpark confidence-scheduled verification
items.author: maocheng23
items.summary: DSpark's confidence-scheduled ("ragged") verification trims low-survival draft tokens before the target verify, but it needs a trained confidence head, so checkpoints without one cannot use it. vLLM's (vllm-project/vllm#52228) replaces the head with a logistic…
items.body:
## Motivation

DSpark's confidence-scheduled ("ragged") verification trims low-survival draft
tokens before the target verify, but it needs a trained confidence head, so
checkpoints without one cannot use it. vLLM's
[online acceptance estimator](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-14-adaptive-verification-online-estimator)
(vllm-project/vllm#52228) replaces the head with a logistic model of the draft
distribution fitted while serving. This PR brings that to SGLang, with a more
robust fit.

## Modifications

- `--speculative-dspark-confidence-source {auto,head,online}` (default `auto`).
  `online` scores each draft position with
  `sigmoid(slope * logit(q_max) + intercept[position])`; `auto` uses the trained
  head when the checkpoint ships one and the estimator otherwise (config
  `enable_confidence_head: false`, or no confidence weights at all).
- `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator` (`srt/speculative/online_acceptance_estimator.py`):
  DSpark drafts and verifies in the same step, so prediction and grading run back
  to back with no per-request state. Labels are the drafts before and at the first
  rejection, restricted to drafts checked against a real target row.
- Fit: exact MAP IRLS on binned `(position, logit(q_max) bin, label)` counts with
  a decayed history (Newton iterations with a batched line search, on device, every
  100 steps). A single Newton step per round, as in vLLM, freezes the slope and
  over-predicts survival when acceptance saturates below 1 for confident drafts
  (sampled targets): in simulation it over-predicted the expected accepted length
  by 0.45 tokens per request, the binned fit by -0.02.
- Two launches per decode step: a Triton pass computes logit(q_max) and the
  prediction together, and one atomic-add kernel bins the labels.
- Fix (pre-existing on main): compact ragged verify padded the trimmed slots of the
  full-width logits with zeros, and the sampling accept's top-p renormalization of a
  uniform row is flashinfer's radix top-p worst case (22 ms vs 0.75 ms for 512 x 152k
  rows). On Qwen3-14B + DSpark at c=64 that was ~15 ms of a 36 ms step and made compact
  ~50% slower than static, whatever the confidence source. Padding rows now hold a point
  mass (they are never accepted from; block verification is lossless for any padding).
- Docs: a confidence-scheduled verification section and the new server argument.

## Losslessness

Trimming is lossless iff whether position i is verified depends only on the
drafts before i (plus independent randomness and history). The estimator's
feature reads `q_i`, never the drafted token; survival is a running product over
positions <= i; ties in the top-B break toward earlier positions; and the budget
is sized from confidences two steps old. An exact rational enumeration (not part of
this PR) confirms
losslessness for token-wise and block verification (and shows the failure modes:
scoring `q(x_i)`, or sizing the budget from current survivals of a
semi-autoregressive drafter). `test_ragged_cutoff_preserves_distribution` checks
the real accept kernels on 400k rows with compact padding and the verify cap,
block and token-wise.

## Accuracy Tests

sgl-eval 0.1.3 gsm8k (full 1319, 64 concurrent), Qwen3-14B thinking mode, T=0.6, top-p 0.95,
max 16384 tokens, with the compact scheduler and a profiled SPS table:

| static (verify all) | head | online | online + block verification |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 96.29% | 96.21% | 96.13% | 96.29% |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Qwen3-14B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_14b_block7`, 1x B300 per arm, trtllm_mha / fa4,
SPEED-Bench throughput_1k per category, T=1.0, top-p 0.95, up to 1024 output tokens, prompts =
4 x concurrency. Cells: output throughput vs static (accept length). `head` uses the checkpoint's
trained confidence head, `online` this PR's estimator; both run the same compact scheduler and
SPS table, with the padding fix.

| category | conc | static tok/s (AL) | head tok/s (AL) | online tok/s (AL) | online-block tok/s (AL) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| high_entropy | 1 | 322 (2.36) | -4.9% (2.36) | -4.1% (2.39) | -3.4% (2.44) |
| high_entropy | 8 | 1913 (2.33) | +1.6% (2.39) | +4.8% (2.35) | +3.2% (2.44) |
| high_entropy | 32 | 5274 (2.41) | +5.6% (2.38) | +7.2% (2.32) | +3.3% (2.34) |
| high_entropy | 64 | 6172 (2.40) | +13.8% (2.16) | +14.4% (2.17) | +12.7% (2.17) |
| high_entropy | 128 | 6963 (2.40) | +24.4% (2.01) | +23.4% (2.02) | +23.7% (2.02) |
| low_entropy | 1 | 402 (2.95) | -3.5% (3.00) | -3.2% (3.01) | -4.5% (3.02) |
| low_entropy | 8 | 2555 (3.01) | -5.9% (2.98) | -9.0% (3.03) | -3.1% (3.09) |
| low_entropy | 32 | 6400 (2.98) | +0.6% (2.98) | +5.6% (2.90) | +4.6% (3.00) |
| low_entropy | 64 | 7876 (3.00) | +6.0% (2.55) | +4.6% (2.48) | +3.7% (2.49) |
| low_entropy | 128 | 8783 (2.99) | +13.0% (2.23) | +12.8% (2.24) | +11.4% (2.25) |
| mixed | 1 | 418 (3.05) | -5.5% (3.01) | -5.9% (2.99) | -3.9% (3.11) |
| mixed | 8 | 2524 (2.99) | -2.4% (2.98) | -6.3% (3.02) | -0.7% (3.11) |
| mixed | 32 | 7180 (3.01) | -1.7% (2.98) | -1.2% (2.97) | -0.3% (3.08) |
| mixed | 64 | 8999 (3.01) | +6.9% (2.48) | +8.0% (2.48) | +6.5% (2.49) |
| mixed | 128 | 10324 (3.01) | +17.7% (2.23) | +18.5% (2.24) | +17.8% (2.25) |

Repeat runs on other GPUs reproduce the c=128 gains within about one point. Before the padding
fix, every compact arm was 45-50% slower than static at c >= 32 (top-p on zero-logit padding rows
took ~22 ms of a ~36 ms step).

Known limitation: at c <= 8 compact mode is still up to 9% slower than static even though its budget
verifies every draft there; that is the compact pipeline's fixed per-step cost, independent of
the confidence source. `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE` stays `static` by default, so default
deployments are unaffected; reducing that cost is left to a follow-up.

## Tests

- CPU, on this head: estimator unit tests, server-args docs coverage, block-verification args,
  DSpark accept/draft units and the CPU DSpark suites: 152 passed, 2 skipped.
- GPU, 1x B300, on the pre-rebase head (identical diff): `test_draft_top_log_odds.py` (Triton
  parity incl. fused predict and bin counting), `test_block_verification.py` incl. the new
  `test_ragged_cutoff_preserves_distribution`, `test_dspark_kernel_parity.py` incl. the
  point-mass padding, estimator units: 45 passed, 20 subtests; `test_basic_sanity_dspark.py`
  (compact mode): 29 passed, 1 skipped.

- [x] Format with pre-commit hooks (ruff, isort, codespell)

That function accepts `return_intermediate_states` and `last_chunk_indices`, but ignores them and always returns one final state per sequence. `conv_ssm_forward` then indexes that tensor with per-chunk indices. For 513 tokens the chunks are [0, 256), [256, 512), [512, 513), so the index is 2 and the tensor has 1 row. - Even past that, `store_prefill_checkpoint` in `ops/ssd_checkpoint.py` only has a Triton kernel. I tried #54505 (which makes the CPU chunk scan return per-chunk states), and it gets past line 878 but then fails at `_store_prefill_checkpoint_kernel[grid]` with `TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable`. Workaround: `enable_prefix_caching=False`. With that, greedy output matches HF transformers (fp32) token for token on prompts up to 1356 tokens. I've only run granite-4.0-h, on macOS. From the code I'd expect the other `MambaMixer2` models (nemotron_h, falcon_h1, zamba2, mamba2) and Linux CPU to hit the same path, since the CPU chunk-scan override applies to any CPU platform, but I haven't checked. There are two ways to fix this. One is to skip internal prefill checkpoints on CPU. The other is to add CPU versions of the per-chunk states and of `store_prefill_checkpoint`. I have a small patch for the first one. It makes `MambaMixer2.get_kv_cache_spec` leave `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks` at 0 on CPU, the same way GDN does with `_exports_checkpoints`. The scheduler and the KV cache manager then go back to splitting the prefill at block boundaries, as they did before #57329. With it, 513 and 1300 tokens work. I also ran a few requests that reuse 1024 cached tokens, and they give the same tokens as a run with prefix caching off. The cost is fewer cache hits on CPU than on GPU, the same as before #57329. I can open a PR for that, unless you'd rather go the other way. cc @roikoren755 @ZJY0516

items.title: [Security] Reject unresolved multimodal inputs before execution
items.author: jperezdealgaba
items.summary: Reject multimodal requests whose encoder payload is missing before the model runner receives them. A cache-only input can reach the worker unresolved when the corresponding encoder output is absent, causing a request to terminate the engine.
items.body:
## Overview

Reject multimodal requests whose encoder payload is missing before the model runner receives them. A cache-only input can reach the worker unresolved when the corresponding encoder output is absent, causing a request to terminate the engine.

## Claims

- Missing payloads without a matching local encoder output or external encoder cache item finish as request-scoped errors.
- Existing local encoder cache hits, external encoder cache hits, and fully cached prefix tokens remain eligible for scheduling.
- The check covers items later in a chunked prompt, before worker admission.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short`: 224 passed.
- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py -q --tb=short`: 23 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: passed.
- Repository-wide pre-commit run found unrelated macOS failures in `mypy` (`mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE`, `os.posix_fadvise`) and the non-root entrypoint wrapper (`/var` versus `/private/var` path comparison).
- GPU end-to-end validation on the reported `/render` to `/generate` reproducer: **pending maintainer CI run**. Serve `Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct` with `--enable-scale-out --mm-processor-cache-gb 0`, render a previously unseen base64 image with `return_mm_kwargs: false`, forward the render response to `/inference/v1/generate`, and confirm a request-scoped error while a subsequent valid request succeeds.

## Details

`/inference/v1/generate` accepts `features.kwargs_data: null`, which becomes a multimodal feature with `data=None`. Without a receiver-cache hit, the scheduler could admit the request while its encoder output was absent. Qwen's worker can inspect the unresolved feature during request admission, before its placeholder tokens are scheduled; other models can fail later when gathering embeddings. The scheduler now checks unresolved features before admission and again before scheduling encoder computation, then finishes only that request as an error.

This is not duplicate work. The merged layout validation in #51898 does not check for an unresolved encoder payload. The related open work in #60526 and #61656 addresses different cache or continuation paths; #57796 concerns combined feature inputs. The render change in #60728 can produce a null payload but does not reject it downstream.

The change adds no model output or accuracy behavior for valid requests. No model evaluation was run for malformed-input rejection.

---

- [x] **Design Fit:** Adds a request-scoped guard at the shared scheduler boundary.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** CPU tests pass; GPU end-to-end reproducer and maintainer CI run are pending.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changed-file hooks pass; the diff is limited to the guard and regression tests.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Describes the root cause, duplicate check, implementation, and validation status.
</details>

items.title: Support GDN2 and TE CUDA graphs for recurrence offloading
items.author: Pinoeer-kingxi
items.summary: Extend opt-in activation offloading to GDN2 and Transformer Engine CUDA graphs for GDN/GDN2 training. Both variants reuse the GDN base class for the recurrence scope, differentiable prefetch anchor and commit before output normalization.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Extend opt-in `gdn_core_attn` activation offloading to GDN2 and Transformer Engine CUDA graphs for GDN/GDN2 training.

Both variants reuse the GDN base class for the recurrence scope, differentiable prefetch anchor and commit before output normalization. Transfers use the existing manager, pinned pool and callbacks. TE layer graphs replay on the caller's autograd stream to preserve the order of graphs sharing a memory pool; the stream override reproduced NaN gradients in GDN2 whole-layer replay. Native pre-GDR fusion, autotuning and numerical kernels are unchanged.

GDN2 keeps differentiable sigmoid gate outputs resident when gate backward already retains their storage: the write gate, and the erase gate when no head expansion is needed. Expanded erase gates and frozen gates remain eligible for offload. This avoids copying storage that stays live on GPU. Evaluation bypasses the new marking.

Support remains BF16/FLA only. Attention and whole-layer TE capture, `gdn_norm_out` recomputation and delayed offload are covered. Graph offload requires PyTorch >= 2.9, TE >= 2.14 and positive graph warmup. Set `NVTE_CPU_OFFLOAD_V1=1` before launch. GDN2 requires `fla.ops.gdn2`. FP8/FP4, full recomputation and local/full-iteration graphs remain unsupported.

## Dependencies

Merge after #7908 and its #8243 prerequisite. The diff against `main` includes those dependencies; the [extension diff](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/compare/485cb5fa2ffedaaaa0a1a4d095e43ddd99487c1d...1f6eab9ce2453cf55cfeac57add2ed80540f31a7) shows the additional feature and documentation. #8244 is independent. Composition with #7852 is not validated.

## Validation

Head: `1f6eab9ce2453cf55cfeac57add2ed80540f31a7`. GPU source: `367d014c7bf74ba3553c9db58da47fa5bcba906e`. Only documentation differs; the complete `megatron`, `tests` and `tools` trees are identical. [Source identities and tree comparison](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/blob/95ba13de41c85950511bfdb7bb481df2235d1d57/gdn-graph-profile-20261017/final-source-qualification.json) record the exact versions.

Environment: RTX A6000, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, TE 2.20.2, FLA 0.5.1 and Triton 3.6.0.

- On the GPU source, each of two ranks passes 20 scope cases, 18 native GDN2 training cases and 9 real TE graph cases, with zero skips. Coverage includes DP2, TP2+SP and PP2; norm recomputation off/on; fractions 0/0.5/1; attention/whole-layer capture and delayed offload. New regressions check actual gate-copy selection, equal/expanded heads, trainable/frozen gates, outputs and all gradients, plus evaluation with gradients. The old production source fails the targeted live-write-gate copy assertion.
- Complete eight-block GDN2 model comparisons cover linear key/value heads 8/16 and 16/16. All six optimizer steps, including three graph replays, match losses, gradient norms, complete gradients, weights and Adam/master-state fingerprints exactly. Pinned-pool ownership is zero before schedule resets, and allocation counters stay constant during replay.
- Three fresh-process before/after performance pairs match their complete 16-step input hashes, losses and gradient-norm sequences. Separate Nsight controls record actual transfers and kernel counts; profiler timings are excluded from performance qualification. Black, isort, Ruff, project Pylint rules and kernel determinism coverage checks pass.

[Current commands, raw rank logs, state comparisons, traces and samples](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/95ba13de41c85950511bfdb7bb481df2235d1d57/gdn-graph-profile-20261017) are public. The offline verifier checks recorded artifacts; it does not execute GPU tests.

Earlier [two-rank matrices](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/34371ca51fa2dffb5c362f1c52c89b1801670226/gdn-followup-20261016) and [complete Qwen/GDN2 graph-training checks](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/6518374eafc6b64358c1cecb805dc845c4b2ec4a/gdn-graph-training-20261017) retain their original revisions. They include 21 GDN/GDN2 graph cases per rank and full pretrained Qwen3.5-0.8B text-model state comparisons. Those historical results are separate from the current-source GDN2 checks above. [Usage and supported configurations](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/blob/1f6eab9ce2453cf55cfeac57add2ed80540f31a7/docs/developer/gdn_activation_offloading.md) remain in-tree.

## Memory and runtime

The current comparison uses the complete eight-block GDN2/attention model: hidden size 1024, vocabulary 4096, linear key/value heads 8/16 with dimension 128, embeddings, MLPs, vocabulary loss and native BF16 Adam. Weights and tokens are seeded. Both arms enable offloading and whole-layer TE graphs on one A6000, with sequence 2048, four microbatches, unfused pre-GDR, norm recomputation off, fraction 1 and the default 1,048,576-element threshold.

Three fresh-process pairs alternate arm order. Each arm trains three native steps, captures graphs, warms up three replay steps and times ten complete optimizer steps. Timing includes zeroing, forward/backward/finalization, Adam and CUDA completion; inputs, capture, snapshots and reporting are excluded. The optimizer stays eager.

| Metric | Before, `d18040ba5a` | Adjusted, `367d014c7b` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median of process-median step times | 451.71 ms | 424.91 ms |
| Median peak reserved | 4944 MiB | 4922 MiB |
| D2H and H2D bytes per step, combined | 3200 MiB | 2880 MiB |
| Retained pinned buffers | 54 | 48 |

Paired median step-time reduction is 5.93% (5.89–5.95%). Additional reserved savings are a paired median 22 MiB (20–38 MiB); allocated peaks are unchanged. Nsight records 10% fewer transfer bytes with unchanged kernel name/count multisets. These results measure the gate-selection adjustment, rather than a speedup from enabling offloading. Remaining transfer overhead is substantial.

For context, the earlier offload-on/off measurements at `f19ebc5b1da1c9b0075eecfd2f93fc6ca4b3ba8d` used the same sequence, microbatch count and graph settings, before this adjustment:

| Model | Allocated-peak change | Reserved reduction, paired median [range] | Step-time increase, paired median [range] |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, 24 text blocks | +512 bytes | 444 MiB [442, 446] | +21.00% [20.68%, 21.11%] |
| GDN2, 8 blocks | approximately +1 MiB | 258 MiB [248, 286] | +96.45% [96.05%, 96.66%] |

Those results retain their executed revision and do not qualify the adjusted GDN2 implementation. The earlier four-block GDN2 stack measurement at `043e3173451bea74e63c02b197867bf356ad72e9` saved 192 MiB allocated (16.88%), with +58.42% runtime; it excluded vocabulary loss, optimizer updates and CUDA graphs. Its [raw evidence](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/34371ca51fa2dffb5c362f1c52c89b1801670226/gdn-followup-20261016) remains versioned separately. The eager complete-Qwen measurements in #7908 are also separate results.

The option stays disabled by default. These local checks do not qualify upstream GPU CI, four-card GDN2 composition, pretrained GDN2 training or a continuous 200-step graph run.

## Issue tracking

Related to #6757.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests.
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests.
- [x] The existing GDN determinism-manifest association covers this dispatch; the coverage checker passes. No numerical kernel changes are included.
- [x] I have added proper typing to the changed code.
- [x] I have added relevant documentation and reproducible commands.
- [x] I have run Black, isort, Ruff and the project Pylint rules on the changed Python files.

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix M-RoPE positions stride assertion in compile_sizes graphs
items.author: vadiklyutiy
items.summary: Fixes stride symbol handling in piecewise backend that caused assertion failures and silent correctness bugs during torch.compile CUDA-graph profiling for M-RoPE.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #50046. When `compile_sizes` is set, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` with TP=4 dies at start-up, during CUDA-graph memory profiling, with `AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 4097==512 at dim=0`. The cause is `create_concrete_args` in `vllm/compilation/piecewise_backend.py`. It set every symbol, stride symbols included, to the compile size. With this fix, a symbol that Dynamo created only for an input's stride or storage offset keeps its traced value.

Compared with #50445, this fix:

- Also fixes the stride where the graph takes the stride symbol as a SymInt input. [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) still sets that symbol to the compile size, so on Qwen3.5 every single-size graph passes `positions_stride_m` = size to the fused M-RoPE kernel, and the crash becomes silently wrong H/W positions. With vLLM's `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` at compile size 16, [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) gives output that differs from eager (`Tensor-likes are not close!`), and this fix matches eager.
- Does not break a case that works today. Take a tensor with no token dim whose stride is the token count, passed across a split: with [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) the size-16 graph fails with `stride 16==64`, and the old code and this fix both pass.
- Adds a test that catches the bug. [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) adds no test.

## Claims

- The command from the issue now starts and serves requests on 4 x H200 with torch 2.14, instead of failing in CUDA-graph memory profiling.
- Graphs compiled for a single entry of `compile_sizes` now keep input strides and storage offsets that do not depend on the token count. Here that is the M-RoPE positions row pitch, 4097. Sizes, SymInt inputs and unbacked sizes still become the compile size, as before.
- New test `test_compile_sizes_keep_input_strides` in `tests/compile/test_compile_ranges.py`. That file already runs in CI.

## Validation

Hardware and software: 4 x NVIDIA H200, torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7` (commit `49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`), and this commit on top of it for the "after" runs.

Reproducer: the command from the issue. No request is needed, because the bug stops the server at start-up. I added `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` because it was needed to get past NCCL start-up on the test machine. It is not related to the bug.

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 \
VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config.compile_sizes '[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512]' \
  --compilation-config.cudagraph_capture_sizes '[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512]'
```

Before (base commit, 1 run from a source install, failed 1 of 1; the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image of the same commit also failed 3 of 3):

```
assert_size_stride_grouped((arg13_1, arg14_1, arg15_1, arg16_1), ((256, ), (256, ), (262144, 64), (3, 512)), ((1, ), (1, ), (64, 1), (512, 1)), 'input')
AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 4097==512 at dim=0
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After (patched tree, 2 runs: one by me and one by a separate check). Both runs compiled every graph from scratch, and both passed:

```
[backbone] Compiling a graph for compile range (512, 512) takes 118.04 s
Graph capturing finished in 7 secs, took 0.48 GiB
Available KV cache memory: 30.08 GiB
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Neither log has an `AssertionError` or a `Traceback`. In both runs, two chat requests at temperature 0 got correct answers ("Paris", and a count from 1 to 30 in 110 tokens). In the second run, 16 copies of the counting request sent at the same time all gave the same correct answer. Both servers exited with code 0 on SIGTERM.

If you rerun this: the AOT compile cache key does not include `vllm/compilation/*.py`. An entry built by the old code on the same GPU model is loaded as-is, and then the fix never runs. Clear `~/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/` first.

Unit test: `python -m pytest -W error::FutureWarning tests/compile/test_compile_ranges.py -v`. With the fix, 5 passed. With the old `piecewise_backend.py`, the new test fails with `AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 8193==16 at dim=0`, and the 4 existing tests pass.

Older torch: I ran `create_concrete_args` alone on Dynamo graphs with CPU torch 2.10.0 and 2.11.0, and with torch 2.14.0, under `-W error::FutureWarning`. Plain, fixed-offset and strided inputs all give the expected shape, stride and offset on all three versions. For example, the strided input gives `((3, 16), (8193, 1), 0)`.

`pre-commit` passes on both changed files. I did not run an accuracy eval (`lm_eval`).

## Details

Root cause: `create_concrete_args` came in with #35472. It builds the example inputs for graphs compiled for one entry of `compile_sizes`, and it replaced every free symbol in each input's shape, stride and storage offset with the compile size. The M-RoPE `positions` input is `RopeState.positions[:, :num_tokens]`, a slice of a persistent `(3, max_num_tokens + 1)` = `(3, 4097)` buffer. Dynamo gives its row stride a symbol of its own, with traced value 4097. The old code set that symbol to 512, so the size-512 graph asserted stride `(512, 1)`, but the real tensor has stride `(4097, 1)`. Inductor size asserts are on by default for torch >= 2.12, so the assert fails during CUDA-graph capture. On torch < 2.12 the asserts are off by default. There the old code did not crash, but the kernels in the size graphs would read M-RoPE rows 1 and 2 at the wrong offset. This change fixes that case too. I did not run the model on torch < 2.12.

Fix: a symbol is a layout symbol when all of its Dynamo sources (`shape_env.var_to_sources`) are `TensorPropertySource` with a property other than `SIZE`. A layout symbol keeps its traced value, from `shape_env.backed_var_to_val` on torch >= 2.11 or from `var_to_val` before that. Every other symbol takes exactly the old path. I added a temporary debug print and ran the real model with it. The only symbol the fix changes there is `positions.stride(0)`: the old value was the compile size (1 to 512), and the new value is 4097, for every size on all 4 ranks.

Why ask Dynamo where the symbol came from, instead of the simpler options:

- Giving every stride its traced value is wrong for contiguous inputs, whose stride does depend on the size.
- Calling a symbol a size only when it appears in a shape gets it wrong for a size symbol that appears only in a stride, or only as a SymInt input of a subgraph.

Tradeoff: a size graph now fixes each layout symbol to its traced value, not to the compile size. Take a caller that traces with a strided view and later passes a contiguous tensor at a compile size. That worked by chance before, and it now fails the size assert. No vLLM runner does this: MRV1, MRV2 and the spec-decode proposer pass a slice of the same persistent buffer at trace time and at run time.

Not fixed here: one combination fails in the range graph, on the old code and the new code alike. It is unbacked dynamic shapes, plus M-RoPE positions, plus a splitting op. The error is `AssertionError: Shape: 8193 out of considered ranges: [(1, 8192)]`. The cause is that `PiecewiseBackend.__call__` dispatches on the first SymInt input, and there that input is the stride symbol. It needs a different change.

items.title: [Diffusion] ComfyUI: online INT8 quantization for BF16 Qwen-Image-2.1 single files
items.author: OnePunchMonk
items.summary: Users on 24 to 32 GB GPUs often already have the BF16 ComfyUI file for Qwen-Image-2.1 but cannot use online quantization with it. Today they have to find and download a separate pre-quantized file.
items.body:
## Motivation

Users on 24 to 32 GB GPUs often already have the BF16 ComfyUI file for Qwen-Image-2.1 but cannot use online quantization with it. Today they have to find and download a separate pre-quantized file.

Two things blocked this:

1. The plugin preflight rejected `quantization` for any ComfyUI single file.
2. The worker's single-file loader (`comfyui_checkpoints/spec.py`) only built a quant config from per-layer markers in the file. A BF16 file has none, so `--quantization` was silently ignored and the DiT stayed in BF16.

## Modifications

- `runtime/loader/comfyui_checkpoints/spec.py`: when a single file has no quant markers and `quantization` is set, resolve it through the existing `resolve_transformer_quant_load_spec` (same path native directories use), build the matching `WeightLoadPlan`, and run the quant post-load hooks. Methods that need serialized weights (e.g. `mxfp8`) raise a clear error instead of being ignored.
- Plugin `core/preflight.py`: allow `convrot_int8` on BF16 Qwen-Image-2.1 single files. Other models and other methods stay rejected with a clear message.
- Options tooltip and README updated.
- Tests: worker regression test (quant config, param dtype, load device and hooks reach the loader) and preflight accept/reject cases.

Scope is Qwen-Image-2.1 + INT8 ConvRot only. FP8 was tested and left out (results below). Other single-file models can be added once validated.

## Accuracy and speed (Modal, L40S)

ComfyUI v0.41.0, headless API graph through `SGLDUNETLoader` + `SGLDOptions`. `Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1` turbo file, 1024x1024, 8 steps, euler/simple, cfg 1, seed 42. Time is the second (warm) run. Peak GPU is whole-process `nvidia-smi` (includes ComfyUI's text encoder and VAE). PSNR/SSIM are against SGLD BF16 on the same seed.

| Run | Sampling time | Peak GPU | PSNR / SSIM vs SGLD BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native ComfyUI BF16 | 3.43 s | 22.9 GB | 28.19 dB / 0.969 |
| SGLD BF16 | 3.29 s | 26.9 GB | reference |
| **SGLD online INT8 (this PR)** | **2.35 s** | 23.5 GB | **28.55 dB / 0.966** |
| SGLD online FP8 (not enabled) | 4.49 s | 23.5 GB | 21.74 dB / 0.855 |

Worker log for the INT8 run:

```
convrot_int8: quantized 224 linear layers (13.00 GiB of BF16 weights -> 6.50 GiB INT8; jit 0, comfy_kitchen 224), left 0 in BF16
```

INT8 is about 1.4x faster than BF16 and halves DiT weight memory, and its distance from BF16 is in line with native ComfyUI vs SGLD BF16. On L40S (CC 8.9) the JIT INT8 kernels are unavailable, so this ran on the comfy_kitchen backend.

### Why FP8 is not enabled

Online FP8 quantizes the same 224 layers but drifts from BF16 and is slower than BF16 on L40S. Keeping some layers in BF16 (`--quantization-ignored-layers`) did not fix it consistently (2 seeds each):

| FP8 variant | Time | SSIM (seed 42 / 1234) | PSNR dB (seed 42 / 1234) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 reference | 3.17 s | | |
| FP8, all layers | 4.36 s | 0.855 / 0.854 | 21.7 / 20.8 |
| keep `img_mlp.out` in BF16 | 3.75 s | 0.814 / 0.866 | 20.6 / 21.7 |
| keep `attn.to_out` in BF16 | 4.18 s | 0.915 / 0.876 | 24.0 / 21.4 |
| keep both | 3.55 s | 0.879 / 0.884 | 22.6 / 21.8 |
| keep blocks 0 and 31 in BF16 | 4.23 s | 0.955 / 0.881 | 27.2 / 22.0 |

So the plugin rejects `fp8` for single files for now.

### Pre-quantized file note

Loading Comfy-Org's own `qwen_image_2.1_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors` through `SGLDUNETLoader` fails on current main with `Parameter transformer_blocks.1.attn.comfy_attention.config not found in custom model state dict`. That is the serialized-marker path, which this PR does not touch; I can open a separate issue.

## Testing

- Unit tests on Modal (`test_comfyui_checkpoint_spec.py`, `test_comfyui_options.py`, `test_comfyui_generator.py`, `test_comfyui_qwen_image21.py`): 64 passed, 3 skipped.
- Same new tests against unmodified main: 5 failed (the 3 worker regression tests and 2 preflight cases), confirming they guard the change.
- End-to-end ComfyUI runs on L40S as above.

## Limitations

- Only Qwen-Image-2.1 single files are allowed in the plugin; Flux, Qwen-Image, Z-Image and MiniMax-H3 keep the existing rejection until validated.
- FSDP inference with online ConvRot INT8 on single files was not tested.

items.title: [RFC]: PD disaggregation + RL lifecycle (pause, sleep, abort) tracking
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: RFC proposing coordinated lifecycle management (pause, sleep, abort, reset) for PD-disaggregated KV caches during RL training to fix 19 of 27 failing cases.
items.body:
### Motivation.

RL training on PD disaggregation pauses, sleeps, aborts and resets the cache around every weight update. On main (`ce49c47`), only 8 of 27 lifecycle cases pass with MooncakeConnector on GB300. The rest block a pause for 480 s, wedge D, or return 500.

**Tracker:** https://claude.ai/artifact/5yU9HihNDSW86B1oZFL2mc


### Proposed Change.

Merge in this order:

- [x] #59625 Mooncake sleep mode
- [x] #60572 Drain async KV loads in a wait pause
- [ ] aoshen02/vllm#86 Answer every pull and free dropped transfers promptly (R1–R3)
- [ ] aoshen02/vllm#87 Release transfer-held KV before a cache reset (R4)
- [ ] aoshen02/vllm#88 Stop the decode stream when its prefill fails (R5)
- [ ] aoshen02/vllm#104 Let P recompute KV that a cache reset dropped (optional, like SGLang's rebootstrap)

The fork PRs will be opened here one at a time. With all of them, the matrix passes 27 of 27.

Related: #59055 (sleep-mode memory).

items.title: Optimize NCCL MoE dispatch
items.author: Waterpine
items.summary: Reduce ordinary NCCL MoE dispatch from three data all-gathers to one while preserving the batch-invariant path This extracts the NCCL dispatcher optimization from #8114. Hidden states, router probabilities, and routing indices are packed into aligned byte rows…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Reduce ordinary NCCL MoE dispatch from three data all-gathers to one while preserving the batch-invariant path

This extracts the NCCL dispatcher optimization from #8114. Hidden states, router probabilities, and routing indices are packed into aligned byte rows, gathered together, and unpacked into their original dtypes

The optimization covers both equal-token CUDA Graph dispatch and variable-token prefill dispatch. The variable-token path retains its existing token-count metadata gather. Grad-enabled execution, batch-invariant execution, and unaligned layouts retain the original three-gather path. Token combine is unchanged

The helpers handle empty and strided inputs. No model-specific tuning was introduced.

## Validation

Candidate: `210687f5d`. Baseline: unchanged main revision `442d0183d`. All four files in the candidate commit are byte-identical to the validated snapshot

- Distributed unit tests: 84 tests passed on every rank at both EP4 (one node) and EP8 (two nodes), with no failures or skips. Coverage includes equal and ragged token counts, zero-token ranks, all-empty inputs, strided inputs, CUDA Graph replay with updated inputs, alignment fallback, BI fallback, rank-local gradient flags, and autograd preservation
- Bit-exact packing tests: repeated packing and unpacking preserve the original bytes, including signed zero, infinities, subnormals, and NaN payloads. Coverage is registered as `inference_nccl_packed_dispatch` in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py`
- Full-model logits: all 60 comparison cells passed across Nano, Super, and Ultra: five workloads per model, eager/decode CUDA Graph execution, and shared-expert overlap off/on. Every valid prefill, mixed, and decode position and all 131072 vocabulary entries were compared through integer views, without tolerance or downcasting. All eight ranks participated, with two repeats per case per process. Input IDs, positions, generated tokens, and replay results also matched. A one-bit negative control verified the comparator
- Workload coverage: batch sizes 1, 7, 16, 31, and 32; prompt lengths from 1 to 257 tokens; output lengths of 64 or 128 tokens
- Static checks: Black, isort, pylint, Ruff, determinism-manifest coverage, and `git diff --check` passed. `tools/autoformat.sh` was run in check mode. Its non-gating mypy step reported missing local Torch imports/stubs and Optional-access diagnostics in unchanged code.

Full-model validation used GB300, two nodes with four GPUs each, TP8/EP8/ETP1, BF16 weights, FP32 router, and BI disabled. `MAMBA_DETERMINISTIC=1` and `TRITON_CACHE_AUTOTUNING=0` were set identically for baseline and candidate. In decode-graph configurations, prefill and mixed steps remained eager.

## Performance

Measured whole-batch generation through the inference engine on the same three models and topology, using 32–33 prompt tokens and exactly 128 generated tokens per request, decode CUDA Graphs, and shared-expert overlap disabled

Timing includes prefill and decode after enqueue and warmup. Model loading, tokenization, enqueue, and logits-comparison instrumentation are excluded. These are engine end-to-end batch measurements, not HTTP, isolated-kernel, TTFT, or ITL measurements

Each of three independent allocations per model ran four fresh processes per batch size:
- BS16: baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline
- BS32: candidate/baseline/baseline/candidate
- Five timed generations per process.

For each round, speedup is the baseline median batch wall time divided by the candidate median batch wall time, using the two process medians per version. The table reports the geometric mean of the three round speedups. All 360 formal timed batch samples are retained.

| Model | BS16 speedup | BS32 speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nano | 1.0788x | 1.0697x |
| Super | 1.0717x | 1.0668x |
| Ultra | 1.0581x | 1.0471x |

All three models improved in every measured round at both batch sizes.

## Issue tracking

Related PR: [#8114](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8114) (original optimization PR).

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

items.title: [Perf] DSv4.1: Enable encoder bounded replay with shared BCG metadata
items.author: Oasis-Git
items.summary: Encoder SWA bounded replay currently rejects breakable prefill CUDA graphs. Supporting the combination also needs correct live-row metadata at eager graph boundaries and bounded metadata allocation across capture buckets.
items.body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

Encoder SWA bounded replay currently rejects breakable prefill CUDA graphs. Supporting the combination also needs correct live-row metadata at eager graph boundaries and bounded metadata allocation across capture buckets.

## Modifications

- Enable encoder bounded replay with CUDA breakable prefill graphs; keep unsupported graph backends and hardware rejected.
- Refresh request-window metadata and keep dynamic KV stores and low-ratio compression at eager boundaries. Slice bucket-sized locations to live rows and size the request-window workspace for capture buckets as well as scheduled chunks.
- Preserve idle DP ranks when entering the decoder tail by clamping the CPU live-row count consistently with its GPU counterpart.
- Share page-table and c1/c2 index backing storage across prefill buckets, with independent full/tail buffers and stable captured addresses. Release inactive buckets' eager candidate tables without changing captured decode metadata ownership.
- Add focused CPU regressions for replay metadata refresh, idle tails, shared-storage isolation and candidate lifetime.

## Accuracy Tests

Local GB300 validation on the development base (`4fc86f73c`):

- 15 encoder replay CPU tests, 4 packed-KV CUDA tests, and a standalone graph probe passed. The probe checks shared addresses, exact integer outputs across bucket switches and tail isolation.
- Shared and unshared DEP4 servers each passed three 44-response smoke suites covering four DP ranks, 6–8192 input tokens and 1024/4096-token prefix-cache extensions. Both use the same idle-row fix.
- All compared first-token IDs and request/cache usage match. Complete generated sequences are not strictly identical: each version's two consecutive repetitions match on 38/44 sequences under the existing DSPARK configuration. These smoke tests do **not** establish strict numerical equivalence or model-quality accuracy.
- The shared 2048 capture limit also passed the same 44-response suite, including inputs exceeding the capture limit.

On the PR base (`14c4dda24`), the simplified 11-test encoder replay CPU suite passed. The 16 compressed-pool CPU tests and 4 packed-KV CUDA tests also passed before this test-only simplification; production code is unchanged. This also covers pool construction without a configured CUDA graph. The full-model memory/smoke measurements above used the earlier development base; they were not rerun on this newer base. No GitHub CI results are claimed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On four GB300 GPUs with attention-DP4/EP4, encoder and decoder bounded replay, `flashmla_mega`, DSPARK block size 5, memory fraction 0.7 and unchanged context limit:

| Prefill capture limit | Unshared | Shared |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 | 22.67 GiB/GPU | 12.58 GiB/GPU |
| 2048 | ~8 GiB/GPU (memory-only reference) | 5.17 GiB/GPU |

The unshared 2048 capture measured 8.05 GiB/GPU (rounded to ~8 GiB above), but that run subsequently failed startup validation; it is a memory-only reference, not a passing serving baseline.

These are **incremental prefill BCG capture memory** measurements, not total server memory or peak startup allocation. The 8192 shared result repeated across two server startups and all four ranks. No throughput improvement is claimed; sustained workload benchmarking and broader accuracy validation remain outstanding.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed Python files and check imports.
- [x] Add regression tests.
- [x] Provide local memory measurements and explicitly bounded correctness evidence.
- [ ] Run related upstream CI and model-quality accuracy validation.
