items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 on Jetson AGX Thor (sm_110): illegal memory access in GDN `_warmup_prefill_kernels` on cold-cache boots (3 of 4); warm caches 0 of 3
items.author: OriNachum
items.summary: a fresh container), startup crashes in the profile run with an illegal memory access in the GDN prefill warmup. It happens right after FlashInfer JIT-builds. [Discussion: Update: a warm-cache boot crashed too, at a different site.]
items.body:
### Your current environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Device | NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (sm_110, 20 SMs, 122 GB unified memory), JetPack R38.2.2, kernel 6.8.12-tegra, nvpmodel MAXN |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0-ubuntu2404` (`sha256:3fb023cc987c…`) |
| Versions | vLLM 0.31.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0.2 |
| Model | `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` + DFlash drafter `z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash` |

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On a **cold** boot (empty `/root/.cache`, i.e. a fresh container), startup crashes in the profile run with an illegal memory access in the GDN prefill warmup. It happens right after FlashInfer JIT-builds `fp8_gemm_cutlass`. With `/root/.cache/vllm` and `/root/.cache/flashinfer` persisted, every boot succeeds.

| Caches | Boots | Crashed |
|---|--:|--:|
| Cold (new container each boot) | 4 | **3** |
| Warm (cache dirs mounted, filled by a previous boot) | 3 | **0** |

The boot that fills the cache can itself crash, but the JIT module is already on disk, so the next boot loads it and serves.

```bash
docker run --rm --runtime nvidia --gpus all --ipc host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
```

items.title: [Fix] [Intel] kernels: Recognize XPU capabilities
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Fixes kernel capability detection to recognize Intel XPU as a distinct device type instead of incorrectly reporting it as CPU.
items.body:
Stack (5/6), merge in order: [#44851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44851) → [#44852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44852) → [#44853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44853) → [#44854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44854) → [#44863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44863) → [#44869](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44869)

Kernel capability detection currently reports `cpu` when Intel XPU is the available accelerator. Add `DeviceType.XPU` and `CapabilityRequirement.XPU`, and detect XPU after the existing accelerator checks. This lets the inventory describe XPU kernels and excludes XPU processes from CPU-only capabilities.

Validation on an Intel Arc Pro B70 with PyTorch 2.13.0+xpu:

- 123 namespace and fused-op dispatch tests passed across three separate test processes.
- Four Gemma4 XPU serving tests passed, covering one-step and three-step captured MTP.
- The new detection regression fails on the previous source. The patched hardware probe reports `xpu` with XPU available.
- Pre-commit checks passed.

items.title: [Bug]: Breakable prefill CUDA graphs replay corrupted outputs for some buckets: the shared output buffer is only weakly referenced
items.author: lucifer1004
items.summary: The bug is in Python-side memory ownership and does not depend on the model or the GPU. Authors and reviewers of #16609 (BCG in prefill). [Discussion: The fix and test are on https://github.com/lucifer1004/TensorRT-LLM/commit/e77beea626 (branch, base]
items.body:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM main @ acb83ac268, PyTorch backend, breakable prefill CUDA graphs (BCG, `BreakableCUDAGraphRunner`)
- Reproduced on an SM107 GPU, with torch 2.14. The bug is in Python-side memory ownership and does not depend on the model or the GPU.

### Who can help?

Authors and reviewers of #16609 (BCG in prefill).

### Reproduction

`BreakableCUDAGraphRunner.capture_output()` routes every bucket's body output through the largest bucket's output buffer. The first (largest) capture returns its output as `_shared_output`, and every later capture adds `self._shared_output[:num_tokens].copy_(output[:num_tokens])` to its graph. However, `_shared_output` is stored as `make_weak_ref(output)`, and nothing else holds that tensor: `_outputs[n]` is a weak ref too, and the original tensor goes out of scope after the capture. Its blocks are therefore free in the shared graph memory pool, so a later capture can allocate its own temporaries and body output on them.

When a later bucket's body output lands at an offset inside `_shared_output`, its final `copy_` reads and writes overlapping memory. The tensors have different storages, so PyTorch's overlap check does not catch this. Every replay of that bucket then returns a corrupted hidden state, while eager execution of the same inputs is correct.

Minimal reproduction: no model is needed. Each bucket is captured in descending order, then replayed and compared bitwise with eager:

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from tensorrt_llm._torch.pyexecutor.breakable_cuda_graph_runner import BreakableCUDAGraphRunner

hidden, narrow, buckets = 1024, 256, (2048, 1536, 1024, 512)

class Body(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, value):
        scaled = value[:, :narrow] * 2   # narrow temporary allocated before the output
        output = value * 3
        output[:, :narrow] += scaled
        return output

body = Body().cuda()
runner = BreakableCUDAGraphRunner(body)
static_input = torch.zeros(max(buckets), hidden, device="cuda")
active = {}

def engine_forward():
    value = static_input[: active["n"]]
    if runner.is_capturing:
        return runner.capture_model_body(lambda: body(value))
    return body(value)

for n in buckets:
    active["n"] = n
    runner.capture(n, engine_forward)

for n in buckets:
    static_input.normal_()
    expected = body(static_input[:n])
    active["n"] = n
    replayed = runner.execute(n, engine_forward)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    print(n, torch.equal(replayed, expected), (replayed - expected).abs().max().item())
```

On main, buckets 1536 and 1024 replay wrong on every replay; buckets 2048 and 512 are correct. Logging the pointers shows that the body outputs of 1536 and 1024 start 0.5 MiB and 2 MiB below `_shared_output` and overlap it. The output of 512 ends exactly where `_shared_output` begins. I also ran the same pattern with other shapes and with bf16, three processes each and three replay rounds per process. Every bucket whose output overlapped failed on every replay, and no other bucket failed.

We first saw this on a real model with the default prefill bucket list up to 8192 tokens. One large bucket (7168, or 6144 under a different capture order) overlapped the shared output by tens of MiB. Every replay of that bucket returned a wrong hidden state: the max |diff| against eager was the size of the largest reference value. All other buckets were bitwise exact. Whether a bucket overlaps depends on allocation order, so smaller bucket lists may or may not be affected.

### Expected behavior

Every captured bucket replays bitwise identical to eager execution with the same padded inputs.

### Actual behavior

Buckets whose body output is placed on the shared output buffer return corrupted outputs on every replay. Nothing reports an error.

### Additional notes

Fix: keep a strong reference to the first capture's output in `capture_output()`, i.e. `self._shared_output = output` instead of `make_weak_ref(output)`. `clear()` and the failure path of the first capture already reset it. The extra memory is one output tensor of the largest bucket, which stays allocated for the life of the graphs. In our case that was about 0.11 GiB for an 8192-token bucket and about 7 MiB for a 512-token bucket. With that change, the reproduction above and our model-level check, which compares all 24 buckets bitwise and runs a 300-step random replay soak, show no mismatch.

I have a branch with the fix and a unit test, which captures several buckets and compares each replay with eager, bitwise, in `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_breakable_cuda_graph.py`. On main the new test fails for both of its parametrizations; with the fix both pass. I will open the PR when I can.
discussion: The fix and test are on https://github.com/lucifer1004/TensorRT-LLM/commit/e77beea626 (branch `upstream/bcg-pin-shared-output`, based on main @ acb83ac268). It changes one line in `breakable_cuda_graph_runner.py` and adds a parametrized unit test.

items.title: [Kernel][Perf] Add H20 block-FP8 fused MoE config for E=512,N=128 (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 TP8, up to 2.0x)
items.author: yibol9768-alt
items.summary: No tuned config exists for this shape on, so vLLM logs and uses the default config. For M > 64 the default switches to. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

`Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` with TP=8 runs the Triton fused MoE with `E=512, N=128` (K=4096, top-k 10, 128x128 weight blocks). No tuned config exists for this shape on `NVIDIA_H20`, so vLLM logs

```
Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at .../E=512,N=128,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json
```

and uses the default config. For M > 64 the default switches to `BLOCK_SIZE_M=64`. With 512 experts and top-k 10, each expert gets only about M*10/512 rows, so most of each 64-row tile is padding. The tuned config keeps `BLOCK_SIZE_M=16` up to M=512 and uses 32 for most larger M, which roughly halves kernel time for M=96–512.

This PR adds that one config file. No code changes.

The H20-3e and H200 files for `E=512,N=128` are the unquantized (bf16) variants, so they don't apply to this block-FP8 path.

## Change

- New file: `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/E=512,N=128,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json`
- Produced by `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --tune` from main (`a0e7137`): 18 batch sizes, 1920 candidate configs each.

## Performance

Environment:

- 8x NVIDIA H20 (96 GB), driver 595.58.03
- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` (digest `c1c9f6fd5c10…`), torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1
- Model shape: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8`, TP=8, block-FP8 W8A8

Method: the official `benchmark_moe.py` (no `--tune`) on the same GPU. The baseline arm has no config file (default config); the tuned arm points `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` at the new file. The arms ran in the order baseline, tuned, tuned, baseline, and each number below is the mean of the two runs of that arm. For every M, the two runs of the same arm differ by at most 2.4%.

| M | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 30.81 | 30.80 | 1.000x |
| 2 | 38.53 | 38.56 | 0.999x |
| 4 | 55.13 | 52.25 | 1.055x |
| 8 | 76.06 | 76.09 | 1.000x |
| 16 | 119.22 | 118.41 | 1.007x |
| 24 | 164.85 | 158.19 | 1.042x |
| 32 | 187.75 | 187.91 | 0.999x |
| 48 | 240.31 | 229.44 | 1.047x |
| 64 | 276.37 | 255.88 | 1.080x |
| 96 | 623.76 | 308.08 | 2.025x |
| 128 | 671.65 | 328.39 | 2.045x |
| 192 | 717.32 | 347.38 | 2.065x |
| 256 | 733.54 | 362.60 | 2.023x |
| 384 | 748.09 | 375.48 | 1.992x |
| 512 | 759.82 | 401.12 | 1.894x |
| 1024 | 800.27 | 545.03 | 1.468x |
| 1536 | 835.38 | 672.32 | 1.243x |
| 2048 | 874.03 | 874.95 | 0.999x |
| 3072 | 1136.88 | 1131.08 | 1.005x |
| 4096 | 1643.07 | 1450.67 | 1.133x |

Rows within ±1% are treated as unchanged (noise). No batch size is slower beyond noise. An earlier run of the same comparison on an older build (dev20904, same Triton 3.7.1) gave the same numbers within 1%.

End-to-end serving numbers (`vllm bench serve`, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 TP8, before/after) are running and will follow in a comment.

## Test Plan and Results

Numerical check: the tuned config and the default config run on the same inputs through `fused_experts` (`override_config` for the tuned arm). Each output is compared with an fp32 torch reference that dequantizes the 128x128-block FP8 weights. The check covers 3 seeds x 20 batch sizes (1–4096, including M values between tuned keys, such as 3 and 200).

- Tuned vs default output: max relative L2 difference 0.0043, at the M values whose tuned config uses `BLOCK_SIZE_K=64` (1536, 3072, 4096). It is exactly 0 for every M up to 64 and for M=2048, and below 3e-4 everywhere else.
- Tuned vs reference and default vs reference: agree within 1e-5 at every point (about 0.046 relative L2). This error comes from FP8 activation quantization, which both arms share.
- All outputs finite.

```bash
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --tp-size 8 --dtype fp8_w8a8 --trust-remote-code \
  --batch-size 1 2 3 4 6 8 16 24 32 48 64 96 128 192 256 384 512 1024 1536 2048 3072 4096
```

- `python -m json.tool <config>`: passed.

This matches the kernel table. Each decode step runs the MoE with M ≈ the number of running requests. The kernel speedup starts at M=96, so the end-to-end gain shows up at concurrency 128, where TPOT drops by 27%. At concurrency 64 the kernel is only ~8% faster, which doesn't show end to end.

The −1% to −1.4% at concurrency 1 and 8 is within boot-to-boot variation as far as I can tell. In the kernel benchmark, M=1–8 are identical between the two configs (30.81 vs 30.80 us at M=1). items.title: [CI][AMD] Add queue fallback config for AMD GPU queues
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Main builds also run a few probe jobs on the closed queue so it can reopen once it is healthy again. Health is computed only from main builds, so failures on PR builds never close a queue.
items.body:
- Add `health.yaml`: where the queue-health checker publishes its snapshot and which pipeline it watches
- Add AMD `defaults.yaml`: close a queue on a high infra failure rate, then probe it for reopening
- Add `clusters.yaml`: the MI300, MI355 and MI250 queues that share one cluster are judged and closed together
- Add `mi300.yaml`, `mi355.yaml`, `mi250.yaml`: the fallback chain for each AMD device
- Point `ci_config.yaml` at the new `queue_fallbacks` directory

With this config, the pipeline generator moves AMD steps off a queue that the queue-health checker has marked as closed and sends them to the next open device in that device's chain. Main builds also run a few probe jobs on the closed queue so it can reopen once it is healthy again. Health is computed only from main builds, so failures on PR builds never close a queue. The generator side is in vllm-project/ci-infra#827, and the config does nothing until that lands and the `QUEUE_FALLBACK_BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN` secret and the `queue-health` pipeline exist. Until then every queue is treated as open and the generated pipeline is the same as today. NVIDIA queues are left out on purpose for now.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [Bugfix][Offload] Preserve CPU residency for renamed NVFP4 expert weights
items.author: yibol9768-alt
items.summary: Fixes CPU offload losing residency when NVFP4 MoE post-processing renames and repacks expert weights, restoring ~1 GiB of expert memory to CPU.
items.body:
## Overview

Preserve CPU/UVA residency when compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE post-processing renames and repacks expert weights. Restoration currently matches the serialized names and silently leaves the main weights on the GPU despite the offloader's log.

Related to the [NVFP4 rename report by Hivenet-Igor in #58178](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58178#issuecomment-5830101485); this targets that variant rather than every allocation problem in the thread.

## Claims

- Add an identity-by-default quantizer name-resolution hook and the two NVFP4 mappings; retain original/final names when restoring CPU residency. Already-resident parameters remain resident.
- On real Qwen3-30B-A3B NVFP4, expert-only `cpu_offload_gb=1` restores **1,107,296,256 additional expert bytes (1.03125 GiB)**. All **1299 parameter hashes** match baseline/candidate.
- The change runs during weight processing and adds no steady-state host read or synchronization. Capacity is traded for host-transfer latency; no speedup or general accuracy gain is claimed.

## Validation

RTX 5090, 400W, TP=1, MRV2 in-process engine, BF16 output, Triton attention, Marlin MoE and explicit CUTLASS dense. Model `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` at `a4df9f017835830cbb588cfe72bc4e50294183c0`.

Final runs use the **official wheel for exact base `ce49c47cbb241b59a32ef110079a5261dbd08e49`**, `vllm 0.32.0rc1.dev323+gce49c47cb`, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and Triton 3.8.0. Complete versions of the three Python files are copied from the corresponding Git tree into a separate environment; **no function-definition injection** is used in these runs. Compiled artifacts match the base; this PR changes no CUDA code.

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Existing-file regression, UVA on/off | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| Main expert bytes restored to host | 0 | 1,107,296,256 |
| CUDA allocated after engine initialization, 1 GiB fixed KV | 19,267,828,224 bytes | 18,160,531,968 bytes |
| Disjoint GSM8K rows 32–159, greedy, thinking off, cap 512 | 122/128 | 121/128 |
| Missing explicit numeric final answer | 0 | 0 |
| Exact-base decode-Graph real-model check | 8 requests complete | 8 requests complete |
| Decode-Graph fixed 4×24-token median, five repetitions | 0.263s | 1.128s (**4.29× wall time**) |

The regression uses real CUDA tensors and the actual offloader, with transformed byte-exact values and a resident control. It exercises rename/replacement under the loading context; real-model runs additionally execute the complete quantizer/repack/forward path.

### Numerical differences

Repeated identical stock requests vary even in the unmodified engine (selected raw-logit probe maximum difference 7.625). Earlier layer tracing locates the first observed divergence in Marlin MoE, with equal inputs; routed-token packing order changes between invocations. Freezing only that order makes both GEMMs and the real expert output bit-exact across CPU/UVA → GPU → restored CPU/UVA.

In the **exact-base complete model**, a canonical packing-order diagnostic also gives **20/20 bit-exact next-token raw-logit comparisons**, plus identical tokens and top-5 logprobs for all **12 generated requests** across those residency switches. This control adds synchronization and is confined to the reproduction harness; it is not part of the production fix or performance measurements. Stock inference remains non-deterministic, and the 128-question sample does not establish statistical accuracy equivalence.

[Complete-model control](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/evidence/nvfp4-investigate-exact-canonical.json), [paired evaluation](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/evidence/vllm-exact-heldout128-comparison.json), [native regression](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/evidence/native-offload-exact-patched.xml), [frozen versions, scripts, raw stock runs and limitations](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/README.md).

The Graph result exposes a substantial host-transfer cost on this PCIe machine. It is measured after one warmup with identical prompts/output-token counts; cooling occurs outside timings. The earlier eager-only 11–15% overhead must not be generalized to Graph execution. Offload remains an explicit capacity/latency tradeoff; the production change adds no per-token work when offload is disabled.

Full non-UVA pretrained inference fails in **both baseline and candidate** with `b_scales is not on GPU`, matching the externally cached scale issue already handled by open #43453. The unit cases validate tensor residency/restoration with UVA disabled; they do not establish full non-UVA NVFP4/Marlin support. ROCm, other MoE backends, multi-GPU execution and default multiprocessing/HTTP serving were not locally validated. The existing test file is part of the H200/AMD CPU-offload suite; local results do not replace upstream CI.

## Details

`w13_weight_packed` / `w2_weight_packed` become `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` before repacking. Matching only the original names misses those final parameters; unchanged scale names explain the partial offload. The quantizer owns the mapping, avoiding NVFP4-specific suffix guesses in the generic loader; other methods retain identity behavior.

Duplicate check: #56413/#58185/#60909 address allocation/pinning, #54972 allocator release, #57215 XPU transposes, #43453 externally held non-UVA scale references, and #56177/#37190 expert pools. Their inspected diffs do not restore these renamed weights. [Pinned diff audit and search limits](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/final-diff-audit.json).

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, validation and this write-up. The human contributor reviewed the production change and authorized the additional validation and PR updates.

items.title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] modelopt: Keep SM12x FP8 batch-invariant in deterministic mode
items.author: yibol9768-alt
items.summary: On SM12x, ModelOpt static-FP8 linears can change reduction schedules between cold prefill and a shorter prefix-cache-hit batch despite deterministic inference being enabled. The same input sequence then receives different scores.
items.body:
## Motivation

On SM12x, ModelOpt static-FP8 linears can change reduction schedules between cold prefill and a shorter prefix-cache-hit batch despite deterministic inference being enabled. The same input sequence then receives different scores.

Related to #41351's ModelOpt path. Credit to `furedericca-lab` for the [diagnosis and initial fallback](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/41351#issuecomment-5847506820), and `twu3202` for [identifying the small-M gap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/41351#issuecomment-5853051517). This does not claim to resolve every hybrid/GDN issue in that thread.

## Modifications

- In **SM12x deterministic mode only**, reuse Triton scaled MM with fixed N=64/K=128 reduction tiles. M-only tiles 16/32/128 reduce decode waste and improve long-prefill occupancy while retaining exact per-row results. Normal-mode and forced-Marlin dispatch remain unchanged.
- Zero masked A/B loads for partial K tiles.
- Extend the existing SM120 test file with 12 cold/cache row comparisons and two CUDA Graph replay cases covering strided 3D input, bias, BF16/FP16 output and a K=80 tail.

## Accuracy Tests

RTX 5090, 400W, TP=1, `nvidia/Qwen3-8B-FP8` at `2cebc4c89e25abc17668c81b01dceaf3d8b914d5`, BF16 output, Triton attention, deterministic mode.

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| 12 cold/cache native-method cases | 4 failed / 8 passed | 12 passed |
| Complete current SM120 test file | — | **137 passed**, including two new Graph cases |
| Prefixes 128/1024/4096, batches 1/4/2, two repetitions, eager and Graph | selected-score deltas up to 2.500 | **0 in all 12 comparisons**; warm repeats also 0 |
| Disjoint GSM8K rows 32–159, zero-shot greedy, thinking disabled, cap 512 | 119/128 | 117/128 |
| No parseable numeric final answer in that sample | 1 | 2 |

The row-tile optimization is bit-exact against the initial fixed-M=32 candidate in 120 isolated comparisons and produces **identical complete text on all 128 real-model evaluation questions**. The evaluation contains different reasoning errors and answer-format/truncation effects between baseline and candidate; it establishes neither a general accuracy gain nor statistical equivalence.

[Native test log](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/evidence/fp8-rowtiles-full-tests.log), [long-prefix Graph results](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/evidence/sglang-fp8-extended-patched-rowtiles-graph.json), [paired evaluation](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/evidence/sglang-heldout128-comparison.json), [scripts, versions and raw outputs](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/README.md).

Runtime: SGLang 0.5.21 compiled dependencies with the changed main-source Python definitions; affected baseline ASTs match main. This is not a complete main rebuild or upstream CI. The original hybrid TP=2 model, other SM12x devices and torch.compile were not tested locally. The existing registered test file remains SM120-gated.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Four workloads below use 32 forced output tokens per request, one warmup and five measured repetitions. Values are end-to-end medians; cooling to ≤55°C occurs outside each measurement. Graph runs capture decode batches 1/2/4 and prefill token sizes 4/128/256/1024/2048/4096/8192; unsupported partial prefills may fall back to eager.

| Prefix tokens / batch | Eager baseline → candidate | Graph baseline → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| 128 / 1 | 1.626s → 1.778s | 0.284s → 0.336s |
| 128 / 4 | 2.423s → 1.776s | 0.404s → 0.426s |
| 2048 / 1 | 1.666s → 1.784s | 0.500s → 0.597s |
| 2048 / 4 | 2.791s → 2.284s | 0.857s → 0.993s |

Graph wall time remains about **5–20% higher** on this measured matrix. This is an opt-in determinism fix with a measured cost, not a general speedup claim. Full samples and ranges are in the [benchmark records](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/fd948aa99130c601e1f35b50b260edf15d79c11e/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round2/README.md).

Duplicate check: inspected #34429 (small-M dispatch), #42865 (block/MXFP8), #38921 (SM89 prequantized inputs) and #44076 (GDN chunk alignment); these do not implement this static per-tensor deterministic path. [Original pinned diff audit](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/final-diff-audit.json).

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, validation and this description. The human contributor reviewed the original fix and authorized the additional validation and PR updates.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable pre-commit hooks pass.
- [x] Focused regressions extend the existing registered file.
- [x] Real pretrained-model correctness, quality and performance checks are recorded with limitations.
- [x] No new public invocation or interface; behavior and tradeoffs are documented here.

## Review and Merge Process

Maintainer review and upstream CI follow the normal project process. Local validation does not replace upstream CI.

items.title: [Fix] diffusion: Respect ancestor cgroup memory headroom
items.author: yibol9768-alt
items.summary: Diffusion host-memory planning can overcommit pinned memory when a parent cgroup has a larger limit but less remaining headroom than the child. For example, a child using 10GiB of 32GiB under a parent using 60GiB of 64GiB has 4GiB remaining, not 22GiB.
items.body:
## Motivation

Diffusion host-memory planning can overcommit pinned memory when a parent cgroup has a larger limit but less remaining headroom than the child. For example, a child using 10GiB of 32GiB under a parent using 60GiB of 64GiB has 4GiB remaining, not 22GiB. Sibling usage counts against the parent.

## Modifications

Select the ancestor with the least `max(0, limit - usage)` rather than the least numeric limit. Apply the existing file-cache exclusion before comparison. Extend the existing budget tests with four v1/v2 cases, including cache-adjusted headroom.

## Accuracy Tests

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Extended host-budget file | 4 failed / 32 passed | 36 passed |
| Actual delegated cgroup v2 + 512MiB anonymous sibling | Overstates headroom and accepts a 128MiB allowance | Rejects that allowance |
| Real SANA 600M, live nested cgroups, one streamed / 27 resident DiT blocks | Books 41,292,288 persistent pinned bytes | Keeps the streamed block pageable |

Both SANA prompts complete with pixel-identical outputs; both arms have zero OOM/OOM-kill events. Ordinary GPU-resident SANA outputs also match. No production OOM was deliberately induced. The isolated fixture releases its unused allocator/cache pages, then calibrates actual cgroup limits once; the production budget calculation is unchanged apart from this patch.

SANA revision: `28f3af7689de15f3883d5863059a2fca0aa9b829` of `Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_1024px_diffusers`, RTX 5090, TP=1, eager, 512×512, two prompts. **Both model arms use the same AutoencoderDC checkpoint-loading prerequisite whose root fix is already in #44690. That prerequisite is not included in this PR.** The budget unit/live-cgroup probes do not depend on that VAE correction.

[Raw budget probe](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/host-budget-live-cgroup.json), [nested baseline](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/sana-cgroup-baseline.json), [nested candidate](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/sana-cgroup-patched.json), [scripts and raw outputs](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/README.md).

Actual unit entry points in the isolated SGLang runtime:

```bash
python test_host_budget_linux.py --baseline
python test_host_budget_linux.py
```

They select the respective main-source budget module and collect the changed `test_host_memory_budget.py` with real Linux dependencies. The production/source snapshots and guarded model entry points are in the linked evidence package. Runtime uses SGLang 0.5.21 compiled dependencies with relevant main Python definitions; this is not a rebuilt complete main. Relevant baseline definitions match main; upstream CI remains necessary.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speedup is claimed. Respecting the parent budget can intentionally select the existing pageable/staged transfer fallback. The goal is to honor headroom and the existing reserve, not to change inference math. GPU validation retained 400W and a 72°C stop threshold.

Targeted duplicate check: #37917 changes residency quotas, #36727 mapped offload/per-rank sharing, #37811 unified-pool residency, and #44540 HiCache physical ownership. Their inspected diffs do not change this function's binding-ancestor selection. [Pinned heads and search limits](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/final-diff-audit.json).

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and this description. The human contributor reviewed the local changes and validation material before authorizing submission.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit; all applicable hooks passed.
- [x] Add focused regression tests in the existing test file.
- [x] Documentation considered: no new public interface or invocation; behavior and limits documented here.
- [x] Provide relevant accuracy/capacity and speed results below, with their measurement limits.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

Maintainer review and upstream CI are requested through the normal merge-oncall/codeowner process. Local results do not replace upstream CI.

items.title: [RFC]: Request-scoped auxiliary decision heads on a shared generative backbone
items.author: sylvanus4
items.summary: RFC to integrate request-scoped auxiliary decision heads sharing the same generative backbone and forward pass in vLLM, avoiding duplicate weight loads across engines.
items.body:
**Question for maintainers:** can vLLM support request-scoped auxiliary decision readouts inside an existing generation
engine, consumed through the current Decisions / ReadStrategy interfaces, without running an auxiliary branch for
ordinary generation requests?

## Motivation.

Some deployments pair a generative model with a small decision model on the same backbone: a retrieval/evidence gate in
RAG ("answer, retrieve more, or abstain"), a router, a guard. When the decision model is a trained head, or a few
adapted layers, on that backbone, serving it as a second engine loads the backbone twice and splits the GPU, even
though most of the computation is shared.

vLLM now covers the API side well: `/v1/systemone` (#59299) and `/v1/decisions` (#60465) are merged, read strategies
are being made modular (#59365), and D3 decision models (#61565) are served through a read strategy on the classify
task. What is still missing is in the engine:

- `NextTokenStrategy` reads label tokens through the LM head, so a decision is only as good as the model's next-token
  distribution over label words. A trained decision head cannot be used this way.
- `D3Strategy` runs on the pooling runner (`task = "classify"`), which by design does not generate in the same engine.
- Per-request last hidden states (RFC #59542, PR #59543, open) let a client apply its own head to the final hidden
  state. A head that reads an intermediate layer, or a short branch of decoder layers with its own adapter, cannot be
  applied client-side.

We run such a deployment out of tree: **ECP-SB v0.1.0**, a vLLM plugin that serves a 27B Qwen3.5-family model for
generation and, from the same engine and the same single weight load, a 3-way evidence gate. The gate re-runs the last 4
decoder layers (44-47) with a LoRA-merged MLP and an fp32 head ([code](https://github.com/ThakiCloud/ecp-shared-backbone-vllm),
Apache-2.0; [weights](https://huggingface.co/ThakiCloud/ECP-SB-27B-Research)). To fit the current engine it needs three
workarounds:

1. gate requests are recognised by a **token signature** at the end of the prompt;
2. the branch runs on **every scheduled token of every step**, whether or not a gate request is in the batch;
3. the head's fp32 logits are **bit-packed into extra columns of the hidden-state tensor**, and `compute_logits`
   overwrites the LM logits with `-inf` except three label tokens.

This RFC proposes the engine piece that removes those workarounds. It does **not** propose a new decisions API.

**Disclosure.** The gate model behind that deployment is a research model and misses its own safety target (pooled
unsupported-answer rate 6.5% vs a 5% target). It illustrates the serving pattern and is not a recommendation to use it
as a safety control. Its port to vLLM 0.31 also failed our own frozen mixed-traffic generation criterion (1/64
token-divergent vs a 0/64 stock-vs-stock floor in that run). We report that result as recorded and do not revise it.

## Proposed Change.

Two layers. The first is the core of this RFC; the second only connects it to the existing APIs.

### 1. Engine: per-request auxiliary readouts in the generate runner (Model Runner V2)

```python
llm = LLM(model, enable_aux_readouts=True)          # engine flag, default False
sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, aux_readouts=["evidence_gate"])
out = llm.generate(prompt, sp)[0].outputs[0]
out.aux_readouts["evidence_gate"]                     # float32 tensor [len(token_ids), 3]
```

- A readout is returned for each generated token, at the row its logits were computed from (the same rows as
  #59543). The decision-only shape is `max_tokens=1`.
- Requests that do not set `aux_readouts` get `None` and are otherwise unaffected.
- With the flag off, requests that set `aux_readouts` are rejected, and the runner holds no readout state and does no
  readout work.

Model interface:

```python
@runtime_checkable
class SupportsAuxReadout(Protocol):
    supports_aux_readout: ClassVar[Literal[True]] = True
    aux_readout_dims: ClassVar[dict[str, int]]     # name -> width
    aux_readout_stateful: ClassVar[bool] = False   # readout keeps per-request state across steps

    def set_aux_readout_rows(self, rows: torch.Tensor | None) -> None: ...
    def compute_aux_readouts(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, rows: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: ...
```

Per step:

1. Before the forward, the runner passes the row indices of the scheduled requests that asked, or `None` when none
   did. **`None` means the model must do no readout work.**
2. After the forward, if rows were passed, the runner calls `compute_aux_readouts` and gathers the result per request,
   `[num_rows, sum(widths)]` float32, with columns sliced to each request's names.

What a readout reads is up to the model. A head on the final hidden state is a few lines. A branch of decoder layers
with its own KV/recurrent state is also possible (our case), and the engine stays unaware of it.

Engine semantics in the prototype:

- **Steps with readout rows run without CUDA graphs** (`need_eager`). Steps without readout rows dispatch as before.
  - A decision request with `max_tokens=1` lives only in prefill steps. In our 27B workload those steps were above the
    CUDA graph capture size and ran eagerly anyway (see Validation).
  - Open question: excluding readout steps only from FULL graphs, and keeping PIECEWISE, would cover small readout
    steps. The prototype has this behind an experiment switch, but it is **not validated** yet.
- **`aux_readout_stateful = True`** makes readout requests skip prefix-cache reads, because a cached prefix never built
  the readout's own state.
- Rejected at start-up, as in #59543: the V1 runner, non-generate runners, speculative decoding, PP, and CP.
- **Transport and serialization** follow #59543:
  - `ModelRunnerOutput.aux_readouts: dict[req_id, Tensor]`;
  - `EngineCoreOutput.new_aux_readouts`, appended last;
  - accumulated by the output processor and split by name into `CompletionOutput.aux_readouts`.

  Readouts are float32 tensors on the default msgspec path. **No insecure (pickle) serialization is needed.** One of our
  earlier diagnostic runs set `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1`, but only so that the test harness could call
  `LLM.apply_model` with a Python function to read branch counters. The mixed-traffic run below uses default
  serialization throughout. Its counters come from a log written by the model, behind an environment variable.

The prototype is about 300 library lines across 13 files: a protocol, a registry field, a config flag and validation,
a `SamplingParams` field, a runner hook, and transport.

### 2. Decisions: one read strategy, no API change

A read strategy for models that declare readouts would:

- send `max_tokens=1, aux_readouts=[name]`;
- map the readout's columns to the question's options, the way `D3Strategy` maps codes;
- return `QuestionRead` as usual.

`/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions` stay as they are. It would be one entry in `READ_STRATEGIES` today, or one plugin
under the registry #59365 proposes. This step is optional and comes after the engine piece.

### Relationship to existing work

| Work | Relationship |
|---|---|
| #59299 `/v1/systemone`, #60465 `/v1/decisions` (merged) | Unchanged and reused. This RFC adds no endpoint or wire format. |
| #59365 modular read strategies (open) | Complementary. A readout-backed strategy is one more backend for that registry. This RFC does not depend on the registry's design. |
| #59542 / #59543 last hidden states (open) | Same opt-in pattern and the same transport path. We would rather share one per-request auxiliary output channel than add a second one. Hidden states suit client-side heads on the final layer. Readouts suit model-defined heads, including intermediate-layer branches, and return a few floats per token instead of `hidden_size`. |
| #61565 D3 on the classify task (merged) | Unchanged. That path is pooling. This one stays a generate-runner output, so decisions and generation share one engine, which also addresses the "one engine, one task" concern raised in #12249 / #40804. |
| #33736 `extract_hidden_states` | Different goal (export for drafter training). Our model reuses its custom-op-in-graph pattern for the layer-44 capture. |

## Validation.

**Prototype on vLLM nightly `49cb2bb`, Model Runner V2, one B200.** Three engines ran on the same build:

- stock;
- the v0.1.0 workaround (branch every step);
- readouts.

**Tiny real-architecture Qwen3.5.** 8 layers, hybrid GDN/full attention, and a random LoRA + head branch on layers 2-5.
There were 4 gate items and 8 generation prompts. These numbers check the plumbing, not model quality.

- **vLLM-side GPU test:** passes, 8/8 cases. The first version had one bug (an unhashable field in the model-info
  record), which is now fixed.
- **Readout vs the v0.1.0 path:** max |Δ log p| 1.8e-6, with 0/4 decision flips.
- **Generation with the feature on but unused vs stock:** 0/8 token-divergent.

**27B.** Qwen3.8-27B bf16 with the published gate, 256 gate items and 64 RAG generation prompts. Settings were identical
across engines: max_num_seqs 64, CUDA graphs on, no prefix caching, no chunked prefill.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Readout vs the v0.1.0 path, same weights | max \|Δ log p\| 1.7e-4; 0/256 decision changes under the frozen threshold rule |
| Gate branch work when no request asks (counter in the model) | 0 calls after load, after 64 generation-only requests, and during all throughput runs |
| Generation, feature on but unused, vs stock | 0/64 token-divergent, max logprob gap 0 |
| Generation-only throughput vs stock, batch 1 / 8 / 32 / 64, median of 3 | v0.1.0 branch-every-step: −7.3% / −7.7% / −7.8% / −7.7%. Readouts: +0.3% / −0.3% / −0.2% / −0.3% |
| GPU memory after load | 151.8 / 150.8 / 151.9 GiB (stock / v0.1.0 / readouts) |
| Readout of a request alone vs inside a mixed batch (64 generation + 256 readout requests) | 0/256 decision changes; 1/256 items moved by more than .01 in probability (max .016) |

The throughput numbers are three repeats from one setup on one GPU. They are not a general serving-throughput claim.
Zero branch calls also does not mean zero added cost: the model still copies the layer-44 input inside the compiled
graph on every step. The remaining difference of about 0.3% is not attributed.

The first 27B run also found **4/64 generation sequences that changed when readout requests shared the batch**. We ran
a matched control on the same build and inputs. Each condition was repeated 3 times in a rotated order, and stock was
also run in a second process.

| Condition | Engine | Traffic in one `generate` call |
|---|---|---|
| A | stock | 64 generation requests |
| B | stock | 64 generation + 256 plain 1-token requests (same token ids as the readout requests) |
| C | readouts | 64 generation requests (feature unused) |
| D | readouts | 64 generation + 256 readout requests |
| E | readouts | 64 generation + 256 plain 1-token requests |

| Comparison | Token-divergent sequences out of 64 (repeats 1 / 2 / 3) |
|---|---|
| D vs E: same engine and batch, only `aux_readouts` differs | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| B vs A: stock, plain requests join the batch | 5 / 4 / 4 |
| D vs C: readout requests join the batch | 4 / 4 / 4 |
| D vs B: readout engine vs stock, same traffic | 1 / 0 / 0 |
| Identical repeats of one condition (A, B, C, D, E) | at most 1 |

- **The 4/64 is a batch-composition effect that stock shows too.** The same four prompts change at the same token
  positions in stock when the plain requests join (B vs A) as when readout requests join (D vs C).
- **The repeat-to-repeat 1/64 is stock's own run-to-run variation.** It is always one prompt, flipping at token 16, and
  it appears in stock repeats, in a second stock process, and once in a readout-engine repeat.
- **Readout decisions agreed with the v0.1.0 path:** 0/256 changes in every repeat.
- **The branch ran only in the readout runs** (34 calls per D run) and never during C or E.
- **CUDA graph status was checked from a model-side log.** Every readout step, and every matching step in E, ran without
  CUDA graphs: they carry thousands of prefill tokens, above the capture size.

What this does and does not establish:

- We found **no generation change attributable to readouts**: in this experiment, readout requests changed co-batched
  generation exactly as plain requests of the same shape did.
- Our pre-registered rule still returns **INCONCLUSIVE**, not PASS. It requires a zero stock-vs-stock floor, and stock
  was not repeat-stable here (1/64). We keep that verdict as recorded.
- **Generation equivalence under mixed traffic is therefore not established in general.** Readout steps small enough
  for a CUDA graph (short prompts, or readouts during decode) were not exercised, so the eager fallback was not tested
  on steps where it changes the execution mode.
- The v0.1.0 workaround on vLLM 0.28 passed its frozen deployment criteria (generation-only 2/64 vs a 1/64 stock
  floor). Its vLLM 0.31 port failed them, as noted above. Those runs used the older stack and V1 runner and are not
  re-judged here.

## Phased plan

1. **[Core] Per-request auxiliary readouts (MRV2).** This is the first PR, kept minimal:
   - flag and validation, the `SamplingParams` field, and the runner hook with rows / `None`;
   - transport, shared with #59543 if that lands first;
   - the stateless reference test: an OPT-125m head whose readout must equal the engine's own raw logits of three
     tokens, and "no readout work when nobody asks".

   No stateful branches, intermediate-layer capture, or decisions integration in this PR.
2. **[Model] `SupportsAuxReadout` docs and a stateless in-tree example.** Plus `aux_readout_stateful` and its
   prefix-cache rule, with a test.
3. **[Frontend] A readout-backed read strategy** for `/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions` (optional).
4. **Follow-up RFC.** Running a stateful branch on only the asking requests' tokens (today it runs on all tokens of an
   asking step), and a CUDA graph policy for small readout steps.

## Feedback Period.

Two weeks.

## CC List.

@mmastrac (#59299 structured decisions), @Timiku (#59365 read strategies), @aminry (#59542 / #59543 hidden states)

## Any Other Things.

Open questions:

1. One channel for raw hidden states (#59543) and readouts, or two fields? We lean to one container with typed entries,
   and would align with #59543 rather than compete with it.
2. Is a model-owned branch with its own KV/GDN state acceptable as an in-tree pattern? Or should in-tree examples stay
   stateless while stateful branches remain plugins?
3. Readout steps and CUDA graphs: is forcing eager acceptable for a first version? Or should readout steps only be
   excluded from FULL graphs from the start?

Not proposed: a new endpoint or wire format, changes to generation logits, training, or official support for our
specific model.

Disclosure: this RFC and the prototype were prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The numbers come from committed
experiment ledgers. The prototype code has not yet had a full line-by-line human review. That review, the
`pr-checklist`, and the required `Co-authored-by` / DCO trailers will come before any PR.

items.title: [Fix] multimodal: Clear the embedding cache in Scheduler.flush_cache
items.author: bowenwan6
items.summary: The scheduler keeps the vision encoder's output for an image or a video in, keyed by a hash of the input. resets the radix cache, the KV pools and the grammar cache, but not this cache, and nothing else clears it.
items.body:
Clears the multimodal embedding cache when the scheduler flushes its caches. Before this, a server
whose weights were updated kept answering an image it had seen before with the embeddings of the
old vision encoder.

#36468 by @yuanlehome proposed the same change first. This pull request adds a regression test in
the existing flush test file and checks the fix on nine models (images, video and audio) against
fresh servers, bitwise. Happy to work with the author on either pull request, or for the
maintainers to merge whichever they prefer.

## Motivation

The scheduler keeps the vision encoder's output for an image or a video in
`mm_schedule.embedding_cache`, keyed by a hash of the input. `Scheduler.flush_cache()` resets the
radix cache, the KV pools and the grammar cache, but not this cache, and nothing else clears it.

`update_weights_from_disk`, `update_weights_from_tensor`, `update_weights_from_distributed` and
`update_weights_from_ipc` all end in `flush_cache()`. So do `/flush_cache` and
`release_memory_occupation` when it releases the KV cache. After a weight update the radix cache
is empty, but an image the server has seen before still gets the old encoder's embeddings, and the
model answers it as if the vision weights had not changed. A new image already gets the new ones.

The cache is on by default for most VLMs (`SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB`, 100 MiB). Qwen3-VL on large
Hopper GPUs and `--rl-on-policy-target` turn it off unless the variable is set.

The memory is not returned either: `flush_cache()` empties the allocator cache while the cached
tensors are still referenced.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU
- Base: upstream `abf92826ee54`, with and without this change
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, default server arguments and `SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB=512`
  (set because Qwen3-VL turns the cache off on this GPU)
- Updated weights: a copy of the checkpoint with `model.visual.merger.linear_fc2.weight` set to
  zero. The language model is unchanged, so a different answer to an image prompt can only come
  from different image embeddings.
- Requests: two synthetic 448x448 images (image 1: a red circle and a blue square; image 2: a green
  triangle and an orange bar), "Describe this image in one sentence.", greedy, 48 tokens

On each server: ask about image 1, call `/update_weights_from_disk` with the changed checkpoint,
ask about image 1 again and about image 2 for the first time. A fresh server started on the
changed checkpoint gives the reference answers.

| Server | Image 1, before the update | Image 1, after the update | Image 2, after the update |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | ... a red circle and a blue square on a white background. | ... a red circle and a blue square on a white background. | A green triangle sits atop a solid orange rectangle against a plain white background. |
| With this change | ... a red circle and a blue square on a white background. | ... a red circle and a blue rectangle against a plain white background. | A green triangle sits atop a solid orange rectangle against a plain white background. |
| Fresh server, changed checkpoint | | ... a red circle and a blue rectangle against a plain white background. | A green triangle sits atop a solid orange rectangle against a plain white background. |

Every answer to image 1 begins with "The image displays a simple composition of".

On the base server image 1 keeps its old answer after the update, although the radix cache was
flushed (the server log shows the request after the update prefilling all 213 prompt tokens, none
cached). Image 2 matches the fresh server on both, so the weights themselves were updated. With
this change image 1 matches the fresh server too.

The same holds with the ViT CUDA graph and with `/update_weights_from_tensor`, the path RL
trainers use (upstream `a8aaf95b58e0`, same model and images; the tensor update sets the same
weight to zero):

| ViT | Update | Base: image 1 after the update | With this change: image 1 after the update |
|---|---|---|---|
| eager | `update_weights_from_disk` | old answer | identical to the fresh server |
| eager | `update_weights_from_tensor` | old answer | identical to the fresh server |
| `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` | `update_weights_from_disk` | old answer | identical to the fresh server |
| `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` | `update_weights_from_tensor` | old answer | identical to the fresh server |

"Identical" means the same tokens with the same log probabilities, compared with a fresh server
on the changed checkpoint (with the same ViT mode) that flushed its cache before the request, as
the updated server just did. The ViT graph is captured before the update and replayed after it;
its answer equals that of a graph captured with the new weights. Without the flush, a fresh
server's first request takes 4 prompt tokens from the radix cache left by its warm-up, and its log
probabilities differ by up to 0.12.

The same check on eight more models, each with the last layer of its own projector set to zero and
compared bitwise with a fresh server (two H200): Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL2.5-2B (each
also with its ViT CUDA graph), GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking, Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct, DeepSeek-VL2-tiny,
Pixtral-12B, Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct with an audio input, and LLaVA-OneVision-0.5B; and on
Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct with a video input. Every model that goes through the embedding cache gave the
old answer on the base server and the fresh server's answer with this change. LLaVA-OneVision
encodes in its own forward and was not affected.

## Modifications

- Add `clear_mm_embedding_cache()` to `mm_schedule`, next to `init_mm_embedding_cache()`.
- Call it in `Scheduler.flush_cache()` before the allocator cache is emptied, so the memory is
  returned as well.
- Add `test_flush_cache_drops_cached_mm_embeddings` to
  `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_flush_cache_after_retract.py` (CPU): a bare
  `Scheduler` flushes with a real `MultiModalStaticCache` holding one entry, which must be gone
  afterwards.

Not covered here: Kimi-VL's vision tower keeps its own cache of interpolated position embeddings
per image grid, which also survives a weight update; that needs a change in the model and is left
to a separate pull request.

Nothing else holds encoder output across a flush. The tokenizer's preprocessing cache stores
processor output, not encoder output, and is already cleared on `/flush_cache` and after weight
updates. The encoder server of encoder disaggregation has its own embedding cache, but no
weight-update endpoint, so its weights cannot change while it runs.

## Accuracy Tests

No model, kernel or forward code changes.

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_flush_cache_after_retract.py -v
```

Without the change, the new case fails (`AssertionError: 1 != 0`: the cached entry is still
there) and the six existing cases pass. With the change all seven pass. The existing cases
flush without an embedding cache, which covers the `None` check.

```bash
pytest test/registered/unit/managers test/registered/unit/multimodal \
  test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py
```

| Tree | Result |
|---|---|
| upstream `a8aaf95b58e0` | 2 failed, 1190 passed, 43 skipped |
| with this change | 2 failed, 1191 passed, 43 skipped |

The two failures are the same on both trees and unrelated: two cases of
`test_mm_process_config.py` set `tp_size=8` in a single process and stop on
`ValueError: parallel topology is inconsistent`. The extra pass is the new case.

`pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Serving is not affected: the new call runs only when the caches are flushed. After a flush or a
weight update, an input that was cached is encoded once more. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B (one H200, a
448x448 image, 10 runs) the first token after a flush takes 64.1 ms instead of 40.6 ms.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing API or configuration change.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable: no kernel or forward change; the reproduction above shows the answers before and after.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #39009397005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39009397005)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->

items.title: Optimize NVLS MoE dispatch
items.author: Waterpine
items.summary: Reduce kernel launches in ordinary NVLS MoE inference by fusing routing-padding masking into all-gather and BF16 conversion into reduce-scatter When eligible, reduce-scatter also adds the overlapped shared-expert output. The implementation preserves the origin…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Reduce kernel launches in ordinary NVLS MoE inference by fusing routing-padding masking into all-gather and BF16 conversion into reduce-scatter

When eligible, reduce-scatter also adds the overlapped shared-expert output. The implementation preserves the original two-step rounding: convert the FP32 reduction result to BF16, then perform the BF16 addition

This PR extracts the ordinary NVLS changes from [#8114](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8114):

- Fuse routing-padding masking into the existing all-gather
- Write BF16 outputs directly from the FP32 reduce-scatter
- Fuse the shared-expert addition when dtype, layout and autograd conditions allow it
- Preserve the existing computation steps for both ordered and multimem batch-invariant paths.

Router kernels, NCCL dispatch, expert GEMM/alignment/sum kernels and TP reductions are outside this PR. This change does not depend on the fused-router PR [#8296](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8296).

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Validation

The comparison baseline is main `442d018`. All five changed files in the current commit `ab7127a` are byte-identical to the validated snapshot `77a57e4`.

### Correctness

Full-logit validation covered Nano, Super and Ultra on two nodes with four GB300 GPUs per node, using TP8/EP8/ETP1, BF16 weights, FP32 router, MAMBA_DETERMINISTIC=1 and BI disabled

All 60 tested configurations passed bitwise comparisons:
- Three models × five workloads × eager/decode CUDA graphs × shared-expert overlap off/on
- Every valid prefill, mixed and decode position, including all 131072 vocabulary entries, compared through integer views
- Input IDs, positions, generated tokens and repeated runs also matched
- A one-bit negative control verified the comparator.

Prefill and mixed steps remained eager in the decode-graph configurations. Padding rows were excluded from logit comparisons

Additional validation:
- EP4 dispatcher suite: 146 passed and five optional-backend prerequisite skips per rank
- EP8 dispatcher suite: 126 passed and five skips per rank on identical production code, followed by 40 final padding/offset cases per rank. These counts overlap
- Added determinism replay tests covering BF16 rounding ties, overflow, subnormal values and signed zero
- isort, black, ruff, compileall, determinism coverage and git diff --check passed

The optional skips require unavailable DeepGEMM BF16 or specific TE/cuBLASLt support. Literal zero-row tensors reproduce an existing Triton compilation issue on both baseline and candidate; supported padded engine cases are covered.

### Performance

Measured uninstrumented whole-batch generation with 32–33 prompt tokens and 128 generated tokens per request, decode CUDA graphs, BI off and shared-expert overlap off. Loading, warmup, tokenization and enqueue are excluded

Each of three allocations used four fresh processes: ABBA at BS16 and BAAB at BS32, with five timed generations per process

Speedup is baseline latency divided by candidate latency. The table reports geometric means of the three per-allocation median-latency ratios; all formal rounds are retained

| Model | BS16 speedup | BS32 speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nano | 1.013x | 1.006x |
| Super | 1.013x | 1.005x |
| Ultra | 1.010x | 1.005x |

All three models showed modest end-to-end improvements in the three-round aggregate results. No model-specific tuning was introduced

## Issue tracking

Related to [#8114](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8114). Fused sigmoid/router changes are tracked separately in [#8296](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8296).

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.
