items.title: [Bug]: NixlConnector P/D: pulls and deferred notifications against TTL-evicted remote agents block 60s per call in libfabric connect(), starving DP engines to death
items.author: mevince
items.summary: The death is the end state of a stall loop: after a remote (prefill) engine is TTL-evicted (, default 3600 s), any subsequent NIXL call against its agent — a fresh pull, a heartbeat for a still-waiting request, or a deferred per-request notification that does…
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM: 0.31.0 nixl: 1.4.1 Hardware: 8x B200 per node, multi-node, RDMA (EFA) interconnect Platform: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04 based container Topology: P/D disaggregation — prefill TP8 (one pod per node) x12, decode TP1/DP8/EP8 x4 KV transfer: NixlConnector, kv_role: kv_both, pull mode, backends: [LIBFABRIC], kv_load_failure_policy: recompute Model: MLA-based MoE with MTP speculative decoding (not implicated — the failure path is entirely connector/transport level) Relevant defaults: engine_ttl = 3600 s, kv_lease_duration = 30 s ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary** In P/D disaggregation with the NixlConnector (pull mode, libfabric backend), every decode engine we run dies on a cadence of ~2–3.1 h after its own start, with no application-level error, whether or not rollout churn is still in progress. The death is the end state of a stall loop: after a remote (prefill) engine is TTL-evicted (`engine_ttl`, default 3600 s), any subsequent NIXL call against its agent — a fresh pull, a heartbeat for a still-waiting request, or a deferred per-request notification that `_cleanup_remote_engine` does not clear — enters libfabric's `connect()`, which since nixl 1.4.0 blocks up to `NIXL_LIBFABRIC_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` (60 s, a compile-time constant) waiting for a reciprocal handshake the peer will never send: nixl's handshake receive path has no reply — it only stores the sender's agent index — and a handshake is only ever sent from a peer's own connect flow, which an already-connected peer never re-enters. The blocks run serially in the engine worker thread and starve the shared-memory broadcast across all DP ranks; the watchdog or a gloo peer teardown then kills the process. On nixl 1.3.2 the identical fleet and config ran for a week with zero restarts — `connect()` has no wait there — so the blocking wait is the amplifier that turns local registry churn into engine death. **Observed behavior (one representative episode)** 1. `Evicted stale remote engine (inactive for 3800.6s)` — the normal TTL eviction path after an idle window (the loop and log line: base_worker.py:3596-3602 / :3697 at v0.31.0). 2. **25 minutes later**, the same decode worker still issued a deferred `send_notif` to that engine's agent (`_send_pending_recv_notifs`, base_worker.py:3199 at v0.31.0): the call blocked 60 s in ``` Handshake from peer '' not received after 60s; connection cannot be established. ``` (libfabric_backend.cpp:~800-845 at nixl 1.4.1; the 60 s constant is defined at libfabric_common.h:58), then failed with `nixlRemoteDisconnectError`, logged as `notification_failed. P worker blocks will be freed after timeout.` `_cleanup_remote_engine` (base_worker.py:3657) clears every per-engine table but cannot reach the pending-notification map — it is keyed by request id (base_worker.py:849), so notifications keep targeting evicted engines' agents indefinitely. 3. Serial 60 s stalls follow; each one coincides with all 8 `EngineCore_DP*` ranks logging ``` No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds ``` 4. Death by one of three observed terminations: watchdog `TimeoutError: RPC call to take_draft_token_ids timed out` → `EngineDeadError` fan-out to all API servers; a gloo `Connection closed by peer` from a sibling DP rank, followed by force-kill of the remaining engine processes; or (first incident) the `makeXferReq` race below. Always 2–3.1 h after pod start (the TTL-eviction cadence), including after the fleet fully settled. **Churn manufactures stale references faster than they retire** Adjacent log pairs show the eviction racing in-flight transfer setup: ``` T Evicted stale remote engine (inactive for 3800.2s) T+1 s makeXferReq: remote agent '' was invalidated in between prepXferDlist and this call transfer_setup_failed. Deferring failure reporting until outstanding transfers finish ``` The v0.31.0 lifecycle machinery widens the exposure surface: #50047's eager release of replaced peers, #54689's evict-hold (engines with a hung read are pinned indefinitely — the pinned agents keep getting dialed), and #56104's failure deferral (requests retained on transfers that never finish). Each is a source of "locally released remote state that some code path still references". Three code paths produce the post-eviction touches (v0.31.0 line numbers): `start_load_kv` re-handshakes whenever the engine is missing from `_remote_agents` (pull_worker.py:76-92); `_send_heartbeats` calls `_ensure_handshake` for the engine of every waiting request on every scheduler step (base_worker.py:3217) — and at v0.31.0 engine activity is stamped only on handshake completion and read issue (base_worker.py:1336, pull_worker.py:156), so engines with merely *waiting* requests still TTL-evict (#59871), after which every heartbeat becomes a full 60 s re-handshake; and `_send_pending_recv_notifs` (base_worker.py:3199) sends to stored agent names with no registry check. **Prefill-side mirror (the loop is fleet-wide, not local)** Every prefill pod logs KV-lease expirations with zero retrievals, sustained for hours: ``` Worker_TP{0..7}: Releasing expired KV blocks for request chatcmpl- which were retrieved by 0 remote worker(s) before lease expired. NixlPullConnector={'Num successful transfers': 0, ..., 'Num KV expired reqs': 41, ...} ``` Request ids match decode-side failed pull attempts exactly: decode's failed pull for `chatcmpl-` against prefill host X at time T ↔ prefill's `retrieved by 0 remote worker(s)` for the same `chatcmpl-` at T−30 s. Some requests additionally produce the late-retrieval form: ``` ERROR [pull_worker.py:~667] Potentially invalid KV blocks for unrecognized request chatcmpl- were retrieved by a decode worker. They may have expired. ``` i.e. reads completing after lease expiry, against blocks the producer already freed (same family as #61229). Message sources at v0.31.0: the expiry line is base_worker.py:3075; the late-retrieval error is pull_worker.py:664-665 (:668 on current main — the line drifts slightly between revisions). **What the stalls are not (checked live during an episode)** - The target prefill pod is Ready, 0 restarts, healthy prompt throughput and prefix-cache hit rate while the failing decode stalls against it. - TCP to that prefill's NIXL side-channel port connects instantly while the RDMA handshake dead-ends → the decay is strictly at the libfabric/agent layer, not pod, process, or network. The code predicts this exact split: the vLLM handshake's metadata phase runs over ZMQ/TCP with a 5 s timeout (base_worker.py:1006) and succeeds against the live prefill; the 60 s block happens afterwards, inside agent creation in the nixl backend. - Other decode pods pull from the same prefill without error at the same time → the stale state is local to the failing decode. - FD/socket counts identical between young and aged pods (no leak). **Version isolation** - v0.28.0 (nixl 1.3.2): same fleet, same config, one week, zero restarts. Reading both tags side by side: 1.3.2's `connect()` has no wait; the `Handshake from peer` string exists only in 1.4.x (PR map below). - Every current release pins a 1.4.x/1.5.x nixl (v0.30.0 → 1.4.1; current main → 1.5.0), so the amplifier ships in every release image. **Which changes produced this (PR-level breakdown)** No single PR is the regression: the loop exists only where two independently correct change sets intersect — nixl 1.3.2 → 1.4.x on the transport side, and the v0.29 → v0.31 connector lifecycle on the vLLM side. *Half 1 — the severity flip, in the nixl bump.* [#1736](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/1736) — "libfabric: add a handshake phase before establishing connection in order to pass an agent index to be used by sender" (merged 2026-07-21, shipped in the 1.4.x line). What it solved, and why it is a correct fix: on EFA a write receiver could not tell which sender a completed write came from — transfer IDs are unique only within one sender process, so two senders' transfers sharing an ID interfere — and the design's 8-bit agent index in the RDMA immediate data capped a receiver at 256 peers (later removed by [#2294](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2294)). The handshake passes each side's agent index to the other before any data flows. What it changed: in 1.3.2, `connect()` completes with no confirmation step, so after a local eviction, reconnecting to a live peer works instantly — the identical fleet ran crash-free for a week on v0.28.0, whose connector has the same TTL eviction and the same silent cleanup (base_worker.py:508 and 2552-2616 at that tag). From 1.4.x, `connect()` waits for the peer's reciprocal handshake, up to `NIXL_LIBFABRIC_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` (60 s). That wait dead-ends precisely when our side is fresh but the peer's side is stale — the state a one-sided eviction creates — because a peer that believes it is already connected never sends the handshake: `connect()` short-circuits for agents it already holds as CONNECTED (libfabric_backend.cpp:664), the handshake receive path only stores the sender's index and never replies (libfabric_handshake.cpp:150-201), and `sendHandshakeTo` is invoked only from a peer's own `establishConnection`. The design assumes "a reconnect means both sides are setting up fresh"; vLLM's remote-engine lifecycle violates that assumption. *Half 2 — the frequency multipliers, in the vLLM connector lifecycle (v0.29 → v0.31).* None of these crash anything alone; each is a correct fix for a real problem, and each increases how often a transfer path touches an agent whose local state is gone: - [#50047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50047) — "Release a dead peer's NIXL state without waiting for TTL": proactive release, more agent-state transitions during rollouts. - [#54689](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54689) — "Don't evict a remote engine a transfer is still reading from": engines with a hung read are pinned indefinitely, and the pinned agents keep being dialed. - [#56104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56104) — "Fix multiple handles xfer race": failure deferral retains requests on transfers that never finish, keeping dead references alive. The intersection is the regression: the silent TTL eviction is old code (present in v0.28.0) whose failure was self-healing under 1.3.2, and the reciprocal handshake is a correct fix whose reconnect assumption the eviction violates. Neither change is wrong in isolation, which is why neither project sees this as their regression, and why no single upstream issue tracks the assembled loop. One further data point: [#2294](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2294) — "identify senders by source address, remove 256-peer limit" (merged 2026-10-06, in no release tag yet) — already obsoletes the handshake's original purpose: the receiver now identifies a sender from the source address libfabric reports on each completion, and the agent index becomes a plain local number. Yet it deliberately keeps the handshake and the wait ("Do not remove the handshake or that wait"). The amplifier therefore survives on nixl main, and the wait's remaining purpose is connection-readiness ordering — which is what suggested direction 4 asks to make non-blocking or configurable. **Why the already-merged fixes do not stop this loop** #59873 (heartbeats count as remote-engine activity) and #55471 (recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata) both operate on the decode-side registry. #59873 narrows when eviction fires but cannot remove the idle window; #55471 recovers invalidated metadata, but the recovery re-handshake enters the same 60 s `connect()`. Neither touches the nixl transport layer, so neither bounds the block that kills the engine. **How to reproduce (deterministic; compressed variant in minutes)** We reproduce this on demand with an open-loop traffic pattern against a P/D deployment: a burst of requests (handshakes complete normally), then an idle window longer than `engine_ttl`, then another burst whose pulls and deferred notifications target the now-evicted engines. At the default `engine_ttl` (3600 s) every decode pod in our fleet dies within 2–3 h of its start; in a bounded ~130 min replay containing one embedded idle window, the decode engine dies ~85 min in, reproducibly. The model and its size are irrelevant — nothing in the failure path touches model code. Minimum setup: ≥2 RDMA-capable nodes, P/D with NixlConnector (pull mode), decode with DP>1 — the broadcast starvation that ends in process death needs multiple DP ranks; with DP=1 you still get the stalls and failed transfers, just not the crash (a TP-only decode fleet in #59971 shows that variant: no crash loop, but the wedged transfer pins and leaks KV blocks until the cache is ~97% full — degradation instead of death). Note the one death mode that is topology-independent: with speculative decoding, `take_draft_token_ids` is a collective RPC over the engine's workers guarded by `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 300 s), so ≥5 serial 60 s stale-agent touches inside one engine step kill a TP-only engine just the same — matching our first observed incident (five consecutive 60 s handshake stalls, then the watchdog fired at the 300 s mark). Compression: `engine_ttl` is a plain `kv_connector_extra_config` key, so the multi-hour cadence shrinks to minutes without patching anything: ```sh --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"engine_ttl":60}}' ``` 1. Send a few requests; confirm KV transfers succeed. 2. Idle > 60 s — the decode logs `Evicted stale remote engine `. 3. Send requests again. On the decode side, within the first request or two: ``` Handshake from peer '' not received after 60s; connection cannot be established. NIXL transfer failure: transfer_setup_failed ... nixlRemoteDisconnectError No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds (all DP ranks) ``` and on the prefill side, ~30 s earlier: ``` Releasing expired KV blocks for request chatcmpl- which were retrieved by 0 remote worker(s) before lease expired. NixlPullConnector={'Num successful transfers': 0, ..., 'Num KV expired reqs': , ...} ``` 4. Keep the burst/idle cycles going: each stale-agent episode costs a fixed 60 s (`NIXL_LIBFABRIC_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` is a compile-time constant), and the engine dies once enough episodes stack — in our fleet the watchdog (`TimeoutError: RPC call to take_draft_token_ids timed out`) or a sibling rank's gloo teardown ends it. Caveats: verified on the libfabric backend over RDMA; whether libfabric's TCP provider shows the same blocking `connect()` is untested (if it does, the repro needs no RDMA hardware at all). The engine-death step needs repeated episodes — a single cycle demonstrates the stall signature, not the crash. We can attach `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` / `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1` captures from a reproduction on request. **Related issues** — this report assembles a loop whose slices are individually tracked: - vLLM: #59871 (heartbeat eviction; fixed by #59873), #59956 (`remove_remote_agent` UCX-endpoint leak per evict+re-handshake — our variant is the LIBFABRIC equivalent), #59971 (wedged connection strands KV blocks), #59872 (aborted request with unfinished READ pins blocks), #59870 (one agent called from two threads, no sync mode), #60205 (peer stall makes transfers fail permanently), #61229 (lease expiry vs in-flight reads), #61696 (first-handshake stall via THP compaction) - nixl: #1736 (reciprocal handshake + 60 s wait), #2294 (drops the 256-peer cap, keeps the wait) - Not tracked anywhere we could find: `_cleanup_remote_engine` does not clear the pending-notification state — the map is request-keyed (base_worker.py:849), so the per-engine cleanup structurally cannot reach it — and the deferred `send_notif` path sends to stored agent names with no registry check (base_worker.py:3199), so notifications keep targeting evicted engines' agents (observed 25 min post-eviction above). **Suggested directions (happy to contribute)** 1. `_cleanup_remote_engine` should also drop the evicted engine's entries from the pending-notification map — closes the observed post-eviction stalls. 2. A circuit breaker: after the first `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` against an agent, fail subsequent attempts fast (with `kv_load_failure_policy: recompute` serving locally) instead of re-entering the 60 s `connect()` — bounds each stale-agent episode to ≤1 stall regardless of how the stale reference was produced. 3. A lifecycle/deregistration message, so the peer learns the agent is gone instead of waiting on a handshake that never comes. 4. On the nixl side: parameterizing `NIXL_LIBFABRIC_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` or making the wait async would remove the amplifier for stale peers.

items.title: [Bug]: Model Runner V2 hangs during speculative decoding warmup with pipeline parallelism
items.author: chenjr97
items.summary: Model Runner V2 skips speculative decoding warmup on non-last PP stages, causing the last stage to hang waiting for intermediate tensors that never arrive.
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Description** Code version: based on `main` commit [`[de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995). With pipeline parallelism and speculative decoding enabled, Model Runner V2 runs the additional greedy warmup pass only on the last PP stage. Upstream stages skip this pass, leaving the last stage waiting for intermediate tensors that will never arrive. This can be reproduced during GLM-4.7-Flash initialization, before serving any requests. **Reproduction** Use four GPUs for TP2 × PP2. Save the following as `repro.py`: ```python from vllm import LLM if __name__ == "__main__": LLM( model="zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash", dtype="bfloat16", tensor_parallel_size=2, pipeline_parallel_size=2, distributed_executor_backend="mp", max_num_seqs=1024, max_num_batched_tokens=8192, gpu_memory_utilization=0.65, speculative_config={ "method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1, }, kernel_config={"enable_jit_warmup": True}, cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds=120, ) ``` Run: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \ VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ .venv/bin/python repro.py ``` The CPU communication timeout is shortened to 120 seconds to obtain the failure sooner. **Actual behavior** The first PP stage finishes warmup and CUDA Graph capture. The last PP stage blocks during the additional greedy warmup pass and eventually fails: ```text warmup_kernels # additional greedy=True pass → _warmup_kernels → worker_execute_model(prefill_output) → irecv_tensor_dict → recv_object → torch.distributed.recv RuntimeError: ... Timed out waiting 120000ms for recv operation to complete ``` **Relevant code** In [`[vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py#L232)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py#L232), the additional pass is gated on the rank-local sampler: ```python rejection_sampler = model_runner.rejection_sampler # ... temporarily disable adaptive verification ... try: _warmup_kernels(model_runner, worker_execute_model, worker_sample_tokens) if rejection_sampler is not None: # Greedy batches skip logits processing, so rejection kernels # also see model-dtype logits instead of FP32. _warmup_kernels( model_runner, worker_execute_model, worker_sample_tokens, greedy=True ) ``` However, [`[vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L465)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L465) initializes samplers only on the last PP stage: ```python if self.is_last_pp_rank and not self.is_pooling_model: # ... initialize self.sampler ... custom = self.model_state.custom_sampler(self.sampler) if custom: self.vllm_config._check_supports_watermarking(custom_sampler=True) self.sampler, self.rejection_sampler = custom elif self.speculative_config is not None: self.rejection_sampler = RejectionSampler( self.sampler, self.speculative_config, self.device, watermark_key=speculative_target_watermark_key( self.vllm_config.watermark_config ), ) ``` Consequently, non-last stages have `rejection_sampler=None` and skip the second pass, while the last stage executes it and waits for their inputs. **Expected behavior** All PP stages should execute matching warmup forward sequences. The additional speculative warmup pass should use a condition shared across PP stages, rather than the existence of a rank-local rejection sampler. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
discussion: A fix is proposed in #62129.

items.title: [MyPy][5/N] Fix mypy errors in hard tests/ dirs and enforce follow-imports=silent
items.author: adarshxs
items.summary: Part 5 of enabling mypy on (#49569). Fixes the mypy errors in the PR 5 directories and moves them from to in, so they are now checked with and cannot regress:,, (absorbing the previously listed and the separate ),,,,,.
items.body:
## Overview

Part 5 of enabling mypy on `tests/` (#49569). Fixes the mypy errors in the PR 5 directories and moves them from `SEPARATE_GROUPS` to `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so they are now checked with `--follow-imports silent` and cannot regress: `tests/entrypoints/llm`, `tests/entrypoints/openai`, `tests/kernels` (absorbing the previously listed `tests/kernels/{attention,core,helion,mamba,quantization}` and the separate `tests/kernels/moe`), `tests/lora`, `tests/tool_parsers`, `tests/v1/attention`, `tests/v1/e2e`, `tests/v1/ec_connector`.

Builds on #49570 (PR 0/1) and #51043 (PR 2). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these directories for mypy (checked `gh pr list --search "49569 in:body"` and `"mypy tests"`; the open `[MyPy]` PRs are #55485 (PR 4), #55542 (kv-A) and #55901 (kv-B)).

Partial #26533.

## Claims

- 533 mypy errors across the eight directories → 0, with `--warn-unused-ignores` also clean. (The issue's ~650 estimate predates #59428, which disabled `arg-type` and `assignment` under `tests/`.)
- Type-only: no `vllm/` changes, no `cast()`, no bare `# type: ignore`; the 29 ignores added are scoped to an error code and carry a reason (inline when the line fits in 88 columns, on the preceding line otherwise); 12 ignores that no longer suppressed anything are removed.
- 49 mock method assignments replaced with `monkeypatch.setattr`.
- Pre-existing test defects surfaced by the stricter check are fixed where safe, and flagged in a comment where fixing would change what the test exercises (list in Details).

## Validation

Environment: the pre-commit hook env (mypy 1.20.2, no torch/transformers so they resolve to `Any`), Python 3.11 like the hook.

```bash
# 1. the directories are clean at the strictness being enforced
.venv/bin/mypy --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores \
    tests/entrypoints/llm tests/entrypoints/openai tests/kernels tests/lora \
    tests/tool_parsers tests/v1/attention tests/v1/e2e tests/v1/ec_connector
# Success: no issues found in 632 source files   (before: 533 errors in 111 files)

# 2. the hook as CI runs it, with the new grouping in effect
pre-commit run mypy --all-files --hook-stage manual
# passes; the only output is 3 darwin-only errors in vllm/ (posix_fadvise, MADV_HUGEPAGE)
# that exist on macOS before this change and do not appear on Linux CI

# 3. routing proof: each PR 5 directory now lands in the "" (silent) group
.venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/pre_commit'); import mypy; \
  print([k for k,v in mypy.group_files(['tests/lora/utils.py']).items() if v])"
# ['']   (same for a file in each of the other seven directories; tests/v1/core still prints ['tests/v1/core'])

# 4. all other hooks on the changed files
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only main)
# ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, ... all pass
```

Test runs (macOS CPU build of vLLM, so only CPU-runnable suites; everything else collected only):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest --collect-only` on all 116 changed test files | 8316 tests collected; 6 collection errors, all missing optional deps on macOS (triton-cpu, tilelang, datasets), none from this change |
| `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/{chat_completion/test_chat_error,completion/test_completion_error,completion/test_completion_text_offset,responses/test_function_call_parsing,responses/test_response_input_to_harmony,responses/test_responses_utils,responses/test_serving_responses,test_render_parity,test_tool_choice_content_none}.py` | 243 passed, 1 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_*.py` (14 changed files) | 528 passed, 1 skipped, 19 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit tests/v1/attention` (3 pre-existing non-collecting files ignored) | 984 passed, 1150 skipped, 214 failed + 16 errors; the identical set of 230 ids fails on unchanged `main` in the same environment (CUDA/ROCm-only tests, `/dev/shm`, NIXL), so none is from this change |

No model evaluation: the change does not touch `vllm/` and cannot affect output, accuracy or serving.

## Details

Most fixes follow the issue's recipe: `assert x is not None` before an `X | None` access, `assert isinstance(...)` to narrow a union or an abstract base to the concrete class the test builds, annotations on fixtures and helpers, and `monkeypatch.setattr` instead of assigning to a method. Scoped ignores remain only where a test stub intentionally does not satisfy the real interface (`misc` for `None` fallbacks of optional kernel classes and a `Final` attribute, `attr-defined` for `SimpleNamespace` stubs, `type-abstract` where a test instantiates an abstract class through a factory).

Pre-existing defects the stricter check surfaced (all in tests; none changes what a test exercises):

- `tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py`: `StructuredOutputsParams(backend=...)` has no such init field (`_backend` is `init=False`), so the call raised `TypeError`; the kwarg is removed and the helper no longer takes a backend.
- `tests/lora/utils.py`: `DummyLoRAManager.init_lora` passed `embeddings_tensor=` to `LoRALayerWeights(...)`, which no longer accepts it.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_{internlm2,longcat,phi4mini}_tool_parser.py`: `tokenizer.get_vocab = MagicMock()` permanently mutated the module-scoped tokenizer fixture and leaked into later tests; now `monkeypatch.setattr`, undone per test.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`: assignments to a non-existent `FusedMoEParallelConfig.use_dp` removed; the no-DP state already comes from `make_no_parallel()`.
- `tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/{mk_objects,common,cli_args}.py`: registries and `Config` fields were annotated as holding instances although they hold classes; now `type[...]` of the Modular subclasses that are actually registered.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py`: the mock prefill backends' `run_prefill_new_tokens` / `run_prefill_context_chunk` did not match the ABC (`chunk_idx` vs `chunk`, missing `out` / `output_scale`).
- `tests/v1/attention/utils.py`: `try_get_attention_backend` was annotated `type[AttentionImpl]` but `get_impl_cls()` returns `type[AttentionImplBase]`; and the `add_mock_model_methods` block is removed: its `get_num_layers` mock shadowed the real method with the wrong arity, the three `*_for_layer` hooks no longer exist on `ModelConfig`, nothing reads any of them, and no caller passed the flag.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py`: `query_len_support` is a `ClassVar` and was assigned through an instance; the assignment is removed (the inherited default is the value it set).
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`: `get_fake_sample_fn` was annotated `-> SamplerOutput` although it returns a callable.
- `tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_metadata.py`: asserted load entries as `(transfer_id, block_ids)` pairs; the metadata carries `(transfer_id, block_ids, shape)` and the worker unpacks three values, so the test is updated to the real contract.

Deliberately not changed, flagged with a comment and a scoped ignore:

- `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py`: the int8 non-block branch of `moe_quantize_weights_2d` calls `ops.scaled_int8_quant(w, w_s, use_per_token_if_dynamic=...)`, but the signature is now `(input, scale, azp, symmetric) -> (q, scale, azp)`, so it would raise if reached. No test reaches it (every int8 caller uses block quant and the modular-kernel CLI only accepts fp8); a replacement needs a GPU to validate, so it is left for a follow-up.

Typing gaps in `vllm/` that the per-test fixes keep running into, left for follow-ups:

- four identical `type-abstract` ignores: `select_common_block_size` / `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` take `type[AttentionBackend]`, but the indexer backends leave `get_impl_cls` abstract;
- repeated narrowings of `Metric.value` (only `Counter` / `Gauge` have it), `LLMEngine.engine_core` (to `InprocClient`), `EmbeddingCache.get/alloc` (`CacheEntry | None`) and `FusedMoEQuantConfig.*_scale` (`Tensor | None`).

`MockMLAAttentionLayer.forward_impl` in `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` keeps a scoped `override` ignore because the replica deliberately takes only the arguments the test passes; the prefill-registry mocks above were aligned to their ABC instead because they are registered as real backends.

The hook change is routing only: the absorbed `tests/kernels/*` entries become redundant under the `tests/kernels` parent entry and are removed, mirroring what #51043 did for `tests/plugins_tests`.

items.title: [Bug]: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL NVFP4 with --tool_parser qwen3_coder emits arguments "" (not "{}") for no-argument tools; echoing the call back in history then fails with HTTP 400 "arguments must be valid JSON"
items.author: satishalluri
items.summary: When serving with, the model sometimes calls a tool that has no required parameters and the response returns as an empty string instead of. An OpenAI-style agent appends that assistant message to history, and the next request is rejected by the same s…
items.body:
## Summary
When serving `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4` with `trtllm-serve` (`--tool_parser qwen3_coder --reasoning_parser nemotron-v3`), the model sometimes calls a tool that has no required parameters (`run_tests`) and the response returns `function.arguments` as an empty string `""` instead of `"{}"`. An OpenAI-style agent appends that assistant message to history, and the next request is rejected by the same server:

`HTTP 400 {"object":"error","message":"tool_calls[0].function.arguments must be valid JSON.","type":"BadRequestError"}`

The server produces output it then refuses to accept as input.

## Environment
- Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4
- TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29 (nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc29), PyTorch backend, CUDA 13.0
- Hardware: 2x DGX Spark (GB10), TP=2 across the two nodes (mpirun, 1 rank per node)
- Launch: `trtllm-serve <model> --tp_size 2 --backend pytorch --max_batch_size 16 --max_num_tokens 8192 --max_seq_len 131072 --trust_remote_code --tool_parser qwen3_coder --reasoning_parser nemotron-v3 --extra_llm_api_options nemotron-tp2.yaml`
- Extra options: kv_cache dtype fp8, enable_chunked_prefill true, moe backend CUTEDSL, guided_decoding_backend xgrammar
- Requests: /v1/chat/completions, stream=true, max_tokens 1500, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": true}`

## Tool schema (the no-arg tool)
```json
{"type":"function","function":{"name":"run_tests","description":"Run the test suite, optionally filtered",
 "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"pattern":{"type":"string"}},"required":[]}}}
```
Also offered in the same request: read_file(path), write_file(path, content), search_code(query).

## Prompt pattern
System: "You are a coding agent. Use the provided tools to inspect and modify the repository. When done, reply with a short summary."
User (one of): "The function parse_config in src/config.py crashes on empty files. Find and fix it, then make sure tests pass." / "Add input validation to src/api/handlers.py so negative quantities are rejected; update tests." / "tests/test_cache.py::test_expiry is flaky. Investigate and fix the root cause."
The agent loops up to 5 turns, appending each assistant tool_calls message plus a role=tool result. Bad calls occur mostly at turns 4-5, often as the second parallel call (tool_calls[1]).

## Repro
1. Serve as above; run several concurrent multi-turn coding-agent loops with the tools and prompt above.
2. Inspect each response's accumulated `tool_calls[i].function.arguments`: occasionally `name="run_tests", arguments=""`.
3. Append that assistant message to history and request the next turn: HTTP 400 "tool_calls[i].function.arguments must be valid JSON."
4. Minimal server-side check (no generation needed), history containing a run_tests call:
   - `arguments: ""` -> 400 "must be valid JSON"
   - `arguments: "{}"` -> 200
   - `arguments: "\"{}\""` or `"[]"` -> 400 "must be a JSON object"

## Expected vs actual
- Expected: no-argument tool calls are emitted as `arguments: "{}"`, or the server accepts/normalizes `""` in history.
- Actual: `arguments: ""` is emitted and then rejected by the server on the next turn.

## Observed rates (20-minute mixed load, 10 concurrent agents)
- Without a workaround: 5 of 559 requests (0.9%) failed with this 400.
- With a client-side strict `json.loads(arguments)` check plus retry (discard bad response, re-request the same turn at temperature 0.3): 11 bad calls caught out of 689 tool calls, all `run_tests` with `arguments=""`, all fixed on the first retry; 0 of 527 requests failed.

## Workaround
Client-side: replace `""` with `"{}"` before appending to history, or discard and retry.

## Suggested fixes
1. Tool parser (`qwen3_coder` path): emit `"{}"` when a call has no parameters.
2. Server request validation: accept `""` as `{}` for tool_calls arguments in history, consistent with what the server itself emits.
3. Optionally constrain tool-call argument generation (e.g. xgrammar JSON schema) so arguments are always a JSON object.

items.title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] modelopt-nvfp4: Read w13 global scales in the TRT-LLM [up, gate] order
items.author: mmangkad
items.summary: On the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend, ModelOpt NVFP4 experts whose gate (w1) and up (w3) global scales differ are dequantized with the two scales swapped. Under this layout the loader stores w13 rows, and their per-tensor scales, as, but (#27588) reads c…
items.body:
## Motivation

On the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend, ModelOpt NVFP4 experts whose gate (w1) and up (w3) global scales (`weight_scale_2`) differ are dequantized with the two scales swapped. Under this layout the loader stores w13 rows, and their per-tensor scales, as `[up, gate]`, but `_compute_gemm1_alphas` (#27588) reads column 0 as gate.

Standard ModelOpt exports tie gate/up scales (NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1033), so most checkpoints are unaffected. Before Model-Optimizer 0.45 (NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1560), experts never reached during calibration could stay untied, e.g. 6 of 3,840 in `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4`. It was reported on an in-house checkpoint with untied scales. Online NVFP4 (`nvfp4_online.py`) quantizes gate/up together with one shared scale, so it is unaffected.

## Modifications

- `_compute_gemm1_alphas` takes `up_first` and reads the columns in w13 row order; `process_weights_after_loading` passes `up_first=self.use_flashinfer_trtllm_weight_layout`. Other backends are unchanged.
- The TRT-LLM SwiGLU params move into `_compute_trtllm_gated_act_params`. Beta is added to the raw up half, so it now uses `g1_alphas_up`. The kernel applies one clamp limit to both raw halves, which can't be exact for both when their scales differ; it stays in gate-half units and logs a warning.
- Unit tests: the beta/clamp units and the SiTU branch of the moved helper.
- E2E (weekly, 4x B200): serve [`mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up`](https://huggingface.co/mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up) on `flashinfer_trtllm` and require GSM8K >= 0.90 (sgl-eval). Locally: 0.960 with this PR, 0.305 on the base commit.

## Accuracy Tests

`mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up` is `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` with `up_proj.weight_scale_2 *= 4` and `up_proj.weight_scale /= 4` in every expert: gate/up differ, dequantized weights are bit-identical.

sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K, 200 examples, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, TP1, 1x B300 (Qwen3 cookbook recipe, but with an NVFP4 checkpoint and a forced MoE backend):

| Checkpoint | Thinking, before | Thinking, after | Non-thinking, before | Non-thinking, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original (tied) | 98.0% | 97.5% | 95.0% | 95.0% |
| Untied | **51.0%** | **97.0%** | **29.0%** | **95.0%** |

Thinking: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 32768. Non-thinking: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, max_tokens 2048.

Kernel checks for the SwiGLU params: one expert with gate/up scale ratio 0.30, run through `prepare_static_weights_for_trtllm_fp4_moe` and `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` against a dequantized reference (alpha 1.702). Relative error; FP4 noise floor 0.09.

Beta: `1/up_alpha` gives 0.089, `1/gate_alpha` gives 0.508.

Clamp, real limit L, kernel given P. Each row is a hypothesis for the real thresholds the kernel applies:

| Real thresholds | P = L/gate_alpha | P = L/up_alpha |
|---|---|---|
| gate <= P * gate_alpha, abs(up) <= P * up_alpha (both raw) | **0.072** | **0.133** |
| both at P * up_alpha | 0.608 | 0.742 |
| gate only, up unclamped | 0.611 | 0.873 |
| both at P * gate_alpha | 1.989 | 2.155 |

The kernel clamps both raw halves at P, so with untied scales no single P gives both halves the real limit L.

items.title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the cached KV of folded encoder replay rows
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Fixes incorrect KV cache mutation for DeepSeek V4.1 folded encoder SWA replay rows during prefix hits, preventing the compressor from overwriting cached bytes on both fused (SM100+) and unfused paths.
items.body:
- Folded encoder SWA replay rows now get the padding slot (`raw_out_loc` 0) as their compressor write location (`_compressor_out_loc`); their main KV, compressed groups and index keys keep what the prefill that cached them wrote
- The fused c1/c2 compressors (SM100+) used to rewrite those rows on every prefix hit: `compress_skip` only reached the c2 ring write-back, while the c1 store, the c2 pooling store and the index-K store ran over every row
- The unfused compressor (e.g. Hopper) used to drop the replay rows from its input but not from its slots, so each new row landed on another row's slot (since #43166); it now takes every row, and the padding slot skips the replay rows
- Drop `compress_skip`, which the padding slot replaces
- Add `test_extend_metadata_puts_replay_rows_on_the_padding_slot` (on main no row gets the padding slot) and `test_unfused_compressor_writes_each_row_at_its_own_slot` (on main 90 of 282 rows reach the compressor)
- Checked on GB300 by snapshotting the replay rows' cached c1/c2 bytes before each prefix-hit prefill and comparing after it: main changed 3308-3712 of 3712 checked rows per hit on the fused path and all 3712 on the unfused path; this PR changes 0 on both

No behavior change outside `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`, where a prefix hit no longer rewrites the cached KV of its replayed tokens and every new token's KV goes to its own slot.

items.title: [CI][AMD] Mirror ReplaySSM, MiniMax-M3 attention kernels and Kimi K3 prefix cache on MI355
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Adds ROCm test mirrors for ReplaySSM E2E, MiniMax-M3 Attention Kernels, and Kimi K3 Prefix Cache on MI355, with platform-specific skips and test fixes.
items.body:
Adds AMD mirrors for the three test groups in `test_areas` that still had none: ReplaySSM E2E, MiniMax-M3 Attention Kernels and Kimi K3 Prefix Cache. The Kimi K3 Prefix Cache mirror needs two fixes that have not landed yet (see Details).

- `engine.yaml`: ReplaySSM E2E on `mi355_2`. The FlashInfer-only cases in `test_replayssm_decode.py` skip off CUDA.
- `kernels.yaml`: MiniMax-M3 Attention Kernels on `mi355_dpx`, plus a test that checks the AITER indexer against a reference implementation.
- `models_basic.yaml`: Kimi K3 Prefix Cache on `mi355_4` with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. The existing MI355 Kimi K3 jobs now skip `test_prefix_cache.py` so it does not run twice.
- `test_prefix_cache.py`: on ROCm it gates on native MX support instead of SM100. The FlashInfer DCP xfail applies on CUDA only. The Mooncake transport can be set with `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL` (default `rdma`), and the AMD mirror uses `tcp`.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), on current main with its ROCm pins (AITER `v0.1.25`, NIXL `1683cf3b`):

| Group | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ReplaySSM E2E | 10 | 10/10 pass (4 passed, 6 skipped each) |
| MiniMax-M3 Attention Kernels | 10 | 10/10 pass (161 passed, 14 skipped each) |
| Kimi K3 (existing job, with the new `--ignore`) | 1 | 336 passed, 67 skipped |
| Kimi K3 Prefix Cache, current main | 1 | 29 passed, 2 failed (`pd-tp2-dep2-block`/`-partial`, fixed by #61002) |
| Kimi K3 Prefix Cache, with #61002 and the AITER fix | 6 | 31/31 in 4 runs; the other 2 failed when another process on the shared node took the GPU memory |

## Details

The Kimi K3 Prefix Cache mirror depends on two fixes:

- #61002 (NixlConnector): pairs non-divisible hybrid MLA block sizes. Without it the two `pd-tp2-dep2` cases fail at the NIXL handshake.
- ROCm/aiter#6446: fixes an LL128 all-reduce deadlock that can hang the DCP cases under host contention. vLLM picks it up through an AITER release that includes it and a pin bump in `Dockerfile.rocm_base`. `v0.1.25` does not include it yet.

The new Mooncake test needs RDMA NICs (`mlx5_*`) by default, which MI355 runners may not have. The mirror runs it over TCP, which passes locally. The mirror inherits `optional` from the NVIDIA step, so like the 4xB200 job it runs nightly.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [Feat] mem_cache: prepare registered backends before worker graphs
items.author: feichai0017
items.summary: A registered radix-cache factory runs after the scheduler has initialized worker CUDA Graphs. It cannot prepare layer-transfer counters/events that must be present during initial graph capture.
items.body:
## Motivation

A registered radix-cache factory runs after the scheduler has initialized worker CUDA Graphs. It cannot prepare layer-transfer counters/events that must be present during initial graph capture. This adds an optional preparation callback at the existing worker boundary without moving cache construction.

Refs https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44855.

## Modifications

- Add keyword-only `prepare_worker` to `register_radix_cache_backend`. Keep the original factory identity and store factory/callback in one registry entry; invalid or duplicate registration cannot partially overwrite it.
- Dispatch only the published selected backend before any runner in `TpModelWorker.init_cuda_graphs`, passing the same worker and original `capture_decode_cuda_graph` value. Old registrations/default selection are no-ops; unknown backends and callback errors stop before runner initialization.
- Document repeat-call idempotence and the limited boundary. `ensure_decode_cuda_graphs`, independent runner recapture, pending admission and teardown are outside this change.

## Accuracy Tests

32 CPU tests pass in the existing registry suite. These execute the actual registry and unbound `TpModelWorker.init_cuda_graphs` method with recording collaborators, including two workers, multiple runners, repeated True/False calls, published-versus-raw configuration, invalid/duplicate registration, and fail-before-runner behavior. An independent rerun verifies the same boundary. Existing genuine dependencies are used; no replacement runtime modules or CUDA emulation are introduced.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python"
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=999999
export FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE=/tmp/sglang-worker-preparation-cache
python -B -m unittest discover -s test/registered/unit/mem_cache -p test_registry.py -v
```

Tested source base: `4fc86f73c2243e042c55a55d08afb07827d5096e`, using Python 3.11.10, PyTorch 2.13.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, FlashInfer 0.6.18 and NumPy 2.2.6. The checkout supplies the actual SGLang modules via `PYTHONPATH`; the pre-existing dependency environment's installed SGLang metadata is 0.5.20. This is a candidate-source unit gate, not installed-release qualification. GPU capture/replay, inference outputs and deployment qualification have not been run for this prototype; keeping this draft until that boundary is agreed and validated.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance claim or inference benchmark. This changes the optional startup extension point, not a kernel or copy backend.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed files pass the pinned isort 7.0.0 and Ruff 0.15.1 format/check commands.
- [x] Extend the existing registered CPU unit suite.
- [x] Document the API and scope in its module/function docstrings.
- [ ] GPU capture/replay and model accuracy validation (not claimed by CPU tests).

items.title: [Feature] Prepare registered radix cache backends before worker graph initialization
items.author: feichai0017
items.summary: A registered radix-cache backend can need worker-owned layer-transfer events/counters to be installed before CUDA Graph capture. Today the scheduler initializes model workers, pools, attention backends and graphs before building the tree cache.
items.body:
### Motivation

A registered radix-cache backend can need worker-owned layer-transfer events/counters to be installed before CUDA Graph capture. Today the scheduler initializes model workers, pools, attention backends and graphs before building the tree cache. Consequently, the backend factory cannot install dependencies that must appear in the initial captured graph. The existing public radix-cache registration API exposes construction, but no preparation callback at this earlier boundary.

At main `4fc86f73c2243e042c55a55d08afb07827d5096e`, see [worker initialization](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4fc86f73c2243e042c55a55d08afb07827d5096e/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L1100), [runner graph initialization](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4fc86f73c2243e042c55a55d08afb07827d5096e/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py#L426), and [backend registration](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4fc86f73c2243e042c55a55d08afb07827d5096e/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/registry.py#L58).

### Proposed interface

Allow `register_radix_cache_backend(name, factory, *, prepare_worker=None)`. Invoke the selected backend's optional callback as `prepare_worker(tp_worker, capture_decode_cuda_graph)` once at the beginning of each `TpModelWorker.init_cuda_graphs` call, before any runner. Existing two-argument registrations and default cache selection remain unchanged. Resolve the backend from the published runtime configuration; registration itself must neither read that configuration nor invoke preparation. Reject invalid registrations before insertion, and propagate preparation errors before any runner initializes graphs.

This deliberately covers this worker method boundary, including `capture_decode_cuda_graph=False`. It does not add a general lifecycle manager, teardown/drain protocol, pending-query admission API, or coverage for direct runner recapture / `ensure_decode_cuda_graphs`. The backend owns idempotence and any resources it retains.

### Related resources and validation

The dynamic linker factory in #40595 addresses later construction, and whole-process checkpoint/restore in #44523 is a different boundary. I did not find an equivalent worker-preparation proposal in the searched issues/PRs.

A minimal implementation has real CPU registry and worker-method ordering tests. GPU capture/replay and model inference are not validated by those unit tests; the implementation will be proposed as a draft for interface discussion.

items.title: [Doc] Fix NGINX load balancer config: fail_timeout, streaming and keep-alive
items.author: manuhalapeth
items.summary: The NGINX config in has three problems that show up when you serve real traffic through it. This PR fixes the config and adds a short note on each setting. [Discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--62140.org.readthedocs.build/en/62140/]
items.body:
## Overview

The NGINX config in `docs/deployment/nginx.md` has three problems that show up when you serve real traffic through it. This PR fixes the config and adds a short note on each setting.

## Claims

- **`fail_timeout=10000s` turns a short outage into a ~2.8 hour one.** NGINX uses `fail_timeout` both as the failure window and as how long it keeps a failed server out. After 3 errors, a healthy vLLM server gets no traffic for 10,000 s. If every server fails at once, NGINX answers `502 no live upstreams` to every request for that long, even after the servers are healthy.
- **Streaming is buffered.** NGINX buffers proxied responses by default, and vLLM doesn't send `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Streamed tokens reach the client in batches of about 4 KB (about 15 tokens) instead of one at a time, so the first token is late and the stream is choppy.
- **Missing keep-alive guidance.** vLLM closes idle connections after 5 s (`VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`). If upstream keepalive is turned on without a shorter `keepalive_timeout`, NGINX sometimes reuses a connection vLLM is closing, and the request fails with `502` (`Connection reset by peer`). Each such failure also counts towards `max_fails`, which feeds the first problem.

## Validation

A local reproduction with Docker and no GPU: two stand-ins for vLLM's OpenAI server (FastAPI and uvicorn with vLLM's 5 s idle keep-alive, streaming chunks shaped like vLLM's at one token every 20 ms), behind `nginx:1.27` (1.27.5). "Current" is the config in the docs today. "Proposed" is this PR's config, copied from the doc. It passes `nginx -t` and markdownlint.

| Test | Current | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Streaming, time to first token, 64-token answer (median of 20) | 364 ms | 27 ms |
| Streaming, time to first token, 512-token answer (median of 10) | 373 ms | 29 ms |
| One server down for 10 s, then back: traffic to it for the rest of the test (55 s) | none | its half, from the moment it was back |
| Both servers down for 5 s, then back: requests failing afterwards | all, to the end of the test (25 s) | none once `fail_timeout` expired, ~5 s later |
| Keep-alive race: bursts of 32 every ~5 s against a busy server, 270 s | 3 of 1,664 `502` (current config + `keepalive 32`) | 0 of 1,664 |

<details>
<summary>Charts</summary>

![Time to first streamed token](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/manuhalapeth/LLM-Inference-Ops/main/upstream/vllm_nginx_docs/charts/ttfb.png)

![One server down for 10 seconds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/manuhalapeth/LLM-Inference-Ops/main/upstream/vllm_nginx_docs/charts/one_down.png)

![Both servers down for 5 seconds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/manuhalapeth/LLM-Inference-Ops/main/upstream/vllm_nginx_docs/charts/both_down.png)

</details>

Notes:

- The keep-alive race is timing-dependent and rare locally. With an idle server, NGINX notices the close in time, so the stand-in's event loop is blocked in 50 ms slices to model an API server that's busy streaming many responses. It gave the same result, 3 of 1,664 vs. 0, in two separate runs. On real hardware (2x RTX 5090, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, vLLM 0.30.0, NGINX 1.27.5 with keepalive and `max_fails=1`), this mismatch produced 1,574 `502 no live upstreams` errors at 768 concurrent users while both vLLM servers were healthy, because a few resets marked both servers failed. With `keepalive_timeout 4s` and `max_fails=3 fail_timeout=10s`, the same sweep had 0 errors up to 1,024 users.
- The streaming delay depends on chunk size and decode speed. Faster decoding shrinks it, but tokens still arrive in batches.
- `fail_timeout=10s` is NGINX's default. `max_fails=3` is kept from the current doc.

Reproduction scripts, raw results and the chart code: <https://github.com/manuhalapeth/LLM-Inference-Ops/tree/main/upstream/vllm_nginx_docs>

```bash
./run_all.sh                    # every test above, raw output to results/
# or one at a time:
./lab.sh up docs                # or: proposed, docs_keepalive
./lab.sh client ttfb 20 64
./lab.sh client spread 75 10    # take a server down with: docker exec vllm1 sh -c 'touch /tmp/down; pkill -f server.py'
BUSY_MS=50 ./lab.sh up docs_keepalive && ./lab.sh client bursts 270 32
./lab.sh down
```

## Details

- **Root cause:** each problem comes from an NGINX default or setting that doesn't fit long-lived, streaming LLM requests. `fail_timeout` controls both the failure window and how long a server stays out. `proxy_buffering` is on by default. And the idle timeout on NGINX's side of a keepalive connection has to be shorter than vLLM's, or the two race.
- **Tradeoffs:** a shorter `fail_timeout` means NGINX tries a truly dead server again sooner (one failed attempt per 10 s, and connection errors are retried on the next server). `keepalive` is optional. It's included with the right timeout because people commonly add it for performance and then hit the race.
- **Not a duplicate:** I found no open issue or PR about this config. #39738 adds HAProxy and renames this file to `loadbalancer.md`, but doesn't change the NGINX config. If it lands first, I'll rebase onto the new file.
- AI assistance was used for coding the reproduction and for drafting. I reviewed every changed line, ran every test above, and found the original problem while running my own vLLM deployment.

items.title: [Perf] gemma4: Capture single-step frozen-KV drafts
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Enables graph capture for one-step frozen-KV drafts in gemma4, reducing draft TPOT by ~22% on Intel Arc GPU.
items.body:
Stack (4/6), merge in order: [#44851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44851) → [#44852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44852) → [#44853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44853) → [#44854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44854) → [#44863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44863) → [#44869](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44869)

## Motivation

A one-step frozen-KV draft still executes an assistant seed forward. The current `<= 1` capture guard skips that forward and leaves it eager.

## Modifications

Allow capture for one draft step while keeping the zero-step/disabled cases excluded. Add a one-step XPU fixture that verifies repeated generation, acceptance statistics, and nonzero draft graph capture.

Depends on #44853. Target weights and verification are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The new capture regression fails on the old code with `0.0 not greater than 0`; both one-step serving tests pass after the fix. Six greedy prompts match the validated control, including prompts crossing the sliding-window boundary.

GSM8K via `sgl-eval==0.1.3`: 82.5%/200, zero errors, one truncation. This is an accuracy smoke check.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same physical Intel Arc Pro B70, TP1 BF16, original target weights; one draft step/two verification tokens, context 8,192, KV capacity 32,768, max running requests 8. Fixed 256-token OpenAI chat workload, two repeats in control–candidate–candidate–control order, with 8/32 requests at concurrency 1/8.

| Concurrency | Eager draft TPOT | Captured draft TPOT | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 8.812 ms | 6.795 ms | 22.9% |
| 8 | 11.077 ms | 8.695 ms | 21.5% |

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks.
- [x] Serving regression fails before and passes after.
- [x] Greedy parity and 200-example accuracy smoke.
- [x] Same-device serving benchmarks.
- [x] No new configuration required.

discussion:
Agent:

The research supports keeping the change. The strongest evidence is upstream history: this appears to fix a stale guard left behind by an earlier refactor.

Merged [PR #25539 (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25539)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25539) moved the assistant seed forward from eager execution into draft_forward(), specifically to avoid its extra launch and synchronization overhead. It also removed a num_steps > 1 condition around attention initialization, explaining that initialization must now run even with one step.

I inspected that PR’s merged code: it retained the separate num_steps <= 1 graph-capture guard, despite moving a real model forward into the one-step draft path. That mismatch is concrete evidence for changing the threshold. The conclusion that it was overlooked is my inference; I found no documented reason for deliberately keeping one-step frozen-KV drafting eager.

Ordinary EAGLE remains different. Its separate implementation still skips capture for one step and explicitly comments that draft_forward only performs sampling in that case. This PR changes the frozen-KV worker’s guard, leaving EAGLE’s condition intact. [EAGLE source at the PR revision (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/767fa00745f1d16f205a50cf5c47b3ff9186bf7e/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py#L656)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/767fa00745f1d16f205a50cf5c47b3ff9186bf7e/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py#L656)

The performance rationale also matches PyTorch’s guidance: graphs reduce CPU dispatch overhead for repeated, graph-safe GPU work, especially when individual operations are short. One model forward can contain many kernel launches; it need not contain multiple recurrent steps to benefit. [PyTorch documentation (https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda#cuda-graphs)](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda#cuda-graphs)

My recommendation is to retain the implementation and add a one-step eager-versus-replay regression before merging. That would address the validation gap. Restricting the fix to XPU solely because the benchmark used XPU would be unnecessarily narrow—the architectural rationale applies to CUDA too, although CUDA still needs validation.

My earlier answers were too categorical before checking this history. The historical evidence makes the implementation substantially better justified; it does not establish correctness across every backend configuration.

items.title: [Perf] gemma4: Skip ranking for full MTP chains
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Skips probability ranking when constructing full MTP chains for Gemma-4, directly selecting draft logits to avoid softmax/cumulative-score overhead while preserving the generic branching path.
items.body:
Stack (3/6), merge in order: [#44851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44851) → [#44852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44852) → [#44853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44853) → [#44854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44854) → [#44863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44863) → [#44869](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44869)

## Motivation

With top-k 1 and every draft step retained, frozen-KV MTP has a single chain. Probability ranking cannot change which nodes reach target verification, but the current path still computes full-vocabulary softmax, cumulative scores, frontier gathers, and tree ranking.

## Modifications

Select draft logits directly and construct the chain metadata without ranking. Keep the generic path for branching or pruned trees. Return contiguous metadata for the CUDA tree builder's layout contract.

Depends on #44852. Target weights and verification are unchanged; finite-precision softmax ties can resolve differently in assistant proposals.

## Accuracy Tests

Two CPU-tensor unit tests cover six configurations, including the one-step empty-parent boundary and generic-path fallbacks. A deliberate parent-index mutation makes the topology test fail. XPU serving tests and six greedy parity prompts pass.

GSM8K smoke: 82%/200, zero errors, two truncations. No quality-equivalence claim.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same physical Intel Arc Pro B70, TP1 BF16, context 8,192, KV capacity 32,768, max running requests 8; captured MTP with three steps/four verification tokens. Fixed 256-token OpenAI chat requests, two repeats per variant/concurrency. Controls bracket the initial candidate runs; the final contiguous-layout candidate was also measured separately.

| Concurrency | Generic TPOT | Chain TPOT | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.295 ms | 4.171 ms | 2.9% |
| 8 | 5.974 ms | 5.779 ms | 3.3% |

Output throughput increases from 220.6 to 228.8 tok/s and from 1,174.4 to 1,220.0 tok/s, respectively. These are workload-specific measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks.
- [x] Derived topology/layout tests and XPU serving regressions.
- [x] Greedy parity, accuracy smoke, and same-device serving benchmarks.
- [x] No new configuration or documentation required.

items.title: [Perf] [Intel] gemma4: Enable frozen-KV MTP graph capture
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Enables frozen-KV draft graph capture on Intel XPU for MTP, fixing serving failures and improper KV pool usage in the synchronous scheduler.
items.body:
Stack (2/6), merge in order: [#44851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44851) → [#44852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44852) → [#44853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44853) → [#44854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44854) → [#44863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44863) → [#44869](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44869)

## Motivation

Frozen-KV MTP on XPU fails under the synchronous scheduler and uses the draft's dummy KV pool when determining sliding-window translation. It also leaves recurrent assistant forwards eager despite the shared graph runner supporting XPU.

## Modifications

- Accept and forward `pp_proxy_tensors` through target prefill and verification.
- Bind frozen draft attention to the target allocator's KV pool and skip write-slot metadata for this read-only draft.
- Enable frozen-KV draft graph capture on XPU, with a serving regression and an E2B/BMG MTP recipe.

Depends on #44851. No CPU-offload changes or weight quantization.

## Accuracy Tests

Five attention backend unit tests pass, including a pool-ownership regression that fails before the fix. The XPU MTP serving fixture checks repeated decode, per-request verification statistics, and nonzero draft capture. Six greedy prompts match ordinary decoding, including 1,016- and 1,814-token prompts crossing the sliding-window boundary.

GSM8K via `sgl-eval==0.1.3`: 82.5%/200, zero errors, two truncated responses. This is a smoke check, not proof of accuracy improvement or equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same physical Intel Arc Pro B70, TP1 BF16, unchanged target weights, context 8,192, KV capacity 32,768, max running requests 8; MTP top-k 1, three draft steps/four verification tokens. OpenAI chat benchmark, fixed 256 output tokens, two repeats; 8 requests at concurrency 1 and 32 at concurrency 8.

| Concurrency | Ordinary TPOT | Corrected eager MTP | Captured MTP |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 11.168 ms | 7.742 ms | 4.282 ms |
| 8 | 11.774 ms | 9.372 ms | 5.914 ms |

Capture alone improves TPOT by 1.81x/1.58x over corrected eager MTP. The total 2.61x/1.99x over ordinary decoding also includes speculative decoding's benefit.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks and attention unit tests.
- [x] XPU serving regressions and greedy parity.
- [x] Accuracy and serving benchmarks.
- [x] Cookbook and generated-command checks.

items.title: [Feat] gemma4: Support encoder-free text serving
items.author: alexnails
items.summary: Adds --language-model-only mode to skip unused vision/audio encoders in Gemma4 serving, reducing weight memory and increasing KV cache capacity by 8.1%.
items.body:
Stack (1/6), merge in order: [#44851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44851) → [#44852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44852) → [#44853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44853) → [#44854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44854) → [#44863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44863) → [#44869](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44869)

## Motivation

Gemma4 text serving currently loads vision/audio encoders that it never uses. Enable `--language-model-only` while preserving the processor's tokenizer configuration, including BOS handling.

## Modifications

- Omit media towers and skip their checkpoint weights for text-only launches.
- Reuse Gemma4's processor tokenizer so identical text retains identical token IDs; preserve the existing tokenizer loader for other architectures.
- Add text-only XPU coverage for generation, token-ID parity, and media rejection, plus an E2B/BMG cookbook recipe.

This is encoder omission, not CPU offload. The existing CPU-offload work in #44139 is excluded from this branch.

## Accuracy Tests

On an Intel Arc Pro B70 with the original `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` weights: full-model and text-only generation tests, processor-tokenizer parity, and media rejection pass. Prior 200-example GSM8K smoke runs scored 78.5% for both modes; this is not a statistical quality-equivalence claim.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

At TP1 and `--mem-fraction-static 0.70`, reported weight allocation decreases from 9.94 to 9.04 GB. Full-attention KV capacity increases from 353,920 to 382,528 tokens (8.1%). No weight quantization is involved.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks.
- [x] XPU serving and tokenization tests.
- [x] Cookbook update, Mintlify validation and broken-link checks.
- [x] Accuracy and memory measurements.

Base of the Gemma4 serving optimization stack.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Auto derive max_num_batched_tokens from max_model_len and max_num_seqs
items.author: mzgong1121
items.summary: Fixes memory profiling overestimation in vLLM when max_model_len is small by auto-deriving max_num_batched_tokens, preventing KV cache misestimation and engine startup failure.
items.body:
## Summary Fix memory profiling overestimation issue. When `max_model_len` is set small by user, SchedulerConfig uses the default 'max_num_batched_tokens'. This creates oversized dummy batch during memory profiling, leading to much higher peak activation memory estimation than real runtime. In encoder-decoder ASR scenarios (Qwen3-ASR in our test), the profiling calculation reports insufficient KV cache memory, and the engine fails to start, even though the real runtime memory requirement is much lower. This PR: 1. In `SchedulerConfig.__post_init__`, when `max_num_batched_tokens` is not specified, auto set `max_num_batched_tokens = max_model_len`. 2. Add validation to prevent manually set `max_num_batched_tokens` from exceeding manually set upper bound 'max_model_len`. 3. Normal operation is supported under limited VRAM and a smaller max_model_len. 4. Works for multi-model scenarios. ## Reproduction & Verification ### Test code ``` ```python def main() -> None: asr = Qwen3ASRModel.LLM( model=ASR_MODEL_PATH, gpu_memory_utilization=0.05, dtype=torch.bfloat16, max_inference_batch_size=2, max_model_len = 256, max_new_tokens=256, skip_mm_profiling=True, enforce_eager=True, enable_chunked_prefill=True, #encoder_cache_budget=0, enable_prefix_caching=False, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": {"count":1, "length":2048}} ) ``` - **Before fix**: Memory profiling overestimates activation memory, reports insufficient available KC cache memory and fails to start engine. - **After fix**: Memory profiling calculation matches the real runtime requirement, engine runs normally. ## Test Plan - Manual test: Encoder-decoder ASR model. When `max_num_batched_tokens` use the default value, it is automatically bounded by `max_model_len`. Memory profiling dummy batch uses this corrected value, and peak activation memory estimation becomes accurate. ---

items.title: [Bugfix] Exclude cudagraph padding rows from the per-tensor FP8 MoE amax
items.author: yifanFengg
items.summary: Fixes incorrect per-tensor FP8 activation scales caused by CUDA-graph padding rows contaminating the MoE amax computation.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #62124.

With a dynamic per-tensor FP8 activation scale, the Triton fused-MoE path computes the amax over every row of the batch the model runner hands it. Under CUDA graphs that batch is padded to the capture size, and the padding rows hold whatever the previous step left there: stale hidden states, or, once the router skips padding (`VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1`, the default), workspace rows that the first GEMM never wrote. So the scale used for a request's own rows, and with it the request's output, depends on the request that ran before it. The reporter's script shows the first generated token changing with the previous request; `--enforce-eager` is clean because nothing is padded.

Two quantizations see the padding rows: the expert input (`a1`, in `MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEP.prepare`) and the post-activation intermediate (`intermediate_cache2`, in `TritonExperts.apply`). This PR zeroes the padding rows of both right before the quantization, using the `is_padding` mask the model runner already keeps for the router. The second one reuses the existing `a2_scale_is_global` condition, which already documents this hazard for the rows of remote experts under EP. The V2 model runner only filled that mask under `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING`; it now fills it always, so the fix does not depend on that flag. Nothing changes for static or per-token/block activation scales (the masked_fill is skipped), and nothing changes without CUDA-graph padding (the mask is all False).

Not covered here: the legacy functional `fused_experts()` entry point and the distributed prepare/finalize implementations, which quantize `a1` themselves; the local path used by the issue's deployment (TP=1, no DP/EP) is the one fixed.

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` does not change this amax, so the contamination is also present in batch-invariant mode; the run below shows it, and the fix removes it there too. (A dynamic per-tensor scale still depends on the other valid rows of the batch, which is a separate concern from this fix.)

## Test Plan

Everything on one NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), `main` at `ce49c47cbb` vs `main` + this PR, `ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct` with the issue's exact command (`--quantization fp8_per_tensor --moe-backend triton`, capture sizes `[1,2,4,8]`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) and the issue's `repro.py` (claim mode and `--search`; exit code 1 = present, 0 = absent):

- `main`: default, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`, `--enforce-eager` (control), and a repeat of the default.
- this PR: default, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` (the V1 runner), and a repeat of the default.
- Cost: `vllm bench throughput` (random 1024/128 and 64/256, 2000 prompts, seed 0), `main` vs this PR alternating, three rounds each, same model and flags.

## Test Result

`COMMIT:` lines: "clean checkout" is `main` at `ce49c47cbb`; "4 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)" is `main` + this PR.

**1. `main`: the output depends on the previous request (present in every CUDA-graph configuration, absent with `--enforce-eager`)**

items.title: [Bugfix] Keep the Triton attention tiling fixed under batch invariance
items.author: yifanFengg
items.summary: Fixes Triton attention tiling changing based on batch composition in batch-invariant mode, causing deterministic output failures for head_size=256 on SM100 GPUs.
items.body:
## Purpose

`unified_attention` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`) switches to a tuned large-head launch (`BLOCK_M=32`, a 128-wide KV tile, 8 warps, 2 stages) when `head_size == 256`, the batch contains a query longer than one token, `num_queries_per_kv <= 16` and the GPU is SM100-family. The condition is evaluated for the whole batch, so a decode request's attention is tiled, and its online softmax accumulated, differently when another request in the same step happens to be prefilling. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` that makes the output of a request depend on its batch mates: the batch-invariance suite's ragged chunked-prefill test fails on every head-size-256 model on Blackwell (Gemma 3 here).

This PR keeps the default tiling in batch-invariant mode (one extra condition). Nothing changes when the flag is off.

## Test Plan

One NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), `main` at `ce49c47cbb` vs `main` + this PR, `unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it` (head size 256, 4 query heads per KV head), TP=1, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`:

- the seven `TRITON_ATTN` ids of `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py`, one pytest process each, `main` (GPU 1) and this PR (GPU 2);
- `test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill[TRITON_ATTN]` three more times on each side.
