EngineCore encountered a fatal error. Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 361, in execute_model self._apply_mm_cache(scheduler_output) File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 354, in _apply_mm_cache req_data.mm_features = mm_cache.get_and_update_features( File "vllm/multimodal/cache/shm.py", line 228, in get_and_update_features File "vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py", line 458, in get_and_update_features File "vllm/multimodal/cache/shm.py", line 241, in get_and_update_item return self._shm_cache.get(address, monotonic_id) File "vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_object_storage.py", line 613, in get raise ValueError( ValueError: Data for address:id '4817824:4' has been modified or is invalid. vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause. ``` Every in-flight and later request then fails, and `/health` stops answering 200. `/pause?mode=keep` is documented to ignore `clear_cache` ("Ignored when mode=keep"), so tecnically a keep pause is not expected to touch any cache at all. ```bash VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --mm-processor-cache-type shm --mm-processor-cache-gb 2 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 8192 python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms keep ``` Each round of the client below does an idle pause+resume, then sends 12 streamed requests with distinct 448 px images (4 run, 8 wait behind `--max-num-seqs 4`). 300 ms later it pauses and resumes, then sends 8 requests with distinct 1344 px images. Results on RTX A5000, one fresh server per row: | server | pause call | result | |---|---|---| | shm | `/pause?mode=keep` | engine dead in round 1 (3/3 servers) | | shm | `/pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true` (1344 px images sent during the drain) | engine dead in round 1 (1/1) | | shm | `/pause?mode=keep&clear_cache=false` | alive after 67 rounds; the same server then died in round 1 of the `mode=keep` arm | | lru | `/pause?mode=keep` | alive after 51 rounds |
repro.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone client (stdlib only): /pause clears the shared-memory multimodal cache under requests that still hold handles into it, and the engine dies when one of them is scheduled. vLLM 0.31.0 with `--mm-processor-cache-type shm`. A request's image travels to the engine as an (address, monotonic_id) handle into the SHM ring buffer; the worker resolves it only when the request is first scheduled (v1/worker/worker_base.py:348-356 -> multimodal/cache/shm.py:241 -> shm_object_storage.py:608-614). `POST /pause` defaults to clear_cache=true (entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/api_router.py:34; its docstring says the flag is ignored for mode=keep) and AsyncLLM.pause_generation clears the frontend cache for every mode (v1/engine/async_llm.py:950-951). For the SHM cache that resets the ring buffer -- addresses and ids back to 0 (shm_object_storage.py:163-170) -- while requests queued behind --max-num-seqs still carry handles into it. New images written after the clear reuse those slots; when a kept request is scheduled its handle fails the id check, `ValueError: Data for address:id ':' has been modified or is invalid.` is raised in execute_model, and EngineCore exits (EngineDeadError; every later request fails, /health is no longer 200). Server: VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --mm-processor-cache-type shm --mm-processor-cache-gb 2 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 8192 Run: python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms keep Round: an idle /pause?mode=keep + /resume (nothing in flight, so it only resets the SHM ring); then 12 streamed chat requests, each with its own 448 px noise image (4 run, 8 wait behind --max-num-seqs 4); `--pause-after-ms` later the pause call; then /resume and at once 8 more requests with distinct 1344 px images. Arms (the pause call): keep /pause?mode=keep (clear_cache left at its default, true) keep_noclear /pause?mode=keep&clear_cache=false (control) wait /pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true; the 8 large images are sent while the pause drains none no pause (control) Exit 1 when the engine dies (/health not 200, or a response carrying EngineDeadError / "EngineCore encountered"). """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import base64 import http.client import json import random import struct import sys import threading import time import urllib.parse import zlib from collections import Counter DEAD_MARKERS = ("EngineDeadError", "EngineCore encountered", "engine is dead", "Engine is dead") def png(seed: int, size: int) -> str: rnd = random.Random(seed) raw = bytearray() for _ in range(size): raw.append(0) raw += rnd.randbytes(size * 3) def chunk(tag: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes: return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF) body = (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", size, size, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(bytes(raw), 1)) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")) return "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(body).decode() class Client: def __init__(self, base: str, timeout: float): u = urllib.parse.urlparse(base) self.host, self.port, self.timeout = u.hostname, u.port or 80, timeout def _req(self, method: str, path: str, body=None, timeout=None) -> tuple[int, str]: c = http.client.HTTPConnection(self.host, self.port, timeout=timeout or self.timeout) try: c.request(method, path, body=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) r = c.getresponse() return r.status, r.read().decode(errors="replace") except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 return -1, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" finally: c.close() def health(self) -> int: return self._req("GET", "/health", timeout=10)[0] def chat(self, model: str, image: str, nonce: str, stream: bool, max_tokens: int) -> dict: body = {"model": model, "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image}}, {"type": "text", "text": f"{nonce} Describe this image in detail."}]}]} st, text = self._req("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", body) err = None if st == 200 and stream: for line in text.splitlines(): if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]": try: d = json.loads(line[6:]) except ValueError: continue if "error" in d: err = json.dumps(d["error"])[:400] elif st != 200: err = text[:400] return {"status": st, "error": err} def run_round(cl: Client, model: str, arm: str, k: int, a) -> Counter: small = [png(a.seed + k * 100 + i, a.small_px) for i in range(a.streams)] large = [png(a.seed + k * 100 + 50 + i, a.large_px) for i in range(a.large)] out: Counter = Counter() lock = threading.Lock() def send(img, nonce, stream, mt, tag): res = cl.chat(model, img, nonce, stream, mt) with lock: if res["status"] == 200 and not res["error"]: out[f"{tag}:ok"] += 1 else: out[f"{tag}:fail"] += 1 if res["error"] and any(m in res["error"] for m in DEAD_MARKERS): out["engine_dead_response"] += 1 if out["samples"] < 3: out["samples"] += 1 print(f" [{arm} r{k}] {tag} status={res['status']} {res['error']}", flush=True) if a.prelude_clear: # Idle clear first (nothing in flight): the round's 448 px images then sit at the start of the SHM ring, # where the large images written after the mid-round clear land. Without it they would sit right after # the previous round's large images, which the new large images exactly refill, so no stale handle is # ever overwritten. cl._req("POST", "/pause?mode=keep") cl._req("POST", "/resume") first = [threading.Thread(target=send, args=(small[i], f"r{k}s{i}", True, a.max_tokens, "small"), daemon=True) for i in range(a.streams)] for t in first: t.start() time.sleep(a.pause_after_ms / 1000) second = [threading.Thread(target=send, args=(large[i], f"r{k}L{i}", False, a.large_max_tokens, "large"), daemon=True) for i in range(a.large)] if arm in ("keep", "keep_noclear"): q = "/pause?mode=keep" + ("&clear_cache=false" if arm == "keep_noclear" else "") st, _ = cl._req("POST", q) out[f"pause_{st}"] += 1 time.sleep(a.pause_ms / 1000) st, _ = cl._req("POST", "/resume") out[f"resume_{st}"] += 1 for t in second: t.start() elif arm == "wait": res = {} pt = threading.Thread(target=lambda: res.update(st=cl._req("POST", "/pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true")[0]), daemon=True) pt.start() time.sleep(0.05) for t in second: # rendered (and written to SHM) while the pause drains t.start() pt.join(a.timeout) out[f"pause_{res.get('st')}"] += 1 st, _ = cl._req("POST", "/resume") out[f"resume_{st}"] += 1 else: time.sleep(a.pause_ms / 1000) for t in second: t.start() for t in first + second: t.join(a.timeout + 5) h = cl.health() out[f"health_{h}"] += 1 if h != 200: out["engine_dead_health"] += 1 return out def main() -> int: p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("base", nargs="?", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") p.add_argument("--base-url", default=None) p.add_argument("--out", default=None) p.add_argument("--arms", default="keep", help="comma list of keep, keep_noclear, wait, none") p.add_argument("--arm-minutes", default="", help="e.g. keep_noclear=4,keep=10 (default --minutes)") p.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=10.0) p.add_argument("--max-rounds", type=int, default=100000) p.add_argument("--streams", type=int, default=12) p.add_argument("--small-px", type=int, default=448) p.add_argument("--large", type=int, default=8) p.add_argument("--large-px", type=int, default=1344) p.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=96) p.add_argument("--large-max-tokens", type=int, default=8) p.add_argument("--pause-after-ms", type=int, default=300) p.add_argument("--pause-ms", type=int, default=100) p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=180) p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261016) p.add_argument("--no-prelude-clear", dest="prelude_clear", action="store_false", help="skip the idle pause+resume (cache clear) at the start of each round") a = p.parse_args() cl = Client(a.base_url or a.base, a.timeout) st, text = cl._req("GET", "/v1/models") model = json.loads(text)["data"][0]["id"] print(f"model={model} args={vars(a)}", flush=True) mins = {kv.split("=")[0]: float(kv.split("=")[1]) for kv in a.arm_minutes.split(",") if kv} summary = {"model": model, "args": vars(a), "arms": {}} dead_arm = None for ai, arm in enumerate(a.arms.split(",")): t_end = time.monotonic() + mins.get(arm, a.minutes) * 60 tot: Counter = Counter() rounds = 0 dead_round = None while time.monotonic() < t_end and rounds < a.max_rounds: c = run_round(cl, model, arm, ai * 10000 + rounds, a) rounds += 1 tot.update(c) print(f"[{arm}] round {rounds:4d} " + " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(c.items()) if k != "samples"), flush=True) if c["engine_dead_health"] or c["engine_dead_response"]: dead_round = rounds break tot.pop("samples", None) summary["arms"][arm] = {"rounds": rounds, "engine_died_in_round": dead_round, "counts": dict(tot)} print(f"== arm {arm}: {rounds} rounds, engine died in round {dead_round}", flush=True) if dead_round: dead_arm = arm break summary["engine_died_in_arm"] = dead_arm if a.out: with open(a.out, "w") as f: json.dump(summary, f, indent=1) print("BUG PRESENT: engine died in arm " + dead_arm if dead_arm else "not reproduced (engine alive)", flush=True) return 1 if dead_arm else 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
Possible fixes: skip the frontend cache clear for `mode=keep`, as documented; for abort/wait, clear only once no queued request holds a handle; make `clear()` respect the reader flags; or fail just the affected request instead of the engine? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
discussion:
Thanks for the detailed report and the reproducer — the round table makes the failure mode very clear.

I'd like to take this one: making `/pause` honor the documented "`mode=keep` ignores `clear_cache`" semantics so the SHM multimodal cache isn't reset under requests that still hold handles into it. I'll put up a PR shortly.

PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_yibozhao ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` documents that it cannot give prompt log-probs. `AsyncLLM.add_request` (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py`) refuses them with ``` --kv-sharing-fast-prefill produces incorrect logprobs for prompt tokens, please disable it when the requests need prompt logprobs ``` but only when `params.prompt_logprobs` is truthy. `prompt_logprobs=0` is a legal value (the prompt token's own log-prob, no alternatives) and gets through. So do the routes that set it implicitly: * `/v1/completions` with `echo=true, logprobs=0`; * `/v1/chat/completions` with `echo=true`, whose `top_logprobs` defaults to 0 and is inherited as `prompt_logprobs`; * `/v1/chat/completions` with `prompt_logprobs=0`. What happens next depends on the model runner: * **V2 runner (the default on CUDA): HTTP 200, and every prompt log-prob is wrong.** The values are tens of nats off. Nothing in the response says so. * **V1 runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`): HTTP 500, and EngineCore dies** on the backstop `assert not self.num_prompt_logprobs` in `gpu_model_runner.py`. Every other client loses the server (`/health` 503). This is the face #51846 describes. `prompt_logprobs=1` is refused with 400 on both runners, as documented. **To Reproduce** We run two servers of the same model on one 48 GB card, one with the flag and one without: ```bash vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --generation-config vllm --port 8000 --kv-sharing-fast-prefill vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --generation-config vllm --port 8001 python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 http://127.0.0.1:8001 # stdlib only ``` (For the V1, start the first server with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`.) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Minimal client: under --kv-sharing-fast-prefill, prompt_logprobs=0 (and echo routes) answer 200 with wrong prompt log-probs on the V2 model runner, and kill EngineCore on the V1 runner. Two servers of the same model, one with the flag and one without (vLLM 0.31.0): vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --generation-config vllm --port 8000 --kv-sharing-fast-prefill vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --generation-config vllm --port 8001 Run: python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 http://127.0.0.1:8001 (stdlib only) For each way of asking for prompt log-probs it compares the log-prob of the prompt's own token at every position. prompt_logprobs=1 is refused (400), as documented. The falsy-zero asks pass the truthy admission check. Exit 1 when any of them comes back wrong or kills the engine. """ import json import sys import urllib.error import urllib.request FP = (sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://127.0.0.1:8000").rstrip("/") REF = (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "http://127.0.0.1:8001").rstrip("/") MODEL = "google/gemma-4-E2B-it" PROMPT = ("one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve. A B C D E F G H I J K L M N O P. " "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Monday Tuesday Wednesday Thursday Friday Saturday Sunday.") ASKS = [("completions prompt_logprobs=1", "/v1/completions", {"prompt_logprobs": 1}), ("completions prompt_logprobs=0", "/v1/completions", {"prompt_logprobs": 0}), ("completions echo + logprobs=0", "/v1/completions", {"echo": True, "logprobs": 0}), ("chat echo", "/v1/chat/completions", {"echo": True}), ("chat prompt_logprobs=0", "/v1/chat/completions", {"prompt_logprobs": 0})] def post(url, body): req = urllib.request.Request(url, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"content-type": "application/json"}) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r: return r.status, json.loads(r.read()) except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code, e.read().decode(errors="replace")[:200] except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 return -1, repr(e)[:200] def own_logprobs(doc, chat): h = doc if chat else doc["choices"][0] ids, plp = h["prompt_token_ids"], h["prompt_logprobs"] return [None] + [plp[i][str(ids[i])]["logprob"] for i in range(1, len(ids))] def main(): bad = 0 for name, ep, extra in ASKS: chat = "chat" in ep body = {"model": MODEL, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "return_token_ids": True, **extra} body.update({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}]} if chat else {"prompt": PROMPT}) st, doc = post(FP + ep, body) if st != 200: print(f"{name:32s} fast-prefill: HTTP {st} {str(doc)[:110]}") bad += st >= 500 or st < 0 if st >= 500 or st < 0: print(" a 1-token completion after it: HTTP", post(FP + "/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": "Hi", "max_tokens": 1})[0]) break continue rst, rdoc = post(REF + ep, body) a, b = own_logprobs(doc, chat), own_logprobs(rdoc, chat) gaps = sorted(abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(a[1:], b[1:])) wrong = sum(g > 0.5 for g in gaps) print(f"{name:32s} fast-prefill: HTTP 200, {wrong}/{len(gaps)} positions > 0.5 nat off the no-flag server " f"(median {gaps[len(gaps) // 2]:.2f}, max {gaps[-1]:.2f}); position 1-3 {a[1:4]} vs {b[1:4]}") bad += wrong > 0 print("BUG PRESENT" if bad else "not reproduced") return 1 if bad else 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ``` **Some experiments we ran on (0.31.0, RTX A6000)** The flag server compared with the no-flag server, per position of the prompt's own token: | ask | V2 runner (default) | V1 runner | |---|---|---| | completions `prompt_logprobs=1` | 400 (documented refusal) | 400 | | completions `prompt_logprobs=0` | **200, 84/84 positions wrong, median 25.73 nat, max 57.91 nat** | **500, EngineCore `AssertionError`, `/health` 503** | | completions `echo=true, logprobs=0` | 200, 84/84 wrong, median 25.73 nat | (engine already dead) | | chat `echo=true` | 200, 93/93 wrong, median 30.93 nat | (engine already dead) | | chat `prompt_logprobs=0` | 200, 93/93 wrong, median 30.93 nat | (engine already dead) | | control: the no-flag server compared with itself | max gap 0.00 on every route | -- | These numbers come from our fuller probe (same requests, a longer prompt). The condensed `repro.py` above asks the same five requests. V1 engine log: ``` AssertionError: --kv-sharing-fast-prefill produces incorrect logprobs for prompt tokens, tokens, please disable it when the requests need prompt logprobs ``` Generated tokens are unaffected: greedy outputs of the two servers agreed on every request we compared. **Possible cause (v0.31.0, assisted by Claude):** * `Gemma4Model.fast_prefill_forward` (`model_executor/models/gemma4.py`) runs the self-decoder over every token. It runs the cross-decoder (the trailing `num_kv_shared_layers` = 20 of 35 layers, which read a lower layer's KV through `kv_sharing_target_layer_name`) only at `logits_indices_padded`. * It scatters that result into a clone of the self-decoder's hidden states. So at every prompt row that is not sampled, the hidden state is the 15-layer self-decoder's, not the model's. * The V2 runner's `PromptLogprobsWorker.compute_prompt_logprobs` (`v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) then calls `compute_logits` on that tensor at every prompt row, so the values are those of a truncated model. * The V1 runner has the `num_prompt_logprobs` assert as a backstop. It holds every request whose `prompt_logprobs is not None`, so 0 reaches it, and the assert takes the whole engine down rather than failing the request. * The admission check is the only line of defence, and it uses truthiness. * 0.31.0 also refuses `prompt_logprob_token_ids` under the flag (`v1/engine/input_processor.py`, "disable it for scoring"). The OpenAI routes do not use that field. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Image chat requests on the default LRU processor cache sometimes can fail with **HTTP 500 `Expected a cached item for mm_hash='...'`** right after a P0/P1 processor-cache diverge. The divergence itself is the documented, self-healing case (`Multi-modal cache miss ... P0/P1 cache drift; returning a retryable response`). Not the 500 error, this is an `AssertionError` raised in the frontend's multimodal processor while it renders another request for the same image. Every assert in our test runs follows a divergence line for the same hash: ``` WARNING [core.py:1934] Multi-modal cache miss for request chatcmpl-997e...-af3f231e (mm_hashes=['c7b8e1c2...']): P0/P1 cache drift; returning a retryable response so the items are resent with data. ERROR [exception.py:16] Exception caught. Request id: None File "vllm/renderers/base.py", line 868, in _process_multimodal mm_inputs = mm_processor.apply(mm_processor_inputs, mm_timing_ctx) File "vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py", line 1812, in apply mm_res = self._cached_apply_hf_processor(inputs, timing_ctx) File "vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py", line 1537, in _cached_apply_hf_processor mm_kwargs, mm_prompt_updates = self._merge_mm_kwargs( File "vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py", line 1431, in _merge_mm_kwargs kwargs, updates = cache.get_and_update_item(item, item_hash) File "vllm/multimodal/cache/lru.py", line 60, in get_and_update_item assert mm_item is not None, f"Expected a cached item for {mm_hash=}" AssertionError: Expected a cached item for mm_hash='c7b8e1c2bc5b78ab3747af7d636df9b50eb973fd6f27e476883465cbca753d83' ``` The divergence comes from `POST /pause` (`clear_cache` defaults to true, for `mode=keep` as well), which clears P0 and then P1 while image requests are still being rendered. `/pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true` and `/reset_mm_cache` clear the same way. Repro (stdlib-only client below): ```bash VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms trigger,control --minutes 10 ``` Results on one RTX A5000 (one server, 10 min per arm): | arm | rounds | rounds with the 500 | `Expected a cached item` 500s | divergence lines in the server log | |---|---|---|---|---| | trigger: 3x `/pause?mode=keep` + `/resume` per round, then 24 concurrent requests for the round's 3 images | 314 (942 pauses) | **20** | **20** | 251 | | control: same traffic, no pause | 264 | 0 | 0 | 0 | The engine stays up. Only the affected requests fail.
Open repro.py here ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone client (stdlib only): the frontend's P0/P1 drift recovery races the multimodal processor. vLLM 0.31.0, AsyncLLM: when the engine reports a P0/P1 processor-cache drift miss (`mm_cache_miss_hashes`), the output handler calls `mm_processor_cache.invalidate(mm_hash)` on the asyncio thread (v1/engine/async_llm.py:838-846). The multimodal processor runs on the renderer's single-worker `_mm_executor` thread and reads the same cache twice: `is_cached()` (multimodal/processing/processor.py:1351) and later `get_and_update_item()` (processor.py:1431). An invalidate between the two makes `MultiModalProcessorSenderCache.get_and_update_item` hit `assert mm_item is not None` (multimodal/cache/lru.py:60) and the request fails with a non-retryable HTTP 500 "Expected a cached item for mm_hash=...". The drift is made with `/pause?mode=keep` (clear_cache defaults to true) while requests carrying the same image are being rendered. AsyncLLM.pause_generation clears the P0 sender cache first (async_llm.py:950-951), renders that land between that clear and the engine's own P1 clear (core.py:874-879 -> _reset_caches -> reset_mm_cache, core.py:826-827) re-cache the image in P0 only, and every later request for it is sent hash-only and misses on P1. Right after /resume a burst of concurrent requests for the same images is fired (streamed and non-streamed chat), so drift invalidates arrive while other renders of that image are in the processor. Server (needs the dev endpoints): VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 8192 --generation-config vllm Run: python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 # trigger arm then control arm python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms trigger --minutes 20 Each round uses fresh random images. Arms: `trigger` = `--cycles` pause(keep)+resume cycles, then the burst; `reset` = the same traffic with `POST /reset_mm_cache` every `--reset-every-ms` (the dev endpoint does the same P0-then-P1 clear without pausing, so drift is made many times a second); `control` = the same traffic and burst with neither. Exit 1 when any response is the "Expected a cached item" 500. Also counted: 500s from the drift miss itself (the by-design "retryable" response, which reaches an HTTP client as "Internal server error") and empty streams (HTTP 200, no token, no finish_reason, no error event). """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import base64 import http.client import json import random import struct import sys import threading import time import urllib.parse import zlib from collections import Counter ASSERT_TEXT = "Expected a cached item" def png(seed: int, size: int) -> str: rnd = random.Random(seed) raw = bytearray() row = size * 3 for _ in range(size): raw.append(0) raw += rnd.randbytes(row) def chunk(tag: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes: return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF) body = (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", size, size, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(bytes(raw), 1)) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")) return "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(body).decode() class Client: def __init__(self, base: str, timeout: float): u = urllib.parse.urlparse(base) self.host, self.port, self.timeout = u.hostname, u.port or 80, timeout def conn(self) -> http.client.HTTPConnection: return http.client.HTTPConnection(self.host, self.port, timeout=self.timeout) def get_json(self, path: str): c = self.conn() try: c.request("GET", path) r = c.getresponse() return r.status, json.loads(r.read() or b"null") finally: c.close() def post(self, path: str, body=None) -> tuple[int, str]: c = self.conn() try: data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else b"" c.request("POST", path, body=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) r = c.getresponse() return r.status, r.read().decode(errors="replace") finally: c.close() def chat(self, model: str, image: str, nonce: str, stream: bool, max_tokens: int) -> dict: body = {"model": model, "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image}}, {"type": "text", "text": f"{nonce} What is the dominant colour? One word."}]}]} c = self.conn() t0 = time.monotonic() try: c.request("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", body=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) r = c.getresponse() None, None, False for raw in r: line = raw.decode(errors="replace").strip() if not line.startswith("data: "): continue if line == "data: [DONE]": done = True break d = json.loads(line[6:]) if "error" in d: err = json.dumps(d["error"])[:600] continue for ch in d.get("choices", []): if (ch.get("delta") or {}).get("content"): tokens += 1 finish = ch.get("finish_reason") or finish return {"status": 200, "stream": True, "tokens": tokens, "finish": finish, "error": err, "done": done, "t": time.monotonic() - t0} except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 - a dropped connection is a result too return arm: {per_arm})", flush=True) return 1 if bad else 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
**Possible cause (Assisted by Claude)** 1. The engine reports drifted hashes in `EngineCoreOutput.mm_cache_miss_hashes`. `AsyncLLM`'s output handler, on the event-loop thread, then calls `mm_processor_cache.invalidate(mm_hash)` for each one (`v1/engine/async_llm.py:838-846`;). 2. The multimodal processor runs on the renderer's single-worker `_mm_executor` thread (`renderers/base.py:121-124`, `:140-141`). It checks the sender cache in `_get_cache_missing_items` (`processor.py:1351`, `cache.is_cached`), runs the HF processor on the missing items, and only then reads the entry again in `_merge_mm_kwargs` (`processor.py:1431`, `cache.get_and_update_item(None, hash)`). 3. If the invalidate lands between those two reads, `MultiModalProcessorSenderCache.get_and_update_item` (`multimodal/cache/lru.py:51-60`) finds no entry and no data, and asserts. All other P0 cache mutations are serialized on `_mm_executor`: `clear_mm_cache_async` ("Serialize clear_mm_cache through the multimodal executor to avoid races with concurrent process_inputs on the mm_processor_cache", `renderers/base.py:364-367`). `invalidate` is the one that is not. Running it through `_mm_executor` (or taking a lock around the P0 cache), or making `get_and_update_item` fall back to "not cached, send data" instead of asserting, would close the window. On main the call is at `async_llm.py:896-900` and the assert at `lru.py:60`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
discussion:
I investigated the race between P0 (sender/LRU) invalidation and the renderer's
single-worker multimodal executor on current main (a0e7137c).

**Reproduction.** A deterministic CPU regression using the real HF Qwen2-VL
processor, LRU sender cache and `OutputProcessor` (engine I/O replaced by an
asyncio queue, events force the invalidation to land between the `is_cached`
lookup and the `get_and_update` merge) fails on main with exactly the reported
`AssertionError: Expected a cached item` at `lru.py:60`. This is a constructed
interleaving, not something I hit in a production workload.

**Proposed direction.** The output handler synchronously enqueues only the
missed hash strings on a thread-safe queue *before* publishing the miss output,
and every `_process_multimodal` call drains that queue before its first cache
lookup. A render already running is never interrupted; a render queued before
the miss still observes the invalidation before it starts processing. There is
no extra executor job, Future callback or event-loop wait, so unrelated outputs
keep flowing while the multimodal worker is occupied.

**Relation to prior work.** #34749 (older cache layout) replaces the
missing-entry assertion with a request error but does not serialize the
mutation with an in-flight render; #61656 adds endpoint-level retries after P1
misses and does not touch this cache-mutation path. This change only closes
the P0 lookup/merge race — it does not eliminate P1 drift or add automatic
HTTP retries, and the SHM queued-handle case in #62123 is out of scope.

**End-to-end check (A800 80GB, Qwen2-VL-2B, your pause/resume + background
image load shape, localhost HTTP, no server-side hook):**

| arm | rounds | "Expected a cached item" asserts | image requests | ok | other 500 | stream error events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, 5 min trigger | 164 | **18** | 32,138 | 31,794 | 196 | 130 |
| patched, 5 min trigger | 164 | **0** | 31,934 | 31,565 | 199 | 170 |
| main, 2 min no-pause control | 56 | 0 | 24,632 | 24,632 | 0 | 0 |
| patched, 2 min no-pause control | 56 | 0 | 25,070 | 25,070 | 0 | 0 |

12/12 fixed public-image responses (ordinary + streamed) are byte-identical
before/after the patch (text, finish_reason, completion_tokens). To be
transparent about the remaining errors: the non-target 500s/stream error
events are the same P1-miss class both arms produce under this adversarial
cache-reset load (server-side internal-error lines 344 → 369, 1.07% → 1.16%
of requests; no new error class appears — the patched log contains zero ASGI
assertion exceptions vs 18 on main). I'm not claiming an overall error-rate
improvement from this patch.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation
and validation runs; every command and environment is documented so the
results are reproducible. I'll open a PR with the regression test and these
numbers.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes two follow-up issues from #8233 in `examples/tpu/sft`:

1. **`examples/tpu/sft/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh`**: Because the script starts with `set -xeuo pipefail`, line 115 (`DEFAULT_MASTER_ADDR="${TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES%%,*}"`) aborts with `TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES: unbound variable` whenever `TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES` is unset (for example on single-host TPU v6e-4 VMs or single-host GKE TPU pods where the webhook does not inject `TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES`), before reaching the `127.0.0.1` fallback on line 116 (and even when `MASTER_ADDR` is explicitly provided). Default `TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES` to `127.0.0.1` before stripping `,.*`.
2. **`examples/tpu/sft/README.md`**: #8233 changed `run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh` to default to `SFT_TRAINER_MODE=torchrun` (was `ray`), so the README's `ray job submit` commands need `SFT_TRAINER_MODE=ray` and the `verl-hardware-plugin` runtime environment (`VERL_PLATFORM=tpu`, `VERL_USE_EXTERNAL_MODULES=verl_hardware_plugin`, matching `examples/tpu/grpo/README.md`).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+tpu+sft (no open PR modifies `examples/tpu/sft/`).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

- Verified the single-host TPU v6e-4 `torchrun` (`MASTER_ADDR=127.0.0.1` when `TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES` is unset in the pod) and `ray` SFT smoke tests in TPU E2E CI (`e2e_sft_llm_tpu`: 8 steps, Ray `train/loss` `1.3779 -> 0.5452` / `val/loss` `0.7239 -> 0.6082`; `torchrun` `train/loss` `1.3818 -> 0.5464` / `val/loss` `0.7234 -> 0.6084`).
- Verified bash parameter expansion under `set -u`:
  ```bash
  for v in UNSET localhost h0,h1; do
    (set -u; [[ $v != UNSET ]] && export TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES=$v; D="${TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES:-127.0.0.1}"; D="${D%%,*}"; echo "$v -> ${MASTER_ADDR:-$D}")
  done
  # UNSET -> 127.0.0.1
  # localhost -> localhost
  # h0,h1 -> h0
  ```
- Ran `SKIP=autogen-trainer-cfg pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD` (all passed).
- AI assistance was used to draft and verify this PR.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
# Single-host TPU v6e-4 (torchrun default, works even when TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES is unset)
NNODES_TRAINER=1 N_CHIPS_TRAINER=4 DATA_PARALLEL_SHARD_SIZE=4   bash examples/tpu/sft/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `examples/tpu/sft/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh`: replace `DEFAULT_MASTER_ADDR="${TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES%%,*}"` with `DEFAULT_MASTER_ADDR="${TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES:-127.0.0.1}"` followed by `DEFAULT_MASTER_ADDR="${DEFAULT_MASTER_ADDR%%,*}"`.
- `examples/tpu/sft/README.md`: update the default mode description and add `SFT_TRAINER_MODE=ray` + `RUNTIME_ENV` to the `ray job submit` examples.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: Covered by the TPU SFT example script and TPU E2E CI (`e2e_sft_llm_tpu`).

items.title: [CI] Move B200 Kernels and MoE Refactor evals from manual to automatic shards
items.author: Thangnguyenvn98
items.summary: Replaces manual Buildkite shard partitioning for B200 kernel and MoE integration tests with automatic pytest-based sharding, eliminating hand-maintained shard configs.
items.body:
## Overview

Moves three steps that split their tests by hand onto `automatic_shard`, following #62077 and #62084. `kernels-b200` ran a hand-written `case "$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB"` block per shard. The two MoE Refactor integration steps read a different config list in each shard (`config-*-shard-$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB.txt`). Each now runs plain pytest, the planner splits it using main's timings, and new tests or configs no longer need placing in a shard by hand.

## Claims

| Step | Was | Planned shards |
|---|---:|---:|
| `kernels-b200` | 3 hand-written `case` shards | 3 |
| `moe-refactor-integration-test-b200-temporary` | 4 config-list shards | 6 |
| `moe-refactor-integration-test-h100-temporary` | 4 config-list shards | 3 |

- Every test and every config runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment as before.
- A test file or config added later is placed by the planner, not by editing a `case` arm or a shard list.
- Labels drop `Shard %N`; the generator names jobs `<label> shard N/M`.
- The AMD mirrors (NVFP4 Dense Emulation, both MoE Refactor mirrors) are short. They stop inheriting the fixed shards and run as one job each.

## Validation

- Planned each step with ci-infra main's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against this branch and main's timings.
- Rendered each step with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper. Every test of every command ran in exactly one shard, with the same env (6/6 cases).
- For the config-list steps, also ran the generated shard jobs against vLLM's real `tests/evals/gsm8k/conftest.py` and config files, with the test body stubbed. All 19 B200 configs and all 12 H100 configs ran once each across the shards. No shard printed `not in the plan`, so the plan matched every config ID that main has timings for.
- `/ci run` covers `kernels-b200`. The two MoE Refactor steps are optional, so a build scoped to their keys and their AMD mirrors follows the `/ci run` build.

## Details

- **`kernels-b200` setup.** `python3 examples/basic/offline_inference/chat.py` was in shard 1 only. The planner needs plain pytest after the first pytest command, so it now runs as a setup command, once in each shard.
- **Config lists.** `moe-refactor/config-b200.txt` already listed exactly the union of the four B200 shard lists. `config-h100.txt` is the union of the four H100 shard lists. The per-shard lists are removed.
- **ROCm list kept twice.** The H100 step's AMD mirror now reads a new combined `config-rocm.txt`. `config-rocm-shard-*.txt` stay because the separate `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` still reads them.
- **`moe-refactor-integration-test-h100-temporary`** plans 3 shards at about the old slowest shard's length, so its wait stays about the same with one job fewer. The planner flags it slightly over the 20-minute target.
- **Timeouts unchanged (human).** As in #62077 and #62084, `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job. A single-job fallback (no plan, or the `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` rollback switch) would outrun it. Fallback-aware timeouts belong in a central timeout setting.
- **Left out.** `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` and `lora-tp-distributed`, with their AMD mirrors, are rewritten the same way on a separate branch. They wait for the L4 queue to be back so they can be validated. `basic-models-tests-extra-initialization`, `spec-decode-mtp-other-acceptance-nightly` and the Humming A100/H100 steps stay on fixed shards: their plans are longer than today's, they have no timings, or they fail on main.

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] GDN chunk/prefill path: honor fp32 SSM state precision
items.author: miggle711
items.summary: This PR fixes the decode-update kernel... the chunk-path kernels are a straightforward follow-up. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

Closes #62116.

#54146 fixed the GDN decode-update kernel overflowing fp16 with a large fp32 SSM state, but its own description flagged that the same bug exists on the chunk/prefill path:

> The same materialize-in-activation-dtype pattern exists in the chunk/prefill kernels (`chunk_o`, `chunk_delta_h`, `wy_fast`) and the `core_attn_out` buffer. This PR fixes the decode-update kernel... the chunk-path kernels are a straightforward follow-up.

This PR is that follow-up for `chunk_delta_h.py` and `chunk_o.py` (the two files that actually need it; `wy_fast.py` turned out not to, see below).

## Root cause

The recurrent SSM state is accumulated in fp32 inside the chunk-path Triton kernels, but several buffers and `tl.dot` operands silently downcast it to the activation dtype (fp16/bf16) before it's normalized:

- `chunk_delta_h.py`: the per-chunk state buffer `h` was allocated in `k`'s dtype instead of the state's. Two internal `tl.dot` calls also downcast the fp32 state (and its correction term `b_v`, which inherits the state's magnitude) to fp16 before accumulating.
- `chunk_o.py`: the output buffer `o` was allocated in `v`'s dtype, and its `tl.dot(b_q, tl.trans(b_h))` downcast the (possibly fp32) state `b_h` before computing the raw, unnormalized readout.
- `chunk.py`: `chunk_gated_delta_rule`'s public API unconditionally cast its return value back to `q`'s dtype, which would silently undo a correct fp32 computation from the two fixes above.

I initially suspected `wy_fast.py` had the same pattern (it also allocates output buffers in the activation dtype), but its `tl.dot` calls operate on per-token key/value transforms with no fp32 accumulator carried across iterations, not state, so it doesn't need this fix.

## Fix

Same approach as #54146: gate each buffer's dtype on `initial_state.dtype == torch.float32`, and upcast the activation-dtype operand (not downcast the state) in the two `tl.dot` calls. The fp16/bf16-state path is unchanged, these are no-ops when the state is already fp16, so behavior and performance for the common case are byte-for-byte identical.

**Known gap (scoped out, same as #54146 only fixed the decode kernel):** the real model code in `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py` allocates its own `core_attn_out` buffer ,unconditionally fp16/bf16, at 5 separate call sites across the CUDA/HIP/XPU/CPU/fused-spec-decode backends,  and passes it into the chunk path via the `core_attn_out` in-place-write parameter, bypassing this PR's allocation fix entirely. Making this reach real inference end-to-end needs those 5 call sites updated too. Opening this as the library-level fix first since it's independently correct and testable; I'd happy to follow up on the caller sites in a separate PR if that's the preferred scope.

## Test Plan

Adds `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule_finite_under_large_fp32_state` to `tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py`, mirroring #54146's own test: drives `chunk_gated_delta_rule` with fp16 activations and a large (`1e6`, past fp16's ~65504 max) fp32 `initial_state`, and asserts the output and final state are finite and preserve the true magnitude (not saturated).

Also ran the full existing file (18 pre-existing decode-path tests + the new one) to check for regressions.

## Test Result

- Before (on current main): `chunk_gated_delta_rule`'s output is 100% non-finite (all 65536/65536 elements) and `final_state` is non-finite, while an fp32 `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` reference from the identical inputs and initial state stays fully finite (`max|o| ≈ 3.7e6`) -- isolating the failure to the chunk path's own precision handling, not the input magnitude.
- After this fix: output and final state are both fully finite, `max|o| ≈ 3.736e6` vs. the reference's `≈3.738e6` (max abs diff ≈1944, mean ≈125,  consistent with ordinary fp32 chunked-vs-recurrent rounding, not corruption).
- `pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py -v`: 19 passed, 0 failed (18 pre-existing + 1 new).

Validated on NVIDIA L40S.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR's investigation, fix, and test were developed with Claude (Anthropic) as described in [CONTRIBUTING.md's AI Assisted Contributions section](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing/#ai-assisted-contributions). I reviewed and understand every changed line, ran the validation above myself, and I'm responsible for this PR's content.

items.title: [CI] workflows: Don't cancel in-flight post-merge runs on main
items.author: JerryChaox
items.summary: In, every to lands in the same concurrency group with enabled. Each merge therefore cancels the previous merge's in-flight post-merge run.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44832.

In `pr-test-{npu,xpu,xeon,musa,rust}.yml`, every `push` to `main` lands in the same concurrency group (`...-refs/heads/main`) with `cancel-in-progress` enabled. Each merge therefore cancels the previous merge's in-flight post-merge run. Recent data: NPU had 39 of its last 60 `main` push runs cancelled, Xeon 18 of 30, XPU 11 of 31. As a result, breaking commits can reach `main` without a completed run on these backends, and the culprit range grows when something finally fails.

## Modifications

In these five workflows, change only `cancel-in-progress`. The concurrency groups are unchanged.

```yaml
cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```

- **`pull_request`:** unchanged. A new push to a PR still cancels that PR's older run.
- **`push`, `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` on `main`:** runs queue instead of cancelling the run in progress. GitHub keeps at most one pending run per group, and a newer pending run replaces an older one. Runner cost is therefore bounded at one running plus one queued run per workflow, not one run per commit.
- **`workflow_call` callers** (`release-branch-cut.yml`, `bot-bump-sglang-version.yml`): still never cancelled. The old `!= 'workflow_call'` check could never match, because a reusable workflow sees the caller's `event_name`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, CI configuration only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

- [x] Ran `actionlint` on the changed files. The only findings are pre-existing ones (custom runner labels, shellcheck notes); none are on the changed lines.
- [ ] Add unit tests: N/A
- [ ] Update documentation: N/A

items.title: [CI] Post-merge runs on main cancel each other in NPU/XPU/Xeon/MUSA/SMG workflows
items.author: JerryChaox
items.summary: Whenever the merge rate is higher than one run's duration, rarely finishes a full post-merge run on these backends. Cancelling superseded runs is correct for PRs, where only the newest head commit matters.
items.body:
## Problem

Several hardware CI workflows that run on `push` to `main` put every post-merge run into the same concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress` enabled:

| Workflow | Concurrency group | `cancel-in-progress` |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-test-npu.yml` | `pr-test-npu-${{ inputs.ref \|\| github.ref }}` | `${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_call' }}` |
| `pr-test-xpu.yml` | `pr-test-xpu-${{ inputs.ref \|\| github.ref }}` | same |
| `pr-test-xeon.yml` | `pr-test-xeon-${{ inputs.ref \|\| github.ref }}` | same |
| `pr-test-musa.yml` | `pr-test-musa-${{ inputs.ref \|\| github.ref }}` | same |
| `pr-test-rust.yml` | `gateway-tests-${{ github.ref }}` | `true` |

For a push to `main`, `github.ref` is always `refs/heads/main`, so **each new merge cancels the still-running test of the previous merge**. Whenever the merge rate is higher than one run's duration, `main` rarely finishes a full post-merge run on these backends.

## Evidence (recent `push` runs on `main`, via `gh run list -e push -b main`)

- `pr-test-npu.yml`: 39 of the last 60 cancelled, 19 succeeded
- `pr-test-xeon.yml`: 18 of 30 cancelled
- `pr-test-xpu.yml`: 11 of 31 cancelled
- `pr-test-rust.yml`: 8 of 60 cancelled
- `pr-test-musa.yml`: 3 of 60 cancelled (short runs, so it is hit less often)

## Impact

- A breaking commit can land on `main` without any completed post-merge run on these backends.
- When a run finally completes and fails, the range of suspect commits is large, so bisecting takes much longer.
- Compute already spent on the cancelled runs is wasted.

Cancelling superseded runs is correct for PRs, where only the newest head commit matters. It is wrong for `main`, where every commit is a candidate culprit.

Side note: `github.event_name != 'workflow_call'` does not do what it seems to intend. Inside a reusable workflow, `github.event_name` is the *caller's* event (for example `workflow_dispatch` or `schedule`), never `workflow_call`.

## Proposed fix

Only cancel in-progress runs for `pull_request` events:

```yaml
cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```

`push`, `schedule` and called runs then queue instead of killing the in-flight run. GitHub keeps at most one pending run per concurrency group (a newer pending run replaces an older pending one), so cost stays bounded at one running plus one queued run per workflow. This matters for scarce runners such as NPU. PR behaviour does not change.

items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp) deadlocks on RTX 6000D (SM120) — hangs in JIT warmup and at first real request (GDN/hyperconnection kernels); Qwen3.8-27B works fine on the same box
items.author: zhuochengs
items.summary: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 deadlocks on SM120 GPUs during Triton JIT kernel warmup and first request, while smaller Qwen3.8-27B runs fine on identical hardware.
items.body:
### Your current environment

```text
vLLM:        0.31.0 (pip wheel)
PyTorch:     2.13.0 (triton 3.7.1, the torch-pinned version; also tried triton 3.8.0 — identical behavior)
GPU:         2x NVIDIA RTX 6000D (China SKU, Blackwell SM120, 84GB GDDR7 each, no NVLink)
Driver:      595.99.02 / CUDA 13.2
OS:          CentOS Stream 9, kernel 5.14.0-756.el9
Python:      3.12.14
Model:       Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (official release, ~180GB, PLE 51B n-gram table offloaded to host RAM)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 on SM120 deadlocks — in three distinct places depending on flags, all reproducible:

Hang 1 — JIT kernel warmup (default flags): Startup hangs during warmup_kernels inside Triton lazy init. py-spy of the worker:

```text
_init_handles (triton/compiler/compiler.py:469)
launch_metadata (triton/compiler/compiler.py:485)
run (triton/runtime/jit.py:760)
fused_post_conv_prep (vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_gdn_prefill_post_conv.py:245)
_forward_core (vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:1419)
...
_warmup_kernels (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py:355)
```

No nvcc/ptxas processes are alive at this point (compilation already done — it hangs at module handle loading).

Hang 2 — same warmup, different kernel: With VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 (wrapper frame confirmed gone from the stack), the hang persists but moves to causal_conv1d_fn (vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/causal_conv1d.py:712), again inside _init_handles.

Hang 3 — runtime, with warmup disabled and eager mode: With kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup = False (patched default) and --enforce-eager: startup completes (Application startup complete), the first chat completion request runs prefill (scheduler stats: num_running_reqs=1, 58 prefix queries, kv_cache_usage=0.011), then the engine times out and dies:

```text
TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out.
```

py-spy of the worker at hang time shows it deep inside the model forward:

```text
__torch_function__ (vllm/model_executor/parameter.py:124)
default_unquantized_gemm (vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py:89)
apply (vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py:239)
forward (vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py:610)
_down_and_inject (vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/hyperconnection.py:156)
mix (vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/hyperconnection.py:171)
forward (vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/model.py:315)
...
execute_model (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:2007)
```
During the runtime hang, nvidia-smi shows both GPUs at 100% util but only ~95W (idle-spinning kernels waiting on each other), and both worker processes at 100% CPU.

```bash
NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
vllm serve /data/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.8-flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
# then: curl POST /v1/chat/completions with a trivial prompt
```

What we already ruled out
NCCL / transport: a standalone 2-GPU allreduce via torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 (with NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1) passes in seconds. Note: on this box NCCL comm init itself hangs unless P2P is disabled — a separate platform quirk of the 6000D, but transport itself is fine.
Breakable CUDA graphs: disabled via env — hang persists (Hang 2).
Triton version: 3.7.1 (torch pin) and 3.8.0 behave identically.
JIT warmup: patched off — hang moves to the first real request (Hang 3).
torch.compile / CUDA graphs: --enforce-eager — hang persists.
Weight loading / KV allocation / graph capture: all complete successfully before the hang.
Key observation pointing at qwen4_exp on SM120
Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 — which also uses a GDN hybrid backbone but through the qwen3.5/next-style code path (no PLE n-gram table, no MTP, no hyperconnection) — serves correctly on a single GPU of the same machine, same driver/vLLM environment. Text, vision (image input), and response_format=json_object all pass.

This localizes the deadlock to the qwen4_exp-specific components (PLE host offload of the 51B n-gram table — note host RAM usage ~51GB with EngramConfig(cpu_offload=True) auto-enabled — hyperconnection, MTP) on SM120.

Expected behavior
Flash-Next FP8 should serve on SM120 the same way it does on other Blackwell boards, or at least fail with a clear error instead of a silent kernel-level deadlock.

Additional context
Related PR: #59869 (subscribed there as well).
Full journalctl logs and all three py-spy dumps available on request.
Suspicion (unverified): the hang sits at Triton module loading / kernel execution interacting with the driver on sm_120; possibly also worth checking with a newer driver.
Anyone else seeing qwen4_exp deadlocks on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090 class)? Any known workaround env/flag?



### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
discussion:
Update on the #59869 reference: that PR is a (now closed, unmerged) perf-tuning change adding sm_120
skinny-GEMM plan tables — not a fix for this deadlock. Linking it only as related context.

One useful data point from that PR's discussion: its author appears to have run
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (with the PLE table offloaded) successfully on a **standard RTX PRO 6000
(SM120, 96GB)** while profiling. If so, the deadlock reported here may be specific to the
**RTX 6000D** (the cut-down China SKU) and/or driver 595.99.02, rather than SM120 in general.
Happy to test specific flags or collect additional diagnostics if that helps narrow it down.

items.title: [Attention] Support NVFP4 KV cache at head_dim 512 (Gemma 4) on SM100
items.author: xuanzic
items.summary: This PR adds that support through the FlashInfer backend on SM100/SM103 (B200/B300). Adds NVFP4 KV cache support for headdim 512 attention layers (Gemma 4 global layers) on SM100/SM103 through the FlashInfer backend.
items.body:
## Overview


This PR adds that support through the FlashInfer backend on SM100/SM103 (B200/B300).

Adds NVFP4 KV cache support for head_dim 512 attention layers (Gemma 4 global layers) on SM100/SM103 through the FlashInfer backend. Context attention materializes the active NVFP4 pages to FP8 (nvfp4_kv_materialize_fp8) and runs the existing FP8 trtllm-gen context kernel; decode uses FlashInfer PrimTS. Also fixes NaN outputs when KV groups with different NVFP4 page layouts share the block pool, and supports MTP with full CUDA graphs.

Depends on FlashInfer #5720 (PrimTS NVFP4 decode at H512), #6445 (NVFP4 KV prefill at H512) 




## Claims


- [Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4 ](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4) runs with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` on B200/B300, including MTP with full CUDA graphs.
- Accuracy is close to FP8 KV: GPQA Diamond 85.20 vs 85.16, MMLU-Pro 86.21 vs 86.20, AIME 2025 85.26 vs 87.55.
- Throughput matches FP8 KV within a few percent: -2.6% on the perf-eval 8k-in-1k-out workload.
- NVFP4 KV holds 1.65-1.78x more tokens. On a prefix-reuse workload where only NVFP4 fits the shared prefixes, TTFT and E2E improve about 3x.
- No NaN or degenerate outputs; without the zeroing fix, 7-11% of Gemma 4 AIME responses degenerate.
- No JIT compiles while serving: PrimTS decode is planned for every batch size at startup, which takes about +40 s without MTP and about +2 min with MTP.

## Validation


**Unit test**
```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_trtllm_attention_integration.py -k nvfp4_kv_head_dim_512
```

**Server** (flags as in vllm-project/perf-eval, plus the KV dtype and attention backend)
```bash
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=HND vllm serve nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --reasoning-parser gemma4 --tool-call-parser gemma4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null,"allow_global_per_layer_attribute_access":true}}'
```
- The FP8 baseline uses `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
- MTP adds `--speculative-config '{"model":"<gemma-4-31B-it-assistant>","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`.

**Accuracy** (B300, TP1 x DP2, `--max-model-len 262144 --block-size 64`, ModelOpt-calibrated KV scales)

| | FP8 KV | NVFP4 KV |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AIME 2025 (avg@64) | 87.55 +- 0.75 | 85.26 +- 0.53 |
| GPQA Diamond (x16) | 85.16 | 85.20 |
| MMLU-Pro | 86.20 | 86.21 |

- AIME, GPQA and MMLU-Pro use simple-evals with temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 131072 and the Gemma 4 thinking chat template; AIME answers are graded by an LLM judge.
- GSM8K (B200, NVFP4 KV, lm-eval 0.4.12, CoT zero-shot with chat template):
  - TP1 x DP2: 95.00
  - TP2: 94.39
  - TP4: 94.09
  - TP1 x DP2 + MTP: 94.39 (acceptance 78.9%)
  - TP4 + MTP: 94.24

**Throughput** (B200, TP1)
```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model <served-model> \
  --dataset-name random --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 128 \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 128
```
- Over 3 runs: FP8 2218 tok/s, NVFP4 2160 tok/s. FP8 with the default attention backend gets 2212.
- AIPerf (ISL 128-30000, concurrency 1-64, prefix caching off): NVFP4 / FP8 = 0.96-0.99 at concurrency >= 8, about 0.94 at concurrency 1.

## Details


<summary>Prefix reuse vs KV cache size (B300)</summary>

Workload: 60 groups, each a 25-27K shared prefix plus a 2-3K unique tail, OSL 100. Server flags add `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 8192 --kv-cache-memory <bytes>`. Numbers are from the second pass, averaged over 3 runs.

| Config | Concurrency | Prefix hit FP8 -> NVFP4 | Mean TTFT ms | Mean E2E ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP1, 128 GiB KV / GPU | 32 | 32% -> 86% | 8087 -> 2447 | 21269 -> 6331 |
| TP2, 64 GiB KV / GPU | 32 | 33% -> 86% | 4704 -> 1461 | 12243 -> 3769 |
| TP2, 128 GiB KV / GPU (both fit) | 32 | 86% -> 86% | 1428 -> 1537 | 3700 -> 3779 |

- **NaN root cause:** Gemma 4 head_dim 256 and 512 groups share one block pool with different NVFP4 page layouts. A reused block's stale E2M1 bytes can sit where the other layout keeps its E4M3 block scales, and attention multiplies masked positions by them (0 * NaN). New blocks are zeroed only when several NVFP4 layouts share the pool, as vLLM already does for mamba and mixed-precision caches, so models with a single NVFP4 layout are unchanged.
- **Block size:** head_dim 512 kernel block sizes are capped at 64 tokens, because FP8 head_dim 512 context has no 128-token-page kernel.
- **Limitations:** an FP8 query is required, as for the native NVFP4 kernels. The FP8 copy is a temporary workspace outside the KV-cache budget, 4 KiB per token for Gemma 4.

items.title: [Bug]: GDN chunk/prefill path overflows fp16 with a large fp32 SSM state (chunk-path follow-up to #54146)
items.author: miggle711
items.summary: Anyone running a GDN model (e.g. Qwen3-Next/3.5) with (the setting meant to prevent exactly this problem) can still hit an fp16 overflow during prefill/chunked processing, not just decode.
items.body:
## Overview

Anyone running a GDN model (e.g. Qwen3-Next/3.5) with `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32` (the setting meant to prevent exactly this problem) can still hit an fp16 overflow during prefill/chunked processing, not just decode. `chunk_gated_delta_rule` (the GDN chunk/prefill path) produces inf/NaN output and a corrupted recurrent state once that state grows large over a long prompt, the same decode-collapse symptom #54146/#54308 describe, but triggered from the prefill side instead. This is the chunk-path follow-up #54146 explicitly flagged as still needed:

> The same materialize-in-activation-dtype pattern exists in the chunk/prefill kernels (`chunk_o`, `chunk_delta_h`, `wy_fast`) and the `core_attn_out` buffer. This PR fixes the decode-update kernel... the chunk-path kernels are a straightforward follow-up.

## Root cause

The recurrent SSM state is accumulated in fp32 inside the chunk-path Triton kernels, but several intermediate buffers and dot-product operands silently downcast that fp32 value to the activation dtype (fp16/bf16) before it's safely normalized:

- `chunk_delta_h.py`: the per-chunk state buffer `h` is allocated in `k`'s (activation) dtype rather than the state's dtype, and the kernel's two internal `tl.dot` calls downcast the fp32 state (`b_h1..4`) and its correction term (`b_v`) to fp16 before accumulating, even when the state cache is fp32.
- `chunk_o.py`: the output buffer `o` is allocated in `v`'s (activation) dtype, and its `tl.dot(b_q, tl.trans(b_h))` downcasts the (possibly fp32) state `b_h` before computing the raw, unnormalized readout.
- `chunk.py`: `chunk_gated_delta_rule`'s public API unconditionally casts its return value back to `q`'s dtype, which would undo a correct fp32 computation anyway.

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.chunk import chunk_gated_delta_rule
from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.fused_recurrent import fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule

torch.manual_seed(0)
device = "cuda"
B, T, H, K, V = 1, 256, 4, 64, 64

q = torch.randn(B, T, H, K, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
k = torch.nn.functional.normalize(torch.randn(B, T, H, K, dtype=torch.float32, device=device), p=2, dim=-1)
v = torch.randn(B, T, H, V, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
g = torch.full((B, T, H), -0.01, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
beta = torch.full((B, T, H), 0.5, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

# fp32 state at a magnitude reachable over long context -- same order of
# magnitude #54146 uses (1e6 > fp16's ~65504 max) for the decode kernel's own test.
initial_state = torch.randn(B, H, V, K, device=device, dtype=torch.float32) * 1e6

# Ground truth: fp32 recurrent reference from the same inputs/state.
o_ref, final_state_ref = fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule(
    q=q, k=k, v=v, g=g, beta=beta, initial_state=initial_state.clone(), inplace_final_state=False,
)
assert torch.isfinite(o_ref).all() and torch.isfinite(final_state_ref).all()  # passes

# Chunk path under test, fp16 activations (as used in real decoding).
o, final_state = chunk_gated_delta_rule(
    q=q.half(), k=k.half(), v=v.half(), g=g.half(), beta=beta.half(),
    initial_state=initial_state.clone(), output_final_state=True,
)
print((~torch.isfinite(o)).sum().item(), "/", o.numel(), "non-finite")  # 65536 / 65536
print((~torch.isfinite(final_state)).any().item())  # True
```

With this fp32 reference confirmed finite, `chunk_gated_delta_rule`'s output is **100% non-finite** (all 65536 elements) and `final_state` is non-finite, from identical inputs and the identical initial state. This isolates the failure to the chunk path's own precision handling, not to the input magnitude being inherently unstable.

## Environment

- vLLM 0.31.0 (also confirmed present on current `main` as of 2026-10-17, the three files below haven't changed since the version this was reproduced against).
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, NVIDIA L40S (Triton backend, bundled with vLLM).

## Suggested fix

A PR extending #54146's dtype-gating approach (materialize in the state's dtype only when `initial_state.dtype == torch.float32`, so fp16-state behavior is unchanged) to `chunk_delta_h.py`, `chunk_o.py`, and `chunk.py`'s return path will follow.

Note: this only fixes the library-level `chunk_gated_delta_rule` function. The real model code in `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py` allocates its own `core_attn_out` buffer (unconditionally fp16/bf16, at 5 separate call sites across the CUDA/HIP/XPU/CPU/fused-spec-decode backends) and passes it into the chunk path via the `core_attn_out` in-place-write parameter, bypassing the library's own allocation. Making this fix reach real inference end-to-end will need those call sites updated too, left as a follow-up, same as #54146 scoped only its one kernel.

I'll open a PR for this shortly.

items.title: [Bugfix] Swap ipc_cache tensors into meta placeholders in place
items.author: Kylinny
items.summary: Fixes MoE router crashes during IPC cache loading by swapping tensors in-place into meta placeholders instead of replacing them with new parameters, preserving object identity.
items.body:
## Summary

`IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` replaced each meta placeholder with a **new** `nn.Parameter` object. Objects that captured the placeholder during model construction kept pointing at the meta tensor. MoE routers are such objects: models pass `gate.e_score_correction_bias` into the MoE layer, and the router (a plain `FusedMoERouter`, not an `nn.Module`) keeps it as a plain attribute — so after loading via `--load-format ipc_cache`, every router still held the meta placeholder and failed at runtime (CUDA illegal memory access / meta-tensor errors). Thank you to the reporter for the thorough issue and the minimal reproducer, which made the root cause easy to confirm.

This PR swaps the cached tensor **into the existing placeholder** with `torch.utils.swap_tensors`, preserving object identity so every captured reference sees the cached data. A plain `param.data` assignment cannot do this — it fails for meta tensors (`RuntimeError: ... incompatible tensor type`, verified on torch 2.14.1).

Two supporting changes, each verified necessary with a failing-then-passing check:

- **Buffers are applied before parameters.** `MambaMixer2` registers `conv_weights` as a view of the meta `conv1d.weight`, and `swap_tensors` refuses while such a view is alive (verified: `RuntimeError: Expected use_count of t1 to be 1 or 2 ... got 3`). Replacing the buffer first releases the view. The sort is stable, so relative order within each kind is preserved.
- **The tied-weight alias path only re-points, never swaps.** The canonical object already holds the cached data after the in-place swap; swapping an alias placeholder into it would move the meta tensor *back* into the canonical entry (verified: canonical `is_meta` becomes `True` again — silent corruption into uninitialized weights).

## Not a duplicate

I checked the issue timeline (no cross-referenced PRs) and searched open PRs for `ipc_cache`, `_apply_entries`, and `swap_tensors` — no open PR addresses this issue. Fixes #62105.

## Reproduction (CPU-only, copy-paste runnable)

The issue's minimal reproducer, run verbatim:

```python
import torch
from torch import nn

class Gate(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.e_score_correction_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(4), requires_grad=False)

class Router:  # plain object, like GroupedTopKRouter
    def __init__(self, e_score_correction_bias):
        self.e_score_correction_bias = e_score_correction_bias

def build():
    with torch.device("meta"):
        gate = Gate()
    return gate, Router(gate.e_score_correction_bias)

cached = torch.arange(4.0)

# What IpcModelLoader._apply_entries did before this PR
gate, router = build()
gate._parameters.pop("e_score_correction_bias")
gate.register_parameter("e_score_correction_bias", nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False))
print("replace:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias)

# What it does after this PR
gate, router = build()
torch.utils.swap_tensors(gate.e_score_correction_bias, nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False))
print("swap:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias)
```

Before (old behavior):
```
replace: True False
```
After (this PR):
```
swap: False True
```

## Tests

New CPU-runnable regression test: `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ipc_loader.py` (5 tests covering router-identity preservation, buffer-view ordering, tied-weight aliases, post-quant tensors absent from the meta model, and no leftover meta tensors).

Test commands and results — a full vLLM build is not available in this environment, so I validated the shipped `_apply_entries` implementation directly via a stub harness that loads the real `ipc_loader.py` and runs the same scenarios as the new test file, on both the old and new code:

- Old code: `FAIL router_identity` (router stranded on the meta placeholder — bug reproduced)
- New code: all 7 scenarios pass (`router_identity`, `buffer_view_order`, `tied_alias`, `new_param`, `no_meta_left`, `copy_mode`, `alias_no_swap`)

The new `pytest` file should be run in CI: `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ipc_loader.py`.

No GPU end-to-end run was possible here; the existing `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py` e2e suite covers the daemon path in CI.

## Checklist notes

- **Design fit:** change is isolated to the weight-cache loader (`_apply_entries` only, one caller); ~50 lines; no new abstractions or API changes.
- **Performance:** load-time only; adds one stable sort over the entry dict. No steady-state inference impact, no new synchronization.
- **Compatibility:** `torch.utils.swap_tensors` requires torch>=2.1, well below vLLM's floor. On shape/dtype mismatch it behaves with the same leniency as the old replace path (verified). Non-meta placeholders fall back to the old registration path.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was implemented with AI assistance (agentic coding assistant). Every changed line was reviewed by the submitting human, the fix mechanism was verified empirically (not taken on faith from the issue's proposal — including finding and guarding the alias-path corruption case the proposal missed), and the test scenarios were run against both the old and new code.

items.title: [Fix] muse: recover channel headers after unframed prose
items.author: peihan-dev
items.summary: Muse can emit unframed prose followed by a framed tool header without an intervening. Both detectors remain inside the unframed body.
items.body:
## Motivation

Muse can emit unframed prose followed by a framed tool header without an intervening `<|eom|>`. Both detectors remain inside the unframed body. The client receives raw protocol text instead of a structured tool call.

```text
Let me check.<|start|>assistant to=get_weather<|message|><atem:function_calls><atem:invoke name="get_weather"><atem:parameter name="city">Paris</atem:parameter></atem:invoke></atem:function_calls>
```

## Modifications

Let a reserved `<|start|>` marker end unframed prose in both the Muse reasoning detector and tool detector. Limit recovery to an unset recipient. Explicit answer channels retain quoted tool headers, and tool arguments retain marker-like text.

The reasoning detector also recovers subsequent reasoning and answer channels. This complements the parser-handoff flag fix in https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/16717.

## Accuracy Tests

The unchanged runtime reproduces the missing call. All 25 tests in the Muse detector suite pass with the patch. The new coverage checks every two-part split, character chunks, buffered input, marker-like arguments, and the reasoning-to-tool chain after an unframed preamble.

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/function_call/test_muse_glimmer_detector.py -v
```

These CPU checks use the runtime image with the upstream patch and test file. No model weights or GPU are required.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This change affects response parsing only.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit passes for all three changed files.
- [x] Add coverage to the existing registered CPU suite.
- [x] Preserve existing quoted-header and channel-scoping tests.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve token IDs in completion derender responses
items.author: dskwe
items.summary: Fixes completion derender responses to preserve requested token IDs in both batch and streaming modes, mirroring a prior chat completion fix.
items.body:
## Overview

Preserve requested generated token IDs in batch and streaming completion derender responses, following the chat fix in #61065.

## Claims

- Both completion derender modes forward each input choice's generated `token_ids` when `completion_request.return_token_ids=true`.
- Null/false flags retain null ID fields; decoding, usage accounting and stream state are unchanged.
- Prompt-ID metadata, echo parity and stop/logprob behavior are out of scope.

## Validation

Regression and neighboring tests were run in a Linux CPU Docker environment (Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.19.0). At tested base `5bf3d9f6653e53485f0ca74149f958dc6cbd3b82`:

| Selection | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New batch/stream × null/false/true regression | 2 failed, 4 passed | 6 passed |
| Regression plus existing neighboring cases | — | 11 passed |

Exact expanded test command:

```sh
docker exec -w /validation/completion-ids-20261017 \
  -e PYTHONPATH=/validation/completion-ids-20261017 \
  -e VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
  vllm-tokenizer-validation-20261013 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -p completion_ids_local_assets \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  -k 'preserves_requested_token_ids or finish_reason_matches_chat_completion or tool_call_id_matches_chat_completion or keeps_parser_tool_call_id' \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

Rerun before publication: **11 passed, 46 deselected in 6.25s**, exit 0. The private local-assets plugin substitutes a real cached OPT tokenizer for the suite's unavailable Llama fixture and skips the full distributed/environment/memory teardown. The default Llama fixture was not run. For the standard repository regression selection, use:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  -k test_derender_completion_preserves_requested_token_ids -v
```

A separate normal render-module CLI/Uvicorn HTTP A/B probe used real cached OPT config/tokenizer assets and caller-supplied generated IDs. It exercised missing request/omitted flag/false/true, multi-prompt batch flattening, and per-index carried streaming across multiple deltas plus empty terminal deltas. Each variant returned 28 POST 200 responses; baseline had 12 ID-specific assertion failures, fixed had none; text/index/disabled controls remained unchanged. Actual child imported-module paths/hashes were checked. Independent agent reviews found no blocking patch issue and audited saved HTTP evidence; they did not independently rerun the server.

The submission branch is based on `f8112704d54a15828c30496d49a73238be66f997`; the changed production and test files are unchanged between the tested base and that upstream SHA. Tests ran on the separately copied earlier source tree, not a whole-tree execution at the new SHA. All applicable pinned patch-scoped hooks were freshly rerun and passed, including mypy and CI test tethering:

```sh
pre-commit run --files vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py
```

These are supplied-token postprocessing/HTTP tests, not model generation, SSE, GPU inference or model evaluation. Native CPU inference is unavailable in this environment because loading its installed `vllm._C` raises SIGILL. No generation-quality or throughput claim is made.

## Details

The completion derender methods receive the original `CompletionRequest` but omit generated IDs when constructing both batch and stream choices. Resolve the opt-in flag before each loop and forward the original choice IDs, matching the existing chat behavior without changing detokenization.

Fresh open-PR searches for `61065 in:body`, `derender token_ids`, and `completion return_token_ids`, plus inspection of related changes, found no exact competing fix. #59510 handles stops, #60082 adds inline derender mode, #57990 preserves prompt logprobs; merged #60286 handles the separate Rust completions route. This patch is independent of request-body logging PR #62108 and changes different files.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, tests and review. The submitter additionally confirmed personally running related tests before requesting publication; the reported automated results above are from the agent-executed commands.
