items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] attention: Add opt-in table-gated CUDA verify for Frozen-KV MTP
items.author: riversky0014
items.summary: On CUDA, Frozen-KV MTP target verify on the Triton backend runs the generic, which reads the whole prefix serially for every few draft queries. The split-KV verify kernels already serve this case on gfx95, but are not enabled on NVIDIA.
items.body:
> **Depends on #44466 and #44468.** This branch includes their commits (the first two); review only the last commit. I will rebase once they merge.

## Motivation

On CUDA, Frozen-KV MTP target verify on the Triton backend runs the generic `extend_attention_fwd`, which reads the whole prefix serially for every few draft queries. The split-KV verify kernels (`verify_splitkv`, `verify_shared_kv`) already serve this case on gfx95, but are not enabled on NVIDIA. This PR lets them run on CUDA behind a default-off flag, only for shapes and GPU architectures whose tiles have been validated.

## Modifications

- New env var `SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_VERIFY_SPLITKV` (default `false`), documented in `environment_variables.mdx`.
- `TritonAttnBackend` routes a target-verify layer to the CUDA path only when all of these hold: the flag is on, Frozen-KV MTP target worker, `topk == 1`, causal, BF16 without KV scales, a dense head-dim tensor contract, and a validated tile for this layer's per-rank shape, query width and GPU capability. **No model name is checked.** Any other case keeps `extend_attention_fwd`. The GPU capability is resolved once at backend construction.
  - Full-attention layers with one local KV head → grouped-head `verify_shared_kv_fwd`.
  - Sliding-window layers → per-head `verify_splitkv_fwd`.
- Tile tables (`_CUDA_SHARED_KV_TILES` in `verify_mla.py`, `_CUDA_SPLITKV_TILES` in `verify_splitkv.py`) both gate eligibility and supply the launch parameters, so the two can't disagree. Current entries (SM89, SM90):
  - shared-KV: KV group 16, head_dim 512, padded width 1/2/4 → `(BLOCK_H, BLOCK_N, num_warps) = (16, 16, 8)`
  - split-KV: Q16 / KV8 / head_dim 256, width 1–5 → `(BLOCK_N, num_warps) = (32, 4)` (same as the existing head_dim-256 default)
- `verify_splitkv`: supports sliding windows as a per-query left bound in both the prefix and the draft-draft stage. `kv_indices` already address the retained SWA-pool tail, so absolute offsets cancel. Fully masked rows are guarded against `-inf - -inf`.
- `verify_mla` combine: an empty prefix returns the draft-only result.
- AMD behaviour is unchanged: the gfx95 paths still exclude sliding windows at the backend, and HIP never takes the CUDA tiles.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K on H20, `google/gemma-4-12B-it` BF16 TP1 with its matching assistant (NEXTN, steps 2, topk 1, 3 draft tokens). Fixed seeded 400-question subset, temperature 0, thinking disabled, max_tokens 2048, concurrency 128. All arms reach decode batch 128 with CUDA graphs.

| Arm | Correct / 400 | Accuracy | Truncated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No speculation | 382 | 95.50% | 2 |
| MTP, flag off | 383 | 95.75% | 0 |
| MTP, flag on | 384 | 96.00% | 0 |

Flag on vs flag off: 1 wrong→right, 0 right→wrong (exact McNemar p = 1.0). The one discordant item is formatting only: for gsm8k-test-0830 the reference is 1128 (minutes), and off answers "18 hours and 48 minutes" while on answers "1128 minutes". So this is no regression, not an improvement. Weighted acceptance length: 2.8075 off, 2.8062 on.

The split-KV paths reduce in a different order, so outputs are not bitwise-identical to the extend kernel (2/8 greedy smoke prompts identical).

Kernel tests, 55 passed / 0 skipped on both H20 (SM90) and RTX 4090D (SM89):
- `test_verify_shared_kv_cuda.py`, `test_verify_swa_cuda.py`: FP64 oracle, cancelling prefix values, strided QKV projection views, paged KV, CUDA graph replay with changed lengths (including empty ↔ non-empty prefixes)
- `test_verify_empty_prefix.py`, `test_verify_shared_kv.py`, `test_verify_splitkv.py`
- `test_triton_verify_metadata.py` (CPU): tile coverage, unvalidated architectures/shapes/widths, backend routing and fallback (flag off, KV scales, `score_mod`, cross-attention, non-verify mode, unsupported width, unsupported arch)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H20 96 GB, driver 580.82.07, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Server:

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path google/gemma-4-12B-it --attention-backend triton \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tp-size 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --max-running-requests 256 \
  --context-length 4352 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.28125 \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 8 32 64 128 256 \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-draft-model-path <gemma-4-12B-it assistant> \
  --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3
# A: SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_VERIFY_SPLITKV=0   B: SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_VERIFY_SPLITKV=1
```

With the flag off, CUDA runs exactly the upstream path, since the existing split-KV verify is gfx95-only.

**Kernel profile** (4 verify rounds per setting): off runs 48 `_fwd_kernel` calls per round. On runs 8 shared-KV and 40 split-KV layer pairs, with 0 `_fwd_kernel`. The median attention-kernel time per verify round drops from **5.452 ms → 1.754 ms**.

**End-to-end throughput** on fixed C4 inputs, 128 output tokens per request, radix cache flushed before each timed run. Three repetitions in order off/on, on/off, off/on. Every cell reaches the requested batch with CUDA graphs and zero retractions; max elapsed-time CV 0.26%. Throughput = output tokens / total batch time including prefill.

| Input | Batch | Off tok/s | On tok/s | Gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 256 | 1 | 137.10 | 177.41 | +29.4% |
| 256 | 8 | 698.28 | 874.75 | +25.3% |
| 256 | 128 | 1078.87 | 1481.70 | +37.3% |
| 4096 | 128 | 128.04 | 147.32 | +15.1% |

Decode-only view (same runs):

| Input / batch | Tokens per verify, off → on | Steady decode tok/s, off → on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 256 / 1 | 2.03 → 2.25 | 146.4 → 215.0 |
| 256 / 8 | 2.30 → 2.33 | 1107 → 1461 |
| 256 / 128 | 2.33 → 2.36 | 1872 → 3395 |
| 4096 / 128 | 2.28 → 2.29 | 720 → 2408 |

Outputs differ slightly between paths, so the end-to-end numbers include some acceptance variation. This is most visible at batch 1, where a single request's trajectory decides acceptance. The kernel profile above isolates the attention gain.

**Tile selection.** The SWA tile was swept on H20 and RTX 4090D: `BLOCK_N` {16, 32, 64, 128} × `num_warps` {4, 8} × `n_splits` {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} at width 3, window 1023, batch 1/8/128, context 256/1023. All 240 combinations pass the correctness check, and finalists were re-timed in forward and reverse order. The existing `(32, 4)` with the current split policy has the best geometric-mean latency on H20 (nearest alternative 3.8% slower overall). On 4090D the alternatives trade small gains for regressions, so the table keeps it. Other widths are correctness-validated but not performance-tuned.

**Scope.** Measured on a single H20, BF16, TP1. Shapes outside the tables (e.g. other TP sizes or models with different per-rank head layouts) fall back to the existing kernel; adding them needs new tile entries.

## Checklist

items.title: [Refactor] rust-server: name the literal arguments on the tokenize/detokenize paths
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Adds inline parameter-name comments to bare literals in Rust tokenize/detokenize call sites for readability; no behavior change.
items.body:
Stacked on #44767 (base branch `oss-sync-f54680cc5b`); it should merge after that one. The diff shown here is only this follow-up.

## Motivation

The `/v1/tokenize` and `/v1/detokenize` routes added in #44767, and their tests, pass several bare `true`/`false`/`None` arguments whose meaning is only visible in the callee, for example `detokenize(token_ids, true)` or `load_chat_formatter(None, None, None, Some("chatml"))`. A reader has to open the callee to know what each literal selects.

## Modifications

Each such literal now carries an inline comment naming the parameter or binding it fills (`true /* add_special_tokens */`), using the callee's real parameter or binding name:

- the `/v1/completions` echo decode: `detokenize(token_ids, true /* skip_special_tokens */)`;
- the chat-template branch of `/v1/tokenize`: `false /* add_special_tokens */`;
- the `(decode_logprob_text, no_stop_trim)` tuple for tokenize, detokenize and control requests in `register_detok`;
- the `registered` flag in `push_tokenize_to_pool`'s `fail` call;
- in tests: the `CoreHandle::tokenize`/`detokenize` calls, `decode_once`/`handle_decode`, the tokenizer worker's `run(text, add_special_tokens)` helper, `load_chat_formatter(None, None, None, Some("chatml"))`, and the `test_mm(_, true /* enabled */)` call.

Literals that are already named (struct fields, well-named locals, assert expectations) and code #44767 does not add are left as they are. In multi-line argument lists rustfmt places the comma before the comment (`true, /* skip_special_tokens */`) and rewrapped a few calls. Comments only; no behavior change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: comments only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: comments only.

## Test plan

- `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`: 338 passed, 0 failed (on top of #44767's head).

items.title: [Fix] qwen2_moe: Replicate the shared expert under DWDP
items.author: QNan0513
items.summary: Under DWDP (#29778), sparse MoE runs on DP-local tokens and is True, so skips the all-reduce after the experts. replicates its shared expert only for the a2a backends.
items.body:
## Motivation

Under DWDP (#29778), sparse MoE runs on DP-local tokens and `post_experts_output_is_complete()` is True, so `reduce_moe_output` skips the all-reduce after the experts. `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` replicates its shared expert only for the a2a backends. Under DWDP it stays TP-sharded with `reduce_results=False`, so each rank adds 1/TP of the shared expert's output for its own tokens, and nothing sums the shards.

Shared-expert fusion is wrong under DWDP too: DWDP prefetches only the routed experts, and the fused shared slot's routing weight is pre-scaled by 1/ep_size for the post-experts all-reduce that DWDP skips. Qwen3-Next enables this fusion on CUDA.

This affects every model built on `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` with a shared expert: Qwen1.5/Qwen2 MoE, Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 MoE and Qwen3.8 (`qwen4_exp`). Qwen3 MoE has no shared expert. #39802 fixes the same problem for DeepSeek-V2.

## Modifications

- `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock`, under DWDP:
  - The shared expert is built with `parallel_group="replicated"`, as for the a2a backends.
  - Shared-expert fusion is turned off with a warning, so the block falls back to the separate (now replicated) shared-expert MLP. The loaders read the decision from the built layer (`num_fused_shared_experts`), as for the existing per-rank-slot fallback.
- Test (CPU, fails before this change): `TestQwen2MoeSharedExpertUnderDwdp` in `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` builds the block on a DWDP layout and checks that the shared expert holds its full weights and stays out of the fused MoE. The same topology without DWDP keeps the TP shard and the fusion.

Cost: the shared expert's weights in full on every rank. At load, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B goes from 12.78 to 12.99 GB per rank and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next from 24.13 to 24.54 GB (its FP8 checkpoint keeps the shared experts in BF16).

## Accuracy Tests

Setup:
- One node, 8x H20. DWDP: `--tp-size 8 --dwdp-size 8 --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --load-balance-method total_tokens --mm-enable-dp-encoder` in the default `--disaggregation-mode null`, no speculative decoding.
- The non-DWDP baseline is plain TP8. Qwen3.8 adds `--ep-size 8`: its FP8 128x128 blocks cannot split the 640-wide experts 8 ways.
- GSM8K: chat API, 5-shot, thinking disabled, 200 questions.
- Image: nightly 2026-10-14 (684fea8a). Its `qwen2_moe.py` is byte-identical to `main` a038a0d, and the fixed arm mounts this PR's file.
- Qwen3.8 also runs with its cookbook GDN flags and, under DWDP, `SGLANG_USE_ATTN_TP_NGRAM=1` (as in #44763).

| Model | Shared expert | TP8 | DWDP8, main | DWDP8, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (BF16) | separate MLP | 0.975 | 0.170 | 0.975 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (FP8) | separate MLP | 0.975 | 0.915 | 0.985 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (BF16) | fused on CUDA | 0.965 | fails at startup | 0.970 |

- On `main`, Qwen3-Next fails in DWDP setup with `cuMemcpyDtoD: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` in `_copy_local_weights_to_handles`: each rank's expert tensors carry the fused shared slot on top of the routed shard that DWDP sized its handles for. With this PR every rank logs the fusion-off warning and the model serves.
- The separate-MLP models run on `main` but lose accuracy, more for Qwen3.5 than for Qwen3.8.

No speed numbers: this is a correctness fix, and DWDP's prefill throughput is covered in #29778 and #44763.

Related: #22084 tracks DWDP. #39802 (open) fixes the same shared-expert sharding for DeepSeek-V2. The Qwen3.8 runs in #44763 (DWDP + MTP) mounted this fix.

cc @yhyang201

Ran ruff 0.15.1 (check + format), isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` and `check_registered_tests.py` on the changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The full `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` passes.

items.title: [Perf][Attention] 16-byte-align per-token-head KV slots so Triton vectorizes loads
items.author: noon-at-cgn
items.summary: Pads int8/fp8 per-token-head KV cache slots to 16-byte alignment, enabling Triton vectorized loads and achieving up to 1.96× kernel speedup with minimal memory overhead.
items.body:
## Overview

TRITON_ATTN packs int8/fp8 per-token-head KV as `[K | k_scale | V | v_scale]`. The slot stride (520 B at head_size 256, 264 B at 128) and the V offset (+260/+132 B) are not multiples of 16, so `kernel_unified_attention` loads K/V one byte at a time. This PR pads each K/V half to 16 bytes. Related: #56081, #56164, #61925.

AI assistance was used: an AI coding agent wrote the code and tests under my direction, drafted this description, and automated the test and benchmark runs; I chose the approach and reviewed every changed line and the results.

## Claims

- `ld.global.b8` K/V loads: 64 → 0 (sm_86 PTX).
- `int8_per_token_head` kernel time, RTX 3080: 1.56–1.83× faster for decode at 8k–128k, 1.25–1.50× for 8-token verify and 1.65–1.96× for an 8k prefill chunk at 32k–128k; every int8 cell measured is ≥ 1.25× faster.
- End to end (TP=2, 27B hybrid, MTP): 128k TTFT −21 %, 128k decode pass 62.1 → 48.0 ms.
- Memory: +4.6 / +9.1 / +17.6 % at head_size 256 / 128 / 64 (KV pool −4.3 % in the run below). INT4 unchanged.
- Kernel outputs bit-identical to main; writer and kernels unchanged.

## Validation

**Test plan** (nightly image with this PR's files mounted):

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_unpadded_page_size_includes_per_token_head_scales
pytest -v tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k splitk
pytest -v tests/models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k int8
```

**Test result** (passed/failed/skipped):

| suite | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_kv_cache_utils.py` (per-token-head) | 1/0/0 | 4/0/0 |
| `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` | 59/23/0 | 67/21/6 |
| `test_triton_unified_attention.py -k splitk` | 25/5/0 | 25/5/0 |
| `models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k int8`, public mirror model | 1/0/0 | 1/0/0 |

*RTX 3080 (sm_86), 220 W cap, image `8c1434bf…5035e`, vLLM `g49cb2bbf7`, Triton 3.8.0.*

All failures are fp8 cases that also fail on main (no `fp8e4nv` on sm_86); the 6 skips are fp8 cases of the extended test, whose 12 int8/int4 cases pass. The model-level test ran with `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, as we cannot access the gated meta-llama model.

Intel CI (build 14433): Quantization jobs passed; the one failing job, Benchmarks CLI (test_bench_forward: Event.__new__() got an unexpected keyword argument external), does not touch this change.

**Kernel benchmark** (`benchmarks/attention_benchmarks` with #62112, cache populated; `TRITON_ATTN`, 8 layers, block 16, CUDA graphs; per layer, median (IQR) of 5 processes, arms alternated). bf16 is main's `auto` cache; this PR does not change it (0.998–1.008× in all 12 bf16 cells).

| Hq/Hkv/D | cell | bf16 | int8 main | int8 this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12/2/256 | q1s8k | 48.8 µs | 103.9 (0.1) µs | 60.3 (0.2) µs | 1.72× |
| | q1s32k | 171.4 µs | 393.3 (18.3) µs | 215.2 (6.4) µs | 1.83× |
| | q1s128k | 667.5 µs | 1424.4 (0.6) µs | 781.2 (0.3) µs | 1.82× |
| | q8s128k | 1155.0 µs | 1772.7 (2.3) µs | 1413.7 (7.9) µs | 1.25× |
| | q8ks32k | 186.7 ms | 283.6 (0.2) ms | 144.4 (0.3) ms | 1.96× |
| | q8ks128k | 855.7 ms | 1265.5 (0.7) ms | 673.2 (3.9) ms | 1.88× |
| 32/8/128 | q1s8k | 58.4 µs | 87.2 (1.1) µs | 55.7 (0.1) µs | 1.57× |
| | q1s32k | 205.8 µs | 338.3 (1.9) µs | 216.9 (1.3) µs | 1.56× |
| | q1s128k | 814.4 µs | 1364.4 (1.0) µs | 860.2 (1.7) µs | 1.59× |
| | q8s128k | 1240.8 µs | 2023.9 (3.8) µs | 1347.4 (4.2) µs | 1.50× |
| | q8ks32k | 200.6 ms | 301.8 (0.5) ms | 166.2 (0.1) ms | 1.82× |
| | q8ks128k | 903.2 ms | 1346.0 (1.6) ms | 817.7 (1.1) ms | 1.65× |

*RTX 3080 (sm_86, 68 SMs), 220 W cap, image `8c1434bf…5035e`, vLLM `g49cb2bbf7`, Triton 3.8.0.*

**To reproduce the kernel numbers.** They need the benchmark-tool change in #62112 (int8_per_token_head support, and filling the KV cache before timing); main's tool cannot time this cache. Check out that branch, put this PR's `triton_attn.py` on top, and run:

```bash
cd benchmarks/attention_benchmarks
python benchmark.py --backends TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype {auto,int8_per_token_head} \
  --num-layers 8 --block-size 16 --head-dim {256,128} --num-q-heads {12,32} --num-kv-heads {2,8} \
  --batch-specs q1s8k q1s32k q1s128k q8s128k q8ks32k q8ks128k
```

The end-to-end numbers below need no tool change: stock `vllm serve` with the launch line given there.

#61925's single-query rule on top (not in this PR) adds up to 2.7× for kernel-level decode (12/2/256 q1s32k 220.9 → 83.3 µs, cache populated) but only ~2 % end to end below (48.0 → 47.1 ms per 128k pass): MTP verify steps have 4 query tokens, which that rule leaves at 16 segments.

**End to end.** 27B hybrid Qwen3.5-family model, W4A16 AutoRound, MTP k=3 (checkpoint `Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-MTP-W4A16-AutoRound`). Medians; 32k prompts hit ~7k cached prefix tokens in both arms. Launch line, identical in both arms (this PR's `triton_attn.py` was the only difference):

```bash
NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 vllm serve <checkpoint> --tensor-parallel-size 2 --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --long-prefill-token-threshold 1024 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":32,"custom_ops":["+rms_norm","+silu_and_mul"]}'
```

| metric | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT 8k / 32k / 128k (s) | 6.03 / 25.99 / 250.38 | 5.73 / 22.79 / 198.90 | 0.95 / 0.88 / 0.79 |
| N=1 decode 8k / 32k / 128k (tok/s) | 97.0 / 76.7 / 43.7 | 99.8 / 89.7 / 57.4 | 1.03 / 1.17 / 1.31 |
| N=1 ms per forward pass 8k / 32k / 128k | 29.9 / 36.1 / 62.1 | 29.0 / 33.2 / 48.0 | 0.97 / 0.92 / 0.77 |
| two concurrent 128k prompts: pair TTFT (s) / per-stream decode (tok/s) | 482.0 / 23.5 | 368.6 / 28.8 | 0.76 / 1.22 |
| MTP tokens per step, N=1 128k | 2.730 | 2.779 | |
| GSM8K n=200 accuracy | 0.96 | 0.97 | |
| 128k needle, depth 0.5 and 0.9 | retrieved | retrieved | |
| KV pool (tokens) / attention block size | 418,496 / 816 | 400,705 / 784 | 0.957 |

*2× RTX 3080 20 GB (sm_86), 220 W cap, TP=2, `--max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 2 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94`, prefix caching, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-x86_64@sha256:8c1434bfee7d7626eef78ef70600434ffba4a1b8813cb1d1c8707ad25f47035e`, vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7` (attention files = `fa75d3456d`), Triton 3.8.0.*

**Numerics.** With a populated cache, int8 K/V bytes, scales and prefill / decode / 4-token-verify outputs are bit-identical to main (12/2/256, 32/8/128; kernel probe on one RTX 3080, same image). Model logprobs (30,617-token document) differ from main by 0.0224 nats mean abs (99.9 % top-1 agreement) only because the hybrid model's attention block size follows the page size (816 → 784); with `--block-size 816` they are bit-identical. Against a bf16-KV reference: main 0.02181, this PR 0.02198 nats, paired +0.00017 (95 % CI −0.00032 to +0.00068), non-inferior.

## Details

**Root cause.** Triton 3.8.0 marks an argument 16-divisible only if `arg % 16 == 0` / `data_ptr() % 16 == 0` (`triton/backends/compiler.py:75-92`). Offline compile of `kernel_unified_attention` (3D, D=256, GQA 6, TILE 16, 4 warps):

| layout | slot stride | V offset | `ld.global.v4.b32` | `ld.global.b32` | `ld.global.b8` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 KV | 512 B | – | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| int8 per-token-head, main | 520 B | 260 B | 4 | 24 | 64 |
| int8 per-token-head, this PR | 544 B | 272 B | 4 | 4 | 0 |

*sm_86 compile, image `8c1434bf…5035e`, Triton 3.8.0; the RTX 3080 benchmark runs JIT-compiled the same counts.*

The kernel test missed this (separate aligned K/V tensors, 2D path only). It now reads the packed cache, runs `seq_threshold_3D` ∈ {0, 8} with a q=4 batch, and asserts split-K ran.

**Change.** `customize_spec` sizes each INT8/FP8 half as `round_up(head_size * dtype_size + 4, 16)`; `_ensure_scale_caches` takes `head_size` from the layer. Scale placement and the `content // 2` split are unchanged.

| head_size | bytes per token and KV head | change | vs bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 136 → 160 | +17.6 % | 0.53 → 0.63 |
| 128 | 264 → 288 | +9.1 % | 0.52 → 0.56 |
| 256 | 520 → 544 | +4.6 % | 0.51 → 0.53 |

*Computed by `customize_spec`; the RTX 3080 runs above (image `8c1434bf…5035e`, Triton 3.8.0) saw 544/288 B strides.*

**Alternative: one pad.** `[K | V | k_scale | v_scale | pad]` (528/272/144 B, +1.5/+3.0/+5.9 %) also removes every byte load and passes the same tests. Cache populated (n=5 processes per arm): 8k prefill chunks at head_size 256 take 9–17 % less time with this PR (q8ks32k/q8ks128k at 12/2, 24/4); decode and verify match within ±3 % except 32/8/128 q1s8k (this PR −7 %). Hence two pads; one pad is ready if reviewers prefer a smaller cache.

**Related.**
- #56081: same misalignment in a gather-based sparse kernel (sm_121) needing 128-byte alignment or side tensors; not fixed here.
- #56164 is not a duplicate: it opts out of inline scales, this PR pads them. They conflict in `customize_spec` and `_ensure_scale_caches` but compose (its early return stays first).
- Inline packing from #36893 (closed PR) / #38378 (merged PR) is kept.

**Layout change.** Persisted offload stores and prefill/decode pairs on different versions are invalid across this PR. On hybrid models the attention block size follows the page size (816 → 784 above).

**Limits.**
- Measured only on RTX 3080 (sm_86, power-capped); A100, L4 and H100 not measured; PTX compiled only for sm_86.
- fp8 per-token-head shares the layout code but cannot run on sm_86; not timed.

**CI.** No sm_86 runner. `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` runs in the H200 Quantization step (`.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml:5`), attention kernel tests on L4 (`kernels.yaml:315`).

**Duplicate search** (2026-10-16):

```bash
gh issue view 56081 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "56081 in:body"               # #56164
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "int8_per_token_head"          # no layout PR
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "inline scales customize_spec" # #56164
```

items.title: [Benchmark][Attention] Support int8_per_token_head KV cache in attention_benchmarks
items.author: noon-at-cgn
items.summary: Adds int8_per_token_head KV cache support to attention benchmarks, fixing cache allocation, per-layer scale binding, and proper KV write-before-timing.
items.body:
## Overview

`benchmarks/attention_benchmarks` cannot currently time attention on an `int8_per_token_head` KV cache. `--kv-cache-dtype` accepts only `auto` and `fp8`. Also, `_create_kv_cache` builds the spec without `kv_quant_mode`, so `TritonAttentionBackend.customize_spec` adds no inline scales. Also, the runner never writes the KV cache, so every kernel is timed over an all-zero cache. This PR allocates the cache the way the attention layer does, writes it before timing, gives each layer its own impl, rejects the dtype on backends that cannot read it, and adds a config.

AI assistance was used: an AI coding agent wrote the code and tests under my direction, drafted this description, and automated the test and benchmark runs; I chose the approach and reviewed every changed line and the results.

The kernel numbers in #62113 (16-byte-aligned per-token-head KV slots) were measured with this tool change and can be reproduced with it.

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head` allocates the packed `[K | k_scale | V | v_scale]` cache through the backend's `customize_spec`, so `TRITON_ATTN` runs on the layout it serves.
- Each layer gets its own impl, as in a model. `TritonAttentionImpl` binds its scale views to the first cache it sees, so with a shared impl every layer read layer 0's scales.
- Before timing, the runner writes random K/V for every cached token through `impl.do_kv_cache_update`, the path the attention layer uses. Until now it called only `forward`, which for `TRITON_ATTN`, `FLASH_ATTN` and `FLASHINFER` does not write the cache (`forward_includes_kv_cache_update = False`), so all of them were timed over zeros. Backends whose `forward` writes the cache are left as they were.
- New `configs/int8_per_token_head.yaml` (decode, 4-token verify, prefill; head_dim 128 and 256).
- `--kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head` on a backend whose `supports_kv_cache_dtype` rejects it (only `TRITON_ATTN` lists it) or on any MLA backend raises an error instead of timing a different cache.
- `auto` and `fp8` allocations are unchanged.

## Validation

**Why it is needed.** On main, `int8_per_token_head` is slower than the bf16 cache in all 12 cells we measured, at 1.48–2.29× the bf16 time, although it reads about half the bytes. This tool change is what made that measurable. Per layer, median (IQR) of 5 processes, cache populated by this PR:

| Hq/Hkv/D | cell | bf16 (`auto`) | int8_per_token_head | int8 / bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12/2/256 | q1s8k | 48.8 (0.0) µs | 103.9 (0.1) µs | 2.13 |
| | q1s128k | 667.5 (1.0) µs | 1424.4 (0.6) µs | 2.13 |
| | q8s128k | 1155.0 (3.4) µs | 1772.7 (2.3) µs | 1.53 |
| | q8ks128k | 855.7 (0.9) ms | 1265.5 (0.7) ms | 1.48 |
| 32/8/128 | q1s8k | 58.4 (0.2) µs | 87.2 (1.1) µs | 1.49 |
| | q1s128k | 814.4 (1.2) µs | 1364.4 (1.0) µs | 1.68 |
| | q8s128k | 1240.8 (3.6) µs | 2023.9 (3.8) µs | 1.63 |
| | q8ks128k | 903.2 (1.7) ms | 1346.0 (1.6) ms | 1.49 |

*RTX 3080 (sm_86), 220 W cap, image `8c1434bf…5035e`, vLLM `g49cb2bbf7` (attention files = `fa75d3456d`), Triton 3.8.0, this branch's `benchmarks/` mounted read-only.*

Equivalent command (5 processes per arm; each ran both head configs and both dtypes through the tool's `run_benchmark`):

```bash
cd benchmarks/attention_benchmarks
python benchmark.py --backends TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype {auto,int8_per_token_head} \
  --num-layers 8 --block-size 16 --head-dim {256,128} --num-q-heads {12,32} --num-kv-heads {2,8} \
  --batch-specs q1s8k q1s32k q1s128k q8s128k q8ks32k q8ks128k
```

**Cache fill on GPU.** After the fill, 99.0 % (12/2/256) and 99.1 % (32/8/128) of the int8 K/V bytes are non-zero (the rest are quantized zeros), the scales are real (0.013–0.046, none equal to the zero-cache value 1.0), the bf16 cache is 100 % non-zero, and the attention output is finite and non-zero in every probed case. Without the fill, the same probe gave an all-zero output.

The fill changes the numbers. Compared with earlier runs over a zero cache (same image, tool without the last commit), prefill/extend kernels take 8–24 % longer for int8 and 17–37 % longer for bf16. For the per-token-head slot alignment change we measured with this tool, the int8 speedup on those cells dropped by 0.10–0.21× (e.g. 2.09× → 1.88×); on decode cells it moved by at most 0.10×.

**Checks.**
- `pre-commit run --from-ref f8112704d5 --to-ref HEAD` passes on all 6 changed files. In the nightly image with no GPU visible, `python benchmark.py --help` works, `runner` and `mla_runner` import, and the guard rejects `int8_per_token_head` for `FLASH_ATTN`, `FLASHINFER`, `TRITON_MLA`, `FLASHMLA` and `FLASHINFER_MLA` while `TRITON_ATTN` passes it.
**GPU checks** (RTX 3080 20GB, sm_86, nightly image `sha256:8c1434bf…`, branch head):
- `benchmark.py --config configs/int8_per_token_head.yaml`: all 18 cells ran in one process with finite times, for int8 and with `kv_cache_dtype: auto`. Without a wait after the cache fill, cell 13 (`2q4s128k`) hit an illegal memory access, because `do_bench_cudagraph` times on a side stream; the fill now ends with a device sync.
- Cache fill on FLASH_ATTN, FLASHINFER and TRITON_ATTN (bf16 and int8), 12/2/256 and 32/8/128, q1s8k/q1s32k/q8ks32k: cache non-zero (bf16 100 %, int8 99 %), output finite and non-zero.
- `--kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head` on FLASH_ATTN / FLASHINFER, and `fp8` on TRITON_ATTN (sm_86), print a per-cell error instead of timing a different cache.
- All 10 runs completed without errors.
- The kernel received the packed cache: 520-byte slots at D=256 and 264-byte slots at D=128, with the V pointer at `% 16 = 4`.
- A `torch.profiler` run confirmed that q8s128k takes the 3D split-K path (`reduce_segments` launched) and q8ks128k the 2D path.

## Details

- `runner.py` maps the dtype with `STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE` and passes `kv_quant_mode=get_kv_quant_mode(kv_cache_dtype)`, as `Attention.get_kv_cache_spec` does. For `fp8` the spec now carries `FP8_PER_TENSOR`, which no backend's `customize_spec` acts on.
- Only `int8_per_token_head` is added to the CLI choices, because it is the mode validated here.
- Cache fill: request `i` owns blocks `[i * max_blocks_per_request, ...)` of the benchmark's block table, so its `kv_len` tokens map to slots `i * max_blocks_per_request * block_size + arange(kv_len)`. One random K/V pair per request is written into every layer's cache; the transient tensors are one request's K/V. The fill ends with a device sync, because `do_bench_cudagraph` times on a side stream that does not wait for the default stream.
- Known tool limits, not changed by this PR:
  - The tool hard-codes the `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` config, which is a gated repo; our runs used a local stand-in config. The `auto` cache and q/k/v take that config's dtype (bf16 here); `BenchmarkConfig.dtype` is not used for them.
  - The metadata builder is built without a speculative config, so split-K scratch is sized for one query token.
  - The tool exports only mean and std, so the medians above are taken across processes.
- No unit test: `attention_benchmarks` has no test suite.
- Measured only on RTX 3080 (sm_86); other GPUs were not run.

**Duplicate search** (2026-10-16):

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "attention_benchmarks kv-cache-dtype"    # #59774
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "attention_benchmarks do_kv_cache_update" # none
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "attention_benchmarks per_token_head"    # none
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "int8_per_token_head"                    # none touch benchmarks/
gh pr diff 59774 --repo vllm-project/vllm   # runner.py: same spec change inside a ROCm backend PR
```

Draft #59774 (ROCm Octave KV backend, 27 files) includes an equivalent spec change in `runner.py`: it passes `kv_quant_mode` and opens `--kv-cache-dtype` to every cache dtype. It does not write the cache, give each layer its own impl, or add the config. This PR is the small, standalone version. If #59774 lands first, this PR reduces to the cache fill, the per-layer impl and the config.

items.title: [None][feat] Staircase: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 low-latency decode target for Rubin (modeling_v2, TP16)
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Adds a modelingv2 (Staircase) target for GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on Rubin (sm107) at TP16: tensor-parallel attention and experts over 16 ranks, no attention DP, no expert parallelism, with one-model MTP-Eagle (any draft length) or no speculative decoding. It is the gene…
items.body:
## Description

Adds a modeling_v2 (Staircase) target for **GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on Rubin (sm_107)** at **TP16**: tensor-parallel attention
and experts over 16 ranks, no attention DP, no expert parallelism, with one-model MTP-Eagle (any draft length) or no
speculative decoding. It is the generation server of a disaggregated low-latency deployment (one DEP4 context server on
the built-in implementation, one TP16 generation server on this target, `modeling_v2: require`).

**Routing.** `models/glm_moe_dsa/routing.py` claims `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` only for compute capability (10, 7), the
GLM-5.2 shape (78 layers, hidden 6144, 256 routed experts, q_lora_rank 2048), the TP16 mapping above and MTP-Eagle /
no speculation. Every other deployment gets `NoTarget` and stays on `modeling_deepseekv3`.

**Target** (`models/glm_moe_dsa/glm_5_2_nvfp4__sm_107__tp16/`). The modules and weights are the built-in GLM-5.2 ones,
loaded by the built-in loader, so the KV and indexer-K caches keep the layout the context server writes.
`PrefillTarget` runs the built-in modules. `DecodeTarget` runs a one-request generation step (verify rows <= 8) on
GLM-owned kernels:

- **Attention:** fused-A GEMM with the indexer's rows, q_b with FP8 RoPE in the epilogue, the KV half written straight
  into the cache, a sparse-MLA flash decode that maps the selection to cache rows itself, and o_proj publishing its
  shard for the next hop. On indexer layers q_b runs on a side stream beside the top-k; on layers that reuse a
  selection the KV half is written at entry and flash decode gathers early.
- **DSA indexer:** key-sharded over the 16 ranks: K tail on a side stream, FP8 paged MQA logits on the rank's key
  shard, and an exact histogram top-k merged across ranks.
- **Communication:** MNNVL Lamport hops for post-attention, post-MLP and MoE-finalize, with the residual add and
  RMSNorm fused in; an all-gather for the verify logits.
- **MLP / MoE:** small-M dense MLP; MoE through the TRTLLM-Gen runner with a fused router, quantize late join and FC2
  at K=128; router GEMV; split-K shared expert.
- **Verify logits:** a split-K LM head over the vocabulary shard.
- **MTP draft loop:** a target-owned `MTPDraftWorker` (an `MTPEagleWorker` subclass). For a generation step of one
  request with greedy drafting at the configured draft length, it runs the draft steps on the same kernels: a
  token-table eh_proj, a reused top-k selection after step 0, a low-M BF16 MoE for the MTP layer, and fused
  sample/glue kernels for the argmax exchange and the next step's inputs. The draft steps reuse the step's DSA
  metadata instead of rebuilding it, and the verify step's acceptance (strict count or the forced count) is one
  kernel. Every other step runs the built-in loop.

Larger batches and anything the fast path does not cover fall back to the built-in modules inside the same target.

**Kernels.** GLM-only CUDA kernels are in `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/glmMoeDsa/`, exposed as `torch.ops.trtllm.glm_*`
(`cpp/tensorrt_llm/thop/glm*Op.cpp`). CuTe DSL kernels live in the target's `ops/`. Each op is a catalog `OpWrapper`
with certified cells and a GPU test.

**Shared code changes** (general, not sm-gated):

- `3rdparty`: a DeepGEMM patch so DeepJIT builds for the 10.0 family target on 10.x devices past 10.3. The bundled
  CUTLASS enables TMA and tcgen05 only for targets it knows; without this the context server's warm-up hits a device
  assert on Rubin.
- `fmhaKernels.h`: the token-sparse MLA generation kernels pad the Q tile to 8 rows, as the dense MLA selection does.
  With fewer than 8 heads per rank (64 MLA heads over 16 ranks) the SmemTile check fails at warm-up.
- `modeling_deepseekv3.py`: with the fused post-MLP all-reduce, the dense MLP keeps the full TP instead of capping it at
  GPUs per node. The fused all-reduce sums over the whole TP group, so the capped MLP counted each partial sum
  tp / mlp_tp times.
- TRTLLM-Gen MoE runner: opt-in fused router, quantize late join, a K=128 FC2 kernel and a routed-experts entry. All are
  default off for existing callers.
- modeling_v2: `Arch.SM_107`, the `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` router entry, a GLM cell for the FP4 quantize entry, and fake
  registrations for the new ops.

Per-step work around the decode graph of an overlap-scheduler speculative step (general; the step is GPU-bound, so
every eager op between two graph replays adds to it):

- `DecoderRunner._preprocess_inputs` refreshes the KV-length metadata once per step under the overlap correction.
- DSA metadata, one-model linear speculative decoding: `prepare()` leaves the decode outputs the graph head rebuilds
  in `on_update_kv_lens` (generation indptrs, `req_idx_per_token`, slot mappings, the DeepGEMM schedules, the dense
  top-k) to the graph, and clamps only the graph-padding rows of the INDEX_KEY table.
- Step staging: `host_staging.copy_if_changed()` skips an upload whose destination still holds the same payload
  (previous-batch slots and positions, gather ids, Eagle3 batch indices, sampler store slots); the unread
  `num_accepted_draft_tokens` upload is removed; the overlap offset buffers are zeroed only outside the rows the step
  rewrites.
- KV cache manager V2: `copy_batch_block_offsets` honors `max_blocks` (the copy kernel and its binding take a column
  bound). Under linear speculative decoding the attention metadata bounds the copy by the batch's maximum KV length
  plus two verification windows, the most the overlap correction and the draft steps can add on the device. The DSA
  INDEX_KEY offsets and block table upload only when they change.
- `SpecMetadata` uploads the per-request Philox state only with rejection sampling, its only reader.

## Performance

Disaggregated c1 (1 ctx DEP4 + 1 gen TP16, 20 Rubin GPUs), MTP K=7 with forced acceptance 2.91 tokens/step;
x = 1000 / p90 inter-token latency (tokens/s/user). The generation server sets
`sparse_attention_config.use_cute_dsl_paged_mqa_logits: false`: the target scores keys with its own kernels, and the
CuTe DSL setting only adds metadata work for the built-in indexer.

| Build | x (tok/s/user) | p50 / p90 ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 886.4 | 1.098 / 1.128 |

Without this PR, main does not run this deployment on Rubin: the context server dies in the DeepGEMM warm-up, and the
built-in TP16 generation server fails the sparse-MLA SmemTile check.

## Accuracy

GSM8K (1,319 questions) on the same disaggregated deployment with real acceptance: strict-match 0.9697,
flexible-extract 0.9712 (threshold 0.9). Measured acceptance length 5.52 tokens/step at K=7.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/modeling_v2/models/glm_moe_dsa/glm_5_2_nvfp4__sm_107__tp16/`: one GPU test per op entry over
  its certified cells, plus 4-rank matrices for the collective ops. sm_107 only; the files skip at module level
  elsewhere.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/modeling_v2/test_modeling_v2_routing.py`: GLM routing, including near misses (other shape,
  ADP, ep16, tp8, vanilla MTP, NGram, sm_103). CPU.
- `test_modeling_v2_claims.py`, `test_modeling_v2_no_stale_claims.py`, `test_modeling_v2_target_contract.py`,
  `thop/parallel_hw_agnostic/test_custom_ops.py` (fake registrations).
- No CI test list covers Rubin yet, so the GPU tests are local developer tests. Locally on sm_107 (4 GPUs), the list
  above passes in full: 382 passed.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix multi-layer MTP module selection for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next
items.author: spandantiwari
items.summary: Fixes multi-layer MTP speculative decoding to route each draft step to its own MTP module instead of always using module 0, restoring expected draft acceptance rates.
items.body:
## Overview

Multi-layer MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next silently uses only MTP module 0 for every draft step, instead of the distinct module trained for each step. This PR threads `spec_step_idx` through the drafter forward and fixes the multi-module routing so each draft step uses its own MTP module.

## Claims

- **Bug fix:** multi-layer MTP for Qwen3.5 (`Qwen3_5MTP` / `Qwen3_5MoeMTP`) and Qwen3-Next (`Qwen3NextMTP`) now selects `self.layers[spec_step_idx % num_mtp_layers]` per step instead of always module 0.
- **No output-correctness impact:** speculative decoding is lossless (the target verifies every drafted token). The bug only lowers the draft acceptance rate, and hence it directly affects **spec decoding speedup**, for multi-layer MTP checkpoints.
- **Latent today, future-proofing:** all currently published Qwen3.5 checkpoints ship `mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1`, so behavior is unchanged today; the fix activates correctly the moment a multi-layer MTP checkpoint ships.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (`tests/test_config.py`, no model weights — committed CI coverage):
- `use_multi_module_mtp()` detects `mtp_num_hidden_layers` both top-level and under a nested `text_config` (the multimodal Qwen3.5 layout).
- Outer `forward` threads `spec_step_idx` into the inner predictor (parametrized over Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next).
- Inner predictor selects a distinct module per draft step (`spec_step_idx % num_mtp_layers`): steps 0..3 → modules `[0, 1, 0, 1]`.

**Manual end-to-end** on ROCm (MI300-class GPU, `num_speculative_tokens=2`, `enforce_eager`). No public Qwen MTP checkpoint ships >1 MTP layer, so I built a synthetic 2-layer checkpoint from the real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B` by duplicating module 0 → module 1 (with a small perturbation so the modules differ), and compared the speculator actually selected before vs. after the fix on the **same** checkpoint:

| Checkpoint | Code | Speculator selected | mean accept len |
|---|---|---|---|
| synthetic 2-layer | before | `MTPSpeculator` (single-module) | 2.530 |
| synthetic 2-layer | after | `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` | 2.543 |
| real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B` (1-layer) | before | `MTPSpeculator` | 2.515 |
| real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B` (1-layer) | after | `MTPSpeculator` | 2.557 |

The decisive signal is the **speculator class**: before the fix a 2-layer checkpoint silently falls back to the single-module speculator (reusing module 0 every step); after, it routes to `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` and engages module 1 on step 2. Acceptance numbers are close only because the synthetic module 1 is a near-copy of module 0; a genuinely-trained module 1 would diverge. On the real 1-layer checkpoint the fix is a no-op (2.515 → 2.557 is within run-to-run noise), confirming no regression. The synthetic checkpoint is a multi-GB derived artifact, so it is not committed.

## Details

Three issues combined:

1. **Dropped `spec_step_idx`:** the outer `Qwen3_5MTP.forward` / `Qwen3NextMTP.forward` did not pass `spec_step_idx` to the inner multi-token predictor, so the per-step module selection always resolved to module 0.
2. **Routing field name:** `SpeculativeConfig.use_multi_module_mtp()` only recognized DeepSeek-style `num_nextn_predict_layers`. Qwen3.5 declares its module count via `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, so multi-layer Qwen3.5 MTP never routed to `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` (the only speculator that varies `spec_step_idx`).
3. **Nested `text_config`:** on multimodal Qwen3.5 configs `mtp_num_hidden_layers` lives under the nested `text_config`, so the routing check falls back to `get_hf_text_config()`.

All three are required for multi-layer MTP to behave correctly.

items.title: [Fix] unified-memory: Bound joint reclaim and preserve cached prefixes
items.author: ch-wan
items.summary: Joint FULL/SWA allocations can evict more cached prefixes than needed. FULL/SWA/Mamba allocations can fail despite recoverable capacity, or discard the entire cache before rejecting an impossible demand.
items.body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44826
* __->__ #44827

CI is run only on the top PR, #44826, which contains both changes.

## Motivation

Joint FULL/SWA allocations can evict more cached prefixes than needed. FULL/SWA/Mamba allocations can fail despite recoverable capacity, or discard the entire cache before rejecting an impossible demand.

This continues #39294, preserving Seokwoo Song's original commits, rebased onto `b62a48ee15b94ba428660ca7e021d44946b0802d`.

## Modifications

- Stop allocation-driven eviction at a read-only sufficient-reclaim predicate; prepare and verify the physical layout at bounded phase boundaries.
- Reject demands proven impossible by byte or ID bounds before eviction, and bound token/state reclaim quotas.
- Compute exact unsharded paged-extend demand for the unified SWA allocators while preserving conservative demand elsewhere.
- Adapt the closed-move-gate regression to the current physical-page copy interface. Preserve main's SWA-preferred reclaim planning for storage-backed HiCache and decode disaggregation.

## Accuracy Tests

Fresh validation of this rebased change:

- H200 host, Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130: **220 tests / 1,050 subtests passed** across 14 allocator/cache files using Python TreeCore. These are CPU allocator tests.
- Freshly built current-main Rust TreeCore on the H200 host: **38 tests / 155 subtests passed** in the focused reclaim suite; session cases use the supported Python fallback. A separate probe asserted that the ordinary cache selected `RustUnifiedTreeCore`.
- With the compaction fix from #44097 applied in a separate combined snapshot on B300, Torch 2.14.1+cu130: **61 tests / 201 subtests passed**, including the CUDA compaction cases.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Controlled real-allocator comparisons against unchanged main production code, with the same test fixtures, reproduced these results in both eager and lazy modes:

| Case | Main | This change |
|---|---|---|
| FULL/SWA, 6-token demand | Succeeds; evicts 5 cached tokens | Succeeds; evicts 3 |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 4-token demand | Fails | Succeeds; evicts 1 cached token |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 200-token impossible demand | Fails; evicts all 96 cached tokens | Fails; preserves all 96 |

The selected regression cases fail on main and pass on the candidate. Review checked quota semantics, deferred frees, page rounding, locked prefixes, changing move gates, pending reuse, and the compatibility of the rebase.

The FLOAT geometry predicates are sufficient certificates, not a complete feasibility solver. No fresh model-serving, full HiCache, or multi-GPU result is claimed. Historical serving evidence remains in #39294 and is not represented as validation of this head.

The controlled allocator comparisons above validate cache preservation and successful recovery, not serving throughput. No new serving-speed claim.

items.title: [Fix] unified-memory: Avoid gather scratch during Mamba and Conv compaction
items.author: ch-wan
items.summary: Unified Mamba/Conv compaction uses a gathered state tensor when relocating slots, which can OOM precisely when the allocator is reclaiming memory. This continues #44097, preserving Seokwoo Song's original commits, stacked on #44827, whose base is main.
items.body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #44826
* #44827

CI is run only on the top PR, #44826, which contains both changes.

## Motivation

Unified Mamba/Conv compaction uses a gathered state tensor when relocating slots, which can OOM precisely when the allocator is reclaiming memory.

This continues #44097, preserving Seokwoo Song's original commits, stacked on #44827, whose base is main `b62a48ee15b94ba428660ca7e021d44946b0802d`.

## Modifications

- Copy disjoint physical state envelopes directly with the existing `copy_pages` kernel, removing the main-state gather temporary.
- Preserve main's `move_physical_pages` entry point, which calls the optimized move implementation.
- Retain sibling-state copying and ordinary copy-on-write behavior.
- Cover Mamba and Conv-only pools, both growth directions, eager/urgent/opportunistic compaction, state payloads and mappings, CUDA stream ordering, and CUDA graph readback.

## Accuracy Tests

Stacking changes commit ancestry only: all four compaction patches are unchanged by `git range-diff`, and the resulting tree matches the previously validated combined changes.

Fresh validation on B300, Python 3.12 / Torch 2.14.1+cu130:

- Focused compaction/views suite: **12 tests / 47 subtests passed**, with CPU and CUDA cases actually executed.
- Adjacent state-transfer, pending-event, tri-pool, page-layout, and byte-accounting suite: **114 tests / 787 subtests passed**.
- Both this fix and the reclaim fix from #39294 in a separate combined snapshot: **61 tests / 201 subtests passed**.
- All **18 CUDA scratch-bound configurations** fail against unchanged main production code and pass with this change: 12 Mamba configurations and 6 Conv-only configurations.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Review verified the physical-slot/page contract, disjoint move sources/destinations, current-stream execution, envelope layout and sink handling, sibling payload copying, and ordinary COW behavior. The pending-reader test injects the pending-reuse state after a real copy and validates the CUDA drain/reuse boundary; it does not claim end-to-end reproduction of that routing race.

The CPU fallback and sibling callbacks retain their own scratch-allocation behavior. No fresh model-serving, full HiCache, or multi-GPU validation is claimed. Historical serving/performance evidence remains in #44097 and is not represented as validation of this head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fresh regression tests validate the reduced allocation peak and preserved payloads. No new latency or serving-throughput claim.

items.title: [reward, ray, cfg, doc] feat: share async scorer concurrency across reward workers
items.author: NaCr05
items.summary: Add optional reward.runmaxconcurrent to bound cooperative async scorers across the workers owned by one RewardLoopManager. Two workers with local maxconcurrent=2 reach a peak of four without a shared limit and two with runmaxconcurrent=2.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add optional reward.run_max_concurrent to bound cooperative async scorers across the workers owned by one RewardLoopManager. Two workers with local max_concurrent=2 reach a peak of four without a shared limit and two with run_max_concurrent=2. An unnamed, non-restarting Ray coordinator owns idempotent grants. The controller validates configuration without loading the scorer module; scorer loading and async validation remain in reward workers.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [focused query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20%22run_max_concurrent%22). Refreshed on 2026-10-17 against main `18cfb74852a0`.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

Existing rate_limited concurrency/RPM/TPM limits are process-local. #5327 changes a SearchTool limiter actor's lifetime; #8015 repairs a math_verify process pool; #8101 fixes reward input padding. None implements manager-wide async scorer admission. No issue-closing claim is made.

### Test

Agent-run CPU validation: **38 passed**. The test command is:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/experimental/reward_loop/test_run_reward_budget_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/reward_loop/test_async_token_bucket_on_cpu.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Pre-commit: all 14 upstream hooks passed.

The review regressions use a scorer module that raises if imported in the controller. Both shared-budget scenarios fail on the previous implementation. After the fix, real workers load an async scorer and preserve peak concurrency 4 without the limit and 2 with it; real workers still reject a synchronous scorer when the shared budget is enabled.



WSL Ubuntu, uv-managed Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.12.1, Ray 2.55.1. Installed CPU/test dependencies match the current uv.lock; Megatron-Core's source dependency was omitted. This is not a complete frozen environment or official CI/GPU result. The existing CPU workflow discovers the new `*_on_cpu.py` tests; no workflow change is required.

### API, Design and Boundaries

Set reward.reward_manager.name=rate_limited, an async custom_reward_function, and reward.run_max_concurrent=4. Default null preserves behavior. Admission has its own reward.timeout, then the scorer timeout starts. This is not a hard end-to-end deadline: cancellation still drains in-flight coordinator RPCs and scorer cleanup, and timeout=null keeps unlimited waits. Admission/coordinator failure propagates; scorer exceptions retain existing zero-reward semantics. Cancellation drains scorer cleanup before release. Worker hard death conservatively retains its grant; a later admission timeout requests a job restart after checking outstanding requests, never silently reissues potentially active external work. RPM/TPM stay local; no FIFO fairness, detached-task accounting, or account-wide HTTP quota is promised. Tests use real Ray workers plus deterministic local race controls, without paid APIs or models.

items.title: [data, ckpt, cfg, doc] feat: check dataset identity before v1 checkpoint restore
items.author: NaCr05
items.summary: Add opt-in data.resumecheck=off error (default off). A versioned datamanifest.json records source-byte and effective-row identities plus text preprocessing/tokenizer settings.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add opt-in data.resume_check=off|warn|error (default off). A versioned data_manifest.json records source-byte and effective-row identities plus text preprocessing/tokenizer settings. The v1 trainer checks it before restoring actor, critic, dataloader or TransferQueue state. Identical relocated files pass; changed contents or order fail under error policy. Reusing a checkpoint directory invalidates its old sidecar before any worker write, so disabled checking or a partial overwrite cannot leave an older identity certifying new checkpoint contents. The replacement manifest is published only after dataloader and synchronous TransferQueue saving succeeds, preventing a new identity from certifying an older queue after a failed overwrite.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [focused query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20%22resume_check%22). Refreshed on 2026-10-17 against main `18cfb74852a0`.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

#7819 makes max_samples selection reproducible; this detects incompatible inputs and does not save/replay sampled indices. #8056 finalizes asynchronous model writes; this leaves finalization and tracker behavior unchanged. #7974 changes epoch-boundary loader restore and #8114 changes retention, neither checks input identity. No issue-closing claim is made.

### Test

Agent-run CPU validation: **65 passed**. The test command is:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/utils/dataset/test_resume_identity_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_checkpoint_data_identity_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_checkpoint_callback_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Pre-commit: all 14 upstream hooks passed.

The original sidecar-invalidation negative control made all six overwrite regressions fail. For the review follow-up, both new split regressions and all four TransferQueue-publication regressions failed before their respective production fixes; all now pass. The tests retain the original dataset signature and config, reject unverifiable splits under error policy, and reject restoration after a failed queue overwrite before any worker/loader/queue state is loaded.

WSL Ubuntu, uv-managed Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.12.1, Ray 2.55.1. Installed CPU/test dependencies match the current uv.lock; Megatron-Core's source dependency was omitted. This is not a complete frozen environment or official CI/GPU result. The existing CPU workflow discovers the new `*_on_cpu.py` tests; no workflow change is required.

### API, Design and Boundaries

Enable data.resume_check=error from the initial run. Old checkpoints without a sidecar are allowed by off, warned by warn, and rejected by error. Custom datasets explicitly own get_resume_signature(); a plain subclass is unverifiable. The built-in path supports local plain-text data and fast tokenizers. Ordinary dataset construction scans the source files and processed rows. Split datasets skip those discarded identity scans and remain unverifiable unless they provide their own signature. The check does not guarantee deterministic training, and a present sidecar does not prove asynchronous model shards are durable. Worker RPCs and TransferQueue transport are stubbed in trainer ordering tests; actual dataset loading and fresh-process StatefulDataLoader resume are exercised.

items.title: [AMD] [GLM5] skip redundant -inf pre-fill of KPool MQA-logits
items.author: Raiden-Makoto
items.summary: This affects prefill serving of GLM-5.3-Flash, which uses the pooled DSA. calls with, which initializes the full FP32 logits buffer to before the scorer writes each row's valid range.
items.body:
## Motivation

This affects prefill serving of GLM-5.3-Flash, which uses the pooled DSA `IndexerKPool`.

`IndexerKPool._kpool_topk_by_row_chunks` calls `fp8_mqa_logits` with `clean_logits=True`, which initializes the full `[query rows x concatenated pooled KV rows]` FP32 logits buffer to `-inf` before the scorer writes each row's valid range. The buffer can be several GiB at long context.

The downstream KPool top-k already receives `row_starts` and `pool_lens` and reads only `score[row, row_start : row_start + pool_len]`. Initializing positions outside those ranges is therefore redundant. This is the KPool equivalent of the non-pooled indexer optimization merged in #28757.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py`: pass `clean_logits=False` to the ragged KPool MQA-logits call. Valid logits are unchanged; positions outside each row's declared range remain uninitialized and are not read by KPool top-k.
- Extend the gfx950 real-kernel test to compare `clean_logits=True` and `False` through the production KPool top-k transform at GLM-5.3-Flash geometry (`32 x 128`, KPool 4, token top-k 2048).
- Make KPool chunking unit tests require `clean_logits=False` on both ROCm/AITER and CUDA/DeepGEMM paths.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 snapshot `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`, MI355X/gfx950, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, thinking enabled, seed 0, and separate fresh caches.

TP4 used context 65,536, 1,319 GSM8K questions, 64 threads, and max output 32,768. TP8 used context 131,072, 1,319 questions, 1,200 threads, and max output 4,096.

| configuration | GSM8K | truncated | errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4 baseline (`clean_logits=True`, `d8dd49d21d`) | 97.27% | 0% | 0% |
| TP4 candidate (`clean_logits=False`, `440cf03231`) | 96.66% | 0% | 0% |
| TP8 baseline (`clean_logits=True`, `d8dd49d21d`) | 96.89% | 0.08% | 0% |
| TP8 candidate (`clean_logits=False`, `440cf03231`) | 96.59% | 0.53% | 0% |

These are single stochastic scoring passes. All four runs completed 1,319 questions without errors.

Focused correctness:

| path | result |
|---|---|
| AITER FP8 MQA logits → ordinary masked top-k | identical selected sets |
| AITER FP8 MQA logits → KPool fused top-k transform | identical selected sets |

- `test_dsa_skip_logits_clean.py`: 2 passed.
- `test_kpool_stream_scheduling.py`: 13 passed.

No model arithmetic inside the valid logits ranges changes.

## Speed Benchmarks

MI355X/gfx950, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`, SGLang `84bd7ab1884cee885fafce9c94f5c9ad80a4f0b8`, AITER `e7d2453f25e5aaeea72a3a40b284ba453e026624`, PyTorch `2.11.0+rocm7.2`, Triton `3.7.0`. FP8 MQA scorer GPU-event medians after warmup, seven measurements per cell, `H=32`, `D=128`.

| query rows | concatenated KV rows | clean=True (ms) | clean=False (ms) | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 4,096 | 0.048 | 0.042 | -11.3% |
| 1,024 | 16,384 | 0.129 | 0.119 | -7.2% |
| 4,096 | 65,536 | 1.547 | 1.203 | -22.2% |
| 8,192 | 131,072 | 7.120 | 6.353 | -10.8% |

A separate concurrency-64-shaped segmented case used 64 requests, 128 query rows and 2,048 pooled KV rows per request (`8,192 x 131,072` output, 4 GiB). Skipping initialization reduced scorer time from 2.605 ms to 1.960 ms (**-24.8%**) and produced identical KPool top-k selections.

These are component timings only; no end-to-end performance improvement is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Park chunked prefill continuation when decode headroom exhausts the budget
items.author: erikwijmans
items.summary: With many decode requests running, their reserved decode headroom can drive negative. then falls back to the full so an in-progress chunked request can make progress, but it never checks that those tokens are free.
items.body:
## Motivation

With many decode requests running, their reserved decode headroom can drive `PrefillBudget.remaining_total` negative. `available_chunk_tokens` then falls back to the full `chunk_limit` so an in-progress chunked request can make progress, but it never checks that those tokens are free. The scheduler then crashes in `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend`:

```
RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size.
Try to allocate 16384 tokens.
Available full tokens: 3200 (full_available_size=3200 + full_evictable_size_=0)
```

## Modifications

- `PrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens` returns `None` when the budget is exhausted, so the continuation parks until running decodes free their headroom. This matches `SWAPrefillBudget`.
- The fallback dates from #12333, when an unadmitted chunked request leaked memory. The scheduler now handles a parked chunk: it skips the stash when the chunk computed no new KV, which hybrid-SWA already relies on. A parked chunk cannot starve, since new requests are not admitted while the budget is negative, and decodes finish or are retracted.
- Added a regression test to `test_prefill_adder.py`. It fails on `main` (the chunk is admitted) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: scheduler admission only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

items.title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Evict loaded shards when checkpoint exceeds RAM
items.author: adi-suresh01
items.summary: Evicts individual shards from the Linux page cache after their tensors are consumed when loading safetensors checkpoints exceeding 90% of available RAM, preventing OOM during large model loads.
items.body:
## Overview

When a safetensors checkpoint is larger than 90% of available RAM, `safetensors_weights_iterator` now evicts each shard from the page cache (`posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)`) once the caller has released its tensors, so a load keeps about one shard cached instead of the whole checkpoint. For DeepSeek-V4.1 this builds on #58857: on main the VL wrapper sorts the full weight stream, which keeps every shard mapped until loading ends, and mapped pages cannot be evicted. Refs #57469, #58625.

## Claims

- Default mmap path only (`--safetensors-load-strategy` unset or `lazy`), Linux only, and only when the checkpoint exceeds 90% of available RAM, the same rule that already turns off auto-prefetch. Checkpoints that fit, and eager, torchao and prefetch loads, behave as before. One info line when it is on.
- A shard is evicted only after the last tensor handed out from it is gone. A caller that holds tensors gets no eviction for those shards.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 in a 702 GiB container: page cache stayed at 6.2 to 12.9 GiB (median 9.6) for the first 13 minutes of a 475 GiB load and peaked at the largest shard, 92.1 GiB, instead of growing with the checkpoint. That run also had the same streaming change as #58857 and other fixes applied; details below.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -k "evicts_released_shards or drop_checkpoint_cache"`: 5 passed. The new test writes a 3-shard checkpoint and mocks `os.posix_fadvise` to record which shard it was called on and to assert that every tensor from that shard is already gone.

| Case | Shards evicted |
|---|---|
| caller streams, holding only the current tensor | 1 and 2 (3 is still referenced when the iterator ends) |
| caller holds every tensor, like `sorted()` | none |
| checkpoint fits in RAM | none |

Each case fails when its part of the change is removed (the whole change, the weakref check, the RAM gate). The test is skipped off Linux; I ran it on macOS with `sys.platform` patched to `linux` and a stub `posix_fadvise`, so CI on Linux is its first run as committed. The rest of `test_weight_utils.py` and `model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py` pass locally (95 passed, 1 skipped; one test errors at setup because the local run did not load `tests/conftest.py`). `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean, and mypy reports no new errors in `weight_utils.py`.

**GPU.** 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, PCIe), RunPod container with a 702.2 GiB memory limit, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (48 shards, 475.25 GiB), `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --engram-config.cpu_offload true`, DSpark with 5 speculative tokens, CUDA graphs. Both runs on nightly `49cb2bbf` plus #60762 (needed to boot DSv4.1 on sm_120). cgroup memory sampled every 5 s.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Extra code | none | the same wrapper change as #58857 (my own overlay of it, without a `clone()`), this PR's eviction, and a `drop_checkpoint_cache` call after the VL wrapper's load (not in this PR) |
| Env | | `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_max_round_threshold_mb:64`, so torch pins the Engram tables at exact size (the problem #59849 addresses in vLLM) |
| Checkpoint on | network FUSE volume | local overlay disk |
| Load | progress bar finished in 7m35s, then memory climbed about 9 GiB/min with workers in D state | 814 s main weights, 302 s DSpark draft pass, ready in 1339 s |
| Peak container memory | 695.1 GiB, then RunPod stopped the container at 98% of its limit | 290.6 GiB: anon 8.2, shmem 189.2 (pinned Engram tables), other page cache 92.1 |
| Served | never | 10.7K and 106K-token prompts |

The after run is not an isolated test of this PR, since it also changed the wrapper, the pinned allocation size and the disk. What it shows for this change is the cache during the load. The container sat at 204.6 to 211.4 GiB of 702.2 GiB for the whole stream, so the cgroup was never near its limit, yet page cache outside the Engram shmem stayed at 6.2 to 12.9 GiB until the last 25 s. There page cache reached 80.9 and then 92.1 GiB as the two Engram table shards came through. The iterator evicted the first (80.9 to 15.9 GiB by the next sample); the last one is the shard this PR leaves to the kernel, and the post-load `drop_checkpoint_cache` released it (92.1 to 6.2 GiB within 10 s). vLLM logged `Checkpoint size: 475.25 GiB. Available RAM: 499.62 GiB.`, so the 90% gate here would have been on; the code in that run evicted unconditionally.

## Details

**Why.** The default loader reads every shard through an mmap. Once a shard's tensors are on the GPU its pages are clean page cache, and that cache is charged to the container's cgroup. The kernel does not reclaim it until the cgroup reaches its limit or the host runs short, but some runtimes act earlier: RunPod stops a container at 98% of its memory limit, which is how the before run ended. With a checkpoint this size next to large pinned host allocations (189 GiB of Engram tables at TP4 here), the cache alone can carry a container to that line.

**Gate.** It reuses the existing 90%-of-available-RAM rule, so a checkpoint that fits stays cached for the next load, which was the objection to the unconditional release in #59527. Available RAM is read once when the iterator starts, honoring cgroup limits through `_get_available_ram_bytes`.

**Why the last tensor.** Every tensor from a shard keeps the shard mapped, and `DONTNEED` skips mapped pages, so evicting earlier does nothing. Loaders release tensors in order, and only once the next one reaches them, so the iterator keeps a weakref to the last tensor it handed out from each shard and checks them after every yield. If a caller holds tensors, as the DSv4.1 VL wrapper's `sorted()` does on main, those shards are never evicted; that is why DSv4.1 needs #58857 to benefit.

**Not changed here.**

- The last shard is still referenced when the iterator returns, so it stays cached until the kernel needs the memory. For the DSv4.1 VL wrapper a `drop_checkpoint_cache` after its load releases it; that sits on top of #58857's change to the same function, so I left it out of this PR.
- With several TP ranks on one host, a rank that finishes a shard first can evict pages a slower rank has not read yet, and that rank reads them from disk again. This only happens when the checkpoint does not fit. I did not measure load time with and without eviction, so I make no claim about load time.
- `multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator`, fastsafetensors, RunAI and instanttensor loading are unchanged. #58625 (opt-in release after loading) is complementary: it frees the cache after the load, this keeps it bounded during the load.
- `_drop_page_cache` returns early off Linux, which also clears the two macOS mypy errors in `drop_checkpoint_cache` that #61836 fixes.
- Not a fix for #57469: that report's remaining failure is pinned host memory (shmem-rss), which is #59849's area.

**AI assistance.** The code, test and this description were drafted with Claude (the commit carries `Assisted-by: Claude`). I reviewed the full diff, and the GPU runs above are mine.

items.title: [Observability] Add tool-calling inference tracing
items.author: tessapham
items.summary: Adds tool-calling summaries to Chat Completions and Messages inference spans, with a shared span lifecycle for tool and non-tool requests. Builds on and aligns vllm.toolcalling. attributes with.
items.body:
## Overview

Adds tool-calling summaries to Chat Completions and Messages inference spans, with a shared span lifecycle for tool and non-tool requests.

Builds on [the metrics PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61571) and aligns vllm.tool_calling.* attributes with [render-server tracing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61683).

## Claims

- Start inference spans at frontend admission and finish after API response conversion or streaming cleanup.
- Report received tool metadata, emitted-call counts, surfaced parser failures, and interrupted streams.
- Preserve trace context and sampling without adding payload content to spans, tool metadata to headers, or changing metrics.

## Validation

- Focused serving, engine, parser, and tracing tests and changed-file pre-commit checks passed.
- Live Qwen3-0.6B CPU testing covered Chat/Messages JSON/SSE, sampling controls, injected parser failures, and real disconnects. Exported spans matched response counts, statuses, and incoming trace context.

items.title: [DSv4.1] Run encoder SWA bounded replay inside the breakable prefill CUDA graph
items.author: kpham-sgl
items.summary: rejected every prefill CUDA graph backend, so DSv4.1 with encoder replay (admitted with DP attention since #43813) ran eager prefill. This admits the breakable backend, the same way #43736 did for the decoder replay.
items.body:
## Motivation

`--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` rejected every prefill CUDA graph backend, so DSv4.1 with encoder replay (admitted with DP attention since #43813) ran eager prefill. This admits the breakable backend, the same way #43736 did for the decoder replay.

## Modifications

- Hook: the encoder gate rejects only prefill graph backends other than `disabled`/`breakable`.
- Prefill graph runner: the static batch carries the four `encoder_swa_*` fold fields.
- DSv4 backend: BCG capture/replay prep set the fold's row floor and activate the window layout; `refresh_for_breakable_cuda_graph_replay_` copies `request_window_layout` in place; under the graph the layout uses a fixed group count (`req_to_token_pool.size`) and the workspace is reserved at the first capture.
- `window_layout(pad=...)`: padding rows (DP fill, graph bucket fill; `out_loc == 0`) take a spare group and never commit. Grouped with the last request they shortened its commit range and committed garbage at its ring slot 0; this was latent in the eager DP path too.
- In-graph ratio-1/2 compressors skip the folded replay rows via a bucket-sized `DSV4Metadata.low_ratio_replay_rows` mask.
- DP prefill-graph vote counts the folded replay rows so every rank votes on the rows the runner replays.

## Accuracy / Performance

Not yet run on GPU; CPU unit tests only (the new cases fail on main). Validation on DSv4.1 Flash with `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --attn-dp-size N` is pending.
