items.title: [Bugfix] Skip request body JSON serialization when its log level is disabled
items.author: dskwe
items.summary: Restores a logger-level guard to skip unnecessary JSON serialization of request bodies when the configured request-body log level is disabled in vLLM's frontend request logger.
items.body:
## Overview

Avoid serializing request JSON when the configured request-body logging level is disabled. This restores the logger-level guard removed by #60630 while preserving configurable body log levels.

## Claims

- Disabled request-body logging no longer calls `model_dump_json`.
- Enabled INFO body logging still works when DEBUG is disabled; existing body truncation remains unchanged.
- No measured end-to-end speedup is claimed.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Scoped searches (open and all-state) for `log_request_body`, `60630`, `isEnabledFor` + request logging, and request-body serialization found no PR adding this guard. Nearest work inspected: #60498 (Prometheus counters), #38583 (opt-in INFO prompt summaries), #58712 (LoggingConfig log_color/log_stream fields), RFC issue #57200. None touches the eager serialization in `log_request_body`.

## Validation

Tests were run against `ae8f41238cc7316781ef4359890940749735b209` and re-verified unchanged at `e7a5bdb4542ca13e70a1ef0a1d9fb628b632c691`; `vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/request_logger.py` and its test file are unchanged between that SHA and current `main` (`523d74e2ac78867aa35d535835e14f78fb7433af`), where the bug is still present. Real CPU Docker environment, Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, pytest 9.1.1. No GPU, successful generation E2E or model evaluation was performed.

On unchanged production source with the new regression test: **2 failed, 12 passed**. Both failures show one serialization instead of zero for disabled DEBUG/INFO and WARNING/ERROR combinations. Enabled INFO passes.

After the three-line guard:

```sh
docker exec -w /validation/overnight-frontend-20261017 \
  -e PYTHONPATH=/validation/overnight-frontend-20261017 \
  -e VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu vllm-tokenizer-validation-20261013 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_responses_utils.py -q --disable-warnings
```

**60 passed, 14 warnings in 17.53s.** Adding `tests/test_logger.py` to the same command: **82 passed, 16 warnings in 50.64s**. All applicable patch-scoped pinned pre-commit hooks passed; verbose mypy reported no issues in 2 files targeting Python 3.11. `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only patch review found no code blocker.

A real FastAPI completion-route validation reproduced unnecessary serialization on a 404 unknown-model request: baseline DEBUG serialized once, fixed zero; enabled INFO remained once, with unchanged error responses. The harness initializes only early-rejection dependencies, not an engine; this is not successful serving E2E or model evaluation.

Serialization-only microbenchmark in the same CPU container, five repeats of 200 calls, body DEBUG/logger INFO, max_log_len=100: median helper cost for 32-byte/1MiB ASCII prompts was 16.844/1123.862 µs before versus 3.375/3.397 µs after. These are helper costs, not end-to-end performance results.

A normal render-server startup/HTTP A/B probe used the cached OPT-125m config/tokenizer snapshot `27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`: real `render.entry` CLI, normal app initialization, Uvicorn loopback HTTP. Expanded A/B covered `/v1/completions/render`, `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/responses/render`: all 12 render requests and 4 health checks returned 200; DEBUG body serialization changed 1→0 for each endpoint; enabled INFO remained 1; all six corresponding complete response bodies matched across variants; prompt token IDs agreed with independent Transformers encoding using each endpoint's special-token defaults (diagnostic chat template; not OPT chat quality validation). This is preprocessing only, not generated-token equivalence, inference E2E or evaluation. Full generation serving validation remains blocked in this environment: importing the native `vllm._C` terminates with SIGILL in the CPU container; the exact instruction mismatch is undiagnosed.

Independent read-only audits of the saved harness evidence confirmed serializer marker counts, the six parsed-JSON response pairs, HTTP status fields, parent exit codes and imported-module source hashes; the auditors did not rerun HTTP or tests. Equality is parsed-JSON, not wire-byte equality; recorded module hashes are selected-source, not whole-environment provenance.

## Details

Python evaluates `model_dump_json(...)` before `logger.log` checks its level. `BaseServing._check_model` calls this helper when request logging is enabled, including completions, chat completions and Responses paths. With the default DEBUG body level and INFO logger threshold, request bodies are needlessly serialized even though no body record is emitted. Request logging is opt-in; deployments without it are not affected. Pooling overrides `_check_model`, so this report does not claim pooling impact.

The fix checks `logger.isEnabledFor(level)` after resolving the configured level and before serialization, matching the existing `isEnabledFor` use elsewhere in this file. It does not try to predict later handler/filter rejection. Tests use a real CompletionRequest and real logger, tracking the serializer through a wrapper instead of substituting a fabricated request.

On configuration mechanism: markmc's post-merge comment on #60630 suggests the body log level belongs in the typed `--logging-config` (#57200) rather than a new env var. This guard is independent of where the level comes from: whether the level continues to be read from the env var or moves into `LoggingConfig`, serialization should still be skipped when that level is disabled. This PR intentionally does not restructure the configuration.

AI assistance was used for identifying, reproducing and validating this fix; the full validation record above reflects commands actually run in a local CPU container.

items.title: [Attention][KV Connector] FlashInfer: optional separate K/V head slots for unquantized KV
items.author: jimburtoft
items.summary: With it, FlashInfer stores an unquantized (fp16/bf16) KV cache with K and V as separate head slots (, content = ), instead of packing K|V in the content dim. This is the same split the NVFP4 KV cache already uses, and the same idea as ROCm attention and b12x.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds an opt-in `--attention-config.flashinfer_separate_kv_head_slots`. With it, FlashInfer stores an unquantized (fp16/bf16) KV cache with K and V as **separate head slots** (`num_head_slots = 2 * num_kv_heads`, content = `head_size`), instead of packing K|V in the content dim. This is the same split the NVFP4 KV cache already uses, and the same idea as ROCm attention and b12x.

Under LBHNC, each page becomes `[K heads (H, N, D) | V heads (H, N, D)]`. The NIXL worker registers the K half and the V half of each page as two regions that step by the full page. A remote engine that keeps K and V in **separate per-layer slabs** then maps onto it region for region, with no post-transfer permute and no extra copy.

## Claims

- New flag, off by default. Nothing changes when it is unset: the spec, layouts, kernels, NIXL regions and compat hash are all as before.
- With the flag on, FlashInfer decode, prefill and mixed batches match the SDPA reference for bf16 and fp16 under LBHNC and BLHNC, including the KV write path.
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct gives **identical greedy outputs** with and without the flag (7/7 prompts, 48 tokens each) on both H100 (SM90, XQA decode) and B200 (SM100, trtllm-gen decode and TRTLLM prefill).
- Throughput is unchanged. Results are below.
- NIXL registers two half-page regions per layer, so a peer with separate K/V slabs (two dense regions per layer, same `block_len`) handshakes and pulls blocks. Heterogeneous TP still works per region, because each region keeps its heads contiguous.
- The NIXL compatibility hash includes the flag. Two vLLM engines that differ only in this flag therefore refuse to pair instead of exchanging pages with mismatched layouts.

## Validation

Runs were on 1x H100 (SM90) and 1x B200 (SM100), at this branch on base `523d74e2a`, using `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

| Suite | H100 | B200 |
|---|---|---|
| New tests (`-k "split or separate_kv_head_slots or heterogeneous_tp_slices"`, across the 3 test files below) | 24 passed | 24 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k flashinfer` | 42 passed, 7 skipped | 43 passed, 6 skipped |
| `test_nixl_connector.py` + `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` + `test_nixl_split_kv_head_slots.py` | 417 passed | 417 passed |
| `test_b12x.py` + `test_attention_backends_selection.py` | 24 passed, 29 skipped | 24 passed, 29 skipped |
| `test_mooncake_connector.py` | 119 passed, 2 failed* | 119 passed, 2 failed* |

\* `test_register_worker_retries_on_read_timeout` and `test_register_worker_raises_after_max_attempts` fail identically on unpatched `main` on these hosts: name resolution is unavailable in the sandbox. Unrelated to this change.

New tests:
- `test_attention_backends.py::test_flashinfer_separate_kv_head_slots`: FlashInfer vs SDPA reference with split slots; LBHNC/BLHNC × decode/prefill/mixed × bf16/fp16. Covers the KV write path.
- `test_nixl_split_kv_head_slots.py`: spec on/off; layout restriction; compat hash; two regions per layer at exact K/V addresses (LBHNC, BLHNC); handshake with a separate-slab peer (exact remote descriptors); heterogeneous TP (D TP1 ← P TP2, D TP2 ← P TP1), checking each read stays inside one K or V region.
- `test_mooncake_connector.py::test_head_resharding_rejects_separate_kv_head_slots`: Mooncake rejects head re-sharding for split-slot pages, as it does for NVFP4.

`customize_spec` refactor check: the flattened version returns the same spec as the first version for all 96 combinations of KV quant mode × head size × dtype × flag.

Serving, `vllm bench serve` (2048 in / 256 out, concurrency 16, 64 prompts, seeds 1 and 2):

| GPU | Layout | Median TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| H100 | packed | 9.16 / 9.35 | 1413 / 1413 |
| H100 | split | 9.32 / 9.35 | 1413 / 1413 |
| B200 | packed | 4.65 / 4.69 | 2747 / 2756 |
| B200 | split | 4.51 / 4.95 | 2750 / 2750 |

Negative control: with `forward()` forced back to packed views while the flag is on, the new kernel tests fail as expected (`2 failed`). So the tests do exercise the split path.

To check that the split path is actually taken at serve time, a probe on `_has_separate_kv_head_slots` recorded the logical cache `(H_slots, N, C)` of every layer in an offline `LLM` run:
- flag on: `(16, 16, 128)` → split path;
- flag off: `(8, 16, 256)` → packed path.

Both runs produced the same greedy text.

End to end:

```
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --attention-backend FLASHINFER --max-model-len 4096 \
    [--attention-config.flashinfer_separate_kv_head_slots=true]
vllm bench serve ... --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 \
    --ignore-eos --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 16 --seed {1,2}
```

The split K/V NIXL path has also been exercised against a remote engine with separate K/V slabs: Llama-3.1-8B, TP4↔TP4 and TP1→TP4, both pull directions, on vLLM 0.29 with an earlier version of this patch. Greedy outputs matched each decode engine's own single-instance output at the cross-device numerics ceiling.

## Details

**Why.** Since the KV-cache layout refactor (RFC #42082, #51718), unquantized FlashInfer and FlashAttention pack K|V into each token's content dim. That makes zero-copy NIXL KV exchange impossible with an engine whose attention keeps K and V in separate per-layer slabs, a common layout outside vLLM's CUDA backends. The RFC's model already allows separate K/V head slots, and NVFP4, ROCm and b12x use them. This exposes the same layout for unquantized FlashInfer, behind a flag.

**What changes:**
- `AttentionConfig.flashinfer_separate_kv_head_slots`: new flag, default `False`.
- `FlashInferBackend.customize_spec`: for unquantized KV with the flag on, returns the NVFP4-style spec (`num_head_slots=2H`, `state_content_bytes = head_size * dtype_size`). Page size is unchanged.
- `FlashInferBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts`: restricted to `(LBHNC, BLHNC)` when the flag is on. Each K or V half of a page is contiguous only when `[H, N, C]` is contiguous in a block.
- `FlashInferImpl`: `forward` and `do_kv_cache_update` split the cache by head slot instead of by content. The impl detects the split from the cache shape: the last dim is `head_size` for split slots and `2 * head_size` for packed. It therefore always matches however the cache was allocated, with no extra config lookups on the hot path.
- `NixlConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches`: a split-slot attention page (detected from the spec and layout) is registered as two regions `(base, page/2, stride)` and `(base + page/2, page/2, stride)`.
- `compute_nixl_compatibility_hash`: includes the flag.
- `gpu_model_runner.get_kv_cache_spec` (MRV1) and `gpu/attn_utils.get_kv_cache_spec` (MRV2): call `customize_attention_spec` under `set_current_vllm_config`, so a backend can read `attention_config` when packing its spec. Without this, `customize_spec` runs with no current config in the worker, and the impl's KV write would see a spec/cache mismatch.

**Scope and limits:**
- FlashInfer only. FlashAttention is not changed.
- Unquantized KV only. fp8 and NVFP4 keep their current paths.
- Only the NIXL connector is taught about the two-region split. Mooncake rejects head re-sharding for split-slot pages, as it does for NVFP4; same-TP transfers move whole pages and are unaffected. Other connectors are unchanged.
- Sliding-window / HMA specs go through the same `customize_spec`, but were only covered by the existing test suite, not by new tests.

**Line count.** About 110 added lines in `vllm/` (about 60 in `flashinfer.py`, 37 in `base_worker.py`, 5 in Mooncake). Tests add about 470. Docs add 3 lines.

**CI coverage.** The new kernel test runs wherever `test_attention_backends.py` already runs FlashInfer. The NIXL and Mooncake tests are CPU-level unit tests in existing files and directories, so no new CI step is needed.

## Purpose

Disable all L4 jobs on CI by marking every step with `device: l4` in `.buildkite/test_areas/` as `optional: true` (37 steps across 14 files; the 3 L4 steps that were already optional are unchanged).

items.title: [Bug]: `--load-format ipc_cache` leaves MoE routers on meta placeholders (illegal memory access, meta-tensor errors)
items.author: nealvaidya
items.summary: Fixes IpcModelLoader re-registering meta placeholders as new nn.Parameters, breaking MoE router bias references and causing illegal memory access during IPC cache model loading.
items.body:
### Your current environment
Output of vllm collect-env ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-1010-oracle-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H200 GPU 1: NVIDIA H200 GPU 2: NVIDIA H200 GPU 3: NVIDIA H200 Nvidia driver version : 610.57.04 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.31.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: 7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Loading an MoE model with an expert-score correction bias through the weight cache (`--load-format ipc_cache`) either crashes or fails to start. The same model loads and generates correctly from disk. `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` replaces each meta placeholder parameter with a new `nn.Parameter` object ([ipc_loader.py#L256-L264](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L256-L264)). Objects that captured the placeholder while the model was being constructed keep the meta tensor. MoE routers are such objects: - MoE models pass their gate's parameter into the MoE layer, for example `e_score_correction_bias=self.gate.e_score_correction_bias` in [nemotron_h.py#L244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L244), [lfm2_moe.py#L155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_moe.py#L155), [deepseek_v2.py#L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L390), and [ernie45_moe.py#L193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/ernie45_moe.py#L193). - The router keeps that tensor object: [grouped_topk_router.py#L274](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/grouped_topk_router.py#L274) and [fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369). After `_apply_entries`, the gate holds the cached tensor and every router still holds the meta placeholder. `_apply_entries` is unchanged on `main`. ### Reproduction This needs a single GPU larger than 80 GB (tested on a 141 GB H200). Start the daemon: ```bash vllm preload --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 \ --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 ``` Run the engine (`fallback: False`, so a disk fallback can't mask the result): ```python import os os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0" # in-process, so the model can be inspected from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams llm = LLM( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16", load_format="ipc_cache", model_loader_extra_config={"fallback": False}, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=1, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, ) out = llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=24)) print(repr(out[0].outputs[0].text)) ``` Output: ```text [rank0]: RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered [rank0]: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The process then aborts (exit code 134). On smaller GPUs, `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (~17 GB) reproduces the same way.
Minimal Reproducer (no GPU or model needed) ```python import torch from torch import nn class Gate(nn.Module): def __init__(self): super().__init__() self.e_score_correction_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(4), requires_grad=False) class Router: # plain object, like GroupedTopKRouter def __init__(self, e_score_correction_bias): self.e_score_correction_bias = e_score_correction_bias def build(): with torch.device("meta"): gate = Gate() return gate, Router(gate.e_score_correction_bias) cached = torch.arange(4.0) # stands in for the daemon's tensor # What IpcModelLoader._apply_entries does today gate, router = build() gate._parameters.pop("e_score_correction_bias") gate.register_parameter("e_score_correction_bias", nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("replace:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) # Swapping in place keeps every holder on the same object gate, router = build() torch.utils.swap_tensors(gate.e_score_correction_bias, nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("swap:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) ``` ```text replace: True False swap: False True ```
### Results across models Same settings for every load: `enforce_eager=True`, `max_model_len=4096`, greedy decoding, 24 tokens. | Model | Router | `ipc_cache` (current) | |---|---|---| | `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 23/23 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 22/22 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `moonshotai/Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 26/26 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` | `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | Engine fails to start: `NotImplementedError: _moe_C::topk_softmax: attempted to run this operator with Meta tensors` in `profile_run` | ### Proposed fix When the existing parameter is a meta placeholder, swap the cached tensor into it in place with `torch.utils.swap_tensors`, so every reference sees the cached data. Register buffers before parameters. `swap_tensors` refuses a parameter while a view of it is alive, and `MambaMixer2` registers `conv_weights` as a view of `conv1d.weight` ([mamba_mixer2.py#L460-L463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L460-L463)). `export_entries` emits parameters before buffers ([daemon.py#L159-L163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L159-L163)), so without reordering the swap of `conv1d.weight` fails with `It is not possible to get the gradient edge for a Tensor that does not require gradients`. ```diff def _register(name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor, is_param: bool) -> None: module_name, _, leaf = name.rpartition(".") module = modules.get(module_name) if module is None: raise RuntimeError(f"Cached tensor {name} has no matching module") - # Replace via registration rather than param.data assignment, - # which fails for meta tensors. Entries may also introduce - # post-quantization tensors absent from the meta model. - module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) - module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) if is_param: obj: torch.Tensor = ( tensor if isinstance(tensor, nn.Parameter) else nn.Parameter(tensor, requires_grad=False) ) - module.register_parameter(leaf, obj) + placeholder = module._parameters.get(leaf) + if placeholder is not None and placeholder is not obj and placeholder.is_meta: + # Swap in place: objects built with the model (e.g. MoE + # routers) hold references to the placeholder. + torch.utils.swap_tensors(placeholder, obj) + obj = placeholder + else: + module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) + module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) + module.register_parameter(leaf, obj) else: + module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) + module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) obj = tensor module.register_buffer(leaf, obj) registered[name] = obj - for name, entry in state.entries.items(): + # Buffers first: replacing them releases views of meta parameters + # (e.g. MambaMixer2.conv_weights), which would block the swap. + entries = sorted(state.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[1].kind == "param") + for name, entry in entries: tensor = entry.rebuild(device_index) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
discussion:
Thanks for the detailed report and the reproduction steps.

The root cause looks clear: `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` re-registers each placeholder with a *new* `nn.Parameter` object, so any object that captured the original meta placeholder during model construction — like the MoE routers holding `gate.e_score_correction_bias` — keeps pointing at the meta tensor and fails at runtime. The fix should keep those captured references coherent while applying the cached entries.

I'd like to take this one and send a PR.
The fix is up: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62115 — thank you again for the detailed report and reproducer, it made the root cause straightforward to verify.

items.title: [Fix] MiMo-V2: Normalize images with the checkpoint's image_mean/image_std
items.author: koladefaj
items.summary: normalizes images with hard-coded OpenAI-CLIP mean/std. MiMo-V2.6 checkpoints now specify ImageNet stats in, so SGLang normalizes V2.6 images differently from HF with the same checkpoint, by up to 0.4941 per channel in the reproduction below.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44789.

`MiMoProcessor` normalizes images with hard-coded OpenAI-CLIP mean/std. MiMo-V2.6 checkpoints now specify ImageNet stats in `preprocessor_config.json`, so SGLang normalizes V2.6 images differently from HF `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` with the same checkpoint, by up to 0.4941 per channel in the reproduction below.

The CLIP constant matched MiMo-V2.6 when #40888 was merged. The checkpoint config later changed to ImageNet stats in Xiaomi's [`6a7f202e`](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD/commit/6a7f202e) ("Align preprocessor config to training values").

Different MiMo-V2 checkpoints now specify different stats:

| Checkpoint (`MiMoV2ForCausalLM`) | Normalization |
|---|---|
| MiMo-V2.6-Pro/Flash, -RL, -MOPD | ImageNet |
| MiMo-V2.5, MiMo-V2.5-Base | CLIP |
| MiMo-V2.5-Pro, -Pro-FP4-DFlash | text-only; multimodal disabled |

So no single hard-coded normalization is correct for all of them.

## Modifications

- `processors/mimo_v2.py`
  - Read `image_mean`/`image_std` from the loaded image processor, with the existing CLIP values as fallback.
  - Key the normalization cache by `(device, mean, std)` instead of only the device, so processors with different stats do not share cached tensors.
- `models/mimo_v2.py`, `disaggregation/encoder/preprocessor.py`
  - Pass the encode server's already-loaded `image_processor` to the MiMo hook through the existing `invoke_encoder_preprocessor` mechanism. The image call already used it; the video and audio calls now do too, so whichever modality arrives first builds the processor with the checkpoint's stats.
  - Log a warning when no image processor is loaded and the encoder falls back to CLIP.
- `test_mimo_v2_image_normalization.py`
  - Regression coverage for CLIP and ImageNet checkpoints sharing one device.
  - Encode-server coverage with a video request arriving first.

Pixel bounds are unchanged: SGLang reads them from `config.json`'s `processor_config`, which already has 8192/8388608 for V2.6. The FA4 vision sliding-window issue mentioned in #44789 (#38871) is separate.

## Accuracy Tests

Compared against HF `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` loaded from each checkpoint's own preprocessor config, with GPU preprocessing (`SGLANG_ENCODER_IMAGE_PROCESSOR_USE_GPU=1`) on both the regular and encode-server paths.

Setup: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (sm89), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0.

| Checkpoint | Path | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiMo-V2.5 (CLIP) | regular | match | match |
| MiMo-V2.5 (CLIP) | encode server | match | match |
| MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD (ImageNet) | regular | max diff 0.4941 | match |
| MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD (ImageNet) | encode server | max diff 0.4941 | match |

With this PR, the normalization cache holds separate `cuda:0` entries for the CLIP and ImageNet stats.

Unit tests (the new test plus `test_encode_server.py`, `test_kimi_k3_encoder_mode.py`, `test_processor_async_call_sites.py`):
- main: the new ImageNet cases fail, with greatest absolute difference up to 0.4941.
- This PR: 115 passed, 0 failed, with and without `SGLANG_ENCODER_IMAGE_PROCESSOR_USE_GPU=1`.

I did not run a full MiMo-V2.6 serving comparison; the change is isolated to preprocessing and is checked directly against the HF processor.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Normalization does the same arithmetic as before; the tensors are still cached per device, with the stats added to the cache key.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Accuracy only; speed not applicable.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: Refactor schedule node activation ownership
items.author: vthumbe1503
items.summary: MXFP8 NCCL EP Dispatch is currently not functional due to absence of MXFP8 GroupedTensor outputted by Dispatch Op not having functionality of untypedstorage.resize(0). It also doesnt make sense to implement such functionality for custom tensor with no unifying…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
MXFP8 NCCL EP Dispatch is currently not functional due to absence of MXFP8 GroupedTensor outputted by Dispatch Op not having functionality of untyped_storage.resize_(0). It also doesnt make sense to implement such functionality for custom tensor with no unifying backing storage.

Aims at solving 2 main problems
1. Gets rid of inputs member variable ScheduleNode. inputs doesnt need to be saved in ScheduleNode. Only reason it is there, is because grads need to be propogated by autograd. This can be done by wrapping the inputs in a ScheduleNodeWrapper which lets the grad flow to the wrapper without having to save the inputs in the Schedulenode object. Even the outputs doesnt need to be saved and rather the autograph graph's output edge needs to be saved to start the node.backward
2. Rearranges the code for dispatch/grouped_mlp/combine so that the permuted_local_hidden_states gets garbage collected early by pytorch instead of us having to manually releasing memory using untyped_storage.resize_(0)

Has been verified on DSV3 4n Proxy Config. And there is not meaningful change in memory allocated.

items.title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: route unquantized BF16/F16/F32 checkpoints off the MXFP4 expert path
items.author: Kylinny
items.summary: Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44810. A DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint carries no. [Discussion: <!-- pr-check-comment runs=38982233324 --> Required checks failed on 2a1f11e; this PR cannot be merg]
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44810.

A DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint carries no `quantization_config`. In `ModelConfig`, `is_fp4_experts` is initialized from the `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS` env var (default `True`) and is only overridden when `try_detect_fp4_experts()` returns a non-`None` value. That detector returned `None` for any dtype other than the mxfp4-packed (`U8`/`I8`/`F4`) or FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3`) layouts — including unquantized `BF16`/`F16`/`F32`. As a result, an unquantized DSV4 checkpoint kept `is_fp4_experts=True` under default settings and the auto MoE-runner backend routed it to the `flashinfer_mxfp4` path, while the rest of the stack treated it as unquantized, crashing the first request with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py`: `try_detect_fp4_experts()` now returns `False` for unquantized routed-expert dtypes (`BF16`/`F16`/`F32`), so unquantized checkpoints take the unquantized expert path instead of falling back to the FP4-experts env default. Genuine MXFP4 (`U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`) and FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3` → `False`) detection is unchanged; unknown or unreadable headers still return `None` and fall back to the user/env default.
- `test/registered/unit/configs/test_deepseek_v4_fp4_detect.py`: new unit tests covering `BF16`/`F16`/`F32` → `False`, `U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`, `F8_E4M3` → `False`, and `None` for unreadable/empty checkpoint dirs.

## Reproducer (no GPU required)

A full GPU repro is infeasible here (needs 8x B300 plus a DSV4 BF16 checkpoint), so the bug is demonstrated at the config-routing layer where it lives. Save the script below as `repro_44810.py` in the repo root and run `python3 repro_44810.py`. It builds fake checkpoint dirs (a single safetensors shard whose header declares one routed-expert weight tensor of the given dtype) and drives the real `try_detect_fp4_experts()` plus the real `probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype()` (AST-extracted from the repo; the only stubs are `transformers`/`QuantizationConfig` class-level deps and `find_local_repo_dir`, which is unreachable for local dirs), then applies the same `None`-vs-env-default logic `ModelConfig` uses.

```python
import ast, json, os, re, struct, sys, tempfile, types
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

weight_utils_src = open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py").read()
tree = ast.parse(weight_utils_src)

def _wanted(n):
    if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
        return any(getattr(t, "id", "") == "_ROUTED_EXPERT_KEY_RE" for t in n.targets)
    return getattr(n, "name", None) == "probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype"

seg = [n for n in tree.body if _wanted(n)]
wmod = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils")
wmod.__dict__.update({"re": re, "json": json, "struct": struct, "os": os,
                      "Path": Path, "Optional": Optional,
                      "logging": __import__("logging")})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=seg, type_ignores=[]), "<wu>", "exec"), wmod.__dict__)

def make_pkg(name):
    m = types.ModuleType(name); m.__path__ = []; sys.modules[name] = m; return m

for pkg in ["sglang", "sglang.srt", "sglang.srt.configs",
            "sglang.srt.model_loader", "sglang.srt.utils"]:
    make_pkg(pkg)
sys.modules["sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils"] = wmod
sys.modules["sglang.srt.utils"].find_local_repo_dir = lambda *a, **k: None

dv4_tree = ast.parse(open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py").read())
fn_node = next(n for n in dv4_tree.body
               if getattr(n, "name", None) == "try_detect_fp4_experts")
dv4 = types.SimpleNamespace()
dv4.__dict__.update({"os": os, "logging": __import__("logging"), "Optional": Optional})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[fn_node], type_ignores=[]), "<dv4>", "exec"), dv4.__dict__)

KEY = "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.w1.weight"

def make_ckpt(dtype_str):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    header = json.dumps({KEY: {"dtype": dtype_str, "shape": [2048, 4096]}}).encode()
    with open(os.path.join(d, "model.safetensors"), "wb") as f:
        f.write(struct.pack("<Q", len(header))); f.write(header)
    return d
```

items.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Count only checkpoint elements for padded online-quant MoE weights
items.author: faresobeid
items.summary: Fixes excessive peak memory during layerwise reload of online-quant MoE weights by setting weight_loader_numel to the unpadded checkpoint size, reducing memory from 54.8 GiB to 1.8 GiB on H200.
items.body:
## Purpose

Online-quant MoE methods can pad the intermediate size (`fp8_per_block` rounds it up to 128, so Qwen3-30B-A3B with MoE TP 4 stores 256 instead of 192), but the online MoE weights did not set `weight_loader_numel` like `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` does. Layerwise loading therefore never saw a MoE layer as fully loaded and deferred all of them to `finalize_layerwise_processing`, keeping a bf16 copy of every expert weight on the device. This sets `weight_loader_numel` to the unpadded checkpoint size so each layer is processed as soon as it is loaded.

## Test Plan

New unit test in `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py` (fails on main for the padded case). Qwen3-30B-A3B, `quantization="fp8_per_block"`, TP 4 on H200, layerwise reload with weights streamed one layer at a time: peak extra memory per GPU is 54.8 GiB (48 MoE layers pending until finalize) on main and 1.8 GiB with this change. Greedy outputs after reload are unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6944606][fix] Recognize Rubin GPUs in VisualGen performance tests
items.author: daichu-nv
items.summary: LTX2 performance tests reject Rubin engineering samples with generic or pre-production GPU names before generation starts. Read CUDA-visible device 0, preserve existing model-name mappings, and fall back to SM107 detection for Rubin.
items.body:
## Description

LTX2 performance tests reject Rubin engineering samples with generic or pre-production GPU names before generation starts. Read CUDA-visible device 0, preserve existing model-name mappings, and fall back to SM107 detection for Rubin. Store results under a separate `vr200` GPU key and allow VR200 in the LTX2 configuration.

This fix enables LTX2 performance-test execution on Rubin. The existing CI performance-regression logic is unchanged.

Fixes [NVBug 6944606](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6944606).

## Validation

All three recipes completed real generation and benchmark collection on four Rubin GPUs (CFG2 × Ulysses2). These runs validated execution and metric collection. The bring-up runner disabled OpenSearch baseline lookup, so no performance-regression comparison or latency acceptance threshold was evaluated.

| Recipe | Benchmark execution |
| --- | --- |
| Two-stage BF16 image-to-video | Completed successfully |
| Two-stage BF16 text-to-video | Completed successfully |
| NVFP4-named image-to-video | Completed successfully |


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: [Perf] qwen3.5: fuse GemmaRMSNorm with FP8 / NVFP4 input quant
items.author: zcnrex
items.summary: In Qwen3.5 dense NVFP4/FP8 checkpoints (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4), every norm that feeds a quantized projection runs as two kernels:, then a separate activation quant ( before, before the attention ).
items.body:
## Motivation

In Qwen3.5 dense NVFP4/FP8 checkpoints (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4), every norm that feeds a quantized projection runs as two kernels: `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm`, then a separate activation quant (`fp4_quantize` before `gate_up_proj`, `static_quant_fp8` before the attention `qkv_proj`). flashinfer already ships fused residual-add + RMSNorm + quant kernels for both formats. `RMSNorm` uses the FP8 one through `fuse_input_quant`; `GemmaRMSNorm` uses neither.

## Modifications

- `GemmaRMSNorm.fuse_input_quant(linear)`, mirroring `RMSNorm`. In `forward_cuda` the norm emits a pre-quantized input when the consumer qualifies:
  - static per-tensor FP8 linear: flashinfer `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant` / `rmsnorm_quant` -> `(fp8, scale, orig_dtype)`
  - NVFP4 W4A4 ModelOpt linear (non-AWQ, non-Marlin, `_accepts_prequantized_fp4`): flashinfer `add_rmsnorm_fp4quant` / `rmsnorm_fp4quant` -> `(fp4, block_scale)` in the same layout `fp4_quantize` returns (uint8 `[M, K/2]`, 128x4-swizzled uint8 `[round_up(M,128), K/16]`)
  
  Both use the stored `gemma_weight` (`1 + w`) as a plain RMSNorm weight.
- The FP8 helper is factored out of `RMSNorm.forward_with_per_tensor_quant_fusion` so both norms share it.
- `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod` is now recognized as a static per-tensor FP8 consumer (unless Marlin). Its `apply` accepts the `(fp8, scale, dtype)` tuple on every path: the SM12x small-M dispatcher (`try_sm120_fp8_linear`) and `apply_fp8_linear_bmm_flashinfer` now take an already-quantized fp8 input instead of re-quantizing; `apply_fp8_linear` already did.
- Qwen3.5 wiring: post-attention norm -> `mlp.gate_up_proj` in every dense layer; input norm -> `qkv_proj` in full-attention layers. GDN layers keep the bf16 input norm because `in_proj_ba` consumes it. `forward_prepare_cuda_fused` reads `seq_len` from `qkv` so a tuple input works.

Numerics: the fused kernels quantize the fp32 normed value directly instead of the bf16-rounded one. On random inputs about 1-2% of FP4 codes / FP8 values land one step away from the unfused chain; valid block scales differ by at most one code.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/layers/test_layernorm_fusion.py` on sm_121 (flashinfer 0.7.2): 8 passed, 38 subtests. New cases:
  - `TestGemmaRMSNormInputQuantFusion`: FP8 and NVFP4 outputs vs the unfused reference (0-dim scales, as ModelOpt layers hold them), residual update, and the unfused fallback.
  - `TestPrequantizedFp8Linear`: a pre-quantized fp8 input gives bit-identical output to the bf16 input through `apply_fp8_linear_bmm_flashinfer` and `try_sm120_fp8_linear`.
- GSM8K on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (base vs this PR): **pending** (test box offline), will be added.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel chain at bs1, hidden 5120, sm_121, CUDA-graph timed:

| chain | unfused | fused |
|---|---|---|
| add + Gemma RMSNorm + static FP8 quant | 2.33 us | 1.68 us |
| add + Gemma RMSNorm + NVFP4 quant | 3.22 us | 1.73 us |

For Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 bs1 decode this removes 64 FP4-quant + 16 FP8-quant kernels per step, an expected ~0.1 ms of an ~81 ms step, so it is a small win; the gain is larger relative to step time at low per-step GEMM cost. End-to-end decode A/B: **pending**, will be added.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

items.title: [None][feat] Add initial Beam component implementation
items.author: Mgluhovskoi
items.summary: This draft adds the initial Beam layer and decoder-block implementation to the TensorRT-LLM PyTorch backend. The current MoE implementation uses a correctness-oriented PyTorch expert loop with FP32 accumulation; production fused MoE execution remains unfinishe…
items.body:
This draft adds the initial Beam layer and decoder-block implementation to the TensorRT-LLM PyTorch backend. **Work in progress: this is not yet a functional full-model serving implementation and is not ready for deployment.**

The implementation includes fused QKV/gate projection, Q/K RMSNorm, sliding-window RoPE, SSMax scaling for full-attention layers, output gating, sandwich norms, depth-scaled residuals, SwiGLU, and grouped top-k routing. The current MoE implementation uses a correctness-oriented PyTorch expert loop with FP32 accumulation; production fused MoE execution remains unfinished.

The attention selector also keeps paged-context requests on FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen when the fallback build lacks the required fused context kernel. The port preserves main's existing page-size restriction and adds a regression test for kernel presence/absence.

### Validation and limitations

- The preserved development baseline has individual-layer and small-block differential validation using generated weights. This is not full-checkpoint or end-to-end acceptance.
- Python syntax, Ruff lint/format, and isolated CPU checks of kernel lookup and the fallback-selection condition pass on this port. Full TensorRT-LLM/GPU tests have not been rerun against this upstream-main base.
- Scoped pre-commit checks pass (including lint/format, spelling, private-key/large-file checks, legacy-config validation and pinned-memory policy). The aggregate hook run could not install its pinned `setuptools==84.0.0`; repository-wide vendor/test-list checks were blocked by the sparse checkout and local Python 3.9 runtime. These checks still need a supported full checkout/environment.
- Evidence-dependent model QA tests and their fixtures remain outside this PR; portable model tests and CI coverage are still to be added.
- No checkpoint weights, serialized tensors, reference captures, private checkpoint identifiers, or internal logs are included.

### Incremental bring-up plan

- [ ] Add portable model tests and complete model registration/checkpoint loading.
- [ ] Validate actual-weight layers and blocks, including production fused MoE and NVFP4 support.
- [ ] Validate a small composed stack, then full-model eager execution and required multi-GPU execution.
- [ ] Qualify chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, overlap scheduling, long contexts, and batching incrementally.
- [ ] Complete end-to-end serving and representative accuracy evaluation, including GSM8K, before marking ready for review.

Known routing/token differences from reduced-model integration remain open follow-up work. This draft does not declare those differences resolved or change numerical acceptance rules. Follow-up progress will be added as coherent commits on this branch.

items.title: [Perf][Model] Cohere2MoE: attention/MoE dual stream, single TP all-reduce per layer, fused add + RMSNorm
items.author: XiaochunTong-Cohere
items.summary: Optimizes Cohere2MoE decode throughput by overlapping attention and MoE computation on separate CUDA streams, merging TP all-reduces, and fusing all-reduce with RMSNorm.
items.body:
## Overview

This PR makes Cohere2MoE decode **1.14–1.36× faster** (TPOT) on CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0, with no accuracy change. Measured on the bf16, FP8, and W4A16 checkpoints at TP2 on H100.

Cohere2MoE layers are parallel blocks: attention and the MLP/MoE read the same normed input, and their outputs are summed. The PR makes three changes to that block:
- **Attention/MoE dual stream** (`VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM=1`). During decode, the MLP/MoE runs on a side CUDA stream, overlapping with attention. This accounts for nearly all of the speedup.
- **Single TP all-reduce per layer.** Attention and the MLP are reduced together instead of separately. At TP > 1, the dual stream relies on this: the layer's only collective then runs after the join, so no all-reduce runs on the side stream alongside the main-stream one.
- **vLLM fused add + RMSNorm.** It lets the existing `allreduce_rms` pass fuse that all-reduce with the next layer's norm.

The changes are confined to `cohere2_moe.py`, plus two env vars. Related: #61508 (`swiglu_limit`) edits the MLP/MoE constructors and does not overlap with this PR.

## Claims

- **Dual stream:** decode TPOT improves by 1.14–1.36× across the bf16, FP8, and W4A16 checkpoints at concurrency 1–64.
- **Default path (dual stream off):** up to 1.05× from the single all-reduce and the `allreduce_rms` fusion. The pass goes from `Replaced 0 patterns` to `Replaced 1 patterns` in every compiled subgraph.
- **No quality change:** gsm8k stays within noise. Speculative decoding acceptance is unchanged with both the EAGLE and Eagle3 drafts.
- **No new GPU→CPU syncs:** every dual-stream run passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

## Validation

**Setup:** TP2 on 2×H100 80GB, `--max-model-len 8192`, base 4f49b55c1f unless noted.
- TPOT (ms) comes from `vllm bench serve` on the random dataset, 1024 input / 512 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`.
- Speedup is main TPOT ÷ this PR's TPOT.
- gsm8k is 5-shot over all 1319 questions at concurrency 64; its standard error is about ±0.8 points.
- Each configuration was run once.

**main vs. this PR with dual stream on:**

| Checkpoint | Configuration | gsm8k | TPOT (c=1) | TPOT (c=8) | TPOT (c=32) | TPOT (c=64) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0) (bf16) | main | 0.899 | 4.07 | 7.00 | 10.59 | 14.04 |
| | this PR | 0.898 | 3.04 (**1.34×**) | 5.61 (**1.25×**) | 9.29 (**1.14×**) | 11.97 (**1.17×**) |
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-fp8](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0-fp8) | main | 0.895 | 5.34 | 6.93 | 10.00 | 12.32 |
| | this PR | 0.908 | 4.31 (**1.24×**) | 5.89 (**1.18×**) | 8.80 (**1.14×**) | 10.68 (**1.15×**) |
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-w4a16](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0-w4a16) | main | 0.905 | 4.19 | 5.57 | 8.00 | 10.17 |
| | this PR | 0.908 | 3.07 (**1.36×**) | 4.62 (**1.21×**) | 6.59 (**1.21×**) | 8.93 (**1.14×**) |

After rebasing onto 153a17166e, the bf16 re-run gives main 4.08 / 6.82 / 10.68 / 14.28 ms and this PR 2.82 / 5.67 / 9.15 / 12.71 ms, i.e. 1.45× / 1.20× / 1.17× / 1.12×. gsm8k is 0.899 vs. 0.898.

The FP8 run uses the `VLLM_CUTLASS` MoE backend. W4A16 uses NVFP4 weights; for it, vLLM enables `act_quant` by default rather than `allreduce_rms`, so its gain comes from the single all-reduce and the dual stream only.

**Speculative decoding** (bf16, 3 speculative tokens). Acceptance is aggregated over gsm8k at concurrency 64 (1319 questions) and concurrency 1 (100 questions).

| Draft | Configuration | Acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-eagle](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0-eagle) (EAGLE) | main | 0.503 | 2.510 |
| | this PR | 0.503 | 2.508 |
| [North-Mini-Code-1.0-EAGLE3](https://huggingface.co/AlexWortega/North-Mini-Code-1.0-EAGLE3) (Eagle3, community) | main | 0.289 | 1.868 |
| | this PR | 0.290 | 1.869 |
| | this PR, aux states with the residual dropped (negative control) | 0.005 | 1.016 |

The Eagle3 draft reads aux hidden states from layers 2/24/46, which is the path the residual-flow change touches. The negative control confirms that this comparison catches a broken aux capture.

**Unit tests:** `tests/models/test_cohere2_moe_parallel_block.py` runs in the CPU "Basic Models Other" job. It covers:
- the deferred-reduction decision and the single all-reduce;
- the residual flow across layers;
- Eagle3 aux capture under in-place residual updates;
- dual-stream gating and its inline fallbacks;
- a CUDA side-stream race test.

The race test is skipped on CPU and passes on H100. It fails if the join stops waiting on the side stream.

**Per-commit ablation (bf16):**

| Configuration | gsm8k | TPOT (c=1) | TPOT (c=8) | TPOT (c=32) | TPOT (c=64) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.899 | 4.07 | 7.00 | 10.59 | 14.04 |
| + single all-reduce | 0.900 | 4.05 (1.00×) | 6.67 (1.05×) | 10.43 (1.02×) | 13.73 (1.02×) |
| + fused add + RMSNorm (default path) | 0.899 | 4.02 (1.01×) | 6.81 (1.03×) | 10.54 (1.00×) | 13.42 (1.05×) |
| + dual stream on | 0.898 | 3.04 (1.34×) | 5.61 (1.25×) | 9.29 (1.14×) | 11.97 (1.17×) |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# Default path: drop the env var. Swap in the -fp8 / -w4a16 checkpoint for the quantized rows.
VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
  vllm serve CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0 --served-model-name north-mini-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192

# TPOT, for C in 1 8 32 64
vllm bench serve --model north-mini-code --tokenizer CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts $((C * 8 > 16 ? C * 8 : 16)) --max-concurrency $C --seed 0

# gsm8k
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64

# Speculative decoding: add to the serve command, then read
# vllm:spec_decode_num_{drafts,draft_tokens,accepted_tokens}_total from /metrics.
#   --max-num-seqs 128 --speculative-config \
#   '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "AlexWortega/North-Mini-Code-1.0-EAGLE3", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'

# allreduce_rms matches: compile with debug logging for
# vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.allreduce_rms_fusion and grep "Replaced".

pytest -v tests/models/test_cohere2_moe_parallel_block.py
```
</details>

## Details

**Dual stream.** The MLP/MoE is wrapped in two custom ops, `vllm::cohere2_mlp_fork` and `vllm::cohere2_mlp_join`. They find the layer through the forward context, so Dynamo keeps the stream switch while attention stays the piecewise splitting op.
- Fork runs the MLP on a dedicated side stream. It is separate from `aux_stream()`, which FusedMoE already uses for the shared-expert overlap.
- Join makes the main stream wait for the side stream before the layer's single all-reduce.
- The MLP runs inline instead in these cases:
  - batches above `VLLM_COHERE2_ATTN_MOE_DUAL_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` (default 256);
  - piecewise CUDA graphs, i.e. prefill and mixed batches, since a fork cannot span a graph boundary;
  - breakable CUDA graph capture.

  In practice, the overlap covers full CUDA graph decode and small eager batches.
- The flag is ignored with a warning in these cases:
  - MoE layers that reduce internally under TP;
  - EP all2all MoE;
  - microbatching (DBO), because each layer keeps a single fork/join state;
  - non-CUDA platforms.

**Single all-reduce.** Both branches of the parallel block end in row-parallel partial sums, so a single `all_reduce(attn + mlp)` is equivalent to reducing them separately.
- `o_proj` and the dense MLP now return unreduced outputs.
- A routed-only MoE passes `reduce_results=False` to `FusedMoEFactory` at TP > 1. When FusedMoE has to reduce internally anyway (EP all2all, sequence parallel), `Cohere2Moe.output_is_reduced` records that, and the decoder then reduces only attention.
- MoE layers with shared experts keep their existing internal reduction.

**Fused add + RMSNorm.** The model-local torch `RMSNorm` is replaced with vLLM's `RMSNorm`, using the same residual flow as Llama.
- Each layer returns its reduced block output and the residual separately; the next layer's norm (or the final norm) adds them.
- Eagle3 aux states add the residual back via `EagleModelMixin._maybe_add_hidden_state`.
- The first layer's residual is the embedding tensor itself, and the fused norm updates the residual in place. So the start-layer aux capture is cloned, only when that layer is captured.
- Checkpoints that use Cohere's LayerNorm keep the old flow.

**Limitations**
- The token threshold was tuned without speculative decoding. With speculation, each request adds `1 + k` tokens per step, so the threshold is reached at lower concurrency.

These changes are ported from Cohere's vLLM fork and adapted to current upstream. AI assistance was used in preparing this PR.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

items.title: [RFC][Experimental]: Model- and platform-customized KV cache planning
items.author: ivanium
items.summary: Proposes an experimental pluggable KVCacheConfigBuilder API to let models and platforms define custom KV cache plans instead of relying on core heuristics.
items.body:
**Status:** draft · **PRs:** #53558 (builder, model hook, checks), wangxiyuan/vllm#2 (Qwen3.8 and Kimi-K3 hooks, golden plans) · **Related:** #58638 (grouping with drafters), #42449 / #61452 (KV cache spec refactor) This RFC updates the design of #44276 ("Model customized KVCache Planning"). The design changed substantially during review of #53558, so we track it here as a separate RFC; #44276 keeps the earlier discussion. Design doc with comments: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZnTISAsNuP9qNsbpF4FIPGPsYd_5TbdaBTrVhpW0N4A/edit?tab=t.v32av17qd6tq ## TL;DR We currently heavily rely on a heuristic-based KV cache grouping method in core, `get_kv_cache_groups()`, for every model. The heuristic still works so far, but new hybrid models, drafters, cache precisions and platforms will likely add further complexities to this method. Some examples: quite a few new models changed it (DSV4, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DSV4.1-Flash); a drafter can re-cut a whole model (Kimi-K3 + DSpark: 4 → 20 groups); and vllm-ascend monkey-patches about 680 lines of vLLM to use its own DSV4 plan. This RFC proposes an **experimental** pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` API, which lets models and platforms own their KV cache plan, while core keeps the planning flow and checks every plan: | part | who | what | where | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | builder | platform | overrides grouping and placement | #53558 | | grouping hook | model | returns the model's KV cache groups | #53558 | | checks | core | rejects a malformed plan at startup, from any source | #53558 | | golden plans | tests | one readable plan file per model | wangxiyuan/vllm#2 | The APIs are experimental: their signatures can change, in particular when #61452 changes the KV cache group data structure. Non-goals: for models where the existing heuristic already works well, we don't change anything. The API is mainly for (1) new model and speculator support and (2) platform customization for now. --- ## 1. The problem Currently, we heavily rely on the heuristic-based `get_kv_cache_groups()` in vLLM core for all models, especially recent hybrid models. We see these issues. ### 1.1 Models Recent models, such as DSV4, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and DSV4.1-Flash, have complex architectures: 1. More than three types of `KVCacheSpec`: full attention / MLA, SWA, linear attention / Mamba state, circular buffer, etc. 2. Different precisions for layers. DSV4 has an fp8 main KV cache, but the indexer cache can be fp4 or fp8. This is not only a memory question: precision changes the page size, and the page size decides the grouping. On DSV4.1-Flash, an mxfp4 indexer changes the plan from 7 groups to 9, although the SWA layers did not change: ``` packed layout: block size = widest group (main MLA + indexer pages) fp8 indexer: block 135,168 B → 8 SWA pages fit → 40 SWA layers / 8 = 5 groups mxfp4 indexer: block 114,688 B → 6 SWA pages fit → 40 SWA layers / 6 = 7 groups ``` 3. Different speculators. A drafter can use MLA or GQA, with or without SWA. In many cases its layers cannot merge with the target layers, so they form a new bucket. The heuristic sizes all groups by the smallest bucket, so a small draft bucket re-cuts every target group: ``` Kimi-K3: buckets [69 KDA, 24 MLA] group size 24 → 4 groups Kimi-K3 + DSpark: buckets [69 KDA, 24 MLA, 5 SWA] group size 5 → 20 groups ``` For many models, like Kimi-K3, Qwen3.5/3.6 and MiMo-V2.5, adding a DSpark/DFlash drafter blows up the groups from a few to 20 or more (Qwen3.5-27B + DFlash: 70). Each group prepares its own attention metadata every step, so this eats much of the drafter's speedup. #58638 has the measurements and improves the heuristic for these cases. ### 1.2 Features Additionally, there are new features that make KV cache grouping and planning more complex: 1. Different KV cache layouts: block-major or layer-major, for example. The layout is chosen before grouping and selects the grouping algorithm (block-major packs pages of different sizes into one block; layer-major first makes all page sizes equal). So a grouping decision depends on a placement decision. 2. HiSparse, which optionally keeps the indexer KV in GPU HBM but offloads the main attention KV. It adds layers that the model does not have and a second (host) memory pool, and today it is a separate branch inside the heuristic. 3. Speculators that add a hidden-state cache. This exists: the hidden-state extraction method adds one hidden-state cache layer, and the heuristic has a special case to keep it in its own group. ### 1.3 Parallelism and P/D In addition, we need to handle different parallelism, and P/D with heterogeneous TP: * TP can partition some specs but not others (like MLA). Each spec must declare this correctly; a missing declaration once changed a drafter's grouping (#59733). * P/D disaggregation with heterogeneous TP requires the same KV cache grouping on P and D: NIXL sends block IDs as one list per group and pairs the lists by position. This is implicitly assumed today, but not enforced: the NIXL compatibility hash does not include the grouping. With custom plans, P and D can more easily end up with different plans, for example when one side runs a platform builder and the other does not. ### 1.4 Why one heuristic does not scale All of these create uncertainties for the heuristic. They also make day-0 model support harder: a new model must modify the heuristic to match the grouping plan it has in mind, while being careful not to break other models. In practice, DSV4, Kimi-K3, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DSV4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash each changed core planning, and most of them needed follow-up fixes. The heuristic now has checks by model name, and it finds draft layers by guessing from layer positions. This also makes adding speculators tricky: a speculator can silently change the KV cache grouping plan and add a high metadata preparation cost. In other words, the KV cache grouping plan is implicit and error-prone. It is also hard for other (non-NVIDIA) platforms to use their own KV cache grouping and allocation plans. For example, vllm-ascend uses a different plan for DSV4-Pro (it groups layers into tuples and pads SWA pages to the MLA page size), and it has to monkey-patch vLLM to make that plan work. ## 2. Goals vLLM core: 1. Hooks that allow platforms and each model to customize KV cache planning. Platform overrides come at a higher priority. The APIs are general enough to cover all the cases above. 2. vLLM core stays stable and robust. 1. Stable: a day-0 model does not need to modify the core heuristic to get a new grouping plan, and all its changes stay in the model's directory. 2. Robust: vLLM core detects a malformed custom plan and rejects it at startup. Platforms and models: 1. The grouping logic is simple and intuitive. A model can directly define its groups and their roles (e.g., "full", "SWA1", "SWA2", "compressor state"). 2. The logic stays in Python to be generic. A static, structured form of each plan (YAML) is generated for humans and agents to read: the "golden" KV cache plan. 3. Tests check whether a commit, for example a new speculator, changes a grouping plan. The change becomes explicit in review instead of a silent regression. Non-goals: worker-driven allocation (#42449); several memory pools in the builder interface (HiSparse stays in core); custom schedulers, prefix-cache coordinators or admission rules. ## 3. Design ### 3.1 Overview Core keeps one planning flow, and no plugin can change it. Plugins make only two decisions: how to group the layers, and how to place a list of groups in memory for a given number of blocks.

*Figure 1: Core runs the planning flow and calls the builder for grouping and placement. The gold box is future work.* The flow, once at startup: merge the specs of all workers → group → check → project the groups onto each PP stage → find the number of blocks (block-count override, automatic max model length, admission check) → place each worker's KV cache → reduce all ranks to the same number of blocks. Memory profiling at startup uses the same builder. Keeping the flow in core matters, because the steps after grouping (PP projection, memory accounting, the block-count override, cross-rank agreement) must behave the same for every model and platform. vllm-ascend's patches today copy and change parts of this flow; with the builder, they only make the two decisions. PP also needs nothing new: core projects any plan onto the stages, whatever its source. ### 3.2 Platforms: the builder A platform selects a builder class (`Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls`). The builder has two methods: ```python class KVCacheConfigBuilder: def get_kv_cache_groups(self, vllm_config, kv_cache_spec) -> list[KVCacheGroupSpec]: ... def get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(self, vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, num_blocks) -> KVCacheConfig: ... ``` The default builder calls the model hook if the model has one, else the core heuristic. A platform builder that overrides grouping has priority; it reaches the model hook only through `super()`. Core finds the bytes per block by asking the builder to place one block, so a platform with a different placement does not need to compute memory separately. A plan that depends on the hardware belongs here. vllm-ascend's DSV4 plan is one: its grouping (layer tuples, padded SWA pages) and its placement depend on each other, so both decisions should come from one shared function in the builder. vllm-ascend#18359 moves the Ascend plans into a builder and removes most of the patches. ### 3.3 Models: the grouping hook A model class can implement `SupportsKVCacheGrouping` and return its groups directly: ```python class SupportsKVCacheGrouping(Protocol): @classmethod def get_kv_cache_groups(cls, vllm_config, kv_cache_spec) -> list[KVCacheGroupSpec]: ... ``` The model author knows the architecture, so the hook states the intended grouping instead of hoping the heuristic finds it. Two examples: **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.** Its 48 layers repeat a period of 4: three GDN (linear attention) layers and one QSA layer. A QSA layer has three caches: the main cache, a compressed key cache and a raw key ring. One replicated PLE state also exists. The hook returns 6 groups: | group | layers | why apart | | :---- | :---- | :---- | | GDN, position 0 | layers 0, 4, …, 44 | one group per position in the period | | GDN, position 1 | layers 1, 5, …, 45 | | | GDN, position 2 | layers 2, 6, …, 46 | | | PLE state | layer 1 | replicated across TP, the GDN state is sharded | | QSA raw key ring | layers 3, 7, …, 47 | scratch ring, not prefix-cached | | QSA main + compressed keys | layers 3, 7, …, 47 | share one block table | This is the same plan the heuristic gives today; the hook makes it explicit, so a change in the heuristic cannot change it. **Kimi-K3 + DSpark.** The hook groups the target layers as if there were no drafter, and puts the 5 draft layers in a group of their own: 4 + 1 groups instead of 20. This is only an example. The better fix is in the core heuristic, which RFC #58638 and its PRs (#58207, #58380) improve for drafters. The point is that a hook can unblock a model first, without waiting for a core change, and the hook can go away when core catches up. Three rules for hook authors, learned from these two hooks: 1. **Group in the layout's terms.** On a layer-major layout, all groups must have one page size. The first Kimi-K3 hook made the page sizes equal for target and draft layers separately, so the plan had two page sizes, and core rejected it at startup. The hook can reuse core's helpers: make page sizes equal over all layers first, then split. 2. **Work on any subset of layers.** During startup profiling, a worker calls the hook with only its own PP stage's layers. 3. **Keep the hook a function of the config and the specs.** Then the golden plan (§3.5) captures its behavior. ### 3.4 Checks Core checks every plan right after grouping, from any source (heuristic, model hook, platform builder), and stops startup with an error that names the problem: 1. Every layer is in exactly one group. 2. For a group whose layers have different specs, the group's spec describes exactly the group's layers. Placement problems also stop startup: core places one block with the builder before it computes the number of blocks, so a plan that the layout cannot hold fails there (this is how the first Kimi-K3 hook failed). Core cannot check more than the structure. It cannot compare a group's spec with the merge of its layers' specs, because core itself changes specs during grouping (it pads pages and changes block sizes). And it cannot judge whether a valid plan is a good plan, for example whether 20 groups are too many. That is the job of the golden plans. ### 3.5 Golden plans Each model has one plan file that shows its KV cache grouping in a readable form. A GPU script starts the real engine for each case (real model config, dummy weights), records the plan through the platform builder and the model hook, and checks that every worker received its part. The script writes the file; nobody edits it by hand. A PR that changes a grouping includes the new plan, so reviewers see the change as a diff. Part of the Kimi-K3 plan: ``` cases: tp1: {structure: tp1, groups: 4} tp4: {structure: tp1, groups: 4} tp1-dspark: {structure: tp1-dspark, groups: 5} structures: tp1-dspark: - kind: MambaSpec layers: ['language_model.model.layers.{0-88:4}.self_attn'] # ... two more MambaSpec (KDA) groups and one MLA group, as in tp1 - kind: SlidingWindowSpec sliding_window: 2048 layers: ['model.layers.{93-97}.self_attn.attn'] ``` A plan records only the grouping decision: which layers share a block table, the spec type of each group, and flags that are not default (for example, eagle group or host memory). Every grouping source produces exactly this, so one format covers all of them. The file has no bytes, block sizes, page sizes or block counts. A file lists each distinct plan once and maps cases to it (above, `tp1` and `tp4` share one plan), and it writes layer ranges compactly (`{0-88:4}` is layers 0, 4, …, 88). CPU tests read only the plan files and check two rules across cases: tensor parallelism does not change the grouping, and a speculator keeps the target grouping. These rules are policies, not laws. A precision change, for example, changes the grouping on purpose (§1.1). So each known exception is listed with its reason, for example DSV4.1 + DSpark. For now, a plan is a reviewed snapshot, not a formal spec, for three reasons: 1. **The plan depends on inputs the file does not record.** The grouping depends on page sizes, and page sizes depend on the GPU, the attention backend and the KV cache layout. The current plans come from GB200; Hopper can give different plans. A formal spec would have to name these inputs, and the file would no longer be simple. 2. **The format follows an experimental API.** #61452 will change the group data structure, and a versioned schema now would freeze choices that will change. 3. **Nothing regenerates the plans yet.** No CI job runs the GPU script, so a plan can drift from the code. As a first step, each case should record the layout it was made with, because the layout selects the grouping algorithm. A versioned schema and a CI job that regenerates the plans on GPUs (first optional, then gating) are future work. ## 4. Future work - **Core knows the draft layers.** The worker knows which layers belong to the drafter, but sends core only the specs. If it also sent the draft layer names, core could group target and draft layers apart by default (as the Kimi-K3 hook does today) and mark eagle groups exactly, instead of guessing from layer positions. - **Explicit P/D grouping match.** When a model or platform customizes the grouping, P and D can compare their plans when they connect, and reject a mismatch. This would also be the first reader of plans outside the tests, which is the point where a versioned plan format becomes necessary. - **Golden plans in CI.** Regenerate the plans on GPUs in CI, first as an optional step, then as a gate once its runtime and stability are known. ## 5. Alternatives considered | alternative | why not | | :---- | :---- | | Only improve the heuristic (#58207, #58380) | Helps every model and should land, but platforms still cannot use their own placement, and each new model still has to fit one shared heuristic. | | A role per layer instead of full groups (core builds the groups from the roles) | It hides layout details from the hook, but it is less direct and less general than stating the groups, and core would still decide the final grouping. | | A YAML file as the model's input | YAML cannot see spec properties (TP replication, precision) or draft layers, which exist only at runtime. YAML is the right output, not input. |
