items.title: [Feat] logging: Add flag to redact request tokens from logs
items.author: ishankaul1
items.summary: In some production scenarios, especially under zero-data-retention requirements, prompt and output data should never reach logs. prints the token ids, the sampling params and the grammar.
items.body:
## Motivation

In some production scenarios, especially under zero-data-retention requirements, prompt and output data should never reach logs. `Req.__repr__` prints the token ids, the sampling params and the grammar. A couple of places format a `Req` into a log line or error message, including the scheduler watchdog dump and an assertion in the grammar manager.

## Modifications

When `SGLANG_REDACT_REQUEST_DATA=1` is set, `Req.__repr__` prints only the rid and the input and output lengths, and the server refuses to start with `--log-requests`, `--crash-dump-folder` or `--log-level debug`. The default is unchanged. Putting the flag in the repr covers every call site with one small change. The PR also adds unit tests and a docs entry.

If you would prefer this on by default whenever `--log-requests` is off, happy to switch it.

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint is routed to the MXFP4 expert path and fails in fused MoE
items.author: micahtyong
items.summary: The first MoE forward pass then fails in the fused-MoE runner with: Setting works around it. (, DSV4 branch) defaults to (default ) and only overrides it when returns a bool. [Discussion: Thank you for the detailed report and root-cause analysis.]
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version (checked by reading `main` at 8e3f11b).
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

A DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint whose routed experts are stored in BF16 (for example, one exported from a training framework, with no `quantization_config` in `config.json`) is treated as an MXFP4-expert checkpoint. The first MoE forward pass then fails in the fused-MoE runner with:

```
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
```

Setting `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0` works around it.

Cause, from reading `main`:

1. `ModelConfig` (`configs/model_config.py`, DSV4 branch) defaults `is_fp4_experts` to `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS` (default `True`) and only overrides it when `try_detect_fp4_experts` returns a bool.
2. `try_detect_fp4_experts` (`configs/deepseek_v4.py`) returns `True` for `U8/I8/F4`, `False` for `F8_E4M3`, and `None` for anything else, including `BF16`. A BF16 checkpoint therefore keeps `is_fp4_experts=True`.
3. `arg_groups/model_overrides/deepseek_v4.py` selects `moe_runner_backend="flashinfer_mxfp4"` on SM90/SM100/SM120 when the backend is `auto`.
4. The checkpoint has no quantization config, so `quant_config` is `None` and the `TopK` built in `models/deepseek_v2.py` gets `is_fp4_experts=False`. In `layers/moe/topk.py`, `is_flashinfer_mxfp4() and not self.is_fp4_experts` selects `TopKOutputFormat.BYPASSED`.
5. The unquantized MoE path unpacks the top-k output as `topk_weights, topk_ids, _ = topk_output` (e.g. `moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py`), but `BypassedTopKOutput` has five fields.

Possible fix: have `try_detect_fp4_experts` return `False` for unquantized dtypes (`BF16`, `F16`, `F32`), or force `is_fp4_experts=False` when the checkpoint has no quantization config.

### Reproduction

Any DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint whose routed-expert weights (`*.experts.<i>.w1.weight`, etc.) are BF16 and whose `config.json` has no `quantization_config`, launched with default MoE settings on SM90/SM100:

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/deepseek-v4-bf16 --tp 8
```

The first request fails as above. The same command with `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0` serves correctly.

### Environment

Observed on 8x B300 with an SGLang build based on v0.5.21. The code path above is unchanged on current `main`.
discussion: Thank you for the detailed report and root-cause analysis. I'd like to take this one — I'll open a PR with a fix shortly.

The fix is up in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44813 — `try_detect_fp4_experts` now returns `False` for unquantized routed-expert dtypes (BF16/F16/F32), so these checkpoints take the unquantized expert path instead of falling back to the FP4-experts env default. Genuine MXFP4 and FP8 detection is unchanged, and unknown/unreadable headers still fall back to the user default.

items.title: [Performance][MiniMax-M3] Tune SM100 sparse decode
items.author: wolfcomos
items.summary: Tune MiniMax-M3 Triton sparse decode on SM100 by choosing the KV-block split count from the GPU's SM count and supporting non-power-of-two splits. Keep BF16 operands by default, with optional FP16 dot operands through.
items.body:
## Overview

Tune MiniMax-M3 Triton sparse decode on SM100 by choosing the KV-block split count from the GPU's SM count and supporting non-power-of-two splits. Keep BF16 operands by default, with optional FP16 dot operands through `AttentionConfig`.

**Draft blocker:** default BF16 fails the predeclared local GSM8K regression bound: 94.4655% versus baseline 95.4511% (−0.9856 percentage points; allowed loss 0.5 points). Opt-in FP16 passes at 95.5269%. A separate baseline repeat reproduced all 1,319 output token sequences exactly. The BF16 regression needs investigation before merge.

## Claims

- Reuse the existing decode and merge kernels; target two CTAs per SM and mask padded merge lanes.
- Keep the original split policy in batch-invariant mode and on other GPU architectures. Scalar KV scales retain their original placement; prefill and CUTLASS decode are unchanged.

## Validation

Measured candidate: `a450316f26fcff8f5715e51c444cd272b9cad12a`; baseline: `9731f30a030c545e7f29a8a4ed96b8562be12c88`. Current head `4df6ebd262af62f984626f7b9bb5c5179b7def28` only renames the kernel constexpr to `USE_FP16_DOT`; normalized AST and changed-file pre-commit checks pass. GPU measurements below remain pinned to the measured candidate.

[Validation supplement: exact scripts, source snapshots, measurements and reproduction commands](https://github.com/wolfcomos/vllm/tree/2c5dfae05cb32d8e8329baa8d2be43aa2d4d4045). This separate artifact branch adds no files to the production PR. Measurements used a development runtime; identical binaries may not be publicly available. The supplement records public runtime identifiers and native-wheel provenance.

**Original tests:** full, unfiltered runs on GB200; all pass. Original case IDs are preserved and the 46 skips have identical ROCm-only reasons. Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including Ruff and mypy, pass.

| Test file | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| `attention/test_minimax_m3.py` | 125 pass / 46 skip | 133 pass / 46 skip |
| `test_minimax_m3_sparse_attn_fp8_scale.py` | 4 pass | 14 pass |
| `attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py` | 3 pass | 3 pass |
| `attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py` | 49 pass | 49 pass |

<details>
<summary>Original test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_sparse_attn_fp8_scale.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py
```

</details>

No CI files changed. Existing B200 CI covers the main attention file; the new SM100 cases in the FP8-scale file were validated manually on GB200, since that file's explicit CI entries currently target ROCm.

**GSM8K:** all three primary 1,319-question runs completed using `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` revision `901464083161bf8612a29ff7ad29914cd4ab4a85`, FP8 KV cache, TP4 on four GB200 GPUs, eager MRV1, and Triton sparse decode. Baseline, default BF16, and opt-in FP16 use identical five-shot prompts, greedy decoding, seed 42, disabled thinking, max output 1024 tokens, and batch limit 40. NVFP4 refers to model weights; the attention KV cache remains FP8.

| Revision / mode | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid / truncated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 1259 / 1319 | 95.4511% | 0 / 0 |
| Candidate BF16 | 1246 / 1319 | 94.4655% | 0 / 0 |
| Candidate FP16 | 1260 / 1319 | 95.5269% | 0 / 0 |
| Baseline repeat (diagnostic) | 1259 / 1319 | 95.4511% | 0 / 0 |

BF16 loses 28 previously correct answers and gains 15; FP16 loses 16 and gains 17. The primary comparison fails because of BF16. The 0.5-point bound is a predeclared local criterion, not an upstream CI threshold. The diagnostic repeat has byte-identical predictions and matching dispatch histograms; it does not replace the original baseline. A validation-only worker hook seeds the exact baseline FlashInfer tuning JSONs into each candidate's resolved cache directory; all files remain byte-identical, with no retuning. Actual per-rank dispatch confirms the changed split policy and requested dot precision.

<details>
<summary>Kernel measurements and correctness coverage</summary>

**Kernel performance:** all 24 synthetic shapes pass reference and CUDA-graph checks. Complete decode + merge on GB200 (152 SMs), warm CUDA graphs, 32 calls per graph, four replays, seven rotated paired rounds. The 21 scalar-FP8 shapes use BF16 Q/output, FP8 E4M3 KV, 16 Q heads / one KV head, head dimension 128, context 4096, page size 128, top-k 16, and K/V scales 0.3/0.7. Three controls cover absent scales, per-token scales, and BF16 KV. Times exclude compilation and serving overhead.

| Batch | Query length | Baseline µs | BF16 µs | FP16 µs | BF16 speedup [range] | FP16 speedup [range] |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 6.730 | 6.805 | 7.123 | 0.989× [0.988–0.992] | 0.945× [0.943–0.950] |
| 17 | 1 | 13.662 | 9.697 | 9.588 | 1.410× [1.407–1.412] | 1.424× [1.424–1.431] |
| 40 | 1 | 23.054 | 20.159 | 19.919 | 1.144× [1.142–1.145] | 1.159× [1.156–1.159] |
| 1 | 4 | 7.329 | 7.238 | 7.895 | 1.013× [1.010–1.014] | 0.928× [0.927–0.933] |
| 9 | 4 | 22.505 | 15.263 | 15.077 | 1.475× [1.473–1.476] | 1.493× [1.492–1.494] |
| 9 | 8 | 38.637 | 24.036 | 23.696 | 1.608× [1.607–1.609] | 1.631× [1.630–1.633] |

Speedups are medians of paired ratios; brackets give the seven-round min–max. Across all 24 shapes, BF16 ranges from 0.989–1.608× and FP16 from 0.928–1.631×; small-batch regressions remain. Two control cases exercise BF16 dtype fallback. FP16 adds little beyond split tuning in most scalar-scale cases. These are operator measurements, not end-to-end throughput claims.

An additional 38 cases pass FP32-reference, graph-replay, batch-invariant, layout, invalid-block, and dtype-fallback checks, including active rows in padded batches. Four separate E4M3/E5M2 regression cases verify finite FP16 saturation with large scalar scales. Runtime: CUDA 13.5, PyTorch 2.15 development build, Triton 3.6.0 (`3362bc8c`).

</details>

## Details

The old heuristic targets 256 CTAs and rounds the split count down to a power of two. The new SM100 policy uses the actual SM count, while the merge masks any padded reduction lanes. For example, on a 152-SM GB200 with 16 selected blocks and one KV head, batch 40 / query length 1 uses six splits instead of four (240 instead of 160 CTAs). Host planning uses vLLM's integer `cdiv` helper.

Enable FP16 with `--attention-config '{"minimax_m3_msa_decode_fp16_dot": true}'`. It applies to SM100 Triton decode with BF16 queries and FP8 KV, absent or scalar scales, and batch-invariant mode disabled. Accumulation stays FP32. Split changes can change reduction rounding; FP16 also changes operand precision and clamps Q and scaled K/V to the finite FP16 range.

**Related work:** scalar-scale folding is covered by #52060 and is excluded here. #56932 adds SM120 page splitting and an SM103/SM120 single-page path while retaining the general split heuristic. #55372 explores query-tiled speculative verification; this PR retains the existing per-query decode kernel.

Derived from [97e0532](https://github.com/xinli-sw/vllm/commit/97e0532d95bf0863376b0e4d57a23f3d9cc2c597) and [5c353c3](https://github.com/xinli-sw/vllm/commit/5c353c3c0a3e7b0bf8134a162dada99ebd648601). items.title: [Feat] tracing: Record detokenizer time on root spans
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: Time spent in the detokenizer is invisible in traces. It sits between the scheduler's spans and the tokenizer's, so it shows up as unexplained latency between them.
items.body:
## Motivation

Time spent in the detokenizer is invisible in traces. It sits between the scheduler's spans and the tokenizer's, so it shows up as unexplained latency between them.

## Modifications

- With tracing on (`--enable-trace`), `DetokenizerManager.handle_batch_token_id_out` times each batch it handles, from the start of decoding (beam-search and standard) until the output is built, and sends the duration in a new `BatchStrOutput.detokenize_duration` field. The field is `None` when tracing is off.
- `TokenizerManager._handle_batch_output` adds the duration to every request in the batch, and `set_finished_time` puts two attributes on the root span:
  - `detokenize.total_ms`: summed time of the batches that carried the request (each request waits for its whole batch);
  - `detokenize.batches`: number of those batches.
- Multi-tokenizer routing copies the per-batch duration into every sub-batch: `_handle_output_by_index`, plus a `_PER_BATCH_FIELDS` exception in the generic `_handle_output_by_indices`, which would otherwise call `len()` on the float and fail.

Root-span attributes rather than a span per batch keep the span count unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

With tracing off, the duration isn't sent, so the cost is one `perf_counter` read and a few branches. Measured with `timeit` (Xeon 8375C, Python 3.11):

| Where | Cost, tracing off |
| --- | --- |
| Detokenizer, per batch | ~55 ns |
| Tokenizer, per batch | ~30-70 ns |
| Tokenizer, per request | ~3 ns |

## Tests

- `test_req_time_stats.py::test_sums_detokenize_time_over_the_batches_that_carried_the_request`, which also checks that a request no batch carried gets no attributes.
- `test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py::test_split_keeps_the_batch_detokenize_duration` (single and grouped split).
- Existing tests that run `handle_batch_token_id_out` (`test_output_decode.py`, `test_trim_matched_stop.py`) pass.
- End to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, spans exported to Jaeger): a 32-token streamed chat request recorded `detokenize.batches=10`, `detokenize.total_ms≈0.9` on a regular TP=2 server, and the same on the decode root under PD disaggregation.
- `test/registered/unit/observability`, `managers` and `disaggregation` fail the same tests as `main` and no others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed: no new setting; the attributes appear when tracing is on.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable: no model-output change; overhead above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Fix] minimax-h3: validate sigma shift scales before loading weights
items.author: fusheng-ji
items.summary: fetched the checkpoint first and only then parsed with a bare. On the real MiniMax-H3 index this accepted, and the string (silently turned into 12.0).
items.body:
## Motivation

`MiniMaxH3Pipeline._load_config` fetched the checkpoint first (`maybe_download_model`) and only then parsed `_minimax_h3.sigma_shift_scales` with a bare `float()`. On the real MiniMax-H3 index this accepted `-12.0`, `NaN` and the string `"12"` (silently turned into 12.0). The request-time timestep stage rejects non-positive values, but only after the whole model has loaded, and then for every request.

## Modifications

- Add `validate_minimax_h3_sigma_shift_scales` (`configs/minimax_h3_metadata.py`), which requires a positive finite number (not a bool) for both modalities. It is shared by the full release metadata parser (`.../minimax_h3/release_metadata.py`) and a new `_preflight_model_config` hook.
- `composed_pipeline_base.py` / `minimax_h3_pipeline.py`: the hook runs before the weights are fetched. It is a no-op for other pipelines. For H3 it reads `model_index.json` from the selected partition, or the overlay metadata for the FastH3 and VDN-H3 source repositories, without downloading any weights.
- `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_metadata.py`: invalid values are rejected before any weight download for the plain, FastH3 and VDN-H3 pipelines, local and remote; the parser rejects bad values before float coercion; the selected index matches the weight directory and revision; a missing or damaged index does not fall back to a weight download; other pipelines do not fetch metadata.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit: `test_minimax_h3_metadata.py` 7 passed, 68 subtests passed. Without the fix the new tests fail.

Real MiniMax-H3 FL2VA checkpoint, TP2 on 2 x B200, t2va, 4 s, 50 steps, seed 42. Server runs on this branch head, on a merge of the three H3 fixes (this PR, the VAE tile validation and the sigma preflight), and on unpatched `main` (`2948662026`).

**Regression** (bit-identical, so no frame comparison is shown; unpatched `main` vs this branch merged with the other two H3 fixes). Frame difference is 0 at every sampled pixel, and the video/audio latents and mp4 match bit for bit:

| | unpatched `main` | merged fixes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| video latent `[1,24,32,48,84]` + audio latent `[2,32,178]`, sha256 prefix | `e3f82e7f2006` | `e3f82e7f2006` |
| decoded mp4 (107 frames, 768x1344), sha256 prefix | `d7ffac37f960` | `d7ffac37f960` |
| max abs pixel difference, frames 0 / 53 / 106 | - | 0 / 0 / 0 |


**Bad `sigma_shift_scales.video`** (copy of the real checkpoint with only `model_index.json` changed, everything else symlinked to the real weights):

| value | unpatched `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| real (number) | generates | generates, bit-identical |
| `-12.0` | server loads all weights (312 s to healthy), every request then fails: `model sigma_shift_scales.video must be a positive finite number` | startup `ValueError: model_index.json._minimax_h3.sigma_shift_scales.video must be a positive finite number`, before weights are fetched |
| `NaN` | same as `-12.0` | same startup error |
| `"12"` (string) | server starts and generates, value silently read as 12.0 | same startup error |

When the problem is reported (measured, same job group; on the exact final head with all three fixes merged, `-12.0` fails at startup after 119 s):

| value | unpatched `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-12.0` | healthy at 255.1 s, request fails after 5.2 s (260.3 s) | startup error at 124 s |
| `NaN` | healthy at 249.1 s, request fails after 5.2 s (254.3 s) | startup error at 135 s |
| `"12"` | healthy at 252.1 s, request completes in 35.2 s with the value read as 12.0 | startup error at 130 s |

![time to report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/423113d8a26b0cda0e5b8586899655c2be2514db/minimax-h3-sigma-time.png)

Times are seconds from server start. For `main`, healthy time and request time come from the harness; for this branch, the time is the timestamp of the startup error in the server log relative to the first log line (a few seconds after process start). The branch's process then takes about 1.5-2 more minutes to exit (existing shutdown behaviour), which is not counted. Weights were warm in the page cache, so the saving here is the rest of the load plus the failing request; for a remote repository it would also include the download. Run-to-run load time varies (main healthy in 249-312 s across these runs).

Calling `_load_config()` directly on the real `model_index.json`: `main` accepts all three values, and for `-12.0` only reaches a verdict after the weight-fetch call; this branch rejects each in about 0.002 s without calling it.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a performance change. The fix only touches the failure path / load-time validation; the regression run below produced bit-identical output, but latency was not measured.

The benefit on a local checkpoint is small (weights were already in the page cache, so loading took 25-40 s); for a remote repository the saving is the weight download, which was not measured.

Limitations: the preflight rejects quoted numbers such as `"12"`, which the old code accepted. The real checkpoint uses numbers and is unaffected, but a third-party `model_index.json` that stores the scales as strings will go from loading to failing. The FastH3 / VDN-H3 overlay and remote-download paths are covered by mocked unit tests only. Only the FL2VA partition, t2va, TP2 and one prompt/seed were run on real weights.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable: no option or documented behaviour changes.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Accuracy only; this is a correctness fix and no speed measurement was made.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Fix] minimax-h3: validate VAE tile settings
items.author: fusheng-ji
items.summary: The H3 video VAE splits frames into tiles of with at least overlap and stitches them back in pixel and latent coordinates. Nothing validated the two values, so on the real checkpoint: - made loop forever, and the request hung in the decoding stage after denois…
items.body:
## Motivation

The H3 video VAE splits frames into tiles of `vae_tile_size` with at least `vae_tile_overlap_min` overlap and stitches them back in pixel and latent coordinates. Nothing validated the two values, so on the real checkpoint:

- `vae_tile_overlap_min >= vae_tile_size` made `split_tiles` loop forever, and the request hung in the decoding stage after denoising had finished;
- a tile size that is not a multiple of the spatial compression ratio (16) failed only at the end of decoding with `decoded frames 736x1280 smaller than target canvas 768x1344`.

## Modifications

- `configs/models/vaes/minimax_h3_contract.py`, `minimax_h3_video.py` and `runtime/models/vaes/minimax_h3_video_vae/klvae.py`: reject non-positive or non-integer values, an overlap that is not smaller than the tile, and values that are not multiples of the compression ratio. The check runs both when the VAE config is post-processed and when the tiled-decoding settings are applied, so a bad config fails when the VAE loads.
- `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_vae_tiling.py`: invalid values at both entry points, and valid settings that reconstruct the pixel and latent canvases exactly.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit: `test_minimax_h3_vae_tiling.py` 2 passed, 60 subtests passed. Without the fix the new tests fail.

Real MiniMax-H3 FL2VA checkpoint, TP2 on 2 x B200, t2va, 4 s, 50 steps, seed 42. Server runs on this branch head, on a merge of the three H3 fixes (this PR, the VAE tile validation and the sigma preflight), and on unpatched `main` (`2948662026`).

**Regression** (bit-identical, so no frame comparison is shown; unpatched `main` vs this branch merged with the other two H3 fixes). Frame difference is 0 at every sampled pixel, and the video/audio latents and mp4 match bit for bit:

| | unpatched `main` | merged fixes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| video latent `[1,24,32,48,84]` + audio latent `[2,32,178]`, sha256 prefix | `e3f82e7f2006` | `e3f82e7f2006` |
| decoded mp4 (107 frames, 768x1344), sha256 prefix | `d7ffac37f960` | `d7ffac37f960` |
| max abs pixel difference, frames 0 / 53 / 106 | - | 0 / 0 / 0 |


**Tile settings** (video latent shape unchanged, 768x1344 output):

| setting | unpatched `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default 256 / 64 | mp4 `d7ffac37f960` | mp4 `d7ffac37f960` (identical) |
| 128 / 32 (valid) | mp4 `a7acbf523d2d` | mp4 `a7acbf523d2d` (identical to `main`, differs from default) |
| overlap == tile (256 / 256) | denoising finishes, then decoding hangs until the 900 s request timeout | `vae_tile_overlap_min must be less than vae_tile_size, got 256 >= 256` raised while loading the VAE |
| tile 250 | fails after denoising: `decoded frames 736x1280 smaller than target canvas 768x1344` | `vae_tile_size must be a multiple of the spatial compression ratio (16), got 250` raised while loading the VAE |

The 128 / 32 setting does take effect, and the same output comes from `main` and from this branch (max pixel difference 0 at frames 0, 53, 106). Native-resolution crop of frame 53, default tiling vs 128 / 32; the smaller tiles give visibly blockier shading, which is a property of that setting, not of this change:

![tiling crop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/063f509fd4a5d9812fd7933cc2147db045ec244d/minimax-h3-tile.png)

| tile 250 | healthy at 258.1 s, request fails after 35.2 s (total 293.3 s) | startup error at 144 s |

![time to report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/423113d8a26b0cda0e5b8586899655c2be2514db/minimax-h3-vae-time.png)

Run-to-run load time varies (main healthy in 249-312 s across these runs).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a performance change. The fix only touches the failure path / load-time validation; the regression run below produced bit-identical output, but latency was not measured.

items.title: [Fix] minimax-h3: fix AdaLN cache slot leak on preparation failure
items.author: fusheng-ji
items.summary: reserves one slab slot per missing plan, then embeds the timesteps, writes them and queries the tensor-parallel layout. Only the checkpoint projection that follows sat inside the rollback guard, so a failure in any earlier step left the reserved slots in neith…
items.body:
## Motivation

`MiniMaxH3AdalnCache.build` reserves one slab slot per missing plan, then embeds the timesteps, writes them and queries the tensor-parallel layout. Only the checkpoint projection that follows sat inside the rollback guard, so a failure in any earlier step left the reserved slots in neither the free list nor the resident map. Each failed request shrank the cache until a later build died with `IndexError: pop from empty list`, which then failed every request.

## Modifications

- `runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`: move the embedding, timestep writes and tensor-parallel queries into the existing rollback guard, so every failure returns the reserved slots.
- `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`: CPU regressions for repeated failures at each stage, with and without resident plans (eviction included). They check the free list, resident map, slot lengths and counters after every failure, and a successful retry at the end.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit: `test_minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py` 30 passed. Two host-tier tests depend on available host memory and need the override named in the commit message on small hosts; without it they fail (28 passed, 2 failed). Without the fix the new tests fail.

Real MiniMax-H3 FL2VA checkpoint, TP2 on 2 x B200, t2va, 4 s, 50 steps, seed 42. Server runs on this branch head, on a merge of the three H3 fixes (this PR, the VAE tile validation and the sigma preflight), and on unpatched `main` (`2948662026`).

**Regression** (bit-identical, so no frame comparison is shown; unpatched `main` vs this branch merged with the other two H3 fixes). Frame difference is 0 at every sampled pixel, and the video/audio latents and mp4 match bit for bit:

| | unpatched `main` | merged fixes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| video latent `[1,24,32,48,84]` + audio latent `[2,32,178]`, sha256 prefix | `e3f82e7f2006` | `e3f82e7f2006` |
| decoded mp4 (107 frames, 768x1344), sha256 prefix | `d7ffac37f960` | `d7ffac37f960` |
| max abs pixel difference, frames 0 / 53 / 106 | - | 0 / 0 / 0 |


**AdaLN cache, direct test** (real 50-layer AdaLN weights and real time-embedder weights, one rank, capacity 4; the embedding callable is made to raise). Measured on the head before the last rebase; the cache file is byte-identical on the current head.

| injected failures | free slots, `main` | free slots, this branch | outcome on `main` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 3 | 4 | injected error |
| 2 | 2 | 4 | injected error |
| 3 | 1 | 4 | injected error |
| 4 | 0 | 4 | injected error |
| 5 | 0 | 4 | `IndexError: pop from empty list` |
| 6 | 0 | 4 | `IndexError: pop from empty list` |
| then a valid build | `IndexError` | succeeds, layer 0 bit-equal to `F.linear` | |

![free slots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/063f509fd4a5d9812fd7933cc2147db045ec244d/minimax-h3-slots.png)

**Fault injection on the live server** (request 1 raises inside the time embedder, request 2 is normal):

| | request 1 | request 2 | request 2 mp4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unpatched `main` | fails (injected) | fails: `pop from empty list` | none |
| this branch (merged) | fails (injected) | completes | `d7ffac37f960`, identical to the regression run |

![request outcomes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/063f509fd4a5d9812fd7933cc2147db045ec244d/minimax-h3-fault.png)

items.title: [Feat] sgl-router: Continue W3C traces, record and forward request IDs, mark errors on spans
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: The existing doesn't cover the second point: it picks the first matching header as a single (generating one if none is present) for correlation inside the gateway. It doesn't record the raw values of several IDs, and the engine never sees what it picked.
items.body:
## Motivation

- The gateway's `http_request` span always starts a new trace, even when the caller sent a `traceparent`, so the caller's trace and SGLang's are disconnected.
- A request the gateway rejects (no worker, rate limit, bad request) never reaches an engine, so the gateway's span is the only record of it, and that span carries no request ID a caller would know.
- 4xx/5xx responses aren't marked on the span, so samplers and alerts that key on errors can't see gateway failures.

The existing `--request-id-headers` doesn't cover the second point: it picks the first matching header as a single `request_id` (generating one if none is present) for correlation inside the gateway. It doesn't record the raw values of several IDs, and the engine never sees what it picked.

## Modifications

1. **Continue incoming W3C traces and record request IDs.**
   - `RequestSpan` sets the span's parent from an incoming `traceparent` (`extract_trace_context_http`).
   - Request headers named in `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` are recorded on the span as `http.request.header.<name>`, cut to 1024 bytes. This is the same variable, attribute name and limit as the engine (#<request-headers PR>), so one setting covers both. Header values are visible ASCII, so bytes and characters agree.
   - Headers named in `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` or the existing `SGLANG_LOG_REQUEST_HEADERS` are forwarded to workers, so the engine can record or log them too.
   - `ResponseLogger` records an `error` attribute on 4xx/5xx (the router's error code, or the HTTP reason phrase) and sets `otel.status_code=ERROR` on 5xx only, following the OpenTelemetry HTTP conventions for server spans.
2. **Don't forward hop-by-hop and framing headers named in those lists.** If a list names a hop-by-hop header (`host`, `connection`, `transfer-encoding`, `proxy-authorization`, ...) or `content-length` (say, to log it on the engine), copying the client's value onto the request the gateway builds for the worker would misroute or misframe it. Those are skipped with a warning, reusing the hop-by-hop list the gateway already applies to worker responses (`should_forward_header_no_alloc`). Other listed headers are recorded and forwarded as configured.
3. **Docs** in `production_request_trace.mdx`.

### Behavior changes

- `http_request` spans join the caller's trace when a valid `traceparent` is present; before, they always started a new one.

items.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Account for CLIP CLS rows in LLaVA-NeXT-Video tower mappings
items.author: liulanze
items.summary: Fixes an undercount in tower LoRA token mapping for LLaVA-NeXT-Video where the CLIP CLS token row was omitted, causing assertion failures at engine startup.
items.body:
## Overview

This fixes tower LoRA for LLaVA-NeXT-Video. `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` counted `patch_grid_length**2` (576) tower rows per frame, but vLLM's CLIP tower prepends a CLS token, so the LoRA-wrapped tower linears process 577 rows per frame. This PR covers item 7 of #61608 (thanks @anshulkulhari7). #61799 fixes the same undercount for LLaVA (`llava.py`) only.

## Claims

- `vllm serve llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf --enable-lora --enable-tower-connector-lora` with otherwise default settings no longer fails at engine startup with `assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M` in `lora_shrink`. This applies to GPUs under 160 GB, where the serve default `max_num_batched_tokens` is 2048 or 8192.
- The tower LoRA mapping now covers every row the tower runs:
  - A request without LoRA is unaffected when a LoRA request shares its encoder batch.
  - A batch whose videos add up to `budget // 144` frames no longer asserts at runtime.
- Connector counts are unchanged, and so is the count for towers without a CLS token (SigLIP).
- Nothing changes without `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, because every caller of `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` is gated on it.

## Validation

Setup:
- Hardware and software: 1x A100 80GB PCIe, torch 2.14.0+cu132, transformers 5.19.0.
- Code: this PR applied on 5bf3d9f665 and installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`. The `main` runs swap in the base version of `llava_next_video.py`.
- Model: `llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf` at revision f417d9ed.

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm serve llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf --enable-lora --enable-tower-connector-lora`, all other settings default (`max_model_len` 10240, encoder budget 10224) | exits during encoder profiling with the `lora_shrink` assert | `Application startup complete` |
| `LLM(...)` with `max_model_len=4096` and `max_num_batched_tokens=2048` / `8192` | assert during encoder profiling, at both settings | starts at both settings |
| `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, default `max_model_len`: one batch with a 70-frame and a 43-frame video (113 = 16384 // 144 frames) and a tower adapter | starts, then the assert fires in the CLIP `qkv_proj` LoRA layer on that batch | completes |
| No-LoRA requests in a `[LoRA, none, LoRA, none]` batch vs. the same requests in a batch without LoRA | request 1 changes (max \|Δlogprob\| 0.0124); request 3 is bit-exact | bit-exact |
| All-LoRA batch vs. a checkpoint with the adapter merged into its weights: max \|Δlogprob\| over 4 × 32 greedy tokens, all tokens identical | 0.0390 (last video; the others are at most 0.0126) | 0.0120 (`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`), 0.0123 (`16384`) |

How the last two rows were produced:
- Adapter: a random rank-8 adapter (alpha 16) on the CLIP `q/k/v/out_proj` and `fc1/fc2` of all 23 tower layers. The merged checkpoint stores `W + (alpha / r) * B @ A`, computed in fp32.
- Batches:
  - Each batch is 4 eight-frame videos with `max_model_len=4096`, greedy decoding and `ignore_eos`.
  - All 4 are sent in one `generate` call with the in-process engine core (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), so they share one encoder batch.
  - `main` used `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, because it cannot start at 8192.
- Controls:
  - Two runs without LoRA were bit-exact with each other.
  - Without the adapter, outputs differ from the merged checkpoint by up to 0.18 in logprob, so the adapter has a visible effect.

Other checks:
- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_next_video.py`: 6 passed.
- On the changed files, with the versions and file groups pinned by pre-commit, these pass: ruff 0.14.0 (check and format), typos 1.43.5, and mypy 1.20.2 with `--python-version 3.11`.

## Details

**Root cause.** `LoRAModelManager` sizes the tower punica wrapper from `get_mm_lora_token_counts(mm_kwargs=None, num_mm_embeds=<encoder budget>)`, which gives `(budget // 144) * 576` rows.

- **Startup.** Encoder profiling runs the maximum number of dummy videos through CLIP before any tower mapping is set. CLIP adds one CLS row per frame (`CLIPVisionEmbeddings.forward`), so the LoRA layers see `frames * 577` rows. That can exceed the buffer, and `lora_shrink` then asserts.
  - With the model's default `max_model_len` of 10240, profiling runs one 71-frame video: 71 × 577 = 40,967 rows against a 40,896-row buffer.
  - A smaller `max_num_batched_tokens` doesn't help, because the encoder budget is floored at the 10,224 tokens of one dummy video.
- **Runtime.** Startup passes in some configurations, for example `LLM(...)` on H100 or `vllm serve` on B200 (default `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`).
  - There, the per-video mapping is one row per frame short. Each video's last rows take the next video's adapter, and the batch's last rows get none.
  - A step whose videos add up to exactly `budget // 144` frames hits the same assert.
- **History.** The miscount dates from #48594, which validated the tower output `(frames, 576, 1024)` after CLS removal. Default configurations have failed at startup since #47985 added encoder profiling to the default MRV2 runner. The V1 runner always profiled the encoder.

**Fix.** The hook now computes the tower tokens per frame from `self.config`, with `get_vision_encoder_info(...).get_num_image_tokens(...)` at the encoder image size, as `llava_next.py` and #61799 do.
- That gives 577 for the CLIP-336/14 tower used by every `llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-*` checkpoint, and an unchanged count for SigLIP.
- Frames are still counted from the pooled placeholder count (144 per frame), so the sizing bound still covers any batch within the encoder budget.
- The grid lengths cached in `__init__` were used only by this hook, so they are removed.

**Test.** The existing test in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_next_video.py` asserted `num_frames * patch_grid_length**2` tower rows (576 per frame) on grid lengths that the test computed itself. It now calls the hook on the real `llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf` config, which gives 577 rows per frame, and on synthetic CLIP-336, CLIP-224 and SigLIP-384 configs.

**Not a duplicate.** #61799 changes only `llava.py`. Two other open PRs touch `llava_next_video.py`, but not its LoRA token counts: #53735 adds `supports_encoder_tp_data`, and draft #60666 renames weights. I searched for `61608`, `llava_next_video`, `LlavaNextVideo`, `LLaVA-NeXT-Video LoRA`, `get_mm_lora_token_counts` and `CLS`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to analyze the issue, write the patch and the validation scripts, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

items.title: [Feat] tracing: Record configured request headers on root spans
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: A request's root span carries only SGLang's own. Clients, gateways and load balancers know a request by their own IDs (, a correlation ID,...), so finding its trace means correlating timestamps across systems.
items.body:
## Motivation

A request's root span carries only SGLang's own `rid`. Clients, gateways and load balancers know a request by their own IDs (`x-request-id`, a correlation ID, ...), so finding its trace means correlating timestamps across systems.

## Modifications

1. **Create root spans in one function.** `start_root_span` replaces the identical root-span code in `TraceReqContext` and `TraceReqContextAsync`, so the change below applies to both sync and async tracing. Pure refactor, no behavior change.
2. **Record configured request headers on root spans.** `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` (comma-separated, case-insensitive) names the request headers to record. Each one present on a request is set on its root span as `http.request.header.<name>`, the OpenTelemetry semantic-convention attribute for request headers.
   - Values are cut to 1024 characters, a fixed limit rather than a setting: request IDs and hashes (UUID 36, SHA-256 hex 64, SHA-512 hex 128) are far shorter, and the limit only exists so a caller can't attach unbounded data to spans.
   - Headers are recorded exactly as listed, with no filtering, as `SGLANG_LOG_REQUEST_HEADERS` already does for request logs. The operator chooses what goes on spans.
   - `extract_trace_headers` picks these headers up alongside `traceparent`/`tracestate`, so the Engine API and gRPC paths that pass `external_trace_header` record them too.

Docs: new "Finding a Request's Trace" section in `production_request_trace.mdx`, and `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` in `environment_variables.mdx`.

### Behavior changes

None while `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` is unset (the default).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. With tracing off, nothing changes; header extraction and attribute recording only run when tracing is enabled. With tracing on, it adds one dict lookup per configured header per request.

## Tests

- `test_trace.py::TestTraceFunctions::test_extract_trace_headers_adds_configured_headers`
- `test_trace.py::TestTraceReqContextEnabled::test_root_span_records_configured_headers_up_to_1024_chars`: a value longer than 1024 characters is cut, and an empty header isn't recorded.
- End to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, spans exported to Jaeger), both with a regular server at TP=2 and with PD disaggregation: root spans recorded the listed `x-request-id` and a second custom header, and a 2000-character `x-request-id` was recorded as its first 1024 characters.
- `test/registered/unit/observability`, `managers` and `disaggregation` fail the same tests as `main` and no others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

(Not applicable: no model-output change.)

items.title: [Feature]: Default to NextTokenPrediction Read strategy for text generation models for /v1/systemone and /v1/decisions
items.author: nishtahir
items.summary: Default NextTokenPrediction read strategy for all text generation models on /v1/systemone and /v1/decisions endpoints instead of only Qwen models.
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

It appears that only [Qwen models](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/153a17166e5d07bc38184dedeea542d2e8885e55/vllm/entrypoints/openai/decisions/strategies.py#L1160-L1169) are supported for next token prediction read strategies for systemone use cases. However, this should theoretically work with any text generation model. I'd like to propose that the default read strategy for any text generation model be next token to open up the API to a lot more models. 

### Alternatives

Alternatively, the list could be expanded to encompass a lot more models. My usecase requires that I use gemma4 adding it to the list worked for me

```
READ_STRATEGIES: dict[str, type[ReadStrategy]] = {
    "ClefFlashForJointSchema": ClefFlashStrategy,
    "ClefOmniForJointSchema": JointSchemaStrategy,
    "Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration": LiquidStrategy,
    "Qwen3ForCausalLM": NextTokenStrategy,
    "Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration": NextTokenStrategy,
    "Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration": NextTokenStrategy,
    "DiffusionGemmaForBlockDiffusion": DiffusionGemmaCanvasStrategy,

    # Patch for Gemma4
    "Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration": NextTokenStrategy,
}
```

### Additional context

Relevant rfc: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59365

items.title: [Chore] attention: Remove the tokenspeed_mla backend and dependency
items.author: zcnrex
items.summary: Removes the tokenspeed_mla attention backend and its pinned dependency since cutedsl_mla already provides equivalent MLA decode coverage on Blackwell GPUs.
items.body:
## Motivation

Remove the `tokenspeed_mla` attention backend and the `tokenspeed_mla==0.1.8` hard dependency it brings into every `pip install sglang`. On Blackwell, `cutedsl_mla` already covers the same ground as the default MLA decode backend: FP8 or BF16 KV, page size 32/64, decode context parallelism, and speculative verify of any width. Keeping a second CuTe DSL MLA backend means an extra pinned external package, an extra registry/dispatch/draft path, and extra override branches.

## Modifications

- **Backend removed:** `layers/attention/tokenspeed_mla_backend.py`. Also removed:
  - the `tokenspeed_mla` registry entry and DeepSeek MLA dispatch handler
  - the EAGLE draft decode/prefill factories and the `eagle_worker_v2` graph-support entry
  - `is_tokenspeed_mla_available`
- **Server args:**
  - `tokenspeed_mla` is dropped from the attention / prefill / decode / chunked-prefix choices, the page-major and DCP allowlists, and the page-size and KV-dtype checks.
  - The Kimi-K3 DCP override no longer accepts `tokenspeed_mla` as a decode backend; it accepts `cutedsl_mla` or `aiter`.
  - `_dspark_verify_on_decode_backend` drops its now-unused `kv_cache_dtype` argument.
- **Dependency:** `tokenspeed_mla==0.1.8` is removed from `python/pyproject.toml`.
- **Docs:**
  - The Kimi-K2.5/K2.6/K2.7 cookbook commands on B300/GB300 switch from `--attention-backend tokenspeed_mla` to `cutedsl_mla`, still with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`.
  - When speculative decoding is enabled, the K2.5/K2.6 commands also add `--speculative-attention-mode decode` (see Speed Tests).
  - The attention-backend table, server-argument choices and the Kimi-K3 note drop the entry.
- **Tests:**
  - GB300 Kimi-K2.5 NVFP4 TP/DP switch to `cutedsl_mla` with `--speculative-attention-mode=decode`.
  - The Kimi-Linear DCP4 / DCP+DSpark / PD-DCP4 tests switch to `cutedsl_mla`.
  - Removed `mla/test_tokenspeed_mla.py`, the tokenspeed stride-parity case and the tokenspeed DCP-metadata class.
  - Allowlist and LSE-base assertions are updated.

Not touched: `.agents/skills/llm-torch-profiler-analysis` still recognizes TokenSpeed and vLLM kernel names when triaging traces from those frameworks. That is trace tooling for other engines, not an sglang dependency.

## Why `--speculative-attention-mode decode` with speculative decoding

`cutedsl_mla` is decode-only; prefill resolves to `trtllm_mla`. With the default `--speculative-attention-mode=prefill`, target verify runs on the prefill backend (`trtllm_mla`), while `tokenspeed_mla` used to run verify itself. That made decode up to 21% slower at long context. `decode` routes verify to `cutedsl_mla` and recovers parity (tables below).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy (`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`), 4x GB300, TP4:

| Config | `tokenspeed_mla` (this PR's base) | `cutedsl_mla` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-K2.5 INT4 (`moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5`) | 0.942 | 0.945 |
| Kimi-K2.5 NVFP4 + EAGLE3, node A | 0.938 | 0.936 |
| Kimi-K2.5 NVFP4 + EAGLE3, node B | 0.937 | 0.939 |
| Kimi-K2.5 NVFP4 + EAGLE3, decode-mode verify | 0.934 | 0.939 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup:**
- **Hardware:** 4x GB300 (TP4), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`.
- **Arms:** `tokenspeed_mla` runs on this PR's base commit; `cutedsl_mla` runs on this PR.
- **Method:** `python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server` on random prompts. Arms are interleaved tokenspeed, cutedsl, cutedsl, tokenspeed, and each cell is the mean of 2 server launches per arm. Launches agree within 0.5%, except one tokenspeed INT4 8K bs1 run (160 vs 167 tok/s).
- **Metrics:** decode is steady-state output tok/s; TTFT is the last-batch time to first token.
- **NVFP4 + EAGLE3** uses the GB300 nightly-test flags: `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --mem-fraction-static 0.8`, EAGLE3 with 3 steps, topk 1 and 4 draft tokens. bs64 is skipped because EAGLE caps max running requests at 48. Accept length is 3.9–4.0 on both arms.

Decode tok/s, `tokenspeed_mla` → `cutedsl_mla`:

| Input/output | bs | INT4, no spec | NVFP4+EAGLE3, default verify mode (`prefill`) | NVFP4+EAGLE3, `--speculative-attention-mode decode` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K/512 | 1 | 163.5 → 169.6 (+3.7%) | 567.9 → 568.4 (+0.1%) | 559.8 → 570.4 (+1.9%) |
| 8K/512 | 4 | 499.8 → 505.1 (+1.0%) | 1404.4 → 1387.0 (−1.2%) | 1403.1 → 1398.0 (−0.4%) |
| 8K/512 | 16 | 1067.6 → 1075.8 (+0.8%) | 3144.6 → 2996.4 (−4.7%) | 3140.6 → 3149.1 (+0.3%) |
| 8K/512 | 64 | 2087.6 → 2101.1 (+0.6%) | — | — |
| 64K/256 | 1 | 148.4 → 154.2 (+3.9%) | 511.4 → 486.7 (−4.8%) | 509.8 → 523.0 (+2.6%) |
| 64K/256 | 8 | 622.8 → 627.8 (+0.8%) | 1802.4 → 1422.8 (**−21.1%**) | 1803.7 → 1807.7 (+0.2%) |

The default-mode column was reproduced on a second GB300 node: −4.7% at 8K bs16, −4.4% at 64K bs1, −21.1% at 64K bs8.

TTFT, `tokenspeed_mla` → `cutedsl_mla`:

| Input/output | bs | INT4, no spec | NVFP4+EAGLE3, decode-mode verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K/512 | 1 | 0.30 → 0.26 s | 0.20 → 0.20 s |
| 8K/512 | 16 | 3.49 → 3.55 s (+2%) | 2.29 → 2.35 s (+3%) |
| 8K/512 | 64 | 13.90 → 14.15 s (+2%) | — |
| 64K/256 | 1 | 2.16 → 2.35 s (+9%) | 1.57 → 1.76 s (+12%) |
| 64K/256 | 8 | 17.11 → 18.65 s (+9%) | 12.39 → 13.96 s (+13%) |

**Known cost:** long-prompt TTFT is 9–13% higher at 64K. `tokenspeed_mla` had its own prefill kernel; `cutedsl_mla` prefills through `trtllm_mla`. Decode is at parity or better once verify runs on `cutedsl_mla`.

Not run: the GB300 nightly MMMU-Pro gate itself, the DP-attention variant (`test_kimi_k25_nvfp4_dp.py`), and the Kimi-Linear DCP tests on `cutedsl_mla`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code: `ruff check` (repo selection), `ruff format --check` and `isort --check-only` pass on all changed Python files with the pinned versions. Full pre-commit not run.
- [x] Add unit tests: existing tests updated; no new tests.

items.title: [Feat] tracing: Stable span names, record rid as is, and don't trace health checks
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: With a per-request or per-process ID in the name, every span gets a unique name, which breaks grouping and aggregation by span name in tracing backends. The IDs are already recorded as attributes.
items.body:
## Motivation

- Root spans are named `Req <first 8 chars of rid>`, and thread spans `Scheduler [TP 0] (host:<id> | pid:<pid>)`. With a per-request or per-process ID in the name, every span gets a unique name, which breaks grouping and aggregation by span name in tracing backends. The IDs are already recorded as attributes.
- The `rid` attribute is the rid split on `_`, to drop a MultiTokenizer worker prefix that rids no longer carry. It truncates any rid containing `_`: `req_abc_123` is recorded as `123`, so a request can't be found by its rid.
- `/health` and `/health_generate` submit a one-token generation request (rid `HEALTH_CHECK_<uuid>`), and the tokenizer traces it like any other. With tracing on, every probe of every server adds a trace, burying user requests in trace search and sampling.

## Modifications

1. **Create root spans in one function.** `start_root_span` replaces the identical root-span code in `TraceReqContext` and `TraceReqContextAsync`, so the changes below apply to both sync and async tracing.
2. **Stable span names; `rid` recorded as is.**
   - Root spans are named `Req`, or `prefill Req` / `decode Req` under PD disaggregation.
   - Thread spans are named `<label> [TP n] [PP n] [DP n]`; `host_id` and `pid` stay attributes.
   - The `rid` attribute is the full rid.
3. **Don't trace health checks.** `init_trace_ctx` gives `HEALTH_CHECK_*` rids a null trace context, in both sync and async tracing. `request_metrics_exporter` already skips these rids for the same reason.

Docs: new "Span Names" section in `production_request_trace.mdx`.

### Behavior changes for existing tracing users

| What | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root span name | `Req 6f97ea7f`, `decode Req 6f97ea7f` | `Req`, `decode Req` |
| Thread span name | `Scheduler [TP 0] (host:1a2b3c4d \| pid:123)` | `Scheduler [TP 0]` (`host_id`, `pid` still attributes) |
| `rid` attribute | last `_`-separated part of the rid | the full rid |
| Health checks | traced | not traced |

Queries or dashboards that match span names by prefix (`Req <id>`) or by the host/pid suffix need updating.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. Span names are built with the same work as before, and a health check now skips trace setup entirely.

## Tests

- `test_trace.py::TestTraceReqContextEnabled::test_span_names_leave_out_request_and_process_ids`: root and thread span names for unified and decode roles, and the rid `req_abc_123` recorded whole.
- `test_req_time_stats.py::TestInitTraceCtx::test_health_checks_are_not_traced`
- End to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, spans exported to Jaeger):
  - Regular server, TP=2: the root span is `Req` and the thread span is `Scheduler [TP 0] [PP 0]`.
  - PD disaggregation (NIXL): roots are `prefill Req` and `decode Req`, thread spans are `Prefill Scheduler [TP 0] [PP 0]` and `Decode Scheduler [TP 0] [PP 0]`.
  - The rid `e2e_rid_abc_123` was recorded whole, and repeated `/health_generate` probes produced no traces.
- `test/registered/unit/observability`, `managers` and `disaggregation` fail the same tests as `main` and no others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable: no model-output change.)

items.title: [Feat] tracing: Record why requests failed, and mark only server faults as errors
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: Traces don't tell a failed request from a normal one, and they mark the wrong things as errors: - A request's root span shows that it finished, but not whether it failed or why: an overloaded server, a rejected prompt and a client abort all look like a normal …
items.body:
## Motivation

Traces don't tell a failed request from a normal one, and they mark the wrong things as errors:

- A request's root span shows that it finished, but not whether it failed or why: an overloaded server, a rejected prompt and a client abort all look like a normal request.
- Every `trace_ctx.abort(abort_info=...)` sets the thread span's status to ERROR, whether the request hit a server fault, was rejected as invalid, or was aborted by its caller. A sampler or alert that keys on error spans counts every bad request and every client disconnect as a server failure.
- A request that fails in the tokenizer before reaching the scheduler (invalid input, a LoRA or encoder error) never has its trace ended. With sync tracing its root span is never exported, so rejected requests don't appear in traces at all.

## Modifications

1. **Thread spans are errors only for server faults.** Each abort that has an HTTP status passes it in `abort_info["status_code"]`, matching the status the client gets:
   - scheduler: 400 for a missing bootstrap room or a bad sampling mask, 503 when the queue is full, and the `FINISH_ABORT`'s own status when retiring an unadmitted or chunked request;
   - PD prefill: 400 over KV capacity, 500 on KV transfer or bootstrap failure, and the sampling-mask reason's status;
   - EPD encoder: 504 on timeout, otherwise `MMError.code` or the worker's error code, falling back to 500.

An aborted thread span is marked ERROR only for a 5xx, as the OpenTelemetry HTTP conventions do for server spans. Attributes whose value is None are left out instead of being exported as empty values.
2. **Root spans record how aborted requests ended.** When the tokenizer finishes an aborted request (from the scheduler's abort message, or a batch output with an abort finish reason), it sets `error.type` on the root span to the status code (e.g. `"503"`), or `"abort"` when there is none, and sets status ERROR only for a 5xx. This is implemented once, in `set_root_span_error`, for both sync and async tracing. `_handle_abort_req` now ends the trace after computing the finish reason, since attributes set after the root span ends are dropped.
3. **Traces of requests that fail before reaching the scheduler now end.** `_release_req_states_on_failure` now takes the exception. For each undelivered request it records the status the HTTP entrypoints return for that exception (an `HTTPException`'s own code, 400 for `ValueError`, 500 for any other `Exception`, none for a cancellation) and ends the trace. Dispatched requests are unchanged: their trace ends on the scheduler's abort response.

Docs: new "Failed Requests" section in `production_request_trace.mdx`.

### Behavior changes for existing tracing users

- Aborted thread spans without a 5xx status are no longer ERROR. That includes client aborts, 4xx rejections, a cancelled encode, the Mooncake sender's own abort, and spans auto-closed at garbage collection, all of which were ERROR before.
- Root spans of aborted requests gain `error.type`, plus ERROR status for a 5xx.
- Requests rejected before reaching the scheduler now end their trace with a status. Before, sync tracing didn't export them at all, and async tracing ended the root span at garbage collection with no status.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No hot-path cost: status codes are only added on abort paths, and with tracing off the new calls go to `TraceNullContext` or return early.

## Tests

- `test_trace.py::test_aborted_thread_span_is_an_error_only_for_server_faults` (400, no status, 500)
- `test_trace.py::test_aborted_request_records_its_status_on_the_root_span` (503, 400, no status, and a non-abort finish)
- `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py::TestTraceRecordsAbortStatus` (the status is recorded before the root span ends, on the scheduler-abort and batch-output paths)
- `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py::test_undelivered_trace_ends_with_the_status_the_client_gets` (`HTTPException` 503, `ValueError`, `RuntimeError`, `CancelledError`)
- The existing `_release_req_states_on_failure` tests pass the new `error` argument.
- End to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, spans exported to Jaeger), both with a regular server at TP=2 and with PD disaggregation (NIXL): an over-length prompt (400) ended its root spans with `error.type=400` and no ERROR status; a streamed request the client closed early ended with `error.type=abort`, not ERROR.
- `test/registered/unit/observability`, `managers` and `disaggregation` fail the same tests as `main` and no others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

(Not applicable: no model-output change.)

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply stop strings only after reasoning ends
items.author: robertgshaw2-redhat
items.summary: Fixes premature termination of reasoning-capable models by deferring client stop-string matching until after the reasoning block completes.
items.body:
## Overview

Client stop strings are matched against the model's reasoning as well as its answer. If the reasoning contains a stop string, generation ends inside `<think>` and the response has no content. This PR keeps stop strings dormant until the request's reasoning parser sees reasoning end.

Fixes #62085. Also fixes #53066, and item 3 of #58647.

## Claims

- On a server with `--reasoning-parser`, chat requests (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`) whose prompt leaves the model mid-reasoning no longer stop inside the reasoning. Stop strings still apply to the response that follows.
- A stop string has to start in the response. A match that spans the end of the reasoning is ignored, which matters when the end marker decodes to no text.
- No change for requests without stop strings, prompts that are not mid-reasoning (thinking disabled), servers without a reasoning parser, or endpoints that do not resolve reasoning state (`/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, offline `LLM`).

## Validation

**End to end:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=8 on H100, `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`. The repro from #62085 is a classifier prompt with `stop_sequences: ["</block>"]`; it is the same request Claude Code's auto-mode safety check sends.

| Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/messages`, `stop_sequences: ["</block>"]` | 100/100 empty (stopped inside reasoning) | **50/50 `<block>no`** |
| `/v1/chat/completions`, `stop: ["</block>"]` | `content: null` | **20/20 `<block>no`**, reasoning kept |
| `/v1/chat/completions`, thinking disabled (control) | `<block>no` | 20/20 `<block>no` (stop still applies) |

<details><summary>Repro command</summary>

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "max_tokens": 2048,
  "stop_sequences": ["</block>"],
  "system": "You are a security classifier. Decide whether the shell command should be blocked.\nIf it should be blocked, output <block>yes</block>. Otherwise output <block>no</block>.",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Command: ls -la\nYour response MUST begin with <block>."}]
}' | jq -c '{stop_reason, text: [.content[]|select(.type=="text")|.text]}'
```
</details>

**Unit tests:** in `tests/detokenizer/test_stop_string_while_stop_model_terminates.py`. All 8 new cases fail with the new behavior disabled.
- A stop string in the reasoning is ignored and the one in the response is honored, with tokens fed 1, 3 or all at a time (as with speculative decoding).
- A stop string spanning a reasoning end that decodes to no text does not match.
- With the real `qwen3` parser and Qwen3 tokenizer, `reasoning_ended=False` defers stops and `reasoning_ended=None` keeps the old behavior.

**Existing suites:** `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py tests/v1/engine/test_fast_incdec_prefix_err.py tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py tests/detokenizer/{test_check_stop_strings,test_min_tokens,test_stop_string_while_stop_model_terminates}.py` gives 692 passed and 1 failed. The failure, `test_logprobs_processor[7-5-FINAL_ONLY]`, was intermittent: it passes 8/8 when rerun on both this branch and `main`. CI runs `tests/detokenizer` in "Detokenizer" (`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`).

**Model evals:** the GSM8K eval sends stop strings only in `/v1/completions` mode, which this change does not touch. The end-to-end table above is the evidence for the affected path.

## Details

**Root cause.** `BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update()` runs `check_stop_strings` over all detokenized text. With think-in-prompt templates (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, Qwen3, GLM, ...), that text starts inside the reasoning. A stop string there ends the request before `</think>`, so the parser returns no content.

**Design.** This reuses the reasoning-state plumbing that structured outputs already has, rather than matching marker strings:
- The chat serving layer already resolves `reasoning_ended` per request from the request's own parser and template kwargs (`resolve_reasoning_ended`), and sends it on `EngineCoreRequest` together with `reasoning_parser_kwargs`. Stop strings are deferred only when it is `False`, so thinking-off requests and endpoints that do not resolve it keep today's behavior.
- A new `ReasoningEndFinder` in `detokenizer.py` finds the end of reasoning in the output token ids. It uses the same parser class structured outputs uses (`--reasoning-parser`, built with the request's `reasoning_parser_kwargs`).
  - Engine-based parsers: `find_reasoning_end`, which also handles implicit ends such as a tool-call start token, where content starts at that token.
  - Legacy parsers: `is_reasoning_end_streaming`.
- Once reasoning ends, `check_stop_strings` gets `search_start` at the first content character, so a match cannot start in the reasoning text. `min_tokens` and dropping overflow tokens after a stop are unchanged.
- `OutputProcessor` resolves the parser class by name the first time it is needed. Only API-server chat paths set `reasoning_ended=False`, and they have registered the parser by then, so a plugin parser cannot fail offline `LLM` startup.

**Cost.** Only requests that have stop strings and are mid-reasoning pay anything. On DeepSeek-V4.1 and Qwen3 parsers that is about 90–150 µs per request to build the parser, and about 0.7 µs per decode step until reasoning ends. There is no change to the model runner or scheduler, and no GPU work.

**Behavior change.** A chat client that relied on a stop string to cut reasoning short now gets it applied only to the response. This matches the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, where stop sequences apply to the output text.

**Limitations.**
- `resolve_reasoning_ended` returns `True` for `include_reasoning=False` and for grammar-from-parser (Mistral) requests. That is a structured-outputs choice, and those requests keep today's behavior.
- `/v1/responses` does not resolve reasoning state yet.

**Related PRs.** #52486 and #38533 also target this.
- #52486 searches the output text for a hardcoded `</think>` and arms itself when the prompt's last token is `<think>`. It never reads the deployment's parser markers (its config lookup raises on the frontend and is swallowed) and does not handle special-token markers that are stripped from the text. It also conflicts with the current `update()`.
- #38533 uses the parser on token ids, as this PR does, but it is built on the old parser classes, has merge conflicts, and does not use the per-request `reasoning_ended` resolution.

items.title: [Fix] hicache: Order write-back host copies after the forward that produced the KV
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Fixes a race condition in hicache write-back where KV pages could be copied to host before the producing forward pass completed, causing stale KV data to be served to other requests.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--hicache-write-policy write_back`, KV pages could be copied to host before the forward pass that produced them had finished. The host copy then held whatever the page contained at submit time, and a later load-back served that stale KV to another request. Two paths reached the device-to-host copy without any dependency on the forward stream:

- **Insert-time SWA window backups.** Write-back defers Full and Mamba backups to eviction, but the tree core still published an unbacked SWA window when a request's nodes were inserted. That backup was queued while the request's own forward could still be writing the window.
- **The blocking write-back drain.** Eviction submits everything queued in the tick on the device-to-host stream with no fence, and an evicted SWA page can belong to a checkpoint whose producing forward has not completed.

## Modifications

- `UnifiedTreeCore` (Python) and `unified_tree_core.rs` (Rust): under write-back, insertion never returns a `BackupKV` action, so SWA windows are no longer published at insert time. The incremental-component check no longer special-cases SWA under write-back.
- `HiCacheController.start_writing(wait_for_forward=...)`: a new keyword-only flag. When set and a `write_fence_stream` is configured, the device-to-host stream waits on it before the copies are submitted. The scheduler sets `write_fence_stream` to the model runner's forward stream next to the existing `load_fence_stream`.
- `UnifiedRadixCache.writing_check(write_back=True)` passes `wait_for_forward=True` on the blocking drain. Write-through and the asynchronous write-back flush are unchanged, and the default keeps every other caller as it was.
- Tests:
  - `test_hicache_write_back_ordering.py` (new): a checkpointed request whose forward is still writing on a separate stream; evicting an older SWA window of that request must copy the values the forward wrote, not the pre-forward contents.
  - `test_unified_hicache_regressions.py`: the blocking drain waits for the fence stream before copying both a tick's queued backup and the eviction victim.
  - `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` and the Rust crate tests: write-back insertion of backed Full nodes publishes no SWA window and leaves no pending ack; the Mamba pending-ack eviction test now queues its window backup explicitly instead of relying on insert-time publication.

## Accuracy Tests

- `cargo test` for `rust/sglang-radix-tree` (`--no-default-features`, as `pr-test-rust-workspace.yml` runs it): 931 passed, 0 failed.
- On one CUDA GPU, with both `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust` and `=python`: `test_hicache_write_back_ordering.py`, `test_unified_hicache_regressions.py::TestTransferStreamOrdering`, and the two touched cases in `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` pass.
- Without the runtime changes, `test_hicache_write_back_ordering.py` fails on both backends: the host copy holds the pre-forward contents instead of what the forward wrote.
- No numerics change: the fix only orders existing copies after their producer and removes an early backup that eviction performs later.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The new wait is a single `wait_stream` on the blocking write-back drain, which already blocks on every ack; the asynchronous paths do not take it.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

items.title: [Feat] tracing: Trace only the first rank of each attention TP/CP group by default
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: Every scheduler process initializes tracing, so with TP 8 each request gets eight sets of scheduler spans. The ranks of an attention TP/CP group run the same requests in lockstep, so the copies describe the same batches.
items.body:
## Motivation

Every scheduler process initializes tracing, so with TP 8 each request gets eight sets of scheduler spans. The ranks of an attention TP/CP group run the same requests in lockstep, so the copies describe the same batches. They multiply span volume (export cost, collector load, storage) by the group size and crowd the trace view, without adding information for request-level debugging.

This changes a default, so it is kept to one small PR, with an environment variable to restore the previous behavior.

## Modifications

- `should_trace_rank()` in `trace.py` returns true when the process's attention TP rank and attention CP rank are both 0, read from `get_parallel()` (published before `run_scheduler_process` sets up tracing).
- `run_scheduler_process` initializes tracing only when `should_trace_rank()` returns true.
- `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS=1` traces every rank, as before, e.g. to debug a rank that diverges.

With DP attention, each DP group keeps its own tracing rank (attention TP rank 0 of the group), and each PP stage keeps one too. A trace context sent to a rank that does not trace arrives disabled, as it already does for any process without tracing (`TraceReqContext.__setstate__`, `TraceReqContextAsync.__setstate__`).

Docs: `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS` in `environment_variables.mdx`, and a note under the span-structure diagram in `production_request_trace.mdx`.

### Behavior changes for existing tracing users

- By default only scheduler processes with attention TP rank 0 and attention CP rank 0 export spans; `Scheduler [TP n]` spans for other ranks no longer appear.
- The Mooncake KV transfer worker spans of those other ranks no longer appear either, since they run in the same scheduler process.
- `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS=1` restores the previous behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. With tracing on, scheduler span volume drops by the attention TP × CP group size; with tracing off nothing changes.

## Tests

- New: `test_trace.py::TestShouldTraceRank::test_only_the_first_rank_of_each_attention_group_traces` covers TP rank 1, CP rank 1, and the `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS` override.
- Existing: `TestTraceReqContextDisabled::test_setstate_disabled` covers contexts arriving at a process without tracing.
- End to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, TP=2, spans exported to Jaeger): by default only TP rank 0 emitted scheduler spans; after a restart with `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS=1`, both ranks did.
- `test/registered/unit/observability`, `managers` and `disaggregation` fail the same tests as `main` and no others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

(Not applicable: no model-output change.)

items.title: [Perf] muse-spark: remove o-proj and moe tail from Helion verify megakernels
items.author: ethche
items.summary: With optimizations to the o-proj and tail kernels, the TP4 verify megakernels' lead over today's default (EP4) on the E07 OpenHands replay shrank from 1.10x to 1.03x TPOT. We simply remove the helion overrides for tail and o-proj and restore: o-projection, all…
items.body:
## Motivation
With optimizations to the o-proj and tail kernels, the TP4 verify megakernels' lead over today's default (EP4) on the E07 OpenHands replay shrank from 1.10x to 1.03x TPOT.

We simply remove the helion overrides for tail and o-proj and restore: `dev` o-projection, all-reduce, and attention-boundary norms. This brings us back to **1.08x** output tok/s vs dev EP4 on the OpenHands eval. 

This keeps the performant moe and attention megakernels:

| Megakernel | Default EP4 kernels | Default | Helion | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Attention | QK norm + RoPE (Triton), attention (FlashInfer), norm + gate (CUDA) | 12.3 µs | 10.1 µs | 1.22× |
| Router | pooler (FlashInfer), router GEMM (cuBLASLt), quant + top-8 (CUDA) | 13.4 µs | 12.7 µs | 1.06× |
| MoE | MoE (FlashInfer), finalize + combine (CuTe DSL) | 61.9 µs | 55.6 µs | 1.11× |
| LM head | GEMM + split-K reduce (cuBLASLt) | 137.4 µs | 135.9 µs | 1.01× |

## Modifications
- Restore stock O-projection, all-reduce and attention-boundary norms. Got rid of tail megakernel.
- `attention_boundary_verify_megakernel.py`: drop roots A/B/C; the input is the stock pre-FFN-normed hidden state.  Pooler K block 64 and 8 warps (tuned on GB300).
- `moe_tp4_verify_megakernel.py`: trigger dependents at entry so the stock unpooler GEMM prefetches during R3. The tail megakernel stays in-tree, unused (can go in a follow-up).
- `integration.py` / `megakernel_verify.py`: compose the stock modules around the megakernels.

## Accuracy Tests
Megakernel TP4 on this branch, real outputs (no forced acceptance):
- AIME26 (sgl-eval, thinking, reasoning effort xhigh, temperature 1, top-p 0.95, 400K max tokens, 2 repeats, 4 x
  GB300): **58/60 pass@1 (96.7%)**, pass@2 30/30, 0 truncated, 0 errors (reference 94.6%).

## Speed Tests and Profiling
- 4 x GB300
- E07 OpenHands replay (13-turn conversations, ~79K-token prompts, 220 output tokens per turn), c=1, DFlash2
- T=8 with forced acceptance 4.5, 3 repeats on each of 2 nodes.

| arm | TTFT p50 | TTFT p90 | TPOT p50 | TPOT p90 | TPOT mean | ITL p50 | interactivity p50 | verify step (sglang timer) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev EP4 (default) | 255 ms | **384 ms** | 2.12 ms | 2.19 ms | 2.108 ms | 9.52 ms | 472.8 tok/s | 9.38 ms |
| megakernel TP4 (this PR) | 255 ms | 431 ms | **1.94 ms** | **2.00 ms** | **1.945 ms** | **8.74 ms** | **515.5 tok/s** | **8.65 ms** |
| ratio | | | | 1.09x | 1.09x | 1.084x | 1.089x | 1.090x | 1.084x |


For 2x4xGB300, using PD disagg we have:

PD disaggregation (2 x 4 GB300: EP4 prefill on node 0, decode arms in turn on node 1, mooncake over RDMA; same
workload, c=1, 3 repeats, 0 failed). Decode speed is ITL p50 / tokens per step (evalscope's TPOT reads low under PD,
since the first streamed chunk lands after a few decode steps):
| setup | TTFT p50 | TTFT p90 | TTFT p99 | decode ms/token | vs EP4 decode | verify step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PD -> megakernel TP4 decode (this PR) | 302 ms | 490 ms | 2.06 s | **1.940** | **1.092x** | 8.62 ms |
| PD -> dev EP4 decode | 301 ms | 475 ms | 2.06 s | 2.118 | 1.000x | 9.37 ms |
| PD -> dev TP4 decode | 298 ms | 338 ms | 2.06 s | 2.198 | 0.964x | 9.75 ms |
