items.title: [Bug] [AMD] Keep fp32 MoE correction bias in select_experts for the aiter fp32 path
items.author: Kylinny
items.summary: downcast the correction bias to the router logits' dtype whenever the aiter grouped-topk path was taken. For GLM-5.x, keeps in fp32 since #37133, and the aiter branch of upcasts the gating logits to fp32 when it sees an fp32 bias.
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #44794.

`select_experts` downcast the correction bias to the router logits' dtype whenever the aiter grouped-topk path was taken. For GLM-5.x (`GlmMoeDsa`), `MoEGate` keeps `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32 since #37133, and the aiter branch of `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` upcasts the gating logits to fp32 when it sees an fp32 bias. The downcast in `select_experts` silently disabled that branch, so GLM-5.x on ROCm routed with a bf16 bias (the offset bias collapses to a handful of distinct values in bf16 and reorders top-k) while CUDA kept fp32 routing.

The fix skips the downcast when the bias is already fp32, so #37133's fp32 aiter path engages. Behavior is unchanged for:

- non-fp32 biases (they still get the pre-existing cast to the gating dtype that `aiter_biased_grouped_topk` expects),
- the JIT-router path (`SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK`),
- the dynamic-expert-bias path,
- non-aiter platforms (CUDA, MUSA, ...): the whole block is gated on `_use_aiter`, so **CUDA routing is byte-identical**.

## Reproducer

Unit-level (no ROCm GPU needed; `_use_aiter` is simulated since this machine has no MI355X):

```python
from unittest.mock import patch
import torch
from sglang.srt.layers.moe import topk as topk_module
from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import TopKConfig, select_experts

captured = {}
def fake_biased_grouped_topk(hidden_states, gating_output, correction_bias,
                             topk, renormalize, num_expert_group, topk_group,
                             num_fused_shared_experts, routed_scaling_factor,
                             apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output):
    captured["bias"] = correction_bias
    return (torch.zeros((gating_output.shape[0], topk)),
            torch.zeros((gating_output.shape[0], topk), dtype=torch.int32))

bias = torch.randn(256, dtype=torch.float32)  # fp32, like GlmMoeDsa's bias (#37133)
config = TopKConfig(top_k=8, use_grouped_topk=True, topk_group=8,
                    num_expert_group=32, correction_bias=bias)
router_logits = torch.randn(4, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16)  # like aiter_dsv3_router_gemm

with (patch.object(topk_module, "_use_aiter", True),
      patch.object(topk_module, "biased_grouped_topk", fake_biased_grouped_topk)):
    select_experts(torch.randn(4, 16, dtype=torch.bfloat16), router_logits, config)

print("input bias dtype:                ", bias.dtype)
print("bias reaching aiter grouped topk: ", captured["bias"].dtype)
```

Before (on main):

```
input bias dtype:                 torch.float32
bias reaching aiter grouped topk:  torch.bfloat16
```

After (with this fix):

```
input bias dtype:                 torch.float32
bias reaching aiter grouped topk:  torch.float32
```

## Measured effect

Per the reporter's measurement on a GLM-5.3 TP8 server (MI355X, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, eager, 38,325 token-layer pairs): the routed top-8 differed from the same bf16 logits routed with the fp32 bias in 67.6% of token-layer pairs (1.32 of 8 experts on average; layers 3–7 differed for nearly every token). The reporter also confirmed that skipping the downcast restores fp32 routing on the aiter path (0.0–0.1% differing pairs). CUDA behavior is unchanged.

## Tests

- New `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_topk_fp32_bias_aiter.py` (CPU, registered with `register_cpu_ci`):
  - fp32 bias reaches the grouped-topk kernel untouched — fails on main, passes with the fix;
  - bf16/fp16 biases keep the pre-existing cast to the logits dtype;
  - a mechanism check: the bf16 cast of an offset bias demonstrably reorders top-k routing.
- Existing `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_topk_correction_bias_cache.py`: 3 passed.

Thank you for the detailed report and measurements — they made this straightforward to pin down.

TRTLLM has a config option, checkpoint IO policy, to set what weight loading method to load checkpoint weights.
Previously this option is `str` type, this PR changes it to its own enum `CheckpointIOPolicy`.

Benefits:
- Functions using the option becomes easier to understand as its input/output now has type `CheckpointIOPolicy` instead of a `str`
- Easier to use this option as you have a typed enum to track legal policy names.

items.title: [Fix]: tracing: Generate 128-bit trace IDs from the OS entropy pool
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: has two problems with the IDs it generates: - Trace IDs come from, so the upper half of the 128-bit W3C trace ID is always zero. Processes started at the same clock reading, such as the TP scheduler processes of one server, draw identical ID sequences, so the…
items.body:
## Motivation

`TraceCustomIdGenerator` has two problems with the IDs it generates:

- Trace IDs come from `getrandbits(64)`, so the upper half of the 128-bit W3C trace ID is always zero.
- Each process seeds its own `random.Random` with `time.time()`. Processes started at the same clock reading, such as the TP scheduler processes of one server, draw identical ID sequences, so their trace and span IDs can collide. Avoiding collisions across scheduler processes is why this custom generator exists.

## Modifications

- Draw IDs from `random.SystemRandom` (the OS entropy pool), so there is no seed to collide on.
- Trace IDs are 128-bit. Span IDs stay 64-bit, as W3C trace context requires.
- Skip the all-zero ID, which is invalid in W3C trace context.
- Preset span IDs for async tracing (`preset_next_span_id`) are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Tracing off: no change. IDs are only generated for traced requests.
- Tracing on: `SystemRandom` costs about 1 µs more per draw (`getrandbits(64)`: ~1.2 µs vs ~0.2 µs with `random.Random`, Xeon 8375C). Each traced request draws one trace ID, plus one span ID per span.

Verified end to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, TP=2, spans exported to Jaeger): all 8 engine-started traces had non-zero upper 64 bits. `test/registered/unit/observability`, `managers` and `disaggregation` fail the same tests as `main` and no others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new test: existing tracing tests exercise the generator.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed: no user-facing change.)

(Not applicable: no model-output change; overhead above.)

items.title: [Bug]: Adaptive verification fails at startup with the default attention backend on FA2 GPUs
items.author: waynehacking8
items.summary: The varlen graph check that rejects it runs later, in, and FA2's metadata builder declares (; FA3 and FA4 declare ). With the same config starts and serves.
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.22.1 Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.14.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.11 (main, Oct 7 2025, 15:34:39) [Clang 20.1.4 ] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-138-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to : GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition Nvidia driver version : 580.178.04 cuDNN version : Could not collect HIP runtime version : N/A MIOpen runtime version : N/A Is XNNPACK available : False ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.1 [pip3] nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.8.0 [pip3] torch==2.14.0+cu130 [pip3] triton==3.8.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : Could not collect vLLM Version : 0.32.0rc1.dev199+g8f111b22e (git sha: 8f111b22e) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X 0-23 0 N/A ```
The relevant code is unchanged on today's main (`153a17166e`). ### Describe the bug With `enable_adaptive_verification: true` and no `--attention-backend`, startup fails on an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120): ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --max-model-len 4096 --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3", "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "enable_adaptive_verification": true}' ``` ``` ValueError: Adaptive verification replays decode cudagraphs whose per-request query lengths vary up to 5, but FlashAttentionBackend allows none. Pass enable_adaptive_verification=false in the speculative config, or use a backend that does. ``` The selector picks FLASH_ATTN (FA2 on this GPU) because the only adaptive check in `validate_configuration` is `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch`, which FA2 passes. The varlen graph check that rejects it runs later, in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/adaptive_verification.py`, and FA2's metadata builder declares `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH` (`flash_attn.py`; FA3 and FA4 declare `ALWAYS`). With `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` the same config starts and serves. With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, FA2 is excluded for the KV dtype and the selector lands on TRITON_ATTN by itself, so the failure only shows up with BF16 KV. From the source I'd expect every FA2 GPU (SM8x, SM12x) to behave the same; I've only run it on SM120. Would it be right to have the selector skip backends whose decode graphs can't replay varlen batches when adaptive verification is on, so these GPUs fall through to TRITON_ATTN? I can put up a PR if that's the preferred direction.
discussion:
Confirmed the mechanism on current main (be25977532):

- FA2 declares `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py:617`), so varlen decode graphs cannot replay on it.
- The rejection you hit lives in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/adaptive_verification.py:498` (manager creation at worker startup), long after backend selection.
- `_validate_adaptive_verification` (`vllm/config/vllm.py:3074`) currently guards LoRA / full-cudagraph mode / pipeline parallelism, and never consults the selected backend's CG support. So the combination is only caught once the worker comes up.

Your direction looks right to me, with one refinement: rather than teaching the selector to silently skip FA2, reuse the same predicate the worker check uses (`get_varlen_cudagraph_unsupported_backend`) or check the resolved backend's `AttentionCGSupport` during `_validate_adaptive_verification`, and raise there with the actionable message. Failing fast at config time keeps the choice visible to the user; silently falling through to TRITON_ATTN would leave people wondering why FA2 was bypassed. If the project prefers auto-fallback over a hard error, the same check belongs in the same place, just downgraded to a warning plus an explicit backend re-select.

Since you offered first, the PR is yours; happy to review the draft.

I put the check in the selector rather than `_validate_adaptive_verification`: backends are only resolved per layer during model construction, and #47808's review moved the other adaptive-verification check there too. Automatic selection now skips FA2 for verifier layers and logs what it skipped, and an explicit FLASH_ATTN on FA2 fails at selection before the weights load: #62154.

items.title: [#20138][fix] Preserve Qwen3-VL video layout across E/PD
items.author: maheshrbapatu
items.summary: Qwen3-VL's encoder processes video as timestamped frame groups, but E/PD prefill rebuilds the prompt from the original text and embedding row counts. That removes timestamps and frame boundaries while retaining the encoder's mRoPE positions.
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #20138.

Qwen3-VL's encoder processes video as timestamped frame groups, but E/PD prefill rebuilds the prompt from the original text and embedding row counts. That removes timestamps and frame boundaries while retaining the encoder's mRoPE positions. In the local 40-frame reproduction, prefill receives 1,011 prompt tokens instead of 1,169 and generated tokens diverge from aggregated inference.

Carry the encoder's exact prompt and multimodal layout in an optional `DisaggregatedParams.multimodal_input_layout` payload. Qwen3-VL exports it before encoder submission, and prefill consumes it while retaining embedding-shape validation. The payload survives `asdict`/JSON transport and is cleared after prefill. Other processors keep their existing reconstruction path through a default no-op export hook.

Reject mismatched mRoPE shapes before inference. Legacy image handoffs still work; legacy video handoffs with a mismatched reconstructed prompt now raise an error instead of silently using incompatible positions.

## Test Coverage

- CPU regressions cover timestamp and sparse-run preservation, multiple items, serialization, embedding-shape failures, caller-owned metadata, encoder submission, legacy image handoffs, text-only inputs, and prefill-to-decode cleanup.
- Three GPU cases compare aggregated inference with the public encoder-to-prefill API: 8 frames, 40 frames, and two videos. They include a JSON handoff and assert exact prompt-token and generated-token equality.
- The new cases are selected by the existing multimodal directory entries in `l0_cpu.yml` and `l0_h100.yml`.

## Validation

Local hardware: one GH200. Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, revision `89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203`. Runtime: TensorRT-LLM **1.3.0rc29** with the Python patch applied, transformers **5.5.4**, greedy generation capped at 64 tokens, and `do_sample_frames=False`.

- **78 CPU tests passed**, covering the changed prompt/handoff tests plus multimodal runtime and text-only regressions.
- **3 GPU regression tests passed** in `test_mm_encoder_standalone.py::test_video_encoder_handoff_preserves_timestamps`.
- A separate reproduction with the PD worker's vision encoder disabled matched aggregated prompt and output tokens for all three video cases and an image control. All video outputs matched for 64 tokens; the image matched through EOS after 12 tokens. The aggregated outputs also match the original pre-fix baseline exactly.
- Chunked prefill and prefix reuse: a 1,157-token video prompt with a 256-token prefill budget produced identical 64-token outputs for cold/warm aggregated and E/PD requests. Separate cache salts kept both cold paths at zero reused tokens; both warm paths reused 1,156 tokens.
- Formatting/lint and repository pre-commit checks passed.

This is Python-source validation on release binaries, not a full current-main build. AST comparisons confirm the patched handoff methods match the checkout. Rebased onto `fc52f0ad`; none of the eight changed files changed upstream since the original tested base, and the patch is byte-identical after rebase. Three existing protocol tests require newer `remote_tail_start`/multimodal-span fields absent from rc29; the same failures reproduce with the original parameters class and unchanged OpenAI protocol, and those cases are excluded from the 78-test compatible run. Current-main CI remains required. Multi-node serving, a Dynamo HTTP deployment, and other models sharing this processor have not been GPU-qualified by this PR.

## PR Checklist

API classification: `api-compatible` (optional metadata and processor argument). A maintainer needs to apply the label; this account cannot label upstream PRs.

- [x] Reviewed the coding guidelines, test coverage, API compatibility, documentation, and ownership requirements. The handoff field and processor keyword are optional; no dependency, serving configuration, or ownership changes.

items.title: [None][fix] Apply the drafter's declared logit transform in DFlash
items.author: moraxu
items.summary: A DFlash drafter scores tokens through the target's. When the target scales and soft-caps its own logits, its drafters are trained on logits transformed the same way, and their repeats the transform:, then.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

A DFlash drafter scores tokens through the target's `lm_head`. When the target scales and soft-caps its own logits, its drafters are trained on logits transformed the same way, and their `dflash_config` repeats the transform: `output_multiplier`, then `final_logit_softcapping`. Both public Muse Spark Open drafters (`nvidia/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-DFlash2`, `RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2`) declare `0.17677…` and `20.0`, the target's own values. vLLM and SGLang apply them to the draft logits.

TensorRT-LLM did not. The drafter shares the target's `lm_head` but gets the generic logits processor (the target's `MuseSparkOpenLogitsProcessor` is installed after the drafter is built), and nothing read the two fields, so draft logits stayed unscaled: about 5.7 times the trained scale. A position's argmax doesn't change, but the DFlash 2 path selector adds the draft logits to its pairwise scores, and draft sampling (`use_rejection_sampling`) reads them as a distribution, so both ran off the trained scale.

`DFlashForCausalLM` now resolves the transform from `dflash_config` (`resolve_draft_logit_transform`), and `DFlashWorker` applies it to the draft logits before the selector and sampling: the multiplier, then `softcap * tanh(logits / softcap)`, in FP32 and in place. Drafters that declare neither field are unchanged, and the init log line now shows the transform.

## Test Coverage

- New CPU cases in `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_dflash2_semantics.py`: no transform unless declared; multiplier then soft cap, in FP32; and a selector walk that the transform flips while every position's argmax stays the same. With the change, the CPU cases of that file, `test_dflash_worker.py` and `test_dspark_worker.py` pass (39 passed; CUDA-only cases skipped).
- End to end on one 4x GB300 node, Muse Spark Open NVFP4 by Hub id: SPEED-Bench qualitative `coding` (80 prompts, first turn), chat-template defaults, up to 4,096 output tokens, 32 concurrent requests, draft length 7. Acceptance length, before → after:

  | Drafter | Temperature 0 | Temperature 1, top_p 0.95, greedy drafts | Temperature 1, top_p 0.95, `use_rejection_sampling` (guided decoding off) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2` | 3.92 → 4.27 | 3.30 → 3.53 | 3.36 → 3.76 |
  | `nvidia/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-DFlash2` | 3.94 → 3.92 | 3.31 → 3.30 | 3.31 → 3.39 |

  The RadixArk drafter, whose `dflash_config` has always declared the transform, gains 7–12%. NVIDIA's drafter is within noise, matching vLLM's own before/after for it.

items.title: [ROCm][AITER] Enable AITER by default on CDNA3+, keep AMD CI on the non-AITER path
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Enables AITER as the default ROCm inference path on CDNA3+, adds per-shape safety gates for FP8/int8 kernels, fuses SiLU-mul with FP8 quantization, and optimizes kernel launch parameters for bit-identical performance gains.
items.body:
- Default `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` to on (`envs.py`). When it is unset, `_aiter_ops.py` turns AITER on only on CDNA3+ with aiter installed. An explicit value is kept, and RMSNorm priority and the MoE oracles use the gated check.
- Keep AMD CI off AITER unless a test opts in: `ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` in the `ci_base` stage of `Dockerfile.rocm`, plus the same default in `run-amd-test.sh` until `ci_base` is rebuilt.
- Only select AITER kernels for shapes they handle: int8 scaled-mm needs per-token × per-channel scales, and FP8 block-scaled MoE needs hidden size % 512.
- On gfx942, skip AITER RMSNorm, the fused add+RMSNorm+FP8 per-token quant and the fused allreduce+RMSNorm, including with an explicit `=1`, because AITER v0.1.25 rounds bf16 by truncation there. Each has a TODO to revert.
- Fuse SiLU-mul with AITER's static per-tensor FP8 quant (`matcher_utils.py`, `act_quant_fusion.py`) so per-tensor FP8 models keep that fusion when AITER is on.
- Launch 4 blocks per token up to 512 tokens in `silu_and_mul_quant` (`activation_kernels.cu`). With 1 block per token from 33 tokens, the fused kernel was slower than the unfused path. Output is bit-identical.
- Don't enable the QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion without a model config (`vllm.py`).
- Tests: a shared `use_aiter` fixture (`conftest.py`) runs the fusion, config and backend-selection tests with AITER both on and off, and the rest are updated for the new defaults.

AITER is the fast path on MI300/MI355, but users had to export `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` to get it. Running the suites with it on, at the pinned AITER v0.1.25, turned up problems that every `=1` user already hits:
- the int8 kernel asserts on valid configs and silently computes garbage for per-tensor scales;
- FP8 block-scaled MoE faults the GPU for hidden sizes that are not a multiple of 512;
- on gfx942, truncated bf16 stores cost gsm8k strict-match on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: 66.0 vs 70.4 (bf16), 64.6 vs 70.0 (FP8-dynamic) and 67.0 vs 70.3 (bf16 TP=2).

The RMSNorm rounding is fixed upstream in ROCm/aiter#6300, which is not tagged yet; the custom allreduce module still truncates on aiter main (fix in ROCm/aiter#6640). AMD CI stays pinned off for now, so CI coverage does not change.

Behavior changes to be aware of when AITER is on:
- `fuse_norm_quant` defaults on for every model, because the AITER FP8 linear path adds `+quant_fp8` (since #25552).
- With a KV connector, attention auto-selection picks AITER FA before unified attention.
- An explicit `=1` with an unsupported FP8 block-scaled hidden size now errors at startup instead of faulting.
- Known AITER v0.1.25 issue, already hit with `=1`: the persistent fused-MoE kernels launch more workgroups than they plan for when `inter_dim / tile` does not divide the CU count, so FP8 block-scaled and per-token MoE outputs are off during prefill for e.g. Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3-235B and GLM-4.5-Air. Per call this is about 5% relative error, but gsm8k and serving on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 are unchanged. The fix is ROCm/aiter#6639 and arrives with the next AITER bump.
- Two fusions still have no AITER pattern, both already the case with `=1`: fused add+RMSNorm + static per-tensor FP8 quant, and MLA attention + static FP8 output quant. Their AITER-on test variants are strict xfails, so they flag themselves once a pattern lands.

#61595 attempts the same default flip. This PR differs in three ways: it keeps AMD CI off, it gates on hardware for every consumer of the flag, and it fixes the kernel-selection bugs above rather than leaving them reachable.

Validation on MI300X, pinned AITER v0.1.25, with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset, `=1` and `=0`:
- `pytest` runs (fresh compile cache each run):
  - `compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py`, `test_functionalization.py`, `test_fusion.py`, `ir/test_inplace_functionalization.py`: 10/10 in the unset mode.
  - The tests with AITER on/off variants pass in every mode, e.g. `compile/test_config.py` (89 passed).
  - `kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`, `test_mxfp8_aiter_backend_selection.py`, `test_fp8_tp_loading.py`: 10/10 in each mode.
  - `quantization/test_quark.py::test_quark_int8_w_per_tensor_a_per_tensor`: 10/10 on aiter 0.1.24.post1 and v0.1.25.
  - `quantization/test_quark.py::test_quark_fp8_w8a8_per_block_moe`: 10/10 on aiter 0.1.24.post1 and v0.1.25 with the variable unset. Its model has hidden size 128, so with an explicit `=1` it errors at startup, as described above.
  - With `=0` (what CI runs), the compile, config, MoE, quantization and attention-selection groups all pass.
- `lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot (full 1319) after the gfx942 gates, branch defaults vs control:
  - Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct FP8-dynamic: 69.9 / 69.5 vs 70.0 (paired McNemar p = 0.70 / 0.43).
  - bf16 TP=2: recovers to the unfused level (p = 6e-5 vs the old fused default).
- SiLU-mul + AITER per-tensor FP8 fusion on RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8, with #61716: median TPOT at concurrency 4 is 0.99x unfused, throughput at rate inf is 1.01x, and gsm8k shows no significant change.
- `silu_and_mul_quant` launch grid on MI300X: bit-identical on 2400 shapes plus 2720 more at 130-609 tokens. The kernel is 1.8-2.6x faster at 17-128 tokens and 1.0-1.56x at 129-512, unchanged elsewhere; above 512 four blocks per token stops paying off (3-9% slower at 576-608 tokens), hence the cutoff. `vllm bench latency` on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 is 1.0% faster at batch 32 and 2.2% at batch 64; the 129-512 step is below its ~0.5% resolution. `tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py` passes 10/10. Not measured on NVIDIA, where the old 16/32 cutoffs may have been tuned.
- `vllm bench serve` cost of the gfx942 gates: +3.2% median TPOT at concurrency 4 for the FP8 fused-add gate. The allreduce+RMSNorm gate is within noise.

AITER on (new default) vs off, MI300X (gfx942), AITER v0.1.25:

`on` = `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset (new default), `off` = `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0`. `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, `--ignore-eos`, 40 warmups, `--max-model-len 4096`, fresh server per run, 3 interleaved repeats per arm. Values are the median of 3; `*` = on/off min-max ranges do not overlap.

| Model | Config | Output tok/s on / off | ratio | TPOT p50 ms on / off | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct bf16, TP1 | 400 prompts, rate inf | 4807 / 4788 | 1.004 | 58.64 / 58.21 | 1.007 |
| | 100 prompts, conc 4 | 684 / 680 | 1.006 | 5.74 / 5.75 | 0.998 |
| | 200 prompts, conc 32 | 3434 / 3420 | 1.004 | 8.32 / 8.41 | 0.989 |
| | gsm8k 5-shot flex (2 runs per arm) | 0.7703, 0.7824 / 0.7824, 0.7786 | | McNemar p 0.033, 0.55 (same-arm on1 vs on2: p 0.033) | |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct bf16, TP2 | 400 prompts, rate inf | 5675 / 5680 | 0.999 | 46.03 / 46.77 | 0.984 |
| | 100 prompts, conc 4 | 973 / 963 | 1.010* | 4.00 / 4.04 | 0.990* |
| | 200 prompts, conc 32 | 4793 / 4811 | 0.996 | 5.97 / 5.98 | 0.999 |
| | gsm8k 5-shot flex (2 runs per arm) | 0.7710, 0.7832 / 0.7794, 0.7786 | | McNemar p 0.16, 0.36 (same-arm on1 vs on2: p 0.023) | |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 (per-tensor), TP1 | 400 prompts, rate inf | 6401 / 6444 | 0.993* | 45.78 / 44.53 | 1.028* |
| | 100 prompts, conc 4 | 935 / 966 | 0.968* | 4.15 / 4.00 | 1.037* |
| | 200 prompts, conc 32 | 4734 / 4796 | 0.987* | 6.03 / 5.92 | 1.019* |
| | gsm8k 5-shot flex | 0.7733 / 0.7771 | | McNemar p 0.72 | |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (block FP8 MoE), TP1 | 400 prompts, rate inf | 6684 / 5382 | 1.242* | 44.26 / 54.09 | 0.818* |
| | 100 prompts, conc 4 | 688 / 509 | 1.351* | 5.62 / 7.70 | 0.730* |
| | 200 prompts, conc 32 | 3132 / 2278 | 1.375* | 9.30 / 12.77 | 0.728* |
| | gsm8k 5-shot flex | 0.8302 / 0.8294 | | McNemar p 1.00 | |

Caveats: on gfx942 the new default changes nothing that runs for bf16 TP1 Llama (ROCM_ATTN and native RMSNorm in both arms; the logs confirm this, and one on run and one off run produced byte-identical gsm8k generations). For bf16 TP2 the only change is AITER custom all-reduce, which is neutral within noise. The clear win is the AITER FP8 MoE and block-scaled GEMM path on Qwen3-30B-A3B (+24-38% throughput). Per-tensor FP8 Llama shows a small, reproducible decode regression (+2-4% TPOT): `+quant_fp8` makes the FP8 quant a standalone AITER kernel, and the RMSNorm+quant fusion then matches 0 patterns because AITER RMSNorm is gated off on gfx942. That mechanism is inferred, not proven. gsm8k sampling is not deterministic run to run at seed 1234 (same-arm reruns differ by up to p=0.023), so no accuracy change is detectable in any model.

items.title: [Bug] [AMD] select_experts casts the fp32 MoE correction bias to bf16 before #37133's fp32 aiter path, so GLM-5.x still routes with a bf16 bias
items.author: jhinpan
items.summary: keeps in fp32 for GlmMoeDsa (, #37133). On this path the router logits are bf16: returns. [Discussion: Hi @jhinpan — thanks for the thorough report and the detailed repro data.]
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, GLM-5.x (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) still routes its MoE with a bf16 correction bias. #37133 keeps the bias in fp32 for this architecture, but on main (4cca7fcd3e) the bias is cast back to bf16 before the code #37133 added can use it:

1. `MoEGate.__init__` keeps `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32 for GlmMoeDsa ([deepseek_v2.py#L513-L529](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py#L513-L529), #37133).
2. On this path the router logits are bf16: `aiter_dsv3_router_gemm` returns `tgemm.mm(..., otype=hidden_states.dtype)` ([rocm_linear_utils.py#L30-L35](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/layers/rocm_linear_utils.py#L30-L35)).
3. `select_experts` replaces the bias with a cached copy in the logits' dtype, `topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype)`, whenever `_use_aiter and use_grouped_topk and not SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK and dynamic_expert_bias is None` ([topk.py#L2616-L2626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py#L2616-L2626), from #33838).
4. The aiter branch of `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` keeps an fp32 bias and upcasts the logits instead ([topk.py#L1944-L1954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py#L1944-L1954), #37133), but the bias it receives is already bf16, so that branch does not run.

#37133's unit test checks the parameter dtype in `MoEGate` only, so it does not cover step 3.

Effect on GLM-5.3 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`): the bias of the 75 MoE layers lies between 3.7 and 34.6, with a per-layer standard deviation of 0.04 to 0.14. In bf16, the 256 values of a layer collapse to 3 to 16 distinct values (median 7), and the largest rounding error of a layer (median 0.031) is close to the spread itself (median standard deviation 0.040). On layer 3, 174 distinct values in [33.985, 34.623] become 3.

On a GLM-5.3 TP8 server on MI355X (eager, decode steps of 1 and 8 rows, 38,325 token-layer pairs), SGLang's routed top-8 differs from the top-8 of the same bf16 logits with the fp32 bias in 67.6% of token-layer pairs, 1.32 of 8 experts on average. Layers 3 to 7 differ for nearly every token; the least affected layer (41) differs for 28%.

CUDA keeps the bias in fp32 (flashinfer `fused_topk_deepseek` and the JIT router), so the two platforms route GLM-5.x differently. As #37133 notes for GLM-5.2, standard benchmarks may not show this; I did not measure the accuracy effect.

Skipping the downcast in step 3 for an fp32 bias restores fp32 routing on the aiter path (`NO_PRECAST=1` below: 0.0% to 0.1% of tokens differ). Setting `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1` also avoids it (0.0%), through the JIT router.

### Reproduction

`repro_topk.py`, on one MI355X with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`: `select_experts` with GLM-5.3's fp32 bias and random bf16 logits, against the same routing in fp32.

```python
"""select_experts on ROCm (SGLANG_USE_AITER=1) with GLM-5.3's fp32 correction bias
and bf16 router logits, against the same routing done in fp32.
Usage: repro_topk.py <GLM-5.3 checkpoint dir> [layer]"""

import json
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from safetensors import safe_open

from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import TopKConfig, select_experts

if os.environ.get("NO_PRECAST") == "1":
    # what skipping select_experts' bias downcast does: the aiter branch sees fp32
    TopKConfig.correction_bias_for_dtype = lambda self, dtype: self.correction_bias

root = sys.argv[1]
layer = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3
name = f"model.layers.{layer}.mlp.gate.e_score_correction_bias"
index = json.load(open(f"{root}/model.safetensors.index.json"))["weight_map"]
with safe_open(f"{root}/{index[name]}", "pt") as f:
    bias = f.get_tensor(name).cuda()  # fp32, as MoEGate keeps it for GlmMoeDsa

torch.manual_seed(0)
tokens = 4096
# bf16, as aiter_dsv3_router_gemm returns them
logits = torch.randn(tokens, 256, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
cfg = TopKConfig(
    top_k=8,
    use_grouped_topk=True,
    topk_group=1,
    num_expert_group=1,
    renormalize=True,
    correction_bias=bias,
    scoring_func="sigmoid",
    routed_scaling_factor=2.5,
)
hidden = torch.empty(tokens, 6144, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
out = select_experts(hidden_states=hidden, router_logits=logits, topk_config=cfg)
got = out.topk_ids[:, :8].long()
ref = (torch.sigmoid(logits.float()) + bias).topk(8, dim=-1).indices
same = (F.one_hot(got, 256).sum(1) * F.one_hot(ref, 256).sum(1)).sum(-1)
print(
    f"layer {layer}: bias {bias.dtype} in [{bias.min().item():.3f}, {bias.max().item():.3f}], "
    f"{bias.unique().numel()} distinct values, {bias.bfloat16().unique().numel()} in bf16"
)
print(f"tokens whose top-8 set differs from fp32 routing: {(same < 8).float().mean().item():.1%}")
```

```
$ SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 repro_topk.py /path/to/GLM-5.3 3
layer 3: bias torch.float32 in [33.985, 34.623], 174 distinct values, 3 in bf16
tokens whose top-8 set differs from fp32 routing: 99.8%
```

| default | 99.8% | 89.6% | 95.8% |
| `NO_PRECAST=1` (aiter top-k with the fp32 bias) | 0.1% | 0.0% | 0.1% |
| `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1` | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% |

items.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Read GPU Engram tables from peers' HBM instead of DP collectives
items.author: Juntian777
items.summary: Decode runs in FULL CUDA graphs, which do not honor, so these collectives are captured next to MegaMoE's cross-rank kernels. In DEP decode on GB200, every rank then blocks in of the same decode graph at the first real step (seen with ); host-offloaded tables,…
items.body:
## Purpose

With `cpu_offload: false`, DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables live in HBM, but every lookup still goes through DP collectives: a pynccl `all_gather` of the hash ids and an `all_to_all_single` of the rows on the node-local `edp` group. Decode runs in FULL CUDA graphs, which do not honor `eager_break_during_capture`, so these collectives are captured next to MegaMoE's cross-rank kernels. In DEP decode on GB200, every rank then blocks in `graph.replay()` of the same decode graph at the first real step (seen with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`); host-offloaded tables, with no NCCL in the graph, never hang. I did not pin down the exact NCCL/MegaMoE interaction. This PR removes the collectives instead: GPU tables are row-sharded over the Engram DP group in symmetric memory, and each rank looks up only its own tokens, reading every row from the owning peer's HBM. Lookups need no collective, barrier or graph break.

* **Kernel.** `_engram_lookup_kernel` gains `PEER_ROWS`. With it, `weight` is a per-rank pointer table: a row's owner is `id // PEER_ROWS`, and its scales follow the rows in the same symmetric buffer. Tables are read-only after loading, so reads need no synchronization.
* **When.** `cpu_offload: false`, TP=1 and an Engram DP group (co-located DP replicas). The table sets `dp_size = 1`, as `dp_shared_memory` does, and `DeepseekV4Model` reads that to skip the hash gather and dummy hashes. Host tables keep `dp_shared_memory` / `EngramPeerExchange`, since symmetric memory cannot map another process's host memory.
* **Across nodes.** By default the group stays node-local. With `embedding_across_dp: true` (off by default), GPU tables are split over every DP rank, e.g. 1/32 of the table per GPU at DEP32; all DP ranks must then share one NVLink domain, as on GB200 NVL72. A group with the DP group's ranks reuses `_DP` instead of building a second communicator: a separate 32-rank group cost ~1.1 GiB/GPU and failed `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`.
* **Not covered.** GPU tables with TP > 1 keep head sharding and its collectives. Peer mode stages BF16 rows per layer rather than `EngramBatch`'s packed MXFP8 rows, so `wkv` quantizes its own input; feeding packed peer rows to `EngramBatch` is a possible follow-up.

## Where it matters

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode-only on GB200, DEP16 / DEP32 (DP x TP1 + EP), 16 requests/rank, MegaMoE, MegaAttention, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance 3.51), EPLB, full decode CUDA graphs, `DecodeBenchConnector` replaying an agentic coding trace. Unprofiled steady state (+60 to +240 s), one run each, on a development tree based on `fe4df3df` with #61767; its Engram code is identical to main. Without this PR, `cpu_offload: false` hangs in this setup, so the baseline is the default host offload. GPU tables use `embedding_across_dp: true`.

| | host offload | GPU tables, peer read |
| -- | --: | --: |
| DEP16 step (ms) | 14.13 | 13.71 |
| DEP16 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,777 | 3,827 |
| DEP32 step (ms) | 13.15 | 12.90 |
| DEP32 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,877 | 3,939 |
| Model memory, DEP16 / DEP32 (GiB/GPU) | | 28.9 / 20.3 |

## Microbenchmark

Both Engram layers' lookups for one decode step, 96 tokens/rank, 16 ranks on 4 GB200 nodes, CUDA graph replay with fresh ids, median over ranks.

| Table layout | us/step |
| -- | --: |
| Host UVA (offload) | 233-324 |
| HBM, heads over 4 GPUs + `all_gather` + `all_to_all` (main; hangs in FULL graphs) | 46.7 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs + `all_gather` + `reduce_scatter` | 180.6 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs, peer read (this PR) | 19.8 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
```

* `test_engram_table_shared_across_dp_replicas` (4 GPUs): the TP1 x DP4 GPU-table case now takes the peer path, asserts that no DP `all_gather` runs, and replays a FULL CUDA graph with fresh ids.
* `test_engram_group_creation_honors_model_and_options`: TP1 x DP4 cases for the node-local group vs `embedding_across_dp`, and `_DP` reuse.

## Test Result

On 4 x GB200: 29 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaAttention, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, DSpark (5 tokens), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`.

| | Engram tables | strict match | flexible extract |
| -- | -- | --: | --: |
| this PR, DEP8 over two GB200 nodes | GPU, rows over all 8 DP ranks (peer read) | 92.57% (±0.72) | 92.72% |
| #61371, DEP4 | host offload | 92.87% (±0.71) | |

The first revision of this PR gave 92.87% / 92.95% on the same setup.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# head node
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --port 8123 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --data-parallel-address <head> --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false,"embedding_across_dp":true}' \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --numa-bind
# second node: the same command plus --headless --data-parallel-start-rank 4

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8123/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024
```

</details>

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `engram symmetric memory`, `engram peer`, `engram cpu_offload`, `engram hang` and `engram DP`. #59923 and #56512 cover the exchange for host-offloaded tables; #60625 changes head sharding for TP16/TP32 and keeps the collectives.

items.title: [Feat] decisions: Support cold shared-prefix prefill with MIS
items.author: Jiminator
items.summary: A cold request can prefill the same input once per question. The engine already supports MIS query sharing and Qwen3.5/3.8 GDN state branching from #33922, but the decisions route rejects and submits full prompts as separate items.
items.body:
## Motivation

A cold `/v1/decisions` request can prefill the same input once per question. The engine already supports MIS query sharing and Qwen3.5/3.8 GDN state branching from #33922, but the decisions route rejects `--enable-mis` and submits full prompts as separate items.

## Modifications

- Pack the questions' common token prefix as the MIS query and their remaining tokens as independent items. Preserve per-question labels, temperature, raw label mass and caller order. Keep the ordinary path unchanged.
- Check the complete packed prefill budget and reject images and speculative decoding. Keep the existing System One behavior. `usage.prompt_tokens` reports the packed sequence.
- Propagate MIS positions to the mRoPE tensor consumed by Qwen3.5/3.8. Empty-query delimiters receive a valid dummy position, avoiding an invalid fused-RoPE lookup.
- Extend the existing CPU suites and document the opt-in behavior and limits. No new GDN kernels or cache support.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Render question prompts] --> B[Common prefix + question tails]
    B --> C[Existing MIS score request]
    C --> D[Item-relative positions + mRoPE]
    D --> E[Shared query prefill + independent GDN branches]
    E --> F[Per-question label scores]
```

## Accuracy Tests

Validation covers the serving contract on a fixed synthetic workload:

- `test_serving_decisions.py`: **30 passed**; `test_gdn_mis_metadata.py`: **5 passed**.
- Existing `test_qwen35_gdn_multi_item_scoring.py`, with the pinned **Qwen3.8-27B** checkpoint: **3 passed**, including empty queries, sibling changes/reordering and concurrent requests.
- Negative controls reproduce the original MIS refusal and wrong mRoPE coordinates. Removing the empty-query clamp reproduces the invalid RoPE index; the final long empty-query replay returns 200 with finite scores.
- `/v1/decisions` equals manually packed `/v1/score` exactly. Changing a sibling's contents without changing its shape leaves the other rows bit-identical.
- Additional GPU edge checks cover single/identical questions, concurrency, image and oversized-input refusals, and valid requests after errors. These exercise unchanged no-speculation/nonempty-prefix paths; final-commit API parity, content isolation and the long empty-query replay were executed again.

**Scores are not numerically interchangeable with the original prompts.** All eight top-scoring labels matched on the main workload, but normalized probabilities differed by up to **0.152**; separate single-question probes reached **0.191** because the prefix split changes. Expected numeric scores can therefore change too.

A fixed-query packed-versus-single check measured **0.02236** with the default BF16 readout, failing an initially chosen 0.02 normalized bound. That bound was incorrectly derived from #33922's **unnormalized** score test; it is not presented as passing. BF16 logit steps amplify small layout differences. With the existing FP32 LM-head flag, the measured maximum was **0.01270**. An independent, unchanged SIS reference with an FP32 head moved **0.02500** when only prefill chunking changed. These are measurements, not accuracy or determinism guarantees. No test tolerance was relaxed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One NVIDIA GB300, TP=1, Qwen3.8-27B revision `1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`, BF16 weights/KV and FP32 GDN state. Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. Eight questions share 3,985 tokens. Both arms disable radix caching, chunked prefill and CUDA graphs; concurrency 1, three kernel warmups, ten measured HTTP round trips, zero errors.

| Mode | Median complete-request latency | Computed tokens | Cached tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SIS, base `456231e251` | 1217.5 ms | 32,155 | 0 |
| MIS, this change | 320.0 ms | 4,269 | 0 |

**3.81× faster on this workload, with 86.7% fewer computed tokens.** The API input is the same; MIS delimiter semantics differ as described above. The final profile records 48 `_forward_extend_mis` calls and 96 `_forward_mis_segments` calls: one query phase and one item phase for each GDN layer.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the measured workload</summary>

Run the base without `--enable-mis`, and the candidate with it, on the same GPU. All other settings are the same:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --revision 1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0 \
  --served-model-name qwen38-decisions --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31500 \
  --tp 1 --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton \
  --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --context-length 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 16 --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --enable-mis
```

```python
import statistics
import time
import requests

state = "\n".join(
    f"[{i:03d}] customer: order #{4400 + i} "
    f"{'was charged twice' if i % 5 == 0 else 'shows as shipped but has not arrived'}; "
    f"agent: we escalated to {'billing' if i % 5 == 0 else 'logistics'} "
    f"and will update within {(i % 4) + 1} business days."
    for i in range(110)
)
questions = [{'id': 'team',
  'type': 'choice',
  'question': 'Which team should own this thread?',
  'options': [{'name': 'billing'}, {'name': 'logistics'}, {'name': 'technical'}]},
 {'id': 'refund', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Does any customer ask for a refund?'},
 {'id': 'urgency',
  'type': 'score',
  'question': 'How urgent is the thread?',
  'levels': ['low', 'medium', 'high']},
 {'id': 'escalate', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Should a supervisor review this thread?'},
 {'id': 'sentiment',
  'type': 'score',
  'question': 'Overall customer sentiment',
  'levels': ['angry', 'upset', 'neutral', 'happy']},
 {'id': 'channel',
  'type': 'choice',
  'question': 'Which channel is this?',
  'options': [{'name': 'email'}, {'name': 'chat'}, {'name': 'phone'}]},
 {'id': 'fraud', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Is there any sign of fraud?'},
 {'id': 'resolved', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Is every issue in the thread resolved?'}]
payload = {
    "model": "qwen38-decisions", "input": state, "questions": questions,
    "return_prompt_token_ids": False,
}
session = requests.Session()
latencies = []
for i in range(13):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    response = session.post("http://127.0.0.1:31500/v1/decisions", json=payload, timeout=240)
    elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    response.raise_for_status()
    if i >= 3:
        latencies.append(elapsed_ms)
print("median ms:", statistics.median(latencies))
print("usage:", response.json()["usage"])
```

</details>

This is a **cold, text-only prototype**. MIS disables warm prefix reuse server-wide. Use a dedicated scoring server without speculative decoding; mixed generation traffic is not supported. The validated 32K prefill envelope stays below the inherited 65,535-token per-item MIS limit. Clef's trained joint-head path is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on the exact candidate.
- [x] Focused CPU regressions and real Qwen3.8 GPU checks passed.
- [x] Documentation updated; Mintlify build and link checks passed.
- [x] Measured latency, dispatch and numerical limitations recorded.
- [ ] Upstream CI has not been requested.

items.title: [TRTLLM-17014][infra] migrate build artifacts to artifactory.nvidia.com
items.author: sharabeshj-nvda
items.summary: <!-- Please explain the issue and the solution in short.
items.body:
Publish build_info.txt, the packaged builds (*.tar.gz) and waive_list/ to sw-tensorrt-llm-generic-local on artifactory.nvidia.com instead of sw-tensorrt-generic on urm.nvidia.com, and read them from there first.

- Readers fall back to urm only when a file is absent (HTTP 404), so builds published before the switch stay readable. A rejected credential fails fast with a message that names the credential, and never falls back.
- jenkins/scripts/fetch_build_artifact.sh is the read helper for the pipelines, the Slurm launcher, the image build and BOLT profile generation; jenkins/scripts/check_artifactory_access.sh checks the CI identities in each environment.
- LLM_ARTIFACTS_PRIMARY=urm on the Jenkins controllers returns publishing and first reads to urm without a code change. A parent pipeline passes its value to the jobs it starts.
- Build reuse copies within one instance, and rebuilds when the earlier build is only on the other one.
- While under test, jenkins/L0_MergeRequest.groovy loads trtllm-jenkins-shared-lib from the branch of the library change that adds the artifactory.nvidia.com destination to uploadArtifacts.
- specs/001-migrate-builds-aws-artifactory/ carries the design documents for review while the pull request is a draft. They are removed before it is marked ready.

items.title: [CI][Unit Test] Patch MoE layer unit tests for Blackwell and Rubin
items.author: johncalesp
items.summary: Why the buffer grouping is necessary The test runs multiple MoE configurations within the same distributed workers. NIXL retains a process-wide communication buffer whose expert capacity is established during its first initialization.
items.body:
## Overview


Why the buffer grouping is necessary

  The test runs multiple MoE configurations within the same distributed workers. NIXL retains a process-wide communication buffer whose expert capacity is established during its first initialization.

  In the failing sequence, the first configuration allocates capacity for eight experts. Later configurations request 64 experts, but receive the same buffer. NIXL then rejects the request with its active/maximum expert-bound assertion. Running the affected configurations in fresh processes removes that assertion.

  Calling the manager’s destroy() between configurations does not resolve this: it intentionally retains the buffer to support elastic expert-parallel scaling.

  Why rename _group_deepep_ll_configs

  The existing helper already implements the required pattern: group compatible configurations and launch separate workers for incompatible groups. Its purpose now applies to both ROCm DeepEP low-latency and NIXL EP.

  Renaming it to _group_configs_by_buffer_requirements describes that shared responsibility and avoids maintaining two implementations of the same grouping logic. The key includes:

  • Routed hidden size.
  • Expert-parallel size.
  • Total expert count.

  For latent MoE, the routed hidden size is k // 2, so grouping must account for the input transform. Token capacity and the other allocation settings are fixed within the outer test case.

  Fresh workers provide a clear lifetime boundary without changing production buffer management or its elastic-scaling behavior. Grouping also retains buffer reuse among compatible cases: this matrix needs four worker groups, rather than restarting workers for every one of its 52 subcases.

  Why preserve padded weights

  The latent configurations generate 1024-wide expert weights, while NIXL requires a supported hidden size of at least 2048. The layer correctly allocates padded parameters, but the test replaces them with smaller tensors. Activations remain padded, producing:

  Hidden size mismatch 2048 != 1024

  The patch keeps the allocated parameter, zeros its padding, and copies the original weights into the valid hidden-dimension slice. This preserves W13’s input padding and W2’s output padding. Other dimension mismatches still fail an assertion.

  Both corrections belong in the test setup: one respects the communication buffer’s lifetime, and the other respects the layer’s allocated weight layout.

  Related work, PR #61156 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61156), limits NIXL dispatch token capacity. It addresses a different dimension of buffer sizing and does not fix these test weight-loading or cross-configuration lifetime problems.

## Validation



Executed the exact original case:

  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
    'tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py::test_moe_layer[False-nixl_ep-2-1-True]'

| Configuration.  |  passed   |  failed  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | --------------- |
| Original test.     |             24             |        28               |
| Patched test     |             52             |         0                |

Validation used two SM107 and SM100 GPUs with the Oct16 nightly container, NIXL 1.5.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, and PyTorch 2.16.0.dev20261009+cu134.

Additional worker launches increase test setup overhead and change random draw sequences. This validates the same configuration matrix with unchanged numerical checks; it is not an identical-tensor replay.

items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] fp8-gemm: L2-aware CTA swizzle for the SM12x blockwise FP8 GEMM
items.author: puncsky
items.summary: On GB10 (DGX Spark, SM121, 48 SMs, 24 MiB L2), Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 prefills at 850 tok/s (32K prompt) with the default, which resolves to on SM12x. vLLM v0.31.0 on the same machine reaches 1852 tok/s.
items.body:
## Motivation

On GB10 (DGX Spark, SM121, 48 SMs, 24 MiB L2), Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 prefills at 850 tok/s (32K prompt) with the default `--fp8-gemm-backend auto`, which resolves to `cutlass` on SM12x. vLLM v0.31.0 on the same machine reaches 1852 tok/s. `--fp8-gemm-backend deep_gemm` gets to 1757, but it forces UE8M0 scales on SM12x (linear-layer error 3.8% vs 2.6%) and is 15% slower at decode sizes. So the default kernel needs fixing; switching backends is not the answer.

The cause is CTA rasterization. With `max_swizzle_size` left at 1, the persistent scheduler's heuristic raster walks the shorter tile dimension first. That re-reads the smaller operand once per tile row or column of the larger one. While that operand fits in L2 this is free. At prefill-sized M neither the weight nor the activation fits in 24 MiB, every re-read goes to DRAM, and the gate_up_proj GEMM drops from 175 TFLOP/s at M=2048 to 51 at M=8192.

vLLM's SM120 blockwise kernel already sets `max_swizzle_size = 8` whenever the weight exceeds L2 (`csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_blockwise_sm120_fp8.cu`). This PR does the same, but only when *neither* operand fits. The narrower condition avoids a 3% (up to 15% per GEMM) regression at M=512–1024, measured below.

Related: #33629 (SM120 FP8 blockwise GEMM optimization on Qwen3.6-27B shapes; it covered M < 64 and was closed for inactivity), #30438 (moved the SM120 kernel to JIT, added swapAB).

## Modifications

One file changes: `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/fp8_blockwise/fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120.cuh`.

- A new helper `blockwise_fp8_swizzle_size(device, weight_bytes, act_bytes)` returns 8 when `min(weight, activation) > 3/4 × L2` and 1 otherwise. L2 size is read with `cudaDevAttrL2CacheSize` and cached per device, the same way `get_sm_count` is.
  - If you prefer, it can move to `sgl_kernel/runtime.cuh` as `get_l2_cache_size` next to `get_sm_count`.
- Both launchers set `args.scheduler.max_swizzle_size` from it.
  - The swapAB launcher matters at large M too: `sm120_fp8_blockwise_dispatch_shape` sends every `m % 4 != 0` there (the MN-major activation scales need M % 4 == 0), so uneven prefill batches, e.g. 7 requests totalling 7533 tokens, take it.
  - For M ≤ 256 the activation stays far below 3/4 of L2, so those calls keep size 1.

Effects:

- Parts whose L2 holds the operands (RTX PRO 6000 / 5090: 96–128 MiB) keep the default order.
- Decode sizes are unaffected.
- Data-parallel launches produce bit-identical outputs.
- Stream-K launches (last-wave waste > 0.5) change only in the last bits, because the swizzled order changes the Stream-K split of the K loop. Relative error against an FP32 reference moves by at most 1.9e-9.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Kernel.** `out_sha256` is identical for 59/70 (shape, M) points against the unpatched kernel.
  - The 11 that differ are exactly the swizzled launches whose last wave is less than half full, predicted from the tile count and the rule (11/11).
  - In the non-swapAB launcher those are the Stream-K launches.
  - Run twice, the unpatched kernel gives 70/70 identical outputs, and so does the patched one.
  - Relative error against an FP32 matmul of the dequantized weight is 2.576e-2 on both sides, and differs by at most 1.9e-9 at any point. That figure is mostly the shared per-token FP8 activation quantization.
- **End to end.** GSM8K test, 200 questions, seed 0, greedy, `enable_thinking=false`, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8:
  - default, vLLM's rule and this PR: 96.5% (193/200) each;
  - all three miss the same 7 questions.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Environment.**

- Hardware: DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.0, kernel 7.0.0-1019-nvidia.
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130@sha256:b1259f3e…` with the patched file bind-mounted (the file is identical on main as of 2026-10-16). sglang 0.5.21, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.18.
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (block 128×128 e4m3, revision 017b9c7a), TP=1.

**Kernel.** Shapes are the five Qwen3.8-27B FP8 linears at TP=1, the same table as #33629:

| linear | (N, K) | per forward |
|---|---|---|
| gate_up_proj | (34816, 5120) | ×64 |
| down_proj | (5120, 17408) | ×64 |
| in_proj_qkvz | (16384, 5120) | ×48 |
| qkv_proj | (14336, 5120) | ×16 |
| out_proj / o_proj | (5120, 6144) | ×64 |

Each timed call is `cutlass_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`: per-token-group activation quantization plus the GEMM. Timing uses `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(use_cuda_graph=True)`, median of the repeats. cupti-python is not in the image, so FlashInfer falls back to CUDA-graph replays timed by CUDA events. **Edit:** I first wrote "with cold L2" here, but these tables were timed with the operands captured in a closure, which FlashInfer cannot rotate, so L2 was not cold between replays. Re-timed with the activation, weight and scales passed as `input_args` (FlashInfer then rotates copies of them for a cold L2), each of the four arms in the next table moves by at most 2.7% at any M (median under 1%), about the run-to-run spread noted below, and the outputs are bit-identical (70/70 points). The gap to vLLM's rule at M = 512–1024 stays: 176.0 vs 170.3 ms at M=512 and 326.7 vs 311.2 at M=1024.

FP8 linear time per forward pass, in ms (sum over shapes × linears per forward):

| M | default | vLLM rule (weight > L2) | this PR | vLLM 0.31.0 CUTLASS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 110.3 | 110.1 | 110.3 | 108.6 |
| 16 | 111.3 | 111.5 | 110.6 | 110.6 |
| 256 | 131.8 | 132.1 | 131.6 | 131.7 |
| 512 | 170.4 | 175.6 | 169.8 | 175.4 |
| 1023 (M % 4 ≠ 0) | 312.3 | 322.8 | 309.9 | 323.0 |
| 1024 | 310.9 | 319.0 | 304.7 | 315.7 |
| 2048 | 670.9 | 653.7 | 645.4 | 660.1 |
| 4095 (M % 4 ≠ 0) | 2110.7 | 1309.4 | 1318.2 | 1315.5 |
| 4096 | 2058.9 | 1326.8 | 1315.5 | 1310.8 |
| 8191 (M % 4 ≠ 0) | 7598.5 | 2581.7 | 2577.8 | 2601.0 |
| 8192 | 7634.4 | 2585.1 | 2593.6 | 2573.5 |

TFLOP/s for the two largest linears:

| M | gate_up default | gate_up this PR | down_proj default | down_proj vLLM rule | down_proj this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 168.1 | 172.0 | 145.5 | 126.9 | 146.5 |
| 2048 | 176.0 | 175.4 | 106.1 | 123.9 | 119.7 |
| 4095 | 113.3 | 167.6 | 68.4 | 125.7 | 122.3 |
| 4096 | 122.5 | 164.7 | 67.7 | 121.3 | 125.8 |
| 8191 | 50.2 | 172.3 | 58.3 | 125.1 | 124.9 |
| 8192 | 49.9 | 171.5 | 58.6 | 124.2 | 123.7 |

`M % 4 ≠ 0` rows go through the swapAB kernel; this PR fixes them as it does the aligned ones. Without the swapAB-launcher change the M=8191 row stays at the default's 7598 ms.

Other rules tried, each a one-line change to the helper (per-forward ms):

| rule | M=1024 | M=4096 | M=8192 |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (size 1) | 313.7 | 2139.1 | 7534.2 |
| weight > L2, size 2 | 305.1 | 1657.1 | 4414.0 |
| weight > L2, size 4 | 307.5 | 1413.7 | 2894.2 |
| weight > L2, size 8 (vLLM's rule) | 324.0 | 1311.3 | 2582.9 |
| weight > L2 and activation > L2/2, size 8 | 323.3 | 1309.4 | 2572.3 |
| weight > L2 and activation > 3/4 L2, size 8 | 307.5 | 1303.1 | 2557.7 |
| min(weight, activation) > 3/4 L2, size 8 (this PR) | 310.7 | 1322.6 | 2584.6 |

The "weight > L2 and activation > 3/4 L2" rule and this PR give the same outputs at every point (55/55 `out_sha256`): for these shapes the weight always exceeds L2, so the conditions agree. Repeat runs of the same kernel vary by up to ~2% per forward and ~5% for a single GEMM cell.

**End to end.** Server: `python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --context-length 131072 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 --reasoning-parser qwen3`. Client: `vllm bench serve` (vLLM v0.31.0) with random token prompts, greedy:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --base-url http://localhost:30000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --temperature 0 --seed 0 --dataset-name random --ignore-eos \
  --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 3 --max-concurrency 1
# 127K prefill: --random-input-len 126976 --num-prompts 2
# concurrency 32: --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 32
```

| | default | vLLM rule | this PR | vLLM 0.31.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 32K prompt, tok/s | 850 | 1774 | 1776 | 1852 |
| prefill 127K prompt (126976 tokens), tok/s | 703 | 1212 | 1212 | 1217 |
| concurrency 32 (1K in, 256 out, 128 prompts), output tok/s | 98.3 | 130.0 | 129.3 | 133.0 |
| same, median TTFT | 29.6 s | 12.9 s | 12.9 s | 3.3 s |
| single stream, ITL | 128 ms | 128 ms | 129 ms | 128 ms |

Prefill is 2.1× the default at 32K and 1.7× at 127K, within 4% of vLLM.

- A second launch of each arm gave 1768 / 1209 tok/s (vLLM rule) and 1758 / 1212 (this PR).
- Within a launch the three 32K requests agree to 0.2%. Across launches they differ by up to 6%: an earlier launch took the same kernel path at 32K and gave 1672, since every 8192-token chunk is aligned and only the 53-token tail goes through swapAB.
- So this PR and vLLM's rule tie end to end. The rule only matters at the M = 512–1024 kernel points above.
- The c32 TTFT gap that remains to vLLM is scheduling (prefill chunks and decode run in synchronized waves), not the GEMM.

The kernel numbers come from a standalone script that times `cutlass_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` at the shapes above. I can add it under `benchmark/kernels/` if that would help review.

items.title: [Doc] hicache: Explain HiCache host pool sizing with a storage backend
items.author: feixiangpeng
items.summary: Reproducing the issue's configuration on main (Qwen3-1.7B,, backend) shows that the storage lookup works and finds the prompt. The hit is then dropped as, because the host pool has no free room to stage it.
items.body:
Refs #38452

## Motivation

#38452 reports that a prompt cached to the storage backend is not loaded back after cache pressure, but is loaded after `/flush_cache`. Reproducing the issue's configuration on main (Qwen3-1.7B, `--max-total-tokens 20000 --hicache-size 2`, `file` backend) shows that the storage lookup works and finds the prompt. The hit is then dropped as `host_capacity`, because the host pool has no free room to stage it.

Under `write_through`, every token cached on the GPU keeps a host copy, and host eviction only frees entries no longer on the GPU. `--hicache-size 2` gives a 17,439-token host pool for a 20,000-token GPU pool. Once the GPU pool is full, every host page holds a copy of GPU-resident KV, so no storage hit can be staged.

| Host pool flag | Host vs GPU pool (tokens) | Found in storage | Dropped as `host_capacity` | Cached on re-send |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--hicache-size 2` (issue config) | 17,439 < 20,000 | 338 | 338 | **0** |
| `--hicache-ratio 1.1` instead of `--hicache-size` | 22,001 > 20,000 | 338 | 0 | **338** |
| `--hicache-size 4` | 34,878 > 20,000 | 338 | 0 | **338** |

The existing startup warning ("L2 cache effectiveness is reduced") fires for this configuration, but it does not say that storage hits will be dropped. The docs do not explain the sizing rule either. `--hicache-size` is given in gigabytes while the GPU pool is reported in tokens, so the comparison is easy to miss.

## Modifications

Add a "Host Pool Sizing" subsection to `docs/docs/advanced_features/hicache_best_practices.mdx`, under "Key Configurations with Storage Backends Enabled", in the same flag-block-plus-guidelines format as the other subsections. It covers:

- The two host pool flags, and that `--hicache-size` is in GB and overrides `--hicache-ratio`.
- Why storage hits need free host room, and why `write_through` leaves at most the host pool minus the GPU pool for them.
- The symptom of an undersized host pool, and the metric that shows it.
- Checking both pool sizes in tokens from the startup log when using `--hicache-size`.

Docs only. No code changes.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: docs only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: docs only.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests: not applicable, docs only.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results: not applicable, docs only.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Bug] MiMo-V2.6: MiMoV2Processor hard-codes CLIP mean/std, checkpoint preprocessor_config specifies ImageNet
items.author: bjolo
items.summary: hard-codes OpenAI-CLIP normalisation ( = 0.48145466… / 0.26862954…). The comment says ImageNet values were wrong for MiMo-VL and scrambled colours (#40888) — that was right for MiMo-VL, but MiMo-V2.6 now ships ImageNet values in its own: - at rev (commit "Ali…
items.body:
### Summary
`python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/mimo_v2.py` hard-codes OpenAI-CLIP normalisation (`_QWEN2VL_PIXEL_MEAN/STD` = 0.48145466… / 0.26862954…). The comment says ImageNet values were wrong for MiMo-VL and scrambled colours (#40888) — that was right for MiMo-VL, but **MiMo-V2.6** now ships ImageNet values in its own `preprocessor_config.json`:

- `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD` at rev `6a7f202e` (commit "Align preprocessor config to training values"): `image_processor_type: Qwen2VLImageProcessor`, `image_mean: [0.485, 0.456, 0.406]`, `image_std: [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]`.

So whichever constant is hard-coded, one of the MiMo families gets the wrong normalisation.

### Measured effect (small)
Vision tower only, B300, nightly 684fea8a, compared with the HF reference in fp32 using the checkpoint's own config: CLIP vs ImageNet normalisation changes the ViT output measurably but modestly (on a synthetic scene the lowest per-token cosine was 0.69 with the hard-coded CLIP stats). It is not the main source of the image errors we saw on this model — that is the missing sliding window in the FA4 vision path (#38871) — but it is a silent mismatch with the checkpoint.

### Suggestion
Read `image_mean` / `image_std` from the checkpoint's preprocessor config (it is already loaded for `Qwen2VLImageProcessor`) and keep the CLIP values only as a fallback when the config has none, so MiMo-VL and MiMo-V2.6 both get what their checkpoints specify.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
discussion: I'd like to take this: read `image_mean`/`image_std` from the checkpoint's preprocessor config and fall back to the current CLIP constants. MiMo-V2.5's preprocessor config specifies the CLIP values, so its behavior remains unchanged, while MiMo-V2.6 gets the ImageNet stats it specifies. I'll add a CPU regression test as well.

items.title: [Fix] lang/runtime: Raise HTTP errors in async generation
items.author: rohitg00
items.summary: silently returns no output when rejects a request with a JSON HTTP error. The client only processes SSE data, so a 400 response looks like a successful empty generation.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Runtime.async_generate` silently returns no output when `/generate` rejects a request with a JSON HTTP error. The client only processes SSE data, so a 400 response looks like a successful empty generation. `add_request` has the same behavior.

## Modifications

Check the HTTP status before consuming the stream. Add a CPU regression test using a local HTTP server, covering both methods and preserving text deltas and error events sent inside HTTP 200 streams.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/lang/test_runtime_http_errors.py -v
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```

All three tests pass on macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.7 and aiohttp 3.14.5. Against the unmodified base, the six HTTP 400/422/503 cases fail; both HTTP 200 behavior tests pass. The tests use the real HTTP client and server without import stubs or model loading. Pre-commit passes.

No model accuracy evaluation was run; model computation is unchanged. Linux CPU CI is pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This checks the response status once before reading streamed data.

Not applicable to this client-side error check.

items.title: [ROCm][Quantization] Add AITER hipBLASLt MXFP8 linear kernel
items.author: rkayaith
items.summary: Requires and hipBLASLt >= 1.3. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

**This draft PR is for demonstration purposes only.** It demonstrates MXFP8 linear operations on gfx950 using AITER activation quantization and `hipb_mm` with swizzled operand scales.

Requires [ROCm/aiter#6582](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6582) and hipBLASLt >= 1.3.

## Claims

- Enable the demonstration by setting `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR_HIPBMM=1` before starting vLLM. It is disabled by default.
- Swizzle weight scales once during loading and produce swizzled activation scales during quantization; FP8 weight values keep their ordinary layout.
- Support `torch.compile` through registered custom operations and their fake implementations.

## Validation

### Model prefill

We requantized the original BF16 Muse Glimmer 30B and Qwen3.8-27B checkpoints to MXFP8 for this demonstration. Qwen3-32B uses the existing INCModel MXFP8 checkpoint.

Measured on one MI355X (gfx950) using the official [ROCm 10.1 vLLM image](https://hub.docker.com/r/rocm/vllm/tags?name=rocm10.1.0_ubuntu24.04_py3.14-pytorch_2.13.0_vllm-0.29.0), which contains vLLM `0.29.1.dev0+g98dff2a81.d20261002.rocm101` and PyTorch 2.13.0. Both implementations used the same image and MXFP8 checkpoints; native vLLM used unswizzled scales, and AITER + hipBLASLt used swizzled scales.

Each latency is the arithmetic mean of model prefill execution times from two independent performance processes, measured from profiler timestamps. Each process ran one unprofiled warm-up with the same shape for each prompt before measurement. The maximum spread between repeats was 3.274%, measured as `(max/min - 1) × 100`. Speedup is native latency divided by AITER latency.

| Model checkpoint | Prefill tokens | Native vLLM (ms) | AITER + hipBLASLt (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound) | 16384 | 2207.97 | 1444.47 | 1.53× |
| [INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound) | 2048 | 196.55 | 105.40 | 1.86× |
| [rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8) | 16384 | 1478.95 | 852.26 | 1.74× |
| [rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8) | 2048 | 158.81 | 89.84 | 1.77× |
| [talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8) | 16384 | 1552.26 | 931.46 | 1.67× |
| [talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8) | 2048 | 162.51 | 157.43 | 1.03× |

These runs produced matching smoke-token outputs between the native and AITER paths. They do not establish full model accuracy.

### Kernel validation

The same kernel implementation passed **65 test cases** on MI355X (gfx950) with vLLM 0.31.0, ROCm 7.2.3, and hipBLASLt 1.5:

```sh
HIP_ONLINE_TUNING=0 PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 pytest -q -x --noconftest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py::test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_matches_dequant_reference \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py::test_gfx950_scale_layout_linear_compiles
```

The tests compare native and AITER outputs against dequantized references and check compiled execution with padded scales.

## Details

```sh
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR_HIPBMM=1
```

The selection log reports `Using RocmHipbmmMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM`. The implementation requires `K` divisible by 128 and uses `BLK32_UE8M0_32_8_EXT` for both operands with automatic hipBLASLt algorithm selection. It also respects an explicitly set `HIP_ONLINE_TUNING`; validation used `0`.

Separate standalone validation found correctness failures for two prefill shapes with `K=29568` in the existing AITER quantizer. The model checks above do not cover those shapes.

This is a hipBLASLt backend for gfx950 dense MXFP8 linears. Related [#60169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60169) uses FlyDSL for DeepSeek's 32x32 block scales, and [#60384](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60384) targets gfx942 decode with an A16W8 assembly kernel. Neither adds this `hipb_mm` path.

items.title: [CI][Bugfix] Ignore AMD CI webhook no-op builds in /amd-ci run and retry
items.author: aarushjain29
items.summary: Fixes AMD CI bot incorrectly treating no-op webhook builds as real runs, blocking valid /amd-ci run and retry commands from authors without write access.
items.body:
Every push to a PR creates an amd-ci webhook build. bootstrap-amd.sh exits for those builds without running any tests ("AMD CI does not start automatically on PRs"), so they pass with nothing tested. The bot treated them as real runs:

1. /amd-ci run from a PR author without write access was refused with "AMD CI already ran on this commit" (for example, https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14851). Pushing again didn't help, because every push creates another no-op build.
2. /amd-ci retry picked the no-op build and replied "No failed jobs need retrying" instead of telling the author to use /amd-ci run.

The fix skips builds with source webhook for AMD CI commands in both places. This is the same condition bootstrap-amd.sh uses. Builds started from the Buildkite UI, or by comment, still count. /ci behavior is unchanged.

Test plan: new unit tests for both cases; they fail on main and pass with this change. All 62 tests in test_run_ci_command.py pass.


### Replay against real PR data

I replayed `run_ci_command.py` from upstream `main` and from this PR against the real data for #62032:
- the live PR from the GitHub API;
- every amd-ci build on the PR, from Buildkite. The only build on the head commit `f03aefad5b` is [#14851](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14851), a `webhook` build that ran no tests.

All writes (comments, reactions, branch updates, build create, retry) were stubbed and recorded, not sent. The `main` replay reproduces the bot's actual reply on #62032.

| Scenario (PR author without write access) | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/amd-ci run` (bot merges `main` into the stale branch, as in production) | ❌ "AMD CI already ran on this commit: …/builds/14851" | ✅ Merges `main`, then starts an AMD CI build on the new head |
| `/amd-ci run --allow-stale` | ❌ "AMD CI already ran on this commit: …/builds/14851" | ✅ Starts an AMD CI build on `f03aefad5b` |
| `/amd-ci retry` | Retries no-op #14851: "No failed, timed-out, or expired jobs need retrying" | "No AMD CI build exists for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` first." |
| `/amd-ci run` when a comment-triggered build already finished on the head | ❌ "already ran" | ❌ "already ran" (unchanged) |
| `/amd-ci run` when a Buildkite UI build already finished on the head | ❌ "already ran" | ❌ "already ran" (unchanged) |
| `/amd-ci retry` when a comment-triggered build failed on the head | Retries that build | Retries that build (unchanged) |

Unit tests: the two new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. All 62 tests in `test_run_ci_command.py` pass.
discussion: ✅ No earlier CI build exists for this PR. Use `/ci run` first.

items.title: [Perf] Add VLLM_GC_THRESHOLDS to set GC thresholds after the heap freeze
items.author: faresobeid
items.summary: ), applied in right after the freeze. Unset keeps the current behaviour. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

EngineCore, the GPU workers and the API server freeze their startup heap but keep CPython's default GC thresholds, so under high request load EngineCore still spends a noticeable share of each step in gen-1/gen-2 collections. This adds an opt-in `VLLM_GC_THRESHOLDS` (e.g. `50000,20,100`), applied in `freeze_gc_heap()` right after the freeze. Unset keeps the current behaviour.

New unit test in `tests/utils_/test_gc_utils.py`. GLM-4.5-Air TP8 on H200, `enable_return_routed_experts`, 400 concurrent `/inference/v1/generate` requests: `50000,20,100` gives +3.0% to +4.5% generation tok/s (2 nodes; EngineCore GC time 4.6% -> 0% of wall time).

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.
