items.title: [None][fix] Let --disagg_cluster_uri override the config file uri
items.author: spicysharkco
items.summary: is documented to take precedence over in the config file (see the comment in above the call, and the docstring of that function). In practice the command line value is ignored whenever the config file also sets, and the uri from the file is used instead.
items.body:
## Description

`trtllm-serve --disagg_cluster_uri` is documented to take precedence over `disagg_cluster.cluster_uri` in the config file (see the comment in `tensorrt_llm/commands/serve.py` above the `extract_disagg_cluster_config` call, and the docstring of that function). In practice the command line value is ignored whenever the config file also sets `disagg_cluster.cluster_uri`, and the uri from the file is used instead.

**Root cause.** `extract_disagg_cluster_config()` builds `DisaggClusterConfig(cluster_uri or cluster_config_dict["cluster_uri"])`, so the argument is used for the constructor. It then runs `update_dataclass()` over the same object with the whole `cluster_config_dict`. That loop sets every non-`None` key, including the dict's own `cluster_uri`, and overwrites the value that was just passed in. The override only worked when the file had no `cluster_uri` at all.

**Repro** (no GPU needed):

```python
from tensorrt_llm.llmapi.disagg_utils import extract_disagg_cluster_config

cfg = extract_disagg_cluster_config(
    {"cluster_uri": "http://file-host:8000"}, "http://cli-host:2379")
print(cfg.cluster_uri)
# before: http://file-host:8000
# after:  http://cli-host:2379
```

**Fix.** Apply the override after the config file values have been copied onto the dataclass. When no override is given, nothing changes. A config with neither a file uri nor an argument still raises `KeyError` as before.

`release/1.3` has the same code and the same bug. #20128 also edits the import list in `test_disagg_utils.py`; whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.

This was found by reading the code path and confirmed with the unit test below. I did not launch a disaggregated deployment, so the `trtllm-serve` side of the behavior is covered only through `extract_disagg_cluster_config`, which is the single place `serve.py` takes the value from.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_disagg_utils.py::test_extract_disagg_cluster_config_uri_argument` has two cases: no argument keeps the uri from the config, and an argument replaces it (the other fields still come from the config). The second case fails before this change.

Run on CPU only with Python 3.12 and pytest, against the real `disagg_utils.py`. The compiled bindings are not built there, so `mpi4py` and `tensorrt_llm._utils.global_mpi_rank/global_mpi_size` were replaced by small stubs; `extract_disagg_cluster_config` uses neither. GPU CI and a real `trtllm-serve` launch were not run.

| `disagg_utils.py` | `test_disagg_utils.py` |
|---|---|
| base (`a857768f9`) | 1 failed (the argument case), 41 passed |
| with this fix | 42 passed |

Formatting hooks (yapf, isort, autoflake) pass on both touched files.

items.title: [Perf] DSv4.1: Skip discarded KV rows during window commit
items.author: Oasis-Git
items.summary: Request-window commit copies every input KV row, routing discarded rows to a shared sink even though only the final window survives. Long prefills therefore move KV bytes that will never be read.
items.body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

Request-window commit copies every input KV row, routing discarded rows to a shared sink even though only the final window survives. Long prefills therefore move KV bytes that will never be read.

## Modifications

Add a Triton commit kernel that skips KV loads and stores for discarded rows, computes retained ring destinations, and writes position tags in the same launch. Keep history validation and the existing window retention policy unchanged. The launch grid still covers all input rows; this change removes discarded-row memory traffic rather than bounding the grid.

## Accuracy Tests

The tested patch passed 22 local tests on GB300: 4 packed-copy/commit GPU tests, 5 encoder replay CPU tests, and 13 compressed-pool CPU tests. Added byte-exact coverage for both KV layouts, ragged and 16K-token input, ring wrap, padded strides, untouched discarded destinations, layer isolation, and CUDA graph metadata refresh. These checks do not establish full-model semantic accuracy.

Transplanted onto main at 456231e25: all three changed files are byte-identical to the tested candidate, their baseline versions are unchanged, and syntax/diff checks pass. GPU results below were measured on base 30ca1dffc, not rerun on the new main revision. Pre-commit passed on the tested patch; CI on this PR is pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On 4x GB300, TP4/EP4 with encoder bounded replay, the unchanged high-concurrency replay subset had median E2E latency of 3561.52 ms before this change and 3299.75 / 3315.78 ms in two candidate runs (6.9–7.4% lower). All 816 request/usage maps and cached-token totals matched. One baseline and two candidate runs were measured; DSPARK used simulated acceptance 5.4.

A 16K-token eager commit microbenchmark decreased from 142.24 us to 14.79 us. This includes destination calculation and tag updates and is not an end-to-end speedup. Later direct-packed and sparse-prefill experiments are excluded from this PR and these measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the tested patch with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused unit tests.
- [x] Provide scoped correctness and speed results with limitations.
- [ ] Run upstream CI on the PR revision.

items.title: [Fix] dumper: harden filter evaluation against scheduler RCE
items.author: Eryx-Z
items.summary: accepts a string that was evaluated with while exposing /. Those function objects keep, so a client with an ordinary API key can import modules and run arbitrary Python in the scheduler process when.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44188.

`/dumper/configure` accepts a `filter` string that was evaluated with `eval()` while exposing `re.search` / `re.match`. Those function objects keep `__globals__`, so a client with an ordinary API key can import modules and run arbitrary Python in the scheduler process when `DUMPER_SERVER_PORT=reuse`.

A previous attempt at this fix was closed with the author's other open PRs; the `eval()` path is still on `main`.

## Changes

- Replace `eval()` with a restricted AST walker that only allows constants, names, comparisons, boolean/arithmetic ops, lists/tuples, subscripting, and calls to an allowlisted set of helpers (`search`, `match`, `len`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `any`, `all`).
- Block attribute access in filter expressions entirely, and wrap the regex helpers so attribute access cannot reach `__globals__` even if that restriction is relaxed later.
- Keep `SyntaxError` behavior for invalid expressions so existing tests stay green.
- Add regression tests for the known escape payloads from #44188.

Legitimate filters used in tests and docs (`layer_id == 0`, `'keep' in name`, `search(r'attn|mlp', name)`, etc.) continue to work.

## Test plan

- [x] Local assertions covering allowlisted expressions and the RCE payloads from #44188
- [ ] CI: `test/registered/debug_utils/test_dumper.py` filter cases

items.title: Add full_recompute_input to fine-grained activation offloading
items.author: avigyabb
items.summary: Adds to: with full activation recompute, each checkpoint's hidden-states input is moved to host memory through the existing fine-grained activation offloading manager and reloaded right before that checkpoint is recomputed in backward. The only tensors autogr…
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds `"full_recompute_input"` to `offload_modules`: with full activation recompute, each checkpoint's hidden-states input is moved to host memory through the existing fine-grained activation offloading manager and reloaded right before that checkpoint is recomputed in backward.

## Why it is needed

With `recompute_granularity="full"`, `checkpointed_forward` runs each layer (or each chunk of `recompute_num_layers` layers) under `no_grad` inside `CheckpointFunction`. The only tensors autograd keeps across the forward are the checkpoint inputs that `CheckpointFunction.forward` passes to `ctx.save_for_backward`. The large one is the hidden-states input, one per checkpoint. It stays on the GPU from the moment the checkpoint runs in forward until backward reaches that layer, and nothing reads it in between. Its size scales with sequence length times hidden size times the number of checkpointed layers on the rank, so at long context these inputs are one of the largest terms in peak memory once recompute has removed everything else.

Megatron's existing offloading features do not cover these tensors:

- `cpu_offloading` (TE layer-level offload) rejects any recompute: `TransformerConfig.__post_init__` raises "CPU offloading does not work when activation recomputation is enabled".
- `fine_grained_activation_offloading` offloads the inputs of submodules (`attn_norm`, `core_attn`, `expert_fc1`, ...) by opening an offload group around them. Under full recompute those submodules run inside the checkpoint's `no_grad` forward, so they save nothing and their groups offload nothing. The checkpoint's own `save_for_backward` happens outside every group.

## The change

This extends fine-grained activation offloading instead of adding a separate mechanism:

- `checkpointed_forward` (shared by `TransformerBlock` and `HybridStack`) wraps each checkpoint call in `FineGrainedActivationOffloadingInterface(..., "full_recompute_input")` and commits the group on the checkpoint output with `group_offload`. The saved-tensor hooks of `PipelineOffloadManager` then catch the checkpoint's `save_for_backward`. The input is copied to host on the manager's D2H stream after the checkpoint's forward, and the copy runs while the next chunk's forward executes. In backward, the group's commit node runs just before `CheckpointFunction.backward` and waits for the reload, and the group's start node issues the reload of the previous chunk's input.
- The other checkpoint arguments (attention mask, rotary embeddings, context, padding mask, token IDs) are the same tensors for every chunk. Copying them would free no GPU memory, so they are marked with `mark_not_offload` and stay on device.
- Everything else comes from the existing manager unchanged: the pinned host tensor pool reused across iterations, keeping on GPU the group that backward needs first, PP/VPP chunk handling, `min_offloaded_tensor_size`, `activation_offload_fraction` and `delta_offload_bytes_across_pp_ranks`.
- Validation in `TransformerConfig`: `"full_recompute_input"` requires `recompute_granularity="full"` and cannot be combined with other `offload_modules`. Those modules run inside the checkpointed region, where their groups would open in the `no_grad` forward and again in the recompute during backward. With `recompute_method="block"`, only the checkpointed layers are offloaded.
- Off by default. Usage:

  ```bash
  --recompute-granularity full --recompute-method uniform --recompute-num-layers 1
  --fine-grained-activation-offloading --offload-modules full_recompute_input
  ```

- `docs/user-guide/features/fine_grained_activation_offloading.md` gains the new module in the module table and a "Combining with Full Recomputation" section.

## Alternatives considered

- **Wrap `checkpointed_forward` in `torch.autograd.graph.save_on_cpu`.** This is how SkyRL ships it today, as a monkeypatch ([NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2412](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2412)). It is a few lines, but it offloads every saved checkpoint argument (including the shared RoPE and mask tensors, once per layer), copies on the compute stream, has no prefetch, and allocates pinned memory through PyTorch's caching host allocator on every step. SkyRL had to add an explicit `torch._C._host_emptyCache()` after each step to keep that cache from holding the host RAM the CPU optimizer needed. It would also be a second, parallel offload mechanism next to fine-grained offloading.
- **A separate boolean such as `offload_full_recompute_inputs`.** This reads more directly, but it would duplicate the fine-grained offloading settings (minimum size, fraction, PP balancing, warmup) or leave them unused. An `offload_modules` entry reuses all of them.
- **Offloading inside `CheckpointFunction` itself.** This would also catch checkpoints that are not layer-level, such as MTP's own `_checkpointed_forward` and `CheckpointWithoutOutput`. Those already interact with fine-grained offloading in different ways, so this PR keeps the change at the block-level call site.

## Scope and limitations

- Covers `checkpointed_forward` in `megatron/core/recompute.py`, which is used by `TransformerBlock` and `HybridStack`. MTP layers have their own `_checkpointed_forward` and are not covered.
- Host memory: each offloaded input takes the same number of bytes in pinned host memory, per microbatch in flight. The pool reuses buffers across iterations, so this is a standing host allocation.
- Offloading needs the TE CPU-offload module, the same requirement as the existing fine-grained offload modules.

## Test plan

- New CPU test `test_full_recompute_input_offloads_only_checkpoint_hidden_states` in `tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_fine_grained_activation_offloading.py`, parametrized over `uniform`/1, `uniform`/2 and `block`/3 on a 4-layer toy block. It runs the real `checkpointed_forward`. The offload interface is replaced by a recorder that keeps host copies, and the checkpoint is replaced by torch's reentrant checkpoint, which saves inputs with `save_for_backward` like `CheckpointFunction`. It checks that:
  - each checkpoint opens one `full_recompute_input` group;
  - exactly the checkpoint's hidden-states input is offloaded, while the mask and RoPE tensors are saved inside the group but kept on device;
  - the group is committed;
  - outputs and all gradients, computed from the offloaded copies, match the run without offloading;
  - no group opens when the option is off.
  With this change: 3 passed. Without the `recompute.py` change: all 3 fail (`assert 0 == 4` and similar, no groups opened).
- New CPU config tests in `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_transformer_config.py`: the option is accepted with full recompute, rejected with no or selective recompute, and rejected when combined with another offload module. 4 passed.
- Both files on a CPU-only run (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`): 69 passed, 35 skipped (CUDA required).
- New GPU test `test_gpt_full_recompute_input_offloading_correctness_and_memory` (8-layer GPTModel with TE, full recompute, uniform/1): checks that logits and grads match the run without offloading, that offloaded bytes are non-zero, and that peak memory is lower. **Not run for this PR.** `_build_gpt_model` gains a `full_recompute` flag for it, and existing callers are unchanged.
- black, isort, pylint and ruff (versions pinned in `pyproject.toml`) are clean on the changed files.

## Validation (SkyRL)

The same tensors have been offloaded in SkyRL with the `save_on_cpu` monkeypatch described above ([NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2412](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2412)), so these numbers come from that implementation, not from this PR's code path. The memory effect should carry over, because the same tensors leave the GPU. The step-time numbers will not transfer directly, because the copy paths differ. All step times were measured in SkyRL with a per-step `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` enabled.

| Setting | Peak memory per GPU | Step time |
|---|---|---|
| 256k tokens, no offload | 142 GiB | 84 s |
| 256k tokens, offload (pinned) | 98 GiB | 102 s |
| 256k tokens, offload (pageable) | — | 130 s |

items.title: Shard KPool indexer selection across tensor-parallel ranks
items.author: avigyabb
items.summary: Adds an opt-in flag that splits KPool indexer scoring across the tensor-parallel group by query rows, so TP ranks stop recomputing the same O(queries x pools) scores; the selected indices are unchanged. Follows up NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7522 (by @HollowMan6), whic…
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in flag that splits KPool indexer scoring across the tensor-parallel group by query rows, so TP ranks stop recomputing the same O(queries x pools) scores; the selected indices are unchanged.

Follows up NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7522 (by @HollowMan6), which added the KPool DSA indexer.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Mechanism

Under sequence parallelism, `DSAIndexer.forward_before_topk` gathers `x` and `qr` over the TP group before projecting, and the indexer projections are duplicated across TP ranks (`average_gradients_across_tp_domain`; without the indexer loss they are frozen). Without sequence parallelism the activations are already replicated across TP. Either way, every TP rank calls `fused_qk_topk_kpool` with the same `q`, `k`, `weights`, gate scores and mask/varlen bounds, and every rank computes the same full `[batch, queries, pools]` score matrix and top-k. At TP=8, seven of the eight scorings are redundant. That cost grows with the square of the sequence length, so it takes up more of the step as context grows.

Each query row's pool selection depends only on that row and the pooled keys. The rows can therefore be split across ranks and the results concatenated, with every row matching the unsharded computation.

## Change

- `fused_qk_topk_kpool(..., query_shard_group=None)`: when a group is passed (requires `return_index_scores=False`), rank `r` scores rows `[r*ceil(sq/G), min(sq, (r+1)*ceil(sq/G)))` through the existing chunked path `_kpool_topk_from_score_chunks`. That path gains `query_start`/`query_end` and keeps its `_KPOOL_SCORE_CHUNK_BYTES` (2 GiB) cap on the score buffer per chunk. The local pool IDs are cast to int32, padded to equal length, combined with one `all_gather_into_tensor`, and reassembled into the full `[batch, sq, budget]` tensor. Pool expansion, tail append and mask filtering then run unchanged on the full tensor, so every rank returns the same indices.
- New `TransformerConfig.dsa_indexer_kpool_shard_queries_across_tp: bool = False` (CLI `--dsa-indexer-kpool-shard-queries-across-tp`). When it is set and TP > 1, `DSAttention` passes the TP group for the KPool top-k. `DSAIndexer.forward_with_scores` passes it when `return_index_scores=False`, which is the path `DSAIndexer.forward` uses.
- `DSAttention` skips sharding when the attention query rows are already sequence-local per TP rank (`sequence_parallel_query_is_local`). In that case `q`/`weights` are already sliced to the local rows and differ across ranks.
- Default off. With the flag off, behavior is unchanged: `query_start=0`, `query_end=sq`, and no collective.

Communication per indexer call: one all-gather of `batch * ceil(sq/TP) * (index_topk / kpool)` int32 per rank. At 512k tokens, `index_topk=2048`, `kpool=4` and TP=8, that is 128 MiB per rank.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the indexer replicated (status quo).** This is simplest, but the redundant scoring grows with the square of the sequence length.
- **Shard the keys/pools instead of the queries.** This needs a distributed top-k (a local top-k plus a merge of `TP x budget` candidates per row) and changes tie-breaking. Splitting by query needs only a concatenation and keeps results identical.
- **All-gather the expanded token indices instead of pool IDs.** The payload would be `kpool`x larger (and int64). Gathering the pool IDs and expanding after the gather moves the least data.
- **Turn it on unconditionally.** It adds one collective per indexer call. At short sequences the scoring is cheap and the collective may not pay for itself, so it is opt-in.

## Test plan

- New `tests/unit_tests/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/test_kpool_query_shard.py` (43 cases, CPU-runnable, uses CUDA if available). It simulates every rank of a group in one process: a fake group provides `size()`/`rank()`, and `torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor` is replaced by one that returns the shards every simulated rank produced. Each simulated rank's output is compared bitwise to the unsharded call:
  - causal explicit mask, shard sizes 2/3/8, `sq` in {5, 24, 37} (ragged last shard, and empty shards when `sq < TP`), batch 1/2, with and without a small `_KPOOL_SCORE_CHUNK_BYTES` so shard edges fall inside the chunk loop;
  - packed THD (`cu_seqlens_kv` + varlen bounds), shard sizes 2/4;
  - each rank scores only `ceil(sq/TP)` rows;
  - the shard bounds cover every row once;
  - `query_shard_group` with `return_index_scores=True` raises.
- `tests/unit_tests/models/test_hybrid_moe_model.py`: added the new field to `GOLDEN_CONFIG`. Not run locally because it needs the distributed GPU harness.

Run locally (CPU only, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`):

```
pytest tests/unit_tests/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/test_kpool_query_shard.py
43 passed
```

Formatting: `black --skip-magic-trailing-comma --skip-string-normalization` (26.3.0), `isort` (5.13.2), `ruff check` (0.9.x) and `pylint` (3.2.6, 10.00/10) on the changed files.

Not run here: the multi-GPU DSA unit tests and a real NCCL run of this exact port.

## Validation (from SkyRL)

The same change, with the same contiguous query split and the same int32 all-gather, has been running in SkyRL on a vendored copy of the #7522 KPool code: [NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2422](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2422). The model is GLM-5.3-Flash, run on 64 B200 (8 nodes x 8) with TP8:

| Measurement | Unsharded | Sharded (TP8) |
|---|---|---|
| KPool selection microbenchmark, 512k tokens, one B200, per rank | 21.07 s | 2.63 s |
| Full model, 256k tokens/seq, steady-state training step | 218 s | 102 s (2.1x) |
| Full model, 256k tokens/seq, peak allocated memory | 98.5 GiB | 98.4 GiB |
| Full model, 512k tokens/seq, warm fwd+bwd ([#2422](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2422)) | 1545 s | 1094 s |

The 256k step times and the microbenchmark come from SkyRL's long-context benchmark runs. Those runs used SkyRL-specific settings, including a per-step `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`, so the absolute step times will differ elsewhere. The speedup depends on how much of the step the indexer takes, which grows with sequence length. In SkyRL's 2-rank NCCL test (`test_dsa_kpool_tp_shard.py` in #2422), sharded selections were bitwise identical to a single rank.

## Risks / notes for reviewers

- The change relies on TP ranks having identical indexer inputs. This holds for the gathered SP path and for non-SP TP, and the sequence-local-query case is excluded. If ranks ever diverged numerically, the gather would make all ranks use the same selection, rather than each rank keeping its own.
- Only the KPool path (`dsa_indexer_kpool > 1`) is covered. The per-token indexer (`fused_qk_topk_naive` / fused kernels) is unchanged.

items.title: Add bf16 reduce-scatter option for 2-rank expert-TP MoE combine
items.author: avigyabb
items.summary: Adds (default off), which lets the alltoall dispatcher's expert-TP reduce-scatter in the token combine run in bf16 instead of the FP32 router dtype when the expert-TP group has exactly two ranks. In that case the result is bit-identical, and the change removes…
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds `moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype` (default off), which lets the alltoall dispatcher's expert-TP reduce-scatter in the token combine run in bf16 instead of the FP32 router dtype when the expert-TP group has exactly two ranks. In that case the result is bit-identical, and the change removes an FP32 copy of every token-expert row.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Why the upcast costs memory

`MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher.combine_preprocess` reduce-scatters expert outputs across the expert-tensor-parallel group as

```python
reduce_scatter_to_sequence_parallel_region(
    hidden_states.to(self.probs.dtype), group=self.tp_group, ...
).to(hidden_states.dtype)
```

With `moe_router_dtype='fp32'`, `self.probs` is FP32, so this allocates an FP32 copy of every token-expert row this rank received, and the collective sends twice the bytes of the bf16 tensor. At long context this copy is the largest single allocation in the MoE layer. In SkyRL, on GLM-5.3-Flash (TP8, EP32 x ETP2), it was 19.31 GiB/GPU at 576k tokens, the allocation that ran that length out of memory.

The upcast exists so that the cross-rank sum does not round to bf16 at every step. That only matters when there is more than one step:

- **2 ranks:** each output element is one addition, `a + b`. NCCL's Ring and PAT kernels compute a bf16 sum by accumulating in FP32 and rounding once, so `reduce_scatter(bf16)` gives the same result as `reduce_scatter(fp32).to(bf16)`.
- **More than 2 ranks:** Ring adds partial sums hop by hop, and a bf16 reduction rounds after each hop. That differs from the FP32 path, so the upcast is kept.
- **NVLS:** the reduction happens inside the NVSwitch with different rounding. A forced `NCCL_ALGO=NVLS` bf16 reduce-scatter differs from the FP32 path in roughly 10-20% of elements, by at most 1 bf16 ulp. The upcast is kept whenever `NCCL_ALGO` asks for NVLS.

## Change

- `TransformerConfig.moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype: bool = False`. The CLI flag `--moe-combine-reduce-in-activation-dtype` is generated from the config field.
- `MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher._tp_reduce_dtype(hidden_states)` returns the activation dtype when the flag is set, `self.tp_size == 2`, and `NCCL_ALGO` does not ask for NVLS. In every other case it returns `self.probs.dtype`, which is today's behavior. `combine_preprocess` calls it in place of `self.probs.dtype`. Nothing else in the method changes.
- `_nccl_algo_may_use_nvls()` matches `NCCL_ALGO` values that contain `nvls` (for example `NVLS`, `Ring,NVLS`, `reducescatter:nvls`), and does not match the exclusion form `^NVLS`.
- One row added to the Token Dispatching table in `megatron/core/transformer/moe/README.md`.

With the flag off, the code path is unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

- **Always reduce in the activation dtype.** Not exact for expert-TP groups larger than 2, and not exact under NVLS, so it would change numerics for those configurations.
- **Chunk the upcast and reduce-scatter.** This bounds the FP32 peak, but every byte is still sent in FP32 and the code gets more complex, even though for 2 ranks the FP32 path buys no accuracy.
- **Ask NCCL which algorithm it will pick.** PyTorch does not expose NCCL's per-collective algorithm choice, so the guard reads the `NCCL_ALGO` that the user set. With `NCCL_ALGO` unset, a 2-rank reduce-scatter selected Ring at every size from 1 KiB to 1 GiB in SkyRL's measurements (NCCL 2.29.7, B200).
- **Enable by default.** The result is bit-identical under Ring/PAT, but that depends on NCCL's reduction kernels, so this PR leaves the flag off. Reviewers may prefer it on.

The allgather dispatcher's `token_combine` has the same upcast pattern over the `tp_ep` group. It is out of scope here.

## Validation (from SkyRL)

The same change has been running in SkyRL as a monkeypatch, [NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2414](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2414) (split out of [#2341](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2341)):

- **Exactness:** 2-rank bf16 reduce-scatter compared with the FP32 reduce-scatter cast back to bf16: 0 of 64M elements differ (Ring/PAT). The SkyRL patch notes record that the bit-for-bit check passed on up to 512M elements spanning five orders of magnitude, within a node and across nodes (NCCL 2.29.7, B200).
- **Memory:** On full GLM-5.3-Flash at 512k context (64 B200, ETP2), the FP32 combine ran out of memory and the bf16 combine fit at 144 GiB. At 576k tokens (TP8, EP32 x ETP2), the FP32 copy this removes was 19.31 GiB/GPU.

## Test plan

- New `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_combine_reduce_dtype.py`:
  - `TestTpReduceDtype` (CPU): dtype decision for flag off/on, expert-TP sizes 2/4/8, bf16 and fp16 activations, and `NCCL_ALGO` values (`NVLS`, `nvls`, `Ring,NVLS`, `reducescatter:nvls`, `^NVLS`, `Ring`, `PAT`). It also checks that `combine_preprocess` hands the reduce-scatter the expected dtype and returns the activation dtype.
  - `TestCombineReduceInActivationDtype` (GPU, 8 ranks, TP2 x EP4, `NCCL_ALGO=Ring`): runs dispatch/combine through two MoE layers with identical weights, flag off and flag on. Each expert-TP rank gets a different bf16 partial result, and the test asserts that the combined outputs are `torch.equal`.
- Ran locally on CPU: `pytest tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_combine_reduce_dtype.py`. Result: 17 passed, 1 skipped (the 8-rank GPU test).
- The GPU test has not been run on this branch. It needs an 8-GPU `torchrun` in CI.
- black, isort, ruff, and pylint run on the changed files: clean.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

items.title: Release router probs in the all-to-all dispatcher after combine
items.author: avigyabb
items.summary: The all-to-all MoE token dispatcher now drops its reference to the router probabilities at the end of, so under full activation recompute every MoE layer's recomputed autograd graph is no longer kept alive for the rest of the backward pass. That tensor carrie…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

The all-to-all MoE token dispatcher now drops its reference to the router probabilities at the end of `combine_postprocess`, so under full activation recompute every MoE layer's recomputed autograd graph is no longer kept alive for the rest of the backward pass.

## Why it happens

`MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher.dispatch_preprocess` stores the router output on `self.probs`. That tensor carries the router's `grad_fn`. Only `combine_preprocess` reads it, later in the same forward, and only for its dtype. Nothing clears it afterwards, so the reference lasts until the next forward through that layer overwrites it, and it keeps that forward's autograd graph reachable the whole time.

Without recompute this costs almost nothing: the next microbatch's forward overwrites the reference. With `recompute_granularity=full`, the forward re-runs inside each layer's backward. Each recomputed MoE layer stores a new `self.probs` whose graph reaches back to the checkpoint's detached input and that input's `.grad`. No later forward overwrites it, so every MoE layer keeps its recomputed graph for the rest of the backward pass. Memory therefore grows with the number of MoE layers and with sequence length.

This applies to any MoE model that uses the all-to-all dispatcher with full recompute. Nothing in it is model-specific.

## The fix

At the end of `MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher.combine_postprocess`, set `self.probs = None`. Every MoE forward goes through this step: the plain `MoELayer.forward` and the fine-grained overlap callables (`fine_grained_callables.py`, `shortcut_block.py`) all reach it through `MoELayer.postprocess`. Nothing reads `self.probs` after `combine_preprocess`. The other `.probs` reads in megatron-core are on `cudagraph_tensor_store`, which is a separate object. The partial-CUDA-graph attribute plumbing (`cudagraph_attrs` / `_get_token_dispatcher_attrs`) reads `probs` right after preprocess, while it is still set, so it is unaffected.

## Alternatives considered

- **Clear it in `MoELayer.postprocess`.** SkyRL does this as a monkeypatch, because SkyRL also replaces dispatcher methods with its own and wanted the release to survive those patches. In megatron-core the dispatcher sets the attribute, so the dispatcher should also clear it. `MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher` is the only dispatcher that sets `self.probs`, so both placements behave the same.
- **Clear it right after the last read in `combine_preprocess`.** This releases it slightly earlier within the same forward. The leak is about the reference outliving the forward, so that difference does not matter. `combine_postprocess` is the last step of the dispatcher's forward.
- **Store `probs.detach()`, or only `probs.dtype`.** Either one also breaks the graph pin. But `probs` is listed in `cudagraph_attrs`, which the `moe_preprocess` partial CUDA graph returns and restores. Changing what the attribute holds would touch that surface, while clearing it after use does not.

## Scope and limitations

- When `MoELayer.postprocess` runs inside a captured partial CUDA graph (`_forward_mlp_postprocess`), the Python assignment runs only during capture, not on replay. This PR does not change that path.
- `MoEAllGatherTokenDispatcher.local_probs` and the flex dispatcher managers (`token_probs`, `dispatched_probs`) store probs the same way, for the same forward. This PR does not touch them because the measurements below cover only the all-to-all dispatcher. They could get the same treatment in a follow-up.

## Test plan

- New CPU unit test `test_alltoall_combine_postprocess_releases_router_probs` in `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_token_dispatcher.py`. It builds the dispatcher's combine state directly and stores a non-leaf `probs` (softmax of a leaf that requires grad). It then checks that `combine_postprocess` returns the expected unpermuted output, leaves `self.probs` as `None`, and that a `weakref` to the probs tensor is dead afterwards, meaning nothing else holds the graph.
  - With this change: passes. Without the change in `token_dispatcher.py`: fails on `assert dispatcher.probs is None`.
  - The rest of `test_token_dispatcher.py` on a CPU-only host: 16 passed, 72 skipped (CUDA not available).
- The existing GPU dispatcher tests (`test_a2a_token_dispatcher.py`, `test_token_dispatcher.py`) exercise forward/backward through `combine_postprocess` and should pass unchanged in CI. I did not run them on GPU for this PR.

## Validation (SkyRL)

The same release has run in SkyRL as a monkeypatch on `MoELayer.postprocess` since [NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2433](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2433). It is applied to every Megatron model build there.

- GLM-5.3-Flash (42 MoE layers, TP8) with full recompute: about 21 GiB per GPU at 64k tokens and about 42 GiB per GPU at 256k tokens were held by these references and are freed by the release.
- End-to-end parity test on B200, 4-layer GLM-5.3-Flash slice, full recompute vs. none with the release applied ([NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2411](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2411)):
  - Grad relative error 0.0219, against run-to-run noise of 0.0234 / 0.0227.
  - Activation peak 15.7 -> 8.8 GB. This number compares recompute against no recompute, so it does not isolate this change alone.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none. This is a small bug fix.

items.title: [Attention] Add CuTe DSL backend selection for MLA context prefill
items.author: wzhao18
items.summary: Add an opt-in CuTe DSL kernel for MLA attention over cached context. Default dispatch and new-token prefill remain unchanged. [Discussion: This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be merged.]
items.body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in CuTe DSL kernel for MLA attention over cached context. Default dispatch and new-token prefill remain unchanged.

```bash
--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"trtllm_ragged_backend":"cute-dsl"}'
```

For Kimi K3, this requires FP8 KV cache.

## Claims

- Enable CuTe context prefill without changing the default TRTLLM path.
- Align packed indptrs on the CPU, avoiding additional GPU copies.
- Reject unsupported dimensions and dtypes before kernel launch.

This is separate from #56784, which adds CuTe decode selection.

## Validation

Validated on GB300 with FlashInfer 0.7.1: **76 passed, 49 skipped** across kernel correctness, chunk metadata, and prefill selector/registry tests.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  -k test_chunked_context_backend_correctness
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py
```

CUDA-graph microbenchmarks with Kimi's 12 local heads, FP8 Q/K/V, BF16 output, and packed V:

| Query tokens | Cached-context tokens | TRTLLM µs | CuTe µs | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 8,192 | 71.8 | 56.2 | 1.28× |
| 8,192 | 8,192 | 221.0 | 184.8 | 1.20× |
| 16,384 | 8,192 | 467.2 | 369.8 | 1.26× |

Times are medians of three CUDA-graph timing rounds. These measure context attention, not whole-model throughput.

### End-to-end GSM8K

Validated on 8 GB300 GPUs (two 4-GPU nodes)

Kimi K3 MXFP4 target weights, DSpark draft weights, FlashInfer Python/cubin 0.7.1 and JIT-cache 0.7.1+cu130, TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3, and PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132.

**`max-num-batched-tokens=256` forces chunked prefill for the GSM8K prompts.** A short trace of a cold 775-token GSM8K prompt before evaluation confirmed **72 CuTe context-attention kernel launches on rank 0** (`kernel_cutlass_kernel_cuteblackwellkernelattentionfmhafmhaBlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionForward…`). Profiling was stopped before the full evaluation.

| Task | Questions | Few-shot | Flexible-extract exact match | Strict-match exact match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 1,319 | 5 | **96.36%** (1,271/1,319) | **96.29%** (1,270/1,319) |

Server configuration (run on each node; `NODE_RANK` is 0 or 1, and rank 1 also passes `--headless`). `TARGET_MODEL` and `DRAFT_MODEL` point to the local target/draft checkpoints:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
export VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8

vllm serve "$TARGET_MODEL" \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$MASTER_ADDR" --master-port 29547 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --load-format fastsafetensors --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 256 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --profiler-config "{\"profiler\":\"torch\",\"torch_profiler_dir\":\"$TRACE_DIR\",\"torch_profiler_with_stack\":false}" \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"trtllm_ragged_backend":"cute-dsl"}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$DRAFT_MODEL\",\"attention_backend\":\"TOKENSPEED_MLA\",\"method\":\"dspark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":4,\"draft_sample_method\":\"greedy\",\"rejection_sample_method\":\"block\"}"
```

No online weight quantization, EP/SP, Mooncake, Dynamo, or synthetic speculative acceptance was enabled. Decode uses TokenSpeed MLA; CuTe is selected only for cached-context prefill. A cached-prefix extension smoke test passed before evaluation.

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,max_length=8192,max_gen_toks=256,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=32' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0 \
  --seed 42 --log_samples --output_path "$OUTPUT_DIR/gsm8k"
```

## Details

- CuTe requires FP8 queries for head dimension 192 and does not support dimension 256. Runtime validation and test skips share one compatibility helper until FlashInfer exposes a public API.
- CuTe requires packed V. Generic MLA's strided V is copied only when CuTe is selected; already-contiguous V incurs no copy.
- That copy can erase or reverse the speedup on small workloads, so CuTe remains opt-in.

items.title: [Fix] multimodal: expand single-channel GPU JPEG tensors to RGB on load
items.author: Eryx-Z
items.summary: Grayscale JPEGs decoded on GPU via (default unchanged mode) come back as. returned those tensors unchanged, so Qwen-VL (and similar) processors that normalize with three RGB channel means fail: Related: #35101 forces at the decode call site.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44748.

Grayscale JPEGs decoded on GPU via `torchvision.io.decode_jpeg` (default unchanged mode) come back as `[1, H, W]`. `BaseMultimodalProcessor._load_single_item` returned those tensors unchanged, so Qwen-VL (and similar) processors that normalize with three RGB channel means fail:

```
RuntimeError: output with shape [1, 1, H, W] doesn't match the broadcast shape [1, 3, H, W]
```

Related: #35101 forces `ImageReadMode.RGB` at the decode call site. This PR is defense in depth at the load boundary so any 1-channel tensor is expanded before processing, including when the decode path is unchanged.

## Modifications

- Add `ensure_rgb_image_tensor` and use it from `smart_to_rgb` for tensors.
- Route GPU-decoded tensors through `smart_to_rgb` in `_load_single_item` instead of returning them raw.
- Add unit tests that mock `load_image` returning 1-channel / HW / RGB tensors.

## Accuracy Tests

- New unit tests in `test_base_processor_image_decode.py` (`TestLoadSingleItemGrayscaleGpuTensor`).
- Helper smoke-checked for CHW `[1,H,W]` → `[3,H,W]`, HW → `[3,H,W]`, and RGB passthrough.

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep per-expert gate/up halves separate under stacked mappers
items.author: pasta-paul
items.summary: Fixes silent weight corruption in RoutedExperts.load_weights where per-expert gate and up halves were incorrectly fused, causing gate rows to be overwritten by stacked mappers.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes silent weight corruption in `RoutedExperts.load_weights`. A model mapper with `orig_to_new_stacked` (e.g. `LlamaModel.hf_to_vllm_mapper`) renames per-expert `experts.E.gate_proj` / `experts.E.up_proj` to `experts.E.gate_up_proj` and tags the tensor with `shard_id`. `RoutedExperts` then loads each half as a fused `[gate; up]` block, so `up` overwrites `gate` and the gate rows of `w13` are never loaded. Nothing errors, and the output is garbage for any model that combines such a mapper with per-expert expert checkpoints (GPTQ/AutoRound exports, BF16 experts in mixed checkpoints).

Found while bringing up MuseSpark (#61879, a `LlamaModel` subclass) with `intel-ai/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-INT4`. The change is independent of #61879.

## Claims

- Under a stacked mapper, a per-expert tensor tagged `shard_id` 0 is loaded as `gate_proj` and one tagged 1 as `up_proj`. Before this change both went through the fused `gate_up_proj` chunking path.
- Fused all-expert tensors (no expert id in the name) are unchanged.
- Untagged per-expert `gate_up_proj` tensors (real per-expert fused checkpoints) are unchanged.
- `down_proj` and all other names are unchanged.
- The fix covers every param suffix: `weight`, `qweight`, `scales`, `qzeros`.
- On MuseSpark, MoE block output vs an fp32 reference goes from cos-sim −0.07 (layer 0, BF16 experts) and −0.11 (layer 5, INT4 experts) to 0.99999 (layers 0, 1, 5).

## Validation

**Unit test** (new, CPU-only), on `main` @ `8e25bbc` + this commit:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_per_expert_gate_up.py -v --noconftest
# 8 passed
```

- `test_unstack_per_expert_gate_up` (7 cases): shard 0 → `gate_proj`, shard 1 → `up_proj` (including `qweight`), plus negative cases (untagged per-expert, fused all-expert, `down_proj`).
- `test_llama_style_mapper_round_trip`: per-expert gate/up weights go through a Llama-style `WeightsMapper(orig_to_new_stacked=...)`, and the helper restores `5.gate_proj.weight` / `5.up_proj.weight`.

**Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format` (ruff 0.14.0, the pre-commit pin) are clean on both files. mypy and the full pre-commit suite were not run.

**End to end.** Run on the #61879 branch (MuseSpark, 8x A100-80G, TP8). The commit is identical apart from line offsets.

- **Symptom before the fix:** rank 0 `w13_weight[e]` for a layer-0 BF16 expert held `up[0:256]` in rows 0:256 and `up[2048:2304]` in rows 512:768. Every other row was zero, with no gate data. `w2` and `expert_bias` loaded correctly.
- **Method:** forward hooks captured MoE block inputs and outputs on rank 0 (12-token prompt). These were compared to an fp32 CPU reference built from the checkpoint, with int4 dequantized from `qweight`/`scales`. Pooler, router logits and pre-expert norm already matched at cos 1.0 before the fix; only the expert output was wrong.

| Layer | Experts | cos-sim before | cos-sim after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | BF16 | −0.07 | 0.99999 |
| 1 | BF16 | not measured | 0.99999 |
| 5 | INT4 (Marlin WNA16) | −0.11 | 0.99999 |

- **Generation:**
  - Before: garbage.
  - After (greedy): `"...Germany is"` → `" Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome"`.
- **Serving quality after the fix:**
  - arithmetic word problems 10/10 exact match;
  - Dickens passage perplexity 1.21 (fp8 KV) / 1.22 (bf16 KV);
  - needle retrieval at 17,847 prompt tokens: pass;
  - images 4/4.
- On that branch this test passes together with the existing MuseSpark MoE tests (30 passed).

## Details

**Root cause** (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py`):
- `WeightsMapper.orig_to_new_stacked` matches by substring, so the `.gate_proj` → `.gate_up_proj` (shard 0) and `.up_proj` → `.gate_up_proj` (shard 1) rules meant for the dense MLP also rewrite `mlp.experts.E.gate_proj` / `up_proj`. The mapper sets `tensor.shard_id`.
- `RoutedExperts.load_weights` resolves the per-expert name `E.gate_up_proj.*` through the expert mapping as a fused gate/up tensor. It chunks the half-tensor in two and TP-shards each piece into the `w13` gate and up slots, so `up` overwrites what was written from `gate`.

**Fix:**
- New helper `_unstack_per_expert_gate_up(name, tensor)`, called at the top of the per-weight loop in `RoutedExperts.load_weights`.
- It rewrites `gate_up_proj` → `gate_proj` / `up_proj` only when both of these hold:
  - the name has an expert id (`(?:^|\.)\d+\.gate_up_proj\.`);
  - the tensor carries a mapper-assigned `shard_id` in {0, 1}.
- **Why it's scoped this way:**
  - Fused all-expert tensors have no expert id, so the regex skips them.
  - Real per-expert fused checkpoint tensors have no `shard_id`, so the attribute check skips them.
  - No mapper, model or quant-method changes.
  - The diff is +20 lines in `routed_experts.py` plus a 55-line test.

**Alternatives considered:**
- *Fix in the model's `load_weights`.* This was the first version, in `MuseSparkRoutedExperts.load_weights` on #61879. Rejected because every model with a stacked mapper and per-expert checkpoints is exposed.
- *Drop gate/up from the mapper, or exclude `experts.` in `WeightsMapper`.* The dense MLP still needs stacking, and a change to `WeightsMapper` touches the name mapping of every model.
- *Raise on an ambiguous `gate_up_proj`.* Turns silent corruption into an error but leaves the checkpoint unloadable.

**Risk:**
- Low. Only names with an expert id and a mapper-set `shard_id` are affected, and those were already loaded wrong.
- Restored names are always `gate_proj` / `up_proj`. That assumes the expert mapping uses those checkpoint names, as the HF-style mappings that produce this pattern do.
- Only MuseSpark was verified end to end. Other models on `main` that combine stacked mappers with per-expert expert checkpoints were not audited.
- **Unit test coverage:** the unit test covers the helper and the mapper interaction. The `w13` load path itself is covered by the end-to-end check above, not by a unit test.

items.title: [Fix] function_call: Accept more Harmony call shapes in GptOssDetector
items.author: spicysharkco
items.summary: only recognizes a call written exactly as. Three other valid Harmony shapes are not parsed in non-streaming responses: - The call is the first message of the completion. The generation prompt already ends with, so a call emitted without an analysis message f…
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #41315.

`--tool-call-parser gpt-oss` only recognizes a call written exactly as `<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary to=... <|constrain|>json<|message|>...`. Three other valid Harmony shapes are not parsed in non-streaming responses:

- **The call is the first message of the completion.** The generation prompt already ends with `<|start|>assistant`, so a call emitted without an analysis message first starts with `<|channel|>commentary to=...`. `has_tool_call()` only looks for `bot_token = "<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary"`, finds nothing, and the raw Harmony markup is returned as `content`. The streaming path parses the same text, so the two paths disagree.
- **The call has no `<|constrain|>json`.** The Harmony format treats `<|constrain|>` as optional, but `tool_extract_pattern` requires `<|constrain|>json<|message|>`. The call is dropped and `content` is empty, so the request returns neither a tool call nor text.
- **The recipient is in the role header** (`<|start|>assistant to=functions.X<|channel|>commentary ...`). The Harmony spec allows it, and openai-harmony renders history this way. The whole call comes back as `content`.

Repro, CPU only:

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.gpt_oss_detector import GptOssDetector

tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(name="get_weather", parameters={
    "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}}))]
call = '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather<|message|>{"city": "Paris"}<|call|>'
res = GptOssDetector().detect_and_parse(call, tools)
print(res.calls, repr(res.normal_text))
```

Before this change: `[] '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather<|message|>{"city": "Paris"}<|call|>'`. After: one `get_weather` call with `{"city": "Paris"}` and empty content.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/function_call/gpt_oss_detector.py`:
  - `has_tool_call()` also matches a `<|channel|>commentary` header that carries a recipient (`to=`), and a role header `<|start|>assistant to=functions.`. The existing `bot_token` check stays, so previously detected text is unchanged. A recipient outside `functions.` in the role header, such as `to=browser.search`, is still not treated as a function call.
  - `tool_extract_pattern` makes `<|constrain|>json` optional and accepts the `<|channel|>commentary` header between the recipient and the message, so the three shapes above reach `json.loads` the same way as the common shape.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_gpt_oss_call_shapes.py`: new CPU tests for the shapes above (detector only, the forced channel-first payload from #41747, and after the gpt-oss reasoning parser), a streaming increment without `<|constrain|>`, and plain text that must stay content.

Streaming: a call without `<|constrain|>` that arrives in one increment is now parsed too, because the streaming path uses the same extraction pattern. This PR does not change the streaming buffering logic, so per-token streaming and the recipient-in-role-header shape in streaming are not covered here.

Overlap: #41826 changes the same `has_tool_call` line. Its pattern (`<|channel|>commentary\s+to=`) is the first alternative of `tool_start_pattern` here, so this change covers it. The channel-first payload in #41747 (`tool_choice: "required"`) takes the same path, and the detector now parses it. #41045 and #43243 rework the streaming path, which this change does not touch.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: parser-only change, no model forward or kernel code touched.

Unit tests (CPU, `PYTHONPATH=python pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/test_gpt_oss_call_shapes.py`):

- Base commit with the new tests: 7 failed, 5 passed. 2 tests fail (recipient in the role header, streaming call without `<|constrain|>`) and 5 subtests fail (the first-message call in its plain and forced forms, the call without `<|constrain|>` with and without a preceding analysis message, and the same call after the reasoning parser). With this change: 7 passed (10 subtests passed). Neighbouring suites (`test_function_call_parser.py`, `test_harmony_parser.py`, `test_reasoning_parser.py`) plus the new file: 438 passed (167 subtests passed).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one extra regex search on text that previously failed the `bot_token` check.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion: Support per-token shift/scale in the fused norm_scale_shift kernel
items.author: Linda-Stadter
items.summary: FLUX.3 modulates every token separately, so its blocks pass per-token shift/scale tensors to. The fused CUDA kernel only handled one shift/scale row per batch, so on Blackwell every FLUX.3 block fell back to the slower CuTe-DSL kernel.
items.body:
## Motivation

FLUX.3 modulates every token separately, so its blocks pass per-token shift/scale tensors to `fused_norm_scale_shift`. The fused CUDA kernel (`kda_kernels/norm_scale_shift`) only handled one shift/scale row per batch, so on Blackwell every FLUX.3 block fell back to the slower CuTe-DSL kernel. This PR adds a per-token variant of the fused kernel and routes those calls to it.

## Modifications

- `norm_scale_shift.cuh`: a `kPerTokenMod` template parameter that offsets the shift/scale loads by the token row, and a `NormScaleShiftPerTokenKernel` BF16 entry point (non-residual path).
- `norm_scale_shift_jit.py`: `try_fused_norm_scale_shift` keeps the per-batch row path and additionally dispatches contiguous per-token shift/scale (`[1, S, D]` or `[S, D]`, matching `x`) to the new entry point. Other inputs still fall back to CuTe-DSL as before.
- `test_norm.py`:
  - The per-token path matches the CuTe-DSL reference for FLUX.3 token counts (text stream and 1024x1024 joint stream) and both modulation ranks, and the public `fused_norm_scale_shift` op returns the same output.
  - Strided (non-contiguous) per-token modulation is rejected and falls back.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel-level: the per-token kernel matches the CuTe-DSL reference (`test_norm.py`, atol/rtol 5e-2). Against an FP32 reference on B200, both kernels have the same max abs error (~0.03) at every token count in the table below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel, B200, per-token shift/scale, hidden 3072, cold L2 (`marker.do_bench`):

| Tokens | Fused (this PR) | CuTe-DSL fallback | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,024 | 5.2 us | 6.5 us | 1.25x |
| 4,608 | 17.7 us | 22.0 us | 1.24x |
| 9,216 | 33.9 us | 41.6 us | 1.23x |
| 18,432 | 65.3 us | 80.9 us | 1.24x |

At 9k tokens the fused kernel reaches ~84% of B200 HBM bandwidth (CuTe-DSL: ~68%).

items.title: [CI][Tests] Account for FP8 KV-cache rounding in MLA reference
items.author: wzhao18
items.summary: Make the MLA correctness reference account for FP8 KV-cache rounding. The reference currently uses the original BF16 values even when decode reads an FP8 cache, which can produce input-dependent assertion failures. [Discussion: ✅ Triggered for commit.]
items.body:
## Overview

Make the MLA correctness reference account for FP8 KV-cache rounding. The reference currently uses the original BF16 values even when decode reads an FP8 cache, which can produce input-dependent assertion failures. Related: #62002.

## Claims

- Decode references use quantized/dequantized KV values; prefill references use rounded cached context and original new tokens.
- Preserve backend outputs, tolerances, and random-input generation. This changes only the existing test helper.

## Validation

Validated on **GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.2, FlashInfer 0.7.2**, using the CI Python checkout `b5674c11ba`. CI uses **B200 (SM100), CUDA 13.0**; the original CI failure still needs confirmation there.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Reported GLM/mixed-small/FP8 case, reproduced with input seed 6113 | CUTLASS_MLA and TOKENSPEED_MLA max error: 0.163086 before, 0.048828 after; both pass |
| Captured outputs for all four available backends | Bit-identical before/after the reference change |
| Replay of 557 selected CI-prefix cases | 471 passed, 93 skipped, including collection skips |
| Existing chunked-context cases | 12 passed, 4 skipped |
| CUTLASS input sweep, seeds 2048–8191 | All 6,144 inputs passed |
| Pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` | Passed |

Commands used included `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s -p diagnostics tests/v1/attention` with a temporary plugin selecting the ordered CI-prefix node IDs, and `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py`. The diagnostic plugin and seed sweep were investigation harnesses, not committed tests. Existing context coverage can be run with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  -k test_chunked_context_backend_correctness
```

Model evaluation and serving benchmarks are not applicable to this test-only change.

## Details

The captured FP8 query/cache values match the expected casts. Even FP64 attention on the actual FP8 Q/K/V differs from attention on the original inputs by 0.1568 on the reproduced input, exceeding the test's bound near that coordinate. The reference should model the cache format independently of the backend. It now applies the cache scale, FP8 rounding, and dequantization before computing expected attention, while preserving unquantized new tokens for prefill.

Duplicate-work check: #62047 addresses the same CI symptom by seeding each case. This PR takes a materially different approach: correct the cache representation in the reference while preserving varied inputs. Seeding does not resolve the demonstrated reference discrepancy on other valid inputs. TokenSpeed 2.0.2 and 2.0.3 produced identical outputs in the controlled reproduction.

AI assistance (Codex) was used for investigation, implementation, validation, and this description.

items.title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Verify pull reads against producer lease slots
items.author: vadiklyutiy
items.summary: Fixes KV data leakage in pull-mode decoders by verifying producer lease slots, preventing decoded tokens from being misattributed when a lease lapses during read.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61229: a pull-mode decoder could decode another request's KV when the producer's lease lapsed before or during the READ. The producer now exports a per-request lease slot that the decoder reads after the transfer, and the KV is used only if the producer still held the blocks.

Also fixes a second path to the same result: when a request id is reused on the producer (request id randomization disabled and the router retries with the same id), a late read notification for the earlier attempt was counted against the retry and released its blocks while the retry's decoder had not read them yet. Read notifications now carry the lease nonce, and the producer ignores those of an earlier lease.

## Claims

- A pull whose producer released the KV blocks before the READ completed fails the KV load (`kv_load_failure_policy` applies) instead of returning another request's tokens. This covers a read that starts after the lease lapsed and a lease that lapses mid-read; the check uses no clocks or heartbeat accounting.
- The producer ignores read notifications that carry the lease nonce of an earlier request with the same id, so a late reader can no longer release blocks that the current reader still needs.
- With `kv_lease_verification` on (the default), a pull that cannot be verified fails as well (no lease fields in `kv_transfer_params`, slot READ failed), and an instance that cannot register its lease slots in DRAM fails to start. `kv_lease_verification=false` restores the old behavior.
- TTFT and ITL unchanged at concurrency 1; at concurrency 16 median TTFT +1.3 ms (about one decoder step), ITL and throughput unchanged.

## Validation

**Reproducer** (1P1D on 2x B200, Qwen2.5-0.5B, default UCX, P limited to 1000 KV blocks so that freed blocks are reused): prefill on P, wait 34 s so the 30 s lease lapses (D has not seen the request, so no heartbeats), send 40 other prompts to P, then send the original request to D with the saved `kv_transfer_params`; compare D's output with P computing the same prompt locally. Each prompt carries a unique tag so D cannot hit its own prefix cache.

| Configuration                          | No wait (control) | Wait 34 s + reuse                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Base (`75e3b17c05`)                    | matches           | HTTP 200 with the other request's text ("Fact 100 about volcano eruption 32..."), 2/2            |
| This PR, `kv_load_failure_policy=fail` | matches           | HTTP 500, 2/2; D logs "Declining KV pulled ... released the KV blocks before the read completed" |
| This PR, `recompute`                   | matches           | matches the reference, 2/2                                                                       |
| This PR, P TP1 / D TP2, `fail`         | matches           | HTTP 500; both D ranks decline                                                                   |
| This PR, P TP2 / D TP1, `fail`         | matches           | HTTP 500                                                                                         |

**Request id reuse** (P with `VLLM_DISABLE_REQUEST_ID_RANDOMIZATION=1`, same `X-Request-Id` for both attempts): prefill attempt 1, wait 34 s, prefill attempt 2 with another prompt, send attempt 1's params to D (a late reader), flood P, then send attempt 2's params to D.

| Configuration | Late reader of attempt 1                                                  | Reader of attempt 2                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Base          | HTTP 200; its read notification releases attempt 2's blocks               | HTTP 200 with the other request's text, 2/2 |
| This PR       | HTTP 500 (lease check fails); P ignores its notification (nonce mismatch) | matches the reference, 2/2                  |

The DRAM lease slots were readable with the default UCX transports.

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_nixl_connector,test_nixl_heartbeat,test_nixl_connector_hma,test_bidirectional_kv_transfer,test_nixl_push_connector,test_nixl_desc_geometry,test_nixl_simple_cpu_offload,test_multi_connector}.py` on B200: 677 passed, 2 failed (base commit: 667 passed, 2 failed). The same 2 fail on the base commit in the same environment (gated `google/gemma-3-1b-it` in `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma`, `test_multi_example_connector_consistency`). New tests cover slot reuse within a step, the exported lease, verified and released pulls, a failed slot READ, pulls without a lease with verification on and off, slot zeroing on both release paths, and stale notifications. `create_vllm_config` in the test utils turns verification off by default, since the fake remotes export no lease slots.

**Serving benchmark** (1P1D through `toy_proxy_server.py`, Qwen2.5-0.5B, random 1024 in / 32 out, `--ignore-eos`, CUDA graphs, FlashInfer attention; median of 3 runs):

|                    | Concurrency 1, base / PR | Concurrency 16, base / PR |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| Median TTFT (ms)   | 25.1 / 25.0              | 43.8 / 45.1               |
| P90 TTFT (ms)      | 26.7 / 26.6              | 57.1 / 57.8               |
| Median ITL (ms)    | 1.14 / 1.13              | 1.53 / 1.51               |
| Throughput (req/s) | 16.6 / 16.6              | 165.4 / 166.1             |

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 \
  --random-output-len 32 --ignore-eos --seed 0 --num-prompts 800 --max-concurrency 16
```

## Details

**Root cause.** In pull mode P frees a request's blocks when its lease expires, without knowing whether D is about to read them (the READ is one-sided). D reads by block number, so after the blocks are reused the READ still succeeds and D decodes the new owner's KV:

1. P finishes the prefill, holds the blocks and grants a 30 s lease.
2. Heartbeats stop (D stalled, network delay) or never start (the request has not reached D yet).
3. P's reaper releases the blocks; another prefill reuses them.
4. D posts the READ with the old block ids; it completes normally and D generates from foreign KV.

**Fix.** Each P worker registers an int64 array in DRAM with NIXL and advertises it in the handshake metadata.

1. When a `do_remote_decode` request is first scheduled, the P scheduler assigns a slot and a nonce; workers write the nonce in that step, before the request can finish and export its lease.
2. `kv_transfer_params` carry `remote_lease_slot` and `remote_lease_nonce`.
3. A P worker zeroes the slot before reporting the request in `finished_sending` (read notification or lease expiry); the scheduler reuses a slot only after `finished_sending`, and workers apply clears before writes within a step.
4. D submits the block READs without a completion notification. Once they completed, it reads the request's lease slot on every remote rank it read from (the checks of all requests that complete in the same step share one READ per remote rank), and reports the request as received only if every slot still holds the nonce. Only then does it send the read notification, which now carries the nonce.

Zeroing precedes any reuse of the blocks and the slot READ starts after the block READs completed, so a matching nonce proves P held the blocks for the whole READ. Declined pulls are counted in `vllm:nixl_num_lease_check_failures`.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- The check delays the KV load by about one decoder step. A bounded spin on the slot READ in the same step could remove it; left out to keep the change smaller.
- Turn-2 readbacks from D in bidirectional mode are not verified yet; `_is_turn2_read_expired` still guards them.
- Lease slots live in DRAM, so the NIXL backend must transfer DRAM between the instances; with verification on, a failed registration stops the instance at startup and failed slot READs fail their pulls.

**Duplicate check.** [#61549](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61549) (draft) estimates the producer lease on D from clocks and heartbeat timing; it cannot rule out a heartbeat that was sent but not delivered, or clock-offset error. [#61578](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61578) adds opt-in KV checksums. This PR is an exact check that is on by default and costs one small READ per remote rank.

items.title: [None][fix] Reject padded-vocabulary draft tokens before xgrammar
items.author: moraxu
items.summary: Fixes a server crash under speculative decoding with xgrammar guided decoding, and follows up on #20463. gives xgrammar the padded size, and xgrammar's lists the extra ids as special tokens but keeps no decoded string for them.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Fixes a server crash under speculative decoding with xgrammar guided decoding, and follows up on #20463.

**Crash.** Models pad the LM head past the tokenizer's vocabulary; Muse Spark Open has 201,818 tokens and 202,048 LM-head rows. `XGrammarMatcherFactory` gives xgrammar the padded size, and xgrammar's `TokenizerInfo` lists the extra ids as special tokens but keeps no decoded string for them. Asked to accept one, xgrammar before 0.2.6 (TRT-LLM pins 0.1.32) rejects it, but first prints its decoded string: an out-of-bounds read that segfaults the process. The target model never emits these ids under a grammar, since the bitmask excludes them. Drafts are not grammar-constrained, though: `GuidedDecoder` calls `accept_token` on every draft token, and a drafter whose argmax spans the whole LM head can propose a padded id. With Muse Spark Open, DFlash2 and `guided_decoding_backend: xgrammar`, one request sequence crashed all four ranks on the deployment guide's guided-JSON example, twice in a row.

`XGrammarMatcher.accept_token` now rejects ids at or above the tokenizer's vocabulary size without calling xgrammar. xgrammar rejects them too, so guiding is unchanged: the draft loop stops at the rejected token, and the target's constrained token decides acceptance. The guard stays correct after an xgrammar upgrade.

**Docs.** The Muse Spark Open guide still told readers to use "the Hub id once published". It now says the Hub id works and that the repository is gated, so serving it by id needs approved access and `HF_TOKEN`.

**Follow-up to #20463.** Its test notes said the published drafter's `config.json` was byte-identical to the one first tested. The drafter's current Hub revision adds `output_multiplier` and `final_logit_softcapping` to `dflash_config` (the target's logit transform, which vLLM applies to drafter logits); the weights are unchanged. TRT-LLM's DFlash path does not read these fields: the previous and current revisions give bit-identical results, so the #20463 docs stand. The published NVFP4 checkpoint matches the one tested there in every weight shard, the tokenizer and the configs; its chat template differs only in how tool definitions render.

## Test Coverage

- New `tests/unittest/_torch/misc/test_grammar_matcher.py`, 3 CPU cases marked `cpu_only` and registered in `l0_cpu.yml`: a padded id is rejected without reaching xgrammar and leaves the matcher where it was; in-vocabulary ids still go to xgrammar. Run against the previous `grammar_matcher.py`, the first case segfaults inside xgrammar's `accept_token`.
- End to end on one 4x GB300 node: Muse Spark Open with both checkpoints given by Hub id and the README's DFlash recipe (`serve_config.yaml` + `spec_dflash.yaml`, xgrammar on), replaying the request sequence that crashed the server. All checks pass, including the guided-JSON example. With the chat template's `current_date` pinned to the day of the #20463 measurements, the greedy completions without tools match those measurements exactly.
- `pre-commit` passes on the four changed files.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities

- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
