items.title: [Model] MuseSpark: Ampere (sm80) + AutoRound/GPTQ INT4 experts
items.author: pasta-paul
items.summary: Enables serving MuseSpark 816B INT4 on Ampere GPUs via Marlin WNA16 experts, achieving ~48 tok/s per stream with ~11.5 GiB freed per GPU by sizing RoPE cache to max_model_len.
items.body:
## Overview

Lets MuseSpark Open (816B-A42B) serve on **Ampere (sm80)** with the AutoRound INT4 checkpoint `intel-ai/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-INT4`, using route-major Marlin WNA16 experts. Stacked on #61879 (`muse-spark-support` @ `6cc692b`). Before this, the NVIDIA path in #61879 required Hopper (route-major) or Blackwell (FlashInfer TRT-LLM) and accepted only NVFP4/BF16 checkpoints.

Commit 1 is the same fix as PR A: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62068, which targets `main`. It is included here because INT4 output is garbage without it. Drop it on rebase once PR A lands.

## Claims

- MuseSpark INT4 (AutoRound/INC, `auto_round:auto_gptq` packing) loads and serves on 8x A100-80G at TP8:
  - 47.6 tok/s at 1 stream;
  - 628 tok/s aggregate at 32 concurrent;
  - 865,400 KV tokens at 32k context.
- MoE block output matches an fp32 reference: cos-sim 0.99999 for BF16 experts (layers 0, 1) and INT4 experts (layer 5).
- Quality on sm80:
  - arithmetic 10/10;
  - perplexity 1.21;
  - needle retrieval pass at 17,847 tokens;
  - images 4/4;
  - audio WER 0.06 / 0.10 / 0.00 on 3 LibriSpeech clips (with an audio-aware system prompt).
- The RoPE cos/sin cache is sized by `max_model_len` instead of the 1M-token config, which frees about 11.5 GiB per GPU at TP8.
- Route-major experts (Triton BF16, Marlin NVFP4/WNA16) run on any non-Blackwell CUDA GPU. Blackwell still uses FlashInfer TRT-LLM.
- `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM` accepts `INCConfig` and `AutoGPTQConfig`:
  - symmetric int4/int8 only;
  - act-order and asymmetric checkpoints are rejected with `NotImplementedError`.

## Validation

**Setup:**

| | |
|---|---|
| GPUs | 8x A100-80G PCIe; NVLink in pairs (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7), PCIe between pairs |
| Driver / CUDA | R570, CUDA 12.9 wheels (toolkit 12.9) |
| Software | torch 2.13.0+cu129, transformers 5.21.0.dev0, vLLM built from this branch for sm80 |
| Checkpoint | `intel-ai/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-INT4` (466 GB, local copy) |

**Serve command** (`serve.sh` with its defaults expanded):

```bash
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.9 \
vllm serve /ephemeral/muse-int4 --served-model-name muse-spark-int4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-memory=5543755776 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":4,"video":0,"audio":1}' \
  --reasoning-parser muse --tool-call-parser muse --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

`/ephemeral/muse-int4` is a local copy of `intel-ai/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-INT4`. `--kv-cache-memory=5543755776` is 5.16 GiB per GPU, the headroom vLLM reported for TP8 with fp8 KV.

**Unit tests** (CPU, `--noconftest`): **30 passed**.

```bash
python -m pytest -v --noconftest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_per_expert_gate_up.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_wna16_config.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_moe_deployment.py
```

The first two files are new; `test_muse_spark_moe_deployment.py` is from #61879.

**Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format` (ruff 0.14.0) are clean on all 4 commits. mypy and the full pre-commit suite were not run.

**Numerics.** Forward hooks captured MoE block inputs and outputs on rank 0 (TP8, 12-token prompt). These were compared to an fp32 CPU reference built from the checkpoint, with int4 dequantized from `qweight`/`scales`:

| Layer | Experts | cos-sim without commit 1 | cos-sim with commit 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | BF16 (Triton route-major) | −0.07 | 0.99999 |
| 1 | BF16 (Triton route-major) | not measured | 0.99999 |
| 5 | INT4 (Marlin WNA16) | −0.11 | 0.99999 |

Pooler, router logits and pre-expert norm already matched at cos 1.0 without commit 1.

**Throughput and KV capacity.** `bench.py`: 512 output tokens, `ignore_eos`, temperature 0, streaming. Columns c8 and c32 are per-stream / aggregate tok/s.

| Config | KV tokens (max conc. @32k) | c1 tok/s | c8 | c32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8, bf16 KV, util 0.92, text-only | 370,044 (11.29x) | 48.2 | 33.1 / 262.9 | — |
| TP8, bf16 KV, util 0.92, MM | 312,099 (9.52x) | 48.2 | 34.1 / 271 | 19.9 / 634 |
| TP8, fp8 KV, util 0.92, MM | 388,827 (11.87x) | 47.6 | 32.9 / 261.7 | 19.7 / 624.8 |
| TP8, fp8 KV, `--kv-cache-memory` 5.16 GiB, MM | 865,400 (26.41x) | 47.6 | 32.0 / 254 | 19.0 / 605 |
| TP4×PP2, fp8 KV, MM | 1,048,201 (31.99x) | 44.2 | 17.6 / 140 | 11.6 / 370 |
| **This 4-commit series**, TP8, fp8 KV, 5.16 GiB, MM | **865,400** | **47.6** | **32.4 / 257** | **19.7 / 628** |

- Rows 1–5 ran on the pre-split tree: the same code plus VM-only debug instrumentation. The last row is the exact 4-commit series with the serve command above.
- Mean TTFT at c1 was 0.082–0.105 s.
- GPU memory used: 76,239 MiB per GPU (text-only, bf16 KV) and 79,327 MiB per GPU (fp8 KV, 5.16 GiB) of 81,920 MiB.

**Quality:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Arithmetic word problems (10, exact match) | 10/10 in every config |
| Dickens passage perplexity | 1.21 (fp8 KV) / 1.22 (bf16 KV) |
| Needle retrieval, 17,847 prompt tokens | pass (fp8 KV configs, TP4×PP2, this series) |
| Images | 4/4: tabby cat; Eiffel Tower → Paris; exact invoice OCR (`INVOICE #48213 … Total due: $1,274.50`); two-image prompt |
| Audio, 3 LibriSpeech clips, 16 kHz | WER 0.06 / 0.10 / 0.00 with an audio-aware system prompt. The only differences are "Mr." vs "MISTER". Content questions answered correctly |
| Smoke prompts | coherent: factual QA, code, translation |

## Details

**Commits:**

1. **`[Bugfix][MoE] Keep per-expert gate/up halves separate under stacked mappers`** (same as PR A: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62068)
   - `LlamaModel.hf_to_vllm_mapper` stacks per-expert `gate_proj` / `up_proj` into `gate_up_proj` and sets `shard_id`.
   - `RoutedExperts.load_weights` then chunks each half as a fused tensor, so `up` overwrites `gate`.
   - The fix restores the name from `shard_id` for per-expert names only.
   - This is the root cause of the garbage output (see the numerics table).
2. **`[Model] MuseSpark: size the RoPE cache by max_model_len`** (`model.py`, +3/−4)
   - The cache was sized by `max(config.max_position_embeddings (1M), max_model_len)`: a 1M-entry fp32 cos/sin cache per RoPE layer, about 11.5 GiB per GPU at TP8.
   - The first load OOMed during Marlin repacking at 78.15 GiB allocated per GPU.
   - The rotary embedding is unscaled `RotaryEmbedding`, so positions never exceed `max_model_len`.
   - This commit could equally be a review suggestion on #61879.
3. **`[Model] MuseSpark: route-major experts on pre-Blackwell CUDA (Ampere/Ada)`** (`muse_moe_runner.py`, +15/−4)
   - Replaces `is_device_capability_family(90)` with `_use_route_major_on_this_gpu()` (CUDA and not ≥ sm100) in `MuseSparkUnquantizedFusedMoE` and `MuseSparkModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE`.
   - Nothing in the route-major path is Hopper-specific.
   - BF16 experts (layers 0 and 61 of the INT4/NVFP4 checkpoints) now run on `TritonExperts`.
   - NVFP4 can use Marlin W4A16 on sm75+, matching vLLM's generic ModelOpt NVFP4 Marlin fallback.
4. **`[Model] MuseSpark: GPTQ-format INT4/INT8 experts (AutoRound/INC, GPTQ) on Marlin`** (+210/−4, including a 53-line test)
   - `MuseSparkWNA16FusedMoE(AutoGPTQMoEMethod)`: route-major Marlin experts. The MuseSpark post-expert-norm finalize is attached in `process_weights_after_loading`. Requires SwiGLU.
   - `_inc_experts_bits` resolves per-expert bit widths from AutoRound `extra_config`. The checkpoint lists its BF16 experts (layers 0 and 61) individually, and those layers fall back to `MuseSparkUnquantizedFusedMoE`.
   - Symmetric int4/int8 only. Act-order and asymmetric checkpoints raise `NotImplementedError`.
   - `MuseSparkRoutedExperts.load_weights` sends per-expert HF tensors (`<E>.<proj>.<param>`) through the per-expert mapping in `RoutedExperts`. The consolidated NVFP4/BF16 path is kept for stacked tensors.
   - `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM.supported_quantization_configs` gains `INCConfig` and `AutoGPTQConfig`.
   - New test: `tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_wna16_config.py`.

**Why INT4 on Ampere:** NVFP4 activations and the TRT-LLM MoE kernels are unavailable on A100/A800. The INT4 W4A16 checkpoint (466 GB) fits on 8x80 GB with room for the KV cache. The NVFP4 checkpoint (533.0 GB) does not.

**Limitations:**
- **Custom all-reduce is unavailable on this topology.** vLLM refuses custom all-reduce on more than two PCIe-only GPUs, and here NVLink only joins pairs. That applies at TP8 and at TP4, so PyNCCL is used. TP4×PP2 gives more KV (1.05M tokens) but about 45% lower throughput.
- **Audio needs a system prompt.** With no system prompt, 2 of 3 clips got "I don't have the ability to listen" even though the audio tokens reach the model. This is model behaviour, not a vLLM bug, and belongs in the model recipe.
- **Private DeepGEMM pin.** #61879 pins a private `Inferact/DeepGEMM` fork that could not be fetched (tarball 404 / clone hangs). For this build it was stubbed by pointing `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR` at an empty directory. The sm80 path ran end to end without it, but the pin itself has to be fixed in #61879.
- **NVFP4 on sm80 is unlocked by commit 3 but not run end to end.** The checkpoint needs about 73 GiB per GPU for weights alone at TP8, which leaves no KV room at util 0.92.
- **Fused paths not available on Ampere.** The FlashInfer TP-MoE finalize and the CuTe-DSL finalize are unavailable, so the native/Triton finalize is used. FP32 router input is off (`HAS_ROUTER_OUTPUT=False`).
- **Not tested:**
  - non-INC GPTQ MuseSpark checkpoints (shared code path, but no checkpoint available);
  - INT8;
  - Ada (sm89);
  - video input.
- **Docs.** #61879 has no supported-models or recipe entry for MuseSpark yet. Once it does, add: INT4 (AutoRound/GPTQ) on sm80+ via Marlin, and NVFP4 on sm75+ via Marlin W4A16 (memory permitting).

**AI assistance:** This PR was submitted by a human reviewer with the assistance of [Digby.ai](https://digby.ai), which was used for debugging, benchmarking scripts and drafting. The human author reviewed all changed lines.

---

items.title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Fix PLE layerwise reload with CPU offload and TP
items.author: faresobeid
items.summary: Fixes OOM during PLE layerwise weight reload with CPU offload and tensor parallelism by skipping non-local shards and restoring the pinned-host PLE table on CPU.
items.body:
## Purpose

Layerwise weight reload of Qwen4Exp with a CPU-offloaded PLE table (`engram_config.cpu_offload`) materializes the replacement table on the GPU, because reload restores every layer on the default device. It also buffers every PLE checkpoint shard until the layer completes, including shards outside the local TP vocab range. At full size this OOMs (+23.8 GiB/rank at TP4).

Fix: skip non-local PLE shards before calling the weight loader, and restore the pinned-host PLE table on the CPU.

## Test Plan

Two new tests in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py`. TP4 on H200 with the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next PLE config (1 GiB table per rank, shards arriving on the GPU): peak extra CUDA memory during reload went from 2.0/3.0/4.0/5.0 GiB (ranks 0-3) to 1.0 GiB on every rank; values, pinned storage and pointer are preserved.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep data_parallel_index in DFlash/DSpark draft configs
items.author: faresobeid
items.summary: Fixes speculative decoding crash under data parallelism by preserving data_parallel_index in draft configs to avoid shared torch.compile cache collisions.
items.body:
## Purpose

With dense (independent) data parallelism, every DFlash/DSpark drafter on a node shares one torch.compile cache directory, so a cached restart loads artifacts compiled on another replica's GPU and crashes (`CUDA driver error: invalid argument` in the draft's compiled graph).

The draft parallel config is built with `replace(parallel_config, ...)`, which re-derives the `init=False` field `data_parallel_index` from `data_parallel_rank` (0 on independent DP ranks). Fix: copy the target's `data_parallel_index` into the DFlash and DSpark draft parallel configs. (Keeping the field across `replace` in `ParallelConfig` itself would be a broader alternative.)

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py`. E2E on H200: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --data-parallel-size 2` with `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark`, cold then cached start: main writes only `rank_0_0/dspark_head` and the cached start crashes; with this change both replicas get their own draft cache dir and both starts serve.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep per-expert gate/up halves separate under stacked mappers
items.author: pasta-paul
items.summary: Fixes silent weight corruption in RoutedExperts.load_weights where per-expert gate/up halves were fused under stacked mappers, overwriting gate with up.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes silent weight corruption in `RoutedExperts.load_weights`. A model mapper with `orig_to_new_stacked` (e.g. `LlamaModel.hf_to_vllm_mapper`) renames per-expert `experts.E.gate_proj` / `experts.E.up_proj` to `experts.E.gate_up_proj` and tags the tensor with `shard_id`. `RoutedExperts` then loads each half as a fused `[gate; up]` block, so `up` overwrites `gate` and the gate rows of `w13` are never loaded. Nothing errors, and the output is garbage for any model that combines such a mapper with per-expert expert checkpoints (GPTQ/AutoRound exports, BF16 experts in mixed checkpoints).

Found while bringing up MuseSpark (#61879, a `LlamaModel` subclass) with `intel-ai/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-INT4`. The change is independent of #61879.

## Claims

- Under a stacked mapper, a per-expert tensor tagged `shard_id` 0 is loaded as `gate_proj` and one tagged 1 as `up_proj`. Before this change both went through the fused `gate_up_proj` chunking path.
- Fused all-expert tensors (no expert id in the name) are unchanged.
- Untagged per-expert `gate_up_proj` tensors (real per-expert fused checkpoints) are unchanged.
- `down_proj` and all other names are unchanged.
- The fix covers every param suffix: `weight`, `qweight`, `scales`, `qzeros`.
- On MuseSpark, MoE block output vs an fp32 reference goes from cos-sim −0.07 (layer 0, BF16 experts) and −0.11 (layer 5, INT4 experts) to 0.99999 (layers 0, 1, 5).

## Validation

**Unit test** (new, CPU-only), on `main` @ `8e25bbc` + this commit:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_per_expert_gate_up.py -v --noconftest
# 8 passed
```

- `test_unstack_per_expert_gate_up` (7 cases): shard 0 → `gate_proj`, shard 1 → `up_proj` (including `qweight`), plus negative cases (untagged per-expert, fused all-expert, `down_proj`).
- `test_llama_style_mapper_round_trip`: per-expert gate/up weights go through a Llama-style `WeightsMapper(orig_to_new_stacked=...)`, and the helper restores `5.gate_proj.weight` / `5.up_proj.weight`.

**Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format` (ruff 0.14.0, the pre-commit pin) are clean on both files. mypy and the full pre-commit suite were not run.

**End to end.** Run on the #61879 branch (MuseSpark, 8x A100-80G, TP8). The commit is identical apart from line offsets.

- **Symptom before the fix:** rank 0 `w13_weight[e]` for a layer-0 BF16 expert held `up[0:256]` in rows 0:256 and `up[2048:2304]` in rows 512:768. Every other row was zero, with no gate data. `w2` and `expert_bias` loaded correctly.
- **Method:** forward hooks captured MoE block inputs and outputs on rank 0 (12-token prompt). These were compared to an fp32 CPU reference built from the checkpoint, with int4 dequantized from `qweight`/`scales`. Pooler, router logits and pre-expert norm already matched at cos 1.0 before the fix; only the expert output was wrong.

| Layer | Experts | cos-sim before | cos-sim after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | BF16 | −0.07 | 0.99999 |
| 1 | BF16 | not measured | 0.99999 |
| 5 | INT4 (Marlin WNA16) | −0.11 | 0.99999 |

- **Generation:**
  - Before: garbage.
  - After (greedy): `"...Germany is"` → `" Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome"`.
- **Serving quality after the fix:**
  - arithmetic word problems 10/10 exact match;
  - Dickens passage perplexity 1.21 (fp8 KV) / 1.22 (bf16 KV);
  - needle retrieval at 17,847 prompt tokens: pass;
  - images 4/4.
- On that branch this test passes together with the existing MuseSpark MoE tests (30 passed).

## Details

**Root cause** (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py`):
- `WeightsMapper.orig_to_new_stacked` matches by substring, so the `.gate_proj` → `.gate_up_proj` (shard 0) and `.up_proj` → `.gate_up_proj` (shard 1) rules meant for the dense MLP also rewrite `mlp.experts.E.gate_proj` / `up_proj`. The mapper sets `tensor.shard_id`.
- `RoutedExperts.load_weights` resolves the per-expert name `E.gate_up_proj.*` through the expert mapping as a fused gate/up tensor. It chunks the half-tensor in two and TP-shards each piece into the `w13` gate and up slots, so `up` overwrites what was written from `gate`.

**Fix:**
- New helper `_unstack_per_expert_gate_up(name, tensor)`, called at the top of the per-weight loop in `RoutedExperts.load_weights`.
- It rewrites `gate_up_proj` → `gate_proj` / `up_proj` only when both of these hold:
  - the name has an expert id (`(?:^|\.)\d+\.gate_up_proj\.`);
  - the tensor carries a mapper-assigned `shard_id` in {0, 1}.
- **Why it's scoped this way:**
  - Fused all-expert tensors have no expert id, so the regex skips them.
  - Real per-expert fused checkpoint tensors have no `shard_id`, so the attribute check skips them.
  - No mapper, model or quant-method changes.
  - The diff is +20 lines in `routed_experts.py` plus a 55-line test.

**Alternatives considered:**
- *Fix in the model's `load_weights`.* This was the first version, in `MuseSparkRoutedExperts.load_weights` on #61879. Rejected because every model with a stacked mapper and per-expert checkpoints is exposed.
- *Drop gate/up from the mapper, or exclude `experts.` in `WeightsMapper`.* The dense MLP still needs stacking, and a change to `WeightsMapper` touches the name mapping of every model.
- *Raise on an ambiguous `gate_up_proj`.* Turns silent corruption into an error but leaves the checkpoint unloadable.

**Risk:**
- Low. Only names with an expert id and a mapper-set `shard_id` are affected, and those were already loaded wrong.
- Restored names are always `gate_proj` / `up_proj`. That assumes the expert mapping uses those checkpoint names, as the HF-style mappings that produce this pattern do.
- Only MuseSpark was verified end to end. Other models on `main` that combine stacked mappers with per-expert expert checkpoints were not audited.
- **Unit test coverage:** the unit test covers the helper and the mapper interaction. The `w13` load path itself is covered by the end-to-end check above, not by a unit test.

**AI assistance:** This PR was submitted by a human reviewer with the assistance of [Digby.ai](https://digby.ai), which was used for debugging and drafting. The human author reviewed all changed lines.

items.title: [MoE] Stage UVA-offloaded expert weights in VRAM for large steps
items.author: mushroomcarbon
items.summary: With UVA weight offloading, the fused-MoE kernel reads offloaded experts from host memory in place, once per M-tile (64 tokens with the default config here) of the tokens routed to each expert, so in prefill every offloaded expert crosses PCIe several time…
items.body:
## Overview

With UVA weight offloading (`--offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb N --cpu-offload-params experts`), the fused-MoE kernel reads offloaded experts from host memory in place, once per M-tile (64 tokens with the default config here) of the tokens routed to each expert, so in prefill every offloaded expert crosses PCIe several times per step. This adds an opt-in `--cpu-offload-stage-min-tokens` (default 0 = off; `auto` = every step that runs without CUDA graphs): such steps copy each layer's offloaded `w1`/`w2` into a reusable device buffer right before the expert kernel, which reads the copy. Decode and every graph-captured step keep today's zero-copy reads.

## Claims

vLLM 0.31.0 with this patch against stock 0.31.0; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8, one RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0 x16), 16 GiB of experts offloaded.

- **End to end** (16 multi-turn sessions, 16–19k-token prompts, 4 turns, 2 in flight; 3 interleaved runs per arm, spread < 0.1%): wall time **1.785× shorter at 2048-token chunks, 2.687× at 8192**; new-session TTFT p50 17.52 → 8.51 s and 21.89 → 4.93 s.
- **Decode unchanged** (ShareGPT at 1 and 4 in flight within 0.05 tok/s). **Exact:** staging off vs `auto` in one build gives byte-identical greedy output on 18/18 requests; GSM8K 0.896 vs 0.900 (±0.019) against stock.
- **Cost:** one buffer per offloaded expert-weight shape (576 MiB here), allocated in the profiling run so the KV cache is sized with it: −6,144 KV tokens at 8192-token chunks (exactly the buffers), −6,752 at 2048 (~57 MiB more, not traced).
- **235B-A22B FP8, TP8** (16 GiB experts/GPU, one run per arm): 1.52× on 4 sessions × 2 turns at 1 in flight, 1.39× on a following 16-request run at 2 in flight; decode unchanged. Not checked for identical output: this setup is not reproducible run to run even without the patch.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/model_executor/offloader/                        # RTX 4090: 15 passed
pytest tests/basic_correctness/cpu_offload/test_cpu_offload.py   # RTX 4090: 11 passed (3 new + the existing offload tests)
```
Run on the nightly wheel of this PR's base commit with the patched files applied (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14).

- Unit tests: `auto`/0/N resolution (in `VllmConfig`, excluded from `compute_hash`); pass-through below the threshold, for non-offloaded weights and when off; an identical copy that keeps strides, one buffer reused across layers, separate buffers per slot; no staging or allocation inside a CUDA graph capture; and through `FusedMoEKernel.apply` (Triton experts): at the threshold the experts receive the staging buffers (checked by `data_ptr`) and match the same weights in VRAM, one token below they receive the UVA views.
- End to end: `TitanML/tiny-mixtral` (eager, every step staged; CUDA graphs, prefill staged) and `Adamji/tiny-qwen3-moe-fp8-per-block` (CUDA graphs), threshold off vs on: identical greedy output.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: no sync error. Pre-commit hooks pass.

| setup (30B unless noted) | metric | base | PR (`auto`) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent workload, chunk 2048 | wall s; new-session TTFT p50 | 1154.9 (1154.7–1155.0); 17.52 s | 646.9 (646.8–646.9); 8.51 s | 1.785×; 2.06× |
| same, chunk 8192 | wall s; new-session TTFT p50 | 1030.7 (1030.5–1030.9); 21.89 s | 383.5 (383.4–383.8); 4.93 s | 2.687×; 4.44× |
| ShareGPT 256 out, 1 / 4 in flight | output tok/s | 20.83 / 22.87 | 20.88 / 22.92 | none |
| KV cache, chunk 2048 / 8192 | tokens | 75,504 / 68,480 | 68,752 / 62,336 | −6,752 / −6,144 |
| GSM8K (lm-eval, 250, greedy) | exact match flexible / strict | 0.900 / 0.880 | 0.896 / 0.876 | within ±0.02 |
| 235B TP8, `--numa-bind`, chunk 2048, 1 run | 4 sessions × 2 turns at 1 in flight, wall s; ShareGPT c4 tok/s | 111.0; 18.77 | 72.8; 18.90 | 1.52×; none |

<details>
<summary>Server command and kernel microbenchmark</summary>

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --cpu-offload-stage-min-tokens auto
```

One step through all 48 MoE layers (checkpoint FP8 block shapes, random weights, routing from recorded chat traffic): the MoE part is 2.4× faster at 2048 tokens, 6.9× at 8192, 11.3× at 16384. UVA reads 2.32× / 7.75× / 15.05× the offloaded bytes per step; the copy reads them once at 26.3 GB/s. Copying loses below 256–512 tokens (0.91× at 256) and wins from 512 (1.09×), which is what `auto`'s floor of 512 is based on.

Clients: the agent rows replay 16 long ShareGPT conversations as sessions (turn 0 sends the first ≥16k tokens of the conversation, each later turn appends the dataset's next exchange, so prompts are 16–19k tokens and each extends the previous one; 4 turns, 64 output tokens per turn, 2 sessions in flight) with [`agent_sessions.py` + `agent_load.py`](https://gist.github.com/mushroomcarbon/a84affdf83e8e3be9269e3985030a1f8) (exact commands in their headers); the decode rows are `vllm bench serve --dataset-name sharegpt --sharegpt-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 1|4`; GSM8K is `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 250` (greedy).
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `fused_moe_kernel` gives each program one M-tile of one expert and streams that expert's weights, so every tile re-reads the expert. In VRAM that is cheap; over UVA each re-read crosses PCIe (0.97–0.98 host reads per tile). A tuned `BLOCK_SIZE_M` 128 config helps UVA 1.4–1.9× but copying in is still 1.1–6× faster, and it slows the all-in-VRAM case 8–12% at ≥ 2048 tokens.

**Design.** `BaseOffloader.maybe_stage(weight, num_tokens, slot)` returns the weight unchanged except in `UVAOffloader`, whose `UVAExpertStager` copies a weight carrying the UVA marker when the step meets the threshold and the stream is not capturing. `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl.apply` calls it for `w1`/`w2` after `_prepare`, unless the experts set `reads_weight_args = False` (FlashInfer MoE-EP and b12x run on weights prepared at load time). It is a copy, not a cache: no routing inspection (no device-to-host sync), no eviction, any layout the kernel reads, nothing to invalidate after EPLB or weight updates. One buffer per (slot, shape, stride, dtype, device) is shared by all layers; copy and kernel run on the same stream, so layer l+1's copy waits for layer l's kernel (also under DBO, whose micro-batches share the stream). `auto` resolves in `VllmConfig.__post_init__` to `max(max_cudagraph_capture_size + 1, 512)`; an explicit N at or below the capture size warns, since captured steps never stage. The threshold is left out of `compute_hash` (it acts inside the opaque `moe_forward` op). Like the other offload options, the flag is documented through the CLI help; there is no offload docs page to extend.

**Why opt-in.** It shrinks the KV cache of every `--cpu-offload-gb` user by the buffers (several GiB for large BF16 MoE layers), and it is unmeasured on NVLink-C2C systems and APUs, where reading in place may already be fast enough.

**Limitations.** CUDA only: ROCm AITER kernels read a per-tensor attribute (`is_shuffled`) that the buffer does not carry, and a backend keyed on the weight's `data_ptr` would see one address for every layer (none in the modular path is); such backends must opt out via `reads_weight_args`. Measured with Triton experts and FP8 block weights only; FlashInfer, DeepGEMM and CUTLASS experts untested. Only the modular fused-MoE path; monolithic kernels read in place as before. Under DBO each micro-batch copies the layer. With all2all EP the threshold counts tokens before dispatch. The buffers are not in the sleep-mode pool, and come on top of `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`. Copy and compute are sequential: double-buffering would save 4% at 2048-token steps and 12–19% at 8k–16k (microbenchmark), for a second buffer; left as a follow-up.

**Not a duplicate.** #37190 (open) is an opt-in GPU expert *cache*: it inspects routing each forward (`topk_ids.unique().tolist()`, a sync per layer), copies missing experts one by one, evicts with LFRU, and runs the MoE layer outside CUDA graphs (it caps `cudagraph_mode` at PIECEWISE). RFC #38256 asks to load each distinct expert once in batched prefill; this is the narrow form of that for the existing UVA path. Residency work (#54610, #56177, #57794, #57943) decides which experts live in VRAM; this composes with it, since only weights carrying the UVA marker are staged. #51710 extends the *prefetch* backend, which copies every step including decode. #54972 edits a different `UVAOffloader` method. Searched 2026-10-09 and rechecked 2026-10-16: none stages UVA experts for large steps.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

items.title: [ROCm][CI] Persist compile and AITER JIT caches across native AMD CI jobs
items.author: aarushjain29
items.summary: Patches AMD CI to persist TORCHINDUCTOR, TRITON, and AITER JIT caches on a shared NFS volume, dramatically reducing warm-up times in nightly builds.
items.body:
Native AMD CI pods are ephemeral and point TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR, TRITON_CACHE_DIR and VLLM_CACHE_ROOT at /tmp/vllm-native-<job>, so every job compiles from scratch: in nightly build 14707, 1,613 torch.compile runs had 14 cache hits, and AITER rebuilt the same MoE modules in every MI300 MoE Kernels shard (~10 min per module, 116 min per nightly).

Behind VLLM_CI_PERSISTENT_COMPILE_CACHE=1, restore one archive per job (Inductor, Triton, vLLM cache root including modelinfos, and newly built AITER .so modules) from the persistent HF volume before the tests and save it after them. The key covers GPU arch and torch/triton/aiter versions; the archive is replaced atomically by its own job key, so no file locks are needed on the shared NFS volume. PR builds only restore.

Measured on MI300X with the CI image of build 14821:
- MoE padding-matrix test: 201 s cold -> 79 s warm (AITER build of 113 s here; 587 s on CI MI300 pods).
- MRV2 eagle test, first two engine starts: 206 s -> 76 s; torch.compile 18.3 s -> 0.2 s and model-info inspection 11.8 s -> 0.3 s per start.

items.title: [KV Offload] Check /dev/shm for every local DP engine; explain EFAULT
items.author: mushroomcarbon
items.summary: With data parallelism, CPU KV offload sizes that fit one engine at a time but not all together make the engines fail after loading the model with. Nothing in that error mentions. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

With data parallelism, CPU KV offload sizes that fit `/dev/shm` one engine at a time but not all together make the engines fail after loading the model with `OSError: [Errno 14] Bad address`. Nothing in that error mentions `/dev/shm`. This PR refuses such sizes before any engine starts and turns the EFAULT into an error that names `/dev/shm`.

## Claims

- `--data-parallel-size 8 --kv-offloading-size 32` against a 251.9 GiB `/dev/shm` now stops before any engine starts, with: *"/dev/shm cannot hold the CPU KV offload buffers: 8 data-parallel engines on this host each need 32.0 GiB (256.0 GiB in total), but /dev/shm is 251.9 GiB. Lower --kv-offloading-size or enlarge /dev/shm (e.g. --shm-size for containers)."* Before this change, all 8 engines loaded the model, then 6 of them failed with "Bad address" and the server exited after 90 s.
- If a full `/dev/shm` is still hit while pre-faulting (other processes using it, or launch modes the check cannot see), the error says so: *"Ran out of /dev/shm while pre-faulting the CPU KV offload shared region (… GiB; /dev/shm has … GiB free of … GiB)…"*, chained from the original `OSError`.
- No new refusals where `/dev/shm` is not used: the CPU spec on ROCm and CPU keeps a private tensor per rank and is not checked (on XPU it maps the shared region, so it is checked). Config-only construction is not checked either; `VllmConfig` is untouched.

## Validation

- Unit tests, `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py` and `tests/v1/engine/test_startup_watch_processes.py`: 98 pass. The 12 new cases include one that drives the real `CoreEngineProcManager` with 8 engines and asserts that it refuses before spawning anything, and EFAULT cases for the per-worker and sharded pre-fault that check the message, the chained `OSError`, that peers waiting at the barrier are released and that the file is removed. All 12 fail on `main`. `test_startup_watch_processes.py` builds `CoreEngineProcManager` from a stub config, which now needs `kv_transfer_config=None`.
- `tests/v1/kv_offload`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` and `test_hisparse_connector.py`: 1396 passed, 2 skipped.
- The offload config tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py`, `test_hma_auto_config.py`, `tests/test_config.py`) pass with a 64 MiB `/dev/shm` (Docker's default), mounted as a private tmpfs with `unshare -m`: 25 passed, as on `main`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0, as pinned in pre-commit) pass on every changed file.
- mypy through vLLM's own `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` (mypy 1.20.2 as pinned, Python 3.11 and 3.13): clean.
- All of the above on the nightly wheel of this PR's base commit with the patched files applied (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14).
- End to end on 8× RTX 4090, Qwen3-8B, `--data-parallel-size 8 --kv-offloading-backend native`, `/dev/shm` 251.9 GiB:

  | | `--kv-offloading-size` | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main` | 32 | all 8 engines load the model, then 6 fail with `Bad address` and the server exits (90 s) |
  | this PR | 32 | refused before any engine starts (18 s); 0 `Bad address`, no model loaded |
  | this PR | 24 | healthy, all 8 engines serving (169 s); no false refusal |

- A GPU-free reproduction of the race: 4 processes each create a 1.5 GiB `SharedOffloadRegion` in a private 4 GiB tmpfs. On `main`, all 4 fail with "Bad address", in 3 of 3 runs; with this PR all 4 report the `/dev/shm` error instead, in 3 of 3.

## Details

**Root cause.** Each region's creator checks `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm").free` against its own size and then calls `ftruncate`. On tmpfs, `ftruncate` creates a sparse file and reserves nothing, so N engines starting together all see the full tmpfs free and all pass. Pages are only claimed when `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` faults them in. On a full tmpfs, shmem returns `VM_FAULT_SIGBUS`, which `madvise` reports as `EFAULT`.

**Why the check is in `CoreEngineProcManager`.** It is the one place that knows how many engines will share this host's `/dev/shm`. Inside an engine, a dense model's DP rank runs as an independent engine (`reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank`) with `data_parallel_size_local = 1`. A first version checked in `VllmConfig`, which had two problems. It refused configs on machines that never allocate anything, which broke the config tests above wherever `/dev/shm` is small. It also refused ROCm setups, where the CPU spec never uses `/dev/shm`. The launcher covers internal LB (MoE and dense), multi-node `--nnodes`, `--headless` with `--data-parallel-size-local`, and hybrid LB with `--data-parallel-start-rank`.

**Which specs are checked.** The launcher asks the spec class (`_uses_shared_region`, now a classmethod): true for `CPUOffloadingSpec` on CUDA and XPU and for `TieringOffloadingSpec` everywhere. A custom spec that does not subclass these is skipped. With `spec_module_path`, the front-end therefore imports that module once. An out-of-tree subclass that overrides the (private) `_uses_shared_region` as an instance method would now fail at launch with a `TypeError`.

**Why total and not free.** The engines being launched hold their regions at the same time, so their sum must fit the tmpfs's total size. Comparing against free space would refuse whenever something else briefly holds `/dev/shm`. That makes the check necessary but not sufficient: other users of `/dev/shm` are covered by the existing per-region check and, failing that, by the clearer EFAULT message.

**Rejected: reserving with `posix_fallocate`.** It would make the check and the claim atomic, but on tmpfs it allocates the pages under the caller's memory policy. Measured: a file fallocated from NUMA node 3 and then populated from node 5 had 512 of 512 sampled pages on node 3. Every TP rank's slots would land on the creator's node instead of each rank's own.

**Related.** Recent changes to the same region: #59546 splits it across several `/dev/shm` files, #59545 and #60869 spread the pre-fault across workers (`populate_shard`), and #59544 pins only each worker's own slots. None changes how much `/dev/shm` the region needs, when that is checked, or what a full tmpfs reports; the `EFAULT` translation here covers every pre-fault path (per worker, whole region, sharded). Open: #59547 gives each rank its own region and file, and its review notes the same under-detection when several ranks create regions at once; the launcher's per-engine total stays correct under that design. #53073 reworks ownership and cleanup in the same constructor and #61680 adds segments to the HiSparse pool at the call this PR edits, so whichever lands second rebases. #59430 (closed unmerged) had parallelised the pre-fault with a thread pool.

**Limitations.**
- Launch modes where each process starts one engine are not covered by the check, only by the error message: external LB (`--data-parallel-rank`), `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb` (its children run with a local size of 1), offline DP with one `LLM` per rank, and independent single-engine servers sharing a host. The Ray backend (`CoreEngineActorManager`) is not checked either.
- Only an `OffloadingConnector` configured directly is checked: one nested in a `MultiConnector` (e.g. with a PD connector) and HiSparse's shared host pool are not added to the sum, though both get the clearer `EFAULT` message.
- After an `EFAULT` in a region without a barrier (the tiering scheduler's), the partly faulted file stays in `/dev/shm`, as it does today, so lowering the size may not be enough until it is removed (#51730, #54619 address cleanup).
- On kernels older than 5.14, there is no `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`, and the per-page fallback hits a SIGBUS that cannot be translated.
- Under a memory-cgroup limit, the failure is `ENOMEM` or the OOM killer, not `EFAULT`.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

items.title: Optimize sigmoid MoE inference routing with bit-exact outputs
items.author: Waterpine
items.summary: Reduce sigmoid MoE inference routing overhead for Nemotron Nano, Super, and Ultra while preserving bit-exact expert indices and FP32 probabilities relative to the original compiled router.:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact),…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Reduce sigmoid MoE inference routing overhead for Nemotron Nano, Super, and Ultra while preserving bit-exact expert indices and FP32 probabilities relative to the original compiled router.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Implementation

- For small top-k, including Nano's 128 experts / top-6 configuration, fuse sigmoid, expert selection, normalization, and scaling into one kernel
- For larger top-k, including Super/Ultra's 512 experts / top-22 configuration, use parallel expert selection while retaining the original compiled sigmoid and probability computation
- Tune launch configurations for small decode batches and larger prefill batches
- Preserve existing fallback behavior for unsupported configurations and environments

For larger top-k, a scoped runtime dispatch mode replaces only aten.topk. The original compiled graph, cache lookup, and normalization kernels remain unchanged. This preserves the reference reduction order, including when reusing an existing compiler cache

The optimization requires Triton tl.topk and PyTorch's private TorchDispatchMode.ignore_compile_internals hook for the large-top-k path. When these capabilities are unavailable, routing retains the original compiled implementation.

## Performance

End-to-end batch generation latency against the original compiled routing at `442d0183d`:

| Model | Baseline | This PR | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Nemotron Nano | 1.101 s | 1.073 s | 2.56% |
| Nemotron Super | 1.875 s | 1.845 s | 1.58% |
| Nemotron Ultra | 3.100 s | 3.045 s | 1.76% |

Measurement setup:

- Two nodes, 8 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, TP8 / EP8
- Official BF16 checkpoints converted to Megatron Core, with FP32 routing
- The same 16 prompts in both versions, each containing 32–33 input tokens
- Exactly 128 generated tokens per request, using greedy decoding
- Decode CUDA graphs enabled; batch-invariant mode disabled
- Baseline → candidate → candidate → baseline, with two timed generations per process: four measurements per version
- Median rank-0 wall-clock batch latency, with GPU synchronization at the timing boundaries
- Per-rank compiler caches shared across baseline and candidate to control unrelated Inductor autotuning differences.

Timing starts after request enqueue and ends when all requests have finished generating. It includes prefill, decode, and generation-loop CPU overhead. Model loading, compilation/warmup, tokenization, and external serving/network overhead are excluded.

These are fixed-workload measurements using public checkpoints, rather than a reproduction of the original reviewer's unavailable launch configuration.

## Validation

All tested routing comparisons require identical expert indices and identical FP32 probability bits. No numerical tolerances were relaxed

- 87 targeted tests passed on each of 8 ranks
- 120 TP8 router cases passed, covering Nano, Super, and Ultra dimensions with 2, 32, 256, 512, and 8192 tokens per rank
- 292 production-path comparisons passed with both reused and fresh compiler caches, including 36 CUDA Graph replay checks with updated inputs
- 3,552 candidate router comparisons using real checkpoint weights and activations passed bit-exact comparison
- Generated tokens matched across all ranks, runs, and versions for all three models

Tests also cover tied scores, strided expert bias, fallback configurations, gradient-enabled execution, and preservation of the batch-invariant path.

Bit-exact replay tests were added or updated, and the kernel module is registered in the determinism manifest.

Validation used PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130 and Triton 3.7.1 on GB300. Checkpoint comparisons validate the original and optimized Megatron Core paths; full Hugging Face-versus-Megatron forward parity was not tested.

- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests

items.title: [ROCm][Model] Add Beam 1.0 support on ROCm
items.author: jamesETsmith
items.summary: Adds ROCm-native Triton implementations of Beam 1.0 and its DFlash2 drafter, handling FP32-critical arithmetic and MoE routing on AMD GPUs without modifying shared inference infrastructure.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**ROCm-only changes:** [diff from the head of #61978 to this branch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/compare/00fe254cd01b1d6b9f69370750f113cffb90e474...jamesETsmith:rocm/beam-1.0-day0) (1,968 additions, 2 deletions).

ROCm follow-up to [#61978](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61978), which adds day-0 support for Reflection's [Beam 1.0](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B) and its [DFlash2 drafter](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2).

This PR adds AMD-owned implementations under `vllm/models/beam/amd/` for both `BeamForCausalLM` and `DFlash2BeamDraftModel`. The NVIDIA implementation from #61978 is unchanged in the relative diff. Shared package dispatch selects the AMD classes on ROCm and the NVIDIA classes elsewhere.

## Claims

- Beam 1.0 BF16 loads and serves on 8x MI350X with TP8 and expert parallelism through the AMD model path.
- Beam's required FP32 activation, normalization, Q/K preprocessing, attention-output gate, and logit-softcap arithmetic is retained in AMD-local Triton kernels.
- The AMD target uses standard vLLM ROCm attention and KV-cache updates, linear layers, finalized MoE output, and RCCL collectives rather than NVIDIA direct-cache, CuTe/FlashInfer, or MNNVL fast paths.
- The AMD DFlash2 implementation loads the released 1.93B drafter, generates successfully, and delegates cache writes and cache-format handling to the selected ROCm attention backend.
- The change adds no HIP/C++ kernels and does not modify the scheduler, KV-cache manager, model runner, attention backends, or NVIDIA Beam implementation.

### Serving commands

Target only:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --reasoning-parser beam \
  --tool-call-parser beam \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

With DFlash2:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --speculative-config '{
    "method": "dflash",
    "model": "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 8
  }'
```

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 10.1, PyTorch 2.13, TP8 with expert parallelism, Beam 1.0 BF16 and the BF16 DFlash2 drafter.

| Check | Target only | DFlash2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ruff checks and formatting | Passed | Passed |
| Current-source ROCm build | Passed | Passed |
| Full 501B checkpoint and drafter load | Passed | Passed |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, strict extraction | 1,202/1,319 (91.13% ± 0.78%) | 1,200/1,319 (90.98% ± 0.79%) |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, flexible extraction | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) |

The GSM8K used 5-shot chat, greedy decoding, `max_gen_toks=1024`, TP8, and expert parallelism.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B,tensor_parallel_size=8,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=16384,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enable_expert_parallel=True \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024
```

The lm-eval vLLM wrapper also accepts the top-level speculative aliases:

```text
spec_method=dflash,spec_model=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2,spec_tokens=8
```

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model beam \
  --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dataset-name random \
  --num-prompts 10 \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 10 \
  --max-concurrency 10 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 42
```

</details>

### Short concurrency sweep
On NVIDIA SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` / `low_entropy`, with a fixed 1,024-token output, greedy decoding, 16 warmup requests per point, and `10 * concurrency` measured requests:

| Concurrency | Prompts | Target tok/s | DFlash2 tok/s | Speedup | Target TTFT | DFlash2 TTFT | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10 | 117.40 | 168.47 | 1.44x | 234.66 ms | 241.48 ms | 3.41 |
| 4 | 40 | 331.88 | 443.00 | 1.33x | 657.87 ms | 297.50 ms | 3.51 |
| 8 | 80 | 492.26 | 769.78 | 1.56x | 634.83 ms | 240.43 ms | 3.63 |
| 16 | 160 | 803.81 | 1,263.22 | 1.57x | 788.46 ms | 265.18 ms | 3.57 |

All 580 measured requests across both modes succeeded. DFlash2 token acceptance ranged from 30.13% to 32.83%. These are single runs without variability estimates.

<details>
<summary>SPEED-Bench run configuration</summary>

Both servers used the same target configuration:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --served-model-name beam \
  --disable-log-requests
```

The DFlash2 server added:

```bash
--speculative-config '{
  "method": "dflash",
  "model": "/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 8
}'
```

Each server was reused across all four concurrency points. `vllm bench serve` issued its initial probe and 16 warmup requests before the measured requests at each point:

```bash
for concurrency in 1 4 8 16; do
  num_prompts=$((10 * concurrency))
  vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --model beam \
    --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
    --dataset-name speed_bench \
    --dataset-path /path/to/prepared/speed-bench \
    --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_8k \
    --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
    --speed-bench-output-len 1024 \
    --num-prompts "${num_prompts}" \
    --num-warmups 16 \
    --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \
    --request-rate inf \
    --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 0 \
    --seed 42
done
```

</details>

### Remaining validation

- [ ] Accuracy benchmarks (with and without dflash2)
  - [X] GSM8k 
  - [ ] GPQA-diamond
  - [ ] AIME2025
- [X] Performance baseline using NVIDIA [speedbench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) 8k with low entropy and 1k fixed OSL
- [ ] Same checks for gfx942

## Details

- **Vendor ownership:** All ROCm target and DFlash2 implementation code lives under `vllm/models/beam/amd/`. The relative diff does not modify `vllm/models/beam/nvidia/`.
- **Platform dispatch:** `vllm.models.beam` exports AMD target and draft classes on ROCm and NVIDIA classes on other platforms.
- **Target execution:** AMD attention uses ordinary backend-owned K/V cache updates. AMD projections use standard vLLM linear layers, MoE returns finalized output normally, and distributed reductions use standard RCCL paths.
- **DFlash2 cache handling:** AMD-local Triton computes context K normalization and RoPE. Cache layout, slot scattering, optional shuffling, and quantization are delegated to each ROCm attention backend's native cache-update API rather than hard-coded pointer arithmetic.
- **Numerics:** AMD-local Triton kernels retain Beam's required FP32 operations and intermediate BF16 rounding boundaries.
- **HIP launch compatibility:** AMD kernels omit CUDA-only Triton launch options such as `enable_reflect_ftz` and `launch_pdl`.
- **Footprint:** 1,968 additions and 2 deletions across 12 Beam model files; no core execution or NVIDIA implementation changes.

AI assistance was used. The submitter should review every changed line and this description before converting the PR from draft.

items.title: [Feature][AuxOutput] Support routed experts with P/D disaggregation
items.author: faresobeid
items.summary: A decode instance never computes the remotely prefilled prompt, so it has no rows for it, and its first forward starts mid-block. With this PR a P/D decode request emits rows only from its first local forward (fixed at first schedule, so after any rewind for a…
items.body:
## Purpose

`--enable-return-routed-experts` is rejected with P/D connectors (NIXL, MoRIIO, Mooncake), so RL runs that need routed experts (R3) must serve colocated. A decode instance never computes the remotely prefilled prompt, so it has no rows for it, and its first forward starts mid-block. With this PR a P/D decode request emits rows only from its first local forward (fixed at first schedule, so after any rewind for a failed KV load, and kept across preemption), the worker skips the partially loaded first block, and responses carry `routed_experts_start` so a proxy can prepend the prefill rows (`prefill[:decode_start - prefill_start] + decode`). This supersedes #45419 (warn-only; decode rows stay wrong). RFC #55584 proposes moving rows over NIXL instead; this is the proxy-merge alternative.

## Test Plan

New unit test in `tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py` (fails on main). 2-node NIXL 1P1D, Qwen3-30B-A3B, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: merged P/D rows and tokens identical to a colocated server for 12/12 prompts (64-6000 tokens, incl. block-edge lengths and `routed_experts_prompt_start` > 0) at concurrency 1 and 6, and on a repeat pass with prefix hits.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Keep push progress off model thread
items.author: avininjamay8
items.summary: Fixes NixlPushConnector hang by moving heartbeat and WRITE completion polling off the model thread to a dedicated writer thread, preventing missed EP collectives.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix a `NixlPushConnector` hang in 2P2D EP16.

The model thread was calling NIXL for heartbeats and outgoing WRITE completion polling. If one rank blocked in either call, it missed the next expert-parallel collective and the request timed out.

This change is required by the 2P2D EP16 write step in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62007.

## Changes

- Move push heartbeat processing to `nixl-push-writer`.
- Move outgoing WRITE completion polling to `nixl-push-writer`.
- Return completed and failed request IDs to the model thread through a queue.
- Keep WRITE completion and failure accounting under the transfer lock.
- Serialize writer NIXL calls with handshake setup.
- Add unit coverage for thread ownership and WRITE completion accounting.

The change is limited to `NixlPushConnector`.

## Test plan

Set the UCX environment on all four nodes:

```bash
export UCX_TLS=rc_verbs,ud_verbs,tcp,self,rocm
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=ionic_0:1,lo
export UCX_IB_GID_INDEX=1
export UCX_UD_VERBS_ETH_DGID_CHECK=n
export UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=yes
export UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y
export UCX_PROTO_EMULATION_ENABLE=n
```

Use this KV configuration on prefill:

```bash
KV='{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX"],"kv_lease_duration":180}}'
```

Use the same configuration on decode with `"kv_role":"kv_consumer"`.

Start the prefill master:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --port 20005 -tp 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address $PREFILL_MASTER --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

Start the second prefill node with the same command and:

```bash
--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 8
```

Start the decode master with the prefill command adjusted to:

```bash
--data-parallel-address $DECODE_MASTER \
--all2all-backend mori_low_latency \
--kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

Remove `--enforce-eager` on decode. Start the second decode node with `--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 8`.

Start the router:

```bash
vllm-router --vllm-pd-disaggregation --kv-connector nixl \
  --prefill http://$PREFILL_MASTER:20005 \
  --decode http://$DECODE_MASTER:20005 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 7200 --port 30000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --intra-node-data-parallel-size 8 --policy round_robin \
  --prefill-policy round_robin --decode-policy round_robin
```

Run GSM8K:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=DeepSeek-V3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True
```

Run static checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/push_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

## Results

2P2D EP16/DP16 completed with GSM8K exact_match `0.96`.

Regression runs also completed:

- 1P1D TP8: `0.96`

items.title: [MoE] Use the sorted fused-MoE path for host-resident expert weights
items.author: mushroomcarbon
items.summary: At small batch (, e.g. up to 4 tokens for Qwen3 MoE) the Triton fused-MoE path skips and gives every (token, expert) pair its own block (#29354, #39016). [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

At small batch (`num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= num_experts`, e.g. up to 4 tokens for Qwen3 MoE) the Triton fused-MoE path skips `moe_align_block_size` and gives every (token, expert) pair its own block (#29354, #39016). That saves the alignment kernel when weights are in device memory. With UVA weight offloading (`--offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-params experts`) the expert weights are read from host memory in place, and an expert routed to several tokens is then read over PCIe once per token. This PR takes the sorted path when the expert weights carry the UVA offload marker, so each routed expert is read once per step. Device-resident weights keep the naive path.

## Claims

On RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0 x16), natural-text chat requests, 128 output tokens:

- Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8, one GPU, 16 GiB of experts offloaded: **+7% / +10% / +15–19% output throughput at 2 / 3 / 4 requests in flight**; unchanged at 1, 8 and 16.
- Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8, TP8, 16 GiB per GPU offloaded: **+7% / +10% / +18% at 2 / 3 / 4**; unchanged at 1.
- Base is the vLLM 0.31.0 wheel, whose two touched files are byte-identical to the base commit. Measured on CUDA only; ROCm's Triton path takes the same branch.
- No change without offloading: the code path is the same; measured on the 30B at TP2 with weights in VRAM (one start per build).
- Quality: GSM8K (lm-eval 0.4.13, 5-shot, greedy, first 250 questions, 4 requests in flight so decode steps take the changed path), 30B with 16 GiB offloaded: 0.888 flexible / 0.880 strict exact match for both builds, and all 250 responses byte-identical.
- Output: greedy completions identical to unpatched on the 30B (all starts). On the 235B at TP8 greedy output varies from start to start *without* the patch (three unpatched starts gave three different completions and three patched starts two, with one completion common to both builds), so it cannot distinguish the builds there.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "host_resident_weights or naive_block_assignment"`: 44 passed on an RTX 4090, on the original base and again after rebasing onto current main (nightly wheel of the base commit, patched files applied). The new `test_host_resident_weights_take_sorted_path` runs UVA-mapped weights (and device weights as the control) at 1/2/4 tokens through both the modular `TritonExperts` path and the legacy `fused_moe`, asserts that `moe_align_block_size` is called exactly when the weights are host-resident, and compares the output with `torch_moe` (inputs scaled to O(1) outputs, `atol=rtol=2e-2`). Without the change its 6 host-resident cases fail.
- Every applicable pre-commit hook passes: ruff check/format, mypy 3.10–3.13, `check_torch_cuda`, test tethering, typos, SPDX, lazy imports, forbidden imports, boolean context manager.
- End to end, base vLLM against this PR, one `vllm serve`, requests from a client sending natural-language chat prompts (32 topics × 8 tasks, temperature 0.7, a fixed seed per request, `ignore_eos`):

  | setup | in flight | starts (base / PR) | output tok/s, base | output tok/s, this PR | change |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 30B, 1 GPU, 16 GiB on host | 1 | 2 / 2 | 20.7 | 20.5–20.7 | −0.5% (within spread) |
  | | 2 | 2 / 2 | 22.2 | 23.8 | +7% |
  | | 3 | 2 / 2 | 22.6 | 24.9–25.0 | +10% |
  | | 4 | 2 / 2 | 23.1 | 26.5–27.4 | +15–19% |
  | | 8 | 2 / 2 | 34.5–34.9 | 33.5–35.0 | within spread |
  | | 16 | 2 / 2 | 49.0–49.1 | 48.5–49.1 | within spread |
  | 235B, TP8, 16 GiB/GPU on host | 1 | 1 / 1 | 16.6 | 16.6 | 0% |
  | | 2 | 3 / 3 | 17.9–18.3 | 19.1–19.5 | +7% |
  | | 3 | 3 / 3 | 19.0 | 20.9 | +10% |
  | | 4 | 3 / 3 | 19.7 | 23.2–23.3 | +18% |
  | 30B, TP2, all in VRAM | 1–4 | 1 / 1 | 196.8 / 300.3 / 364.1 / 474.8 | 197.0 / 300.6 / 363.0 / 473.5 | within 0.3% |
  | | 8 | 1 / 1 | 741.5 | 727.1 | −1.9% (one start; both builds run the same code here) |

- Reproducible with vLLM's own benchmark (`vllm bench serve --dataset-name sharegpt --sharegpt-output-len 128 --ignore-eos --num-prompts N --max-concurrency c --seed 1`, ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split; N = 8 for c < 4, else 2c), 30B on one GPU with 16 GiB offloaded, two starts each:

  | `--max-concurrency` | output tok/s, base | output tok/s, this PR | change (midpoints) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 20.3 | 20.3 | 0% |
  | 2 | 21.3–22.2 | 23.4–23.6 | +8% |
  | 3 | 21.6–22.6 | 25.3–25.4 | +15% |
  | 4 | 22.2–23.0 | 25.6–26.7 | +16% |

<details>
<summary>Server commands</summary>

```
# 30B, one GPU (GPU 0 on NUMA node 3 here), 16 GiB of experts on the host
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 numactl --cpunodebind=3 --membind=3 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts
# 235B, TP8
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts --kv-cache-dtype fp8
```
The table above the benchmark used our own client sending natural-language chat prompts (32 topics × 8 tasks, temperature 0.7, fixed seed per request, 128 tokens with `ignore_eos`; N requests at concurrency c, N = 8 for c < 4, else 2c; one unrecorded warm-up per level).

</details>

## Details

**Why.** With experts in host memory, a decode step's cost is dominated by the bytes it reads over PCIe, and on the naive path an expert routed to several of the step's tokens is read once per token. The sorted path reads each routed expert once per step. How much that saves depends on how often a step's tokens share experts: on natural-text prompts the gain is in the Validation table; on random-token prompts with greedy decoding, whose routing is far more repetitive, the same change doubles throughput at 4 requests in flight. We report natural text.

**Implementation.**

- `_prepare_expert_assignment` takes `weights_host_resident` (default `False`), which disables the naive block assignment.
- `TritonExperts.apply` and the legacy `fused_experts_impl` pass `_weights_host_resident(w1, w2)`: true when either weight has `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded`, which the UVA offloader sets (and `device_loading_context` re-sets after `process_weights_after_loading`). `w1`/`w2` are the layer's own parameters on this path, so it is a getattr per forward inside the `moe_forward` custom op; the result depends only on the parameters, so CUDA-graph capture per size is unaffected. "Either", because UVA offloads per parameter and a budget cut-off can leave w13 on the host and w2 on the device.
- Other MoE paths are unaffected: Marlin and `TritonWNA16Experts` always align; the prefetch offloader copies weights to the device before compute and never sets the marker. Two model-specific callers of `_prepare_expert_assignment` (`models/k2_horizon.py`, `models/dots3_note/nvidia/vision_moe.py`) do not pass the flag and keep today's behaviour; they can opt in separately.
- Why a per-forward check rather than a decision when the kernel is built: `replace_parameter` in `process_weights_after_loading` installs a new Parameter without the marker, and `device_loading_context` re-marks it only afterwards, so a setup-time check would read False.

**Related.** No open or merged PR makes this change (searched 2026-10-07, rechecked 2026-10-16). The naive path came from #29354 and #39016; #34920 (closed, stale) proposed making it tunable from configs; #55268 (open) warms up Triton MoE variants per batch size, and this PR changes which variant host-resident weights use at ≤ 4 tokens. #57215 (open) keeps MoE experts offloaded during weight post-processing on XPU, the marker lifecycle this PR relies on; #56177 (open) is a shared GPU expert pool. RFC #38256 discusses expert caches for offloaded MoE, where a comment reports the same effect with a GPU-side slot buffer (the naive path stops sharing an expert's weight tile between tokens at batch ≥ 2). #37190, #57794 and #57943 decide which experts stay in VRAM; this PR is independent of that and helps whichever experts remain on the host.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

items.title: [Fix] kda: Use raw beta in prefill CUDA graphs
items.author: Hrithvik-Alex
items.summary: KDA eager and graph extend both receive raw beta, but the graph helper infers beta activation from gate rank. Kimi-K3 supplies a 4D gate, causing graph replay to skip the required beta sigmoid.
items.body:

items.body:
Fixes #20485

## Description

This PR fixes two logic defects in `NGramPoolManager.get_draft_tokens`:

1. **Candidate pruning:** Removing elements from an `OrderedSet` while iterating over it can skip candidates, leaving shorter matches in the pool. Iterating over a snapshot (`list(pool[pattern])`) ensures all shorter matches are considered for removal.
2. **Single-match invariant:** When `is_keep_all=False`, the existing update branch can allow additional matches to be added to the pool. Guarding that branch with `self.is_keep_all` preserves the single-match behavior.

## Test Coverage

Added regression tests in `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_ngram.py`:

- `test_ngram_pool_manager_prunes_all_shorter_matches`

items.title: [Bug]: NGramPoolManager skips candidate pruning and violates the is_keep_all=False invariant
items.author: kunalsanga
items.summary: NGramPoolManager fails to prune candidates and violates is_keep_all=False by retaining multiple matches per pattern in speculative decoding.
items.body:
### System Info

- **CPU architecture:** x86_64
- **CPU/Host memory:** 16 GB RAM
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU, 6 GB VRAM. GPU inference was not used for this investigation.
- **TensorRT-LLM branch:** `main`
- **TensorRT-LLM commit:** `dac84b01a6` (verify against `git rev-parse HEAD` before submitting)
- **Python:** 3.13.1
- **PyTorch:** `2.14.0+cpu` (as reported by the local investigation; verify before submitting)
- **ordered-set:** 4.1.0 (as reported by the local investigation; verify before submitting)
- **OS:** Windows; confirm the exact version using `winver`.
- **Container:** No TensorRT-LLM container used.
- **TensorRT, CUDA, ModelOpt, cuBLAS and NVIDIA driver versions:** Not verified for this investigation.
- **Execution:** CPU-only Python-level reproduction without model downloads or GPU inference.
- **Testing limitation:** The standalone reproduction ran successfully, but the full repository pytest test was blocked by environment-specific imports of compiled TensorRT-LLM components and dependencies.

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Check out the affected TensorRT-LLM revision and inspect `tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/ngram.py`.
2. Reproduce candidate insertion and pruning using the actual `NGramPoolManager` implementation.
3. Insert multiple short matches for the same pattern, followed by a longer match, then inspect the pool and returned draft tokens.
4. Repeat with `is_keep_all=False` and verify whether the pool retains more than one match for a pattern.

### Minimal reproduction for candidate pruning

```python
from tensorrt_llm._torch.speculative.ngram import NGramPoolManager


class MockNGramConfig:
    def __init__(self, is_keep_all=True, is_use_oldest=True):
        self.tokens_per_gen_step = 6
        self.max_matching_ngram_size = 2
        self.is_keep_all = is_keep_all
        self.is_use_oldest = is_use_oldest
        self.is_public_pool = True


cfg = MockNGramConfig(is_keep_all=True, is_use_oldest=True)
manager = NGramPoolManager(cfg, max_num_requests=4)

# Insert short matches for the same pattern.
manager.get_draft_tokens(
    prefix=[100, 101, 1],
    request_id=0,
    max_sequence_length=100,
)
manager.get_draft_tokens(
    prefix=[100, 101, 2],
    request_id=1,
    max_sequence_length=100,
)
manager.get_draft_tokens(
    prefix=[100, 101, 3],
    request_id=2,
    max_sequence_length=100,
)

# Insert a longer match.
manager.get_draft_tokens(
    prefix=[100, 101, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    request_id=3,
    max_sequence_length=100,
)

# Query draft tokens for the same pattern.
draft = manager.get_draft_tokens(
    prefix=[50, 100, 101],
    request_id=4,
    max_sequence_length=100,
)

print("Pool contents:", list(manager.pool[(100, 101)]))
print("Draft returned:", draft)
```

### Reported output from the local investigation

```text
Pool contents: [(2,), (4, 5, 6, 7)]
Draft returned: [2]
```

The short candidate `(2,)` reportedly remains even though its length is smaller than that of the longer candidate.

### Important reproduction note

Please verify the script's request-ID handling and manager initialization against the exact checked-out implementation before submission. Also include a separate minimal executable reproduction for `is_keep_all=False` if reporting that defect. Do not claim that this single script reproduces both defects.

No external model or dataset is required for this investigation.

### Expected behavior

### Expected behavior

**Candidate pruning**

When a longer candidate is inserted for a pattern, all existing candidates satisfying the pruning condition `len(match) < len(new_match)` should be removed. Modifying the pool during pruning should not cause eligible candidates to be skipped.

For the reported scenario, the expected pool is:

```python
[(4, 5, 6, 7)]
```

The drafter should then return the candidate permitted by the pool's selection policy, rather than a shorter candidate that should have been pruned.

**Single-match mode**

When `is_keep_all=False`, the pool should retain only one match for each pattern, as described by the configuration's documented behavior. Subsequent shorter or equal-length matches should not accumulate additional entries in the pool.

### actual behavior

### Actual behavior

The local investigation reported two logic defects in `NGramPoolManager.get_draft_tokens()`.

**1. Candidate pruning skips entries**

The implementation iterates over `pool[pattern]` while removing entries from the same collection. Because removal shifts elements in the underlying ordered collection, some candidates can be skipped.

Reported result:

```python
Pool contents: [(2,), (4, 5, 6, 7)]
Draft returned: [2]
```

The shorter candidate `(2,)` remains in the pool, and the drafter reportedly returns it instead of the longer candidate.

**2. Single-match mode accumulates candidates**

When `is_keep_all=False`, a subsequent candidate that does not satisfy the replacement condition can fall through to an `elif` branch that appends it to the pool.

Reported pool:

```python
[(1, 2, 3), (1, 2), (9,)]
```

This contains three matches despite single-match mode being enabled.

These behaviors were reported by a local Python-level investigation. The full repository pytest suite could not be executed in the Windows environment because of imports requiring compiled TensorRT-LLM components and other dependencies.

### additional notes

### Additional investigation

The suspected defects are located in:

`tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/ngram.py`

A candidate correction for the pruning issue is to iterate over a snapshot before removing entries:

```python
for match in list(pool[pattern]):
    if len(match) < len(new_match):
        pool[pattern].remove(match)
```

A candidate correction for the single-match invariant is to ensure that adding another candidate in the relevant branch is allowed only when `is_keep_all=True`. Both changes should be validated against the intended behavior and regression tests before a fix is proposed.

### Historical investigation

- **PR #5732:** https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/5732  
  The local investigation reports that this PR corrected a condition involving `is_keep_all=False` but did not modify the candidate-pruning loop.
- **PR #11434:** https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/11434  
  The local investigation reports that this PR introduced a suffix-automaton implementation and did not modify `ngram.py`.

A local search reportedly found no duplicate issue or PR matching the suspected defects. This is not a guarantee that no related report exists.

### Testing limitations

The standalone Python investigation completed successfully according to the local report. The full repository pytest suite was blocked by environment-specific dependencies.

The reported defects and proposed corrections should be validated against the unmodified upstream implementation and the repository's supported test environment.

No model weights or GPU inference are required for the reported Python-level reproduction.

The goal of this report is to request maintainer confirmation of the observed behavior and the intended candidate-pool invariants before a fix is submitted.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the [documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM/) and [examples](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/examples) for answers to frequently asked questions.

items.author: bjolo
items.summary: (the L3 storage backend) reads one page file at a time on each rank's single prefetch I/O thread ( + per page). On a node-local NVMe tier with large prompts this serializes restores: in our tests (MiMo-V2.6-Pro, TP4 on B300, ) a rank read ~1.3 GB/s single-thre…
items.body:
## Motivation

`HiCacheFile` (the `file` L3 storage backend) reads one page file at a time on each rank's single prefetch I/O thread (`open` + `readinto` per page). On a node-local NVMe tier with large prompts this serializes restores: in our tests (MiMo-V2.6-Pro, TP4 on B300, `--hicache-storage-backend file`) a rank read ~1.3 GB/s single-threaded, and when many sessions resumed at once loads queued until prefetches timed out and fell back to recompute.

The existing multi-I/O-worker work (#31440 / #31797) parallelizes whole operations, which can reorder them across ranks. This change only parallelizes the file reads *inside one* `batch_get` / `batch_get_v2` call and returns after all of them, so operation order across ranks is unchanged.

## Modifications

- New env `SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_READ_WORKERS` (default `1` = current behaviour), documented in `environment_variables.mdx`.
- `HiCacheFile._map_reads`: runs the reads of one call on a lazily created `ThreadPoolExecutor`, waits for all of them, keeps input order; a read that raises becomes a miss (`None` / `False`) instead of failing the batch.
- `batch_get` uses it; `_batch_io_v2` (used by `batch_get_v2`) reads pages into private staging pages on the pool, chunked (4 × workers), while every `set_from_flat_data_page` stays on the calling thread in page order. That last point matters: a unified host pool takes a thread-local layout lease in `set_from_flat_data_page` and the caller already holds it for the whole transfer; our first version wrote pages from pool threads and deadlocked (a pool thread with lease depth 0 waited for a pending compaction, which waited for the I/O thread's lease → one rank's prefetch ack never arrived).
- Writes (`batch_set*`) stay serial.
- New CPU test `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_file_parallel_reads.py`: parallel equals serial (bit-exact, same order), pool writes stay on the calling thread, a missing page is a miss, `batch_get` parallel equals serial, and reads really run on several threads (this one fails without the change).

## Accuracy Tests

No model code changes. With the same change on `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (nightly 684fea8a), 8 workers, MiMo-V2.6-Pro on 4× B300: 0 hangs, 0 tracebacks, answers identical to a cold run after restores from disk (temperature 0), and ~14 h of reasoning benchmarks with the disk tier on afterwards without errors.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Honest numbers, measured on that setup (8 workers vs serial):
- raw read throughput of real page files per rank: 1.27 GB/s (1 thread) → 3.35 GB/s (8 threads);
- end-to-end restores: ~+25 % at 32 concurrent resumes of 56k-token prompts (30.3 s vs 37.9 s, all from disk), no gain for a few large ones (4 × 741k: 78.2 s vs 71.8 s). The file read stops being the main limit; what remains is serial (existence check, per-page staging copy, page-by-page `set_from_flat_data_page`).

So this is a modest, opt-in improvement for node-local storage, not a big win; it is off by default.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 as pinned)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (The e2e `test_hicache_storage_file_backend.py` needs a GPU server and was not run locally.)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Related: #44774 (flat pages for asymmetric K/V host pools, needed for the file backend on MiMo-V2; independent of this change).
