items.summary: Second slice of #61978 (Reflection Beam), after #62042: the reasoning and tool parsers, in Python and in the Rust frontend. They take effect only with or. [Discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--62052.org.readthedocs.build/en/62052/]
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Second slice of #61978 (Reflection Beam), after #62042: the `beam` reasoning and tool parsers, in Python and in the Rust frontend. They take effect only with `--reasoning-parser beam` or `--tool-call-parser beam`. This does not enable the model end to end.

## Claims

- **New parsers:** `--reasoning-parser beam` and `--tool-call-parser beam` parse output with the checkpoint's `response_template` metadata, as `hf` does. They also derive a structural-tag grammar from the template, which constrains:
  - strict tools;
  - required and named tool choice;
  - structured outputs;
  - by default, every other request, so output follows the template's format. `VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT=0` turns this off.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/tool_calling.md` documents the parser.

## Validation

Results on this branch next to upstream main (fa75d3456d), on the same machine:

| Command | This PR | main |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/parser tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers --ignore=tests/parser/cohere` | 8267 passed | 8064 passed |
| `cargo test -p vllm-parser` | 578 passed | 561 passed |
| `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` | 357 passed | 356 passed |

- **Same failures on both trees, all from this machine's setup:**
  - Python: 10 failed and 117 errors in `tests/parser/mistral` and the Step-3.5 parser tests, because their tokenizers can't be downloaded into the read-only shared HF cache.
  - Rust: the `vllm-chat` `roundtrip` and `grammar_replay` tests, because they need write access to a lock file or that same HF cache.
- **Not run:** `tests/parser/cohere` needs the optional `cohere_melody` package, which isn't installed here.

## Details

- **Shared code touched:**
  - `ParserManager` now picks any response-template parser, not just `hf`. A parser opts in through `unified_parser_cls()`. The `hf` behavior is unchanged except for error messages, which now name the selected flags.
  - `OnlineRenderer` passes the prompt token IDs to the parser before `adjust_request`. Beam needs this to see whether the prompt already opened reasoning or an answer. Only the response-template parsers (`hf`, `beam`) override `set_prompt_token_ids`; for all other parsers the base class method does nothing.
  - `ResponsesRequest` gets two private attributes, so a parser-built grammar can replace `text.format` without changing the request's public fields.
- **Response-template parser fixes**, which also apply to `hf`:
  - When output stops inside a closer whose last part is the next message's start anchor, the parser completes the closer instead of reporting it as malformed.
  - Reasoning tokens are counted incrementally from the template.
- **Size:** about 2.3k non-test lines. Most of it is the grammar builder (`vllm/parser/response_template_grammar.py`) and the Rust `beam` parser.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR adds a Beam parser.

items.title: Support standard DCP save/load with MFSDP v2 state-dict hooks
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: Make standard PyTorch/DCP checkpointing work with MFSDP v2's packed shards and separate compute weights. State-dict hooks attach the correct shard offsets before DCP saves or loads, and refreshes BF16 compute weights from the restored main weights before the n…
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Make standard PyTorch/DCP checkpointing work with MFSDP v2's packed shards and separate compute weights. State-dict hooks attach the correct shard offsets before DCP saves or loads, and `model.load_state_dict()` refreshes BF16 compute weights from the restored main weights before the next forward pass.

The model and optimizer hooks call V2 preprocessing functions that derive metadata from `GlobalLayout` and the local buffer range, without collectives. The preprocessing functions handle module prefixes and optimizer parameter IDs; the existing explicit metadata helper remains available. Standalone checkpoint helpers rely on these hooks instead of repeating preprocessing and weight refresh.

For MCore models wrapped in `Float16Module`, attach FSDP ownership and checkpoint hooks to the inner model, where the wrapper delegates state-dict operations. Preserve the wrapper for forward execution.

## Issue tracking

Depends on #8230. Set the GitHub diff base to `pull-request/8230`; merge after #8230 and retarget to `main` before merging this PR.

## Validation

- Two GPUs: **32 passed, 1 skipped per rank**, covering checkpointing, optimizer checkpointing/steps, shared pipeline context, and focused adapter tests. EP=4 is skipped because only two GPUs are available.
- A plain BF16 `nn.Module` saves and loads with DCP and finishes with `model.load_state_dict()`, without manual metadata preprocessing or compute-weight refresh. Its forward output matches exactly, including nested FSDP units.
- EP=1/2 regression coverage loads through the unwrapped inner model and compares resumed losses exactly. The no-collective test now covers automatic metadata hooks as well as the explicit helper.
- Fresh end-to-end BF16 EP=2: save steps 1–2, restart in a new process for steps 3–4, and compare with an uninterrupted four-step run. Logged losses, all **84 model/Adam tensors**, and optimizer/scheduler metadata match exactly (459 entries).
- Black, isort, and Ruff pass; Pylint reports only the existing `bad-builtins` configuration warning. Mypy reports three existing adapter import/call diagnostics and no new diagnostics.

## Contribution process

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests.
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests. End-to-end validation uses an external script.
- [x] I have added typing and API docstrings for the new preprocessing helpers.
- [x] I have run `tools/autoformat.sh` on my PR.
- No GPU kernels are changed.

items.title: [compile] Remove layer_name from unified_kv_cache_update
items.author: ragulk143
items.summary: By hoisting this layer-specific identifier out of the operator call, (Dynamo/Inductor) can cleanly recognize the execution patterns as identical across all sequential blocks. This prevents graph fragmentation into separate artifacts per layer and successfully …
items.body:
### Purpose
This pull request removes the `layer_name` string parameter from the `unified_kv_cache_update` custom operator signature. 

By hoisting this layer-specific identifier out of the operator call, `torch.compile` (Dynamo/Inductor) can cleanly recognize the execution patterns as identical across all sequential blocks. This prevents graph fragmentation into separate artifacts per layer and successfully slashes cold-start compilation overhead for large model architectures (like Qwen and DeepSeek).

Closes #33267

### Test Plan
1. **Mock Tracing Validation**: Verified via a custom compilation trace script that running a `torch.compile` loop across sequential decoder block mockups executes seamlessly without graph fragmentation or caching trace errors when dropping layer-specific string tokens from the operator signature.
2. **Regression Check**: Ensured structural alignment with the context-hoisting patterns established in previous architectural updates (#32805 and #33184).

### Test Result
```text
 Tracing layers with torch.compile...
 Layer 0: Successfully traced graph chunk!
 Layer 1: Successfully traced graph chunk!
 Layer 2: Successfully traced graph chunk!
 Layer 3: Successfully traced graph chunk!
 Layer 4: Successfully traced graph chunk!

 Verification Complete! The operator functions with zero graph tracing errors.
```

items.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Map lm_head LoRA to batch tokens for prompt logprobs (…
items.author: BeichenHuang
items.summary: Fixes prompt_logprobs silently dropping or mixing up lm_head LoRA adapter deltas across requests in mixed-adapter batches on both V1 and MRV2 runners.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #51594: with an lm_head LoRA, `prompt_logprobs` silently drop the adapter's lm_head delta, and in mixed batches they pick up other requests' adapters. This fixes both model runners with one mechanism. It supersedes #51597 (V1 path, @jialoop-git) and #53842 (MRV2 path, @HuskyLYL), who are credited as co-authors.

## Claims

- `prompt_logprobs` include the lm_head LoRA delta of each request's own adapter, on both V1 and MRV2 (the default since #53183).
- In a batch that mixes adapters, a request's prompt logprobs are no longer affected by other requests' adapters (including requests with no adapter).
- Also covers the MRV2 `prompt_logprob_token_ids` path (#56984), which neither of the two earlier PRs handles.
- No change when LoRA is disabled or the model has no lm_head LoRA layer, and no change to the sampling path.

## Validation

**Reproducer**: Qwen3-8B (untied embeddings), two random adapters on `q_proj,v_proj,lm_head` plus a copy of adapter A with lm_head stripped. Six requests: no-adapter, chunked-prefill (3000 tokens, `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`), and mixed adapters. Each request is scored in one batch and alone, and compared per token against HF+PEFT. Mean |vLLM − HF+LoRA| in nats:

| Variant | V1 | MRV2 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 1.0–1.8 on every LoRA request (≈ base); the no-adapter request in the mixed batch is off by 0.87 (V1) / 0.36 (MRV2) | same |
| #51597 only | ✅ | ❌ |
| #53842 only | ❌ | ✅ |
| **this PR** | ✅ 0.015–0.055 | ✅ 0.016–0.052 |
| this PR, CUDA graphs + `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | ✅ 0.017–0.050 | ✅ 0.017–0.052 |

For reference, the adapter's real effect (|HF+LoRA − HF base|) is 1.0–1.8 nats, and the bf16 noise floor is about 0.04 nats.

<details><summary>Reproducer script</summary>

```python
"""Repro / validation for vllm-project/vllm#51594.

lm_head LoRA delta is dropped from prompt_logprobs. We compare per-token
teacher-forced logprobs from HF transformers + PEFT (reference) against
vLLM prompt_logprobs, for a batch mixing two adapters and no adapter.

  python 51594_prompt_logprobs.py make-adapters --out DIR
  python 51594_prompt_logprobs.py hf   --adapters DIR --out hf.pt
  python 51594_prompt_logprobs.py vllm --adapters DIR --out vllm.pt
  python 51594_prompt_logprobs.py compare hf.pt vllm_a.pt vllm_b.pt ...

The model runner (V1 vs MRV2) is selected with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER.
"""

import argparse
import os
from pathlib import Path

import torch

MODEL = os.environ.get("MODEL", "Qwen/Qwen3-8B")  # untied embeddings
README = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "vllm" / "README.md"

# Adapter A: lm_head + q/v. A_nolmhead: same tensors minus lm_head.
# Adapter B: different seed, lm_head + q/v.
ADAPTERS = {"A": 1, "A_nolmhead": 2, "B": 3}

# (name, prompt length, text offset, adapter). Length 3000 > the
# max_num_batched_tokens=2048 used below, so it is chunk-prefilled; 1500 and
# 3000 cross MRV2's 1024-row prompt-logits chunk.
REQUESTS = [
    ("r0_A_400", 400, 0, "A"),
    ("r1_B_1500", 1500, 500, "B"),
    ("r2_none_37", 37, 2000, None),
    ("r3_A_3000", 3000, 300, "A"),
    ("r4_B_400", 400, 1200, "B"),
    ("r5_Anolm_400", 400, 0, "A_nolmhead"),
]


def all_ids(tok):
    ids = tok(README.read_text())["input_ids"]
    while len(ids) < 8000:
        ids = ids + ids
    return ids


def req_ids(tok):
    ids = all_ids(tok)
    return {name: ids[off:off + n] for name, n, off, _ in REQUESTS}


def make_adapters(out):
    from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
    from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM

    base = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    cfg = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.0,
                     target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj", "lm_head"])
    for name, seed in [("A", 0), ("B", 1)]:
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        model = get_peft_model(base, cfg)
        # PEFT zero-inits B; give it random values. lm_head gets a large
        # delta (several nats) so a missing delta is unmistakable.
        for pname, p in model.named_parameters():
            if "lora_B" in pname:
                std = 0.3 if "lm_head" in pname else 0.002
                torch.nn.init.normal_(p, std=std)
        model.save_pretrained(f"{out}/{name}")
        base = model.unload()  # drop LoRA layers, reuse base weights
    # A_nolmhead: copy of A with its lm_head tensors removed.
    src, dst = Path(out, "A"), Path(out, "A_nolmhead")
    dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    sd = load_file(src / "adapter_model.safetensors")
    sd = {k: v for k, v in sd.items() if "lm_head" not in k}
    save_file(sd, dst / "adapter_model.safetensors")
    (dst / "adapter_config.json").write_text(
        (src / "adapter_config.json").read_text())
    print("saved adapters to", out, "| A_nolmhead keys:", len(sd))


def token_lp(logits, ids):
    lp = torch.log_softmax(logits.float(), -1)
    return lp[:-1].gather(1, ids[1:, None])[:, 0]


def run_hf(adapters, out):
    from peft import PeftModel
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda")
    model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, f"{adapters}/A", adapter_name="A")
    for name in ("A_nolmhead", "B"):
        model.load_adapter(f"{adapters}/{name}", adapter_name=name)
    model.eval()
    res = {}
    for name, ids in req_ids(tok).items():
        x = torch.tensor([ids], device="cuda")
        with torch.no_grad():
            with model.disable_adapter():
                res[name + "/base"] = token_lp(model(x).logits[0], x[0]).cpu()
            for ad in ADAPTERS:
                model.set_adapter(ad)
                res[name + "/" + ad] = token_lp(model(x).logits[0], x[0]).cpu()
    torch.save(res, out)
    for name, _, _, ad in REQUESTS:
        if ad:
            eff = (res[f"{name}/{ad}"] - res[f"{name}/base"]).abs().mean()
            print(f"hf {name}: mean |lora - base| = {eff:.3f} nats")


def run_vllm(adapters, out):
    os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
    from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt
    from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

    llm = LLM(MODEL, enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16, max_loras=3,
              max_model_len=4096, max_num_batched_tokens=2048,
              gpu_memory_utilization=0.6, seed=0,
              enforce_eager=os.environ.get("EAGER", "1") == "1")
    def _runner_name(worker):
        r = worker.model_runner
        return type(r).__module__ + "." + type(r).__name__

    runner_name = llm.collective_rpc(_runner_name)[0]
    print("model runner:", runner_name)

    ids = req_ids(llm.get_tokenizer())
    loras = {ad: LoRARequest(ad, i, str(Path(adapters, ad).resolve()))
             for ad, i in ADAPTERS.items()}
    sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0, prompt_logprobs=0)

    def to_lp(o, toks):
        return torch.tensor([d[t].logprob for d, t in
                             zip(o.prompt_logprobs[1:], toks[1:])])

    res = {"runner": runner_name}
    # 1) all requests in one batch (mixed adapters + no adapter)
    prompts = [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids[n]) for n, *_ in REQUESTS]
    reqs = [loras[ad] if ad else None for *_, ad in REQUESTS]
    outs = llm.generate(prompts, sp, lora_request=reqs)
    for (name, *_), o in zip(REQUESTS, outs):
        res[f"batch/{name}"] = to_lp(o, ids[name])
    # 2) each request alone
    for (name, *_, ad), p in zip(REQUESTS, prompts):
        o = llm.generate([p], sp, lora_request=loras[ad] if ad else None)[0]
        res[f"single/{name}"] = to_lp(o, ids[name])
    torch.save(res, out)
    print("saved", out)


def compare(hf_path, paths):
    hf = torch.load(hf_path)
    for p in paths:
        r = torch.load(p)
        print(f"\n== {p}  [{r['runner'].rsplit('.', 1)[-1]}]")
        print(f"{'mode/request':24s} {'|vllm-hf_lora|':>15s} "
              f"{'|vllm-hf_base|':>15s} {'|hf_lora-base|':>15s}  verdict")
        for mode in ("batch", "single"):
            for name, _, _, ad in REQUESTS:
                v = r[f"{mode}/{name}"]
                ref = hf[f"{name}/{ad}"] if ad else hf[f"{name}/base"]
                base = hf[f"{name}/base"]
                d_ref = (v - ref).abs().mean().item()
                d_base = (v - base).abs().mean().item()
                eff = (ref - base).abs().mean().item()
                ok = d_ref < 0.1 * max(eff, 1e-9) or d_ref < 0.05
                print(f"{mode + '/' + name:24s} {d_ref:15.4f} {d_base:15.4f} "
                      f"{eff:15.4f}  {'OK' if ok else 'BAD'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("mode", choices=["make-adapters", "hf", "vllm", "compare"])
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--adapters")
    ap.add_argument("--out")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.mode == "make-adapters":
        make_adapters(a.out)
    elif a.mode == "hf":
        run_hf(a.adapters, a.out)
    elif a.mode == "vllm":
        run_vllm(a.adapters, a.out)
    else:
        compare(a.files[0], a.files[1:])
```

</details>

**Tests**: new `test_qwen3_unembed_lora_prompt_logprobs[V1/MRV2]` in `tests/lora/test_qwen3_unembed.py`. It teacher-forces generated sequences in a batch with two lm_head adapters and two no-adapter requests, then checks that:
- the prompt logprobs match the generation logprobs;
- the LoRA effect is non-trivial;
- the no-adapter requests match standalone base scoring;
- on MRV2, `prompt_logprob_token_ids` matches as well.

The test fails on main (`assert tensor(0.) > 0.5` on both runners) and passes with this PR. A small CPU unit test, `tests/lora/test_token_logits_rows.py`, checks that MRV2 chunked prompt logprobs wrap each `logits_fn` call with the right batch-token rows across the 1024-row chunk boundary, which the e2e prompts are too short to reach. All of these run in the existing `tests/lora` CI shards.

Commands run (1× H20):

```bash
pytest -v tests/lora/test_token_logits_rows.py   # 1 passed
pytest -v tests/lora/test_qwen3_unembed.py   # 3 passed (incl. the new test on V1 and MRV2)
pytest -v tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_layers.py -k "logits or manager"
# 47 passed, 18 skipped; test_from_lora_tensors errors at fixture setup (HF download offline in my env)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER={0,1} [EAGER=0 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error] python 51594_prompt_logprobs.py vllm ...
```

## Details

**Root cause.** `LogitsProcessorWithLoRA` → `punica.add_lora_logits` maps logits rows to adapters through `prompt_mapping_meta`, which is built from `sampler_indices`: one row per *sampled* token. Prompt logprobs call `compute_logits` on *prompt* hidden states. As a result, the kernel only processes rows `[0, num_reqs)` and gives row `i` the adapter of request `i`. Every other row gets no delta, and rows near the start of the batch get other requests' adapters.

**Fix.** `PunicaWrapperBase.token_logits_rows(start, end)` is a context manager that points `prompt_mapping_meta` at `token_lora_indices[start:end]` (the per-token mapping) for one `compute_logits` call and restores the sampled-row mapping on exit, including on exceptions. It is exposed through `LoRAModelManager` → `WorkerLoRAManager` → `LoRAModelRunnerMixin`, and each prompt-logprob call site wraps its `compute_logits` call:
- V1 `_get_prompt_logprobs_dict`;
- MRV2 `compute_prompt_logprobs_with_chunking`;
- MRV2 `compute_prompt_token_id_logprobs`.

Compared with #51597/#53842, this needs no second punica wrapper or `LoRAMapping` and no runner-specific mapping logic. It also gives each runner a single call site, so new logits-on-non-sampled-rows paths only need to add a `with` block. Both PRs also add a `get_lm_punica_wrapper` with different definitions, so they can't be merged together as-is.

**Why V1 too.** MRV2 is the default, but V1 is still selectable and has the same bug (validated above). The V1 change is two lines.

**Tradeoffs / limitations.**
- `prepare_tensors` is a small host-synchronizing op. With the fix it runs twice per prompt-logprob logits chunk, only when LoRA is enabled and the model has an lm_head LoRA layer, wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. The decode/sampling path is untouched. Restoring once after the chunk loop would save one call per chunk. I kept the per-call `with` because it gives each call site one line and leaves the sampled mapping intact on exceptions.
- The CPU and XPU punica wrappers index `sampler_indices` directly in `add_lora_logits`, so they likely have the same bug. They keep the no-op default and a TODO for now. I don't have hardware to validate them.

items.title: Chenshuz/gigatoken integration
items.author: jupiterepoch
items.summary: Support while maintaining HF parity (with fallback on a fixed set of unicode characters). The default path remains, this change requires user to explicitly opt in via usegigatoken=True --use-gigatoken encodefiles rust-toolchain.toml https://github.com/jupiter…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Support `use_gigatoken=True` while maintaining HF parity (with fallback on a fixed set of unicode characters). The default path remains `use_gigatoken=False`, this change requires user to explicitly opt in via use_gigatoken=True` or the `--use-gigatoken` flag. The tokenization encoding time is 10x - 40x faster depending on input. The functional support is achieved through:
1. Support right-aligned numeric grouping [Gigatoken PR](https://github.com/jupiterepoch/gigatoken/pull/1/changes). The current Gigatoken supports NT3, where a number string "12345" is broken into "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", whereas NT4 would break it into "12", "345".
2. Wire gigatoken into Megatron-LM
3. Fall-back to HF when Gigatoken process unicode characters differently. Gigatoken's ICU 2.2 Unicode 17 character classes differ from HF tokenizers 0.22's Unicode 16 regex. A compiled guard covers the 28 affected ranges and routes the entire input or batch through HF to preserve token boundaries. ASCII skips the regex; compatible Unicode uses Gigatoken. The guard also checks characters introduced by rendered chat templates. Direct native encoding and bulk `encode_files` bypass this guard.

### Validation

Validated with end2end run, with transformers 5.15.1 and tokenizers 0.22.2:

- All **38 new tokenizer tests** and **283 existing serving tests** passed. Tests are added to the existing tokenizer test file.
- Local parity checks against a complete HF tokenizer configuration covered all **1,112,064 valid Unicode scalars** in contextual inputs, in both normal and ordinary-text encoding modes: zero ID or round-trip differences.
- Public HTTP handlers with the real tokenizer configuration and a canned inference client passed prompt-ID and response comparisons, native/fallback routing, template-introduced Unicode, tokenizer copying and **16 concurrent requests**. 

### Setup for right-aligned tokenizer configurations

Install the required fork into the same Python environment used by the serving/RL processes, including the container used on worker nodes. After the normal Megatron environment and Gigatoken dependencies are installed, replace only Gigatoken with the tested revision:

```bash
python -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps \
  "gigatoken @ git+https://github.com/jupiterepoch/gigatoken.git@522b4fadabd2a6d475fc355b0b4b54ee691c24f2"
```

This source build requires Git and the Rust nightly toolchain specified by the fork's `rust-toolchain.toml`. Verify the loaded module and recorded source revision:

```bash
python - <<'PYTHON'
import gigatoken as gt
from importlib.metadata import distribution

print(gt.__file__)
print(distribution("gigatoken").read_text("direct_url.json"))
PYTHON
```

The recorded repository should be `https://github.com/jupiterepoch/gigatoken.git` and `vcs_info.commit_id` should be `522b4fadabd2a6d475fc355b0b4b54ee691c24f2`.  

## Contribution process

- [ x I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

items.title: [Feat] profiler: Add the forward pass id to detailed step span labels
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Adds forward_pass_id to detailed step span labels so consecutive forward steps with identical shapes are uniquely distinguishable in traces.
items.body:
## Motivation

With detailed step annotations enabled, consecutive forward steps can produce identical `step[...]` span labels: two decode or target-verify steps with the same batch size and the same prefix-sum terms (`g_sq`, `g_sqsq`, ...) cannot be told apart in a trace. A tool that wants to pair a step span with per-forward data recorded elsewhere, such as the expert-distribution recorder, which is keyed by the model runner's `forward_pass_id`, currently has to match by shape and order, which breaks exactly when shapes repeat.

## Modifications

- `build_step_span_name` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/profile_utils.py`) gains a keyword-only `forward_id: int | None = None`. When detailed annotations are enabled and `forward_id` is given, the label ends with `forward_id=<n>`, placed after the aggregate suffix (or directly after the base label when the CPU mirrors are missing). With detailed annotations disabled the label is unchanged, so the default trace output does not change.
- `ModelRunner.forward` passes `forward_id=self.forward_pass_id`, which is the same counter the expert-distribution recorder uses for that forward. The other caller (the multi-layer draft-extend replay span) keeps the default.
- `test_detailed_annotations.py` adds one case: the same shape under two forward ids yields two distinct labels for both the target (`VERIFY`) and draft (`DRAFT`) stage, the disabled path still emits the base label, and a batch without CPU mirrors emits `step[VERIFY bs=2 forward_id=42]`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model outputs; only the profiler span label changes, and only when detailed annotations are enabled.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one extra keyword argument per forward and one f-string append when detailed annotations are enabled.

`test/registered/unit/managers/test_detailed_annotations.py` run locally on this head (CPU, `pytest`): 17 passed.

items.title: [ROCm][CI] Enable batch invariance for the ngram scheduling accuracy test
items.author: djramic
items.summary: The ngram acceptance check for async scheduling without preemption fails by one accepted token: Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14602> Sync and async scheduling build different batches, and hipBLASLt picks GEMM solutions by batch shape, …
items.body:
## Purpose
`test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding` is flaky in `mi300_1: (MI300) E2E Scheduling Accuracy`. The ngram acceptance check for async scheduling without preemption fails by one accepted token:
```text
E   AssertionError: config=[executor=mp, preemption=False, async_sched=True, chunk_prefill=False, spec_decoding=True, spec_method=ngram_gpu, spec_mml=None], params={'logprobs': 2}: acceptance=0.07036590269400884, baseline=0.07420924574209246
E   assert 0.07036590269400884 >= (0.07420924574209246 * (1 - 0.05))
```
Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14602>

Sync and async scheduling build different batches, and hipBLASLt picks GEMM solutions by batch shape, so the BF16 results differ slightly and occasionally flip near-tie greedy tokens. That changes which ngram drafts match, while the HF accuracy checks still pass. 

This PR enables `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` for this test on ROCm only. 
## Test Plan
MI300X (gfx942), in the ROCm CI image:
```bash
cd tests
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling_accuracy.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding
```

## Test Result
With default ROCm kernels the check was flaky, while with batch invariance enabled all 15 runs passed and async acceptance was bit-identical to sync (0.07605).

items.title: [CI][Test] Seed each MLA backend correctness case (fix B200 V1 Attention shard 1/6)
items.author: kimseunghyun-kr
items.summary: Seed the random inputs of each MLA backend correctness case, so that a case gives the same result in every CI shard. Fixes #62002 (B200 V1 Attention shard 1/6 fails on since 16 Oct). [Discussion: @wzhao18 @Harry-Chen could one of you run here?]
items.body:
## Overview

Seed the random inputs of each MLA backend correctness case, so that a case gives the same result in every CI shard. Fixes #62002 (B200 V1 Attention shard 1/6 fails on `main` since 16 Oct).

## Claims

- `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` no longer depend on which tests ran before them in the same pytest process.
- Expected: the failing case `test_backend_correctness[glm-MLAPrefillBackendEnum.TRTLLM_RAGGED-1.0-1.0-fp8-4-deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-mixed_small]` (CUTLASS_MLA and TOKENSPEED_MLA, max diff 0.154297 against `atol=0.15`) gets the inputs it has when it runs first in a process. It passed that way on GB300 ([#62002 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62002#issuecomment-6219889830)). The B200 V1 Attention step of this PR's CI checks it on SM100.

## Validation

- The fix is test-only. Lint, format and test collection pass (`pytest --collect-only tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py`: 349 tests). I have no SM100 GPU; the B200 V1 Attention shards of this PR's CI run every case of the file.
- Root-cause evidence, from the CI logs (details in [#62002](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62002#issuecomment-6220068776)):
  - 126 B200 V1 Attention logs of `main` and PR builds from 8 to 16 Oct run this case. Grouped by the exact ordered list of tests that ran before it in the same process, there are 40 orders, and every order is all-PASSED or all-FAILED. All 16 failing logs (builds 95318–95411) share one order (549 tests before the case); the order before it (614 tests, builds 95282–95298) passed 9 of 9.
  - No code change explains the boundary: the only `main` commits between the last passing base (`dd9e07a25f`, #95296) and the first failing one (`642c18d64c`, #95323, a ROCm-only PR) are #58872 (DeepSeek-V4.1, SM90 only), #60356 (XPU Dockerfile) and #61867 (Kimi K3 model files). The failing `main` build #95334 reuses the dependency layer that #95296 built.

## Details

- Root cause: `_run_backend_correctness` creates its queries, KV and weights with `torch.randn` and never seeds; the file seeds only once at import (`torch.manual_seed(42)`), and `tests/conftest.py` has no per-test seed fixture. The runtime-shard plugin splits `test_mla_backends.py` by test ("812 of 2379 tests, split by test"), so each layout change gives the cases different inputs. In the current layout the failing case lands on an input where one element of the CUTLASS_MLA and TOKENSPEED_MLA output is 0.154297 from a reference of about 0, just over the fp8 `atol` of 0.15.
- The seed is 42, the module's existing seed, applied with `vllm.utils.torch_utils.set_random_seed` at the start of the shared helper, so both correctness tests are covered.
- Limitation: this makes the result stable, but it does not show whether these two backends have an accuracy edge for GLM dims with an fp8 KV cache on some inputs, or whether `atol=0.15` is only tight. Running the case with a few seeds on B200 would answer that; I cannot run SM100.

items.title: [Bugfix][Sampler] Carry the boundary tie count across blocks in the split top-p mask kernel
items.author: cipheraxat
items.summary: The split top-p mask kernel restarts its count of tied boundary tokens at every 8192-entry block. Slices longer than one block therefore keep too many copies of the boundary value. [Discussion: ✅ @cipheraxat, CI is now available for this PR.]
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61997. The split top-p mask kernel (`_topp_sb_mask_kernel`) restarts its count of tied boundary tokens at every 8192-entry block. Slices longer than one block therefore keep too many copies of the boundary value. This PR carries the count across blocks, as the monolithic kernel already does.

## Claims

- In the split top-p pipeline (top-p-only rows, batch ≤ 64, CUDA/ROCm), the number of copies of a tied boundary value that are kept now matches the sort-based reference. The kept copies are the first ones in index order, as the cross-slice logic intends.
- Rows without an exact tie at the boundary, and rows whose ties fit in one block, are unchanged.

## Validation

All runs on an NVIDIA L4 (58 SMs, so S=1 at B=64; torch 2.14.0+cu132), branch at `bc6de71192`, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

**New test, unfixed kernel (`main` version of `topk_topp_triton.py`):** fails as expected.

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k test_topp_ties_across_blocks
E   AssertionError: kept [4160], expected [2300]
1 failed, 133 deselected
```

**Fixed kernel, the whole Triton class:**

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k TestTritonTopkTopp -v
95 passed, 39 deselected in 210.12s
```

**Issue's repro script** (4096 tied tokens at the boundary, B=64, p=0.7, run against the `main` kernel file; the script patches its own copy with the same line as this PR):

| kernel | ties over 8 blocks | ties in 1 block |
|---|---|---|
| float64 reference | 1913 (mass 0.700) | 1913 (mass 0.700) |
| `main` | 4160 (mass 0.994) | 1913 (mass 0.700) |
| this PR | 1913 (mass 0.700) | 1913 (mass 0.700) |

**End to end:** `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` routes top-p through these Triton kernels. With it set, `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")` generated 16 prompts with `SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=48)`, which uses the split path at batch ≤ 16. All 16 completions came back with no errors, and the text reads normally.

## Details

**Root cause.** A copy of the boundary value `dup` gets rank `num_preceding + cumsum(dmask)`, and only copies with rank ≤ `numkeep` are kept. Here `num_preceding` is the number of copies in lower-indexed slices. The block loop never advanced `num_preceding`, so every block of a slice ranked its copies starting from the same base. Each block could keep up to `numkeep - num_preceding` copies of its own. Only slices longer than `BLOCK=8192` are affected, i.e. `S < V / 8192`. On current GPUs, S is 1 or 2 at batch 64, so every current vocab hits this.

**Fix.** Add `num_preceding += tl.sum(dmask.to(tl.float32))` after each block. It counts every copy, kept or not, which matches how the cross-slice `num_preceding` is built from `nmin`. The monolithic kernel counts kept copies (`num_kept += tl.sum(duplicate_keep_mask)`), which is equivalent here. The added work is one block reduction per block, and it runs only when the row has a tie at the boundary.

**Test.** `test_topp_ties_across_blocks` spreads 4096 tied tokens over every block of the row, at stride 37 in a 151936-entry vocab. It adds 64 higher tokens and a `-8.0` tail, and sets `p=0.75`, so the boundary falls mid-copy inside the tie group. That keeps the fp32 reference from landing one copy off. The tail matters: if the tied value were the row's minimum, the ladder search could not place a pivot below it, and the row would take the keep-everything fallback before reaching the mask loop. The test asserts that the kept count equals `apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch`, and that the kept copies are an index-ordered prefix. The existing `test_topp_tie_break_deterministic` puts all its ties in one block, so it can't catch this. B=64 gives multi-block slices on any GPU with fewer than 256 SMs. That includes the H200 MIG slice used by the "V1 Sample" CI step. The test also still covers this after #61996, which shrinks slices to about 9.5K entries (two blocks) at this vocab.

**Not duplicating:** the issue has no comments or assignee, and searches for the issue number, `num_preceding`, `topp_sb_mask` and "split top-p tie" turned up no PR. #61996, also by the reporter, changes `_topp_split_count` but not the mask loop.

**Model evals:** the `tests/evals/gsm8k` configs either decode greedily or sample without `top_p`, so none of them reaches the split top-p path. They can't measure this change. The kernel-level comparison against a float64 reference is above.

cc @njhill @abmfy

items.title: [Fix] hicache: Support flat pages for asymmetric K/V host pools (head_dim != v_head_dim)
items.author: bjolo
items.summary: HiCache's storage backend (like the other flat-page L3 backends) moves one page between the host pool and storage through / /. For models with (e.g.
items.body:
## Motivation

HiCache's `file` storage backend (like the other flat-page L3 backends) moves one page between the host pool and storage through `get_data_page` / `get_dummy_flat_data_page` / `set_from_flat_data_page`. For models with `head_dim != v_head_dim` (e.g. MiMo-V2, K 192 / V 128) `AsymmetricMHATokenToKVPoolHost` raises `NotImplementedError` in all three. There is no start-up guard and backups/prefetches catch the exception, so with `--hicache-storage-backend file` the L3 tier silently stores nothing and the log fills with tracebacks. The error message also names hf3fs/eic/nixl only, although `file` takes the same path.

## Modifications

- `AsymmetricMHATokenToKVPoolHost`: a flat page is K of the page flattened, followed by V of the page flattened. Since K and V live in two buffers with different head dims, `get_data_page` returns a copy (`torch.cat`); `set_from_flat_data_page` splits it back and rejects a page of the wrong size. Supported for the two layouts the class already supports (`page_first`, `page_first_direct`); `flat=False` still raises.
- `_flat_page_unsupported` message updated (now only for `flat=False`).
- New CPU test `test/registered/hicache/test_asymmetric_mha_flat_page.py`: round-trips pages through the real `HiCacheFile` backend for both layouts, restoring into different slots, bit-exact; plus wrong-size and `flat=False` rejection. It fails on current main (3 failed) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Does not change model forward code. Run in production-like conditions on our side with the same patch on `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (nightly 684fea8a), MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD, TP4 on 4× B300, `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-storage-backend file` (hybrid SWA pool, DFlash draft pool):
- prompts of 56k / 250k / 800k tokens restored from disk after an 8M-token flood evicted them from GPU and host memory; answers identical to a cold run (temperature 0, text and token count), 0 tracebacks;
- reasoning benchmarks on the same deployment (AIME 2025+2026, GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench, IFEval, HLE-Verified Gold, ARC-AGI-2, …) over ~14 h with the disk tier on: no errors attributable to the cache.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a hot path for models that do not use the file backend. With it, restore times on the setup above (cold / host RAM / disk, seconds): 56k 4.13 / 0.47 / 2.2; 250k 10.7 / 0.56 / 6.1–7.1; 800k 55.8 / 1.37 / 19.5–19.9.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 / ruff-format as pinned)

- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing option changes)

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Bugfix] Keep ranks in step when the FlashInfer autotune cache fails to load or save
items.author: kanusahai
items.summary: Two paths in can still break a multi-rank start when the persisted cache is bad: 1. If it raises on one rank (for example, an entry from a different FlashInfer build fails to parse), that rank exits warmup while its peers wait in the gather.
items.body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #57635. Two paths in `flashinfer_autotune` can still break a multi-rank start when the persisted cache is bad:

1. **Load error → hang.** `tuner.load_configs()` runs before the `all_gather_object` of the loaded flags. If it raises on one rank (for example, an entry from a different FlashInfer build fails to parse), that rank exits warmup while its peers wait in the gather. Now a raising load counts as "not loaded", so every rank in the tuning group clears its cache and re-tunes together, the same as when a rank's `load_configs` returns `False`.
2. **Save error → startup failure.** `tuner.save_configs()` is unwrapped, so a full disk, a read-only cache directory, or FlashInfer's `RuntimeError` (raised when another writer changed the file since it was loaded) fails the engine after tuning has already finished. The tuned configs are already in memory, so the save failure is now logged and the next start re-tunes.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py
```

New cases in the existing fake-world harness:
- `test_cache_load_error_retunes_every_rank_in_its_tuning_group[pp, tp]` for (1, 1), (1, 4) and (2, 4): one rank's `load_configs` raises, every rank in its tuning group re-tunes and saves, and collectives match across ranks.
- `test_cache_save_error_does_not_fail_startup[OSError | RuntimeError]`: one rank's save raises, startup completes, and the other ranks still save.

## Test Result

- With this change: 19 passed.
- Without the `kernel_warmup.py` change: the 5 new cases fail and the existing 14 pass.

We run the same two changes as a local backport on B200 with several replicas sharing one cache directory.

items.title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Fix routed-experts store overflow at full KV
items.author: faresobeid
items.summary: Fixes a BlockObjectStoreError crash at 100% KV cache usage by resizing the routed-experts store to account for scheduler block reuse delays.
items.body:
## Purpose

With `enable_return_routed_experts`, the engine crashes once KV usage reaches 100%: `BlockObjectStoreError` is raised in the AuxOutput writer thread.

The routed-experts store is sized to the KV cache. A finished or preempted request's KV blocks are reused at the next schedule, but its keys are released only after the in-flight step is processed, so at full KV the referenced keys exceed the store.

Fix: size the store at the KV block count plus the most blocks the scheduler can reuse and re-key before those deferred releases arrive (`(max_concurrent_batches - 1) * (cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, hash_block_size) + max_num_seqs)`). Also send hashes only for scheduled blocks and stop rescanning the whole store on every `put` when it is full.

## Test Plan

Updated unit tests. Reproduced with GLM-4.5-Air TP8 at full KV: crashes on v0.31.0, runs clean with this change.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Wait for idle before completing abort-mode pause
items.author: AnkitNakhawa
items.summary: A streamed client can disconnect and release its tokenizer reader lock while its request is still active in the scheduler. previously returned success as soon as that lock was free, although the abort was fire-and-forget and scheduler cleanup was incomplete.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44745.

A streamed client can disconnect and release its tokenizer reader lock while its request is still active in the scheduler. `pause_generation(mode="abort")` previously returned success as soon as that lock was free, although the abort was fire-and-forget and scheduler cleanup was incomplete. An immediate `release_memory_occupation` then hit its idle assertion and killed the scheduler.

## Modifications

- Add an internal scheduler-idle probe using the existing fan-out communicator.
- In abort-mode pause, wait for both the tokenizer reader lock to clear and every scheduler replica to report `is_fully_idle()`.
- Keep scheduler inference enabled during the wait so normal abort cleanup, including overlap results, can drain. Retain the memory-release idle assertion.
- Share the abort drain helper between TokenizerManager and the multi-HTTP-worker override, so both paths wait for scheduler cleanup.
- Shield each in-flight probe from caller cancellation and retain it in the manager task set. The existing communicator FIFO lock stays held until all replies drain, preventing stale replies from satisfying a retry.
- Add seven CPU regression tests covering disconnect cleanup, all-replica idle checks, tokenizer readers, other pause modes, the full-idle predicate, multi-HTTP-worker pause, and cancellation/retry with delayed responses from two scheduler replicas.

## Reproduction and validation

Tested upstream base `a038a0dca05cefca1e0edc4ac43e3bfbec2e064c` and the patch on one NVIDIA A10 (23 GB), using `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, CUDA 13.0 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, and the reporter's unmodified stdlib repro script from #44745.

Server:
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 30000 \
  --enable-memory-saver --max-total-tokens 6000 --max-running-requests 32
python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:30000
```

The runtime used `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (digest `sha256:0b3e39704480c423d8a00ca15ebee63154defc62944df2d4b11c594563bab457`) with the source checkout mounted, FlashInfer updated from 0.7.1 to the source-required 0.7.2, and the image's bundled Rust tree-core extension copied into the checkout. Default overlap scheduling and the Rust tree core were enabled.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unmodified baseline | Trial 0: pause HTTP 200, release HTTP 500, server down; scheduler raised the reported idle assertion |
| Patched, original repro | 10/10 trials passed, alternating 0 ms and 1 ms after disconnect; every pause/release/resume/continue returned HTTP 200 and health remained HTTP 200 |

Baseline scheduler exception:
```text
File ".../scheduler_components/weight_updater.py", line 339, in release_memory_occupation
    assert self.is_fully_idle(
AssertionError: release_memory_occupation should be called only when server is idle.
SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.
```

Patched repro:
```text
trial 0: pause(abort) 0 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 1: pause(abort) 1 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 2: pause(abort) 0 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 3: pause(abort) 1 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 4: pause(abort) 0 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 5: pause(abort) 1 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 6: pause(abort) 0 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 7: pause(abort) 1 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 8: pause(abort) 0 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
trial 9: pause(abort) 1 ms after the disconnect -> pause 200, release 200, resume 200, continue 200; alive
not reproduced
```

Regression command:
```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_abort_pause_idle.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py
```
Result after the edge-case fixes: **104 passed, 51 subtests passed** (20 dependency/configuration warnings).

The original GPU repro was rerun against commit `53d1442141979fcdfa28410ad7ca909610e356af`:

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default single HTTP worker | 10/10 trials passed; all control calls HTTP 200, health HTTP 200 |
| `--tokenizer-worker-num 2` | 10/10 trials passed; all control calls HTTP 200, health HTTP 200 |

Both runs used the unchanged reporter script, alternating 0 ms and 1 ms disconnect delays. Multi-HTTP-worker validation uses two HTTP/tokenizer workers on the same A10; it is not multi-GPU validation.

Multi-GPU and disaggregated runtime validation were not performed; the all-replica wait is covered by a unit test.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-forward or sampling changes. The end-to-end repro verifies generation can continue after memory resume; no separate accuracy benchmark was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark was run. Scheduler-idle polling occurs only during abort-mode pause, with a 10 ms delay between unsuccessful probes.

## Checklist

- [x] Add CPU regression tests and register them for CPU CI.
- [x] Reproduce the baseline crash and rerun the original GPU repro with the patch.
- [ ] Upstream CI and multi-GPU/disaggregated validation.

items.title: [Bugfix][Qwen3-Omni] Pass lm_head prefix for NVFP4 exclusion
items.author: Killer-Queue
items.summary: Fixes missing lm_head prefix propagation in Qwen3-Omni that caused NVFP4 quantized checkpoint loading to fail due to BF16 head being misclassified as NVFP4.
items.body:
## Overview

Fix Qwen3-Omni Thinker `lm_head` prefix propagation for the NVFP4
quantization path.

This mirrors the related fix merged in
[vllm-omni#4528](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/4528).

## Claims

- Pass the `lm_head` prefix to `ParallelLMHead`.
- Prevent the BF16 `lm_head` from being incorrectly treated as an NVFP4
  layer.
- Fix the 1024-vs-2048 weight loading failure for Qwen3-Omni NVFP4
  checkpoints.

## Validation

Local validation:

- `git diff --check`: passed.

External end-to-end validation was performed on a separate server with:

- vLLM `0.29.0`
- `vllm:v0.29.0`
- RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell GPU
- `dizuo-ModelOpt-NVFP4` checkpoint

Before this change, loading failed with:

```text
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1024) must match
the size of tensor b (2048)
```

After this change:

- The NVFP4 checkpoint loaded successfully.
- All checkpoint shards loaded successfully.
- `Application startup complete` was reached.
- `/v1/models` reported `nvfp4`.
- A 32-token completion returned valid Chinese text.

The external validation used the vLLM serving path with:

```bash
vllm serve <NVFP4_CHECKPOINT> \
  --served-model-name nvfp4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --enable-prefix-caching
```

## Details

`Qwen3MoeLLMForCausalLM` constructed `ParallelLMHead` without passing its
prefix. As a result, the ModelOpt NVFP4 exclusion rule could not match
`lm_head`, and the BF16 head was incorrectly treated as an NVFP4 layer.

The fix passes `maybe_prefix(prefix, "lm_head")`, matching the existing
Qwen3 MoE implementation. The change is limited to one model constructor
and does not alter behavior for other models or unquantized checkpoints.

No additional unit test was added because this failure requires a real
NVFP4 checkpoint and quantized weight-loading path. The affected path was
validated end to end on the required GPU environment.

items.title: [Kernel] Add router GEMM kernels for (5120, 256) and BF16 output to ll_bf16_gemm
items.author: WoosukKwon
items.summary: First, low-risk slice of #61978 (Reflection Beam): kernel coverage for Beam's router shape and a BF16 output for. Nothing here selects Beam-specific code, and existing shapes, dtypes and dispatch are unchanged. [Discussion: ✅ Triggered for commit.]
items.body:
## Overview

First, low-risk slice of #61978 (Reflection Beam): kernel coverage for Beam's router shape and a BF16 output for `ll_bf16_gemm`. Nothing here selects Beam-specific code, and existing shapes, dtypes and dispatch are unchanged. This does not enable the model end to end.

## Claims

- `fp32_router_gemm` supports `(hidden=5120, experts=256)` for up to 48 tokens, with a Blackwell-tuned launch geometry. `GateLinear` uses it for that shape: on SM100 with BF16 input, up to 48 tokens when the count is a multiple of 8, otherwise up to 16. Larger batches go to BF16x3.
- `ll_bf16_gemm` accepts `output_dtype=torch.bfloat16`. It still accumulates in FP32 and only the epilogue changes. This PR also adds tuned split-K configs for K=5120, N∈{1792, 3584}. FP32 output stays the default, and both dtypes keep separate compile-cache entries.
- BF16x3 router GEMM fixes:
  - It raised `KeyError` when a shape had overrides but none for the current token bucket; it now falls back to the heuristic.
  - It returns early for zero tokens.
  - It adds a `(5120, 256)` tile override.
- `grouped_topk` returns empty outputs for zero tokens, e.g. on an idle DP rank, instead of launching the kernel.

## Validation

GB200, run on this branch:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_fp32_router_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py
```

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_fp32_router_gemm.py`: all M in 1..48 for the new shape, range errors per shape, `GateLinear` FP32 precision and top-k with CUDA graph replay | 278 passed |
| `test_ll_bf16_gemm.py`: BF16 output next to FP32 in the cache, CUDA graph replay | 144 passed |
| `test_routing.py`: zero-token `grouped_topk` | 509 passed |

## Details

- The new router GEMM instantiations cover M=1..48 for `(5120, 256)` only. The other shapes keep their limit of 32.
- An existing model would also switch to the FP32 kernel if it has an FP32 router weight, hidden size 5120 and 256 experts, since that pair is now in `GateLinear.FP32_SUPPORTED_SHAPES`.
- Beam's remaining pieces will follow in separate PRs: MegaMoE deferred finalize, parsers and the model itself.
- Not a duplicate: open PRs that touch the router GEMMs (#61903, #50177, #60681) cover other shapes, architectures or compile behavior.

items.body:
## Motivation

`test_lora_eviction.py` fails during model loading on the 5090 runner in [this extra-a CI job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38833170655/job/116756528883?pr=43387), before any eviction assertions run:

```text
RuntimeError: Cannot find any model weights with `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`
```

The test still uses the legacy repository ID. Hugging Face redirects its model API to `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, which is already used by the other Llama 3.1 LoRA tests. Repository IDs also determine local Hugging Face cache paths, so the legacy name does not directly reuse a cache populated under the canonical ID. The job log does not establish why the legacy snapshot had no usable weights.

## Modifications

Use `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` as the eviction test's base model ID, avoiding the legacy alias and aligning its cache lookup with the other tests. The model, adapters, eviction sequences, and output comparisons are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- Confirmed the legacy Hugging Face model API redirects to the canonical ID and the canonical metadata lists four safetensors shards.
- Python AST parsing, Ruff lint/format, isort, and `git diff --check` passed.
- GPU eviction tests were not run locally: this workspace is macOS without a CUDA GPU. The registered `extra-a` test still needs CI validation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable; test model identifier only.

items.title: [Fix] diffusion: Unmerge LoRA layers the next adapter does not cover
items.author: OnePunchMonk
items.summary: Its base weight still holds A's merged delta, so keeps applying A. also returned early on, so deactivate/unmerge could not remove it either. [Discussion: <!-- pr-check-comment runs=38937216267 --> Required checks failed on e9a8141; this PR cannot be merg]
items.body:
## Problem
If adapter A is merged into a layer and `set_lora` switches to adapter B that does not cover that layer, the layer is only marked `disable_lora`. Its base weight still holds A's merged delta, so `forward` keeps applying A. `unmerge_lora_weights` also returned early on `disable_lora`, so deactivate/unmerge could not remove it either.

## Fix
- `_apply_lora_to_layers`: a layer no new adapter covers is unmerged (if merged) and cleared before being disabled. Clearing matters: `merge_lora_weights` re-enables any layer that still has `lora_A` set.
- `unmerge_lora_weights` guards on `merged` only. All callers already check `merged` first.
- The existing clearing block in `set_lora_weights` moved into `clear_lora_weights()` so both paths share it.

## Tests

**Regression tests** (`test/unit/test_lora_pipeline.py`), fail on main, pass here:
- `test_switching_adapters_unmerges_layers_the_new_adapter_skips`
- `test_unmerge_restores_base_even_when_lora_disabled`

On main both fail with `assert not True` on `layer.merged`.

**LoRA unit tests** (CPU):
```
pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_*lora*.py  (excluding cuda-only file)
136 passed, 23 skipped (CUDA-only)
```

**Full multimodal_gen unit suite**, CPU, run on main and on this branch in the same env and diffed. The only difference is the two new tests going from FAILED to passed:
```
main:   416 failed, 2837 passed, 736 skipped, 95 errors
branch: 414 failed, 2839 passed, 736 skipped, 95 errors
```
The remaining failures/errors are identical on both sides and come from the CPU-only macOS env (no CUDA, missing optional deps).

**GPU e2e**, NVIDIA L4, Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers through `DiffGenerator`, 256x256, 5 frames, 4 steps, seed 0, `merge_mode="merge"`. Adapter A: rank 4 on `self_attn.{q,k,v,o}` of all 30 blocks. Adapter B: only `blocks.0.self_attn.q` with a zero up-projection, so it adds no delta and leaves every other A layer uncovered. Max abs pixel diff vs the base output (0-255):

| step | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| A merged | 200 | 200 |
| switch to B | 178 | 0 |
| `unmerge_lora_weights()` | 178 | 0 |

On main, A's delta survives both the switch and the unmerge. With this PR the output matches base exactly.

## Note
When an adapter does not cover every layer, A -> B -> disable -> B now takes the full re-apply path instead of `_reactivate_cached_dynamic_lora_layers`. Output is the same; only that narrow case is slower.

## Logs and run details

<details><summary>CPU regression tests: main vs this branch</summary>

Env: macOS arm64, Python 3.11.15, torch 2.14.1 (CPU).

```
$ pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_pipeline.py -k "skips or disabled"

FAILED sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_pipeline.py::test_switching_adapters_unmerges_layers_the_new_adapter_skips
FAILED sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_pipeline.py::test_unmerge_restores_base_even_when_lora_disabled
2 failed, 18 deselected, 2 warnings in 1.60s

# this branch
2 passed, 18 deselected, 2 warnings in 1.25s

$ pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_*lora*.py   # minus cuda-only file
136 passed, 23 skipped, 3 warnings in 7.43s
```
</details>

<details><summary>GPU e2e log (L4)</summary>

Setup: Modal, `nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04`, Python 3.11, sglang at ed2ebad342 installed with `pip install -e 'python[diffusion]'` (`SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none`). Each variant runs `DiffGenerator` in a fresh process; the patched variant copies this PR's `linear.py` and `pipeline.py` over the install. Text encoder and VAE use `layerwise_offload_components`; the DiT stays resident. Sequence: generate base, `set_lora(A, merge_mode="merge")`, generate, `set_lora(B, merge_mode="merge")`, generate, `unmerge_lora_weights()`, generate.

```
NVIDIA L4, 23034 MiB
===== origin/main rc=0
RESULT {"a_vs_base": 200.0, "switch_to_b_vs_base": 178.0, "unmerge_vs_base": 178.0}
```

<details><summary>Repro script</summary>

```python
"""GPU e2e: does a merged LoRA leak into layers the next adapter skips?

Runs the real DiffGenerator (Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B) once on origin/main, then again
with the patched linear.py / pipeline.py copied over the install.
"""

import modal

COMMIT = "ed2ebad342"
REPO = "/sglang"
RT = f"{REPO}/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime"
PATCH = "<checkout of this PR>/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime"

image = (
    modal.Image.from_registry("nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04", add_python="3.11")
    .apt_install("git", "ffmpeg", "libgl1", "libglib2.0-0")
    .run_commands(
        f"git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git {REPO}",
        f"cd {REPO} && git checkout {COMMIT}",
        f"cd {REPO} && SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none pip install -e 'python[diffusion]'",
    )
    .env({"HF_HOME": "/hf", "PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF": "expandable_segments:True"})
    .add_local_file(f"{PATCH}/layers/lora/linear.py", "/patch/linear.py")
    .add_local_file(f"{PATCH}/pipelines_core/lora/pipeline.py", "/patch/pipeline.py")
)
hf = modal.Volume.from_name("hf-cache-lora-leak", create_if_missing=True)
app = modal.App("sglang-lora-leak", image=image)

WORKER = r'''
import json, sys, numpy as np, torch
from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file
from sglang.multimodal_gen import DiffGenerator

# Synthetic adapter A sized for Wan2.1-1.3B (dim 1536, 30 blocks).
g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
sd = {}
for i in range(30):
    for proj in ("q", "k", "v", "o"):
        base = f"diffusion_model.blocks.{i}.self_attn.{proj}"
        sd[base + ".lora_A.weight"] = (torch.randn(4, 1536, generator=g) * 0.05).to(torch.bfloat16)
        sd[base + ".lora_B.weight"] = (torch.randn(1536, 4, generator=g) * 0.05).to(torch.bfloat16)
a_path = "/tmp/lora_a.safetensors"
save_file(sd, a_path)
# Adapter B covers one layer of A with a zero up-projection: no delta of its
# own, and every other A layer is left uncovered.
down = "diffusion_model.blocks.0.self_attn.q.lora_A.weight"
up = down.replace("lora_A", "lora_B")
b = {down: sd[down].clone(), up: torch.zeros_like(sd[up])}
b_path = "/tmp/lora_b.safetensors"
save_file(b, b_path)
print("A keys", len(sd), "B keys", list(b), flush=True)

gen = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained(
    model_path="Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers", num_gpus=1, layerwise_offload_components=["text_encoder", "vae"],
    pin_cpu_memory=False
)
kw = dict(prompt="a red ball on a table", height=256, width=256, num_frames=5,
          num_inference_steps=4, seed=0, save_output=False)

def frames():
    r = gen.generate(sampling_params_kwargs=dict(kw))
    r = r[0] if isinstance(r, list) else r
    return np.asarray(r.frames, dtype=np.float32)

def drift(x, y):
    return float(np.abs(x - y).max())

base = frames()
gen.set_lora("a", a_path, merge_mode="merge")
with_a = frames()
gen.set_lora("b", b_path, merge_mode="merge")
after_switch = frames()
gen.unmerge_lora_weights()
after_unmerge = frames()
out = {
    "a_vs_base": drift(with_a, base),
    "switch_to_b_vs_base": drift(after_switch, base),
    "unmerge_vs_base": drift(after_unmerge, base),
}
print("RESULT", json.dumps(out), flush=True)
'''


@app.function(gpu="L4", timeout=3600, volumes={"/hf": hf}, memory=32768)
def run():
    import json, shutil, subprocess

    def once(label):
        import textwrap
        with open("/tmp/worker.py", "w") as f:
            f.write("if __name__ == '__main__':\n" + textwrap.indent(WORKER, "    "))
        p = subprocess.run(["python", "/tmp/worker.py"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        hf.commit()
        tail = "\n".join(l for l in (p.stdout + p.stderr).splitlines() if "Error" in l or "error" in l or "Traceback" in l)[-4000:]
        res = [l for l in p.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("RESULT ")]
        print(f"===== {label} rc={p.returncode}\n{tail if not res else res[0]}")
        return json.loads(res[0][7:]) if res else None

    subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=name,memory.total", "--format=csv"])
    main = once("origin/main")
    shutil.copy("/patch/linear.py", f"{RT}/layers/lora/linear.py")
    shutil.copy("/patch/pipeline.py", f"{RT}/pipelines_core/lora/pipeline.py")
    print(subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "diff", "--stat"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
    fixed = once("patched")
    return {"main": main, "patched": fixed}


@app.local_entrypoint()
def main():
    print(run.remote())
```
</details>

items.title: [Feat] [Intel] lora: Add intel_xpu LoRA backend
items.author: srujan-thomdapu
items.summary: On Intel XPU, multi-LoRA serving currently has to use the generic,, or backends. This PR adds an LoRA backend that runs the native Intel XPU LoRA kernels from on both the prefill and decode paths.
items.body:
# [Feat] [Intel] lora: Add intel_xpu LoRA backend

## Motivation

On Intel XPU, multi-LoRA serving currently has to use the generic `triton`, `csgmv`, or `torch_native` backends. This PR adds an `intel_xpu` LoRA backend that runs the native Intel XPU LoRA kernels from [sgl-kernel-xpu](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu) on both the prefill and decode paths.

Usage:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path <base-model> \
    --device xpu \
    --enable-lora \
    --lora-paths <name>=<adapter-path> \
    --lora-backend intel_xpu
```

## Dependency: sgl-kernel-xpu

The backend imports these ops from `sgl_kernel` (sgl-kernel-xpu):

| Op | Used for | PR (merged and closed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `embedding_lora_a_fwd` | Embedding LoRA A | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#207](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/207) |
| `sgemm_lora_a_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/262) |
| `sgemm_lora_b_fwd` | LoRA B expand, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/356) |
| `qkv_lora_b_fwd` | Fused QKV LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/393) |
| `gate_up_lora_b_fwd` | Fused gate/up LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#490](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/490) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, decode | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/506) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_fwd` | LoRA B expand, decode (single, QKV, and gate/up slices) | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#523](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/523) |

These kernels especially decode kernels are optimized. To get the best performance, build sgl-kernel-xpu from the PR below:

- [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#550](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/550) - <Decode LoRA kernels are optimized>

This PR should merge after the above PR got merged in sgl-kernel-xpu.

## Modifications

**New backend**: `python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/intel_xpu_backend.py` (`IntelXpuLoRABackend`)
- Prefill (contiguous batch metadata, `permutation is None`): per-shape XPU kernels (`sgemm_lora_a_fwd`, `sgemm_lora_b_fwd`, `qkv_lora_b_fwd`, `gate_up_lora_b_fwd`).
- Decode: tokens are sorted by adapter (`compute_sgemm_routing`), and the chunked-SGMV shrink/expand pair are gather fused DPAS kernels. The shrink output layout `(num_tokens, num_slices * max_rank)` is exactly the expand's input, so decode stays on XPU from A to B. The expand fuses per-adapter scaling and the `base_output` residual.
- Supports decode and prefill graph capture (`supports_prefill_cuda_graph = True`, 32 fixed prefill segment slots). Batches with more requests fall back to eager prefill.
- Batch preparation (segment routing, lm_head pruning, graph metadata) follows the triton backend's `LoRABatchInfo` layout.

**Registration and CLI**
- `lora/backend/lora_registry.py`: register `intel_xpu`.
- `arg_groups/choices.py`: add `LORA_BACKEND_CHOICES` (including `intel_xpu`). `arg_groups/fields/lora.py` now reads `--lora-backend` choices from it instead of a hardcoded list, and `server_args.py` re-exports it with the other choice lists.

**Validation**
- `arg_groups/validation_hook.py`: `validate_device_lora_backend` rejects `--lora-backend intel_xpu` without `--device xpu` at argument-check time. Without it, the error only appears later as an import failure inside `LoRAManager` init. This mirrors the existing `--sampling-backend intel_xpu` check.

**Tests**
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: `TestIntelXpuLoRABackend` (CPU CI) checks that the backend is registered and selectable from the CLI, rejected off XPU, and accepted on XPU.
- `test/manual/lora/test_lora_xpu_basics.py`: add `intel_xpu` to `DENSE_BACKENDS`, so it runs the HF+PEFT logprob comparison and the multi-LoRA batching / drainer routing tests next to `triton`, `csgmv`, and `torch_native`.

## Accuracy Tests

Models and adapters are the ones defined for `test/manual/lora/test_lora_backend.py`. Each case runs 4 engines (SRT+LoRA, SRT base, HF+LoRA, HF base) with `--lora-backend intel_xpu` and compares top input/output logprobs against HF plus ROUGE-L of the decoded text. fp16, `max_new_tokens=32`, 2 prompts per case (values are prompt 0 / prompt 1); limits: logprob diff `< 1e-1`, ROUGE-L `1.0`.

| Base model | Adapter | Max prefill logprob diff | Max decode logprob diff | ROUGE-L |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | nvidia/llama-3.1-nemoguard-8b-topic-control | 0.0155 / 0.0339 | 0.0310 / 0.0234 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Llama-2-7b-hf | winddude/wizardLM-LlaMA-LoRA-7B | 0.0161 / 0.0312 | 0.0310 / 0.0312 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | algoprog/fact-generation-llama-3.1-8b-instruct-lora | 0.0177 / 0.0312 | 0.0312 / 0.0301 | 1.0 / 1.0 | 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct

**Setup**
- Model: `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `--tp-size 8` on 8 Intel XPU cards, `--dtype bfloat16`, `--attention-backend triton`, `--disable-radix-cache`, graph capture on.
- LoRA: 4 bf16 adapters (`adamkarvonen/llama3.3_70b_shuffled_e3_v2`, `jeongseokoh/llama3.3_70b_sft`, `jeongseokoh/llama3.3_70b_speed60_bos`, `vineetdaniels/llama33_70b_icd_cpt`), `--max-loras-per-batch 4`, adapters drawn uniformly per request. `base` is the same model served with LoRA disabled.
- Client: SGLang serving benchmark, random dataset with lengths pinned (`--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `ignore_eos` on, so every request emits exactly `output_len` tokens), request rate inf, fixed concurrency. Every run completed all requests with exactly `num_requests * output_len` generated tokens.

**prefill_4k_4lora**: 512 in / 8 out, 128 requests, concurrency 8, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--max-running-requests 8`

| Backend | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | Mean E2E (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base (no LoRA) | 1547.27 | 2014.09 | 2290.23 | 2681.61 |
| `csgmv` | 1145.49 | 2849.50 | 3163.06 | 3618.87 |
| `triton` | 1121.21 | 2915.09 | 3210.81 | 3694.60 |
| `intel_xpu`* | **1295.14** | **2337.53** | **2881.13** | **3203.76** |

`intel_xpu` vs `csgmv`: total throughput +13.1%, mean TTFT -18.0%.

**decode_128_4lora**: 16 in / 64 out, 3000 requests, concurrency 128, `--max-running-requests 128`

| Backend | Total tok/s | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean E2E (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base (no LoRA) | 1273.85 | 1031.98 | 104.67 | 118.98 | 1204.15 | 7798.18 |
| `csgmv` | 833.90 | 675.56 | 163.75 | 178.60 | 1578.59 | 11894.63 |
| `triton` | 796.88 | 645.58 | 172.12 | 184.33 | 1602.02 | 12445.56 |
| `intel_xpu`* | **979.72** | **793.69** | **124.45** | **146.70** | 2299.36 | **10139.78** |

`intel_xpu` vs `csgmv`: total throughput +17.5%, mean TPOT -24.0%.

**mixed_1k_4lora**: 1024 in / 128 out, 400 requests, concurrency 20, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--max-running-requests 20`

| Backend | Total tok/s | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | Mean E2E (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base (no LoRA) | 1150.92 | 127.99 | 7195.63 | 100.81 | 151.64 | 19998.48 |

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Allow memory release with paused grammar compilation
items.author: AnkitNakhawa
items.summary: A retract pause leaves requests whose grammars are still compiling in the grammar queue. The paused scheduler stops polling that queue, but still treats it as active work even with.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44744.

A retract pause leaves requests whose grammars are still compiling in the grammar queue. The paused scheduler stops polling that queue, but `release_memory_occupation` still treats it as active work even with `ignore_waiting=True`. A successful pause can therefore be followed by an assertion that kills the scheduler.

## Modifications

- Treat the grammar queue like the ordinary waiting queue when checking idleness with `ignore_waiting=True`.
- Preserve checks for requests that own KV rows and for outstanding HiCache operations.
- Keep the pending grammar future and request queued so compilation and generation can finish after memory is restored and generation continues.
- Add deterministic CPU regression coverage in the existing registered scheduler test file for the pause/release/resume lifecycle, KV ownership, and outstanding HiCache operations. The three added tests fail against the original code.

### Related work

- #32153 exempts the ordinary waiting queue after a retract pause, but leaves the grammar queue's emptiness requirement unchanged; its tests use an empty grammar queue.
- #36869 refactors idle-check diagnostics and still requires an empty grammar queue.
- #43896 changes request scanning; its current diff also retains the unconditional grammar-queue check.

This PR addresses the remaining grammar-compilation case in #44744. These PRs touch the same scheduler area, but their current changes do not fix this failure.

## Accuracy Tests

### Unit tests

```bash
python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_grammar_manager.py \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_base_grammar_backend.py -q
python test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py -f
```

Results: 98 tests passed, including 27 subtests; the direct CI-style invocation passed all 30 scheduler tests.

Changed production-line coverage: 100% (3 executable lines), exceeding the documented 60% incremental threshold.

### A10 reproduction

Tested on one NVIDIA A10 (23 GB), Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1, FlashInfer 0.7.1, and xgrammar 0.2.7. The original reproduction and GPU validation used the issue's revision, `7224fce1b`, plus this fix; the final branch is based on current main and was checked again with the CPU tests.

Server configuration:
```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --enable-memory-saver --max-total-tokens 6000 --max-running-requests 32
# HiCache variant adds:
# --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through
```

The unmodified revision reproduced the exact `release_memory_occupation should be called only when server is idle` assertion and scheduler exit on the first trial when a test-only hook held grammar compilation open for 500 ms. The hook signals when compilation starts before the client issues the pause; it is not part of the production patch.

After the fix:

| Configuration | Ordinary 5/10 ms pause timing | Compilation held open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without HiCache | 20/20 cycles passed | 20/20 cycles passed |
| HiCache write-through | 20/20 cycles passed | 20/20 cycles passed |

Each cycle exercised generate → retract pause → release memory → restore memory → continue generation. Every control call and resumed generation returned HTTP 200; no scheduler exception occurred.

The issue's 128-token output cap produced length-limited responses in these runs. Five additional bounded-schema cycles per configuration completed with valid JSON (10/10 total), separately checking resumed constrained generation rather than interpreting truncated JSON as a failure.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this changes the paused-engine idleness check, with no model-forward, kernel, or sampling changes. No inference speed or accuracy benchmark claim is made.

## Checklist

- [x] Run the repository's configured pre-commit hooks on both changed files.
- [x] Add focused regression tests to the existing CPU CI-registered test file using `CustomTestCase` and the standard entry point.
- [x] Review documentation applicability: restores the existing pause/release/resume workflow; no API change.
- [x] Review accuracy and speed applicability; lifecycle and constrained-output checks are reported above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style and PR title guidance.

items.title: [MRV2] Collect KV transfer results before the drafter runs
items.author: njhill
items.summary: With a speculator, collect the KV connector's transfer results right after sampling and defer only and until after the drafter, via a new. Finished loads are then reported without waiting for the drafter, and async loads start before it.
items.body:
With a speculator, collect the KV connector's transfer results right after sampling and defer only `wait_for_save()` and `clear_connector_metadata()` until after the drafter, via a new `finalize_step()`. Finished loads are then reported without waiting for the drafter, and async loads start before it.

Note this doesn't involve any changes to the KVConnector interface itself.
