items.title: [Feat] rust-server: Serve /v1/tokenize and /v1/detokenize from the Rust frontend
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Adds /v1/tokenize and /v1/detokenize endpoint support to SGLang's Rust frontend, matching Python's request/response shapes so clients can use these endpoints without falling back to the Python server.
items.body:
## Motivation

The Rust frontend answers 404 on `/v1/tokenize` and `/v1/detokenize`, which Python serves through `OpenAIServingTokenize` and `OpenAIServingDetokenize`. A client that counts tokens before sending a prompt, or decodes ids it received, cannot use a Rust-mode server.

## Modifications

Serve `/v1/tokenize` and `/v1/detokenize`, plus the unversioned `/tokenize` and `/detokenize` aliases, from the Rust frontend with Python's request and response shapes:

- `/v1/tokenize` takes `prompt` (a string or a list of strings) or chat `messages`, and `add_special_tokens` (default true). It returns `tokens`, `count` and `max_model_len`. Messages render through the chat template and encode without auto-added specials, as on the chat path.
- `/v1/detokenize` takes `tokens` (a list, or a list of lists) and `skip_special_tokens` (default true), and returns `text`.
- Errors use Python's flat `ErrorResponse` body. A malformed body, or both or neither of `prompt` and `messages`, is a 400 of type `Bad Request`. A rejected input is a 400 `BadRequestError`; other failures are a 500 `InternalServerError`.

How it is wired:

- Encoding runs on the tokenizer pool as a new `RequestKind::Tokenize`, which the pool answers through the request's own sink with a `ResponseItem::TokenIds`; intake does not register it with a detok shard.
- Decoding reuses the detok shards' `RequestKind::Detokenize`, which now carries `skip_special_tokens`. The `/v1/completions` echo path still decodes with it set.
- `max_model_len` is the Python tokenizer's `model_max_length`, or the context length when that is not a 64-bit integer, derived at launch the way `OpenAIServingTokenize` derives it (the `getattr` mirrors that code; the tokenizer is `None` under `skip_tokenizer_init`) and stamped into the Rust `ServerArgs` as `tokenizer_model_max_length`.
- A dropped tokenize or detokenize call (client gone, or `try_join_all` dropping the rest of a list after one failure) releases only its Rust-side state through a new `AbortSource::Local`. It never reached the scheduler, so it queues no scheduler `AbortReq`; otherwise a cancelled list of thousands of prompts would push thousands of aborts ahead of generation requests.
- `ChatRequest` in `openai/chat.rs` becomes `pub(super)` so the tokenize route can render `messages` with the same parser; its PD routing fields are accepted and ignored there.

Differences from Python, on purpose:

- Negative token ids are a 400 here (validated before decoding); Python fails inside the tokenizer with a 500.
- Media in `messages` is rejected, as on the Rust chat route.

This PR is independent of #44533 and #44532: it touches neighbouring lines of `ServerArgs` and `rust_server/config.py` but shares no hunk with either.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the new routes do not sit on the generation path. The only change on it is one extra `bool` on the `Detokenize` message.

## Test plan

- `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`: 335 passed. The one failure, `chunk_event_frame_stays_small`, fails identically on untouched `main` on this aarch64 machine (`ChunkEvent` is 152 bytes there against a 144-byte ceiling) and is unrelated to this change.
  - New: `tokenize_answers_through_the_sink_without_returning_to_intake`, `tokenize_goes_to_the_pool_without_detok_registration`, `tokenize_returns_python_response_shape`, `detokenize_returns_python_response_shape`, `invalid_requests_get_the_flat_python_error`, `token_operations_mint_internal_rids`; `every_abort_source_deregisters_and_stops_the_scheduler` now also covers `AbortSource::Local` pushing no scheduler abort.
- Python: `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 23 passed, including the new `test_tokenizer_model_max_length_matches_python_tokenize` (no tokenizer, no attribute, configured value, HF's `int(1e30)` unset sentinel).
- Lint: isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 (`check` and `format`), codespell 2.4.1 clean on the touched files.
- Not run here: an end-to-end server. The routes were exercised against a Rust-mode and a Python-mode server with the same small instruct model and matched status and body for string and list prompts with and without `add_special_tokens`, `""`, `[]`, `messages` with and without a system message, the aliases, nested token lists, `skip_special_tokens` true and false, `[[9906], []]`, and the malformed bodies listed above (same `object`, `type` and `code`; the messages differ, serde's text against pydantic's).

items.title: [Feat] sglang-server: Serve /flush_cache from the Rust frontend
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Implements the missing /flush_cache HTTP endpoint in sglang's Rust frontend to match Python frontend parity for cache flushing during benchmarks.
items.body:
## Motivation

A server running the Rust frontend answers 404 on `/flush_cache`, so a
client that clears the prefix cache between benchmark or evaluation phases
(`POST /flush_cache?timeout=30` on every engine) fails against it. The
Python frontend has served this route for a long time, and the
scheduler-side handler (`SchedulerFlushWrapper`) already runs whichever
frontend is in use; only the HTTP route and its control request were
missing on the Rust side.

A second gap sits behind the first. A flush that has to wait for running
requests (`timeout > 0` on a busy server) is answered later, from
`SchedulerFlushWrapper.check_pending`, and that deferred reply went
straight to the zmq tokenizer socket. In Rust mode nothing reads that
socket, so the HTTP call would never return.

## Modifications

- `rust/sglang-server/src/message/io_struct.rs`: add the `FlushCacheReqInput`
  control message with the same positional wire layout as the Python
  msgspec struct: `[tag, rid, http_worker_ipc, timeout_s]`.
- `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/core/handle.rs`: `CoreHandle::flush_cache`
  sends that request through the existing control path and decodes the
  scheduler's `FlushCacheReqOutput` (`success`, `message`).
- `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/info.rs`: route `GET|POST
  /flush_cache?timeout=<s>` with the Python contract: 200 and Python's
  plain-text `Cache flushed. ...` body once flushed; otherwise 400 with the
  scheduler's reason, or `Flush cache failed.` when it gave none. No content
  type, like Python's bare `Response`. A negative `timeout` is a 400 before
  anything reaches the scheduler.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: the control-reply branch of
  `process_input_requests` becomes `Scheduler.send_control_output`, which
  takes the embedded Rust server's egress ring when there is one and the
  tokenizer socket otherwise. Behaviour at dispatch time is unchanged.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/flush_wrapper.py`: the
  wrapper takes a `send_output` callable instead of the IPC channels and
  answers a deferred flush through it, so the reply follows the same path
  as every other control reply.

Python's `TokenizerManager.flush_cache` also clears the multimodal
processor's preprocessing cache; the Rust multimodal pipeline keeps no such
cache, so there is nothing to clear there.

Tests:
- `flush_cache_relays_the_scheduler_outcome` (Rust): `GET` and `POST` send
  one `FlushCacheReqInput` carrying the query timeout, then answer 200 with
  Python's text, 400 with the scheduler's message, or 400
  `Flush cache failed.`, with no content type; a negative timeout never
  reaches the scheduler.
- `flush_cache_req_msgpack_shape` (Rust): pins the four-element wire array.
- `test_scheduler_flush_cache.py`: the existing wrapper tests now check the
  `send_output` callable, and
  `test_control_output_goes_to_the_embedded_rust_server` pins the deferred
  reply's routing (Rust egress ring when a Rust server is embedded, tokenizer
  socket otherwise).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: a control route; no model forward or sampling change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no change on the generation path.

Validation run locally in `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and
`cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`: 332 passed, including the two new
tests; the one failure, `chunk_event_frame_stays_small`, fails identically
on untouched `main` on this aarch64 host (a `size_of::<ChunkEvent>()` bound)
and is unrelated to this change. `python -m pytest
test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_flush_cache.py`: 8 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

items.title: [Fix] openai: Enforce --trust-request-chat-template on responses, decisions and systemone
items.author: MrAnayDongre
items.summary: is off by default, so a request can't swap the server's chat template by sending in (#28135). That check only lives in, so it only covers the routes that go through it.
items.body:
## Motivation

`--trust-request-chat-template` is off by default, so a request can't swap the server's chat template by sending `chat_template` in `chat_template_kwargs` (#28135). That check only lives in `OpenAIServingChat._validate_request`, so it only covers the routes that go through it. `/v1/responses`, `/v1/decisions` and `/v1/systemone` also take `chat_template_kwargs` and hand it straight to `apply_chat_template(**kwargs)`, so on a default server the override went through on all three.

I hit this on `/v1/responses` first and then went looking for other routes with the same field. `/v1/messages` doesn't have the field in its schema, so it isn't affected.

## Modifications

- Moved the check into `OpenAIServingBase._request_chat_template_error`. The chat route uses it with the same behavior as before.
- `create_responses`, `OpenAIServingDecisions._validate_request` and `SystemOneServing._validate_request` now call it and return a 400.
- One rejection test per route, added to the existing test files. The image-marker test in `test_serving_decisions.py` sends a request `chat_template` on purpose, so I set `trust_request_chat_template=True` there.

Checked on a live server (Qwen3-0.6B), sending `{"chat_template": ...}` with the default flags:

| route | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 400 | 400 |
| `/v1/tokenize` | 400 | 400 |
| `/v1/responses` | 200, template applied | 400 |
| `/v1/decisions` | template applied | 400 |
| `/v1/systemone` | template applied | 400 |

With `--trust-request-chat-template` the override is still accepted everywhere, and ordinary kwargs like `enable_thinking` work the same on every route.

One behavior change to be aware of: a Harmony request that includes `chat_template` now gets the 400 too, where before the value was silently ignored. I haven't run a Harmony model.

If you'd rather keep this to `/v1/responses` and handle decisions/systemone separately, I'm happy to split it.

cc @JustinTong0323 @Sunt-ing

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, no change to model outputs.

items.title: [Feat] rust-server: Report Python's launch-time /server_info fields from the Rust frontend
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Aligns the Rust frontend /server_info endpoint with Python's by exposing launch-time fields (server_args, launch_command, kv_events, startup timings) so clients reading those keys work in Rust mode.
items.body:
## Motivation

Python's `/server_info` returns every resolved `server_args` field, `launch_command`, the scheduler's init info, `kv_events` and the startup timings. The Rust frontend returned an allowlisted handful, so a client that reads launch configuration off `/server_info` (for example `load_format` or `startup_time`) fails with a missing key as soon as the server runs in Rust mode.

## Modifications

- At launch the scheduler hands the Rust server the `/server_info` fields that are fixed by then, as one JSON snapshot built with Python's own `build_server_info` and redacted with the same `redact_watermark_secrets` the HTTP and gRPC frontends apply: the resolved `server_args`, `launch_command`, `kv_events`, and `status`, `max_total_num_tokens` and `max_req_input_len` (`rust_server/config.py`, `_launch_server_info`; carried as a new `launch_server_info` field of the typed `ServerArgs` handoff, extracted into a `LaunchServerInfo` JSON object).
- The Rust `/server_info` reports the snapshot beneath its runtime fields, which take precedence on a shared key, so the key set matches Python's apart from Rust's own `max_context_length`. The scheduler's internal state in `internal_states` keeps its existing allowlist. The native gRPC `GetServerInfo` is unchanged.
- `enable_http2` is reported false whatever the flag says: the Rust listener is HTTP/1 only and a router reads that key to pick its protocol.
- `startup_time` takes Python's engine-level shape (`load_weight`, `kv_cache_allocation`, `scheduler_e2e`, `cuda_graph`, `tokenizer_e2e`). Python's `tokenizer_e2e` runs from launch until the schedulers are ready; the Rust frontend serves from inside the scheduler process, so its phase runs from that process's spawn until initialization ends. The scheduler records it once initialization ends (`RustServer.set_startup_time`), it reaches Rust through the internal state `/server_info` already requests (`rust_server_startup_time`), and the HTTP response lifts it to the top level.
- Not covered: `tokenizer_path` stays the Rust server's own value, `kv_event_sources` (native gRPC only) is only known after the Rust server starts, and the timings are those of the scheduler hosting the listener rather than a maximum over every rank.

Tests:
- `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean; `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`: 330 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `message::response::tests::chunk_event_frame_stays_small`, a `size_of::<ChunkEvent>()` bound this branch does not touch; it fails identically on a clean checkout of `main` on the aarch64 host the tests ran on.
  - `server_info_route_serializes_only_the_typed_public_subset` (extended): the launch fields come first in order, a runtime field replaces a launch field in place, the internal state's startup timings move to the top-level `startup_time`, and the internal-state allowlist still drops `api_key`.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_server_info.py` (`test_http_and_both_grpc_roles_share_startup_metadata` now also checks that the Rust snapshot equals the gRPC leader's startup metadata apart from the two stamped init-info keys, and that it reports `enable_http2` false for a server launched with `--enable-http2`), `test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py` (new `test_startup_time_takes_the_engine_shape`) and `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 53 passed, 14 subtests.
- `pre-commit` (isort, ruff format, codespell, whitespace) passes on the changed Python files.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model execution.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: `/server_info` only. The snapshot is built once at launch and cloned per request.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep a full uniform-decode batch reachable by FULL graphs
items.author: abmfy
items.summary: Fixes CUDA graph capture skip in uniform-decode batches when query length doesn't divide capture sizes, forcing eager draft execution instead of using FULL graphs.
items.body:
## Overview

A full `max_num_seqs` uniform-decode batch can end up with no FULL CUDA graph when the manager's query length does not divide the capture sizes. The DSpark draft (`sample_from_anchor`) decodes `num_speculative_tokens` tokens per request, but the default sizes follow the target's `1 + num_speculative_tokens` (#50488). With `max_num_seqs=72` and 5 draft tokens:

- 352 rounds up to 355, which is 71 requests;
- 368 rounds up to 370, which is 74 requests, so it is skipped;
- every full-batch step therefore runs the draft eagerly.

This PR clamps the rounded size to `max_num_seqs * query_len` for managers with a single query length.

Not a duplicate:
- No open or merged PR changes this skip. The new test fails on main, on main + #56136 and on main + #61882.
- #61882 refactors the same loop. It is a textual conflict only, with no behavior overlap.
- #56136 changes the candidate ladders in the same function. It is orthogonal and applies cleanly together with this PR.
- #50488, #53407 and #57355 fixed other "batch has no graph" cases: the target's sizes, padding up, and q=1 respectively.

## Claims

- On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark and `max_num_seqs=72`, a full batch's draft now runs from its FULL graph instead of eagerly. Decode throughput rises +4.4% at DEP4 on main.
- Dynamic speculative decoding (several query lengths) is unchanged. Clamping there would add graphs for tiers that never reach a full batch, and those graphs would shadow other tiers' FULL graphs.
- Each affected manager gains at most one FULL graph, plus its LoRA and DBO variants. The graph is added only when the full batch was unreachable.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py` on GB200: 30 passed. On main, 29 passed and the new test fails.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB200 node:
  - Config: DEP4, default MoE backend (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`), DSpark with 5 tokens, `max_num_seqs=72`.
  - Load: 288 requests, 72 pinned to each DP rank. Each has a ~1k-token prompt and 14k output tokens (`ignore_eos`, temperature 0).
  - Throughput is measured over 30 s while all 288 requests are decoding. Main and this PR ran interleaved, two rounds each.

  | | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | Decode throughput, rounds 1 / 2 (tok/s) | 62,752 / 60,899 | 64,586 / 64,528 |
  | Draft acceptance rate | 0.988 / 0.988 | 0.987 / 0.987 |
  | DSpark FULL graphs captured | 40 | 41 |
  | Draft kernels in a 4 s CUDA profile | eager (graph id 0) | in their own graph |

  - Throughput is +4.4%, and every PR round is above every main round.
  - The profile also shows decode steps at 40.6 ms on main vs 26.8 ms with this PR. The profiler inflates the cost of each eager launch, so treat that ratio as qualitative only.

- Host time per decode step, on a downstream branch with the same `CudaGraphManager` code: DEP16, 72 requests per rank, steady state, 2000-step windows.

  | | main logic | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | Full-batch draft dispatches that ran eager | ~80% | 0% |
  | `propose` (host) | 9.7 ms | 0.4 ms |
  | `sample_tokens` (host) | 11.0 ms | 1.6 ms |
  | Host slack per step | 7.5 ms | 17.4 ms |
  | Step time | 24.2 ms | 24.2 ms |

  At DEP16 the step is GPU-bound, so its step time does not change; the freed host time only shows up where the host is on the critical path, as at DEP4 above.

## Details

- The clamp leaves the existing `max_decode_tokens` and `max_num_reqs` checks in place. Those checks still drop oversize sizes for dynamic speculative decoding.
- #61869 copies the old rounding rule into `AttnMetadataCudaGraphs.capture_keys` for the target's query length. That copy may want the same treatment once both PRs land.

items.title: [Feat] dwdp: Support MTP speculative decoding on DWDP prefill
items.author: QNan0513
items.summary: rejects every, so a DWDP prefill server cannot run an MTP draft. MTP can still be enabled on the decode server alone, but then decode gets neither the draft KV of the prompt nor the first-step draft input (top-k and hidden state), which the prefill server nor…
items.body:
## Motivation

`handle_dwdp` rejects every `--speculative-algorithm`, so a DWDP prefill server cannot run an MTP draft. MTP can still be enabled on the decode server alone, but then decode gets neither the draft KV of the prompt nor the first-step draft input (top-k and hidden state), which the prefill server normally produces with its draft extend. That costs accept length, mostly at short outputs, where the first decode round has no draft input. With DWDP8 prefill, GLM-5.3-Flash gets 1.81 instead of 2.95 at 8 output tokens and 3.92 instead of 4.53 at 1024; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next gets 1.87 instead of 2.37 and 2.64 instead of 2.67; MiMo-V2-Flash gets 1.41 instead of 1.70 and 2.76 either way (tables below).

Letting the prefill server run the draft takes more than dropping the assert:

1. **The MTP layer's MoE is computed from 1/N of the routed experts.** Under DWDP, sparse MoE runs on DP-local tokens and `post_experts_output_is_complete()` is True, so no sum follows the experts. The target's MoE layers still see every expert through the prefetch pipeline. The draft runner, however, returns early from `maybe_init_dwdp`, so the draft's `FusedMoE` keeps its EP shard (36 of 288 experts for GLM-5.3-Flash on DWDP8) and silently drops the other experts' contributions.
2. **Draft forwards trigger the target's prefetch.** `ModelRunner.forward` calls the global manager's `prefetch_first_layers()` for every runner, so each draft forward copies the target's first two MoE layers from peers (~12 GiB of NVLink traffic for GLM-5.3-Flash) that no forward consumes.

Related:
- #22084 tracks DWDP. #29778 added DWDP for MoE prefill together with the `handle_dwdp` check ("DWDP does not support speculative decoding") that this PR relaxes.
- #39802 (open) fixes the same mn-major scale layout in the target's `_allgather_small_params` that `_all_gather_experts` keeps here. The two PRs change different functions in `dwdp_manager.py`, and #39802's diff applies cleanly on top of this one. Once both land, the two gathers could share one helper.
- I found no open PR on DWDP with speculative decoding.

cc @yhyang201, who added DWDP and this check in #29778.

## Modifications

- `dwdp_manager.replicate_routed_experts(model)`: for every EP-sharded `FusedMoE` in `model`, all-gathers `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` and the expert-sharded side tensors (`named_per_expert_tensors`, e.g. quant scales) over the MoE EP group, then binds them with EP collapsed to 1. The gather runs in memory order, so a permuted layout such as DeepGEMM's mn-major scales keeps its strides. Fused shared experts raise `NotImplementedError`.
- `FusedMoE.bind_full_expert_weights(..., *, prefetched=True)`: `prefetched=False` keeps a fully resident layer out of DWDP's `wait_prefetch` / `record_compute_and_prefetch_next` hooks. The DWDP manager's call is unchanged.
- `ModelRunner`:
  - `maybe_init_dwdp`: the draft runner calls `replicate_routed_experts(self.model)` instead of returning.
  - `forward`: skips `prefetch_first_layers()` on the draft runner.
- `handle_dwdp`: accepts `EAGLE` / `NEXTN` on `--disaggregation-mode prefill`. Other algorithms and null mode are still rejected (see "Why prefill only" below).
- Tests (CPU, both fail before this change):
  - `test_moe_runner_config_placement.py`: replication gathers weights and scales in global expert order and in their memory layout (an mn-major scale keeps its strides), collapses EP and leaves the layer out of the prefetch.
  - `test_server_args.py`: `handle_dwdp` accepts EAGLE/NEXTN on prefill and rejects EAGLE3, DSPARK and null mode.

Cost: one MoE layer's experts per draft layer. For GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8, 288 experts) that is ~6.75 GiB per rank instead of the ~0.84 GiB EP shard. The draft weights are counted in the KV budget, so in the setup below the prefill KV pool went from 1,048,576 (the `--max-total-tokens` cap) to 419,840 tokens per rank. For Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (FP8, 512 experts) it is ~2.34 GiB instead of ~0.29 GiB, and the KV pool stayed at the cap.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup:
- GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8), PD over two 8x H20 nodes, mooncake over RoCE.
- Prefill: `--tp-size 8 --dwdp-size 8 --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --load-balance-method total_tokens --mm-enable-dp-encoder`.
- Decode: TP8.
- MTP on both sides: `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`.
- Image: nightly 2026-10-14 (684fea8a). Its DWDP files and the touched `fused_moe_triton/layer.py` are byte-identical to `main` 4e85e8e, and the `model_runner.py` / `parallel_hook.py` hunks match. This change was mounted on the prefill side. Two sessions: the first predates the prefill-only condition in `handle_dwdp` (its runs satisfy it), the second ran the final version of this change.
- GLM-5.3-Flash under DWDP also needs the shared-expert TP1 condition from #39802, which is mounted in every DWDP run here and is not part of this PR.

GSM8K (20-shot, 200 questions) and a ~53k-token needle test (16 prompts), through the router:

| Prefill | GSM8K | Needle |
|---|---|---|
| DWDP8, no MTP | 0.940 / 0.960 | 15/16 |
| DWDP8, MTP on decode only | 0.965 / 0.960 | - |
| DWDP8 + MTP (this PR) | 0.955 / 0.955 / 0.955 | 13/16 |
| DWDP8 + MTP, assert dropped only | 0.940 / 0.945 / 0.960 | - |
| TP8 + MTP | 0.950 / 0.940 / 0.955 | 15/16 |

Up to three runs per row for GSM8K, one for the needle test. Every needle miss is a refusal: the model treats the planted code as an injected instruction, and the missed depths differ between runs.

Accept length per stage (ShareGPT text truncated to exact lengths). The decode server is flushed before each stage, which resets its speculative counters, and its `avg_spec_accept_length` is read afterwards; `bench_serving` alone prints the average since the decode server started. Second session:

| Prefill | GSM8K | p64k (48 x 64k, out 8) | p2k (200 x 2k, out 8) | d2k (200 x 2k, out 1024) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 + MTP | 3.76 | 2.10 | 2.99 | 4.53 |
| DWDP8, MTP on decode only | 3.29 | 1.66 | 1.81 | 3.92 |
| DWDP8 + MTP (this PR) | 3.80 | 2.13 | 2.95 | 4.53 |
| DWDP8 + MTP, assert dropped only | 3.75 | 2.12 | 2.94 | 4.51 |

MTP on decode only loses 22-39% at 8 output tokens, where the first decode round has no draft input, and still 13% at 1024 and on GSM8K. Most of the gain comes from the prefill server running the draft at all: dropping the assert alone stays within 1.3% of this PR in PD. The MTP layer's attention runs before its MoE, so the draft KV that prefill ships is correct either way; only the first decode round's draft input comes from the partial expert sum, and decode runs every later draft step itself with all experts. The assert-only build still computes that input from 1/8 of the experts and pulls the target's prefetch on every draft forward.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (FP8, `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`; 512 routed experts, top-10, plus a shared expert) is a second MoE MTP model, built from different model code: its one MTP layer is a full-attention layer with a `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock`. `replicate_routed_experts` gathers all 512 experts of `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts`. Both sessions used the final version of this change.
- Spec flags: `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`.
- Model flags, as in the cookbook's FP8 config: `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer --linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer --linear-attn-verify-backend triton --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`. Same nodes, image and harness as above.
- Decode and the non-DWDP prefill use TP8 with `--ep-size 8`: the FP8 128x128 weight blocks cannot split the 640-wide experts 8 ways.
- The DWDP prefill sets `SGLANG_USE_ATTN_TP_NGRAM=1`. Without it the model's n-gram embedding refuses to start under DWDP's DP attention.
- Under DWDP, `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` keeps the shared expert TP-sharded (it is replicated only with an a2a backend), the same problem #39802 fixes for DeepSeek-V2. A one-line local fix is mounted in every DWDP run here and is not part of this PR.
- GSM8K uses the chat API, 5-shot, thinking disabled, 200 questions. With the 20-shot completion prompt the model stops after one token.

First / second session; accept length per stage, from the second session:

| Prefill | GSM8K | Accept GSM8K / p64k / p2k / d2k | p64k input tok/s | p2k input tok/s | d2k output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DWDP8, no MTP | 0.980 | - | 52,738 | 56,889 | 2,391 |
| DWDP8, MTP on decode only | 0.990 / 0.990 | 3.30 / 2.11 / 1.87 / 2.64 | 60,090 / 52,434 | 57,874 / 56,214 | 3,249 / 3,253 |
| DWDP8 + MTP (this PR) | 0.990 / 0.990 | 3.55 / 2.76 / 2.37 / 2.67 | 57,349 / 65,018 | 53,765 / 54,833 | 3,220 / 3,333 |
| TP8 / EP8 + MTP | 0.980 / 0.980 | 3.51 / 2.80 / 2.39 / 2.70 | 20,755 / 20,816 | 22,504 / 22,528 | 3,349 / 3,314 |

- Accept length matches the non-DWDP prefill within 1.5% on every stage, and DWDP keeps 2.4-3.1x its prefill throughput.
- MTP on decode only loses 21-24% at 8 output tokens and 7% on GSM8K, but only 1% at 1024, so d2k output throughput is about the same (3,220 / 3,333 vs 3,249 / 3,253 tok/s). The missing prompt draft KV matters much less here than for GLM.
- The draft extend adds ~4% to the prefill time of a 64k request (8.10 → 8.40 / 8.43 s in the prefill server's `ReqTimeStats`). The p64k input throughput is set by the busiest DP rank and differs by 13-15% between sessions of the same config. At 2k, prefill with the draft is 2-7% below the arms without one.

### MiMo-V2-Flash

MiMo-V2-Flash (FP8, 256 routed experts, no shared experts) has three dense MTP layers, so `replicate_routed_experts` has nothing to gather. The run covers the rest of the change, with several draft runners under multi-layer EAGLE.
- Spec flags, as in `test_mimo_v2_flash.py`: `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --enable-multi-layer-eagle`.
- Model flags: `--attention-backend fa3 --page-size 64`. Same nodes and harness as above.
- Decode and the non-DWDP prefill use `--attn-dp-size 8` (attention TP 1, as on a DWDP prefill). MiMo's FP8 QKV block scales cannot be split for attention TP 8. Also, decode at attention TP 2 behind a DWDP prefill returned garbage (GSM8K 0.000) with or without MTP, and matching the attention TP avoided it.

First / second session; accept length per stage from the second session, averaged over the decode server's 8 DP ranks:

| Prefill | GSM8K | Accept GSM8K / p64k / p2k / d2k | p64k input tok/s | p2k input tok/s | d2k output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DWDP8, no MTP | 0.705 | - | - | 27,103 | - |
| DWDP8, MTP on decode only | 0.695 / 0.700 | 2.90 / 1.41 / 1.41 / 2.76 | 27,124 / 27,155 | 27,772 / 26,654 | 4,555 / 4,585 |
| DWDP8 + MTP (this PR) | 0.750 / 0.730 | 2.95 / 1.73 / 1.70 / 2.76 | 26,111 / 29,414 | 28,798 / 30,064 | 4,584 / 4,529 |
| Attention DP 8 + MTP | 0.700 / 0.725 | 2.94 / 1.75 / 1.67 / 2.79 | 12,480 / 12,721 | 24,727 / 25,746 | 4,680 / 4,807 |

Accept length matches the non-DWDP prefill within 2%, and DWDP keeps 2.1-2.3x its 64k prefill throughput. MiMo's MTP layers attend over a 128-token window, so the prompt's draft KV stops mattering after the first decode steps: MTP on decode only loses 17-19% at 8 output tokens and nothing at 1024.

### Why prefill only

DWDP also allows `--disaggregation-mode null`. There the draft runs decode steps too, and under DWDP they run eagerly. In those steps every row of the draft MoE input arrives masked as padding: on a 1-row draft batch, 8 of 8 expert ids were -1.

- With this PR, the replicated layer's Triton runner treats every id as local (`filter_expert` is off once `num_local_experts == num_experts`). It faults with an illegal memory access in `invoke_fused_moe_kernel`.
- With the assert dropped only, the EP-sharded layer filters the -1 ids, so its draft decode steps compute no routed experts at all. It still reached accept length 4.25 and GSM8K (100 questions) 0.970.
- DWDP null mode without speculative decoding is unaffected: the target's decode batches carry the right non-padded count.

Fixing the draft-decode padding count is a separate change, so this PR enables speculative decoding only on PD prefill servers, where the draft only runs extend.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GLM-5.3-Flash, same setup, first / second session:

| Prefill | p64k input tok/s | Prefill time per 64k request | p2k input tok/s | d2k output tok/s | d2k mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DWDP8, no MTP | 30,429 | 14.64 s | 29,514 | 1,842 | 28.9 ms |
| DWDP8, MTP on decode only | - / 35,054 | - / 14.64 s | 29,672 / 28,978 | 3,060 / 3,056 | 16.5 / 16.4 ms |
| DWDP8 + MTP (this PR) | 29,341 / 29,388 | 15.04 / 15.07 s | 29,677 / 28,393 | 3,375 / 3,605 | 14.5 / 13.7 ms |
| TP8 + MTP | 13,435 / 13,431 | - | 20,043 / 20,045 | 3,796 / 3,791 | 13.4 / 13.6 ms |

- With this PR a DWDP prefill node keeps 2.2x TP8's prefill throughput at 64k and 1.4-1.5x at 2k, and runs the draft for decode. At d2k that gives 10% / 18% more output throughput than MTP on decode only (TPOT 16.5 → 14.5 ms and 16.4 → 13.7 ms), and 83% more than no MTP.
- The draft extend adds 2.8% to the prefill time of a 64k request (14.64 → 15.04 / 15.07 s; 14.96 s with the assert dropped only). This is the prefill server's `ReqTimeStats` forward duration minus the KV transfer tail. The p64k throughput itself is set by the busiest DP rank: with 48 requests on 8 ranks, a session in which one rank serves 7 of them instead of 6 takes ~1/6 longer, which is why the decode-only row reached 35.1k in the second session.
- With short prompts at c64, TP8 prefill still gives lower TTFT (d2k mean / median 1.39 / 0.39 s vs 2.49 / 1.50 s with this PR). DWDP runs one prefill per rank, which is the existing DWDP trade-off and is unchanged here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Ran ruff 0.15.1 (check + format), isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` and `check_registered_tests.py` on the changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Also re-ran the full `test_server_args.py`, `test_moe_runner_config_placement.py`, `test_resolution_declarations.py`, `test_moe_output_reduction.py`, `test_runtime_context.py` and `test_moe_runner_extensions.py`; all pass.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Not covered: null mode (rejected, see above), B200 / the FABRIC handle path (H20 falls back to POSIX fd), and a GPU CI test. The existing DWDP CI test uses gpt-oss-120b, which has no MTP layer.

items.title: [CI] Shard E2E Scheduling, Benchmarks CLI and six AMD mirrors automatically
items.author: Thangnguyenvn98
items.summary: Turns on for two long NVIDIA steps and six AMD mirrors that run longer than 20 minutes as one job. Picked by p90 duration over the last day on main. [Discussion: ✅ Triggered for commit.]
items.body:
## Overview

Turns on `automatic_shard` for two long NVIDIA steps and six AMD mirrors that run longer than 20 minutes as one job. Picked by p90 duration over the last day on main. Only the flag changes; no commands or tests change.

## Claims

- Each step below runs as parallel jobs planned from main's per-file timings, and each job runs only its share of the tests:

| Step | Command shape | Planned shards |
|---|---|---:|
| `e2e-scheduling-1-gpu` | one `pytest` file, split by test | 2 |
| `amd-e2e-scheduling-1-gpu` (mirror) | same | 2 |
| `benchmarks-cli-test` | one `pytest` over `benchmarks/` | 2 |
| `amd-kernels-root-misc-test-b200` (mirror) | one `pytest` over a list of kernel test files, with `--deselect` | 2 |
| `amd-spec-decode-eagle-nightly-b200` (optional mirror) | one `pytest` over a directory; its large file is split by test | 2 |
| `amd-spec-decode-speculators-mtp-nightly-b200` (optional mirror) | two `pytest` commands over directories | 2 |
| `amd-lm-eval-large-models-ep-2xb200` (optional mirror) | `export` setup, then `pytest` on the gsm8k eval with `--config-list-file`, split by test | 2 |
| `amd-lm-eval-large-models-4xh100` (optional mirror) | `export` setup, then `pytest` on the lm-eval harness test with `--config-list-file` and `--tp-size`, split by test | 2 |

- `kernels-root-misc-test-b200`, `spec-decode-eagle-nightly-b200` and `spec-decode-speculators-mtp-nightly-b200` are enrolled so their mirrors can shard (a mirror shards only when its base step is enrolled). Their own runs plan to one shard, so they stay one job.
- Every test runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment as the single job. If planning fails, the step runs as one job, as it does today.

## Validation

- Planned each step on this branch with ci-infra's `runtime_shard.plan_step`, using main's timings on the step's own queue.
- Rendered each step with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper. Every test ran in exactly one shard, with the same env. The three single-shard base steps were confirmed to stay one job.
- `/ci run` exercises E2E Scheduling, Benchmarks CLI and the E2E Scheduling and Miscellaneous Kernels mirrors. The four optional mirrors need a build scoped to their keys.

## Details

- **Uneven or tight plans.** `amd-lm-eval-large-models-ep-2xb200`'s planner output is marked over budget: one eval test takes most of 20 minutes by itself, so its slowest shard sits near the target.
- **Left out.**
  - `language-models-test-extended-generation` and its mirror: each job first builds mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d from source, which every shard would repeat. They wait for #58795, which prebuilds both in the test image.
  - `entrypoints-integration-api-server-generate`'s mirror: two of its files assert on `caplog`, the pattern that took `entrypoints-integration-multimodal` out of sharding.
  - `benchmarks-cli-test`'s mirror runs under 20 minutes, so it stays one job.
  - Long steps whose commands aren't plain pytest (PyTorch Fullgraph, NixlConnector PD accuracy, Examples, Spec Decode MTP + Other) can't be planned.
- **Where to look.** The `automatic_shard: true` lines in `.buildkite/test_areas/{engine,benchmarks,kernels,spec_decode,lm_eval}.yaml`.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject NaN logit_bias values instead of banning the token
items.author: vineethsaivs
items.summary: NaN values in logit_bias were silently clamped to -100 (banning tokens) due to NaN comparison semantics; this PR adds explicit NaN validation to reject invalid inputs with VLLMValidationError.
items.body:
## Overview

A NaN value in `logit_bias` is clamped to -100 and silently bans the token, instead of being rejected.

## Claims

- `SamplingParams.from_optional` raises a validation error (`parameter="logit_bias"`) when any bias is NaN.
- Finite and infinite values behave as before: they are clamped to [-100, 100].

## Validation

`tests/test_sampling_params.py` (2 new tests):

```
pytest tests/test_sampling_params.py
  main:        2 failed, 62 passed
  this branch: 64 passed
```

Also, on main a JSON body with `"logit_bias": {"5": NaN}` parsed into `ChatCompletionRequest` gives `to_sampling_params(...).logit_bias == {5: -100.0}`; on this branch it raises `VLLMValidationError`. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files. I ran the tests on CPU with the xgrammar import stubbed. I did not run a live server, so the HTTP path is checked at the request-model level only. Model evaluation does not apply: no sampling math changes for valid input.

## Details

`min(100.0, max(-100.0, bias))` returns -100.0 for NaN because every comparison with NaN is false. Python's JSON parser accepts the `NaN` literal and pydantic accepts it for `float`, so a request can reach this. The clamp now goes through one helper used by both the fast path and the non-integer-key path in `from_optional`.

Not a duplicate: open PRs and issues searched for `logit_bias` with NaN, non-finite, validation and clamp. #52686 (tests) and #55164 (size limit) do not touch NaN; #46612 (non-integer keys) is merged.

items.title: [None][feat] Visual Gen token-sharded TP: gather FP8 block-scale inputs
items.author: chang-l
items.summary: Follow-up to #19713 (token-sharded TP, merged). This is the same change as chang-l#9, rebased onto as one clean cherry-pick (no conflicts; the only differences to that PR's head are main's own changes to the two touched files, the attention import path and the…
items.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #19713 (token-sharded TP, merged). This is the same change as chang-l#9, rebased onto `main` as one clean cherry-pick (no conflicts; the only differences to that PR's head are main's own changes to the two touched files, the attention import path and the doc section).

Token-sharded TP all-gathers each column projection's input between blocks. Today that gather is BF16 unless the consumer has a static NVFP4 input scale. For an `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` `Linear` on the DeepGEMM path (SM100 family, no CuTe DSL / `disable_deep_gemm`, `K % 128 == 0`) the consumer quantizes its bf16 input per token with 1x128 UE8M0 block scales. That quantize is row-local, so each rank can quantize its own rows before the gather and move FP8 plus packed scales (half the BF16 bytes) while the GEMM sees exactly the bytes it would have produced on all rows.

```text
TokenShardedColumn.forward / TokenShardedMLP.forward
  tp.gather_input(consumer, x_loc [m, K] bf16)
    static_nvfp4_input_scale(consumer)?        -> NVFP4 gather (unchanged)
    fp8_block_scale_prequant_ok(consumer)?     -> NEW
      quantize_fp8_block(x_loc)                   # trtllm::fp8_quantize_1x128_packed_ue8m0, the Linear's own CUDA quantizer
      all_gather(payload as bytes, scales as rows); drop per-sample padding from both
      fp8_scales_mn_major(...)                    # (M, K/512) int32, strides (1, pad4(M)) as DeepGEMM reads them
      -> Fp8BlockScaledActivation(fp8 [B*S, K], scales)
    else                                       -> BF16 gather (unchanged)
  super().forward(...)                         # FP8BlockScalesLinearMethod.apply's existing pre-quantized path:
                                               # fp8_prequantized_swap_ab_gemm -> the same deep_gemm.fp8_gemm_nt call
```

`fp8_block_scale_prequant_ok` mirrors `FP8BlockScalesLinearMethod.apply`'s own dispatch and is decided per call (the quant method is final only after loading), after the static-NVFP4 rule. A LoRA is not part of the rule: `MLP` attaches a `LoraLayer` to its projections whether or not adapters are loaded, so the adapters keep the input bf16 only for a call that passes `lora_params`. An FP8 pair reaching a consumer the rule rejects raises before any collective; a bare tuple is rejected so an FP8 pair cannot be mistaken for an NVFP4 one.

`TokenShardPlan.build` / `TokenShardedTP` also take `row_align` (default 1 reproduces today's plans field for field; 4 removes the quantizer's per-rank scale pad rows). Constructor argument only, no config field; the served path keeps 1.

It deliberately does not fuse the gather into the GEMM; overlap is a later, kernel-free step (copy-engine per-source pipelines on the symmetric-memory pool of #20308).

```text
tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/parallel/
├── token_sharded_tp.py          # Fp8BlockScaledActivation, fp8_block_scale_prequant_ok, quantize_fp8_block,
│                                #   fp8_scales_mn_major, FP8 branch of gather_input / all_gather, row_align
└── token_sharded_modules.py     # gather-dtype rule in the adapter docstrings
docs/source/models/visual-generation.md                       # one sentence on the gather dtype per checkpoint kind
tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/
├── test_token_sharded_tp.py                                  # CPU
├── token_sharded_tp_test_utils.py
└── multi_gpu/test_token_sharded_tp_collectives.py            # gloo + NCCL
    multi_gpu/test_wan_token_sharded_tp.py                    # FP8 block-scale WanBlock at tp 2/3/4/8
```

**What a token-sharded TP all-gather moves, after this PR** (decided per call from the consuming projection; `TokenShardedColumn` and `TokenShardedMLP` share the rule):

| Consumer (column `Linear` / MLP up-projection) | Gathered as | Bytes per element | Since |
|---|---|---|---|
| Static (calibrated) NVFP4 input scale, 16-element blocks, no AWQ pre-scale | NVFP4 payload + 128x4-swizzled SF | 0.5 + 0.0625 | #19713 |
| `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` on the DeepGEMM path (SM100 family, `K % 128 == 0`, no CuTe DSL / `disable_deep_gemm`) | FP8 + packed 1x128 UE8M0 scales | 1 + 0.03 | this PR |
| Anything else (BF16, per-tensor FP8, dynamic NVFP4, an active LoRA call) | BF16 | 2 | — |

Both quantized paths hand the GEMM exactly the bytes it would have produced itself on all rows (`torch.equal` in the tests); the 8× B200 run of this head (gpuenv job 5061502 on umb-b200-260, 2026-10-16, nightly `1.4.0rc1.dev202610140007` image with this head overlaid) exercised both: `test_kernels_nccl[2,3,4,8]` (static-NVFP4 adapters, compile + CUDA-graph chain), `test_fp8_block_scales_nccl[2,3,4,8]`, and the D = 5120 `WanBlock` under token-sharded TP as static NVFP4 and as FP8 block scales at tp 2/3/4/8.

## Evidence

- **Before:** every FP8-block-scale boundary gathers BF16 (2 bytes/element) and the Linear quantizes all `B*S` rows itself. Site level on 8x B200 (gather + FP8 GEMM, K = 5120, median of 20, max over ranks): 1.112 / 2.332 / 4.848 ms at TP 2 / 4 / 8 for m = 18,900 rows per rank, N_local = 3,840.
  **After:** FP8 rows + packed scales cross NVLink (369 → 186 MiB per gather at TP2, 1,477 → 744 MiB at TP8): 0.834 / 1.717 / 3.805 ms (1.33x / 1.36x / 1.27x), `torch.equal` to the BF16 path on every shape, incl. after `autotune()`; the CUDA and Triton 1x128 quantizers agreed bitwise at every shape tested.
- 8x B200 (1.3.0rc29 image with the branch overlaid, measured on chang-l#9, same code): the FP8 selections and the token-sharded regression suite pass, 233 passed / 0 failed (`test_fp8_block_scales_nccl[2,3,4,8]`, FP8 block-scale `WanBlock` bitwise vs the emulated-all-reduce block at tp 2/3/4/8 with exactly three FP8 gathers per block, `test_kernels_nccl[2,3,4]`, `test_logic_nccl`, `test_wan_token_sharded_tp.py`, `test_token_sharded_tp_norm.py`, `test_wan_tp.py`).
- **Rebased head on `main`, 8x B200** (job 5061502, nightly `1.4.0rc1.dev202610140007` image + this head overlaid): `test_token_sharded_tp_collectives.py -k nccl` **8 passed** (`test_logic_nccl`, `test_kernels_nccl[2,3,4]` = static-NVFP4 adapters + fullgraph/CUDA-graph chains, `test_fp8_block_scales_nccl[2,3,4,8]`); `test_wan_token_sharded_tp.py` **14 passed** incl. `test_static_nvfp4_block[tp2,tp3,tp4,tp8]` and `test_fp8_block_scales_block[tp2,tp3,tp4,tp8]` (both bitwise vs the emulated all-reduce block), compile and CUDA-graph cases; CPU lane 191 passed.
- Rebased head on `main`, dev box: CPU/gloo lane 191 passed (incl. the LoRA-dispatch test added in 56f3ea2660), 8 NCCL cases deselected (`test_token_sharded_tp.py`, `test_token_sharded_tp_layout.py`, `test_token_sharded_tp_collectives.py -k "not nccl"`) on a 2026-10-14 nightly image with main's Python overlaid; `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.
- Module level (Wan2.2-A14B high-noise expert, BF16 checkpoint with `quant_config={"quant_algo": "FP8_BLOCK_SCALES", "dynamic": true}`, token-sharded TP, CFG batch 2, 720x1280x81f, per-block `torch.compile`, CUDA graphs off, 3 warmup + 6 timed DiT forwards, slowest rank, two rounds), #19713 head with and without this change:

| TP | without (ms, r1 / r2) | with (ms, r1 / r2) | DiT forward |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 5130.6 / 5131.2 | 4987.9 / 4992.3 | -2.7% |
| 4 | 2961.5 / 2965.0 | 2797.1 / 2775.3 | -5.7% |

  Plain TP on the same checkpoint at TP4 is 3153.6 ms, so token-sharded TP is -6.0% and token-sharded TP with this change -11.7% against it. TP8 x `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` does not run on Wan2.2-A14B with or without this change: `ffn.down_proj` has K_local = 1728 at TP8, not a multiple of the 128 block, and the weight-scale shard fails to load (`size of tensor a (14) must match ... (13)`); that is a pre-existing checkpoint-sharding bug outside this PR.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Reverting restores BF16 gathers for FP8 block-scale consumers; no model or config change.

**Blast Radius:** token-sharded-TP-FP8

Only models that run `tp_layout: token_sharded` with `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` on SM100-family GPUs change behaviour (the Wan2.2 dynamic FP8 block-scale recipe). Plain TP, NVFP4, per-tensor FP8, BF16 and non-SM100 paths are untouched. Numerics: bitwise vs the Linear's CUDA quantize tactic; the autotuned Triton quantizer follows the same scale rule but is not guaranteed bitwise, and the NCCL test reports whether it agrees.

## Test Coverage

- CPU (`test_token_sharded_tp.py`, gloo cases of `test_token_sharded_tp_collectives.py`): plan row alignment (tp 2/3/4/8 x B 1/2/3), packed-scale re-layout vs a pure-Python reference, simulated FP8 all_gather incl. padded / straddling / `m % 4 != 0`, bad-pair rejection, every clause of the engagement rule, FP8 pair round trip at `row_align` 1 and 4. Covered by the existing `l0_cpu` entries.
- NCCL, SM100-family only (`test_fp8_block_scales_nccl[2,3,4,8]`): pinned quantizer equals the Linear's CUDA tactic bitwise; real `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` column `Linear` and `MLP` converted by the adapters are `torch.equal` to the plain modules fed all rows, untuned and after `autotune()` (reported), at shapes incl. `m = 209` and `m = 105` (unpadded, `m % 128 != 0`, `m % 4 != 0`); gathered bytes halve; a BF16 consumer rejects the pair; `fullgraph=True` compile and CUDA-graph replay of an FP8 boundary chain. Covered by the existing `l0_dgx_b200` entry (`-k "nccl"`).
- Wan block (`test_wan_token_sharded_tp.py`): a D = 5120 `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` `WanBlock` under token-sharded TP is bitwise equal to the emulated-all-reduce block at tp 2/3/4/8, with exactly three FP8 gathers per block. Covered by the existing `l0_dgx_b200` entry. GPU tests skip off SM100f.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:

items.title: [Attention] Add an FA4 backend with a fixed split-KV schedule
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: Adds: FA4 (CuTe) attention with a fixed split-KV schedule, so a token's attention output is bitwise independent of the batch. This is for batch-invariant inference that a training-side replay can reproduce with the same kernel and schedule.
items.body:
## Overview

Adds `FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend`: FA4 (CuTe) attention with a fixed split-KV schedule, so a token's attention output is bitwise independent of the batch. This is for batch-invariant inference that a training-side replay can reproduce with the same kernel and schedule.

This is one self-contained part of #62017 by @aoshen02, split out unchanged for separate review. The commit keeps his authorship. An earlier revision was reviewed as aoshen02/vllm#93.

## Claims

- Bitwise-identical rows: a sequence's attention rows are the same whether it runs alone or batched with other sequences, and in prefill or decode. Decode includes a verify row of 2 or 3 query tokens.
- Unsupported layers are rejected when the impl is constructed, with a reason, instead of exceeding the schedule at runtime.
- No existing path changes. The backend is not registered as a selectable backend; a model opts in with `Attention(..., attn_backend=FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend)`. The Nemotron-H batch-invariant wiring in #62017 does this.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_fixed_split.py
```

- `test_fixed_schedule_rejects_what_it_cannot_serve`: unsupported head size, KV-cache dtype, sliding window and `max_model_len` get a reason.
- `test_fixed_schedule_rows_ignore_batch_and_phase` (SM10x, FP8 and BF16 KV cache): rows are bitwise equal alone, batched, and as decode after prefill.

| Where | Code | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GB200, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, run by @aoshen02 on #62017's head | the same files at `fa75d3456d` | 9 passed |
| B300 (SM103) | earlier revision aoshen02/vllm#93 (`2d588c3b5b`) | 5 passed; the SM10x rows test ran. The upstream wheel's FA4 already has `seqlen_k_per_split` and `disable_scheduler_metadata`. |
| H100 (SM90) | same earlier revision | 4 passed, 1 skipped (the SM10x rows test) |
| CPU only, this branch | this branch | the 7 rejection cases pass; the 2 rows cases need a GPU |

`pre-commit` mypy (Python 3.11) and ruff pass on the changed files.

## Details

Schedule:
- `SEQLEN_K_PER_SPLIT=8192` keys per split, `NUM_SPLITS=32`;
- `max_seqlen_q` and `max_seqlen_k` fixed at 262144;
- scheduler metadata disabled;
- `tile_mn=(128, 128)`, `pack_gqa=True`.

Each split therefore covers the same keys for any batch composition, sequence length or phase.

Scope; anything outside it raises `ValueError` at construction:
- an SM10x GPU;
- a vllm-flash-attn build whose `_flash_attn_fwd` has `seqlen_k_per_split` and `disable_scheduler_metadata`;
- head size 128;
- FP8 E4M3 or BF16 KV cache;
- no sliding window;
- `max_model_len <= 262144`;
- plain causal decoder attention: no ALiBi, soft cap, sinks, KV sharing or DCP.

At runtime, `forward` also rejects fused output quantization and non-causal metadata.

`FlashAttentionImpl.__init__` is deliberately not called. It picks a vllm-flash-attn version and rejects FP8 KV caches, while this impl calls the CuTe FA4 kernel directly, so only the attributes other code reads are set.

Compared with aoshen02/vllm#93:
- the schedule now covers `max_model_len` up to 262144;
- a BF16 KV cache is accepted;
- the cascade-attention check is gone, because #61126 removed cascade attention.

It is meant for batch-invariant serving only and is not registered for general backend selection.


Duplicate check (open PRs): searches for "fixed split-KV attention batch invariant", "seqlen_k_per_split" and "FA4 batch invariant" find only #62017, which this PR is split from. #54955 (DeepSeek-V4 preview, do not merge) has its own batch-invariant kernels.

items.title: [Quant] ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4: fix layerwise reload
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: Fixes layerwise reload ( → → ) for ModelOpt checkpoints with W4A16 NVFP4 layers (, or with W4A16 layers). This is one self-contained part of #62017 by @aoshen02, split out unchanged for separate review.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes layerwise reload (`initialize_layerwise_reload` → `load_weights` → `finalize_layerwise_processing`) for ModelOpt checkpoints with W4A16 NVFP4 layers (`W4A16_NVFP4`, or `MIXED_PRECISION` with W4A16 layers).

This is one self-contained part of #62017 by @aoshen02, split out unchanged for separate review. The commit keeps his authorship. An earlier revision was reviewed as aoshen02/vllm#90.

## Claims

- During a layerwise reload, a W4A16 NVFP4 layer is processed as soon as its weights arrive. Its `input_scale` placeholders no longer hold the whole layer back until finalize.
- A deprecated `input_scale` that arrives after the layer was processed is ignored. Without this, it would raise `ValueError` in `AutoWeightsLoader` or `AttributeError` in `RoutedExperts`.
- FP8 layers are unchanged: their input scales still load, and reload still waits for them. Cold loading and kernels are unchanged.

## Validation

New test `test_modelopt_w4a16_reload_ignores_legacy_input_scale[late=False|True]` (CUDA):
- Builds a toy model with one W4A16 and one FP8 `ReplicatedLinear` under a mixed-precision config.
- Reloads it layerwise, with the deprecated `input_scale` arriving before (`late=False`) or after (`late=True`) the W4A16 layer's weights.
- Checks that the W4A16 layer is processed without its `input_scale`, the FP8 layer still waits for its own, and the reloaded state dict equals the cold-loaded one.

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py
```

| Where | Code | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GB200, run by @aoshen02 on #62017's head | this PR's change at `fa75d3456d`, plus #62017's FP8 W8A16 additions to the same two files, which are not in this PR | 95 passed, 3 skipped (checkpoints unavailable offline) |
| B300 | earlier revision aoshen02/vllm#90 (`53a5c3f0ce`) | both new reload cases pass |
| H100 | same earlier revision | 38 passed, 4 skipped (base: 36 passed, 4 skipped) |
| CPU only, this branch vs base `fa75d3456d` | this branch | existing cases unchanged: 87 passed, 2 skipped, 3 errors in both. The errors come from CPU-only `dist_init`. The new cases need CUDA. |

`pre-commit` mypy (Python 3.11) and ruff pass on the changed files.

## Details

Root cause: weight-only NVFP4 checkpoints carry no `input_scale`, or a deprecated one. vLLM still registers `input_scale` placeholders for W4A16 layers: `w13_input_scale` and `w2_input_scale` on routed experts, and linear layers through `_DropInputScale`. That causes two problems.

1. **Reload never processes the layer early.**
   - Layerwise reload processes a layer once the numel it has loaded reaches the layer's total. The placeholders count toward that total, but the checkpoint never fills them.
   - So every W4A16 layer stays deferred until finalize and keeps all its staged tensors alive. On Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4 (128 experts) this was 16.5 GiB extra on one GPU during a weight update (measured in aoshen02/vllm#90).
   - Fix: set `weight_loader_numel = 0` on those placeholders. Only the reload trigger reads this attribute.
2. **A late `input_scale` raises.**
   - With (1), a deprecated `input_scale` in a later weight bucket arrives after the layer was processed and `input_scale` was dropped.
   - Fix:
     - ModelOpt configs with W4A16 layers add `.input_scale` to `_ignore_unexpected_suffixes`. That list is only consulted when the parameter is absent, so FP8 input scales still load.
     - `RoutedExperts` skips a missing `input_scale` for NVFP4 W4A16 MoE.

`base_config.py` only gains a type annotation, so that the subclass override type-checks.

Tradeoff: in a mixed-precision checkpoint the ignored suffix applies to the whole config. An `input_scale` that matches no parameter, such as a misnamed FP8 one, is then dropped instead of raising. This is noted in the code.

Duplicate check (open PRs): searches for "W4A16 NVFP4 layerwise reload" and "modelopt W4A16 input_scale" find only #62017, which this PR is split from.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6939002][fix] Tell the agentx aiperf fork from PyPI aiperf before skipping its install
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: The GB300 AgentX perf-sanity lane has failed on every release/1.3 post-merge run since build 29, and on main since build 3020, before sending a single request:
items.body:
## Description

The GB300 AgentX perf-sanity lane `disagg_upload-e2e-gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-dspark_agentx_con1456_ctx3_dep8_gen1_dep16_eplb0_dspark5_ccb-NIXL` has failed on every release/1.3 post-merge run since build 29, and on main since build 3020, before sending a single request:

```
[agentx] aiperf + deps already usable; skipping install
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp ...
Unknown option: --scenario. Did you mean --slice-duration?
RuntimeError: aiperf exited 1 and wrote no .../profile_export_aiperf.json
```

### Root cause

`agentx_client.ensure_aiperf` skips installing the pinned agentx-harness build when `aiperf_is_usable()` succeeds. That check only imported `aiperf` (plus its deps) and checked that `datasets` is 4.x or newer. `requirements-dev.txt` pins the upstream PyPI `aiperf==0.8.0`, which has the same import name. While `requirements.txt` pinned `datasets==3.1.0`, the check always failed and the fork was installed. #19909 (release/1.3) and #20175 (main) unpinned `datasets` (now 4.7.0). Since then the check passes on the PyPI aiperf, the fork is never installed, and PyPI aiperf rejects `--scenario`.

CI history matches. On release/1.3, post-merge 28 (without #19909) passed and 29 onward (with it) failed. On main, 3018 passed, while 3020 and 3021 (with #20175) failed.

### Fix

- `aiperf_is_usable()` now also requires the fork's scenario registry to resolve `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, and logs the reason when a check fails. With the PyPI aiperf present, the pinned fork is installed as before.
- The scenario name is a module constant shared with `build_aiperf_cmd`.
- New CPU unit test `tests/unittest/scripts/test_perf_agentx_aiperf_probe.py`, already collected by `unittest/scripts` in `l0_cpu.yml`. On the old client, 5 of its 6 cases fail.
- Removes this bug's waiver.

## Test Coverage

Original case, oci-jhb, 10x GB300, CI image `pytorch-26.09-py3-sbsa-ubuntu24.04-skip-tritondevel-202610130623-20146`, release/1.3 post-merge 34 wheel:

| after | this PR | fork installed; `health OK: 79373 requests over 3629.9s, submission_valid=true`; pytest 1 passed |

`tests/unittest/scripts`: the new test passes, and `test_subprocess_timeouts` passes.

items.title: [Perf][Parser] Stream MiniMax M2 tool argument values incrementally (16 KB call: 5.9 s to 26 ms)
items.author: deadstrobe5
items.summary: The MiniMax M2 parser re-runs its argument converter and the engine's safe-prefix scan over the whole argument on every streamed delta, so a long parameter value (writefile, code edits) costs quadratic CPU. This adds an for the MiniMax M2 config, the same mech…
items.body:
## Overview

The MiniMax M2 parser re-runs its argument converter and the engine's safe-prefix scan over the whole argument on every streamed delta, so a long parameter value (write_file, code edits) costs quadratic CPU. This adds an `arg_value_extender` for the MiniMax M2 config, the same mechanism glm47 (#61253) and gemma4 (#61494) use.

## Claims

- Parser CPU for a streamed write_file call, one Qwen3 token per delta: 1 KB 31.8 ms to 2.1 ms, 4 KB 387 ms to 6.7 ms, 16 KB 5.9 s to 26 ms. At 32 KB the old path took 22.6 s.
- Streamed output is unchanged.

## Validation

- A/B in fresh processes, 7 runs per side, median [min-max]: 16 KB 5921 [5859-6003] ms vs 25.6 [25.2-26.2] ms.
- Differential fuzz over 44k random streams (random chunking, split and spaced tags, quotes in names, unclosed values, truncated input, several invokes, with and without a schema): every per-delta `DeltaMessage` matches the parser without the extender. Disabling each guard in the extender makes the fuzz fail.
- New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_minimax_m2.py`: streamed arguments match non-streaming extraction with and without a schema, converter calls do not grow with argument length, split closing and next-parameter tags end the value, and the cases where no extender should be built.
- `pytest tests/parser/engine tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m2_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning` passes; ruff and mypy are clean.

## Details

The converter is split into `_minimax_m2_parse_args`, which also returns the match of the open trailing value. The extender is built only when that value is the last JSON value and its opener can't re-parse once more text arrives, which rules out an earlier unmatched `<parameter name=` and a bare name that starts with a quote. It keeps a small window from the last `<` so a value end split across deltas (`</param` + `eter>`, `< parameter` + ` name =`) is still detected, and then hands back to the converter.

items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion/FLUX.3: Run dynamic LoRA through PrimsTS GEMMs
items.author: Linda-Stadter
items.summary: With dynamic LoRA, FLUX.3 disables the FlashInfer PrimsTS GEMMs and falls back to the generic quantized path, which makes LoRA requests much slower than base requests. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585 adds an optional epilogue input to the PrimsTS GEMMs, so the L…
items.body:
## Motivation

With dynamic LoRA, FLUX.3 disables the FlashInfer PrimsTS GEMMs and falls back to the generic quantized path, which makes LoRA requests much slower than base requests. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585 adds an optional `delta` epilogue input to the PrimsTS GEMMs, so the LoRA contribution can be added inside the fused kernels instead.

This PR depends on flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585 for the speedup, but is safe to merge before that is released: the new path is only enabled when the installed FlashInfer exposes `delta` on all PrimsTS GEMM entry points. With current FlashInfer releases the behavior is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `BaseLayerWithLoRA.fused_lora_delta` computes the per-layer LoRA delta `[M, N]` (strength, runtime scale, alpha/rank, output offset, stacked QKV, SwiGLU row interleave) with cached factors.
- `flux3_fused_ops` passes the delta of LoRA-wrapped layers to the PrimsTS linear, SwiGLU and QKV/QK-norm/RoPE GEMMs. The NVFP4 packed SwiGLU handoff is skipped for layers with an active LoRA.
- PrimsTS stays enabled with LoRA, and runtime `set_lora` is accepted, only when the installed FlashInfer supports `delta` (`flux3_prims_ts_supports_lora`). With older FlashInfer, PrimsTS is disabled under `--lora-path` and late LoRA on PrimsTS weights is rejected, as before.
- Unit tests:
  - `test_lora_dynamic_delta_in_gemm.py`: the fused delta matches the LoRA layer forward (scaling, stacked QKV, runtime scale, output offset, SwiGLU order, cache invalidation, inactive layers).
  - `test_flux3_image_dit.py`: deltas reach the PrimsTS epilogues; LoRA skips the packed NVFP4 handoff.
  - `test_flux3_image_served.py`: late LoRA is rejected without `delta` support and accepted with it.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end images, PrimsTS + LoRA vs. the generic LoRA path (B200, 1024x1024, 50 steps, same seeds, mean PSNR over 4 images per prompt). "No LoRA" is the noise floor between the two GEMM paths; "LoRA effect" is generic LoRA vs. generic without LoRA, i.e. how much the adapter changes the image.

| Prompt | Variant | PrimsTS vs generic, no LoRA | PrimsTS vs generic, LoRA | LoRA effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Generic prompt | FP8R  | 39.8 dB | 37.0 dB | 13.8 dB |
| Generic prompt | NVFP4 | 32.8 dB | 28.8 dB | 13.7 dB |
| Adapter trigger prompt | FP8R  | 36.4 dB | 31.0 dB | 9.7 dB |
| Adapter trigger prompt | NVFP4 | 30.1 dB | 26.2 dB | 10.0 dB |

With LoRA, the two paths stay within 3-5 dB of their no-LoRA agreement, far above the 10-14 dB change the adapter itself makes.

Single DiT forward (FP8R): the LoRA effect (LoRA output minus base output) of the PrimsTS path matches the generic path with cosine similarity 0.92; swapping the SwiGLU value/gate column order drops it to 0.26.

The kernel-level `delta` epilogue is covered by the FlashInfer tests in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585; the SGLang delta is unit-tested against the LoRA layer forward. With FlashInfer 0.7.1 (no `delta`), PrimsTS is disabled under `--lora-path` as before, and the unit tests pass against both FlashInfer versions.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, FLUX.3 image, 1024x1024, 50 steps, rank-16 LoRA, `bench_offline_throughput`, median latency per image, FlashInfer built from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585:

| Variant | LoRA, generic path | LoRA, PrimsTS + delta | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP8R  | 4.20 s | 3.29 s | 1.28x |
| NVFP4 | 3.79 s | 2.72 s | 1.39x |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed yet: no new flags; the FLUX.3 docs can be updated when the FlashInfer pin is bumped.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

items.title: [Fix] modelopt: Preserve explicitly quantized NextN drafts
items.author: sshleifer
items.summary: unconditionally discards quantization. This is correct for legacy checkpoints with bundled BF16 MTP weights, but makes a separately serialized NVFP4 MTP draft allocate unpacked weights instead of packed weights and scales.
items.body:
## Codex notes

### Motivation

`DeepseekModelNextN` unconditionally discards `modelopt_fp4` quantization. This is correct for legacy checkpoints with bundled BF16 MTP weights, but makes a separately serialized NVFP4 MTP draft allocate unpacked weights instead of packed weights and scales.

### Modifications

- Preserve the NextN quantizer only when the checkpoint explicitly sets `quantized_mtp: true`. Checkpoints without this flag retain the BF16 fallback.
- Exclude packed MTP drafts from the legacy BF16-to-FP8 helper. Both decoder construction and expert weight conversion use this helper, so the environment flag cannot select FP8 buffers or convert packed NVFP4 weights. Legacy BF16 drafts remain eligible with the flag and DeepGEMM backend enabled.
- Read `use_per_token_activation` from checkpoint metadata so the draft can select its activation-scaling mode without a process-wide environment override that also affects the target. An explicit value takes precedence over the environment; an absent value retains the current behavior.
- Reject per-token activation metadata outside serialized W4A4 NVFP4 and reject `quantized_mtp` for non-serialized weights.

For example, the draft's `config.json` can contain:

```json
{
  "quantization_config": {
    "quant_method": "modelopt",
    "quant_algo": "NVFP4",
    "group_size": 16,
    "quantized_mtp": true,
    "use_per_token_activation": true
  }
}
```

These fields describe the exported weights; they do not convert BF16 weights. Existing exclusion metadata still controls which modules are quantized.

Related: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37322 addresses the same NextN loading problem through broader exclusion-mapping changes. This PR provides a smaller explicit opt-in and preserves the legacy fallback. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44032 covers Qwen auxiliary modules; this change is limited to the DeepSeek NextN path and ModelOpt FP4 metadata.

### Validation

The ModelOpt NVFP4 and NextN quantization CPU suites pass: **12 tests, 13 subtests**. The three added tests cover metadata precedence, legacy/default versus explicit MTP selection, and invalid format combinations. They fail against unpatched upstream `2c2986be2b05`, confirming that they exercise the new behavior. The NextN regression covers the flag on/off with DeepGEMM and FlashInfer TRT-LLM, checking both legacy and packed drafts. It fails on the packed-draft/flag-on/DeepGEMM combination before the shared-helper guard and passes after it.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_nextn_quant_config.py -q
```

No full checkpoint load, model-output accuracy evaluation, or GPU benchmark was run on this upstream branch. This PR makes no throughput claim.

-Robot

items.title: [Perf] pythonic: Resume streaming bracket matching instead of rescanning the buffer
items.author: deadstrobe5
items.summary: calls on every chunk, and it walks the whole buffered call in a Python loop each time. Streaming one long call, such as a with a 16 KB file, is quadratic: about 420 ms of CPU per call on top of the final parse.
items.body:
## Motivation

`PythonicDetector.parse_streaming_increment` calls `_find_matching_bracket` on every chunk, and it walks the whole buffered call in a Python loop each time. Streaming one long call, such as a `write_file` with a 16 KB file, is quadratic: about 420 ms of CPU per call on top of the final parse.

## Modifications

`_find_matching_bracket` stores the text it scanned without finding the closing bracket, plus the bracket depth at its end. On the next chunk it resumes after that text if the buffer still starts with it. Otherwise it rescans from the start, for example when stripping a special token changed the buffer. Matching rules are unchanged.

Two tests: streaming a nested call in 1, 2 and 3 character chunks, and the case where stripping rewrites the buffered prefix.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes. A differential test against the previous detector compared `normal_text`, calls and the buffer after every chunk over 70,000 random streams (about 430,000 chunks): nested brackets, brackets, quotes and escapes in strings, multiple calls, truncated input, special tokens and random chunk sizes. All matched. Pythonic tests in `test_function_call_parser.py` pass; the 15 DeepSeek V3.2/V4 failures in that file locally are the same on main (missing triton on CPU).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CPU only, Llama 3 tokenizer, one `write_file` call streamed one token per chunk, 7 alternating fresh processes per side, median:

| Content | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 13.1 ms | 5.6 ms | 2.3x |
| 4 KB | 46.6 ms | 11.9 ms | 3.9x |
| 8 KB | 159.1 ms | 25.6 ms | 6.2x |
| 16 KB | 668.7 ms | 273.9 ms | 2.4x |

At 16 KB most of the remaining time is the `tool_call_regex` search in `detect_and_parse` on the last chunk, which #18397 and #32107 cover. #44505 and #38869 change the same function to skip brackets inside strings; whichever lands second needs a small rebase, and the cache would then also carry the string state.

## Checklist

items.title: [CI][ROCm] Use AITER prebuilt fp8 MoE modules when inter dim is 256 aligned
items.author: aarushjain29
items.summary: The modular-kernel harness only pre-shuffles weights (so AITER picks its prebuilt preshuffleon CK MoE modules) for unquantized and fp8 block schemes. fp8 per-tensor and per-token were excluded entirely because of ROCm/aiter#5766, so every such test JIT-compile…
items.body:
The modular-kernel harness only pre-shuffles weights (so AITER picks its prebuilt preshuffle_on CK MoE modules) for unquantized and fp8 block schemes. fp8 per-tensor and per-token were excluded entirely because of ROCm/aiter#5766, so every such test JIT-compiles a preshuffle_off module (about 10.5 minutes each in CI). On MI300 this pushes MoE Kernels Shard 1 to about 55 minutes against its 55 minute timeout.

aiter#5766 only rejects intermediate sizes that are not a multiple of 256 (e.g. inter_dim=384). Pre-shuffle fp8 per-tensor/per-token weights too when the intermediate size is a multiple of 256; the 384 padding cases keep JIT-compiling.

On MI300X (rocm/vllm-ci image from amd-ci #14761):
- not multigpu: 48 passed, 6 skipped (same skips as CI); JIT builds drop from 4 kernels (per-tensor/per-token stage 1 and 2) to 2 (stage 2 only).
- multigpu: 27 passed (same as CI).

items.author: thorjohnsen
