items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
The test triggers rebalance after every active request has generated at least eight tokens. It records each request’s token count when `adjust()` runs and checks that exactly one rebalance occurs while every prompt is in flight. The comparison permits a near-tie flip only at or after that prompt’s rebalance point. It requires at least one exact match and warns when it accepts a flip. The B300 overlap waiver was removed. Current review findings were not supplied.

## QA Engineer Review
The modified test covers rebalance with overlap enabled and disabled, including output agreement and near-tie handling. Both test IDs appear in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_h100.yml` and `tests/integration/test_lists/qa/llm_function_core.txt`. The author reports that both cases passed locally on one H100 with Gemma-3-1B, with all four prompts matching exactly; the negative checks also failed as expected. B300 overlap still needs a QA run, and the test remains skipped everywhere until dependency `#20476` merges. Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up**.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_kv_pool_rebalance_accuracy.py`: Covers mid-generation KV-pool rebalance and output agreement for both overlap modes. Both test IDs are listed in H100 CI and manual QA lists; verify B300 overlap after the dependency merges.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt`: Removes the B300 overlap waiver for this test. Verify that the B300 overlap case passes when run.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Follow-up to #19809 (nvbugs/6838020). It delivers the change promised in [this review thread](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19809#discussion_r4190134592) and removes the B300 waiver.

**The test never rebalanced mid-generation.** `_inject_pool_ratio_mismatch` forced the rebalance precondition before `generate()`. The executor acted on it on its first iteration, before any request was scheduled. I confirmed this by instrumenting `_rebalance_kv_pools_now`: it ran at `iter_counter == 0` with no active requests, in both scheduler modes. So `adjust()` resized empty pools, and the suspend → `adjust()` → resume of live KV the test is meant to cover never ran. The pool-ratio assertion still passed because the ratio did move.

**Changes to `test_kv_pool_rebalance_accuracy.py`:**
- `_arm_mid_generation_rebalance` replaces `_inject_pool_ratio_mismatch`. It forces the precondition from inside the executor's rebalance hook, on the first iteration where every in-flight request has generated at least `_REBALANCE_AFTER_TOKENS = 8` tokens. It also records, per request, how many tokens had been generated when `adjust()` ran.
- `_generate_tokens` asserts that exactly one rebalance ran and that every prompt was in flight when it did.
- From the #19809 review (@brnguyen2):
  - A near-tie flip is tolerated only at or after that prompt's rebalance point. Before it, both arms are configured identically, so an earlier flip can't be the rebalance's doing, and it would leave none of that prompt's post-rebalance tokens checked.
  - At least one prompt must match exactly, so at least one output is checked end to end across the rebalance.
  - Accepted flips are reported with `warnings.warn` instead of `print`, so they show up in the CI summary.

**`waives.txt`:** removes `full:B300/...[overlap] SKIP (https://nvbugs/6838020)`.

**Stacked on #20476.** It removes the platform-wide `nvbugs/6930163` waivers; without that, this test is skipped everywhere, B300 included. This branch is rebased on #20476's branch, so until #20476 merges, this PR also shows its commit (`433ada259e`, the two 6930163 lines in `waives.txt`). Please review only the top commit. Once #20476 merges, I'll rebase this onto main so only this PR's own change remains.

## Test Coverage

`accuracy/test_kv_pool_rebalance_accuracy.py::TestKvPoolRebalanceAccuracy::test_rebalance_matches_baseline[no_overlap|overlap]`. It's in `l0_h100.yml` and `qa/llm_function_core.txt`; B300 runs come from the QA list.

Local runs on 1x H100, Gemma-3-1B. The `tensorrt_llm` build was older than main, but it has the same rebalance hook call chain. #20294's `threadleak_exclude` was applied.

| Case | Tokens generated per prompt at rebalance | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `[no_overlap]` | `[9, 8, 8, 8]` | PASSED, all 4 prompts exact |
| `[overlap]` | `[10, 10, 10, 9]` | PASSED, all 4 prompts exact |

Negative checks (`[no_overlap]`):
- Arming before generation, as the old code did, now fails: `the rebalance did not land mid-generation (in flight at the time: {} ...)`.
- Never arming still fails the existing ratio assertion.

The comparison helper was also checked on synthetic inputs: an exact match, a flip after the rebalance point, a flip at it, a flip before it, and a wide-gap divergence.

B300 `[overlap]` still needs a QA run after merge.

items.title: [Perf] glm47: Match streaming tool calls with str.find instead of a lazy regex
items.author: deadstrobe5
items.summary: (parsers and ) runs over the whole buffered tool call on every streamed chunk. The lazy groups make the regex engine step through the buffer one character at a time, so a long call (a file write, say) costs quadratic time on the tokenizer manager's event loop.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Glm47MoeDetector.parse_streaming_increment` (parsers `glm47` and `iquest_q1`) runs `re.search(r"<tool_call>(.*?)(?:(<arg_key.*?))?(?:(</tool_call>)|$)", ...)` over the whole buffered tool call on every streamed chunk. The lazy groups make the regex engine step through the buffer one character at a time, so a long call (a file write, say) costs quadratic time on the tokenizer manager's event loop. A 64 KB argument took about 7 s of CPU for one request.

## Modifications

- `_match_partial_tool_call` finds the same spans with `str.find`: the first `<tool_call>`, then whichever of `<arg_key` or `</tool_call>` comes first. It returns the same stripped name, stripped arguments, end marker and match end the regex groups gave, and replaces the regex and `_extract_match_groups`.
- Two tests: one checks the helper against the old regex on every prefix of some tricky inputs, the other streams a long value containing tag-like text in 3-char chunks.

## Accuracy Tests

Parser-only change, model output is untouched. I ran a differential test of the old and new detectors (`Glm47MoeDetector` and `IQuestQ1Detector`) on 108k random inputs mixing well-formed calls and tag soup, random chunking and 6 argument types. Every chunk's normal_text and calls, plus `finish()` and the final state, matched exactly. The helper also matched the regex on about 2.7M prefixes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One write_file call streamed token by token with the GLM-4.5-Air tokenizer, CPU only, median of 7 alternating fresh processes per side:

| Content | Deltas | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 480 | 10.5 ms | 2.4 ms | 4.4x |
| 8 KB | 1885 | 136.6 ms | 12.5 ms | 10.9x |
| 25 KB | 4737 | 896.5 ms | 57.1 ms | 15.7x |
| 64 KB | 13086 | 6988 ms | 323 ms | 21.6x |

Before, 97% of the parse time was in `re.Pattern.search`; afterwards the profile is flat.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Reject prefill caps smaller than an intact item
items.author: Justee21
items.summary: Adds validation to reject nonzero long-prefill caps smaller than the maximum multimodal item when chunking is disabled, preventing permanent request stalls.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #62031.

Reject a nonzero long-prefill cap smaller than the configured maximum multimodal item when item chunking is disabled. This replaces an accepted configuration that can permanently stall contended requests with an actionable startup error.

## Claims

- Validate the cap alongside the existing maximum-item versus batch-budget check.
- Cover fixed and adaptive caps; retain disabled-cap, equal/larger-cap, chunkable-input, and disabled-modality behavior.
- Preserve the scheduler, hard budgets, whole-item guard, and fairness policy. Defaults remain unchanged.

## Validation

On macOS arm64, Python 3.11.2, PyTorch 2.14.1, Transformers 5.19.0:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' PYTHONPATH=. \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

**269 passed in 50.67 seconds** on publication commit `776389ac699bdc3761cf596dd7ae8e6236a6da35`, based on upstream `8a6c0449b36e7aba29c2a6b1720ca3c08cfafa32`, including nine new cases. Before/after regressions were also checked at base `642c18d64c4cb6db3ded8fbe1786718cd4005fcb`: four rejection cases fail on unchanged production code and five valid controls pass. The five-file target patch is byte-identical after rebasing. The default commit hooks, sign-off hook, and current-head hook rerun pass, including mypy, Markdown lint, and CI test tethering; git diff --check passes. Existing CPU CI covers the tests. After removing the temporary CPU inference dependency, all nine new cases also pass in isolation with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1; these flags avoid a DNS failure in the existing public-model configuration lookup.

At base `642c18d`, real CPU MRV1 inference was checked with a seeded local tiny LLaVA checkpoint, four image tokens, float32, and batch budget 128. Both image requests were queued while scheduling was paused, then resumed together to guarantee contention.

| Check | Baseline | Patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cap 2, two queued image requests | Startup accepted; generation stalls until the 30-second watchdog | Intended ValueError at startup, reporting cap 2 and item maximum 4 |
| Cap 0, same requests | Both complete | Both complete; identical output tokens |
| Cap 4, same requests | Both complete | Both complete; identical output tokens |

Each valid run produces eight greedy tokens per request. The initial unpaused baseline run completed because overlap was not guaranteed; it is not counted as a stall reproduction.

Both inference checkouts temporarily included the same CPU slot-mapping compatibility change from [open PR #61151](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61151), head 5e0ac9d76f4ddbfa8290f488cebca39645ff81a5. Its two native tests pass locally. Without that dependency, both versions fail in the same pre-existing CPU fallback. The dependency was removed after testing and is excluded from this PR.

GPU/MRV2, HTTP serving, and pretrained-model quality were not tested. No post-rebase inference rerun is claimed; the inference matrix is attributed to base `642c18d`.

## Details

The scheduler caps proposed prefill work before checking whole-image boundaries. If the cap is below an intact item, the boundary guard schedules zero tokens. With multiple eligible requests, the cap stays active and the same state repeats. The baseline remained stuck for 1,000 scheduling passes. Adaptive fair share can also stay below the item size.

The fix adds a 12-line check to compute_mm_encoder_budget, following its existing batch-budget validation. The error tells users to disable the cap with zero or raise it sufficiently. The optimization guide and field documentation explain that validation uses the configured maximum item size, even if a particular request is smaller or alone. Encoder-decoder configuration already resets the threshold to zero.

This matches the fail-fast approach proposed in the [review of #52412](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52412#pullrequestreview-5407246881), while preserving the merged boundary fixes in [#52412](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52412) and [#59721](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59721). The proposal itself has not received maintainer approval.

Tradeoff: conservative startup rejection. A low cap that would work for one request, small images, or light adaptive contention is rejected because later requests could make it unschedulable. Default cap zero and configurations allowing item chunking are unaffected. No performance or output-quality improvement is claimed.

Duplicate searches on October 16, 2026 found no matching open cap-validation fix. [#59030](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59030) changes waiting-queue requeueing. [#61733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61733) validates whole prompts when chunked prefill is disabled after startup; this validates a multimodal item's per-request cap in configurations that still allow chunked text prefill.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests, and preparation. Publication was authorized by the human submitter. The automated validation commands described above were run by Codex; no human-executed validation is claimed. The commit includes AI attribution and the submitter's DCO sign-off.

items.title: [Attention] Use trtllm-gen for the FlashInfer DCP prefill context pass
items.author: GagandeepKang-cohere
items.summary: Run the FlashInfer DCP prefill context pass on the trtllm-gen context kernel (non-causal, with LSE) instead of the native FlashInfer kernel, under the same conditions in which non-DCP prefill auto-selects trtllm-gen. No existing PR switches this kernel; #58519…
items.body:
## Overview Run the FlashInfer DCP prefill context pass on the trtllm-gen context kernel (non-causal, with LSE) instead of the native FlashInfer kernel, under the same conditions in which non-DCP prefill auto-selects trtllm-gen. No existing PR switches this kernel; #58519 is complementary (it reduces overhead around the same pass). ## Claims - On 8×B200 (TP8, DCP2), 100k input / 512 output: mean TTFT −39–48% and output throughput 1.23–1.79× across concurrency 1–32. - Accuracy matches the native path (MRCR, GSM8K), and a new kernel test checks the pass against the native one. - Applies on SM100/SM103 when trtllm-gen prefill is available (`--attention-config.use_trtllm_attention` not 0) with an unquantized KV cache, to layers without a sliding window or soft-capping. Other layers keep the native kernel. ## Validation Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP8 / DCP2 / EP8, a2a DCP combine, prefix caching off, one run per arm. | Concurrency | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT ms | Mean TPOT ms | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 106.9 → 131.5 (1.23×) | 2190 → 1332 | 5.1 → 5.0 | | 2 | 151.3 → 204.6 (1.35×) | 3203 → 1881 | 7.0 → 6.1 | | 4 | 190.8 → 287.2 (1.51×) | 5061 → 2832 | 11.1 → 8.4 | | 8 | 221.7 → 364.9 (1.65×) | 8722 → 4675 | 19.0 → 12.8 | | 16 | 239.3 → 414.0 (1.73×) | 12875 → 6792 | 41.6 → 25.3 | | 32 | 250.7 → 448.8 (1.79×) | 16277 → 8460 | 95.6 → 54.5 | TPOT improves at higher concurrency only because decode steps share batches with shorter prefill chunks. | Eval (real weights) | Native | trtllm-gen | |---|---|---| | MRCR match ratio (40 samples) | 0.480 | 0.496 | | GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot) | 0.888 | 0.899 | Both accuracy differences are within noise. A kernel-level comparison against the native kernel (all layers and ranks, real metadata) gave max relative output error 2.3e-4 and matching LSE. These runs used an earlier revision of this PR that was opt-in through an env var and included `q_scale` (1.0 for this checkpoint) in `bmm1_scale`; the kernel path is otherwise unchanged. `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_attention.py -k dcp_prefill` on B200: TODO.
Commands ```bash # Baseline: the parent commit. --load-format dummy for perf vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 2 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \ --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --max-model-len 128000 --max-num-seqs 256 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --generation-config vllm vllm bench serve --backend openai --dataset-name random --random-input-len 100000 --random-output-len 512 \ --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts $((C*4 < 8 ? 8 : C*4)) --max-concurrency $C --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 0 python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py --port 8000 --num-samples 40 --concurrency 8 python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64 ```
## Details - **Kernel.** `trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache(causal=False, return_lse=True)` over the DCP-local paged KV. Its LSE is base 2 like the native kernel's, so the combine and merge are unchanged. Non-causal mode and LSE output (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3020, #3116) postdate the original FlashInfer DCP support (#25438). The native context wrapper is not planned when this kernel runs. - **Requests with no local context.** The kernel's LSE for these rows is unspecified: FlashInfer computes it from softmax stats in the reused workspace, which the kernel never writes for `kv_len == 0`. Stale values corrupted the merge intermittently. These rows are masked as empty shards in the combine (`seq_lens` / `query_start_loc`), as on the trtllm DCP decode path, and the output is zero-initialized because the all-gather combine multiplies it by a zero weight. - **Test.** `test_flashinfer_dcp_prefill_trtllm_context` compares the pass with the native one, including requests with no local context, and runs in the "(B200) Kernels" CI job. The GQA DCP end-to-end test in `tests/distributed/test_context_parallel.py` needs 4 GPUs and only runs on SM90, so it does not cover Blackwell. - **Limitations.** FP8 KV keeps the native kernel; FlashInfer DCP with FP8 KV currently fails at startup on SM100 independently of this PR, to be fixed separately. `use_trtllm_attention=0` disables this together with trtllm-gen decode, as it does for non-DCP prefill. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

items.title: ci(autobot): enable formal review approvals
items.author: ko3n1g
items.summary: Autobot requires a default-branch policy before it can publish native APPROVE or REQUESTCHANGES reviews. Without that opt-in, the workflow downgrades those verdicts to COMMENT. [Discussion: Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository.]
items.body:
Autobot requires a default-branch policy before it can publish native APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES reviews. Without that opt-in, the workflow downgrades those verdicts to COMMENT.

Add `.github/autobot/review-config.yml` with `approval.enabled: true`. Permit active members of the existing repository engineering/maintainer and CI automation teams:

- `NVIDIA/mcore-engineers`
- `NVIDIA/mcore-reviewers`
- `NVIDIA/mcore-leadership`
- `NVIDIA/mcore-automation`
- `NVIDIA/ci`

The policy takes effect after merge to `main`; the review service checks the requester's active team membership before publishing a formal verdict.

Tested:

- `python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import yaml; p = yaml.safe_load(Path(".github/autobot/review-config.yml").read_text()); a = p["approval"]; assert a["enabled"] is True; t = a["eligible_teams"]; assert isinstance(t, list) and t and all(isinstance(x, str) and x and "/" not in x for x in t) and len(t) == len(set(t)); print("approval config valid")'` — passed YAML and approval-policy shape checks.
- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD` — passed.
- `gh api orgs/NVIDIA/teams/<slug>` for every configured team — verified each team exists in the repository's organization.
- `BASE_REF=main CHECK_ONLY=true SKIP_DOCS=false bash tools/autoformat.sh` — passed; no Python changes.

items.title: Fix duplicate parameter all-gathers across MoE distributed optimizers
items.author: ewan0x79
items.summary: Restrict each to synchronizing the bucket groups it owns, avoiding duplicate parameter all-gathers when the dense and expert optimizers of an MoE model share the same DDP model chunk. The fix targets the synchronous parameter-gather path with and does not chan…
items.body: - [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR. # What does this PR do? Restrict each `DistributedOptimizer` to synchronizing the bucket groups it owns, avoiding duplicate parameter all-gathers when the dense and expert optimizers of an MoE model share the same DDP model chunk. The fix targets the synchronous parameter-gather path with `overlap_param_gather=False` and does not change the Adam update rule. ## Problem The dense and expert child optimizers manage different parameter buffers but can hold the same `model_chunks`. Currently, `start_param_sync_for_bucket_group_subset()` excludes LayerWise-managed groups without checking ownership by the current optimizer. Consequently, each child optimizer gathers both dense and expert groups after its update, and every parameter bucket is gathered twice per step. ```text Before: dense optimizer update -> gather dense + expert groups expert optimizer update -> gather dense + expert groups After: dense optimizer update -> gather dense groups expert optimizer update -> gather expert groups ``` Simply skipping synchronization for the second optimizer is not correct: the expert parameters have not yet been updated when the first gather occurs. Each owner must still synchronize its parameters after updating them. ## Fix - Select groups owned by the current optimizer using the identities of the buckets in `self.buffers`. - Skip groups with no owned buckets, and assert that every bucket in a selected group belongs to the current optimizer to reject mixed ownership. - Preserve the existing exclusions for empty and LayerWise-managed groups, and do not initiate synchronization for stub optimizers. - Keep each group intact and continue to call `DDP._start_bucket_group_param_sync()`, preserving the existing parameter-publication and quantization post-processing entry point. The production change is confined to one method, with no new configuration option. The implementation and dispatch regression tests are in this PR's [Files changed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8292/files) tab. ## Reproduction and profiling results The reproduction uses the pinned official baseline [7a0024e2ca8317740af2e2e3ac245ba3cfe34bc1](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/commit/7a0024e2ca8317740af2e2e3ac245ba3cfe34bc1) on a single node with 4 x H20 GPUs: a two-layer BF16 GPT MoE, hidden size 128, four experts, and top-k 2; TP=PP=CP=ETP=1, EP=2, dense DP=4, and expert DP=2. Parameter-gather overlap is disabled. The reproduction runs the real DDP, optimizer updates, and NCCL collectives; the counters track only gathers for parameter buckets. | Per rank, per step | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Parameter AG calls per dense or expert bucket | 2 | 1 | | Parameter AG GPU kernels inside `optimizer_step` | 4 | 2 | All four ranks show the same reduction: each child optimizer goes from two parameter AG kernels to one. The screenshots compare the same rank and configuration before and after the fix. Two unrelated all-gathers remain unchanged, so the full-step total drops from six to four. The profile confirms removal of redundant communication; end-to-end performance is measured separately below. **Before (baseline): 4 parameter AG GPU kernels inside `optimizer_step`, 2 per child optimizer.** **After (candidate): 2 parameter AG GPU kernels inside `optimizer_step`, 1 per child optimizer.** ## Correctness validation The GPU experiments below were executed on the pinned official baseline [`7a0024e2`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/commit/7a0024e2ca8317740af2e2e3ac245ba3cfe34bc1) and its patched candidate. - **Four-GPU training comparison:** From the same initial state, five consecutive training steps produce bit-exact loss, post-ReduceScatter gradient shards, BF16 model parameters, FP32 master parameters, and Adam state on all four ranks. The maximum absolute difference is zero. - **Sixteen-GPU fixed-gradient optimizer regression:** On 2 nodes x 8 H20 GPUs, with EP=4, expert DP=4, and dense DP=16, a small BF16 MoE exercises FusedAdam, ChainedOptimizer, and NCCL using identical initial parameters, gradients, and Adam state. Both cold-start and nonzero-history cases run for five consecutive updates. A/A, B/B, and A/B comparisons are bit-exact across 54,064 tensor comparisons (A: baseline; B: patched candidate). **Synchronization is checked without repairing the model:** No extra model-parameter gather is performed before comparison. After each update, DP/expert-DP parameter replicas match a reference independently reconstructed from the owners’ updated FP32 master shards. Validation collectives operate only on detached snapshots and never write back to the model. The PR is based on [`3888b348`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/commit/3888b34882eb85aecf6ec9ecc3f4020b7608b497). The optimizer file is byte-identical between the validation baseline and the PR base, both before and after applying the fix. These experiments are not a full CI rerun on the PR base. ## Repository tests and checks `tests/unit_tests/optimizer/test_distrib_optimizer_param_sync.py` covers bucket ownership, shared model chunks, multi-bucket groups, stub optimizers, LayerWise exclusions, and ownership edge cases. **All 8 cases pass** at [`0bdc21e6`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/commit/0bdc21e61a551d914d14910b305c73ead3be6480), with no failures, errors, or skips, on Linux with one H20 GPU and the original upstream conftest. The original five cases fail on the unpatched validation baseline. These are dispatch tests; real-NCCL correctness validation is described above. Run with Megatron’s test dependencies installed: ```bash PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1 python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=1 \ -m pytest tests/unit_tests/optimizer/test_distrib_optimizer_param_sync.py -q --capture=fd ``` - **Formatting/lint:** Black, isort, Pylint, Ruff, and autoformat checks pass. The non-gating mypy check has dependency/type diagnostics and is not reported as passing. - **Upstream GPU/test CI:** Pending maintainer authorization via `copy-pr-bot`. ## Scope Runtime correctness validation covers BF16 with synchronous parameter gathers. The overlap scheduling and existing deferred-synchronization gates are unchanged. Retaining the DDP post-processing entry point is not a claim of runtime FP8/MXFP8 coverage. ## Additional performance results A randomly initialized synthetic training workload using the Qwen3-30B-A3B architecture was measured on two nodes with 16 x H20 GPUs: BF16, sequence length 2048, EP=4, EDP=4, dense DP=16, global batch size 16, and both parameter- and gradient-communication overlap disabled. Eight paired A/B runs on the same GPUs show a median step-time reduction of **8.43%** and a median throughput increase of **9.21%**. Each run uses 200 warmup steps followed by 1,000 measured steps. A Student-t 95% interval over the eight paired log time ratios, transformed to step-time reduction, is **7.93%-9.80%**; this is not a confidence interval for the median. These results characterize performance under the stated synthetic workload. The performance runs were not used to establish end-to-end numerical equivalence; optimizer-update and parameter-synchronization correctness was validated separately by the bit-exact fixed-gradient regression. ## Issue tracking Related to [NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#1527](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/1527). A maintainer requested a new minimal reproduction/profile. The results above provide communication counts and profiling observations from the executed reproduction on a pinned official SHA. ## Contribution process ### Pre-checks - [x] I have added relevant unit tests - [ ] I have added relevant functional tests - **N/A:** GPU kernel bit-exact determinism tests and manifest registration (no new or modified GPU kernel). - [ ] I have added proper typing to my code - [x] I have added relevant documentation (updated the parameter-sync method docstring). - [x] I have run the [autoformatter](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

items.title: [Diffusion] Wan2.2-S2V: fp32 RoPE via _apply_rotary_emb, as in wanvideo.py
items.author: murthy-l-habana
items.summary: Routes Wan2.2-S2V's RoPE through in fp32, matching the existing Wan I2V path in rather than introducing a new mechanism. Device-agnostic; no XPU-specific code.
items.body:
Routes Wan2.2-S2V's RoPE through `_apply_rotary_emb` in fp32, **matching the existing Wan I2V path in `wanvideo.py`** rather than introducing a new mechanism. Device-agnostic; no XPU-specific code.

## Change
S2V built its rotary embedding inline with a different dtype policy from its sibling model. This reuses `wanvideo.py`'s helper so the two Wan DiTs apply RoPE identically.

1 file (`dits/wan_s2v.py`), +23/−15.

## Measured
2 × B60, SP=2 Ulysses, 576×768, `dit=layerwise-offload`: **−8.3 % per step (−3.3 s/step)**. The saving comes from dropping fp32 intermediate concatenations, not from lower precision — the rotary math stays in fp32, as in `wanvideo.py`.

## Review note
This changes RoPE's numerics relative to the previous S2V path (it now matches `wanvideo.py` instead). Output parity was checked by eye on the reference clip, **not** bit-exactly — if upstream wants a stricter bar, say so and I will add a numerical comparison against the pre-change path.

## Base
⚠️ **Stacked on #43279** (the S2V port), included here as the first commit. Independent of #44755, the wav2vec2 fix (audio encoder only). **The modulation-fusion PR (#43288, retitled) is stacked on top of this one** — its modulation-fusion commit builds on this one, so merge this first.

Split out of #43288.

items.title: [Diffusion] Wan2.2-S2V: take the last wav2vec2 layer from last_hidden_state
items.author: murthy-l-habana
items.summary: Fixes broken Wan2.2-S2V lip sync on transformers ≥ 5.17. The checkpoint uses, so the encoder's final LayerNorm belongs to the last layer's output — and transformers 5.17 returns before that norm, where 5.12 returned it after.
items.body:
Fixes broken Wan2.2-S2V lip sync on transformers ≥ 5.17. **Correctness only — no performance change, and it is not XPU-specific.**

## The bug
The S2V audio encoder took its last layer as `result.hidden_states[-1]`. The checkpoint uses `do_stable_layer_norm`, so the encoder's final LayerNorm belongs to the **last layer's output** — and transformers 5.17 returns `hidden_states[-1]` *before* that norm, where 5.12 returned it after. The audio features were therefore un-normalised, and lip sync degraded with no error anywhere.

`last_hidden_state` is post-norm in **both** versions, so it is used as the last layer:

```python
hidden_states = (*result.hidden_states[:-1], result.last_hidden_state)
feat = torch.cat(hidden_states) if return_all_layers else hidden_states[-1]
```

This is version-robust rather than pinning a transformers release. Verified against 5.17 and 5.19.

The call also narrows from `self.model(...)` to `self.model.wav2vec2(...)`: feature extraction does not use the LM head, and calling the bare encoder avoids computing and discarding it.

1 file, +6/−6.

## Base
⚠️ **Stacked on #43279** (the S2V port), included here as the first commit — S2V does not exist on `main` yet. Independent of #44756 and #43288, the other two PRs split out of it: this touches only `encoders/wan_s2v_audio.py`, with **zero file overlap** with either (they touch `dits/wan_s2v.py` and the shared layer modules).

Split out of #43288 so the correctness fix is not gated behind reviewing the performance work.

items.title: [Perf][Parser] Stream Qwen3 tool argument values incrementally (12 KB call: 2.1 s to 11 ms)
items.author: deadstrobe5
items.summary: Streaming a Qwen3 XML tool call re-parses the whole argument on every delta:, then, a per-character Python loop over the full JSON. A long parameter value, such as a file written by a coding agent, costs quadratic CPU on the API server.
items.body:
## Overview

Streaming a Qwen3 XML tool call re-parses the whole argument on every delta: `_qwen3_arg_converter`, then `_safe_arg_prefix`, a per-character Python loop over the full JSON. A long parameter value, such as a file written by a coding agent, costs quadratic CPU on the API server. This adopts the `arg_value_extender` hook from #61253 (GLM) and #61494 (Gemma4) for the Qwen3 grammar.

## Claims

- Parser cost per delta no longer grows with argument length: 1.1 ms at 12 KB and 2.2 ms at 25 KB become about 4 us at every size.
- A 12 KB `write_file` call (2,788 Qwen3 tokens) goes from 2.1 s to 11 ms of parser time. A 25 KB call goes from 8.4 s to 22 ms.
- Streamed deltas are unchanged, including newline trimming, schema coercion and truncated calls.
- Covers every parser on `qwen3_config` (qwen3_coder, qwen3_xml, Seed-OSS, Step3p5, Nemotron-v3, Granite thinking, MiniCPM-V). MiMo gets a variant without newline trimming, since its converter keeps values verbatim.

## Validation

`pytest tests/parser/engine`: 6026 passed. Also passed: the qwen3coder, step3p5 and minicpm5xml tool parser tests, the qwen3, nemotron_v3, granite_thinking and step3p5 reasoning tests, and `tests/parser/test_streaming.py`, `test_parse.py` and `test_abstract_parser.py`. ruff and mypy pass on the changed files.

New tests in `TestArgValueExtender`: long Qwen3 and MiMo calls with escapes, blank lines and prefixes of the closing tags stream the same arguments as `extract_tool_calls`; converter calls stay constant from 20 to 200 lines (they grow on `main`); a closer split across deltas and a split next `<parameter=`; and the cases where no extender is created.

A local differential fuzz streamed 27,500 random Qwen3 and MiMo calls with and without the extender: random chunk sizes, schemas with string, integer, boolean, object and nullable keys, repeated keys, whitespace-variant closers, tag fragments inside values, and truncated calls. Every per-delta `DeltaMessage` was identical, and about 194K deltas went through the extender. Breaking the newline hold-back, the split-closer window or the leading-newline strip made the fuzz fail.

Benchmark: `Qwen3Parser.parse_delta`, one real Qwen3 token per delta, Apple M5, Python 3.12, 7 alternating runs.

| Argument size | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 KB | 187-192 us | 3.9-4.1 us |
| 12 KB | 1.09-1.44 ms | 3.8-4.6 us |
| 25 KB | 2.21 ms | 3.8 us |

A short three-parameter call also gets about 10% faster (338 us to 304 us), because each delta skips a conversion. I couldn't run a GPU server end to end; model output is unchanged by construction.

## Details

The extender reads the open value with the same regexes as the converter. It refuses when the open key repeats an earlier one, since that key keeps its first position in the JSON. A delta that completes `</parameter>` or the next `<parameter=` (whitespace variants included, even split across deltas) returns None, and the converter takes over again. A future change to `_PARAM_RE` needs a matching change to `_PARAM_VALUE_END_RE`.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).

items.title: [Refactor] RoPE: Support RotaryEmbedding class usage for DiT models
items.author: Allor-maker
items.summary: Each DiT implements its own RoPE: the same flashinfer / AITER / eager cascade is written out four times across and, and Z-Image has eleven RoPE call sites. already exists to unify this.
items.body:
## Motivation Each DiT implements its own RoPE: the same flashinfer / AITER / eager cascade is written out four times across `wanvideo.py` and `lingbot_world.py`, and Z-Image has eleven RoPE call sites. `RotaryEmbedding` already exists to unify this. This PR moves Wan-Video, LingBot-World, Causal-Wan/LongLive2 and Z-Image onto the class and hoists each model's frequency table into its top-level `forward`, which also gets them the class's complex-table path off CUDA. CUDA keeps the same flashinfer kernel. ## Modifications 1. `runtime/models/dits/wanvideo.py` Removed the hand-written `CUDA`/`AITER` cascade from `WanTransformerBlock` and the `VSA` variant; both now hold a `RotaryEmbedding` and receive a `complex_freqs` table built once per `WanTransformer3DModel.forward`. The per-forward `rope_cos_sin_cache` plumbing is gone, forward_cuda rebuilds the same cache internally and calls the same `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace`. 2. `runtime/models/dits/lingbot_world.py` Same change for `LingBotWorldCausalSelfAttention` and` LingBotWorldTransformerBlock`: the `_is_cuda` branch and the duplicated `cat([cos, sin])` cache build are replaced by one class call that takes cos/sin, the existing `cos_sin_cache` and `complex_freqs`. The `AITER` branch is untouched. 3. `runtime/models/dits/causal_wanvideo.py` `CausalWanSelfAttention` gets a `RotaryEmbedding`; `complex_freqs` is built once in `CausalWanTransformer3DModel.forward` and threaded through the block as a keyword-only argument. 4. runtime/models/dits/longlive2.py Forwards `complex_freqs` through the overridden block so the `LongLive2` subclass keeps the parent's new signature. 5. runtime/models/dits/zimage.py Collapsed five `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope` call sites and six direct `RoPE` calls into two branches: fused QK-norm or no QK-norm goes to the class, otherwise `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope with` the cache it already had. `_get_rope_cache` lost its CUDA-only gate and now returns (cos_sin_cache, positions, freqs_complex) for all three groups (x / cap / unified), built once per forward by a new pure `_build_rope_cache`. 6. `runtime/models/dits/ming_image.py` Builds the same three tables via `_build_rope_cache` and passes them down. Required: Ming reuses `Z-Image's` attention but has its own forward, so without this it would reach `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope(cos_sin_cache=None)` and get QK-norm without `RoPE`. 7. `runtime/layers/layernorm.py, runtime/layers/elementwise.py` Fix per-frame [B, F, 1, C] modulation on NPU, which the branch hits before any `RoPE` code: the fused kernel flattens the modulation to one row, so `MulAdd.forward_npu` falls back to eager when it is wider, and the new `_expand_npu_modulation` broadcasts shift/scale to [B, L, C] instead of letting a plain multiply produce [B, F, L, C]. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling
Wan-Video **Setup** - Hardware: Ascend , NPU - Model: `` - Commands: **Server** ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true sglang serve --model-path ~/models/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers --ulysses-degree 8 --num-gpus 8 --attention-backend fa --port 30088 --warmup-steps 10 --warmup-mode "server" ``` **Bench command** ```bash python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving --dataset vbench --task text-to-video --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1 --port 30088 --num-inference-steps 20 ``` **Serving benchmark results (e2e, s):** | branch| Latency Mean | | --- | --- | | main | 223.02 | | this PR | 222.71 |
LingBot-World v2 **Setup** - Hardware: Ascend, NPU, - Model: `lingbot-world-v2-14b-causal-fast-diffusers` - Driven by a headless WebSocket client; `bench_serving` cannot drive a realtime camera model. - Command: **Server** ```bash sglang serve --model-path ~/models/lingbot-world-v2-14b-causal-fast-diffusers --pipeline-class-name LingBotWorldCausalDMDPipeline --num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 4 --dit-cpu-offload false --enable-torch-compile false --port 30000 ``` **Runner** ```bash python script_lingbot.py run --tag --actions "w:48,d:24,:36" ```
Measurement script Reuses the helpers in `multimodal_gen/test/server/realtime_consistency.py`. `run` writes an mp4, a lossless frame dump and `chunk_stats`; `compare` prints PSNR between two dumps. ```python """Headless LingBot-World realtime client: scripted camera, mp4 + frames + chunk_stats. Run: python lingbot_rt_client.py run --tag main --image ref.jpg python lingbot_rt_client.py compare lingbot_out/main_frames.npz lingbot_out/branch_frames.npz """ import argparse import asyncio import json from pathlib import Path import numpy as np from sglang.multimodal_gen.test.server.realtime_consistency import ( collect_realtime_output, encode_realtime_frames_to_mp4, prepare_realtime_first_frame, summarize_realtime_perf_stats, ) def parse_actions(spec: str) -> list[list[str]]: # "w:24,d:12,:12" -> 24 frames of ["w"], 12 of ["d"], 12 of [] (idle). actions: list[list[str]] = [] for part in filter(None, spec.split(",")): keys, count = part.split(":") actions += [list(keys)] * int(count) return actions def run(args) -> None: init = { "type": "init", "prompt": args.prompt, "first_frame": prepare_realtime_first_frame(args.image), "size": args.size, "fps": args.fps, "num_frames": args.num_frames, "seed": args.seed, "num_inference_steps": args.steps, "guidance_scale": 1.0, "max_chunks": args.num_chunks, # No realtime_output_format -> lossless delta-gzip RGB, needed for frame diff. "condition_inputs": {"camera_actions": parse_actions(args.actions)}, } result = asyncio.run( collect_realtime_output( ws_url=args.url, init_payload=init, events=[], num_chunks=args.num_chunks, require_chunk_stats=True, ) ) out = Path(args.out_dir) out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (out / f"{args.tag}.mp4").write_bytes( encode_realtime_frames_to_mp4(result.frames, fps=args.fps) ) np.savez_compressed(out / f"{args.tag}_frames.npz", frames=np.stack(result.frames)) summary = summarize_realtime_perf_stats( result.chunk_stats, ignore_initial_chunks=args.ignore_initial_chunks ) per_chunk = [ { "chunk": s.chunk_index, "forward_ms": s.scheduler_forward_ms, "total_ms": s.chunk_total_ms, } for s in result.chunk_stats ] (out / f"{args.tag}_stats.json").write_text( json.dumps({"summary": summary, "per_chunk": per_chunk}, indent=2) ) print(f"[{args.tag}] frames={len(result.frames)}") for key in ( "avg_scheduler_forward_ms", "p95_scheduler_forward_ms", "avg_chunk_total_ms", ): print(f" {key:28s} {summary[key]:9.1f}") fps_gen = ( summary["total_frames"] / sum(s.chunk_total_ms for s in result.chunk_stats) * 1e3 ) print(f" {'generated_fps (all chunks)':28s} {fps_gen:9.2f}") def compare(args) -> None: a = np.load(args.a)["frames"].astype(np.float32) b = np.load(args.b)["frames"].astype(np.float32) n = min(len(a), len(b)) if len(a) != len(b): print(f"frame count differs: {len(a)} vs {len(b)}, comparing first {n}") diff = a[:n] - b[:n] mse = (diff**2).reshape(n, -1).mean(axis=1) psnr = 10 * np.log10(255.0**2 / np.maximum(mse, 1e-10)) print( f"max_abs_diff={np.abs(diff).max():.0f} " f"mean_abs_diff={np.abs(diff).mean():.3f}" ) print(f"PSNR dB: min={psnr.min():.2f} mean={psnr.mean():.2f} (100 = identical)") print("PSNR per frame:", " ".join(f"{p:.1f}" for p in psnr)) def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True) r = sub.add_parser("run") r.add_argument("--tag", required=True) r.add_argument("--url", default="ws://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/realtime_video/generate") r.add_argument("--image", required=True, help="first frame: local path or URL") r.add_argument( "--prompt", default="A slow aerial orbit around a pastel floating island hotel in the open " "ocean, hazy sunlight, turquoise water, clean horizon, cinematic but playful.", ) r.add_argument("--size", default="832x480") r.add_argument("--fps", type=int, default=16) r.add_argument("--num-frames", type=int, default=9, help="frames per chunk") r.add_argument("--num-chunks", type=int, default=12) r.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=4) r.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42) r.add_argument("--actions", default="w:48,d:24,:36", help="per-frame camera script") r.add_argument("--ignore-initial-chunks", type=int, default=2) r.add_argument("--out-dir", default="lingbot_out") r.set_defaults(func=run) c = sub.add_parser("compare") c.add_argument("a") c.add_argument("b") c.set_defaults(func=compare) args = parser.parse_args() args.func(args) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
**Per-chunk time, s:** | | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | avg_scheduler_forward_ms | 2949.5 | 2851.7 | | p95_scheduler_forward_ms | 3286.0 | 3160.0 | | avg_chunk_total_ms | 2965.6 | 2864.4 | | generated_fps| 3.93 | 4.02 |
Causal-Wan / LongLive2 **Setup** - Hardware: Ascend, NPU - Model: `LongLive-2.0-5B-Diffusers` - Needs a base that contains the NPU per-frame modulation fixes; this PR carries them in `layernorm.py` / `elementwise.py`. - Command: **Server** ```bash sglang serve --model-path ~/models/LongLive-2.0-5B-Diffusers --num-gpus 1 --dit-cpu-offload false --text-encoder-cpu-offload --enable-torch-compile false ``` **Bench command** ```bash python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving --dataset vbench --task text-to-video --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1 --port 30000 --num-inference-steps 4 --num-frames 61 --width 832 --height 480 --fps 16 ``` **Serving benchmark results (e2e, s):** | branch| Latency Mean | | --- | --- | | main | 10.04 | | this PR | 10.04 |

items.title: [Fix] dsv41: Preserve tool-result image order and current-turn thinking
items.author: JustinTong0323
items.summary: Port the upstream chat-encoding fix into the V4.1 prompt encoder, which has the same two bugs: 1. When tool results arrive out of order and carry images, the prompt's placeholders are reordered but the returned image list keeps arrival order, so images bind to…
items.body:
## Motivation

Port the upstream chat-encoding fix [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash@314113f](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6) into the V4.1 prompt encoder, which has the same two bugs:

1. **Tool-result images out of order.** `encode_messages()` collected images before tool messages were merged and tool results re-sorted by call order. When tool results arrive out of `tool_call` order and carry images, the prompt's `<｜deepseek_image｜>` placeholders are reordered but the returned image list keeps arrival order, so images bind to the wrong placeholders.
2. **`drop_thinking` drops current-turn reasoning across tool calls.** A merged tool-result-only user message counted as a new user turn, so the reasoning of the current-turn assistant message preceding the tool results was stripped. Tool results alone do not start a new user turn; the current turn's reasoning should be kept until a real new user request arrives.

## Modifications

items.title: [Kernel] Allow registering OOT block-scaled FP8 linear kernels
items.author: R3hankhan123
items.summary: Lets out-of-tree platforms register block-scaled FP8 linear kernels by adding to. [Discussion: Looks good to me, the new branch matches the existing fp8/mxfp ones.]
items.body:
## Overview

Lets out-of-tree platforms register block-scaled FP8 linear kernels by adding `kernel_type="fp8_block"` to `register_linear_kernel`.

## Claims

- `register_linear_kernel(..., kernel_type="fp8_block")` adds the kernel to `_POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS`.
- OOT platforms can now serve `--quantization fp8_per_block`, which previously failed during kernel selection because the OOT platform had no entry in the block-kernel list.
- The docstring now lists every `kernel_type` the function accepts. It previously listed only `mp`, `int8` and `fp8`.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX).
- The change adds one `elif` branch that matches the existing `fp8`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, `mxfp4` and `mxfp6` branches. Existing kernel types behave as before.

## Details

`Fp8PerBlockOnlineLinearMethod` (and `Fp8LinearMethod` with `block_quant`) use a `GroupShape(1, 128)` activation key. Because `is_per_group()` is true for that shape, `init_fp8_linear_kernel` picks the kernel from `_POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS`. That dict only has entries for CUDA, ROCm, CPU and XPU, and `register_linear_kernel` had no way to add to it. An OOT platform that registered its FP8 kernel with `kernel_type="fp8"` therefore got per-tensor and per-channel FP8 but never block-wise.

To support both, an OOT plugin registers the same class twice, once as `"fp8"` and once as `"fp8_block"`. If that class subclasses `FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, the block path already builds it with `layer_param_names` (see the `issubclass` branch in `init_fp8_linear_kernel`), so no new base class or interface change is needed.

items.body:

## Motivation

Nemotron-H’s ModelOpt mixed-precision override rejects flashinfer_cutedsl for checkpoints containing W4A16_NVFP4 experts, even when the existing W4A16 opt-in is enabled.
Allow this supported explicit configuration, following the Qwen precedent in #39126 and using the implementation already introduced in #35120. Preserve the automatic Marlin selection established by #33543.

## Modifications

- Allow --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl when SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1 on SM100-family GPUs.
- Preserve auto → marlin, explicit Marlin support, and Nemotron’s existing --moe-a2a-backend none requirement.
- Update the validation error and add regression coverage for backend selection, the environment flag, unsupported hardware, and A2A restrictions.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 200 questions, thinking enabled, using the existing Nemotron CI evaluator.
B200, TP1, SGLang 0.5.21 / FlashInfer 0.6.18, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4;
temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 32, 16,384-token cap, speculation disabled.
Results from the confirmation run:

| Backend | Correct | Accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Marlin | 188/200 | 94.0% |
| CuTe DSL W4A16 | 190/200 | 95.0% |

No degradation observed in this run. The small difference is consistent with noise.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

### End-to-end serving

B200, TP1, SGLang 0.5.21 / FlashInfer 0.6.18, same NVFP4 checkpoint, concurrency
32, static 57,600 shared-prefix + 6,400 new input tokens and 400 output tokens,
8 warmup + 160 measured requests, AIPerf 0.12.0.

| MoE backend | Output tokens/s | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| Marlin | 1,576.63 | 1.00× |
| CuTe DSL W4A16 |  2,199.04 | 1.40× (+39.9%) |

Both measurements completed all 160 requests with zero errors and 64,000 output 
tokens.

### Isolated grouped-GEMM microbenchmarks

A separate B200 study invoking kernels directly (FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1).
Replayed nine expert-assignment patterns captured from Nemotron-3.5-Lightning,
using its checkpoint's NVFP4 expert weights and BF16 activations. These exercise
Nemotron's actual MoE workloads and help explain the serving speedup above.
Logical up K→N: 2688→1856; down: 1856→2688.

Selected cases below. Times are median milliseconds per grouped-GEMM invocation,
covering all assigned experts for one projection, without activation or final
combine. 
T is the number of input tokens before routing, and each case replays its full
captured per-expert assignment vector. These measurements help illustrate 
the kernel-level gains behind the serving speedup.

| Case | T | Projection | Marlin (ms) | CuTe DSL (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 32 | Up | 0.0439 | 0.0242 | 1.81× |
| A | 32 | Down | 0.0430 | 0.0231 | 1.86× |
| F | 16 | Up | 0.0675 | 0.0431 | 1.57× |
| F | 16 | Down | 0.0665 | 0.0448 | 1.48× |
| G | 2,129 | Up | 0.8267 | 0.1986 | 4.16× |
| G | 2,129 | Down | 0.7558 | 0.1988 | 3.80× |
| H | 14,896 | Up | 4.1495 | 0.8799 | 4.72× |
| H | 14,896 | Down | 3.4406 | 0.8886 | 3.87× |
| I | 15,436 | Up | 4.2833 | 0.9067 | 4.72× |
| I | 15,436 | Down | 3.5455 | 0.9163 | 3.87× |

CuTe DSL was faster in every tested case: **1.44–4.72×** for pure up/down GEMMs
and **1.67–5.10×** for up+ReLU² (fused CuTe DSL versus Marlin plus standalone
activation), across all nine measured patterns.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6939562][fix] Bound module_out_sizes read in LoRA param-fill kernel
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: fails on H100 (L0PostMerge 3021, DGXH100-PyTorch-Post-Merge-1) with at the first CUDA-graph LoRA decode step. In the block, every thread reads, where.
items.body:
## Description

`examples/test_gpt.py::test_gpt_oss_20b_lora_torch[gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter_NIM_r8-gpt-oss-20b]` fails on H100 (L0_PostMerge 3021, DGX_H100-PyTorch-Post-Merge-1) with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` at the first CUDA-graph LoRA decode step.

**Root cause.** `loraGroupGEMMParamFillRowReorderFusionKernel` runs with at least 256 threads per block. In the `OUT_SIZES_INDEX` block, every thread reads `module_out_sizes[module_id]`, where `module_id = threadIdx.x / max_lora_count`. That tensor has only `MODULE_COUNT` entries (3 int32 = 12 bytes for fused QKV), so threads past `max_lora_count * MODULE_COUNT` read out of bounds. `BlockStore3` drops their rows, so the result was never wrong, but the read faults whenever the allocation sits at the end of mapped memory. A GPU coredump names this kernel and block (Warp MMU Fault on the `module_out_sizes` load). With the caching allocator disabled, compute-sanitizer reports 10 invalid 4-byte reads past the 12-byte allocation. #20188 changed the allocation layout enough that this test now hits it every time; the bug itself dates back to #8279.

**Fix.** Read `module_out_sizes` only for `module_id < MODULE_COUNT`. The output for real problems is unchanged.

## Test Coverage

On computelab H100-80GB with the CI image `pytorch-26.09-...-202610130652-20175`:
- Same source built with and without the fix, failing test run 5x each: base fails 5/5 with the IMA, fix passes 5/5 with the expected text.
- The same op call under compute-sanitizer memcheck (`PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`): 10 errors before, 0 after; `out_sizes` is correct.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/peft/{test_lora,test_lora_autotuner,test_fp8_lora_grouped_gemm_regressions,test_moe_lora_cuda_graph_params}.py` and `thop/parallel_hw_agnostic/test_custom_ops.py`: 37 passed.
- l0_h100 LoRA entries `unittest/_torch/modules/tests_lora_modules` and `test_qwen_moe_routed_expert_multi_lora_varying_ranks[eager|cudagraph]`: passed.

No waiver exists for this bug.

Fixes https://nvbugs/6939562

- The reported CUDA-graph failure and test results were not independently verified.

items.title: [Bugfix][Mistral] Route json_schema without tools to schema-only grammar
items.author: joa-stdn
items.summary: Fixes MistralToolParser generating an overly permissive Lark grammar when json_schema is specified without tools, failing to enforce structured output constraints.
items.body:
## Why

When a chat completion request sets `response_format=json_schema` (or an equivalent `structured_outputs`) and omits tools, `MistralToolParser.adjust_request` normalizes `tool_choice=null` to `MistralToolChoiceEnum.auto` and falls through to `grammar_factory.get_lark_from_jinja` with `tools=None, json_schema=X, json_only=False`.

That renders:

```lark
start: body | SAFE_WS? %json {USER_SCHEMA}
body: content | (content? fcalls)
fcalls: ([TOOL_CALLS] SAFE_WS? /.+/ [ARGS] SAFE_WS? %json {"type":"object"} SAFE_WS?)+
content: ...
```

The grammar permits free text and wildcard `[TOOL_CALLS] /.+/ [ARGS] {anything}` tool-call emissions alongside the schema branch. The user asked for a schema-constrained output; the grammar does not enforce it. In practice a model trained with tools-in-prompt is biased against emitting `[TOOL_CALLS]` without tools, so outputs are *usually* fine — but the structural guarantee the API advertises isn't held.

## Reachability

Reachable from the OpenAI-compatible API with `tools=None` and `response_format=json_schema` when either:
- `tool_choice: null` is explicitly in the JSON (several OpenAI SDK clients send this by default), or
- `tool_choice` is unset *and* the client uses `structured_outputs` (through the equivalent null path).

The request validator at `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py` rejects `tool_choice="auto"` / `"required"` without tools, so only `null` / `"none"` (/omitted) reach the parser.

## Fix

Route `(json_schema set, no tools)` to `get_lark_for_json_schema` regardless of `tool_choice`. The previously-handled `tool_choice="none"` + tools + schema case is preserved by an added match arm.

```python
has_tools = mistral_tools is not None and len(mistral_tools) > 0
match tool_choice, has_tools, json_schema is not None:
    case _, False, True:
        lark_grammar = grammar_factory.get_lark_for_json_schema(...)
    case MistralToolChoiceEnum.none, True, True:
        lark_grammar = grammar_factory.get_lark_for_json_schema(...)
    case _, _, _:
        lark_grammar = grammar_factory.get_lark_from_jinja(..., json_only=False)
```

Resulting grammar for the buggy request becomes:
```lark
start: SAFE_WS? %json {USER_SCHEMA}
```

## Duplicate-work checks

- \`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search "mistral json_schema tools"\` — no overlapping PR.
- \`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search "get_lark_from_jinja"\` — nothing.
- \`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search "parser/mistral"\` — related but unrelated (`[Bugfix][Mistral] Map arbitrary tool call IDs`, docs clarifications, etc.).

## Tests

Added `test_adjust_request_json_schema_without_tools_uses_json_schema_factory` parametrized over the two API-reachable `tool_choice` values when `tools` is unset (`null` and `"none"`). The test stubs `get_lark_for_json_schema` with a sentinel return value and wraps `get_lark_from_jinja` to assert it is never called directly, defending against the delegation inside `get_lark_for_json_schema`.

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py -v
...
167 passed in 52.07s
```

Pre-commit (`pre-commit run --files vllm/parser/mistral.py tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py`) is green including mypy, SPDX headers, forbidden-imports, and test-tethering checks.

## Model evaluation

This change tightens an existing structured-output grammar from "schema OR text OR wildcard tool call" to "schema only" when no tools are present. It does not affect any path where tools are provided, nor any non-schema path. Model behavior on grammar-constrained generation is unchanged for all tool-using requests; for the fixed path, output is already dominated by the schema branch at inference time due to the training distribution (models rarely emit `[TOOL_CALLS]` without tools in the prompt), so observable output quality is not expected to regress. A full generation eval was not run because the change is a grammar-structure correctness fix rather than a numerical change, and the test suite covers the routing contract.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to prepare this patch. The reporting human reviewed every changed line and ran the test commands above.

items.title: [None][doc] Fix CI overview description of post-merge pipeline
items.author: sharabeshj-nvda
items.summary: The "CI pipelines" section of says the post-merge pipeline is "defined in " and "runs every test marked ". Both parts are wrong: - The post-merge pipeline is a separate Jenkins job that runs the same as pre-merge.
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
- The documentation now identifies `jenkins/L0_MergeRequest.groovy` as the post-merge job definition and `jenkins/L0_Test.groovy` as the child-job stage mapping.
- The unit-test section now describes tests as entries in test-db YAML files that run through mapped `L0_Test.groovy` stages. No source code, configuration, or test-list files changed.

## QA Engineer Review
No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `docs/source/developer-guide/ci-overview.md`: No behavior changes. Verify the pipeline and unit-test descriptions match the current Jenkins stage selection and test-db YAML mappings.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

The "CI pipelines" section of `docs/source/developer-guide/ci-overview.md` says the post-merge pipeline is "defined in `jenkins/L0_Test.groovy`" and "runs every test marked `post_merge`". Both parts are wrong:

- The post-merge pipeline is a separate Jenkins job that runs the same `jenkins/L0_MergeRequest.groovy` as pre-merge.
- `jenkins/L0_Test.groovy` holds the stage-name → test-db YAML map, including the `Post-Merge` stages. It runs as a child job in both pipelines.
- Post-merge runs the pre-merge stages as well as the multi-GPU and `Post-Merge` stages.

This PR rewrites that sentence. It also corrects the "Unit tests" section, which said unit tests are invoked from `L0_MergeRequest.groovy` and need no hardware-stage mapping. Nothing else in the doc changes.

### Evidence

Links are pinned to dac84b01a6.

1. **There is no separate post-merge Jenkinsfile.** `L0_MergeRequest.groovy` recognizes the post-merge job by name (`env.JOB_NAME ==~ /.*PostMerge.*/`). For that job it turns fail-fast off ([L95][mr-95]) and sets `IS_POST_MERGE` in `testFilter` ([L247][mr-247]).
2. **The child test jobs receive `testFilter`, including `IS_POST_MERGE`, as JSON.** In `launchStages`, each `launchJob(...)` call for `L0_Test-{x86_64,SBSA}-{Single,Multi}-GPU` passes `testFilter` serialized with `writeJSON` ([x86_64 Single-GPU][mr-x86-single], [x86_64 Multi-GPU][mr-x86-multi], [SBSA Single-GPU][mr-sbsa-single], [SBSA Multi-GPU][mr-sbsa-multi]). `L0_Test.groovy` merges it back from `env.testFilter` ([L7573-L7574][test-7573]).
3. **Post-merge adds stages to the pre-merge set.** In `launchTestJobs` in `jenkins/L0_Test.groovy`:
   - Selection starts from the pre-merge set, `parallelJobs - multiGpuJobs - postMergeJobs - onDemandJobs`. `postMergeJobs` is every stage whose name contains `Post-Merge` ([L7255-L7258][test-7255]).
   - When `IS_POST_MERGE` is set, it adds `multiGpuJobs` and `postMergeJobs` ([L7278-L7283][test-7278]).
   - `getMakoArgsFromStageName` renders `stage=post_merge` for `Post-Merge` stages and `stage=pre_merge` for every other stage ([L4358-L4361][test-4358]). So post-merge also runs the `pre_merge` test entries, not only the `post_merge` ones.

**Unit tests.** `L0_MergeRequest.groovy` has no `pytest` call. Its `tests/unittest/` paths appear only in the changed-file lists of `getMultiGpuFileChanged` and `getOnlyOneGroupChanged`. Unit tests are `unittest/...` entries in 21 test-db YAML files, including `l0_a30.yml`, which this doc already quotes. `L0_Test.groovy` stages run them like any other entry; the test-list parser maps them to `test_unittests.py::test_unittests_v2[...]` ([test_list_parser.py][parser-172]).

**`/bot run --post-merge` is not the post-merge job.** It also sets `IS_POST_MERGE`, so a PR run gets the post-merge stage set. In every other respect it stays a pre-merge run, and the doc does not describe it as the post-merge job:

- Fail-fast stays on ([L95][mr-95]).
- The multi-GPU stages it forces on ([L1690-L1693][mr-1690]) still need the multi-GPU approval label; only the post-merge job name is exempt ([L1090-L1093][mr-1090]).
- CBTS can still narrow the tests. CBTS defers for the post-merge job ([L1243-L1246][mr-1243]), but `IS_POST_MERGE` is deliberately not one of its defer flags ([L1600-L1611][mr-1600]).
- No Docker images are built ([L3093-L3096][mr-3093]).

## Test Coverage

Documentation only; no tests apply. `pre-commit run --files docs/source/developer-guide/ci-overview.md` passes.

items.title: [megatron, ckpt] fix: synchronize overlapping parameters before checkpoint save
items.author: ewan0x79
items.summary: Fix checkpoint saving in SFT and RL training using the Megatron engine with standard DDP, distributed optimization, and parameter-gather overlap enabled (DP > 1). After an optimizer step, the updated weights are normally synchronized before the next forward pa…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix checkpoint saving in SFT and RL training using the Megatron engine with standard DDP, distributed optimization, and parameter-gather overlap enabled (DP > 1).

After an optimizer step, the updated weights are normally synchronized before the next forward pass. If training saves a checkpoint before that synchronization—for example, at a periodic checkpoint or the end of training—the save can succeed while some model weights are still out of date. **Both native Megatron-Core (MCore) checkpoints and Hugging Face-format exports can be affected**, because both backends read weights from the model. The saved weights may therefore not fully reflect the completed training step or match the saved optimizer state.

This PR completes parameter synchronization before either checkpoint backend reads model weights. FP8/FP4 configurations are excluded. Two-GPU BF16 validation covers both formats, including save/load correctness and training continuation.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for similar PRs: [overlap_param_gather](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+overlap_param_gather), [start_param_sync + checkpoint](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+start_param_sync+checkpoint), and [megatron + checkpoint](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+megatron+checkpoint). On October 16, 2026, the duplicate-work check also examined the titles and bodies of 731 open PRs using parameter-synchronization keywords. The closest matches were inspected, and no open PR implementing this save-boundary fix was identified. The focused searches were repeated before opening this PR.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`. No breaking API change.

**Not duplicate work:** [PR #8029](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8029) establishes weight readiness before fused LM-head consumption, whereas this PR synchronizes model parameters at the checkpoint-save boundary. This change neither depends on nor includes that implementation. [#5617](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/5617) adds `aggressive_empty_cache(force_sync=True)` after saving; its device/cache synchronization is not a DDP parameter all-gather. [#8003](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8003) and [#8056](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8056) drain async checkpoint queues at trainer shutdown; they do not replace synchronization before the checkpoint snapshot.

No dedicated public issue for this synchronous-save reproduction was identified.

### Test

#### GPU validation

**Setup:** 2 × H20-141G, Qwen3-1.7B, BF16, standard DistributedOptimizer, DP2 / TP1 / PP1 / CP1, synchronous saving. The final implementation was tested with overlap off/on in two separate runs: HF/Bridge model save/load, and native MCore model-shard save/load with HF export alongside it.

##### Checkpoint correctness

**Goal:** verify that saved and restored model weights include the completed optimizer update.

Train for two steps and save immediately after the optimizer update, without another forward pass. Compute the **expected updated model weights** from the optimizer's FP32 master weights, cast to BF16 in independent tensors. This computation does not synchronize or overwrite the live model.

- **HF export:** compare the saved files elementwise against the expected updated weights converted to HF layout.
- **Post-save model:** compare the in-memory model parameters against the expected updated weights.
- **Fresh-process restore:** call the unchanged `engine.load_checkpoint()` API, then compare restored model parameters against BF16 weights reconstructed from the restored optimizer's FP32 master weights.

**Unpatched baseline (HF/Bridge):** overlap disabled produced correct weights; overlap enabled produced mismatches in both the HF export and the restored model.

**Final fix:** all elementwise comparisons pass:

| Model save/load backend | Parameter-gather overlap | HF-export mismatches | Restored-model mismatches |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| HF/Bridge | Off | 0 | 0 |
| HF/Bridge | On | 0 | 0 |
| Native MCore | Off | 0 | 0 |
| Native MCore | On | 0 | 0 |

Restored-model and post-save model mismatches are zero on both ranks in all four configurations. HF weights were also exported in the native MCore run; native model restore loaded `model/dist_ckpt`, not the HF export, with no HF fallback. The unpatched baseline used HF/Bridge; an unpatched native MCore GPU negative control was not run.

##### Training continuation

**Goal:** verify that saving or resuming a checkpoint does not change subsequent training.

For the fixed implementation, compare three training paths for each backend and overlap setting:

- **A:** train four steps continuously.
- **B:** save at step 2, then continue in the same process.
- **C:** restore B's step-2 checkpoint in a fresh process, then continue.

- **Training metrics:** B matches A's loss, grad_norm, and learning rate exactly for all four steps; C matches A's steps 3–4 exactly.
- **Final states:** at step 4, model, optimizer, scheduler, and RNG hashes match for corresponding ranks across A/B/C.

Both model backends pass with overlap enabled and disabled. The unpatched baseline did not include this continuation comparison.

These experiments validate engine checkpoint save/load and continuation in the BF16 synchronous-save setup above, not a full SFT/RL trainer end-to-end run. Other precision, parallelism, and offload configurations were not tested.

See the expandable validation details below for the environment, comparison methodology, and numerical results.

### API and Usage Example

No CLI arguments, configuration fields, function signatures, checkpoint formats, or loading APIs change. Eligible configurations need no additional setting, and training overlap remains enabled. Checkpoint saving pays the necessary gather/wait cost; no throughput improvement or zero-overhead claim is made.

### Design & Code Changes

The distributed optimizer updates the parameter shards owned by each rank. With parameter-gather overlap, publication of the full model weights can be deferred until the next forward pre-hook. Checkpoint writers read model weights directly and do not execute that forward boundary.

#### Save boundary

In `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`, call `start_param_sync(force_sync=True)` under `torch.no_grad()` after GPU restoration and before the checkpoint manager reads the model. A synchronization exception prevents that rank from entering checkpoint writing; cross-rank failure recovery is not claimed. Existing barrier, offload, and load logic is unchanged.
#### Eligibility

Synchronize a chunk only when all five conditions hold:

- The chunk is a Megatron `DistributedDataParallel` wrapper.
- `chunk.ddp_config.use_distributed_optimizer` is enabled.
- `chunk.ddp_config.overlap_param_gather` is enabled.
- The effective `self.tf_config.fp8` is disabled.
- The effective `self.tf_config.fp4` is disabled.

FP8/FP4 paths can require optimizer staging before an explicit gather, particularly MXFP8 with shared parameter/gradient buffers. This PR does not implement that lifecycle. Excluded configurations retain their previous save behavior; their checkpoint correctness is not guaranteed by this change. items.title: [Fix] SamplingParams: validate stop_token_ids against vocab_size
items.author: saitarrun
items.summary: A entry outside crashes the server whenever any request in the batch sets: checked keys against but not, so the bad id reached, where into a CUDA tensor trips a device-side assert and takes down all in-flight requests (not just the offending one). Fixes …
items.body:
## Motivation

A `stop_token_ids` entry outside `[0, vocab_size)` crashes the server whenever
any request in the batch sets `min_new_tokens > 0`: `SamplingParams.verify()`
checked `logit_bias` keys against `vocab_size` but not `stop_token_ids`, so the
bad id reached `BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer._prepare`
(`penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:65`), where `scatter_add_` into a
`[batch, vocab_size + 1]` CUDA tensor trips a device-side assert and takes down
all in-flight requests (not just the offending one).

Fixes #44535 (item 2 of #31597, whose fix PR #31561 was auto-closed before
review).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py`: `SamplingParams.verify()`
  now rejects `stop_token_ids` outside `[0, vocab_size)` with a `ValueError`,
  mirroring the existing `logit_bias` check. The check runs at admission time
  in `TokenizerManager` before any GPU work, so `http_server` maps it to
  HTTP 400 — the same behavior the issue asked for. This single point covers
  `/generate`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/v1/completions`, since all three
  funnel through `verify()`.
- `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py`: added four
  `TestSamplingParamsVerify` cases — out-of-vocab id raises, negative id
  raises, `[0, vocab_size - 1]` boundaries accepted, and unset
  `stop_token_ids` skips the check.

## Tests

- Exercised the actual `verify()` method (extracted verbatim from the repo
  source via AST, run with a stub `self` and a stub for
  `get_request_reasoning_end_token_ids`): in-range set passes, `None` passes,
  `1000000` / `-1` / `32000` with `vocab_size=32000` raise with message
  `"stop_token_ids must be in [0, 31999], got <id>"`, including the issue's
  exact repro combination (`min_new_tokens=1`, `stop_token_ids=[1000000]`).
- New unit tests in `test_sampling_params.py` assert the same behavior.
- Not verifiable here: a live server end-to-end run (no GPU on this machine),
  and the full registered CPU suite (the `sglang` package needs heavy
  third-party deps not installed in this environment).
- `ruff check --select F401,F821,F823,UP037`: pass. `ruff format --check`:
  pass. `py_compile`: pass. `git diff --check`: clean, no added line over
  88 columns.

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: reject routing replay when vLLM ran a different prompt
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Rollout routing replay (R3) returns one routed-experts row per token vLLM ran. The agent loop places those rows on the trainer's prompt by position. [Discussion: This may take a few minutes, please wait...]
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Rollout routing replay (R3) returns one routed-experts row per token vLLM ran. The agent loop places those rows on the trainer's prompt by position. Nothing checks that the two prompts are the same token sequence.

They can differ for multimodal prompts. vLLM's multimodal processor expands each image placeholder into a span, so the prompt vLLM runs can be longer than the prompt the trainer replays on. When that happens, every row from the first divergent token on lands on the wrong token, and the tail is cut by `routed_experts[: len(prompt_ids) + response_length]`. Nothing fails. In the multimodal DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash run reported in vllm-project/vllm#61097, R3 made the train-inference mismatch worse than running without it.

This PR compares vLLM's prompt (`RequestOutput.prompt_token_ids`) with the trainer's prompt before returning routed experts, and raises if they differ. A row is the routing of one token in one context. A different prompt has different tokens and contexts, so no reordering of rows can be correct. With R3 enabled, failing is the only safe option.

The comparison uses the prompt the trainer holds, not the deduplicated one sent to vLLM. Qwen2.5-VL's deduplicated `<|image_pad|>` runs are re-expanded by vLLM to the same span, so they still pass.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=routed+experts
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

`tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_submitter_gate_on_cpu.py` gets one parametrized case that drives `vLLMHttpServer.generate` with R3 enabled, against a mocked engine that records the prompt it is sent and reports the prompt it ran:

| case | vLLM prompt | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `same-prompt` | same as the trainer's | routed experts returned |
| `qwen-vl-dedup-reexpanded` | the trainer's span, as vLLM re-expands the deduplicated Qwen2.5-VL prompt | one placeholder sent; routed experts returned |
| `engine-expanded-further` | the image expanded to more placeholders | `ValueError` |
| `same-length-other-tokens` | same length, different tokens | `ValueError` |

The whole file passes (20 tests) with the vLLM nightly `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7` on GB200. Each mutation fails only the listed cases:
- removing the check fails `engine-expanded-further` and `same-length-other-tokens`;
- comparing only lengths fails `same-length-other-tokens`;
- comparing against the deduplicated prompt sent to vLLM fails `qwen-vl-dedup-reexpanded`;
- sending the undeduplicated prompt to vLLM fails `qwen-vl-dedup-reexpanded`.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. Only the failure behavior changes: a rollout with `enable_rollout_routing_replay=True` whose prompt differs from the one vLLM ran now fails with:

```
ValueError: Rollout routing replay for request <id>: the prompt vLLM ran (270 tokens) differs from the trainer's prompt (77 tokens) from position <i>. Multimodal placeholders must expand to the same tokens on both sides.
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `vLLMHttpServer.generate`: keep the trainer's `prompt_ids`; send the Qwen2.5-VL-deduplicated copy to vLLM as `engine_prompt_ids`; with R3 enabled, raise if `final_res.prompt_token_ids != prompt_ids`.
- Test as above.

Scope: only the vLLM server. The SGLang server also returns routed experts, but its output does not report the prompt it ran, so there is nothing to compare against there.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `ruff format` and `ruff check` (v0.12.2) pass on the changed files.
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). Not needed: no user-facing option changes.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. The case is in an existing `*_on_cpu.py` file.
