items.title: [Feat] beam: Add native Beam serving support
items.author: Jiminator
items.summary: Add native serving support for Beam, a 501B-parameter MoE model with 23B active parameters and a 1M-token context configuration. [Discussion: <!-- mintlify-preview-comment-lmsysorg-beam --> Preview deployment for your docs.]
items.body:
## Motivation

Add native serving support for Beam, a 501B-parameter MoE model with 23B active parameters and a 1M-token context configuration.

## Modifications

- Implement Beam's hybrid sliding-window/full attention, SSMax query scaling, attention output gating, sandwich normalization, depth-scaled residuals, and grouped MoE routing.
- Support BF16, ModelOpt NVFP4, and compressed-tensors FP8 checkpoints, with BF16 LoRA serving.
- Integrate DFlash2, attention data parallelism, unified hybrid KV allocation, prefix caching, and HiCache. DFlash attention DP supports the matching FlashInfer MegaMoE runner/all-to-all configuration.
- Add Beam reasoning and tool-call parsing across Chat Completions, Responses, and Messages, including checkpoint response-template handling and structured-output constraints.
- Add fused projection/norm/residual/collective paths, router GEMV/BF16x3/cuTile kernels, and GB300 MoE tuning, together with registered unit, kernel, and end-to-end coverage.
- Include the serving dependency and Docker updates used by this implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

items.title: [Fix] unified-memory: Refuse allocation before post-capture resize
items.author: mmangkad
items.summary: aborts with exit -6 ( in ) since #42930. It was seen on the 5090 runner and reproduces on H200 (SM90); the parent of 8d229d96e0 passes. [Discussion: /rerun-test test/registered/unit/memcache/testunifiedpostcapturesizing.py]
items.body:
## Motivation

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_post_capture_sizing.py` aborts with exit -6 (`CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `_zero_pages_kernel`) since #42930. It was seen on the 5090 runner and reproduces on H200 (SM90); the parent of 8d229d96e0 passes.

With post-capture KV sizing, `UnifiedKVPool.finalize_backing` backs only the final byte prefix of the reserved VA, but the unified SWA allocator keeps pricing the whole reservation until `resize()` runs. An allocation in that window gets a top-end SWA page past the backed bytes (page 131071 of a 64 MiB reservation with 16 MiB backed). Before #42930 this only touched bookkeeping for MHA pools. #42930 zeroes MHA page envelopes on hand-out, so the same allocation now writes to unmapped memory.

The production path (`kv_pool_runtime.py`) calls `finalize_backing` and then `resize` straight away, so this was hit only by the test. It is still a latent fault for any allocation before `resize`.

## Modifications

- `UnifiedSWAAllocatorBase.__init__` sets `_awaiting_resize` when post-capture backing is active; `UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.resize()` clears it. `ensure_capacity()` raises until then; every allocation path goes through it.
- Test: add "allocation before finalize_backing" (the construction-to-finalize window, where graph capture and prewarm run) and "allocation between finalize_backing and resize" subtests that expect the new error. The "resize with live allocations" subtest now allocates after `resize` and checks that a second `resize` is rejected as non-empty.

## Test plan (H200)

- `test_unified_post_capture_sizing.py`: OK (was 2 errors / MMU fault on HEAD)
- `test_multi_ended_allocator`, `test_kv_index_translator`, `test_kv_cache_configurator_draft_gate`, `test_unified_handout_zeroing`, `test_fused_draft_placement`: OK

### End-to-end (H200)

`openai/gpt-oss-20b` (hybrid SWA, fa3) with the cookbook flags (`--reasoning-parser gpt-oss --tool-call-parser gpt-oss`, TP1) plus `--enable-unified-memory`. sgl-eval 0.1.3 gsm8k, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, reasoning effort low, max_tokens 8192.

| Run | Startup path | gsm8k | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING=1` | Reserved VA, graph capture, then `finalize_backing` and `resize` (105 GB of KV) | 96.0% | 0 |
| Baseline (post-capture off) | Pool allocated up front | 95.5% | 0 |

The post-capture server started cleanly with no "cannot allocate before resize" error, so nothing on the real startup path allocates before `resize`.

items.title: Add SVE Paged Attention FP32/FP16 and BF16 kernels
items.author: sanketkaleoss
items.summary: Adds SVE-accelerated Paged Attention kernels for FP16/FP32/BF16 on ARM CPUs, improving register utilization and instruction scheduling over NEON.
items.body:
This PR enables and optimizes the Paged Attention kernel on ARM CPUs for the FP16/FP32 and BF16 paths. It optimizes the SVE CPU attention GEMM kernel by improving register utilization, FP16 widening, FP32 FMLA efficiency and instruction scheduling, and adds an SVE256 BFMMLA kernel for BF16.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Depends on #50573.** This PR is built on top of the changes in #50573. Build with those changes applied to test it, and merge this PR only after #50573 is merged.

**Major changes**:

- Add/enable the SVE attention path for PA (Paged Attention) on ARM CPUs.
- Improve utilization of the SVE256 datapath through better register allocation and kernel scheduling, rather than relying on a raw width advantage over NEON.
- Remove intermediate register-allocation abstractions and move the SVE implementation into a self-contained ISA-specific file for performance gain.
- Apply dtype-specific optimizations for FP16 and FP32 while preserving the best-performing instruction patterns.
- BF16 PA kernel (SVE256 BFMMLA):
  - Follows the upstream NEON BFMMLA structure: Q packed once in `copy_q_heads_tile`, K/V caches in the `[..][32]` group layout.
  - Each SVE256 `bfmmla` computes two 2x2 tiles (one `ld1rq` A load feeds both 128-bit segments), with tile width chosen by row count (up to 32 columns).
  - Independent of `ProbabilityTokenStore`: P is packed inside the PV GEMM.
- Builds that are not SVE256 (e.g. SVE128) fall back to the NEON GEMM and NEON BFMMLA kernels.

**Performance** (Graviton3):

| Dtype    |     NEON |          SVE | SVE vs NEON gain |
| -------- | -------: | -----------: | ---------------: |
| **FP32** | 76.30 ms | **71.95 ms** |        **+5.7%** |
| **FP16** | 76.27 ms | **74.19 ms** |        **+2.7%** |
| **BF16** | 29.65 ms | **25.59 ms** |       **+13.7%** |

**Testing**:

- Added tests for the SVE PA path covering FP32, FP16 and BF16.
- Benchmarked with `benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_attn.py`

SVE is approximately 5.7% faster for FP32, 2.7% for FP16 and 13.7% for BF16 than NEON on the tested Graviton3 workload.

BF16 workload: decode, batch 64, 32 query / 8 KV heads, head size 128, KV length 2048, block size 32, single core; mean of 3 runs.

Co-Authored by:
@abhijain1204fujitsu
@madhur-fujitsu

items.title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Use a file rendezvous for offline single-node DP
items.author: stefankoncarevic
items.summary: Fixes a probe-then-bind race in the offline data-parallel launcher by switching to a file-based rendezvous for port selection, eliminating EADDRINUSE flakiness.
items.body:
## The failure

[AMD CI build 14810](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14810), group `(MI300) Distributed Features`, on the `data_parallel_offline.py` example:

```
torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to listen on any local network address. port: 44122, useIpv6: false, code: -98, name: EADDRINUSE, message: address already in use
```

## The problem

An offline data-parallel launcher picks the group's port by probing: it binds port 0, reads back whatever the kernel assigned, closes the socket, and hands the bare number to every rank through `VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT`. The ranks bind it later, from other processes.

Nothing owns the port in between, so any process on the host can take it and the kernel will hand it out again on the next probe. Rank 0 then cannot open the store and the remaining ranks wait out the full init timeout, so a job that fails this way also runs about ten minutes longer than normal. This is the generic probe-then-bind race: the launcher chooses a port it never binds.

## Where it is tracked

[RFC #51275](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51275) catalogues the probe-then-bind sites and lists `data_parallel_offline.py` as **Uncovered**. This PR covers that row. Related, none of which cover this path:

- #51018 fixed the same race for the DP world group, but only when a coordination store exists, which offline runs do not have.
- #61102 changes the port pool the probe draws from, so the race remains.
- #58312 applies the file-store pattern to the MoE test launcher.

## How often

Rarely, but it blocks the whole group, and it depends on the state of the node rather than on the code, which is why it looks random.

- One failure in the last ten AMD nightlies (14162 through 14707 passed, 14810 failed). Retrying on a different node cleared it.
- Of 2000 consecutive port probes on a CI host, 141 (about 7%) returned a number an earlier probe had already handed out.
- Under sustained connection churn, 3 of 25 probed ports could no longer be bound 3 seconds later, with the same `EADDRINUSE`. Ports that passed through `TIME_WAIT` are the usual reason.

## The change

The number stays, but it is no longer used as a port. Ranks treat it as a rendezvous token and meet on a file store named after it, in a temporary directory owned by the launcher. Every rank derives the same path on its own from values it already has, so no extra coordination is needed and concurrent runs get separate directories. The launcher removes its directory once the ranks exit; one left behind by a killed run is harmless, because the next run's writes shadow it.

This applies only when every rank rendezvous on this host. Multi-node rendezvous and AITER custom all-reduce, which requires a TCP store, keep the previous behaviour.

## Tests

`tests/v1/engine/test_dp_world_group_port.py` gains a case that holds the launcher's port with another socket and then brings up two offline ranks; it reproduces the CI failure exactly on `main` and passes with this change. `tests/utils_/test_network_utils.py` covers the new path helpers.

items.title: Validate stop_token_ids against vocab_size in SamplingParams.verify
items.author: saitarrun
items.summary: A entry outside crashes the server whenever any request in the batch sets: checked keys against but not, so the bad id reached, where into a CUDA tensor trips a device-side assert and takes down all in-flight requests (not just the offending one). Fixes …
items.body:
## Motivation

A `stop_token_ids` entry outside `[0, vocab_size)` crashes the server whenever
any request in the batch sets `min_new_tokens > 0`: `SamplingParams.verify()`
checked `logit_bias` keys against `vocab_size` but not `stop_token_ids`, so the
bad id reached `BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer._prepare`
(`penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:65`), where `scatter_add_` into a
`[batch, vocab_size + 1]` CUDA tensor trips a device-side assert and takes down
all in-flight requests (not just the offending one).

Fixes #44535 (item 2 of #31597, whose fix PR #31561 was auto-closed before
review).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py`: `SamplingParams.verify()`
  now rejects `stop_token_ids` outside `[0, vocab_size)` with a `ValueError`,
  mirroring the existing `logit_bias` check. The check runs at admission time
  in `TokenizerManager` before any GPU work, so `http_server` maps it to
  HTTP 400 — the same behavior the issue asked for. This single point covers
  `/generate`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/v1/completions`, since all three
  funnel through `verify()`.
- `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py`: added four
  `TestSamplingParamsVerify` cases — out-of-vocab id raises, negative id
  raises, `[0, vocab_size - 1]` boundaries accepted, and unset
  `stop_token_ids` skips the check.

## Tests

- Exercised the actual `verify()` method (extracted verbatim from the repo
  source via AST, run with a stub `self` and a stub for
  `get_request_reasoning_end_token_ids`): in-range set passes, `None` passes,
  `1000000` / `-1` / `32000` with `vocab_size=32000` raise with message
  `"stop_token_ids must be in [0, 31999], got <id>"`, including the issue's
  exact repro combination (`min_new_tokens=1`, `stop_token_ids=[1000000]`).
- New unit tests in `test_sampling_params.py` assert the same behavior.
- Not verifiable here: a live server end-to-end run (no GPU on this machine),
  and the full registered CPU suite (the `sglang` package needs heavy
  third-party deps not installed in this environment).
- `ruff check --select F401,F821,F823,UP037`: pass. `ruff format --check`:
  pass. `py_compile`: pass. `git diff --check`: clean, no added line over
  88 columns.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] MoRIIO: treat FINISHED_STOPPED as producer decode completion
items.author: Hmache
items.summary: Fixes MoRIIO KV connector to export prefill KV blocks when a request completes via FINISHED_STOPPED (EOS/stop token), not just FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED.
items.body:
Fixes #61389

## What the issue was
On the prefill (producer) side, a request with `do_remote_decode=True` and `max_tokens=1` that samples EOS or a stop token as its first token finishes with `FINISHED_STOPPED`. MoRIIO ignored this status, so the prefill KV blocks were never exported and the decode side got no remote block metadata.

## Why it happened
`MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.request_finished()` in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py` only continued when `request.status == FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED`. `check_stop()` sets `FINISHED_STOPPED` before the length cap is checked, so the method returned `(False, None)` early. The NIXL connector (`nixl/pull_scheduler.py`) already accepts both statuses.

## The fix
Accept `FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED` and `FINISHED_STOPPED`. Other statuses (e.g. aborted) still return early. Two files, 46 insertions, 3 deletions.

## Not covered
No end-to-end test with a real MoRIIO P/D deployment (needs ROCm hardware). I did not audit other MoRIIO paths for similar status assumptions.

## Validation
Run:
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on both changed files: pass.
- `python -m py_compile` on both files, `git diff --check`: pass.
- An isolated harness that executes the actual `request_finished` method body (extracted from the source) with stubbed dependencies, before and after the change. Before: `FINISHED_STOPPED` returned `delay_free=False, params=None`. After: `delay_free=True`, params with `remote_block_ids` returned, request tracked for deferred send. `FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED` unchanged; `FINISHED_ABORTED` still returns `(False, None)`.

Not run: the new pytest tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_routing.py`). torch is not installable in my environment, and the module imports vLLM. Please run them locally; the stop-status case should fail without the source change and pass with it.

## Steps to test
```
git fetch https://github.com/Hmache/vllm fix/moriio-finished-stopped-remote-decode
git checkout FETCH_HEAD
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_routing.py -v
# to confirm the regression test fails without the fix:
git checkout HEAD~1 -- vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_routing.py -v
```

AI assistance was used to prepare this change; I reviewed it.

items.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Honor apply_router_weight_on_input in MoE LoRA
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Fixes MoE LoRA path to correctly respect apply_router_weight_on_input for top-1 routing by fixing W13 input scaling and double-weighting of W2 delta.
items.body:
## Purpose

With `apply_router_weight_on_input` (top-1 routing, e.g. Llama4), `prepare()` multiplies the MoE input by the routing weight and the base GEMMs skip the weight on the output. The MoE LoRA path did not follow that contract, in two places, on every LoRA-capable experts class:

1. **W13 LoRA input missing the weight.** The modular kernel stashed the unscaled `hidden_states` as `lora_ctx.original_hidden_states`, which the W13 LoRA reads (Triton experts on a single rank, quantized TRTLLM path). Fix: stash the input scaled the same way prepare scales it.
2. **W2 LoRA delta weighted a second time.** `apply_w2_lora` always multiplied the delta by `topk_weights` (`add_lora_w2` hardcodes `mul_routed_weight=True`). Fix: `apply_w2_lora(..., mul_routed_weight=...)`; the Triton, Marlin and OAI Triton experts pass `not apply_router_weight_on_input`. Inside, unit weights are used rather than passing `False` to the op, because the op's `mul_routed_weight` also selects the W2 row mapping.

The TRTLLM LoRA experts also passed the weights to FlashInfer's fused MoE finalize, which has no such switch; they now use unit weights when the flag is set (as `DeepGemmExperts` does).

The two errors sit on either side of the activation, so they do not cancel.

## Test Plan

New `tests/lora/test_moe_lora_router_weight_on_input.py`: modular kernel (`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular` + `TritonExperts`, BF16) with a real `PunicaWrapperGPU` LoRA context, top-1. With LoRA active, the layer on `(x, w, on_input=True)` must match the layer on `(x * w, ones, on_input=False)`, for both the naive (M=2) and sorted (M=32) LoRA block assignments.

## Test Result

GB300, vLLM nightly image af7f9488c with the changed files overlaid:
- without the fix: both cases fail (max abs diff 1.49 and 3.63);
- with the fix: 2 passed.

The TRTLLM change is not covered by the new test (needs SM100 + FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE LoRA); it follows the same contract.

items.title: fix(inference): support request-local FlashInfer sampling seeds
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Enable request-local seeded sampling in dynamic FlashInfer inference. Pass per-request and absolute token-position tensors through all four sampling dispatches, including saved positions for pending logits during async overlap.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Enable request-local seeded sampling in dynamic FlashInfer inference. Pass per-request `seed` and absolute token-position `offset` tensors through all four sampling dispatches, including saved positions for pending logits during async overlap. Reserve a disjoint 2^32-draw interval per token for rejection sampling.

Group seeded requests by filter mode so batch mates cannot change their sampling algorithm. Sample unseeded requests with the shared generator; seeded draws leave its state untouched. Allow seeded FlashInfer requests through engine admission while preserving speculative-seeding and missing-metadata errors.

**Draft — merge after the FlashInfer dependency bump.** Builds on the merged #7828 and depends on the merged [per-row tensor-indexing fix](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5745), and [FlashInfer #6251](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6251) for batch-independent Philox subsequences. The current dependency pin does not include the required fixes. The batch-reordering tests now pass normally against the upstream patch, and the engine backend restriction is removed in this draft.

## Validation

On GB200 with kernels JIT-built from the upstream FlashInfer patch:

- **66 passed** across `test_flashinfer_sampling.py`, `test_request_seed_sampling.py`, and `test_http_request_seed.py`, using `torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node 1`.
- Coverage includes all four FlashInfer dispatches, exact replay under side-stream contention, per-row seed/position changes, permutations, compaction and singleton batches, mixed seeded/unseeded RNG isolation, filter-mode isolation, gathered logits, output buffers, async position snapshots, engine admission, and HTTP seed propagation.
- Black, isort, Pylint, Ruff, kernel determinism coverage, and `git diff --check` passed. The repository formatter's nonblocking mypy step reports existing typing issues and unavailable dependency stubs; this is not a clean type-check result.

## Issue tracking

Related to #7827 and #7828. Replaces #7976, which closed after its stacked parent #7828 merged. This PR targets `main` directly.

items.title: [Perf] Fuse admission-time staged writes into fewer kernel calls
items.author: odysseusy
items.summary: A 3-commit series that extends the existing (introduced in #44944 for ) to three more places that still apply correlated writes with multiple separate calls, each paying its own CPU-side dispatch and kernel-launch overhead: 1.: + + -- always staged togethe…
items.body:
## Overview

A 3-commit series that extends the existing `FusedStagedWriter` (introduced in #44944 for `BlockTables`) to three more places that still apply correlated `StagedWriteTensor` writes with multiple separate calls, each paying its own CPU-side dispatch and kernel-launch overhead:

1. `RequestState` (`states.py`): `total_len` + `all_token_ids` + `num_computed_tokens` -- always staged together in `add_request()`. 3 calls -> 1.
2. `BadWordsState` (`bad_words.py`): `bad_word_token_ids` + `bad_word_offsets` -- always staged together. 2 calls -> 1.
3. `LogitBiasState` (`logit_bias.py`): `allowed_token_ids` + `logit_bias_token_ids` + `stop_token_ids` -- all int32, fused into 1. `logit_bias` itself is float32 and `FusedStagedWriter`'s content buffer is hardcoded to int32, so it keeps its own separate call (4 calls -> 2).

## How this was found

`py-spy` profiling (30 Hz, raw collapsed-stack format) of a running EngineCore process under decode-heavy concurrent load (128 concurrent requests, varied prompts, `vllm serve` on 2x RTX 5090) showed `UvaBufferPool.copy_to_uva` as a real, measurable chunk of self time, spread across many independent small call sites in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`. Grepping for `.apply_write()` call sites found 12+ places invoking it, only one of which (`BlockTables`) already uses the fused path.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `gh pr list`/`gh issue list` for `FusedStagedWriter`, `StagedWriteTensor`, `copy_to_uva`. Found:
- #44944 (merged): introduced `FusedStagedWriter` for `BlockTables` -- the mechanism this series extends, not a duplicate.
- #51334 (open): optimizes the *data representation* of staged writes (NumPy chunks instead of Python list boxing) in `rope.py`/`buffer_utils.py` -- a different, complementary layer (makes each call cheaper; this series reduces the *number* of calls). No file overlap with this series' commits.
- #60206 (open): CPU-backend-only override files (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu/*`) -- does not touch any file this series changes.
- #58403 (open): skips the block-table H2D copy entirely when unchanged -- different file, different mechanism.

No open PR does what this series does.

## Testing

Ran the existing GPU-backed unit tests that exercise `RequestState`/`BadWordsState`/`LogitBiasState` admission and downstream consumption (these were not written for this PR; reused as-is per the project's test guidance):

```
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_bad_words.py
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logit_bias.py
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_trace_replay.py
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_gpu.py
tests/v1/streaming_input/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming.py
tests/models/language/pooling/test_splade_sparse_pooler.py
```
77 passed, 0 failed.

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `mypy --ignore-missing-imports`: all clean on the 3 changed files.

## Performance

Each commit's message has its own isolated-benchmark numbers (CUDA events, fresh state object per trial so there's no cross-trial pollution, old vs new order alternated per iteration, correctness checked bit-exact against the pre-patch implementation before timing). Summary:

| Commit | Calls before -> after | Speedup | Saving per admission batch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RequestState` | 3 -> 1 | 1.33x-2.16x | 65-109us |
| `BadWordsState` | 2 -> 1 | 1.34x-1.46x | 43-46us |
| `LogitBiasState` | 4 -> 2 | 1.18x-1.27x | 34-45us |

In all three, the saving shrinks as the number of requests admitted in the same step grows -- expected, since this removes fixed per-call Python/kernel-launch overhead that's amortized over more real work at larger batch sizes. It's largest (and most representative of real traffic, where admission is usually 1-a-few requests per step, not dozens at once) at the small end.

This is admission-time overhead (triggered by `add_request()`, not every decode step), so its share of total engine time scales with how often new requests enter the running batch relative to total steps -- larger for high-QPS/short-completion workloads (high admission churn) than for long-generation workloads where each request is admitted once and then decodes for a long time.

## Pull Request Checklist

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the existing `FusedStagedWriter` mechanism rather than introducing a new one; no new public API.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Reused 9 existing GPU test files (77 tests) covering the affected classes' downstream consumers; added isolated correctness + performance microbenchmarks per commit (not checked in -- see benchmark numbers above; happy to add them under `benchmarks/` if preferred).
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** ruff/mypy clean; each commit does one thing, following the same established pattern.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Duplicate-check performed and documented above; claims backed by measured data in each commit message.

items.title: [Model][Kernel] Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4: batch-invariant serving aligned with training
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: The actor's forward then reproduces rollout log-probs bit for bit. This is the vLLM side of the Nemotron-H train/inference consistency work described in the vLLM blog post; the form follows the DeepSeek-V4 preview #54955.
items.body:
## Purpose

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, make every Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4 layer
(Mamba2, FP8 attention, NVFP4 W4A16 MoE, NVFP4/FP8 linears, norms, router)
independent of batch composition, chunking and the prefill/decode split, using
kernels a training actor can call directly. The actor's forward then reproduces
rollout log-probs bit for bit. This is the vLLM side of the Nemotron-H
train/inference consistency work described in the vLLM blog post
(`2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency`); the form follows the DeepSeek-V4
preview #54955.

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` unset, the only behavior changes are the new
CuTe-DSL W4A16 experts path (W4A16 checkpoints on the `flashinfer_cutedsl`
MoE backend) and the ModelOpt W4A16 layerwise-reload fix. No new CUDA
extension: every BI path is an existing vLLM/FlashInfer kernel pinned to a
fixed configuration.

This is a squashed rebase onto main `fa75d3456d` of the code used for the
final Nemotron-H RL runs (developed on `6e517b15c1`, head `7a0244d0dc` in
aoshen02/vllm#85). 50 files, +5666/−182. The second commit is a review
follow-up (SM10x check at config time).

## What it adds

| Area | Change | Main files |
|---|---|---|
| Mamba2 BI exact replay | Port of #55905 (stacked on #57539, #55627, #55895): bitwise prefill = chunked prefill = decode; decode replays the partial chunk from the FP32 boundary state through the same SSD path; pinned SSD tiles; row-gated decode in full CUDA graphs; `chunk_size` plumbing in four Mamba2 models | `layers/mamba/*`, `v1/attention/backends/mamba2_attn.py`, `v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`, `models/{mamba2,falcon_h1,granitemoehybrid,zamba2}.py` |
| ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4 layerwise reload | W4A16 layers do not wait for `input_scale` during layerwise reload and ignore a deprecated copy arriving after processing | `quantization/{modelopt,base_config}.py`, `fused_moe/routed_experts.py` |
| FlashInfer CuTe-DSL W4A16 MoE | New experts class + NVFP4 oracle branch. Each output element is one CTA's FP32 accumulation over the full K (no split-K); top-k combine is an FP32 sum in slot order; under BI one pinned tactic for every token count. Gated to the Nemotron-H geometry | `fused_moe/experts/flashinfer_cutedsl_w4a16_moe.py`, `fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py` |
| BI GEMM dispatch | Router: BF16 x BF16 -> FP32 logits with one persistent matmul under BI (on top of #59985, which turns the specialized router tiers off); FP8 `bmm` pinned to `cutlass`; W4A16 linears use Humming; Blackwell BI-matmul table entries | `router/gate_linear.py`, `determinism/*`, `utils/flashinfer.py`, `kernels/linear/*` |
| Fixed split-KV FA4 | `FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend`: one split count independent of batch; rejects unsupported configs at construction | `v1/attention/backends/flash_attn_fixed_split.py` |
| Nemotron-H wiring | Under BI: select the components above, `CudaRMSNorm` and the grouped gated norm, standalone `+quant_fp8`, no norm/act+quant fusion; TP=1 and SM10x checks at config time; MTP loads only `mtp.*` weights and shares the target embedding/LM head | `models/{nemotron_h,nemotron_h_mtp,config}.py`, `layers/layernorm.py` |

### Decisions made in the rebase

- Dropped our cherry-pick of #57635 (now on main).
- GateLinear: kept #59985's behavior; Nemotron-H keeps its BF16 gate weight
  under BI (`force_fp32_compute` only when BI is off), as the trainer does.
- Mamba2: exact replay writes no internal prefill checkpoints (#57329), so
  `MambaMixer2` requests no checkpoint blocks under BI; `update_block_table`
  handles both the checkpoint metadata and the exact-replay decode buffer.
- NemotronHMTP uses `is_unused_checkpoint_weight` (#60152).
- Fixed split-KV FA4: dropped the cascade check (#61126 removed cascade).
- `utils/flashinfer.py`: kept the pinned `bmm_fp8` backend; the `*_mm_out`
  helpers were removed on main (#60517).

## Why this is not a duplicate

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Nemotron-H batch invariant"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "nemotron batch invariant"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "mamba2 batch invariant"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "cutedsl w4a16"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fixed split flash attention"
```

- The Mamba2 BI stack (#55627, #55895, #55905, #57539, by @NolenLiang, on our
  team) is the Mamba2 part of this PR. It is included here so the full
  Nemotron-H path can be reviewed and tested as one unit; we will reconcile with
  whichever lands first. #56244 (gate inside the scan) is a different approach
  and is not used.
- #57123 (fp32 eps in the BI RMSNorm Triton kernels), #60047 (`aten::mm`
  `out_dtype` overloads) and #60681 (GateLinear custom op) touch nearby code
  but not the paths changed here.
- No open PR covers CuTe-DSL W4A16 MoE under BI, fixed split-KV FA4, the
  ModelOpt W4A16 reload fix or Nemotron-H BI.

## Test plan and results

GB200, bare-metal uv venv with the precompiled wheel for
`fa75d3456d` (torch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0, flashinfer 0.7.2,
cutlass-dsl 4.8.0), tree run from source.

| Test | BI | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_emit.py` | unset / 1 | 23 / 23 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 7 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_exact_replay.py` | 1 | 3 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_batch_invariant.py` | 1 | 12 passed |
| `tests/v1/determinism/test_mamba2_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 4 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_cutedsl_nvfp4_moe.py` | unset | 36 passed |
| `tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py` | unset | 63 passed, 2 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py` | unset | 136 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_fixed_split.py` | 1 | 9 passed |
| `tests/model_executor/test_nemotron_h_quantization.py` (head) | unset / 1 | 22 / 22 passed |
| `tests/v1/determinism/test_nemotron_h_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 7 passed |
| `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` | unset | 95 passed, 3 skipped (checkpoints unavailable offline) |
| main's `test_mamba2_checkpoint_state` / `test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints` / `test_gpu_draft_lm_head` | unset | 8 / 6 / 8 passed |

`test_nvfp4_batch_invariant.py` fails only because its model is not in the
offline HF cache; this PR does not touch it.

### Full model (Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4)

16 prompts of 7 to 12000 tokens, 48 greedy tokens; each comparison checks token
ids and FP32 logprob bits.

| Comparison | Requests that differ (of 16) |
|---|---|
| BI=1: alone vs batch vs reversed batch | 0 |
| BI=1: decode vs `prompt_logprobs` re-feed (`max_num_batched_tokens` 16384 and 2048) | 0 |
| BI=1: `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 vs 16384 | 0 |
| Negative control, BI unset: alone vs batch | 16 (7 with token flips) |
| This PR vs the pre-rebase head `7a0244d0dc` (the code of the RL runs), Triton/flashinfer/cutlass-dsl pinned to that image's versions | 0 (all 547 module outputs equal) |

With main's default library versions, this PR differs from `7a0244d0dc` in the
last bit of Mamba's `rms_norm_gated` (same source and inputs; Triton 3.8.0 vs
3.7.1 rounds 2 of 1,048,576 elements differently). A trainer that calls these
kernels must use the same torch/Triton/flashinfer/cutlass-dsl versions as
serving.

### End to end (on `7a0244d0dc`)

Megatron actor vs rollout on Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4, GB200 DP4/EP4:
`actor/ppo_kl` = 0 at every step of the 100-step SWE-bench Pro run.

### Not tested on this head

TP>1 (rejected by the config check), MTP/spec decode and prefix caching under
BI.

## Known limitations

- BI is validated only for this model on SM10x (B200/GB200/B300), TP=1.
  BI=1 Nemotron-H raises at config time on other GPUs or TP>1.
- Under BI, Nemotron-H always selects `FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend`, which
  raises at construction unless vllm-flash-attn has fixed split-KV scheduling,
  head size is 128, the KV cache is FP8 E4M3 and there is no sliding window.
- Under BI, W4A16 NVFP4 linears are forced to `HummingNvFp4LinearKernel`
  without a fallback; validated on SM100 only.
- BI relies on torch.compile with Inductor: the trainer compiles the same
  pointwise glue (MoE combine, norms), so `enforce_eager` breaks bitwise
  equality.

Implemented, tested and described with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human
submitter reviews every changed line and is responsible for the change.

items.title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DP NUMA affinity regression and add GELU-tanh MoE support for Gemma-4
items.author: bigPYJ1151
items.summary: Fixes a CPU data-parallel NUMA affinity regression and adds GELU-tanh activation support across all CPU-backed MoE quantization paths.
items.body:
## Summary
Two independent CPU-backend fixes:

- **NUMA affinity regression (#47328):** PR #45026 replaced env-var-based device isolation with an in-process `assigned_physical_gpu_ids` config field for GPU/XPU, but CPU's NUMA-binding path (`get_visible_memory_node()`) still only reads `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES` from `os.environ`, which nothing set per rank anymore — so all CPU DP ranks ended up bound to the same NUMA node. Restores per-rank env var mutation before each rank's `proc.start()`, scoped to CPU only, resolving every rank's node ids up front to avoid a later rank's resolution misreading an earlier rank's mutation. Resolve #47328
- **GELU-tanh MoE activation support:** `amd/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w8a8-llmcompressor` configures `gelu_pytorch_tanh` for its MoE blocks, but every SGL-kernel-backed CPU MoE path (INT8/INT4/FP8 W8A8, FP8/MXFP4 W8A16) only supported SiLU. Partially syncs the vendored SGLang CPU kernels to pick up generic `CPUActMethod` dispatch scaffolding (4 files with unrelated upstream changes left unsynced, noted in `common.h`'s pin marker), adds a `gelu_tanh_and_mul` AVX512 primitive and threads it through all 5 `CPUQuantMethod` kernel impls, the `fused_experts_cpu` op schema, and each `CPUExperts*` class's activation gating in `cpu_moe.py`. DeepSeek-style shared-expert kernels are untouched (different code path, not needed).

## Changes
- `vllm/v1/engine/utils.py`, `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` — NUMA affinity fix + regression test.
- `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/{common,gemm,moe,moe_int4,moe_int8,vec}.h/.cpp`, `csrc/cpu/torch_bindings.cpp`, `vllm/_custom_ops.py`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/cpu_moe.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py` — GELU-tanh MoE support.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` — new regression test for per-rank `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`; live-verified with a real DP=2 server on a 6-NUMA-node host (each `EngineCore_DP*` rank binds a distinct node).
- [x] `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py` — 20 new GELU-tanh tests across all 5 quant configs, each checked against a plain-PyTorch reference; full suite 524 passed, 200 skipped (zero regressions vs. 504/198 baseline).
- [x] End-to-end smoke test against `amd/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w8a8-llmcompressor`: engine selects the INT8 CPU MoE backend, and a chat-templated prompt at `temperature=0.0` produces a correct response (`"The capital of France is Paris."`).

items.title: [Perf] logprob: Keep input top-k and token-ids logprobs off the host sync path
items.author: mmangkad
items.summary: Input top-k and token-ids logprobs ( with plus or ) blocked the overlap scheduler on the in-flight forward once per prefill (and per logprob chunk): - Top-k: results only went through async pinned copies when graph-pool borrowing was on (off by default). Other…
items.body:
## Motivation

Input top-k and token-ids logprobs (`return_logprob` with `logprob_start_len >= 0` plus `top_logprobs_num` or `token_ids_logprob`) blocked the overlap scheduler on the in-flight forward once per prefill (and per logprob chunk):

- **Top-k:** results only went through async pinned copies when graph-pool borrowing was on (off by default). Otherwise they were read back with `.tolist()`.
- **Token-ids:** the GPU logprobs were indexed with a Python list, an implicit synchronous H2D copy.

This affects `/v1/completions` with `echo` + `logprobs`, `/generate` prompt scoring, and setwise scoring in the Score API.

## Modifications

- `layers/logprob_processor.py`: on CUDA, top-k / token-ids results always leave the device as async pinned copies with a copy-done event; borrowing now only decides where the scratch memory lives. The token-ids index is staged through `async_h2d`.
- `finalize_input_logprobs()` already converts the pinned spans before every consumer reads them (prefill, disagg prefill, PP). Multi-item scoring and non-CUDA devices are unchanged.
- `test_logprob_fast_input.py`: the test helper finalizes results the way the scheduler does.

## Accuracy Tests

Values are computed exactly as before; only the D2H transport changes.

- `test_logprob_fast_input.py` + `test_logprob_chunk_stitching.py`: 16 passed on H200.
- `test/registered/core/test_srt_endpoint.py`: 20 passed, including all logprob tests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3-0.6B, 1x H200, TP=1 bf16 with default flags, `main` vs this PR. 64 concurrent `/generate` requests with random prompts, `logprob_start_len=0`, 1 output token. Fresh server per run; two rounds each, numbers are the mean.

| Workload | Before (req/s) | After (req/s) | Change | p50 latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| top-k=5, 1024-token prompt | 166 | 252 | +52% | 385 -> 252 ms |
| top-k=5, 256-token prompt | 571 | 744 | +30% | 111 -> 85 ms |
| token-ids (10 ids), 1024-token prompt | 187 | 236 | +26% | 342 -> 270 ms |
| token-ids (10 ids), 256-token prompt | 602 | 685 | +14% | 106 -> 93 ms |
| no logprobs (control) | 1683 | 1671 | ~0 | - |

With 256-token decode traffic sharing the server, top-k scoring throughput goes from 525 to 683 req/s (+30%).

The gain grows with prompt length (the removed `.tolist()` covered every prompt position) and is largest when the forward is short.

items.title: [XPU][Attention] Route multimodal prefix masks through the Triton/FlashAttention composite
items.author: mganczarenko
items.summary: Only image batches need the mask; text prefill and decode pay for Triton for nothing (3–4× slower per attention call than SYCL FlashAttention on Arc Pro B70). Reuse the Triton/FlashAttention composite from #56305: image-masked batches → Triton, causal batches …
items.body:
## Purpose

On XPU, multimodal prefix-LM models (Gemma 3/4) run Triton attention for every batch: the SYCL FlashAttention kernel cannot apply the image mask, and `Gemma4Config` forces `TRITON_ATTN` when FA4 is unavailable. Only image batches need the mask; text prefill and decode pay for Triton for nothing (3–4× slower per attention call than SYCL FlashAttention on Arc Pro B70).

Reuse the Triton/FlashAttention composite from #56305: image-masked batches → Triton, causal batches → FlashAttention, shared KV cache.

- `FlashAttentionBackend.supports_head_size`: allow ≤ 512 on XPU (SYCL kernels support 512; Gemma 4 global layers).
- `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` composite: FA3/FA4 and Hopper requirements apply to CUDA only (`device_major` moved into the FA route's `supports_compute_capability`; CUDA selection unchanged).
- `platforms/xpu.py`: select the composite for mm-prefix models with head size 256/512 and bf16/fp16 when no backend is requested; float32 or other head sizes fall back to Triton.
- `Gemma4Config`: no longer forces `TRITON_ATTN` on XPU. Side effect: with multimodal disabled, Gemma 4 defaults to FlashAttention.

No kernel changes.

## Test Plan

- Backend selection checked on XPU: composite for head 256/512 with image mask; Triton for head 128 and float32; FlashAttention without image mask. No unit test in this PR.
- 4× Arc Pro B70, TP=4, `--enforce-eager`, vLLM 0.32.0rc1 nightly: Gemma-4-26B-A4B text-only prefill (16 × 2048) and decode (bs32, 128/256) with `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` vs new default; Gemma-4-31B greedy outputs on image and text prompts, both backends.
- Not covered: graph mode, mixed image+text batches.

## Test Result

- Text-only 26B: prefill 8.9k → 11.8k tok/s (+32 %), decode 385 → 576 tok/s (+50 %).
- Images, 31B: composite selected (`TRITON_FLASH_ATTN`, block 64); 4/7 greedy outputs identical to Triton-only, the rest diverge after 21–47 identical tokens (within TP=4 run-to-run variation); 21.9 s → 16.6 s for the set.
- Decode traces: Triton attention 283 µs (26B) / 399 µs (31B) per call at bs64 vs ~60 / 95 µs SYCL FlashAttention; with graphs, FlashAttention is 25–41 % faster end to end at bs32–64 on 26B.

items.title: [Perf] NIXL: prepared dlists for hybrid-model state transfer
items.author: iyastreb
items.summary: Hybrid-model state (Mamba/GDN, SWA, DSA indexer, QSA, MiniMax, MXFP8 block scales) was sent with a fresh per request, rebuilding and re-validating every descriptor. With the data path is one SGL put per transfer, so this host-side descriptor work is what remai…
items.body:
## Motivation

Hybrid-model state (Mamba/GDN, SWA, DSA indexer, QSA, MiniMax, MXFP8 block scales) was
sent with a fresh `initialize_xfer` per request, rebuilding and re-validating every
descriptor. With `NIXL_UCX_SGL_ENABLE=1` the data path is one SGL put per transfer, so
this host-side descriptor work is what remains on the transfer worker.

## Modifications
- At peer registration, build one strided source/destination dlist pair per decode peer
  covering all whole-slot state components; per request, one `make_prepped_xfer` with
  int32 selectors instead of one `initialize_xfer` per component.
- Decode advertises its state pool lengths (new registration frame 23) so prefill can
  size the destination dlist. An older decode without the frame stays on the generic path.
- Components the fast path cannot address (TP-sliced layouts, PP/CP/DCP, unpaired
  entries) stay generic per component. A stride mismatch is recorded at registration and
  fails every transfer to that peer with the reason, instead of addressing the decode
  with the prefill stride or killing the bootstrap thread.
- State completion is one standalone `{room}_state_{rank}` notification sent after every
  handle of the chunk settles (NIXL UCX flushes the endpoint before DONE). This replaces
  per-component attached notifs, which let decode treat the first component's arrival
  as state complete.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the same bytes move through prepared descriptors. Byte-for-byte
equivalence of the prepared and generic paths was checked with a memcpy fake agent
across Mamba, SWA on MHA, DSA with elided layers, QSA with layer ids, MLA peers with
mismatched TP, a decode with an extra DSA entry, and multi-component requests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DSv4-Flash, GB200, ISL=1k, cost of state preparation:

items.title: [Feat] minimax-h3: Add an opt-in SMD4 release sampling preset
items.author: LeslieWylie
items.summary: Loading an SMD Ref2VA student LoRA does not select its trained sampling grid. This draft adds an explicit release sampling preset: four updates, five sigma boundaries, a final half-sized raw interval, and separate video/audio shifts of 12/3.
items.body:
## Motivation

Loading an SMD Ref2VA student LoRA does not select its trained sampling grid. This draft adds an explicit `smd-ref2va-4step` release sampling preset: four updates, five sigma boundaries, a final half-sized raw interval, and separate video/audio shifts of 12/3. It does not automatically detect adapter metadata or add an adapter loader.

The student checkpoint source is [SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-4step](https://huggingface.co/zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-4step). No new distillation method or speed/quality improvement is claimed here.

## Modifications

- Accept optional `_minimax_h3.sampling_preset: "smd-ref2va-4step"` in an existing native Ref2VA model index. The package owner must supply the matching student transformer or use the existing LoRA loading mechanism. The preset does not download, apply, or identify a LoRA.
- Validate request steps and modality shifts before encoding; reject PDD/DMD stacking and untrained tasks. Warmup uses a prefix of the serving grid, including when a request already contains a cached serving grid.
- Include the preset in timestep dedup identity only when enabled. Default schedules and default dedup keys retain their previous values. The Euler loop, LoRA loading, and default model recipes are unchanged.
- Document the opt-in release declaration and pending GPU/quality validation in the existing H3 cookbook.

Open-PR searches for `SMD`, `MiniMax student`, `H3 distill`, and `consistency H3` found no matching sampling-preset change. The FastH3 AdaLN, LoRA shape-check, and attention PRs returned by the broader searches address other paths.

## Accuracy Tests

Local isolated CPU validation passed the new contract cases: sigma values, serving/warmup step errors, modality-shift errors, release metadata admission, PDD/DMD exclusion, warmup truncation, and dedup identity. The actual time-request, release-metadata, resolved-plan, dedup, and timestep-stage modules ran; unrelated serving-bootstrap/protocol dependencies were substituted, and package `conftest` was disabled.

The default 1/4/50-step grids at shifts 12 and 3 were also compared exactly with the unmodified base commit, as was the default timestep fingerprint.

The normal installed-package test command remains pending:

```bash
python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_smd.py -q
```

Full pipeline creation, student adapter loading, GPU end-to-end generation, audio/video quality, and CI validation are **pending**. The CPU bootstrap run is not an end-to-end serving result.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This draft makes no performance claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Changed Python files pass isort 7.0.0 and Ruff 0.15.1 formatting and the configured Ruff checks; the full pre-commit collection was not run.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Isolated CPU contracts passed; normal package collection remains pending.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

AI assistance was used for the implementation, tests, and this draft. Human model validation has not been represented as complete.

items.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Support online W8A8 INT8 quantization for diffusion
items.author: OrangeRedeng
items.summary: Port the diffusion W8A8 support from #29048 into a separate PR. This adds online INT8 quantization for unquantized FP16/BF16 diffusion transformers on Ascend NPU.
items.body:
## Motivation Port the diffusion W8A8 support from #29048 into a separate PR. This adds online INT8 quantization for unquantized FP16/BF16 diffusion transformers on Ascend NPU. The SRT LLM and MoE changes from #29048 are outside this PR. ## Modifications - Add `NPUOnlineW8A8DiffusionConfig` and its linear method: quantize weights after loading, dynamically quantize activations per token, and return outputs in the original FP16/BF16 dtype. - Register `w8a8_int` for diffusion and forward `--quantization-ignored-layers` so selected layers stay in checkpoint precision. - Keep the W8A8 operations in the diffusion implementation without importing the SRT online-quantization module from #29048. - Update `--quantization` help and diffusion quantization documentation. ## Accuracy Tests ### MiniMax-H3

items.title: [Fix] /v1/responses: fix reasoning.effort in non-streaming responses and max_output_tokens=1 validation
items.author: hhy-seven
items.summary: Two independent bugs on: ### 1. echoed as in the response The response carried "reasoning": {"effort": null,...} even though the tier was accepted and applied to generation.
items.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Summary

 Two independent bugs on `/v1/responses`:

 ###  1. `reasoning.effort` echoed as `null` in the response

 ```json
  curl -X POST http://<server>/v1/responses \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model": "...", "input": "hi", "stream": false, "reasoning": {"effort": "max"}}' 
```

  The response carried "reasoning": {"effort": null, ...} even though the tier was accepted and applied to generation.   OpenAI's API echoes the requested tier back, so clients that round-trip the response (e.g. agents replaying previous_response_id payloads) see a setting that silently differs from what they asked for.

  Root cause: ResponsesResponse.from_request masked the effort through ECHOABLE_REASONING_EFFORTS ({minimal, low, medium, high}). That mask exists to protect the non-harmony streaming path only: the typed OpenAI SDK stream events (ResponseCreatedEvent, ResponseCompletedEvent, ...) validate the embedded response against the SDK's narrower Reasoning.effort literal, and echoing none/xhigh/max there raises a pydantic ValidationError that kills the stream before the first SSE byte. But the mask lived in from_request, which is shared by the non-streaming path and the harmony streaming path (whose events are plain dicts with no such validation) — so responses that could safely echo the real tier returned null instead.

  ###  2. "max_output_tokens": 1 rejected with HTTP 400

  ResponsesRequest.to_sampling_params subtracted the 2-token BOS/EOS headroom unconditionally, so an explicit max_output_tokens=1 became max_new_tokens=-1, which fails SamplingParams validation (max_new_tokens must be at least 0, got -1.) and surfaces as a 400. The headroom only makes sense for the server-derived default budget, not for a cap the client asked for explicitly.

## Modifications

  - protocol.py (ResponsesResponse.from_request): echo request.reasoning.effort verbatim instead of filtering it through the echoable set.
  - serving_responses.py: hoist the stream-event sanitizer to module level (_sanitize_response_dict) and extend it to also mask reasoning.effort to None when the tier is outside the SDK-echoable set. It is applied only in the non-harmony streaming path (response.created, response.in_progress, terminal events, response.failed), where the SDK validation lives. Non-streaming responses and harmony streaming events now echo the requested tier as-is.
  - protocol.py (ResponsesRequest.to_sampling_params): apply the BOS/EOS  headroom (-= 2) only to the default budget derived when max_output_tokens is unset; an explicit max_output_tokens is passed through as-is.
  - Updated test_responses_protocol.py accordingly (see below).

## Tests

 - [x] test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_responses_protocol.py:
  the reworked test_effort_echoed_verbatim_and_masked_only_for_typed_stream_events
  asserts (a) from_request echoes every tier verbatim, including
  none/xhigh/max, and (b) _sanitize_response_dict masks the
  non-SDK tiers and the masked payload validates inside
  ort.ResponseCreatedEvent — covering both the fix and the streaming
  constraint it preserves.
  - [x] Manual: the curl above now returns "reasoning": {"effort": "max"}.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

items.title: Skip out-of-window partial-tail store jobs instead of crashing EngineCore (#61970)
items.author: Virtuoso461
items.summary: Fixes #61970 ## What does this PR do? In the native KV-offloading scheduler, asserted, crashing the whole EngineCore when a retained Mamba boundary-state snapshot exceeds the request's current offloadable window (e.g.
items.body:
Fixes #61970

## What does this PR do?

In the native KV-offloading scheduler, `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs()` asserted `boundary <= max_boundary`, crashing the whole EngineCore when a retained Mamba boundary-state snapshot exceeds the request's *current* offloadable window (e.g. after a resume with a smaller `max_offload_tokens` / `num_prompt_tokens`) — the exact scenario of hybrid Attention/Mamba deployments in the issue (Kimi-K3, long context, high concurrency).

The sibling path for the **same** handoffs, `_build_aligned_boundary_store_jobs()`, already handles the identical out-of-window condition by **skipping the store job** (`continue`). The mooncake connector's analogous boundary handling skips the same way. This PR makes the partial-tail path mirror that established semantics — log a warning (with req id, boundary and window numbers) and skip — instead of crashing.

The removed assertion guarded a runtime-recoverable race, not an invariant: all structural checks (`boundary > 0`, hash alignment, single boundary per request, CoW block consistency) are preserved and still assert.

## Tests

New `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_offloading_partial_tail_skip.py` (CPU-only, no GPU needed): loads the real module source with minimal dependency stubs, hand-assembles the hybrid Attention + Mamba-CoW configuration and drives `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs` directly.

- Red (pristine module): the exact `AssertionError: boundary <= max_boundary` from the issue reproduces (boundary=40 vs window=32).
- Green (patched): the job is skipped with zero state pollution (no jobs/counters/transfer side effects), the warning fires; a normal in-window partial-tail job is still built with all fields intact; the preserved hash-alignment invariant still asserts; the aligned path behaves bit-identically before and after the fix. 9/9 pass.

## Notes

GPU/e2e reproduction (real hybrid model under load) was not possible on this machine; the unit test drives the actual scheduling code path directly instead.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix auto truncation without an output token limit
items.author: bzsuni
items.summary: Fix automatic prompt truncation in Chat Completions and Responses when no output token limit is specified. Previously, truncation could fill the entire context window, leaving no room for generation and causing requests to fail.
items.body:
## Overview

Fix automatic prompt truncation in Chat Completions and Responses when no output token limit is specified. Previously, truncation could fill the entire context window, leaving no room for generation and causing requests to fail.

## Claims

- Reserve one token for generation when automatic truncation is enabled without an explicit output limit.
- Preserve existing behavior for explicit output limits and zero-output budgets.
- Keep pooling requests able to use the full input context.

## Validation

Added regression tests covering text and token-ID prompts, Chat serving, and unspecified, zero, and positive output budgets.

Validated with `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B` (`max_model_len=512`):

| Request | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat, output limit omitted | HTTP 400: `max_tokens` is 0 | HTTP 200 |
| Responses, output limit omitted | HTTP 400: prompt fills context | HTTP 200 |

Both requests produced 511 input tokens and 1 output token after the fix. Requests with explicit output limits remained unchanged.

- **54 tests passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including mypy.

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/renderers/test_completions.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_sampling_params.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_serving_chat_mistral_token_ids_prompt_is_validated \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_serving_chat_mistral_token_ids_prompt_too_long_is_rejected
```

## Details

Both request protocols converted an unspecified output limit from `None` to `0` when constructing `TokenizeParams`. Automatic truncation interpreted this as a zero-output budget, allowing the prompt to fill the entire context window.

Preserve `None` for unspecified output limits so automatic truncation reserves one token for generation. Keep the `TokenizeParams` default at `0` to preserve behavior for callers that do not generate output.

```python
            "temperature": 0,
        },
    ),
    (
        "/v1/responses",
        {
            "model": "truncation-test",
            "input": text,
            "truncation": "auto",
            "temperature": 0,
        },
    ),
]

for endpoint, payload in cases:
    response = requests.post(url + endpoint, json=payload, timeout=120)
    print(endpoint, response.status_code, response.text)
```

**Results:**

| Endpoint | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | HTTP 400: `max_tokens must be at least 1, got 0` | HTTP 200 |
| Responses | HTTP 400: prompt length 512 exceeds `max_model_len` | HTTP 200 |

Both requests used 511 input tokens and generated 1 output token after the fix.

The issue is triggered by an overlong prompt with automatic truncation enabled and no explicit output token limit.

items.title: [Perf][EPLB][DSv4] Add a symm_mem weight-migration backend and fuse MegaMoE replica mapping
items.author: abmfy
items.summary: This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things: - adds an opt-in weight-migration backend; - fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the D…
items.body:
## Overview

This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things:

- adds an opt-in `symm_mem` weight-migration backend;
- fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the DeepGEMM MegaMoE staging kernels;
- takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path.

Not a duplicate. No open or merged PR adds a symmetric-memory EPLB backend or fuses the MegaMoE mapping. #61176 and #61839 enable EPLB for the ROCm AITER MegaMoE backend. Related: #61767 (`cpu_all_reduce_`, reused here), #57549, #56716, #61643.

## Claims

- EPLB raises decode throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 NVL72 by +3.7% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank and +7.7% at DEP32 with 128 req/rank. At DEP16 the step is about 3% shorter, but the throughput gain is within run-to-run noise.
- `symm_mem`: senders push expert rows into the receiver's `expert_buffer`, which is allocated in CUDA symmetric memory. There is no staging buffer, and it needs no memory beyond `expert_buffer`. Cross-node peer copies run at about 800 GB/s, against about 88 GB/s for NIXL, and a 40-layer rearrangement transfers in 0.3–0.6 s at DEP32.
- MegaMoE layers no longer launch a separate EPLB mapping kernel, which saves 5–6 µs per layer. The replica choice is shared with the router through one Triton helper, so physical ids and load counts match `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` exactly.
- Async EPLB no longer adds a GPU→host sync to the decode loop. It also raises on every rank when the worker fails on any rank, instead of stalling.

## Validation

Hardware: GB200 NVL72, 4 GPUs per node.

Serving setup: DSpark with 5 draft tokens, MRV2, FULL CUDA graphs, async scheduling.

EPLB setup: `{"num_redundant_experts": <DP>, "window_size": 1000, "step_interval": 3000, "use_async": true, "communicator": "symm_mem"}`, i.e. one redundant expert per rank.

Workload: decode only, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached), 16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, and requests pinned evenly to DP ranks. Throughput is the output rate over the window in which every request is decoding.

Off and on arms ran interleaved (ABAB) on the same nodes. These runs used a branch of nightly fe4df3df (2026-10-12) with this change set and #61767, before the rebase and without the second commit.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | EPLB on (tok/s) | Δ | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 223.6k ± 2.0k (n=4) | 228.1k ± 4.2k (n=4) | +2.0% | 2.0 (not resolved) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 419.5k ± 1.3k (n=4) | 435.1k ± 5.8k (n=4) | +3.7% | 5.3 |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 500.7k ± 5.1k (n=3) | 539.4k ± 9.7k (n=3) | +7.7% | 6.1 |

- DEP16 step time, p50 of 2000-step windows at full batch, same build: 24.34 / 24.28 ms off vs 23.61 / 23.25 ms on.
- At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, one pass per arm is excluded. A host stall unrelated to EPLB cut that pass by 13–34%.

Per-step breakdown, DEP32 with 128 req/rank:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|---|---|
| Step time (CUDA events, unprofiled) | 38.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| GPU idle at the step boundary | 0.27 ms | 0.27 ms |
| Main-model MegaMoE (5 s CUDA profile) | 18.1 ms | 13.4 ms |
| All other kernels (same profile) | 21.5 ms | 21.2 ms |

The GPU never waits on the host, so the MegaMoE saving turns into step time. MegaMoE is about 40% of the step, which caps the end-to-end gain.

Microbenchmarks (GB200):

- **Fused EPLB staging**, one MoE layer, hidden 5120, top-k 6, 384 logical experts. Each arm is timed as a CUDA graph replay, median of 200. Outputs, ids and load counts match main bit for bit in every case.

  | Format | Tokens | Physical experts | main: `torch.where` + map kernel + staging | Fused | Saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MXFP8 | 432 | 400 | 9.4 µs | 4.2 µs | 5.1 µs |
  | MXFP8 | 768 | 416 | 11.0 µs | 4.7 µs | 6.3 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 432 | 400 | 49.5 µs | 44.0 µs | 5.5 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 768 | 416 | 49.1 µs | 43.8 µs | 5.3 µs |

  That is about 0.2 ms per decode step across 40 MoE layers.
- **Weight-migration bandwidth**, 2 nodes, one MegaMoE layer of 25 experts (470 MB):

  | Path | Bandwidth |
  |---|---|
  | `symm_mem` peer copies, intra- or cross-node over multi-node NVLink | ~808 GB/s (bulk), ~294 GB/s (100 per-tensor copies) |
  | NIXL, cross-node | ~88 GB/s (UCX picks RoCE, not multi-node NVLink) |
  | NIXL, cross-node, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp` | ~0.12 GB/s (TCP) |

- **MegaMoE kernel time under serving load**, DEP16 with 72 req/rank, layers 2–40: p50 per call drops 12.6–14.0% across three profiled runs (222→194 µs). Layer 1 is excluded because it absorbs cross-rank arrival skew.

Tests on this branch, one GB200 node with 4 GPUs. They ran before the rebase onto 64175d3827; the 5 newer commits on main touch none of these files.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` (incl. `test_prepare_megamoe_eplb_matches_router_under_graph_replay`) | 110 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k eplb` | 18 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` | 35 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU) |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k nixl`, NIXL installed | 7 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 6 passed, 28 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` | 13 passed, 7 passed |

GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (one node):
- Setup: 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, `num_redundant_experts=16`, `window_size=100`, `step_interval=300`. Every arm rearranged all 40 layers four times during the eval.
- Command: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`

| Arm | Accuracy (2 passes) | 40-layer rearrangement |
|---|---|---|
| EPLB off | 0.898, 0.901 | — |
| `symm_mem` | 0.897, 0.895 | 2.9–3.3 s |
| `symm_mem`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 0.889, 0.883 | 2.9–3.3 s, no sync error |
| `nixl` | 0.892, 0.886 | 2.7–3.2 s |

The EPLB-off and `nixl` arms ran on the commit before the final cleanup, which does not touch either path. Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate; `symm_mem`'s advantage is across nodes over multi-node NVLink.

## Details

**`symm_mem` backend**
- The receive buffer is one symmetric `uint8` buffer per EP group, set up with a single rendezvous and carved into per-tensor views. The backend checks the NVLink/MNNVL domain before allocating.
- Senders and receivers derive each receive row from the global placement with the same helper, so `add_recv` is a no-op. Push backends get every rank's rows through a new `recv_rows` argument to `set_transfer_context`. This argument is optional and other backends ignore it.
- Each `execute()` runs two CPU barriers. GPU spin barriers can deadlock against MegaMoE's cooperative launches.
- Rejected with elastic EP. The buffer lives outside the caching allocator, so sleep mode does not free it.

**Fused mapping**: `fused_moe/eplb_triton.py` holds the replica hash, map lookup and gated load count. The MXFP8/BF16 and NVFP4 staging kernels call it, and so does the router kernel. Routed-experts capture still sees logical ids.

**Async EPLB**
- Per-layer maps are committed with pinned non-blocking copies, and the worker thread fences `expert_buffer` reuse.
- Balancedness stats are read back non-blocking and logged in order once they land.
- `should_record_tensor` is rewritten only when its value flips.
- The per-step "all ranks ready" check runs over `cpu_all_reduce_`. A gloo ring all-reduce costs several ms per step at DP16/DP32.

**Also**
- `logical_to_physical_map` is sized to R+1 slots unless elastic EP is on.
- `compute_logical_maps` is vectorized.
- DeepSeek V4.1 decoder-replay padding and dummy rows are marked as padding, which complements #61643.

**CI**: the `symm_mem` execution tests need NVLink peers. They are added to the optional 8×H100 "Distributed DP + EP" job; the 4×L4 EPLB job skips them. The MegaMoE parity test needs SM100.

**Limitations**
- In mixed prefill/decode serving, per-rank prefill imbalance bounds the step. There, EPLB mostly lowers tail TTFT rather than raising throughput.
- Likely rebase overlap with #61786, #59168 and #41141. Offline placements without elastic EP (#41141) could exceed R+1 replicas.

items.summary: Alerts run only for uncancelled runs in targeting the repository's default branch, when at least one testing job fails. Scheduled and manually dispatched runs do not send these alerts.
items.body:
## Background

Report failures from Megatron-LM's merge-queue testing jobs to the CI Slack channel using the shared notifier from NVIDIA-NeMo/FW-CI-templates#593.

## What changed

Add `notify-merge-group-failure` to `cicd-main.yml`, covering the four H100/GB200 unit and integration testing jobs. Alerts run only for uncancelled `merge_group` runs in `NVIDIA/Megatron-LM` targeting the repository's default branch, when at least one testing job fails. Scheduled and manually dispatched runs do not send these alerts.

## Details

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Merge queue checks requested] --> B[H100 and GB200 unit and integration tests]
  B --> C{Testing job failed and run uncancelled?}
  C -->|Yes, canonical default branch| D[Shared failure summary]
  D --> E[CI Slack channel]
```

Check `github.event.merge_group.base_ref` against `refs/heads/<default_branch>` so synthetic queue head refs are accepted. Keep existing workflow triggers and testing jobs unchanged. Pin `notify-ci-failure` to `631c404d00a9e60afc591cd071d35d2e18f82fc6`, use `environment: main` for `SLACK_WEBHOOK`, and give the notification job no token permissions or failed-run checkout. Add dependency-free wiring tests to the existing CPU lint job. `populate-build-cache.yml` is unchanged.

## Tested

Validated commit `57f8bf2d22` after merging upstream `main` at `adcd90f4b2`:

- `python3 .github/scripts/test_ci_notifications.py`: all four tests passed.
- `node /tmp/mlm-pr8289-merge-group/verify-condition.mjs`: 4,200 cases passed using `@actions/expressions` 0.3.61, including every testing-job failure, cancellation, alternate targets, fork repositories, synthetic queue refs, schedule, dispatch, push, and pull-request events.
- Parsed YAML comparison against upstream `main`: existing triggers and jobs unchanged after removing the notifier and its lint test step; cache workflow unchanged.
- `actionlint -format '{{json .}}' -stdin-filename .github/workflows/cicd-main.yml -`: candidate and upstream have the same 42 diagnostics; no new findings.
- `uvx --from black==26.3.0 black --check .github/scripts/test_ci_notifications.py` and `uvx --from isort==5.13.2 isort --check-only .github/scripts/test_ci_notifications.py`: passed.
- `BASE_REF=main CHECK_ONLY=true SKIP_DOCS=false bash tools/autoformat.sh`: passed; no applicable changes under its `megatron/core` and `tests` scope.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- GitHub API: the `main` environment currently has no deployment branch restrictions or protection rules, so queue refs can use its secret.

Hosted CI and real Slack delivery remain unverified; no test Slack messages were sent.

items.summary: Fixes #61970 ## What does this PR do? In the native KV-offloading scheduler, asserted, crashing the whole EngineCore when a retained Mamba boundary-state snapshot exceeds the request's current offloadable window (e.g.
items.body:
Fixes #61970

## What does this PR do?

In the native KV-offloading scheduler, `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs()` asserted `boundary <= max_boundary`, crashing the whole EngineCore when a retained Mamba boundary-state snapshot exceeds the request's *current* offloadable window (e.g. after a resume with a smaller `max_offload_tokens` / `num_prompt_tokens`) — the exact scenario of hybrid Attention/Mamba deployments in the issue (Kimi-K3, long context, high concurrency).

The sibling path for the **same** handoffs, `_build_aligned_boundary_store_jobs()`, already handles the identical out-of-window condition by **skipping the store job** (`continue`). The mooncake connector's analogous boundary handling skips the same way. This PR makes the partial-tail path mirror that established semantics — log a warning (with req id, boundary and window numbers) and skip — instead of crashing.

The removed assertion guarded a runtime-recoverable race, not an invariant: all structural checks (`boundary > 0`, hash alignment, single boundary per request, CoW block consistency) are preserved and still assert.

## Tests

New `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_offloading_partial_tail_skip.py` (CPU-only, no GPU needed): loads the real module source with minimal dependency stubs, hand-assembles the hybrid Attention + Mamba-CoW configuration and drives `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs` directly.

- Red (pristine module): the exact `AssertionError: boundary <= max_boundary` from the issue reproduces (boundary=40 vs window=32).
- Green (patched): the job is skipped with zero state pollution (no jobs/counters/transfer side effects), the warning fires; a normal in-window partial-tail job is still built with all fields intact; the preserved hash-alignment invariant still asserts; the aligned path behaves bit-identically before and after the fix. 9/9 pass.

## Notes

GPU/e2e reproduction (real hybrid model under load) was not possible on this machine; the unit test drives the actual scheduling code path directly instead.

items.author: Virtuoso461
items.summary: Fixes #43743 ## What does this PR do? 's large-batch path still used the old DeepGemm contract: it allocated a output and passed explicitly to. [Discussion: <!-- pr-check-comment runs=38894547921 --> Required checks failed on 1eafc22; this PR cannot be merg]
items.body:
Fixes #43743

## What does this PR do?

`mhc_fused_post_pre`'s large-batch path still used the **old DeepGemm contract**: it allocated a `{n_splits, m, n}` output and passed `num_splits` explicitly to `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`. The current contract (and the pin `sgl-deep-gemm` exposes via its C++ assertion) only accepts `{1, m, n}` when `num_splits` is given — split-K is now reduced internally — so CUDA-graph capture crashes on the assertion.

The only form valid under **both** the old pinned wheel and the new contract is: 2D `{m, n}` output, no `num_splits` argument (the form `deepseek_v4.py` already uses for its plain GEMM). This PR rewrites all four remaining old-contract call sites to that form:

- `mhc.py::mhc_fused_post_pre` (the issue's crash): 2D output, then `unsqueeze(0)` to `{1, m, n}` with `n_splits=1` for the downstream big-fuse kernel — same shape the fallback branch already feeds it; also removes the now-useless large `{n_splits, m, n}` pre-allocation.
- `mhc.py::mhc_pre` (same old contract, reachable via the default-on path and `prewarm_mhc_pre`)
- `mhc.py::hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm` (2 GEMMs + reduce with `NUM_SLICES=1`, offsets proven elementwise-equivalent to the previous 3D layout)
- `deepseek_v4.py::_flashinfer_hc_pre` (behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_FLASHINFER_MHC`; removes the dead squeeze branch)

## Verification (GPU e2e not runnable here — stated plainly; mock/CPU level)

- Mocked `deep_gemm` implementing **both** contracts, injected into the real (AST-extracted) old and new function sources: old code crashes the new-contract assertion with exactly the issue's shape error; new code passes both contracts, and downstream kernels receive `{1,m,n}` with `n_splits=1`. Small-batch FMA (`{4,m,n}` TileLang partials) and fallback paths verified unchanged. 17/17 checks.
- The pinned `sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.2` wheel was unpacked: its embedded assertion text proves `num_splits>1` requires `{n_splits,m,n}` there, i.e. the no-`num_splits` 2D form is the only dual-compatible choice.
- Local wheel execution-level verification is not possible on this machine (the wheel aborts inside its C++ entry for any input on sm120, before any kernel of ours), stated explicitly.

## Notes

- Dead code left behind on purpose (`_flashinfer_mhc_pre_num_splits` etc.) — cleanup can follow once maintainers confirm the contract migration.
- Old-contract callers lose the explicit caller-side split-K, which the issue reporter measured as no-benefit on this fused path anyway.

items.title: [CI][ROCm][Disagg] Add DeepSeek-V3 NIXL accuracy steps
items.author: avininjamay8
items.summary: Read: 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, 2P2D EP16/DP16. Write: 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, and 2P2D EP16/DP16. [Discussion: @lcskrishna please review.]
items.body:
## Purpose

Add DeepSeek-V3 disaggregated prefill/decode accuracy steps that use NIXL over UCX RDMA on MI350, next to the existing MoRIIO steps. Read uses `NixlConnector`. Write uses `NixlPushConnector` for 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8, and 2P2D EP16.

The 2P2D EP16 write step needs https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62055. That change keeps push heartbeats and outgoing WRITE polling on the writer thread, so a blocked NIXL call cannot miss an expert-parallel collective.

## Changes

- `pipeline-disagg.yaml`: six DeepSeek-V3 steps. Read (`NixlConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, 2P2D EP16/DP16. Write (`NixlPushConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, and 2P2D EP16/DP16.
- `run-slurm-disagg-test.sh`, `run_xPyD_disagg.slurm`: add `KV_CONNECTOR` (default `MoRIIOConnector`) and pass it to the containers. For NIXL, start vllm-router with `--kv-connector nixl` and fixed `--prefill`/`--decode` URLs, because NIXL has no discovery service.
- `vllm_disagg.sh`: when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`, use that name in the NIXL KV transfer config (UCX backend). On 2P2D EP16 prefill, set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. At 0.85 the AITER MoE sort buffer runs out of memory. EP8 stays at 0.85.
- `cluster.sh`: for either NIXL connector, set UCX defaults for the ionic RoCE NICs (RC verbs on `ionic_0`, GPU-direct RDMA) and run accuracy with one concurrent request. The router flag stays `--kv-connector nixl` for both.

MoRIIO steps do not change. All new settings apply only when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`.

Requirement: the image's UCX must support `rc_verbs` on ionic NICs that report `max_srq=0`. The results below used UCX 1.22 with that support. The 2P2D EP16 write result also used the writer-thread ownership from #62055.

## Test plan
