items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv4: Swap-AB sparse decode attention up to 24 rows with PDL and a narrow combine
items.author: DarkSharpness
items.summary: Past 8 rows, SM100 used FlashMLA on 64 zero-padded heads; swap-AB is faster up to 24 rows, and FlashMLA wins from 32. waits before its first load and triggers its dependents after its last global load.
items.body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

Split from #44626 by @YAMY1234 (the sparse decode attention part), without the `--enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode` switch.

## Modifications

- `can_use_swapab_attention` takes up to `SM100_MAX_ROWS = 24` rows (was 8). Past 8 rows, SM100 used FlashMLA on 64 zero-padded heads; swap-AB is faster up to 24 rows, and FlashMLA wins from 32.
- `swapab_attention` launches the split-KV kernel and the combine with PDL (`pdl=True` by default). `partial_gluon` waits before its first load and triggers its dependents after its last global load. The combine waits, then triggers right away, so `fused_rope_wo_a` streams its weights during the combine.
- Narrow combine (`narrow_combine=True` by default): one-warp programs over 128 columns when there is an extra key range.
- gfx950 is unchanged: `swapab_gluon_hip` passes `pdl=False, narrow_combine=False` and still dispatches at most 8 rows.

## Accuracy

B300: `test_swapab_attention.py` passes. Ad hoc cases at 1-24 rows (eager and CUDA graph, with and without PDL / narrow combine) match the fp64 reference at the bf16 rounding floor. PDL and the trigger position are bit-identical to the non-PDL path. At 9-24 rows, swap-AB is closer to the reference than FlashMLA (RMS error 1.00x vs 1.27-1.38x the bf16 floor).

## Speed

B300, one CUDA graph of `fused_q_norm_rope` -> attention -> `fused_rope_wo_a_bf16` (all with PDL), cold L2, us, median of 5 processes:

| Rows | main | this PR | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 19.37 | 16.71 | 1.16x |
| 8 | 19.63 | 16.85 | 1.17x |
| 12 | 29.14 | 17.28 | 1.69x |
| 16 | 29.19 | 20.24 | 1.44x |
| 24 | 29.58 | 21.52 | 1.37x |

PDL alone accounts for 1.6-2.5 us of the chain at every row count. In the end-to-end decode of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300 (TP4, EP1, DSpark), sparse attention per step drops from 824 to 363 us at batch 2 (12 rows) and from 827 to 519 us at batch 4 (24 rows).

items.title: [Feature] Chi-squared and perplexity watermarking
items.author: KristianMin
items.summary: Adds the chi-squared watermark and the two perplexity watermarks, and, from. The implementation is built on top of the watermarking infrastructure introduced in #53916 / #54053. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Adds the chi-squared watermark and the two perplexity watermarks, `ppl_hard` and `ppl_soft`, from [Gloaguen et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06754). The implementation is built on top of the watermarking infrastructure introduced in #53916 / #54053. 

## Claims

- `--watermark-config '{"algorithm": "chi_squared", "key": 42}'` samples from `q = p * w`, where `p` is the unwatermarked distribution, and `q` maximizes the expected watermark score minus a chi-squared distance from `p` (Theorem D.6 of the [Gloaguen et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06754)). Each token score is Binomial(30, 1/2), computed using the Philox PRF from the key and the last `context_width` tokens (default 4). The variable `delta` (default 1.0) sets the strength of the watermark.
- `"algorithm": "ppl_hard"` and `"ppl_soft"` use the same scores, but bound the expected surprisal `-log p` of the watermarked token above the model's entropy. The variable `epsilon` (default 0) is that budget in nats, met for every key (`ppl_hard`) or on average over keys (`ppl_soft`).
- `BinomialScoreWatermarkDetector` returns a one-sided binomial p-value for all three.
- All three reject speculative decoding, also with `allow_target_only_watermarking: true`.

## Validation

Tests: `tests/watermarking/test_chi_squared.py`, `test_perplexity.py` and `test_binomial.py` (new), the new golden candidates (`tests/watermarking/golden_candidates.py`, `watermarking_goldens.json`), `tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py`, `test_watermarking.py`, `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py`.

**Parity with the reference implementation.** A separate harness ran each watermark in vLLM and in the authors' implementation ([eth-sri/unified-watermarking](https://github.com/eth-sri/unified-watermarking), as Model Runner V1 logits processors) with the same model, prompts, sampling settings and keys: Qwen3.8-27B, 100 prompts each from ELI5 economics, ELI5 mathematics, WildChat and MMLU-Pro, 5 keys, temperature 0.7, top-k 50, 10 to 512 new tokens, context width 4, and vLLM's context deduplication off, as the reference has none. The two sides derive their randomness differently (Philox over the ordered context in vLLM, SumHash in the reference), so their texts differ, and the harness compares distributions: intervals come from a bootstrap over prompts and keys, and |z| ≥ 3 flags a difference. For chi-squared, the reference's `log w` is multiplied by `T`, so that both sides sample `p * w`.

| Watermark | Strength | TPR@1% FPR: reference -> vLLM |
|---|---|---|
| chi-squared | delta = 1.0 | 0.865 -> 0.861  |
| `ppl_hard` | epsilon = 0.2 | 0.849 -> 0.841  |
| `ppl_soft` | epsilon = 0.1 | 0.942 -> 0.936  |

The signal is the mean standardized score of a generated token. Excess surprisal is the mean of `-log p(x) - H(p)` over generated tokens, in nats, where `p` is the distribution the watermark saw. 

**Cost.** The following evaluations were run on an NVIDIA H200 GPU, on Model Runner V2 at temperature 1.0 without top-k/top-p. Each cell is the change against no watermark.

| Benchmark | No watermark | Chi-squared | `ppl_hard` | `ppl_soft` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Qwen3-0.6B (FP16)** | | | | |
| `vllm bench serve`, 100 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens, concurrency 1: TPOT | 1.611 ms | +10.1% | +10.6% | +19.4% |
| `vllm bench serve`, 1000 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens, concurrency 32: output throughput | 9,572 tok/s | -6.6% | -5.6% | -12.8% |
| `vllm bench serve`, 1000 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens, concurrency 32: TPOT | 2.776 ms | +9.1% | +7.4% | +17.1% |
| `vllm bench latency`, 512 input / 256 output tokens, batch 1 | 421 ms | +10.3% | +9.6% | +17.5% |
| `vllm bench latency`, 512 input / 256 output tokens, batch 32 | 613 ms | +11.0% | +10.4% | +19.1% |
| `vllm bench throughput`, 1000 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens: output tok/s | 16,641 | -6.3% | -5.2% | -8.9% |
| **Qwen3-4B (BF16)** | | | | |
| `vllm bench serve`, 100 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens, concurrency 1: TPOT | 3.528 ms | +3.3% | +4.8% | +10.2% |
| `vllm bench serve`, 1000 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens, concurrency 32: output throughput | 3,881 tok/s | -3.0% | -3.1% | -5.4% |
| `vllm bench serve`, 1000 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens, concurrency 32: TPOT | 6.057 ms | +4.8% | +3.7% | +8.2% |
| `vllm bench latency`, 512 input / 256 output tokens, batch 1 | 932 ms | +4.6% | +2.7% | +6.8% |
| `vllm bench latency`, 512 input / 256 output tokens, batch 32 | 1,373 ms | +5.1% | +5.0% | +8.8% |
| `vllm bench throughput`, 1000 requests, 1024 input / 128 output tokens: output tok/s | 5,628 | -2.0% | -1.5% | -2.6% |

The Qwen3-4B cells and the throughput rows are means over 3 runs. The Qwen3-0.6B node's baseline drifted between runs, so its serve and latency cells are medians over 8 interleaved rounds. 

Reproduce with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` for both runs, adding `--watermark-config '{"algorithm":"chi_squared","key":42}'` (or `ppl_hard`, `ppl_soft`) to `vllm serve`, `vllm bench latency` and `vllm bench throughput` for the watermarked one:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --dtype float16 --generation-config vllm --no-enable-prefix-caching
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 \
    --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 1000 --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0
vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --dtype float16 --input-len 512 --output-len 256 --batch-size 1
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --dtype float16 --dataset-name random \
    --input-len 1024 --output-len 128 --num-prompts 1000
```

## Details

- **Fused sampling:** after a log-sum-exp pass, `_philox_score_levels_kernel` reads each row's logits once more and reduces them to the 31 score levels. Each algorithm then works on the levels instead of the vocabulary, without host synchronization:
  - chi-squared solves for its normalizer on the levels and adds `log w` to the logits, and the request's Gumbel sampler draws the token;
  - `ppl_hard` solves the linear program on 32 candidates, the most probable token of each score and the least probable token of the top score, and draws from the solution with the noise `gumbel_sample` uses;
  - `ppl_soft` finds `beta` by bisection over 128 Monte Carlo draws, each drawn as the ranks at which the scores first appear in probability order, instead of scoring the vocabulary 128 times.
- **Faithfulness:** each kernel follows a function adapted from reference code. As in the reference implementation, an output's first `context_width` tokens are sampled without the watermark and are not scored. Two differences are deliberate: `ppl_soft` draws and selects among the 4096 most probable tokens only, and `ppl_soft` derives its Monte Carlo draws from the context with a public Philox key instead of drawing them anew at every step, so its output is reproducible and independent of the rest of the batch.
- **Logprobs:** processed logprobs report the logits before the watermark, same as for Gumbel-max.
- **Detection:** a token's score is the number of Binomial(30, 1/2) CDF thresholds below its Philox uniform, so the detector recomputes it from token IDs alone. In case of no watermark, the summed score of `n` tokens is Binomial(30n, 1/2). The p-value is the survival probability of the summed score under Binomial(30n, 1/2).
- **Docs:** `docs/features/watermarking.md` has chi-squared and perplexity sections with usage.

Co-authored-by: Thibaud Gloaguen <thibaud.gloaguen@inf.ethz.ch>
Co-authored-by: Robin Staab <robin.staab@inf.ethz.ch>

items.title: [Quantization] Report the resolved kernel per layer in model inspection
items.author: awesome-pro
items.summary: Model inspection now reports the quantization kernel or backend that was actually selected for each layer, instead of only the quant method class name. This implements the "log selected kernels/backends by layer type" item from the Q4 roadmap (#61024, SIG Quan…
items.body:
## Overview

Model inspection now reports the quantization kernel or backend that was actually selected for each layer, instead of only the quant method class name. This implements the "log selected kernels/backends by layer type" item from the Q4 roadmap (#61024, SIG Quantization), which was requested in #52167.

Before:

```
QLinear(quant=Fp8Config, in_features=16, out_features=8)
```

After:

```
QLinear(quant=Fp8Config(kernel=CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel), in_features=16, out_features=8)
```

## Claims

- Each quantized layer reports its resolved kernel, or the backend enum name for MoE methods that record one.
- MoE layers now report a kernel at all. The load time log moved out of `create_model` to the end of `load_model`, after `process_weights_after_loading`. That step is where `moe_kernel` gets assigned, because it starts as `None` in `fused_moe/fused_moe_method_base.py:33`. Before this change every MoE layer printed no kernel while linear layers printed one, so the output was inconsistent.
- Works with the full set of kernel attribute names used across quant methods (`moe_kernel`, `fp8_linear`, `linear_kernel`, `ocp_mx_linear`, `kernel`, `experts_cls`), and with the compressed-tensors `module.scheme`. A kernel object is preferred over a backend enum, because the enum is set earlier and can go stale. `FusedMoEKernel` has no name of its own, so it prints as `FusedMoEKernel(experts=<ExpertsClass>)`.
- Unquantized layers, and inspection that runs before weights are processed, still report only `quant=<Name>`. Nothing is guessed.

## Validation

Tests, 31 total, all CPU only:

```
python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_model_inspection.py -q
31 passed
```

Pre-commit on the changed files passes, including `check-test-tethering`, `mypy`, `check-spdx-header` and `validate-config`.

Two of the new tests were confirmed to fail against the old code before the fix, so they do catch the bugs:

- load order: `assert [None] == ['MarlinMxFp4LinearKernel']`
- stale enum: `assert 'MARLIN' == 'MarlinMxFp4LinearKernel'`

Wider run over `tests/model_executor/` and `tests/config/` with and without the change gives the same failures and errors (125 failed, 70 errors both times, all pre-existing and caused by no network access and no GPU). The passed count goes from 1111 to 1142, which is the 31 new tests.

Not run: a real `vllm serve` with a quantized checkpoint. The machine used for this only has an ARM Mac, so there is no vLLM CPU build, no Triton and no GPU. The kernel attribute names were instead derived by scanning the quant method sources, and a test now does that scan automatically so the list cannot silently go stale. A run on real hardware would still be good to have.

## Details

Motivation is #52167, where 200lz asked for the resolved path per module, and fxmarty-amd agreed. This PR covers the kernel and backend stage of that. It does not cover the dequantizer or the checkpoint source.

Design decisions:

- The log call was moved rather than duplicated. `create_model` runs before the weights are processed, so it cannot see MoE kernels. It is also called on its own by the weight cache daemon, so that path now calls the log directly and keeps the old behaviour.
- The other entry point, `LLM.__repr__` through `WorkerBase.get_model_inspection()`, already runs after loading and did not need changes.
- The kernel attribute name is not the same in every quant method, so the code checks a fixed list of known names. If a method stores its kernel somewhere else it will not be reported until that name is added. `test_kernel_attributes_cover_every_selector_call_site` re-derives the list from the source and fails when a new name appears, so this should not go unnoticed.

Tradeoff and limitations:

- Kernel differences now split layers into separate groups in the inspection output, because `_get_child_signature` hashes the per module string. Output gets longer on mixed precision models. This is intended, but it does change existing inspection output.
- Selected kernel only. No dequantizer or checkpoint source information.
- Inspection still does not run on weight reload, only at load time.
- No accuracy evals. The change only formats attributes that already exist and moves one log call, so kernel selection and numerics are untouched.

Duplicate work check:

- Open PRs matching `model_inspection`, `VLLM_LOG_MODEL_INSPECTION` and `log_model_inspection`: none.
- The only open PRs that reference #52167 are #51808 and #53847, both unrelated to inspection output.
- #59460 by mgoin makes activation quantization fallbacks explicit and adds `VLLM_STRICT_QUANT_SCHEME`. It changes `quant_utils.py` and the kernel base classes, not `model_inspection.py`. That PR warns at selection time, this one reports the selection in the inspection output. They should compose through `executed_activation_key()`.

AI assistance was used to write this change. I reviewed every line, ran the tests above myself, and am accountable for the change.

items.title: [Fix] hicache: Separate storage keys for incompatible host layouts
items.author: lhzds
items.summary: Dense MHA and MLA host pools currently use the same storage keys across host memory layouts. With L3 caching enabled, restarting with after writing pages with, while retaining the same model, rank configuration, page size, and storage directory, lets a matchi…
items.body:
## Motivation

Dense MHA and MLA host pools currently use the same storage keys across host memory layouts. With L3 caching enabled, restarting with `page_first` after writing pages with `layer_first`, while retaining the same model, rank configuration, page size, and storage directory, lets a matching prefix reuse incompatible KV pages. The file backend accepts these pages because their byte counts are equal.

On an NVIDIA L20 with Qwen3-0.6B, three requests each reported a 240-token storage hit after this layout change and produced different token sequences from the cold-cache control. A GPU page round-trip reproduced the incorrect KV values for both MHA and MLA.

## Modifications

- Add layout-specific `storage_format_tag` values to the dense MHA and MLA host pools, using the existing storage model-name tagging path.
- Keep `layer_first` and `page_first_direct` in the same namespace because their flattened page byte order is identical.
- Add file-backend regression tests for compatible and incompatible layout pairs, including MHA `page_head`, and for untagged legacy pages.

Existing untagged MHA/MLA L3 entries will miss after this change, even if the host layout is unchanged. The cache must warm again under the new keys. Existing entries are not deleted or migrated.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU regressions: **65 tests and 37 subtests passed**.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_format_tag.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mem_pool_host.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_file_lru_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_hicache_attach.py
```

The new regression cases produce 16 failing subtests on the unmodified base. The storage-format test also passes when executed directly, as in registered CI.

Manual validation on one NVIDIA L20, using the file backend:

- **GPU page round-trip:** actual device-to-host and host-to-device transfers for MHA and MLA. All four incompatible `layer_first`/`page_first` cases now miss. All four same-layout cases restore every element exactly.
- **Qwen3-0.6B:** three 253-token prompts, 16 generated tokens each, TP=1, Triton attention, CUDA graphs disabled, `buffer_only`, `write_through`, and page size 16. After switching layouts, all three requests miss the incompatible entries and match the cold-cache outputs token for token. A subsequent same-layout run hits 240 tokens per request and matches the unmodified same-layout warm-cache control token for token.

GPU transfer validation covers `layer_first` and `page_first`. The `page_first_direct` and `page_head` cases are covered by CPU page-format tests. MLA validation covers GPU page transfers; the full-model run uses Qwen3-0.6B. Other storage backends were not exercised.

Local coverage collection crashed during imports on both the unmodified base and patched source, so no coverage percentage is reported.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. This change separates incompatible cache entries; it does not change transfer kernels.

items.title: [Fix] DeepSeek-V4.1: Keep one decode graph per batch size under DP attention
items.author: ChangLi811
items.summary: With and CUDA graph decode, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash silently produces wrong output; nothing errors or crashes. Reproduced on MI355X with current main (TP4 + DP4 attention, paged FP8 KV, default DP communication settings): - a short prompt sent alone decodes token …
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-dp-attention` and CUDA graph decode, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash silently produces wrong output; nothing errors or crashes. Reproduced on MI355X with current main (TP4 + DP4 attention, paged FP8 KV, default DP communication settings):

- a short prompt sent alone decodes token 0 after its first token, or repeats one word until `max_tokens`;
- long prompts (about 16k tokens and up), alone or several at once, are correct;
- long and short prompts sent together: the long ones go wrong as well.

**Root cause.** For each batch size, DeepSeek-V4.1 captures several decode graphs (`Dsv41CandidateGraphVariants`: `candidate_all` up to 512 tokens, `candidate_c2_all` up to 1024, `candidate_unfiltered` up to 16384, filtered beyond that) and picks one from the longest request in the batch, so short contexts can skip low-ratio indexer scoring or candidate filtering. `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` picks from **this rank's** `seq_lens_cpu`; the DP ranks never agree on the pick.

Under DP attention the ranks replay their decode graphs together, and the collectives around the MoE are inside the graph. When one rank holds only short requests while another holds a long request or is idle, the ranks replay **different** graphs. The aiter custom all-gather, reduce-scatter and all-reduce register each captured graph's own buffers for IPC, so a rank reads the peer buffer that belongs to the other graph, i.e. stale data, and every rank's tokens are corrupted.

**Evidence.** Logging each rank's pick (local debug logging, not part of this PR) on main with TP4 + DP4 attention showed the ranks replaying different variants on most decode replays while the output was wrong, e.g. one rank with a 220-token request on `candidate_all` while the three idle ranks replayed `candidate_filtered`. With `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, or with all three aiter collectives kept off per-graph registered buffers (local debug patch), the output is correct although the ranks still replay different variants.

**Relation to #43077.** #43077 added `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN` (default 0), which stages the aiter all-gather and reduce-scatter through the pre-registered IPC pool during capture instead of registering per-graph buffers. It does not cover the custom all-reduce, so on its own it does not fix this bug. The InferenceY DeepSeek-V4.1 DP recipe sets it together with other settings, and with the full recipe the output is correct; removing only `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN` from the recipe brings the bug back (a short prompt sent alone loops "Weohohoh..." until `max_tokens`). With the default settings on ROCm, DeepSeek-V4.1 with DP attention is exposed. Rather than making each in-graph collective tolerate ranks on different graphs, this PR makes all DP ranks replay the same graph.

The variants come from #38798 and were enabled on gfx950 by #41308.

## Modifications

- `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: `_rank_consistent_attention_graph_variants()` drops the DeepSeek-V4.1 per-rank variants (`create_dsv41_candidate_graph_variants`) under DP attention, so each batch size captures the single graph that long contexts already use, which is correct for any length. This covers the decode graphs and the DSpark target-verify graphs (same runner). The server logs what it drops, e.g. `DP attention: per-rank attention graph variants ('candidate_all', 'candidate_c2_all', 'candidate_unfiltered', 'candidate_filtered') disabled`. Without DP attention nothing changes; the dLLM runner does not go through this path.
- `test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: the variants are dropped with DP attention and kept without it.

## Scope

- Validated only on ROCm gfx950 (MI355X). NVIDIA SM100 enables the same variants and also picks them per rank under DP attention; not verified there.
- Only the DeepSeek-V4.1 variants change. The HIP DSA dense / sparse decode graphs (`DsaGraphVariants`, e.g. DeepSeek-V3.2) are also picked per rank and may have the same issue under DP attention; this PR neither changes nor tests them.

## Reproduction

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x MI355X, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm720-mi35x-20261015`:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --fp8-gemm-backend aiter \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion --max-running-requests 256 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --mem-fraction-static 0.70

curl -s localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of Australia? Answer in one sentence."}]}'
```

- main: `We之星之星之星之星…` until `max_tokens`.
- This PR: a one-sentence answer naming Canberra.

The InferenceY DP recipe (TP2 + DP2 + DSpark, which sets `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN=1`) answers correctly on main; with only `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN` removed from that recipe, main returns `Weohohohoh…` until `max_tokens` for the same request, and this PR answers correctly.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm720-mi35x-20261015` with the branch's whole `python/sglang` mounted over the image's, this PR rebased onto `06b81b120`, model default context (1M), server as in Reproduction (TP4 + DP4 attention, default DP communication, `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN=0`).

sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K, the settings of `test_deepseek_v41_flash_gb300.py` (`--load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --max-tokens 4096 --num-threads 64`), all 1319 questions:

| | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | **11.14%** | **95.83%** |

The same comparison with lm-evaluation-harness (`local-chat-completions`, 5-shot, through the InferenceX eval entry; strict-match / flexible-extract): main 0.9128 / 0.8931, this PR 0.9719 / 0.9712, and main with `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN=1` 0.9689 / 0.9629. With the InferenceY DP recipe (TP2 + DP2 + DSpark), this PR scores 0.9750 / 0.9742 on the same harness.

No server faults or NaN in any run.

An earlier revision of the same change (on top of #44031, main `d8f85223`) was also used for cross-node PD with DP attention on the decode side (TP8 + DP8 and TP4 + DP4): GSM8K 0.9719–0.9757 through the router.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Graph capture**: TP4 + DP4 decode graphs 61.3 s / 1.97 GB on main vs 61.6 s / 1.91 GB with this PR; the DP recipe's target-verify graphs 42.1 s / 2.57 GB vs 37.8 s / 2.53 GB.

**Cost**: under DP attention, short-context decode (16k tokens or less) no longer skips low-ratio scoring and candidate filtering.

Short-context throughput: InferenceY DP recipe (TP2 + DP2 + DSpark, where main is correct), `bench_serving` with random token ids, 1k input / 1k output, 4 x concurrency requests; main and this PR side by side on one node (2 GPUs each). Second of two rounds; the first round right after startup varied in both directions.

| Concurrency | main: output tok/s, TPOT | This PR: output tok/s, TPOT |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1258, 2.79 ms | 1187, 2.83 ms |
| 32 | 4458, 5.80 ms | 4166, 5.90 ms |
| 64 | 6210, 7.80 ms | 5855, 7.96 ms |

With this PR, TPOT is 1.4–2.1% higher and output throughput 5.6–6.5% lower (throughput also moves with the DSpark acceptance rate). This is the cost of the short-context variants under DP attention; the "Alternatives" section below would keep them.

## Alternatives considered

- **All DP ranks pick by the global longest request.** One more integer in the existing per-step DP sync would keep the short-context speedup, but it touches the scheduler, the batch, `ForwardBatch` and the variant classes, and an off-by-one between the synced length and the length used for the pick selects a wrong graph at the 512 / 1024 / 16384 boundaries without any error. It can be a follow-up if reviewers want to keep the short-context path.
- **Turning `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN` on by default.** It only covers the aiter all-gather and reduce-scatter, not the custom all-reduce, and the ranks would still replay different graphs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Feat] [AMD] DeepSeek-V4.1: Prefill CP fixes on top of #43465: zero-row groups, decode attention TP, image inputs
items.author: ChangLi811
items.summary: Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with it on MI355X under long-context, mixed-length load, we hit three remaining gaps, which this PR closes: 1. a one-token extend lands on another rank).
items.body:
## Motivation

#43465 (@At1a8) enables prefill context parallel (CP) for DeepSeek-V4.1 on HIP. Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with it on MI355X under long-context, mixed-length load, we hit three remaining gaps, which this PR closes:

1. **GPU memory fault at concurrency 64.** Under CP, a request group can own no rows on a rank (e.g. a one-token extend lands on another rank). The HIP low-ratio indexer still launched the fp4 prefill logits kernel for that group, and with 0 rows the kernel reads a null page table (address 0). The kernel-side issue is ROCm/aiter#6562.
2. **`--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` does not work for DeepSeek-V4.1.** On gfx950, the V4.1 block-fp8 linears run from scale copies derived at load time (`weight_scale_mx_e8m0`, `weight_scale_inv_mx`, `weight_bf16`), which were not narrowed along with the weight.
3. **Image requests are wrong under CP.** The CP runner drives the language model directly, so image spans never reached the embeddings, and image pad hashes reached Engram / hash / vision routing unmapped.

### Relation to #43465

The first commit is #43465 unchanged (author Wang, FangYuan, head `ffcc41d2`). It is carried only so this PR builds and tests on its own, and it drops out on rebase once #43465 merges. **Please review only the last two commits.** If the author of #43465 prefers, the two commits can also be folded into #43465.

## Modifications

1. `[AMD] DeepSeek-v4.1: Support prefill context parallel`: #43465, unchanged.
2. **Zero-row groups and MXFP8 scale slicing**:
   - `low_ratio_backend_hip.py`: skip a request group that has no rows on this rank and publish no candidate mask for it (with 0 rows the fp4 logits kernel reads a null page table, and top-k cannot launch on an empty batch);
   - `cp_decode_attn_tp.py`: when narrowing the attention linears per rank, slice the gfx950 scale copies on the same dim as the weight; reject the MXFP8-native route, whose weights are pre-shuffled into scaled-MFMA lane order at load time and cannot be narrowed, with an error that names `--fp8-gemm-backend aiter` or `triton`;
   - tests: `test_dsv41_low_ratio_zero_row_hip.py`, `test_cp_decode_attn_tp.py`.
3. **Image inputs under CP**:
   - `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.prepare_cp_inputs` reuses `prepare_language_model_inputs` to prepare the image embeddings and the remapped ids on the whole sequence before sharding; the CP runner shards them and hands the ids the hook returns to the logits step;
   - under the late-layer tail, the ids the MoE routes are gathered like its hidden states (local rows under MoE A2A); the DP attention branch is unchanged;
   - test: `test_eager_runner_cp_inputs.py`.

## Supported scope and limitations

- Validated only on ROCm gfx950 (MI355X).
- The vision tower itself is **not** context-parallel: every CP rank runs it on the whole sequence, as every TP rank does today. Vision under CP is only allowed without MoE A2A.
- `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` needs `--fp8-gemm-backend aiter` (or `triton`). With the default `auto`, gfx950 takes the MXFP8-native route and the server refuses to start with a `NotImplementedError` that names the fix.
- CP on HIP does not support the breakable prefill CUDA graph; all runs below use `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`.
- The zero-row skip is a framework-side guard; the kernel-side fix is tracked in ROCm/aiter#6562.
- Two cases of `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py` fail on a ROCm GPU because of #43465's HIP 16-token floor (they fail with #43465 alone as well); this test runs on CPU only in CI.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm720-mi35x-20261015` with the branch's whole `python/sglang` mounted over the image's, main `e5274752` (this PR is rebased onto `06b81b120` without conflicts), model default context (1M), paged FP8 KV, vision tower built. Common flags: `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --fp8-gemm-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-running-requests 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.85`.

sgl-eval 0.1.3 with the settings of `test_deepseek_v41_flash_gb300.py` (`--load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --num-threads 64`; GSM8K all 1319 questions with `--max-tokens 4096`, MMMU-Pro 200 questions with `--max-tokens 32768`), this PR rebased onto `06b81b120`:

| Configuration | GSM8K | MMMU-Pro (image inputs) |
|---|---|---|
| TP8, no CP | 96.29% | 76.50% |
| TP8 + CP8 (this PR) | 96.59% | 77.00% |

With DSpark (the InferenceY deployment recipe, see below), TP4: GSM8K 96.29% without CP and 96.66% with CP4 + `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`.

With lm-evaluation-harness (5-shot GSM8K through the InferenceX eval entry, strict-match / flexible-extract): TP4 + CP4 + `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` 0.9727 / 0.9719, TP8 + CP8 0.9697 / 0.9689.

No server faults or NaN in any run. Without commit 2, a ~600k-token request batched with a one-token extend under CP4 faults at address 0 every time; with it, the batch completes.

Unit tests: the three new test files pass; on the commits without the corresponding fix, the new cases fail.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR fixes functionality; the prefill CP speedup itself is #43465's. `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`, which works for DeepSeek-V4.1 with commit 2, shards attention over the CP group in decode. `bench_serving`, TP4 + CP4, random token ids, 8k input / 1k output, 5 x concurrency requests (at least 16), same flags as above:

| Concurrency | CP4: output tok/s, TTFT, TPOT | CP4 + decode-attn TP: output tok/s, TTFT, TPOT |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 158.8, 288 ms, 6.02 ms | 179.8, 291 ms, 5.28 ms |
| 16 | 1622, 1454 ms, 8.45 ms | 1624, 2254 ms, 7.65 ms |
| 32 | 2647, 1447 ms, 10.68 ms | 2628, 2842 ms, 9.40 ms |
| 48 | 3177, 2006 ms, 13.15 ms | 3831, 1607 ms, 10.96 ms |

Decode-attention TP lowers TPOT by 9–17%. Mean TTFT is higher at concurrency 16 and 32 in this run; we have not looked into it.

**On top of DSpark.** CP and decode-attention TP also work with DSpark speculative decoding. The InferenceY DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 recipe (`--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5`, `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`, `--prefill-decode-interval 96`, `--swa-prefix-tails 1024`, `--max-running-requests 32`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.70`, INT8 quick reduce, OPUS sparse prefill) without and with `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`; `bench_serving` with random token ids, 5 x concurrency requests (at least 16):

| Input / output | Concurrency | TP4 + DSpark: output tok/s, mean TTFT | + CP4 + decode-attn TP: output tok/s, mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64k / 1k | 1 | 375.8, 1.37 s | 375.2, 1.34 s |
| 64k / 1k | 4 | 943.8, 1.91 s | 984.3, 1.81 s |
| 64k / 1k | 8 | 695.2, 8.50 s | 786.4 (+13%), 7.13 s (−16%) |
| 64k / 1k | 16 | 772.1, 16.38 s | 848.6 (+10%), 14.42 s (−12%) |
| 8k / 1k | 1 | 679.7, 0.14 s | 580.1 (−15%), 0.14 s |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 2386.4, 3.96 s | 2485.8 (+4%), 3.65 s |

With long inputs under concurrency, CP shortens the queue behind long prefills; for a single short request, decode with DSpark is slower here (TPOT 1.59 vs 1.34 ms). Each point is a single run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [None][feat] Add a Mooncake store backend for unified KV sharing
items.author: chuangz0
items.summary: This PR adds the store backend for RI-08D, with Mooncake as its first store. Nothing is wired into the executor yet, so the path stays off until a runtime assembles it.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the store backend for RI-08D, with Mooncake as its first store.
- `BlobBackend` serves #20117's `Backend`/`Attempt` contract on top of #20217's private `StoreDriver` boundary.
- `MooncakeDriver` maps that boundary onto the pinned Mooncake 0.3.13 SDK.
- `BlobAssembly` has the `factory(regions, wake, config)` shape that RI-02's TransferManager expects.

Nothing is wired into the executor yet, so the path stays off until a runtime assembles it.

The initial profile follows the design: KVCM v2, TP1/DP1/PP1/CP1, one pool, host staging from the #19722 lender, and `None` hints only. Names like RI-08D are items of the Runtime Integration design; M1–M5 are milestones of the Store Backend design. Both documents are linked below.

## Design

- [Unified KV Sharing: Runtime Integration, tab "v1: design and roadmap"](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mGPenQwYacIOqVoEB2TMkPO_Gs2uuR38pAOB-IAVEuc/edit?tab=t.px3o2phq226j), with RI-08D and RI-09 in [M2](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mGPenQwYacIOqVoEB2TMkPO_Gs2uuR38pAOB-IAVEuc/edit?tab=t.cnteczxnlr27).
- [Unified KV Sharing: Store Backend](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Y5O4WhH2tKSfS1_xdfA212fTFlyK3WY5L0XIz8Dobp0/edit?tab=t.jth9eb23u87v). This PR covers M3, the Mooncake driver, plus the M1 backend that M3 needs in order to run.

| Design item | Where |
|---|---|
| RI-08D: "Assembly creates BlobBackend; TransferManager retains it" | `blob/assembly.py`: `BlobAssembly(lender, open_driver)` is the factory, and its `finalize` only releases the lender hold |
| RI-08D: the store owns batching, the driver, the pinned SDK, registration and holds, cancellation and access-end evidence; hold calls run on the manager thread | `blob/assembly.py` takes the lender hold before it registers anything. `RegionBinding` (`blob/backend.py`) releases the hold on the owner thread, and only after every region is confirmed unregistered. If a registration fails and is fully rolled back, the builder thread releases it instead. |
| RI-08D: the store owns SDK capacity | `BlobConfig.workers` (default 4) bounds concurrent driver calls. Publishes take at most `workers − 1` of them, and fetches go first, with one publish batch after every four. |
| RI-08D: "initial Store accepts only None as its hint" | A non-`None` hint raises `InvalidSubmission` before dispatch, and the driver declares `hints=False` |
| RI-09: backend-owned hold cleanup runs on the manager thread after deregistration | `test_blob_assembly.py::test_finalize_releases_the_hold_only_after_shutdown_and_never_closes_the_sdk` and `test_blob_backend.py::test_shutdown_never_calls_the_driver_and_unregisters_in_the_background`; every CPU endpoint also checks that the hold is released on the owner thread |
| Store §3.1: delivery and ended access are separate facts; partial delivery and a fault can coexist; a frozen Outcome never changes | `BlobAttempt.poll()` and `quiesced()` report separate facts, and each is set once under the backend lock |
| Store §3.2: resources come back only after access has ended | A batch counts as started before it enters the SDK. An attempt quiesces only when every started batch has proven that its access ended. |
| Store §3.3: advisory cancel, a WakeFn call on the outcome and on access end, bounded and repeatable shutdown | Cancel drops queued batches. `wake()` runs after the state is published, outside the lock. `shutdown(timeout)` never calls the driver; drain and unregister run on the progress thread. |
| Store §3.5: put is READY only for a complete, readable object, never on "already exists" alone | A session put ends only the rows whose ranged write returned the full size. A key that already exists is READY only if `batch_is_exist` sees it committed. |
| Store A.2: what a driver must answer | `blob/mooncake.py`; see "Mooncake mapping" below |
| Store §5 M3: SDK mapping and real-service tests that reuse the round-trip cases | `test_mooncake_real.py`; `test_blob_backend_round_trip.py`, which uses a real lender on GPU; #20217's `driver_conformance` suite run against `MooncakeDriver` |
| Store §6: `kv_sharing.backends: [{type: mooncake, config: <path>}]`, with store parameters in the store's own file | `blob/mooncake_setup.py` reads a YAML file with `blob` and `mooncake` sections; no LLM args are added |

Where the implementation departs from the design text:

- **Outcome freezing.** Store §3.1 freezes the Outcome at the first fault. With several workers, a later batch can fail while an earlier one is still landing, and freezing at that point would drop rows from the earlier batch that a prefix needs. Instead, the backend stops dispatching at the first fault and freezes the Outcome once the batches that already started have reported. The #20117 contract allows this.
- **Cancel is not forwarded to the driver.** Store §3.3 asks the backend to try to cancel started operations when the SDK supports it. Mooncake 0.3.13 has no cancel, so the backend only drops queued batches, which the contract's advisory cancel allows. Forwarding can be added once a production driver declares `cancel`.
- **No trailer.** Store §3.5 describes a format of payload plus trailer, but #20217 has since left the object format to each driver. A Mooncake object is the payload alone. It is checked by the SDK's size check and protected by the SDK's read lease (-707).

## Mooncake mapping

- **put** calls the session API: `batch_put_session_start`, then `batch_put_from_multi_buffer_ranges` (one scatter for the whole batch), then `batch_put_session_end`. Rows that did not land get `batch_put_session_revoke`.
  - The transfer engine's scatter `wait()` has no timeout. It returns only once every fragment has physically finished.
  - So once that call returns, its access has ended, even if it answered TRANSFER_FAIL, and a failed row is revoked only after its write has stopped.
  - With `batch_put_from`, by contrast, a transfer that times out after 60 s is revoked at once while RDMA writes may still be in flight. A late write could then land in space the master has already given to another object.
- **get** uses `batch_get_into`, one SDK call per batch.
  - A session get makes three SDK calls, and each return must reacquire the GIL.
  - Next to a thread running Python nonstop, a 32 × 1 MiB session get took 16 ms at p99, against 5.6 ms for `batch_get_into`.
- **Results**:

  | Mooncake answer | Row result |
  |---|---|
  | get: object not found (-704) | MISS |
  | Object still held by an unfinished write: get -703 (which also covers a stale replica endpoint), put start -600 (this client's own session), or -705 (not yet committed) | NOT_READY |
  | Pool full (-200) | DECLINED |
  | Lease expired (-707) | Read once more; FAULT if it expires again |
  | Wrong size, or any other code | FAULT |

- **Access-end evidence**:
  - A put's access ends when its ranged write returns an answer for every row, whatever the answers are, TRANSFER_FAIL included.
  - A get's access ends when `batch_get_into` answers every row and no answer is TRANSFER_FAIL.
  - In every other case `access_unprovable` turns true: a TRANSFER_FAIL on a get, an exception, or a wrong answer count. The backend then counts the call, stops polling it and keeps its attempt's slots.

## Scope

| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| Add BlobBackend, the public backend over a store driver | `backend.py`, `keys.key_stem`, and CPU behavior tests over #20217's `MemoryDriver` |
| Add the Mooncake store driver | `mooncake.py`, a fake SDK, mapping tests, and the conformance suite run over the fake SDK |
| Assemble a Mooncake blob backend from a store config | `mooncake_setup.py`, `assembly.py`, configuration and layering tests |
| Run the blob backend over a real Mooncake pool | Opt-in tests (`TRTLLM_MOONCAKE_REAL=1`) against `mooncake_master` and a segment provider, plus the conformance suite on the real store |
| Round-trip KV blocks between two staging lenders through the blob backend | GPU test with real KV cache managers, over in-memory and real Mooncake stores |
| Keep a worker for fetches and tune store workers and batch rows | Publishes take at most `workers − 1` workers; defaults `workers=4`, `bytes_per_batch=128 MiB`, `rows_per_batch=256` |

Production code: +1673 / −6 lines. Tests: +3245 lines.

## Verification

At `f1b1689682`, on main `9ec1bf3e58`'s prebuilt wheel with this branch's Python files on top:

- **CPU (the blob tests, run without torch):** 269 passed, 1 strict xfail, 33 skipped (23 need a real pool; 10 are conformance checks that do not apply to a driver's declared capabilities). pre-commit is clean over the six commits.
- **One GB200 node, real Mooncake over RDMA:** 1100 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing, below), 16 skipped, 2 strict xfail over `_torch/disaggregation/blob`, `_torch/disaggregation/test_backend_contract.py`, `_torch/executor/kv_cache/sharing`, plus `_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_mamba_cache_manager.py` and `disaggregated/test_kda_mamba_transfer.py`, the two files where main's recent commits meet #20117.
- **Conformance on the real store:** #20217's suite against `MooncakeDriver` gives 11 passed and 1 strict xfail (explained below). The other 6 checks are skipped as not applicable: the driver has no cancel, probe or row limit, and it declares both directions.
- **TCP:** the real-Mooncake and round-trip tests give 19 passed, 6 skipped, 1 strict xfail, the same as over RDMA.
- **Pre-existing failure, unrelated:** `test_backend_contract.py::test_lender_layout_and_arrays_fit_the_contract_with_explicit_field_mapping`. The lender renamed `StagingRegion` after #20117 was written.

**Why one conformance check cannot pass on Mooncake.** The check is `test_an_object_of_the_wrong_size_is_a_fault_not_a_miss`.
- If the object is shorter than the slot (a 4-byte object read into an 8-byte slot), Mooncake writes the object into the head of the slot and returns the object's size (`real_client.cpp:5169-5180`, `client_buffer.cpp:162-190`). The driver reports FAULT, and its access ends normally, but the slot is no longer untouched as the check requires.
- If the object is longer than the slot, Mooncake refuses it with -600 before any transfer (`real_client.cpp:5134-5141`).

The check is marked strict xfail until the rule is settled in #20217.

**Performance.** The microbenchmark behind these numbers will follow in a separate PR.
- Setup:
  - two GB200 nodes over RDMA, with segments on the other node;
  - 4 workers and 128 MiB per call.
- NIC use:
  - one process uses the two NICs of the NUMA node where its staging memory lives;
  - four ranks use all four NICs.
- "Busy" means another thread runs Python nonstop. This is the worst case for an executor that never releases the GIL.

| setup | main thread | put GB/s | get GB/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| one process, 4 MiB rows | idle | 89–91 | 94 |
| one process, 4 MiB rows | busy | 15–19 | 31–43 |
| one process, 1 MiB rows | busy | 12.5–14 | 24–27 |
| four TP ranks on one node, NUMA-bound, 1 MiB rows, node total | idle | 160 | 179 |
| same | busy | 52 | 95 |

A row is one KV block (32 tokens) across all layers of a layer group, holding this rank's heads. With TP the rows shrink, so realistic rows are 0.25–2.5 MiB. Examples:
- Llama-3.1-8B at TP4: 1 MiB;
- Llama-3.3-70B at TP4: 2.5 MiB;
- DeepSeek-V3 (MLA): 2.1 MiB.

## Please confirm

- **@chienchunhung**:
  - A call that cannot prove its access ended keeps its attempt's slots for good, and the binding ends in the profile's containment (executor-fatal for M1).
    - A fetch reaches this state on a TRANSFER_FAIL answer, an exception, or a wrong answer count from `batch_get_into`.
    - A publish reaches it only on an exception or a wrong answer count from the ranged write, because that write returns only after every fragment has finished.
  - A put call has no time bound. Any store call still running after 60 s is logged once, within about two minutes of its start.
  - `BlobAssembly` must run before the executor loop starts, because the lender's hold bookkeeping has no lock.
  - RI-02 treats any construction error other than RI-01's `FactoryRejected` as uncertain. Once RI-01 lands, one of two things must happen: `ConstructionRejected` becomes `FactoryRejected`, or the wiring re-raises it as `FactoryRejected`. Otherwise a clean refusal, such as an unreachable master, starts the containment path.
- **@nv-xtf / @Shixiaowei02**:
  - `keys.key_stem` is a small addition to #20217's `keys.py`.
  - Please settle the wrong-size conformance rule described above.
  - This PR overlaps with the planned BlobBackend PR. The backend here can serve as a reference or be replaced, since the Mooncake driver depends only on `blob/store.py`.

## Known limitations

- **The data path does its per-row work under the GIL.**
  - With the real SDK this costs 2–5 µs per row. At line rate the backend therefore holds the process's GIL 70–80% of the time with 0.25 MiB rows, and 20–35% of the time with 1 MiB rows.
  - The executor stays responsive. A thread sleeping 1 ms at a time wakes at most 0.5–0.8 ms late at p99, and up to 1.3 ms late with 0.25 MiB rows.
  - The store's throughput, however, drops sharply when the executor is busy (see the table above).
  - A GIL-free data path would bring busy throughput close to idle. It could come from a batched Mooncake API with completion notification, or from a C++ worker. Whether that is worth building should wait for the end-to-end TTFT measurement (Store M4).
  - With `sys.setswitchinterval(0.0005)`, busy throughput rose 2–7x, and the busy thread lost 9–13% of its loop rate while transfers ran. This is an observation; the PR does not change the switch interval.
- **Fetch latency next to a sustained publish load.**
  - With an idle main thread and 4 MiB rows, fetch p99 is 4.5x the no-load p99 (+2.4 ms).
  - With a busy main thread, p99 rises by 12.6 ms, and by 20–40 ms with 0.25–0.5 MiB rows.
- **Deployment.**
  - Bind each rank to its GPU's NUMA node. The lender's pinned staging lands on the NUMA node of the thread that allocates it, and the transfer engine uses the NICs local to the buffer's first page. Unbound ranks can therefore all end up on one node's two NICs.
  - One process tops out near 100 GB/s; four bound ranks reach 160–180 GB/s together.
- **Other.**
  - Session puts carry no checksum.
  - The SDK is pinned to 0.3.13, and the access-end reasoning relies on that version's transfer engine.
  - Production code never calls the SDK's `close()`: it holds the GIL and sends RPCs, while finalize runs on the executor thread.
  - The store's own config (the `blob` and `mooncake` sections of its YAML) is read into frozen dataclasses with strict type checks rather than Pydantic models; it does not become LLM args. Converting them to Pydantic is a small change if reviewers prefer it.
  - The real-Mooncake tests are opt-in and do not run in CI.

## Notes

Stack: main `9ec1bf3e58` → backend contract #20117 → blob driver boundary #20217 → this PR.
- The prerequisite commits are replays that keep their original authors.
- There was one conflict, in #20117's `test_mamba_cache_manager.py`. The resolution keeps main's Kimi fixture `mapping=Mapping()` and `spec_config=None`; the replayed commit message notes this.
- Review only the last six commits: [Mooncake-only diff](https://github.com/chuangz0/TensorRT-LLM/compare/5d504e0ace2853f74ec14467a748d646916188a8...f1b1689682f8b82241d788502db1deb67c306a15).

- [x] Contribution checklist reviewed: tests are included; there are no new dependencies and no new public LLM configuration fields; the new path is off unless a runtime assembles it.

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: fails on PRs whenever it lands on a smaller 5090 runner: launches its server with, a fixed 100 GB pinned host pool, and on runners with roughly 51-81 GB of host memory the server is OOM-killed at launch: The same shard passes when it draws a larger runner, so…
items.body:
## Motivation

`base-b-test-1-gpu-small (7)` fails on PRs whenever it lands on a smaller 5090 runner: `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage.py` launches its server with `--hicache-size 100`, a fixed 100 GB pinned host pool, and on runners with roughly 51-81 GB of host memory the server is OOM-killed at launch:

```
CI_OFFLINE: Offline launch failed (Server process exited with code -9), retrying with online mode...
Exception: Server process exited with code -9. Check server logs for errors.
✗ FAILED: .../test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage.py returned exit code 5
```

The same shard passes when it draws a larger runner, so affected PRs only get through by rerunning until they do. It hit four unrelated PRs on 2026-10-16 (#44583, #44533, #44613, #44614).

## Modifications

On CUDA the test no longer passes `--hicache-size`. With neither `--hicache-size` nor `--hicache-ratio` set, the server uses the default host/device ratio and `--hicache-host-memory-fraction` (0.8 by default) reduces it until the host pools fit the machine's available memory, including the cgroup limit. The test still exercises the hierarchical cache with the `file` storage backend and the same MMLU threshold. ROCm keeps its explicit `--hicache-size 200`.

## Test plan

- `black`, `isort`, `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037` clean on the changed file.
- Not run locally: the test's model (`meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`) is gated on the available machine, and its environment predates main's kernel requirements. This PR's own `base-b-test-1-gpu-small (7)` runs the test on the affected 5090 runners and is the validation.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6939212][fix] Bind the CUDA context for KVCM2 teardown on any thread
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: KV cache manager V2 objects can be destroyed on a Python thread that has no current CUDA context. Their teardown then fails with and poisons KVCM2 for the rest of the process.
items.body:
## Summary

KV cache manager V2 objects can be destroyed on a Python thread that has no current CUDA context. Their teardown then fails with `CUDA driver error: 201 (invalid device context)` and poisons KVCM2 for the rest of the process. This PR binds each object's CUDA context for its teardown.

Fixes https://nvbugs/6939212

## Root cause

- `~KvCache` → `close()` → `recordEventScope()` → `CachedCudaEvent(stream)` → `cuEventRecord`. `~Batch`, `~PlannedDropHandle` and `~KvCacheManager` also call the driver. All of them run on whichever thread destroys the object.
- `test_dsa_indexer` (V2 by default since #20097) leaves its `KVCacheManagerV2` reachable only through a reference cycle: the test-local `MockMetadata.__init__` closure captures `cache_manager`. Only the cyclic GC frees it, on whichever thread's allocation triggers the collection.
- In CI that can be the `--timeout-method=thread` or periodic-junit hang-watchdog thread. That thread has no CUDA context, so `cuEventRecord` returns 201 and the process-wide poison latch is set. Every later V2 test then fails with `CorruptedError` (479 failures in L0_PostMerge 3020, DGX_H100-PyTorch-5). Which thread runs the GC depends on timing, so the failure is flaky across H100/B200/B300/GB300.

## Fix

- New `kv_cache_manager_v2/utils/cudaContext.h`: `CudaContextBinding` records the CUDA context at construction.
- The first statement of each destructor calls `enterForTeardown()`. If the destroying thread does not already have the context current, this pushes it for the destructor body and the member destructors. The context is popped when the binding, declared before every driver-touching member, is destroyed.
- Applied to `KvCacheManager`, `KvCache`, `Batch` and `PlannedDropHandle`, the objects Python can drop on any thread.
- New regression test `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_teardown_without_cuda_context.py`. It destroys each object on a thread with no CUDA context. Its directory is already in the l0_h100, l0_b200 and l0_a10 test lists.

## Verification (H100, base 6544bcd91a2d, CI image)

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Real DSA test, GC on a fresh thread, then the next test | KVCM2 poisoned (201), next test `CorruptedError` | passes |
| `test_teardown_without_cuda_context.py` | 2 failed, 3 errors (201) | 3 passed |
| `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests` | – | 336 passed, 0 failed |
| `unittest/_torch/attention` (via `test_unittests_v2`, as CI runs it) | 4041 passed (the race did not trigger) | 4041 passed, 0 failed |

Not covered: only H100 was run; the code path does not depend on the GPU.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Dev Engineer Review
`CudaContextBinding` records a CUDA context and makes it current during teardown when needed. `KvCacheManager`, `KvCache`, `Batch`, and `PlannedDropHandle` use the binding so destructor work and member cleanup can access the owning context. The new `cudaContext()` accessor exposes the manager’s context to child objects. No current review findings were supplied; finding counts are unavailable. Reported validation is limited to H100; other GPU types were not tested.

## QA Engineer Review
The added CUDA-gated test file defines three regression tests. They cover teardown of a cache and manager together, teardown of a cache while its manager remains usable, and teardown of a published batch. Each test finalizes on a fresh thread, checks that the thread has no CUDA context before or after teardown, and checks that KVCM2 is not poisoned. The test directory is included in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_h100.yml`, `l0_b200.yml`, and `l0_cpu.yml`; no matching manual-QA list entry was found. Coverage verdict: sufficient for the listed teardown paths; reported validation covers H100 only. The author reports 3 regression tests passed, 336 KVCM2 tests passed, and 4041 attention tests passed.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kv_cache_manager_v2/batch.cpp`: `Batch` binds the manager context before destructor cleanup. Verify context restoration and batch event/resource cleanup when destruction occurs on a thread without a current context.
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kv_cache_manager_v2/batch.h`: The binding member precedes members whose destructors may call CUDA. Verify member destruction order keeps the context available through resource cleanup.
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kv_cache_manager_v2/kvCache.cpp`: `KvCache` and `PlannedDropHandle` bind the manager context during teardown. Verify cache close and conditional planned-drop behavior with and without a current context.

items.title: [Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs for faster Gated DeltaNet standard decode
items.author: Johnny-Liou
items.summary: Introduces ReplaySSM to cache recent SSM inputs and periodically flush recurrent state, reducing HBM bandwidth during Gated DeltaNet standard decode.
items.body:
Supersedes [#48792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48792), closed when the source fork was deleted.

## Background

This is the second sub-PR split from the large draft PR [#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576), which presents the full ReplaySSM design across Mamba2 and Gated DeltaNet for both standard and speculative decode. The first sub-PR, Mamba2 standard decode ([#48018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48018)), landed as `866fea2b9`, so this is a plain diff against main. It lands the next stage: Gated DeltaNet (GDN) standard decode. ReplaySSM caches recent SSM inputs instead of writing the recurrent state back to HBM on every step. It is a collaboration between Dao AI Lab and NVIDIA, and the full derivation and figures are in the [blog post](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/). AI assistance was used for parts of this work, and the authors have reviewed every changed line.

## Core concept

GDN decode is memory-bound. Each step loads and stores the delta-rule recurrent state (a `head_v x head_k` matrix per value head), and that per-step state store dominates HBM traffic. ReplaySSM keeps a small ring buffer of recent per-step inputs (the key `k`, the corrected value `d`, and the scalar gate `g`) together with a periodic checkpoint state. On most steps it reconstructs the state and reads the output from the checkpoint plus the buffer, and it writes the full state back only on periodic flushes, once every `L` steps, where `L` is the buffer length. On the non-flush steps the per-step state store becomes a small input append, which removes the dominant traffic.

The baseline only becomes bandwidth-bound at large batch. The table below reports the DRAM bandwidth the baseline `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` reaches, as a percentage of peak, measured in isolation with cold L2 at `L=16`.

| bs | H100 fp32 | H100 fp16 | B300 fp32 | B300 fp16 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 9.0% | 5.9% | 6.5% | 3.9% |
| 8 | 35.2% | 27.5% | 24.2% | 18.0% |
| 32 | 71.3% | 54.8% | 56.7% | 39.1% |
| 128 | 84.5% | 79.6% | 78.3% | 68.6% |
| 256 | 86.3% | 83.4% | 82.4% | 74.5% |
| 512 | 87.5% | 85.3% | 84.5% | 77.4% |

At small batch the per-request state footprint is tiny and the launch grid is small, so too few memory transactions are in flight to cover HBM latency, and the kernel is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound. In a hybrid model the small-batch step is also dominated by the MLP layers, not the SSM layers. Small batch is therefore not the target regime. ReplaySSM targets serving batch, where the GDN kernel saturates HBM and the per-step state store is the bottleneck.

## What this PR adds

Everything here is opt-in. With the feature off, the decode path is byte-for-byte the baseline.

- The GDN cached decode kernel `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_replayssm` (state-reconstruction route), plus its hardware-keyed launch-config helper (`_gdn_decode` in `replayssm_config.py`).
- No new config flags. It reuses the two flags added in #48018: `--use-replayssm` turns on cached decode, and `--replayssm-buffer-len` sets the history buffer length `L` (default 16).
- Integration. The Qwen3.5 GDN mixer dispatches to the kernel under the flag, the GDN attention metadata builder carries the per-row ring cursor, and the state-shape and state-dtype calculators size the extra `d`/`k`/`g` caches on the paged state. Single-token prefill rows route to the prefill path rather than the cached decode kernel. The conv path reuses vLLM's `causal_conv1d_update` unchanged.
- Prefix caching. Align mode (`--mamba-cache-mode align`) is supported: the builder re-anchors the ring at each mamba block start and forces a flush on the block-completing step, so the checkpoint carries the exact block-boundary state for reuse and cached prefixes match the baseline.

This covers standard (non-speculative) decode only.

## Design notes

### Paged cache layout

The input ring caches (`d`, `k`, `g`) and the checkpoint state live inside the paged KV block, appended as extra tensors on the baseline `(conv, ssm)` state, for five tensors total. They stay live across decode steps, the checkpoint until the next flush and the ring across many steps, so they must sit in HBM between kernel launches. Appending them onto the paged state reuses vLLM's per-request block allocation and block-table indexing directly. `g_cache` is fp32; the `d` and `k` caches use fp16 when activations are bf16 for better numerical precision.

### CUDA graphs and continuous batching

Whether a row flushes is per-row runtime data. Under continuous batching the rows in one captured batch sit at different buffer positions, so the flush status varies across the batch and cannot be a compile-time constant, even for standard decode. The write position is `decode_step mod L`, computed on the host each step from scheduler token counts and copied to the device asynchronously, so no device-to-host sync is needed. The metadata builder computes the per-row flush flag on the host (a row flushes at its last buffer slot, `write_pos == replayssm_buffer_len - 1`, and, in align prefix-caching mode, on the step that completes a mamba block) and passes it to the kernel as a per-row input, so one captured graph per batch size covers both the non-flush and the flush rows. Deriving the cursor from `decode_step mod L` each step also means recycled paged blocks need no zero-init.

## Results

Unlike the Mamba2 sub-PR, GDN has no tuned/default baseline split. The shipped launch config is the swept per-hardware optimum, and the baseline is vLLM's `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` at its own config, so every speedup below is a single honest number.

Two models are evaluated: Qwen3.5-4B (BF16) on one H100 and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 on one B300, at buffer length 16 with fp32 and fp16 SSM state, greedy, and CUDA graphs on. End-to-end numbers are produced with `benchmarks/replayssm/e2e_decode_speedup.py`.

> **Blackwell (B300) support:** this sub-PR ships a Triton kernel only, and on B300 that Triton kernel is bandwidth-capped for fp16 state (44% DRAM utilization). fp16 state on B300 is therefore not enabled in this sub-PR. fp32 state is not capped this way and reaches 1.49x at bs512, but is still suboptimal.
> A CuTe-DSL kernel targeting Blackwell removes the cap, and is planned as a subsequent separate PR. At bs512 it lifts the B300 kernel-level speedup from 1.49x to 1.66x for fp32 state, and from 1.05x to 1.61x for fp16 state.

### End-to-end speedup

Whole-model per-step speedup, `standard ms/step / ReplaySSM ms/step`, greedy, CUDA graphs on.

| bs | Qwen3.5-4B H100 fp32 | Qwen3.5-4B H100 fp16 | Qwen3.5-122B B300 fp32 |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.99x | 0.99x | 0.96x |
| 8 | 1.03x | 1.01x | 1.03x |
| 32 | 1.08x | 1.03x | 1.09x |
| 64 | 1.14x | 1.05x | 1.11x |
| 128 | 1.21x | 1.06x | 1.16x |
| 256 | 1.27x | 1.07x | 1.20x |
| 512 | 1.30x | 1.08x | 1.22x |

ReplaySSM wins most at serving batch, where the GDN layers take a growing share of the step, and stays roughly break-even at bs 1 to 8. fp16-state end-to-end on the dense 4B is lower than fp32-state because the fp16 GDN kernel is a smaller share of the MLP-dominated step.

### Kernel-level speedup

Isolated per-kernel CUDA-time speedup.

| bs | H100 fp32 | H100 fp16 | B300 fp32 | B300 fp16 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.88x | 0.58x | 0.51x | 0.39x |
| 8 | 1.34x | 1.07x | 1.16x | 0.85x |
| 32 | 1.54x | 1.27x | 1.37x | 0.94x |
| 128 | 1.66x | 1.37x | 1.44x | 1.04x |
| 256 | 1.68x | 1.39x | 1.46x | 1.05x |
| 512 | 1.67x | 1.41x | 1.49x | 1.05x |

Kernel speedup rises with batch and saturates by about bs 128 to 256. fp16 state on blackwell is not supported in this sub-PR.

### Buffer length

Isolated per-kernel speedup vs the baseline. Each cell lists buffer length `L` = 8 / 16 / 32, with the best of the three in bold.

| model | bs 8 | bs 32 | bs 256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B (H100) fp32 | 1.27x / **1.33x** / 1.21x | 1.46x / **1.54x** / 1.43x | 1.58x / **1.68x** / 1.59x |
| Qwen3.5-4B (H100) fp16 | 1.04x / **1.05x** / 0.94x | 1.24x / **1.27x** / 1.10x | 1.34x / **1.39x** / 1.20x |
| Qwen3.5-122B (B300) fp32 | 1.13x / **1.17x** / 1.11x | 1.28x / **1.37x** / 1.31x | 1.36x / **1.46x** / 1.40x |

Speedup is bell-shaped in buffer length, trading flush frequency against per-step traffic. `L=16` is best in every entry and is the shipped default.

## Tests

Correctness is checked at four levels, all on GDN.

Per-step kernel correctness lives in `tests/kernels/test_replayssm_standard_decode_gdn.py`. Every decode step is checked against the baseline packed-decode kernel over multi-flush sequences, across six state and activation precision combinations, the production model geometries (small, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-122B), buffer lengths 4 and 16, strided and contiguous layouts, and continuous batching with per-row buffer positions and null-padded slots. A separate case sweeps per-row write positions across a batch. Tolerances are near-exact at fp32 (output rtol 1e-4, atol 1e-4; state rtol 1e-3, atol 2e-3), tight enough to catch a TF32 matmul-precision regression, and looser at bf16 and fp16 where rounding dominates.

Prefill and decode equivalence lives in `tests/kernels/test_replayssm_teacher_decode_equivalence_gdn.py`. Because the delta-rule recurrence is path-independent, the chunked prefill kernel (`chunk_gated_delta_rule`, the path the model runs at prefill) and step-by-step decode must give the same per-position outputs and final state. Both the baseline and the ReplaySSM step decoders are anchored on the chunked-prefill teacher, whose inputs are built with the same shared `fused_post_conv_prep` the model uses.

Metadata-builder unit tests live in `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`. The per-row write position and flush flag are the riskiest new logic, so they are covered on CPU with no model: fresh decode, flush boundary, buffer wrap, resume re-anchor after preemption, and per-row independence across a batch. Align mode adds the block re-anchor, the forced boundary flush, and a buffer length that does not divide the mamba block size. Two cases pin the batch split: a final single-token prefill chunk stays in the decode group so a full cudagraph replays with a refreshed cursor, and a first-token prefill stays a prefill. One case asserts the builder rejects stochastic rounding.

Engine-level parity lives in `tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py`. It compares the baseline (feature off) against ReplaySSM (feature on) with greedy decode and `check_logprobs_close` on Qwen3.5-4B, at TP1 and, under `@multi_gpu_test`, at TP2.

On current main, the two kernel files are 92 passed (one H100), and the builder file is 79 passed on CPU (17 ReplaySSM cases; the rest are main's). TP1 and TP2 engine parity both pass for decode and align-mode prefix caching; the TP2 run confirms the per-rank sharded caches and checkpoint stay correct.

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_replayssm_standard_decode_gdn.py \
       tests/kernels/test_replayssm_teacher_decode_equivalence_gdn.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py \
       tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py -q
```

## Model evaluation (GSM8K)

Evaluated on Qwen3.5-4B (1x H100), greedy, fp32 SSM state, CUDA graphs on, with the `<think>` block disabled in the chat template (`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False}`). Accuracy is reported under CoT prompting. Baseline and ReplaySSM use the identical prompt and seed, so the parity comparison is unaffected by the prompt choice.

CoT prompt (verbatim; `{question}` is the GSM8K problem):

```
{question}

Solve step by step, then give the final answer as 'The answer is <number>.'
```

Answer extraction: the number following an `answer is`, `answer:`, `####`, or `\boxed{}` marker (last match), falling back to the last number in the output.

| config | accuracy (CoT, N=1319) |
|---|---:|
| baseline (no ReplaySSM) | 0.917 +/- 0.008 |
| ReplaySSM (L=16) | 0.920 +/- 0.008 |

The 0.003 difference is within one binomial standard error, so ReplaySSM matches the baseline.

Prefix caching (align): on a 20-shot CoT run (N=200) with `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, `get_metrics()` reports a prefix-cache hit rate of 0.90 for the baseline and 0.86 for ReplaySSM, and accuracy is 0.925 for both. The align cached path is also covered by the e2e test `test_replayssm_prefix_caching_matches_baseline`, which asserts cache hits.

## Duplicate check

No open PR addresses ReplaySSM GDN standard decode. This PR is split from the large draft PR [#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576) (also closed when the source fork was deleted), and builds on the Mamba2 standard-decode sub-PR [#48018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48018). The related prior ReplaySSM PRs we are aware of are Mamba2-focused and do not cover GDN:

- [#43102](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43102) and [#43439](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43439), earlier PRs from our collaborator on the same ReplaySSM effort. This is the newer, more complete version.
- [#46239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46239), opened by another contributor based on our original fork. We have since made substantial changes, intend to land the feature ourselves, and have notified the author.

## Out of scope

- Stochastic rounding for low precision state.
- Speculative decode for GDN, which will land in a later sub-PR.
- Model Runner V2. Like the Mamba2 Triton path on main, GDN ReplaySSM requires `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`.

items.title: [Docs] [AMD] Qwen3.8-27B cookbook: Add an MI355X MXFP4 recipe
items.author: vorapolsiloai
items.summary: The Qwen3.8-27B cookbook page has no AMD recipe. AMD publishes an MXFP4 checkpoint for CDNA4,: the language model is MXFP4 W4A4 and the vision encoder stays bf16.
items.body:
## Motivation

The Qwen3.8-27B cookbook page has no AMD recipe. AMD publishes an MXFP4 checkpoint for CDNA4, `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`: the language model is MXFP4 W4A4 and the vision encoder stays bf16. It runs on a single MI355X.

## Modifications

- `qwen3.8-27b.jsx`:
  - adds `mi355x` hardware and an `MXFP4` quantization option;
  - maps the model name to the AMD checkpoint;
  - sets the ROCm docker image (`lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261014`).
- New `mi355x` / `mxfp4` cell, single GPU like the other cells. Flags come from the AMD nightly performance config for this checkpoint at TP1:
  - `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--quantization quark`, `--attention-backend aiter`;
  - `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.9`, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384`;
  - the qwen3 reasoning and tool-call parsers.

  The cell reports **Final Verification In Progress** until the accuracy results below are in.
- The DSPARK overlay is disabled on MI355X: it pins a FlashInfer draft attention backend, which ROCm does not ship.
- Page text: MI355X added to the supported cards. A note recommends `--mm-enable-dp-encoder` when serving at `--tp-size 2`, so that each GPU encodes whole images instead of splitting every vision layer across both GPUs.

`node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passes.

## Accuracy Tests

Pending (MI355X): GSM8K (1319 questions, `run_eval`) for the new cell, and MMMU at TP2 with `--mm-enable-dp-encoder` off/on.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Pending (MI355X): image-serving throughput at TP2 with `--mm-enable-dp-encoder` off/on.

items.body:
# PR description

- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Restore the tensor-value assertion in `TestSerialization.test_empty_load`.

The test gives rank 3 the main replica containing `[3, 3]`, while other tensor replicas contain different values. After loading, it checks the returned keys but discards the result of the tensor-value comparison. Consequently, an incorrect payload such as `[4, 4]` can pass the test.

Add the missing `assert` to enforce the existing expectation that the loaded tensor contains the values saved by rank 3. The change is one line in `tests/unit_tests/dist_checkpointing/test_serialization.py`.

## Issue tracking

No linked issue.

## Validation

- Ran `tools/autoformat.sh` in check mode: Black, isort, Pylint, Ruff, and mypy passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Executed the test's extracted post-load validation block with real PyTorch CPU tensors: all 41 experiment checks passed. Correct payloads pass both versions; 20 corrupted-payload cases across the rank 3–7 branches incorrectly pass before the fix and raise `AssertionError` afterward. Existing common-value and key checks retain their behavior.

The isolated experiment validates assertion sensitivity. The complete distributed checkpoint save/load test remains to be run in CI: the local environment has Python 3.10 and two GPUs, while the project requires Python ≥3.12 and this test uses TP2/PP4.
