items.title: [Perf][MRv2] Add static split selection for token logprobs
items.author: RichterWang
items.summary: This implementation uses vector-tiled reduction, a two-stage merge, and static vocabulary-split selection. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Addresses [[#60095](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60095)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60095) with an alternative token-logprob implementation to [[#60097](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60097)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60097). This implementation uses vector-tiled reduction, a two-stage merge, and static vocabulary-split selection.

## Claims

- On an NVIDIA H200, the candidate was **3.54× faster in CUDA Graph device time** and **1.36× faster in synchronized wall time** than #60097, using geometric means across 57 shapes.
- Compared with the pre-PR baseline used in the experiment, the candidate was **12.20× faster in device time** and **2.19× faster in synchronized wall time**. This is not a comparison against current `main`.
- All 57 benchmark shapes passed the correctness checks in three runs per implementation.

## Validation

- H200 kernel microbenchmark: 57 combinations of vocabulary size, batch size, and K; three runs per implementation; correctness checks passed.
- The measurements compare complete source snapshots. The candidate is based on a newer `main` snapshot than #60097, so the comparison does not isolate the split-selection change.
- These are synthetic-logits kernel measurements. No end-to-end model-serving, TTFT, or throughput evaluation has been run.
- The benchmark scripts, raw results, environment snapshot, and analysis are archived [[here](https://github.com/RichterWang/vllm-lab/tree/e569cbdb316493b3b3f56c05467302ec1831c71a/benchmarks/kernels/issue60095/h200_reference)](https://github.com/RichterWang/vllm-lab/tree/e569cbdb316493b3b3f56c05467302ec1831c71a/benchmarks/kernels/issue60095/h200_reference). To regenerate the three-way analysis, run `python analyze_three_way.py --input-dir results` from that directory.

## Details

#60097 uses online reduction and its own split heuristic. This implementation instead computes per-tile max/sum partials with vector loads, merges those partials in a second kernel, then gathers the requested token logits. A static rule selects the split count from vocabulary size, batch size, and the GPU's SM count; no startup calibration or autotune cache is used.

The candidate comparison is against #60097's implementation at `0ddd6017793c943a2091a5800f0cbac1daaa3e02`. The pre-PR baseline is `d09ff7763747bbe7cd153edd8017479804f47be7`, the direct parent of #60097. Because the candidate is based on a newer `main` snapshot, the baseline-to-candidate result compares full implementations rather than attributing the entire gain to one change.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor the constructor chat template in offline scoring
items.author: mottopanikeiku
items.summary: Fixes offline `LLM.score` ignoring the constructor's `chat_template`, causing incorrect scores for rerankers that require one.
items.body:
## Overview

`LLM(chat_template=...).score(...)` ignores the constructor's template unless it is passed again to every `score()` call, so cross-encoder prompts are built without a template. For rerankers that need one, like Qwen3-Reranker, the scores are wrong. This makes offline scoring fall back to the constructor's template, as online scoring and offline `chat()` (#61061) already do.

## Claims

- `LLM.score()` uses the template passed to the `LLM` constructor when no `chat_template` is given to the call.
- A `chat_template` passed to `LLM.score()` still overrides it, and scoring without any template is unchanged.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU, Python-only install):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py -q
# main: 1 failed, 13 passed. This PR: 14 passed.
```

The new `test_offline_scoring_uses_default_template_unless_overridden` builds offline requests through `get_request_factory_offline` with a constructor template, a per-call template, both, or neither, renders them with `get_score_prompt` and checks the text and token IDs.

End to end on an L4, comparing the wheel for fa75d3456 (`main`) with the same wheel plus this change: `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B", runner="pooling", hf_overrides={"architectures": ["Qwen3ForSequenceClassification"], "classifier_from_token": ["no", "yes"], "is_original_qwen3_reranker": True}, chat_template=TEMPLATE, enforce_eager=True, dtype="bfloat16")`, where `TEMPLATE` is the reranker's query/document prompt, then `llm.score("What is the capital of France?", documents)`. The reference applies the same template with the tokenizer and takes the softmax over the "no"/"yes" logits of the Hugging Face model.

| Document | `main` | This PR | Hugging Face reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The capital of France is Paris. | 0.9829 | 0.9972 | 0.9973 |
| The capital of Germany is Berlin. | 0.9535 | 0.0984 | 0.1097 |
| Pasta is often served with tomato sauce. | 0.5200 | 0.0116 | 0.0115 |
| Prompt lengths (tokens) | 14 / 14 / 16 | 84 / 84 / 85 | 84 / 84 / 85 |

With this change the prompt token IDs match the templated reference exactly for all three documents, and the scores match the reference within `atol=0.01, rtol=0.02` (bf16).

`pre-commit run --files` on the four changed files: all hooks passed.

## Details

`PoolingOfflineMixin` passes the constructor's template to the scoring processors, and `CrossEncoderIOProcessor.get_request_factory_online` uses it (`self.chat_template`). `get_request_factory_offline` instead copied only `ctx.chat_template`, the template passed to `LLM.score()`, which defaults to `None`, so `get_score_prompt` took the path without a template. It now uses `self.chat_template` when `ctx.chat_template` is `None`. I updated the `score()` docstring, which said `None` means the model's default template, and added a sentence to the scoring docs.

Duplicate check: I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `LLM.score` with `chat_template`, "offline template ignored", `CrossEncoderIOProcessor chat_template` and the file paths. #61061 (merged) fixed the same fallback for `chat()`/`enqueue_chat()` but not `score()`. Open PRs that touch these files (#60877 saved CrossEncoder templates, #55359 CrossEncoder heads, #61772 token embeddings in `embed()`) don't change this fallback.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to find, fix and test this bug and to write this description.

---

items.title: [Feat] scheduler: Overlap prefill scheduling and KV loading with model execution
items.author: ttaohe
items.summary: During prefill, layer traversal, input preparation, kernel launches, and communication submission can occupy much of that call. Retiring C, preparing B, and discovering B's cached-KV load can therefore happen late.
items.body:
**Implementation status:** runtime integration, CPU regression checks, and initial PD experiments have been performed locally against main base `92580581da`. The implementation has not been pushed: this Draft PR still has an intentionally empty diff. Supporting authoring files remain local. Further validation and performance investigation are in progress; this is not ready for merge. **Design RFC:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44721 ## Motivation **Native overlap can leave only A's GPU tail to hide the next batch's preparation.** The scheduler regains control after the synchronous CPU model call returns. During prefill, layer traversal, input preparation, kernel launches, and communication submission can occupy much of that call. Retiring C, preparing B, and discovering B's cached-KV load can therefore happen late. **V2 moves that preparation into A's CPU model-call window.** One persistent forward worker runs A's model call while the scheduler retires independent C results, receives ready requests, prepares B, and starts its KV loading earlier. A = current batch, B = next batch, C = an earlier batch. ```mermaid %%{init: {"theme": "base", "gantt": {"displayMode": "compact", "barHeight": 30, "barGap": 8, "fontSize": 13, "sectionFontSize": 14, "leftPadding": 190, "rightPadding": 45}, "themeVariables": {"taskBkgColor": "#dff2e8", "taskBorderColor": "#318463", "taskTextColor": "#172b4d", "activeTaskBkgColor": "#fff0bb", "activeTaskBorderColor": "#ba8a20", "critBkgColor": "#ffe5e5", "critBorderColor": "#bd5656", "doneTaskBkgColor": "#e4edff", "doneTaskBorderColor": "#3b6bb5", "sectionBkgColor": "#f7f9fc", "sectionBkgColor2": "#eff7f2", "sectionBkgColor3": "#f7f9fc", "taskTextDarkColor": "#172b4d", "taskTextOutsideColor": "#172b4d", "gridColor": "#d8e0e9"}}}%% gantt title Move preparation and KV loading into A's model-call window dateFormat YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss axisFormat %S tickInterval 10second todayMarker off section Native / Scheduler Prep A : a0, 2026-01-01T00:00:00, 5s CPU model call A : done, a1, 2026-01-01T00:00:05, 20s Retire C / prepare B : a2, 2026-01-01T00:00:25, 12s CPU call B : done, a3, 2026-01-01T00:00:40, 10s section Native / GPU A forward window : active, a4, 2026-01-01T00:00:07, 21s Exposed boundary : crit, a5, 2026-01-01T00:00:28, 14s B forward : active, a6, 2026-01-01T00:00:42, 8s section Native / B KV Load B : a7, 2026-01-01T00:00:32, 12s section V2 / Scheduler Prep A : b0, 2026-01-01T00:00:00, 5s Retire C : b1, 2026-01-01T00:00:06, 6s Receive : b2, 2026-01-01T00:00:12, 7s Prepare B : b3, 2026-01-01T00:00:19, 6s Handoff : b4, 2026-01-01T00:00:25, 5s section V2 / Forward worker CPU model call A : done, b5, 2026-01-01T00:00:05, 20s CPU call B : done, b6, 2026-01-01T00:00:30, 10s section V2 / GPU A forward window : active, b7, 2026-01-01T00:00:07, 21s Gap : crit, b8, 2026-01-01T00:00:28, 4s B forward : active, b9, 2026-01-01T00:00:32, 8s section V2 / B KV Early load B : b10, 2026-01-01T00:00:21, 12s ``` *Horizontal positions are schematic, in arbitrary units. Blue = CPU model call, green = scheduler work / KV loading, yellow = GPU forward window, red = exposed batch boundary. The bars do not represent measured durations or continuous GPU activity. B consumes KV as its required layers become ready, so its forward can overlap the loading tail.* Agent requests can also arrive while A's model call is running. V2 advances bounded, rank-consistent receive and preparation work during that window. A future turn that still depends on Decode completion must wait for that dependency. ## Modifications ### 1. Keep one scheduler-state owner The scheduler remains the only writer of requests, radix state, allocation, admission, and retirement. The forward worker executes the current model call and submits GPU work; existing backend paths perform KV loading. - **A:** the current prefill batch. - **B:** the next batch, prepared early when independent of A. - **C:** a previous batch whose independent result handling and PD completion can advance during A. **One state owner, separate execution and loading paths** ```mermaid %%{init: {"theme": "base", "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": true, "curve": "linear", "nodeSpacing": 35, "rankSpacing": 55}, "themeVariables": {"fontFamily": "Arial, sans-serif", "fontSize": "15px", "lineColor": "#7a8699", "edgeLabelBackground": "#ffffff", "clusterBkg": "#f7f9fc", "clusterBorder": "#d8e0e9"}, "fontFamily": "Arial, sans-serif"}}%% flowchart LR accTitle: One scheduler owner, separate forward and KV loading paths S["Scheduler owner
Retire C and prepare B
Only writer of shared state"] F["Forward worker
A model call
Kernel submission"] L["KV backend
HiCache / Mooncake
Load B's cached KV"] subgraph GPU["GPU"] A["A forward
Compute + communication"] B["B cached KV
Per-layer readiness"] end S -->|Run A| F S -->|Load B| L F -->|Kernels| A L -->|Transfer| B classDef owner fill:#dff2e8,stroke:#318463,stroke-width:2px,color:#172b4d classDef worker fill:#e4edff,stroke:#3b6bb5,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d classDef load fill:#eee5ff,stroke:#8159ba,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d classDef compute fill:#fff0bb,stroke:#ba8a20,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d class S owner class F worker class L,B load class A compute style GPU fill:#f7f9fc,stroke:#d8e0e9,stroke-width:1px,color:#596579 ``` ### 2. Advance independent work while A is being submitted At bounded, rank-consistent checkpoints, the scheduler can retire C, receive fresh independent requests, advance bootstrap, and prepare B. Target submission completion ends this preparation window; EAGLE Draft waits for preparation to finish before using shared TP/MoE state. These checkpoints bound eligibility and repeated progress, not the duration of each Python operation. Current V2 advances work during A's CPU model call; it does not restrict that work to explicit GPU-feedback waits. Evaluation therefore includes any extra A submission time rather than treating early work as free overlap. Each batch retains its own loading dependency snapshot. Preparing or loading B does not replace A's active dependencies. CUDA device/stream and relevant execution contexts are explicitly established in the forward worker. ### 3. Prepare a full B when safe; otherwise warm eligible KV | Situation | Early work | | --- | --- | | B is independent of A | Match prefixes, allocate, form B, and start its cached-KV load. | | B advances A's active chunk request | Warm eligible waiting requests' KV; retain shared-request advancement and final grouping at the normal boundary. | | A future agent turn has not been produced | Preserve the session dependency; it cannot be scheduled before it exists. | Speculative KV warming uses a shared page-aligned budget across candidates and outstanding transfers, while reserving compute headroom. The prototype scans up to eight candidates and uses an experimental 2M-token envelope for a 16K compute chunk. This is a tuning choice to validate, not an upstream default commitment. Normal admitted demand loads remain complete. ### 4. Use each backend's loading and lifetime rules | Backend | Loading path and ownership | | --- | --- | | HiCache | Background direct DMA; supported demand tails can use a bounded 16-CTA kernel, with direct fallback. Preserve current layout leases, address translation, allocator move protection, and completion events. | | Mooncake direct linker | Fully prepare an independent B using request-private load slots and a frozen per-batch dependency. Retain slots through its forward and publish through normal successful result handling. Preserve load failures and MLA dedup broadcasts. Chunk-follower KV-only warming is not enabled for this backend. | Cancelled or stale reservations retain transfer ownership until the associated writes have stopped. Request cancellation does not permit early page reuse. ### 5. Provide one opt-in switch Proposed switch: `--enable-overlap-schedule-v2`, default off. Existing settings select HiCache or the external linker backend. The switch is not implemented in upstream main yet. Initial compatibility targets are text-only CUDA PD prefill, PP1/DCP1, no independent DP request replicas, disabled CUDA graphs, and the CP8 DSA layer-split/EAGLE reference deployment. HiCache support here is host-L2 cache mode without a storage tier or buffer pipeline; HiCache L2 plus Mooncake L3 is not enabled. The direct linker bypasses the local host tier. Other combinations require explicit follow-up validation. The disabled path must preserve native scheduling, pause, shutdown, and chunk behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Local CPU protocol/profiler regressions and targeted real-PD cold/restored/mixed nonce checks have passed. These are not a comprehensive model-accuracy evaluation. Merge validation must retain and extend coverage of: - Registered owner/worker and cache-lifetime regression tests, including cancellation, delayed loads, failures, shared readers, reset, and shutdown. - GPU copy checks for nonidentity pages, untouched guards, and target/indexer/packed MTP layer mapping. - Model-output/logprob and task-appropriate accuracy checks against matched flag-off controls. - Consistent rank decisions and target/Draft handoff in the supported configurations. HTTP success, fixed output length, and byte-copy checks alone do not establish model accuracy. ## Speed Tests and Profiling These are **local main-port results against base 92580581da**, not results from the published empty diff. Each run uses GLM-5.3 FP8 with a separate 8×H200 Prefill node and 8×H200 Decode node. Native overlap remains enabled in both flags. | Backend | V2 | Input tokens/s | TTFT P50 | TTFT P99 | Total token cache hit | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | HiCache host L2 | OFF 1 | 194,454 | 4.397 s | 20.213 s | 88.834% | | HiCache host L2 | ON 1 | 204,389 | 3.978 s | 19.768 s | 88.834% | | HiCache host L2 | ON 2 | 203,438 | 3.881 s | 22.316 s | 88.834% | | HiCache host L2 | OFF 2 | 193,790 | 4.437 s | 19.627 s | 88.849% | | Mooncake direct linker | OFF 1 | 161,631 | 5.823 s | 20.246 s | 88.834% | | Mooncake direct linker | ON 1 | 172,085 | 5.183 s | 22.724 s | 88.834% | | Mooncake direct linker | ON 2 | 171,888 | 5.165 s | 23.548 s | 88.834% | | Mooncake direct linker | OFF 2 | 162,031 | 5.761 s | 21.715 s | 88.834% | HiCache's two-run mean throughput increased **5.04%**, and the mean of run-level median TTFTs fell **11.04%**; mean run-level P99 increased **5.63%**. Mooncake changed **+6.28%**, **−10.67%**, and **+10.27%**, respectively. These are means of run metrics, not pooled percentiles or a statistical guarantee. The order was OFF1 → ON1 → intervening experiments → ON2 → OFF2; a separate diagnostic run also preceded Mooncake OFF2. **Tail latency is not consistently improved.** Additional pairs change only the global HTTP budget to 10; active roots remain 20 and actual warmup/formal payload sets match concurrency 20: | Backend / concurrency 10 | V2 | Input tokens/s | TTFT P50 | TTFT P99 | New input tokens | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Mooncake | OFF | 157,597 | 2.726 s | 14.025 s | 5,895,395 | | Mooncake | ON | 166,313 | 2.562 s | 13.581 s | 5,895,331 | | HiCache | OFF | 184,821 | 2.179 s | 12.585 s | 5,895,331 | | HiCache | ON | 194,906 | 1.996 s | 11.102 s | 5,895,395 | These single pairs show throughput / median TTFT / P99 changes of +5.53% / −6.04% / −3.17% for Mooncake and +5.46% / −8.43% / −11.78% for HiCache. Their improved P99 direction does not generalize to concurrency 20. **Workload and controls.** Public Weka 256K agent traces, 80 root trajectories, seed 20261016: 21 historical primer calls are fully drained, then 903 previously unmeasured formal requests are completed. Per-session and subagent dependencies are retained; the HTTP budget is released only after the full response. Every run completed 903/903 with zero errors/cancellations and matching actual payload sets. Formal input totals 52,867,171 tokens; outputs are fixed at 16 tokens/request, totaling 14,448. Formal inputs are not repeatedly replayed for warmup. Closed-loop arrival times and batch grouping can differ between flags. **Capacity and configuration.** P uses TP8/CP8 interleave, DSA layer split, 16,384-token prefill chunks, page size 64, FP8 KV, disabled CUDA graphs, and L1 capacity 524,288 tokens. Local host-cache payload and external Mooncake capacity are approximately 256 GiB each. D uses TP8/DP8 attention, HiSparse and EAGLE. The primary comparison is OFF/ON within each backend. Seven of eight concurrency-20 runs compute 5,902,947 new tokens; HiCache OFF2 computes 7,616 fewer (0.0144 percentage points of total input). Concurrency-10 pairs differ by 64 new tokens. Equal capacities do not imply equal L1/L2 replacement or metadata costs. HiCache ON also enables the proposed bounded demand-transfer policy, so its gain does not isolate the CPU scheduling change. Mooncake cache segments are registered by the eight P processes on the P host. This tests backend integration, **not cross-host cache bandwidth or scalability**; cross-host P→D KV transfer is a separate path. The second Mooncake pair includes CPU-profile coverage fixes with profiling disabled. items.title: [Fix] detokenizer: Use chunk-relative read offsets after state eviction
items.author: aiqubits
items.summary: After detokenizer state eviction, the next incremental chunk rebuilds the state. Its read offset is still relative to the cumulative surrogate/decode buffer, which can skip fresh tokens, including short final chunks.
items.body:
## Motivation

After detokenizer state eviction, the next incremental chunk rebuilds the state. Its read offset is still relative to the cumulative surrogate/decode buffer, which can skip fresh tokens, including short final chunks.

Related to #41236.

## Modifications

- Send a chunk-relative read offset, clamped to zero, before advancing `send_decode_id_offset`.
- Add offline CPU regression coverage using a real byte-level BPE decoder for prompt lengths, eviction points, batched/per-row decoding, split UTF-8, and stop trimming/retention.

## Accuracy Tests

- Committed regression: **48 subcases passed**.
- Expanded suite, 16 related files: **300 tests and 104 subtests passed.
- Qwen2.5/Qwen3.5 tokenizer replay: **1,296 configurations per code revision**; baseline **384 passed / 912 failed**, patched **1,120 passed / 176 failed**. **736 recoveries, zero new regressions**.
- Cross-process CPU IPC replay: **16/16 cases passed for each of Pickle and MessagePack**, with interleaved requests and forced eviction.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed, including Rust checks. Changed executable production line coverage: **100% (1/1)**.

```bash
python test/registered/unit/managers/test_detokenizer_streaming.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CPU microbenchmark of accumulator construction/`accept`/`to_payload` plus `handle_batch_token_id_out`, comparing `7098ec3` with `1ad9871`. Intel i7-12700, WSL2, Python 3.12.3, Qwen2.5 tokenizer, 19 fixed tokens/request, no eviction; one logical CPU, tokenizer parallelism disabled. Medians of 11 alternating paired samples targeting 100 ms of timed work per sample; setup, IPC, HTTP, and model generation excluded.

Microseconds per request per chunk (lower is faster):

| Decode mode | Batch size | Baseline | Patched | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Batch | 1 | 21.398 | 21.953 | +2.59% |
| Batch | 32 | 5.498 | 5.593 | +1.72% |
| Batch | 128 | 4.976 | 5.078 | +2.05% |
| Per-row | 1 | 17.668 | 18.271 | +3.41% |
| Per-row | 32 | 5.987 | 6.123 | +2.26% |
| Per-row | 128 | 5.577 | 5.624 | +0.85% |

items.title: [Perf][Bugfix] Prefer MNNVL for single-node FlashInfer allreduce again
items.author: khluu
items.summary: Restores mnnvl as preferred FlashInfer allreduce backend for single-node NVSwitch systems, fixing a 3-5% decode throughput regression introduced in v0.32.0.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes a 3-5% decode regression in v0.32.0, caused by #56891.

#56891 changed automatic FlashInfer allreduce selection to use `trtllm` for every node-local process group. Before it, single-node runs used `mnnvl`, falling back to `trtllm` on nodes without NVSwitch multicast. The PR included no perf data, and on single-node NVSwitch systems `trtllm` is slower.

## Evidence

The perf-eval nightlies show a step in the 14 commits between the 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04 nightlies, and #56891 is the only distributed change among them. Only TP>1 workloads moved:

| workload | before (10-03) | after (10-04 on) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200 | ~5650 tok/s, TPOT 20.8 ms | ~5460 tok/s, TPOT 21.6 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP4, H200 (same host) | 10883 tok/s, TPOT 11.20 ms | 10571 tok/s, TPOT 11.54 ms |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200 | ~2770 tok/s | ~2650-2720 tok/s |
| MiniMax-M3 TP8, H200 | TPOT 35.9 ms | TPOT 36.8 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP1, B200 | unchanged | unchanged |

A/B on the v0.32.0rc2 image with `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` forced:

| workload | default (`trtllm`) | `mnnvl` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200, 8k/1k conc 128 | 5462 tok/s, TPOT 21.78 ms | **5728 tok/s, TPOT 20.22 ms** |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200, 3 repeats | 2533 / 2753 / 2771 tok/s | **2581 / 2811 / 2845 tok/s** |

## Change

For node-local groups, auto-selection goes back to `mnnvl` with `allow_trtllm_fallback=True`. The existing fallback still builds a `trtllm` workspace when `mnnvl` can't create one (no NVSwitch multicast). Multi-node selection from #56891 is unchanged: `mnnvl` on Blackwell, disabled on Hopper. The unit test's expectations are updated to match.

cc @elvircrn: is there a case where single-node `mnnvl` misbehaved that #56891 was fixing? The PR description only covers the multi-node cases.

## Test Plan

- `test_flashinfer_auto_backend_uses_group_topology` updated for the single-node cases.
- ruff check/format pass.
- Perf A/B above (perf-eval build 680).

items.title: [Fix] gateway: Drop unused npyz dev-dependency to unbreak builds after zip yank
items.author: JustinTong0323
items.summary: On 2026-10-16 the maintainer yanked every release except 9.0.3 after security advisories GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627, GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26, and GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp; old lines such as 0.6.x will not get backports (zip-rs/zip2#1075). declares with the feature as a dev-de…
items.body:
## Motivation

On 2026-10-16 the `zip` maintainer yanked every release except 9.0.3 after security advisories GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627, GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26, and GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp; old lines such as 0.6.x will not get backports (zip-rs/zip2#1075). `sgl-model-gateway` declares `npyz` with the `npz` feature as a dev-dependency, which requires `zip ^0.6` (still the case in the latest npyz, 0.9.1). The gateway does not commit a `Cargo.lock`, so every fresh resolve — docker image builds, fresh checkouts — now fails:

```
error: failed to select a version for the requirement `zip = "^0.6"`
required by package `npyz v0.8.0`
    ... which satisfies dependency `npyz = "^0.8"` of package `sgl-model-gateway v0.3.2`
```

Example: the release-docker build in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38871712398 fails at the `maturin build` step with this error.

## Modifications

- Remove the `npyz` dev-dependency. No gateway code references `npyz`, and with it gone `zip` is no longer in the dependency graph.
- Remove `scripts/generate_vision_golden.py`, the CI step in `pr-test-rust.yml` that installs torch/transformers to run it, and the `.gitignore` entry for its output. No gateway test reads the `.npz` fixtures it produced.

## Verification

On clean `git archive` trees of `sgl-model-gateway`:

| | `cargo metadata --format-version 1 -q` |
|---|---|
| `upstream/main` | exit 101 (`failed to select a version for the requirement zip = "^0.6"`) |
| this PR | exit 0 |

On this PR, `cargo fetch` succeeds, `cargo metadata` from `bindings/python` (the maturin entry point) and `bindings/golang` exits 0, and `cargo tree -e normal,build,dev -i zip` finds no `zip` package.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Separate lookup submission and per-request results
items.author: Alex-ai-future
items.summary: Fixes async KV offload lookup correctness bug where a failed promotion in one request incorrectly mutates another request's verdict when they share the same cache key.
items.body:
## Overview

Fix async KV offload lookup consistency when multiple requests share the same
key. This PR supersedes [#61754](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61754)
by keeping its generation-aware protection and adding request-scoped verdicts.

## Claims

- A failed promotion changes only the originating request's lookup verdict.
- A stale load completion cannot modify a newer lookup generation.
- Submission lifecycle and per-request result state are represented separately.
- Main-branch cached-MISS and lookup behavior is preserved.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering -q`: 542 passed, 1 skipped.
- Pre-commit hooks pass.

## Details

### Trigger scenario

Requests A and B can share one `LookupState` and lookup generation:

1. A and B probe the same key and both receive `HIT`.
2. A starts a secondary-tier promotion.
3. A's promotion fails, possibly after A has finished.
4. `mark_miss()` runs while B still holds the shared lookup state.

With a shared verdict, A's failed promotion can incorrectly change B's result.

### Before and after

```text
Before:
A HIT, B HIT
mark_miss(A)
A/B -> MARKED_MISS

After:
A HIT, B HIT
mark_miss(A)
A -> MARKED_MISS
B -> HIT
```

`LookupToken(key, req_id, generation)` makes `mark_miss()` generation-aware,
covering the stale-completion case addressed by #61754. The request ID also
ensures that a correction from A cannot modify B when both requests share the
same generation.

### Data structure

```python
_lookup_state: dict[OffloadKey, LookupState]
_req_keys: dict[str, set[OffloadKey]]  # reverse index for cleanup


@dataclass
class LookupState:
    generation: int
    submission_status: LookupSubmissionStatus
    request_statuses: dict[str, LookupResultStatus]
```

`LookupSubmissionStatus` contains only `PENDING`, `IN_FLIGHT`, and `RESOLVED`.
`LookupResultStatus` contains each request's `PENDING`, `HIT`, `MISS`, or
`MARKED_MISS` result. `request_statuses` is the single ownership and result
mapping; `request_ids` is no longer maintained separately.

items.title: [Model][Spec Decode] Migrate HY V3 to the Flat Model layout
items.author: AlejandroParedesLT
items.summary: Next slice of #61024's "Migrate speculative model code to Flat Model" bullet (RFC #44219). Moves the HY V3 model and its MTP drafter from the legacy layout into the new layout.
items.body:
## Overview

Next slice of #61024's "Migrate speculative model code to Flat Model" bullet (RFC #44219). Moves the HY V3 model and its MTP drafter from the legacy `vllm/model_executor/models/` layout into the new `vllm/models/<name>/<hw>/` layout.

## Claims

- Moves `vllm/model_executor/models/hy_v3.py` and `hy_v3_mtp.py` to `vllm/models/hy_v3/common/{model,mtp}.py`, repointing the `HYV3ForCausalLM` and `HYV3MTPModel` registry entries to `vllm.models.hy_v3`.
- No logic change. The only diff inside the moved files is fixing imports that crossed the old package boundary (`.utils`, `.interfaces` → `vllm.model_executor.models.{utils,interfaces}`, and the MTP file's `from .hy_v3 import HYV3DecoderLayer` → `from .model import HYV3DecoderLayer`), verified by diffing old vs. new file content.
- HY V3 needs only a `common/` directory, no `nvidia`/`amd`/`cpu`/`xpu` split: zero custom kernels, and zero platform-conditional code (`grep -c "is_rocm\|is_cuda\|sm90\|sm100"` → 0). HY V4 (`vllm.models.hy_v4`), by contrast, needed a real `nvidia`/`amd` split for `flashmla_sparse`/`triton_ihc` -- V3 predates those optimizations.
- Unlike every other remaining legacy drafter, `hy_v3.py`/`hy_v3_mtp.py` have zero dependency on any other model file -- confirmed by grep across the whole tree, they're the only two files that reference each other. That made this pair the next candidate after Medusa.

## Validation

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -q -k HYV3
# 2 passed

pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py vllm/models/hy_v3/__init__.py vllm/models/hy_v3/common/__init__.py vllm/models/hy_v3/common/model.py vllm/models/hy_v3/common/mtp.py
# all hooks passed (ruff check/format, mypy, SPDX headers, etc.)
```

No e2e acceptance-rate test exists for HY V3 under `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/` (unlike Medusa, which had one) and I don't have a validated local checkpoint-loading path for it on this change, so the above is the available coverage. `tests/models/registry.py` lists `tencent/Hy3-preview` as the example checkpoint if a reviewer wants to validate a real weight load.

## Details

**Why HY V3 and not another drafter:** every remaining legacy drafter (EAGLE/EAGLE3 variants, the other MTP variants, DFlash) imports its base model's decoder-layer class directly from a still-legacy file (`llama`, `qwen2`, `qwen3`, `deepseek_v2`, etc.), so migrating any of them means migrating a shared, heavily-reused base model too -- a much bigger, higher-blast-radius change. HY V3 is the one pair with zero such entanglement.

**Previous attempt:** #61357 targeted Medusa as the first migration in this series, but Medusa was removed from vLLM entirely in #61701 while that PR was in flight ("Medusa is not supported by Model Runner V2, and EAGLE/MTP/DFlash/DSpark cover its use case"). Closed #61357 as superseded by that removal rather than resurrect deleted code.

**Duplicate-work check:** searched open issues/PRs for existing HY V3 Flat Model migration work; found none.

**Scope:** this PR only moves HY V3 + its MTP drafter. The remaining legacy drafters are out of scope here and need their base model migrated alongside them, which is a larger, separate decision per model family.

items.body:

Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

sgl_kernel_npu implements block verification for the chain-mode EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN rejection-sampling kernel, but the `--speculative-use-block-verification` gate in sglang rejects `device=="npu"`, so NPU users cannot enable it. This PR admits NPU for the chain path while keeping every other device's behavior unchanged.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py`: allow `device=="npu"` in the block-verification gate for the EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN chain path only. and all other non-CUDA/ROCm devices are still rejected. The implicit enforcement of `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` (which strictly requires `--speculative-eagle-topk=1`) is unchanged.
- `arg_groups/fields/spec.py`: update the flag's help text to document NPU support.
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_block_verification_args.py`: add `test_supported_on_npu` (EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN accepted on NPU) and update the negative cases — DFLASH/DSPARK on NPU now hit the algorithm gate instead of the device gate, and cpu/xpu test the new device-gate message.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests: `test_block_verification_args.py` 5 passed (including `test_supported_on_npu`).

End-to-end on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NEXTN (NPU, TP2, `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-use-block-verification`, 6 fixed prompts):

items.title: [Mamba] Store hicache checkpoints without a GPU slot
items.author: chien-an-chen
items.summary: Mamba radix checkpoints currently donate a GPU slot for every matched prefix. On a Kimi-K3 c=48 recipe that slot floor is (480), so the GPU mamba pool stays large even when ReplaySSM already covers live verify and the checkpoint itself only needs to be reloade…
items.body:
## Motivation

Mamba radix checkpoints currently donate a GPU slot for every matched prefix. On a Kimi-K3 c=48 recipe that slot floor is `max_running_requests * 5` (480), so the GPU mamba pool stays large even when ReplaySSM already covers live verify and the checkpoint itself only needs to be reloaded from host.

## Modifications

Add `--enable-mamba-host-only-checkpoint` (default off). The flag requires `--enable-hierarchical-cache` and rejects `--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint`.

When it is on:

- A finished request copies its flushed state into the hicache host pool and does not keep or donate a GPU slot.
- The mamba ratio drops to the live request plus ping-pong tracking slots. With the extra buffer and overlap that is 3 (1 active + 2 ping-pong), so a 96-wide decode pool is 288 slots. `no_buffer` with page size 1 is the path that returns 1.
- The Rust insert accepts `mamba_host_value` without a donated `mamba_value`.
- Under HiCache, a host checkpoint still counts as a device-prefix match, so the Full KV indices of that node stay reachable. Load-back still runs when the host hit length is non-zero.

The flag-off path is unchanged: the same ratio, the same donated GPU slot, and a host-only node does not advance `last_device_node`.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py`: host-only ratio is 1 / 2 / 3 for no-buffer, lazy, and overlap. Flag-off cases stay at the previous ratios.
- `sglang-radix-tree` mamba component tests, including host-only insert with no GPU slot and the HiCache device-prefix match.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not in this PR. A c=48 AgentX run with the flag, `max-mamba-cache-size 288`, and `mem-fraction-static 0.87` is in progress separately.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Honor RGB PNG transparency when loading images
items.author: mottopanikeiku
items.summary: Fixes RGB PNG transparency handling so tRNS-chunk pixels are composited onto the background color instead of remaining opaque with their hidden color.
items.body:
## Overview

An RGB PNG can mark one color as transparent with a tRNS chunk. vLLM loads such images as opaque, so the transparent pixels keep their hidden color instead of the white (or `rgba_background_color`) background that RGBA and palette images get. This covers the RGB case that #44974 meant to handle (`_has_transparency` lists tRNS in RGB PNGs) but that the same-mode early returns skip.

## Claims

- Transparent pixels of RGB PNGs with a tRNS chunk are now filled with the default white or the configured `rgba_background_color`, both for image URLs/data URLs and for PIL images passed offline, so the two pipelines give the same pixels.
- Opaque RGB images and `image_mode=None` are handled as before.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU, Python-only install):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py -q
# main: 6 failed, 51 passed. This PR: 57 passed.
```

`test_transparency_offline_matches_online` passes the same PIL image to the offline parser and, saved as a PNG data URL, through `MediaConnector`. It checks that both give the same pixels as Pillow's own RGBA conversion composited onto white. The cases are an RGB PNG with tRNS, a GIF whose transparent and opaque palette entries are both black, an RGBA PNG, and the PNG and the GIF after `convert("RGB")`. `test_image_media_io_rgb_png_transparency` loads an RGB PNG with tRNS through `ImageMediaIO` with the default and a custom background color. `test_hash_collision_media_io_config` now also runs with such a PNG, so loads with different backgrounds don't share a processor-cache entry.

End to end on an L4 with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct --enforce-eager --trust-request-mm-kwargs`, comparing the wheel for fa75d3456 (`main`) with the same wheel plus this change. The image is a 448x448 RGB PNG, red with a blue square, with red marked transparent. The question is "What color is the background behind the blue square? Answer with one color word.", once with the default background and once with `media_io_kwargs: {"image": {"rgba_background_color": [0, 255, 0]}}`. For reference, the same image composited onto the background with PIL and sent as an opaque PNG gets the answers "White" and "Green".

| Background | `main` | This PR | Pixels that differ from the PIL reference, `main` → this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default (white) | Red | White | 184,320 → 0 |
| `[0, 255, 0]` | Red | Green | 184,320 → 0 |

The end-to-end runs used the first commit. The source in this PR is back to that commit's version, so the results still apply; since then, only the tests have changed.

`pre-commit run --files` on the six changed files: all hooks passed.

## Details

`convert_image_mode` returned `image` when `image.mode == to_mode`, before `_has_transparency` was checked, and `ImageMediaIO._convert_image_mode` had its own same-mode return before calling it. I moved the same-mode return in `convert_image_mode` after the transparency check, and `ImageMediaIO` now calls `convert_image_mode` for every conversion instead of special-casing RGBA (which `convert_image_mode` already composites the same way).

The automated review pointed out that `Image.open(gif).convert("RGB")` keeps the GIF's transparent color in `info`, so opaque pixels that share that color are treated as transparent too. The second commit applied the color key only to images vLLM decodes itself, but that made the offline and online pipelines disagree: Pillow saves `info["transparency"]` as a tRNS chunk, so the same image sent to the server as a PNG was still composited. Following review, the third commit goes back to handling it in `convert_image_mode` for both pipelines, which also matches what Pillow's `convert("RGBA")` does with that image, and replaces the unit test with the offline vs online comparison above.

The docs said the background color only applies to RGBA images; I updated them to say it applies to images with transparency, including tRNS PNGs.

Duplicate check: I searched open and closed PRs and issues for transparency, tRNS, `convert_image_mode`, `ImageMediaIO`, `rgba_background_color` and the file paths. #44974 (merged) added the tRNS handling but kept both same-mode returns. Open PRs touching these files are #60308 (decompression-bomb errors as HTTP 400) and #57752 (a "don't merge" lazy-decoding experiment that keeps the same-mode return); neither changes this.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to find, fix and test this bug and to write this description.

It uses the verification utility already tracked in the repository, recreates the move in a temporary worktree, applies the configured formatters, and requires an empty diff against the relocation commit.

```bash
python3 /path/to/verify_muse_layers.py
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

FILES = (
    'muse_spark_audio.py',
    'muse_spark_bf16_moe.py',
    'muse_spark_fp4_moe.py',
    'muse_spark_int4_moe.py',
    'muse_spark_layers.py',
    'muse_spark_navit.py',
    'moe/muse_spark_megamoe.py',
    'quantization/muse_spark_nvfp4_moe.py',
)

def transform(root):
    root = Path(root)
    layers = root / 'python/sglang/srt/layers'
    target = layers / 'muse_spark'
    target.mkdir()
    replacements = {
        'sglang.srt.layers.' + path[:-3].replace('/', '.'):
        'sglang.srt.layers.muse_spark.' + Path(path).stem
        for path in FILES
    }
    tracked = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'ls-files', '-z'], cwd=root).split(b'\0')
    for entry in tracked:
        if not entry:
            continue
        path = root / entry.decode()
        if not path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():
            continue
        data = path.read_bytes()
        updated = data
        for old, new in replacements.items():
            updated = updated.replace(old.encode(), new.encode())
        if data != updated:
            path.write_bytes(updated)
    for path in FILES:
        (layers / path).rename(target / Path(path).name)
    (target / '__init__.py').touch()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd() / '.agents/skills/mechanical-refactor-verify/scripts'))
    from mechanical_refactor_reproduction_utils import verify_mechanical_refactor
    verify_mechanical_refactor(
        '90785dc87625d82e18c148826f99e01fefdbb503',
        'd6bcf11e3b9fdbf4afd6f0555411af9b36acf052',
        transform,
    )
```

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP4 indexer K cache for GLM-5 / DeepSeek-V3.2 DSA
items.author: whx-sjtu
items.summary: On gfx950 with AITER, now also serves DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x, MTP drafts included: their indexer writes the paged MXFP4 K cache that #58671 added for DeepSeek-V4.1, and the existing ROCm MXFP4 indexer scores it in place. FP8 stays the default.
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx950 with AITER, `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'` now also serves DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x, MTP drafts included: their indexer writes the paged MXFP4 K cache that #58671 added for DeepSeek-V4.1, and the existing ROCm MXFP4 indexer scores it in place. FP8 stays the default. The code applies to main on its own; the gains below are measured on top of #61943, which should land first. Related: #48558, #60834.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, on top of #61943: KV cache +3.0% tokens; 128K/1K TPOT -5.4% / -5.9% at c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 -6.8%, TTFT -7% to -8%; c1 and 8K/1K within noise; gsm8k and passkey unchanged.
- Against main: 128K/1K TPOT -7.6% / -9.6% / -9.5% at c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 -6.7%.
- DeepSeek-V3.2, TP4, on top of #61943: KV cache +10.2% tokens; 128K/1K c8 TPOT -12.5%; c1 and 4K/1K c16 within noise; gsm8k unchanged.
- The FP8 default, gfx942, AITER off and non-ROCm platforms are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py`, `test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py`, `test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`, MI355X: 274 passed, 8 skipped. pre-commit clean.
- Serving, mean TPOT (ms), 4 runs per arm for GLM-5.2 128K c8 / c16, MTP3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 4K, 2 elsewhere, no failed requests:

| workload | #61943 | + this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c1 / c8 / c16 | 13.90 / 43.17 / 76.66 | 13.69 / 40.82 / 72.15 | -1.5% / -5.4% / -5.9% |
| GLM-5.2 MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 33.95 | 31.63 | -6.8% |
| GLM-5.2 8K/1K c8 | 17.50 | 17.49 | within noise |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c1 / c8 | 13.74 / 66.02 | 13.67 / 57.78 | -0.5% / -12.5% |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16 | 22.85 | 23.34 | +2.1%, one outlier run (below) |

- gsm8k strict: GLM-5.2 20-shot 0.9272 to 0.9325 (stderr 0.007), DeepSeek-V3.2 5-shot 0.9515 to 0.9575 (stderr 0.006). GLM-5.2 passkey 26/26 in both arms.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel data and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running #61943 at 0473a1e and this branch cherry-picked onto it (no conflicts), from source, MI355X. GLM-5.2 runs use `--max-model-len 133120`; DeepSeek-V3.2 runs keep the default (163840).

The new kernel tests compare the written K pages byte for byte with a reference built from the layout description, score them with AITER's kernel, and check the MXFP4 query against torch. A transposed scale plane, scales in natural order or a wrong `n_per_tile` each make them fail. MTP3 acceptance length: 3.49 without, 3.45 with this PR.

Mean TPOT per run (ms). Sessions, one server each: #61943 | PR, PR | #61943, then for the 4-run points PR, PR | #61943, #61943. MTP3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 follow the same order.

| workload | #61943 | + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 8K/1K c8 | 17.45, 17.55 | 17.58, 17.40 |
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c1 | 14.14, 13.66 | 13.81, 13.58 |
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c8 | 43.41, 43.07, 43.05, 43.15 | 41.02, 40.68, 40.84, 40.73 |
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c16 | 77.92, 76.08, 76.51, 76.12 | 74.48, 71.18, 71.55, 71.38 |
| GLM-5.2 MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.80, 33.38, 33.91, 33.69 | 32.33, 31.51, 31.26, 31.42 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16 | 22.68, 23.09, 22.86, 22.77 | 23.09, 24.46, 22.89, 22.92 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c1 | 13.79, 13.70 | 13.69, 13.65 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c8 | 66.49, 65.55 | 57.96, 57.60 |

- Median ITL (ms): GLM-5.2 128K c1 13.80 to 13.69, c8 17.12 to 16.74, c16 20.24 to 19.54, MTP3 c8 25.44 to 24.34; DeepSeek-V3.2 128K c8 20.78 to 19.38, 4K c16 21.26 to 21.37.
- Mean TTFT (s): GLM-5.2 128K c1 8.20 to 7.84, c8 36.9 to 33.9, c16 68.2 to 63.3, MTP3 c8 38.1 to 35.0; DeepSeek-V3.2 128K c8 62.4 to 53.6. Output throughput at 128K: GLM-5.2 c8 +7.0%, c16 +7.0%, MTP3 c8 +7.8%; DeepSeek-V3.2 c8 +15.2%.
- The DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16 run at 24.46 ms had tail stalls (p99 ITL 33.7 ms, 22-25 ms in the other seven runs); without it the PR mean is 22.97 (+0.5%).
- KV cache tokens: GLM-5.2 3,206,592 to 3,303,424 (MTP3 2,969,088 to 3,058,112); DeepSeek-V3.2 2,074,240 to 2,286,656. DeepSeek-V3.2 has an indexer on every layer, GLM-5.2 on 21 of them.
- Against main, earlier sessions with the same flags (main | PR, PR | main; MTP3 PR, PR | main, main): 128K/1K TPOT 14.69 / 44.95 / 79.01 to 13.58 / 40.63 / 71.52, MTP3 c8 34.65 to 32.31, TTFT -9%, 8K/1K c1 / c8 / c16 within 1%, gsm8k 20-shot strict 0.9181 to 0.9212. Its PR arm matches the PR arm above within 1.5%.

Decode indexer per step (us), GLM-5.2 indexer (32 heads, k=2048, 64-token pages), scoring and top-k for 21 layers captured in one graph, LLC flushed before each replay, median of 20. FP8 scorer with AITER top-k (#61943) to this PR's MXFP4 path, its per-step schedule included:

| context | 1 row | 8 rows | 16 rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4K | 209 to 210 | 230 to 263 | 257 to 252 |
| 32K | 406 to 413 | 580 to 487 | 745 to 570 |
| 128K | 762 to 704 | 1419 to 972 | 2027 to 1274 |

At 128K and 8 rows the scorer alone drops from 816 to 334 us; top-k is the same AITER kernel on both sides. With 4 rows per sequence (MTP3) the MXFP4 path takes native next_n rows: 128K, 8 sequences 2573 to 1209 us.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 133120 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'
# MTP3: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# DeepSeek-V3.2: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2, same env and flags without --max-model-len.

# 128K/1K: num-prompts max(C, 3), --seed 43. 8K/1K c8: --random-input-len 8192,
# 24 prompts, --seed 42. DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16: --random-input-len 4096, 48 prompts, --seed 42.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 43

# --num_fewshot 5 for DeepSeek-V3.2
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py
```

Passkey: a 5-digit key at a random depth of 32K / 64K / 120K tokens of filler, chat completion with thinking off, 26 prompts.

</details>

## Details

- Write path: AITER's `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache` (DeepSeek-V4.1) applies RMSNorm and RoPE on the last dims; the V3.2 and GLM indexer key takes LayerNorm with bias and interleaved RoPE on the first 64 dims. So `fused_norm_rope` and `fused_q` quantize the key and query themselves, with AITER's scale rule and the page order from AITER's `cache_format()`.
- Gain: the scorer reads 68 instead of 132 bytes per key, and prefill scores the paged cache in place instead of gathering K. Both grow with context and batch. Short contexts pay the per-step decode schedule (about 25 us at 8-16 rows); 8K and 4K serving shows no change beyond noise.
- Limits: 64- or 128-token pages (other `--block-size` values fail at startup), no DCP or PCP (rejected at startup), gfx950 with AITER only. The new kernel tests need gfx950 and run in the optional MI355 kernels step.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, related PRs and duplicate search</summary>

- MTP draft layers that reuse the target's top-k skip the query quantization. The model check uses `architectures`, because MTP drafts carry the rewritten `deepseek_mtp` model_type.
- #60834 (open) edits the same check in `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4` to add DeepSeek-V4 by model_type and adds its backend class next to this one; whichever lands second takes the union.
- #48558 (open, needs rebase) adds an MXFP4 indexer cache for GLM-5.2 on CUDA sm_100 through the legacy `deepseek_v2` indexer and the `use_fp4_indexer_cache` flag that #52550 replaced. It does not touch ROCm and reports +3.5% KV with neutral latency on B200.
- #57517 and #56834 add ROCm MXFP4 indexing for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 only. #60042, #60294 and #60756 change the ROCm FP8 scorer kernels and #59421 adds native FP8 decode above next_n=2; each would narrow the gain if it lands. #53953 edits `deepseek_v32/amd/rocm.py`.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "mxfp4 indexer ROCm", "fp4 indexer cache", "indexer_kv_dtype", "MXFP4 indexer GLM", "mxfp4 indexer DeepSeek-V3.2", "paged mxfp4 indexer", "RocmSparseAttnIndexer", "fused_norm_rope mxfp4", "GLM-5 ROCm indexer", "indexer cache fp4 AMD".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #48558 covers CUDA through a removed flag, and the ROCm MXFP4 indexer PRs (#57517, #56834, #60834) cover DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 only.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

items.title: [Bugfix] Resolve disabled thinking effort in Anthropic render
items.author: bzsuni
items.summary: Fixes render endpoint bypassing disabled-thinking effort resolution, causing GPT-OSS render requests to fail with Harmony rejecting reasoning_effort=none.
items.body:
## Overview

Fix `/v1/messages/render` bypassing the disabled-thinking effort resolution used by `/v1/messages` and token counting. This caused render requests with `thinking.type="disabled"` to fail on GPT-OSS and ignore `--anthropic-disabled-thinking-effort`.

## Claims

- Apply the existing disabled-thinking effort resolution to Messages render requests.
- Honor configured effort in both API and standalone render servers.
- Preserve existing behavior for requests without disabled thinking.

## Validation

Added parameterized regression tests covering automatic fallback, explicit effort, explicit `none`, and requests without disabled thinking.

- Before the fix, the automatic-fallback and explicit-effort cases failed.
- With the fix, all regression cases passed; **152 tests passed** across the related suites.
- HTTP validation with `openai/gpt-oss-20b` confirmed disabled-thinking render requests succeed and produce the same tokens as Chat render with the resolved effort.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff and mypy.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_protocol_exports.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/render/test_app_state.py -q
```

## Details

Messages render previously converted disabled thinking to `reasoning_effort="none"` without applying the configured override or automatic fallback. Harmony rejects `none`, causing GPT-OSS render requests to fail.

Extract the existing effort probe and caching logic into a reusable resolver, and pass the configuration through both server initialization paths. The probe rules remain unchanged, and resolution only runs for disabled-thinking requests.

## Overview

Bump Transformers to [v5.20.0](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases/tag/v5.20.0). Follows #60381.

## Claims

- `requirements/common.txt` allows `transformers >= 5.16.1, < 5.21.0`.
- Test requirements pin `transformers==5.20.0` (cuda, rocm, xpu, cpu, nightly-torch).
- `min_transformers_version="5.20.0"` on `Kolibri1ForCausalLM` is kept, since 5.16.1 to 5.19.x are still supported. The `transformers-upgrade` skill now says to keep such gates until the floor reaches them, instead of removing them on a pin bump.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes. The `pip-compile` hooks for cuda, rocm, xpu and cpu resolve 5.20.0 and leave the hand-edited lock files unchanged.
- `pytest tests/transformers_utils tests/config tests/tokenizers_` on 5.20.0 (macOS, no GPU): 1202 passed, 253 skipped, 2 failed. Neither failure is from this change: `test_ray_runtime_env` needs Ray, and `test_mp_reducer` can't start an engine on this machine (it fails the same way on 5.19.0).
- Checked against the 5.20 breaking changes:
  - Every vendored config that declares `sub_configs` builds and round-trips through `to_dict()` (`SubConfigSpec`, huggingface/transformers#48282).
  - The `embedding_gemma2` imports vLLM uses still resolve (huggingface/transformers#49473).

items.title: [Fix] Inkling: frame constrained output in native message tokens
items.author: JustinTong0323
items.summary: With,, and constraints do not follow Inkling's wire format. Inkling frames every message with native tokens ( …, then … before EOS). [Discussion: /rerun-test testreasonergrammarbackend.py testgrammarmanager.py testinkling.py testinklingun]
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--reasoning-parser inkling`, `response_format`, `regex` and `ebnf` constraints do not follow Inkling's wire format. Inkling frames every message with native tokens (`<|message_model|><|content_thinking|>` … `<|end_message|>`, then `<|message_model|><|content_text|>` … `<|end_message|>` before EOS). On `main` the constraint waits for a reasoning terminator re-encoded from its printed spelling, whose IDs the model never emits. With thinking on, the constraint never starts. With thinking off, it constrains raw text that lacks the answer header.

On `main` @ `06b81b120e`, live on `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4`, constrained requests fail as follows:
- the answer header is missing;
- prose appears before the JSON, or extra data after it (`{...}{}`);
- whitespace runs on until `max_tokens`;
- regex payloads repeat (`Yesyes`);
- `continue_final_message` combined with a constraint fails every case.

## Modifications

Inkling's format knowledge lives with its reasoning detector. `BaseReasoningFormatDetector.get_answer_frame()` returns `None` by default; Inkling's detector returns an `InklingAnswerFrame` (`parser/answer_frame.py`). The frame owns the framed constraint types, the framing token IDs, the open-text-block check, the frame's structural tag and the canonical auto-tool tag. `ReasonerGrammarBackend` only composes a detector's frame with the payload grammar. Without a frame, other detectors and backends keep their dispatch through identity/no-op defaults on `BaseGrammarBackend`.

**Native reasoning terminator** (`reasoner_grammar_backend.py`; this contains #40894)
- The reasoning-deferred grammar takes its think-end IDs from the detector, so Inkling's native `<|end_message|>` (200010) ends thinking.
- The canonical Inkling auto-tool structural tag, recognized by the frame, skips deferral; its schema is built once.

**Whole-turn frame for constrained output**
- Under the Inkling detector, `json`, `regex` and `ebnf` constraints compile into one token-level structural tag: an optional thinking message, then `<|message_model|><|content_text|>`, the payload and `<|end_message|>`. EOS is the stop token.
- The frame owns the turn, so the output keeps Inkling's message framing whether or not the model thinks first.
- When the prompt already ends in an open text block (`continue_final_message`), the payload starts inside that block. `GrammarManager` asks the backend for a request-specific key (`get_request_grammar_key`), so this variant is cached separately.

**Strict thinking**
- With `--enable-strict-thinking`, the same frame caps the thinking message at the request's thinking budget. Without a request budget, the server's `SGLANG_MAX_THINK_TOKENS` applies. A request budget overrides the server value, as it does for the unconstrained strict wrapper.
- A budget that differs from the server's selects its own frame through the grammar key. Equivalent budgets share one key (all negatives mean unlimited, and the server value is the default frame). Only the 32 most recent budget variants stay in the grammar cache.

**xgrammar backend** (`xgrammar_backend.py`)
- `compile_framed_grammar` embeds the already-compiled payload grammar, so JSON whitespace settings carry over.
- Framed grammars compile on an uncached `GrammarCompiler`. The cached compiler mixes up token-level structural tags of different shapes; this is fixed upstream by mlc-ai/xgrammar#943, which is not yet released ([reproducer](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/951#issuecomment-6159764165)). The uncached compiler can go once the pin includes that fix.
- Inkling's control tokens decode to their literal spellings and are not special in the tokenizer, so a JSON string could otherwise contain `<|end_message|>`.
  - The framing compiler uses a vocabulary in which those IDs cannot match text (`reserve_framing_tokens`).
  - The main compiler keeps the original vocabulary, because required/named tool tags spell the markers as strings.
- Backends without `compile_framed_grammar` keep the deferred constraint.

**Known limitation (unchanged here):** under strict thinking, an unconstrained Inkling request ends its first thinking message at the budget, but the model can then open another thinking message.

This is split out of #42844, which moves Inkling prompt rendering and output parsing to `tml-renderers` and builds on this change. It works on `main`'s existing Inkling renderer and parsers.

## Accuracy Tests

Devbox: 4x GB300, `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4` @ `42a75a99a40eb2ba1e0717db6357a0bf15205044`, with the cookbook GB300 NVFP4 TP4 recipe plus `--reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling`:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4 \
  --tp 4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --attention-backend fa4 --page-size 128 \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed \
  --enable-torch-symm-mem --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.1 --enable-multimodal \
  --reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling --port 30000
```

The strict rows add `--enable-strict-thinking` with `SGLANG_MAX_THINK_TOKENS=48`. The reasoning-parser-only rows drop `--tool-call-parser`.

| Check | `main` @ `06b81b120e` | This PR @ `85a72d9195` |
|---|---|---|
| Constrained output: Chat `json_schema` / `json_object` / `regex` / `ebnf` and Responses `json_schema` / `json_object`, thinking on and off, stream and non-stream; required and named tools; Chat non-stream also checks the framed token sequence | 11/28 | 84/84 (3 rounds) |
| Same rows, reasoning parser only | — | 40/40 |
| `continue_final_message` with `regex` / `json_schema` / `ebnf`, effort high and none, stream and non-stream, 3 rounds, interleaved with ordinary constrained requests | 0/54 | 48/54 |
| Strict thinking: `regex` and `json_schema` with request budgets 6, 20 and 48 and with none, 3 rounds | — | 24/24; thinking stops at exactly 6, 20 or 48 tokens, then a valid answer |
| Strict thinking: one thinking message within the budget, natural and budget-forced end, stream and non-stream | — | 12/12 |
| Constrained rows on the strict server | — | 28/28 |

On this PR, every continuation response contains only the payload, starts inside the open block and ends with `<|end_message|>`. The 6 misses are effort-high `ebnf` `[0-9]+` answers that keep adding digits (`426`) instead of ending the sentence. A digits-only grammar cannot end with `.`, so this is a grammar/prompt mismatch.

Unit tests at `85a72d9195`, xgrammar 0.2.7:
- `unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py`, `test_grammar_manager.py` and `test_base_grammar_backend.py`, plus `unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: 268 passed.
- `unit/constrained/` and `unit/function_call/`: 775 passed.

At `4c0c9a0530` (merged with `main`, framing owned by the detector), live on the same recipe: constrained rows 28/28, reasoning parser only 40/40, continuation 48/54 (the same 6 `ebnf` digit misses), strict budgets 24/24, strict thinking 12/12, constrained rows on the strict server 28/28. Compiled grammars, dispatch and per-step token masks are identical to `9e3021662b` on 200 probe cases (Inkling and Qwen3 detectors, strict on and off, `json`/`regex`/`ebnf`/`structural_tag`, plain and continuation prompts, five budgets). Unit recipe above at `4c0c9a0530`: 271 passed.

Unconstrained requests without strict thinking do not take the changed paths.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not performance-related. Framed grammars compile once per distinct constraint (and budget variant) on an uncached compiler; the compiled grammar is cached as before.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Fix] bailing: MoE gate dtype follows config.router_dtype
items.author: JustinTong0323
items.summary: forces the MoE gate GEMM to bf16, overriding from Ling checkpoints. The bf16 gate perturbs top-k routing enough to cause output variance (reported by the Ling team on Ling-3.x checkpoints; the fp32 gate is what the checkpoint was trained/tuned against).
items.body:
## Motivation

`BailingMoeV3` forces the MoE gate GEMM to bf16, overriding `router_dtype="fp32"` from Ling checkpoints. The bf16 gate perturbs top-k routing enough to cause output variance (reported by the Ling team on Ling-3.x checkpoints; the fp32 gate is what the checkpoint was trained/tuned against).

## Modifications

Gate dtype follows the checkpoint config: `router_dtype == "fp32"` (or absent) → fp32 gate; any other value → bf16. No behavior change for configs that don't set `router_dtype="fp32"`.

## Accuracy Tests

Routing-affecting change: greedy outputs shift back to the fp32-gate reference. Ling team validated on their internal branch and the ling-v3-open branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On Hopper the fp32 gate GEMM does not use tensor cores, so decode gives back part of the bf16-gate speedup; correctness takes priority.

Co-authored-by: 文贤 <luoyuan.luo@antgroup.com>

items.title: [Fix] openai: keep the tool-call parser on under tool_choice="none"
items.author: renning22
items.summary: currently does two things: the prompt side withholds or soft-disables tools, and the response side turns the tool-call parser off ( returns False). Nothing stops the model from writing a call anyway, for example when the user explicitly insists on a tool.
items.body:
## Motivation

`tool_choice="none"` currently does two things: the prompt side withholds or soft-disables tools, and the response side turns the tool-call parser off (`_tool_call_parsing_active` returns False). Nothing stops the model from writing a call anyway, for example when the user explicitly insists on a tool. When it does, the call reaches the client as **raw template syntax in `message.content`**, because no parser consumes it.

Seen in production with Kimi K3 (`--tool-call-parser kimi_k3`). The user prompt was "query the weather, you must call get_weather", sent with `tools` and `tool_choice: "none"`. On engines that run this code path, 3 of 6 responses had content like:

```
<|open|>tools<|sep|><|open|>call tool="get_weather" index="1"<|sep|>...
```

The same failure class has come up before for other formats:
- #35393, closed: post-hoc stripping of unparsed K3 syntax.
- #40237, open: DeepSeek tool markup returned as content.
- #43006, merged: withholds DSV tools from the prompt under `none`, but cannot stop the model from emitting a call.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`:
- **`_tool_call_parsing_active`** is now true whenever tools and a parser are configured, including `tool_choice="none"`. The parser consumes the call's template syntax instead of leaking it.
- **New `_drop_tool_calls(request)`:** under `"none"`, parsed calls are discarded.
  - Non-streaming returns no `tool_calls`, and a `tool_calls` finish becomes `stop`.
  - Streaming emits no tool-call deltas, never sets `has_tool_calls`, and skips the leftover-argument flush.
- **Under `"none"` with tools present, `skip_special_tokens=False`, as under `"auto"`.** This keeps the markers the parser matches decodable. The glm47 full-assistant grammar case is left as is.
- **Unchanged:**
  - What goes into the prompt under `"none"` (`tools=None` on the jinja path, `tool_choice="none"` for the K3 encoder, DSV omission).
  - The K3 `TOOLS_CLOSE` stop stays scoped to active tools (`test_kimi_k3_tool_call_stop_is_scoped_to_active_tools` still passes).

A model that obeys `"none"` behaves exactly as before. A model that calls anyway now returns its text without the call, instead of the call's raw syntax.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output or kernel change. Response post-processing only.

Unit tests (CPU), in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`:
- `test_tool_choice_none_keeps_tool_call_parser_active`
- `test_kimi_k3_tool_choice_none_drops_call_non_stream`: `"none"` returns content `"I'll check the weather."`, no `tool_calls`, finish `stop`. The `"auto"` control returns 1 call with finish `tool_calls`.
- `test_kimi_k3_tool_choice_none_drops_call_stream`: the stream is fed in 7-character pieces. `"none"` streams only `"I'll check."`, with no tool-call deltas. The `"auto"` control still streams the call.

**Without the fix, the new tests fail with the production symptom:** `'<|open|>' unexpectedly found in "I'll check the weather.<|open|>tools<|sep|><|open|>call tool=\"get_weather\"…"`.

**Regressions:** `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/` and `test/registered/function_call/` were run on CPU with and without the patch.
- Same pre-existing environment failures on both (5 dsv4/dsv32/kimi-k3 encoding-detection tests need real model configs, and 3 modules failed to collect locally).
- With the patch: 510 passed, versus 507 without, the difference being the new tests. No new failures.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The extra cost only applies to `tool_choice="none"` requests with tools, which now run the same parser `"auto"` requests already run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Ran isort 7.0.0, ruff-format 0.15.1 and codespell 2.4.1 on the changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no user-facing flag changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

A stronger fix would be to stop the model from *starting* a call under `"none"`. For Kimi K3 that means a structural tag excluding `TOOLS_OPEN`, mirroring `get_kimik3_structural_tag(..., "required")`. It is left out here because grammar-constrained decoding under DSPARK with TP > 1 can currently deadlock (#41449), and DSPARK is a common K3 deployment recipe.

items.title: [Fix] hicache: Reset storage existence cache on backend attach
items.author: lhzds
items.summary: In mode, detaching a storage backend and attaching another retains the old storage existence cache. For example, after switching the backend from directory A to an empty directory B, pages stored in A are still considered present and their backups to B are ski…
items.body:
## Motivation

In `buffer_only` mode, detaching a storage backend and attaching another retains the old storage existence cache. For example, after switching the `file` backend from directory A to an empty directory B, pages stored in A are still considered present and their backups to B are skipped. A later storage-query miss can invalidate these entries, but the backend change itself leaves them stale.

## Modifications

Clear the storage existence cache after a new backend is successfully attached. Policy updates on the currently attached backend, failed attachments, and rejected backend changes preserve the existing entries.

Add CPU regression tests for switching between two file directories, invalidating KV and auxiliary-pool entries, and preserving entries on the other paths.

## Validation

- The five new tests pass on two Linux x86_64 hosts with Python 3.11.2 and PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu. On the original code at `a448fdf`, the empty-backend backup test and the pool-invalidation test fail.
- Combined with the existing buffer-mode sidecar, prefetch lifecycle, scheduler attachment, and anchor-lock tests: **30 tests and 19 subtests passed on each host**.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including the repository-wide test registry check.

The new tests use a mocked controller lifecycle and real `HiCacheFile` I/O. Model inference and accelerator transfers were not tested. The four existing `TestUnifiedRadixCacheStorageAttachBackfill` tests could not initialize a device in this environment; CPU-engine mode also requires the unavailable `sgl_kernel` package.

Run the new regression tests with:

```bash
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_attachment.py
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused unit tests and register them for CPU CI.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [x] Perform a self-review of the code.
