items.title: [Doc] cookbook: Refresh SemiAnalysis AgentX launches for Qwen3.5 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GB300
items.author: nvpohanh
items.summary: The cookbook's Agentic Long-Context Deployment sections (#42726, #43083, #43799, #43983, #44065, #44228, #44654) mirror SemiAnalysis InferenceX AgentX submissions as raw launch commands, each linked to the run that measured it. That PR retires the four earlier…
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

The cookbook's **Agentic Long-Context Deployment** sections (#42726, #43083, #43799, #43983, #44065, #44228, #44654) mirror SemiAnalysis InferenceX AgentX submissions as raw launch commands, each linked to the run that measured it. This PR:

1. **Replaces the Qwen3.5 NVFP4 GB300 Dynamo+SGLang deployments** with the nine points of the open [InferenceX #4162](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4162). That PR retires the four earlier configs of this lane.
2. **Refreshes DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GB300 SGLang** to the open [InferenceX #4033](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4033): the 20261014 nightly, the fastokens tokenizer, decoder SWA bounded replay and a new DEP2 c160 point.
3. **Syncs to InferenceX `main`** (`12dbddac`). All seven InferenceX PRs of #44654 have merged, and so has [InferenceX #4155](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4155), which retunes Muse Spark Open B200.

## Source

[InferenceX](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX) `main` (`12dbddac`), with these open InferenceX PRs overlaid:

| PR | Page | Lanes | Pinned to |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#4162](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4162) Qwen3.5 NVFP4 GB300 Dynamo+SGLang | Qwen3.5 | `qwen3.5-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-agg-src`, `-disagg-src` (new); retires `-agentic-agg`, `-agentic-disagg`, `-agentic-agg-pareto`, `-agentic-pp-pareto` | no `/use` yet: in progress at head `cd917605` |
| [#4033](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4033) DSV4.1-Flash GB300 SGLang | DeepSeek-V4.1 | `dsv41flash-fp4-gb300-sglang-agentic-dspark` | no `/use` yet: in progress at head `a61b7eba` |

"In progress" lanes are rendered at the PR head and labeled "In progress in SA InferenceX AgentX". A later sync pins them once the PR gets a `/use` run or merges.

The overlays of #44654 have all merged into InferenceX `main`, and their lanes now come from `main`, pinned to the run the dashboard shows. Their commands are unchanged:

| PR | Lane | Now pinned to |
|---|---|---|
| [InferenceX #4146](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4146) | `musespark-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-dflash` | [run 38825818513](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38825818513), verified (was in progress) |
| [InferenceX #4141](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4141) | `musespark-fp4-gb300-sglang-agentic-dflash` | [run 38835086328](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38835086328), verified (was in progress) |
| [InferenceX #4112](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4112) | `dsv41flash-fp4-gb200-sglang-agentic-dspark` | [run 38749229680](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38749229680), verified (was in progress) |
| [InferenceX #4111](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4111) | `dsv41flash-fp4-b200-sglang-agentic-dspark` | [run 38749770474](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38749770474), the run its `/use` named |
| [InferenceX #4094](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4094) | `dsv41flash-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-dspark` | [run 38705241139](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38705241139), the run its `/use` named |

[InferenceX #4147](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4147) and [InferenceX #4140](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4140) were already pinned from `main` in #44654. #4147's B200 lane is now replaced by #4155 (below).

## What this PR does

| Page | Lanes | Deployments | Points | Hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 | 16 | 27 | 67 | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200 |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 10 | 20 | 61 | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | 9 | 22 | 74 (was 73) | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200, H100 |
| Qwen3.5 | 17 (was 19) | 47 (was 50) | 208 (was 221) | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200, H100 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 4 | 4 | 22 | GB300, B300, B200, H200 |
| Muse Spark Open | 4 | 4 | 41 (was 40) | GB300, GB200, B300, B200 |

Only the generated data files change. The component (`_agentx.jsx`), page text, Deployment panels and Playgrounds are untouched.

- **Qwen3.5 NVFP4 GB300 Dynamo+SGLang ([InferenceX #4162](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4162)), replaced.** All new points run MTP 6-1-7 (NEXTN, the checkpoint's BF16 draft head) with HiCache (host DRAM), on `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-qwen35-agentx-gb300-ccebaceeeca3`. That image is built from the SGLang branch `nvidia/qwen35-agentx-gb300` at `ccebacee`.

  | Before (measured on `main`) | After (#4162, in progress) |
  |---|---|
  | Agg TP2 MTP 3-1-4 c1–c64; Agg TP8 (2 nodes) c7; Agg TP2 c44 (two `--max-running-requests` variants); Disagg 1P1D TP4/TP4 no spec c8–c128; Disagg 1P1D TP2/TP2 c72; Disagg 3P4D c565; Disagg 3P2D c704 | Agg TP2 c5, 7, 10; Agg TP4 c7; Agg TP8 (2 nodes) c7, 10 (all `--max-running-requests 1`); Disagg 1P1D TP1 prefill + TP2 decode on one node (3 GPUs) c38, c56; Disagg 3P1D (3 × PP4 prefill, DEP8 decode on 2 nodes, 20 GPUs) c704 |
  | 4 configs, 8 deployments, 19 points; `nightly-dev-cu13-20260724-433429b1` / `20260831-bb5e6198` | 2 configs, 5 deployments, 6 points (the PR's nine concurrencies) |

  - Aggregated points were submitted with the SGLang router, disaggregated ones with Dynamo (KV router; 2 frontends behind nginx at c704). The disaggregated launches use Dynamo built from source at [`b208989f`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/commit/b208989fbe1cfbfde64d11334d8af4ff04fe1a99), shown as the cell's install note.
  - The workers set the branch's `SGLANG_Q35MF_*` switches, mirrored as submitted. They are off by default, and each point enables the ones its recipe lists.
  - The Mooncake tier is now offered (derived): this image includes the external linker, which the retired lanes' images predated.
  - The four retired configs leave the page because #4162 deletes them. Their measured `main` versions ([run 31042542308](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/31042542308) of [InferenceX #2477](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/2477), [run 34345050756](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34345050756) of [InferenceX #2812](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/2812)) remain HiCache donors only as a fallback, which no deployment needed this time. No other Qwen3.5 command changes.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GB300 SGLang ([InferenceX #4033](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4033)).** The image moves from `nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935` to `nightly-dev-cu13-20261014-684fea8a` (pinned by digest). The same three deployments get these changes:
  - `--tokenizer-backend fastokens` on every point except DEP2 c160, which keeps `huggingface`;
  - `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` on DEP2 c64 / c128 and TP4 c1;
  - TP4 c1: `--max-running-requests 1` (was 2) and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`;
  - a new **Agg DEP2 c160** point (c128 settings with `--prefill-decode-interval 8`).

  The lane is in progress until #4033 gets a `/use` run. Its measured `main` version ([InferenceX #3859](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3859), [run 38221097558](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38221097558)) stays a donor-only fallback.
- **Muse Spark Open B200 ([InferenceX #4155](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4155), merged).** The lane is pinned to [run 38851010434](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38851010434), the run #4155's `/use` named. It moves from Agg TP4·EP4 (c1–c32) to Agg TP8·EP8 on all 8 GPUs:
  - c1–c12 run without KV offload;
  - c16–c48 run HiCache (`--hicache-size` 120 GB at c16, 160 GB from c24) with prefill sequence parallelism and MegaMoE;
  - all points use `--attention-backend trtllm_mha`, `--page-size 128`, `--max-running-requests 192`, breakable prefill CUDA graphs, `--speculative-use-block-verification` and `--enable-http2`.

  c1–c12 now also offer a derived HiCache tier, using the B200 lane's own HiCache flags. B300 and GB300 still have no HiCache tier, since they have no Muse Spark Open HiCache lane on the same hardware.
- **GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next**: no command changes.
- `qwen3.5-fp8-h100-sglang-agentic` is still not mirrored, as before: no dashboard changelog names it, so it was never measured.

## How the commands are produced

The pipeline is the same as in #44654, with these changes:

- **Retired configs.** A config key that an overlaid InferenceX PR deletes now leaves the page with the overlay, as it will when the PR merges. Before, the pipeline ignored deletions, so these four keys would have stayed next to their replacements. Their measured `main` versions are kept only as KV-offload donors, like a key that an overlay overrides.
- **Run attribution.** When two InferenceX PRs name the same key on one dashboard date (#4147, then #4155, on 2026-10-16), the lane is credited to the PR whose run produced the dashboard rows. No other lane's attribution changed.
- **Rules.** These are kept as serving configuration:
  - worker flags `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend`, `--speculative-use-block-verification` and `--enable-http2` (Granian HTTP server with HTTP/2);
  - env `SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN` and `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND`;
  - the `SGLANG_Q35MF_*` switches of the #4162 image.

  `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` is kept as a timeout.

Each lane is still rendered at the exact commit of the run that produced its dashboard data, or at the PR head while in progress. SA-only settings are removed: the benchmark harness, cluster paths and caches, telemetry, and InferenceX's synthetic speculative acceptance (disclosed per deployment). Placeholders replace IPs, ports and NICs. Router and KV-offload variants that were not run are derived and labeled "Derived — not run". `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` from the SemiAnalysis cluster environment (#44228) applies to the new lanes as well: their GB300 and B200 clusters export it.

The data files are generated, so there is no hand-written code to review here.

## Validation

- `mint validate` (strict build) and `mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` pass. `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passes, and so does `pre-commit run --all-files`.
- **Browser click-through.** A headless browser clicked through every combination of hardware, checkpoint, deployment, concurrency, KV tier and router on all six pages under `mint dev`, opening every tab. That is 2,384 command sets: GLM-5.2 328, DeepSeek-V4 316, DeepSeek-V4.1 444, Qwen3.5 1,018, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 76 and Muse Spark Open 202.
  - The rendered commands match the expected text exactly, with no browser errors.
  - The "Copy link" URL of every deployment was reopened in a fresh tab and restored the same selection and tab (124 links).
  - The Deployment-panel footer link and section placement checks pass on all six pages, and two pages that did not opt in show no link. The copy buttons work on a plain-HTTP preview.
- **Decoder and KV flags.** The component's own decoder, run through Node, reproduces the Python-generated commands for all 2,384 combinations, including every point's measured tier. Every KV-cache flag in a shown command exists in the SGLang commit of its deployment's image (190 image/flag pairs). For the #4162 image that is `ccebacee` on `nvidia/qwen35-agentx-gb300`.
- **Diff against `main`.**

  | Page | Command sets |
  |---|---|
  | GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | all byte-identical |
  | Qwen3.5 | 982 identical; 76 removed (the four retired configs), 36 added (#4162) |
  | DeepSeek-V4.1 | 396 identical; 42 changed and 6 added (GB300 SGLang, #4033) |

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix decoded logprob tokens that continue a split UTF-8 character
items.author: mottopanikeiku
items.summary: Fixes U+FFFD replacement characters in decoded logprob tokens when UTF-8 characters are split across tokens in LogprobsProcessor and OnlineDerenderer.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Decoded logprob tokens can contain U+FFFD even though the generated text is valid. With Qwen3, the logprob tokens of `🍰이 맛있다` join to `��이 맛�다`. This fixes the correction in `LogprobsProcessor` for tokens that start with the rest of a split UTF-8 character and then contain more text, and the copy of that correction in `OnlineDerenderer`, which the `/derender` endpoints use.

## Claims

- Sample logprobs (streaming and non-streaming) and prompt logprobs of such tokens now decode to the right text in `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` (including `top_logprobs`), `/inference/v1/generate` with `output_mode="text"`, and `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender`: for Qwen3 and `🍰이 맛있다`, the logprob tokens join to the same string as the output text.
- Tokens whose decoded text ends with U+FFFD are corrected as before.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU, Python-only install):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py -q
# main: 4 failed, 3 passed. This PR: 7 passed.
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py -q
# main: 4 failed, 5 passed. This PR: 9 passed.
python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -q -k TestCorrectDecodedToken
# 11 passed, 53 deselected (existing UTF-8 correction tests)
```

The new `test_utf8_continuation_before_valid_suffix` in `test_logprobs_processor.py` feeds the Qwen3 token IDs of `🍰이 맛있다` through `LogprobsProcessor` as sample and prompt logprobs, with both logprob storage formats, and also with the emoji's first bytes split over two byte tokens. It checks that the decoded logprob tokens join to the decoded text. The test of the same name in `test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py` does the same for `OnlineDerenderer._resolve_logprobs`, for whole responses and one-token chunks, and also checks the top-candidate strings and the `bytes`.

End to end on an L4 with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enforce-eager`, comparing the wheel for fa75d3456 (`main`) with the same wheel plus this change. `/v1/completions` with `logprobs: 0`, once with `echo: true, max_tokens: 0` on the prompt `Caption: 🍰이 맛있다`, and twice (non-streaming and streaming) generating `🍰이 맛있다` with `structured_outputs: {"regex": ...}`:

| Request | Logprob tokens on `main` | Logprob tokens with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt logprobs (`echo`) | `Caption`, `:`, ``, ` 🍰`, `이`, ``, ` 맛`, ``, `�다` | `Caption`, `:`, ``, ` 🍰`, `이`, ``, ` 맛`, ``, `있다` |
| Generation, non-streaming | ``, ``, ``, `🍰`, `이`, ` `, ``, `맛`, ``, `�다`, `<\|im_end\|>` | ``, ``, ``, `🍰`, `이`, ` `, ``, `맛`, ``, `있다`, `<\|im_end\|>` |
| Generation, streaming | same as non-streaming | same as non-streaming |

The generated text is `🍰이 맛있다` in both runs; only the decoded logprob tokens differ.

A second run with `--enable-scale-out` sent `/v1/chat/completions` (`logprobs: true, top_logprobs: 3`), `/inference/v1/generate` with `output_mode: "text"`, and the token output of `/inference/v1/generate` through `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender`, each streaming and non-streaming (8 requests). The logprob tokens matched the generated text in 0 of 8 on `main` and in 8 of 8 with this PR. With only the `LogprobsProcessor` change, the two derender endpoints still returned `�다`.

`pre-commit run --files` on the four changed files: all hooks passed.

## Details

Qwen3 tokenizes `🍰이 맛있다` into tokens that decode individually as `['�', '��이', ' �', '�', '�', '�다']`: `��이` holds the last bytes of 🍰 followed by 이. `_verify_tokens` only corrected tokens whose decoded text ends with U+FFFD, so `��이` and `�다` were returned as is. In `_correct_decoded_token`, the context search stopped at the first context whose decoded text no longer ended with U+FFFD, which can still contain an incomplete character earlier in the string. Both checks now look for U+FFFD anywhere in the text. The rest of the correction, including the four-token context limit, is unchanged.

`OnlineDerenderer` (`vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py`) has its own copy of `_correct_decoded_token` and the same trailing-only checks in `_resolve_logprobs`, so the second commit makes the same change there.

A literal U+FFFD in the text is dropped from the logprob tokens both before and after this change, since it can't be told apart from an incomplete byte sequence this way.

Duplicate check: I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `LogprobsProcessor`, `_correct_decoded_token`, `decoded_token`, the file path, and "logprobs" with "utf-8", "unicode", "replacement character" and "emoji". The earlier UTF-8 fixes for #27300 (#28874, #34875) are merged and this case fails with them. Open PRs that touch `vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py` or its tests (#60542, #60915, #60918, #57442, #35961) change logprob storage, rendering and fast paths, not this correction. #60437 changes the parsed streaming path in `online_derenderer.py`, but not `_correct_decoded_token` or the checks in `_resolve_logprobs`.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to find, fix and test this bug and to write this description.

items.title: [CI] 5090: Cut the install's disk footprint and guard against full disks
items.author: nvpohanh
items.summary: Since 2026-10-15, jobs have been failing with (#44479). The pool moved to new vast.ai hosts that start with empty caches and small disks; #44383 says the trial machines have 32 GB.
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

Since 2026-10-15, `1-gpu-5090` jobs have been failing with `No space left on device (os error 28)` (#44479). The pool moved to new vast.ai hosts that start with empty caches and small disks; #44383 says the trial machines have 32 GB. On these hosts, a few jobs are enough to fill the disk:

- `UV_LINK_MODE=copy` keeps three full copies of the CUDA torch stack:
  - the uv cache;
  - the kept venv `/opt/sglang-ci-py3.12`;
  - the build environment for the editable sglang install, which needs torch because it is in `[build-system].requires`.
- Nothing evicts Hugging Face checkpoints. For example, base-b 1-gpu-small loads `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, about 16 GB.
- The 5090 diffusion canary's `minimax_h3_t2va_consumer_budget_1gpu_5090` case downloads the 134 GiB MiniMax-H3 `FL2VA` variant on any host that doesn't have it cached.
- When the disk fills, the failure shows up deep inside uv, and nothing in the log says how much space was free.

This PR shrinks the install's footprint and makes 5090 hosts either free space or fail with a clear error. It does not remove the need to give these hosts enough disk.

## Modifications

1. **Hardlink instead of copy.** `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh` now sets `UV_LINK_MODE=hardlink` instead of `copy`. The venv and the build environment hardlink files from the uv cache, so the CUDA stack is stored once. When the cache and the venv are on different filesystems, uv falls back to copying and prints a warning; I checked both cases with uv 0.8.15. Hardlinks would let an in-place edit of an installed file change the cache too, but I found no CI step that edits installed files in place.
2. **New `scripts/ci/cuda/ensure_disk_headroom.sh`, run as the first install step.**
   - **Every CUDA runner:** print free space for the filesystems holding `/opt`, the uv cache, and the HF cache. When the lowest is below 40 GiB, run `uv cache prune`, capped at 5 minutes; it removes only entries nothing references.
   - **`SGLANG_CI_DISK_GUARD=strict`:** additionally:
     - evict least-recently-used HF repos until 40 GiB is free, skipping any repo used in the last 2 hours;
     - print the largest cache directories;
     - fail with an `::error::` if less than 10 GiB is still free.
   - **Where strict is set:** only for jobs whose `runs-on` is `1-gpu-5090`, in `_pr-test-stage.yml`, `pr-test-jit-kernel.yml`, `pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml`, `rerun-test.yml`, and `diffusion-ci-gt-gen.yml`. These hosts keep the HF cache on their own disk. On a cache volume shared by many hosts, eviction only moves the failure to the next job; `scripts/ci/amd/check_hf_cache_space.sh` documents this.
3. **New `scripts/ci/utils/evict_hf_cache.py`,** which uses only the standard library because it runs before the venv exists, plus a unit test, `test_evict_hf_cache.py`.
4. **Remove `minimax_h3_t2va_consumer_budget_1gpu_5090` from the per-PR 5090 canary** (the case and its 5090 perf baseline).
   - Per-PR CI no longer covers H3's constrained-placement path.
   - `flux_image_t2i_layerwise_cpu_offload_5090` still covers layerwise offload, with a small model.
   - The case can come back on a lane whose hosts have the checkpoint pre-cached.

Not changed: `ci_cleanup_venv.sh` still runs `uv cache prune --ci` when the disk is at least 85% full. With hardlinks, that frees less space, because entries also linked into the venv stay on disk, and later installs re-download what it removed. It is worth revisiting once the hosts have enough disk.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, CI only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. On a runner with enough free space, the guard only runs a few `df` calls.

## Testing

- `python -m unittest discover -s scripts/ci/utils -p 'test_evict_hf_cache.py'`: both tests pass. Each one fails when I break the logic it guards (eviction order reversed, or the 2-hour window ignored).
- I ran `ensure_disk_headroom.sh` with the thresholds raised, against a temporary HF cache:
  - **Report mode:** exits 0.
  - **Strict mode:** evicts only the idle repo, keeps the recent one, and exits 1 with the error.
- uv 0.8.15 hardlinks on the same filesystem (the venv file and the cache file share an inode) and falls back to copying across filesystems.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- Not yet run on a 5090 runner, and CI has not been triggered.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Related: #44479. cc @em-dreyer

items.title: [Feat] valen: add native multimodal shared-state decisions
items.author: Liuziyu77
items.summary: Valen's complete dense Qwen3.5 checkpoints answer Choice, Noul, and Score questions using one shared causal prefill and a trained FP32 Mixer. This adds native checkpoint loading and text/image/video decisions through. [Discussion: Local validation passed.]
items.body:
## Motivation

Valen's complete dense Qwen3.5 checkpoints answer Choice, Noul, and Score
questions using one shared causal prefill and a trained FP32 Mixer. This adds
native checkpoint loading and text/image/video decisions through `/v1/valen`.
All questions read the same processed state and retain the trained role/readout
layout and original answer formulas.

## Modifications

- Register `valen_qwen` and `ValenQwenForDecisionMaking`, reuse Qwen3.5 language
  and vision kernels/fused loaders, and strictly validate backbone and Mixer
  loading. Keep the Mixer parameters and computation in FP32.
- Carry request-local layouts through embedding IPC, scheduling, and forward
  batches. Require TP=PP=1 with complete prefill, disabled radix/chunking/CUDA
  graphs, and explicit errors for unsupported quantization or prompt truncation.
- Preserve Choice order, fixed bilingual Noul descriptions, and 2–255-level
  native Score. Add `/v1/valen` and a limited text/image `/v1/systemone` adapter.
- Use checkpoint HF media settings before appending schema tokens; transfer
  expanded IDs, pixels, and grids as `processor_output`. Preserve the training
  processor's video wrapper semantics with current Transformers. Reuse bounded
  URL loading, count assets before bundling, and clean temporary media on errors.
- Validate reserved controls against tokenizer.json added-token metadata as well
  as the tokenizer's special-token map. Add API documentation and CPU regressions.

## Accuracy Tests

- **39 CPU tests passed, 1 skipped** (37 Valen tests and two neighboring Clef CPU
  tests; the skipped neighboring test requires CUDA). Includes prompt/layout,
  FP32 head math, packed request isolation, media/limit errors, URL staging and
  cleanup, response semantics, and generator lifecycle.
- Ten component cases match the original Valen compiler, role spans, media
  pixels, MRoPE, and answer function. Random shared Mixer weights with FP32/BF16
  hidden inputs: maximum logit error 1.2e-7. Nine cases with the actual released
  2B Mixer weights and random hidden inputs: 1.4e-6. Real SGLang CPU media
  splitting/offset/MRoPE checks passed image, video, and interleaved fixtures.
- **Native GPU validation on one H200**, with complete Valen-2B weights and
  `model_impl=sglang`: strict loading, vision encoding, hybrid GDN/attention,
  pooling, and serving passed eight synthetic text/image/video/mixed multi-turn
  cases, including mixed Choice/Noul/Score questions.
- Original HF reference: FP32 stored backbone + BF16 autocast, PyTorch 2.6 and
  Transformers 5.4. Native runtime: BF16 backbone + FP32 Mixer, PyTorch 2.14.1
  (CUDA 13), Transformers 5.19, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, and FlashInfer 0.7.2.
  Language/GDN attention used Triton; vision used FA3. Prompt IDs matched exactly.

| Full-model comparison to original HF | Maximum absolute error | Smoke tolerance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Probability / Noul | 0.005102 | 0.02 |
| Score | 0.009516 | 0.1 |
| Confidence | 0.014274 | 0.05 |
| Raw candidate logits | 0.439496 | Reported separately |

All Choice decisions matched. These are synthetic correctness checks, not a
workload-level quality evaluation. Raw logits are not bitwise equivalent across
these storage/compute precisions and kernels.

- Concurrent versus isolated native requests: Choice decisions matched; maximum
  probability change 0.007273, below the explicit 0.01 tolerance. Raw logit change
  reached 0.036502 on a soft-label case; the report retains that drift rather
  than claiming identical BF16 reductions across batch shapes.
- **Actual HTTP server**: eight isolated and eight concurrent `/v1/valen`
  requests passed, including image/video/mixed inputs and response token counts.
  A tokenizer.json control-token injection was correctly rejected with 400.
- Ruff/isort/formatting, registered-test lint, diff whitespace, Mintlify build
  validation, and internal link checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No controlled performance benchmark yet. The validation records smoke forward
and HTTP timings, including initial compilation. The HF baseline uses its torch
fallback, so those timings are not presented as a speedup claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Native model/config and trained decision API implemented.
- [x] Text, image, and video frontend parity and CPU CI regressions.
- [x] Complete native weights/backbone/Mixer execution on an H200.
- [x] Original HF comparisons with numerical differences explicitly reported.
- [x] Concurrent requests and actual multimodal HTTP checks.
- [x] API docs, formatting, and Mintlify checks.
- [ ] Broader workload accuracy and controlled performance profiling.
- [ ] Upstream GPU regression registration with checkpoint/fixture availability.

This is a draft for review. Initial supported scope is unquantized dense
Qwen3.5 + Mixer, shared-state execution, TP=PP=1. The tested checkpoint is
Valen-2B; TP/PP, quantization, and other head architectures are outside this PR.

items.title: [XPU] Use per-token dynamic FP8 activation quantization on XPU
items.author: zufangzhu
items.summary: keeps its CUTLASS-only meaning. No behavior change on CUDA, ROCm, or CPU. [Discussion: Close this, since we already have one: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61362/changes]
items.body:
## Purpose

With `activation_scheme="dynamic"`, FP8 linear layers pick per-token activation scales only when `cutlass_fp8_supported()` is true. That helper is CUDA-only, so XPU always falls back to **per-tensor** dynamic quantization. Per-tensor dynamic quant needs a separate global max-reduction pass before quantizing, which is noticeably slower on XPU.

`XPUW8A8FP8LinearKernel` already lists `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` as supported, and `torch.ops._xpu_C.fp8_gemm` already accepts `[M, 1]` activation scales, so only the selection logic needs to change.

## Changes

- Add `dynamic_per_token_fp8_supported()` in `w8a8_utils.py`, returning `current_platform.is_xpu() or cutlass_fp8_supported()`. `cutlass_fp8_supported()` keeps its CUTLASS-only meaning.
- Use it in `Fp8LinearMethod` and `Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod`.

No behavior change on CUDA, ROCm, or CPU.

Note: on XPU this affects the W8A8 path (`XPUW8A8FP8LinearKernel`, e.g. `--kernel-config '{"linear_backend": "xpu"}'`). With `linear_backend=auto`, XPU currently selects the weight-only `XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel`, where activations are not quantized.

## Test Plan

Intel Arc Pro B70, single GPU, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, `quantization="fp8"` (online), `linear_backend="xpu"`:

- Check the selected activation quant key and the scale shape passed to `fp8_gemm`
- Greedy generation, baseline vs patched
- Op-level timing of dynamic quant + `fp8_gemm`, per-tensor vs per-token

## Test Result

**Selection**: baseline `QuantKey(f8e4m3fn, scale(f32, dynamic, per_tensor))` -> patched `QuantKey(f8e4m3fn, scale(f32, dynamic, per_token))`.

**Generation**: 3 of 4 greedy prompts produce identical output. The fourth diverges after about 40 tokens with an equivalent continuation (normal numerical drift).

**Op-level (ms, dynamic quant + fp8_gemm, bf16 input, per-tensor FP8 weight)**:

| m, n, k | quant T -> K | gemm T -> K | total T -> K | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096, 256, 8192 | 0.729 -> 0.215 | 0.233 -> 0.237 | 0.736 -> 0.486 | 1.51x |
| 4096, 1024, 8192 | 0.463 -> 0.217 | 0.908 -> 0.921 | 1.461 -> 1.233 | 1.18x |
| 4096, 2048, 8192 | 0.467 -> 0.221 | 1.857 -> 2.057 | 2.604 -> 2.362 | 1.10x |
| 4096, 4096, 4096 | 0.295 -> 0.137 | 1.935 -> 2.091 | 2.429 -> 2.283 | 1.06x |
| 8192, 8192, 8192 | 0.977 -> 0.450 | 17.204 -> 17.357 | 18.195 -> 17.651 | 1.03x |
| 32, 4096, 4096 | 0.053 -> 0.030 | 0.054 -> 0.054 | 0.091 -> 0.068 | 1.34x |
| 512, 4096, 4096 | 0.053 -> 0.030 | 0.229 -> 0.229 | 0.271 -> 0.263 | 1.03x |

Relative error vs fp32 reference is the same for both (about 0.037).

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass.

items.title: [Feat] [NPU] speculative: Support --speculative-draft-window-size/-sink-size via draft-decode KV mask
items.author: Estrella-xx
items.summary: and (StreamingLLM-style sink + windowed KV visibility for the multi-step draft decode path) are supported on the Triton and FlashInfer draft attention backends via KV index clipping, but not on the Ascend (NPU) backend. This PR adds equivalent support for NPU …
items.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

`--speculative-draft-window-size` and `--speculative-draft-sink-size` (StreamingLLM-style sink + windowed KV visibility for the multi-step draft decode path) are supported on the Triton and FlashInfer draft attention backends via KV index clipping, but not on the Ascend (NPU) backend. This PR adds equivalent support for NPU so the flags no longer silently fall back to full-KV draft attention.

## Modifications

Sink+window is implemented as an **attention mask** :

- `spec_utils.py`: add `build_draft_window_mask`, which builds a contiguous KV visibility band `[min(sink, seq_len), max(seq_len - window, s_eff))` per request for each draft-decode step — the mask equivalent of the `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` Triton kernel's visible set (first `sink` tokens + most recent `window` tokens, plus the always-visible per-step draft tree tokens).
- `ascend_backend.py`: resolve the window/sink pair in `AscendAttnMultiStepDraftBackend.__init__` and thread them into every per-step backend; consume the mask in `init_forward_metadata` and `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` via an early exit to `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (BSH layout) before paged attention, since the mask is unsupported by `_npu_paged_attention`.
- MLA / hybrid-SWA drafts are gated off as on CUDA (window/sink reset to 0 with a warning): a draft that already windows itself per layer via its native SWA would be double-windowed by the uniform backend-level mask.
- Tests: new unit test `test/registered/unit/npu/attention/test_npu_draft_window_mask.py` pins the mask semantics against a pure-Python oracle of the kernel's visible-set definition; extend `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_draft_decode_window.py` with backend-wiring checks for the Ascend multi-step backend.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests (all passing):

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_draft_decode_window.py`: 5 passed, including the new Ascend backend wiring checks.
- `test/registered/unit/npu/attention/test_npu_draft_window_mask.py`: mask construction validated against the closed-form visible-set oracle across sink/window/step combinations.

End-to-end on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NEXTN (NPU, TP2, `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, 6 fixed greedy requests):

- Identity-window control (`--speculative-draft-window-size 8192 --speculative-draft-sink-size 0`, mask path active with an empty band): all 6 outputs **byte-identical** to the no-window baseline, including identical per-request accept-length sequences — proving the mask plumbing is lossless.
- Real window (`--speculative-draft-window-size 16 --speculative-draft-sink-size 4`): outputs byte-identical across CUDA-graph and eager modes and across same-config reruns (engine deterministic); `avg_spec_accept_length` 3.04 vs 3.12 baseline (same ballpark — expected to drift slightly as accept-pattern changes alter verify batch shapes).

items.title: [Fix] lora: support PEFT rsLoRA and GDN adapters on Qwen3.5-family hybrid MoE
items.author: philip-pentatonic
items.summary: SGLang can't serve PEFT LoRA adapters that target the Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers of Qwen3.5-family hybrid models (for example and ). There are three separate problems: 1.
items.body:
## Motivation

SGLang can't serve PEFT LoRA adapters that target the Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers of Qwen3.5-family hybrid models (for example `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` and `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`). There are three separate problems:

1. **rsLoRA scaling is ignored.** Adapters trained with `use_rslora=True` are applied at `alpha/r` instead of `alpha/sqrt(r)`. At rank 64 that makes them 8× too weak, and served outputs look close to the base model's.
2. **GDN projections aren't loaded.** The target allowlist omits PEFT's GDN names (`in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `in_proj_a`, `in_proj_b`). PEFT's combined `in_proj_qkv`/`in_proj_z` tensors aren't packed into the runtime `in_proj_qkvz`, and there is no packed target for the gating projections.
3. **Shared-expert-only adapters wrap the routed experts.** An adapter that targets only the dense shared expert still has the routed-expert bank wrapped for LoRA and gets expert LoRA buffers, because both paths use `gate/up/down_proj` names. That allocates unused memory. It also rejects MoE runner backends without routed LoRA support (for example native NVFP4 `flashinfer_cutlass`), even though the adapter never touches the routed experts.

## Modifications

Three commits, each reviewable on its own:

- **`fix(lora): honor rank-stabilized adapter scaling`.** Use `alpha/sqrt(r)` when the PEFT config sets `use_rslora`; ordinary LoRA is unchanged.
- **`fix(lora): load PEFT GDN projections for Qwen3.5 hybrids`.**
  - Normalize and pack combined QKV/Z into `in_proj_qkvz`. PEFT's shared `lora_A` is repeated per Q/K/V rank block.
  - Pack B/A into a new `in_proj_ba` target, in the base layer's order.
  - Add the target names, stacked multipliers and dimensions.
  - Add a synthetic public-model reproducer, `test/manual/lora/repro_qwen35_peft_dense_adapters.py`.
- **`fix(lora): leave untargeted routed experts on the base backend`.**
  - Infer from the initial adapters' tensors whether routed-expert LoRA is needed. When it isn't, leave the routed `FusedMoE` modules unwrapped and skip their LoRA buffers.
  - Starting with no initial adapters keeps the previous behaviour, so dynamic MoE loading still works.
  - Loading routed-expert tensors later into a dense-only pool raises a clear error instead of failing silently.

This adds no quantization kernel and no routed-expert LoRA implementation. The shared expert stays on its dense LoRA path (`--disable-shared-experts-fusion`).

## Accuracy Tests

- **Packing:** unit tests check that packed GDN products equal the original PEFT products, for both QKV/Z and B/A.
- **Synthetic public adapter**, rank 8 and 620 factors, generated from the public config only by the reproducer:
  - On `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` (revision `1355db6a`) with TP=2, all three public prompts change their next-token logprobs against the base.
  - Both TP ranks match all 380 normalized live factors exactly to their expected tensor slices.
  - Dynamic load and unload work.
- **Trained adapter:** a rank-64 rsLoRA adapter trained with PEFT on synthetic data, on attention, GDN and the shared expert. We compared fact recall on 445 held-out questions per adapter, served against local PEFT inference:
  - bf16 (`Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`, TP=2): within ±0.007 for all three adapters tested.
  - NVFP4 with `flashinfer_cutlass` (TP=1 and TP=2, bf16 or fp8_e4m3 KV): 0.007 to 0.025 below local, consistent with quantization.
  - Without these patches, the same adapters can't be loaded, or they recall at base-model level.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel changes. For dense-only adapters, routed experts now skip the LoRA wrapper and buffers, so they run on the unmodified base MoE backend. We haven't benchmarked speed.

## Reproduction

```bash
python test/manual/lora/repro_qwen35_peft_dense_adapters.py \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 --base-model nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --revision 1355db6a052410cfd62085d94b58866fd0f2c3c5 --output-dir /tmp/qwen-dense-lora

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 --revision 1355db6a052410cfd62085d94b58866fd0f2c3c5 \
  --served-model-name qwen --tp-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --enable-lora --lora-backend triton --lora-strict-loading --lora-paths dense-example=/tmp/qwen-dense-lora \
  --max-lora-rank 8 --max-loras-per-batch 2 --max-loaded-loras 2 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000

python test/manual/lora/repro_qwen35_peft_dense_adapters.py --output-dir /tmp/qwen-dense-lora \
  --check-only --already-loaded --check-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --served-model qwen --adapter-name dense-example
```

The adapter is selected as `model=qwen:dense-example`. The random adapter shows the adapter is applied; it says nothing about task quality.

Validated on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) with torch 2.14.1+cu130, transformers 5.19.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GPU runs used the Python radix-tree backend, because the dev container lacked the source checkout's Rust extension.

items.title: [Feat] model-loader: Apply model-owned MTP shard selection to RunAI ModelStreamer
items.author: QwenApp
items.summary: Depends on the model-selection interface introduced in #44702. This single-commit branch includes the shared model hooks and Default Loader changes from that companion PR, plus the RunAI-specific integration and tests.
items.body:
## Motivation

Closes #43196. Depends on the model-selection interface introduced in #44702.

Both PRs target `main`. This single-commit branch includes the shared model hooks and Default Loader changes from that companion PR, plus the RunAI-specific integration and tests. After the companion lands, this branch can be rebased to leave only the RunAI-specific changes.

In two-pass MTP loading, main and draft can share a checkpoint while the draft needs only a small subset of its weights. If RunAI ModelStreamer receives the full file list before model-level filtering, it can read many main-model shards whose tensors the draft will discard, increasing object-storage reads, data processing, and startup cost.

Default Loader and RunAI use different weight iterators, so Default-loader selection does not automatically apply to ModelStreamer. [vLLM #60152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60152) provides model-owned Default shard selection but does not cover RunAI; the corresponding vLLM RunAI integration is [#60759](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60759).

This PR reuses model-owned rules before RunAI starts weight reads. It also provides a shared entry point for cold loading and storage fallback in [ModelExpress #805](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/issues/805), avoiding a second set of model-naming rules in MX or the generic Streamer loader.

## Modifications

1. **Reuse the model-selection interface.** Pass the actual model's `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name)` into RunAI weight preparation, sharing the rule with `load_weights`. This PR adds no model-adapter table.
2. **Select files before constructing the Streamer iterator.** Local checkpoints reuse safetensors-header selection. Object-storage checkpoints use the prepared `model.safetensors.index.json` to map required tensor names to shard URIs, then pass the selected list to `runai_safetensors_weights_iterator`. Selection does not require staging the full checkpoint locally.
3. **Preserve compatibility.** Keep mixed shards, extra files not described by the index, and original ordering. Missing hooks, missing or unusable optional metadata, unsupported name transformations, or an empty selection retain the original file list. Errors from the model rule or weight reading still propagate.
4. **Coordinate distributed selection.** When ranks have identical original ordered file lists, use the existing WORLD CPU communication group to take the union of required files. If any rank requires the full list, keep the full list for the group. If original lists differ, each rank keeps its own list rather than substituting another node's local paths.

This is whole-file selection, not tensor-range reading. Mixed shards may still be read by both main and draft. Weight mapping, quantization, and parameter loading continue to use the existing model logic.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The measurements below were collected before this rebase and have not been rerun on the current head.

### Object-storage RunAI loading

Qwen3.5 MTP 122B, H20×8, TP=8. The baseline and modified configurations used the same node, checkpoint, BF16 compute setting, launch arguments, and resource requests, with `torch.compile`, CUDA Graph, and warmup enabled on both sides. Main and draft loaded object-storage weights through RunAI ModelStreamer.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main shards | 49 | 49 |
| Draft shards | 49 | **1** |
| Main iterator items | 75,881 | 75,881 |
| Draft iterator items | 75,881 | **1,121** |
| TP0 main load | 116.51s | 106.62s |
| TP0 draft load | 130.73s | **9.09s** |
| Engine-reported combined weight load | 247.26s | **115.75s** |
| Engine-container start to Kubernetes Ready | 484s | **351s** |

In this comparison pair, draft loading decreased by **121.64s, approximately 93.0%**, and observed engine startup decreased by **133s**.

Both configurations reached Kubernetes Ready and completed four fixed generation requests, producing 256 completion tokens per configuration.

These are observations from one comparison pair; cache state and object-storage load were not controlled. Shard and iterator-item counts are not measured OSS bytes. Weight-load intervals are included in startup time and should not be added to it. Generation requests are serving-function checks, not accuracy or acceptance-rate evaluations.

### Automated and distributed validation

Regression coverage includes:

- Applying the model rule before constructing the Streamer.
- Selecting shards from local safetensors headers and object-storage indexes.
- Mixed shards, extra files, missing metadata, and no-hook fallback.
- Two-process Gloo coordination of file selection and fallback.
- Real RunAI reads against a local S3 emulator, checking the requested shard files and returned tensor values.

Synthetic-checkpoint I/O and rule-integration tests are reported separately from real-model GPU performance measurements.

## Relationship to Default Loader and MX

#44702 provides the shared model rules and Default Loader integration; this PR applies the same rules to RunAI ModelStreamer.

MX can reuse framework-owned checkpoint selection by calling a SGLang loader entry point that receives the actual main/draft model. Main/draft P2P pairing, NIXL resource management, shared-tensor handling, and publication lifecycle remain MX responsibilities and are outside this PR's scope.

## Accuracy Tests

The generation-request checks described above verify serving behavior, not a full model-quality evaluation. This change does not modify model forward computation.

## Local validation

- Pre-commit on all changed files after rebasing: passed.
- The earlier full-repository pre-commit run passed Python/style/registration checks; the two YAML-based checks passed when rerun in the existing test environment. Rust formatting and Clippy hooks could not run because this macOS environment has no Rust/Cargo toolchain.
- Eight isolated CPU diagnostics passed; these are not a substitute for the registered SGLang runtime tests. The registered RunAI test could not import SGLang locally because Triton is unavailable.
- Full upstream runtime validation requires a maintainer to enable `run-ci`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

items.title: [Feature][KV Offload] Add filesystem I/O deadlines with safe buffer retention
items.author: hongzhi-gao
items.summary: Add opt-in filesystem KV-offload I/O deadlines while retaining primary buffers until physical I/O completion. Implements Item 2 of #54363; related lifecycle work: #61667. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Add opt-in filesystem KV-offload I/O deadlines while retaining primary buffers until physical I/O completion. Implements Item 2 of #54363; related lifecycle work: #61667.

## Claims

- `io_timeout_seconds: float | None = None` uses monotonic submission deadlines and preserves the default behavior.
- Expired loads become misses while their destination slots remain quarantined; expired stores retain their source pins. Late completion releases resources without reporting a second logical result.
- Physical inflight accounting remains valid through cancellation, drain, reset, and shutdown. New promotions/cascades to a tier pause while timed-out I/O remains unfinished.
- FS deadlines do not change object-storage or P2P protocol behavior, file formats, checksums, cleanup, or retry policies.

## Validation

Environment: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu; native `fs_io_C` built from the unchanged source. Both Python fallback and native I/O variants executed.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused FS/tiering/metrics tests | 147 passed |
| Tiering, CPU manager/shared-region, offloading connector regressions | 1264 passed, 3 skipped |
| Same-key recomputation followed by late old I/O | Passed |
| Shutdown negative control using upstream thread pool | Fails as expected; fixed implementation passes |
| Repository pre-commit checks, including Ruff and mypy | Passed |
| GPU serving/model evaluation and serving performance benchmark | Not run; CPU-only environment |

The three skips are the unavailable optional `kvcr` package and two empty worker-backend parameter sets. Event-controlled tests cover deadline equality, completion races, queued cancellation, late physical completion, slot non-reuse, physical inflight counts, and reset/shutdown safety.

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -q

git diff --name-only -z upstream/main...HEAD |
  xargs -0 .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files
```

**Outstanding validation:** the human submitter must run and record serving end-to-end validation and relevant model evaluation before publication, as required by the repository's contribution policy and `/pr-checklist`. CPU lifecycle tests do not establish GPU serving behavior. Update the results above after validation; no performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

A filesystem syscall may block indefinitely while accessing a primary KV buffer. Returning an ordinary failed completion would allow the allocator to reuse that buffer too early. The manager therefore separates one-time logical failure from physical resource release. Promotions detach failed keys but retain the slot IDs; cascades retain read pins. A late result only releases the retained resources. Primary read/write occupancy remains charged throughout retention.

Pool cancellation and worker start share a condition lock. Never-started jobs are canceled through an index and skipped by workers; running jobs remain physically inflight until they return. Completion is acknowledged under the pool lock, so a result published at or after its deadline is conservatively treated as expired. Timeouts are observed at the next manager poll.

Blocked syscalls cannot be forcibly canceled safely. This PR adds no per-block cancellation to either I/O path: running batches may continue, and drain/reset/shutdown can wait indefinitely. Native tests execute real I/O after a controlled delay; they do not emulate an indefinitely stalled NFS/FUSE syscall.

Duplicate check on 2026-10-16, against upstream `642c18d64c`: issue discussion, open issue-reference/area searches and recent merged history found no overlapping FS deadline implementation. #57912 covers checksums and #61780 covers failed-store backpressure. Recheck these searches before submission.

#61667 covers P2P consumer lifetime. This change aligns the small primary quarantine API with that proposal, but shared manager/metrics changes still need reconciliation according to merge order. No P2P transport/session changes are included. The common-layer changes are limited to deadline decisions, buffer ownership and accounting; OBJ deadline integration is deferred.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, independent source review, and local test execution. The human submitter remains responsible for understanding and reviewing every changed line and rerunning relevant tests.

items.title: [Feat] model-loader: Reuse model-owned MTP rules for shard selection
items.author: QwenApp
items.summary: A main model and its MTP draft can share a checkpoint while requiring different weights. Existing model implementations usually filter unused tensors inside, after the Default Loader iterator or prefetcher has started processing files.
items.body:
## Motivation

Closes #43196.

A main model and its MTP draft can share a checkpoint while requiring different weights. Existing model implementations usually filter unused tensors inside `load_weights`, after the Default Loader iterator or prefetcher has started processing files. On whole-file paths, an unnecessary shard may already have been read into memory before the model discards its tensors.

Following [vLLM #60152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60152), this PR extracts existing model-owned selection rules into a reusable interface and excludes wholly unused shards before weight-payload reads and prefetch. This avoids unnecessary reads, memory copies, and tensor iteration.

The same need arose in [ModelExpress #805](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/issues/805). Keeping the rules in SGLang lets native loaders and downstream integrations share one implementation, instead of requiring MX to duplicate architecture-specific checkpoint naming rules and keep them synchronized with upstream changes.

## Modifications

1. **Model-owned weight selection.** Add an optional `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name)` hook. It receives a raw checkpoint tensor name and returns `True` when the model does not use that weight. Pre-read selection and `load_weights` share the same rule, preserving shared weights and pipeline-parallel embedding requirements.
2. **Select files before Default Loader reads.** Pass the rule through `Source.is_unused_weight`, inspect safetensors headers, and retain a shard whenever it contains at least one required tensor. Apply selection before weight iteration and prefetch, preserving the original file order.
3. **Keep actual weight loading unchanged.** Renaming, quantization, fusion, parallel sharding, and parameter assignment remain in the existing model code. The generic loader has no model allowlist and does not assume an `mtp.` prefix.
4. **Preserve compatibility.** Models without the hook, non-safetensors formats, and name transformations that cannot safely map to raw checkpoint names keep their existing loading behavior. If selection rejects every shard, retain the original list so the model's existing missing-weight validation still runs.

Selection is at whole-shard granularity, not tensor-range granularity. Mixed shards containing both main and draft weights can still be selected by both roles.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The measurements below were collected before this rebase and have not been rerun on the current head.

### Default Loader: whole-file reads

H20×8, TP=8, with checkpoints prepared locally. Each model completed one baseline/modified comparison pair with identical launch arguments on both sides, `--weight-loader-disable-mmap`, and two reader threads.

| Model | Load phase | Shards: baseline → this PR | TP0 load time: baseline → this PR |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5 MTP 122B | Main | 49 → 49 | 72.44s → 67.74s |
| Qwen3.5 MTP 122B | Draft | 49 → 1 | **64.32s → 9.58s** |
| GLM-5.3 | Main | 141 → 140 | 353.49s → 350.51s |
| GLM-5.3 | Draft | 141 → 3 | **379.45s → 12.99s** |

In these comparison pairs, draft-load time decreased by **85.1%** for Qwen and **96.6%** for GLM. TP0 logical reads during draft loading decreased from **121.00 GiB to 8.38 GiB** and from **703.75 GiB to 15.00 GiB**, respectively.

Both configurations of both models completed main/draft loading on all eight ranks, passed HTTP health checks, and completed two 32-token generation requests each.

Logical read counts come from process `rchar`, not physical disk or OSS traffic. Host page cache was not cleared for these pairs. These results describe the local whole-file path and should not be interpreted as the benefit of the default mmap path.

### Default Loader: mmap

Qwen3.5 MTP 122B completed **five interleaved comparison pairs** with mmap enabled and checkpoint prefetch disabled. Before each engine launch, only the test-private checkpoint files were evicted from page cache, and `mincore` confirmed zero resident pages. Normal cache reuse between the main and draft loads was preserved.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Draft shards | 49 | 1 |
| TP0 draft-load median | 2.34s | **0.99s** |
| TP0 draft-load range | 2.32–2.38s | 0.95–1.03s |
| Slowest-rank draft-load median | 2.68s | **1.34s** |
| Slowest-rank draft-load range | 2.64–2.73s | 1.30–1.37s |

All ten launches passed health checks and completed two fixed generation requests each. The draft-stage reduction was repeatable; main loading still selected all 49 shards.

Median engine-start-to-HTTP-health time was **265.06s → 268.07s**, so these runs do not establish an overall startup improvement. This interval includes initialization, compilation, and warmup, but excludes checkpoint preparation.

### Regression coverage

Regression coverage includes real safetensors files, selection before iterator/prefetch construction, mixed shards, shared weights, pipeline-parallel embeddings, layer-selection rules, and fallback for incompatible name transformations. Generation requests are serving-function checks, not model-accuracy evaluations.

## Scope and downstream reuse

This PR provides the model-selection interface and Default Loader integration. A companion PR applies the same interface to the separate RunAI ModelStreamer path. The reference vLLM #60152 does not cover RunAI; the corresponding vLLM RunAI integration is [#60759](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60759).

This PR does not change model execution, scheduling, RunAI internals, or MX P2P. It also does not change Hugging Face downloads that happen before local file resolution. MX can reuse this optimization through a framework loader entry point that passes the actual model and its selection rule, without maintaining separate checkpoint-naming rules.

## Accuracy Tests

The generation-request checks described above verify serving behavior, not a full model-quality evaluation. This change does not modify model forward computation.

## Local validation

- Pre-commit on all changed files after rebasing: passed.
- The earlier full-repository pre-commit run passed Python/style/registration checks; the two YAML-based checks passed when rerun in the existing test environment. Rust formatting and Clippy hooks could not run because this macOS environment has no Rust/Cargo toolchain.
- Eight isolated CPU diagnostics passed; these are not a substitute for the registered SGLang runtime tests. Importing the SGLang runtime locally is blocked by the unavailable Triton dependency.
- Full upstream runtime validation requires a maintainer to enable `run-ci`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Feature][LoRA][MoE] Expert LoRA for FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4 experts
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Add expert LoRA to the fused FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE kernel for MXFP4 expert weights with BF16 activations (, next to ). TP > 1 relies on #61235 (merged). [Discussion: ✅ Triggered for commit.]
items.body:
## Overview

Add expert LoRA to the fused FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE kernel for MXFP4 expert weights with BF16 activations (`TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts`, next to `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`). TP > 1 relies on #61235 (merged).

## Claims

- MXFP4 MoE models can serve expert LoRA adapters on `moe_backend="flashinfer_trtllm"` instead of falling back to Marlin / unfused Triton.
- Opt-in: `moe_backend="auto"` selects the same backend as before. `flashinfer_trtllm_afp8` (MXFP8 activations) with expert LoRA is rejected with an explicit reason.
- Requires FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 (`gemm1_lora_delta` on `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3987); vLLM pins 0.7.2.

## Validation

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly arm64 image built from `af7f9488c` (flashinfer-python 0.7.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130), NVIDIA GB300, with the changed files of this PR and #61235 backported onto that commit and mounted over the image. Not run on the PR base itself; the changed files apply to it without conflicts.

**Kernel-level** — `pytest tests/lora/test_trtllm_mxfp4_lora_moe.py -v`: 9 passed. Random MXFP4 weights through vLLM's TRTLLM weight conversion, float64 reference from the dequantized weights, with and without an FC1/FC2 bias:

- delta in `[up | gate]` order: output and FC1 activation within 2% relative error of the reference; the swapped order is off by more than 30%;
- zero delta vs. the non-LoRA path: within 2%;
- the four incoming delta layouts are converted exactly;
- oracle: unchanged without LoRA, `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` first with LoRA + BF16 activations, explicit error with MXFP8 activations.

**End-to-end** — `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, offline `LLM`, `enable_lora=True`, fixed-token logprobs (`prompt_logprobs`) of 16 prompts x 200 tokens. Adapters are seeded random expert-only LoRAs (rank 8, alpha 32, only `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` nonzero; B std 0.01 = small, 0.05 = large). Reference: `moe_backend="triton_unfused"`, TP 1. On the reference the adapters move the logprobs by 0.53 (small) and 1.89 (large) mean abs. "Effect" is adapter minus base logprob per token; projection is `<new, ref> / <ref, ref>`.

| backend | TP | set | MAE vs ref | median abs | effect projection | effect correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 1 | base | 0.136 | 0.038 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.132 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.963 | 0.629 | 0.84 | 0.79 |
| `marlin` | 1 | base | 0.126 | 0.040 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.137 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.973 | 0.621 | 0.82 | 0.79 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 2 | base | 0.149 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.146 | 0.051 | 0.74 | 0.81 |
| | 2 | large | 1.023 | 0.665 | 0.81 | 0.76 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm`, without #61235 | 2 | small | 0.472 | 0.232 | 0.33 | 0.42 |
| | 2 | large | 1.703 | 1.193 | 0.54 | 0.49 |
| `triton_unfused` | 2 | base | 0.137 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.144 | 0.051 | 0.80 | 0.84 |
| | 2 | large | 0.993 | 0.619 | 0.83 | 0.79 |

The base rows are the floor between two backends or TP sizes on this text (same size for Marlin and for Triton at TP 2 against Triton at TP 1; the mean is tail-heavy, see the median). With the small adapter the new backend stays on that floor; with either adapter it tracks the reference as closely as Marlin does. At TP 2 it needs #61235 (now on main). The large adapter breaks the model (mean logprob -4.6) and is only there to make the direction of the effect visible. Repeating a request gives identical logprobs on `flashinfer_trtllm` at TP 1 (Marlin: 0.07 MAE between two passes). One run per configuration.

**Throughput** — same model, TP 1, 64 concurrent requests, 256 output tokens each, output tokens/s (second of two passes):

| backend | base requests | with expert LoRA |
|---|---|---|
| `triton_unfused` | 5828 | 4593 |
| `marlin` | 10510 | 7047 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 13388 | 7699 |

Supplementary, on a 384-expert, top-6 MXFP4 MoE at TP 4 (prototype of this change on an older base, 128 requests of ~3.3k output tokens): with an expert adapter 1.5-1.65x the throughput of `triton_unfused` and 1.02-1.16x Marlin; base requests 2.5-2.7x `triton_unfused`.

Not validated: EP, `fully_sharded_loras`, per-expert (2D) adapters end-to-end, more than one loaded adapter, CUDA graph specialization per LoRA, GPT-OSS at TP 4 / 8. `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed files.

## Details

Design. `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` subclasses `_TrtLlmLoRAExpertsBase` and reuses its flow unchanged: the gate/up delta is computed by punica and passed as `gemm1_lora_delta`, so the kernel adds it before the activation; the down delta is computed from the post-activation FC1 output the kernel returns, and the base finalize and the delta reduction happen in one FP32 pass. Kernel arguments (`gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`, unpadded hidden size) come from the existing `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsBase`.

Three things differ from the BF16 class, each behind the new `prepare_gemm1_lora_delta` hook or a small base change:

- FC1 bias. The kernel has one FC1 bias slot, used either by the static `gemm1_bias` or by the per-token delta. On the LoRA path the static bias (GPT-OSS has one) is un-shuffled to logical order and added to the delta; `gemm1_bias` is then not passed. The sum is rounded to BF16, the dtype the kernel takes for the delta.
- Delta layout. The kernel takes `[up | gate]` halves. Per-expert adapters already arrive that way (or as interleaved pairs for `SWIGLUOAI`); fused 3D adapters arrive in checkpoint row order. All four cases are converted.
- Hidden padding. MXFP4 TRTLLM pads the hidden size (2880 -> 3072 for GPT-OSS) and returns an unpadded output, so the shared finalize now writes `output.size(1)` columns instead of the padded width. No change for the BF16 class, where the two are equal. The modular kernel also sized its output from the padded input and asserted on the narrower result in the no-op finalize; it now asks the experts for the output hidden size (`FusedMoEExpertsModular.output_hidden_dim`, default: the input size; the TRTLLM MXFP4 experts return the unpadded size) and allocates `output` at that width up front, so the result is used without a copy on a single rank. This also applies to the non-LoRA `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`. This was found by the end-to-end run, not by the kernel tests.

MXFP8 activations are not supported because the kernel then returns the FC1 activation as uint8 without block scales (observed with FlashInfer 0.6.18), so the down delta cannot be computed.

Limitations.

- DP is rejected (explicit `flashinfer_trtllm` + LoRA + DP raises, as before this PR): the inherited no-LoRA fast path reads the local batch's adapter flag, while under DP the experts see the gathered batch. `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts` has the same gap; left for a separate fix.
- Top-1 routing with the weight applied on the input double-weights through the shared LoRA base (also `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`); fixed separately in #62019.
- The kernel tests need SM100, so the H200/L4 LoRA CI shards skip them; they were run on GB300 only.
- Not chunked, like `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`: the LoRA token mapping covers the whole batch. The TRTLLM-Gen grid limits one call to about `(65535 - num_experts) * 8 / top_k` tokens (~130k for GPT-OSS).
- `SITU` activation is not enabled for the LoRA class (untested).
- With a static FC1 bias, a delta far below the BF16 step of the bias is rounded away.

Related work, not duplicated: #47226 adds FlashInfer MoE LoRA for FP8 / MXFP8 / MxInt4 (not MXFP4, not updated since July) and uses the same opt-in rule; #34421 routes NVFP4 LoRA to Marlin; #61164 and #61165 fix other parts of the MoE LoRA path and do not overlap.

items.title: [Fix] deterministic: Disable mixed chunked prefill
items.author: aarnetalman
items.summary: Deterministic inference promises the same output for a request whatever else is in the batch, but breaks that. With it, the scheduler can put a prefill chunk and decode tokens into one batch, and the whole batch runs the prefill (extend) attention path.
items.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference promises the same output for a request whatever else is in the batch, but `--enable-mixed-chunk` breaks that. With it, the scheduler can put a prefill chunk and decode tokens into one batch, and the whole batch runs the prefill (extend) attention path. So a decode token's result depends on whether a prefill happened to share its step:
- the extend and decode kernels reduce in different orders, so they give slightly different results for the same tokens (the prefill vs decode difference that `test_deterministic --test-mode p_vs_d` measures);
- with per-phase backends (`--prefill-attention-backend` / `--decode-attention-backend`), they can even be different backends.

Mixed chunked prefill is off by default, so this only bites users who turn it on together with `--enable-deterministic-inference`. Found in the review of #44489 (AITER decode attention in deterministic mode), where a mixed batch would run its decode tokens on the prefill backend.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/attention_hook.py` (`handle_deterministic_inference`): in deterministic mode, `--enable-mixed-chunk` is switched off with a warning, as deterministic mode already does for `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`.
- `test_model_overrides.py`: deterministic mode resolves `enable_mixed_chunk` to `False`; without it, the flag is kept.
- Unchanged: deterministic mode off; deterministic mode without `--enable-mixed-chunk`.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, Qwen3-8B TP1. Deterministic mode with Triton attention and `--enable-mixed-chunk`, with the open fixes #43788 and #34543 applied (deterministic mode on MI350X needs them):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference --enable-mixed-chunk
```

`python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode {single,prefix,radix_cache} --n-trials 50`, `--test-mode prefix --return-logprob`, and a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses; token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response), each on a fresh server:

| | single | prefix (4 prompts) | prefix logprobs | radix_cache | bitwise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before (`enable_mixed_chunk: True`) | 1 output | 1, **2**, 1, 1 outputs | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| after (server logs "Disable --enable-mixed-chunk because deterministic inference is enabled.", `enable_mixed_chunk: False`) | 1 output | 1, 1, 1, 1 | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |

Before, the 511-character prompt of `prefix` mode, sent with other prompts of different lengths, produced two different outputs across 293 samples: its decode steps sometimes shared a batch with a prefill chunk. `single` and the bitwise check send one prompt per batch, so nothing is mixed there.

Unit tests, `python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py -k deterministic` (same image): before, the new test fails (1 failed, 3 passed); after, 4 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change without `--enable-mixed-chunk`. With it, deterministic mode now runs without mixed batches, as when the flag is not given.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

discussion: Not a stopper, but why a warning instead of raising error?

> Not a stopper, but why a warning instead of raising error?

Thanks, good question. I followed what deterministic mode already does with options it can't honour: in the same function, `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` is switched off with a warning, and the dLLM and UNO paths switch `--enable-mixed-chunk` off the same way. Mixed chunking only changes how prefill and decode are scheduled, not which kernels compute the results, so deterministic mode can still give the user what they asked for without it. That's different from the attention-backend and RCCL checks, which raise because there's no safe substitute to pick for the user.

items.summary: returns HTTP 400 when the scheduler reports failure, but its response body still says the storage backend was cleared. For example, this happens when neither hierarchical cache nor LMCache is enabled. [Discussion: This small fix is ready for review.]

## Motivation

`POST /hicache/storage-backend/clear` returns HTTP 400 when the scheduler reports failure, but its response body still says the storage backend was cleared. For example, this happens when neither hierarchical cache nor LMCache is enabled.

items.title: [AMD] Use aiter pa_prefill_sparse for unified-KV sparse prefill on gfx1250
items.author: kawhil-amd
items.summary: On gfx1250, the DSV4 unified-KV path already dispatches sparse decode to aiter, but sparse prefill still falls back to SGLang's, because the aiter OPUS prefill is gfx950-only. aiter ships a gfx1250 Gluon with exactly the same signature (two sources:…
items.body:
## Motivation

On gfx1250 , the DSV4 unified-KV path (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`) already dispatches sparse **decode** to aiter `pa_decode_sparse`, but sparse **prefill** still falls back to SGLang's `_sparse_attn_v4_paged_prefill_triton`, because the aiter OPUS prefill (`_HAS_OPUS`) is gfx950-only. aiter ships a gfx1250 Gluon `pa_prefill_sparse` with exactly the same signature (two sources: prefix + extend, attention sink), so it can be used directly.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_prefill.py`:
  - Import `aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_prefill_sparse.pa_prefill_sparse` when available; enabled only on gfx1250 (`_HAS_AITER_GFX1250`).
  - In `sparse_attn_v4_paged_prefill`, after the OPUS branch, call `pa_prefill_sparse(...)` when `q`, `unified_kv` and `kv` share a bf16/fp16 dtype; otherwise keep the Triton fallback.
  - Opt-out via `SGLANG_DSV4_AITER_SPARSE_PREFILL=0` (default on).

## Accuracy

Kernel-level, DSV4-Pro shapes (H=128, D=512, topk=1024, SWA=128, bf16, 300k-page pool), aiter vs SGLang Triton:

| T | max_abs | max_rel | cosine |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 1.95e-3 | 3.7e-3 | 0.999995 |
| 4096 | 3.91e-3 | 3.8e-3 | 0.999995 |

End-to-end (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 4x MI455, TP4/DP4/EP4 + DP attention): needle-in-haystack PASS at 19.5k / 65k / 325k tokens.
