items.title: [Fix] hicache: Ignore stale prefetch queries after reissue
items.author: lhzds
items.summary: In mode, a storage prefetch can be cancelled and reissued with the same while the original query is still in flight. The hit-queue drain looks up the current prefetch by handle, so processing the terminated old operation revokes the replacement and removes its…
items.body:
## Motivation

In `buffer_only` mode, a storage prefetch can be cancelled and reissued with the same `CacheRequestHandle` while the original query is still in flight. The hit-queue drain looks up the current prefetch by handle, so processing the terminated old operation revokes the replacement and removes its prefix context. The same problem occurs when an old hit remains queued for allocation after cancellation.

## Modifications

- Require `info.operation is operation` before updating the current prefetch from a query result or retrying a queued allocation. Storage-belief updates still run when consuming the synchronized query result, before this check.
- Add regressions for late misses, late hits, and queued hits consumed after cancellation and reissue. Check that the replacement and its prefix context survive, and that its own query result is still processed.

## Verification

CPU unit tests on two Linux hosts, each using Python 3.11 and PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_buffer_mode_sidecar.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_pp_prefetch_ticket.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_hicache_transfer_lifecycle.py
```

Both hosts: **41 passed, 22 subtests passed**. Running the new regressions with `UnifiedRadixCache` from `dfc89580f1225d2806f7d60ed105761cc5aff067` fails in all three scenarios: the replacement has been removed from `ongoing_prefetch`.

The new tests use fixture-backed cache state and the actual prefetch lifecycle methods. No model inference or accelerator transfer was exercised.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the repository's pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add regression tests to the registered CPU unit suite.
- [x] Follow the repository's code style.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.

items.title: [Model] Add Reflection Beam
items.author: WoosukKwon
items.summary: Add day-0 support for Reflection's Beam-1.0, a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, and its DFlash2 drafter. [Discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--61978.org.readthedocs.build/en/61978/]
items.body:
## Overview

Add day-0 support for Reflection's Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`), a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, and its DFlash2 drafter.

**Depends on FlashInfer nightly.**

## Claims

- **Model support:** reasoning, tool calling and structured outputs, with tensor, data or expert parallelism. Architecture:
  - hybrid sliding-window (RoPE) and full-attention NoPE layers with SSMax;
  - per-head Q/K norm and a sigmoid output gate;
  - DeepSeek-V3-style MoE with an FP32 router;
  - sandwich norms and depth-scaled residuals.
- **Parsers:** `--reasoning-parser beam --tool-call-parser beam` read the response template that ships with the checkpoint. Every response is constrained to that template by default; `VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT=0` turns this off.
- **Fused kernels for Blackwell:** compared with the first implementation, TP8 batch-1 decode goes from 8.95 ms to 3.30 ms per step (2.71×), and an 8 × 2K prefill from 328 ms to 176 ms (1.87×).
- **Attention DP + MegaMoE:** `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` with DP4 and expert parallelism reaches 1.71× TP4's peak prefill throughput.
- **DFlash2 speculative decoding:** works with FP8 KV cache and adaptive verification.

## Validation

**Serving:** Beam-1.0 NVFP4 + DFlash2 (7 draft tokens), TP8 on GB200, SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k` low-entropy subset, greedy decoding:

| Concurrency | Fixed draft (tok/s) | Adaptive (tok/s) | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 708 | 707 | 3.71 → 3.61 |
| 128 | 15,012 | 16,632 | 3.68 → 3.23 |

**Prefill**, 4×GB300, 32K input / 1 output token:

| Configuration | Peak input throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|
| Attention DP + MegaMoE | 168.8K |
| TP4 | 98.7K |

```bash
vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --reasoning-parser beam --tool-call-parser beam --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER"}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep scheduling running requests after a priority self-preemption
items.author: apex-mochen
items.summary: Fixes priority-scheduler self-preemption bug that incorrectly broke out of the scheduling loop, starving higher-priority requests after a KV-block failure.
items.body:
## Purpose

Under `--scheduling-policy priority`, when a running request cannot get KV blocks the scheduler preempts the lowest-priority running request. `self.running` is in admission order, not priority order, so that request can sit in the middle of the list, for example when higher-priority requests arrived after it. If it is the request currently being scheduled, it preempts itself, and the running loop then `break`s:

```python
if new_blocks is None:
    # Cannot schedule this request.
    break
```

Every running request after it gets no tokens in that step, even though they all have higher priority, the self-preemption just freed blocks, and budget remains. This is a priority inversion: the requests the policy is meant to protect lose a step whenever a lower-priority request ahead of them runs out of KV.

After a self-preemption the request has already been removed from `self.running` (`del self.running[victim_index]` with `victim_index == req_index`), so `req_index` already points at the next request. The fix continues the loop in that case. Nothing changes for FCFS: it preempts `running[-1]`, so a self-preemption there only happens on the last request. Other reasons for a failed allocation (a deferred free that will not help, pending connector frees) still end the loop.

Related but different: #49097 (fixed by #49206) adjusted `req_index` when the victim sits before the cursor. #39375, a larger rework of this preemption path that has been open since March, would also remove this `break`.

## Test Plan

- New `test_priority_self_preemption_keeps_scheduling_later_running_requests`. Setup: one free block, `running = [A(p0), B(p5), C(p0)]`; A and B both need a new block on the same decode step, C does not. A takes the block, B preempts itself, and C must still be scheduled.
- `tests/v1/core` in full, main vs this PR.
- A random-workload stall check on the real `Scheduler` (small per-step budgets, priority/FCFS mixed, hybrid attention+Mamba and full-attention layouts, 40 seeds each). It flags a running request that gets 0 tokens while the step has budget left for its whole remainder; this is how I found it.

## Test Result

(CPU only.)

- New test: fails on main (`{'A': 1}` scheduled, C skipped), passes with this PR.
- `tests/v1/core` in full: same failed/errored set on main `fa75d3456d` and on this PR (68 environment failures on both trees, e.g. missing `torchvision` and offline model configs); 0 failures only on this PR; 953 → 954 passed (the new test).
- Stall check, hybrid layout: main stalls on 1/40 seeds (this bug), this PR on 0/40. Full-attention layout: 0/40 on both, with identical per-run action counts. A KV-content check over 60 more seeds on this PR found nothing.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

AI-assisted (Claude Code). I reviewed the change and ran the tests listed above myself.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
discussion:
Hi @yewentao256 — would you be able to take a look at this when you have a moment? You merged #58259 in this part of the scheduler recently, so I thought you might be a good fit.

Under `--scheduling-policy priority`, when the request being scheduled is the lowest-priority running request and cannot get KV blocks, it preempts itself, and the running loop then `break`s. Since `running` is in admission order, higher-priority requests that arrived later sit behind it and get no tokens that step, even when they need no new blocks and budget remains.

The fix is to `continue` instead of `break` after a priority self-preemption; `req_index` already points at the next request because the preempted one was removed from `running`. FCFS and the other allocation-failure paths are unchanged. Verification on `fd33f32468`: the new test fails on main and passes here; `tests/v1/core` has the same failure set as main (+1 pass). A random-workload stall check went from 1/40 stalled seeds on main to 0/40.

One review focus: I limited the `continue` to the PRIORITY self-preemption case and kept `break` for the other ways the allocation can fail (deferred frees, pending connector frees). Happy to adjust if you'd prefer it broader.

items.title: [Feature][KV Connector][Mooncake] Add MooncakePullConnector for decode-side reads
items.author: CAICAIIs
items.summary: Adds, a READ-mode sibling of: the decoder reads the prefiller's KV cache over the Mooncake TransferEngine, instead of the prefiller writing into the decoder's registered memory. Registered under its own name; keeps its wire format, metadata and behavior.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `MooncakePullConnector`, a READ-mode sibling of `MooncakeConnector`: the decoder reads the prefiller's KV cache over the Mooncake TransferEngine, instead of the prefiller writing into the decoder's registered memory. Registered under its own name; `MooncakeConnector` keeps its wire format, metadata and behavior.

Part of the Mooncake connector roadmap in [#60523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523) (Phase 2, first item).

## Claims

- **New connector, decoder-side READ transfers.** The prefiller holds its KV blocks, publishes its address book and block ids, and releases a request once every reader reports the read as finished; the decoder issues `batch_transfer_sync_read` at its own scheduling pace. `--kv-connector MooncakePullConnector` on both sides with the existing proxy and `kv_transfer_config` fields; `KV_CONNECTOR=MooncakePullConnector` selects it in the example script.
- **KV layout on the handshake, not on every batch.** The decoder fetches each peer worker's layout once and caches it (keyed by a `layout_id`, so a restarted peer is detected and re-fetched). Per-request messages carry block ids only. With 146 registered regions and a batch of 8 requests × 4 blocks, the pull request payload is 309 B against 7297 B for the push handshake payload (7164 B of which is the address book).
- **Compatibility-hash isolation.** Both sides hash model, dtype, KV heads/head size/layers, KV cache dtype, attention backend, HMA, EAGLE/MTP configuration, connector version and transfer mode, and compare digests during the handshake. TP size, block size and KV cache layout stay out of the hash and are validated against the peer's address book instead, so heterogeneous TP keeps working. A mismatched pair fails the request with a message naming the reason.
- **Push path unchanged.** `MooncakeXferMetadata`, `MooncakeXferResponse` and the send logic are untouched; the existing connector only gains the seams both modes share (`_handle_side_channel_message`, `_send_side_channel_error`, `_send_idle`), the connector name in its bootstrap registration, and an aborted-transfer event that its own path ignores.

## Validation

Unit tests, on the commit in this PR:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_pull_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
# 185 passed
```

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_pull_connector.py` runs two workers against each other over the real ZMQ side channel and the bootstrap server, with the transfer engine replaced by a byte-copying engine that keeps the memory-registration table, so a descriptor pointing outside registered memory fails the test. It covers: byte-for-byte reads, the address book being fetched once per peer and a restarted peer being re-fetched, heterogeneous TP (one decoder rank reading two prefiller ranks), release on a decoder-side prefix hit, request failure on an incompatible peer (compatibility hash, block size, connector mode), reader failure and abort releasing the prefiller's blocks, and prefiller timeout failing the reader.

End-to-end serving on an 8×H20 node with a same-host P/D pair over RDMA (both sides log `The Mooncake Transfer Engine is using rdma as its protocol`), driven through the example proxy with three greedy prompts, each completion compared character by character:

| Model | pull vs. non-disaggregated | push vs. non-disaggregated | pull vs. push |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dense 0.5B | identical | identical | identical |
| hybrid 2B | identical | identical | identical |

The worker logs show which side moves the bytes. In pull mode the decoder reads and the prefiller only serves metadata:

```text
# decoder, pull mode
DEBUG mooncake_pull_connector.py:725]  Reading kv_caches for {'cmpl-...'} from producer worker tcp://172.31.32.3:39029
DEBUG transfer_plan.py:270]            Reading kv_caches for request cmpl-... (9 blocks) from <engine> tp0 pp0
DEBUG mooncake_pull_connector.py:1098] Reading from 172.31.32.3:15108 done, took 0.00666

# prefiller, push mode (same instrumentation, same run shape)
DEBUG mooncake_connector.py:2058]      Sending to 172.31.32.3:16093 done, took 0.00833
```

Three prompts read 9, 9 and 3 blocks for the dense model (6.7 ms, 0.2 ms, 0.15 ms) and 4, 4 and 4 blocks for the hybrid model (7.1 ms, 1.0 ms, 1.0 ms); the decoder log has no error line. The pull-mode prefiller log has no transfer line at all, while the push-mode prefiller logs one write per prompt.

## Details

**Protocol.** The decoder sends `MooncakePullRequest` (protocol marker, compatibility hash, reader identity, `{request id: (transfer id, needs bytes)}`, and whether it wants the layout), the prefiller answers with `MooncakePullResponse` (layout and/or producer block ids per request, or an error), the decoder reads the blocks, then reports `MooncakePullDone` and waits for `MooncakePullAck`. Blocks are held by the prefiller from the moment it hands out block ids until every expected reader reports in; the expected reader count comes from the same `TransferTopology` rules the push connector uses for its TP/PP fan-out, and a request that no reader takes is released after `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.

**Read planning.** `mooncake/transfer_plan.py` plans reads with the same registered regions and the same per-region arithmetic as the push path, with the two sides swapped: the prefiller's blocks become the remote descriptors and the decoder's blocks the local ones. Region alignment, asymmetric-TP validation and head-resharding checks reuse the helpers in `mooncake_connector.py`.

**Failure handling.** Reads and planning failures go through the connector's existing failure path (`_handle_failed_recv`, `get_block_ids_with_load_errors`), so the scheduler recomputes or fails the request according to `kv_load_failure_policy`, and the prefiller releases the blocks of a failed read. A prefiller that drops a request (abort, or its own expiry) sets the new `aborted` event so a waiting reader fails immediately instead of waiting for its own timeout.

**Mixed pairs.** A decoder that runs the pull connector and finds a prefiller registered as `MooncakeConnector` (or as nothing at all, since an unset name means a prefiller that predates connector names) fails the request at discovery with a message naming both connectors. The bootstrap server refuses to register two different connector names under one `dp_rank`.

**Not included, tracked elsewhere in [#60523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523):** layerwise transfer overlap (Phase 4, owned by another contributor), DCP/PCP and the wider heterogeneous-TP work (Phase 3), and de-HTTP-izing bootstrap (Phase 2 evaluation item). `kv_both` inherits the push scheduler's existing role semantics and is not exercised by tests.

**Why this is not a duplicate:** no open or merged PR adds a pull connector for the Mooncake P2P path (checked by name and by search); the closest open work fixes failure reporting on the existing push connector, which this connector already routes through. Sending the KV layout once per peer for the push handshake already landed on `main`; this change applies the same idea in the read direction rather than reworking that path.

**Validation limit:** the Mooncake transfer engine is not available in CI, so the connector's unit tests use the byte-copying engine described above and require GPU/RDMA validation outside CI.

items.title: [Bugfix] Preserve batch audio handler error status codes
items.author: bzsuni
items.summary: Fixes vllm run-batch incorrectly mapping audio handler errors to 400 instead of preserving 500/503 status codes from engine failures and retryable errors.
items.body:
## Overview

Fix `vllm run-batch` incorrectly reporting audio handler failures with status 400. Preserve the standard error mapping for transcription and translation requests, including 500 for engine failures and 503 for retryable errors.

## Claims

- Map audio handler exceptions through the existing batch error handling.
- Preserve status 400 for audio download and request preparation failures.
- Keep successful responses and handler-returned errors unchanged.

## Validation

Added a parameterized regression test covering transcription and translation with engine, retryable, and validation errors.

- Before: all four 500/503 cases failed; both 400 cases passed.
- After: **26 selected tests passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff and mypy.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py \
  -k 'batch_audio or download_bytes or transcription_wrapper or upload_data' -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/launchers/run_batch.py \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py
```

## Details

`make_transcription_wrapper` previously caught both request preparation and handler exceptions, converting all failures to status 400.

Move the handler call outside the preparation `try/except` so `run_request` applies the existing exception mapping. Audio download and request preparation errors retain their previous behavior.

items.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share MegaAttn int32 positions across layers
items.author: Juntian777
items.summary: MegaAttn converts the same RoPE positions from int64 to int32 in every layer. In a full CUDA graph those casts are separate GPU kernels: 40 per target forward on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
items.body:
## Overview

MegaAttn converts the same RoPE positions from int64 to int32 in every layer. In a full CUDA graph those casts are separate GPU kernels: 40 per target forward on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Share the converted tensor within the forward context so the graph records one cast.

## Claims

- Removes 39 redundant cast kernels per 40-layer target forward.
- Target GPU time drops from 17.903 to 17.834 ms (0.39%) in the DEP8 decode measurement below.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8 x GB300 across two nodes, DP8 x TP1 + EP, 64 requests/rank, 131,072 input tokens, 2,048 output tokens, attention top-k 1024, DSpark with 5 draft tokens (384 target tokens/rank). FlashMLA built with CUDA 13.4, MegaMoE, Engram on GPU, full decode CUDA graphs. Both runs restore and freeze the same EPLB mapping.

| Target forward | Before | Shared positions |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU time, median (ms) | 17.903 | 17.834 |
| GPU time, p10 / p90 (ms) | 17.847 / 17.996 | 17.793 / 17.941 |
| Full-batch samples | 366 | 342 |
| Kernels in the captured forward | 766 | 727 |

One run per version on a development tree, using real weights and synthetic KV through `DecodeBenchConnector`. Times are CUDA events around the target graph, without the profiler, taking the slowest of eight ranks for each step and discarding the first ten full-batch steps. Kernel counts come from a separate CUDA-only trace. This measures GPU target time, not request latency or serving throughput.

The measurements used the equivalent helper implementation; the final diff inlines it. The final `forward_mqa` was checked locally on GB300 with a copy consumer: 40 uses share one converted buffer during full capture, offset views stay distinct, replays see updated positions, independent captures do not reuse another graph's cast, and separate piecewise graphs sharing a context remain correct. NONE, FULL and PIECEWISE cases pass. These local checks are not added to the PR.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py
```

Existing layout suite on the development tree: 7 passed. Pre-commit, including Ruff, formatting and mypy: passed. No accuracy evaluation was run; the integer conversion is unchanged. The capture checks above were run outside CI.

## Details

The cache is keyed by the input tensor and scoped to `ForwardContext`. The cast still executes on every graph replay. Eager execution and PIECEWISE capture keep their per-call conversion, since separate piecewise graphs must own their buffers. Check actual stream capture as well as runtime mode: MRV2's full capture can run with mode NONE.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `mega attention positions`, `positions int32`, `mega_attn_positions_int32`, and `MegaAttention reuse`. #60613 fixes a prefill index sentinel; #60543 autotunes the indexer GEMM. Neither shares the RoPE position conversion. No linked issue.

items.title: [Perf] Fix watermark redaction walking every token id in request logging
items.author: JustinTong0323
items.summary: Both and redact the whole request object before truncation and before filtering, so every call walks the full element by element (~0.5us/token). With long prompts this costs tens of ms per log call on the tokenizer-manager event loop, on receive and again on f…
items.body:
## Motivation

#37577 (Aaronson-Gumbel text watermarking) added `redact_watermark_secrets` to the request-log formatters. Both `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` and `_transform_data_for_logging` redact the whole request object **before** truncation and **before** `skip_names` filtering, so every `--log-requests` call walks the full `input_ids` element by element (~0.5us/token). With long prompts this costs tens of ms per log call on the tokenizer-manager event loop, on receive and again on finish, and shows up directly in TTFT.

On main, formatting an 80k-token `GenerateReqInput` at `--log-requests-level 2` costs ~62 ms (text) / ~61 ms (json); with this PR it is ~1 ms.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/utils/request_logger.py`:

- New `_redact_field`: redact by field/key name. Fields named `watermark_key` / `watermark_key_b` / `watermark_config` become `<redacted>`; `watermark` / `sampling_params` / `preferred_sampling_params` are redacted recursively; everything else passes through untouched. `skip_names` fields are dropped before redaction.
- The truncated-list branch of `_transform_data_for_logging` now redacts the printed head/tail halves, matching `_dataclass_to_string_truncated`.

`python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking/core.py`:

- The watermark field-name sets are now module-level `WATERMARK_SECRET_FIELD_NAMES` / `WATERMARK_CONTAINER_FIELD_NAMES`, shared by all redact branches and the logger instead of being re-listed in five places.
- New scalar fast-path: a list/tuple with no dict/list/tuple/Struct/dataclass element cannot hold a secret (secrets only sit under dict keys or struct/dataclass fields), so it returns the input unchanged. This bounds every caller — including the `dump_requests` / crash-dump path in `tokenizer_manager.py`, which redacts full request tuples synchronously on the event loop, and batched requests whose `input_ids` is a list-of-lists with a short outer list.

Log output is unchanged at every `--log-requests-level`.

## Accuracy Tests

Logging-only change; no model path touched.

New `test/registered/unit/utils/test_request_logger_redaction.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):

- Secrets are redacted in both formatters, for 16 and 100k input ids.
- Truncated lists keep their printed halves redacted.
- The redaction walk is bounded at each level's real `(max_length, skip_names)` — this test fails on main.
- Scalar sequences are returned by identity while containers are still redacted.

Output equivalence vs main was checked with both formatters over 20 payload shapes (levels 0-3 metadata, nested secrets, long secret-bearing lists, batched `input_ids`, finish `out` dicts, tuples, None secrets, unicode text): byte-identical in all 40 runs, no secret string in any output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CPU, single thread, one formatter call on an 80k-token request carrying a watermark config:

| case | main (ms) | PR (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| level 2, text | 62.5 | 1.1 |
| level 2, json | 61.2 | 1.0 |
| level 1, text | 58.8 | 0.05 |
| level 3, text (prints every id) | 128.1 | 43.3 |
| batched 32x4k `input_ids`, level 2 | 219.7 | 69.4 |
| crash-dump-shaped redact (80k prompt + 20k `output_ids`) | 15.1 | 8.8 |

Level 3 and batched requests remain dominated by `str()` of the ids they print; the redaction walk on top is now a flat scan instead of a full recursion.

Related: #44683 fixes the same logger path with a different split (it skips the walk only for `skip_names` fields and long non-watermark lists). This PR redacts strictly by field name and additionally bounds the other `redact_watermark_secrets` callers via the core fast-path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A, no user-facing change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Fix] DeepSeek-V4.1: keep the mHC next-layer link out of the module tree
items.author: guapisolo
items.summary: Keep DeepSeek-V4.1 weight updates from missing layers 1+ after links decoder layers.
items.body:
## Summary
Keep DeepSeek-V4.1 weight updates from missing layers 1+ after `bind_next` links decoder layers.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** in radixark/miles CI on SGLang `v0.5.22` (`993bf90200`), check `stage-c-8-gpu-h200 (0) / run` ([job 116833022894](https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/38851892750/job/116833022894), attempt 1), `test_deepseek_v4_1_4layer_ci.py` crashed the scheduler on its first weight update after logging `model.layers.1.mlp.gate.weight not found in params_dict`, with `KeyError: 'model.layers.1.mlp.shared_experts.gate_up_proj.weight'` in `load_weights`.
- **Reproduction:** `test_linked_layers_keep_their_own_parameter_names` fails on `main` (`92580581da`), where the parameter names come back as `0.weight`, `0._next_layer.weight`, ...; it passes with the fix.

## Root Cause
1. `NonCudaDecoderMixin.bind_next` assigns `self._next_layer = next_layer` after every load.
2. `nn.Module.__setattr__` registers that layer as a submodule of the previous one.
3. `named_parameters()` dedups each layer under its first path, `layers.0._next_layer...`.
4. The next `load_weights` misses `model.layers.{i>=1}.*` in `params_dict` and raises `KeyError`.

## Fix
Store the link with `object.__setattr__`, a plain reference outside the module tree, as `inkling_common/util.py` does. Only V4.1 (`hc_pre_from_prev_sublayer=True`) reaches this; V4 returns early and is unchanged. On `main` the CUDA decoder completes mHC in `deepseek_v4_boundary`, so this fixes the non-CUDA platform decoders; `v0.5.22` still has the same line in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.bind_next`.

## Verification
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_platform_dispatch.py`: 7 passed with the fix; the new case failed before it.
- `ruff format` / `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037` (ruff `0.15.1`): clean.
- Not run: a GPU weight update on a non-CUDA platform.

## Review Focus
- `NonCudaDecoderMixin.bind_next`: nothing may rely on `_next_layer` appearing in `named_modules()` or `state_dict()`.

items.title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune dead code and fix tests that never ran
items.author: BBuf
items.summary: Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in, and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without …
items.body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.
- **RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120):** FA4 sm120 + FA4 + dense FA4 + sm120 paged MQA logits + sm120 fp8 linear + mxfp4 sm120 + diffusion fp8 FA sm120 + kernel namespace: all pass, same as main.
- **Multi-GPU:** every CUDA diffusion standalone file run on 2xH200 through the CI runner path (incl. `test_ar_models` and `test_diffusion_bcg_tp2_zimage_turbo` at the final head); Kandinsky 6 4-GPU cases on 4xH200.
- `pytest --collect-only` over the test trees: no new collection errors; import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `sglang.multimodal_gen`, `sglang.srt.{layers,models,...}`: no new import failures.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA (HIP-only deletions are traced through backend selection and import-checked on CUDA), a full AOT wheel link (affected TUs compiled for sm90/sm100), 4-GPU cases on Blackwell.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

items.title: [Feat] sgl-model-gateway: Add --decode-dispatch-limit to pick PD decode workers near KV arrival
items.author: AMD-yanfeiwang
items.summary: In PD mode the gateway picks the decode worker (the DP rank with ) on arrival, but decode starts only after prefill has queued, computed and sent the KV, so under long prefill queues running batches stay uneven across ranks.
items.body:
## Motivation

In PD mode the gateway picks the decode worker (the DP rank with `--dp-aware`) on arrival, but decode starts only after prefill has queued, computed and sent the KV, so under long prefill queues running batches stay uneven across ranks. #44402 makes the same change in `experimental/sgl-router`.

## Modifications

- `--decode-dispatch-limit N` (PD only; unset keeps today's behaviour): prefill gets every request on arrival; at most N per prefill worker (DP rank with `--dp-aware`) go on to decode until decode answers or prefill finishes, and the rest pick their decode worker when sent. Needs prefill `--optimistic-prefill-attempts` above 0.
- `decode_gate.rs`: a FIFO semaphore per prefill worker. `pd_router.rs`: prefill first, then gate, select and send decode; a disconnect or `--request-timeout-secs` ends the wait. Plus config, CLI, bindings, docs.

## Testing

- New `pd_routing_tests::test_pd_decode_dispatch_limit_holds_decode_not_prefill`: with one slot, prefill receives both requests at once and the second decode request arrives only after the first one's slot frees (~600 ms). With the gate bypassed, both decode requests arrive within ~1 ms and the test fails.
- Passing: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, nightly rustfmt on the touched files, `cargo test --lib`, `--test routing_tests` and `--test reliability_tests` (apart from `redis_test_server`, which needs a local `redis-server`), and `test_arg_parser.py` / `test_pyo3_binding.py` after `maturin develop`.

## Benchmark (MI355X)

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 1 prefill + 1 decode engine with 8 DP-attention ranks each, AgentX trace replay with AIPerf (multi-turn agentic sessions, 96% prefix-cache hit), 1 h per concurrency. Gateway `--pd-disaggregation --policy consistent_hashing --dp-aware --decode-policy power_of_two --request-timeout-secs 14400`, built at 1e86143bf0 with #42027, #43483's `SGLANG_ROUTER_P2C_LOAD_METRIC=least_requests` (decode goes to the rank with the fewest router in-flight requests), and this change (read from an environment variable at the time). Both arms ran the same build and recipe, including prefill `--optimistic-prefill-attempts 2`, and neither had request errors.

Unset → `--decode-dispatch-limit 8`, AIPerf summary:

| conc | output tok/s/GPU | TTFT p50 (s) | TTFT p90 (s) | TPOT p50 (ms) | TPOT p90 (ms) | E2E mean (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 384 | 563.1 → 571.8 (+1.5%) | 9.18 → 8.83 | 35.44 → 32.87 | 16.00 → 15.49 (-3.2%) | 19.25 → 18.30 (-4.9%) | 32.90 → 32.10 |
| 512 | 562.8 → 585.4 (+4.0%) | 18.53 → 18.48 | 76.48 → 74.80 | 16.44 → 16.23 (-1.3%) | 20.62 → 19.95 (-3.3%) | 50.90 → 48.47 |

Decode engine, per-second samples over the hour; engine TPOT is `sglang:request_time_per_output_token_seconds`, and received → first token is decode's own TTFT:

| conc | engine TPOT (ms) | busiest rank's running batch | running batch, CV across ranks | running, 8 ranks | waiting on KV, 8 ranks | received → first token (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 384 | 19.17 → 18.69 (-2.5%) | 25.8 → 24.2 | 0.13 → 0.10 | 172 → 168 | 136 → 51 | 14.7 → 5.7 |
| 512 | 20.05 → 20.03 (-0.1%) | 27.6 → 26.4 | 0.15 → 0.10 | 179 → 184 | 293 → 58 | 31.7 → 6.4 |

Prefill engine, same hour:

| conc | queue per rank | new tokens per forward | new tokens/s | chunked prefills paused (optimistic yield) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 384 | 12.8 → 12.6 | 7216 → 7165 | 44.9k → 44.9k | 1 → 294 (0.6% of requests) |
| 512 | 32.1 → 29.7 | 7650 → 7788 | 46.9k → 48.0k | 1 → 408 (0.8% of requests) |

- Decode now receives a request about 6 s before its first token instead of 15–32 s, so what it holds waiting on KV drops 62–80%, and the running batches even out: CV -24% / -33%, busiest rank's batch -6% / -4%. TPOT p50 -3.2% / -1.3%, p90 -4.9% / -3.3%.
- At 512 decode also ran 3% more requests at the same engine TPOT, and output throughput rose 4.0% with prefill new tokens/s up 2.3%. At 384 throughput rose 1.5% with prefill unchanged.
- Prefill is not held back: its queue, forward size and throughput match the unset run. The optimistic yields are chunked prefills that paused because their decode had not connected yet while a request with decode connected was waiting; they resume from the radix cache.
- TTFT changed with prefill queue time (p50 -3.8% / -0.3%, p90 -7.3% / -2.2%), which varies between runs.

### Per-rank decode load

Same runs, computed as in #43511: each decode rank's `Decode batch` log lines sampled every second; outstanding = running + waiting on KV transfer (prealloc, retracted and queue stayed 0). Stdevs are across the 8 ranks, p50 over the hour; busiest ÷ mean running excludes the first 5 min of ramp-up. With the limit, requests waiting for a decode slot are at the gateway, not in decode's outstanding count. Unset → `--decode-dispatch-limit 8`:

| conc | outstanding stdev (req) | waiting-on-KV stdev (req) | running stdev (req) | waiting ÷ outstanding | busiest ÷ mean running, p50 / p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 384 | 0.78 → 0.87 | 2.78 → 1.97 | 2.74 → 2.05 | 44% → 23% | 1.20 / 1.32 → 1.14 / 1.22 |
| 512 | 0.78 → 0.97 | 3.27 → 2.18 | 3.20 → 2.28 | 62% → 24% | 1.23 / 1.40 → 1.14 / 1.23 |

![Per-rank outstanding, waiting-on-KV and running requests at concurrency 512, unset vs --decode-dispatch-limit 8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AMD-yanfeiwang/sglang/pr-assets-sgl-router/gateway-decode-dispatch-c512-per-rank.png)

![Busiest ÷ mean running, waiting on KV and prefill queue over the hour at concurrency 512](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AMD-yanfeiwang/sglang/pr-assets-sgl-router/gateway-decode-dispatch-c512-over-the-hour.png)

- As with #44402: waiting drops to 23–24% of decode's requests, its spread by 29–33%, and the running spread with it (-25% / -29%), while outstanding requests are slightly less even.

Before marking this ready, I will rerun the A/B on a gateway built from current main with this PR.

items.body:
Preserve legacy CLI, YAML, model imports and weight-update APIs while adapting to SGLang's new configuration and weight-update sessions.

Align Docker and Conda with straw 0.1.3, the batch-invariant DeepGEMM 0.2.0 fork, and the TMS host-memory fallback. Retain DeepEP v1 alignment and pin Mooncake to the version validated after KV memory remapping.

Refresh the GLM deterministic patches and freeze the v0.5.21 patch stack. Enable CUDA compatibility libraries automatically at container startup.

Validated GLM deterministic and zero-difference layerwise checks, targeted streaming/recovery/checkpoint GPU CI, and new/legacy SGLang CPU contracts.

items.title: [HiCache] Support partial transfer groups for GLM-5.3
items.author: ZTJiu
items.summary: GLM-5.3 can hit the following warning when HiCache selects the CUDA register-based transfer kernel: A 576-byte KV row contains four complete 128-byte transfer groups and a 64-byte tail. The current CUDA register-kernel capability check rejects that tail and fa…
items.body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3 can hit the following warning when HiCache selects the CUDA
register-based transfer kernel:

```text
Unsupported element_size = 576 for JIT HiCache kernel
```

A 576-byte KV row contains four complete 128-byte transfer groups and a
64-byte tail. The current CUDA register-kernel capability check rejects
that tail and falls back to the AOT transfer kernel, even though the row
is aligned to the vector package used by each lane.

This PR makes the register kernel handle the partial final group. It
does not change TMA selection, transfer layouts, or ROCm copy-round
selection. On upstream revisions with TMA transfers enabled, the
existing TMA route remains available; this fix covers the register
route when TMA is disabled or not applicable.

## Modifications

- Copy complete transfer groups with the existing unrolled, branch-free
  loops; predicate only the lanes responsible for the final partial group.
- Allocate local storage for the full groups plus the optional tail, and
  apply the same bounds to both loads and stores.
- Admit CUDA rows divisible by the selected 4-, 8-, or 16-byte vector
  package rather than requiring a multiple of 128 bytes.
- Preserve the existing ROCm narrow-round selection and block quotas.
- Add the 576-byte shape to correctness tests and the benchmark matrix.
  The tests represent it as 288 BF16 values; the transfer kernel copies
  bytes and does not depend on the model's KV quantization format.
- Slice benchmark buffers to the required element count before reshaping,
  so the new 288-element case does not require the backing allocation to
  be divisible by 288.
- Explicitly disable TMA in the register-kernel correctness tests so a
  TMA-capable GPU cannot mask a regression in this path.

## Accuracy Tests

Tests run on one NVIDIA B200 on October 16, 2026, using the upstream
checkout plus this patch:

- CPU copy-round regression: **7 passed**, including **1,945 subtests**.
- HiCache round-trip and staged write-back tests: **56 passed**.
- Dedicated page-first staged write-back tests: **18 passed, 2 skipped**.
  The skipped tests require `get_device_accessible_ptr`, which is absent
  from the installed AOT kernel package. The skips are unrelated to this
  patch and were not weakened or removed.
- `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --target-processes all
  --error-exitcode 1` on the 576-byte and staged-only-alignment cases:
  **11 passed; ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors**.
- The two new 576-byte MLA round-trip cases fail on the unmodified
  upstream baseline and pass with the patch, confirming that the tests
  exercise the actual unsupported-size regression.
- Benchmark outputs are checked against the source tensors with
  `rtol=0, atol=0` for both AOT and JIT providers.

No model-level GLM-5.3 accuracy benchmark was run for this upstream
patch. The change only copies KV bytes; the results above verify
bit-exact transfers, including write-back and load-back.

Reproduction from the repository root:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python"
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
export SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER=0

python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_copy_rounds.py -v
python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache.py -v
python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py -v
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --target-processes all --error-exitcode 1 \
  python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache.py \
  -k '288 or staged_only_alignment' -v
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Environment:** one otherwise idle NVIDIA B200, driver 580.82.07,
PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12; measured October 16, 2026.
Upstream baseline: `81f2b43ab512cbc1e2ca0aef97b93e224d400a69`.

**Method:** 576-byte MLA rows in pinned host memory, layer-first layout,
page size 16, 524,288-token pools, default register-kernel block quota 2.
H2D copies one layer; D2H copies eight layers. Each CUDA graph rotates
through 32 random page-index pairs; timings are the median of 120
CUDA-event samples after 10 warm-up replays. Provider order is balanced
across forward/reverse cyclic permutations. AOT and JIT use the same
buffers and indices. TMA is disabled to isolate the affected path.

| Direction | Tokens | AOT latency (us) | JIT latency (us) | Speedup | JIT payload bandwidth (GB/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H2D, one layer | 128 | 9.73 | 4.11 | 2.36x | 17.92 |
| H2D, one layer | 1,024 | 64.63 | 15.83 | 4.08x | 37.27 |
| H2D, one layer | 8,192 | 500.83 | 118.64 | 4.22x | 39.77 |
| D2H, eight layers | 128 | 12.77 | 12.42 | 1.03x | 47.51 |
| D2H, eight layers | 1,024 | 179.75 | 106.04 | 1.70x | 44.50 |
| D2H, eight layers | 8,192 | 1,488.04 | 972.80 | 1.53x | 38.80 |

Bandwidth is transferred payload divided by elapsed time, in decimal
GB/s; it does not count the payload twice as read-plus-write traffic.

**Aligned-size regression check:** the baseline and patched JIT kernels
also run in the same process on identical buffers, with balanced provider
ordering. Across 512- and 1,024-byte rows, both directions, and all three
token counts, patched median latency differs from baseline by **-0.035%
to +0.204%**. For 512-byte MLA rows, all four per-layer/all-layer and
int32/int64-index specializations have identical SASS instruction hashes.
Earlier unbalanced runs showed a large-transfer D2H timing difference;
balancing provider positions removed it. Those exploratory runs are not
used for the reported comparison.

The repository's registered benchmark also completes for both CI shapes,
including the new 288-BF16-element case:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER=0 SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1 \
  DISABLE_TORCH=1 PAGE_SIZE=16 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
  python3 test/registered/kernels/benchmark/kvcache/bench_hicache.py
```

That benchmark intentionally invokes its explicit `tma` provider even
when runtime TMA routing is disabled. Its MHA timings are not mixed with
the MLA microbenchmark results above.

These are transfer-kernel microbenchmarks, not end-to-end GLM-5.3
serving throughput claims. Earlier downstream live-load measurements
are intentionally not used here because their request mixes differ.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint touched files with the repository's pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add regression coverage and verify failure on the unmodified baseline.
- [x] Provide bit-exact transfer tests and reproducible kernel benchmarks.
- [x] Preserve existing TMA and ROCm behavior.
- [ ] Run ROCm hardware CI; no ROCm machine was used locally.
- [ ] Run model-level GLM-5.3 evaluation if requested by reviewers.

The `no-commit-to-branch` pre-commit hook was skipped for local validation
because the target checkout is on `main`; no commit or push was made.

# GLM-5.3 HiCache partial-transfer-group benchmark

## Scope and revisions

Measured on October 16, 2026. This report accompanies the community port
of downstream commit `8d9011f6d0ea94700e33331ecf59102a44b28122`.

- Community baseline: `81f2b43ab512cbc1e2ca0aef97b93e224d400a69`.
- Final patch: `community.patch`, covering six existing files.
- Authoritative measurement: `balanced-benchmark.json`.
- Benchmark implementation: `bench_hicache_mla_pr.py`.
- Raw timings and correctness assertions: `balanced-benchmark.log`.

The target checkout remains on `main` with uncommitted changes. No commit,
branch, push, PR creation, existing deployment replacement, or model
server launch was performed.

## Environment and methodology

- One NVIDIA B200 on the prefill node; all eight GPUs were idle at setup.
- NVIDIA driver 580.82.07, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.
- Pinned host memory and BF16 tensors; a 288-value row is exactly 576 bytes.
  This models the byte-copy size, not GLM-5.3 model arithmetic.
- Layer-first layout, 524,288-token pools, 16-token pages; GPU 0 only.
- Default register-kernel block quota 2; `SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER=0`.
- H2D copies one MLA layer; D2H copies eight MLA layers.
- 32 random page-index pairs rotate through each CUDA graph. The providers
  share all buffers and indices; no provider-specific allocations are used.
- 10 warm-up graph replays per provider and 120 measured replays. Each
  graph replay contains 32 transfers. CUDA-event elapsed time is divided
  by 32 to report per-transfer median latency.
- Provider positions are balanced through cyclic rotations of forward
  and reverse orders, rather than always measuring the same provider
  immediately after a particular predecessor.
- Bandwidth is decimal transferred-payload GB/s, not read-plus-write GB/s.
- Every provider is checked against source values with `rtol=0, atol=0`.
- Baseline JIT specializations for aligned sizes are loaded from the
  unmodified upstream header under a distinct module identity, in the
  same process as the patched JIT specializations.

## 576-byte MLA transfer results

| Direction | Tokens | Layers | Payload bytes | AOT median (us) | Patched JIT median (us) | Speedup | JIT payload GB/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H2D | 128 | 1 | 73,728 | 9.73 | 4.11 | 2.36x | 17.92 |
| H2D | 1,024 | 1 | 589,824 | 64.63 | 15.83 | 4.08x | 37.27 |
| H2D | 8,192 | 1 | 4,718,592 | 500.83 | 118.64 | 4.22x | 39.77 |
| D2H | 128 | 8 | 589,824 | 12.77 | 12.42 | 1.03x | 47.51 |
| D2H | 1,024 | 8 | 4,718,592 | 179.75 | 106.04 | 1.70x | 44.50 |
| D2H | 8,192 | 8 | 37,748,736 | 1,488.04 | 972.80 | 1.53x | 38.80 |

The unmodified CUDA register kernel rejects 576-byte rows, so there is
no baseline register-JIT timing for this size. The valid comparison is
the existing AOT fallback versus the patched register kernel. Upstream
TMA routing remains unchanged and is not the baseline for this table.

## Aligned-size JIT regression check

The delta is `(patched / baseline - 1) * 100`; positive means slower.
The exact values in JSON are used for deltas, before table rounding.
The full-precision delta range is -0.034739% to +0.203875%.

| Row bytes | Tokens | Direction | Baseline JIT (us) | Patched JIT (us) | Latency delta |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 | 128 | H2D | 3.924 | 3.932 | +0.20% |
| 512 | 128 | D2H | 13.523 | 13.521 | -0.01% |
| 512 | 1,024 | H2D | 12.799 | 12.803 | +0.03% |
| 512 | 1,024 | D2H | 80.074 | 80.122 | +0.06% |
| 512 | 8,192 | H2D | 84.098 | 84.149 | +0.06% |
| 512 | 8,192 | D2H | 756.710 | 756.846 | +0.02% |
| 1,024 | 128 | H2D | 5.283 | 5.288 | +0.09% |
| 1,024 | 128 | D2H | 20.116 | 20.134 | +0.09% |
| 1,024 | 1,024 | H2D | 23.026 | 23.019 | -0.03% |
| 1,024 | 1,024 | D2H | 159.270 | 159.256 | -0.01% |
| 1,024 | 8,192 | H2D | 165.941 | 165.936 | -0.00% |
| 1,024 | 8,192 | D2H | 1,293.250 | 1,293.530 | +0.02% |

For 512-byte MLA rows, the final and baseline SASS instruction hashes
match in all four specializations: per-layer/all-layer and int32/int64
indices. See `sass-comparison.json` and `sass-comparison.log`.

Earlier separate-process or unbalanced-provider measurements exhibited
approximately 7% large-transfer D2H differences despite identical SASS.
The balanced same-buffer comparison removes that difference. The earlier
JSON/logs are retained as exploratory evidence, not presented as final
results: `base-benchmark`, `patched-benchmark`, `base-repeat-benchmark`,
`final-benchmark`, and `shared-buffer-benchmark`.

These measurements support no measurable aligned-size regression in
this microbenchmark; they are not a guarantee for every platform or
workload. Small 512-byte D2H transfers still favor AOT over JIT in this
setup, as they already did before the patch.

## Correctness and static checks

| Check | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU copy-round regression | 7 passed, 1,945 subtests passed | `cpu-tests.log` |
| Final HiCache round-trip/staging suite | 56 passed | `final-kernel-tests.log` |
| Dedicated page-first write-back suite | 18 passed, 2 skipped | `writeback-tests.log` |
| Baseline 576-byte round-trip regression | 2 failed as expected | `baseline-regression.log` |
| Memcheck on 576-byte/staged-only cases | 11 passed, 0 errors | `memcheck.log` |
| Registered kernel benchmark, CI shapes | Exit 0; AOT/JIT/TMA complete | `registered-benchmark.log` |
| Touched-file pre-commit hooks | Passed, branch guard skipped | `pre-commit.log` |

The two existing skips require `get_device_accessible_ptr`, which the
installed AOT kernel package does not expose; see `skip-reasons.log`.
No ROCm hardware suite, model download, model-level GLM-5.3 evaluation,
or end-to-end serving benchmark was run. The patch retains ROCm group
selection, and the CPU regression tests still cover its tiling contract.

## Reproduction

The script supports any checkout containing this patch. To include the
aligned-size comparison, first extract the baseline header from that
checkout's Git history:

```bash
cd /path/to/patched/sglang
git show 81f2b43ab512cbc1e2ca0aef97b93e224d400a69:python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/kvcacheio/hicache.cuh \
  > /tmp/hicache-upstream-base.cuh

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER=0 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
  python3 /path/to/bench_hicache_mla_pr.py \
  --label balanced \
  --baseline-source /tmp/hicache-upstream-base.cuh \
  --output /tmp/hicache-benchmark.json
```

Optional subsets use `--element-bytes 576` or
`--element-bytes 512 1024 --batch-tokens 8192`.

Run the repository benchmark with the reduced CI matrix:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER=0 SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1 \
  DISABLE_TORCH=1 PAGE_SIZE=16 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
  python3 test/registered/kernels/benchmark/kvcache/bench_hicache.py
```

The repository benchmark uses MHA buffers and explicitly invokes its
`tma` provider on SM90+ even when automatic runtime TMA routing is off.
Its numbers are not combined with the MLA table in this report.

The correction to backing-buffer slicing is required by the new
288-element shape: flatten, take the required number of elements, then
reshape. Without it, reshaping the entire 1,024-element backing allocation
as 288-element rows raises an invalid-shape error before any kernel runs.

All remote files are under `/tmp/sglang-hicache-pr-20261016`; the existing
deployment is untouched, and the benchmark processes release GPU 0.

items.title: [Doc] cookbook: Add Muse Spark Open SWA ratio calculator
items.author: Fridge003
items.summary: Muse Spark Open users need a starting value for at their target context length. Add a calculator at the end of Deployment: a 100,000-token request produces.
items.body:
## Motivation

Muse Spark Open users need a starting value for `--swa-full-tokens-ratio` at their target context length. Add a calculator at the end of Deployment: a 100,000-token request produces `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.02048`.

## Modifications

- Add one context-length input (input + output tokens, up to 1,048,576), a theoretical balanced ratio, and a copyable launch flag. Zero and invalid inputs do not emit a flag.
- Compute `min(1, 2048 / L)` for the 2,048-token SWA window and explain the equal-length, steady-state assumptions, token-capacity versus memory ratios, and HiCache/DFLASH budgeting.
- Add boundary and invalid-input tests, with the calculator export evaluated in isolation as Mintlify loads it.

items.title: [AMD] Extend MiniMax-M3 mono decode kernels to TP2 on gfx950
items.author: sahirema
items.summary: Extends #44319 (MiniMax-M3 whole-layer fused decode monokernel on gfx950 / MI355X, by @zijiecode) from TP4-only to TP2. This branch is built on top of that PR's commit; #44319 is the basis for everything here. [Discussion: Thanks for the TP2 extension!]
items.body:
## Motivation

Extends #44319 (MiniMax-M3 whole-layer fused decode monokernel on gfx950 / MI355X, by @zijiecode) from TP4-only to TP2. This branch is built on top of that PR's commit `60a1c4f1ac`; #44319 is the basis for everything here.

## Modifications

- Kernel shape constants (`LOCAL_Q_HEADS`, `LOCAL_KV_HEADS`, `LOCAL_INDEX_HEADS`, `INTER`) are derived from TP instead of being TP4 literals. TP4 values are unchanged.
- Per-head indexer selection. At TP2 a rank holds 2 index heads and 2 KV heads, so index head `h` selects blocks for KV head `h`. The previous code refused `count > 1` as context parallelism; an own-pair is not context parallelism. The split stage now runs one pass per KV head — the KV cache is addressed by head, so one split pass is one KV head and its GQA group.
- Several expressions that were correct at TP4 only by coincidence are now sized by TP: the merge and MoE mid thread maps, the narrow MoE LDS pool (sized from `INTER`, not `HIDDEN`), and the projection scratch bound.
- At TP2 the LDS budget caps the step width at 12; wider steps route to the module path, which is the existing supported fallback.

## Validation

- `SGLANG_MONO_CHECK` against the module path at TP2, widths 1-4 and 12, 456 rows each, no NaN; also at a 70k-token context exercising the long-selection path, and under CUDA graph capture.
- TP4: unchanged constants (the new code is TP-conditional), compiles clean at S=16, and mono-check passes 912 rows with no NaN.
- The per-head selection was checked by a negative control: deliberately making both split passes use index head 0's blocks — the pre-change behaviour — moves the TP2 width-1 residual median from 0.074-0.090% across three clean runs to 0.178%. So the check does discriminate this failure mode.
- 43 CPU unit tests covering the per-TP constants.

## Remaining work

- TP8 is not done (the merge needs a masked tail round at H=8, plus a padded MoE scale stride).
- A pre-existing fault on contexts shorter than one 128-token page, reproduced on #44319's own commit at TP4 — not introduced here.
- RFC #43949 conformance (directory layout, single `--enable-monokernel` switch, bounded cross-GPU waits) is not addressed yet.
- No throughput measurement yet.

Making widths TP-dependent in the framework is on our list, which would let the framework route these steps itself.

items.title: [Dev] Add KPool DSA indexer, NoPE MLA support, and FP8 precision controls for the indexer and MLA attention (dev port of #7522)
items.author: buptzyb
items.summary: Dev port of #7522 (merged to as eb001528f). Adds: - KPool DSA indexer: softmax-weighted key pooling with a BF16 per-token gate and an FP32 per-slot positional bias, pool selection expanded back to token indices, optional causal-tail append, and per-doc…
items.body:
## Summary

Dev port of #7522 (merged to `main` as eb001528f). Adds:

- **KPool DSA indexer** (`dsa_indexer_kpool > 1`): softmax-weighted key pooling with a BF16 per-token gate and an FP32 per-slot positional bias, pool selection expanded back to token indices, optional causal-tail append (`dsa_indexer_kpool_always_select_tail`), and per-document pooling for packed THD. The fused cuDNN DSA path is bypassed for KPool.
- **NoPE** (`qk_pos_emb_head_dim == 0`) for `DSAIndexer` and `AbsorbedMLASelfAttention`.
- **Precision controls**: `dsa_indexer_qk_proj_use_quantization`, `dsa_indexer_kpool_use_quantization`, and `mla_proj_use_quantization`.
- Chunked indexer score / indexer-loss backward computation, FP32 k-norm via explicit `layer_norm`, TileLang sparse-MLA top-k width padding, and a cuDNN indexer weights dtype guard.

### Dev-specific adaptations

- `absorbed_mla.py`: keeps dev's split K/V up-projection support (both combined and split builds are wrapped in the MLA projection precision context) and dev's fused MLA RoPE path (`should_use_fused_mla_rope`); NoPE skips RoPE setup entirely.
- `dsa.py`: keeps dev's fused indexer RoPE (`fused_mla_rope_inplace`) and CP-layout imports; NoPE returns early in `_apply_rope`.
- `transformer_config.py`: keeps dev's DSA CP `cp_comm_type=allgather` validation alongside the new KPool checks; only `mla_proj_use_quantization` is added to `MLATransformerConfig` (main-only fused MLA fields from the conflict context are not ported).
- Tests: the `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/*` updates are dropped (that framework does not exist on dev). Dev's `test_dsa_indexer_fused_rope_matches_unfused` now sets `dsa_indexer_loss_coeff=1.0` so it keeps comparing parameter gradients, since indexer parameters are frozen when the indexer loss is disabled. Dev-only AbsorbedMLA stand-in tests (`test_absorbed_mla_qkv_rope_uses_microbatch_cp_group`, `test_dsa_integration.py`) now provide `use_rope` and the MLA projection precision context.

### Behavior note

As on `main`, indexer parameters are set to `requires_grad=False` when `dsa_indexer_loss_coeff` is unset or `<= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `CHECK_ONLY=true BASE_REF=dev tools/autoformat.sh` (black 26.3.0, isort, pylint, ruff)
- [x] Unit tests on 8x H100 with the `Dockerfile.ci.dev` image (`run_ci_test.sh`, dev environment), all passing:

items.title: Honor per-module quantization override in the fused GroupedMLP path
items.author: xrennvidia
items.summary: The TE op-fuser builds its quantizers from the ambient autocast recipe, so a --te-precision-config-file override that keeps the experts quantized but with a different recipe (e.g. MXFP8 MTP experts under a global NVFP4 recipe) was ignored by the fused kernels:…
items.body:
The TE op-fuser builds its quantizers from the ambient autocast recipe, so a --te-precision-config-file override that keeps the experts quantized but with a different recipe (e.g. MXFP8 MTP experts under a global NVFP4 recipe) was ignored by the fused kernels: forward ran under NVFP4 while the module and its GTP gather were MXFP8, and backward then failed in the NVFP4 amax lookup.

Enter the module's own quantization autocast around the fused call, exactly as TEGroupedLinear.forward does on the unfused path. fc1 and fc2 must carry the same override since fusion spans both. A bf16 override still disables fusion.

Requires the matching Transformer Engine change that quantizes GTP-gathered BF16 weights inside the fused grouped MLP.

## Accuracy Validation

items.title: [Bugfix][Sampler] Support TP-sharded logits in MinTokensLogitsProcessor
items.author: solin28825
items.summary: Fixes OOB crash in MinTokensLogitsProcessor when TP-sharded vocab-parallel logits are fed to the sampler by translating global token IDs to rank-local indices.
items.body:
## Overview



`MinTokensLogitsProcessor` writes `-inf` at stop-token positions using **global** token ids.
When the LM head output is TP-sharded (vocab-parallel logits fed to the sampler), `logits`
only spans the rank-local vocabulary shard, so those ids index out of bounds and crash all
TP ranks. This change translates the ids to rank-local columns when the CPU-side index
tensors are built.

Fixes #61966

## Claims



- Fixes the OOB crash (`index 248044 exceeds bounds 31040`) on backends that feed sharded
  logits to the sampler (observed on vllm-ascend, 910B2C, TP8, 248320-vocab model).
- Unsharded path (default, all current GPU flows) is byte-identical: the translation is the
  identity mapping when `tp_size == 1`.
- Hot kernels (`apply()`, `_mask_stop_token_logits()`) are untouched: no new device ops, no
  shape changes at mask time.
- Adds CPU-only unit tests that reproduce the crash on main (`IndexError`) and pass with
  the fix.

## Validation



- New tests `tests/v1/sample/test_min_toks_sharded_logits.py` (CPU-only, no model weights;
  the TP rank is simulated by monkeypatching `get_tensor_model_parallel_rank`):
  - On pristine main, 4/5 tests fail with `IndexError: index 30 is out of bounds for
    dimension 1 with size 25`, hitting all three consuming paths (`apply()`, the restore
    read in `_mask_stop_token_logits()`, `apply_with_spec_decode()`).
  - With this change: 5/5 pass. Run: `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_min_toks_sharded_logits.py -v`
- Independent simulation (8 ranks, vocab 248320, EOS ids 248044/248046): per-rank masking is
  bit-identical to full-vocab masking on every rank; no duplicate index pairs; padded vocab
  bounds covered.
- Production soak on vllm-ascend (910B2C, TP8, 1P1D + MTP3): crash reproduced 100% before
  the fix; 0 occurrences across a 2h44m multi-stage benchmark (5 concurrency levels up to
  32, prompt lengths up to 64k) after.

## Details



- Root cause: the index tensors are built in the **global vocabulary coordinate system**,
  while the tensor being indexed is in the **rank-local shard coordinate system**; both
  `update_state()` and `apply_with_spec_decode()` consume global ids.
- Fix: compute `shard_start` / `shard_end` in `__init__` via the existing helpers
  `pad_vocab_size()` + `vocab_range_from_global_vocab_size()` (padding-correct); new
  `_local_stop_ids()` helper maps in-shard ids to `tok - shard_start` and drops ids owned by
  other ranks; index-list construction in `update_state()` / `apply_with_spec_decode()` goes
  through it.
- Why build-time translation instead of clamped indices + `torch.where` at mask time:
  clamped out-of-shard entries can collide with a valid entry on the same column, and
  duplicate-index assignment has undefined write order, so an invalid entry can revert a
  legitimate `-inf`. Build-time translation never creates duplicate indices. These index
  tensors are already rebuilt with data-dependent sizes on every `update_state()` (sparse
  processor), so build-time filtering introduces no new shape-variance class.
- Limitation: the default GPU flow all-gathers logits before sampling, so the buggy path is
  not naturally reachable in mainline CI; the unit tests exercise it directly. The indexing
  contract is violated by any caller that feeds sharded logits (first-party ecosystem
  backends, e.g. vllm-ascend `enable_reduce_sample`).
