Thanks for addressing the sharded-logits case. I compared the real `MinTokensLogitsProcessor` on CPU at baseline `fa75d3456d60a5ffe923818c4b495295675b38e1` and PR head `86586a11e352c14a870282bc28a3cb0f6c81f15d`, and found two compatibility issues worth covering before merge.

The environment was macOS arm64, Python 3.14.6, PyTorch 2.13.0, and pytest 8.4.2, using separate source snapshots and an isolated environment. Only `get_tensor_model_parallel_rank` was mocked; there was no distributed process group or model forward. These are processor-level CPU results, not an independent validation of the reported Ascend workload.

**1. TP > 1 with full-vocabulary logits loses stop-token masking**

For all four cases, the vocabulary size is 100, the global stop ID is 40, `min_tokens=1`, and the output-token list is empty. With TP=4, the PR's padded vocabulary is 128, giving 32 columns per shard.

| Input to the processor | Expected masked columns | Baseline | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP=1, rank=0, full logits `[1, 100]` | `[40]` | `[40]` | `[40]` |
| TP=4, rank=0, full logits `[1, 100]` | `[40]` | `[40]` | **`[]`** |
| TP=4, rank=1, local logits `[1, 32]` | `[8]` | `IndexError` | `[8]` |
| TP=4, rank=0, local logits `[1, 32]` | `[]` | `IndexError` | `[]` |

The local-shard cases confirm the fix, but TP size alone does not establish whether the sampler receives local or gathered logits. The [default LM-head path gathers TP logits and trims them to the original vocabulary](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa75d3456d60a5ffe923818c4b495295675b38e1/vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py#L180-L199).

In the TP=4/rank=0/full-vocabulary case, the PR infers the range `[0, 32)`, drops global ID 40, and builds `logits_slice=[[], []]`, even though column 40 exists in the actual input. With a synthetic stop-token logit of 10.0, the baseline changes it to `-inf` and argmax moves from 40 to 99; the PR leaves it at 10.0 and argmax remains 40. This demonstrates the masking regression at the processor boundary; it is not a claim about an end-to-end model generation run.

**2. Three existing min_tokens tests now fail during construction**

I also ran the unchanged `test_min_tokens_` cases in `tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py` against both snapshots:

- Baseline: **3 passed, 40 deselected**.
- PR head: **3 failed, 40 deselected**.

All three failures occur before exercising their masking assertions:

```text
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_vocab_size'
```

The existing [test helper](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/86586a11e352c14a870282bc28a3cb0f6c81f15d/tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py#L450-L451) constructs `MinTokensLogitsProcessor(VllmConfig(), torch.device("cpu"), False)`. That config has `model_config=None`, while the [new constructor](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/86586a11e352c14a870282bc28a3cb0f6c81f15d/vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/builtin.py#L193-L208) unconditionally calls `get_vocab_size()`.

The affected tests are:

- `test_min_tokens_keeps_all_masked_behavior_without_structured_output`
- `test_min_tokens_restores_all_masked_structured_output_stop_token`
- `test_min_tokens_restores_all_masked_structured_output_stop_token_spec_decode`

This may require updating the existing test fixture to provide a valid model config, depending on the intended constructor contract; it should not be read as evidence that a production engine uses `model_config=None`.

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproducer for all four cases and the legacy constructor</summary>

Save the following as `min_tokens_probe.py` outside either source checkout:

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch

from vllm import SamplingParams
from vllm.config import VllmConfig
from vllm.v1.sample.logits_processor.builtin import MinTokensLogitsProcessor
from vllm.v1.sample.logits_processor.interface import BatchUpdate

for tp, rank, width in [(1, 0, 100), (4, 0, 100), (4, 1, 32), (4, 0, 32)]:
    config = SimpleNamespace(
        model_config=SimpleNamespace(get_vocab_size=lambda: 100),
        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(tensor_parallel_size=tp),
    )
    try:
        with patch("vllm.distributed.get_tensor_model_parallel_rank", return_value=rank):
            processor = MinTokensLogitsProcessor(config, torch.device("cpu"), False)
            processor.update_state(BatchUpdate(
                batch_size=1, removed=[], moved=[],
                added=[(0, SamplingParams(min_tokens=1, stop_token_ids=[40]), None, [])],
            ))
            logits = torch.arange(width, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1, width) / 100
            if width == 100:
                logits[0, 40] = 10.0
            elif rank == 1:
                logits[0, 8] = 10.0
            indices = [index.tolist() for index in processor.logits_slice]
            result = processor.apply(logits)
            masked = torch.isneginf(result[0]).nonzero().flatten().tolist()
            print(f"TP={tp} rank={rank} width={width}: indices={indices}, "
                  f"masked={masked}, argmax={result.argmax(-1).item()}")
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"TP={tp} rank={rank} width={width}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")

try:
    MinTokensLogitsProcessor(VllmConfig(), torch.device("cpu"), False)
    print("Legacy VllmConfig() constructor: OK")
except Exception as error:
    print(f"Legacy VllmConfig() constructor: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Commands used for the processor probe and existing tests</summary>

Use a dependency-ready environment and run these commands once per source checkout: baseline `fa75d3456d60a5ffe923818c4b495295675b38e1`, then PR head `86586a11e352c14a870282bc28a3cb0f6c81f15d`. Keep the Python environment identical between runs.

```bash

printf '[pytest]\naddopts =\n' > "$REPRO_DIR/pytest-min-tokens.ini"

  -c "$REPRO_DIR/pytest-min-tokens.ini" \
  --confcutdir="$VLLM_SRC/tests/v1/logits_processors" \
  "$VLLM_SRC/tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py" \
  -k test_min_tokens_ -vv --tb=short
```

The environment had neither Triton nor the compiled `vllm._C` extension; import warnings were present, but the targeted CPU processor calls and tests executed. This targeted invocation is not a full CPU CI run.

</details>

Could we make the logits-layout contract explicit so that TP>1 gathered logits retain global stop-token indexing, and add that full-vocabulary case alongside the local-shard tests? It would also be useful to keep the three existing min_tokens tests runnable with the intended config contract. I am happy to rerun these CPU comparisons against an updated revision.

items.title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] gfx942 sparse MLA decode: BLOCK_K=16 with 2-stage pipelining
items.author: lohiaj
items.summary: On gfx942 the split-K sparse MLA decode kernel was running with the 32-row K tile that was tuned for gfx950, and a single-stage loop That loop is latency bound, not compute bound. Each iteration loads the slot indices for the tile, gathers that many scattered …
items.body:
On gfx942 the split-K sparse MLA decode kernel was running with the 32-row K tile that was tuned for gfx950, and a single-stage loop

That loop is latency bound, not compute bound. Each iteration loads the slot indices for the tile, gathers that many scattered rows (fp8 nope + bf16 rope) and their scales out of the paged cache, dequantizes them, then does two small dots against a few heads. The dots are tiny, so with `num_stages=1` the MFMAs mostly sit idle waiting on the current tile's gather

The fix is to let Triton pipeline the loop. With `num_stages=2` the next tile's index load and row gather are issued while the current tile is still in the dots. Holding two 32-row tiles in flight is a lot of on-chip storage for MI300X (64 KiB LDS per CU, MI355X has 160 KiB), so the tile drops to 16 rows, where two fit comfortably. Smaller tiles also waste less work on the masked tail of each split

`block_k` also feeds `_decode_num_splits`, so the split count on gfx942 can shift a bit for the same batch. That's expected, the heuristic is already written in terms of `block_k`

gfx950 has its own partial kernel and split heuristic, both tuned around 32-row tiles with a lot more LDS, so it's left alone. Archs that are neither gfx942 nor gfx950 take the generic fallback earlier in the function and don't see this either

Numerics: same math, and the online softmax still accumulates in fp32. Only the order the KV rows are reduced in changes (tile size and split boundaries), so outputs differ from before at bf16 rounding level, not bit for bit

No other open PR changes this tile. #57880 is in the same function but only touches the gfx950 split logic, and it is still open, so there is a small conflict risk if both land close together. #61967 sends big decode steps to the HIP kernel, while this Triton path still handles small steps and builds without the HIP op

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` on MI300X: same pass/skip/fail set as main on this image, all gfx942 split-K decode cases pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure: `test_v41_rocm_combine_uses_shared_kernel`)
- [ ] outputs compared against the old launch config at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode shapes - done earlier, not re-run after this rebase
- [ ] kernel time at those shapes - done earlier, not re-run after this rebase
- [x] pre-commit default and `--hook-stage manual` clean on the changed files
- [ ] end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash - done earlier (serving within noise, accuracy unchanged), not re-run after this rebase

#18721 removed the two-model speculative decoding path but left behind the code that only served it. This is the follow-up promised in the review of #20188. No `LlmRequest` is created with `is_draft=True` any more, so everything removed here was unreachable:

- `d2t` handling in `TorchSampler` and `LlmRequest`: only the removed drafter put `d2t` into the model outputs;
- the executor creator's `draft_model_engine`, which was always `None`;
- the drafter branches of the overlap executor loop. Drafter modes force the overlap scheduler off, and the hooks those branches called (`should_forward_draft_model`, `generate_draft_tokens_with_overlap`, `cleanup_previous_draft_resources`) were defined only by the removed `ModelDrafter`.

**API compatibility.** No public API changes: the removed symbols are `_torch` internals, and the LLM API arguments and the `Drafter` interface are unchanged. items.title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] HIP sparse MLA decode kernel for batched decode on gfx942
items.author: lohiaj
items.summary: Adds a gfx942-specific HIP sparse MLA decode kernel that keeps K in registers and V through LDS to convert a latency-bound Triton split-K kernel into a compute-bound path for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 batched decode.
items.body:
On gfx942 the Triton split-K sparse MLA decode path for DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 spends most of its time gathering scattered fp8 rows out of the paged cache. At batch the MFMAs mostly wait on those gathers, so the kernel is latency bound rather than compute bound

This adds a gfx942-only HIP kernel that keeps K in registers as the MFMA A operand, pipelines tiles through a small register ring, and brings V through LDS. It is registered as `_rocm_C::sparse_mla_decode_fp8_ds_mla` and covers the per-rank DSv4 / V4.1 decode shape (16 heads x 512 = 448 nope + 64 rope) over fp8_ds_mla caches, including the SWA main cache, optional top-k extra cache, optional attention sink, ragged indices with -1 holes, and a split-K plus reduce

`rocm_sparse_attn_decode` dispatches to it on gfx942 when the op is present, the output is bf16 (no MXFP8 epilogue), the head shape matches, and the step has at least `_HIP_SPARSE_DECODE_MIN_TOKENS` (64) decode tokens. Below that gate the HIP path's fixed cost (split-K plus a separate reduce kernel) is not paid back, and Triton is as fast or faster, so smaller steps stay on the Triton split-K kernel. Like the aiter path it returns 0 so the caller applies the inverse RoPE

NaN elements of gathered rows count as zero, matching what the Triton scrub intends. Device code is compiled only under `__gfx942__`. Other targets build empty kernels and the host op refuses to run off gfx942. CUDA builds never see `csrc/rocm`

Complementary, not overlapping: #60583 turns on AITER sparse MLA on gfx942 for other models and excludes DSv4 / V4.1. #60731 is an opt-in mono decode path for very small steps. This PR is the batched decode path at 64+ tokens on the Triton fallback shapes those leave alone. #61968 retunes the Triton tile on gfx942 for the small steps that stay on that path

## Test plan

- [x] new / extended kernel tests compare the HIP path against the fp32 reference on gfx942 at DSv4 / V4.1 decode shapes (re-run on this tip)
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` on MI300X: same pass/skip/fail set as main on this image, plus the new HIP cases (one pre-existing unrelated failure: `test_v41_rocm_combine_uses_shared_kernel`)
- [x] `_rocm_C` builds clean with vLLM's existing warning flags on this tip
- [x] pre-commit default and `--hook-stage manual` clean on the changed files
- [ ] qualitative end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (decode throughput up at high concurrency, low concurrency unchanged since the path is not taken, accuracy unchanged vs main) - done earlier on an older tip, not re-run after this rebase
- [x] `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rocm_sparse_mla_decode.py` is in the tree for reproducing the Triton vs HIP crossover

items.title: [Perf] request_logger: don't walk omitted or truncated fields during watermark redaction
items.author: Kangyan-Zhou
items.summary: Redaction is key-based, but it walks every element, so every request-log call is now O(prompt length), even for fields the log never prints. With (, and / in, so they are never printed), each call walks the full list.
items.body:
## Motivation

#37577 (Aaronson-Gumbel text watermarking) made `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` and `_transform_data_for_logging` call `redact_watermark_secrets` on the whole request **before** truncation and **before** `skip_names` filtering. Redaction is key-based, but it walks every element, so every request-log call is now O(prompt length), even for fields the log never prints.

With `--log-requests --log-requests-level 1` (`max_length = 1 << 30`, and `input_ids` / `output_ids` in `skip_names`, so they are never printed), each call walks the full `input_ids` list. The tokenizer manager's event loop pays for this on receive, before the request is dispatched to the scheduler, so it adds directly to TTFT. It pays again on finish.

Measured on our deployment (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4×B300, replaying production traffic with a mean prompt of ~84k tokens), the API server's received→dispatched time went from ~3 ms to ~25 ms per request compared with a pre-#37577 build.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/utils/request_logger.py`:
- New helper `_redact_fields_for_logging(values, max_length, skip_names)`, used by the dict and dataclass branches of both formatters in place of redacting the whole object:
  - Fields in `skip_names` are never redacted. The log omits them anyway.
  - Lists and tuples longer than `max_length` outside the watermark-bearing fields (`watermark`, `watermark_key`, `watermark_key_b`, `watermark_config`, `sampling_params`, `preferred_sampling_params`) skip the whole-object walk. Everything else is redacted exactly as before.
- In `_transform_data_for_logging`, the truncated-list branch now redacts the printed head and tail halves, as `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` already did. Secrets in a long list are still redacted wherever they are printed.

Log output does not change at any `--log-requests-level` (0–3).

## Tests

New `test/registered/unit/utils/test_request_logger_redaction.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):
- Watermark secrets are redacted in both formatters, for short and 100k-token requests, at level 1 and inside a long `sampling_params` list.
- The longest list handed to `redact_watermark_secrets` is bounded at each level's real `(max_length, skip_names)` (levels 0–2; level 3 prints every id).
- Truncated output keeps its head and tail.

Results with the installed tree copied to a scratch dir and only `request_logger.py` swapped:
- `upstream/main` `request_logger.py`: **1 failed, 5 passed**. `test_redaction_walk_is_bounded_at_every_log_level` fails with `AssertionError: 100000 not less than or equal to 2048 : level=0 _dataclass_to_string_truncated`.
- This PR: **6 passed**.

**Output equivalence.** I compared old and new output for both formatters at levels 0, 1, 2 and 3, using each level's `RequestLogger(...).metadata`. The inputs were `GenerateReqInput` with 16 / 3k / 100k `input_ids` (with and without watermark params), text input, batched input, a long `sampling_params` list, `EmbeddingReqInput`, finish `out` dicts (16 / 5k `output_ids`), and OpenAI-style dicts (the `log_openai_received_request` path, no `skip_names`). The output was byte-identical in 72/72 cases (text and JSON), and no secret appeared in any output.

**Microbenchmark.** Per log call at `--log-requests-level 1`, plain `sampling_params`, mean of 30 calls, single-threaded on a dev-box CPU:

| `input_ids` | formatter | before (ms) | after (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30k | `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` (text) | 6.87 | 0.057 |
| 30k | `_transform_data_for_logging` (json) | 6.89 | 0.051 |
| 80k | `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` (text) | 18.43 | 0.057 |
| 80k | `_transform_data_for_logging` (json) | 18.40 | 0.051 |
| 120k | `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` (text) | 27.56 | 0.057 |
| 120k | `_transform_data_for_logging` (json) | 27.73 | 0.051 |

After this PR the cost no longer depends on prompt length.

items.author: e-mon
items.summary: Adds reasoning and tool call parsers for LLM-jp-4.1 (https://huggingface.co/llm-jp/llm-jp-4.1-8b-thinking, also 32b-a3b and 33b). The model uses the gpt-oss Harmony format, but the tokenizer decodes a space after every special token, and parallel tool calls ar…
items.body:
## Motivation

Adds reasoning and tool call parsers for LLM-jp-4.1 (https://huggingface.co/llm-jp/llm-jp-4.1-8b-thinking, also 32b-a3b and 33b).

The model uses the gpt-oss Harmony format, but the tokenizer decodes a space after every special token, and parallel tool calls are separated by `<|end|>`:

```
<|channel|> analysis<|message|> I need both cities.<|end|>
<|start|> assistant to=functions.get_weather<|channel|> commentary <|constrain|>  json<|message|> {"city": "Tokyo"}<|end|>
<|start|> assistant to=functions.get_weather<|channel|> commentary <|constrain|>  json<|message|> {"city": "Osaka"}<|call|>
```

The `gpt-oss` parsers return no tool calls for this output, also with the changes in #38222.

## Modifications

- `llm-jp-harmony` reasoning and tool call parsers. The tool call parser builds its own grammar for `required`, named, `strict` and `parallel_tool_calls=false`, since the xgrammar `harmony` tag expects no spaces and `<|call|>` after every call.
- `auto` picks `llm-jp-harmony` when the chat template has `chat_format=llm-jp-harmony-v1`.
- Outside the new files: registration and two lines in `_patch_reasoning_skip_special_tokens`.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model outputs. With `llm-jp/llm-jp-4.1-8b-thinking`, reasoning, single and parallel calls, `required`/named and streaming work, and on 400 BFCL v3 prompts the parsed output matches the reference parser of the LLM-jp vLLM plugin (https://github.com/llm-jp/llm-jp-vllm) for all 400.

items.title: [Fix] Name and bound the symmetric-memory window registration
items.author: hope1262946533
items.summary: With, is called from the forward path whenever the symmetric-memory pool grows a new segment. That call blocks in NCCL's Unix-domain-socket fd-exchange rendezvous, which has no timeout of its own.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-symm-mem`, `ncclCommWindowRegister` is called from the forward
path whenever the symmetric-memory pool grows a new segment. That call blocks
in NCCL's Unix-domain-socket fd-exchange rendezvous, which has no timeout of
its own. When the rendezvous wedges, every rank in the group parks in `recvmsg`
and nothing is ever printed: the engine stays up, `/health` keeps returning
200, and no batch makes progress (#36943).

We hit exactly this on a single-node TP8/EP8 Kimi-K3 deployment with MegaMoE:
the engine hung on the first warmup prefill and the server log contained no
error line at all — the only way to tell it apart from an idle engine was to
notice that the log had stopped advancing. Roughly one cold-compile-cache start
in five hung this way.

The scheduler watchdog does eventually notice and dumps, but it cannot say
*what* was in flight, and it waits its full `--watchdog-timeout` (300 s by
default) before it does.

## Modifications

- The registration runs on a worker thread bounded by
  `SGLANG_SYMM_MEM_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_S` (default 120 s), so a wedge is
  reported sooner than the watchdog would report it.
- On timeout the registration is named in the log, `pyspy_dump_schedulers()` and
  `faulthandler.dump_traceback()` capture the native and Python stacks, and the
  parent is sent `SIGQUIT` — the same exit path the scheduler and the watchdog
  use, so the normal crash handling runs. The process does not continue: the
  wedged thread still holds the C++ segment mutex, so it could never register
  again.
- `describe_registration_in_progress()` publishes what is in flight, and the
  scheduler watchdog's `dump_info()` includes it, so a stall there reads as
  "symmetric-memory registration in progress: comm=… group=…" instead of a bare
  watchdog timeout.

This does **not** remove the underlying deadlock; it makes it named, fast and
diagnosable. The root cause is tracked in #36943.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - no change to numerics.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A - the registration call itself is unchanged. The added work is one thread
start plus one join per registration round, and a round only happens when the
symmetric-memory pool grows a segment.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with
      pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit
      tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
      `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_pynccl_allocator_registration_timeout.py`
      covers the bound, the exception passthrough, the timeout path and the
      published state; 5 tests pass on the 0.5.21 image.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write
      documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
      Not applicable: the new env var is a diagnostic bound, not a user-facing
      feature, and no behaviour changes when the registration succeeds.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the
      accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)
      and [Benchmark the
      speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
      N/A, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style
      [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [dev] Mask padding before HybridEP dispatch under an expert-rank budget
items.author: xiaoyao0115
items.summary: Extends the HybridEP padding mask from NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#5542 to runs with a static expert-rank budget. It did this only for dropless HybridEP: the condition requires both and, and its test lists among the configurations that keep padding routes.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Extends the HybridEP padding mask from NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#5542 to runs with a static expert-rank budget (`--moe-expert-rank-capacity-factor`).

#5542 made `TopKRouter.routing()` zero the probabilities and clear the routing-map entries of padding rows before dispatch. It did this only for dropless HybridEP: the condition requires both `moe_expert_capacity_factor is None` and `moe_expert_rank_capacity_factor is None`, and its test lists `("flex", "hybridep", None, 1.0)` among the configurations that keep padding routes. HybridEP with an expert-rank budget consumes the same sparse routing map, so the second condition is not needed. This PR removes it. HybridEP now masks padding whenever per-expert capacity (`--moe-expert-capacity-factor`) is off. Other dispatchers, and HybridEP with per-expert capacity, keep their fixed-route behavior, as in #5542.

Why it matters: with a rank budget, `_HybridEPManager` gives HybridEP a static receive budget of `local rows × topk × factor` (rounded up for alignment), and padding rows are part of the local rows. Padding rows that keep their routes are dispatched like real tokens. They take receive-buffer and expert-input rows and count against the receiving rank's budget, leaving less headroom for load imbalance among real tokens. Padding rows can also route alike: with hash routing, for example, all padding rows with the same pad token id go to the same experts. When a rank receives more rows than the budget, HybridEP drops the excess in that attempt and sets its over-budget flag. In the Megatron training loop, `PagedStashRunner` wraps the step whenever `moe_expert_rank_capacity_factor` is set. It all-reduces the flag after forward-backward. If any rank was over budget, it discards the attempt (zeroes the gradients) and reruns the step once in dropless mode: the capacity factor is cleared, paged stash is off, and HybridEP sizes dispatch with a host sync. A captured TE whole-MoE CUDA graph cannot fall back, so in that case the runner raises an error.

In the Megatron training loop, routed padding therefore never silently drops tokens. It costs throughput: steps with padding carry extra dispatch and expert rows, and a step in which a rank goes over budget pays for a second, dropless forward-backward. With a captured TE whole-MoE graph, such a step stops the run instead. With this PR padding takes none of the budget. Routing of real tokens does not change: the new test checks that probabilities and routing maps equal, exactly, the routing computed without a rank budget. We have not measured how often the rerun triggers with and without this change.

We found this while benchmarking dynamic context parallelism with CUDA graphs (NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6479). There, packed sequences are padded up to a fixed per-rank capacity, so every pack whose sequences do not fill that capacity carries padding rows.

## Tests

In `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_routers.py`:

- New `test_hybridep_rank_capacity_masks_padding` covers eager and CUDA-graph-captured routing, with and without hash routing, replayed with 2, 5, 0 and 2 valid tokens. It checks three things:
  - padding rows get no routes;
  - every valid token gets its top-k routes;
  - probabilities and routing maps equal, exactly, the routing computed without a rank budget.
- `test_hybridep_dense_routing_masks_padding` now also runs with a rank capacity factor.
- The `("flex", "hybridep", None, 1.0)` case leaves `test_padding_mask_preserves_routes_outside_dropless_hybridep`, because that configuration now masks padding.

On 8×H100 (torch 2.11 container, TE 2.19), `test_routers.py` gives 72 passed, 2 skipped and 2 failed. The two failures, `test_router_gating_linear[router_dtype1]` and `test_router_gating_linear_bias[router_dtype1]`, fail the same way on dev c3010d6d5.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none. Follow-up to NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#5542; found during NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6479 benchmarking.

## Contribution process

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation

items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Documents DFlash2 speculative decoding for Muse Spark Open, now that the drafter checkpoint is public at [`nvidia/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-DFlash2).

Two commits:

1. **Add the docs** (Brian Nguyen). The deployment guide gets DFlash2 in the feature list and the Speculative Decoding section: the drafter Hub id, `K = 7`, and a note that DFlash runs on the `TRTLLM` attention backend (FlashInfer target attention is refused at startup). `supported-models.md` sets the Spec Dec column to DFlash for `MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration`, with a footnote naming the drafter. `examples/musespark_open` gains the `spec_dflash.yaml` overlay, and its README the merged-config launch recipe.
2. **Correct the temperature-0 caveat** (Michal Guzek). The docs said that at temperature 0 speculation "may rarely" produce a different completion than a run without it. Measured with DFlash2, 7 of 8 greedy completions differed from the non-speculative run, usually early in the reasoning, while the non-speculative server reproduced its own outputs exactly across runs. Each divergent token was the target's second or third candidate at a low-confidence position (0.06–0.69 nats behind the top candidate), and the non-speculative server alone flips tokens by the same margin between a fresh send of a prompt and a resend served from the KV-cache prefix. The guide, the README and the `spec_dflash.yaml` comment now say that temperature-0 completions often differ, and why.

Documentation only.

## Test Coverage

Checked on one 4x GB300 node (TP4/EP4) with a Muse Spark Open NVFP4 checkpoint, served with the README recipe as written: `cat serve_config.yaml spec_dflash.yaml`, `--custom_tokenizer musespark_open --tool_parser musespark --reasoning_parser musespark`, and the drafter given by its Hub id, which TRT-LLM resolves through `snapshot_download`. `per_request_spec_decode_stats: true` was added for measurement only.

- The server starts; the drafter runs on `VANILLA` attention for its non-causal sliding window, the target on `TRTLLM`.
- Under DFlash, every functional check is correct: plain answers, streaming, 8 concurrent requests, tool calls, JSON object and JSON schema output, a 15.7k-token chunked-prefill prompt and its prefix-cache resend, and the README and guide request examples sent verbatim.
- Aggregate acceptance length 3.32 over 15 requests (1,329 verify steps); single-request decode 1.95–2.29x faster than without speculation.
- The published drafter is byte-identical to the checkpoint first used for these measurements (sha256 of `model.safetensors`, git blob of `config.json`). Rerun with the drafter downloaded from the Hub: identical greedy completions on all 9 compared checks and identical acceptance statistics (aggregate 3.32, 1,329 verify steps).

items.title: [CPU][Bugfix] Flatten >2-D activations in the AMX int8 W8A8 linear path
items.author: harshaladhav-amd
items.summary: Fixes AMX int8 W8A8 linear kernel rejecting 3D+ activations by flattening them to 2D before calling the SGL matmul kernel, matching the existing onednn fallback path.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #61964.

On AMX CPUs, `CPUInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel` routes symmetric W8A8 linears with aligned shapes to `_apply_weights_sgl` (the SGLang-derived `int8_scaled_mm_with_quant` kernel), which has been the default since #50801. That path passes activations straight to the kernel, and the kernel enforces `CHECK_DIM(2, mat1)`. The Whisper encoder runs on `B x T x D`, so W8A8 Whisper fails on AMX machines with `RuntimeError: mat1 must be a 2D tensor`. Non-AMX CPUs fall back to `_apply_weights_onednn`, which already flattens to `[M, K]` and restores the leading dims, so the model works there.

This PR applies the same flatten/reshape in `_apply_weights_sgl`. It matches `_apply_weights_onednn` and `CPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` in the same file, and the W4A16 fix in #58268. 2-D inputs (all decoder-only models) are unaffected.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs and issues for `_apply_weights_sgl`, `int8_scaled_mm_with_quant`, and CPU/Whisper W8A8. The only related item is #56029, which fixes the ROCm Triton `scaled_mm` path (#56024) and doesn't touch the CPU kernel.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_cpu_sgl_int8_linear_accepts_3d_input` in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py` (already a `cpu_test` file). It builds a layer through `CPUInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.process_weights_for_sgl`, runs `apply_weights` on a `[2, 3, K]` input, and checks the result is bit-identical to the flattened `[6, K]` call reshaped back. The test is skipped when `int8_scaled_mm_with_quant` is not built.
- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py -v`
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`

## Test Result

Run on an AVX512-BF16 host (AMD EPYC 9454). It loads the same `_C` library, so the SGL int8 op runs there through its non-AMX fallback.

- Without the fix, the new test fails with `RuntimeError: mat1 must be a 2D tensor`.
- With the fix:

```text
tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py  11 passed
```

- pre-commit: all hooks passed (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, test tethering, ...).

I don't currently have AMX hardware available, so I haven't run an end-to-end W8A8 Whisper accuracy check on GNR/SPR. The change only affects inputs that previously raised, and the 2-D path is unchanged. I'd appreciate an AMX run from CPU CI or reviewers (cc @bigPYJ1151).

*AI assistance was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.*

items.title: [CI] tests: Fork the gloo exchange test's ranks from a preloaded forkserver
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: starts each gloo rank from a context, so every rank is a fresh interpreter that re-imports the whole package before it exchanges a single row. On a small CPU runner that import dominates the test.
items.body:
Stacked on #44622 (which adds `TestSyncRowExchangeGloo`); this PR's diff is the one commit on top of it, and it retargets to `main` when #44622 merges.

## Motivation

`TestSyncRowExchangeGloo` starts each gloo rank from a `spawn` context, so every rank is a fresh interpreter that re-imports the whole package before it exchanges a single row. On a small CPU runner that import dominates the test.

## Modifications

The ranks start from a `forkserver` context that preloads the test module, so the import happens once in the server and each rank forks from it. The forkserver process is single-threaded, so ranks fork from a clean interpreter rather than from the multi-threaded test process. Worlds, rounds and assertions are unchanged; the comment about the runner's memory cap is reworded since it no longer depends on spawning.

## Test plan

- `TestSyncRowExchangeGloo` on top of #44622: passes under `pytest` (1 passed) and as `python3 test_dp_attn.py TestSyncRowExchangeGloo` (OK), the way the CPU test runner invokes it.
- Cost, on four pinned cores at the 8-rank world: about 84 CPU-seconds with `spawn`, about 8 with `forkserver`; peak resident memory about 7.8 GB either way, so the world cap is kept.
- `black`, `isort`, `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037` clean on the changed file.

items.title: [Fix] nixl: Stop an aborted room from parking the transfer worker forever
items.author: Sworol
items.summary: In PD disaggregation with the NIXL backend, a decode-side abort marks the room and registers a deferred ACK target, but does not cancel the submitted NIXL handles nor interrupt a prefill transfer worker already inside. The wait is bounded only after an is obs…
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44369.

In PD disaggregation with the NIXL backend, a decode-side abort marks the room `KVPoll.Failed` and registers a deferred ACK target, but does not cancel the submitted NIXL handles nor interrupt a prefill transfer worker already inside `_await_handles()`. The wait is bounded only after an `ERR` is observed: while every handle reads healthy-but-non-terminal (`PROC`), the deadline stays `None` and the worker polls forever.

Each aborted room therefore leaves one transfer worker parked, `_staging_outstanding[room] == 1`, and the deferred abort ACK unsent. Since `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` defaults to `4`, four aborted rooms with never-settling handles can exhaust the default prefill transfer worker pool.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`: `_await_handles()` now takes an optional `room` argument. While polling, if the room is already `KVPoll.Failed` and no handle has errored yet, the batch is treated as broken so the existing `NIXL_ERR_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_S` deadline bounds the wait. Both call sites in `transfer_worker()` pass `room=room`.
- The worker then exits through the existing failure path, which poisons the deferred ACK (`_deferred_ack_poisoned_rooms`) instead of sending it. This is safe: a handle that never settled does not prove the write into the decode's KV pages is over, so decode must not be told those pages are free.

## Test Plan

- New registered CPU test `test_abort_during_unsettled_transfer_does_not_park_worker` in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`. It drives the real `transfer_worker()` with a fake agent whose handle stays `PROC`, dispatches the abort notification while the worker is inside the wait, and asserts the worker exits bounded (via `KeyboardInterrupt` from the test queue), the room is `Failed`, the staging count stays `1`, and no abort ACK is sent.
- Verified red→green: the test fails on pre-fix code and passes on the fix.
- All 8 tests in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py` pass (6 subtests).
- `pre-commit run --files ...` passes on both changed files.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

discussion:
This PR addresses the same issue as #44570, with one deliberate semantic
difference in the abort path.

Both fixes make the worker's wait room-aware so an abort cannot park a
transfer worker on a handle that never settles. The divergence is what
happens to the deferred abort ACK:

- **#44570** ends the wait immediately on room abort and fires the ACK
  (`_maybe_ack_drained_abort`) right away, while the submitted handles may
  still read `PROC`.
- **This PR** keeps the wait bounded — it arms `NIXL_ERR_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_S`
  when the room is found `Failed` while polling — and lets the worker exit
  through the existing failure path, which poisons the deferred ACK instead
  of sending it.

The ACK is the prefill rank's proof that it will no longer write into the
decode's KV pages: decode-side `is_abort_release_safe` gates the page
release on receiving ACKs from every prefill rank that could still write.
A handle still reading `PROC` does not prove the write has stopped. Sending
the ACK before every handle settles can therefore make the decode release
and reuse pages that the in-flight transfer may still touch. This PR keeps
the "ACK only after every handle settles" contract, leaves the room poisoned
so no stale ACK fires later, and lets the decode-side release timeout (30s)
be the backstop for the never-settling case — while still freeing the worker
so it returns to its queue.

Both approaches unblock the worker; this one additionally preserves the
deferred-release safety invariant.

items.title: [#20460][perf] Skip unused history for single-token beam stop words
items.author: yifanQi98
items.summary: Beam-search request admission currently materializes all token histories and constructs one CPU tensor per beam even when every stop word is a single token. This PR skips that unused work and initializes the history tensor directly on CUDA for those requests.
items.body:
Beam-search request admission currently materializes all token histories and constructs one CPU tensor per beam even when every stop word is a single token. This PR skips that unused work and initializes the history tensor directly on CUDA for those requests. The shared tensor shape is preserved, including when another request needs multi-token history or triggers buffer growth. Multi-token stops, single-beam requests, and EOS/length handling retain their existing paths. No public setting or API change is introduced.

Fixes #20460

### Validation

- 36 new GPU tests pass: history materialization is skipped, the shared shape is preserved, fallback prompt suffixes are correct, stop hits/misses work in homogeneous and mixed batches, EOS/length precedence and first-finish reasons are preserved, and buffer growth/slot reuse work. Streaming and non-streaming request flags are covered at the handler level.
- The unchanged baseline passes the 27 behavior/fallback cases and fails the 9 checks that require avoiding history reads. The candidate passes all 36.
- 16 existing finish-reason/fused-finish tests pass with the candidate method.
- The new test file is covered by the existing sampler-directory entries in `l0_h100.yml` and `l0_b200.yml`.
- `pre-commit run --files ...` and `git diff --check` pass. The repository's lightweight mypy mode was used because this checkout has no compiled bindings.

The final in-tree method also passed an exact-output A/B comparison on Qwen3-0.6B at beam capacity 500: **560 measured calls**, two independent LLM startups with AB/BA order, seven cases, 20 measured calls per case/side after five warmups (a separate diagnostic call is not timed). Cases cover a real single-token stop hit, a hit on the second of multiple single-token stops, a non-hit, a multi-token stop hit, mixed requests, `ignore_eos=True`, and eight-token VBWS. Every case had one stable full-output hash per side and matching hashes between baseline and candidate. Stop hits were independently verified from the handler's `STOP_WORDS` result and early output termination. Output comparison includes the API finish-reason labels as returned, including existing rc0 beam-finalization labeling behavior.

**Runtime scope:** changes are based on `main` at `9e8e5a270ecd03919f914680581f8c1cc4e5bf25`. I cannot build current-main binaries in this environment. GPU validation used TensorRT-LLM **1.4.0rc0**, PyTorch **2.14.0+cu132**, and an RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell. Before this change, the complete affected `finish_reasons.py` file on that main revision and in the installed wheel was byte-identical (SHA-256 `d3c2323c32d877e04ce51e8c3aed7ff372cd291dc3638ce50e76418156246d50`). The candidate method was loaded directly from this PR's source into the test process; installed files were not modified. These results are not a claim that a complete current-main build was tested.

### Independent performance measurement

Qwen3-0.6B, BF16, public weights revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, beam capacity 500, no other local optimizations. These measurements preceded the in-tree patch and used an isolated prototype of this same early return against the byte-identical rc0 baseline.

| Workload | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | Latency reduction | Exploratory 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 generated tokens, submitted batch 1 | 43.364 | 42.112 | 2.89% | [2.11%, 3.66%] |
| 3 generated tokens, submitted batch 2 | 69.480 | 66.584 | 4.17% | [3.24%, 5.09%] |
| 8 generated tokens, submitted batch 2 | 161.390 | 158.750 | 1.64% | [1.16%, 2.11%] |
| Multi-token-stop fallback, 3 tokens, batch 2 | 70.268 | 70.252 | 0.02% | [-1.13%, 1.16%] |

Six independent pairs of fresh processes, alternating AB/BA; 10 warmups and 60 measured calls per case/condition. CUDA synchronization surrounds the complete `LLM.generate` call. Model initialization, warmup, instrumentation, and output hashing are excluded. Table latencies are means of six per-process medians. The reduction is calculated from the geometric mean of paired ratios, with a paired t interval on six log ratios; repeated calls within a process are not treated as independent replicates. No samples were removed.

The 2,880 measured public-model calls had identical output hashes across both conditions for each case; hashes include all returned beam token IDs, beam order, finish reasons, and the cumulative-score field (`None` with the benchmark's `logprobs=None`; numeric score parity is not measured). These fixed prompts are performance cases, so stop-hit correctness is separately covered above.

This is single-client, closed-loop latency measurement, with **no fixed QPS or saturated-throughput claim**. Submitted batch 2 means two requests per `generate`, not guaranteed co-scheduling at every executor step. The savings occur at admission/history reprocessing, not on every decode step, so the percentage benefit decreases as generation work grows. With current request conversion, `ignore_eos=True` clears stop words and does not enter this path; it receives no benefit.

**Additional validation limitation:** fixed-width-4 trials, including 32-token generation, were not internally deterministic even in the unchanged baseline. This also occurred in the `ignore_eos=True` control where this history path is never called, and persisted with overlap disabled. Those runs are retained but are **not** used as an exact-output equivalence result or a performance claim. Their cause has not been established. Small-beam stop semantics are covered by the deterministic handler tests; model-level exact parity for that regime remains inconclusive. The performance claim above is restricted to the measured wide-beam workloads.

<details>
<summary>Configuration and reproduction</summary>

- Three-token VBWS: `[20, 300, 500]`; eight-token VBWS: `[20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 300, 500]`.
- `ignore_eos=False`, explicit `stop_token_ids=[151643]`; the fallback case also supplies `stop="UNLIKELY STOP SEQUENCE 8675309"` (13 tokens).
- Prompts: `The capital of France is` and `A good way to learn mathematics is` (5 and 7 input tokens).
- `max_batch_size=32`, `max_seq_len=1024`, `max_num_tokens=1024`, KV token budget 128000, block reuse disabled, CUDA Graph batch sizes `[1, 2]`, overlap enabled.
- Run the following script in fresh baseline and candidate runtime processes, keeping the model path/settings identical. Repeat six pairs in alternating order and summarize each run by its median before computing paired ratios. The final patch requires no runtime flag. To reproduce with the installed rc0 wheel, run A without `--candidate-source`, and B with `--candidate-source /path/to/this/PR/tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/sampler/finish_reasons.py`. This optional benchmark-only overlay verifies the baseline source checksum and changes only the test process; it is not part of the runtime patch.

```python
"""Run once per fresh process on the baseline or candidate runtime."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import time

os.environ['TLLM_WORKER_USE_SINGLE_PROCESS'] = '1'
import torch
from tensorrt_llm import LLM, SamplingParams
from tensorrt_llm.llmapi import CudaGraphConfig, KvCacheConfig

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument('--model', default='Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B')
p.add_argument('--output', required=True)
p.add_argument('--candidate-source', help='PR finish_reasons.py; optional rc0 process-only overlay')
a = p.parse_args()
if a.candidate_source:
    import tensorrt_llm._torch.pyexecutor.sampler.finish_reasons as original
    baseline_sha = hashlib.sha256(Path(original.__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    assert baseline_sha == 'd3c2323c32d877e04ce51e8c3aed7ff372cd291dc3638ce50e76418156246d50'
    name = 'tensorrt_llm._torch.pyexecutor.sampler.finish_reasons_benchmark'
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, a.candidate_source)
    candidate = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = candidate
    spec.loader.exec_module(candidate)
    original.FinishReasonsHandler._get_past_tokens = candidate.FinishReasonsHandler._get_past_tokens
torch.manual_seed(1234)
llm = LLM(model=a.model, backend='pytorch', dtype='bfloat16',
          max_batch_size=32, max_beam_width=500, max_seq_len=1024,
          max_num_tokens=1024, disable_overlap_scheduler=False,
          kv_cache_config=KvCacheConfig(max_tokens=128000, enable_block_reuse=False),
          cuda_graph_config=CudaGraphConfig(batch_sizes=[1, 2]))
prompts = ['The capital of France is', 'A good way to learn mathematics is']
base = dict(n=500, best_of=500, use_beam_search=True,
            beam_width_array=[20, 300, 500], max_tokens=3,
            ignore_eos=False, detokenize=False, logprobs=None,
            stop_token_ids=[151643])
cases = [
    ('3t_b1', prompts[:1], base),
    ('3t_b2', prompts, base),
    ('8t_b2', prompts, {**base, 'max_tokens': 8,
                        'beam_width_array': [20] * 6 + [300, 500]}),
    ('multi_stop_b2', prompts, {**base, 'stop': 'UNLIKELY STOP SEQUENCE 8675309'}),
]
report = {}
try:
    for name, inputs, settings in cases:
        params = SamplingParams(**settings)
        for _ in range(10):
            llm.generate(inputs, params, use_tqdm=False)
        times, hashes = [], []
        for _ in range(60):
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            start = time.perf_counter_ns()
            outputs = llm.generate(inputs, params, use_tqdm=False)
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            times.append((time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1e6)
            value = [[[o.token_ids, str(o.finish_reason), o.cumulative_logprob]
                      for o in result.outputs] for result in outputs]
            hashes.append(hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest())
        report[name] = {'latency_ms': times, 'output_hashes': hashes}
        with open(a.output, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(report, f)
finally:
    llm.shutdown()
```

</details>

items.title: [Bugfix] Surface initial Cohere streaming errors
items.author: bzsuni
items.summary: Fix initial generation errors being silently dropped by with. Return a Cohere HTTP error response instead of HTTP 200 with only. [Discussion: Sorry there is already an open PR regarding this issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61]
items.body:
## Overview

Fix initial generation errors being silently dropped by `POST /cohere/v2/chat` with `stream=true`. Return a Cohere HTTP error response instead of HTTP 200 with only `[DONE]`.

## Claims

- Preserve the status code and message of errors in the first upstream frame.
- Preserve the first successful chunk and existing SSE behavior.
- Close the prefetched upstream generator when the response closes before body iteration or response-header delivery fails.

## Validation

Added regression tests for initial 400/503 errors, first-chunk preservation, malformed JSON, cancellation, and stream cleanup.

- Error-handling and cleanup regression cases fail without their corresponding fixes and pass afterward.
- Cohere tests excluding model integration: **234 passed**.
- HTTP and Cohere SDK integration tests with `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` on an NVIDIA H800 NVL: **9 passed** (before the final malformed-JSON adjustment and rebase).
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff and mypy.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere/ \
  --ignore=tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_chat_v2.py -q

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_chat_v2.py -q -x

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/cohere/serving.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/cohere/api_router.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_streaming.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py
```

The error cases use controlled upstream frames. The model integration tests cover normal HTTP and Cohere SDK serving.

## Details

The Cohere stream converter expects `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` frames. An initial `{"error": ...}` frame fails validation before `message-start`. Since the exception handler emits an error event only after the stream starts, the client receives HTTP 200 with only `[DONE]`.

Read the first upstream frame before creating the streaming response. Return initial errors through the existing Cohere HTTP error conversion, or forward the frame to the normal converter otherwise. Malformed JSON remains on the existing conversion path.

Since prefetching starts the upstream generator before response-body iteration, ensure it is closed even if body iteration never begins or sending response headers fails.

Response headers now wait for the first upstream frame.

items.title: [MFSDP v2] Record iteration demand order for VPP and combined 1F1B
items.author: shjwudp
items.summary: Add iteration-scoped MFSDP v2 demand recording and cursor-based replay for VPP chunk revisits and mixed forward/backward execution in combined 1F1B. The iteration scope owns recorded cursor resets; static F/B cursors reset in root hooks outside a scope.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Add iteration-scoped MFSDP v2 demand recording and cursor-based replay for VPP chunk revisits and mixed forward/backward execution in combined 1F1B. The iteration scope owns recorded cursor resets; static F/B cursors reset in root hooks outside a scope. No explicit prefetch calls are added to the compute plan. This remains a work-in-progress: GPU replay has a synchronization stall described below.

Depends on #8207. The branch includes its unmerged commit; [review the incremental implementation](https://github.com/shjwudp/Megatron-LM/compare/ac6b3111022bfb401732561beefaae1e8ae93088...feat/mfsdp-iteration-order).

- A successful first iteration records weak `(owner, phase)` occurrences, including repeated materialized owners. Prefetch gathers never enter the recording.
- Replay uses independent execution and prefetch cursors owned by `IterationOrder`. The execution cursor validates each observed demand; the prefetch cursor advances monotonically, independently of buffer materialization. Missing, extra, or changed demand invalidates the cached order; failed recordings are discarded.
- VPP and combined 1F1B entry points add an iteration-scope decorator. Ordinary non-VPP F/B schedules retain static prefetch without recording. Nested combined calls join the outer scope, and training/validation and scheduling configurations use separate cache keys.
- Existing demand hooks retain gather waits; existing release and parameter-completion hooks retain stream and gradient-readiness ownership, including delayed wgrad.
- Static F/B prefetch remains available without recording. `ExecutionOrder` removes `_unique_index` and the item argument to `advance()`, with an explicit `reset()` instead of automatic wrapping. The caller validates each returned occurrence. `prefetch(prefetch_size)` yields successors from the cursor and owns parameter-budget selection without advancing execution; it replaces `next_item(offset)`. Outside a scope, only the first root in each static F/B order resets that cursor; later roots continue it. This preserves unscoped execution of independent roots sharing a context. Comments explain why resetting every root would restart the cursor mid-pass. Recomputation skips the forward reset, and validation leaves backward progress untouched.
- Inside an iteration scope, root hooks never reset static or recorded cursors. The scope owns the weak recorded sequence, phase metadata, strict replay validation, and both replay cursors in `IterationOrder`. No static-order wrapper/cache is introduced.

## Validation

**Not ready for review:** 8-H100 combined VPP replay stalls in the eager reference on the second iteration. With default batched P2P, the stack stops in device-wide synchronization; disabling that synchronization moves the stall to MoE token dispatch stream synchronization. Separate cursors do not resolve speculative collective ordering across communication boundaries. The failing integration test remains included.

**Passed on `15e834c4c`:** 44 focused tests on 8 H100 GPUs: static cursor/prefetch, iteration/checkpoint, context, SGD across sharding strategies and accumulation counts, mixed-precision Adam, optimizer synchronization, sibling-root NVTX, checkpoint roundtrips and packed chunks, and combined 1F1B numerical tests (delayed wgrad on/off). Both checkpoint variants cover ordinary and recorded execution. Reset spies verify five forward resets and three backward resets for unscoped training/validation, and zero root-hook resets inside iteration scopes. The original unscoped shared-root fixtures are restored, including three consecutive forward passes in the shared-context test. Static cases assert prefetch-before-demand, including on the first step. The two VPP tests remain excluded from this passing selection.

**Profiler limitation:** the two selected existing overlap/budget tests fail in the unchanged profiler helper because this container's `FunctionEvent` lacks `linked_correlation_id`. No overlap timing result is claimed. Repository-wide CI remains unvalidated.

Focused local recorder checks, Ruff, isort, syntax compilation, and whitespace checks pass. Local formatting used the installed Black 24.4.2; repository-wide formatting/CI remains pending.

## Limits

Requires a stable compatible schedule across DP peers. A local divergence exception is not a distributed recovery protocol. Iteration recording is disabled for CUDA graph schedules; graph recording/replay lifecycle support and throughput/peak-memory validation are deferred.

- [x] Relevant unit and numerical integration tests added
- [ ] Repository-wide autoformat/CI completed

items.title: [Feature]: Skip unused history for single-token beam stop words
items.author: yifanQi98
items.summary: Matching those stop words only needs the newly generated token. I propose a small early return for beam-search requests whose nonempty stop-word list contains only single-token words.
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`FinishReasonsHandler._get_past_tokens()` materializes `request.get_tokens()`, builds one CPU history tensor per beam, and copies the result to CUDA even when every stop word of a beam-search request is a single token. Matching those stop words only needs the newly generated token.

I propose a small early return for beam-search requests whose nonempty stop-word list contains only single-token words. Allocate zero history directly on CUDA, preserving the handler-wide `[max_stop_word_length - 1, max_beam_width]` shape. Preserve the existing history path for multi-token stop words and single-beam requests. In mixed batches, shorter stop words are left-padded and their history positions are masked by the existing matcher.

The redundant work remains on `main` at `9e8e5a270ecd03919f914680581f8c1cc4e5bf25`. The affected source file is byte-identical to the installed TensorRT-LLM 1.4.0rc0 file used for validation.

An isolated prototype on Qwen3-0.6B / BF16 / RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell reduced complete `LLM.generate` latency by 2.89% (3 output tokens, submitted batch 1), 4.17% (3 tokens, batch 2), and 1.64% (8 tokens, batch 2), with beam capacity 500 and variable beam widths. Six independent baseline/candidate process pairs alternated AB/BA order; each case had 10 warmups and 60 timed calls. These are closed-loop latency measurements, not fixed-QPS or saturated-throughput results. A multi-token-stop fallback control showed no measurable gain.

This saves work during request admission/history reprocessing, not at every decode step. It does not change EOS/stop semantics. With the current request conversion, `ignore_eos=True` clears stop words, so this path is not called and there is no benefit.

### Alternatives

Keep the existing implementation; or optimize general multi-token history materialization separately. This proposal keeps the multi-token path unchanged and introduces no public setting or kernel.

### Additional context

I have prepared a focused implementation and regression tests covering stop hits/misses, mixed single-/multi-token requests, finish-reason precedence, buffer growth, and slot reuse. I will link the implementation PR here through its issue reference. No API-stability reference change is needed.

items.title: [perf] Long prompts are slow to preprocess with the pinned Transformers version
items.author: lbaolin
items.summary: Long prompts sent through a multimodal processor pay this cost even when they contain only text. Hugging Face already fixed this in huggingface/transformers#47580, released in Transformers 5.15.0.
items.body:
### Problem

veRL pins Transformers 5.12.1, which has a slow CPU check for image/video special tokens. Long prompts sent through a multimodal processor pay this cost **even when they contain only text**.

Hugging Face already fixed this in huggingface/transformers#47580, released in Transformers 5.15.0. veRL's default dependencies still select the older version.

### Measured result

Using veRL's processor helper with the public Qwen3.5-2B processor and a 131,084-token synthetic prompt:

| Configuration | Time per processor call |
| --- | --- |
| Transformers 5.12.1, current default | 1.58 s |
| Transformers 5.15.0 | 0.52 s |
| Transformers 5.12.1 with the workaround below | 0.38 s |

These are medians after warmup on the same CPU with identical dependencies except Transformers. Token IDs, masks and image fields matched in the tested text/image examples. This measures preprocessing; full training throughput was not tested.

### Expected behavior

Update veRL's supported dependencies so the fast processor check is available by default.

The upgrade needs coordination: pinned SGLang 0.5.20 requires Transformers 5.12.1. New SGLang 0.5.22 requires Transformers 5.19.0 **and Torch 2.14.1**, while veRL's current backends use Torch 2.13.0. Changing the Transformers pin alone would bypass those requirements.

Temporary workaround, verified for the processor examples above:

```yaml
data:
  mm_processor_kwargs:
    return_tensors: null
```

### Reproduction / system info

Python 3.12.9, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, one CPU thread, Intel Xeon Platinum 8275CL. Benchmarked veRL commit `3e0d79ea`; the helper and pins were unchanged on upstream `d400b3ec`. Public processor revision: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B@15852e8c16360a2fea060d615a32b45270f8a8fc`.

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproduction of the slow check</summary>

Run separately with Transformers 5.12.1 and 5.15.0, keeping Python/Torch identical. This isolates the token check, whose measured time was 518 ms versus 2.47 ms; the table above includes tokenization as well.

```python
from statistics import median
from time import perf_counter
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch
import transformers
from transformers.processing_utils import ProcessorMixin

torch.set_num_threads(1)
processor = SimpleNamespace(image_token="<image>", image_token_id=7)
inputs = {"input_ids": torch.tensor([[1] * 131072])}
check = ProcessorMixin._check_special_mm_tokens
check(processor, ["text without images"], inputs, ["image"])
times = []
for _ in range(5):
    start = perf_counter()
    check(processor, ["text without images"], inputs, ["image"])
    times.append(perf_counter() - start)
print(transformers.__version__, torch.__version__, median(times))
```

</details>

Related: #8255, #7471 and #8256 cover model compatibility; #8072 upgrades vLLM separately. The earlier Transformers bump #8240 was closed without merging. This issue tracks adopting the processor fix without duplicating that work.

Investigation and report prepared with AI assistance.

items.title: [Feat] dflash: Serve SpecForge MLA drafts through the target MLA attention
items.author: maocheng23
items.summary: Serve SpecForge DFlash MLA drafts (, SpecForge #758) with the target's DeepSeek MLA attention. SpecForge exports DeepSeek's MLA parameterization: the same projection names, an optional, and scaling.
items.body:
Serve SpecForge DFlash MLA drafts (`dflash_config.attention_mode: "mla"`, SpecForge #758) with the target's DeepSeek MLA attention. SpecForge exports DeepSeek's MLA parameterization: the same projection names, an optional `q_lora_rank`, `rope_interleave` and `mscale_all_dim` scaling. The draft layer is therefore a thin `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` subclass. It runs the target's absorbed-MLA forward and backend dispatch, and stores one latent row plus one RoPE key per token in `MLATokenToKVPool`.

Only the DFlash-specific parts are new:

- `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` takes `attn_type` and `sliding_window_size`. The defaults are unchanged.
- `DFlashMLAAttention`:
  - sets the layer's DFlash causality (bidirectional by default, causal with `is_causal=true` and `layer_types`);
  - loads SpecForge's separate `q_a_proj` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` into the fused down projection;
  - absorbs `kv_b_proj` into `w_kc` / `w_vc` when that weight loads;
  - projects target-context latents for the worker.
- `ModelConfig` routes an MLA draft through the existing MLA branch.
- Each MLA layer writes its own target-context KV with `DFlashMLAAttention.write_context_kv`: latent rows through `set_mla_kv_buffer`, and accepted-prefix commits through the new masked `MLATokenToKVPool.set_mla_kv_buffer_prefix_valid`. The DFlash worker and DSpark's context-KV writer both call it, so DFlash, DFlash2, Domino and DSpark drafts share one MLA path. DSpark already builds the same layers, and its fused GQA write paths are skipped for MLA drafts.
- The draft backend goes through the existing DFlash resolution: `--speculative-draft-attention-backend` if set, otherwise the target's backend, otherwise the platform fallback.
  - Two backends serve only one attention layout, and each falls back with a warning when it doesn't match the draft: `tokenspeed_mla` serves only MLA drafts, and `trtllm_mha` only non-MLA drafts.
  - A draft worker never inherits `tokenspeed_mla` from the target; it gets it only when named, which the DFlash hook does for MLA drafts. DSpark resolves its backend outside that hook and applies the `trtllm_mha` rule itself.
  - MLA backends take the draft's mask from the layer's `attn_type`. FlashInfer MLA fixes it once per batch, using the same helper the draft layers use.
  - `triton`, `flashinfer` and `tokenspeed_mla` are validated as MLA draft backends, and only `triton` serves sliding MLA layers.

The following are rejected at load or launch:

- quantized draft weights;
- `attention_bias`;
- attention sinks and value scaling;
- RoPE types other than `default`, `yarn` and `deepseek_yarn` (the target layer serves scaling as DeepSeek YaRN);
- MLA mixed with GQA/MHA layers;
- `--dcp-size > 1`.

Each backend checks its own kernel limits, such as TokenSpeed's FP8 KV and page size.

For a BF16 MLA draft, add one of these to the DFlash launch:

```bash
# FlashInfer
--speculative-draft-attention-backend flashinfer \
--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype bf16

# TokenSpeed, with tokenspeed_mla installed
--speculative-draft-attention-backend tokenspeed_mla \
--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
--page-size 32
```

Validation on one GB300 (SM103), TP1, BF16 models. Image: sglang nightly cu13 2026-10-06 (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, TokenSpeed MLA 0.1.8, Transformers 5.17.0).

At `080fb0bd70`:

- **Draft MLA tests:** `test_dflash_mla_backends.py` and `test_dflash_mla.py` passed with no skips.
  - The GPU backend test runs real `triton`, `flashinfer` and `tokenspeed_mla` kernels, with bidirectional and causal masks, eagerly and after one CUDA graph replay with changed prefixes. The reference is independent FP32 SpecForge math.
  - The GPU bounds are relative L2 below 1.2% plus element-wise tolerance 0.025 for BF16 KV, and relative L2 below 5% for TokenSpeed's FP8 KV.
  - The CPU unit test checks:
    - SpecForge reference numerics through the target MLA forward, for both Q parameterizations and both RoPE conventions;
    - loading the split checkpoint and absorbing `kv_b_proj`;
    - compressed KV pool sizing.
- **CPU:** the unit tests and the arg-hook tests pass; ruff, isort and codespell are clean.

The source at `080fb0bd70` is identical to `1663e55397`, where these broader checks ran:

- **Maximum relative L2 against FP32:**

  | Backend / KV | Max relative L2 |
  | --- | ---: |
  | triton BF16 | 0.48% |
  | flashinfer BF16 | 0.50% |
  | triton FP8 | 4.23% |
  | tokenspeed_mla FP8 | 4.52% |

- **Target MLA regressions:** the FlashInfer MLA and TokenSpeed MLA suites, Triton eagle-verify in eager and CUDA-graph modes, and the DFlash hook and draft-config tests gave 26 passed and 12 skipped (skips declared by the suites).
- **Real Engine smoke, one per draft backend:** a Qwen3 MHA target with an MLA draft checkpoint in SpecForge's split `q_a_proj` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` layout. Each run checked:
  - three rounds of 24 tokens: single, batch 2, and a repeated batch 2 with prefix-cache hits;
  - target and draft CUDA graph replay at batch sizes 1 and 2;
  - batched prefix commits into `[slots,1,576]` MLA pools, FP8 for TokenSpeed.

  The checkpoints are deterministic random weights, so this validates integration only, not acceptance rate or quality. The triton-draft smoke used a triton target, because this image's FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 is below the Engine's 0.7.1 minimum for a FlashInfer target.

Later commits, each validated on GB300 as well:

- **`a4f342b3cb` (generic draft-backend resolution and the `--dcp-size` check):** launch-time logic only; its CPU tests pass.
- **`b1d3760dec` (masked prefix commit) and `a36ebf0c0b` (`write_context_kv`):** the GPU backend test passes. Engine smokes for the triton, flashinfer and tokenspeed_mla drafts produce greedy output tokens identical to the earlier runs.
- **`ed0eb908ce` (DSpark MLA drafts):** 31 unit tests pass (38 subtests). Engine smokes with a tiny DSpark MLA draft pass on triton (static and compact ragged verify), flashinfer and tokenspeed_mla.
- **`4e62995d8e` (layout guards for draft workers):**
  - With a `trtllm_mha` target, an MLA DSpark draft builds flashinfer whether its backend is inherited or set to `trtllm_mha`.
  - An explicit triton draft keeps triton.
  - A unit test shows a draft worker no longer inherits a target's `tokenspeed_mla`.

Not yet validated: multi-rank TP, HIP, sliding MLA layers on triton, long-context RoPE scaling, and trained-checkpoint acceptance.

Compressed storage holds `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` values per token and layer, instead of per-head K and V. For latent 512, RoPE 64, 32 heads and K/V widths 192/128, that is 17.78x smaller. Measured on the previous revision: 3,203 MiB vs 180 MiB in BF16 for 32,768 tokens and five layers.

Reproduction:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_mla.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_oot_dflash_hooks.py \
  test/registered/attention/test_dflash_mla_backends.py
```

items.title: [AMD][DSV4.1Flash] Quantize MoE activations to MXFP8 before the MoRI dispatch
items.author: heachary
items.summary: MXFP4 W4A16 experts declare BF16 activations, so MoRI dispatches raw BF16 and AITER quantizes to group-32 MXFP8 on arrival. A token routed to distinct ranks is therefore quantized times — expected ~4.4 of 8 ranks at topk=6 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — and the dis…
items.body:
## Motivation

MXFP4 W4A16 experts declare BF16 activations, so MoRI dispatches raw BF16 and
AITER quantizes to group-32 MXFP8 on arrival. A token routed to `k` distinct
ranks is therefore quantized `k` times — expected ~4.4 of 8 ranks at topk=6 for
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — and the dispatch carries 2 bytes/element instead of
1 + 1/32.

Quantizing in `prepare()` moves that to once per token on the rank that owns it,
and roughly halves the dispatch payload.

AITER already consumes the result: with a pre-quantized FP8 operand and E8M0
scales, its stage-1 path sorts the scales (`mxfp4_moe_sort_fwd`) instead of
running its own quant. This mirrors the MXFP4 W4A4 dispatch added in #59596,
which takes the same pre-quantized route for a4w4.

## Summary of changes

**`all2all_utils.py`** — adds `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` and wires a third
dispatch mode into `maybe_make_prepare_finalize()`. MoRI infers the payload
dtype from the input tensor and transports `scale_dim` scales of
`scale_type_size` bytes per token, so the new branch sets
`scale_dim = hidden_dim / 32` and a 1-byte scale element. E8M0 exponents are
bytes, not the fp32 the per-token/per-tensor FP8 paths use.

**`prepare_finalize/mori.py`** — adds the `use_mxfp8_dispatch` flag and the
corresponding quant in `prepare()`, via `get_hip_quant(QuantType.per_1x32)` with
`scale_type=dtypes.fp8_e8m0`, matching the FP4 branch directly above it. The
mutual-exclusion assert becomes `sum(...) <= 1` now that there are three modes.

**Gating is deliberately narrow.** A pre-quantized operand is only safe when
AITER would have produced MXFP8 itself: a BF16-activation kernel would cast the
FP8 payload back to BF16 and never apply the scales, silently losing the
scaling. `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` therefore asks AITER directly via
`resolve_activation_dtype()`, which is documented for exactly this case ("lets a
caller that produces the activations itself -- an all-to-all dispatch, a fused
epilogue -- emit that dtype directly") and returns `None` rather than guessing
when the answer would have depended on a token count that does not exist yet.
It also fails closed on `ImportError` and on a hidden dim that is not a multiple
of 32.

## Results

8x MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP8/EP8 with `mori_high_throughput`,
speculative decoding off. 8192 in / 1024 out, 256 prompts at concurrency 64,
against a stock nightly (`0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`) with **only this change
applied** — this PR was measured on its own, with no AITER-side patches, so the
numbers are attributable to the dispatch change alone.

Engagement was confirmed rather than assumed: `resolve_activation_dtype(M=None)`
returns `torch.float8_e4m3fn` under the `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` that vLLM
pins for this model, and the dispatch kernel switches from
`EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_bf16` to `EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_fp8_ocp`.

### Performance

| Metric | Baseline | With patch | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 1103.58 | 1309.33 | **+18.6%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 9932.18 | 11783.95 | **+18.6%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 54.16 | 46.83 | **-13.5%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 54.68 | 46.69 | **-14.6%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 51.40 | 44.29 | -13.8% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3392.14 | 2248.40 | -33.7% |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 237.54 | 200.21 | -15.7% |

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, all 1319 questions.

| Arm | strict-match | stderr | Delta | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.9196 | 0.0075 | — | 0.9196 |
| With patch | 0.9280 | 0.0071 | +0.0084 | 0.9287 |

Within ~1 sigma of baseline. The same mxfp8 quantization is applied either way;
this only changes which rank performs it and how many times.

### Reproduction

Server:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1

vllm serve /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --language-model-only \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'
```

Benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 256 \
  --max-concurrency 64 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Accuracy:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,timeout=3600
```
