items.title: [rollout, vllm] fix: reject engine_kwargs that override verl-managed vLLM args
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Some vLLM args are derived from verl's own config (TP, DP, expert parallelism, LoRA, routing replay) but could also be passed through. Which source won depended on where verl wrote the derived value, and neither direction was reported: from replaced verl's, w…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Some vLLM args are derived from verl's own config (TP, DP, expert parallelism, LoRA, routing replay) but could also be passed through `rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm`. Which source won depended on where verl wrote the derived value, and neither direction was reported: `tensor_parallel_size` from `engine_kwargs` replaced verl's, while `enable_expert_parallel` was always overwritten with `expert_parallel_size > 1`. With the default `expert_parallel_size=1`, an explicit `engine_kwargs.vllm.enable_expert_parallel=True` became `False`; every GPU then held all experts (and their LoRA buffers) and vLLM reported no memory for the KV cache.

This PR keeps verl's config as the only knob for these args. `engine_kwargs` naming one of them now fails at server start with the config to set instead:

| vLLM arg | set instead |
|---|---|
| `tensor_parallel_size` | `rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size` |
| `data_parallel_size` | `rollout.data_parallel_size` |
| `enable_expert_parallel` | `rollout.expert_parallel_size` (= TP × DP) |
| `enable_lora`, `max_lora_rank` | `actor_rollout_ref.model.lora` |
| `enable_return_routed_experts` | `rollout.enable_rollout_routing_replay` |

The check replaces the delta_sharded-only TP/DP override checks. The one in-repo script that set `enable_expert_parallel` next to `expert_parallel_size` drops the redundant line, and the perf doc names the rollout config.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+enable_expert_parallel
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

- `TestEngineKwargsManagedArgs` in `tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_cli_args_on_cpu.py`: managed args (including the hyphen spelling) raise with the right config name; other args pass through.
- Ran the module in a vLLM container: 33 passed. `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks.
- [x] Update the documentation (perf best practices).
- [x] Add unit test(s).

items.title: [KV Offload] Load small CPU-tier hits synchronously within the step
items.author: kfirtoledo
items.summary: On wide-EP MoE prefill (such as GLM-5.3), a step takes 0.3 to 0.5 s. Almost every request has a small CPU-tier hit, and an async load parks it for about 2 steps although the copy takes under 1 ms.
items.body:
## Overview

On wide-EP MoE prefill (such as GLM-5.3), a step takes 0.3 to 0.5 s. Almost every request has a small CPU-tier hit, and an async load parks it for about 2 steps although the copy takes under 1 ms.

This adds an opt-in `sync_load_max_tokens` option (`kv_connector_extra_config`, default 0, off): smaller hits load in the same step.

## Claims

- Hits up to the limit load in the same step. The limit exists because the whole batch waits for the copy. A hit that would leave nothing to compute stays async.
- Sync-load blocks are hashed at allocation, so the load range is found by position. Other requests can match them in the same step, which is safe since the forward pass waits for the copy.
- The forward pass waits with a GPU stream dependency (new `OffloadingWorker.stream_wait`), not a host sync, keeping the async scheduling overlap.
- With the option at 0, behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Qwen3-30B-A3B on H100, OffloadingConnector + TieringOffloadingSpec. 12k-token prefix in GPU cache, 2k-token tail only in the CPU tier. Median extra TTFT vs a GPU-hit control, 12 reps:

| Setup | Without fix | With fix (limit 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 node: DP=2 + EP | +272 ms | ~0 ms |
| 2 nodes: TP=8, DP=2, EP over 16 GPUs | +344 ms | +8 ms |

Measured with an earlier host-wait version; `stream_wait` not yet run end to end.

Correctness: greedy continuation with the tail served from the CPU tier is correct 7/7.

    pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/   # 576 passed
    pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py         # 41 passed

## Details

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds sync offload loads (closest: #60574, #58198).

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6621362][fix] Unblock Python disagg transfers stalled by a context-side timeout
items.author: bo-nv
items.summary: Fixes https://nvbugs/6621362: fails on H100 with an aiperf error rate of 75-100% (HTTP 500s). The generation worker ends up permanently deadlocked:, request fetch frozen, part of its KV cache still held, and every later request times out at the router.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes https://nvbugs/6621362: `disaggregated/test_disaggregated.py::test_disaggregated_stress_test[input8k-output1k-conc512-qwen3_5_4b_fp8_stress]` fails on H100 with an aiperf error rate of 75-100% (HTTP 500s). The generation worker ends up permanently deadlocked: `num_scheduled_requests = 0`, request fetch frozen, part of its KV cache still held, and every later request times out at the router.

### Root cause

Three defects on the Python V2 transceiver route (`transceiver_runtime` auto → PYTHON for Qwen3.5) combine whenever the generation worker is the bottleneck, i.e. its request queue makes a peer wait longer than `kv_transfer_timeout_ms` (60 s) before it asks for the KV:

1. **The context-side transfer clock counts the peer's queueing delay.** It starts when the send is posted, but nothing is written until the generation peer sends REQUEST_DATA. With generation `max_batch_size` below the offered concurrency, that request waits in the generation queue, the context send expires before the peer ever asks, and the TxSession is cancelled and cleared.
2. **A late REQUEST_DATA is never answered.** `Sender._respond_with_kv` treats a REQUEST_DATA for a session that is not registered as an early generation-first request and parks it. For a session that was already cleared, nothing ever replies, so the peer's receive task stays TRANSFERRING forever and pins its KV pages and batch slot.
3. **An idle generation worker never acts on its own receive timeout.** Without in-flight cancellation, a timed-out generation receive is cancelled only in `_handle_responses`, which runs only after a forward step. Once every generation slot holds such a receive, nothing is scheduled, the response pass never runs, and the worker stops admitting requests for good.

### Fix

- `Sender` (native/transfer.py) remembers cleared TxSession ids for a while (`_RETIRED_SESSION_TTL_S`) and answers a REQUEST_DATA for one of them FAILED. It matches on the peer's `sender_req_id` too, so a retried generation request whose session is gone is answered as well. Early generation-first REQUEST_DATA is still parked as before.
- `DisaggTransferCoordinator.poll_gen_transfers` cancels timed-out generation receives every iteration, independent of a forward step. It uses the same `cancel_request` + cancelled-session reap path the response pass uses, skips user-cancelled requests, and does not fail a request twice under multi-rank ADP.
- The context transfer clock is moved along while the send still waits for its peer to ask. This uses a new `KvCacheTransceiver.context_transfer_is_waiting_for_peer` hook: it defaults to False, so the C++ runtime is unchanged, and `KvCacheTransceiverV2` implements it from the sender's peer-request bookkeeping. The wait is bounded at 3x `kv_transfer_timeout_ms` so a send whose peer never asks is still reclaimed.
- Removes the test's waiver (`tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt`).

### Relation to other PRs

- #17948 (closed): its named exit, `_deliver_kv_to_agent` with no session, is not the one hit here; the hit exit is `_respond_with_kv`. Its context peer-wait rebase idea is right and is adopted here with the same 3x ceiling, together with the two missing pieces (2 and 3).
- #18517 (main): it fixes the rid mismatch for retried generation requests while the context session is still live. That is complementary. This PR only covers a retried request whose context session was already cleared.

## Test Coverage

Clean A/B on 2x H100 NVL (computelab), release/1.3 `42ca6baa81` with and without this change: two fresh worktrees, the same precompiled CI wheel and environment, differing only by this commit. The diagnostic rows change only the test YAML and were not committed. They put the generation worker in the bottleneck that the CI runs hit; on this node the stock config leaves context as the bottleneck.

| Stress test config | release/1.3 | release/1.3 + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| stock | 0/2705 errors, GSM8K 0.761, PASS | 0/2705 errors, GSM8K 0.756, PASS |
| `kv_transfer_timeout_ms: 30000` | 0/2705, GSM8K 0.766, PASS | 0/2705, GSM8K 0.754, PASS |
| generation `max_batch_size: 48` | 0/2705, GSM8K 0.751, PASS | (not run) |
| generation `max_batch_size: 24` | **75.71% errors (2048 x HTTP 500), FAIL**: 196 context timeouts, 24 generation timeouts, generation worker deadlocked | **0/2705 errors, GSM8K 0.758, PASS**: 0 context/generation timeouts |

- `accuracy/test_disaggregated_serving.py::TestQwen3_5_4B::test_mismatched_block_reuse`: 71.0 (release/1.3) vs 76.0 (with this PR), both PASS.
- New unit tests (CPU):
  - `tests/unittest/_torch/disaggregation/test_disagg_coordinator_transfers.py`: idle poll cancels and fails a timed-out receive, retries a refused cancel through the reap, leaves user cancels alone, and fails once under ADP; the context clock ignores the peer wait and still times out past the ceiling.
  - `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_transfer_ownership_regressions.py`: a REQUEST_DATA for a cleared session is failed rather than parked, including the retried-rid case; an early generation-first REQUEST_DATA is still parked; the tombstone expires; the V2 peer-wait hook.
  - `tests/unittest/_torch/disaggregation/` and the disaggregated transfer/task-handle/bounce unit tests all pass.

Not verified: H100 SXM (no node available); the other waivers filed under this bug (`gpt_oss_120b_eagle_triton_stress`, `full:B200/...qwen3_32b_fp8_stress`) are left in place; #18517's live-session retry case; the port to main.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
- The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR.

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

items.title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the DSpark draft SWA out of the radix tree
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Evicting the draft's SWA then cut prefix hits on Main KV the target could still reuse (#42716 skips the same match gate). No pool needs, so the tree holds no SWA component.
items.body:
- Under `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` the target already keeps SWA in a per-request window, but the DSpark draft still forced a paged SWA allocator, so the radix tree kept an SWA component only the draft used. Evicting the draft's SWA then cut prefix hits on Main KV the target could still reuse (#42716 skips the same match gate).
- The DSpark draft SWA now lives in a per-request ring on CUDA: `swa_ring_rows` (`req_pool_idx * ring + pos % ring`) and `get_draft_swa_ring_size` (sliding window + max draft tokens) own its layout for every reader and writer. No pool needs `needs_paged_swa_allocator`, so the tree holds no SWA component.
- Writes reuse the existing ring path (`_ring_inject_loc`, and `build_unified_commit_inject_layout` renamed to `build_ring_commit_inject_layout`), now keyed on the draft pool's `swa_req_ring_size` instead of the unified_kv gate.
- Reads: `get_dspark_swa_page_indices` builds the draft window from the ring (`BuildDsparkSwaRingIndices`), and the draft block writes its ring rows, both eagerly and in the graph.
- A request placed by a prefix hit starts its ring at the hit (`swa_req_ring_valid_from`), so the draft masks earlier positions instead of reading rows left by the slot's previous request.
- The ring is budgeted as a fixed reservation next to the request windows instead of per SWA token.

Only DeepSeek-V4.1 with encoder SWA bounded replay and DSpark on CUDA changes; HIP keeps the paged draft SWA, and every other configuration is unchanged. After a prefix hit, the draft attends only to rows written since the hit until its window fills again.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (4x GB300, TP4, DSpark, encoder replay), a prompt whose draft SWA was evicted by 400 other prompts re-hits 8448 of its 8565 tokens instead of 0. GSM8K stays at 98.0% with and without decoder replay, and the average accept length is 3.81 against 3.78 before.

items.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Accept residual and skip_bias in the ROCm Conv3d-to-Conv2d VAE patch
items.author: yichiche
items.summary: The ROCm Conv3d-to-Conv2d replacement installs its own that only takes, so the decoder's first patched conv call raises. Reproduced with Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on gfx1250: denoising completes, then DecodingStage fails.
items.body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
Wan VAE decode on ROCm fails with `TypeError: RocmPlatform._replace_conv3d_with_conv2d.<locals>._patched_forward() got an unexpected keyword argument 'residual'`. #38650 made the Wan VAE decoder call `WanCausalConv3d` with `residual=` and `skip_bias=` (the fused conv-bias epilogue). The ROCm Conv3d-to-Conv2d replacement installs its own `forward` that only takes `(x, cache_x)`, so the decoder's first patched conv call raises.

**Where it shows up**
Any ROCm device that enables the patch (`SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D=1` or `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D_BF16=1`) and decodes with the Wan VAE through the non-fused cache path. Reproduced with Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on gfx1250: denoising completes, then DecodingStage fails.

**How to fix**
Accept `residual` and `skip_bias` in the patched forward with the same contract as `WanCausalConv3d.forward`: drop the bias when `skip_bias` is set, add `residual` to the conv output.

## Modifications

- `runtime/platforms/rocm.py`: `_patched_forward` takes `residual=None, skip_bias=False`, passes `None` as bias when `skip_bias`, and adds `residual` to the output.
- `test/unit/test_rocm_conv3d_patch.py`: regression test that the patched conv matches the original `WanCausalConv3d` with `residual` and with `skip_bias`. It fails on the pre-fix code with the same `TypeError` and passes with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Patched vs original conv, fp32 (residual / skip_bias) | `TypeError` | max abs diff 1.9e-6 |
| Patched vs original conv, BF16 compute, channels_last_3d (96ch, 90x160) | `TypeError` | rel. error 0.17% to 0.34%, no NaN |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720, 33 frames, gfx1250 | DecodingStage `TypeError` | decodes; correct content across frames |

Long-video (193-frame) validation is still in progress and will be added.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 1280x720x193f, VAE decode | crash | 119.6 s |

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

items.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Keep gfx1250 FlyDSL BF16 attention out of torch.compile
items.author: yichiche
items.summary: On gfx1250, aiter (ROCm/aiter#5168) routes that call to the FlyDSL kernel, which JIT-compiles in Python. Dynamo traces into it, FlyDSL's sees an MLIR context and takes the nested-trace branch, and then finds no context and raises.
items.body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
With `--enable-torch-compile`, the first DiT forward on gfx1250 fails inside the aiter attention backend with `RuntimeError: An MLIR function requires a Context but none was provided`. #27702 removed `@torch.compiler.disable` from `AITerImpl.forward` so the BF16 `aiter.flash_attn_func` call could be compiled. On gfx1250, aiter (ROCm/aiter#5168) routes that call to the FlyDSL `flash_attn_batch_m32x8` kernel, which JIT-compiles in Python. Dynamo traces into it (`torch_dynamo_resume_in_flash_attn_batch_m32x8_at_2181`), FlyDSL's `JitFunction.__call__` sees an MLIR context and takes the nested-trace branch, and `capture_user_location` then finds no context and raises.

**Where it shows up**
Only gfx1250 with the aiter attention backend and torch.compile. On gfx942/gfx950, `flash_attn_func` dispatches to CK/ASM kernels that compile fine, so they keep the compiled path from #27702. Reproduced with Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on one gfx1250 GPU (`--enable-torch-compile true --regional-compile --attention-backend aiter`); the warmup request fails in DenoisingStage.

**How to fix**
On gfx1250, call the BF16 `flash_attn_func` through a `@torch.compiler.disable` helper, so the FlyDSL kernel runs eagerly while the rest of the DiT block stays compiled.

## Modifications

- `runtime/platforms/aiter.py`: add `USE_AITER_GFX1250`.
- `runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`: move the BF16 call into `_forward_bf16`; on gfx1250 route through `_forward_bf16_eager` (`@torch.compiler.disable`). gfx942/gfx950 and NVIDIA paths are unchanged.
- `test/unit/test_aiter_attention_impl.py`: regression test that compiles `AITerImpl.forward` with gfx1250 enabled and asserts `flash_attn_func` runs outside Dynamo. It fails on the pre-fix code (`[True] != [False]`) and passes with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 1x gfx1250, 1280x720, 8 steps, seed 42, torch.compile + aiter attention (with the VAE fix from the companion PR applied so decode completes):

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Warmup / first request | `RuntimeError: An MLIR function requires a Context` in DenoisingStage | completes |
| FlyDSL `flash_attn_func` vs PyTorch SDPA (B=1, H=40, D=128) | - | max abs diff 2e-3 at S=4096, 2e-4 at S=90000, no NaN |
| 33-frame video | no output | correct content (cat and dog baking in a kitchen), consistent across frames |

Long-video (193-frame) validation is still in progress and will be added.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 1280x720x193f, 8 steps, denoise time per step | crash | 7.73 s |

The extra cost is one graph break per attention call on gfx1250 only. Wrapping the FlyDSL path as an opaque custom op in aiter would remove it; then this workaround can be dropped.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.

items.title: [CI][ROCm][Bugfix] DeepSeek V4.1: don't pass expert intermediate padding to AITER
items.author: micah-wil
items.summary: Hotfixes NaN outputs in DeepSeek V4.1 ROCm decode by passing intermediate_pad=0 to AITER, since FlyDSL MoE leaves padded intermediate columns unwritten.
items.body:
AITER 0.1.25's FlyDSL MoE (ROCm/aiter#6125 configs) leaves the padded intermediate columns unwritten when told about the padding, so stage 2 reads stale memory and small decode batches (M <= 4 tokens) can come out NaN. This hits DeepSeek V4.1 at TP4, where the per-rank expert intermediate size is padded 576 -> 640.

Pass intermediate_pad=0 for V4.1's routed experts so AITER computes over the zero padding instead of skipping it, which is exact. DeepSeek V4 never pads the expert intermediate size and is unchanged. Revert once vLLM pins an AITER with the fix https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6598.

This hotfix was developed to resolve the flakiness in the newly added test group `(MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics`

#### lm-eval results:
| Run | Concurrency | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSv4.1-Flash TP4 + hotfix | 64 | 0.9242 ± 0.0073 | 0.9249 ± 0.0073 |
| DSv4.1-Flash TP4 + hotfix | 2 | 0.9375 ± 0.0121 | 0.9375 ± 0.0121 |

items.title: [Perf][Multimodal] Chunk Qwen3-VL vision blocks to cut the encoder profiling peak
items.author: toan-tq
items.summary: At startup, vLLM profiles the Qwen3-VL-family vision tower (Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 VLMs) on one max-size image (65,536 patches). The activation peak of that eager pass is about 12× the hidden states, and the KV cache loses that memory.
items.body:
## Overview

At startup, vLLM profiles the Qwen3-VL-family vision tower (Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 VLMs) on one max-size image (65,536 patches). The activation peak of that eager pass is about 12× the hidden states, and the KV cache loses that memory. This PR runs the per-token parts of each vision block in 8,192-token chunks for images above that size, which brings the peak down to about 5×. On a 32 GB RTX 5090 serving Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, that gives the KV cache about 1 GiB more, or +14.6 % tokens.

Related: #51537 (open) removes the q/k copy in the same `Qwen2_5_VisionAttention` code to cut latency, and says it leaves the tower-level peak unchanged. The two changes are independent. #49540 changes what the language-model side profiles, not the encoder.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 on 1× RTX 5090: the startup activation peak (CUDA-graph estimate excluded) drops from about 1.69 to 0.70 GiB, and the KV cache grows from 86,935 to 99,641 tokens (+14.6 %) at `--max-num-seqs 32` and from 82,923 to 95,629 (+15.3 %) at `--max-num-seqs 100`.
- On a KV-bound load (1k in / 256 out, concurrency 64), the most requests running at once goes from 25 to 29. Output throughput is +4 to +5 % (3/3 pairs), and median TTFT at concurrency 32 is 27–35 % lower.
- Vision tower latency is unchanged (0.99–1.01×). Images with ≤ 8,192 patches never take the new path, so their output is unchanged.
- Images with more than 8,192 patches (about 2.1 MP) get different bf16 rounding. They are no further from an fp32 reference than before (table below).

## Validation

Setup: 1× RTX 5090 32 GB (power capped at 500 W), main at a8be1500ba, torch 2.14.0+cu130, `vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs {32,100}`. All other options are defaults (MRv2, CUDA graphs, FLASH_ATTN ViT backend, prefix caching). A = main, B = this PR. Each server start was repeated, and the memory numbers are identical across repeats. The GPU runs used an earlier revision of this commit. The only differences are that the backend check is now inlined and `is_compiling()` is checked first; neither changes the eager path.

**Memory / capacity** (from the engine's startup log)

| max-num-seqs | activation peak A → B | KV tokens A → B | max running (c=64) A → B |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 (2 starts/arm) | 1.69 → 0.70 GiB | 86,935 → 99,641 (+14.6 %) | 25 → 29 |
| 100 (2 starts/arm) | 1.69 → 0.70 GiB | 82,923 → 95,629 (+15.3 %) | 24 → 27 |

With image/video profiling turned off (`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'`, warm compile cache), the floor from the language model alone is 0.27–0.28 GiB, so after this PR the peak (0.70 GiB) still comes from the vision tower.

**Serving** (`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --request-rate inf`, 96 prompts at c=32 and 192 at c=64). The three pairs are A/B run back to back:

| pair | output tok/s c=32 | output tok/s c=64 | median TTFT c=32 | median TTFT c=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 seqs, pair 1 | 769.7 → 764.9 (−0.6 %) | 772.0 → 812.3 (+5.2 %) | 1187 → 863 ms | 9944 → 10017 ms |
| 32 seqs, pair 2 | 831.7 → 845.7 (+1.7 %) | 850.2 → 885.4 (+4.1 %) | 1232 → 807 ms | 9310 → 9360 ms |
| 100 seqs | 733.6 → 772.3 (+5.3 %) | 727.5 → 765.2 (+5.2 %) | 1351 → 902 ms | 13420 → 9881 ms |

This workload has a lot of prefill, and B runs more requests per step, so TPOT goes up by about 5–10 % at 32 seqs (it is flat at 100 seqs). Throughput moves much less than capacity. Absolute numbers differ between pairs: the first start of each pair compiled from a cold cache and the second loaded a warm one. Each pair compares like with like.

**Vision tower alone** (real Qwen3.8 vision weights, synthetic inputs, median of 5 runs; peak measured above the inputs)

| patches | peak A → B | latency B/A | B vs A | A vs fp32 ref | B vs fp32 ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65,536 (profiled max) | 1.696 → 0.716 GiB | 0.995 | rel-L2 2.05e-2 | 2.34e-2 | 2.12e-2 |
| 24,576 | 0.636 → 0.337 GiB | 0.989 | rel-L2 1.93e-2 | 2.33e-2 | 2.42e-2 |
| 12,288 (two images, chunked) | 0.321 → 0.231 GiB | 1.008 | bit-exact | | |
| 4,096 | 0.106 → 0.097 GiB | 1.002 | bit-exact | | |

Repeated runs of A are bit-exact. The fp32 reference is the same tower in fp32 with SDPA. The chunked 12,288-patch case is bit-exact, which suggests the differences at larger sizes come from GEMM kernel selection at different M rather than from the chunked code path. I have not tested that directly.

**End-to-end accuracy:** I ran DocVQA validation on 200 questions whose images are larger than 2.2 MP (2.6 MP and larger, so all of them go through the chunked path), greedy, 8 concurrent requests, both arms sharing one compile cache. ANLS went from 0.9622 to 0.9614 (−0.0008; paired bootstrap 95 % CI [−0.018, +0.015]), with 183/200 answers identical. I did not run A against itself, and batching across concurrent requests is not deterministic, so the 17 differing answers are not all due to this PR.

**Tests**
- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_qwen3_vl_vision.py`: 1 passed (CPU, fp32). The test runs a tiny tower with chunk boundaries inside an image and across two images, checks that every block takes the chunked path, and compares the result with the unchunked path. It caught 6/6 injected bugs: wrong RoPE slice, dropped residual, wrong MLP, misplaced K, wrong sin slice, and residual not added after proj.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passed.
- CI: the test is marked `cpu_test`, like `test_conformer_encoder.py` and `test_aria.py` in the same folder. As far as I can tell, no current Buildkite step runs those files. The Qwen3-VL `core_model` tests use images below the threshold, so CI does not exercise the chunked path on GPU.

## Details

- **Where the peak comes from:** while the attention half of a block runs, the eager pass holds the residual, `norm1(x)`, qkv (3u), the contiguous q/k copy (2u), the rotated q/k (2u), the context and the projection. The MLP half holds fc1 and its GELU (3.7u each). `pos_embeds` (1u) also stays alive for the whole forward. Here u = tokens × hidden × 2 B, which is 0.14 GiB for the max image.
- **Change:** in `Qwen3_VisionBlock.forward`, for inputs longer than `_VIT_CHUNK_TOKENS` (8,192) and only when the block is not being compiled, `_forward_chunked` does the following:
  1. Writes norm1 → qkv → RoPE chunk by chunk into preallocated q/k/v buffers.
  2. Runs attention once over the whole sequence, with the same varlen call and `cu_seqlens` as before.
  3. Computes `x + proj(context)` chunk by chunk into a new buffer.
  4. Adds the MLP output in place, chunk by chunk.

  Separately, `Qwen3_VisionTransformer.forward` releases `pos_embeds` once it has been added, but only when it created the metadata itself.
- **Scope:** the chunked path is used with FLASH_ATTN / ROCM_AITER_FA and TORCH_SDPA. It is not used with FlashInfer (cuDNN expects V at the interleaved QKV stride) or with FP8 ViT attention, which quantizes Q/K/V itself. In both cases behavior is the same as today. The `is_compiling()` check comes first, so a compiled encoder (`compile_mm_encoder=True`) traces the same graph as before and gets no size guard.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, TP > 1 for the vision tower (the row-parallel `proj` and MLP `fc2` then each do one all-reduce per chunk, so up to 16 per block for the max image instead of 2), and encoder CUDA graphs with a budget above 8,192 tokens.
- **Where it matters:** GPUs whose KV pool is small compared with the encoder peak. On a 5090, the default `max_num_seqs=256` does not start with or without this PR (OOM while profiling CUDA graph memory; with that fixed, vLLM rejects 256 seqs because only 113 Mamba blocks fit). The gains above are for the reduced `--max-num-seqs` that 5090 users already have to set. On 80 GB GPUs I expect a few percent at most; I have not measured that.
- **Duplicate check:** I searched open and closed PRs for ViT/vision encoder chunking and peak memory (Qwen3-VL, qwen3_vl, MMEncoderAttention, encoder profiling) and found no PR doing this. #51537 and #43580 touch the same code for other reasons.

cc @Isotr0py

items.title: [Fix] [XPU] vision: Keep padded image batches aligned with cu_seqlens in xpu_attn
items.author: desmond-intel
items.summary: On Intel XPU, sometimes answers an image question with repeated until the output limit. On POPE, 126 of 9000 answers came back like this.
items.body:
## Motivation

On Intel XPU, `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6` sometimes answers an image question with `!` repeated until the output limit. On POPE, 126 of 9000 answers came back like this. The affected questions change on every server restart, but stay the same within one server.

Cause:
- The Idefics2 vision encoder pads the image slices in a batch to one common length, `(bsz, seq_len)`. `cu_seqlens`, however, holds the real slice lengths.
- `VisionIntelXPUAttention` passed the padded `q/k/v` and those `cu_seqlens` to `flash_attn_varlen_func`.
- So every slice after a padded one attended over the wrong rows. The real rows past `cu_seqlens[-1]` were never written; the kernel output comes from `new_empty`, so they keep leftover memory.
- When that memory holds NaN, the logits become NaN and argmax returns token 0 (`!`).
- The encoded image is cached, so every question on that image fails until the server restarts.

## Modifications

- `VisionIntelXPUAttention.forward`: when `bsz > 1` and the row count differs from `cu_seqlens[-1]`:
  1. gather the real rows,
  2. run the varlen kernel on the packed tensors,
  3. scatter the result back into a zero-initialized padded output.
  `VisionAscendAttention` already handles this layout the same way (see also #43748).
- No other path changes. `bsz == 1` (packed encoders such as Qwen-VL) skips the check entirely. Unpadded batches still make the original single kernel call.
- New test `test_xpu_attn_padded_batch_attends_within_each_image` in `test/registered/xpu/test_vision_backend_selection.py`. It uses slice lengths 1036/1014/1014 and head_dim 72, from a failing MiniCPM-o batch. It fails on main and passes with this change.

Note for reviewers: the `fa3`, `fa4` and `triton_attn` vision backends receive the same padded layout with packed `cu_seqlens`. This PR does not change them.

## Accuracy Tests

lmms_eval `pope` on `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6`: full set (9000), seed 42, Intel Arc Pro B60, tp-size 2.

| | pope_accuracy | pope_f1_score | `!!!!` answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 86.84 | 87.29 | 126 |
| this PR | **88.09** | **87.30** | **0** |
| H200 reference (CUDA, tp-size 1) | 88.09 | 87.28 | 0 |

```bash
sglang serve --model-path openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6 --device xpu --tp-size 2 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --trust-remote-code --enable-multimodal --attention-backend triton
python3 -m lmms_eval --model openai \
  --model_args model_version=openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6,num_concurrent=16 \
  --tasks pope --batch_size 16 --seed 42
```

Unit test on B60: `pytest test/registered/xpu/test_vision_backend_selection.py`. On main: 1 failed, 4 passed. With this PR: 5 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Only padded batches of more than one image (`bsz > 1`) take the new path. That path adds one gather/scatter of q/k/v per encoder layer. POPE end to end took about 12 min both before and after (12:11 vs 12:32, on separate server runs).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Remove stale `--uds` socket files so a server can restart on the same path
items.author: kuatovakamila
items.summary: Removes stale Unix domain socket files before binding so vllm serve can restart on the same --uds path without requiring manual cleanup.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61959. `vllm serve --uds <path>` could not be restarted on the same path: the socket file was never removed, so the second start failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use` although nothing was listening. Remove a stale socket file before binding and remove our own file on shutdown.

## Claims

- Restarting on the same `--uds` path works without an external `rm` of the socket file (verified end to end on an A100, before/after below).
- A path that a live server still listens on is not taken over: the connect probe succeeds, the file is left alone, and `bind` fails with `EADDRINUSE` exactly as before.
- A regular (non-socket) file at the path is never deleted; `bind` fails on it as before.
- The process that bound the socket removes the file on shutdown: single API server (`run_server`), the multi-API-server launcher (after its workers, which share the socket, have exited), the render server and the snapshot server. Workers in `run_server_worker` do not remove it, so one exiting worker cannot unlink the file under its siblings.
- TCP serving is untouched; the new code runs only when `--uds` is set.

## Validation

**CPU tests** (new `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_unix_socket.py`, no model): stale file replaced and connectable; live listener not taken over (`EADDRINUSE`, still reachable); regular file left alone; `remove_unix_socket_file` removes a socket file, ignores a missing path, leaves a regular file. `4 passed`. The stale-file case fails on `main` with `[Errno 98] Address already in use`.

**End to end** (1x A100-40GB, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enforce-eager`, start → request over the socket → `SIGTERM` → start again on the same path):

| | before (v0.31.0; `create_server_unix_socket` is identical on main) | after (this PR's commit cherry-picked onto v0.31.0, identical hunks) |
|---|---|---|
| socket file after clean shutdown | still present | removed |
| second start on the same path | exits during startup: `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use` | healthy after ~55 s, `/health` → 200; file removed again after the second shutdown |

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy, SPDX and the other local hooks).

## Details

`create_server_unix_socket` now calls `_remove_stale_unix_socket(path)` first: if `path` exists and is a socket, it connects to it; `ConnectionRefusedError` means no server is behind the file and it is unlinked (with a warning in the log); a successful connect or any other `OSError` leaves the file for `bind()` to report. This mirrors what asyncio does for `create_unix_server(path=...)`, which uvicorn relies on in its own `--uds` mode, but is more conservative: asyncio removes any socket file, this only removes one nothing listens on.

`remove_unix_socket_file(path)` unlinks the file only if it is a socket and ignores a missing file. It is called in the `finally` of each socket owner next to the existing `sock.close()`; in `run_multi_api_server` it runs after the API server manager, engines and coordinator have been shut down.

Not changed: abstract-namespace sockets (paths starting with NUL) never create a file and go through the same code without effect.

items.title: fix: bound decoded client audio resource usage
items.author: Bsgg1
items.summary: Bound decoded client audio before an unbounded waveform is retained, addressing the compressed-audio expansion reported in #43708. This budget is not a peak RSS or aggregate concurrency limit.
items.body:
## Summary

Bound decoded client audio before an unbounded waveform is retained, addressing the compressed-audio expansion reported in #43708.

- Add `--max-audio-decoded-bytes` (256 MiB by default; `0` disables) and optional `--max-audio-duration-seconds`, with argument validation and documentation. This budget is **not** a peak RSS or aggregate concurrency limit.
- Enforce the limits on TorchCodec, SoundFile, and PyAV/container decoding paths. Preserve limit errors instead of masking them in decoder fallbacks, and cover additional streaming ASR, transcription, and model-specific decoding paths.
- Add tests for encoded-to-decoded expansion, decoder budgets, argument validation, and the transcription handler's HTTP 400 response without model dispatch.

## Validation

- H20 host with real TorchCodec 0.17.0+cu130, PyAV 19.0.1, and SoundFile 0.14.0: a 5,588-byte, 120-second silent FLAC was rejected at a 30-second duration cap or a 1 MiB decoded-byte budget; a 16 MiB budget allowed decoding to a 7,680,000-byte float32 waveform on the TorchCodec path.
- Transcription and server-argument suites: **37 passed, 6 subtests passed**. The new handler-level test confirms status 400 and no model dispatch for an over-duration input.
- Audio container suite on the same host: **19 passed, 1 skipped, 8 subtests passed** using a temporary test copy that skips the AMR-only case; the host's FFmpeg build lacks the optional `libopencore_amrnb` encoder, so the unmodified suite fails during shared fixture setup before individual tests run.

items.title: [None][infra] Get changed files from base_commit for merge queue L0 builds
items.author: weiminwang-nv
items.summary: The merge queue runs L0MergeRequest.groovy on a commit that has no GitHub PR and no GitLab MR. Today such a build falls into the GitLab MR branch of the changed-file code, calls, fails to parse the 404 reply, and goes on with an empty changed file list.
items.body:
## Description

The merge queue runs L0_MergeRequest.groovy on a commit that has no GitHub PR and no GitLab MR. Today such a build falls into the GitLab MR branch of the changed-file code, calls `projects/null/merge_requests/null/diffs`, fails to parse the 404 reply, and goes on with an empty changed file list. So CBTS, auto trigger tags, the multi-GPU check and the waive list merge all run without knowing what changed.

This PR adds an optional `base_commit` field to `gitlabTriggerPhrase`. The merge queue wrapper sets it to the merge base of the queue commit and `main`.

All callers that read changed files or diffs (changed file list, one-file diff, CBTS diffs, maintenance config check) now go through one function, `getMRChangedFile`, which picks the source:

- When `github_pr_api_url` is set: the GitHub PR files API, with the internal Git mirror as the fallback (as before).
- Else, when `base_commit` is set: `base_commit..gitlabCommit`, read from the internal Git mirror. This reuses `getGitMirrorMRChangedFile` (the existing fallback for GitHub PRs); it now fetches `base_commit` by SHA instead of the `prjob/<n>/base` branch.
- Else: the GitLab MR API, as before.

One behavior change for GitHub PRs: the maintenance config check called the GitHub API without the Git mirror fallback; it now gets the fallback like the other callers.

All callers run after `${LLM_ROOT}` is checked out, which the git diff needs.

The merge base is an ancestor of the queue commit that the wrapper pushes to the mirror, so it can be fetched by SHA even when the mirror's `main` has not synced it yet.

## Test Coverage

- Not yet run in Jenkins. Plan: run the merge queue wrapper (`LLM/Sandbox/weimin/L0_MergeQueue_wrapper`) with this branch as the commit under test, and check that the L0 build logs the expected changed file list.
- Fetching a non-tip commit by SHA from the GitLab mirror with `--depth=1` was checked by hand.
- No change for GitHub PR and GitLab MR builds: those paths are not touched.
