items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve Cohere and Anthropic streaming errors
items.author: KuanJia
items.summary: Fixes lost streaming errors in Cohere and Anthropic API frontends by exposing raw chat chunks and converting at output boundaries without intermediate JSON serialization.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve parser and generation failures in Cohere and Anthropic streaming responses. Follow the [review feedback](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61947#discussion_r4291298497) by exposing raw chat chunks from the shared generator and converting them at each API's output boundary.

## Claims

- Add `OpenAIServingChat.chat_completion_stream_generator_raw`, yielding `ChatCompletionStreamResponse | ErrorResponse` without SSE framing.
- Convert raw objects directly in Cohere and Anthropic, removing intermediate JSON serialization and reparsing. Both preserve the sanitized original error before or during output and close active blocks before the terminal error event.
- Preserve OpenAI's JSON fields, usage metadata and `[DONE]` termination, including when output serialization itself fails.

## Validation

| Targeted CPU tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Cohere protocol, routes and conversion | 213 passed |
| Anthropic request/response and stream conversion | 112 passed |
| OpenAI streaming, reasoning usage, logprobs and parallel tool parsing | 135 passed across two selections |
| Total | **460 passed** |

- The four new Anthropic error cases fail before the fix. Regression cases cover errors before the first chunk and during text, thinking and tool-use blocks.
- HTTP and official SDK checks pass for all three APIs across normal output, parser failure, early generation failure and failure after text output. Cohere/Anthropic checks also forbid intermediate `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` JSON serialization/parsing.
- A comparison against the published PR's original OpenAI generator matches JSON frames and final request metadata for 128 normal configurations and two error cases. Configurations vary usage, continuous usage, echo, token IDs, prompt text, fingerprint and `n=1/2`.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and test CI association, and `git diff --check` pass. Existing Buildkite entrypoint jobs cover all three test files.
- Validation uses controlled engine outputs without model weights or GPU execution. No model-generation, accuracy or performance evaluation was run.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_conversion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_streaming.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/cohere -q

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/anthropic -q

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion \
  -k 'streaming_chunks_keep_usage_and_metadata or streaming_errors_preserve_envelope or streaming_serialization_failure_emits_error_and_done or chat_streaming_metrics_ride_on_usage_chunk or streaming_reasoning_usage_counts_across_deltas or streaming_reasoning_usage_lifecycle_edges or streaming_logprobs_kept_when_parser_suppresses_delta' -q

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion \
  -k streaming_n_gt1_independent_tool_parsers -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/cohere/serving.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_streaming.py \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py

git diff --check
```

</details>

## Details

The shared generator can produce either a normal chat chunk or an `ErrorResponse`. Both API adapters previously expected serialized normal chunks, so an error envelope caused a second validation failure. Cohere could discard it before the first normal chunk; Anthropic replaced the original cause with the validation error.

Extract the existing generation loop into `chat_completion_stream_generator_raw`. OpenAI's existing generator serializes these objects and appends `[DONE]`; Cohere and Anthropic override that serialization boundary to produce their own events directly. Request preprocessing, admission checks and KV-transfer rejection cleanup keep their existing entry points.

Cohere retains its `message-end(ERROR)` followed by `[DONE]`. Anthropic now closes an open block, emits an `error` event with the original sanitized message, and terminates without a success `message_stop`. Normal stream exhaustion still performs block flushing and protocol termination. In-stream failures remain HTTP 200 and are communicated through SSE.

This extends the existing PR as requested; no additional PR was opened. Related [#60309](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60309) handles HTTP error mapping and [#61825](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61825) handles Cohere REQUIRED/tools validation; neither fixes these streaming adapters.

items.body:
## Overview

Fix Unlimited-OCR's underestimated maximum image-token bound, which can reject valid images with a small encoder budget.

## Claims

- Use a 1×32 profiling crop grid to cover the maximum number of newline features.
- Correct the default per-image bound from 3553 to 3793 tokens.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_unlimited_ocr.py -v
```

- New regression: 1 passed; it fails on the original code. Existing processor regression tests: 9 passed. Pre-commit passed.
- Actual `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` serving, BF16 / TP=1, official nightly `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`, using a 640×20480 image:

| `max_num_batched_tokens` | Original | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | HTTP 400: 3793 image tokens exceed the 3553 cache | HTTP 200 |
| 8192 | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 |

Small, ordinary, tall and wide synthetic inputs were compared. Same-budget default compile/graph comparisons preserve output tokens and sampled-token logprobs exactly.

Serving used `TRITON_ALLOW_NON_CONSTEXPR_GLOBALS=1` for an unrelated nightly compile issue. Baseline OCR on some synthetic inputs is empty or incorrect; validation covers request acceptance and output regression, without an accuracy claim.

Both 4×8 and 1×32 grids contain 32 crops, but the latter has more feature rows and therefore more newline tokens. It reaches the true upper bound without changing inference computation.

## Description

Cherry-pick of the first commit of #20031 to release/1.3 for https://nvbugs/6836097.

`test_disaggregated_qwen3_32b_fp8` fails on B200 because the first requests hit the 60 s `kv_transfer_timeout_ms`. items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] hadacore: don't load past the input on a partial last warp
items.author: khluu
items.summary: Fixes an intermittent MMU fault crash in hadamard_transform_kernel where partial-last-warps issue cp.async loads past input bounds in the masked variant.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes an intermittent `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `hadacore::hadamard_transform_kernel`. Since Oct 15 it has crashed the `(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantization` step on main (nightly 95042, builds 95065 and 95066) and on PR runs (95016, 3 of 3 attempts). The crash happens in `test_per_token_kv_cache.py::test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head[int4-0-16-128-1-42]` and aborts the whole pytest process.

**Cause:**
- The masked kernel variant (`enable_mask=true`) issues `cp.async` loads for all `num_chunks` chunks of a warp, even when the warp owns fewer (`real_num_chunks`).
- For the int4 per-token-head KV path, 42 tokens × 128 bf16 = 21 chunks of 256 elements, at 2 chunks per warp. So the last warp reads 512 bytes past the end of the input.
- That over-read only faults when the input ends at the end of a CUDA memory segment. Whether it does depends on what earlier tests left in the caching allocator. That's why it showed up when automatic sharding put `test_online.py` in the same process.
- The `cp.async.wait_group` counts further down already assume only `real_num_chunks` groups were committed (`switch(k + diff_num_chunks)`).

**Fix:** skip the loads past `real_num_chunks` in the masked variant.

## Test Plan

Repro on Buildkite, Quantization step only, on a throwaway branch:

| Build | What it ran | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [95264](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95264) | `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` alone, and after each single suspect file | passes |
| [95264](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95264) | after the full 8-file shard-4 order | **crash** |
| [95275](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95275) | full order, leaving one file out each time | crash unless `test_online.py` is left out |
| [95292](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95292) | **this fix**: full crashing order ×3, plus the file alone | **all pass** (244 passed / 25 skipped each run, 82 passed alone) |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict: GLM-5.2 0.9287 main, 0.9348 PR (stderr 0.007); DeepSeek-V3.2 0.9522 main, 0.9507 PR (stderr 0.006). MTP3 acceptance length 3.29 / 3.30.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel data and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, mean TPOT per run (ms). Order: main, PR, PR, main, PR. A further main run between the two PR sessions was dropped: another process held about 88 GiB per GPU while it started, so its KV cache was 1.23M tokens instead of 3.2M. MTP3 order: main, PR, PR, main, PR, PR, main, main.

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8K/1K c1 | 13.43, 13.53 | 13.44, 13.45, 13.46 |
| 8K/1K c8 | 17.27, 17.47 | 17.27, 17.51, 17.38 |
| 8K/1K c16 | 22.46, 22.86 | 22.44, 22.66, 22.52 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 14.72, 14.75 | 13.66, 13.67, 13.78 |
| 128K/1K c8 | 44.55, 45.56 | 42.95, 42.98, 42.98 |
| 128K/1K c16 | 78.89, 79.00 | 76.58, 76.62, 76.60 |
| MTP3 8K/1K c8 | 8.91, 9.16, 9.08, 9.10 | 9.14, 9.34, 9.08, 9.10 |
| MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.27, 35.52, 34.45, 35.12 | 33.96, 33.67, 34.17, 33.35 |

- Median ITL (ms): 128K c1 14.83 to 13.76, c8 18.22 to 17.01, c16 21.52 to 20.49, MTP3 128K c8 27.04 to 25.39. Output throughput at 128K: +5.8% / +3.7% / +2.8%. KV cache size and startup time match across arms.
- The 128K c1 ITL drop (1.07 ms) matches the kernel estimate of 21 indexer layers x 53 us (1.11 ms).
- gsm8k flexible: 0.9295 main, 0.9363 PR. MTP3 gsm8k, first 400 questions: 0.935 main, 0.9325 PR (stderr 0.012). Passkey at 32K / 64K / 120K: 12/12, 8/8, 6/6 in both arms.
- Operator check: decode logits from AITER's `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (buffer poisoned past each row), prefill logits from `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`, calls mirroring `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`; widths 133120 and 1M, `next_n` 1 (1-D), 2 (native 2-D) and 4 (one row per token), packed multi-sequence prefill, and graph replay with new lengths. Every row has `min(L, k)` distinct indices in `[0, L)` followed by `-1`.

DeepSeek-V3.2 (FP8 checkpoint), TP4, same env and flags but no `--max-model-len` (163840), mean TPOT per run (ms), order main, PR, PR, main; median ITL and output throughput follow TPOT:

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4K/1K c1 | 12.83, 12.80 | 12.91, 12.89 |
| 4K/1K c16 | 22.84, 22.88 | 22.62, 22.60 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 16.24, 16.22 | 13.72, 13.69 |

- 4K/1K c16 mean TTFT: 2333, 2326 ms main, 2465, 2327 ms PR. 128K/1K c1 output throughput +10.0%. KV cache 2.07M tokens in every session. gsm8k flexible: 0.9530 main, 0.9507 PR.
- A static cut-off for 131072-200000 columns would put this deployment back on the in-tree kernel: it would recover the 0.085 ms at 4K c1 and lose the 128K gain (2.53 ms) and the 4K c16 gain. GLM-5.2 at 133120 would lose its 128K gains as well.

Decode top-k per indexer layer (us, in-tree to AITER), GLM-5.2 indexer (32 heads, k=2048); scoring and top-k for 21 layers captured in one graph, LLC flushed before each replay, median of 20:

| width | context | 1 row | 8 rows | 16 rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 133120 | 4K | 17.5 to 20.4 | 17.3 to 22.3 | 17.2 to 22.7 |
| 133120 | 32K | 34.0 to 22.2 | 34.9 to 22.8 | 34.7 to 23.5 |
| 133120 | 128K | 80.8 to 27.9 | 81.8 to 28.8 | 81.3 to 28.5 |
| 1M | 4K | 37.0 to 25.9 | 35.3 to 29.3 | 35.3 to 35.3 |
| 1M | 32K | 42.8 to 26.8 | 42.3 to 29.6 | 43.7 to 32.3 |
| 1M | 128K | 46.3 to 27.1 | 50.0 to 31.2 | 50.2 to 34.4 |

MTP1 (2-D bounds) and MTP3 (one row per token) follow the same pattern. At 262144 columns AITER wins at every measured context.

Prefill top-k GPU time per 16K-row chunk (us, in-tree to AITER): context 16K 304 to 370, 20K 426 to 469, 24K 568 to 558, 32K 757 to 680, 64K 1681 to 1320, 128K 4026 to 2635. 512-row chunks cross over near 20K. Host enqueue per call: in-tree 5-12 us, AITER 27-36 us.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 133120 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# MTP3: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# DeepSeek-V3.2: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2, same env and flags without --max-model-len.

# 128K/1K: num-prompts max(C, 3). 8K/1K: --random-input-len 8192,
# num-prompts max(3C, 6), --seed 42. MTP3 c8: 8 prompts at 128K, 24 at 8K.
# DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K: --random-input-len 4096, 6 prompts at c1, 48 at c16, --seed 42.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 43

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Gate: compress ratio 1 and k=2048 only. Decode always takes AITER (FULL graphs are not keyed by context length); prefill when `chunk.max_seqlen_k`, a host int, reaches 32K.
- Cost: with max_model_len between 131072 and 200000 and up to 48 rows, AITER loses 3-6 us per layer below 8-16K context. DeepSeek-V3.2 (default 163840, 61 indexer layers) measures +0.085 ms TPOT at 4K/1K c1. Keeping the in-tree kernel for that width band would also give up the 2.53 ms gain at 128K on the same deployment, so the gate does not exclude it.
- Not measured end to end: GLM-5/5.1, TP8. CI (MI300, NVIDIA) runs only the new selection test; the GPU tests need gfx950.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, pre-existing failure and related PRs</summary>

- Cause: the in-tree decode kernel has gfx950 policies only for k=512 and k=1024 (#55327). At k=2048 its cost grows with context; AITER's stays near flat.
- Semantics come from #52882's wrappers. ROCm DSA decode carries `(B, next_n)` bounds for native MTP1 and one row per token otherwise, so `seq_lens.reshape(-1)` with `next_n=1` gives AITER each row's exact end. Prefill turns AITER's chunk-global indices into sequence-local ones and keeps `-1`.
- Decode is not split by context length because a FULL graph replays one kernel for every length. Eager decode could use the length, but would then pick a different kernel for the same shape depending on graph mode. AITER's extra host time per call only shows in eager steps.
- `test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp` (from #58167, `requires_gfx950`, so not in CI) fails identically on main: it passes `(B, 1)` seq_lens with `next_n=4` to the in-tree k=512 gfx950 kernel, which reads any 2-D `seq_lens` per row, so its reference rows are wrong. It does not reach the code changed here.
- #60012 (open) tunes the in-tree k=2048 kernel above 200000 columns for #55327. With this PR it still serves AITER-off deployments and short prefill chunks; the gate should be re-measured if it lands. #57844 (open) edits the same selector. #59421 (draft, native MTP above `next_n=2`) is compatible because decode flattens the bounds.
- #50470 (draft) and #46172 also move the k=2048 decode top-k to AITER. Both have merge conflicts and no activity since 2026-08-22, and both swap the call unconditionally, passing vLLM's `next_n` with its 2-D MTP bounds. On both, the author of #52882 noted that AITER v0.1.19 needs those bounds adapted and asked to treat #52882 as the consolidated direction; #52882 then merged with AITER enabled for compressed indexers only. This PR applies its adapters to the k=2048 path, adds prefill and serving results, and leaves every other indexer unchanged. The `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` entry point that #50470 waited for ships in AITER 0.1.25 and is the function called here.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "aiter topk", "top-k ROCm", "topk ROCm", "indexer ROCm", "indexer aiter", "DeepSeek-V3.2 ROCm", "GLM-5 ROCm", "sparse indexer AMD", "top_k_per_row_decode", "top_k_per_row_prefill", "compress_ratio aiter topk".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #50470 and #46172 target the same decode call, have been inactive since 2026-08-22, and were marked superseded by #52882's author; #52882 left k=2048 on the in-tree kernel (details above). Thanks @JH-Leon-KIM-AMD for #50470.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip DSA indexer scoring for short dense-MHA prefills
items.author: whx-sjtu
items.summary: On ROCm, the path (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) now skips the sparse indexer's scoring for pure short prefills that run on dense MHA, as CUDA already does (#48407, #51298). Builds on the ROCm dense-MHA prefill from #49263.
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the `deepseek_v32` path (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) now skips the sparse indexer's scoring for pure short prefills that run on dense MHA, as CUDA already does (#48407, #51298). Builds on the ROCm dense-MHA prefill from #49263.

## Claims

- GLM-5.1-FP8, MI355X, TP4: 1K-token prefill median TTFT -8.1% at c1, -1.6% at c32. gsm8k unchanged.
- GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (indexer on 21 of 78 layers): no significant change.
- Mixed batches, prefills longer than `index_topk`, MTP layers, FULL cudagraph and capture still score. Other platforms are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: 35 passed, 8 skipped (CUDA-only) on MI355X, 7 new. pre-commit clean.
- `test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa` (existing, AMD V1 Attention CI): passed, auto and fp8 KV. Its dense run skips one step whose keys a later 2049+-token decode scores.
- Serving, GLM-5.1-FP8, TP4, output 1 token, 2 runs per arm, ABBA, no failed requests:

| workload | median TTFT (ms), main → PR | change |
|---|---|---|
| 1K in, c1 | 164.5 → 151.2 | -8.1% |
| 1K in, c32 | 1948.6 → 1918.0 | -1.6% |
| 1900 in, c1 | 175.6 → 173.6 | within noise |
| 8K in, c1 (sparse path) | 620.2 → 623.4 | within noise |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict, GLM-5.1-FP8: main 0.9469 / 0.9424, PR 0.9447 / 0.9462 (stderr 0.006).
- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MTP3, 3 runs per arm: TTFT -0.6% to -1.9%, within noise. gsm8k strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, acceptance length 3.31 → 3.31.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, probes, profile and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.1-FP8 (78 indexer layers, no spec decode), median TTFT in ms:

| run | arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | main | 166.5 | 175.8 | 1950.1 | 622.9 |
| F2 | PR | 149.2 | 174.6 | 1916.9 | 623.1 |
| F3 | PR | 153.1 | 172.7 | 1919.1 | 623.6 |
| F4 | main | 162.5 | 175.4 | 1947.0 | 617.4 |

gsm8k flexible: main 0.9462 / 0.9409, PR 0.9439 / 0.9484. 1K c32 total throughput 16616 → 17042 tok/s (+2.6%, within noise).

GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (21 indexer layers plus the MTP layer; TTFT runs use MTP3 with synthetic acceptance 3.0), median TTFT in ms, runs in order A B B A A B:

| arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 152.4 / 154.3 / 152.8 | 148.9 / 150.3 / 152.2 | 1501.8 / 1503.7 / 1513.2 | 471.6 / 475.7 / 473.0 |
| PR | 152.0 / 150.6 / 154.1 | 145.7 / 147.4 / 149.5 | 1489.8 / 1492.2 / 1492.2 | 471.8 / 470.5 / 457.9 |

GLM-5.2 gsm8k with real MTP3: strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, flexible 0.9356 → 0.9363, acceptance length 3.310 → 3.311. At concurrency 1 (250 questions, every prefill a pure short prefill): 0.952 → 0.944 (stderr 0.014). A probe on TP rank 0 counted indexer-layer calls on pure dense-MHA prefills: main scored 8382 of 8382, the PR 382 of 8404, all on the MTP layer.

Why 1K gains more than 1900 (GLM-5.1-FP8, TP rank 0). Prefill runs eagerly, and on main the host needs about 148 ms to issue a step at either length. A probe timed the forward without a profiler (median of 20, ms). Host times move by up to 10 ms between sessions with node load; a first main session under heavy load (1K host issue 187 ms) was repeated:

| arm | 1K: host issue / GPU tail after it | 1900: host issue / GPU tail after it |
|---|---|---|
| main | 147.6 / 4.4 | 149.8 / 12.3 |
| PR, run 1 | 131.3 / 6.9 | 131.1 / 27.6 |
| PR, run 2 | 142.0 / 0.4 | 143.4 / 15.3 |

At 1K the GPU finishes within a few ms of the last launch, so the step is host-bound and the indexer's host work shows up in TTFT. At 1900 the GPU runs 12-28 ms past the host; host + tail stays at 159-162 ms in every run, and only the indexer's GPU time is saved. A torch profiler trace per step: the PR removes 312 kernels (4 per layer), 1.43 ms of GPU time at 1K and 2.17 ms at 1900; on main the indexer op costs 190-198 us of host time but 24-34 us of GPU time per call (host time inflated by the profiler).

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# GLM-5.2: amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4, same flags plus
#   --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

# 1K c1 shown. 1900 c1: --random-input-len 1900 --seed 45.
# 1K c32: --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 46.
# 8K c1: --random-input-len 8192 --num-prompts 16 --seed 47.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts 40 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 44

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  "tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa"
```

</details>

## Details

- Placement: `DeepseekV32MLAAttention._fused_attention`, which already holds the MLA metadata. CUDA passes the layer name into its op only because the op cannot see that metadata.
- Conditions: the CUDA op's, plus the layer taking the dense-MHA branch. The flag in `DeepseekV32Attention` moves from `is_cuda()` to `is_cuda_alike()`.
- K cache: still written by `fused_norm_rope`; only scoring is dropped.
- The gain is host time: an eager 1K prefill is host-bound and each indexer call costs about 0.2 ms on the host; at 1900 the step is GPU-bound and the indexer kernels take about 2 ms per step.
- Not measured: DeepSeek-V3.2 (same code path), GLM-5.1 with MTP, TP8.

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- Moving the check into `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` would mirror CUDA but add an argument to an op that DeepSeek-V4 shares; the model already has the MLA metadata and the dense-MHA decision.
- The ROCm indexer op is built with `skip_k_cache_insert=True`. `fused_norm_rope` writes the indexer keys and clears the top-k buffer before the decision.
- PCP leaves the flag off, as on CUDA; ROCm sparse MLA rejects DCP. MTP layers keep scoring, as on CUDA.
- This model is not torch.compiled. Prefills run eagerly under the default FULL_DECODE_ONLY; under breakable cudagraphs the eager segment re-evaluates the decision on replay. Profile and dummy runs (no metadata) still call the op, so its workspace is reserved.

</details>

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR skips indexer scoring on ROCm.

<details>
<summary>Duplicate search</summary>

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` with "short prefill indexer ROCm", "skip indexer ROCm", "indexer scoring ROCm", "dense mha indexer ROCm", "short prefill topk ROCm", "rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer", "dense_mha_metadata_layer_name", "short prefill skip indexer", "GLM ROCm indexer prefill", "ROCm DSv3.2 indexer". Nearest: #56944 and #60601 (shard indexer prefill rows across TP), #61504 (sparse MLA decode indptr), #60294 (aiter `mqa_logits` for indexer prefill); none skips scoring.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Default AITER fused shared experts on for GLM-5.x MXFP4
items.author: whx-sjtu
items.summary: On gfx950, GLM-5.x MXFP4 checkpoints now turn on when it is unset, because AITER tunes their fused MoE only for the fused shared-expert shape.
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx950, GLM-5.x MXFP4 checkpoints now turn on `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` when it is unset, because AITER tunes their fused MoE only for the fused shared-expert shape. Related: #28985, #59221, #60604.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, MTP: output throughput +7-14%, mean TPOT -6-12%, prefill TTFT -6-7%; gsm8k within stderr, MTP acceptance unchanged.
- An explicit 0 or 1 still wins. Other models, platforms and layouts keep the default (off).

## Validation

- `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py -k "not test_models_fse_init"`: 90 passed, 9 new (the deselected cases need a free GPU). pre-commit clean.
- `create_engine_config()` on real checkpoints: flag on for GLM-5.1/5.2/5.3-MXFP4 at TP4 and GLM-5.2-MXFP4 at TP8; unchanged for TP2, EP, GLM-5.2-FP8, AITER off.
- Serving, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, MTP3, two runs per arm in ABBA order, no failed requests. Flag on is this PR's default:

| workload | output tok/s, flag off → on | mean TPOT (ms), flag off → on |
|---|---|---|
| 1k/1k c16 | 1472.6 → 1671.6 (+13.5%) | 10.09 → 8.89 (-11.9%) |
| 1k/1k c64 | 3095.1 → 3365.6 (+8.7%) | 19.34 → 17.71 (-8.4%) |
| 8k/1k c64 | 1541.9 → 1654.7 (+7.3%) | 35.51 → 33.19 (-6.5%) |

- 8k-in prefill median TTFT: 475.8 → 449.0 ms at c1, 6701.5 → 6240.0 ms at c16.
- This PR's head with the flag unset, one run: 1681.7 tok/s / 8.87 ms at 1k/1k c16, 3503.5 tok/s / 17.32 ms at c64; the server log shows the auto-enable line and every FP4 MoE lookup on the tuned 257 / top-9 rows.
- gsm8k 5-shot strict: 0.9386 flag off, 0.9393 flag on, 0.9333 in both runs of this PR with the flag unset (stderr 0.007). MTP acceptance length 3.31, 3.31, 3.30.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel lookups and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source. The decode rows and gsm8k compare main with the flag set to 0 and 1 (F1-F4). The prefill rows compare main and this branch with the flag unset (P1-P4). P2/P3 ran an earlier revision of this branch with the same enable conditions. R1 is the head (c716073) with the flag unset, one run; its c64 throughput is 4% above the F2/F3 mean, and Claims use F1-F4 only.

| run | arm | 1k/1k c16 tok/s, TPOT | 1k/1k c64 tok/s, TPOT | 8k/1k c64 tok/s, TPOT | 8k/1 c1 / c16 median TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | main, flag 0 | 1463.5, 10.07 | 3105.2, 19.57 | 1515.4, 35.77 | |

```bash
  --num-prompts $((8 * C)) --max-concurrency $C --seed 42

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False
```

</details>

## Details

- Cause: AITER 0.1.25's `glm5_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` tunes this model's gfx950 W4A4 MoE only at 257 experts / top-9 (TP1/2/4/8 per-rank sizes); the unfused 256 / top-8 MoE gets default heuristics.
- Placement: the `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` config hook sets the env var, like the `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` auto-enable: the MoE router reads the process-wide flag, and the env var is in the torch.compile cache key.
- Gate: TP4/TP8 without DP, PCP or EP, as in #59221. The per-layer quantization check still runs, so the BF16 MTP layer of GLM-5.2/5.3-MXFP4 stays unfused (one existing warning per worker).
- Limits: TP8 and GLM-5/5.1/5.3-MXFP4 (same shapes) checked at config level only. TP2 stays opt-in, unmeasured. MI355X serving is not in CI.

Not a duplicate: #59221/#60604 cover GLM-5.3-Flash, #57916 MXFP8, #58904 weight loading; none changes the `glm_moe_dsa` default.

<details>
<summary>Design notes and duplicate search</summary>

- #28985 turned the flag off globally for mixed-precision shared experts (Kimi INT4 routed + BF16 shared), DeepSeek FP4 precision and EPLB. Here the shared expert is MXFP4 like the routed experts, the per-layer quantization check still applies and EP is excluded; gsm8k is unchanged.
- The gate is per model, like GLM-5.3-Flash's `_fused_shared_experts_tuned` and DeepSeek-V4's, because each follows its own AITER table (GLM-5.3-Flash adds gfx942 in #60604; this model's table is gfx950 only).
- A per-layer default inside the model, leaving the env var unset, would also need `GroupedTopKRouter`, `rocm_aiter_grouped_topk`, `FusedMoEConfig` and `RocmPlatform.apply_config_platform_defaults` to stop reading the global flag.
- The env var stays set for the rest of the process, as with the breakable-cudagraph auto-enable. With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset (vLLM's default) nothing changes.
- Searched `gh pr list --state all` for "fused shared experts GLM", "VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS default", "GLM-5 MXFP4 ROCm", "GLM-5.2 MXFP4 AITER" and "shared experts fusion ROCm GLM". Also related: #60831 (opt-in GLM-5 MonoKernel decode, which requires this flag on), #53248 (Quark exclude check), #53953 (AITER fusions for GLM-5.2-MXFP4, no FSE change), #61345 (DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE FSE opt-in).

</details>

items.title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Preserve quoted markers in Apertus arguments
items.author: Arborsen
items.summary: Fixes Apertus tool-call parser incorrectly stripping or leaking literal `<|tools_prefix|>`/`<|tools_suffix|>` markers from JSON argument strings during streaming and non-streaming responses.
items.body:
## Overview

Fix Apertus tool-call parsing when JSON argument strings contain literal `<|tools_prefix|>` or `<|tools_suffix|>` text, in both streaming and non-streaming responses.

## Claims

- Preserve marker text in string values and keys, including nested arguments, escaped quotes, and backslashes.
- Prevent buffered partial markers from leaking into streamed content and emit valid content-only deltas.
- Retain implicit JSON completion, recovery of missing container brackets, and the scientific-notation fix from #61812.

## Validation

The human submitter reviewed and validated the patch. AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and PR preparation.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_apertus_tool_parser.py -q
# 46 passed
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_apertus_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py -q
# 220 passed
git diff --check
```

The added tests exercise every two-chunk split and character-by-character streaming, multiple calls within one array, surrounding content, and omitted/truncated endings. Running the same Apertus test file against the original parser at `dd9e07a25febb05f1a44f2ef9e6c56803ee1a9b6` gives **18 failed / 28 passed**.

Supplementary replay using the real `swiss-ai/Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509` tokenizer at revision `b946d40447b2b597999b9c86d44bee0b452c919f`: **4 non-streaming + 178 streaming cases passed**, versus **140 failures** on the original parser. Literal markers were assembled from ordinary tokens; the enclosing control tokens appeared only once each. This automated validation did not include live model inference or model-quality evaluation.

All 12 applicable Python pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy. The aggregate pre-commit command was blocked while initializing the unrelated actionlint Go environment (`/usr/bin/go` rejects `install`), so a complete aggregate pass is not claimed. The existing Buildkite `tool_parsers` suite covers the added tests.

<details>
<summary>Pre-commit commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/tool_parsers/apertus_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_apertus_tool_parser.py
for hook in ruff-check ruff-format typos check-test-tethering mypy check-spdx-header check-root-lazy-imports check-filenames check-forbidden-imports check-torch-cuda-call validate-config check-boolean-context-manager; do
  .venv/bin/pre-commit run "$hook" --files vllm/tool_parsers/apertus_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_apertus_tool_parser.py
done
```

</details>

## Details

The non-streaming regex stopped at the first suffix even inside a JSON string; streaming `rfind` could likewise mistake quoted markers for block boundaries. A shared quote/escape-aware scan finds the suffix outside strings, and streaming content offsets follow the text actually released by the marker buffer. The change stays inside the Apertus parser and its existing tests, without changing the public parser interface or adding dependencies.

If a JSON string itself is unclosed, subsequent suffix text remains string data: the text-only interface cannot reliably distinguish that text from a control token. Recovery of missing container brackets is covered, but this does not promise identical behavior for every malformed output. Multiple calls within one block are supported; separate tool blocks are outside this change's scope.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR addresses this Python boundary fix. #46813 implements the Rust parser, and #50496 adds Apertus 1.5 support in other files. #61812 is already merged into this baseline and its regression tests still pass.

items.title: [ROCm] Revamp CI/release deployment: collapse image tiers, unify build pipeline
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Adding or debugging any step required understanding all six. The bytes shipped to users were never the bytes tested on GPUs. [Discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--61939.org.readthedocs.build/en/61939/]
items.body:
> **Companion PR:** vllm-project/ci-infra#820 (dual-mode pipeline generator — must merge together or with ci-infra first)

Currently on CI and deployment, we have:

- **Too many image tiers.** The old pipeline had six distinct image layers (base, ci_base, CI image, wheels, test, smoke), each driven by a separate script with its own cache keys and metadata handoffs. Adding or debugging any step required understanding all six.
- **CI and release were disconnected.** CI built images via `ci-bake-rocm.sh`; release rebuilt from scratch using a separate pipeline. The bytes shipped to users were never the bytes tested on GPUs.
- **Thousands of lines of bash nobody could operate.** `ci-bake-rocm.sh` alone was 2,784 lines. The ROCm build/deploy surface totalled ~12,000 lines of shell with no human able to read, modify or debug it under pressure.

In this PR, the purpose is to have:

**Two image tiers, one Dockerfile, one HCL, three readable scripts.**

1. **Stack** (`rocm/vllm-ci:stack-rocm-<Ks>`) — base OS + ROCm + PyTorch. Built only when `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` or `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py` changes (content key `Ks`). Pushed once; reused by every subsequent build.
2. **Per-commit** (`rocm/vllm-ci:build-<build-id>`) — vLLM compiled on top of the stack. The runtime key `Kr` (hash of `Ks` + Dockerfile above the marker + pip requirement files) gates whether the runtime layer is rebuilt. A Python-only commit reuses the runtime; a requirements bump rebuilds it; a csrc-only change rebuilds neither.

**One shared `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`.** A named BuildKit context (`stack`) is injected by the bake HCL, so the same Dockerfile builds on any stack without duplication.

**One static `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl`** replaces the dynamically generated `docker/ci-rocm.hcl`. All parameterisation is through HCL `variable` blocks from environment variables. Targets cover all combinations: stack, runtime, CI test, csrc, wheels, release.

**`build.sh` (240 lines) replaces ~5,000 lines of shell scripts.** Six modes: `keys`, `base`, `ci`, `check`, `csrc`, `release`. Each mode is a self-contained named section, readable end-to-end.

**Release promotes the CI digest — no rebuild.** `build.sh release` reads the exact digest of the CI-tested image and reuses it. A non-blocking `rel-csrc` step compiles csrc for all 9 GPU arches (gfx90a/942/950/1100/1101/1200/1201/1150/1151); because csrc inputs rarely change (~8% of commits), this is almost always a BuildKit cache hit.

**`rocm-release.yaml` (53 lines) + `publish.sh` (200 lines) handle release publishing.** A trigger-only `amd-release` Buildkite pipeline uploads `rocm-release.yaml` once per main commit. `publish.sh` copies digests via `imagetools create` to ECR, Docker Hub, and S3 — no Docker build, no layer transfer.

**ROCm 7.2 (apt) deprecated.** All `rocm_72` stack plumbing removed: `Dockerfile.rocm_72_base`, `stack-rocm_72` bake target, `rocm72-check-amd` CI step, ROCm 7.2 release pipeline group. TheRock 10 (`rocm`) is the only supported stack.

**ci-infra is dual-mode.** The pipeline generator checks for `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh` in the vLLM checkout. Present → new pipeline renders. Absent (old checkouts, forks) → existing pipeline unchanged.

**Image pre-warming.** Runtime tags are content-keyed (`runtime-rocm-<Kr>`). A cluster cron job can pre-pull by checking tag presence before pulling, avoiding the 200-node simultaneous pull on rare runtime rebuilds.

### What is preserved

- **Step key `image-build-amd`** — unchanged. All 229 GPU test steps continue to depend on it.
- **`SETUP_STEP_KEYS = {"refresh-rocm-base-amd", "pre-commit"}`**
- **Smoke tests** — `openai-smoke` and `test-smoke` stages in `Dockerfile.rocm`; `rel-gpu` GPU smoke on `amd_mi250_1` in `rocm-release.yaml`.
- **Process lifecycle** — `run-amd-test.sh` handles: `CONTAINER_TIMEOUT_S` wall-clock timeout (`timeout --foreground`), structured `[amd-ci-teardown]` lifecycle log events, exit-code propagation, DPX GPU partition lock, HF mount check, NFS xet redirect, GPU preflight, diagnostics bundle on failure.
- **Nightly tags** (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly*`, `base-nightly*`), S3 wheels per main commit, perf-eval ECR image, credential boundaries.
- **AITER nightly** — ci-infra old-layout path unchanged; new-layout renders the AITER overlay step via `AITER_SPEC`.

### Net change

39 files, **+1,894 / −8,922** vs `origin/main`.

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` | 1,016 | 483 |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` | 476 | 404 |
| `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl` | 143 | 118 |
| `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh` | — | 240 (new) |
| `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/publish.sh` | — | 200 (new) |
| `.buildkite/rocm-release.yaml` | — | 53 (new) |
| `tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` | — | 49 (new) |
| `docker/context/base-wheels/.keep` | — | new (gfx1250 COPY fix) |
| `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh` | 1,813 | 182 |
| `.buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml` | 88 | 47 |
| `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml` | 1,055 | ~820 |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72_base` | 388 | deleted |
| `docker/ci-rocm.hcl` | 411 | deleted |
| `.buildkite/scripts/ci-bake-rocm.sh` | 2,784 | deleted |
| ROCm `rocm/*.sh` scripts (8 files) | ~1,600 | deleted |
| ROCm release scripts (3 files) | ~300 | deleted |
| `requirements/build/rocm.txt` | 19 | deleted |

**ROCm build/deploy surface after this PR:** 1 Dockerfile (483 lines), 1 HCL (118 lines), 3 bash scripts (build 240, publish 200, run-amd-test 182 = 622 lines total).

### Follow-up infra tasks

- **`amd-release` Buildkite pipeline** — create trigger-only pipeline in vllm-project's org with `ROCM_STACK` env var.
- **`rocm/vllm-ci-pr` Docker Hub repo** — create with push access for the `amd-cpu` agent token.
- **`amd-cpu-pr` queue split** — run PR builds on separate hosts with their own Hub token. One comment in `build.sh` marks the boundary.
- **Cluster pre-warm cron** — pre-pull `rocm/vllm-ci:runtime-rocm-<Kr>` on CI nodes with a tag-presence check.
- **Hub tag retention** — content-addressed tags; define an expiry window.
- **gfx1250 Dockerfiles** (`Dockerfile.rocm_gfx1250`, `Dockerfile.rocm_base_gfx1250`) — kept as-is, not wired into CI or release; needs owner sign-off before removal.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

It also makes the Qwen3-4B example's 100-step run 11% faster with three overlap settings. Only changes; core verl, including, is untouched. [Discussion: 🎉

<]
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

> Moves the TPU GRPO example (`examples/tpu/grpo`) to `google-pytorch/torchtitan` `ea7fec0f` with that commit's TPU package versions, and points the README at the verl-hardware-plugin commit that supports it (`f5876f75`, the merge of verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#60: a standalone TPU TorchTitan engine). It also makes the Qwen3-4B example's 100-step run 11% faster with three overlap settings. Only `examples/tpu/grpo/` changes; core verl, including `verl/workers/engine/torchtitan/`, is untouched.

Two commits:

1. `03751db2`: the image and the plugin pin.
   - `Dockerfile`: torchtitan `f880cc73` -> `ea7fec0f`, with the versions of its `torchtitan/experiments/tpu/requirements.txt`: jax/jaxlib 0.10.2 -> 0.11.1, libtpu 0.0.47 -> 0.0.50, torchao 0.17.0 (new). The rest of the stack is unchanged.
   - `README.md`: checks out verl-hardware-plugin `f5876f75` instead of `e5ab532`, which subclasses core's TorchTitan engine and does not import with this torchtitan.
2. `3b0c9a24`: three overlap settings for the Qwen3-4B example (`run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`, now environment variables), and the README's expected step time.

Related open PRs:
- #8243 also edits this `Dockerfile` and `README.md`, but takes a different direction: Ray 2.59, PyPI `torchtitan` 0.3.0 and a pip-installed plugin. This PR keeps `google-pytorch/torchtitan`, because the TPU engine uses its TPU recipe (SimpleFSDP) and kernels (splash attention), which PyPI `torchtitan` 0.3.0 does not have. items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix Triton MLA decode int32 overflow and logits workspace accounting
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Fixes int32 overflow in Triton MLA decode kernels at large context lengths and ensures logits workspace is reserved during memory profiling to prevent OOM on GPU serving.
items.body:
Triton MLA models crash at their default context length on MI355: `vllm serve` with default settings for Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 and DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat dies with `Memory access fault by GPU ... Write access to a read-only page` during CUDA graph capture. Two bugs are involved, and the second only shows up once the first is fixed:

1. **int32 overflow in the decode kernels.** The split-KV logits offset `cur_batch * stride_mid_ob` is computed in int32. At ≥ 128K context, `_compute_num_kv_splits` picks 512 splits on MI355 (2 × 256 CUs), so with 32 heads one request's logits span 32 × 512 × 513 = 8.4M floats. From batch row 256 onward the offset passes 2^31, and FULL graph capture runs batches up to 512.
2. **The logits workspace is not counted by memory profiling.** #46819 reserves the worst-case logits workspace (32 GiB for LongCat at defaults: 1024 seqs × 32 heads × 512 splits × 513 × fp32) when the metadata builder is created, which happens after profiling. The KV cache is then sized as if that memory were free, and its allocation OOMs (`Tried to allocate 164.67 GiB`, 157.84 GiB free).

To resolve the above, this PR modifies:
- `triton_decode_attention.py`: compute `cur_batch * stride_mid_ob` in int64 at the six logits offsets (stage 1 normal/grouped stores and stage 2 loads), following #47671.
- `MLAAttentionImpl.reserve_profiling_workspace()`: a no-op hook called from the MLA profiling branch, next to the existing `kv_b_proj` scratch simulation.
- `TritonMLAImpl` overrides the hook to reserve the logits workspace at its upper bound (`max_num_seqs × max_decode_query_len`) during profiling. The builder keeps its reservation, which becomes a no-op.
- `test_triton_decode_attention.py`: a regression test whose logits exceed 2^31 elements, for the grouped (MLA) and normal kernels.

## Validation

MI355, TP1. `main` vs this PR:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, default 1M context | memory access fault | serves, GSM8K 87.34 |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8, default 320K context | memory access fault | serves, GSM8K 86.88 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, default backend (`TRITON_MLA`) and 160K context | memory access fault | serves |
| LongCat with only the overflow fix | — | OOM at KV cache allocation |
| LongCat with only the accounting fix | — | memory access fault |

Both models were also served at concurrency 384, where decode rows ≥ 256 run with 512 splits: 0 failed requests.

At 32K context, where `main` works (decode TPOT Δ, + is faster; median of 5 reps, repeated with GPUs swapped):

| Model | C1 | C8 | C32 | C128 | GSM8K main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct | +0.4 / +0.3% | +0.2 / +0.3% | −0.1 / +2.1% | +2.2 / +2.1% | 86.88 → 86.58 (McNemar p = 0.75) |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 | +1.0 / +0.6% | +1.7 / +1.6% | +3.6 / +3.0% | +6.0 / +5.3% | 86.88 → 87.34 (p = 0.57) |

<details>
<summary>Why decode got faster</summary>

A rocprofv3 trace of the same LongCat decode workload (128 × 2048-token prompts, 256 output tokens, 32K context) shows all of the difference in `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1`: 6062 → 5230 ms (−13.7%), with identical grids and register counts. Every other kernel is within ±0.5%. In the stage-1 variants I inspected, the int32 offset lowers the logits stores to scalar `buffer_store_dword`, while the int64 base produces vectorized `global_store_dwordx3`. The kernel microbenchmark is neutral at long sequences (30 shapes, H 16–128, 4K–128K context: median 1.000×, range 0.990–1.005×, run-to-run drift ≤ 0.8%) and 15–17% faster at 512 splits with batch ≥ 128.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `test_decode_attention_int64_logits_offset` faults on `main` (both cases) and passes with this PR in 2.4 s. It uses ~8.6 GB of fp32 logits.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py` + `test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py`: 133 passed, 10/10 loops.
- `v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` + `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` (the CI command): 11 clean runs (751 passed), including all 6 with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. The 7 other runs failed only in tests that behave the same on `main`:
  - The sparse `ROCMAiterMLA` decode test fails about 1 in 20 in isolation: 19/20 on both `main` and this PR.
  - HF API 429 rate limits, from four loops running in parallel.
  - `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` failed only in runs that also hit 429s. It is 20/20 in isolation on both `main` and this PR.
  - One transient engine OOM, where device-wide free memory dropped during profiling.
- `v1/attention` (rest of the CI command, CI environment): 1972 passed.
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat on `ROCM_AITER_MLA` (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0`), where the hook is a no-op, serves normally. AITER MoE was turned off only because this image's AITER `topk_gating` rejects `num_shared_experts` on `main`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- **Effect on KV cache size:** the KV cache now excludes the logits workspace. LongCat at 32K goes from 164.67 to 162.91 GiB (`main` over-commits there too, but its slack absorbs it). At 320K it is 134.86 GiB, where `main` cannot start.
- **Upper bound:** the profiling hook has no builder, so it sizes rows as `max_num_seqs × max_decode_query_len`. That matches the builder's `reorder_batch_threshold` except with DCP on a backend without varlen support, where the builder uses 1 and the profiled reservation is larger than needed.
- **Why the profiling forward:** the impl is built at model load, but the decode metadata builder only exists after profiling. Reserving in the profiling run follows the existing MLA `kv_b_proj` simulation and the sparse-indexer reservations, and avoids touching the worker's profiling code.
- **History:** #33529 made split counts up to 2 × compute units reachable, and #46819 moved the logits into a workspace reserved after profiling. #47671 fixed the same overflow class for page offsets in these kernels.
- **Duplicate check:** no open PR or issue covers this. #46728 (NVIDIA shared-memory OOR) and #57094 (NaN on empty `seq_len`) touch the same kernels for different bugs.

</details>

items.title: Add opt-in expert deployment layout exchange to mLite
items.author: lidongdongbuaa
items.summary: It preserves parameter names, shapes and dtypes, including FP8 values and scalar scales. Copy received byte ranges into aligned storage before reconstructing mixed dtypes.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Add an opt-in mLite checkpoint primitive that redistributes materialized expert deployment tensors between different EP layouts without gathering the full expert set first. For example, EP2 to EP4 requires selecting one source replica and reaching destinations outside a single two-rank source EP group. The caller provides the exchange group; training ownership and existing export defaults are unchanged.

Fixes #8186. Supersedes #8187. Related context: #7050.

## Changes

- `ExpertLayoutPlan` maps global expert IDs to source holders and all required destination replicas using an explicit ordered process group.
- `exchange_expert_layout_tensors` coordinates bounded collective rounds, including empty or exhausted senders, and exchanges opaque tensor bytes with `all_to_all_single`. It preserves parameter names, shapes and dtypes, including FP8 values and scalar scales.
- Validate source ownership, duplicate names, matching plans/budgets and group order before the corresponding tensor exchange. Copy received byte ranges into aligned storage before reconstructing mixed dtypes.
- Add usage and limitations documentation plus real multi-process CPU/Gloo tests for split/merge layouts, replicas, noncontiguous global ranks, unequal stream lengths and invalid inputs.

The PP broadcast and matching-EP local export implementations discussed in #7050 are outside this PR. This change isolates layout mapping and collective transport from model-specific quantization, ordinary-parameter export and rollout loading; it does not enable a new production path by default.

## Collaboration

Expert-layout mapping and source-replica selection were developed jointly with @chenjiaoAngel. This PR isolates those rules in a standalone primitive and adds coordinated streaming transport and distributed validation.

## Validation

Reapplied to `NVIDIA/Megatron-LM:dev` at `16b41e2fa987c79951d1d848b2f36618d8b7e75c`.

```bash
bash experimental/lite/tests/run_tests.sh \
  experimental/lite/tests/unit/primitive/ckpt/test_expert_layout.py
```

20 passed, no skips, exit 0 on macOS with Python 3.9.6 and PyTorch 2.8.0 (CPU/Gloo). The tests run four processes, plus a four-rank subgroup inside six processes, and compare tensor bytes independently.

Direct checks of both changed Python files passed: Black 26.3.0, isort 5.13.2, Ruff E/F/I with the repository's 100-character Python line length, and Python compilation. `git diff --check` passed. The repository autoformatter was also invoked against `dev`; it currently excludes `experimental/lite`, so those files were checked directly.

## Boundaries

- Final-head GPU/NCCL testing and a complete optimizer-update → export → vLLM-reload check are still required before production enablement. This PR claims no end-to-end RL speedup.
- TP/ETP tensor slices must be materialized or handled by the caller. Source replicas must contain identical deployment values.
- Every exchange-group member must fully consume the iterator. The helper cannot repair an incomplete process group or a caller that stops participating.
- The byte budget bounds source bytes before replica fan-out; a single oversized tensor may travel alone. It is not a hard send/receive memory cap.

## Contribution checks

- [x] Distributed CPU correctness tests
- [x] Public API typing and usage documentation
- [x] Formatting, lint and compilation checks
- [ ] Final-head GPU/NCCL validation
- [ ] Full model update/export/reload validation
- [x] Author review

Ready for maintainer review. The remaining GPU/NCCL and full-model validation are listed above.

## Description

Add image inputs to the OpenEngine gRPC `Generate` path and advertise them only when the loaded model can consume them.

- Map image URL, data-URI, and raw-byte sources into the LLM API while preserving order and caller UUIDs.
- Use one cached capability snapshot for both `GetModelInfo` and `Generate`, including `trtllm_supported_modalities: ["image"]`.
- Bound item count, decode concurrency, and aggregate decoded size; report transient fetch failures as `UNAVAILABLE`.
- Keep video, audio, LoRA, and proto changes out of scope.

This follows the existing OpenEngine rule: “Reported capabilities describe what `Generate` accepts.” The change is independent of ai-dynamo/dynamo#15288; Dynamo integration will use a new PR.

## Test Coverage

Validated on one RTX 5880 Ada GPU with `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.4.0rc1.dev202610140007`:

- 139 focused OpenEngine/media tests passed after rebasing onto current `main`.
- Real VLM conformance passed with Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and confirmed expanded prompt usage.
- A real-weights OpenEngine request correctly described an ordered red/blue image; prompt tokens expanded from 19 input IDs to 82 tokens.
- End-to-end Dynamo validation covered data URI, HTTPS URL, two ordered images, text-only input, streaming, and explicit video/audio refusal.

| Request | `main` at `701772a14` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| one data image | `UNIMPLEMENTED` | 200; correct red/blue description; usage 274 + 23 |
| same JPEG over HTTPS | `UNIMPLEMENTED` | 200; correct car description; usage 322 + 2 |
| two ordered images | `UNIMPLEMENTED` | 200; first red, second blue; usage 163 + 32 |
| video / audio | `UNIMPLEMENTED` | `UNIMPLEMENTED` with the image-only capability named |
| VLM discovery | `supports_multimodal=false` | `true`; modalities list contains `image` |
| text-model discovery | `false` | `false` |

Relevant pre-commit hooks pass, including Ruff, formatting, generated-binding checks, and test-list validation.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Reviewed the checklist; the API addition is backward compatible, adds no dependency, and includes regression coverage.

## Dev Engineer Review

OpenEngine now maps image URLs, data URIs, and raw bytes into generation requests. The mapper preserves image order and supplied UUIDs. It limits requests to 64 media items, concurrent loads to eight, and decoded data to 512 MiB. Transient remote-fetch failures map to gRPC `UNAVAILABLE`.

`GetModelInfo` and `Generate` use shared media-capability detection. The service advertises image support only when the loaded model can consume images. The media loader validates resolved addresses, rejects multicast addresses, and rejects non-global addresses unless `TRTLLM_MEDIA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=1`. It also revalidates redirect targets. The aiohttp path ignores the optional caller-provided session and uses a shared validating session; verify that this behavior is compatible with callers. Video, audio, LoRA, and proto behavior remain outside the change. No current review findings were supplied, so finding counts are unavailable.

## QA Engineer Review

The change adds CPU unit coverage for capability detection, image mapping, ordering, UUIDs, limits, cancellation, and error mapping. It modifies async media-loading and URL-validation tests, and adds GPU-gated Qwen3-VL conformance coverage. The CPU OpenEngine tests are listed in `l0_cpu.yml`; the conformance test is listed in `l0_a10.yml`. The input tests are included through the `unittest/inputs` entry in `l0_cpu.yml`. - `tensorrt_llm/grpc/openengine/servicer.py` — Verify cached capability use, generation mapping, and gRPC `UNAVAILABLE` status for transient fetch failures.
- `tensorrt_llm/inputs/media_io.py` — Verify URL failures classify transient errors correctly, address checks cover redirects, and asynchronous byte loading uses the configured executor. Verify that ignoring the optional caller-provided aiohttp session does not break callers.

items.title: [None][test] Pin the MuseSpark structured-output placement
items.author: moraxu
items.summary: The module docstring of described the structured-output placement as "a raw grammar from the first generated token, with no model-specific trigger". No code path does that.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

The module docstring of `tensorrt_llm/serve/extensions/musespark.py` described the structured-output placement as "a raw grammar from the first generated token, with no model-specific trigger". No code path does that. `structured_output_format_for()` looks extensions up by reasoning-parser name, and the MuseSpark extension is registered by model type only (`model_types=("musespark_open_omni",)`). With `--reasoning_parser musespark`, `_response_format_to_guided_decoding_params` therefore takes its generic reasoning-parser branch: a structural tag that forces a private reasoning message (from `" to=self<|message|>"` to `"<|eom|><|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>"`, the parser's `reasoning_start` and `reasoning_end`) and applies the response format to the answer message after it. That matches the comment on `MuseSparkReasoningParser.answer_start`: structured output triggers on the answer header rather than on the first generated token. No test pinned it.

This PR keeps the behavior and:
- corrects the extension's module docstring to describe the placement that applies, including that reasoning tokens count toward `max_tokens` before any constrained output;
- adds `TestStructuredOutputPlacement` (CPU-only) to `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_musespark_serve_extensions.py`, which `l0_cpu.yml` already runs: no structured-output hook is keyed by the `musespark` parser, and for `json_object` and `json_schema`, with and without a `reasoning_effort` kwarg, the structural tag is the forced reasoning tag followed by the JSON-schema constraint.

Whether structured-output requests should instead let the model skip reasoning (a parser-keyed `structured_output_format` that triggers on the answer header) is a separate design question; these tests make any such change explicit.

## Test Coverage

- New: `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_musespark_serve_extensions.py::TestStructuredOutputPlacement` (5 cases).
- `pytest -m cpu_only tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_musespark_serve_extensions.py tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_serving_extensions.py`: 75 passed, including the 5 new cases.
- End to end on one 4x GB300 node (`examples/musespark_open/serve_config.yaml`, `--reasoning_parser musespark`, `guided_decoding_backend: xgrammar`): `json_object` and `json_schema` requests return the reasoning in `reasoning_content` and a valid JSON object in `content`, at `reasoning_effort: "low"` and at the default `xhigh` given enough `max_tokens`.

@coderabbitai summary

## Description

The Muse Spark Open checkpoint's chat template defaults to the highest reasoning effort, `xhigh`, and reasoning tokens count toward `max_tokens`. With that default, two request examples in the docs return no answer: the 64-token basic test (in `examples/musespark_open/README.md` and in the deployment guide) and the deployment guide's 128-token guided-decoding test spend their whole budget on reasoning and come back with `finish_reason: "length"` and an empty `content`.

This PR:
- sets `"reasoning_effort": "low"` in the three request examples and raises `max_tokens` to 512 (basic test) and 1024 (guided-decoding test);

items.body:
TITLE: [None][fix] Load MXFP8 fused weight scales with the rows of their weights
## Description

Fused MXFP8 projections (QKV / gate-up style shards loaded into one `Linear`) sliced each shard's `weight_scale` with the plain tensor-parallel split, while the weights themselves go through `Linear.load_shard`, which honours `override_tp_sharding` (uneven or replicated row ranges). With such an override the loaded scales did not correspond to the weight rows of the rank. Each shard's scale is now loaded through `Linear.load_shard` exactly like its weight and concatenated along the out-features axis, so scales and weights always agree.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/_torch/modules/test_mxfp8_linear.py::test_mxfp8_fused_scales_follow_weight_rows_per_tp_rank`, parametrized over weight modes, shard row counts and even/uneven/replicated `override_tp_sharding`, checks that the loaded fused scales equal the per-rank rows of the reference scales.

items.title: [None][fix] Keep MiniMax-M3 streaming and non-streaming reasoning parsing in step
items.author: pranav-nvidia
items.summary: The MiniMax-M3 streaming and non-streaming reasoning parsers disagreed in three ways that clients can see: - A response that opens and is cut off by before closing it was returned by the non-streaming path as with the tag included, while streaming returned it …
items.body:
## Description

The MiniMax-M3 streaming and non-streaming reasoning parsers disagreed in three ways that clients can see:

- A response that opens `<mm:think>` and is cut off by `max_tokens` before closing it was returned by the non-streaming path as `content` with the tag included, while streaming returned it as `reasoning_content`.
- With thinking enabled the chat template prefills `<mm:think>` into the prompt, so the output carries no opening tag. Non-streaming split correctly on the closing tag, but streaming never entered the reasoning block and returned the whole reasoning followed by the literal `</mm:think>` as `content`. In the template's adaptive mode the model may also open with a bare `</mm:think>`, which streaming returned as content.
- Streaming matched `<mm:think>` anywhere while non-streaming only at the start.

The parser now takes its mode from the template's own `thinking_mode` when the caller passes it, and otherwise from the mode the server resolves off the rendered prompt through the existing `resolves_thinking_from_prompt` hook (`<mm:think>` at the prompt tail means reasoning is already open, `</mm:think>` means it is closed, neither means adaptive). A bare `thinking` flag, which the Responses path injects for `reasoning.effort` and which this template never reads, does not open the block. Both paths follow one contract: the tags are delimiters that never appear in the result, text before an opening tag is content, an unopened closing tag is the empty-reasoning sentinel, and an unclosed opening tag is truncated reasoning. Streaming also withholds a partial tag that follows text so a chunk boundary inside a tag cannot leak it.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/llmapi/test_reasoning_parser.py`: non-streaming shapes across the three modes (prefilled open, prefilled close, adaptive), stream-vs-non-stream parity for every three-way chunking of nine shapes in each mode, a random tag-soup parity test per mode, and the Responses-path case of an injected `thinking` next to a resolved mode of off.

## PR Checklist

items.title: [Feature][Ascend] Support sparse HCCL weight synchronization with pipeline parallelism
items.author: wangx700
items.summary: Add checkpoint-coordinate sparse HCCL synchronization from Megatron training workers to vLLM inference workers, with TP/PP/EP-aware export and native weight loading. The integration uses public sparse patch, trainer lifecycle and checkpoint-loader APIs.
items.body:
## Summary

Add checkpoint-coordinate sparse HCCL synchronization from Megatron training workers to vLLM inference workers, with TP/PP/EP-aware export and native weight loading.

The integration uses public sparse patch, trainer lifecycle and checkpoint-loader APIs. Ascend provides HCCL transport and temporary loader views for transposed MoE weights.

## Update flow

1. Pause generation and start the update lifecycle.
2. Export checkpoint names/shapes and gather changed flat int32 indices and replacement values on training rank 0.
3. Send bounded lists of `SparseWeightPatch` through `SparseHCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine.send_weight_chunk`.
4. All inference workers consume every broadcast before `is_pp_missing_parameter` filters parameters for the current pipeline stage. Native checkpoint loaders handle TP slicing and expert placement.
5. Restore inference-layout views, finish the update and resume generation. Potentially partial update failures prevent updater reuse.

The transfer group contains one independent trainer plus all inference workers: `1 + TP * PP * DP`. EP does not multiply this count again.

## Dependency patches

The NPU image keeps its pinned dependencies:

- vLLM: `e6bfe03ad73a3330cb427885aa90d97a12e1c704`.
- vLLM-Ascend: `fd815467c221ee600137f6bdd53fe354d5e7c999`.

`vllm.patch` retains the image compatibility changes; the pinned source already contains the required common sparse trainer and checkpoint loader. `vllm-ascend.patch` adds the sparse HCCL backend, loader views, communicator shutdown support and regression tests.

## Supported scope

- Separate training/inference devices; unquantized ND weights; static expert placement; EPLB disabled.
- Native per-parameter index/value transmission, without packed sparse transport or MoE direct writes.
- The first synchronization sends all checkpoint indices and values through the native sparse API. BF16 initialization requires six payload bytes per element, versus two for dense HCCL. Initialization must be reported separately from steady updates.
- Receiver checksum and rank-local verification metadata are not available in this protocol. Nonzero `--update-weight-delta-verify-every` fails explicitly; correctness is checked by the independent receiver oracle and trainer reconstruction tests.
- Updates are in-place and nontransactional. Quantized/NZ/split-expert storage and dynamic expert placement are unsupported.

## Validation

Verified in the existing VIME Docker container on an Ascend host, using complete pristine Python source snapshots at the pinned dependency revisions and retaining the installed native/CANN libraries. This is not a fresh Dockerfile image build result.

- Both patches pass pristine-source application and remote reverse-application checks; real imports resolve to the patched source trees.
- Native sparse engine: 45 unit tests passed.
- Expert/layout handling: 14 unit tests passed, including transpose-view storage preservation and exception restoration.
- VIME sparse/factory regression: 29 tests passed, including real four-rank HCCL gather and sparse reconstruction against full Bridge export.
- Five selected native test instances subsequently passed, covering seed/API behavior, two seed buffer capacities and one overlapping steady-update case. Counts from the two sessions must not be added as distinct tests.
- VIME launcher/API CPU suite: 70 tests passed using its expected CUDA platform setting.
- TP2/PP2/EP2 receiver hardware test: one passed, five deselected. Complete parameter hashes on every worker and generated tokens match native dense loading.

The receiver test's 144.55 seconds is the whole pytest session duration, not weight synchronization latency. The initial CPU-suite NPU/CUDA expectation mismatch is retained and explained in the evidence.

Test output is summarized below; validation logs are retained outside the repository.

```text
VIME sparse/factory regression: 29 passed, 37 warnings in 143.58s
Selected native seed/API cases: 5 passed, 17 deselected, 39 warnings in 37.61s
VIME launcher CPU suite: 70 passed, 14 warnings in 10.67s
Sparse engine unit tests: 45 passed, 16 warnings in 0.22s
Expert/layout unit tests: 14 passed, 17 warnings in 0.13s
TP2/PP2/EP2 receiver E2E: 1 passed, 5 deselected, 17 warnings in 144.55s
```

Timing note: all durations above are entire pytest sessions, not weight synchronization latency. Selected tests overlap one earlier case and must not be summed as a distinct total.

## Performance comparison

Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, TP2/PP2/EP2, four training and four inference devices, three training rounds. Both Ray jobs succeeded with driver exit code 0.

| Whole weight synchronization | Full HCCL | Native sparse HCCL |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial seed (s) | 132.6 | 10031.2 |
| Steady round 1 (s) | 97.5 | 116.1 |
| Steady round 2 (s) | 68.9 | 114.4 |
| Steady round 3 (s) | 91.7 | 151.8 |
| Steady mean (s) | 86.0 | 127.4 |
| Seed + three updates (s) | 390.7 | 10413.5 |

Table note: seconds are complete `update_weights` wall time, including update lifecycle, export/diff, gather, transfer and apply; training and generation are excluded. Seed is excluded from the steady mean. The two jobs use matching training arguments except update mode/transport, but run independent rollouts rather than identical-payload replay.

Native sparse steady updates took 48.1% longer in this run. Initialization was approximately 75.7x slower. No performance gain is claimed.

Sparse payload statistics: seed 174706.21 MiB / 441 flushes; steady rounds 297.75 / 445.17 / 474.14 MiB, each one flush. Payload figures count index/value tensor bytes once, excluding metadata and collective fan-out. Reduced payload did not reduce whole-update latency.

The native sender/receiver still issue two broadcasts per nonempty parameter. Both validate sparse indices; the common receiver loader constructs full-shape NaN staging tensors and uses masked model loading. These are code-supported cost sources, not measured per-stage attribution. Packed collectives alone would not remove full-shape reconstruction or trainer diff/gather cost.

The Ray job continued and completed successfully; client timeout is not reported as client success. Logs and source fingerprints are retained outside the repository.
