items.body:
## Summary

Restore CI coverage for the six transfer-lifecycle GPU cases waived under [NVBUG 6902353](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6902353). Repeated remote-cluster verification did not reproduce the worker-startup timeout with the original 120-second setting, supporting re-enabling these cases for validation in CI.

## Scope

Remove only the six case-specific entries in [`waives.txt`](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/c3327dd51466ee52487c4e3709dde534e908fb18/tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt): `baseline`, `cancel_before_publication`, `cancel_late_aux`, `cancel_late_kv`, `source_fatal`, and `timeout_late_aux`.
The existing [DGX B200 test-list entry](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/c3327dd51466ee52487c4e3709dde534e908fb18/tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_dgx_b200.yml#L57) is retained. Upstream subsequently added a `destination_fatal` waiver in [#20457](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20457); this rebase preserves that waiver, so this PR re-enables only the original six cases.
The [test harness](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/c3327dd51466ee52487c4e3709dde534e908fb18/tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_transfer_lifecycle_gpu.py), assertions, 120-second startup timeout, 600-second pytest timeout, and product code are unchanged.

## Verification

**Local checks at `c3327dd51466ee52487c4e3709dde534e908fb18`:** `pre-commit run --files tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt` and `git diff --check` passed, including waiver sorting/duplication, formatting, and AST test-list validation; the original DCO sign-off is retained. Rebasing onto `df4b424b0028a8838effbc4313c6411fb36d299d` resolved one waiver-list conflict by preserving upstream's new `destination_fatal` waiver and removing the same six entries. An independent CPU check executed the repository's CBTS `WaivesRule` on the base-to-head diff and selected the existing four-GPU MPI lifecycle-test block and exactly the three DGX B200 PyTorch stages below.

**Historical remote-cluster evidence, October 15, 2026 — four B200 GPUs:**

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Requested coverage | Seven cases × ten repetitions; 70 unique executions, no replays |
| Reconciled results | 68 JUnit/guard-validated passes |
| Incomplete final evidence | Two additional completed passing case-guard records; final JUnit was lost to ENOSPC |
| Observed test failures / skips / test errors | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Startup-120s / MPI-exit-60s / pytest-600s failures | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Slurm job `5023705` produced 21 validated passes and the two guard-only passes before ENOSPC interrupted result publication. Job `5025564` executed only the 47 never-started identities: all 47 passed, and the job completed with exit `0:0`. Repetition 4 was split across attempts; this is not a claim of ten uninterrupted pytest invocations or 70 fully validated passes. All 70 case-process cleanup guards settled without intervention.

The actual pytest invocations used `python3 -m pytest -p lifecycle_guard -vv -ra --tb=long -o junit_family=xunit2`, explicit lifecycle node IDs, and per-repetition JUnit/temporary directories. The original harness at `dc8451c50864edc07c75dedeafcb91dbb7a5d478` is byte-identical to this PR's harness (SHA256 `c51885ea28f18e879f8cbc1477bd9c7c26317887d340abff1715d39013d49409`); installed native runtime was `da676ffb8b611a1a0a83c862aa094e736f9fe5aa`, version `1.4.0rc1.dev202610140007`. This newer runtime and environment differ from the historical failing CI: intervening code, dependency, or environment changes may explain the difference, but no causal fix has been isolated.

**Rebased-head GPU CI has not been triggered by this workflow.** The multi-GPU stages require `ci: full pre-merge approved`, granted through the review/CI-approver workflow. At the post-rebase check, the required approval label was absent and no Jenkins pipeline had started; automatic GitHub repository checks were running. After approval, validate the current `DGX_B200-4_GPUs-PyTorch-1/2/3` stage family (sharding can move the test), confirming that the six re-enabled cases execute; `destination_fatal` remains waived by #20457. The offline results are supporting evidence, not an exact original-CI replay or a CI pass on this PR's native build; full pre-merge CI remains required separately from a stage-only run.

## Notes

Reverses the six waivers introduced by [#20235](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20235). items.title: fix(inference): AUT-2539 fail impossible KV handoffs on arrival and honor aborts
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: An for a handoff that was still queued or transferring was dropped, so the client never got a reply. A rejected handoff replies once through. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## Background

In disaggregated inference, a decode-side KV handoff that exceeded a fixed limit (the KV pool or the maximum sequence length) waited at the head of the capacity queue forever and blocked every later handoff. An `ABORT_REQUEST` for a handoff that was still queued or transferring was dropped, so the client never got a reply.

## What changed

- `dynamic_engine.py`: a shared `_request_limit_errors` helper checks each handoff against the `add_request` limits before it reserves cache state or joins the queue. A rejected handoff replies once through `_fail_submission`.
- An `ABORT_REQUEST` with no engine entry goes to `_abort_kv_handoff`:
  - A queued handoff replies at once.
  - A transferring import is marked cancelled. It is retired (released or quarantined) after every model-parallel rank reports its transfer terminal, and then it replies once.
- NCCL push path (`transfer_backends/nccl.py`): a rejected or aborted push handoff keeps its FIFO position as a discard. `begin_discard_blocks` posts matching receives into scratch buffers.
- Tests: new `test_disagg_handoff_lifecycle.py` and `test_nccl_transfer_backend.py`, new cases in `test_dynamic_engine.py`, and one updated test in `test_dynamic_engine_async_sched.py`.
- Merges main `ee6baa2e` (#8263). It seeds the models in `test_checkpoint_load_without_microbatch_calculator`, which hung the H100 unit job on `e638ce6a` in an NCCL barrier.

## Details

This fixes two review findings: impossible handoffs (F4) and aborts during a handoff (F5). A rejected or aborted handoff drains its transfer instead of cancelling it mid-flight.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Handoff arrives] --> B{Within request limits?}
  B -- no --> R[Reply failure once; NCCL push posts a discard receive]
  B -- yes --> Q[Capacity queue]
  Q -- abort --> X[Reply aborted once]
  Q --> T[Transferring]
  T -- abort --> C[Mark cancelled; retire after all MP ranks finish; reply once]
  T --> D[Admitted]
```

## Tested

- black, isort, pylint, ruff and py_compile pass on the changed files.
- On 8×H100 with the CI image `sha256:7b4e22a3`, `tests/unit_tests/**/*.py` ran on this head merged with the main tip (`ce8ee4cb`): 3424 passed, 142 skipped, 0 failed. A second pass ran 24 more tests, all passed. The exit code was 0, and `test_checkpoint_load_without_microbatch_calculator` finished.
- GitHub CI on this head has not reported yet.
- No functional test case covers the disaggregated KV handoff path.

items.title: refactor(hybrid): add LayerInputs call shape and core layer interface
items.author: jiemingz
items.summary: Hybrid layers currently require separate call signatures in the hybrid loop, checkpoint replay, shortcut blocks, and MTP depths. This adds across those paths and an experimental for cores that return additive updates.
items.body:
Hybrid layers currently require separate call signatures in the hybrid loop, checkpoint replay, shortcut blocks, and MTP depths. This adds `layer(hidden_states, LayerInputs)` across those paths and an experimental `LayerInterface` for cores that return additive updates. This is PR 1 of the five-part hybrid-layer interface refactor.

The change adds per-core and skeleton adapters, transitional `GraphableMegatronModule` dispatch, and `MoESubmodules.pre_norm` (defaulting to `IdentityOp`). MoE cores return routed and shared-expert outputs as separate addends while preserving dispatcher stream waits and cleanup. Hash routers retain token-ID gating, and checkpoint replay uses the same exact `MambaLayerConfig` predicate for chunkwise CP metadata as eager execution. Unsupported cross-attention calls fail explicitly, and the mHC recompute error points to the supported configuration.

Custom layers supplied to `HybridStack` must accept the new call shape; the migration guide documents this contract. Legacy forward APIs, the GPT `TransformerBlock` path, checkpoint names, CUDA-graph argument sets, functional recipes, and golden values are preserved. Scheduling, two-phase execution, and recurrent-state protocols remain follow-ups.

Validation:

- **Passed:** 35 mocked adapter/equivalence tests, Black 26.3.0, isort 5.13.2, pylint 3.2.6, ruff 0.16.10, and `git diff --check`.
- **Collected, not executed:** 39 GPU cases covering core/skeleton forward and backward equivalence, GDN2/GDP, shared MoE addends and normalization, residual-stream and mHC replay, static prefill/decode state, local CUDA graphs, and NVLS.

items.title: [None][feat] Expose standard gRPC health in OpenEngine
items.author: tanmayv25
items.summary: OpenEngine serves standard on its gRPC listener. Health, Inference, and Control use one port. [Discussion: To avoid overwhelming you with review comments due to an influx of new commits, CodeRabbit has autom]
items.body:
## Description OpenEngine serves standard `grpc.health.v1.Health` on its gRPC listener. Health, Inference, and Control use one port. `Check("inference")` reports whether the engine and frontend group can accept inference. `Control.Health` uses the same readiness conditions. `Check("")` mirrors inference. `Check("liveness")` reports server lifecycle, so temporary inference unavailability does not trigger a liveness failure. `Watch` sends the current status and later observed status changes. Rapid changes can coalesce; the stream reports the latest state and is not an event log. A failed monitor poll sets inference to `NOT_SERVING`; a later successful poll can restore it on a standalone server. The production launcher terminates on engine or coordinator failure and needs an external supervisor to restart it. `Control.Health` and standard Health use the same engine predicate; the background poll can lag a live Control check by up to one interval. Graceful shutdown sends `NOT_SERVING` and ends active streams. A background task checks engine health once each second; Health RPCs read published status. ## Single-port flow ```mermaid flowchart LR K["Kubernetes native gRPC probes"] -->|"Pod IP:30001, Health.Check"| O["OpenEngine gRPC

Build and identify an image from commit `cf918f6c04` before updating a DGD image reference. OpenEngine gRPC does not yet expose sleep or weight updates. When added, those operations must mark inference unavailable while it cannot run. ## Dependency maintenance OpenEngine maintainers own Health API behavior and compatibility with `grpcio-health-checking`. The package is a base TensorRT-LLM requirement, so a test environment missing it is an incomplete installation; skipping two tests would leave other OpenEngine modules unable to collect. Requirements changes receive requirements CODEOWNER review. items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
The current working-tree diff changes only formatting in `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_tool_parsers.py`. It does not modify `gemma4_parser.py`. The parser currently emits a tool name once known and waits until the end token to emit the JSON arguments. The supplied PR description attributes that behavior change to this PR, but the inspected diff does not show it.

## QA Engineer Review
The test file contains `test_streamed_arguments_match_whole_parse`, parameterized for chunk sizes 1, 3, and 8. It compares streamed call names and decoded arguments with one-shot parsing across two tool calls. The test is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`. The working-tree diff does not add this test, so its association with the current diff is unclear. Test execution results were not supplied. Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up**.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `tensorrt_llm/serve/tool_parser/gemma4_parser.py`: No working-tree changes detected. Its current streaming behavior sends the name once known and sends the parsed JSON arguments when the call ends.
- `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_tool_parsers.py`: The diff contains import and whitespace formatting changes. The file also contains a chunked-streaming regression test for matching streamed arguments to whole-call parsing; that test is listed in the CPU CI test list, but it is not added by the inspected diff.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

With `--tool_parser gemma4`, streaming `/v1/chat/completions` returns tool-call arguments that are not valid JSON whenever a call spans more than one increment, which is the normal token-by-token case.

`Gemma4ToolParser.parse_streaming_increment` sent the raw Gemma argument markup as argument deltas while a call was open, then appended the parsed JSON when `<tool_call|>` arrived. The serving layer forwards those deltas unchanged, so a client concatenating them gets, for `<|tool_call>call:get_weather{location:<|"|>Tokyo<|"|>,unit:<|"|>celsius<|"|>}<tool_call|>` streamed token by token:

    location:<|"|>Tokyo<|"|>,unit:<|"|>celsius<|"|>}{"location": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}

while the non-streaming parse returns `{"location": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}`.

The Gemma argument syntax only becomes JSON once the whole call is parsed, so the parser now sends the call name as soon as it is known (as before) and the arguments once, as the same JSON object `detect_and_parse` produces, when the end token arrives. `streamed_args_for_tool` records what was sent. After the change the streamed arguments above are `{"location": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}`.

## Test Coverage

- New `TestGemma4ToolParser::test_streamed_arguments_match_whole_parse[1|3|8]` in `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_tool_parsers.py`: streams two calls in chunks of 1, 3 and 8 characters and checks that the concatenated argument deltas equal the calls from `detect_and_parse`. It fails before the change (`JSONDecodeError`) and passes after.
- The existing Gemma4 tests in the same file pass unchanged.

items.body:
## Summary

The MPI launcher imports TensorRT-LLM again just to send its shutdown message, adding teardown latency to the remote-session tests reported in [NVBUG 6913451](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6913451). Use a standalone authenticated stop sender to avoid that extra import.

## Scope

- Install the [stop helper](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/6c62b795526350b59a1d8486f05641533f46717b/tensorrt_llm/llmapi/_llmapi_mpi_stop.py) beside the launcher, preserving the pickle/HMAC wire format and clearing the inherited session key.
- Use main's existing launcher flow and task/stop/server status precedence. The helper bounds socket send/linger to five/one seconds; it does not impose an end-to-end shutdown deadline.
- Add helper, launcher-routing/status and production Queue coverage to CPU CI, plus shutdown documentation.

## Verification

- Current head `6c62b795`: packaging fixture repaired; local packaging/helper/launcher tests **28 passed, 1 Linux-only skip**; hooks and DCO passed. [Full CI rerun requested](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20434#issuecomment-6220847622); GitHub authorization is queued and Jenkins launch is pending.
- [Main CI #64570](https://prod.blsm.nvidia.com/sw-tensorrt-top-1/job/LLM/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/64570/) at `1906eaf1` **failed**. ARM: **39/42 passed initially**; `flashinfer_workspace`, `flashinfer_temporary_cleanup`, and `client_sys_path` hit the unchanged 60-second watchdog, then passed on the MPI-suite retry. No affected tests were waived or skipped.
- x86 affected tests were unrun because of a build infrastructure failure. No paired baseline comparison was completed; **NVBUG resolution remains unverified**.

## Notes

Adapts the lightweight sender from [#20293](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20293). [#20232](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20232) separately ports lifecycle safeguards and removes main's eight-second polling delay; this PR leaves that polling behavior unchanged. Verification and maintainer review remain pending.

- [x] Reviewed the repository PR checklist; tests and documentation included. No new public API, dependency, ownership or architecture change.

| `gpt_dynamic_inference_tp4_etp1_pp1_ep8_16B_routing_replay_prefix_cache_cudagraph_async_sched` | H100 | `[mr]` → `[mr-broken]` |
| `gpt_dynamic_inference_tp4_pp1_ep4_16B_inference_optimized_swiglu_logitsmatch` | H100 | `[mr, mr-github-broken]` → `[mr-broken, mr-github-broken]` |

# What does this PR do?
<!-- Add a one line overview of what this PR aims to accomplish. -->

Seed both model constructions in `test_checkpoint_load_without_microbatch_calculator` with `torch.manual_seed(123)`.

The fixture seeds CUDA RNGs, but this test initializes its model weights on the CPU. Without an explicit CPU seed, data-parallel ranks can construct different reference weights. items.title: feat(inference): per-token NVFP4 squared-ReLU and SwiGLU MoE via FlashInfer CuTe DSL
items.author: YigongQin
items.summary: Adds a per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 routed-MoE path to Megatron inference for squared-ReLU (Nemotron-family) and SwiGLU experts, running on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped GEMMs. It is CUDA-graph capturable and batch invariant, and comes with the same te…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds a per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 routed-MoE path to Megatron inference for squared-ReLU (Nemotron-family) and SwiGLU experts, running on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped GEMMs. It is CUDA-graph capturable and batch invariant, and comes with the same test coverage the torch MXFP8 path has: a bitwise quantizer reference, a BF16 accuracy check, CUDA-graph replay, batch invariance, and a train-gen parity test against TE NVFP4 training. The NVFP4 weight path, CUDA-graph-stable refresh, batch-invariant finalize and tests are shared by FlashInfer's other NVFP4-weight recipes (per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4 and BF16 x NVFP4), so adding those later only changes the activation side; see "Strength: one integration for every NVFP4-weight recipe" and "How to extend".

## Background

**Recipe.** Weights are NVFP4 with 1x16 E4M3 block scales and one FP32 global scale per expert. Activations are quantized online with one FP32 scale per token instead of a static, calibrated per-tensor input scale. That removes the calibration step and the activation-outlier sensitivity of a per-tensor scale, which matters in RL because the policy weights change every step.

**Kernel level (FlashInfer).** All kernels already exist upstream; this PR only integrates them.
- [flashinfer#3027](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3027) adds per-token NVFP4 quantization (`nvfp4_quantize(..., per_token_activation=True)`) and the per-token TRT-LLM-gen MoE.
- [flashinfer#3645](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645) adds per-token NVFP4 activations to the CuTe DSL MoE (`CuteDslMoEWrapper.run(..., per_token_scale=...)`), the backend this PR uses.
- [flashinfer#3976](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3976) adds the deterministic two-stage finalize (`use_fused_finalize=False`) to the CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE, which batch-invariant mode uses.
- [flashinfer#4618](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4618) adds the ReLU2 (squared-ReLU) activation for per-token NVFP4 MoE, which Nemotron needs.
- FlashInfer 0.7.0 ships per-token NVFP4 with ReLU2 and SwiGLU on both the TRT-LLM-gen and the CuTe DSL (`CuteDslMoEWrapper`, `quant_mode="w4a4"`) MoE backends.

**Engine level (peers of Megatron inference).**
- [sglang#22918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22918) adds `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION`, which replaces the checkpoint's static input scales with 1 so FlashInfer computes per-token scales at runtime.
- [sglang#39199](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39199) routes ReLU2 per-token NVFP4 MoE to TRT-LLM-gen, padding hidden to 512 and intermediate to 128.
- Both are validated with GSM8K accuracy thresholds. Neither tests bitwise behavior, batch invariance, CUDA graphs, or train-gen parity.

**RL level.**
- [NeMo-RL#3566](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/3566) trains with TE NVFP4 (per-token activation scaling on routed experts), refits BF16 weights into vLLM, and quantizes the routed-expert weights to NVFP4 inside the rollout worker.
- [miles#1261](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/1261) does NVFP4 rollout/train with TE's `NVFP4Quantizer` producing the checkpoint and SGLang (FlashInfer TRT-LLM routed MoE) serving it.
- Both keep BF16 as the refit format and quantize on the inference side. This PR brings the same design to Megatron inference, so Megatron RL can roll out in per-token NVFP4 without an external engine.

**What Transformer Engine already has.** TE's `NVFP4BlockScaling` recipe supports `row_scaled_activation=True` (one scale per token), and with `disable_2d_quantization=True`, `disable_rht=True` and `disable_stochastic_rounding=True` it is the training-side form of this recipe. That is what NeMo-RL#3566 trains with, and it is the reference for the train-gen parity test below, in the same way TE MXFP8 is the reference for the MXFP8 inference path ([#8195](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8195)). TE has no inference MoE kernel for this recipe, so inference uses FlashInfer.

## What is added

**New config field.** `inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe: Optional[Literal['per_token']] = None` in `TransformerConfig` (`--inference-moe-nvfp4-recipe per_token`). It is a recipe choice rather than a bool so the other NVFP4 recipes (see "How to extend") can be added as new values. It requires `transformer_impl='inference_optimized'`, `inference_grouped_gemm_backend='flashinfer'`, non-gated `squared_relu` experts or gated `F.silu` (SwiGLU, `gated_linear_unit=True`) experts, without `activation_func_tanh_clamp_scale` and, for SwiGLU, without `activation_func_clamp_value`, `glu_linear_offset` or `moe_mlp_glu_interleave_size`, BF16 expert parameters (no `fp8` / `fp4_param`), and FlashInfer >= 0.7.0 on SM100/SM103. Validation rejects every other combination with a specific error. `batch_invariant_mode` is allowed with this recipe (with the NVLS dispatcher when EP > 1), as it is for FlashInfer MXFP8.

**`megatron/core/inference/moe/flashinfer_nvfp4.py` (new).**
- `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights` quantizes the BF16 FC1/FC2 expert stacks into the CuTe DSL layout: packed E2M1, 128x4-swizzled E4M3 block scales plus their MMA view, and per-expert FP32 alphas. SwiGLU is detected from the shapes (FC1 has twice FC2's input width): MCore's `[gate; up]` FC1 is padded per half and reordered into FlashInfer's alternating 64-row `[up, gate]` blocks. With `out=` it refreshes the existing buffers in place, so addresses captured by CUDA graphs stay valid across refits.
- `quantize_routed_nvfp4_input` pads and quantizes activations per token. The global scale is the recipe constant `1 / (448 * 6)` passed as a Python float, so there is no host sync and it is graph-safe.
- `flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe` runs `CuteDslMoEWrapper`. Wrappers are cached per shape and created outside graph capture. Under `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms` or batch-invariant mode it uses the two-stage finalize, which reduces each token's top-k routes in a fixed order, instead of the fused atomic finalize. With the NVLS dispatcher it writes straight into the reduce-scatter buffer, so `ordered_reduce_scatter_v` keeps the cross-rank reduction order fixed.

**`InferenceGroupedMLP` (`experts.py`).** The BF16 expert stacks stay resident as the canonical weights and refit destination. The NVFP4 copy is built on the first inference forward, and the FlashInfer forward dispatches to it. `refresh_flashinfer_nvfp4_weights()` requantizes it in place.

**Not in this PR: refit and RL.** Nothing calls `refresh_flashinfer_nvfp4_weights()` after a refit or an optimizer step yet, so don't set `inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe` for RL rollouts until the follow-up PR (TODO: link) lands. That PR wires the refresh into `megatron/core/resharding/refit.py` and `megatron/rl/rl_utils.py`; it is split out to keep the refit and RL reviewer groups off this PR. Static inference from a loaded checkpoint is unaffected.

**`moe_layer.py`.** The NVFP4 path checks for the FlashInfer per-token APIs instead of `flashinfer-jit-cache`, because CuTe DSL kernels are JIT-compiled through `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` rather than shipped in the jit-cache wheel.

**Dependencies.** `flashinfer-python` is relaxed from `<0.7.0` to `<0.8.0` and `uv.lock` moves to 0.7.0.post1, which adds `nccl-extensions`. `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` is already a dependency of `flashinfer-python`.

### Why CuTe DSL and not TRT-LLM-gen

Both FlashInfer backends support per-token NVFP4 with ReLU2 and SwiGLU on SM100/SM103. An earlier revision of this PR supported both; we kept only CuTe DSL:
- **No runtime downloads.** TRT-LLM-gen loads its cubins from an artifactory at first use (into `~/.cache/flashinfer/cubins` unless `flashinfer-cubin` is installed). On our test node that download failed with "Disk quota exceeded" and the GEMM then failed at 128 and 256 tokens. CuTe DSL compiles locally through `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`.
- **Controllable determinism.** CuTe DSL exposes `use_fused_finalize` ([flashinfer#3976](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3976)), which gives a fixed-order top-k reduction for batch-invariant mode. #3976 measures its cost at about 1.5-14% over the atomic finalize, highest at 1-4 tokens.
- **Less padding and simpler weight prep.** CuTe DSL pads to 256 (Nemotron 2688 -> 2816 hidden) where TRT-LLM-gen pads to 512 (2688 -> 3072), and it needs no TRT-LLM weight shuffling. A full requantization of 32 local experts (what each refit will cost) takes 16.7 ms against 21.5 ms for TRT-LLM-gen.
- **No speed reason to keep TRT-LLM-gen.** FlashInfer's own per-token comparison in [flashinfer#3645](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645) (`bench_moe_deepseek.py --use-per-token-activation`, DeepSeek-V3 shapes, B200, CUDA graphs) has TRT-LLM-gen about 12% faster at 128-256 tokens and CuTe DSL 1.12-1.29x faster from 512 to 4096 tokens, a 1.08x geomean in CuTe DSL's favor. Our earlier Nemotron-shape runs on GB300 showed the same pattern.

One backend also halves the test matrix and removes a config field.

### Performance

MoE layer forward (router, dispatcher, experts and combine) under CUDA-graph replay, on one GB300 with EP = 1. The shapes are the DeepSeek-V3 shapes that FlashInfer uses for its per-token CuTe DSL vs TRT-LLM-gen comparison in [flashinfer#3645](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645): hidden 7168, intermediate 2048, 256 experts (all local) and top-8. There are two differences from #3645. The experts are squared-ReLU, Nemotron's activation, where #3645 uses SwiGLU. TODO: add the SwiGLU numbers (`bench_moe_layer.py --activation swiglu`). Routing is plain top-8 without group-limited routing, because Megatron's inference router does not support it. All three backends load the same BF16 weights. Times are in µs, the mean over 50 replays.

| Tokens | Default: vLLM BF16 | Default: torch MXFP8 | Default: NVFP4 (this PR) | Batch-inv.: vLLM BF16 | Batch-inv.: torch MXFP8 | Batch-inv.: NVFP4 (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 140.4 | 138.2 | **56.6** | 179.7 | 237.4 | **82.3** |
| 8 | 507.1 | 526.4 | **187.2** | 575.3 | 488.1 | **215.2** |
| 32 | 1389.8 | 1604.4 | **488.7** | 1502.3 | 1188.0 | **522.7** |
| 64 | 1878.8 | 2074.0 | **626.9** | 1990.7 | 1519.1 | **662.7** |
| 128 | 2162.9 | 2352.7 | **704.1** | 2216.6 | 1695.1 | **739.8** |
| 256 | 2247.1 | 2407.9 | **723.7** | 2339.4 | 1739.6 | **758.1** |
| 512 | 2336.9 | 2433.8 | **739.0** | 2498.8 | 1792.4 | **772.5** |
| 1024 | 2732.7 | 2486.9 | **767.4** | 2994.2 | 1889.0 | **810.5** |
| 2048 | 3003.8 | 2650.0 | **822.5** | 3502.6 | 2081.8 | **879.0** |
| 4096 | 4054.7 | 3474.3 | **1015.6** | 5006.8 | 2560.6 | **1107.4** |

Batch-invariant mode uses the `te_native` backend for the non-MoE GEMMs (router) in all three columns.

- **Default mode:** NVFP4 is 2.5x faster than BF16 at 1 token, 3.2x at 512 and 4.0x at 4096, and 3.2-3.4x faster than MXFP8 from 64 tokens up.
- **Batch-invariant mode:** NVFP4 is 2.2x faster than BF16 at 1 token, 3.2x at 512 and 4.5x at 4096, and about 2.3x faster than MXFP8 from 8 tokens up. The deterministic two-stage finalize costs 26 µs at 1 token and 4-15% over default mode from 8 tokens up, in line with the 1.4-14% that [flashinfer#3976](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3976) reports.
- **Where the time goes at 512 tokens (default mode, profiled):** The expert GEMMs take 2180 µs in BF16, 1433 µs in MXFP8 and 656 µs in NVFP4, roughly in proportion to weight bytes. MXFP8 is no faster than BF16 overall because its unpermute kernel takes another 842 µs; in batch-invariant mode, MXFP8's expert-order unpermute takes 61 µs, which is why MXFP8 is faster there than in its own default mode.
- **Accuracy:** cosine similarity to vLLM BF16 is about 0.998 for MXFP8 and 0.98 for NVFP4 in both modes, which is the expected precision gap.
- **Memory:** layer memory after the first forward is 18.4 GB for NVFP4 against 14.4 GB for BF16, because the BF16 expert stacks stay resident as the refit source.

**Known gap with EP > 1.** With the NVLS dispatcher, the expert input buffer is sized for the largest batch across all ranks. The vLLM and MXFP8 paths process only the valid rows (vLLM reads a device-side `valid_tokens` count; FlashInfer MXFP8 takes `inference_flashinfer_mxfp8_token_capacity`), but the NVFP4 path quantizes and routes the whole buffer. On Nemotron-3 Super shapes at EP = 4 with an 8192-token buffer, this gives NVFP4 a floor of about 820 µs per layer, against 80 µs for BF16 at 1 token, although NVFP4 is still 1.4x faster than BF16 at 8192 tokens per rank. TODO: bound the NVFP4 rows the same way before marking this PR ready.

Requantizing a layer's expert weights for a refit takes 16.7 ms for 32 Nemotron-3 Super experts.

### Strength: one integration for every NVFP4-weight recipe

FlashInfer's `CuteDslMoEWrapper` runs three NVFP4-weight recipes on the same expert-weight layout: per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 (this PR), per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4, and BF16 x NVFP4. FlashInfer's own tests (`tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_fused_moe.py`, cases `w4a4-per-token`, `w4a4-per-tensor`, `w4a16` and `w4a16-relu2`) feed identical weight tensors to all three. Everything this PR builds is therefore shared, and the other two recipes only differ in how activations enter the kernel:
- **Weights:** `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights` (BF16 -> packed E2M1 with swizzled E4M3 block scales, padded to 256) and its in-place, CUDA-graph-stable refresh after refit.
- **Kernel plumbing:** the cached wrapper, the two-stage finalize for batch invariance, and writing into the NVLS reduce-scatter buffer.
- **Model integration:** the build, refresh and dispatch in `InferenceGroupedMLP`, and the config validation.
- **Tests:** the BF16 reference, CUDA-graph replay, batch invariance, and the layer and NVLS tests all take the recipe as a parameter.

`inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe` is a recipe choice rather than a bool for this reason: each variant below is a new value, not a new flag.

### How to extend

| | Per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 (this PR) | Per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4 | BF16 x NVFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Config value | `'per_token'` | `'per_tensor'` | `'weight_only'` |
| `quant_mode` | `w4a4` | `w4a4` | `w4a16` |
| FC1 input | `nvfp4_quantize(x, 1/(448*6), per_token_activation=True)` | `nvfp4_quantize(x, a1_scale)` with a fixed scale tensor | BF16 hidden states, padded; not quantized |
| `x_sf` | block scales | block scales | `None` |
| `per_token_scale` | from the quantizer | `None` | `None` |
| `fc1_alpha` / `fc2_alpha` | `1 / w_scale` | `1 / (w_scale * a1_scale)` / `1 / (w_scale * a2_scale)` | `1 / w_scale` |
| `fc2_input_scale` | `1/(448*6)` | `a2_scale` | `None` |
| Use case | RL rollout, no calibration | Serving calibrated (ModelOpt-style) checkpoints | 4x smaller expert weights at BF16 activation accuracy |

`w_scale` is the per-expert weight global scale that `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights` already computes. `a1_scale` / `a2_scale` are the static FC1 / FC2 input scales.

**Per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4 (`'per_tensor'`)**
1. **Config:** add `'per_tensor'` to the `Literal`, plus a way to supply the calibrated FC1 and FC2 input scales per layer (from a ModelOpt checkpoint's `input_scale`, or a calibration pass).
2. **`flashinfer_nvfp4.py`:**
   - Make `quant_mode` an argument of `_get_cute_dsl_wrapper` and part of its cache key; it stays `w4a4` here.
   - Add an input path that calls `nvfp4_quantize(padded_hidden, a1_scale)` without `per_token_activation`, and pass `per_token_scale=None`.
   - In `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights`, fold the activation scales into `fc1_alpha` / `fc2_alpha` and store `a2_scale` in `fc2_input_scale`. The packed weights and block scales don't change.
3. **Graph safety:** keep `a1_scale` / `a2_scale` in fixed device tensors, and confirm the tensor-scale quantizer path triggers no host sync under CUDA graphs.
4. **Tests:** add `'per_tensor'` to the recipe parametrization. The quantizer reference test gains a per-tensor case. The train-gen parity test doesn't apply: TE's per-tensor NVFP4 computes the activation scale from each tensor's amax at runtime, so it has no static-scale counterpart.

**BF16 x NVFP4 (`'weight_only'`)**
1. **Config:** add `'weight_only'` to the `Literal`. No calibration and no new inputs are needed.
2. **`flashinfer_nvfp4.py`:**
   - Create the wrapper with `quant_mode="w4a16"`.
   - Skip activation quantization: pad the BF16 hidden states to `padded_hidden_size` and pass them as `x`, with `x_sf`, `fc2_input_scale` and `per_token_scale` all `None`.
   - Weights, `fc1_alpha`, `fc2_alpha` and the refresh don't change.
3. **Tests:** add `'weight_only'` to the recipe parametrization. The quantizer reference test doesn't apply because there's no activation quantizer. The BF16 reference tolerance can be tighter, since only weights are quantized.

Both variants inherit the rest unchanged: batch invariance through the two-stage finalize (`w4a16` supports it too), CUDA-graph capture, NVLS, refit refresh, and support for squared-ReLU and SwiGLU experts.

## What is tested

The tests mirror the torch MXFP8 coverage from [#7302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7302) (batch invariance) and [#8195](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8195) (train-gen parity) and sit next to those tests. GPU tests skip unless FlashInfer >= 0.7.0 and SM100/SM103 are available; kernel tests are marked `launch_on_gb200`. Results below are from a GB300 4-GPU node (torch 2.11, FlashInfer 0.7.0, TE 2.18).

Run all commands from the repository root. Every NVFP4 kernel, layer, batch-invariance, NVLS and parity test is parametrized over squared-ReLU and SwiGLU.

### 1. Correctness

`tests/unit_tests/inference/test_flashinfer_nvfp4.py`
- **Quantizer bitwise reference** (`test_per_token_nvfp4_quantize_matches_reference`): FlashInfer's per-token quantizer matches a pure-torch reference of the recipe exactly (per-token scales, block-scale bytes and E2M1 codes), including an all-zero row and logspace-spread magnitudes. The reference mirrors TE's NVFP4 quantizer. It runs with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=1`; production keeps FlashInfer's default fast math.
- **Gated weight layout** (`test_gated_fc1_is_padded_per_half_and_interleaved_up_gate`, CPU): the SwiGLU FC1 reordering matches FlashInfer's interleaved `[up, gate]` layout exactly, including per-half padding.
- **MoE against BF16** (`test_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe_matches_bf16_reference`): the fused MoE stays within the expected NVFP4 error of a BF16 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU MoE (per-token cosine mean > 0.97, minimum > 0.95), including non-256-aligned shapes that exercise padding. Like MXFP8, the MoE itself is checked against BF16, not an emulated reference.
- **Layer level** (`TestNVFP4MoELayer`, NCCL and NVLS dispatchers): an `inference_optimized` MoE layer matches the BF16 training layer; refreshing after a BF16 weight update tracks the update; CUDA-graph replay follows new inputs and refreshed weights.
- **Config, dispatch and refresh plumbing**: accepted and rejected configurations, the missing-capability error message, in-place requantization, and dispatch to the NVFP4 path.

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_flashinfer_nvfp4.py
```
Result: 57 passed (squared ReLU and SwiGLU).

### 2. CUDA-graph capture and bitwise replay

`tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_inference_kernels.py` (next to `test_mxfp8_swiglu_moe_replays`): `test_per_token_nvfp4_quantize_replays` and `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_moe_replays`.

`tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py`: `TestMoEModules::test_inference_nvfp4_moe_layer_replays` replays the whole MoE layer.

The new kernels are registered in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` as `inference_flashinfer_nvfp4_moe`, and `test_manifest.py` checks the registration.

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_inference_kernels.py -k "nvfp4 or mxfp8"
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py -k nvfp4
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_manifest.py
```
Results: 9 passed (NVFP4 together with the existing MXFP8 cases), 2 passed, 269 passed.

### 3. Batch invariance

- **Kernel** (`test_inference_kernels.py::test_flashinfer_nvfp4_moe_is_batch_invariant`, next to `test_torch_mxfp8_moe_is_batch_invariant`): a target batch gives bitwise identical output alone and inside batches of 193 and 1024 tokens, where the co-batched tokens are 100x larger and routed to the same experts.
- **Local EP** (`test_flashinfer_nvfp4.py::test_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_is_batch_invariant`): the same check across local expert offsets, in deterministic and batch-invariant modes.
- **NVLS layer** (`test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py::TestNVLSAllGatherVDispatcher::test_cuda_graph_batch_invariant_nvfp4_moe_layer_uses_ordered_rsv`, next to the MXFP8 equivalent): with EP = 4 the layer writes into the reduce-scatter buffer, reduces with `ordered_reduce_scatter_v`, and CUDA-graph replay equals eager execution bitwise.

These run with the commands in sections 1 and 2, plus:

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py \
  -k "nvfp4 or test_batch_invariant_moe_matches_training"
```

### 4. Train-gen parity (expected failure for now)

`test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py::TestNVLSAllGatherVDispatcher::test_batch_invariant_nvfp4_moe_matches_training`, next to the MXFP8 `test_batch_invariant_moe_matches_training` from #8195. It loads the same weights into a TE training MoE layer running NVFP4 with row-scaled activations (`fp4="e2m1"` with the recipe from the Background section) and into the batch-invariant inference layer, then compares outputs.

**TE does not match bitwise yet.** The test asserts that generation is much closer to TE NVFP4 training than to BF16 (relative error less than half of the error against BF16), then calls `pytest.xfail` when the outputs are not bitwise equal. It measures about 0.03 relative error against TE NVFP4 training versus about 0.20 against BF16 for squared ReLU (maximum absolute difference about 0.0018), and about 0.035 versus 0.23 for SwiGLU (about 0.0008). The test reports XFAIL, which does not fail CI, and will start passing once the kernels are aligned. The known gaps are:
- Training applies the routing probabilities before quantizing the FC2 input; the FlashInfer kernel applies them in the finalize, after FC2.
- The CuTe DSL kernel quantizes the FC2 input inside the FC1 epilogue with approximate reciprocals. `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH` only affects the standalone quantizer, so this step can't be made IEEE-exact today.
- The GEMMs differ in how the FC1 output is rounded and in accumulation order.

Command: the `test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py` command in section 3.

Result: 6 passed, 4 skipped, 2 xfailed (the parity test for squared ReLU and SwiGLU). The skips are pre-existing MXFP8 parity cases that need DeepGEMM BF16 or cuBLASLt 13.5.1.

### 5. Regressions

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_flashinfer_mxfp8.py
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py
```
Results: 28 passed for `test_flashinfer_mxfp8.py`; 61 passed, 5 skipped and 2 xfailed (the parity test above) for the dispatching file. The skips are pre-existing torch and MXFP8 cases that need DeepGEMM BF16 or cuBLASLt 13.5.1.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

items.author: andakai
items.summary: Adds RL support for Muse Spark 816B-A42B (NVFP4 MoE) on the FSDP2 engine: GRPO with LoRA against a vLLM rollout that serves the NVFP4 checkpoint, rollout routing replay (R3), and adapter-only weight sync. verl has no Muse Spark model, so the PR adds a verl-nat…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds RL support for **Muse Spark 816B-A42B** (NVFP4 MoE) on the FSDP2 engine: GRPO with LoRA against a vLLM rollout that serves the NVFP4 checkpoint, rollout routing replay (R3), and adapter-only weight sync. verl has no Muse Spark model, so the PR adds a verl-native text model and an example, plus the generic changes the run needs. The trainer reads the same NVFP4 checkpoint as vLLM and dequantizes the routed experts to BF16 while loading its FSDP2 shards. Each commit can be reviewed on its own:

| # | Commit | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `[fsdp] fix: bound the padded micro-batch size when use_remove_padding=False` | dynamic bsz without remove-padding |
| 2 | `[fsdp] feat: support R3 router replay` | FSDP engine, off by default |
| 3 | `[fsdp] feat: opt-in sharded FSDP2 init straight from safetensors` | `VERL_FSDP2_SHARDED_INIT=1` only |
| 4 | `[fsdp] feat: keep _keep_in_fp32_modules in fp32 FSDP units` | models declaring `_keep_in_fp32_modules` |
| 5 | `[fsdp, rollout] feat: stream model-native LoRA exports in adapter-only sync` | models defining `export_serving_lora` |
| 6 | `[rollout, vllm] fix: LoRA weight sync for checkpoint-quantized rollouts` | LoRA sync to vLLM |
| 7 | `[fsdp, model] feat: Muse Spark text model for FSDP2 LoRA RL` | `model_type == "muse_spark_text"` only |

**Dependency on vLLM.** The rollout needs a vLLM build that serves Muse Spark with LoRA on its fused attention
projection and routed experts. Those vLLM changes are being upstreamed separately.

### Test

- GPU: the example recipe on 4 nodes x 4 GB300, 150 steps from scratch. LoRA r32/α64 on attention, the MoE latent projections and the routed experts; GRPO with 32 prompts × 8 samples, lr 1e-5, 4096-token responses, R3. AIME-2024 mean@8 went from 0.56 to 0.85, and the train/rollout k3 KL stayed near 2×10⁻⁴.

![Muse Spark LoRA RL: AIME-2024 mean@8 and train/rollout k3 KL](https://github.com/andakai/verl/blob/8a16367eefcc92179eb99a9d8c476a9cad39fdb1/muse_spark_lora_rl_curves.png?raw=true)

### Usage

```bash
model_path=<Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4> bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_muse_spark_dapo_lora_fsdp.sh
```

Depends on #16309. Only the last commit belongs to this PR.

## Description

- Add `CSA2VanillaAttention` and a weightless `CSA2VanillaIndexer` (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/csa2/vanilla_backend.py`), a pure-PyTorch golden reference for CSA2 sparse attention:
  - On a layer's first call, write the new sliding-window rows and, on the layer that owns the shared cache, every compressed group the forward completes.
  - Publish the selection in production's format, plus the candidate list on the candidate-source layer (ascending blocks, newest block always kept, entries past the visible count masked).
  - Select an exact top-k over visible entries on mapped pages, restricted to the published candidates for a REINDEX consumer.
  - Attend over the window plus the selected rows with the attention sink; an empty selection gives zeros.
- Geometry comes from independent sources: positions from `kv_lens_cuda - seq_lens` and pages from the cache manager's host page lists. The golden never reads the kernel-produced slot tables, page tables or visible lengths.
- Rejected before anything is written: packed attention, decoder replay geometry, remote-tail and precomputed-KV passes, mixed-phase calls and CUDA graph capture. FP8 staging, approximate top-k and pre-packed index queries are accepted, but the golden always decodes, stages and selects exactly.
- Move the RoPE and phase helpers shared with the DSA golden into `sparse/_vanilla_utils.py` (pure move; the `phase_is_generation` error now says "Sparse MLA requires…" instead of "DSA requires…", and `DSAVanillaEmbedding` is no longer listed in the DSA golden's `__all__`).

Scope: the sparse registry and the CSA2 module are unchanged, so `attn_backend="VANILLA"` still raises for `csa2` (the module builds `create_attention("TRTLLM", ...)`). Tests construct the golden directly; plumbing the configured backend into the module is a separate change. Like the other Vanilla goldens, it rejects CUDA graph capture.

`tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/csa2/test_vanilla_backend.py`:
- CPU-tensor tests with hand-derived expected values on shuffled and partly unmapped pages: selection and candidate publication, cache writes, a REINDEX consumer, attention-only decode, and rejection before writing.
- SM100 GPU test running VANILLA, TRTLLM, and TRTLLM with the golden's selection injected on separate cache managers through a prefill forward and a chunked-prefill + decode forward:

items.title: [MoE] Opt-in EP-size-invariant expert combine (exact fixed-point reduction)
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: if you want to take a look I hate this kernel and need a better way but putting up for others in case they need.I dont like the downsides of this kernel. The rounding points therefore move with the expert-parallel size.
items.body:
DONT MERGE! if you want to take a look I hate this kernel and need a better way but putting up for others in case they need.I dont like the downsides of this kernel.

**Problem.** Under `batch_invariant_mode`, the MoE combine sums each token's local expert outputs per EP rank, rounds that partial to fp32, and then adds the rank partials in rank order. The rounding points therefore move with the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout. That rules out, for example, training at EP8 while generating at EP4.

Here is what we measured on Nemotron-3-Nano (top-6, hidden 2688), in our RL setup, which uses the same combine:
- One MoE layer at EP2 vs EP1 gives a different result for 98% of tokens, about 1 ulp per element.
- Over 8 layers, greedy-decode log-probs differ by up to 0.28 between an EP1 and an EP2 engine.
- In an RL run with training at EP2 and generation at EP1, log-probs of sampled tokens differed by up to 0.89.

**Change.** This adds an opt-in flag, `moe_ep_invariant_combine` (default `False`, requires `batch_invariant_mode`).
- With the flag on, each expert output value v becomes two fp64 integer limbs: `hi = floor(v)` and `lo = round((v - hi) * 2^48)`. The token's limbs are then summed.
- Every partial sum is an integer below 2^53, so each addition is exact, and any grouping or order of a token's rows gives the same sums. That holds because top-k is at most 32, checked at config time, and `|hi|` is capped at 2^47.
- The result is rounded once to fp32. Round-to-odd in fp64 makes that the correctly rounded value of the exact sum.
- Values that are multiples of 2^-48 are represented exactly, for example bf16 values ≥ 2^-41. Finer bits are rounded to that grid, which keeps the result EP-invariant.

What the flag covers:
- **Training, AllToAll dispatcher:** the batch-invariant unpermute sums the token's top-k rows through the limbs, without grouping by EP rank. No extra communication is needed, because the AllToAll already returns all k rows to the token's rank.
- **Training, AllGather dispatcher:** each rank builds an fp64 limb partial for its experts, which is reduce-scattered and then finalized.
- **Inference, `torch` grouped-GEMM backend with the NVLS dispatcher:** the unpermute kernel writes the limb partial into the RSV symmetric buffer, which is sized 4x. A limb reduce-scatter kernel then sums it and finalizes. At EP1 the kernel finalizes directly. All of this is CUDA-graph safe.
- **Not covered:** the NCCL inference dispatcher and the FlashInfer/vLLM backends. Batch-invariant mode at EP > 1 already requires NVLS, and the flag rejects backends other than `torch`.

**Cost.** The inference combine moves 16 bytes per element instead of 4, and the RSV symmetric buffer grows by the same 4x. Measured on one GB200 node with the same kernels in our setup:
- Full Nano engine decode at EP4: 8.46 → 8.88 ms per step (+5%).
- Combine per MoE layer at EP4, 128 tokens per rank: 27 → 56 µs.
- Combine per MoE layer at EP4, 4096 tokens per rank (prefill): 0.44 → 1.14 ms.
- Training: no extra bytes, and the unpermute kernel is not slower.

It is off by default because, when both sides use the same EP, the existing combine is already exact and cheaper. The flag is only needed when the training and inference EP sizes differ.

**Testing.** Added `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_moe_ep_invariant_combine.py`. All 11 tests pass on 1 and 2 GB200 GPUs:
- The limbs are exact, and the finalized value is the correctly rounded fp32 sum, checked against `Fraction` arithmetic.
- Any split or order of a token's rows gives the same bits.
- The training unpermute (with and without probs) gives the same bits at EP 1/2/4/8. With the flag off, it is unchanged and still EP-dependent. Gradients match the plain sum.
- The inference unpermute kernel's per-rank limb partials, summed in either rank order, equal the EP1 result and equal the training result.
- The AllGather limb partial gives the same result at EP 1/2/4, and its backward is correct.
- Config validation.

items.title: Refresh MFSDP v2 compute weights on optimizer checkpoint loads; add EP ckpt-resume test
items.author: ahmadki
items.summary: Follow-up to #8230, which refreshes MFSDP v2's BF16 compute weights in after a checkpoint load. Not every load goes through that method. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #8230, which refreshes MFSDP v2's BF16 compute weights in `FullyShardedDataParallelV2.load_state_dict` after a checkpoint load. Not every load goes through that method. The GPT→Hybrid `fsdp_dtensor` load (`gpt_fsdp_model_loaded_in_place` in `megatron/training/checkpointing.py`) writes the main weights in place and then only calls `FullyShardedOptimizer.load_state_dict`, or `optimizer.reload_model_params()` under `--no-load-optim`. Neither refreshed the compute weights, so the first resumed step ran on the pre-load weights.

This PR:
- Refreshes compute weights from `FullyShardedOptimizer.load_state_dict` and from a new `reload_model_params` override. Both iterate the model chunks' parameters rather than `get_parameters()`, because frozen parameter groups also keep separate compute weights and the load writes their main weights too. On a normal resume the refresh now runs twice (adapter and optimizer); the cost is one local cast of each group's main weight per load.
- Adds two EP=2 cases to `test_ep_fsdp_checkpoint_roundtrip`, each with a frozen word embedding, that skip the wrapper's `load_state_dict` the way the GPT→Hybrid load does:
  - `ep2_optimizer_only` loads the optimizer and compares all five resumed losses exactly;
  - `ep2_reload_model_params` loads no optimizer state, calls `reload_model_params()`, and compares the first loss, which depends only on the loaded weights.
- Adds `deepseek_proxy_mfsdp_v2_ep2_resume`, an mr-scope `ckpt-resume` twin of `deepseek_proxy_mfsdp_v2_ep2`. It saves at iteration 25 and resumes, so iterations 26–50 must match. Every other v2 functional test is `TEST_TYPE: regular`, so until now nothing in CI saved a v2 model and read it back through `load_checkpoint`. At 8 GPUs, EP=2 gives expert-DP 4, so expert shards are really split across ranks. Memory metrics are not compared, since a resumed process allocates differently.

## Issue tracking

Depends on #8230 (stacked on its head). Related to #6215.

## Validation

All on 2× RTX 6000 Ada, NGC PyTorch 26.08 (torch 2.14, TE 2.19).

- `test_checkpoint.py` + `test_optimizer_checkpoint.py`: **15 passed, 1 skipped** per rank (EP=4 needs 4 GPUs).
- Negative controls for the two new cases:
  - On #8230 without this change, both fail: `ep2_optimizer_only` on 5/5 losses (max abs diff 0.214), `ep2_reload_model_params` on the first loss (0.200).
  - Refreshing only `get_parameters()` also fails both (0.197), because the frozen embedding stays stale.
- The functional test was not run locally (it needs 8×H100 and the CI datasets). Its golden values (`golden_values_dev_dgx_h100.json` and `_2nd.json`) still need to come from a CI run.
- black 26.3.0, isort 5.13.2, ruff 0.9 and pylint 3.2.6 (10.00/10) pass on the changed Python files.

items.title: fix(inference): AUT-2539 skip prefill token limit for imported decode pr
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: Unless chunked prefill was enabled, failed any prompt longer than with. That limit bounds how much prefill work one step does. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## Background

In disaggregated serving, `_finalize_kv_handoff_import()` admits an imported decode request through `add_request()`. Unless chunked prefill was enabled, `_add_request()` failed any prompt longer than `context.max_tokens` with `TokenOverflowError`. That limit bounds how much prefill work one step does. An imported prompt's KV cache already exists and the request goes straight to decode, so a long disaggregated prompt failed on the decode engine.

## What changed

- `dynamic_engine.py`: `add_request()` and `_add_request()` take a keyword-only `prompt_is_prefilled: bool = False`. `add_request()` forwards it from both of its `_add_request()` call sites (text and VLM). When the flag is set, only the `max_tokens` check is skipped. The max sequence length and KV-pool checks still apply.
- `inference_state_handoff.py`: the import finalizer passes `prompt_is_prefilled=True`.
- Tests:
  - `test_add_request_forwards_prompt_is_prefilled` in `test_dynamic_engine.py`.
  - Parametrized finalizer and limit tests in `test_disagg_handoff_lifecycle.py`.
  - The refit test's `_add_request` double now accepts the new keyword.

## Details

The default is `False`, so every other caller behaves as before. No subclass overrides `_add_request`. This was split out of the inference review and is independent of #8258.

## Tested

- black, isort, pylint (10.00/10) and ruff are clean on the 4 changed files.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6758245][fix] Keep /metrics from blocking the serving event loop
items.author: JunyiXu-nv
items.summary: Fixes https://nvbugs/6758245: turning off made serving slower. A Kimi K3 benchmark on Rubin, scraping every 1-2 s, measured 16.3% lower output tokens/s with the stats off than with them on.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Fixes https://nvbugs/6758245: turning `enable_iter_perf_stats` off made serving slower. A Kimi K3 benchmark on Rubin, scraping `GET /metrics` every 1-2 s, measured 16.3% lower output tokens/s with the stats off than with them on.

`/metrics` serves from the background collector's buffer only when both `return_perf_metrics` and `enable_iter_perf_stats` are on. In every other configuration it reads iteration stats through `get_stats_async(2)`. Since #9980, the executor call behind that (`proxy.aget_stats` / `rpc_proxy.aget_stats`) is a blocking `.remote()` RPC, and the worker side polls until stats arrive or 2 s pass. The call runs on the server's event loop, so every scrape froze every streaming response for the length of the wait. With iteration stats off, no stats ever arrive, so each scrape froze it for the full 2 s.

- **Stats off** (commit by Bowen Fu, from #19517): `/metrics` returns `[]` at once instead of waiting for stats that never come.
- **Stats on without the collector:** the read now runs in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread(self.generator.get_stats, 2)`), so streaming continues while it waits. `LLM.get_stats` returns the same parsed stats as the async path.
- **RPC failures:** on the default MPI proxy, `get_stats` raises the RPC errors that `aget_stats` used to swallow. The handler catches `RPCError` (for example `RPCCancelled` while the executor shuts down) and still returns `[]` rather than a 500.

This supersedes #19517 and carries its commit with its authorship.

`tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_openai_server_iteration_stats.py` was not on any CI list, so none of its tests had run in CI. It is now registered in `l0_cpu.yml`, with the `cpu_only` marker that the CPU stages select on.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_openai_server_iteration_stats.py` (CPU-Generic-x86-1, CPU-Generic-arm-1):
  - `test_metrics_endpoint_does_not_block_the_event_loop` (new): a stats read that blocks for 0.5 s leaves the event loop running.
  - `test_metrics_endpoint_reports_no_stats_when_executor_unreachable` (new): an `RPCCancelled` from the stats read gives 200 with `[]`.
  - The two tests from #19517 cover the stats-off early return at handler and route level.
  - The existing tests cover the buffered and legacy paths.
- Measured on Blackwell (1x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell) with `trtllm-serve` from the 1.2.0rc8 release container. Its `/metrics` handler is main's legacy path (the collector-buffer branch, which this configuration does not take, came later), and its `proxy.aget_stats` / `proxy.get_stats` are the same as main's. The "this PR" rows apply this change to its `get_iteration_stats`. Qwen3-0.6B, ISL 1024 / OSL 768, 32 streaming requests at concurrency 1, and a client that calls `/metrics` 1 s after each response:

  | `enable_iter_perf_stats` | `/metrics` polling | handler | output tok/s | max ITL | ITLs > 0.5 s | `/metrics` p50 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | off | none | - | 392.2 | 9 ms | 0 | - |
  | off | 1 s gap | before | 303.6 (-22.6%) | 2040 ms | 16 | 4026 ms |
  | on | 1 s gap | before | 388.6 | 74 ms | 0 | 2074 ms |
  | off | 1 s gap | this PR | 391.9 | 9 ms | 0 | 1 ms |
  | on | 1 s gap | this PR | 389.0 | 21 ms | 0 | 33 ms |

  A repeat of all five runs matched within 0.1% output tok/s. With `/metrics` called 2 s after each response instead, stats off measured 379.5 tok/s with 10 ITLs over 0.5 s before this change, and 391.9 tok/s with none after it.
- Locally (no build), the shipped `get_iteration_stats` was run with a stats read that blocks for 0.5 s, mimicking the executor RPC:
  - On main, the event loop got 0 turns during the call, with stats on or off.
  - On this branch, it got 49 turns with stats on, and the stats-off call returned `[]` at once without calling the executor.
- Not yet run: this file's pytest suite (it has never run in CI; it runs in this PR's CPU stages) and a Kimi K3 rerun on Rubin.

items.title: [#19726][perf] Add opt-in compact beam execution for VBWS
items.author: yifanQi98
items.summary: Implements an opt-in prototype for #19726. During variable-width beam search, the decoder currently executes rows per request even when only a smaller prefix is active.
items.body:
## Description

Implements an opt-in prototype for #19726. During variable-width beam search, the decoder currently executes `max_beam_width` rows per request even when only a smaller prefix is active. `compact_beam_widths=[20, 300]` permits those decode steps to gather active rows for the model forward, then restore capacity-stride logits for the existing sampler.

The change adds:

- Per-shape attention metadata views that preserve physical KV page IDs and parent-beam indices.
- CUDA graph keys/capture/replay for each configured execution width, with in-place metadata refresh and strict buffer checks.
- Integration with the existing eager workspace reclaimer, including releasing cached references after workspace replacement.
- Configuration validation, the telemetry manifest entry, documentation, and regression coverage.

The default is disabled. Initial support is single-GPU dense Llama/Qwen2/Qwen3, TRTLLM attention, pure single-token decode, and a uniform input beam width across real requests. Configured compact widths must be at least 2; width-one steps retain the beam attention path at capacity. Unsupported model configurations and unconfigured widths retain capacity execution. LoRA combinations are rejected. KV allocation and sampling continue to use capacity-stride layouts. The public-model runtime experiments below cover Qwen3; the other two supported model families still need model-level CI coverage.

**This is a Draft.** The patch targets `main` at `ed87ab0b0152faa6c4bae19fe6acc44dcad86fb5`. Local GPU validation used the corresponding Python change on **v1.4.0rc0 (`cc63e66daf52644f1441e117bb7ba67d20566016`) with matching precompiled rc0 artifacts**, installed editable through `TRTLLM_PRECOMPILED_LOCATION`. Current-main runtime/ABI validation remains for upstream CI; rc0 results are not presented as a current-main runtime pass.

### Numerical behavior needs review

Changing the forward shape can change attention/GEMM kernel selection and floating-point reductions. The option does **not** guarantee bitwise equality or identical beam rankings/top-1, and it does not change the engine's numerical policy.

Public `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, BF16, full vocabulary:

| Experiment | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Capacity 5, schedule `[2,2,4,4,5,5]`, two prompts, eager/CUDA graph × overlap off/on | Full ordered token lists and cumulative scores matched in all four configurations. |
| Prompts of 30 and 62 tokens crossing KV-page boundaries; single-request graph padding; CUDA graphs with overlap off/on | Token ordering matched. One prompt with overlap had a maximum cumulative-score difference of `0.07464695`; other compared scores matched. |
| Capacity 500, schedule `[20,20,300,300,500,500]`, default numerical policy, CUDA graphs + overlap | Top-1 matched for both prompts. Candidate intersections were **487/500 and 255/500**; only **39/500 and 8/500** candidates occupied the same rank. Maximum shared-candidate score differences were `0.28159046` and `2.18630552`. Each configuration's outputs were stable across repetitions. |
| Same capacity-500 case, with **both sides** using MMHA block size 256, cuBLASLt and BF16 reduced-precision/split-K reductions disabled | Both full 500-candidate lists, ordering and cumulative scores matched exactly. |

The shared-policy experiment supports a numerical-path explanation for the observed differences; it is not a proof of equivalence under the default policy. In particular, the default-policy candidate changes above should not be described as merely tail reordering or negligible error. Workload-quality acceptance remains a review item. The shared numerical settings are diagnostic only and are **not introduced by this PR**.

### Performance (exploratory, rc0)

GPU: **NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell**; PyTorch **2.14.0+cu132**; TRT-LLM **1.4.0rc0**. Public Qwen3-0.6B revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, BF16/full vocabulary, capacity 500, schedule `[20,20,300,300,500,500]`, batch of two prompts, CUDA graphs and overlap enabled, block reuse disabled. The comparison switches only `compact_beam_widths`; it uses the default numerical policy and native sampler.

Four fresh-process pairs, alternating A/B and B/A order. Each process ran three warmups and 20 timed calls. Times are wall-clock latency for a **two-request `LLM.generate` call**, including output handling, with CUDA synchronization around the call. The GPU experiments ran sequentially.

| Pair | Capacity execution median | Compact median | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 152.223 ms | 136.919 ms | 10.05% |
| 2 | 150.491 ms | 138.174 ms | 8.18% |
| 3 | 150.943 ms | 137.439 ms | 8.95% |
| 4 | 150.179 ms | 137.546 ms | 8.41% |

Geometric mean reduction across pair medians: **8.90%**. An approximate paired t interval on log ratios is 7.56–10.22%, based on only four process pairs. This is a single-GPU, two-prompt exploratory result, not a general performance or accuracy claim. Capacity-5 validation showed no consistent speedup. Extra graph memory, warmup, metadata packing and full-vocabulary logits padding are costs of this implementation.

<details>
<summary>Public-model reproducer</summary>

Run each side in a fresh process: `python reproduce.py 0` for capacity execution and `python reproduce.py 1` for compact. Repeat in A/B, B/A, A/B, B/A order. Use the patched rc0 source with matching rc0 binaries to reproduce the local measurements, or a matching build of the PR branch for current-main validation.

```python
import json
import os
import sys
import time

os.environ["TLLM_WORKER_USE_SINGLE_PROCESS"] = "1"
import torch
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from tensorrt_llm import LLM, SamplingParams
from tensorrt_llm.llmapi import CudaGraphConfig, KvCacheConfig

compact = bool(int(sys.argv[1]))
model = snapshot_download(
    "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
    revision="c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca",
)
llm = LLM(
    model=model, backend="pytorch", dtype="bfloat16",
    max_batch_size=2, max_seq_len=1000, max_num_tokens=1000,
    max_beam_width=500, compact_beam_widths=[20, 300] if compact else [],
    cuda_graph_config=CudaGraphConfig(batch_sizes=[1, 2]),
    disable_overlap_scheduler=False,
    kv_cache_config=KvCacheConfig(max_tokens=128000, enable_block_reuse=False),
)
prompts = ["The capital of France is", "A good way to learn mathematics is"]
params = SamplingParams(
    max_tokens=6, n=500, best_of=500, use_beam_search=True,
    beam_width_array=[20, 20, 300, 300, 500, 500],
    ignore_eos=True, logprobs=0,
)
for _ in range(3):
    llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
latency_ms = []
for _ in range(20):
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start = time.perf_counter()
    result = llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    latency_ms.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
print(json.dumps({
    "compact": compact, "latency_ms": latency_ms,
    "outputs": [[{"tokens": o.token_ids, "score": o.cumulative_logprob}
                 for o in request.outputs] for request in result],
}))
llm.shutdown()
```

For the separate shared-policy diagnostic, set the following **in both processes**, before constructing `LLM`. These settings must not be used to claim equality with the default-policy baseline:

```python
os.environ["TRTLLM_MMHA_KERNEL_BLOCK_SIZE"] = "256"
torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library("cublaslt")
torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = (False, False)
```

</details>

## Test Coverage

- New `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_beam_compaction.py`: active-row selection across requests, physical KV offsets, cache indirection, width selection with overlap/dummies, fallback/configuration boundaries, metadata isolation, repeated eager/graph execution, actual graph-runner width switching, stale-view rejection, workspace reclamation and explicit host allocation. Its parent directory is already included in `l0_h100.yml`.
- rc0 targeted executor suite: **151 passed, 1 failed, 39 subtests passed**. All **25 new tests passed**. The remaining existing `test_prepare_tp_inputs_with_helix_parallelism` fails because `AttentionMetadata.update_helix_param()` rejects `helix_owned_new_tokens`. It was also reproduced after restoring all modified existing runtime source files to the unmodified rc0 versions; those files were then restored to the patch. Helix is outside the enabled compact scope.
- Public-model experiments described above, with actual compact/replay-width traces and strict graph buffer checking during functional validation.
- Current-main changed Python files: syntax and `git diff --check`; repository pre-commit checks passed.
- Official manifest generator and `--check` passed on patched rc0. The generated `compact_beam_widths` entry was carried into the existing main manifest. Main's full generator check is blocked by its unavailable compiled `tensorrt_llm.bindings`; upstream CI should verify it. **Telemetry/privacy CODEOWNER review is requested for the new public field.**

Relevant local test command:

```bash
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/{test_beam_compaction,test_cuda_graph_capture_replay,test_cuda_graph_runner,test_eager_workspace_engine,test_pytorch_model_engine}.py -q
```

## PR Checklist

- Description, numerical limitations and testing boundaries documented.
- Coding guidelines and repository checks applied; commits are DCO-signed.
- New paths have regression tests and existing GPU CI-list coverage.
- Additive, default-disabled API change; `api-compatible` label requested.
- Documentation and telemetry manifest updated. No dependency or ownership changes.
- Current-main GPU CI, other supported model-family validation, numerical-quality acceptance, and telemetry/privacy review remain pending while this is a Draft.

items.title: fix(inference): AUT-2539 handle string prompts and rejections in KV hand
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: The inference review found two gaps: - accepts a string or a token list and forwards a string unchanged. The decode side called on the prompt, so a string prompt raised inside the engine loop.
items.body:
## Background

Decode engines in disaggregated serving admit prefilled requests through `add_request_with_kv_handoff()`. The inference review found two gaps:
- `InferenceClient.add_request_with_kv_handoff()` accepts a string or a token list and forwards a string unchanged. The decode side called `torch.tensor()` on the prompt, so a string prompt raised inside the engine loop.
- Unlike `SUBMIT_REQUEST`, the `SUBMIT_REQUEST_WITH_KV` handler in `schedule_requests()` had no `try/except`. That error, or any other handoff validation error, escaped the loop and the client never got a reply.

## What changed

- `inference_state_handoff.py`: `prompt` is typed `str | list[int]`. A string prompt is tokenized once with `controller.tokenize_prompt(tokenizer, prompt, sampling_params.add_BOS)` before block hashing. The deferred and pending import records and the finalizer's `add_request()` then all carry the same token IDs.
- `dynamic_engine.py`: the `SUBMIT_REQUEST_WITH_KV` handler wraps `add_request_with_kv_handoff()` and sends any exception to `_fail_submission()`. That registers the same FAILED placeholder the plain submit path already uses. The `_fail_submission` docstring now mentions this caller.
- New tests: `test_schedule_requests_fails_a_rejected_kv_handoff_and_continues` in `test_dynamic_engine.py` and `test_string_handoff_prompt_is_tokenized_once_before_import` in `test_disagg_handoff_lifecycle.py`.

## Details

Every MP rank processes the same broadcast message, so the failure path keeps request state mirrored across ranks. One behavior change: a non-disaggregated engine that receives `SUBMIT_REQUEST_WITH_KV` now fails that one request with a reply instead of raising out of the loop. This was split out of the inference review. It is independent of #8255, which handles replying to a failed KV import.

## Tested

- black, isort, pylint (10.00/10) and ruff are clean on the 4 changed files.
- Run on 8×H100 at this head merged with main `3914483f`, using main's CI image (`sha256:7b4e22a3`):
  - `tests/unit_tests/inference/**/*.py`: 3675 passed, 37 skipped, 0 failed.
  - `tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py`: 254 passed, 2 skipped.
- No functional test case exercises disaggregation.

items.title: Shortcut MoE Inference Overlap Support
items.author: susavlsh10
items.summary: Adds opt-in, CUDA graph compatible Shortcut MoE inference overlap for GDP and FlashAttention layers. Serial inference remains the default, and existing training paths are preserved.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds opt-in, CUDA graph compatible Shortcut MoE inference overlap for GDP and FlashAttention layers. Serial inference remains the default, and existing training paths are preserved.

## Overlap schedule

Two CUDA streams execute independent branches:

- **Main:** mixer normalization, projections, GDP/attention, output projection, then shared experts.
- **Shortcut:** routing → NVLS all-gather → token/expert preparation → routed GEMMs → output reduction → NVLS reduce-scatter.

The streams fork from the pair input and join before the final routed/shared output and residual update.

**Prefill/mixed** use the ordinary atomic mixer forward, supporting chunked prefill and existing graph shape selection. **Decode** uses projection/core/post adapters for launch ordering. GDP and FlashAttention run once for the full batch. Block CUDA graphs capture both branches and their dependencies.

## Configuration

- `--inference-shortcut-moe-overlap`
- `--inference-shortcut-moe-expert-max-blocks 304`

The expert limit bounds the routed GEMM launch grid to reduce compute interference; it does not reserve SMs. Zero disables the cap. Serial and training ignore it.

Supported path: dynamic batching, BF16 `inference_optimized` language layers, TP=CP=1, vLLM fused grouped GEMMs, Triton NVLS, and GDP/FA predecessors. Unsupported combinations are rejected. Vision configs clear the language-only flag.

## Speedup over serial CUDA graph inference

Same-node Nemotron 4 Nano (full attention checkpoint) comparison on four GB300 GPUs, TP1/EP4/DP4, Nano checkpoint iteration 30,000, ISL8k/OSL2k, chunked prefill 4k, two trials per mode/batch. NVLS communication limit:128 blocks, expert cap 304. Attention used FA2 kernels.
