items.body: # PR Draft: Qwen3.5 Transformers 5 DynamicCache Status: prepared for human review; the clean branch is pushed to the personal fork, but no upstream PR has been created. The branch is rebased onto the latest canonical `main` (`5b550b0c3dad8c7bb7aab834a3fe195f8cdfc517`). PR #7471 is still open, so its eventual merge should be checked for overlap before submission. ### What does this PR do? Title: `[model] fix: support Transformers 5 Qwen3.5 dynamic cache` Transformers 5 stores Qwen3.5 gated-delta-net convolution and recurrent state inside layer-scoped `DynamicCache` entries and exposes update methods instead of the legacy top-level arrays. The verl training monkey patch still used the old fields, so a cached forward failed before a GRPO update. Cached multi-token continuations also need the previous convolution context and recurrent state. This patch supports both legacy and Transformers 5 cache APIs, preserves state through chunked continuation, and adds a CPU regression test for prefill, multi-token continuation, single-token decode, and chunk/token equivalence. ### Duplicate-work check - Canonical repository: `https://github.com/verl-project/verl` - Related open PR: [#7471](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7471) resolves current Transformers 5 Qwen3.5 kernel/block-type names in the same module, but does not address the DynamicCache state API or continuation flow. - Related work searched: #6212, #8190, #8192, #7653, #7749, and the vLLM- Ascend Qwen4Exp work. None is an exact DynamicCache duplicate. - Publication must be coordinated with #7471. Preferred form is a cache-only follow-up rebased onto its final merge SHA; the integration merge commit is retained only for conflict and runtime validation. ### Test Environment: Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.10.0, Transformers 5.5.4, `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0`. CPU tests ran in `verlpr_env`. The real GRPO smoke used an A3 container with CANN 9.0.0, `torch_npu 2.10.0.post4`, vLLM 0.22.1, vLLM-Ascend 0.22.1rc1, and Qwen3.5-2B. Rebased cache-only PR branch (`4b37dc93`, based on `5b550b0c3dad8c7bb7aab834a3fe195f8cdfc517`): ```text python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_qwen35_dynamic_cache_on_cpu.py \ tests/models/test_fused_kernels_ulysses_sp_on_cpu.py 27 passed ``` Fresh rebase logs: - `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/rebase-fae3256c/pytest-qwen35-dynamic-cache.log` (`1 passed, 14 warnings`) - `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/rebase-fae3256c/pytest-fused-kernels-ulysses-cpu.log` (`26 passed, 14 warnings`) - `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/rebase-fae3256c/pre-commit-changed-files.log` (all hooks passed) The combined `27 passed` result above is retained as historical evidence from the pre-rebase checkout; the two fresh logs are the acceptance evidence for the current HEAD. Additional compatibility evidence: - Focused DynamicCache/kernel-resolution tests: `13 passed, 1 skipped` on Transformers 5.5.3, 5.5.4, and 5.12.1. Fresh overlay logs for 5.5.3 and 5.12.1 are `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/followup-transformers-553-cpu-20261014.log` and `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/followup-transformers-512-cpu-20261014.log`. - Current-main plus #7471 integration: fused-kernel suite `26 passed` and focused suite `13 passed, 1 skipped`. - Changed-files and all-files pre-commit passed on the prepared checkouts. - Real A3 V1 GRPO two-step run completed with non-constant reward range `0..1`, step-1 advantage range `+-0.7071`, step-1 gradient norm `0.0125406`, and weight synchronization `5.2276 s` / `4.9003 s`. Fresh cache-only PR GRPO one-step smoke on A3 also completed rollout, reward, actor update, and vLLM weight synchronization: reward range `0..1`, advantage range `-0.7071..+0.7071`, non-zero actor gradient norm `0.0086453`, weight synchronization `5.1273 s`, and step time `61.49 s`. This is a path and update smoke, not a convergence claim. The base reproducer fails before the actor update with: ```text AttributeError: 'DynamicCache' object has no attribute 'conv_states' ``` The PR regression passes with `1 passed, 14 warnings`. A fresh PR GRPO run reached vLLM rollout and four reward calls, then stopped in the unrelated generic nested-tensor actor indexer: ```text RuntimeError: split_with_sizes expects split_sizes to sum exactly to 28 (input tensor's size at dimension 1), but got split_sizes=[4, 4, 4, 4] ``` No DynamicCache traceback occurred in that run. items.title: [None][feat] Let BatchedPageCopier prefer the copy engines on coherent links
items.author: tzulingk
items.summary: moves KV pages between the GPU and the pinned host tier for every hot<->host migration of KVCacheManagerV2 since #18541. On coherent NVLink-C2C links (Grace systems) it selects its multi-CTA copy kernel; the copy engines are used only on PCIe-attached GPUs.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

`BatchedPageCopier` moves KV pages between the GPU and the pinned host tier for every hot<->host migration of KVCacheManagerV2 since #18541. On coherent NVLink-C2C links (Grace systems) it selects its multi-CTA copy kernel; the copy engines are used only on PCIe-attached GPUs. This PR adds an opt-in, `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_PAGE_COPY_PREFER_COPY_ENGINE=1`, that selects the copy engines on coherent links as well. The default is unchanged.

### Why

Measured on one GB300 node (NVLink-C2C, 152 SMs, CUDA 13.4) with one 217,055,232 B page, the recurrent-state page of a hybrid model such as Kimi K3, event-to-event over 10 iterations after warm-up:

| GPU state | copy engines | `BatchedPageCopier` kernel |
|---|---|---|
| idle, host->device | 211 GB/s, 1.03 ms | 201 GB/s, 1.08 ms |
| idle, device->host | 193 GB/s | 185 GB/s |
| every SM thread slot occupied, 0.1 ms compute blocks | 1.03 ms per page | 1.2 to 2.0 ms per page |
| every SM thread slot occupied, 5 ms compute blocks | 1.03 ms per page | 3.8 to 4.5 ms per page |

- **Idle, the two paths tie at the link ceiling** (about 210 GB/s per direction per GPU on that node); the copy engines are 4 to 5 % ahead.
- **Under SM saturation the copy engines do not slow down**, because they use no SM. The kernel's 4 to 6 CTAs have to wait for a free slot, and giving the copy stream the highest priority did not help: resident blocks are not preempted. Persistent-scheduled GEMM and attention kernels in a long prefill behave like the 5 ms case.
- **The migration is on the critical path.** The storage manager records an event after each migration batch and consumers wait on it in-stream, so a page that arrives 3 ms later delays the request that needs it.
- **Why not flip the default:** on wide links the kernel reaches a higher ceiling than one copy engine (355 GB/s measured on GH200 in #18541); the GB300 numbers above come from a link of about 225 GB/s per direction, where both paths saturate. An operator who knows the deployment is prefill-bound with saturated SMs can opt in; a measurement on GH200 would be needed before changing the default.

### The change

`BatchedPageCopier::computeConfigs()` (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kv_cache_manager_v2/batchedPageCopy.cu`) reads the variable once per construction with `getBoolEnv` (exactly `1` enables it) and computes

```
kernelViable = chunked || (coherentLink && !preferCopyEngine)
```

so the copy engines are selected on a coherent link when the variable is set, `pageIndexLocation()` reports `kHost` and the codec keeps its index pairs in host memory, exactly as on PCIe today. Chunked host registration (Linux 6.11 to 6.13) still forces the kernel, since a copy-engine descriptor cannot span registration chunks; a WARNING says so. On PCIe the variable has no effect (DEBUG). The header documents the variable (`kPageCopyPreferCopyEngineEnv`) next to the class.

Other files:

- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2TestUtils.h`: `CudaAllocation` / `allocateCuda` and a `ScopedEnv` helper as shared inline definitions (the KVCM2 gtests each carried a copy; the siblings keep theirs for now).
- `docs/source/developer-guide/kv-cache-cold-page-codec.md`: the default codec's copy paragraph described the pre-#18541 codec (one `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` per codec call, `kHost` everywhere); it now describes the platform selection, the chunked-registration rule, where the default codec reports `kHost` versus `kDevice`, and the variable.

## Test Coverage

`cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2ColdPageCopyTest.cu` (existing target, one GPU):

- `PlatformSelectionFollowsTheKnob`: three copiers in one process, variable unset, `1` and `yes`; `kernelEnabled()` equals `coherentLink || chunked` unset, `chunked` with `1`, and unchanged with `yes`; `pageIndexLocation()` follows.
- `PreferredCopyEngineLaunchRoundTrips`: with the variable set, `launch()` onboards 1 x 217,055,232 B, 12 x 15,261,696 B and 140 x 884,736 B through a permuted page-index list (device page (11 i + 3) mod n receives host page i), offloads with the identity, and the slots compare byte-exact against a pseudo-random fill; index pairs live where `pageIndexLocation()` says, so the test also runs on chunked-registration hosts, on the kernel.
- `PathBandwidthInfo`: GB/s of the 217 MB page per direction from a default copier and a knob copier in the same process. Informational, not asserted.

The default-codec and cold-page gtests, and the whole `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests` directory, run with the variable set as validation (below): every host-tier migration then travels through the copy engines on a coherent link.

### Validation

| check | result |
|---|---|
| clang-format, codespell on the changed files | clean |
| GB300 node (aarch64, CUDA 13.4, Linux 6.17, coherent link, no chunked registration), `build_wheel.py --cuda_architectures 103-real --fast_build --install`, `kvCacheManagerV2ColdPageCopyTest` with the variable unset and set | 3 passed in each; `PathBandwidthInfo` on the 217 MB page: kernel 198 to 211 GB/s host->device and 185 GB/s device->host, copy engines 211 GB/s and 193 GB/s |
| same node, `kvCacheManagerV2DefaultColdPageCodecTest` unset and set, `kvCacheManagerV2ColdPageTest` set | 5 passed each; 74 passed |
| same node, `pytest tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests` with the variable set (the log shows the copy engines selected for every codec) | 326 passed, 12 skipped |

Related: #20311 changes the generic host<->device copy helpers, which production on main does not use for hot<->host migrations; the measurements above motivated this change in the path production does use.

items.title: fix(inference): AUT-2539 reply to a KV handoff import that fails before admission
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: The decode side imports a request's KV cache before it admits the request. An import can fail before runs, either because a peer failed or because the local transfer raised.
items.body:
## Background

A review of recent inference changes on `main` found a hang in disaggregated decode. The decode side imports a request's KV cache before it admits the request. An import can fail before `_finalize_kv_handoff_import()` runs, either because a peer failed or because the local transfer raised. The request then never reaches `add_request()`.

`_admit_pending_kv_imports()` releases or quarantines the blocks and fails the import future, but the engine dispatch drops that future. So no `ENGINE_REPLY` is ever sent. The coordinator frees a request's routing entry and pending count only on `ENGINE_REPLY`, so the client request hangs forever.

## What changed

- `inference_state_handoff.py`: in the `except` branch, an import that is not in `self.requests` now calls `_fail_submission()`. This is the same FAILED-placeholder path already used for rejected submissions. Every MP rank applies the same broadcast completion decision to mirrored state, so all ranks register the same placeholder. Only the MP coordinator sends the reply.
- `dynamic_engine.py`: the `_fail_submission` docstring now names this caller.
- `test_disagg_handoff_lifecycle.py`:
  - The peer-failure quarantine test now asserts exactly one failed submission.
  - The submission-failure test now runs the engine's real `_fail_submission`, `_handle_failed_request` and `_complete_request`, with only the coordinator socket mocked. It asserts exactly one FAILED reply for the request.

## Details

Release-once and quarantine behavior are unchanged. A failure after `add_request()` still goes through the existing request path. There are no dependency or lock changes.

The branch was based on `main` at `a54dd737` and now merges `main` at `ee6baa2e`. CI on the previous head (which merged `main` at `3914483f`, run 38816895124) timed out in an NCCL barrier in `test_checkpointing.py::test_checkpoint_load_without_microbatch_calculator` (`torch_dist` cases). `ee6baa2e` is #8263, "test(checkpointing): seed CPU initialization in checkpoint load test". Against `main` at `ee6baa2e`, this branch still changes only the three files above.

## Tested

- black, isort, pylint and ruff are clean on the three changed files.
- `unit:tests/unit_tests/inference/**/*.py` on 1×8 H100 at `49fcf50f` (before the merges), CI image for `a54dd737` (`sha256:5c82eeb5…`): **3674 passed, 37 skipped, 9 deselected, 0 failed**, exit code 0. All 37 tests in `test_disagg_handoff_lifecycle.py` passed, including the two changed failure tests.
- Full `tests/unit_tests/**/*.py` bucket on 8×H100, on this head merged with the `main` tip (`28d5dd15`), image `megatron-lm@sha256:7b4e22a3…`: **3424 passed, 142 skipped, 0 failed**; then 24 of 24 passed in the second session; exit code 0. All 16 `test_checkpoint_load_without_microbatch_calculator` cases passed, including every `torch_dist` case.
- No functional rows were run: no functional test case covers disaggregation.
- GitHub CI on this head is pending.

- `cpp/include/tensorrt_llm/common/packageLocation.h` — Verify ancestor discovery, symlink resolution, pip fallback, and behavior when lookup fails. The cached result means discovery is not retried during the process.
- `cpp/include/tensorrt_llm/deep_gemm/compiler.cuh` — Verify NVRTC and NVCC include paths for wheel and editable installs. When lookup fails, the include list remains empty and the existing warning path runs.
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/trtllmGenKernels/fmha/fmhaKernels.h` — Verify candidate priority and `numb` path selection for editable and wheel installs. Check the existing warning and missing-header error behavior when discovery or candidate checks fail.

## Description

Fixes #20170.

DeepGEMM (`getJitIncludeDirs()` in `deep_gemm/compiler.cuh`) and the trtllm-gen FMHA NVRTC path (`getExecPath()` in `fmhaKernels.h`) find their JIT headers by running `pip show tensorrt_llm` and parsing `Location:`. That depends on whichever `pip` is first on `PATH`. In a `uv venv` there is no `pip` in the venv, so the command either fails or runs a system `pip` that reports a different install (or none). The include paths are then wrong or missing, and block-scaled FP8 warmup fails with `RuntimeError: NVRTC compilation failed`.

This PR adds a small header-only helper, `tensorrt_llm/common/packageLocation.h`:

- `getPackageLocation()` calls `dladdr` on code in the loaded TensorRT-LLM library and walks up from that library to the directory that contains `tensorrt_llm/include`. For a wheel, `<site-packages>/tensorrt_llm/libs/libtensorrt_llm.so` gives `<site-packages>`. For an editable install, `<repo>/tensorrt_llm/libs/...` gives `<repo>`. These are the same directories `pip show` reports as `Location` / `Editable project location`. If the library is a symlink, the resolved path is checked too.
- `pip show tensorrt_llm` is still used as a fallback, with the same parsing as before (an editable location wins), when the library isn't inside a `tensorrt_llm` package (for example a C++-only build) or on Windows. The result is cached.

Both call sites now use the helper, so the two copies of the popen/regex code are gone. Behavior changes:
- FMHA now always tries the editable build directory candidate first. Previously it did this only when `pip show` reported an editable install. The candidate is checked with `exists()`, and `<site-packages>/cpp/build/...` doesn't exist in a wheel install, so wheel installs still use `tensorrt_llm/include/trtllm_gen_kernels/fmha`.
- When no location can be found, both sites now log their existing warning. Before, a `pip show` that printed no `Location` left the include dirs empty and logged nothing.

## Test Coverage

- New host-only gtest `cpp/tests/unit_tests/common/packageLocationTest.cpp` (`unit;common;host`, links only `tllm::common_headers`). It covers the wheel layout, the bindings module next to the package, a symlinked library outside the package, a library outside any package (returns nullopt), and `pip show` parsing (plain `Location`, an editable location winning with CRLF/trailing whitespace, no location).
- I built and ran it locally with g++ (`-std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror`) and system gtest: 7/7 passed.
- End-to-end check with a mock `libtensorrt_llm.so` placed in a fake `venv/.../site-packages/tensorrt_llm/libs/` and loaded with `dlopen`:
  - A decoy `pip` on `PATH` that reports `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages`: the old `pip show` logic returns `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages`, while `getPackageLocation()` returns the venv's `site-packages`.
  - No `pip` on `PATH` at all: the old logic finds nothing, while `getPackageLocation()` returns the venv's `site-packages`.
- Not verified: I haven't built the full library here or run FP8 serving on a GPU, so CI is still needed for `compiler.cuh` / `fmhaKernels.h`.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6713424][fix] Flush the HF streaming detokenizer on the final response; fix the AgentX aiperf install check
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: NVBug 6713424: the AgentX perf-sanity lanes (GB300 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, con1156 and con1456) fail on a single request that aiperf rejects with. is zero-tolerance, so one such request in ~25k fails the 2 h case (main post-merge 2944 con1156; 2996 and 3017 c…
items.body:
## Description

NVBug 6713424: the AgentX perf-sanity lanes (GB300 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, con1156 and con1456) fail on a single request that aiperf rejects with
`InvalidInferenceResultError: No responses with actual content were received from the server (only usage/metadata, null/empty data, or [DONE] markers)`.
`agentx_client.check_run_health` is zero-tolerance, so one such request in ~25k fails the 2 h case (main post-merge 2944 con1156; 2996 and 3017 con1456).

### Root cause: the HF streaming detokenizer drops `flush`

`TransformersTokenizer.decode_incrementally` hands `stream_interval < 24` to `hf_decode_incrementally`, which uses the tokenizers `DecodeStream`. `DecodeStream.step` returns `None` for a token that is not valid UTF-8 yet. That is the first byte-level piece of an emoji, a CJK character, and similar. `DecodeStream` cannot release that piece later. `DetokenizedGenerationResultBase` passes `flush=self._done` on the final response, and the TRTLLM backend honours it. `hf_decode_incrementally` never received it.

A streamed response whose last tokens are such pieces therefore streams no text for them. When the response is a single token, `chat_stream_post_processor` still emits the chunk (it has a token delta) with `content: ""`. The client then sees only role, usage and `[DONE]`. The same request non-streamed returns the full-decode text. On the DSv4 vocab, 1,279 non-special ids (1.0%) produce no streamed text when they are the only token. In a ctx_only run on GB300, with the server instrumented to log every finished request, the empty response was token id 163 (`ä`, byte `0xE4`, the first byte of a 3-byte character). It streamed `text=''`; a full decode gives `'\ufffd'`.

Why AgentX hits it:
- The scenario forces `ignore_eos`, so the single token is a real model token.
- Almost every warmup request (aiperf's `_WARMUP_MAX_TOKENS = 1`) and every ctx_only request decodes exactly one token.
- Measured rate: 15 empty out of 10,695 one-token requests, 0.14%, on oci-aga and oci-jhb, in both warmup and ctx_only.
- The e2e profiling window has only ~60 such requests per run, so it fails once every few runs. The rate does not depend on disaggregation.
- gen_only_no_context hard-codes the first token to 7 (`%`), which always decodes. It had 0 errors in 109k requests.

### Fix

- **`tensorrt_llm/tokenizer/tokenizer.py`**:
  - `decode_incrementally` now passes `flush` through to `hf_decode_incrementally`.
  - `hf_decode_incrementally` records the ids `DecodeStream` holds and the last id that produced text. On `flush` it appends the text a full decode gives the held ids, decoded after that last id. This is the same result `tokenizer.decode` gives for the whole output: 3,000 of 3,000 random DSv4 streams match, with chunk sizes 1-20.
  - Responses before the last one are unchanged, so nothing is emitted early.
- **`tests/integration/defs/perf/agentx_client.py`, special tokens**: the scenario forces `ignore_eos`, so the model can sample its end-of-sequence token as an ordinary output token. With the server's default `skip_special_tokens` that token decodes to no text, so a one-token response that is EOS is empty no matter how the stream is flushed (1 of the 10 empties measured in the unfixed arms). The client now sends `skip_special_tokens:false`. Token counts, and thus every metric, are unchanged because the command also passes `--use-server-token-count`; without that flag aiperf would re-tokenize the text, special-token strings included. With both changes, 0 of the 129,280 DSv4 vocab ids streams as empty text when it is the only token (it was 2,509).
- **`tests/integration/defs/perf/agentx_client.py`, aiperf check**: `requirements-dev.txt` pins the upstream PyPI `aiperf==0.8.0`, which imports cleanly. `#20175` dropped the `datasets==3.1.0` pin, so the 26.09 images carry datasets 4.7.0. Since then `aiperf_is_usable()` passes and the agentx-harness install is skipped. aiperf then exits within seconds with `Unknown option: --scenario`; this hit con1456 in PR 63399 and release/1.3 post-merge #29 and #31. The probe now also requires the fork's `inferencex-agentx-mvp` scenario and logs why it fails (missing module, no scenario registry, scenario missing, datasets too old), and aiperf now runs as `python -m aiperf` under the interpreter the probe checked instead of whatever `aiperf` is first on PATH. This is a separate failure from the empty responses; it is in this PR because the AgentX lanes cannot start without it.

### Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_tokenizer_decode.py` (now listed in `l0_cpu.yml` and marked `cpu_only`; it was not in any CI list before, and the CPU stages drop files without the marker):
  - The final flush releases held tokens: a single partial token, text then a partial token, and a partial token then a special token.
  - The final flush also releases them when the last response brings no new token ids.
  - With a byte-level BPE whose held piece starts with a space and whose decoder strips a leading space, the streamed-and-flushed text equals `tokenizer.decode(all_ids)`. This only holds because the tail is decoded after the previous token; a context-free tail decode fails it.
  - The special-token policy holds on flush.
  - Intermediate responses still hold back incomplete text.
  - On the current tokenizer, 9 of the 13 tests fail.
- `tests/unittest/scripts/test_perf_agentx_aiperf_probe.py` (marked `cpu_only`, so the CPU stages' `unittest/scripts` entry runs it; the A10 entry is waived):
  - An upstream-like aiperf is not usable; the fork is usable unless datasets is 3.x, or the fork lacks the scenario. Each failure logs its reason.
  - The command runs `python -m aiperf` under the checked interpreter, with the scenario the probe checks.
  - The command sends `skip_special_tokens:false`.
  - On the current client, all 7 tests fail.
- GPU verification on GB300 (oci-jhb), DSv4-Pro DSpark agentx `ctx_only` and `gen_only_no_context`. Both arms use the same main CI wheel (GenPostMergeBuilds 2973, `ff7ea92`), and the fix arm overlays only `tokenizer.py`. Without the fix, 9 of 6,015 one-token ctx_only responses were empty from a held partial character; with it, 0 of 5,979. A run with both changes had 0 empty of 2,973 and passed. Details are on the NVBug.

## Description

The Qwen3-Coder parser can convert intentional strings to null. For example, raw `None` under a string-or-null `anyOf` schema passes through Python literal evaluation and becomes JSON `null`.

Validate conversions against the parameter schema and preserve valid strings. Exact `null` remains the null spelling when permitted; `None` becomes null only when the schema permits null and rejects it as a string. Python dictionary/list compatibility is retained for schema-valid, JSON-compatible containers.

items.title: fix(inference): AUT-2539 hold back unstable reasoning in streamed chat deltas
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: A later chunk can still move that text, and text that was already streamed cannot be taken back. This adds (now also used by ) and. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## Background

A review of recent inference changes on `main` found that `StreamingChatParser`, which drives OpenAI-compatible streaming in the dynamic text-gen server, commits reasoning deltas as soon as the reasoning parser returns them. A later chunk can still move that text, and text that was already streamed cannot be taken back.

## What changed

- `openai_streaming.py`: while reasoning is still open, hold back a trailing partial end marker (for example `</thi`, or a partial implicit marker such as `<tool_call>`) instead of streaming it as reasoning. This adds `_partial_marker_start` (now also used by `_safe_content_prefix`) and `_safe_reasoning_prefix`.
- `StreamingChatParser` takes two new arguments, `reasoning_markers` and `force_content`. Some parsers return reasoning as content until a non-empty answer follows, then move it back to reasoning. NemotronV3 does this with `enable_thinking=False` or `force_nonempty_content=True`. For those parsers no deltas are sent until the split is stable. The parser is either named explicitly or detected by a one-time probe of `parse`. The final parse flushes everything.
- Logprobs of tokens whose text the parser holds back are no longer dropped. They are buffered per choice (`pending_logprobs`) and attached to the next chunk that carries text, including the final flush.
- New unit tests in `tests/unit_tests/inference/test_openai_streaming.py`, including `test_openai_stream_keeps_logprobs_of_parser_held_back_text`. It covers a final flush with and without additional tokens.

## Details

The callers are `endpoints/chat_completions.py` and `endpoints/completions.py`. There are no dependency or lock changes.

The branch merges `main` at `ee6baa2e` (#8263, which seeds CPU initialization in the checkpoint load test that timed out on an earlier head). Against that base it changes only the two files above.

Review 5547002215 (logprobs dropped for held-back text) is fixed in `9bd15b20`. Review 5547215667 on this head reports no findings.

## Tested

- black, isort, pylint (10.00/10) and ruff pass on both changed files.
- Torch-free simulation of `test_openai_streaming.py` at this head: 15 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped. Without the fix, the new logprobs test fails in 2 of 2 cases.
- Earlier heads on 8×H100:
  - `tests/unit_tests/inference/**` at `72de4874`: 3680 passed, 37 skipped, 0 failed.
  - Full `tests/unit_tests/**/*.py`, merged with `main` `b8305562`: 3424 passed, 142 skipped, 0 failed, then 24 of 24 in the second session.
- GitHub CI on `9bd15b20` is pending.

items.title: Fix MFSDP checkpoint save/load across pipeline and virtual pipeline chunks
items.author: shjwudp
items.summary: PP/VPP currently assumes a single model dictionary and can resolve optimizer names against the wrong chunk. V2 fused-weight handling also requires its own layout metadata rather than V1-only attributes.
items.body:
## Design
Preprocess every pipeline chunk using local module paths, then emit globally numbered checkpoint names. Restore all raw chunk dictionaries after DCP fills shared storage. Fused v2 checkpoint sections use the owning buffer layout and preserve tensor aliases.

## Why
PP/VPP currently assumes a single model dictionary and can resolve optimizer names against the wrong chunk. V2 fused-weight handling also requires its own layout metadata rather than V1-only attributes.

## Validation
Added ownership, multi-chunk preprocessing/load, and fused uneven-shard regressions. Import sorting, Ruff, and AST checks pass. The prerequisite local-tensor/EP integration passed 14 checkpoint tests per rank on four GB300 GPUs. New PP/VPP end-to-end restart validation is pending.

Related: #7322 and #8230; their implementation is not duplicated here.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6891258][fix] Reserve draft capacity up front for materialized generation dummies
items.author: lowsfer
items.summary: This is an alternative to #19404 (main) and #20047 (release/1.3). With (added in #17801 for the DeepSeek-V4 layer-wise benchmark), the dummy keeps per-request SWA scratch reuse enabled and passes no history hint, so history stays 0.
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
Materialized generation dummies now reserve `token_num + num_extra_kv_tokens + _kv_draft` capacity during the initial resize. The code skips the later target- and draft-cache growth for this path. Other generation dummies retain deferred resizing. The change addresses SWA scratch reuse with uncommitted history. Test execution results are not established by the supplied evidence.

## QA Engineer Review
Modified test file: `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/deepseek_v4/test_deepseek_v4_cache_manager.py`. The new parameterized test covers compression ratios `[1]` and `[1, 4, 128]`, token counts `127`, `128`, `129`, and `513`, and draft-token counts `0` and `3`. It checks scratch reuse, zero history, and expected capacity, then frees requests and shuts down the cache manager. No matching entry was found in the searched integration test lists; list applicability is not established. **Coverage verdict: sufficient** for the capacity and scratch-reuse behavior. Execution results are unavailable.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Verify that materialized generation dummies reserve draft capacity in the initial resize and do not perform the later growth resize for either cache. Confirm that non-materialized generation dummies and context dummies retain their existing behavior.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/deepseek_v4/test_deepseek_v4_cache_manager.py`: The new parameterized test checks initial capacity and SWA scratch reuse for materialized generation dummies. No matching integration test-list entry appeared in the search; applicability of those lists to this unit test is not established.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Fixes NVBug 6891258. This is an alternative to #19404 (main) and #20047 (release/1.3).

**Root cause.** `KVCacheManagerV2.add_dummy_requests` sizes a generation dummy with two resizes: one sized like a prompt of `token_num` tokens, then a second that grows capacity by `kv_draft`. With `materialize_history=True` (added in #17801 for the DeepSeek-V4 layer-wise benchmark), the dummy keeps per-request SWA scratch reuse enabled and passes no history hint, so history stays 0. When `kv_draft > 0`, the growth resize changes capacity on a scratch-reuse cache with no committed history and trips the native invariant:

```
SWA scratch requires old_capacity - max_rewind_len <= history_length <= old_capacity
```

Without draft tokens the second resize does not change capacity, the check is skipped, and nothing fails. That is why the only current caller (the layer-wise benchmark, which passes no draft tokens) works today.

**Fix.** For materialized generation dummies, reserve the final capacity (`token_num + num_extra_kv_tokens + kv_draft`) in the first resize and skip the growth resize, for both the main and the draft KV cache. Growing from capacity 0 with history 0 satisfies the invariant, so per-request scratch reuse stays enabled.

**Why not disable scratch reuse for every generation dummy (#19404)?** #17801 deliberately keeps scratch reuse on for materialized dummies. The benchmark registers `max_batch_size` dummies at full `max_seq_len` and then writes the history with its own prefill pass. With scratch reuse, out-of-window SWA blocks map to shared scratch slots, so each dummy needs only about a window's worth of private SWA pages. Disabling it would back every SWA block privately and reintroduce the allocation failure #17801 fixed (NVBug 6567554).

Non-materialized generation dummies and context dummies are unchanged.

## Test Coverage

- New `test_materialized_dummy_generation_requests_with_swa_scratch_reuse` in `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/deepseek_v4/test_deepseek_v4_cache_manager.py`: compress ratios `[1]` / `[1, 4, 128]`, token counts 127/128/129/513, 0 and 3 draft tokens. Asserts that allocation succeeds and that each dummy keeps scratch reuse enabled, has history 0, and has capacity `token_num + num_extra_kv_tokens + num_draft_tokens`.
- Existing `test_dummy_generation_requests_with_swa_scratch_reuse` covers the unchanged non-materialized path.

Results on B200:
- With the fix: 24 passed (16 new + 8 existing).
- Without the fix: the 8 new cases with 3 draft tokens fail with the assertion above; the 8 cases with 0 draft tokens pass.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6913517][fix] Drop launcher spawn-proxy env in the disagg cancel marathon
items.author: Shixiaowei02
items.summary: <!-- Please explain the issue and the solution in short. [Discussion: /bot run --disable-fail-fast]
items.body:
Under `trtllm-llmapi-launch`, pytest inherits `TLLM_SPAWN_PROXY_PROCESS=1`, the launcher's single `TLLM_SPAWN_PROXY_PROCESS_IPC_ADDR` and its HMAC key. These exist so an LLM created in the pytest process binds to the launcher's one pre-spawned `mgmn_leader_node`. The marathon creates no LLM in-process; it starts six `trtllm-serve` workers that inherit pytest's environment, so all of them bound to that leader (a PAIR-socket RemoteMpiCommSessionServer that serves one client) instead of creating their own MPI session. At most one worker came up and `setup_disagg_cluster` timed out after 1200 s with 0/6 or 1/6 registered.

Remove those three variables for the duration of the marathon test, so the cluster, the disagg server and SIGKILL respawns all start as independent top-level servers. The test's configuration, startup deadline and pass criteria are unchanged.

(cherry picked from commit e9f992d26c92dfaf21091d55098a21f6716b5e20)

items.summary: Fixes the multi-node perf-sanity failures from NVBug 6843484 on. This is the counterpart of the first commit of #20292. [Discussion: /bot run --disable-fail-fast --stage-list "GB200-16GPUs-4Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16]
items.body:
## Description

Fixes the multi-node `gen_only_no_context` perf-sanity failures from NVBug 6843484 on `main`. This is the `main` counterpart of the first commit of #20292 (`release/1.3`).

**Affected stages** (every aggregated multi-node perf-sanity stage):
* `GB200-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-1`
* `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-{1,2}`
* `GB300-32_GPUs-8_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE8-GPU32-Post-Merge-{1,2}`
* The 2-node `PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE2-GPU8` and `PerfSanity-Node2-GPU8` stages go through the same path. They have not failed because of it so far.

**Symptoms in the bug:**
* `ncclGinGdakiCreateContext ... failed: 2`
* `NCCL-EP NVFP4 dispatch requires uint8 tokens`
* `no new log output for 7201s`
* `CANCELLED by 146504` (the idle-GPU reaper)

**Root cause.**
* `runLLMTestlistWithSbatch` requests `--segment=<nodeCount>` only for `Disagg-PerfSanity` and `SingleNvlinkDomain` stages. Aggregated multi-node perf-sanity stages (`aggMultiNodeMode`) get no segment, so Slurm can spread one EP16/EP32 job over several NVL72 racks.
* On oci-hsg, oci-jhb and oci-aga, `topology/block` uses one block per rack.
* Across racks, `NVLinkOneSided` and `NVLinkTwoSided` fail with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE`, because MNNVL memory cannot be mapped across NVLink domains. The MoE communication factory then falls back to `NcclEP`.
* With `NcclEP` the case either crashes or stalls with idle GPUs until the reaper or the 2 h no-output watchdog cancels the job. It crashes in NCCL GIN or with `NCCL-EP NVFP4 dispatch requires uint8 tokens`.

**Evidence: Slurm nodelist vs. outcome for these 5 stages.** Nodelists are read from the Jenkins stage logs (`Slurm job N nodelist:`). Excluded: builds whose logs expired, runs hit by the `main` #3009 DNS outage, and one `release/1.3` #31 run that was SKIP-waived. Every counted pass uploaded results.

| Placement | `main` #3009–#3019 | `release/1.3` #20–#31 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 rack | 6 / 6 passed | 7 / 7 passed |
| 2+ racks | 0 / 29 passed | 0 / 31 passed |

* On `main`, the 4- and 8-node stages have failed in every one of the last 7 builds unless Slurm happened to place them in one rack. GB300 `GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-2` (DeepSeek-R1 con4096) shows this directly: it passed in #3012, #3014 and #3016 on one rack, and failed in #3015, #3018 and #3019 on two.
* `main` #3019, GB200 DeepSeek-R1 con4096 dep16, on `nvl72108-T[04-05],nvl72005-T[08,14]` (2 racks): the archived `gen_server_0.log` shows all 944 MoE layer selections as `NVLinkOneSided not available: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` and then `NcclEP`. Then comes `gin_plugin.cc:916 ... proxyRegMrSymDmaBuf ... failed: 2`. Every rank ends in `ValueError: NCCL-EP NVFP4 dispatch requires uint8 tokens with shape (2, 3584), got dtype=torch.bfloat16`.
* Control: the `Disagg-PerfSanity` stages already pass `--segment`. They landed in one rack in 152/152 runs, up to 14 nodes.

**Fix.** Also request `--segment=<nodeCount>` in `aggMultiNodeMode`, the same as for `Disagg-PerfSanity` and `SingleNvlinkDomain`.
* It is one line in `jenkins/L0_Test.groovy`.
* It affects only multi-node stages whose name contains `PerfSanity`. Every such stage has at most 8 nodes, well under the 18-node block size. Slurm accepts `--segment=4` and `--segment=8` for this shape on oci-jhb and oci-aga (`sbatch --test-only`).
* The local reproduction harness (`jenkins/scripts/perf/local/submit.py`) already emits `--segment=<total_nodes>` for every job.

## Test Coverage

* GPU validation on GB200 (oci-hsg), described below.
* `pre-commit` passes on the changed file.
* Stages to run in PR CI, with the `ci: full pre-merge approved` label (multi-GPU stages are blocked without it):
  * `GB200-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-1`
  * `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-1`
  * `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-2`
  * `GB300-32_GPUs-8_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE8-GPU32-Post-Merge-1`
  * `GB300-32_GPUs-8_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE8-GPU32-Post-Merge-2`

**GPU validation (GB200, oci-hsg, job 7971062): passed.** Setup: the exact `main` CI wheel (GenPostMergeBuilds #2977, `c9b18eefa7`, includes #20256), CI's pre-imported 26.09 container, this PR's tree, and `--nodes=4 --segment=4`. Case: GB200 DeepSeek-R1 con4096 dep16 `gen_only_no_context`.

items.title: fix(coding_agent_rl): snapshot fails when repo .gitignore ignores .harness
items.author: dextermayhewjd
items.summary: excludes the harness metadata directory with a pathspec: When the task repo's own already ignores (for example a rule), treats the pathspec as naming an ignored path and exits 1: then raises, fails, and aborts the rollout before grading. Every rollout on s…
items.body:
## Summary

`examples/coding_agent_rl/swe.py::_repository_tree` excludes the harness metadata directory with a pathspec:

```
git add -A -- . ':(exclude)PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md' ':(exclude).harness/'
```

When the task repo's own `.gitignore` already ignores `.harness` (for example a `.*` rule), `git add` treats the pathspec as naming an ignored path and exits 1:

```
The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
.harness
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.
```

`sb.exec(..., check=True)` then raises, `git_diff` fails, and `generate` aborts the rollout (`exception:RuntimeError`) before grading. Every rollout on such a repo is lost, regardless of the model.

This PR keeps `.harness/` out of the snapshot through a temporary `core.excludesFile` instead of a pathspec.

## How we hit it

Running MiMo-V2.6-RL-oss `format-code-task-002561` (sfcc-ci) with the Claude Code harness, all 4 rollouts aborted. The image ships sfcc-ci's upstream `.gitignore`, which contains `.*` / `!.github` (unchanged since 2019 in SalesforceCommerceCloud/sfcc-ci). On a fresh sandbox, calling `swe._repository_tree` directly:

| state | result |
| --- | --- |
| repo as shipped, no `.harness/` | ok |
| after the harness creates `.harness/` (as `slime/agent/harness/common.py` always does) | fails with the error above |
| `.harness/` present, `.*` removed from `.gitignore` | ok |

Reproduced with git 2.39.5 (in the image) and git 2.50.1.

## Fix

```sh
harness_excludes=$(mktemp)    # removed by the existing EXIT trap
echo .harness/ > "$harness_excludes"
git -c core.excludesFile="$harness_excludes" add -A -- . ':(exclude)PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md'
```

The snapshot content is unchanged:

- `.harness/` stays out whether or not the repo ignores it;
- the repo's own ignore rules still apply;
- `PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md` is still excluded by pathspec (it is not ignored, so that pathspec is safe).

Simply dropping `':(exclude).harness/'` would not be correct: on repos that do not ignore dot directories, `.harness/` would then end up in the patch.

`git_diff`'s `git diff ... ':(exclude).harness/'` is left as is: `git diff` between two trees does not reject pathspecs that match ignored paths.

## Test

Adds `test_patch_when_repo_gitignore_ignores_dot_directories` to `tests/test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py` (already part of the CPU `agent-test` CI job). It uses the existing `LocalShell` / real git setup.

- Without the fix: the new test fails with the error above; the 3 existing tests pass.
- With the fix: 4 passed.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass.

items.title: fix(dist-checkpointing): AUT-2539 key the PG distribution cache by the full proce
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: Different groups can share a minimum rank, for example a data-parallel group over ranks 0-3 and an expert-data-parallel group over ranks 0 and 2. One group could then read or overwrite the other's distribution.
items.body:
## Background

`--ckpt-pg-tensors-cache-path` stores each process group's save/load shard distribution in a file named after the group's minimum global rank (`pg_dist_<min rank>.pkl`). Different groups can share a minimum rank, for example a data-parallel group over ranks 0-3 and an expert-data-parallel group over ranks 0 and 2. One group could then read or overwrite the other's distribution. `validate_args` blocks this only for training runs that mix the save and load groups. Direct callers of the core API are not protected.

## What changed

- In `exchange_utils.py`, `_pg_dist_cache_file_path` names the file after a SHA-256 digest of the group's ordered global ranks. The in-process memo uses the same key. The minimum-rank member still writes the file.
- In `arguments.py`, only the comment and the assert message change. The assert itself is kept.
- A new test, `test_groups_sharing_min_rank_use_distinct_cache_entries`, is added to `test_pg_distribution_cache.py`:
  - It creates caches for a 4-rank group and its subgroups [0,2] and [1,3].
  - It checks that three cache files exist and that cached reads equal the uncached distribution.
  - It is skipped with fewer than 4 ranks.

## Details

This changes the cache file names. Caches written under the old `pg_dist_<min rank>.pkl` names are no longer read, so they must be regenerated with `--ckpt-pg-tensors-cache-create`.

## Tested

- black, isort, pylint and ruff are clean on the changed files under `megatron/core` and `tests/`, which is the scope `tools/autoformat.sh` lints. `arguments.py` compiles.

items.title: fix(inference): AUT-2539 keep PP stages consistent when only some hold recurrent
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: Each stage decided from its own layers whether it was a hybrid model, so the stages disagreed about Mamba prefix caching: - With a Mamba prefix-cache budget, initialization hung. The existing pipeline-parallel MIN all-reduce of the block count now also car…
items.body:
## Background

With pipeline parallelism, a hybrid model can place only attention layers on some stages (for example `M*|**`). Each stage decided from its own layers whether it was a hybrid model, so the stages disagreed about Mamba prefix caching:
- With a Mamba prefix-cache budget (`prefix_caching_mamba_gb > 0`), initialization hung.
- With memory-only prefix caching, the attention-only stage could compute a different prompt-skip count than the recurrent stage.

## What changed

- `DynamicInferenceContext` gets a new `pipeline_has_recurrent_layers` attribute. The existing pipeline-parallel MIN all-reduce of the block count now also carries the local has-recurrent flag (as `has` and `-has`). From that, every stage learns whether any stage, and whether every stage, has Mamba/GDN layers. No collective is added.
- With a Mamba prefix-cache budget, a pipeline where only some stages are recurrent now raises the same `ValueError` on every stage.
- With memory-only prefix caching, `_compute_prefix_match` applies the recurrent-stage rule on every stage of a pipeline that has recurrent layers. All stages then skip the same number of prompt tokens.
- Three new unit tests are added, in `test_dynamic_context.py` and `test_dynamic_prefix_caching.py`.

## Details

The Mamba-budget case is rejected rather than allowed to finish initializing, which differs from the review suggestion. An attention-only stage holds no Mamba state, so it cannot follow the recurrent stage's Mamba-state cache hits. Letting it continue would make the stages process different token counts for the same request. Uniform layouts, where every stage or no stage has recurrent layers, behave as before.

The two review findings on 3f74b3e0 are fixed in this head. The new device literal is now double-quoted, and the two-token assertion is back in the continuation test.

## Tested

- black, isort, pylint and ruff are clean on the changed files.

items.title: [Feature][Training] Add an FSDP2 training backend
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: Implements the design proposed in #478:, a second training backend next to Megatron that shards HF transformers causal LMs with PyTorch FSDP2 over all training ranks. Shared training files get two small hooks: - takes the choices from the registry and mer…
items.body:
Implements the design proposed in #478: `--train-backend fsdp2`, a second training backend next to Megatron that shards HF transformers causal LMs with PyTorch FSDP2 (`fully_shard`) over all training ranks.

The new code is in `vime/backends/registry.py` and `vime/backends/fsdp_utils/`. Shared training files get two small hooks:

- `_pre_parse_mode()` takes the `--train-backend` choices from the registry and merges the selected backend's own flags (`--fsdp-*`). The Megatron parser runs with `ignore_unknown_args=True` and would otherwise drop them silently.
- `RayTrainGroup` resolves the actor class through the registry.

The backend reuses vime's existing training pieces rather than copying them:

- the rollout side's DP/micro-batch schedule (each scheduled micro-batch is packed into one padding-free row with restarting `position_ids`);
- `megatron_utils/loss.py` and `train_metric_utils`, with Megatron's gradient scaling (the actor registers a pure data-parallel layout in `megatron.core.mpu`);
- the vLLM weight-transfer trainers, the same ones the Megatron updaters on this branch use: CUDA IPC for colocated engines, NCCL otherwise. They are fed by a source that materializes HF-named parameters bucket by bucket with `full_tensor()`;
- vime's checkpoint layout, written with `torch.distributed.checkpoint`.

The LR / weight-decay schedule counts samples exactly like Megatron's `OptimizerParamScheduler`, and AdamW uses Megatron's no-decay grouping. The reference model shares the sharded module through host copies of each rank's shards. Megatron stays a dependency: fsdp2 launches go through Megatron's argument parser and validation and pass the usual `MODEL_ARGS`.

**Scope:**

- Supported: dense causal LMs, colocate and separate GPUs, GRPO-style actor with an optional reference model / KL loss, sleep/wake, checkpoint save/resume and HF export.
- Rejected with an explicit error: critic, Megatron OPD teacher, DSpark/MTP draft training, routing replay, multimodal or quantized checkpoints, TP/PP/CP/EP > 1, disk/delta weight sync, and async save.

Model loading, checkpointing, packing and the LR schedule are adapted from slime's former FSDP backend (Apache-2.0); provenance is noted in each file header.

**Commits:**

1. the backend;
2. removal of thin wrappers and unused state;
3. CPU tests against real Megatron when it is installed;
4. a small adaptation to this branch's weight-transfer helpers: `create_nccl_trainer`, and pause + flush on every sync because this branch has no `--flush-cache-interval`;
5. fix: push colocated weights with torch_memory_saver tracking disabled (found on H100, see below);
6. a CPU test for that fix, and a non-vacuous gradient in the alignment test;
7. a CPU test that checks the step gradient, including the KL loss and the reference-model switch, against an unsharded computation of the same loss.

The diff contains only these changes (19 files, +2903/−5) on top of `0z5a-branch` at `8c8b8e8e`.

## Validation

### H100 runs (4× H100, Qwen3-0.6B)

Both runs used the equivalent code on top of `main`; this branch differs from it only in commit 4's weight-transfer helper calls. The second run includes commits 5 and 6; commit 7 only adds a CPU test. In the end-to-end cases vLLM starts with dummy weights, so rollouts can only see weights the trainer pushed.

| Check (second run unless noted) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The three CPU test files inside the GPU image, with real Megatron and torch_memory_saver | 36 passed, 0 skipped |
| Colocated GRPO through `train.py`: 3 rollouts × 2 steps, KL loss with a reference model, a DCP checkpoint per rollout | passed. CUDA IPC weight push works after commit 5; per-step train-vs-rollout log-prob diff 0.014–0.019 |
| Separate training (2 GPUs) and rollout (2 GPUs), NCCL weight push | passed; per-step train-vs-rollout log-prob diff 0.016–0.021 |
| Sleep/wake: the colocated run replayed without ever sleeping | bitwise identical dumps, parameters, Adam moments, step count and LR schedule. Sleep moves the actor's allocated memory from 1.73 GB to 0.06 GB |
| DCP resume: restart from the colocated run's rollout-1 checkpoint and train rollout 2 | bitwise identical to the continuous run's rollout-2 checkpoint |
| Megatron vs fsdp2 alignment test, same weights and batch (flash-attention 2) | **aligned**. Grad norms 0.082196 vs 0.082150 and 0.086195 vs 0.086167 (0.056%, 0.033%). Old-policy log-probs: mean per-sample abs diff 1.84e-2, max 2.48e-2, which is 1.11× Megatron's own train-vs-rollout diff on the same batch (1.66e-2) |
| The same alignment with a k1 KL loss (coefficient 1.0) added | **inconclusive**. Step-0 grad norm Megatron 2.518 vs fsdp2 2.491 (1.07%). The test's built-in 1% grad-norm check stopped the fsdp2 run at that step, so there is no step-1 gradient and no log-prob comparison. fsdp2 was lower than Megatron in all three grad-norm comparisons |
| Packing with real rollout tokens (first run) | flash-attention 2 packed vs per-sample identical; `sdpa` fp32 4.7e-6 |

**How the alignment is judged.** The criterion is relative to bf16 noise and was fixed before the second run:

- log-prob: the fsdp2-vs-Megatron mean per-sample abs diff must be ≤ 1.25 × Megatron's own mean train-vs-rollout diff on the same batch;
- grad norm: both sides nonzero, and the relative diff ≤ 5% at every step.

The test's built-in limits are stricter (log-prob ≤ 2e-2; grad norm within 1%). By those, the plain alignment also passes, and the KL variant fails at step 0.

**KL variant on CPU.** The plain alignment, without the KL term, agrees within 0.06%, and the KL term shares its loss scaling with the rest of the loss, so the gap comes with the k1 term. At coefficient 1.0 that term dominates the gradient (grad norm about 2.5 with it, about 0.08 in the plain alignment run). fsdp2's KL loss and reference-model switch were therefore checked on CPU: real `fully_shard` over gloo, 2 ranks, fp32, a tiny Qwen3 with tied embeddings. The fsdp2 trainer's step-0 gradient was compared with an independent plain-PyTorch computation of the same loss (zero advantages, entropy coefficient 0.01, k1 KL coefficient 1.0):

| Case | Gradient-norm rel diff | Worst per-parameter rel diff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entropy term only | 2.4e-7 | — |
| KL, reference model == actor | 9.4e-8 | 5.1e-7 |
| KL, reference model ≠ actor | 9.4e-8 | 5.1e-7 |

The k1 gradient does not depend on the reference values, and the last two cases agree. So fsdp2's KL loss and its switch between actor and reference weights compute the intended gradient; commit 7 keeps this as a test. This rules out a logic error in fsdp2's KL / reference-model path. It does not cover Megatron's side or bf16 numerics, so the source of the 1.07% gap is not yet determined.

The first run found two problems, both fixed here:

- **Colocated weight push (commit 5).** The first push failed in vLLM's packed IPC producer: `storage._share_cuda_()` raised `CUDA error: invalid argument`. With `--offload-train`, the train group preloads torch_memory_saver with tracking enabled from process start, so every CUDA allocation of the actor is a VMM mapping that CUDA IPC cannot export. The Megatron actor already runs its push under `torch_memory_saver.disable()`. In the second run a standalone probe reproduced the failure under tracking and showed the export succeeding under `disable()`.
- **Vacuous gradient check (commit 6).** In the first run every response was truncated, so rewards, advantages and both gradients were zero, and the alignment test compared zero against zero. Commit 6 adds a small entropy term to the test's loss and stops the test if Megatron's gradient is zero.

### CPU, run on this branch

- `tests/test_fsdp2_backend_registry.py`: 20 passed, 1 skipped without Megatron; 21 passed with Megatron-LM importable.
  - The Megatron-only case runs a full `parse_args()` for an fsdp2 launch.
  - The new weight-push test checks that `torch_memory_saver.disable()` is entered only under `--offload-train`. Removing commit 5 makes it fail.
- `tests/test_fsdp2_data_packing.py`: 9 passed.
- `tests/test_fsdp2_cpu_smoke.py`: 9 passed, with both the `mpu` stub and real `megatron.core.parallel_state`. It runs real `fully_shard` over gloo on a tiny random Qwen3 and checks:
  - packed log-probs against an unsharded reference;
  - identical updates for dp=1 and dp=2 (GRPO, tied embeddings with per-token loss, KL with a reference model, single-step dump);
  - weight export;
  - the step-0 gradient against an unsharded fp32 computation of the same loss: entropy term only, KL with the reference equal to the actor, and KL with a different reference;
  - reference-model switching, DCP round trip and HF export.

  Removing the micro-batch or world-size loss scaling makes the dp comparison fail; removing the switch back to the actor weights after the reference log-probs makes the differing-reference gradient case fail.
- Existing tests touched by the shared hooks: 236 passed, 2 skipped.
- pre-commit hooks passed on the changed files.

The real-Megatron runs on CPU used a local Megatron-LM v0.19.2 checkout (`4b4acac9`), not the commit pinned in this branch's Dockerfile. Buildkite's CPU steps passed on commit 6; the build for commit 7 was still running when this was written.

**Not covered yet:**

- the source of the 1.07% step-0 grad-norm gap in the KL variant (fsdp2's path is exact on CPU in fp32; Megatron's side and bf16 numerics are not yet isolated);
- `--fsdp-cpu-offload`;
- gradient checkpointing;
- multi-node runs;
- larger models;
- a throughput or memory comparison with Megatron.

AI assistance: implementation and tests were prepared with Claude Code at the submitter's request, with attribution and DCO sign-off in each commit. Kept as a draft pending the submitter's line-by-line review and the KL alignment question; no end-to-end training-quality or performance result is claimed.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6692200][perf] Cut KVCacheManagerV2 host overhead in generation steps (release/1.3)
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: Backport of #20349 to for NVBug: 512/512 throughput regressed when GPT-OSS moved to KV cache manager V2 (#16942, already on; GPT-OSS's returns here too). On GB200 (same node, interleaved arms, CI wheel), V2 is 6.3% slower than V1.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Backport of #20349 to `release/1.3` for NVBug [6692200](https://nvbugs/6692200): `gpt_oss_20b_fp4` `trtllm-bench` 512/512 throughput regressed when GPT-OSS moved to KV cache manager V2 (#16942, already on `release/1.3`; GPT-OSS's `get_preferred_kv_cache_manager_version` returns `"V2"` here too).

On GB200 (same node, interleaved arms, CI wheel), V2 is 6.3% slower than V1. The loss is host time in mixed prefill+decode steps once a step carries ≥256 generation requests; GPU busy time per step is identical under both managers. Two V2-only host costs cause it:

1. **GPU pool chunk size, 32 MiB → up to 256 MiB.** `CacheLevelManager::cacheTierGranularity` capped the GPU pool's physical chunks at 32 MiB, so a full-GPU pool (151 GiB on GB200) is 4830 separate `cuMemCreate` mappings. On Grace (ATS) systems that slows every later `cudaMalloc` in the process. The PyTorch caching allocator growing the fp32 logits buffer pays 3.4–4.3 ms per allocation under V2 vs 0.42–0.51 ms under V1, with the GPU idle. A standalone microbenchmark on the same node, without TRT-LLM, reproduces it: 210 MiB `cuMemAlloc` takes 242 µs bare, 703 µs with a 150 GiB pool of 32 MiB chunks, 305 µs with 1 GiB chunks. The cap becomes 256 MiB (604 chunks for the same pool); quotas below 32 GiB keep their granularity. On this branch the pure-Python V2 backend's `CacheLevelManager.cache_tier_granularity` mirror is updated to match.
2. **`_log_window_crossing` queried the log level on every call.** It runs from `try_allocate_generation` for each generation request, every iteration, and called `logger.is_debug_enabled()` (a frame walk) before checking for a crossing. Decode always grows capacity, so the query always ran: 1.0–1.4 ms of host time per iteration at ~300 requests. The window comparison now runs first; the log level is queried only for a call that crosses a window. Logging output is unchanged. `_windowed_layer_group_sizes` is now declared on the class so a manager built without `__init__` still works.

### Measured (GB200, oci-hsg; main-branch CI wheel `fca08032f7`, same node, interleaved)

Throughput change vs stock V2 on the same node:

| arm | nodes | mean | per node |
|---|---|---|---|
| **this fix** (both changes) | 4 | **+4.05%** | +4.8 / +5.0 / +1.4 / +5.0 |
| chunk cap only | 5 | +4.31% | +5.8 / +5.0 / +2.7 / +3.3 / +4.7 |
| log guard only | 2 | +2.15% | +2.5 / +1.8 |
| V1 (reference) | 8 | +6.33% | +4.8 … +7.2 |

Pooled final run: V1 67486, V2 63092, **fixed 65831 tok/s**; the V1–V2 gap goes from −6.5% to −2.5%.

### Measured on this branch (GB200, oci-hsg; `release/1.3` CI wheel GenPostMergeBuilds #80 = `7c2f938`, its own 26.09 image, same node, interleaved)

| node | V1 | V2 (stock) | V2 + this fix | fix vs V2 | V1–V2 gap recovered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| nvl72155-T04 | 51546 / 51688 / 51095 | 49650 / 48885 / 49532 | 50374 / 51567 / 50568 | +3.00% | 71% |
| nvl72016-T18 | 51402 / 51806 / 51128 | 48213 / 48642 / 49286 | 50035 / 51050 / 49722 | +3.19% | 57% |

Pooled medians (6 reps/arm): V1 51474, V2 49085, **fixed 50471 tok/s**; the V1–V2 gap goes from −4.6% to −2.0%. The C++ change was applied with an `LD_PRELOAD` replacement of `cacheTierGranularity` (identical body, cap 7; the shim log shows 256 MiB granularity on every fixed rep) and the Python change was applied to the installed file.

**Platform scope:** the chunk-count cost is specific to Grace/ATS (GB200/GB300). On an x86 B200 (HMM), allocation cost does not change with chunk count, so x86 Blackwell gets only the log-guard change.

## Test Coverage

Run on the `release/1.3` CI wheel (GenPostMergeBuilds #80 = `7c2f938`, this branch's base), x86, A10, with the installed sources swapped stock → patched → stock:

- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py`
  - `test_window_crossing_queries_log_level_only_on_a_crossing` (new): fails on stock (`[100-101-0]`, `[2049-2050-0]`), passes patched.
  - `test_window_crossing_builds_its_window_map_without_init` (new): fails on stock, passes patched.
  - The existing `test_window_crossing_*` and `test_generation_allocation_reserves_dynamic_width` pass patched.
- `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py::TestCacheLevelStorage::test_python_backend_gpu_granularity_grows_with_quota_up_to_256_mib` (new): fails 3/7 cases on stock (the ≥128 GiB quotas), passes 7/7 patched.
- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2SlotAllocatorTest.cpp`: `GpuPoolGranularityGrowsWithQuotaUpTo256MiB`, `NonGpuTierGranularityIsIndependentOfQuota` (new; compiled and run by CI's gtest stage).

All are in CI lists: `l0_cpu.yml` / `l0_h100.yml` (`unittest/_torch/executor`), `l0_a10.yml` (`unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests`), and the `kvCacheManagerV2SlotAllocatorTest` gtest target.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

items.title: [#13957][feat] Add pipelined PyExecutor scheduler loop (enable_pipelined_scheduler)
items.author: Asthenia0412
items.summary: ThreadPoolExecutor(maxworkers=1) 专属 worker 线程跑 forward+sample dispatch 2. 主线程同时 schedule 下一批 + drain 最老批结果 3. [Discussion: The loop schedules batches on the main thread and dispatches forward and sampling work to a worker.]
items.body:
## Background

PyExecutor._executor_loop_overlap single-thread 1-step lookahead scheduler 在高并发 decode 场景下，per-iter host 开销与 GPU 开销相当，导致 GPU 空转 ~580µs/iter。

## Problem

Single-threaded executor loop cannot overlap host scheduling + dispatch with GPU forward.

## Solution

Opt-in 2-batch pipelined executor loop (enable_pipelined_scheduler):

1. ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) 专属 worker 线程跑 forward+sample dispatch
2. 主线程同时 schedule 下一批 + drain 最老批结果
3. CUDA event-based cross-thread synchronization
4. 严格线程隔离：scheduling collectives 仅在主线程执行

## Testing

新增 test_py_executor_pipelined_scheduler.py (200+ lines, 19 test cases):
- _is_pipelined_loop_eligible gate conditions (8 tests: disabled flag, plain TP, speculative, disaggregated, attention-DP, overlap-disable, multimodal encoder, guided decoding)

items.summary: The reason for this PR is to resolve a future or the needs of using non pinned transformers. from current pinned 5.5.3,!=5.6.0,<5.13 [Discussion: <!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai --> The Qwen3.5 decoder forward f]
items.body:
## Motivation
The reason for this PR is to resolve a future or the needs of using non pinned transformers.
from current pinned 5.5.3,!=5.6.0,<5.13

## What is wrong

`qwen3_5_decoder_layer_forward` (the patched `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer.forward`) reads `self.layer_type`.
transformers 5.13.0 renamed that decoder-layer attribute to `block_type`, so on transformers >= 5.13 the first
forward raises:

    AttributeError: 'FSDPQwen3_5DecoderLayer' object has no attribute 'layer_type'

(The `FSDP...` prefix is just FSDP2's dynamic subclass of the layer; the attribute is missing on the layer itself.)

Which transformers versions have which name (checked from the wheels' `modeling_qwen3_5.py`):

| transformers | `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer` attribute |
|---|---|
| 5.10.4, 5.11.0, 5.12.0 | `layer_type` |
| 5.13.0 - 5.17.0 | `block_type` |

## Fix

Read the name that exists: `getattr(self, "layer_type", None) or self.block_type`. Works on both sides of the rename,
so the pin can move later without another change.

## Test

New CPU-only unit test `tests/models/test_qwen3_5_decoder_layer_forward.py` (tiny random full-attention layer).

| transformers | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 5.12.1 | pass | pass |
| 5.17.0 | FAIL (AttributeError above) | pass |

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/cute_dsl_kernels/blackwell/attention/mla/mla_decode_fp8.py`: The diff changes import formatting only. The file contains bounds checks that default out-of-range page indices to page 0, but those checks are not changes in the inspected diff.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Fixes https://nvbugs/6862662: `test_attention_mla` (V1 KV cache, BF16 activations, FP8 KV cache, 64 requests × 10 context tokens, page size 32) intermittently hits a CUDA illegal memory access on B200.

**Root cause.** In the CuTe DSL FP8 MLA decode kernel (`mla_decode_fp8.py`), the K and V TMA load paths read `page_per_tile` page IDs for every KV tile. A 128-token tile can need up to four page IDs at page size 32, even when a request owns only one page. The kernel read those entries without checking the page-table width. For the last request, those reads run past the end of the page-table allocation. Here that allocation is 64 requests × 2 interleaved K/V slots × 1 int32 page ID = 512 bytes. Whether the access faults depends on what the caching allocator has placed after the table, so the failure is order-dependent. The original traceback surfaced later, in the test's reference computation, because CUDA reports the fault asynchronously.

**Fix.** Bound each page-table read by `mPT.shape[0]`. Lanes past the table width use physical page 0. Those lanes are masked out by the sequence length anyway, and still issuing the TMA load keeps each tile's expected byte count unchanged. This mirrors the existing guard in the FP16 kernel's page-table loader (`mla_decode_fp16.py`, `load_page_table`), which zero-fills out-of-range entries.

## Test Coverage

- New `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_cute_dsl_mla_page_table.py` (8 variants): page sizes 32/64, persistent/non-persistent, split-KV 1/2, with one compiled kernel reused across table widths 4, 1, 2, 3, 5. Uses V1-style interleaved K/V page-table strides. Run under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, it detects the out-of-bounds reads before the fix. It is collected by the existing `unittest/_torch/attention` entry in `l0_b200.yml`.
- Existing `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_attention_mla.py`.

| Full `unittest/_torch/attention` suite at the historical failing revision | illegal access after 4,412 passed | 4,786 passed |

The same out-of-bounds reads reproduce on current main (`c9b18eefa7`); a separate PR will carry the fix and waiver removal there.

items.author: yingguo-trt
items.summary: Wan pipelines copied the primary transformer's quantization settings into, even when its Diffusers component config contained different metadata. A primary-only FP8 export could therefore load a BF16 secondary as FP8 and fail on missing scales; a secondary-on…
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
`DiffusionPipelineConfig` now resolves quantization metadata per transformer. User configs with an algorithm take precedence; otherwise, each transformer uses its checkpoint metadata. Components in single-safetensors checkpoints continue to share top-level metadata. Pipeline-level fields remain based on the primary transformer.

Runtime LoRA validation now checks the selected target components. This avoids rejecting an unquantized target because another transformer is quantized. LoRA targeting a quantized transformer remains unsupported. The documentation reflects this restriction. No implementation test result or patched GPU inference result is available; the requested Blackwell QA and maintainer confirmation for mixed FP8/BF16 remain follow-up items.

## QA Engineer Review
Modified `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_model_loader.py` and added it to `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`. Test coverage includes independent transformer metadata, quantization overrides, pipeline-level settings, and Runtime LoRA target validation. The dual-transformer configuration test is marked `cpu_only`. Native repository pytest and GPU validation results are not available. **Coverage verdict: needs follow-up**, pending Blackwell QA for primary-only and secondary-only FP8 cases.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/config.py`: Verify independent checkpoint metadata resolution for both transformers, precedence for explicit user overrides, and primary-only pipeline fields. Verify Runtime LoRA accepts unquantized targets and rejects quantized targets.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_model_loader.py`: Covers dual-transformer quantization configurations and Runtime LoRA target checks. The dual-transformer configuration test is `cpu_only`; the file is listed in the `l0_cpu` CI test list.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`: Adds `unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_model_loader.py` to the CPU CI list.
- `docs/source/models/visual-generation.md`: Documents that Runtime LoRA cannot target a transformer with weight quantization enabled. The startup-fusion limitation on per-request adapter switching is unchanged.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Wan pipelines copied the primary transformer's quantization settings into `transformer_2`, even when its Diffusers component config contained different metadata. A primary-only FP8 export could therefore load a BF16 secondary as FP8 and fail on missing scales; a secondary-only FP8 export could be treated as unquantized. Even two FP8 components lost the secondary's own exclusions and dynamic flags.

Resolve each transformer's checkpoint metadata independently and pass its quantization settings into `DiffusionModelConfig` at construction, preserving Pydantic validation and independent copies. An explicit user quantization algorithm still overrides both transformers; pipeline-level fields still describe the primary, and single-safetensors components retain their existing shared quantization settings.

Runtime LoRA checks now consider the selected `target_components` and identify a quantized target in the error. A BF16 target is no longer rejected merely because an untargeted transformer is quantized; applying LoRA to a quantized target remains unsupported.

ModelOpt can export a checkpoint after quantizing only one Wan transformer. Maintainer confirmation of the intended support for that mixed FP8/BF16 layout remains requested.

## Test Coverage
