items.title: [None][perf] GLM-5.3-Flash C++ kernel speedups: vectorized FP8 1x128 quant and 288-expert router GEMM
items.author: ruocheng-nv
items.summary:
Two C++ kernel speedups found on GLM-5.3-Flash, one commit each. The FP8 quantization change is bit-identical to main. [Discussion: 🎉
ℹ️ Recent review info
<]
items.body:
## Description

Two C++ kernel speedups found on GLM-5.3-Flash, one commit each. The FP8 quantization change is bit-identical to main. The router GEMM change replaces cuBLAS with a kernel that accumulates in a different order, so the 288 x 4096 router logits change at FP32 rounding level.

### 1. Vectorized BF16-to-FP8 1x128 activation quantization

`scale_1x128_kernel` (behind `fp8_quantize_1x128` and the FP8 block-scale GEMM runners) and `scale_1x128_reshape_kernel` (behind `fp8_batched_quantize_1x128_permute102`, the MLA BMM operand) use one warp per 128-wide group, with two 4-byte loads and four 1-byte stores per lane.

This PR adds vectorized variants: 16 lanes own one group, each loads its 8 inputs with one 16-byte load, the group amax is reduced with 4 warp shuffles, and each lane stores its 8 outputs with one 8-byte store. Partial last groups (for example K = 576) are handled in the same kernel. The scale arithmetic, including UE8M0 rounding, is copied unchanged.

The host launchers choose the vectorized kernel when every row holds whole 16-byte lane chunks (`dim_x` and the row stride divisible by 8) and the input and output are 16- and 8-byte aligned. Otherwise they launch the existing element-wise kernels unchanged, so unaligned inputs run the same code as before.

**Kernel time** (B200, profiler-measured kernel duration, median of 5 x 200 launches). All 88 benchmarked cases are bit-identical to main (FP8 bytes and scales).

| Case | main | This PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| dense 1 x 4096 | 1.91 us | 1.87 us | 1.02x |
| dense 256 x 4096 | 3.51 us | 2.96 us | 1.19x |
| dense 1024 x 4096 | 8.17 us | 5.43 us | 1.51x |
| dense 4096 x 4096 | 26.15 us | 15.34 us | 1.70x |
| dense 16384 x 4096 | 107.27 us | 59.75 us | 1.80x |
| dense 16384 x 7168 | 184.34 us | 102.62 us | 1.80x |
| dense 16384 x 576 (partial last group) | 17.01 us | 10.44 us | 1.63x |
| dense 16384 x 4096, UE8M0 | 116.51 us | 63.27 us | 1.84x |
| reshape 8192 x 32 x 512 (row stride 576) | 305.54 us | 161.73 us | 1.89x |
| reshape 1024 x 32 x 128 (row stride 192) | 11.07 us | 6.95 us | 1.59x |
| dense 16384 x 4096, input 4 bytes past a 16-byte boundary (element-wise kernel) | 106.77 us | 107.05 us | 1.00x |
| reshape 8192 x 32 x 128, row stride 130 (element-wise kernel) | 76.11 us | 76.23 us | 1.00x |

No benchmarked case is slower: M from 1 to 16384, K in {576, 2048, 4096, 7168}, with and without UE8M0. Small M is launch-bound and unchanged (about 1.9 us).

**End-to-end:** GLM-5.3-Flash with `trtllm-serve` at TP4/EP4, MTP3, `max_num_tokens` 16384, `max_seq_len` 131072, on 4x B200, aiperf with sonnet prompts, ISL 13312 / OSL 33. Both builds use the same Python code (main); only the native library differs. Medians over 4 rounds from 2 server instances per build.

| Metric | main | This PR | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 TTFT p50 | 372.9 ms | **366.6 ms** | +1.7% (lower in all 4 rounds) |
| C1 request latency p50 | 481.2 ms | 477.6 ms | +0.7% |
| C8 TTFT p50 | 1283 ms | 1243 ms | within run-to-run spread (1088-1553 ms on main) |
| C8 output throughput | 90.1 tok/s | 90.8 tok/s | within noise |

Gain is the improvement over main: the reduction for latencies, the increase for throughput.

Memory is unchanged (warmup peak 98.88 GiB, KV cache 61.20 GiB per GPU on both builds).

### 2. 288-expert dsv3 router GEMM instantiation

`dsv3_router_gemm_op` has low-latency kernels only for 256 experts (hidden 7168 / 6144 / 4096). The expert count is part of `shape_ok`, so any other count, including GLM-5.3-Flash's 288 experts x hidden 4096, silently falls back to cuBLAS. This PR instantiates `invokeRouterGemm<__nv_bfloat16, N, 288, 4096>` for N = 1..16, moves the expert-count check into each dispatch branch, and adds a branch for 288 x 4096. Every other shape keeps the cuBLAS fallback.

Both the low-latency kernels and the cuBLAS fallback read rows of `hidden_dim` elements starting on a 16-byte boundary, but the op checked neither the row pitch nor the alignment. On main, an operand sliced from wider rows gives wrong logits on both paths, and one starting 8 bytes past a 16-byte boundary raises a CUDA error (misaligned address in the 256-expert kernels, a cuBLASLt error in the fallback for 256 x 7168 at 1-8 tokens). Such an operand is now copied once into a packed, aligned layout and passed to whichever path runs; packed, aligned operands, as the model passes them, are used without a copy. The BF16 kernels also now require the weight dtype to match the input.

The new kernel accumulates in a different order from cuBLAS: on the same input, most of the 288 x 4096 logits differ in the last FP32 bits (max absolute difference about 3.5e-4 on random data). Accuracy with this kernel in the model is covered by #20389's GSM8K once both PRs are in; the end-to-end numbers below run main's Python, which does not call this op.

**Router GEMM at 288 x 4096** (B200, BF16 in, FP32 out):

| Implementation | Per call (CUDA events, 1-16 tokens) | GPU kernel time (8 tokens) |
|---|---|---|
| `dsv3_router_gemm_op`, main (cuBLAS fallback) | 12.9-13.2 us | 5.9 us (2 kernels) |
| `dsv3_router_gemm_op`, this PR | **6.6-6.8 us** | **3.3 us** (1 kernel) |
| `cute_dsl_bf16_gemm_blackwell` | 20.3-20.6 us | 12.1 us |

Decode and MTP verification run under CUDA graphs, where the kernel time applies: about 2.6 us saved per MoE layer, about 0.11 ms per forward over GLM-5.3-Flash's 42 MoE layers, once #20389 routes the gate through this op.

**Environment:** B200, `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc25` with a source build of main `91c9b6d1cc` (PyTorch 2.12 nv26.05, CUDA 13.2); rebased onto `ed87ab0b01`.

Notes: The router GEMM part only takes effect after #20389 merges. On current main, `Glm5NextGate` computes its logits with its own FP32 `F.linear` and never calls `dsv3_router_gemm_op`; #20389 switches it to the base `DeepseekV3Gate` GEMM. The FP8 quantization part takes effect on its own.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/_torch/thop/parallel/` (in `l0_b200.yml`):
- `test_fp8_quantize.py::test_fp8_quantize_1x128_vectorized_matches_elementwise[use_ue8m0]`: the same 37 x 576 data (partial last group, padded scale rows) quantized from a 16-byte aligned buffer (vectorized kernel) and from one 4 bytes past the boundary (element-wise kernel) gives identical FP8 bytes and written scales, with and without UE8M0. The reshape kernel is exercised by the existing block-scale BMM tests, which call `fp8_batched_quantize_1x128_permute102`.
- `test_dsv3_router_gemm.py::test_router_gemm_run`: now parametrized over explicit `(num_experts, hidden_size)` pairs (256 x 7168 / 6144 / 4096 and 288 x 4096) so 288 x 4096 runs the new kernel, and over the operand layout: both input and weights packed, starting 8 bytes past a 16-byte boundary, or sliced from wider rows; 1-16 tokens each. The logits are checked at `atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3`, matching FP32 accumulation-order differences.

`test_fp8_quantize.py`, `test_fp8_block_scale_gemm.py` and `test_dsv3_router_gemm.py` pass on B200.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes

- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
- The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR.

items.title: [None][perf] GLM-5.3-Flash: share KDA verify offsets, fuse mHC in every phase, BF16 router GEMM
items.author: ruocheng-nv
items.summary: Three GLM-5.3-Flash optimizations on the Python side, one commit each. Share the KDA verify offsets across layers and pass strided verify inputs (,, ) - During MTP verification, every KDA layer gathered the accepted-draft counts of the generation requests an…
items.body:
## Description

Three GLM-5.3-Flash optimizations on the Python side, one commit each.

**1. Share the KDA verify offsets across layers and pass strided verify inputs** (`kimi_kda_mixer.py`, `kimi_k3_mamba_metadata.py`, `modeling_glm5_next.py`)
- During MTP verification, every KDA layer gathered the accepted-draft counts of the generation requests and rebuilt the per-request token offsets, although the counts live in one buffer shared by all layers and only change after sampling. `Glm5NextModel` now computes `(pending, cu_seqlens)` once per forward and passes them to every KDA layer through `KimiK3MambaMetadata.kda_verify_offsets`. Layers compute their own when no model provides them, so Kimi is unchanged.
- `trtllm::kda_mtp_decode` reads Q/K/V/beta through dynamic token strides, so the fused verify path now passes strided views of the fused projection instead of making four contiguous copies per layer.

**2. Fuse the mHC boundaries in every batch phase** (`modeling_glm5_next.py`)
- `mHC.fused_hc` (post-mapping, pre-mapping and RMSNorm in one kernel) ran only for generation-only batches. The fused loop is phase-agnostic, so prefill and mixed batches now take it too, and the warmup pass measures the same path that mixed batches take.
- The fused kernel rounds differently from the separate post-mapping, pre-mapping and RMSNorm ops, so prefill hidden states change at BF16 rounding level (up to about 1.6e-2 absolute on the same input). Decode already used this path.
- GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layers get the attention aux stream, so their small gate projections overlap the QKV projection as in Kimi.

**3. Use the BF16 router weight in the gate** (`modeling_glm5_next.py`)
- The checkpoint stores the router weight in BF16. `Glm5NextGate` widened the activations and the weight to FP32 for an `F.linear` on every MoE layer. It now keeps the weight in BF16 and uses the base `DeepseekV3Gate` GEMM with FP32 output, like the other DeepSeek-style gates. The correction bias stays FP32.
- The router logits change at FP32 accumulation-order level, which can flip near-tied expert choices.

Commits 2 and 3 change numerics (fused mHC in prefill, BF16 router GEMM); commit 1 does not. GSM8K below covers both.

**End-to-end:** `trtllm-serve` at TP4/EP4, MTP3, BF16 KV cache, `max_num_tokens` 16384, `max_seq_len` 131072, chunked prefill, on 4x B200. aiperf with sonnet prompts, `ignore_eos`, temperature 0. items.body:
### What does this PR do?

This PR fixes several issues observed when running DeepSeek V4 with FSDP-Turbo and vLLM-Ascend on NPU:
- Fix legacy `FusedMoE` weight-layout detection for `w1` and `w3`.
  - To adapt to operators such as Grouped MatMul, the Ascend backend merges the internal weights w1 and w3 within MOE because their input and output dimensions are the same and can be used simultaneously for computation. To adapt to this merged layout, the verL internally performs a transpose operation on the weights through a patch operation, adjusting the view of w13_weight/w2_weight so that the original weights can be correctly merged. The original transpose condition was relatively simple, only checking whether one dimension of w13_weight was equal to the hidden_size dimension. However, it did not consider the case in DeepSeek v4 where the two dimensions of the fused w13_weight were equal, leading to w13_weight being transposed twice. As a result, the final weight layout did not meet expectations, which was also verified in the DeepSeek v4 flash training experiments. This caused precision issues and led to inconsistencies between training and inference. The Qwen3.5 MOE model did not encounter this issue precisely because the last two dimensions of w13_weight were not equal, so it only needed to be transposed once as a whole, satisfying the subsequent weight layout. This has been verified on the Qwen3.5 35B model.
  - Preserve the existing `w2` transpose behavior.
- Fix the issue of duplicate return outputs under TP/Ulysses mixed parallel processing.
- Prevent the `no_sync` mechanism of the standard FSDP from interfering with FSDP-Turbo's own backward communication and synchronization scheduling.
- These modifications will not affect the original FSDP strategy.

items.summary: Fixes: image requests to FP8 Gemma-4-31B-it with an FP8 KV cache fail with using the TRTLLM attention backend. The custom-mask context backend rejects FP8 KV caches and FP8 output buffers. [Discussion: /bot run --disable-fail-fast]
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

Custom-mask context attention now supports FP8 KV caches and FP8 output. The Triton prefill path dequantizes paged-prefix K/V tiles with the supplied KV scale and quantizes output with the supplied output scale. FP8 E4M3 output is clamped to `[-448, 448]` before conversion.

The new scale parameters are optional, preserving existing calls. The support check still rejects INT8 and FP4 KV-cache modes. The FlashInfer TRT-LLM Gen error now reports the unsupported `attention_mask` value. No review findings or severity counts were supplied.

## QA Engineer Review

Three unit-test files changed. They cover backend support and rejection, mask handling, cached-prefix dequantization, FP8 output scaling and saturation, and head dimensions 256 and 512. The changed tests are under `tests/unittest/`, not integration tests; test-db and manual-QA list status is not applicable.

The PR objectives report 52 passing tests from the listed pytest command. Independent test execution is not established. Coverage verdict: **sufficient** for the described behavior.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/fmha/flashinfer_trtllm_gen.py`: Verify that unsupported masks report the raw `attention_mask` value.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/fmha/triton_custom_mask.py`: Verify support for FP8 KV cache and FP8 output, rejection of INT8 and FP4 KV caches, and correct scale forwarding.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/triton_prefill.py`: Verify paged-prefix dequantization, output scaling, E4M3 saturation, and unchanged handling of contiguous extend K/V.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_gen_fmha.py`: Exercises causal and custom-mask support checks; custom masks must be rejected with an unsupported-mask reason. Integration test-list status is not applicable.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_triton_custom_mask_fmha.py`: Exercises context support across BF16 and FP8 output and supported or rejected KV-cache modes. Integration test-list status is not applicable.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_triton_prefill.py`: Exercises cache scaling across head dimensions 256 and 512, BF16 and FP8 output, and FP8 saturation at ±448. Integration test-list status is not applicable.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Fixes [NVBug 6913951](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6913951): image requests to FP8 Gemma-4-31B-it with an FP8 KV cache fail with `Unexpected attention mask type: <CustomAttentionMask.CUSTOM: 'custom'>` using the TRTLLM attention backend.

The custom-mask context backend rejects FP8 KV caches and FP8 output buffers. During backend selection, the FlashInfer TRT-LLM Gen support check also accesses the unsupported `mask_type` property again inside its exception handler, causing selection to fail.

Allow FP8 KV caches and FP8 output in custom-mask context attention. Dequantize cached K/V tiles on load, and apply the output quantization scale with finite E4M3 saturation. Keep new contiguous K/V in the compute dtype and avoid allocating a converted copy of the KV pool. Report unsupported masks using the raw attention-mask value so backend selection can continue.

    tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_triton_prefill.py

items.title: [Investigation] Actor entropy explosion followed by collapse in async multi-turn tool-use RL (GRPO and GSPO, verl v0.9.1)
items.author: Maclaurin1
items.summary: Investigating unstable actor entropy (explosion then collapse) during async multi-turn tool-use RL training with verl v0.9.1, seeking diagnostic guidance to isolate root cause.
items.body: ## Summary We are training a multi-turn, tool-using financial agent with separate asynchronous vLLM rollout and FSDP2 actor training. We have observed unstable actor entropy under more than one policy-loss configuration. The most severe runs show a sharp entropy increase, reward collapse, malformed/repetitive generations, and then a sharp entropy decrease. We have **not** established that this is a verl bug: our agent loop, tools, and reward are customized, and the runs below are not a controlled 2 × 2 ablation. We would appreciate advice on which diagnostics can distinguish a numerical policy-update problem from train/rollout inconsistency or a task-specific reward problem. ## Environment - verl source for the current 9B run: **v0.9.1**, git commit `1876b06d0a3e4e71e06230be10af14492ca8a75b`, with local modifications (including the custom agent/reward and long-context fused fixes). The older 27B runs used a previous customized v0.9.1 checkout; its exact commit is no longer available. - Trainer: `trainer.use_v1=True`, `trainer.v1.trainer_mode=separate_async`, unified `ActorRolloutRefWorker`/`TrainingWorker`; `trainer.use_legacy_worker_impl` is not used in this checkout. - Rollout backend: `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm`, `mode=async`, `n=8`, temperature `1.0`. - **vLLM runtime version still needs verification from the training image.** The current repository pins `vllm==0.24.0` in `pyproject.toml`; this is a declared dependency, not proof of the installed version. We will update this field once `python -m pip show vllm` is run inside the task image. - Actor: FSDP2, AdamW, learning rate `5e-7`, PPO epochs `1`; rollout group batch is 48 prompts × 8 responses = 384 trajectories per training step. No actor KL loss or entropy bonus in the current 9B run. - Workload: private Qwen-family SFT checkpoints (27B and 9B), multi-turn tool calls, variable-length responses, custom reward. We cannot publish the private data/tool endpoints but can share redacted config, metrics, and trajectories. ## Observations ### A. 27B GRPO, token-mean aggregation: full explosion and collapse This was an asynchronous run resumed at global step 30. It used GRPO advantages, the vanilla/PPO policy loss, `loss_agg_mode=token-mean` (default in that checkout), PPO clipping at ±0.1, and a small KL penalty **in the reward** (`kl_coef=5e-4`). Reward combined process and result components, with a different scale from the later runs. Therefore, compare values **within this run only**. | Global step | `actor/entropy` | Train mean reward | Val mean reward | `actor/grad_norm` | `rollout_corr/kl` | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 40 | 0.510 | 1.819 | 1.752 | 0.193 | 0.0181 | | 60 | 0.551 | 1.801 | 1.753 | 0.102 | 0.0178 | | 64 | 0.604 | 1.823 | — | 0.260 | 0.0189 | | 68 | 3.656 | 1.671 | — | 0.765 | 0.0385 | | 70 | 6.172 | 1.214 | 1.421 | 7.286 | 0.1797 | | 71 | 5.281 | 0.146 | — | 1,010.9 | 1.345 | | 72 | 0.232 | 0.229 | — | 12,442.6 | 15.631 | Generation quality deteriorated around this transition. Entropy's final decrease did **not** mean recovery: reward and gradient diagnostics remained severely abnormal. ### B. 27B GRPO, `seq-mean-token-mean`: early upward drift, not a proven collapse In a separate run from the original SFT checkpoint with `policy_loss.loss_mode=vanilla`, `loss_agg_mode=seq-mean-token-mean`, no KL loss/penalty, and temperature 1.0, entropy rose from **0.152 at step 1** to **0.278 at step 20** and **0.326 at step 22**. Train reward was **1.778 at step 1** and **1.720 at step 22**; validation reward was **1.647 at step 10** and **1.613 at step 20**. This run's available record stops at step 22, so it is evidence of early entropy drift, **not** evidence of a later explosion or collapse. ### C. 27B GSPO, `seq-mean-token-mean`: initially stable counterexample Another from-scratch 27B run used `policy_loss.loss_mode=gspo`, `loss_agg_mode=seq-mean-token-mean`, and GSPO clipping at `clip_ratio_low=0.0003`, `clip_ratio_high=0.0004`. Entropy was **0.409 at step 1** and **0.321 at step 80**, with a maximum of **0.441** over steps 1–80. Validation result reward was **0.769 at step 10** and **0.802 at step 80**. This run enabled only result reward. It shows that the failure is **not universal** to GSPO or sequence-mean aggregation; the reward setup and starting point also differed from A. ### D. Current 9B GSPO, `seq-mean-token-mean`: delayed deterioration and reward collapse The current 9B run starts from an SFT checkpoint and uses GSPO/`seq-mean-token-mean` with the same GSPO clipping values as C, **no clip-token mask**, no KL loss or KL-in-reward, and result + format + efficiency rewards (maximum 1.4). The agent context budget is 65,536 input tokens and 4,096 generated tokens per turn; total trajectory budget is 69,888 tokens. The run has 2 rollout nodes and 2 training nodes (8 GPUs per node). | Global step | `actor/entropy` | Train mean reward | Val mean reward | `actor/grad_norm` | `rollout_corr/kl` | Mean response length | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 123 | 0.390 | 1.197 | — | 0.262 | 0.0196 | 2,833 | | 125 | 0.453 | 1.168 | — | 6.136 | 0.2236 | 2,519 | | 127 | 0.072 | 1.129 | — | 0.744 | 0.0386 | 2,885 | | 132 | 0.646 | 1.095 | — | 0.323 | 0.0774 | 2,649 | | 135 | 1.664 | 0.240 | — | 0.029 | 0.1067 | 233 | | 138 | 4.033 | 0.264 | — | 0.175 | 0.0653 | 256 | | 140 | 1.696 | 0.280 | 0.280 | 0.000 | 0.0347 | 197 | | 149 | 0.583 | 0.280 | — | 0.000 | 0.0206 | 161 | Around step 125, a sampled model version produced malformed/repetitive trajectories. Later, response length collapsed from thousands of tokens to a few hundred; by step 149, the per-question-type `result_mean` and `completed_ratio` were **0** for all four task categories. Total reward remained around 0.28 because non-result reward components were enabled; it should not be read as successful task completion. At some late steps `actor/grad_norm=0`. Please note this is an actively running experiment and these are point-in-time observations. ## Questions 1. Have you seen this **entropy rise → reward/length collapse → entropy fall** pattern with the V1 separate-async trainer, GSPO, or Qwen-family hybrid architectures? Are there known fixes in newer verl/vLLM versions? 2. Which metrics or checks best distinguish (a) bad actor updates/numerical instability, (b) actor–rollout log-prob or token alignment problems, and (c) vLLM weight-sync/cache problems? Would comparing teacher-forced log-probs and entropy on fixed prompts across the training actor, a freshly loaded checkpoint, and the live rollout engine be sufficient? 3. Is `actor/grad_norm=0` after the reward/response-length collapse expected when effective advantages become zero, or does it suggest an additional masking/data-pipeline issue? 4. For long multi-turn trajectories, are there known risks in the FSDP2/fused policy-loss path or GSPO loss aggregation that we should specifically test? Which version-specific debug flags would you recommend? We can attach sanitized TensorBoard curves, step-level CSVs, selected rollout trajectories, and the relevant config once you advise which artifacts are most useful. We are not claiming that changing `token-mean` to `seq-mean-token-mean` or switching GRPO to GSPO alone caused or fixed this issue; these runs differ in checkpoint, reward, context length, and other custom code. ### Information - My own modified scripts ### Tasks - My own task or dataset ### Reproduction This was observed in a private multi-turn, tool-using agent task. I cannot yet provide a public standalone reproduction because the dataset and tool endpoints are private. The relevant configuration is: ```yaml verl: v0.9.1 (git commit 1876b06d0a3e4e71e06230be10af14492ca8a75b, with local modifications) trainer.use_v1: true trainer.v1.trainer_mode: separate_async trainer.nnodes: 2 trainer.n_gpus_per_node: 8 actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name: vllm actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode: async actor_rollout_ref.rollout.nnodes: 2 actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n: 8 actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature: 1.0 actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy: fsdp2 actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr: 5e-7 actor_rollout_ref.actor.policy_loss.loss_mode: gspo actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode: seq-mean-token-mean actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_low: 0.0003 actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high: 0.0004 actor_rollout_ref.actor.policy_loss.clip_mask_enabled: false actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss: false algorithm.adv_estimator: grpo algorithm.use_kl_in_reward: false data.train_batch_size: 48 ``` The initial actor is a Qwen-family 9B SFT checkpoint. Each prompt has 8 rollouts (384 trajectories per training step). The task uses multi-turn tool calls and a result + format + efficiency reward with a maximum of 1.4. The context limit is 65,536 input tokens and the per-turn generation limit is 4,096 tokens. Run the training for approximately 150 global steps and monitor `actor/entropy`, `actor/grad_norm`, `rollout_corr/kl`, `train/reward/overall_mean`, `val/reward/overall_mean`, `response_length/mean`, and per-question-type `result_mean` / `completed_ratio`. The repository pins `vllm==0.24.0`, but I have not yet verified the version installed in the training image. ### Expected behavior Entropy and reward may fluctuate during RL training, but the actor should continue producing valid multi-turn tool-use trajectories. We would not expect a sudden transition where entropy spikes, mean response length falls from thousands of tokens to approximately 160–250 tokens, all question types have zero result reward and completion rate, and training/validation reward collapse without recovery.

items.title: perf(kvcache-v2): default to copy engine on coherent NVLink-C2C, adds opt-in SM kernel fallback
items.author: Asthenia0412
items.summary: After the first few host-tier offloads, every decode step becomes persistently ~1.2ms slower (~7%) once CUDA-graph replay starts. The copy engine (cuMemcpyBatchAsync) path is immune to this regression while producing byte-identical output.
items.body:
## Background

On SM107 (Grace-Hopper) with NVLink-C2C (coherent CPU-GPU link), KVCacheManagerV2::BatchedPageCopier always chose the SM copy kernel for GPU<->host-tier page transfers. After the first few host-tier offloads, every decode step becomes persistently ~1.2ms slower (~7%) once CUDA-graph replay starts.

## Problem

Profiling shows the SM copy kernel leaves large idle gaps between CUDA-graph kernel boundaries: replay gaps grow from ~406us to ~1335us per step on the same decode graph. The copy engine (cuMemcpyBatchAsync) path is immune to this regression while producing byte-identical output.

The kernel-selection decision was:

```cpp
bool const kernelViable = mTopology.coherentLink || HostMem::shouldUseChunkedRegistration();
```

This forced the SM kernel on **any** coherent link regardless of graph-replay behaviour. PCIe already used the copy engine, so coherent links were the only class affected.

## Solution

1. Refactored kernel-selection logic into `selectKernelViable()` — a clean two-reason decision tree:
   - `TRTLLM_KV_CACHE_FORCE_SM_COPY=1` → SM kernel (opt-in escape hatch).
   - `HostMem::shouldUseChunkedRegistration()` → SM kernel (copy-engine descriptors cannot cross a registration boundary; the kernel works on contiguous virtual addresses).
   - **Otherwise → copy engine** (default for both PCIe and coherent NVLink-C2C).

2. Added env var `TRTLLM_KV_CACHE_FORCE_SM_COPY` so operators can force the SM kernel back on for A/B perf comparisons or for environments where `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` is unavailable.

3. Preserved chunked-registration correctness:

```cpp
bool const kernelViable = selectKernelViable(mTopology.coherentLink);
```

4. Added INFO-level startup logging so operators can see which path was chosen and why.

5. Added gtest coverage in `kvCacheManagerV2BatchedPageCopierTest.cu` covering path-selection invariants, topology observability, D2H/H2D byte-exact round-trip correctness, and zero-pair no-op smoke test.

## Files changed

- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kv_cache_manager_v2/batchedPageCopy.cu`: `selectKernelViable()`, env var, `computeConfigs()` rewrite
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kv_cache_manager_v2/batchedPageCopy.h`: updated class doc, `KernelConfig::useKernel` doc
- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2BatchedPageCopierTest.cu`: new gtest (~316 lines, 6 test cases)
- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/CMakeLists.txt`: new test target

## Testing

- [x] Path selection logic refactored into `selectKernelViable()` with doc comment
- [x] `TRTLLM_KV_CACHE_FORCE_SM_COPY` env var added (lazy-static, `common::getBoolEnv`)
- [x] Coherent NVLink-C2C + non-chunked registration → **copy engine** (default, was SM kernel)
- [x] PCIe + non-chunked registration → copy engine (unchanged)
- [x] Chunked registration → SM kernel (unchanged, correctness invariant)
- [x] `FORCE_SM_COPY=1` overrides both → SM kernel
- [x] D2H round-trip byte-exact
- [x] H2D round-trip byte-exact
- [ ] Benchmark: decode step time with/without host offloads — CI runner will wire

Fixes: #20363

cc @lowsfer @tzulingk

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Dev Engineer Review

`BatchedPageCopier` now uses the copy engine by default for PCIe and coherent NVLink-C2C. `TRTLLM_KV_CACHE_FORCE_SM_COPY=1` or chunked host registration selects the SM kernel. The change also adds path-selection logging and updates the public class documentation. No exported API declarations change.

The new round-trip tests have correctness risks: the D2H test writes its pattern through a host pointer to `cudaMalloc` memory, and the H2D test supplies a compact host allocation while setting `srcStride` to twice the page size. These can cause invalid host access and out-of-bounds reads. Review finding counts are unavailable.

It is not listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/`; verify and fix the host/device buffer initialization and stride before relying on the round-trip coverage.

items.title: [model, fsdp, cfg] feat: restore freeze_vision_tower and skip the dummy visual forward for frozen vision towers
items.author: richardChenzhihui
items.summary: is present in, the generated trainer YAMLs and the Ascend docs table, but no code consumes it: the implementation was dropped in the 0.8 engine refactor. Pre-0.8 froze the tower ( + ) and forced FSDP1.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`freeze_vision_tower` is present in `ActorConfig`, the generated trainer YAMLs and the Ascend docs table, but no code consumes it: the implementation was dropped in the 0.8 engine refactor. Pre-0.8 `fsdp_workers.py` froze the tower (`get_vl_model_vision_tower()` + `requires_grad_(False)`) and forced FSDP1 `use_orig_params=True`. Relates to #3496 (which added the dummy forward, fixing #3491) and #7833 (a closed, unmerged attempt to delete the dummy unconditionally).

This PR restores the option for the FSDP1/FSDP2 engines, as one rule. With `freeze_vision_tower=true`:

1. Freeze: `requires_grad_(False)` on the whole visual path in `FSDPEngine` — the tower plus sibling modules that also run only on images (Mllama's `multi_modal_projector`, MiniCPM-o's `resampler`; Qwen/GLM keep the projector inside the tower, so nothing changes there) — after model build and before LoRA/QAT/FSDP. Pre-0.8 froze after `get_peft_model`, which froze vision LoRA adapters along with the base; freezing first lets adapters attached later re-enable their own `requires_grad`, so vision LoRA adapters attached after the freeze remain trainable (and, because the tower then holds trainable params, keep the dummy forward — see below).
2. Unwrap: the tower is excluded from per-module FSDP wrapping — a class-name filter for FSDP1 (`get_fsdp_wrap_policy`), a module-identity filter for FSDP2 (`_select_fsdp2_wrap_targets`), and FSDP1's LoRA lambda policy also skips leaves inside the excluded tower. Its params join the root FSDP unit, which all-gathers uniformly on every forward entry. FSDP1 keeps `use_orig_params=True` when excluding, as pre-0.8 did; the flat-parameter mode does not support a root unit with mixed `requires_grad`.
3. Skip: the four multimodal adapters (`qwen3_5`, `qwen3_vl`, `qwen2_vl`, `glm4v`) skip the dummy visual forward on text-only batches, but only when the engine has marked the tower with `_verl_frozen_vision_tower` and no trainable params remain in the visual path.

The marker, not `requires_grad`, is the skip criterion, and only a tower with no trainable params inside is marked. Two non-skipping cases:

- **Language-only LoRA.** PEFT's `_mark_only_adapters_as_trainable` clears `requires_grad` on the whole non-adapter model for every LoRA run, including language-only `target_modules`; there the tower stays per-module wrapped and still needs the dummy to keep cross-rank vision-tower entry counts aligned (#3491). A `requires_grad` check would skip the dummy in these runs and hang mixed-modality batches; the CPU tests pin that the dummy is kept there.
- **Trainable params in the visual path (vision LoRA, QAT linears, a trained projector).** With the tower wrap-excluded into the root FSDP unit, a text-only rank never enters it while an image rank does, so a trainable param inside would receive gradients on some ranks only — FSDP1's root-unit gradient reduce does not support that (verified with a 2-rank mixed-modality probe on torch 2.11: the backward hangs). Such towers keep the dummy forward, which makes every rank enter the tower once.

The engine sets the marker only on paths that also guarantee the exclusion. Paths that cannot guarantee it never mark and keep the dummy forward: the size-based FSDP1 wrap policy (`min_num_params > 0`), `strategy=fsdp_turbo` (freeze applies, exclusion not implemented), and freezing done outside the engine — each warns.

Skipping is safe for both purposes the dummy forward serves (#3496, fixing #3491) when nothing inside the tower trains: frozen params collect no gradients, and with the tower in the root unit there is no per-module all-gather to keep aligned. Mixed image+text batches work without the dummy: image ranks run the frozen tower as a fixed feature extractor, text ranks skip it, and language-model gradients still flow through image embedding positions.

Config plumbing mirrors `use_remove_padding`. `actor.freeze_vision_tower` reaches the engine config for both the actor and the ref; the ref section mirrors the actor flag because pre-0.8 froze them together. `critic.freeze_vision_tower` is plumbed in `trainer_base.py` and in the legacy `RayPPOTrainer` critic path. SFT-style trainers set the engine-level key directly. Engines without the field (megatron/torchtitan/veomni) ignore the flag with a warning. The default is `false`; behavior without the flag is unchanged.

items.title: [#20379][perf] trtllm-gen FMHA: split the KV partials of a row across thread groups in fmhaReductionKernel
items.author: lucifer1004
items.summary: merges the multi-CTA-KV partials of each output row in one thread, serially over all partials. At low batch its grid is only a few CTAs, so the kernel costs a fixed several microseconds per attention call.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #20379.

`fmhaReductionKernel` merges the multi-CTA-KV partials of each output row in one thread, serially over all `numCtasKv` partials. At low batch its grid is only a few CTAs, so the kernel costs a fixed several microseconds per attention call.

This PR adds a `KvSplit` template parameter:

- The 512 threads form `KvSplit` groups. Group g runs the existing online-softmax merge over partials g, g + KvSplit, ... of the same rows. Group 0 then combines the per-group (max, sum, O) through shared memory, rescaling each by `exp2(scaleLog2 * (groupMax - max))` and skipping empty groups. Sinks, softmax-stats export and the store are unchanged and done by group 0.
- In the unrolled loads, a slot past the end re-reads the group's current partial with weight 0, so the running max never moves without rescaling.
- Each CTA covers `1/KvSplit` of the rows (`NumBytePerSlice` is per group), so the host launches `KvSplit` times more slices. `TLLM_FMHA_REDUCTION_KV_SPLIT=<2|4|8|16>` is an upper bound, and the host halves it until every group holds at least one whole row and the slices still fit the existing `2 x SMs / grid` CTA budget. Unset or 1 selects `KvSplit = 1`, which runs the same per-thread loop as before.
- Static shared memory for the merge is 20 KB per CTA, and only for `KvSplit > 1`.

Measured on SM107 with Kimi K3 MLA decode (grouped Q64 kernels, batch 1): per-call time -1.9 / -7.3 / -7.4 / -6.5 us at 2K / 8K / 32K / 128K with KvSplit 8, and an end-to-end decode step of -0.10 / -0.23 / -0.21 ms at 2K / 32K / 128K (details in #20379). It is opt-in for now because SM100 / SM103 are not measured.

## Test Coverage

- No existing unit test calls `runFmhaReduction` directly. With the variable unset the launch is `KvSplit = 1`, the same per-thread loop as before.
- Validated on SM107 (equivalent change): output sums and absolute sums for KvSplit 2/4/8/16 match KvSplit 1 to ~1e-5 at batch 1/2/4 in a `TllmGenFmhaRunner` microbenchmark; end-to-end accuracy unchanged with KvSplit 8.
- This branch: `nvcc -arch=sm_100a` compile of `fmhaReduction.cu` and pre-commit clean. Not yet run on a GPU; SM100 / SM103 not run. Happy to add a dedicated reduction test with synthetic partials if reviewers want one.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] PR follows the [TRT-LLM coding guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of my knowledge.
- [x] Test cases are provided for new code paths.
- [x] No API changes, no new dependencies, no CODEOWNERS changes.
- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

items.title: [#20373][perf] DFlash TRTLLM: run non-causal unwindowed block attention as decode rows up to batch 32
items.author: lucifer1004
items.summary: For a non-causal, unwindowed DFlash draft layer on the TRTLLM backend, called. At small batch that kernel has very little parallelism over a long context.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #20373.

For a non-causal, unwindowed DFlash draft layer on the TRTLLM backend, `dflash_forward` called `trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache`. At small batch that kernel has very little parallelism over a long context. Without a mask, every block query attends the same `seq_lens_after` keys, so this PR runs the attention as `B * block_size` single-token `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` requests over the request's pages (`q_len_per_req=1`, page table and sequence lengths repeated per block query). That gives multi-CTA split-KV over the context.

- `_NONCAUSAL_DECODE_ROWS_MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 32`: the decode-row form is used only when the draft batch is at most this size. Each row reads the whole KV, so the form reads `block_size` times more KV; at small batch the context kernel launches few CTAs, so the rows still win. Kernel-level sweeps have the rows ahead at every batch measured, B = 1..32 on SM107 and B = 1..256 on SM100, at 32K and 128K KV (numbers in the comments below); 32 is the largest batch measured on both. Above the limit the context-FMHA call is unchanged.
- `_prepare_dflash_trtllm_gen_buffers` sizes the workspace and the multi-CTA KV counter buffer for `max(max_batch_size, min(max_batch_size, limit) * block_size)` requests, so the limit also bounds those buffers (at most `32 * block_size` requests for the row form).
- Causal layers and sliding-window layers are unchanged. `validate_block_attention_windows` still rejects non-causal windows on TRTLLM.
- The batch size is static inside a captured CUDA graph, so the branch is fixed per graph. The repeated page table / sequence lengths are built once per forward and shared by all layers.

Kimi K3 + GQA DSpark drafter (block size 7), 8 GPUs, SM107, batch 1: decode step -0.15 ms at 2K context, -1.05 ms at 32K, -2.21 ms at 64K, -3.12 ms at 96K and -4.21 ms at 128K. Acceptance and our accuracy checks were unchanged (details in #20373). Batch > 1 is measured at kernel level only.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_kimi_k3_dspark_semantics.py::test_plain_dflash_trtllm_block_decode_matches_full_attention_reference` (new, added to `l0_b200.yml`): a plain non-causal DFlash drafter on the TRTLLM backend with a paged cache (two pages, disjoint page ranges per request, unequal context lengths). It checks against the existing eager full-attention reference with decode rows at batch 1, 2 and 32 (the ceiling), and with the context FMHA at batch 33 and at batch 2 (ceiling lowered to 1 in the test). It also counts the kernel calls, so a silent fallback to the other form fails. Parity is checked as relative L2 error < 1e-2 and max abs difference <= 8 bf16 ulp at the largest expected magnitude. Skipped without flashinfer or without an SM100-family GPU.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/modeling/test_modeling_speculative.py::test_dflash_trtllm_gen_buffers_cover_noncausal_decode_rows` (new, CPU): checks the request count passed to the workspace and counter sizing below, at and above the ceiling.
- `test_dflash_trtllm_gen_buffers_reject_capture_time_allocation` (existing): its second call now grows the batch to 16 instead of 4. With block size 4 the first version of this PR sized batch 2 and batch 4 both for 4 requests, so the workspace did not grow and the expected capture-time error never fired (the index-buffer check raised instead).
- Results at 13cbe4661c (branch diff applied on a build from an earlier main, single node each), on SM107 and on SM100 (GB200): GPU `-k trtllm_block_decode` 3/3 passed, CPU `-k dflash_trtllm_gen_buffers` 7/7 passed. items.title: [#20371][perf] Fuse the Kimi K3 attention-residual epilogue up to 32 tokens by default
items.author: lucifer1004
items.summary: Under the default topology the fused attention-residual epilogue was taken only for one token per rank, so speculative verify steps and multi-request decode batches ran the unfused add + + RMSNorm chain at every layer. This PR defaults to 32 for every to…
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #20371.

Under the default `per_token` topology the fused attention-residual epilogue (`attn_res_add_rmsnorm_fwd`, `attn_res_rmsnorm_fwd`) was taken only for one token per rank, so speculative verify steps and multi-request decode batches ran the unfused add + `attn_res_fwd` + RMSNorm chain at every layer. This PR defaults `KIMI_K3_FUSED_ATTN_RES_MAX_TOKENS` to 32 for every topology (it already was 32 for `split` / `persistent`, and 32 is the top of the measured window documented in the dispatch code). The per-token kernels themselves are unchanged; `KIMI_K3_FUSED_ATTN_RES=0` still selects the unfused path and the variable still overrides the ceiling.

Numerics: the updated prefix is bit-identical; the normalized output moves by a few bf16 ulps, exactly as for M = 1 decode, which already runs the fused kernel by default (#19182 notes that default numerical-path change).

Measured on SM107 only, with the original `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` checkpoint, whose routed experts TRT-LLM runs as W4A8_MXFP4_MXFP8 (details in #20371): the fused ops take about half the time of the unfused chain at M = 8 / 16, and the Kimi K3 + DSpark decode step is about 0.5 ms faster at 2K-128K context with a single request (M = 8 per rank) and 0.49-0.57 ms (about 3%) faster with 2 / 4 concurrent requests (M = 16 / 32 per rank) at 2K and 32K, with unchanged acceptance and accuracy checks. Not measured: SM100 / SM103 performance, and the NVFP4 checkpoint.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/modules/kimi_k3_attn_res/test_attn_res_rmsnorm_op.py` (in `l0_b200.yml` and `l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml`): new `test_default_token_ceiling_covers_multi_token_steps` checks the default ceiling, and `test_model_helper_dispatches_fused_attn_res_rmsnorm` gains `default_ceiling` cases (1 / 16 / 32 tokens, variable unset, `per_token`) that assert the fused op runs; the existing fused-dispatch tests at 1 / 16 / 32 tokens and the fallback tests above the ceiling (`_above_ceiling_tokens()`, now 33) keep covering both sides. Updated the comment that described the old default.
- Validated end to end on SM107 (W4A8_MXFP4_MXFP8 routed experts): with the variable set to 32 at M = 8 (see #20371), and as an A/B of the variable at 1 vs 32 with M = 16 / 32 (see the PR comments). The test file passed on SM107 at 5a64ea2cc0 (44 passed, 1 existing skip; branch diff applied on a build from an earlier main); 84ccbf47cb only rewords a docstring and folds the three identical parametrized default-ceiling checks into one. SM100/SM103: not run.
- pre-commit on the changed files: clean.

- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] PR follows the [TRT-LLM coding guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of my knowledge.

items.title: Add configurable weight decay for RMSNorm gamma
items.author: mkhona-nvidia
items.summary: RMSNorm gamma currently inherits the generic weight-decay exemption for one-dimensional parameters. Add and to apply a configurable multiple of scheduled global weight decay specifically to gamma.
items.body:
RMSNorm gamma currently inherits the generic weight-decay exemption for one-dimensional parameters. Add `OptimizerConfig.rmsnorm_weight_decay_mult` and `--rmsnorm-weight-decay-mult` to apply a configurable multiple of scheduled global weight decay specifically to gamma.

For example, `--weight-decay 0.1 --rmsnorm-weight-decay-mult 0.5` applies weight decay of `0.05` to RMSNorm gamma. Leaving the multiplier unset preserves current behavior; `1.0` applies full decay and `0.0` explicitly disables it. Explicit values take precedence over `apply_wd_to_qk_layernorm` for RMSNorm gamma only.

Mark gamma in PyTorch, Transformer Engine (including `TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear.layer_norm_weight` and fused residual norms), ModelOpt, and gated Mamba/GDP norm constructors. The existing `wd_mult` scheduler mechanism keeps the multiplier tied to global scheduled decay. Other parameters retain their current policies. Document custom norm tagging and stored-parameter semantics for zero-centered gamma.

Validation: `tools/autoformat.sh` passed Black, isort, Pylint, and Ruff. The new CLI argument block also passes Black. The script's non-blocking mypy step reported type errors and missing GPU dependency stubs in the touched modules; type checking is not claimed clean. Added unit coverage for selection, Q/K precedence, validation, CLI parsing, scheduled AdamW updates, and standalone/fused TE gamma tagging. Registered determinism tests cover PyTorch and TE norm gamma tagging, gated Mamba/GDP norm replay, and fused Adam parameters/moments with unset, zero, half, and full RMSNorm decay. The kernel determinism coverage gate passes locally without an exemption label. Runtime/CUDA tests were not run locally.

items.title: [#20369][fix] Reject prompt token ids outside the vocabulary before submission
items.author: lucifer1004
items.summary: A prompt token id or reaches the embedding lookup, and an unmasked gather turns it into a device-side assert that leaves the CUDA context unusable, so one request takes the whole server down (#20369 has a real case through the tokenizer). only checked the prom…
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #20369.

A prompt token id `>= vocab_size` or `< 0` reaches the embedding lookup, and an unmasked gather turns it into a device-side assert that leaves the CUDA context unusable, so one request takes the whole server down (#20369 has a real case through the tokenizer). `BaseLLM.generate_async()` only checked the prompt length, and `LLM.encode()` did not check the ids at all.

This PR adds `_check_prompt_token_id_range()` next to `_check_arguments()` and calls it from both `generate_async()` and `encode()`:

- negative ids are always rejected;
- ids `>= vocab_size` are rejected unless the request carries multimodal content that replaces prompt ids (a `multimodal_input` or any `multimodal_data` other than `mrope_config`), uses a prompt adapter, or is a generation-only (disaggregated) request, because those legitimately use out-of-vocabulary placeholder ids (`filter_mm_token_from_input_ids()` treats `>= vocab_size` as multimodal tokens when a model has no `mm_token_ids`; p-tuning uses ids past the vocabulary; a generation-only worker receives the context worker's expanded prompt);
- encoder input ids of text encoder-decoder models (from `_preprocess` or `PreprocessedInputs`) get the same check (only a prompt adapter exempts them);
- in `encode()`, every prompt in the batch is checked before the forward pass; only `inputs_embeds` lifts the upper bound (the ids are then not looked up), negative ids are still rejected;
- `vocab_size` is read from `text_config` when present, else from the HF config; when neither has one, only the sign is checked.

The error is a `RequestError`, which `trtllm-serve` already returns as HTTP 400, and the LLM API raises to the caller. On the generation path it covers text prompts, token-id prompts (`/v1/completions`, `prompt_token_ids` / `prompt_token_ids_b64`) and `PreprocessedInputs` alike; `encode()` covers its text and token-id inputs. Lists, NumPy arrays and tensors are accepted; the cost is one min/max pass over the prompt.

Known limits: multimodal requests with replacement content are not range-checked above the vocabulary (their placeholder convention is model specific), and a model whose embedding has rows past `vocab_size` that text-only prompts may use would now get a 400 for those ids (I found none in the PyTorch backend besides Mllama's 8 extra image-token rows, which text-only prompts should not contain). To make such a mismatch easy to spot, the `vocab_size` used for the check is logged at startup and the error message says it comes from the model config. Checking against the real embedding size, or an opt-out, is left for a follow-up: the frontend reads the config before the worker loads weights.

## Release note

Prompt token ids that are negative or `>= vocab_size` (from the model config) are now rejected with a `RequestError` (HTTP 400 in `trtllm-serve`) in `generate()` / `generate_async()` and `encode()`, instead of reaching the embedding lookup. The exemptions above (replacement multimodal content, prompt adapters, generation-only requests, `inputs_embeds` in `encode()`) still allow out-of-vocabulary placeholder ids.

## Test Coverage

- New `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_prompt_token_id_range.py` (CPU only), registered in `l0_cpu.yml`: in-range lists / NumPy / torch prompts pass; an id equal to `vocab_size` and a negative id are rejected for all three types; negative ids are rejected even when out-of-vocabulary ids are allowed; placeholders pass when allowed; unknown vocabulary size and empty prompts; `_prompt_vocab_size()` reads `text_config` first and ignores missing / zero values; only replacing multimodal content (not mRoPE-only metadata) counts as an exemption; and `BaseLLM.generate_async` with `PreprocessedInputs` and a stub executor raises `RequestError` without submitting for out-of-vocab, negative (also generation-only), mRoPE-only and encoder-id cases and for raw text / raw token-id prompts whose preprocessing yields an out-of-vocab id, and submits in-range, generation-only, multimodal-embedding and prompt-adapter cases; `LLM.encode()` with a stub encoder rejects single and batched prompts with an out-of-vocab or negative id before `batch_forward`, and forwards in-range and `inputs_embeds` batches. The generation and encode tests run the real `BaseLLM` methods on an instance built with `BaseLLM.__new__`, replacing only the parts that need a loaded model.
- The crash itself was observed in our deployment through the tokenizer case in #20369; the token-id path is inferred from code and was not run against a live server.
- The new test file passed 35/35 at 1a8309ce3f (branch diff applied on a build from an earlier main; see the test report comment). At 206795d9bb (`encode()` check, logging, `BaseLLM`-based test stubs) the file passes 40/40, including the 5 new `encode()` cases (branch diff applied on the same earlier-main build; without the diff the file fails at import as expected).
- pre-commit on the changed files: clean.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR follows the [TRT-LLM coding guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of my knowledge.
- [x] Test cases are provided for new code paths.
- [x] No public API signature changes, no new dependencies, no CODEOWNERS changes.
- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

items.author: lucifer1004

items.body:
## Description

Fixes #20367.

`ChatCompletionRequest` is `extra="forbid"`, so a request carrying OpenAI's standard `prompt_cache_key` field was rejected with HTTP 400 (`extra_forbidden`). This PR adds the field as `Optional[str] = None`, accepted and otherwise ignored, like `user` and `parallel_tool_calls`: KV cache reuse needs no client hint, and `cache_salt` remains the field that isolates cached prefixes. `ResponsesRequest` already accepts the field through `extra="allow"`.

Other unknown fields are still rejected, and non-string values of `prompt_cache_key` fail validation.

- `tensorrt_llm/serve/openai_protocol.py`: new field on `ChatCompletionRequest`.
- `tests/unittest/api_stability/references/trtllm_serve_api.yaml`: the matching reference row (`kind: openai`, `status: stable`).

## Test Coverage

- New `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_openai_protocol_prompt_cache_key.py` (CPU only), registered in `l0_cpu.yml`: accepted as keyword and from JSON, default `None`, non-string values rejected, other fields unchanged by it, unknown fields still rejected.
- `tests/unittest/api_stability/test_serve_api.py` covers the reference row.
- An equivalent change (with a stricter variant of these tests) passed our CPU test run of the serve unit tests; this branch's new test file has not been run yet (no local environment with the package built); I will report the result here.
- pre-commit on the changed files: clean.

items.title: [#20365][fix] Use the fused DSpark RMSNorm/RoPE kernels on SM107
items.author: lucifer1004
items.summary: gated on, the SM100/SM103 table of the DSV4 DSpark attention kernel, so on SM107 the MLA-backboned DSpark drafter always fell back to the eager RMSNorm/RoPE chain, although the ops' own error messages list SM107. The RMSNorm/RoPE kernels are plain SIMT CuTe k…
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #20365.

`is_fused_dspark_rmsnorm_rope_supported()` gated on `_get_dspark_arch_str()`, the SM100/SM103 table of the DSV4 DSpark attention kernel, so on SM107 the MLA-backboned DSpark drafter always fell back to the eager RMSNorm/RoPE chain, although the ops' own error messages list SM107.

The RMSNorm/RoPE kernels are plain SIMT CuTe kernels, so this PR gives them their own architecture set, `_DSPARK_RMSNORM_ROPE_SM_VERSIONS = {100, 103, 107}`, checked by `_is_dspark_rmsnorm_rope_sm_supported()`. `_get_dspark_arch_str()` and every DSV4 DSpark attention gate are unchanged, so the tcgen05 attention kernel stays SM100/SM103-only; its attention-preparation ops (`*_cache_write`, `*_draft_block`) are only reached when the attention gate also passes.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/test_dspark_cute_dsl_rmsnorm_rope.py`: the module now also runs on SM107, and the new `test_fused_dspark_rmsnorm_rope_supported_architectures` checks the architecture set and that `_get_dspark_arch_str(107)` stays `None`. The file is in `l0_b200.yml`, so the new test runs there; there is no SM107 test list to add it to.
- Validated on SM107 with an equivalent patch: the three drafter call shapes (H = 8 / 16, N = 1 / 3 / 8) match the eager chain bit for bit, and Kimi K3 + DSpark decode is ~0.3 ms/step (~2%) faster. The updated test file passed 21/21 on SM107 (branch diff applied on a build from an earlier main; see the test report comment).
- SM100/SM103: behaviour unchanged (same set membership); not re-run.
- pre-commit on the changed files: clean.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes the rendering of the "Formal derivation" in §3.2.2 *Policy Gradient Loss (with IS/RS Correction)* of [`docs/algo/rollout_corr_math.md`](https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/algo/rollout_corr_math.html#policy-gradient-loss-with-is-rs-correction).

In steps 2–4, each `$$ … $$` block starts on the line right after the list item's text, with no blank line in between. MyST therefore parses it as inline double-dollar math within the paragraph, and the rendered page shows stray `$` signs around the equations (for example `$\( J(\theta) = … \)$`). This PR adds a blank line before each of the three blocks so they render as display math.

items.title: [#20363][perf] Prefer the copy engine for KVCM2 host-tier copies on coherent links
items.author: lucifer1004
items.summary: (#18541) moves KVCacheManagerV2 pages between GPU and the host tier with an SM copy kernel on coherent (NVLink-C2C) links and with on PCIe. This PR makes the copy engine the default on coherent links as well; the kernel stays available through, and chunked ho…
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #20363.

`BatchedPageCopier` (#18541) moves KVCacheManagerV2 pages between GPU and the host tier with an SM copy kernel on coherent (NVLink-C2C) links and with `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` on PCIe. This PR makes the copy engine the default on coherent links as well; the kernel stays available through `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_COHERENT_COPY_KERNEL=1`, and chunked host registration still forces the kernel as before.

Why (details and data in #20363):

- After the SM kernel has accessed registered host memory a few times, every later kernel boundary in the process (including CUDA graph replays) gets slower on our SM107 + NVLink-C2C system: +1.2 ms (~7%) per decode step for Kimi K3 on 8 GPUs, persistent for the rest of the process. The copy engine path in the same binary removes it with token-identical outputs; forcing the kernel back on in that binary brings it back.
- #20311 measured on NVLink-C2C that the copy engines match or slightly beat the kernel on an idle GPU and are 1.2-4x faster when the SMs are busy (the kernel's CTAs wait for resident blocks), and listed this switch as the natural follow-up.
- Cost measured: a fully host-resident 393K-token prefix reload (~13 GB per rank) takes ~0.19 s (~9%) longer TTFT.

Changes:

- `batchedPageCopy.cu`: `computeConfigs()` selects the path through `detail::selectCopyKernel(coherentLink, chunkedRegistration, kernelOnCoherentLink)`; the opt-in is read from the environment when the copier is constructed. The selected path is logged at DEBUG.
- `batchedPageCopy.h`: declares `detail::kCoherentCopyKernelEnv` and `detail::selectCopyKernel()`, and updates the class comment.

No behaviour change on PCIe or with chunked host registration. With the copy engine selected, `pageIndexLocation()` reports `kHost`, which the cold-page codec and the storage manager already handle (it is the PCIe path today).

## Test Coverage

New cases in `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2ColdPageCopyTest.cu`:

- `CopyEngineIsDefaultOnEveryLink`, `CopyKernelOptInAppliesOnlyToCoherentLinks`, `ChunkedRegistrationAlwaysSelectsCopyKernel`: the selection truth table.
- `CoherentCopyKernelEnv/BatchedPageCopierPathTest.SelectsPathAndRoundTripsPages/{Unset,Value0,Value1}`: constructs a copier on GPU 0 with the variable unset / `0` / `1`, checks `kernelEnabled()`, both `KernelConfig::useKernel` and `pageIndexLocation()` against the expected selection for the detected topology, then offloads 8 pages to mapped pinned host memory and onboards them back through two permutations and checks the bytes. On a coherent system this exercises both paths; on PCIe both instances use the copy engine.

Validation:

- End-to-end (an equivalent patch on our build): SM107 with NVLink-C2C, Kimi K3, 8 GPUs / 2 nodes, KVCM2 C++ backend with host tier: decode step without the persistent +1.2 ms, 99/99 outputs identical; forcing the kernel through the variable reproduces the slowdown.
- The new gtest file compiles with nvcc 13.4 (`-std=c++20`). On SM107 (coherent link, branch diff applied on a build from an earlier main) it passed 6/6; not run on a PCIe machine yet.
- Not validated on GB200/GB300 (SM100/SM103) or GH200; the change only affects coherent links.
- pre-commit on the changed files: clean.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] PR follows the [TRT-LLM coding guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of my knowledge.
- [x] Test cases are provided for new code paths.
- [x] No API changes, no new dependencies, no CODEOWNERS changes.
- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

The three should probably converge on one; I'd like the maintainers to pick the direction.

What we measured on SM107 with a coherent NVLink-C2C link (Kimi K3, 8 GPUs over 2 nodes, KVCacheManagerV2 with the host tier on, details in #20363):

- With the SM copy kernel, once pages start going to the host tier every decode step becomes slower by a fixed amount for the rest of the process: +7.0% at a 2K prompt, about +4% at 393K, and +13.5% in a configuration with more kernels per step. In the profile no kernel gets slower; the idle gaps between kernels inside the CUDA graph replay grow. With the copy engine there is no such step (noise level), and outputs are token-identical. Forcing the kernel back on in the copy-engine build brings the step back.
- The cost of the copy engine we saw: reloading a fully host-resident 393K-token prefix takes about 9% longer TTFT than with the kernel.

The trade-off as I see it:

- **Default on (this PR, #20383):** coherent deployments that offload to the host tier do not get the decode slowdown. It is silent and persistent, so users are unlikely to find the knob. The price is the slower bulk reload above, and possibly the higher kernel ceiling on wide links (GH200, #18541).
- **Opt-in (#20426):** keeps today's behavior and the wide-link kernel bandwidth, and needs no new GH200 data. But it leaves the decode regression in place by default on systems like ours. We have not identified its mechanism, so we cannot say whether GB300 or GH200 show it.

If you prefer #20426, I'm happy to close this PR and add our SM107 numbers (and a run with its variable set) there. If the default should change, this PR is ready for review. It has been tested on SM107: the new gtest passed 6/6, and both the default path and the opt-in kernel path were exercised.

items.summary: It now wraps the capture pass of the new in. still monkeypatches the old name, so both parametrizations fail on any branch that contains #20246: It hit in L0 #64229 (PR #20250).
items.body:
## Description

#20246 removed `moe_a2a_steady_state_budget_for_capture` from `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/engine/runners/decoder/runner.py`. It now wraps the capture pass of the new `_warmup_and_capture_cuda_graphs` in `moe_comm_serving_timeouts()`. `tests/unittest/_torch/compilation/test_phase_selective_forward.py::test_decoder_runner_warmup_bypasses_only_auxiliary_phases` still monkeypatches the old name, so both parametrizations fail on any branch that contains #20246:

```
unittest/_torch/compilation/test_phase_selective_forward.py:266: in test_decoder_runner_warmup_bypasses_only_auxiliary_phases
    monkeypatch.setattr(
E   AttributeError: <module 'tensorrt_llm._torch.pyexecutor.engine.runners.decoder.runner' ...> has no attribute 'moe_a2a_steady_state_budget_for_capture'
```

It hit `CPU-Generic-arm-1` in L0 #64229 (PR #20250). That test is in `l0_cpu.yml`, `l0_h100.yml` and `l0_b200.yml`.

This PR patches `moe_comm_serving_timeouts` instead, with the same `contextlib.nullcontext` stand-in. The test's purpose is unchanged: it checks which warmup phases run eagerly and which compiled, and the timeout context is just scaffolding.

- The other six tests in the file passed in the same CI run and don't touch this name.

items.title: DistributedOptimizer: detach quantized params before building fp32 main-param shards
items.author: linmuchuiyang
items.summary: The default optimizer path assigns directly and never validates this, but rebuilds its sub-optimizers through, whose rejects it: #6212 / #6982 fixed the same pattern for native fp32 params ( → ). The quantized branch a few lines below still lacks the; th…
items.body:
## Problem

In `DistributedOptimizer._build_model_and_main_param_groups`, the fp32 main-param shard for a **quantized** model parameter that has no `get_high_precision_init_val()` is built as

```python
shard_main_param = model_param.float().view(-1)[param_range.start : param_range.end]
```

`model_param` requires grad, so `.float()` records a grad_fn and the shard (and its slice) is a **non-leaf** tensor. The default optimizer path assigns `param_groups` directly and never validates this, but `HybridDeviceOptimizer` (`--optimizer-cpu-offload`) rebuilds its sub-optimizers through `torch.optim.Optimizer.__init__`, whose `add_param_group` rejects it:

```text
File ".../megatron/core/optimizer/cpu_offloading/hybrid_optimizer.py", line 57, in __init__
    super(HybridDeviceOptimizer, self).__init__(
File ".../torch/optim/optimizer.py", line 408, in __init__
    self.add_param_group(cast(dict, param_group))
ValueError: can't optimize a non-leaf Tensor
```

#6212 / #6982 fixed the same pattern for native fp32 params (`model_param.view(-1)[...]` → `model_param.detach().view(-1)[...]`). The quantized branch a few lines below still lacks the `detach()`; this PR applies the identical change there. The master copy never needs autograd history (grads are copied into it manually), and for a quantized tensor `.float()` already materializes a new fp32 tensor, so detaching changes nothing else.

## How it was hit

verl GRPO on **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (FP8 attention + MXFP4 routed experts loaded through Megatron-Bridge, bf16 training, `optimizer_cpu_offload=True`, non-precision-aware optimizer) failed at optimizer construction on every rank with the trace above (Megatron-LM `fd1121b8`, July 2026). Wrapping `_build_model_and_main_param_groups` in `torch.no_grad()` from the training script was the workaround we have been carrying since; the same shim is in our DeepSeek-V4-Pro GRPO recipe on H100 (64 nodes). With `--use-precision-aware-optimizer` the branch is skipped, which is why precision-aware runs do not see it.

## Change

One statement in `megatron/core/optimizer/distrib_optimizer.py`: `model_param.detach().float().view(-1)[...]` in the quantized `else` branch, plus a comment. No behavior change for the `get_high_precision_init_val()` path or the non-quantized path.

## Testing

- `python -m py_compile` on the file.
- The non-leaf failure reproduces with any quantized param + `optimizer_cpu_offload=True` without `use_precision_aware_optimizer`; with the `no_grad` workaround (functionally equivalent to this detach) the DeepSeek-V4 GRPO runs train normally (log-prob Pearson 0.994–0.995 between rollout and actor over 5+ steps).

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6384589][fix] Reserve EPLB shared memory before writing host weights
items.author: fredricz-20070104
items.summary: Related to NVBug 6384589. This is a defensive shared-memory allocation fix, not a claim that the original incident has been reproduced or fully resolved. [Discussion: CodeRabbit will regenerate it on the next update, or you can request a refresh with.]
items.body:
## Description

Related to NVBug 6384589. This is a defensive shared-memory allocation fix, not a claim that the original incident has been reproduced or fully resolved.

`HostMoeTensorSharer.finalize_layer_weights` creates POSIX shared-memory mappings for EPLB host expert weights, then writes the payload. Creating a mapping only sets its file length; it does not reserve backing pages. A full tmpfs can consequently deliver SIGBUS during the copy instead of a catchable allocation failure.

### Changes

- Reserve each mapping's backing storage with `posix_fallocate` before exposing it as `own_shm` or writing tensors.
- Preserve the allocation errno and report requested bytes, currently available bytes, and filesystem capacity. Include the MoE layer and local rank in the loader exception.
- Close and unlink the newly created segment if creation/reservation fails, without publishing host-weight views into it.
- Copy directly into `torch.frombuffer` views rather than materializing an additional tensor-sized Python bytes object with `numpy().tobytes()`.
- Keep allocation failure handling local to the loader. Do not add per-layer MPI collectives: parallel module loading does not guarantee matching layer order across ranks.

### Scope and limitations

- No changes to benchmark configuration, EPLB enablement, expert count, Slurm topology, or container mount settings.
- No change to the steady-state EPLB host-weight footprint. A node with insufficient shared-memory capacity will still fail, now with an actionable Python exception rather than an unreserved-mapping SIGBUS.
- Reservation does not guarantee safety against host/cgroup OOM, external truncation, or unrelated file-mapping errors.
- Increasing tmpfs capacity requires validating the complete host/cgroup budget. File-backed fallback or reducing node-local expert storage needs separate architecture/performance validation; this PR does not silently enable either.
- Linux/POSIX shared memory is the target; unsupported reservation is reported rather than falling back to unsafe writes.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/test_mmap_utils.py`: real backing-page allocation; ENOSPC and unsupported-reservation diagnostics.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_load_balancer.py`: failed reservation cleanup, shared-memory creation failure, and bitwise weight/scalar-scale preservation for FP32, FP16, BF16, U8 and FP8 E4M3.
- Both existing test paths are already selected by `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`; new tests are marked `cpu_only`.
- Local isolated CPU validation: **14 passed**. Uses real POSIX shared memory and CPU PyTorch. The exact HostMoeTensorSharer class and new test functions are loaded via AST because this environment does not provide the complete TensorRT/MPI runtime. This is not a full package/runtime test.
- Submission-script regression suite: **82 passed** with the existing CPU-independent import fixtures.
- Local reproduction on an empty 64-MiB tmpfs, requesting 64 MiB + one page: unreserved write exits with **SIGBUS (-7)**; reservation instead returns **ENOSPC (28)**, with zero shared-memory bytes left after cleanup. This is not a GPU/cluster reproduction of the original incident.
- Repository pre-commit hooks: **passed** for all four modified files. Type-check hook had no matching files and was skipped.

### Before merge / incident closure

Run the unchanged affected disaggregated perf cases on the target cluster with this revision. Capture container-visible shared-memory capacity/usage and host/cgroup memory usage. If the new reservation reports ENOSPC, validate the capacity budget and rerun after an approved capacity/storage fix. Do not interpret this guard alone as evidence that the original perf case now passes or that the incident can be closed.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Description explains the scope and limitations.
- [x] Relevant CPU regression tests added to already-listed test paths.
- [x] No public LLM configuration fields or new runtime dependencies.
- [x] Repository pre-commit checks pass.
- Pending, not claimed by this PR: full GPU/runtime validation of the original affected cases.

items.title: Make fused pre-GDR gate backward gradients repeatable
items.author: Pinoeer-kingxi
items.summary: The existing fused pre-GDR backward accumulates and gradients with atomics and selects its tiling through timing-based autotuning. Fresh disabled-offload baselines reproduced low-bit gradient and Adam-state differences, so offload comparisons alone could not e…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

The existing fused pre-GDR backward accumulates `A_log` and `dt_bias` gradients with atomics and selects its tiling through timing-based autotuning. Fresh disabled-offload baselines reproduced low-bit gradient and Adam-state differences, so offload comparisons alone could not establish a repeatable baseline.

Use fixed 128×16 tiles to write independent FP32 partial sums, then reduce them on the existing stream. This changes existing fused backward execution even when activation offloading is disabled. It does not add an offload scope or enable full pre-GDR fusion under `deterministic_mode`.

The kernel replay test covers BF16/FP32 inputs, contiguous/strided upstream gradients, sequence tails, explicit side streams and five byte-exact replays under contention. It checks FP32 parameter gradients before the caller casts them to BF16, and separately compares numerical accuracy with Torch autograd. The kernel registry distinguishes gate backward from the still-exempt full fused path.

Validation for `9d54b8729c9277f1e032110c5e1b149e9654bcc5`, based on upstream `9131593673d037d360d252904f9198d36bc0c246`:

- Kernel manifest checks: 272 passed on CPU; these are registry checks, not GPU replay results.
- Standard Black/isort/Pylint/Ruff and kernel CI coverage checks pass; the four nonblocking mypy diagnostics match that pinned baseline.
- All 16 GPU replay/numerical cases passed on an A6000.
- The old-atomic versus fixed gate-backward wrapper benchmark ran with offload disabled on an A6000: batch={1,4}, sequence={2048,4096}, value heads={16,32}, head dimension 128, BF16. Each of eight shapes has three fresh processes and nine paired samples. Paired runtime medians improve by 5.9%–8.7%; extra allocated peak memory increases by 2–32 KiB. Inputs and the projection-gradient buffer are identical, calls are warmed, pair order alternates, and timing is synchronized. Raw sample ranges are retained; these are wrapper measurements, not end-to-end offload speedups.

[Current-head replay logs, raw benchmark samples, commands and verification](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/8c5cc72379de4e9ef8d80856973dd64f23cc0dac/gpu-20261016) identify both source revisions. [CPU/rebase evidence](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/251ae748bd5566fe57c15ba4e8431dfbd5483675/rebase-20261015) remains pinned separately. Local acceptance is complete; upstream GPU CI awaits vetter approval for this head.

## Issue tracking

Related to #6757. Split from #7908 following [the requested review boundaries](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7908#issuecomment-6182348264). This fix is independently applicable to `main`. #7908 preserves the upstream fused kernels and does not depend on this change; the earlier combined validation remains evidence for the original tested revisions.

items.title: Fix activation offload warmup and pooled transfer ordering
items.author: Pinoeer-kingxi
items.summary: Forward-only evaluation before training warmup can leave the activation-offload policy based on empty saves. Fraction zero can start copying when later microbatches grow, and chunk progression can advance before all forward groups have run.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Forward-only evaluation before training warmup can leave the activation-offload policy based on empty saves. Fraction zero can start copying when later microbatches grow, and chunk progression can advance before all forward groups have run. Separately, a fallback reload can read before D2H completes, and pooled D2H writes can overwrite a buffer still used by queued H2D.

Preserve warmup across forward-only schedules, keep fraction-zero groups resident, advance chunks by remaining forward groups, and order the existing transfer streams before reading or reusing pinned storage. This PR changes the shared manager and its three native schedule call sites; it adds no GDN scope or numerical kernel change.

Tests cover explicit phase/process-group routing, growing saved tensors at fractions zero and one, delayed D2H, and pooled H2D buffer reuse. The generic tests use the existing `core_attn` scope. The fraction policy applies after warmup; warmup can still copy eligible tensors to collect size statistics.

Validation for `af9569270f476dc201484296315a9c30dcaa3feb`, based on upstream `9131593673d037d360d252904f9198d36bc0c246`:

- CPU phase/group-routing tests: 5 passed. These tests do not qualify GPU transfer behavior.
- Standard Black/isort/Pylint/Ruff and kernel CI coverage checks pass; the 34 nonblocking mypy diagnostics match that pinned baseline after line-number normalization.
- A6000 GPU checks: 4 targeted transfer/pool-reuse cases passed on one GPU; 16 shared-manager cases and 24 existing GPT/MoE, EP-overlap and CUDA-graph cases passed on each of four ranks, with zero skips. Counts are per rank, not multiplied by the rank count.

[Current-head GPU logs, commands and verification](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/8c5cc72379de4e9ef8d80856973dd64f23cc0dac/gpu-20261016) include the original per-rank reports and exact source identities. [CPU/rebase evidence](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/251ae748bd5566fe57c15ba4e8431dfbd5483675/rebase-20261015) remains pinned separately. Local acceptance is complete; upstream GPU CI awaits vetter approval for this head.

## Issue tracking

Related to #6757. Split from #7908 following [the requested review boundaries](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7908#issuecomment-6182348264). #7908 depends on this shared-manager fix. #8244 is a separate gate-backward repeatability change and is not required by the offload integration.
