items.title: [model, fsdp, rollout, vllm] feat: Step-5-Preview FP8 GRPO with LoRA on FSDP2
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Adds RL support for Step-5-Preview (FP8 block-quantized MoE with sparse DSA attention) on the FSDP2 engine. It covers GRPO with LoRA against a vLLM rollout, rollout routing replay (R3), and adapter-only weight sync.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds RL support for **Step-5-Preview** (FP8 block-quantized MoE with sparse
DSA attention) on the FSDP2 engine. It covers GRPO with LoRA against a vLLM
rollout, rollout routing replay (R3), and adapter-only weight sync.

verl has no Step5 model, so the PR adds a verl-native text model and an example
recipe, plus the generic changes the run needed. 21 files; each commit can be
reviewed on its own:

| # | Commit | Files | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `[utils] fix: honor tokenizer.json when AutoTokenizer rebuilds the pre-tokenizer` | 1 | all models, only when the loaded tokenizer deletes whitespace that its `tokenizer.json` keeps |
| 2 | `[vllm] fix: treat untagged vLLM source builds as the newest API` | 6 | untagged vLLM builds (`0.1.devN`); the TCP-store path for every build |
| 3 | `[rollout, vllm] perf: stage LoRA buckets in one host block; optionally drop the adapter host copy` | 4 | LoRA sync to vLLM |
| 4 | `[fsdp] feat: support R3 router replay` | 4 | FSDP engine, off by default; LoRA reference routing in every engine |
| 5 | `[fsdp, model] feat: Step-5-Preview text model for FSDP2 LoRA RL` | 6 new + engine hooks | `model_type == "step5"` only |

**Dependency on vLLM.** Upstream vLLM does not serve Step5 yet. The rollout
needs a vLLM build with the Step5 model, LoRA serving on its fused attention
and sparse-indexer projections, and pageable host backups for level-1 sleep
(pinned backups made host memory grow on every sleep/wake cycle until OOM).
Those vLLM changes are being upstreamed separately. Until then this PR is a
draft; the verl side does not depend on any vLLM internals beyond the
existing LoRA/weight-sync paths.

**Overlap with open PRs. Please reconcile before merging.**

- #8193 addresses the same tokenizer failure as commit 1. Commit 1 acts only on
  the observed failure (whitespace deleted on a round trip, kept by the file),
  and refuses to load rather than swap when special tokens, added tokens, the
  vocabulary size, the chat template or the special tokens around plain text
  would change.
- #8194 is the same feature as commit 4. Here the FSDP engine turns R3 on
  while it builds the model, so VeOmni (which builds its own model and has its
  own replay hook) needs no change.

### Test

The PR carries no tests, to keep it reviewable. The checks written for it ran
against the final branch head in a Step5 vLLM image (transformers 5.17, an
untagged vLLM source build), with asserts enabled:

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Tokenizer: real Step-5-Preview tokenizer (swapped, encodes like `tokenizer.json`, same specials); configured `add_prefix_space`, stored truncation, `use_fast=False`, unresolvable ids left alone; refusal propagates through `hf_processor` | 22/22 |
| Version parsing and gates; a one-rank stateless process group built on the installed vLLM | 18/18 |
| R3 packing, alignment and refusals | 10 passed |
| LoRA bucket staging and the vLLM weight-update path | 27 passed, 5 skipped (shared-memory variants) |
| Step5 model pieces, checkpoint naming and sharded reads, LoRA attach and per-expert export, replay, grouped gathers (2 GPUs), startup refusals | 99 passed |

I can add any of them to the PR if reviewers want them in tree.

On this base (`f724e7f2`): ruff check/format pass on every changed file; the
generated trainer configs match `scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh` output.

**Training run.** The example recipe ran from scratch on 4 nodes x 4 GB300 for
194 steps (stopped there on purpose), as one run with two restarts from
LoRA-only checkpoints. It ran the code this PR was cut from: the same model,
LoRA math and sync logic. The review fixes since then add startup refusals and
guards (listed under Known gaps and Rollback) and do not change the numerics
of that configuration.

AIME-2024 during training (4096-token responses, as in the recipe):

| Step | 0 | 40 | 80 | 120 | 160 | 190 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean@8 | 0.375 | 0.375 | 0.500 | 0.575 | 0.571 | 0.658 |
| answers finished within 4096 tokens | 0.400 | | | | | 0.750 |

Most of that gain is answers finishing within the budget. To separate it, the
step-0 and step-190 checkpoints were re-evaluated with a 16384-token budget
(8 samples per problem; maj@8 and best@8 are verl's bootstrap estimates):

| AIME-2024, 16384 tokens | step 0 | step 190 |
|---|---|---|
| mean@8 | 0.804 | 0.829 |
| maj@8 | 0.832 | 0.911 |
| best@8 | 0.930 | 0.963 |
| answers finished | 0.829 | 0.963 |
| accuracy of finished answers | 0.970 | 0.861 |
| median answer length (characters) | 18,732 | 7,803 |

With room to finish, single-sample accuracy moves little (+0.025). The trained
model answers in less than half the length and finishes almost always; majority
voting gains 0.08. Accuracy on finished answers drops because the step-0 model
finishes mostly the problems it solves. Training responses show the same
trend: 41% truncated in steps 1–20, 18% in steps 181–194.

Over steps 1–194, trainer-vs-rollout agreement stayed stable:

- per-token mean abs logprob diff: 0.020–0.023 (20-step means);
- KL: about 0.001;
- rejected sequences: under 1% on average, at most 2.7% on one step;
- entropy: 0.74 → 0.57 (20-step means), smoothly;
- grad norm: mostly 0.004–0.013, with isolated spikes at steps 44 and 184.

These are aggregate run metrics; they do not show that each operation matches
the serving kernels (see the numerics item under Known gaps).

### API and Usage Example

```bash
# Needs a vLLM build that serves Step5 (see "Dependency on vLLM").
# ckpt_dir must be on storage shared by all nodes.
bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_step5_preview_dapo_lora_fsdp.sh
```

- Model: `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview` (FP8). Data: DAPO-Math-17K for training,
  AIME-2024 for validation.
- 4 nodes x 4 GPUs, two TP8 vLLM engines; LoRA r32/α64, lr 1e-5 constant;
  R3; sequence-level geometric rejection (`seq_mean_k1`, 0.995–1.005), no IS
  weights; 4096-token responses.
- The recipe passes its environment to the Ray workers through
  `ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.env_vars`; a plain `export` does not reach
  workers of a pre-started cluster.
- Extra packages beyond verl's: `peft==0.21.2`, `accelerate==1.15.0`.
- Optional, for repeatable LoRA outputs: point `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` at a
  LoRA shrink config with `split_k=1`. The default reduces with atomic adds.
- Cost: about 13 minutes per step, plus about 4 minutes per AIME validation.

New environment variables (all default to the validated behavior):

- `VERL_STEP5_FP8_ACT_QUANT` (default 1): FP8 activation rounding on routed experts.
- `VERL_STEP5_LORA_PER_EXPERT` (default 0): per-expert instead of shared expert factors.
- `VERL_STEP5_ROUTING_AGREEMENT` (diagnostic): logs trainer-router agreement with the replayed routing.
- `VERL_LORA_STAGE_PIN` (default 1): pin the LoRA staging blocks in the vLLM worker.
- `VERL_LORA_DROP_HOST_COPY` (opt-in): release the adapter's host copy in the vLLM worker.

### Design & Code Changes

**Step5 text model** (`verl/models/transformers/step5/`)

- `modeling_step5.py`: the model.
- `loading.py`: FP8 checkpoint loading into FSDP2 shards, and the engine hooks.
- `lora.py`: LoRA attach and adapter export.
- `register.py`: Auto registration.

What it does:

- **Model.** A plain-PyTorch port of the vLLM Step5 text model. It keeps the
  pieces that change numerics:
  - GQA with sliding and sparse (DSA) attention and a head-wise gate;
  - zero-centered RMSNorm and FP32 residual;
  - a FP32 sigmoid router with correction bias;
  - packed routed experts plus a shared expert.

  It has no inference kernels, KV cache or TP. The config class comes from the
  installed vLLM, because transformers has no `step5` type. Registration goes
  through `VERL_USE_EXTERNAL_MODULES=verl.models.transformers.step5.register`.
- **FP8 checkpoint.** Block-FP8 weights are dequantized to BF16 straight into
  each rank's FSDP2 local shard. No rank ever materializes the full model.
- **FP8 activation rule.** Routed experts stored in FP8 see the same 1x128
  UE8M0/E4M3 activation rounding as the serving kernel, with a
  straight-through gradient.
- **LoRA targets.** Attention projections and every MLP, including the routed
  experts through PEFT `target_parameters`. Expert adapters are applied
  unfolded, `s * (x A^T) B^T`, as vLLM does, with FP32 masters. They are never
  folded into a BF16 expert stack. The rank must be a multiple of 8 (grouped
  GEMM alignment).
- **Shared factors.** By default the expert gate/up `A` and down `B` are shared
  across the experts of a layer. The export expands them to the per-expert vLLM
  format.
- **R3.** Recorded rollout routing replaces the native top-k for recorded
  tokens. The weights still come from the trainer router.
- **Packed inputs.** verl's remove-padding rows (`input_ids` + `position_ids`)
  are unpacked into a padded batch and packed back. Any other row whose valid
  tokens do not have strictly increasing positions raises, instead of silently
  attending across sequences. Multi-axis (mRoPE-style) positions are refused.
- **Sync.** The rollout loads the base weights itself. Adapters are streamed
  to it in the per-expert format, using grouped all-gathers. There is no full
  host copy per rank.
- **Engine hooks.** `FSDPEngine` dispatches on `model_type == "step5"` for the
  meta-model build, LoRA attach, sharding/loading, adapter export and the
  refusals below. Other models take the existing path unchanged.

**Known gaps**

- Text-only. The vision tower and MTP layers are not loaded.
- Startup refuses configurations that were not validated or cannot work:
  sequence parallel, liger and fused kernels; activation/param/optimizer
  offload, QAT, a separate reference engine; resuming from
  `lora_adapter_path` (resuming through the verl checkpoint manager works);
  `lora.merge` and merged `hf_model` export (PEFT cannot merge the shared
  expert factors); a LoRA rank not divisible by 8; a base-weight sync
  (`rollout.load_format=dummy` or a non-naive checkpoint engine); adapter
  export from a model built from selected source layers.
- Numerics not yet compared operation by operation with the serving kernels:
  the dense and shared-expert SwiGLU rounds SiLU to BF16 before the
  multiplication, and each routed expert's output is rounded to BF16 before
  the routing weight is applied. Both can move a BF16 result by one ulp. They
  stay as validated until checked against the serving implementation.
- Commit 1 covers tokenizers loaded through `hf_tokenizer`/`hf_processor`. Text
  sent to the rollout server as text is tokenized by the server. Versioned
  tokenizer files (`fast_tokenizer_files`) are not looked up.
- Commit 2 assumes an untagged build is the newest vLLM. An untagged checkout
  of an older vLLM passes the minimum-version checks and fails later inside
  vLLM (for R3 on a pre-0.22 checkout with several KV-cache groups, an
  IndexError in the routed-experts capture). The warning says so; build from a
  tagged checkout to keep the checks.
- Commit 4 checks the R3 prerequisites at startup on the FSDP engine only.
- The grouped adapter gathers are bounded by `max_gathered_bytes`, which is not
  a ceiling on peak memory: a single larger tensor is gathered alone.
- A failure inside a weight sync can still leave the other side waiting, as
  before this PR.

**Rollback / impact on other models**

- Commit 5 is gated on `model_type == "step5"`.
- Commit 4 is gated on `router_replay.mode`, which is off by default, with
  one exception: reference log-probs computed through the actor with the
  adapter disabled (the LoRA reference) now route natively instead of
  replaying the actor's rollout routing, as a separate reference worker does.
  The flag is shared by all engines, so Megatron and VeOmni runs that combine
  a LoRA reference with routing replay change too.
- Commit 1 does nothing unless a probe decodes back with some of its
  whitespace deleted and nothing else changed. A healthy tokenizer costs one
  encode and decode; a tokenizer whose own file also loses the whitespace is
  left alone without a second load.
- Commit 2 changes branch selection only for untagged `0.1.devN` builds
  (prereleases and post-releases of it are parsed as before). A real nightly
  below 0.22, such as `0.21.2.devN`, is still refused for R3. The gates where
  the older path is the safe one (the `mm_processor_cache_gb=0` workaround,
  the NPU 0.23 patch window) keep the raw version. The TCP-store path in
  `stateless_init_process_group` now follows `StatelessProcessGroup`'s fields
  rather than the version, which picks the same path for every tagged release.
- Commit 3 copies LoRA buckets in the vLLM worker as one host block per bucket
  (expert factors in their own block) instead of one clone per tensor, and
  refuses a tensor name sent twice in an adapter-only update. Dropping the
  host copy is opt-in and is ignored with a warning unless the adapter has a
  single slot.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows): tests exist out of tree (see Test); the e2e path needs a Step5-capable vLLM.
- [x] AI assistance: the code, tests and this description were prepared with Claude Code; the generic changes in commits 1–4 and the engine hooks need human review.

items.title: [TRTLLM-17054][refactor] Reuse PyExecutor across profiling resource transitions
items.author: zhaoyangwang-nvidia
items.summary: Memory profiling currently constructs a temporary, shuts it down, and constructs another executor for serving. Reuse one executor across this transition while replacing resources whose size or registration depends on the final KV-cache allocation.
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

The current diff only reformats imports and multiline statements in `py_executor.py`. It does not change executor behavior, APIs, configuration, or runtime logic.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

**Coverage verdict: needs follow-up.** The current diff adds or modifies no tests. The supplied objectives report lifecycle checks in an isolated CPU harness, while full project and GPU/MPI validation remain pending.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor.py`: Changes only import and line formatting. No behavior change requires additional QA verification.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Memory profiling currently constructs a temporary `PyExecutor`, shuts it down, and constructs another executor for serving. Reuse one executor across this transition while replacing resources whose size or registration depends on the final KV-cache allocation.

Introduce `PyExecutorResources` and a shared execution-phase initializer. `release_resources()` stops execution, destroys graphs, unregisters transfers, and releases phase-owned resources while retaining the model, sampler, streams, and distributed context. `rebind_resources()` installs the final resources and warms them before starting the worker. Invalid transitions and initialization failures fail closed; final shutdown remains terminal and idempotent.

Both profiling and final-resource warmups remain necessary and are preserved. The steady-state executor loop, model forward path, and user-facing configuration are unchanged. This is a lifecycle refactor, not a claim of significant startup or inference speedup.

This PR is based directly on main (`306a8a7c30`) and contains the executor-reuse change and its test/review follow-ups touching six files. It has no dependency on #20253. Main's native MPI progress-thread shutdown behavior is preserved during resource release, with regression coverage for normal pipeline shutdown and the hung-worker path.

## Test Coverage

Committed regression tests (run with the project test environment and `LLM_MODELS_ROOT` configured where model weights are needed):

```bash
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_executor_resource_rebind.py
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_estimation.py::test_profiling_failure_releases_resources_and_restores_response_state
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_py_executor_creator_mla_cache_reuse_sync.py::test_startup_allocation_phases
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_py_executor_creator_mla_cache_reuse_sync.py::test_failed_resource_transition_closes_executor
```

There are 17 added CPU-only mock cases: 13 lifecycle cases, three factory failure stages, and one profiling-failure case. Draft-graph and async-sampler teardown assertions share the main teardown case; repeated release shares the final-shutdown case. Existing factory tests also assert single-executor construction without adding model runs. No GPU benchmark or long-running qualification harness is added to CI.

These cover teardown order, model retention, sampler/worker termination, transfer-unregistration failure, invalid/repeated transitions, final shutdown, profiling failure, and final allocation/rebind failure.

**Current revision (`dfb3554774`) validation:** all 132 tests passed across `test_executor_resource_rebind.py`, `test_profile_endpoints.py`, `kv_cache/test_kv_cache_estimation.py`, and `test_py_executor_creator_mla_cache_reuse_sync.py` in an isolated CPU container using current Python source and compatible retained native artifacts (PyTorch 26.08). Pre-commit passed; mypy skips these files. The existing successful-rebind test now executes the real `_initialize_execution`, with GPU/distributed collaborators mocked, and checks phase resets, final-cache binding, profiler markers, and no worker start. Removing the marker-reset assignments in a temporary source copy makes that regression fail. The number of added test cases is unchanged. Full GPU qualification of the main-based revision remains pending.

**CI investigation:** build [64270](http://tensorrt-llm.tensorrt-llm-ci-report.sc2-paas.nvidia.com/?job=%2FLLM%2Fmain%2FL0_MergeRequest_PR&build=64270), on the preceding head, failed `test_llm_disagg_streaming_gen_cancelled[PYTHON]` on A100 with a request timeout and KV-transfer errors. Original shard logs confirm the same test and KV-transfer-error signature in build 64230 (PR #20279, Qwen tool-parser changes) and build 64266 (PR #20290, Blackwell top-k changes). This establishes a shared failure independent of executor reuse; it does not exclude additional impact from this PR without a controlled GPU comparison. SBSA aborts and blocked multi-GPU stages were cascading failures. No manual full-CI rerun was requested for this follow-up.

**Historical GPU qualification only:** the following results compare cleanup baseline `8fe47ceaf` with the previous candidate `1e7f0845b`, before transplanting onto main. They do not establish correctness or performance of current head `dfb3554774`, including its integration with main's newer MPI progress thread. H200 tests used identical native artifacts for those two historical revisions:

- Selected unit regression suite: baseline 657 passed and candidate 676 passed, plus 14 subtests each. Pre-commit passed again before opening this draft; mypy skipped these files because they are outside its allow-list.
- Standalone GPU A/B qualification: normal profiling constructs the executor 2→1 times; skip-estimation stays at one. KV V1/V2, graph/eager fallback, overlap, chunked prefill, observed eviction/recomputation, constrained VRAM, TP2/PP2, speculative decoding, real MLA/hybrid Mamba, nonzero LoRA eviction/reload, and final-KV-allocation failure cleanup passed.
- Real two-GPU NIXL context-to-generation transfer with graph on/off: reference parity, cancellation, orphan-context timeout reclamation, recovery, and shutdown passed. This is not a cross-node bandwidth benchmark.
- Five create/infer/shutdown cycles reclaimed models and workers. Both revisions exhibit the same framework-global cuBLAS workspace retention; clearing only that cache isolates stable executor-owned allocation. Raw measurements were retained.
- Controlled precision comparisons: 80 context/generation-logit tensors matched exactly; a further 10-minute run per revision matched all 3,159 paired requests and cache-hit records with zero same-shape allocation growth. Exact comparisons align batch admission; MLA additionally fixes the execution path by disabling autotuning. Unmodified-baseline repeats reproduced the asynchronous/autotuner differences, so default execution is not claimed to be bitwise deterministic.
- HTTP streaming: three alternating A/B rounds, concurrency 1/8/32, 120 mixed-length requests per phase. Input lengths 64/4096/8192 and output lengths 32/128/256; default autotuning and asynchronous scheduling retained. Throughput medians changed +0.005%/+0.133%/+0.231%. An additional concurrency-8 check used two alternating pairs of 600-request runs. All 2,280 paired HTTP outputs matched.
- The small concurrency-8 TPOT P99 increase was investigated rather than omitted: the larger-sample paired changes were +1.828% and -0.045%, with an aggregate +0.885%; throughput increased +0.213%. Aggregate metrics stayed within the 3% regression gate. Large-sample TTFT P50 varied between approximately 133–163 ms in both revisions, so single-run median shifts are not interpreted as stable gains or regressions.

The GPU qualification harnesses and raw artifacts are retained separately from this production patch; they are not additional committed CI tests. Results establish the tested coverage and tolerance, not universal zero-difference performance.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
- The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR.


- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

## GitHub Bot Help

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6782274][fix] Fail fast with a clear error when FlashInfer cannot fetch a kernel artifact
items.author: xxi-nv
items.summary: When a forward step or warmup fails after FlashInfer could not fetch a kernel artifact it needed, TRT-LLM now raises an error that names the file and says how to provide it. Before, the step failed with an unrelated error that named nothing.
items.body:
## Description

When a forward step or warmup fails after FlashInfer could not fetch a kernel artifact it needed, TRT-LLM now raises an error that names the file and says how to provide it. Before, the step failed with an unrelated error that named nothing. A failed fetch that the step survives, such as one for a tactic the autotuner skips, is logged and does not stop the run.

### Why

FlashInfer fetches some kernel artifacts (checksum files, headers, cubins) the first time it needs them, from its cubin directory or by downloading them. In FlashInfer 0.6.18, a fetch that fails (download retries exhausted, a download-lock timeout, or a sha256 mismatch) makes `flashinfer.jit.cubin_loader.get_artifact` return empty bytes instead of raising. The empty result is consumed somewhere else, so what users see depends on the kernel:

| Where the empty artifact lands | What the user sees | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashInfer JIT module generation (fused MoE, GEMM) | an assertion: `flashinferMetaInfo.h not found` | https://nvbugs/6782274 |
| TRTLLM-Gen batched GEMM (MoE) | `Error occurred when running GEMM!`. The loader keeps the module that failed to load cached, so every later call fails too, until the process restarts. | https://nvbugs/6778221 |
| TRTLLM-Gen FMHA (attention) | `Failed to load cubin for <kernel>` | |

FlashInfer's own log does not name the file either; its last download message is `Max retries reached. Download failed.`. In both bugs, finding out that a download had failed took digging through the CI logs.

### What changed

- **`tensorrt_llm/_torch/flashinfer_artifacts.py` (new).** `install_flashinfer_artifact_monitor()` wraps `get_artifact`, the function FlashInfer's runtime downloads go through, including the cubin callback that FlashInfer's C++ kernel loaders call. The wrapper only observes: it returns what FlashInfer returns and re-raises what it raises. It records each failed fetch and logs an ERROR naming the file, the cubin directory, the download repository, and how to provide the artifacts. References that FlashInfer modules took by importing the function by name, and the `get_cubin` alias, are replaced as well. If a FlashInfer version has no `get_artifact`, it logs a warning and leaves FlashInfer untouched; the GPU unit test below then fails, so a FlashInfer upgrade cannot silently disable the check.
- **`flashinfer_utils.py`** installs the monitor right after `import flashinfer` succeeds. Every LLM process on the PyTorch backend imports this module.
- **`PyTorchModelEngine.forward` and `warmup`** run inside `raise_on_flashinfer_artifact_failure()`. If the step raises after a fetch failed during it, `FlashInferArtifactUnavailableError` is raised instead, listing the failed files, with the original exception as `__cause__`. A step that completes is not failed: both autotuners skip a tactic whose kernel cannot be loaded, and warmup autotunes inside this check, so a fetch that fails only for a skipped tactic is just logged. `warmup` is wrapped separately because it drives the runner directly rather than through `forward`. Only fetches that failed during the step are reported, so a later unrelated error is never blamed on an old download failure. The error pickles with its fields, because an executor worker sends a startup failure to the user's process pickled.

Because the check sits on FlashInfer's download path rather than in a model or module, it covers attention, MLA, MoE, and GEMM kernels alike, including FlashInfer call sites added later. A warmup that fails this way aborts startup; a step that fails this way while serving fails that batch through `PyExecutor`'s existing error handling, now with the artifact named.

Worth a close look: `_install_monitor` replaces references by identity, and only inside the `flashinfer` package.

Example error:

> FlashInfer could not fetch kernel artifacts that it downloads at runtime: 8ec29a98/batched_gemm-fa419f4-31ee4e5/Bmm_Bfloat16_t128x8x128.cubin (download failed or sha256 mismatch, see the FlashInfer log). FlashInfer 0.6.18 reads these artifacts from `<cubin dir>` and downloads missing ones from `<repository>`. To run without runtime downloads, install flashinfer-cubin==0.6.18, or point FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR at a populated cubin directory and set FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1. Some FlashInfer kernels keep a module that failed to load cached, so they can stay unusable until the process restarts.

### Not covered

- This PR does not make the downloads succeed. Providing the artifacts ahead of time in CI (`flashinfer-cubin` plus `FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1`) is a separate change.
- Code that calls FlashInfer outside `PyTorchModelEngine`, such as module-level unit tests like `test_moe_backend.py` and VisualGen, gets the ERROR log naming the file but keeps FlashInfer's original exception.
- A fetch that fails in a step that still completes is only logged. If FlashInfer keeps the module that failed to load cached (TRTLLM-Gen batched GEMM does) and a later step needs that kernel, the later step fails with FlashInfer's original error, because nothing is fetched inside it; the earlier ERROR log names the file.
- FlashInfer 0.6.18 downloads the `checksums.txt` of its CuTe DSL FMHA kernels directly rather than through `get_artifact`, so a failure to fetch that file is not reported. In TRT-LLM only VisualGen's FlashInfer attention backend loads these kernels.
- The root behavior is FlashInfer's: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4925 makes `get_artifact` raise on failure. Once a FlashInfer version with it is pinned, the monitor can be removed.

Related: #19034 gave each rank its own FlashInfer cubin cache, which removed the download-lock timeouts between ranks. This PR makes the remaining failures, such as network errors, explicit.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/_torch/flashinfer/test_flashinfer_artifacts.py` (new, 19 test functions, 21 cases):

- 19 `cpu_only` cases, added to `l0_cpu.yml`, run against a fake FlashInfer package:
  - successful fetches pass through unchanged; empty and raising fetches are recorded, logged with the file name, and returned or re-raised unchanged;
  - every reference inside the package (by-name import, alias) is replaced, references outside it are not; installing twice keeps one monitor; a FlashInfer without `get_artifact` is left unchanged with a warning;
  - the block is transparent without failures, chains the error raised inside it as `__cause__`, lets a block that completes after a failed fetch return with the failure only logged, ignores failures from before the block, reports once when nested, lists a repeated failure once, and its message says where the artifacts come from and how to provide them;
  - the error survives pickling, which is how an executor worker reports a failed startup;
  - `PyTorchModelEngine.forward` and `warmup` raise `FlashInferArtifactUnavailableError` when they fail after a fetch failed inside them.
- 2 cases, added to `l0_a10.yml`, run against the installed FlashInfer:
  - after import, every `flashinfer.*` reference to `get_artifact` is the monitor, so a FlashInfer upgrade that moves or renames the function fails here;
  - a real fetch of a missing file under `FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1` is reported.

Verified on one B200 with the CI image, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and Qwen3-0.6B through `examples/llm-api/quickstart_advanced.py`:

- the test file above, `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/engine/test_runners.py`, and `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_pytorch_model_engine.py` pass;
- generation is unchanged with the default cubin directory, and with an empty `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` that FlashInfer fills by downloading;
- with an empty `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` plus `FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1`, or with an unreachable `FLASHINFER_CUBINS_REPOSITORY`, with and without CUDA graphs, startup fails in warmup. The user's process raises `RuntimeError: Executor worker returned error` caused by `FlashInferArtifactUnavailableError`, which names the missing `fmha/trtllm-gen//checksums.txt`.

These runs predate the change that stops failing a step that completes. In every failing run, warmup itself raised, with FlashInfer's error as the `__cause__`, so the current code fails them the same way. The updated test file has not been rerun on the GPU.

The CI stages above have not run yet.

- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.

items.title: test(moe): refresh goldens for the DeepSeek proxy optimizer CUDA graph test
items.author: ilml
items.summary: Refreshes the goldens of (GB200, ). This test runs only in GitLab's scope and has failed on every pipeline since #7407 added it. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Refreshes the goldens of `moe/deepseek_proxy_mfsdp_v2_ep2_bf16_cg_optim_1node` (GB200, `dev`). This test runs only in GitLab's `mr` scope and has failed on every `main` pipeline since #7407 added it. Only the golden file changes.

Latest failure: [job 487847526](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/ADLR/megatron-lm/-/jobs/487847526) in `main` pipeline [73895766](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/ADLR/megatron-lm/-/pipelines/73895766) at 80781ab0a.

- `mem-allocated-bytes` is 101,978,112 B (+13.2%) above the golden at every step, so the 5% check fails.
- `lm loss` fails the exact check. Step 1 is 10.901482582 against 10.901466370, and the largest relative difference is 2.3e-4. The approximate check passes.

## Why the goldens are wrong

#7407 recorded the goldens from a manual 4-GPU run, not from CI. That run needed `NVTE_CUTEDSL_FUSED_GROUPED_MLP=1` exported by hand to get past Megatron's op-fuser assertion; #7495 later added it to the recipe. This test's history on `main` shows the goldens never matched CI:

| `main` range | CI result |
| --- | --- |
| a2585b244 (#7407, 09-17) → c711dc0a7 (09-21) | Fails at init: the recipe lacks `NVTE_CUTEDSL_FUSED_GROUPED_MLP` |
| dae135048 (#7495, 09-22) → 1cb9fe85c (10-02) | Trains. `mem-allocated-bytes` is +100,667,392 B at every step, and `lm loss` already differs from step 1 |
| 16f377ea2 (#6615, 10-02) → 80781ab0a (10-14) | `mem-allocated-bytes` is +101,978,112 B, and `lm loss` is unchanged |

All 50 `lm loss` values are bit-identical in every run from 09-22 to 10-14. That covers the TE 2.20 bumps, NGC 26.09, the cuBLAS 13.8.1 image change, and #6615.

- **+100,667,392 B, present from the first completed CI run:** Transformer Engine's grouped-tensor GEMM workspaces. TE keeps these allocated on purpose.
  - For bf16 on GB200, every routed-expert GEMM goes through `general_grouped_gemm_for_grouped_tensor`.
  - Since TE#3171, that path keeps one `lru_cache`d cuBLAS workspace per layout (TN fprop, NN dgrad, NT wgrad), each 32 MiB + 1 KiB, plus a setup workspace (a 624 B request, which occupies a 1,024 B block).
  - Total: 3 × 33,555,456 + 1,024 = 100,667,392 B.
  - TE builds without TE#3171 (2.17.x, and some 2.18.0 builds such as `release_v2.18_nemo_26.08`) allocate these per call, so they are freed before memory is sampled at the end of an iteration.
  - Megatron has pinned a TE with TE#3171 since #6917 (08-28), before the goldens were recorded. The golden run therefore used a different TE build, and these goldens could never have matched CI.
  - #7495 saw the same gap ("about 96 MiB above the existing golden") with a bit-identical loss, and left the golden unchanged.
- **+1,310,720 B since #6615:** `_HybridEPManager.topk_idx`, an int16 `[32768, 4]` tensor (262,144 B) in each of the 5 MoE layers.
  - #6615 derives these dense top-k ids from the bool routing map when DeepEP ≥ 10d4dd73 (#7358) is installed.
  - They stay referenced on each layer's dispatcher after `combine()`.
  - The amount is constant from step 1 and is 0.16% of the metric, so it does not cause the failure.
- **`lm loss`:** it moved between 3226303b3, where #7495 still matched the goldens exactly, and dae135048, the first CI run to get past init.
  - In that window, TE 2.19 (#7379) is the only identified change on this config's forward path. Its `ScaledSwiGLU` op now calls the fused `tex.scaled_swiglu`, which rounds `silu(a)·b·prob` to bf16 once instead of twice.
  - The DeepEP pin bump (#7358) also landed then; DeepEP's tests expect it to be bit-neutral.
  - No Megatron change in `3226303b3..main` alters this config's forward math.
  - Library bumps that change numerics refresh their own goldens, but this test runs only on GitLab, so no bump PR ever refreshed it.

## How was the new golden produced?

- The file is copied byte-for-byte from the `results/…/golden_values_dev_dgx_gb200.json` artifact of job 487847526. This is the file `download_golden_values.py --source gitlab` would move.
  - I didn't run that script over the whole pipeline. That pipeline's `hybrid_mhc_tp2_pp2_mtp` job hit `Disk quota exceeded` and left a 0-byte golden file, which the script would have copied over that test's good goldens.
- The job ran the recipe three times, on three GB200 hosts (`nvl72158`, `nvl72082`, `nvl72023`). The TensorBoard scalars for `lm loss`, `num-zeros`, `mem-allocated-bytes` and `mem-max-allocated-bytes` were bit-identical across all three runs.
- I re-ran CI's comparison (`test_pretraining_regular_pipeline.py`, with `--actual-values-path` set to the job's output):
  - with the old goldens it fails on `lm loss, mem-allocated-bytes`, as CI did;
  - with the new goldens it passes.

### Relative-difference summary

Computed with `tests/test_utils/python_scripts/compare_golden_values_kl.py`, where `avg_rel_diff = mean((old − new) / old)` over 50 steps (49 for `iteration-time`).

| metric | avg_rel_diff |
| --- | ---: |
| `lm loss` | +3.56e-05 |
| `mem-allocated-bytes` | −0.1222 |
| `mem-max-allocated-bytes` | −0.0033 |
| `iteration-time` (not checked) | +0.2079 |

`num-zeros` is all zeros in both files.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6649384][test] Add opt-in late-receiver lifecycle characterization
items.author: chienchunhung
items.summary: Temporary investigation draft for NVBUG6649384. Substitute external memory/transport boundaries, not lifecycle algorithms.
items.body:
## Description

Temporary investigation draft for NVBUG6649384. **Not a product fix and not ready to merge.**

Starting from source `da676ffb8b611a1a0a83c862aa094e736f9fe5aa` (published runtime `1.4.0rc1.dev202610140007`), characterize whether a context sender can retire before a late receiver publishes REQUEST_DATA, leaving generation to reach its separate KV-transfer deadline.

items.title: [None][perf] Exchange draft argmax pairs through a private MNNVL mailbox
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Use a dedicated one-shot MNNVL workspace to exchange the small per-rank pairs used by greedy draft sampling. A single packing kernel places each rank's pair in its own zero-padded slot, so SUM produces the same global argmax while keeping the mailbox's Lamport…
items.body:
## Description

Use a dedicated one-shot MNNVL workspace to exchange the small per-rank `(argmax index, max value)` pairs used by greedy draft sampling. A single packing kernel places each rank's pair in its own zero-padded slot, so SUM produces the same global argmax while keeping the mailbox's Lamport buffers separate from model all-reduces.

Use this path for pure-TP, multi-node MNNVL with TP sizes 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, or 64. Keep NCCL for other group sizes, single-node groups, sleep-enabled engines, unsupported mappings, oversized payloads, `TRTLLM_MTP_TAIL_TRIM=0`, and first use during CUDA graph capture. Workspace setup converges errors across the TP group and retains the handles for graph replay.

This extracts the private-mailbox optimization from source commit `9fb12e7c68f6d863ab0bf0fa8e078e2f78976365` (Iman Tabrizian). It is independent of #20323's local-argmax and DSA optimizations and applies beyond GLM to the shared greedy speculative-decoding path. Single-node fallback matches the original source policy.

## Test Coverage

items.title: [None][feat] Honor explicit no-evict admission in the V2 KV scheduler
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: The V2 KV scheduler currently downgrades an explicit request to. Reserve each request's remaining completion footprint in both target and draft pools before admitting its first context chunk or disaggregated generation transfer.
items.body:
## Description

The V2 KV scheduler currently downgrades an explicit `GUARANTEED_NO_EVICT` request to `MAX_UTILIZATION`. Reserve each request's remaining completion footprint in both target and draft pools before admitting its first context chunk or disaggregated generation transfer. Resident requests keep their reservation, and the policy disables suspension and recompute preemption.

This is opt-in: unspecified policies retain the existing V2 default. Supported managers have one full-history KV pool, beam width 1, and no helix or cross-attention cache. This includes the normal GLM-5.2/5.3 DSA + MTP cache layout. Other layouts retain `MAX_UTILIZATION` with a warning. The budget includes each manager's current generation-capacity headroom, including wider dynamic-tree draft slots.

Depends on #20315 for retry-safe overlap batch-index release. The first two commits carry that prerequisite; commit `2f0b22f4103067c03c63de4eae27c7dc6ba5b6ba` is the incremental GNE feature. Drop the prerequisite commits after #20315 merges.

items.title: [None][perf] Gather speculative overlap inputs directly into destination buffers
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Speculative overlap currently gathers sampled tokens, draft tokens and position/KV offsets into temporary tensors before copying them into persistent runner buffers. Gather directly into those buffers with, and subtract the runtime token count only from the g…
items.body:
Speculative overlap currently gathers sampled tokens, draft tokens and position/KV offsets into temporary tensors before copying them into persistent runner buffers. Gather directly into those buffers with `torch.index_select(..., out=...)`, and subtract the runtime token count only from the gathered KV offsets.

This ports the direct-gather portion of internal source commit #37 (`2c4f305fc1e0e835c12fef06177a9207e557030b`). It applies across GPU architectures, including Rubin; dtype-conversion fallbacks, buffer addresses and normal zero resets are preserved. When integrating #19989, retain this behavior in its Torch fallback.

items.summary:

items.body:
## Description

Cherry-pick of #19958 (merged to `main` as `cc63e66daf`) to `release/1.3`.

`accuracy/test_disaggregated_serving.py::TestDeepSeekV3Lite::test_auto_dtype[mtp_nextn=2-overlap_scheduler={False,True}]` hung in the QA run on H20 at 53b392e9 (last pass db7161b6) and was waived as `full:H20/...` (nvbugs/6345827, #15510). The same two cases on H100 were waived the same week (#15504) under nvbugs/6313072, which tracks an unrelated OOM in the aggregated `TestDeepSeekV3Lite::test_bfloat16` and has since been verified fixed and closed. Neither GPU has run the two disaggregated cases since; in L0 the test only runs on `DGX_H200-8_GPUs-PyTorch-Post-Merge-1`.

At the time the test used `backend: DEFAULT`, i.e. the C++ transceiver over UCX. The failing run's teardown log shows the generation ranks blocked in `checkGenTransferStatus` -> `future.get()` on transfers whose KV data the context side never sent (gen rank 3 still mid-`recv` on one request while ranks 0-2 had already received it), with all 16 in-flight requests (the harness's `max_workers=16`) stuck behind it until the pytest timeout. This is consistent with the `CacheSender` lost-wakeup race: `removeResponse()` checked `mReadyResponses.empty()` outside the lock and then cleared `mAnyReady`, which could overwrite a concurrent `sendAsync()` and leave the responder asleep with a ready response queued; once every in-flight request is waiting on generation, no further `sendAsync()` arrives to wake it. That race was fixed by #15737 (nvbugs/6342844), and since #17090 the test uses the Python transceiver (NIXL), so it no longer exercises that path at all.

This PR removes the four stale QA waives (H20 and H100).

## Test Coverage

- Unwaived for QA on H20 and H100 (`qa/llm_function_core.txt`): `TestDeepSeekV3Lite::test_auto_dtype[mtp_nextn=2-overlap_scheduler=False]` and `[mtp_nextn=2-overlap_scheduler=True]`.
- Local 8xH200 (DGX) with a wheel built from main `72688933d5`:
  - `test_auto_dtype[mtp_nextn=2-overlap_scheduler=False]`: PASSED (MMLU 71.37, GSM8K 64.48)
  - `test_auto_dtype[mtp_nextn=2-overlap_scheduler=True]`: PASSED (MMLU 71.37, GSM8K 64.94)
  - Extra probes of the same workload (not part of this PR):
    - the configuration the test used when it was waived (C++ transceiver over UCX, KV cache manager V1) on today's main: PASSED (MMLU 71.30, GSM8K 65.01);
    - the current configuration with every rank's KV pool capped at 160K tokens (~13x smaller than on H20): PASSED (MMLU 71.27, GSM8K 64.10), ruling out a dependence on the smaller H20/H100 memory;
    - the C++/UCX configuration with the 160K cap was ~30% through and still progressing when the node allocation ended.
- CI history: `DGX_H200-8_GPUs-PyTorch-Post-Merge-1` has passed both cases on every `main` post-merge run since 2026-07-10 and on every `release/1.3` post-merge run that reached them (one `release/1.3` build failed the whole stage in setup on `pip install opencv-python-headless`); QA B200/B300 pass all four `test_auto_dtype` variants; QA H20 passes the `mtp_nextn=0` variants.
- Final confirmation is the next QA run on H20/H100 (re-run requested).

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6692200][perf] Cut KVCacheManagerV2 host overhead in generation steps
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: NVBug: 512/512 (maxbatchsize 512) throughput regressed when GPT-OSS moved to KV cache manager V2 (#16942). V2 has been the global default since #17495.
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

The change raises the GPU KV-cache allocation chunk cap from 32 MiB to 256 MiB in C++ and Python. It also checks for capacity growth and a window crossing before querying the debug-log level, reducing host-side work when no crossing occurs. The class-level window map supports managers created without `__init__`; the bare-manager test setup uses an empty map when layer grouping is absent.

No removed API or unrelated configuration change is reported. The supplied summary reports a 4.05% throughput improvement on GB200 across four nodes. It also reports no chunk-count sensitivity in the B200/HMM microbenchmark and no change to decode-only steps. These are reported benchmark results, not independently verified here.

## QA Engineer Review

Changed tests cover C++ and Python granularity schedules, non-GPU tier granularity, window-crossing log-level checks, and lazy window-map construction for a bare manager. The changed Python test files do not appear in CI or manual-QA lists; `test_kv_cache_budget_split.py` has unrelated existing waivers. The supplied CI context reports failures and no follow-up result. Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up**.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kv_cache_manager_v2/storageManager.cpp` — Verify that GPU granularity follows the updated quota schedule and caps at 256 MiB. Host-memory and disk-tier behavior should remain unchanged.
- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2ConfigTest.cpp` — Tests GPU granularity growth and cap, plus unchanged host-memory and disk-tier granularities. This file is outside `tests/`, so it is not covered by the requested `tests/integration/test_lists/` listing check.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py` — Verify that the Python granularity mirror matches the C++ schedule. Verify that the logger level is queried only after a window crossing and that managers without `__init__` build the window map correctly.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py` — Tests the Python GPU granularity schedule and 256 MiB cap. No exact CI or manual-QA list entry was found; existing waivers concern other test cases.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kvcm2_integration.py` — Tests window-crossing diagnostics, lazy window-map construction, and generation-allocation setup. No exact CI or manual-QA list entry was found.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

NVBug [6692200](https://nvbugs/6692200): `gpt_oss_20b_fp4` `trtllm-bench` 512/512 (max_batch_size 512) throughput regressed when GPT-OSS moved to KV cache manager V2 (#16942). V2 has been the global default since #17495. On GB200, same node, current-main CI wheel, with only `use_kv_cache_manager_v2` toggled, V2 is **6.3% slower than V1** (8 nodes, interleaved reps). The loss is all host time in mixed prefill+decode steps. GPU busy time per step is identical under both managers (11.7 ms), and the gap grows once a step carries more than ~256 generation requests.

This PR removes two V2-only host costs that are paid on every step:

1. **GPU pool chunk size: 32 MiB -> up to 256 MiB.** `CacheLevelManager::cacheTierGranularity` sizes the GPU pool's physical chunks at 2 MiB, doubling per power of two of the quota above 1 GiB, capped at 32 MiB. A full-GPU pool (151 GiB here) is therefore 4830 separate `cuMemCreate` allocations, each mapped into the pool's virtual range. That mapping count slows every later `cudaMalloc` in the process. Torch-profiler traces of the same steps show the fp32 logits buffer growing through the PyTorch caching allocator; its `cudaMalloc` takes 3.4–4.3 ms under V2 against 0.42–0.51 ms under V1, and runs every other step once the batch passes ~265 rows. The GPU idles behind it. A standalone microbenchmark on the same GB200 node (no TRT-LLM) reproduces this:

   | 150 GiB device pool built as | cuMemAlloc of a 210 MiB buffer (p50) |
   |---|---|
   | nothing / one cuMemAlloc | 242 / 253 µs |
   | 1024 MiB VMM chunks | 305 µs |
   | 32 MiB VMM chunks (current) | 703 µs |
   | 2 MiB VMM chunks | 14987 µs |

   This PR raises the cap to 256 MiB (exponent 4 -> 7), so the same pool is 604 chunks. Quotas below 16 GiB keep their current granularity; only large pools change. `_gpu_alloc_granularity` (the Python mirror used for the one-request quota floor) is updated to match. NIXL/UCX transfer code already discovers each region's chunk size at runtime (`VmmDescSplitter::detectVramRegionMap`), so disaggregated transfer is unaffected.
2. **`KVCacheManagerV2._log_window_crossing` queried the log level on every call.** It runs from `try_allocate_generation` for each generation request, every iteration. It called `logger.is_debug_enabled()` before checking for a crossing. Decode always grows capacity, so the query always ran, and it walks the caller's frames (`_get_caller_module`). At ~300 requests that costs 1.0–1.4 ms of host time per iteration. The window comparison now runs first, and the log level is queried only for the rare call that actually crosses a window. Logging output is unchanged, including `TLLM_LOG_LEVEL_BY_MODULE` overrides.

### Measured on GB200 (oci-hsg)

Setup: same node, current-main CI wheel `fca08032f7` and its 26.09 image. The harness is the QA one (`trtllm-bench` with `enable_padding`, `avg_seq_len`, `print_iter_log`) with a fresh per-rep HOME, as in CI. Arms are interleaved on each node. The C++ change runs on the stock wheel through an `LD_PRELOAD` replacement of `cacheTierGranularity` (identical body, cap 7), and the Python change is applied to the installed file.

Throughput change vs stock V2 on the same node (mean of the reps on that node):

| arm | nodes | mean | per node |
|---|---|---|---|
| **this PR** (both changes) | 4 | **+4.05%** | +4.8 / +5.0 / +1.4 / +5.0 |
| chunk cap only | 5 | +4.31% | +5.8 / +5.0 / +2.7 / +3.3 / +4.7 |
| log guard only | 2 | +2.15% | +2.5 / +1.8 |
| V1 (reference) | 8 | +6.33% | +4.8 … +7.2 |

Pooled over the 4 nodes of the final run (12 reps per arm): V1 67486, V2 63092, **this PR 65831 tok/s**. The V1–V2 gap shrinks from −6.5% to −2.5%; on 3 of 4 nodes 70–79% of it is recovered. Median mixed-step time at ≥256 generation requests drops from 35.2 ms to 31.5 ms (V1: 29.8 ms). Decode-only steps are unchanged. The two changes overlap (each removes host time from the same steps), so their gains don't add.

Ruled out on the same nodes: `TRTLLM_WORKER_DISABLE_GC=1` (−0.3%), a `getCopyIndex` rewrite that writes through `data_ptr` (+0.1%, so not included), and disabling the host tier (+1.9%, fixed by the chunk change anyway).

**Platform scope.** The chunk-count cost is a Grace/ATS effect: GB200 reports `Addressing Mode: ATS`. The same microbenchmark on an x86 B200 (`Addressing Mode: HMM`) shows no sensitivity to chunk count: a 210 MiB `cuMemAlloc` takes 136–151 µs whether the 150 GiB pool is one allocation or 4800 chunks of 32 MiB. On x86 Blackwell, only change 2 applies. The B200 part of the CI regression (−7.6%) is therefore mostly not explained by change 1 and needs its own profile.

Not addressed here, and the rest of the gap: per-op host time stays ~10% higher under V2 throughout the mixed phase (`aten::view`, kernel launch, `cudaPointerGetAttributes`). This looks like the same driver-side cost of the larger mapping count, now smaller but not zero.

## Test Coverage

- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2ConfigTest.cpp`: `GpuPoolGranularityGrowsWithQuotaUpTo256MiB` and `NonGpuTierGranularityIsIndependentOfQuota` (new) pin the GPU size schedule and the host/disk granularities.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py::TestCacheQuotaPerRequest::test_gpu_alloc_granularity_matches_the_allocator_schedule` (new) pins the Python mirror. On the old code it fails 3 of 7 cases (the large quotas), and it passes on the new code. The existing 68 MiB one-request floor test is unaffected (its quota is < 1 GiB).
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kvcm2_integration.py::test_window_crossing_queries_log_level_only_on_a_crossing` (new): calls that cross no window must not query the logger. Run on the ToT CI build (x86 wheel, A10):
  - stock source: 2 failed / 15 passed (the new test fails, as intended);
  - patched: 17 passed;
  - reverted: 2 failed / 15 passed.

  The existing `test_window_crossing_*` tests cover logged content, severity order and per-module levels.
- All three files are already in CI: `l0_cpu.yml` (`unittest/_torch/executor`) and the `kvCacheManagerV2ConfigTest` gtest target.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Temporarily exclude five auxiliary-loss test functions (30 parameterized cases) from development CI using function-level `flaky_in_dev` markers:

| `test_force_balanced_aux_loss` | 5 |

All five functions reinitialize model parallel after `TestRouterAuxLoss.setup_method` has initialized it, exposing the shared process-group teardown/reinitialization race tracked in #7745. LTS eligibility, parameter values, assertions, and test bodies are preserved.

The confirmed recurring failure is in `test_force_balanced_aux_loss`: after #8206 quarantined `[8-1-1]`, [merge-queue job 116102125211](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38630673719/job/116102125211) reported a 1,800,000 ms store timeout in `[4-2-1]`. Its source includes the earlier quarantine. The four additional functions are precautionary containment of the shared initialization pattern, not claims of independently observed flakes. This expands the previous one-case exclusion to 30 cases, adding 29 development exclusions in total.

## Issue tracking

Related to #7745; extends #8206 while the initialization fix in #8164 is validated. This quarantine does not fix the race. Keep the issue open and restore coverage after repeated distributed validation.

@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Validate native sender WRITE destinations against remote NIXL registrations before backend submission. Invalid ranges and metadata-query errors fail only the affected request, retiring unsubmitted ownership without poisoning the sender. Actual backend submission failures retain the existing conservative ownership handling.

Implement the metadata query in the Python fallback and split C++ descriptor checks at advertised VMM registration boundaries, preserving valid cross-chunk transfers. No new configuration or low-level submission API restriction is introduced.

Scope: registration-range validation is not peer or tenant authorization. Direct backend use and access to deliberately registered/shared memory remain permitted; this change does not fully resolve the broader reported capability-sharing scenario.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6553508][fix] Reject conflicting LoRA adapter identities
items.author: yibinl-nvidia
items.summary: Bind each LoRA adapter ID to its canonical path and checkpoint source within a worker. Reject conflicting registrations before loading or enqueueing them, while preserving same-adapter reuse, path aliases, and existing ID-only lookup.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Bind each LoRA adapter ID to its canonical path and checkpoint source within a worker. Reject conflicting registrations before loading or enqueueing them, while preserving same-adapter reuse, path aliases, and existing ID-only lookup. Serialize registration and retain bindings for partially published adapter state; failed lookups that publish no state remain retryable.

The lock makes the identity check, first load, and binding one atomic operation. Without it, concurrent requests using the same new ID with different paths could both observe the ID as unbound and proceed to load, recreating the first-writer-wins collision that this change prevents.

This prevents silent cache identity collisions. It does not introduce tenant authorization: callers with access to the trusted ID-only API can still request an existing adapter. Adapter ownership and access control remain the application's responsibility.

TRTLLM_DSA_LOGITS_FULL_QUERY=1 lets eligible FP8 DSA logits process all query positions in one atom instead of rereading KV for split atoms. Gate on D=128, Q*H<=256, supported page tiles and FP32 accumulation/epilogue; cap cached weights per thread and retain the existing tail arithmetic.

items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Add default-off for residual-NVFP4 DSA generation. A request-local owner map deduplicates repeated gathers; group mode reuses the map across compatible shared-index layers while gathering each layer's own values and scales.
items.body:
## Description

Add default-off `TRTLLM_DSA_NVFP4_OWNER_WORKLIST=per_layer|group` for residual-NVFP4 DSA generation. A request-local owner map deduplicates repeated gathers; group mode reuses the map across compatible shared-index layers while gathering each layer's own values and scales.

Layout, capacity and group/stream checks retain the native gather on ineligible paths. Hash saturation retains independent owners. Each metadata object owns stable worklist storage, retained across capacity growth for captured users. The full FP8 scratch allocation remains. Startup captures the configured graphs before KV-capacity profiling, so their worklist allocations are included in the measured memory budget.

Stacked on #20339; land that scoped SM107 residual-NVFP4 DSA capability prerequisite first. This draft targets main and includes its prerequisite commit. This feature is independent of sorted TopK remapping.

Source: [internal commit #28](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dongfengy/tekit/-/commit/733aef6321556237a161cd0ee3cd634b0488a924).

items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: An asynchronous prefix hit currently occupies a forward batch's token and request budget before the loader is parked. With, park eligible loads during the scheduler scan so ready requests can use that budget in the same iteration.
items.body:
## Description

An asynchronous prefix hit currently occupies a forward batch's token and request budget before the loader is parked. With `TRTLLM_MOONCAKE_EARLY_ADMISSION=1`, park eligible loads during the scheduler scan so ready requests can use that budget in the same iteration.

Early admission is bounded by owner-local loader credits and full-prompt KV completion reservations. It preserves allocation-stream readiness and the existing cancellation/completion ownership protocol. Misses and unsupported configurations retain the normal path; separate draft/cross pools, PEFT, PP/CP, non-MAX_UTILIZATION policies and connectors using the prefix-reservation protocol are excluded.

Stacked on #20329. The incremental change adds scheduler early admission; its prerequisite async loader and recovery work should merge first.

items.title: [TRTLLM-17015][feat] VisualGen: wire async_ulysses for MiniMax-H3
items.author: karljang
items.summary: Wires the existing knob for MiniMax-H3 self-attention. With and, builds separate Q/K/V projections and dispatches to: V, then Q and K with H3's per-head RMSNorm and partial split-half RoPE, each pushed to the peers over symmetric memory while the next projec…
items.body:
## Description

Wires the existing `parallel_config.async_ulysses` knob for MiniMax-H3 self-attention. With `async_ulysses: true` and `ulysses_size > 1`, `MiniMaxH3Attention` builds separate Q/K/V projections and dispatches to `UlyssesAttention.forward_async`: V, then Q and K with H3's per-head RMSNorm and partial split-half RoPE, each pushed to the peers over symmetric memory while the next projection runs. Attention built with `enable_sequence_parallel=False` keeps the fused projection. The token refiner, which is Ulysses-sharded the same way, follows the same rule. The knob is opt-in and off by default; no public API changes. The docs bullet lists MiniMax-H3 among the models the knob is wired for.

**Performance** (MiniMax-H3, 768×1344, 124 frames, 28 steps, one 8×B200 node, FA4, `torch.compile` on, CUDA graphs off on both sides because the H3 pipeline rejects capture). Whole generations, the shipped path (fused Q/K/V GEMM, NCCL all-to-alls) and `async_ulysses` alternating in one process on the same loaded weights, 5 paired iterations per degree:

| Ulysses | shipped median | async median | S = T(shipped) / T(async) [95 % CI] | time reduction Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 15.68 s | 15.45 s | 1.015 [1.014, 1.015] | 1.5 % |
| 4 | 25.38 s | 24.78 s | 1.024 [1.024, 1.025] | 2.4 % |
| 2 | 45.18 s | 43.65 s | 1.034 [1.034, 1.035] | 3.3 % |

Rank-0 nsys per denoising step: NCCL time not under compute drops 40.7 → 14.0 ms at Ulysses 8, 63.7 → 20.9 ms at 4, 105.4 → 29.1 ms at 2 (the output all-to-all stays on NCCL); the pushes cost 15–30 ms of memcpy per step of which 9–20 ms run under the projection GEMMs; GEMM time rises 5–16 ms per step (three GEMMs instead of one) and GPU idle 2.5 → 8–13 ms. Peak memory per rank is unchanged (138.8 GB). Only the designed graph breaks (FA4 forward, async issue/join); no recompiles.

**Numerics.** Not bit-identical to the shipped path: the shipped path computes Q, K and V in one GEMM over the concatenated weights, this path in three GEMMs over the same rows, so bf16 rounding differs from the first block on and the 28-step denoising amplifies it. LPIPS-AlexNet of the async output against the shipped output is 0.090 / 0.090 / 0.079 at Ulysses 8 / 4 / 2 (PSNR 27 dB). Against a BF16 eager reference (shipped construction, `torch.compile` off), the shipped compiled output reads LPIPS 0.177 and the async output 0.143 at Ulysses 8 (0.173 vs 0.122 at Ulysses 2), so the change keeps the model as close to the eager reference as the shipped compiled path is today. The shipped path itself produces different bytes at Ulysses 2 than at 8 (LPIPS 0.047 between them). One prompt, one seed. There is no MiniMax-H3 golden in the E2E tests; the eager reference stands in for it. With separate projections on both sides, NCCL and async Ulysses are bit-identical.

### What changes

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/models/minimax_h3/transformer_minimax_h3.py`: `MiniMaxH3Attention` takes `enable_sequence_parallel`, chooses `SEPARATE_QKV` when async Ulysses applies, passes `async_ulysses` and `separate_qkv_is_self_attention=True` to `Attention`, and adds `forward_async` (the closures for V, Q and K with norm and RoPE; `forward` dispatches to it).
- `docs/source/models/visual-generation.md`: the Async Ulysses bullet names MiniMax-H3.

### Not in this PR

- CUDA graphs for MiniMax-H3 (the pipeline rejects capture for its packed-layout inputs); a separate feature, where `async_ulysses` would be re-measured with graphs on both sides.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_minimax_h3_transformer.py` (CPU, in `l0_b200.yml`): the async closures produce the sync path's Q/K/V and output (norm and RoPE on Q/K only); a fused-projection module stays on the sync path.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/multi_gpu/test_minimax_h3_parallel.py` (2 and 4 GPUs, in `l0_dgx_b200.yml`): async variant of the two-GPU H3 Ulysses test (VANILLA and FA4), loading the fused reference weights split into `to_q`/`to_k`/`to_v`.
- Both files run on a B200 node with this branch built from source: 82 passed (CPU) and 5 passed (multi-GPU).

The session-reuse cache keeps a finished test's idle MPI pool alive, and the 4-worker pool left by the preceding TP4 Qwen3-30B-A3B test still held about 33 GiB per GPU. `quickstart_advanced.py` runs as a child process, so it cannot use that pool and ran out of GPU memory while loading the model. items.title: MInf: Make logits dtype match the forward output dtype
items.author: tdene
items.summary: Right now, the dtype of the logits tensor pinned in inference does not always match the dtype of the logits emitted by the forward pass. Sampling and logprobs still convert the logits from whatever dtype they're in to FP32.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Right now, the dtype of the logits tensor pinned in inference does not always match the dtype of the logits emitted by the forward pass. Sampling and logprobs still convert the logits from whatever dtype they're in to FP32. But in addition to that, there is an undocumented conversion, where the dtype of the logits emitted by the forward pass is converted to some the params' dtype (which could be completely different) when it goes into the logits tensor. The first commit fixes this.

The second commit forces inference to use FP32 as the dtype of the logits tensor when this is possible.    
This has been discussed over the last year by the inference team; the consensus is that this is optimal, because sampling and logprobs need to convert the logits to FP32 anyway, so this saves both memory and latency.

items.title: refactor(training): migrate model configuration and shared consumers
items.author: cuichenx
items.summary: Make and authoritative for shared model construction and training-loop consumers (C10 of the training-loop consolidation). Callback paths get a typed model-provider config centrally; position capacity stays distinct from actual data sequence length.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Make `cfg.model` and `cfg.model.transformer` authoritative for shared model construction and training-loop consumers (C10 of the training-loop consolidation).

- Preserve GPT/Hybrid builders and BERT/T5/VLM/MIMO provider callbacks. Callback paths get a typed model-provider config centrally; position capacity stays distinct from actual data sequence length.
- Read model precision, topology, attention/MoE, recomputation, graph and freeze settings from config in startup, model setup, training/evaluation, warmup, FLOPs and memory estimates. Derive optimizer precision and runtime batch topology centrally. GPT/Hybrid embedding groups, batch layouts and sampler/collation selection use the same model owner.
- Restore model settings from existing checkpoint config metadata, retaining legacy checkpoint fallback and existing CLI override rules. Preserve nested Hybrid/MTP specs and activation settings through serialization.
- Keep TP user-buffer overrides on the existing model owners, with explicit actual sequence length and microbatch inputs. No new overlap config.
- Pass model-owned TP/divisibility inputs explicitly to tokenizer padding during training bootstrap; preserve explicit padded-vocabulary overrides and existing inference defaults. Tokenizer selection and policy remain separate.

Upcycling policy/native-builder changes remain a follow-up; existing callback upcycling is preserved. `modelopt_enabled` remains with the distillation integration (C17). Tokenizer, optimizer and scheduler ownership migrations are separate.

This is an independent draft on main. Integration with #7778, #8149, #8205 and #8202 must retain their distributed/training/DDP owners and centralized finalization contracts; this PR does not replace those migrations.

## Issue tracking

Related to #3554.

## Validation

Targeted existing unit modules on eight GPUs: **1,150 passed, 116 skipped per rank**, at `18fc331bf5ea10730268186c0ddee9ef59b08318`. Covers model builders/serialization, callback/MIMO boundaries, startup, checkpoint/resume, RNG, warmup, FLOPs/memory, logging, batch layouts and sampler/collation behavior. The skips are 113 layouts requiring more than eight GPUs and three GTP checks requiring Transformer Engine >=2.19. Includes divergent config/CLI inputs for model topology and vocabulary padding. Independent complete-diff and follow-up review are complete. This is not a full unit or functional-suite claim. No GPU kernel algorithm changes or new golden values.

All-files pre-commit reproduces existing Black/Pylint failures outside this change; isort passes. No unrelated formatting changes were included.

items.title: [hardware, doc] fix: update the TPU GRPO example for verl-hardware-plugin main (Ray 2.59 image, pip-installed plugin, no NOSET)
items.author: xiaoxlu
items.summary: Makes (scripts, README and image) work with, and prepares it for the plugin loading its vLLM patches through an entry point. verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#55 removed the plugin's workaround and relies on Ray (>= 2.59) assigning to each actor; with the var…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes `examples/tpu/grpo` (scripts, README and image) work with `verl-hardware-plugin` `main`, and prepares it for the plugin loading its vLLM patches through an entry point. Only `examples/tpu/grpo/` changes.

1. **Drop `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS`** from both scripts and the README. verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#55 removed the plugin's `TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` workaround and relies on Ray (>= 2.59) assigning `TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` to each actor; with the variable set, Ray assigns none and the trainer fails in `init_process_group` with `RuntimeError: create_process_group(): PjRtClient is not initialized.`
2. **Install the plugin with pip instead of shipping its source in `py_modules`**: `"pip": {"packages": ["verl-hardware-plugin @ git+https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin@main"], "pip_install_options": ["--no-deps"]}`. An installed package registers entry points; a directory on `sys.path` does not. verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#58 moves the vLLM patches to a `vllm.general_plugins` entry point and fails fast when it is missing. `--no-deps` keeps the image's torch/verl. The README also shows how to install a local checkout as a wheel (`${RAY_RUNTIME_ENV_CREATE_WORKING_DIR}`).

3. **Build the image on Ray 2.59 with torchtitan 0.3.0** (`Dockerfile`): plugin `main` needs Ray >= 2.59 (above) and supports torchtitan 0.3.0, so the base moves from `rayproject/ray:2.56.0-py312` to `2.59.0-py312` and torchtitan is installed from PyPI (`0.3.0`) instead of the google-pytorch fork at `f880cc73` (drops `/torchtitan`, `PYTHONPATH` and the fork-only `typeguard`/`spmd_types` pins). The other pins (torch, torch-tpu, tpu-sync, jax, libtpu, vLLM, vllm-torchtpu, transformers, TransferQueue) are unchanged.
4. **Pass build credentials as BuildKit secrets**: the build pulls the private `vllm-project/vllm-torchtpu` repository and `torch-tpu` from an authenticated index, which the previous `docker buildx build -t <IMAGE> ...` command had no credentials for. The `Dockerfile` now reads `GIT_AUTH_TOKEN.github.com` and `tpu_index_token` secrets (not stored in the image) and the README documents the command.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+tpu , https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

2x TPU v6e-8 on GKE (`NNODES_TRAINER=2 NNODES_ROLLOUT=2`), Qwen3-0.6B 5-step smoke test. Rows 1-4 use an existing image with Ray 2.59, torchtitan 0.3.0, torch-tpu 0.1.2, vLLM 0.29 + vllm-torchtpu; the last row uses an image built from this PR's `Dockerfile`. verl `main` and verl-hardware-plugin `main`.

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` as is (README `RUNTIME_ENV`, `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS=1`) | Fails in trainer init: `create_process_group(): PjRtClient is not initialized` |
| Only `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` removed (plugin still via `py_modules`) | 5/5 steps |
| This PR's README `RUNTIME_ENV` verbatim (plugin `main` pip-installed from git with `--no-deps`) | 5/5 steps |
| README's local-checkout variant with verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#58 built as a wheel | 5/5 steps; vLLM EngineCore and workers on both rollout hosts patched through the entry point |
| **Image built from this PR's `Dockerfile`** with the README build command (Ray 2.59.0, torchtitan 0.3.0), then this PR's README `RUNTIME_ENV` verbatim | 5/5 steps |


AI assistance (Jetski) was used to debug the failures, write the changes, run the TPU tests, and draft this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line.

Patch release fixing two cases of silently wrong training and three crashes.

Worth calling out: #7505 affects GRPO, RLOO and Distillation on the default generation path (use_vllm=False). Models that end a turn with an id only their generation config declares (Gemma 3/4, Phi-3.5, ...) did not stop at the end of the turn, and everything generated after it was trained on, up to max_completion_length. The only visible sign was completions/clipped_ratio close to 1. With vLLM, generation stopped correctly but the metrics were still wrong, and mask_truncated_completions=True dropped every finished completion. Runs on models whose tokenizer eos is their only end-of-turn id are unchanged.

What's Changed

  • Keep the DFT loss finite on a batch with no trainable tokens by @​albertvillanova in huggingface/trl#7471
  • Fix precompute_ref_log_probs under FSDP with no reference model by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7507
  • Fix: Start the completion where the tokenized prompt and prompt+completion diverge by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7463
  • End completions on every eos id the model declares in GRPO, RLOO and Distillation by @​albertvillanova in huggingface/trl#7505
  • Guard the requests and urllib3 imports in the vLLM client by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7545

Full Changelog: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/compare/v1.14.1...v1.14.2

v1.14.1

What's Changed

  • Fix the server-mode crash at the first weight sync on vLLM 0.20 to 0.25 by @​albertvillanova in huggingface/trl#7410
  • [Fix] Generate one completion per sample after tool calls in vLLM server mode by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7418
  • Preserve explicit model_init_kwargs in CLI scripts by @​DaoyuanLi2816 in huggingface/trl#7394
  • Honor resume_from_checkpoint in CLI scripts by @​DaoyuanLi2816 in huggingface/trl#7391

Full Changelog: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/compare/v1.14.0...v1.14.1

v1.14.0

Features

trl.losses is gone: DPO, KTO and GRPO stream their own log-probs

[!WARNING] from trl.losses import FusedLinearDPOLoss (or FusedLinearKTOLoss, FusedLinearGRPOLoss, FusedLinearJSDLoss) no longer works. The module introduced in v1.13 has been removed.

v1.13 vendored Liger's chunked_loss into trl.losses as a holding action, not a destination (#7063). The problem it was holding: those classes reimplement each trainer's loss math, so TRL carried two copies of every formula, and copies drift. That drift is where the bugs were. GRPO's grad_norm differed from the default path, KTO ignored the reference model under PEFT, KTO class weights and DPO label_smoothing were silently dropped. Worst of all, under plain DDP the fused path ran the loss on the unwrapped model, so DistributedDataParallel's reducer was never armed and gradients were never all-reduced: every rank silently kept its own.

The fix is to stop reimplementing. All DPO, KTO and GRPO need from the fused path is per-token log-probs of the selected tokens, and TRL already had _ChunkedLogProbFunction for exactly that: it streams the vocabulary with an online logsumexp and recomputes in the backward pass. Each trainer now runs backbone -> _ChunkedLogProbFunction -> its own existing loss code, unchanged. One implementation of each loss, and the memory win is kept, because full logits are still never materialized.

Thirteen restrictions existed only because the loss had been rewritten in a form that could not express those options. Most are gone: DPO with use_liger_kernel=True now accepts mixed loss types, f-divergences and precomputed reference log-probs, and GRPO gains entropy and off-policy masking. Still refused: use_weighting, compute_metrics, a PEFT adapter on lm_head, prompt-learning PEFT, and the MoE auxiliary loss.

Single H100, Qwen3-0.6B, bs=4, seq 512:

config median step peak
v1.13 fused, inline ref 0.2243 s 7.05 GB
v1.14 chunked, inline ref 0.2457 s (+9.5%) 7.05 GB
v1.14 chunked, precompute_ref_log_probs=True 0.1971 s (-12.1%) 4.83 GB (-31%)

The third row is the point: that configuration did not exist before, because the fused path rejected precomputed reference log-probs outright.

use_liger_kernel=True still works and still enables Liger's model kernels through transformers. In DPO, GRPO and KTO it now selects TRL's chunked log-probability path instead of Liger's fused loss.
