Updates the requirements on [av](https://github.com/PyAV-Org/PyAV) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from av's releases.

v17.1.0

Breaking

  • Remove the undertested av.option and av.descriptor APIs, along with the related Codec and Filter descriptor accessors.

Features

  • Use FFmpeg 8.1.1 in the binary wheels by @​WyattBlue.
  • Build Linux ARMv7 binary wheels by @​WyattBlue.
  • Expose AVCodecContext.global_quality by @​WyattBlue in #2246.
  • Expose Stream.discard so demuxing and seeking can skip unwanted streams by @​WyattBlue (#2272).
  • Add Stream.set_display_matrix() and Stream.set_display_rotation() to write the container display (rotation) matrix on output streams by @​hmaarrfk in #2287.
  • Add Container.video_codec_id to force a specific video codec on a container by @​WyattBlue (#2243).

Fixes

  • Add cython.final to leaf classes, ensuring that they are not subclassed by @​WyattBlue.
  • Warn that CodecContext.decode() is not memory safe in some cases.
  • Fix memory leaks in FFmpegError, AudioLayout channel layouts, and Frame.opaque, and break a reference cycle between FilterLink and Graph by @​lgeiger.
  • Reduce excessive logging lock contention by @​WyattBlue (#2276).
  • Fix a crash when accessing Stream from multiple threads under FFmpeg 8.1 by @​WyattBlue (#2247).
  • Fix a crash during InputContainer initialization by @​WyattBlue (#2010).
  • Fix enumerate_input_devices and enumerate_output_devices raising AttributeError by @​WyattBlue and @​kazuki (#2264).
  • Map HTTP 429 to HTTPTooManyRequestsError instead of UndefinedError by @​WyattBlue (#2267).
  • Fix crash in VideoFrame.to_ndarray() and to_image() on bottom-up frames with a negative line_size by @​WyattBlue (#2213).
  • Make Disposition an IntFlag so Stream.disposition can be assigned without raising TypeError by @​HotariTobu.
  • Assign parser-inferred pts, dts, and duration to packets from CodecContext.parse() by @​WyattBlue (#1919).
  • Copy time_base in add_stream_from_template() by @​daveisfera in #2249.
  • Fix the remux examples dropping keyframes that demux with no DTS, which produced audio-only output by @​WyattBlue (#1917).
  • Fix subtitle UTF-8 handling by @​jbree in #2271.
  • Fix several incorrect malloc size calculations by @​WyattBlue.

New Contributors

  • @​HotariTobu made their first contribution in PyAV-Org/PyAV#2257
  • @​jbree made their first contribution in PyAV-Org/PyAV#2271
  • @​kazuki made their first contribution in PyAV-Org/PyAV#2288

Sourced from av's changelog.

v17.1.0

Breaking:

  • Remove the undertested av.option and av.descriptor APIs, along with the related Codec and Filter descriptor accessors.

  • Reduce excessive logging lock contention by :gh-user:WyattBlue (:issue:2276).

items.body:
Bumps [transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers) from 5.12.1 to 5.19.0.
Release notes

Sourced from transformers's releases.

Release v5.19.0

New Model additions

EmbeddingGemma2

EmbeddingGemma 2 is a multimodal embedding model from Google built on the Gemma 4 architecture. It encodes text, images, audio, and video, individually or combined in one input, into a shared 768-dimensional vector space for cross-modal retrieval, semantic similarity, clustering, and classification. It uses Matryoshka Representation Learning, so embeddings can be truncated to 512, 256, or 128 dimensions. It also offers configurable visual and video token budgets, and unused vision or audio towers can be disabled at load time to save memory.

Links: Documentation

  • Smthn smthn (#49364) by @​vasqu in #49364

Breaking changes

All MoE models whose routers compute logits now return them when output_router_logits=True, following the Qwen3-MoE pattern (a router_logits recorder on the base model, MoeModelOutputWithPast from the backbone, and a MoE causal LM output from the head), so code that relied on the previous outputs or their absence should read the router logits from these output classes.

  • 🚨 Return router logits from every MoE model that computes them (#48920) by @​qgallouedec

Owlv2ForObjectDetection.embed_image_query now selects the query box with the highest objectness score, as in the original OWLv2 notebook, instead of the OWL-ViT heuristic, so image-guided query embeddings and detections may differ from earlier releases.

  • 🚨 Select the OWLv2 image query by objectness (#49200) by @​qgallouedec

The "paged|" prefix for SDPA and flash attention implementations is deprecated, so users should set the regular attention implementation (e.g. sdpa or flash_attention_2) for continuous batching instead of paged|sdpa or paged|flash_attention_2.

  • 🚨 Attention 🚨 Deprecate "paged|" prefix for SDPA and flash (#49112) by @​remi-or

The regular flash and SDPA attention functions (flash_attention.py, sdpa_attention.py) now support continuous batching directly, and "paged|..." implementations for these are redirected to them, while eager still requires the "paged|eager" prefix.

  • 🚨 Attention 🚨 Make regular attention support CB (#49101) by @​remi-or

In continuous batching, the cache update for the index-based and block-table paths is now fused into a single call, which slightly changes the cache update function's behavior and affects any custom code that calls the separate update paths.

  • 🚨 [CB] 🚨 Fuse update for index and block table path (#49088) by @​remi-or

Continuous batching internals changed in preparation for removing "paged": `max

  • 🚨 [CB] 🚨 Little fixes before removing "paged" (#49069) by @​remi-or

Parallelization

Expert parallelism gains a token-dispatch implementation, selected via the new ep_dispatch_experts plan rule and now the default for Qwen3 MoE and Mellum, which removes the requirement that EP size equal TP size. The Trainer was also adapted to work with expert parallelism, and the docs now note that PEFT adapters support tensor parallelism. A CI-related fix for pipeline-parallel chart2table inference was also included.

  • [distributed]: adapt Trainer to work Expert Parallel (#48873) by @​3outeille in #48873
  • [distributed] Add expert-parallel token dispatch, default for Qwen3 MoE (#48865) by @​3outeille in #48865
  • Fix pp chart2table inference (#49225) by @​zucchini-nlp in #49225
  • [docs] TP for PEFT adapters (#49060) by @​stevhliu in #49060

items.title: [Dev] Bound a chained optimizer's state staging to one manager's windows
items.author: HJSang
items.summary: Bounds a 's chunked-offload staging to one manager's two windows. Each chunked offload manager (#6244) stages state through two GPU windows, and a chain steps its children one at a time, yet a chain held one window set per child: - Every offloading child prefe…
items.body:
# What does this PR do ?

Bounds a `ChainedOptimizer`'s chunked-offload staging to one manager's two windows.

Each chunked offload manager (#6244) stages state through two GPU windows, and a chain steps its children one at a time, yet a chain held one window set per child:

- Every offloading child prefetched its first chunk during gradient finalization and held it through the earlier children's updates.
- A child freed its windows while its last D2H copies were still running. The caching allocator withholds such blocks until their `record_stream()` events complete, so the next child allocated new windows. `max_memory_allocated()` hides this; `active_bytes` shows it.

## Change

- Only the first offloading child prefetches ahead of the update; later children restore their first chunk when their own step begins. A LayerWise child counts as offloading through its nested Muon manager, and a nested chain in a later position defers too (LayerWise honors the flag).
- `ChainedOptimizer.prefetch_optimizer_state_for_step` follows each child's deferral instead of prefetching every child.
- The chain shares one `_StagingSlotPool` across its managers, like its transfer streams, and holds it around the children loop in `_step`. Each child hands the windows to the next instead of freeing them; every H2D already waits for the shared D2H stream, so the handover adds no wait. The windows are freed when the loop ends, before any post-step parameter staging such as the deferred MXFP8 sync.
- When a child starts its step it frees the windows of state dtypes it does not use, so a child with different state dtypes (e.g. Muon fp32 momentum next to Adam bf16 moments) does not keep its predecessor's windows alive.

## Memory

One H200, on `dev` at c3010d6: a bf16 MLP with hidden size 4096 split across a chain of three dense `DistributedOptimizer`s (134M parameters each), precision-aware FusedAdam, offload fraction 1.0, 128 MiB chunks. Peak is the maximum `active_bytes` above the pre-step level during the step:

| | `dev` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| step peak | 1536 MiB | **1024 MiB** (−33%) |
| step time | 108.2 ms | 109.4 ms |

The saving is exactly two staging windows: the second and third optimizers'. The peaks also include each optimizer's master window, which #8232 bounds. Parameters match a non-offloaded chain exactly. Step time rises about 1%, because later optimizers no longer prefetch their first chunk.

## Tests

- New `test_chained_managers_hand_staging_windows_over_while_d2h_drains`: the first manager's D2H is held behind a GPU sleep, so the second starts while it runs. The chain must stay within one manager's peak, and both managers' state must match plain Adam. Without the shared pool it fails at 9.0 vs 5.0 MiB.
- `test_chained_optimizer_defers_later_children_state_prefetch` now compares parameters against a non-offloaded chain; new unit tests cover LayerWise counting as the first child, a nested chain deferred from a later position, a deferred LayerWise prefetching only masters, the chain-level prefetch, and a child with a different state dtype freeing its predecessor's windows.
- `tests/unit_tests/test_optimizer_state_offloading.py` on H200: 58 passed, 1 skipped (`dev`: 51 passed, 1 skipped). `test_layer_wise_optimizer.py` skips entirely at a single rank, on `dev` too.

items.title: [Dev] Bound optimizer-owned master weights by the offload chunk size
items.author: HJSang
items.summary: Makes bound optimizer-owned master weights. Chunked optimizer-state offload (#6244) restored every selected master weight as one full window before the first state chunk, so the chunk size never bounded masters: - Optimizer-owned masters (precision-aware Fused…
items.body:
# What does this PR do ?

Makes `--optimizer-state-offload-chunk-size-mb` bound optimizer-owned master weights.

Chunked optimizer-state offload (#6244) restored every selected master weight as one full window before the first state chunk, so the chunk size never bounded masters:

- **Optimizer-owned masters** (precision-aware FusedAdam's `state['master_param']`, an fp32 copy or the int16 remainder of a bf16 parameter) are read only by the optimizer's own update. They are now ordinary chunk state: staged, updated and copied back with their chunk, and counted by the chunk planner.
- **MCore-owned masters** are read by main-to-model copies after the update, so they keep the full restore window.

One manager still cannot hold both kinds; `_validate_master_storage` rechecks this after lazy init.

## Memory

One H200, on `dev` at c3010d6: a bf16 MLP with hidden size 4096 (268M parameters) under a dense `DistributedOptimizer`, precision-aware FusedAdam (fp32 moments, int16 master remainders, the `store_param_remainders` default), offload fraction 1.0, 128 MiB chunks. Peak is the maximum `active_bytes` above the pre-step level during the step:

| | `dev` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| step peak | 768 MiB | **320 MiB** (−58%) |
| step time | 70.8 ms | 66.4 ms |

On `dev` the peak grows with the model, because the whole master window (2 bytes per parameter here) is restored at once; with this PR it stays at the chunk bound. Parameters match a non-offloaded run exactly.

## Tests

- New `test_optimizer_owned_masters_ride_with_their_state_chunk`: a chunk step never sees the whole master window on GPU, and the result matches a non-offloaded run bit for bit.
- `tests/unit_tests/test_optimizer_state_offloading.py` on H200: 52 passed, 1 skipped (`dev`: 51 passed, 1 skipped).

items.title: [Dev] Release MoE dispatcher routing tensors after combine
items.author: HJSang
items.summary: Releases the routing tensors the all-to-all dispatcher caches for as soon as combine has read them. stores, and the permutation mappings on the dispatcher, and they stayed there until the layer's next forward.
items.body:
# What does this PR do ?

Releases the routing tensors the all-to-all dispatcher caches for `combine_postprocess` as soon as combine has read them.

`MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher.dispatch_preprocess` stores `probs`, `routing_map` and the permutation mappings on the dispatcher, and they stayed there until the layer's next forward. `probs` carries the router's autograd graph back to the layer input, so under full activation recompute every MoE layer kept its checkpointed input and that input's gradient alive for the rest of the step.

`combine_postprocess` now drops them through `_release_routing_tensors()`, which `reset_transient_forward_state()` (#5869) also uses; that reset only runs in the EP A2A-overlap schedule. Shapes stay, because CUDA graph replay of the preprocess restores only tensor attributes.

The Flex dispatcher had the same leak: its comm managers (DeepEP, DeepEP v2, HybridEP, NCCL EP) kept `token_probs` after combine. Its `combine_postprocess` now calls the manager's existing `reset_transient_forward_state()`, whose attributes are documented as reassigned on the next forward and unread by backward.

## Memory

One H200, a `TransformerBlock` of MoE layers (alltoall dispatcher, TE spec), seq 4096, hidden 4096, 8 experts, top-2, forward + backward, on `dev` at c3010d6:

| | peak, `dev` → this PR | held by dispatchers after backward | step time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 layers, full recompute | 3875 → **3458 MiB** (−10.8%) | 481 → 0 MiB | 102.3 / 103.7 ms |
| 16 layers, full recompute | 7461 → **6531 MiB** (−12.5%) | 995 → 0 MiB | 170.4 / 172.5 ms |
| 8 / 16 layers, no recompute | unchanged | 1–2.5 → 0 MiB | within noise |

Flex dispatcher with the DeepEP backend, EP = 8 on 8×H200, 8 layers, full recompute (per rank): peak 2253 → **1836 MiB** (−18.5%), held by the comm manager after backward 482 → 0 MiB. Flex step time is unchanged. Measured in one process, alternating steps with the reset enabled and disabled (ABBA, 20 steps each): 107.6 vs 106.6 ms median with full recompute, 74.9 vs 77.0 ms without. Separate back-to-back runs on this box varied from 117 to 411 ms for the same configuration, so they cannot resolve the difference.

About 62 MiB per layer here, which matches the layer input plus its gradient (2 × 4096 × 4096 × 2 bytes); the saving scales with tokens per rank × hidden size × MoE layers. Not exercised: alltoall with EP > 1, the HybridEP / NCCL EP backends (not installed on the test box), CUDA graphs, the EP A2A-overlap schedule.

## Tests

`tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_a2a_token_dispatcher.py` on 8×H200, excluding `router_padding_for_fp8` (whose cases fail or hang depending on test order on `dev` too; each passes alone): 29 passed, 4 skipped on every rank, the same as `dev`. `test_token_dispatcher.py::TestFlexDispatcher`, DeepEP cases: 15 passed, 16 skipped on every rank, the same as `dev`. No new unit test.

## What does this PR do?

Fix MFSDP v2 checkpoint save and restart for expert-parallel MoE models. After #6215, a BF16 EP=2 run trains two steps but fails at its first checkpoint with `NotImplementedError: MFSDP v2 optimizer checkpointing does not support expert parallelism yet`.

Serialize optimizer state directly under MCore's global parameter names on TE >= 2.18. For TE < 2.18, preserve the empty-shard workaround and gather missing optimizer-state keys within each parameter's own dense or expert-DP mesh. Shard filtering, placeholder reconstruction and removal, and the gradient-clearing fallback run only under explicit TE version guards. This removes the single-mesh restriction that rejected EP checkpointing while preserving older-TE compatibility.

After loading model state, refresh BF16 compute weights from the restored FP32 main weights before the first resumed forward.

Use MCore's existing global expert names and optimizer checkpoint format. The standalone `experimental/checkpoint.py` loader now always refreshes compute weights after restoring state; remove its unused `sync_model_weights` option.

EP checkpoint coverage lives in `test_checkpoint.py`, with model setup local to the test and forward/backward delegated to `mcore_training_utils.run_forward_backward_on_microbatches`. It compares five resumed losses exactly against uninterrupted training. It covers EP=1/2/4 with the precision-aware optimizer enabled and BF16 optimizer state. GPU initialization uses the normal expert-parallel RNG stream to initialize distinct experts across EP ranks. This replaces the old test expecting EP checkpointing to be rejected. items.title: fix: allow background pinning during optimizer CUDA graph capture
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: Prevent background data-loader pinning from invalidating optimizer CUDA graph capture by setting, matching. During the first optimizer capture (step 4 with three warmup steps), a DataLoader pinning thread can need a fresh for a future batch.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Prevent background data-loader pinning from invalidating optimizer CUDA graph capture by setting `capture_error_mode="thread_local"`, matching `FullCudaGraphWrapper`.

During the first optimizer capture (step 4 with three warmup steps), a DataLoader pinning thread can need a fresh `cudaHostAlloc` for a future batch. The optimizer wrapper currently inherits PyTorch's `global` capture mode. In the controlled reproduction, the background allocation returns `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported` (900), invalidates capture, and causes the training thread to fail with an invalidated-capture allocator assertion or error 901.

`thread_local` is appropriate because the background allocation is pinned **CPU** memory for future input; the optimizer graph does not reference it or depend on its allocation being replayed. The optimizer operates on existing GPU parameters, gradients, and optimizer state. This change keeps the capture restrictions on the capturing thread while allowing independent background allocations. It does not add synchronization or make shared-memory races safe. See the [CUDA capture-mode semantics](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__CUDART__STREAM_1g9d0535d93a214cbf126835257b16ba85).

Re-enable `hybrid_llama3_proxy_mfsdp_v2_cuda_graph` in both the internal `mr` and GitHub `mr-github` scopes, removing the quarantine associated with #8218. The existing functional test covers full-iteration and optimizer graph capture with MFSDP v2.

## Validation

- Actual functional harness on PR head `b09a550a3`: `run_ci_test.sh` with the configured `ft_launcher`, `N_REPEAT=5`, and `ENABLE_LIGHTWEIGHT_MODE=false` on 8 H100s (Slurm job `6252334`). **5/5 repetitions passed**, each completing all 50 steps. All 250 logged losses exactly match the existing golden values (maximum difference **0**). Both memory checks passed: maximum difference **4,096 bytes**, under **0.000661%**, versus the existing 5% tolerance. Each repetition has one complete TensorBoard loss stream and only `attempt_0`; no crashes or automatic restarts. No race injection or changes to golden values/tolerances. This used the 26.08 development environment specified below.
- Patched `hybrid_llama3_proxy_mfsdp_v2_cuda_graph`, with real DataLoader pinning deliberately overlapped with optimizer capture: completes all 50 steps; all 50 losses are bit-identical to the existing golden values. The harness retains the first four pinned batches to force a fresh allocation and releases the fifth during optimizer capture. Training uses `torch.distributed.run` without restarts rather than CI's `ft_launcher`.
- Both full-model checks used the available development container with PyTorch `2.14.0a0+4fdf77b940.nv26.08`, CUDA 13.4, and Transformer Engine `2.19.0+5e52befd`. A separate reduced probe on the 26.09 base runtime reproduced failure with `global` in 3/3 trials and succeeded with `thread_local` in 3/3 trials.
- `tools/autoformat.sh`: Black, isort, pylint, Ruff, and mypy passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- The repository recipe parser selects the restored case for `mr`, `mr-github` / `L1`, and merge-group cadence; neither quarantined scope selects it anymore.

## Issue tracking

Fixes #8218. The controlled reproduction establishes this failure mechanism and the fix. The original CI logs show the matching downstream capture failure but do not trace the first invalidating CUDA API. TensorBoard selection of the first, truncated event file after a successful restart is a separate issue.

items.title: [None][feat] Add bounded asynchronous Mooncake prefix loading
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Allow single-rank and attention-DP owners to fetch Mooncake prefixes on background workers while the requests are parked outside the compute batch. Each worker owns its CUDA stream and staging slots, waits for allocation readiness on the manager's execution st…
items.body:
## Description

Allow single-rank and attention-DP owners to fetch Mooncake prefixes on background workers while the requests are parked outside the compute batch. Each worker owns its CUDA stream and staging slots, waits for allocation readiness on the manager's execution stream, and reports completion only after all accepted page groups are copied. Empty accepted offers complete successfully; failed loads use the context-restart path.

Add opt-in `async_load` (default false), `async_load_workers` (default 1), and `staging_buffer_bytes` (default 1GiB) under the current `mooncake_store` settings. Workers share one bounded async staging budget; the node check accounts for synchronous load/save pools plus that additional budget. Initialization waits for worker readiness. Failed drains retain ownership of store and staging buffers until they can be safely released.

The supported speculative configuration remains the unified-pool EAGLE-style MTP context path from the dependency. This uses main's pool/role interface.

**Dependency:** https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20328. This draft targets main and includes the prerequisite commits; merge/rebase after the dependency lands.

## Test Coverage

Carries source cases for asynchronous completion, grouped pages, staging limits, and failure/restart behavior. Python AST parsing, fatal Python static checks, `git diff --check`, and independent source review passed.

No builds, tests, GPU execution, or benchmarks were run. Runtime validation must cover stream ordering, cancellation, worker startup/shutdown, failed writes, and the staging ceiling.

The LLMArgs manifest generator could not run in this source-only checkout because the vendored `triton_kernels` dependency is unavailable. All three new settings use `telemetry=False`, so no golden-manifest change is expected; regeneration and config/telemetry review remain pending.

items.summary: A failed external prefix load can leave a context request with unusable reused KV or let a pending save publish pages that are being discarded. Report recoverable failures for a single owner or attention-DP owner, release the failed cache and reservations, res…
items.body:
## Description

A failed external prefix load can leave a context request with unusable reused KV or let a pending save publish pages that are being discarded. Report recoverable failures for a single owner or attention-DP owner, release the failed cache and reservations, reset the request to prefill, and drop request-bound saves before the pages are freed.

Keep coordinated tensor-parallel load failures fatal. The restart follows main's request-reset and context-rewind APIs and retains the existing pool configuration and shutdown behavior.

**Dependency:** https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20327. This draft targets main and includes the prerequisite commits; merge/rebase after that dependency lands.

## Test Coverage

Carries the source failed-load, request-restart, and stale-save regression cases. Python AST parsing, fatal Python static checks, `git diff --check`, and independent source review passed. No builds, tests, GPU execution, or benchmarks were run. Failure injection and cancellation/retry validation remain required before leaving draft.

items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Enable Mooncake context reuse with attention-DP owners and unified-pool EAGLE-style MTP. Route connector hooks to the local request owner, carry the MTP prefill layout and lookahead/alignment requirements, and reserve completion capacity while preserving cance…
items.body:
## Description

Enable Mooncake context reuse with attention-DP owners and unified-pool EAGLE-style MTP. Route connector hooks to the local request owner, carry the MTP prefill layout and lookahead/alignment requirements, and reserve completion capacity while preserving cancellation and preemption lifetimes.

Support is limited to context-only speculative requests with a cache transceiver and an actual unified target/draft KV pool. Vanilla MTP and separate draft pools remain unsupported; attention DP requires PP=1 and CP=1. Configuration must resolve to the supported model mode after loading its checkpoint metadata.

The implementation uses main's pool/role API and retains checkpoint identity, reuse scope, LoRA/multimodal keys, worker readiness, and shutdown draining. It does not restore the old donor CLI or old connector configuration.

**Dependency:** https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20326. This draft targets main and includes the prerequisite commits; merge/rebase after that dependency lands.

## Test Coverage

Carries the source ADP, connector-layout, Mooncake, and native reuse-alignment cases. Python AST parsing, fatal Python static checks, `git diff --check`, and independent source review passed. No builds, tests, GPU execution, or benchmarks were run. Validate multi-rank reuse, chunk boundaries, cancellation, transfer/recompute boundaries, and MTP correctness before leaving draft.

items.title: [None][fix] Reserve and reclaim speculative KV slack during overlap
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Speculative overlap can advance device-side KV positions beyond host bookkeeping before draft KV is appended. Reserve an additional verification window, track the full allocated draft width through padding and unpaired draft growth, and reclaim unused slots wi…
items.body:
## Description

Speculative overlap can advance device-side KV positions beyond host bookkeeping before draft KV is appended. Reserve an additional verification window, track the full allocated draft width through padding and unpaired draft growth, and reclaim unused slots without shrinking below non-helix committed history.

Use the same upper bound for runtime quotas, static cache sizing, and block-offset metadata. Also fail early when disaggregated one-model MTP through the legacy cache transceiver puts its draft layers outside the transferred target pool; connector-managed layouts keep their own validation.

## Test Coverage

The existing disaggregated transition capacity case now expects 137 slots for a 128-token capacity and four draft tokens. Python AST parsing and `git diff --check` passed; independent source review checked runtime allocation against the common sizing helper.

No builds, tests, model execution, or benchmarks were run. Before leaving draft, validate overlap across block boundaries, padding/ragged speculation, dynamic draft reserves, disaggregated MTP, and helix-specific capacity accounting.

## Description

#13900 moved ADP dummy-role detection from `validated_requests`, which already contained `LlmRequest` objects, into `_update_adp_dummy_role()`, called immediately after routing. At that earlier point, the inputs are still `RequestQueueItem` wrappers.

The move left the parameter type as `List[LlmRequest]` and continued reading `llm_request_type` from each input. The wrappers do not have that field, so the helper misses the request's role. This code later reached main through #15222.

This PR changes the input type to `list[RequestQueueItem]`, reads `candidate.request.request_type` directly, and updates the tests to use queue-item inputs.

## Test Coverage

Updated role-selection tests to use `RequestQueueItem` wrappers with executor request types. Coverage includes context-only, generation-only, role changes, disabled attention DP, non-disaggregated workers, mixed-role ordering, and empty candidate lists. items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes the TPU GRPO examples (`examples/tpu/grpo`) on Ray `< 2.59.0` and ensures the full 100-step Qwen3-4B GRPO training run completes end-to-end without HBM fragmentation/exhaustion:

1. **Remove `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS=1` from TPU GRPO scripts and `README.md`**:
   - Complementing #8233, remove `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS=1` from `examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh`, `examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`, and `examples/tpu/grpo/README.md` so Ray populates `TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` per worker on Ray `< 2.59.0`.
2. **Set default `MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=2` in `examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`**:
   - In #8226 (`MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=4`), only 10 steps (`TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10`) were tested and libtpu already logged `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED ... Fragmentation` allocation retries on the 33.54 GB v6e trainer chips. Over a full 100-step run, `MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=4` eventually hits unrecoverable HBM fragmentation (`tt_jit_gather` / `reduce_scatter_tensor` reservation failure at step 37).
   - Combined with per-micro-batch backward TPU synchronization (`tpu_synchronize(wait=True)` from `verl-hardware-plugin` PR https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin/pull/57, merged as `e5ab532`), setting `MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=2` keeps trainer HBM safely within 33.54 GB across all 100 steps while maintaining the same end-to-end step time (since steps in `separate_async` mode overlap trainer updates with vLLM rollout generation).
3. **Pin `verl-hardware-plugin` commit and update expected step time in `examples/tpu/grpo/README.md`**:
   - Check out commit `e5ab532ae41a582bd2e9183c5deaf2bd8876045f` right after cloning `verl-hardware-plugin`: the current `main`, where https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin/pull/57 landed, so no extra `git fetch` of a PR commit is needed.
   - Update expected Qwen3-4B step time in `README.md` to `20-30 s per step (~25 s average over 100 steps)`.

### Benchmark & Comparison with #8226 (2x TPU v6e-4 slices: 4 trainer chips + 4 rollout chips)

items.title: [None][perf] Defer redundant DSA indexer preparation for speculative decode
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Pure-generation DSA speculative overlap prepares indexer slot mappings and MQA-logits schedules on the host preparation path, then rebuilds both from corrected device KV lengths before the model forward. The first device writes are redundant.
items.body:
## Description

Pure-generation DSA speculative overlap prepares indexer slot mappings and MQA-logits schedules on the host preparation path, then rebuilds both from corrected device KV lengths before the model forward. The first device writes are redundant.

The decoder runner now explicitly defers those indexer-only writes when a complete pre-forward refresh is guaranteed. The gate requires exact DSA metadata, speculative overlap, no attention DP and no context parallelism. Context batches and standalone metadata preparation preserve the existing behavior. Host indexer parameters and the zero context-token count are still prepared. `TRTLLM_STEP_PROLOGUE_TRIM=0` restores the original path.

This PR ports only the deferred indexer preparation portion of the internal step-prologue optimization. #19989 overlaps with shared executor work, but its custom gather/scatter kernels are SM100-only and do not cover every remaining source #37 change. #20353 separately ports direct gathers for the Torch path, and #20354 builds on this PR to remove additional redundant DSA uploads. The original process-global table-copy cache is excluded because it retains destination storage beyond the owning metadata/engine lifetime. This PR remains independent of #19989 and the MTP tail-trim PR.

## Test Coverage

Python AST parsing, Ruff formatting, fatal Python error checks, and `git diff --check` passed. No builds, runtime tests, GPU execution, or performance measurements were run, as requested. Draft pending correctness and performance validation with DSA speculative overlap, CUDA graphs, context-to-generation transitions and draft cache managers.

items.title: [None][perf] Reduce MTP argmax packing and redundant DSA updates
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Speculative decoding with TP-sharded logits currently launches separate local-max, cast, offset and packing operations before gathering draft token candidates. DSA also rebuilds indexer schedules during draft steps that reuse TopK indices and repeats a metadat…
items.body:
## Description

Speculative decoding with TP-sharded logits currently launches separate local-max, cast, offset and packing operations before gathering draft token candidates. DSA also rebuilds indexer schedules during draft steps that reuse TopK indices and repeats a metadata refresh immediately before overlap scheduling replaces the KV lengths.

This change fuses local argmax and pair packing into one Triton launch, retaining the existing TP allgather and first-index/NaN ordering. Unsupported logits take the original path. It skips redundant DSA schedule work only for index-reusing/final MTP steps, continues to refresh cache mappings and indptrs, and rejects fresh TopK computation if the schedule is stale. The existing `TRTLLM_MTP_TAIL_TRIM=0` switch disables the optimizations.

This is a partial extraction of the internal MTP tail optimization. The custom MNNVL mailbox is deliberately deferred: its process-global allocation cache needs integration with current workspace, checkpoint and sleep lifecycles. This PR keeps the existing collective ownership. Main already contains the source hidden-state gather/slice optimization; pending #19989 covers other executor overhead reductions. Neither is a prerequisite for this PR.

## Test Coverage

Python AST parsing, `git diff --check`, Ruff formatting checks on the new helper and modified DSA/runner files, full Ruff checks on the new helper, and fatal Python error checks on the other changed files passed. No builds, runtime tests, GPU execution, or performance measurements were run, as requested. Draft pending correctness and performance validation, including NaN/tie argmax behavior, MTP index sharing, CUDA graphs and overlap scheduling.

items.body:
## Description

Fuse the FP8 DSA indexer LayerNorm, RoPE, Q/K quantization and weight scaling into one Triton launch, with K-cache scatter included on the eager/whole-graph path. ## Description

The scaled-GEMM operator caches one cuBLAS wrapper per host thread, although its underlying cuBLAS handles belong to a CUDA context. Reusing the thread on another device can therefore reuse handles from the wrong context.

Key the workspace cache by CUDA context and stream as well, so distinct contexts on the same device do not share a workspace pointer. items.title: [None][fix] Keep single-tier KV requests active when generation allocation stalls
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: Consider a disaggregated decode worker with GPU-only KV storage and 64-token blocks: - Request A has filled its current block and needs another block for its next token. Previously, A's allocation failure could cause the scheduler to suspend B and then A.
items.body:
## Description

Consider a disaggregated decode worker with GPU-only KV storage and 64-token blocks:

- Request A has filled its current block and needs another block for its next token.
- Request B has used 50 tokens in its current block and will finish at token 60.
- There are no free blocks, but B can still finish using space it already owns.

Previously, A's allocation failure could cause the scheduler to suspend B and then A. With no secondary cache tier, suspension retains their KV pages rather than making those blocks available. B is stopped even though it could have finished and released its blocks.

This PR checks `can_evict` before attempting victim or self-suspension. In the example, A is skipped and B can continue. Once B finishes and releases its blocks, A can proceed. Existing recompute-preemption remains available, and deadlock handling is unchanged: if every request really needs an unavailable new block, skipping alone cannot resolve the shortage.

Two examples explain the accompanying changes:

- **Batch beam width:** Suppose A has beam width 4 but cannot allocate KV, while B has beam width 1 and can run. If A sets the batch beam width before allocation succeeds, skipping A still leaves the batch locked to 4 and incorrectly excludes B. The batch beam width is now established only by a successfully admitted request.
- **Resuming after an overlap gap:** Suppose the previous batch ran A and B, but the current batch runs only B. After the previous results are consumed, A's latest token is already recorded in its host token history. Retaining A's old `py_batch_idx` would make its next decode step use the continuous-overlap input path; in plain decoding, that computes the token position one step too far ahead. Clear A's index after consuming the previous results, while keeping B's current index. This also covers requests that just finished their last context chunk.

The same index cleanup is applied when draining an overlap batch for KV-pool rebalancing. Actual self-suspension still returns `STOP`; allocation failures that do not suspend the request return `SKIP`, including secondary-tier cases where the request is already suspended or has a pending connector load.

## Test Coverage

Focused scheduler, iteration-statistics, and overlap-index tests: **362 passed**, with zero failures, errors, or skips on ComputeLab A10. The small-cache Mooncake integration test passed twice before the test-only simplification; runtime behavior and that integration test are unchanged. Formatting, lint, and diff checks passed.

The CI follow-ups prevent selecting more victims while a connector save is pending, count completed deferred pauses once, and isolate the Mooncake test's per-engine ledger. The simplified tests keep the same assertions in the existing test modules.

## PR Checklist

items.title: [None][fix] Flush overlap KV cache events on every attention DP rank
items.author: dongfengy
items.summary: This PR changes where KV-cache events are flushed, so attention-DP ranks reach the event collective in the same order. KV-cache events are records of cache changes. [Discussion: The rebalance path also flushes events after consuming a previous batch.]
items.body:
## Description

This PR changes **where KV-cache events are flushed**, so attention-DP ranks reach the event collective in the same order.

KV-cache events are records of cache changes. In the **V2 buffered-event path**, flushing these records performs an `allgather`, which requires every participating rank to make the corresponding call—even if its local event list is empty.

Previously, `_add_kv_cache_events()` was called **inside** `_process_previous_batch()`. But the overlap loop only calls that helper conditionally:

```python
if self.previous_batch is not None and should_process_previous_batch:
    self._process_previous_batch()  # Also flushes KV-cache events internally.
else:
    self._enqueue_responses([])
```

That condition can differ between ranks. For example, rank 0 may process its previous batch and enter the event `allgather`, while rank 1 skips that branch. Their collective calls then become misaligned, potentially causing a hang.

The PR removes event flushing from the helper and places it **after the `if/else`**:

```python
if self.previous_batch is not None and should_process_previous_batch:
    self._process_previous_batch()  # No longer flushes events internally.
else:
    self._enqueue_responses([])

if self.enable_kv_cache_events:
    self._add_kv_cache_events()
```

Now both branches reach the same event-flushing point. Keeping it after batch processing also includes events generated by that batch’s resource updates.

There is one additional caller: `_consume_previous_batch_for_rebalance()`. It previously received event flushing indirectly through the same helper. After removing that internal call, the PR explicitly restores it there:

```python
self._process_previous_batch()
if self.enable_kv_cache_events:
    self._add_kv_cache_events()
```

This explains **one deletion and two additions**: remove the call from the shared helper, place it at the common point in the normal overlap loop, and preserve it in the separate rebalance path.

## Test Coverage

- `git diff --check` and Python AST parsing passed.
- Builds, unit tests, multi-rank execution, and benchmarks were not run locally; runtime validation is delegated to CI.
- Validation should cover KV event collection with rank-divergent previous-batch state and with pool-rebalance draining.

items.title: [None][perf] Use the copy engines for large host<->GPU page copies in KVCacheManagerV2
items.author: tzulingk
items.summary: KVCacheManagerV2 has two generic host<->GPU copy helpers, and, that move a batch of pages with a batched copy kernel: one 128-thread CTA per page with 8 KiB in flight, which caps every page at a few GB/s whatever the link. That is fine for the many small atte…
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

KVCacheManagerV2 has two generic host<->GPU copy helpers, `copyHostToDevice` and `copyDeviceToHost`, that move a batch of pages with a batched copy kernel: one 128-thread CTA per page with 8 KiB in flight, which caps every page at a few GB/s whatever the link. That is fine for the many small attention pages of a batch, but a 217 MB recurrent-state page of a hybrid model such as Kimi K3 then takes tens of milliseconds, and the execution stream waits for it. This PR sends calls with large pages to the GPU copy engines instead (one `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` per call on the caller's stream) and leaves everything else on the kernel.

**Where this applies on main.** Since #17512 and #18541, hot<->host migrations (eviction, onboard, prefetch, `copySlotData`) go through `IKvCacheColdPageCodec` and `BatchedPageCopier`, not through these two helpers. On main they serve `CopyEngine::transfer`, i.e. migrations between two cold levels when one of them is a GPU memory level, and the `copy_host_to_device` / `copy_device_to_host` bindings. The end-to-end gain below (+6.0 % output tokens/s per GPU, 0.8 s less TTFT at the median) was measured on a deployment built from a branch that predates the cold-page codec, where these helpers were the only GPU<->host copy path. The change is posted as the measured, self-contained version of the idea; the section "Measurements on main's path" at the end shows what the same comparison looks like against `BatchedPageCopier` and what a follow-up for main would be. If the maintainers consider the helper-level branch redundant on main, closing this PR in favour of that follow-up is a fine outcome.

### The problem

- **The host copy kernel moves one page with one thread block.** `launchBatchedCopy(lowBandwidth=true, ...)` sets `nbSplits = 1`, so each (page, pool) task gets a single 128-thread CTA. The block copies 16 B per thread per step through a ring of four shared-memory buffers, so it never has more than 4 x 128 x 16 B = 8 KiB of loads outstanding. Bandwidth is bytes in flight divided by the latency of those loads, so one task is capped at a few to low tens of GB/s however fast the link is:

  ```
  bandwidth = bytes in flight / load latency
            = 8,192 B / (0.5 to 4 us)  =  16 to 2 GB/s
  ```

  The measured 1.8 to 17.5 GB/s per CTA fit that range. The stores are posted, so device->host is bounded by device-memory load latency and only host->device by the link round trip, which is why the two directions differ. Keeping a 400 GB/s link busy would need about 400 GB/s x 2 us = 800 KiB in flight; one task supplies 8 KiB, about 1 % of that. A batch of many small pages is still fast because every page gets its own block; a single large page is not.
- **Hybrid models have large pages.** Kimi K3 (MLA attention plus KDA linear-attention layers, NVFP4) keeps two recurrent-state pages per rank, 217,055,232 B (KDA SSM state) and 15,261,696 B (conv state), next to its 884,736 B MLA pages. Every request restores one state snapshot from the host tier and later evicts one to it, so the large pages cross the link twice per request.
- **What a profile of one prefill rank shows (44.9 s window at steady load, on the branch described above):**
  - 1,107 single-block host copies adding up to 31.5 s of kernel time in the 44.9 s window. Half of them finished in under 1.9 ms (small pages); the slowest 5 % took longer than 136 ms (state pages), the longest 237.7 ms.
  - A 434 MB fp32 state page took 24.8 to 237.7 ms, which is 1.8 to 17.5 GB/s for its one block.
  - At those rates the 217 MB bf16 state page takes 12 to 120 ms. The copy engines of the same NVLink-C2C system move it in about a millisecond.
- **The time is on the critical path.** The storage manager records an event after each copy and the consumers wait on it in-stream, so a compute-bound prefill stalls until the page has landed. Per request the traffic is modest, about 458 MB out and 442 MB in; the problem is how slowly each large page moves, not how much data moves.
- **Adding blocks is the wrong fix here.** The prefill already uses every SM, while the copy engines sit idle. #18541 reached the same conclusion for PCIe parts and uses `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` there, "which also costs zero SMs".

### The change

`copyHostToDevice` / `copyDeviceToHost` in `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2Utils.cu` share one dispatch, `copyAcrossHostLink<HostToDevice>`: the copy-engine branch when the call is non-empty, `numBytes > 0` and `useCopyEngineForHostCopy(numBytes)` is true, `launchBatchedCopy(true, ...)` unchanged otherwise. `copyDeviceToDevice` is untouched. The predicate is

```
!HostMem::shouldUseChunkedRegistration() && numBytes >= MIN_BYTES
```

| knob | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_HOST_COPY_DMA_MIN_BYTES` | 4 MiB | smallest per-task size that uses the copy engines; `0` = any size, negative = never (today's behaviour) |

With the default an 884,736 B attention page stays on the kernel and the two state pages go to the copy engines. The knob is read once per process; a value that is not an integer, or is out of range, is reported at WARNING and ignored. The copy-engine branch submits all tasks of the call with one `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` on the caller's stream and returns the `CUresult`; on the legacy NULL stream (`0` or `CU_STREAM_LEGACY`), which the batched call does not accept, it issues one `cuMemcpy*Async` per task. The dispatch also rejects a negative byte count, and a byte count the kernel launcher's `uint32_t` cannot carry, with `TLLM_CHECK_WITH_INFO` instead of letting them wrap.

Other files:

- `kvCacheManagerV2Utils.h`: declarations of `hostCopyDmaMinBytes()`, `hostCopyDmaMinBytesFor(rawValue)` (the knob's semantics on a raw value, so tests can drive them without resetting the process-wide cache), `kHostCopyDmaMinBytesEnv` and `useCopyEngineForHostCopy()`, plus the contract of the two entry points: the kernel path requires a multiple of 16 and 16 B-aligned task addresses, the copy-engine path accepts any size and alignment, and the reach stated above.
- `nanobind/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2Utils.cpp`: `use_copy_engine_for_host_copy(num_bytes)` next to the copy helpers, so tests can ask which path a task size takes. The `copy_*` signatures are unchanged.
- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2TestUtils.h`: the `CudaAllocation` / `allocateCuda` and `ScopedEnv` helpers that the sibling KVCM2 tests each carried a copy of, as shared inline definitions (the siblings keep their copies for now).

### Design notes

- **Why one driver call per call.** A call is one `copyHostToDevice` / `copyDeviceToHost` invocation; `CopyEngine::transfer` issues one per pool, so all tasks (pages) of a call have the same size but sit at scattered addresses. `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` takes the destination, source and size of every task and submits them in one driver call, so the CPU cost does not grow with the page count and no task limit is needed. It is the same call `batchedPageCopy.cu` uses on PCIe parts, with the same attributes, and TensorRT-LLM builds with CUDA 13, where it is always available.
- **Why the same stream.** The copies are enqueued on the stream the caller passes, after its prior-event waits and before the finish event it records, so the ready event consumers wait on still covers them. The batch is stream-ordered as a whole; copies inside a batch have no mutual order, which is fine because the tasks of one call read and write disjoint slots, as the kernel launch they replace already requires.
- **Why chunked registration disables it.** One memcpy may not span two `cuMemHostRegister` ranges, and `HostMem` registers the host tier in 2 GiB chunks on Linux 6.11-6.13. Those hosts keep the kernel, which reaches pinned memory through ordinary loads and stores. Same rule as `batchedPageCopy.cu`.
- **Why not `BatchedPageCopier`.** It is driven by `PoolCopyArgs` (base, stride, index pairs) for bulk uniform-page copies and sizes a CTA grid per platform. This path receives the pages of one migration batch as a plain task vector (one or two large state pages per request, a whole batch on eviction or prefetch), where a copy-engine enqueue needs no tuning and no SMs.
- **Exceptions.** Since #19103 the two entry points may throw (the kernel path rejects unaligned sizes with `TLLM_CHECK`); they keep that signature and now also throw on a negative byte count. The policy helpers (`hostCopyDmaMinBytes`, `hostCopyDmaMinBytesFor`, `useCopyEngineForHostCopy`) are `noexcept`; the warning for a bad knob value is guarded so it cannot turn into `std::terminate`. `copyWithCopyEngine` is not `noexcept`, because its descriptor vectors can throw `std::bad_alloc`, which the entry points propagate.

### Measured effect

A/B on a Kimi K3 disaggregated deployment (16 single-GPU prefill workers plus a 16-GPU decode worker, 32 GPUs): fixed concurrency, 1 h windows, identical configuration and observability.

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| output throughput per GPU | 744.2 tok/s | 789.2 tok/s (+6.0 %) |
| TTFT p50 | 5.98 s | 5.19 s |
| prefill iteration p50 | 2.59 s | 2.39 s |
| per-request prefill time p50 | 2.38 s | 2.03 s |
| per-user decode speed p50 | 65.4 tok/s | 64.0 tok/s (-2.1 %) |
| host bytes per request (offload / onboard) | 458 / 442 MB | 443 / 440 MB |

The copies get faster, not fewer. The attention-page batches (140 x 884,736 B per request) keep the kernel and are unaffected.

**Which build was measured.** The A/B ran the first version of this change: one `cuMemcpyHtoDAsync` / `cuMemcpyDtoHAsync` per task on the caller's stream, with calls of more than 8 tasks kept on the kernel (a task-limit knob, since removed), compiled into a production image whose KV cache manager predates the cold-page codec (#17512), so that `copyHostToDevice` / `copyDeviceToHost` were its only GPU<->host copy path. The code in this PR submits each call as one `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` with `CU_MEMCPY_FLAG_PREFER_OVERLAP_WITH_COMPUTE` and no task limit. Per-request state migrations carry one task per pool, so the shapes behind the numbers above are single-task calls on both variants; the submitted path has been timed per page (tables below) but not A/B-tested end to end.

### Measurements on main's path

To see whether the idea still has value on main, where hot<->host migrations run through `BatchedPageCopier`, the three paths were timed on the same shapes on one GB300 node (NVLink-C2C, 152 SMs, CUDA 13.4): this PR's helpers at the default threshold (copy engines), the same helpers with `MIN_BYTES=-1` (the pre-PR single-block kernel) and `BatchedPageCopier::launch`, which selected its multi-CTA kernel on that coherent link (4 blocks for offload, 6 for onboard, sized for the 224 GB/s fallback link figure because NVML reported no C2C bandwidth on that node). Event-to-event, 10 iterations after warm-up, pinned `HostMem` buffers.

Idle GPU:

| shape | copy engines (this PR) | `BatchedPageCopier` kernel (main) | single-block kernel (before) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 x 217,055,232 B, host->device / device->host | 211 / 193 GB/s | 201 / 185 GB/s | 9.6 / 15.9 GB/s |
| 12 x 15,261,696 B | 211 / 193 GB/s | 202 / 185 GB/s | 103 / 189 GB/s |
| 140 x 884,736 B | 209 / 192 GB/s (kernel path at the default) | 203 / 186 GB/s | 209 / 192 GB/s |
| 64 x 4,194,304 B | 211 / 193 GB/s | 202 / 185 GB/s | 211 / 193 GB/s |

Both the copy engines and main's kernel sit at the link ceiling of that node (about 210 GB/s per direction per GPU); the copy engines are 4 to 5 % ahead. The single-block kernel is 13 to 22x slower on a single large page, which is the gap the A/B above closed.

Same node, every SM thread slot occupied by a spin kernel on another stream (blocks of 0.1 ms or 5 ms, launched back to back), host->device, milliseconds per copy:

| shape | load | copy engines (this PR) | `BatchedPageCopier` kernel (main) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 x 217 MB | none | 1.03 ms | 1.08 ms |
| 1 x 217 MB | 0.1 ms blocks | 1.03 ms | 1.2 to 2.0 ms |
| 1 x 217 MB | 5 ms blocks | 1.03 ms | 3.8 to 4.5 ms |
| 12 x 15 MB | 5 ms blocks | 0.87 ms | 3.9 to 4.5 ms |

The copy engines use no SM, so their time does not change under load; the kernel's blocks wait for a free slot, and giving the copy stream the highest priority did not help, because resident blocks are not preempted. Persistent-scheduled GEMM and attention kernels in a long prefill behave like the 5 ms case. So on coherent links main's production path ties the copy engines when the GPU is idle and loses 1.2 to 4x in copy latency when it is saturated. The follow-up for main is #20426, an option that lets `BatchedPageCopier` prefer its existing copy-engine path on coherent links (keeping the kernel where pinned memory is registered in chunks); this PR does not touch `BatchedPageCopier`.

## Test Coverage

### New tests

`cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2HostCopyTest.cu` (gtest target `kvCacheManagerV2HostCopyTest`, one GPU, linked with `kvCacheManagerV2PoisonCheck.cpp` like its neighbours). The knob is cached per process, so the tests pick shapes on both sides of the default instead of changing the environment, and every path-dependent expectation asks the predicate first, which lets the same binary run under any knob value:

- `ThresholdFromRawValue`: `hostCopyDmaMinBytesFor()` on raw values: unset, empty, `4abc` and a 20-digit value give the default, `0` gives 0, `-1` gives never, `16777216` gives 16 MiB.
- `ThresholdFollowsEnvironment`: the cached accessor equals the parser applied to the process environment, and the predicate over {16 B, 884,736 B, 4 MiB - 1, 4 MiB, 15,261,696 B, 217,055,232 B} follows it.
- `HostToDeviceToHost` (parametrised): byte-exact `HostMem` -> `cudaMalloc` -> `HostMem` round trips in the slot layout of a host pool for (884,736 B x 1 / 140 / 300), (16 B x 300), (15,261,696 B x 1 / 12), (217,055,232 B x 1) and (4 MiB x 8 / 64). 300 > 256 exercises the kernel's multi-launch remainder; the x 12 and x 64 shapes send many large pages through one batched call. The fill is pseudo-random per 64-bit word, so no two slots carry the same bytes and a permuted or slot-0 source read is caught.
- `NonMultipleOf16`: 3 x 24 B and 3 x (4 MiB + 8 B). A size the predicate sends to the copy engines must round-trip (they accept any size); a size it keeps on the kernel must throw `TllmException` from both entry points before any CUDA work. At the default the first throws and the second round-trips.
- `NegativeByteCountIsRejected`, `EmptyTaskListIsANoOp`, `NullStreamAccepted` (the per-task fallback on `0` and on `CU_STREAM_LEGACY` with 1 and 3 large pages, and the kernel) and `StreamOrderingThroughEvents` (producer stream -> recorded event -> consumer stream sees the bytes; a host-function gate holds the producer until everything is enqueued, so the check is deterministic rather than won by timing).
- `StateSlotBandwidthInfo`: records the GB/s of one 217 MB page per direction and the path that moved it as test properties. Not asserted.

`tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_copy_engine_host_copy.py` (one GPU; the directory is already in the `l0_a10`, `l0_h100` and `l0_b200` lists): round trips through the bindings for (884,736 B x 140 / 300), (16 B x 300), (4 MiB x 44), (15,261,696 B x 1), (217,055,232 B x 1) and 3 x (4 MiB + 8 B), with torch pinned and device buffers on a non-default stream; the predicate against an expectation computed from the environment and the kernel version, not from the predicate itself; a 24 B task, which the kernel rejects and the copy engines accept; the legacy NULL stream; and a consumer stream observing a copy through a recorded event. `test_copy_helper_exceptions.py` skips its two host-helper cases when the knob sends a 1 B task to the copy engines, so the directory runs under `MIN_BYTES=0` as well.

### Existing coverage

`test_copy_helper_exceptions.py` is the only existing test that calls `copy_host_to_device` / `copy_device_to_host`; it never performs a copy (1 B, unaligned, fake addresses) and, with the default threshold, is rejected on the kernel branch before any CUDA work. The host-tier cases of `test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py` do not reach the two entry points: `StorageManager::submitMigrationBatch` routes GPU<->host migrations through `IKvCacheColdPageCodec::encode` / `decode`. The two new tests are therefore the only coverage of the copy-engine branch and of `useCopyEngineForHostCopy`.

|---|---|
| clang-format, cmake-format, codespell, ruff, ruff-format on the changed files | clean |

Thanks for spelling out the `BatchedPageCopier` follow-up; I opened it as #20364 (issue #20363). One data point that bears on this PR's default threshold:

On an SM107 system with NVLink-C2C (Kimi K3, 8 GPUs, CUDA graphs) we see that SM copy kernels touching registered host memory leave the whole process slower afterwards: every kernel boundary in later CUDA graph replays gets ~0.2 us longer, about +1.2 ms (~7%) per decode step, and it never recovers (details and nsys findings in #20363). It is triggered by small pages too, not only by the large recurrent-state pages:

- With `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_BACKEND=python`, i.e. through `copyHostToDevice` / `copyDeviceToHost`, offloading only MLA KV blocks (attention pages well below 4 MiB; the state pool never filled in that run) produced the same +1.2 ms step as soon as KV blocks started to be offloaded.
- Replacing the two helpers' kernel with per-task `cudaMemcpyAsync` for every size removed it, with byte-identical outputs. The cost was ~0.19 s (~9%) more TTFT when reloading ~6K KV blocks (~13 GB per rank) from the host tier.

So with the default `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_HOST_COPY_DMA_MIN_BYTES` of 4 MiB, the attention pages would still go through the kernel and keep this slowdown on coherent links. Would you consider defaulting to the copy engines for every size on coherent links (or making the threshold link-dependent), in line with #20364?

I think this is mostly for a deprecated code path. With recent code page codec change, the H2D and H2D of pages mostly go through the default codec, which has both kernel and DMA path, and the kernel path is also well optimized for perf/resource (not absolute perf because the migration is meant to run concurrently with inference, and I wanted it to use minimum amount of resource and achieve >80% peak throughput).

Did you see perf problems for page H2D/D2H with the default codec path?

BTW, python backend has been removed, so TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_BACKEND=python has no impact.

The LeptonAI metadata override needs CI compatibility validation; the focused smoke check does not cover every LeptonAI path. No GPU test was run locally because the host NVIDIA runtime has a driver/library mismatch.

Compose V4.1 CSA2, Engram and single-pass mHC on the existing HybridStack layer loop. A model-owned live-field schema carries state through PP/VPP, one-layer full recomputation and explicit Torch/TE graph capture. items.summary: Add V4.1 tokenizer-aware hashing and gated conditional memory on shared EP-sharded embedding tables. Carry causal token history across contiguous CP cuts and reset it at packed sequence boundaries, using explicit process groups.
items.body:
Add V4.1 tokenizer-aware hashing and gated conditional memory on shared EP-sharded embedding tables. Carry causal token history across contiguous CP cuts and reset it at packed sequence boundaries, using explicit process groups.

Independent prerequisite, based on main. Shared EP embedding implementation adapted from @BestJuly in #7231; V4.1 Engram adapted from @guihong-nv in #7501 and @hxbai in #7224.

Validation: two-rank EP lookup/gradient and shard-metadata checks, CP hash/history and RNG-preservation tests passed. The assembled stack passed H100 SBHD/THD, PP/VPP, CP2 and 8-GPU DP2/EP2/PP2/CP2 training with Engram; checkpoint save/resume passed with model-side shared-buffer replica metadata. Black/isort/Ruff/Pylint and diff checks passed.

Revalidated with the refreshed V4.1 stack, including EP/CP history, PP/VPP and multi-GPU training. No Engram algorithm change is needed for the mHC/CSA2 performance updates.

items.title: [DSv4.1] CSA2 Full/Reindex/Reuse and bounded candidate indexing
items.author: FDecaYed
items.summary: Add CSA2 ratio-1/ratio-2 compression with Full/Reindex/Reuse ownership, BF16 bounded candidate scoring, indexer loss and fused attention. Reuse main's packed metadata and contiguous CP primitives; dev-only MXFP8 workspace APIs are outside this change.
items.body:
Add CSA2 ratio-1/ratio-2 compression with Full/Reindex/Reuse ownership, BF16 bounded candidate scoring, indexer loss and fused attention. Reuse main's packed metadata and contiguous CP primitives; dev-only MXFP8 workspace APIs are outside this change.

Independent prerequisite, based on main. CSA2 math comes from @hxbai in #7224; main-side composition comes from @guihong-nv in #7500.

Validation on H100: real Full/Reindex/Reuse forward/backward parity for r1/r2; output cosine >=0.999993 and meaningful gradient cosine >=0.9999356 in the wrapper audit. CP1/CP2 outputs matched for single and padded multiple documents; gradient cosine >=0.99999. The assembled stack completed 16K single-document CP2 training/eval with sparse indexer loss. Black/isort/Ruff/Pylint and diff checks passed.

Existing Hybrid registry/default snapshots are updated. Real r1/r2 parity passed on eight H100 ranks; the test reports skip only when the installed FlashMLA binary lacks kernels for the GPU (the standard CI image disables SM90). Numerical assertions are unchanged.

Score tiles now use up to 2048 query rows while retaining the existing 32 MiB score-workspace cap. The 8K no-candidate Full/Reindex/Reuse probe improved from 60.45 ms to 48.34 ms with unchanged peak allocated memory. Both ordinary and candidate selection passed 128-vs-2048-query forward/gradient parity.

The MiniMax-M3 FP4 disaggregated perf recipes on release/1.3 set `kv_cache_config.dtype: nvfp4` together with `fuse_qkv_index_projection: true`. items.title: [DSv4.1] Single-pass mHC
items.author: FDecaYed
items.summary: Carry each sublayer's FP32 pre-mix coefficients explicitly into the next sublayer, including entry/exit handling. This provides V4.1 single-pass mHC while preserving existing mHC behavior.
items.body:
Carry each sublayer's FP32 pre-mix coefficients explicitly into the next sublayer, including entry/exit handling. This provides V4.1 single-pass mHC while preserving existing mHC behavior. Compile the FP32 coefficient mapping and let fused post-mixing kernels store directly in the activation dtype, retaining FP32 coefficients and accumulation.

Independent prerequisite, based on main. Original changes by @guihong-nv in #7500 and @hxbai in #7224, split and adapted here.

Validation: H100 native/fused output and gradient tests, coefficient precision, autocast and graph replay passed. The assembled V4.1 stack also passed PP/VPP, full recompute and 8-GPU training. Black/isort/Ruff/Pylint and diff checks passed.

Performance: an 8K-token, hidden-size-2048 H100 forward/backward probe improved from 6.17 ms to 3.66 ms; the same probe on the source implementation was 4.27 ms. The existing state/PP/CP design and runtime options are unchanged.

items.title: [None][feat] Add SymmMemPool: one symmetric-memory allocation per process group for copy-engine collectives
items.author: chang-l
items.summary: The base layer for VisualGen's copy-engine collectives: one torch symmetric-memory allocation per process group, carved into slots of per-rank regions, with the signal channels, the rank-agreed sizing and the teardown rules every copy-engine protocol on top of…
items.body:
## Description

The base layer for VisualGen's copy-engine collectives: one torch symmetric-memory allocation per process group, carved into slots of per-rank regions, with the signal channels, the rank-agreed sizing and the teardown rules every copy-engine protocol on top of it needs. No caller is in the tree yet; this PR exists so the consumers can land as small stacked PRs against one shared base instead of each carrying its own symmetric-memory mechanism.

**Stack:** this PR (base) ← chang-l#11 (copy-engine all-gather for FP8 block-scale consumers, rebases onto this and drops its copy) ← chang-l#12 (copy-engine reduce-scatter fused with the row FP8 GEMM). The head-chunked Ulysses exchange follows as a third protocol on the same base. chang-l#9 / chang-l#11 / chang-l#12 themselves stack on #19713.

```text
tensorrt_llm/_torch/distributed/
└── symm_mem_pool.py                 # NEW: PoolLayout, SymmMemPool, probe_symmetric_memory
tests/unittest/_torch/distributed/
└── test_symm_mem_pool.py            # NEW: CPU unit test (gloo + fake tensors)
```

What the pool guarantees to a protocol built on it:

```text
SymmMemPool(group)
  reserve(slot_nbytes, slots, min_channels)   # collective, grow-only (max of all ranks' requests), never under
                                              #   CUDA-graph capture; reallocation fences the group, zeroes this
                                              #   rank's signal pad, runs the addressing self-check, logs the size
  region(slot, src_rank, offset, nbytes)      # consumer view: what source `src_rank` pushed into my slot
  peer_region(peer, slot, offset, nbytes)     # producer view: my region inside `peer`'s copy of the allocation
  signal(peer, channel) / wait(src, channel)  # put_signal / wait_signal on the pad, device-side deadline (trap)
  barrier()                                   # group fence on the pad's reserved last channel
  release()                                   # collective fence, then free; call before destroy_process_group
probe_symmetric_memory(group, device)         # rank-agreed go / no-go with the reason, for a caller's fallback
```

Rules the pool enforces rather than documents: the layout is identical on every rank whatever each asked for; `symm_mem.empty` sub-allocates from torch's implicit pool, so every peer view adds `handle.offset` and a collective marker check at allocation catches an addressing mismatch before any protocol pushes bytes; a wait past the deadline is a device-side trap, so a protocol that skips its `done` ends in a diagnosable timeout, never in silent corruption. Nothing is read from the environment, no symmetric-memory backend is bound, no multicast is used.

Extracted byte-identical from chang-l#11 (`git diff` against its head is empty for both files), so the consumers rebase without a diff; any pool improvement goes in a later PR.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no shared symmetric-memory layer; chang-l#11 and chang-l#12 each carry the pool inside the feature PR.
  **After:** the pool is its own 967-line change with no caller; the unit test on the rc29 container (CPU, no GPU needed):
  ```
  pytest tests/unittest/_torch/distributed/test_symm_mem_pool.py -> 93 passed in 8.59s
  ```
  covering `PoolLayout` arithmetic against a pure-Python reference (world 2/3/4/8 × slots 1/2/3 × sizes), custom alignment and out-of-range rejection, the grow-only merge, the probe declining on gloo without CUDA, `reserve` raising on an unsupported group and rejecting bad requests before touching the group, constructor validation, every local precondition naming its failure, and a two-rank gloo probe-and-agreement run.
- Multi-GPU behaviour (reserve + rendezvous, addressing check, pool grow + release, signal protocol under eager, compiled and CUDA-graph paths) is exercised by the consumers' collectives tests on 8× B200 in chang-l#11 and chang-l#12 (`test_token_sharded_tp_collectives.py` at tp 2/3/4/8), which land on top of this PR.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. New module and test only; reverting removes them and nothing else.

**Blast Radius:** none

No existing code imports the module. The test is covered by the existing `l0_cpu` entry for `unittest/_torch/distributed` (CPU only, `pytest.mark.cpu_only`).

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/distributed/test_symm_mem_pool.py` (new, CPU): layout, reserve guards, probe fallback, agreement on gloo; registered through the directory entry already in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`.
- GPU coverage arrives with the first consumer (chang-l#11) and is listed there.
