items.title: fix(ssm): batch-invariant Mamba decode without a z replay buffer
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Batch-invariant Mamba decode no longer keeps a replay buffer: the chunk scan gates only the target row, so it reads the current token's directly. Outputs are bitwise unchanged; per-request decode memory drops by per Mamba layer.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Batch-invariant Mamba decode no longer keeps a `z` replay buffer: the chunk scan gates only the target row, so it reads the current token's `z` directly. Outputs are bitwise unchanged; per-request decode memory drops by `chunk_size x d_inner x dtype bytes` per Mamba layer.

A second commit replaces the decode step's tile kernels with row kernels that compute only the consumed row (bitwise the same; about 1.9x faster per Mamba layer at 64 to 256 rows), and fuses the step's bookkeeping into one kernel.

## Problem

`BatchInvariantDecodeBuffers` stores x, z, dt, B and C for every token of the current chunk, per request slot and Mamba layer, so decode can replay the training chunk scan for one row. `z` is not needed for that. In `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`, z only enters through the row-local gate `acc *= z * sigmoid(z)`. In target-rows mode (the decode path), only the target row is stored. So no buffered z row other than the current token's ever reaches an output.

The z buffer is `max_requests x chunk_size x d_inner` per layer, the same size as the x buffer. Per request slot (chunk 128; ssm state fp32, as batch-invariant mode requires):

| per-rank shape (TP=1) | z buffer per slot, bf16 / fp32 activations | per sequence at 8k context, before -> after (bf16) |
|---|---|---|
| Nemotron-3-Nano-30B (23 Mamba layers, 64 x 64 heads) | 23 / 46 MiB | 153 -> 130 MiB (+18% sequences per GPU) |
| Nemotron-3-Super-120B (40 layers, 128 x 64) | 80 / 160 MiB | 408 -> 328 MiB (+24%) |
| 2x-width / 50-layer stand-in for larger hybrids | 200 / 400 MiB | 913 -> 713 MiB (+28%) |

With fp32 in_proj activations the gains are larger: +28% (Nano), +37% (Super) and +42% (stand-in) at 8k context. These numbers are derived from the buffer shapes plus conv/SSM state and fp16/bf16 KV, under the assumption that decode is limited by per-request state memory. They were not measured end to end.

## The change

- `ssd_chunk_scan._chunk_scan_fwd`: in target-rows mode, `z` is one row per entry, shape `(nchunks, nheads, headdim)`. Every M-lane of the target tile reads that row (row stride 0); the gate arithmetic is unchanged. The full-sequence (non-target-rows) path is untouched.
- `batch_invariant_decode`: removes `z` from `BatchInvariantDecodeBuffers` (field, `allocate`, `seed`). `batch_invariant_decode_buffered_scan` passes the current token's `z` to the scan. `MambaBatchInvariantDecode.seed` no longer takes `z`.
- `MambaMixer`: the prefill seed call drops its `z` argument.

## Tests

- `tests/unit_tests/ssm/ops/mamba2/test_batch_invariant_decode.py`:
  - existing bitwise decode == full-scan tests, updated to the new `seed` signature.
  - new `test_independent_gate_across_chunk_boundaries`: z independent of x (the existing tests reuse x as z, which would hide a wrong z row); two slots decoded in one call; prefill tails on both sides of a chunk boundary; 2 x chunk + 3 decode steps. Every step must equal `mamba_chunk_scan_combined(..., z=z)` bitwise.
  - new `test_replay_buffers_hold_no_gate`: buffer-size check.
- `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_ssm_kernels.py`: new `test_batch_invariant_decode_step_replays`, a bit-exact replay of one decode step (target-rows chunk scan with z) that includes a chunk-boundary crossing. `tools/check_kernel_determinism_coverage.py` passes.
- Before this change, MCore's decode with every buffered z row overwritten by noise gave 0 differences over 1.8M outputs (300 steps, two chunk crossings, final state equal). Production use is NeMo-RL's batch-invariant RL engine on Nemotron-3 hybrids, where the same gate-only-the-target-row change is checked bitwise against the z-buffer decode.

## Risk

- Semantics change in `_chunk_scan_fwd` target-rows mode: `z` must now be per entry. That mode's only caller is the batch-invariant decode, updated here; the shape is asserted.
- API: `BatchInvariantDecodeBuffers.seed` / `MambaBatchInvariantDecode.seed` drop the `z` parameter, and the `z` field is gone. Both are internal to the batch-invariant decode path.
- Independent of `fix/mamba-ssd-train-inference-parity` (training on the generation kernels). The two PRs touch different source files and different tests.

Not in this PR: `DynamicInferenceContext` sizes the hybrid Mamba share of the inference buffer from conv + SSM state only. The batch-invariant replay buffers (x, dt, B, C, out; still ~200 MiB per slot at Super width in fp32 after this PR) are allocated lazily for every `max_requests` slot outside that budget, so a configured concurrency can overcommit GPU memory. That accounting gap is a separate fix.

## Row kernels for the decode step (second commit)

The decode step still ran the training kernels in target-rows mode: a full training M tile per (entry, head) for the chunk scan and for CB, and chunk-state plus state-passing programs for every entry, although only entries that fill their chunk (about 1 in `chunk_size`) commit a boundary state. The new `megatron/core/ssm/ops/mamba2/batch_invariant_decode_rows.py` computes only what the step consumes:

- `_chunk_scan_row_kernel`: the chunk scan on the 16-row MMA tile that holds the target row, gate included. It uses the training tile's `BLOCK_SIZE_N` / `BLOCK_SIZE_K` and causal bound `K_MAX`, so it sums the same zero-weight products.
- `_bmm_row_kernel`: CB with the training kernel's config, loading and storing only the target row.
- `_chunk_state_passing_rows_kernel`: chunk state (training config) and the state-passing update fused, run only for crossing entries. The update `exp(dA) * S + new` is written as one `tl.fma`, because the state-passing kernel compiles it to `fma.rn.f32`. A mul + add would round twice and change committed states by an ulp. Tests that let `exp(dA)` underflow over a chunk miss this, so the tests below draw per-head decay `|A|` from 1e-4 to 2.
- `_decode_step_prep_kernel` (in `batch_invariant_decode.py`): the step's bookkeeping in one launch instead of ~25 small ops. It writes the current token into the replay buffers and sets target rows, chunk flags and chunk starts. It also zeroes the output and advances the cursor. It does integer updates and copies only.

**Why the bits are the same.** A tensor-core MMA computes each output row from that row of A alone. With the same instruction, the same k decomposition and the same accumulation order, the target row's bits do not depend on how many other rows share the tile. The tile is not guessed: each row kernel takes its block sizes (and, for CB / chunk state, `num_warps` / `num_stages`) from the one config the training autotuner launches with. `_pin_mamba_autotuners` pins that config in batch-invariant mode. `row_kernel_configs` falls back to the existing tile pipeline in three cases:
- an autotuner is not pinned to a single config;
- `dstate > 128` (the scan then splits K over several dots);
- the chunk-scan tile compiles to warpgroup / tcgen05 MMAs (`num_warps >= 4` and `BLOCK_SIZE_M >= 64`).

That last condition is measured: on GB200, every such candidate differs from the 16-row `mma.sync` tile in fp32, and every `mma.sync` candidate matches it bitwise.

**Speed.** One decode step of one Mamba layer, `batch_invariant_decode_buffered_scan` captured in a CUDA graph, GB200. Per-rank Nemotron-3-Nano shape: 64 heads x 64, 8 groups, dstate 128, chunk 128. Each value is the best of 3 runs x 500 replays.

| rows | dtype | before | prep fused, tile kernels | prep fused + row kernels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | fp32 | 48.4 us | 22.1 us | 18.5 us |
| 8 | fp32 | 58.6 us | 32.7 us | 25.1 us |
| 64 | fp32 | 170.3 us | 142.7 us | 91.6 us |
| 256 | fp32 | 524.6 us | 488.8 us | 274.6 us |
| 1 | bf16 | 47.1 us | 20.5 us | 17.6 us |
| 8 | bf16 | 56.1 us | 29.7 us | 22.7 us |
| 64 | bf16 | 143.9 us | 115.7 us | 75.3 us |
| 256 | bf16 | 419.3 us | 384.9 us | 212.2 us |

End to end, the same kernels have run in NeMo-RL's batch-invariant engine. There they are applied as a patch over Megatron with fp32 replay buffers and the gate as a separate kernel. Results on full Nemotron-3-Nano with CUDA graphs:
- device time per Mamba layer: 113 -> 74 us at 64 rows and 414 -> 251 us at 256 rows;
- wall time per decode step at EP1: 15.68 -> 14.84 ms at 64 rows and 25.29 -> 21.91 ms at 256 rows;
- wall time per decode step at EP4: 10.71 -> 9.87 ms at 64 rows per rank and 20.06 -> 16.61 ms at 256;
- greedy generations are bitwise identical with the kernels on and off, at EP1 and EP4, with graphs on and off.

Those end-to-end numbers were not re-measured with this Megatron-native version.

**Tests** (new class `TestBatchInvariantDecodeRowKernels` in `test_batch_invariant_decode.py`). The class pins the autotuners the way batch-invariant mode does.
- `test_row_pipeline_matches_tile_pipeline`: 256 entries hitting every target row 0..127, about 1 in 5 crossing a chunk boundary, shuffled slots, a padding lane and signed zeros. Per-head decay `|A|` runs from 1e-4 to 2. It covers scales 1e-3 / 1 / 30, fp32 and bf16, `D` per head and per channel, and runs with and without the gate. Outputs and committed SSM states must match the tile pipeline bit for bit (raw bits) in all 72 cases.
- `test_row_kernels_follow_the_pinned_tiles`: pins each training kernel (chunk scan, CB, chunk state) to every candidate in its autotune list, in fp32 and bf16. The row kernels must either decline or match that tile bitwise. Tiles the training kernel itself cannot launch are skipped.
- `test_many_step_decode_matches_tile_path_and_training_scan`: 300 decode steps over five slots with prefills 1..300 (several crossings per slot), mixed decay, an independent gate and a padding lane. It runs eagerly and as a CUDA graph replay. Outputs and final states must equal the tile pipeline's; in bf16 every output must also equal `mamba_chunk_scan_combined` over the full sequence.
- `test_row_kernels_selected_when_pinned`: the pinned configs select the row kernels (including the dims of the existing decode tests, so those tests now run through them), and an unpinned scan keeps the tiles.
- Run on GB200: `test_batch_invariant_decode.py` plus the two Mamba determinism replay tests: 22 passed, 131 subtests passed. `tests/unit_tests/ssm/ops/mamba2/`, `test_ssm_kernels.py` and `test_manifest.py`: 343 passed, 2 xpassed. The 2 failures are `test_gdn_torch_l2norm_matches_fla_and_replays[compiled-*]`, which fail the same way on the base commit and are unrelated.
- The new module is registered in `manifest.py` under `ssm_mamba2_batch_invariant_decode`. `check_kernel_determinism_coverage.py` passes. black / isort / ruff are clean, and pylint 3.2.6 gives 10.00.

**API.** `BatchInvariantDecodeBuffers` gains a `chunk_starts` field, which `allocate` creates. `_mamba_chunk_scan_decode_rows` gains `use_row_kernels=True`. `batch_invariant_decode_buffered_scan` now asserts int32 `batch_indices` (as `_masked_update_rows` already required) and contiguous buffers.

For more info, see /.coderabbit.yaml.

## Description

At small decode batches, a speculative MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 step on GB300 at TP4/TP8 is bound by many small kernels, the boundaries between them, and host work between CUDA graph replays. This PR adds two `modeling_v2` targets for that configuration, `minimax_m3_nvfp4__sm_103__tp4` and `minimax_m3_nvfp4__sm_103__tp8`, plus the executor seams they need. It has two main parts: the TP4 target with the runtime hooks, and the TP8 target. The router picks the target for the matching checkpoint and hardware, `modeling_v2: require` makes it mandatory, and every kernel it adds is a catalog entry with a torch reference and unit tests.

### Step-loop runtime hooks

The hooks are `RuntimeHooks` in `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/runtime_hooks.py`; a model declares them through `runtime_hooks_of(model)`. Every hook defaults to off and no in-tree model declares one, so existing models are unchanged. There are no `llm_args` changes.

- **Packed step inputs** (`step_inputs.py`, with the `trtllm::step_inputs_scatter` op): copies made between replays are staged and issued as one upload plus one scatter. The scatter applies host copies first, then device copies, both in recording order.
- **Skipped unchanged uploads** (`h2d_cache.py`): metadata copies whose values the destination already holds are skipped.
- Both are owned per engine and are active only inside that engine's forward. On a failed step, the pack is discarded and the skip cache is cleared.
- **Private metadata pool:** an engine that skips unchanged uploads gives its CUDA graph metadata a buffer pool of its own. Otherwise another engine could overwrite a buffer this one still treats as unchanged.
- **Executor and sampler:**
  - the overlap loop can run on the execution stream;
  - autotuned tactics can be merged across ranks;
  - the greedy RNG upload can be skipped;
  - a speculative step-fold protocol lets the sampler read its rows from the model's buffers;
  - the sampler takes greedy tokens straight from the model when it produced them.
- **MSA policy:**
  - an identity block table for short sequences;
  - a hook for the KV update;
  - skipping of unchanged block offsets;
  - reusable cache-pool views.
  - The short/long CUDA-graph threshold is now resolved from the model.
- **Small op additions:** `mxfp8_quantize_autotuned`, `flashinfer_mxfp8_gemm_cute_dsl`, and a `split_k` argument on the CuTe DSL index scorer.

Greedy-only outputs (greedy tokens without logits) are kept only when nothing downstream reads the logits. An executor-side guided decoder turns them off.

### The TP4 decode target

A pure generation step of up to 48 tokens runs a fused decode path. Prefill, mixed steps and wider steps take the generic layer path.
- **Attention:** megakernels with long-context block selection and the KV update; a pre-wait-staged NVFP4 QKV/indexer producer; an index scorer that prefetches older index-K pages before its grid wait; long-context sparse decode staged before its grid wait; the dense decode's KV split sized for one request.
- **Boundaries:** multicast all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm, with the routed experts' finalize folded in (batched top-k loads). The Eagle3 capture layers stay on the fused boundary.
- **GEMMs:** tcgen05 MXFP8 GEMVs at low row counts, and stock's autotuned MXFP8 GEMM elsewhere with tactics agreed across ranks.
- **MoE:** CuTe DSL engines for 1–13 rows, with rank-agreed prebuilds.
- **Speculation:** a vocab-parallel greedy verify, an exact sampled verify, an early drafter fc fork, and a fused draft loop. The draft loop's boundaries keep stock Eagle3's structure.
- **Heads:** the target and draft heads stream a lossless 12-bit coding of their BF16 weights. Each coding is checked bit for bit against the weights before use; if the check fails, the BF16 path runs.

**Explicit dispatch.** `dispatch.py` lists the row range each fast path serves. Every covered row count is a certified cell of the entry that serves it. Under `modeling_v2: require`, a covered shape whose precondition is missing raises; it never falls back silently. Every item is on by default and has one constant that turns it off. The target reads no environment variables.

**Kernels.** The kernels are compiled ops (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/minimaxM3`, `trtllm::minimax_m3_*`) and CuTe DSL modules. Nothing compiles at runtime from source strings, and every compile happens before warmup.

**Numerics.** Weights and activations keep stock M3's precisions; the drafter and both LM heads run in BF16 over the full vocabulary. Results differ from stock only by floating-point summation order, so at most a few BF16 units in the last place. The greedy verify reproduces stock's acceptance bit for bit, and the MoE-finalize adds the shared expert in stock's order.

One known difference: the long-context block selector breaks score ties toward the smaller block, as its contract says. The in-tree selector instead takes tied blocks in atomic arrival order when more than 1024 blocks tie exactly.

The one change outside the target and the executor seams is a small hook in `fmha/msa_decode.py`. It lets a layer cap the dense decode's KV-split length, and it is a no-op unless a layer sets the cap.

### The TP8 decode target

`minimax_m3_nvfp4__sm_103__tp8` serves the same checkpoint on 8 GB300s across two trays (attention and experts both tensor-parallel 8). It runs the TP4 target's exact decode path at the TP8 geometry, plus:
- **MoE:** router, routed experts and shared expert in one CuTe DSL launch for 1–8 tokens, with the sum pushed into the boundary all-reduce.
- **Attention:** an 8-head long-context sparse decode (`minimaxM3Tp8/sparseDecodeLc8`), and index scoring fused with block selection for up to 2 requests (`minimaxM3Tp8/fusedScoreSelect`).
- **Drafter and heads:** fixed-tactic low-M BF16 GEMMs, and BF16 target and draft heads with no coded copies.

The two targets are isolated. The TP8 target imports nothing from the TP4 target, owns copies of the MoE engine and MX GEMV it changes, and a drift test pins the files it copies unchanged. Outside the target, the TP8 part touches only `routing.py` (the tp8 branch), the new `minimaxM3Tp8` kernels and their thop ops, and a two-line no-op hook in `fmha/flashinfer_trtllm_gen.py` that applies a layer's KV-split cap.

## Test Coverage

- **Unit tests** under `tests/unittest/_torch/modeling_v2/models/minimax_m3/minimax_m3_nvfp4__sm_103__tp4/`: a torch-reference test for every catalog entry; dispatch tables vs certified cells; the require-mode raise; and exact-numerics tests of the verify and drafter against stock Eagle3. All 1156 pass on GB300.
- **Runtime hook tests** under `tests/unittest/_torch/` (`executor/`, `sampler/`, `speculative/`, `attention/sparse/msa/`): all 548 pass on GB300.
- **Accuracy vs stock** (same build, `modeling_v2` off):
  - GSM8K (1319 questions), McNemar test: greedy 97.35% vs 97.04% (p = 0.52); sampled at temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, 96.82% vs 96.97% (p = 0.80);
  - Eagle3 natural acceptance length over 264 requests: 2.561 ± 0.029 vs 2.536 ± 0.029.
- **TP8 unit tests:** 1019 pass on GB300. 2 are skipped because they need a world size of 8 across two trays; those comm cells were run at 2 and 4 ranks instead.
- **TP8 accuracy vs stock:**
  - GSM8K greedy 97.12% vs 97.27% (p = 0.82); sampled 96.74% vs 97.04% (p = 0.57);
  - natural acceptance length 2.536 vs 2.553.
- **End to end** on GB300: about 1.55x interactivity for TP4 and ~1.84x for TP8 over the baseline configuration.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Lazy-import aiohttp in rm_hub to unblock reward CPU tests
items.author: Asthenia0412
items.summary: This coupled every submodule of (e.g.,, ) to the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need synchronous rule-based reward functions. [Discussion: Thanks for the review!]
items.body:
## Background

`vime.rollout.rm_hub.__init__` imported `aiohttp` at module load time. This
coupled every submodule of `rm_hub` (e.g. `math_utils`, `f1`, `gpqa`) to
the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need
synchronous rule-based reward functions.

## Problem

Running reward CPU tests in a lightweight contributor environment fails
during pytest collection, before any test body executes:

```
tests/test_rm_math.py:21: in <module>
    from vime.rollout.rm_hub.math_utils import (...)
vime/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py:5: in <module>
    import aiohttp
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aiohttp'
```

This blocks contributors who want to run `test_rm_math.py`,
`test_rm_f1.py`, `test_rm_deepscaler.py`, etc. locally without installing
the full vLLM / Ray / Megatron runtime stack.

## Solution

Defer the `aiohttp` import into `_get_shared_session()` — the only
function in `__init__.py` that actually needs it — guarded by
`from __future__ import annotations` (PEP 563) so type annotations
referencing `aiohttp.ClientSession` do not evaluate at import time.

The change is 5 insertions, 3 deletions in a single file:

- Add `from __future__ import annotations`
- Remove top-level `import aiohttp`
- Add `import aiohttp` inside `_get_shared_session()`

## Testing

Verified by running the full reward CPU test suite without aiohttp
installed:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest -q tests/test_rm_math.py \
    tests/test_rm_math_dapo.py tests/test_rm_f1.py \
    tests/test_rm_deepscaler.py tests/test_rm_gpqa.py
collected 106 items
... 106 passed in 2.16s
```

Also verified that `_get_shared_session()` still works correctly when
aiohttp IS installed (the production path).

## Related

Fixes #304.
discussion:
Thanks for the review! I have added a `TYPE_CHECKING` block that imports `aiohttp` for static type checkers while preserving the lazy import behavior at runtime:

```python
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
...
if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import aiohttp
```

This keeps the eager-import-unblocking fix while resolving the pyright/mypy type annotation resolution. Pushed as commit 3a9e2555 — let me know if the CI picks it up.

items.title: CI: hybrid MFSDP CUDA-graph validation receives only 3 of 50 metric steps
items.author: balasaajay
items.summary: CI validator for hybrid MFSDP CUDA-graph training on H100 only captures 3 of 50 metric steps, then reports inf, despite training running successfully to iteration 50.
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`hybrid_llama3_proxy_mfsdp_v2_cuda_graph` repeatedly fails `tests/functional_tests/python_test_utils/test_pretraining_regular_pipeline.py::test_regular_pipeline` in the H100 development merge-queue suite. The validator receives only steps 1–3 for loss and memory metrics against 50 golden steps, although training stdout reaches iteration 50 with finite loss. Both jobs below reproduce the same signature in all three attempts.

@NVIDIA/mcore-oncall

**Failing runs**

| Triggering queue PR | Run | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#8143](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8143) | [38463033885](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38463033885) | [115555303205](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38463033885/job/115555303205) |
| [#7896](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7896) | [38540553777](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38540553777) | [115795926504](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38540553777/job/115795926504) |

These are triggering PRs, not established causes.

**Error**

```text
actual_values = {'lm loss': Values (1,3,1): (1, 11.097804069519043), (2, 11.113619804382324), (3, 9.975851058959961), ...}
Golden comparison for lm loss [DETERMINISTIC]: FAILED; 47/50 samples outside tolerance; atol=0, rtol=0, precision=full
first_outside_tolerance at 4: golden=9.897618293762207, actual=inf
AssertionError: The following metrics failed: lm loss, lm loss, mem-allocated-bytes, mem-max-allocated-bytes
```

Both exact and approximate loss comparisons fail, along with allocated and peak allocated memory. All four checks report 47/50 samples outside tolerance beginning at step 4. The displayed `inf` does not establish divergent training: the validator's actual series contains only three steps, while stdout continues through iteration 50 (final loss `7.001180E+00` in both inspected jobs).

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

Re-run either linked functional-test job with its original checkout and development container. The recipe is `tests/test_utils/recipes/h100/mamba.yaml`, test case `hybrid_llama3_proxy_mfsdp_v2_cuda_graph`, environment `dev`, platform `dgx_h100`.

**Additional context**

The evidence points to incomplete metric logging or extraction; the exact cause is unconfirmed. Investigate the emitted TensorBoard events, flushing and CUDA-graph logging behavior, and metric-reader selection before changing golden values or tolerances.

Temporarily quarantine the recipe scopes as `mr-broken` and `mr-github-broken` to prevent further queue disruption while preserving the test and references. Re-enable after validation receives all 50 expected steps and the existing metric checks pass.

items.title: Fix aux-loss token-count tensor creation under CUDA graph capture
items.author: ZhiyuLi-Nvidia
items.summary: That is a pageable host-to-device copy, which CUDA graph capture rejects when the \ scope is captured together with \: \ \ \ ## Fix Use \: a device-side fill, same 0-dim int64 value as before, so the \ and the \ multiply are unchanged.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## Problem
\`TopKRouter.attach_and_log_load_balancing_loss\` builds the per-token-loss scale with \`torch.tensor(python_int, device=cuda)\`. That is a pageable host-to-device copy, which CUDA graph capture rejects when the \`moe_router\` scope is captured together with \`calculate_per_token_loss\`:

\`\`\`
RuntimeError: Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture unless the CPU tensor is pinned.
  router.py: routing -> _apply_seq_aux_loss -> attach_and_log_load_balancing_loss -> torch.tensor(...)
\`\`\`

## Fix
Use \`torch.full((), n, dtype=torch.int64, device=cuda)\`: a device-side fill, same 0-dim int64 value as before, so the \`all_reduce\` and the \`aux_loss * scale\` multiply are unchanged.

## Verification
- Before: nemotron3 Super release recipe (64 GB200 nodes, TE CUDA graphs \`attn mamba moe_router moe_preprocess\`, \`--calculate-per-token-loss\`, \`seq_aux_loss\`) crashed on every rank at graph capture (job 1239887).
- After: the same recipe trained 20 iterations with no tracebacks (job 1241517, W&B https://wandb.ai/adlr/mbridge-dev-zhiyul/runs/dycx4m4p).

## Contribution process

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [x] I have added relevant functional tests (modified existing)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation

items.title: [NPU] Sync main training and serving
items.author: Meihan-chen
items.summary: Continue the Ascend/main integration after #413. This PR includes the earlier streaming rollout updates, Qwen3.5 NPU test restoration, and the subsequent training/serving stack update—not just the latest serving patch changes.
items.body:
Continue the Ascend/main integration after #413. This PR includes the earlier
streaming rollout updates, Qwen3.5 NPU test restoration, and the subsequent
training/serving stack update—not just the latest serving patch changes.

- Sync main through `4ad3486c`: multi-epoch data-source cursor handling (#416),
  request-scoped streaming aborts (#410), the ROCm colocate device fix (#418),
  and the Slime v0.4.0 training-stack/release update (#441).
- Reconcile Ascend's Qwen3.5 test restoration (#455) and disk-checkpoint serving
  support (#431) with the merged main implementation. These Ascend changes are
  retained and integrated, not presented as newly authored features.

Keep main's shared training, rollout, recovery and native model-loading
structure. Confine NPU-specific behavior to the existing platform/provider
interfaces and vendor patches instead of maintaining separate orchestration.
Do not restore Bridge, legacy worker extensions or manual IPC coordination.

## Main changes and NPU integration

### Streaming rollout and serving contracts

- Carry over main's request-scoped cancellation and partial-response
  continuation, including remaining-token budgets and loss masking of reused
  prefixes, without introducing an NPU-only abort/continuation flow.
- Adapt the NPU serving patch to preserve empty terminal chunks and their
  finish reasons, token/log-probability alignment, sampling-mask chunks and
  per-request metrics. Carry over in-flight queue diagnostics.
- Follow the shared cache-reset and engine offload lifecycle: updated engines
  use level-2 sleep, while frozen engines retain weights through level-1 sleep.
- Preserve main's multi-epoch sample cursor handling and accompanying
  rollout/agent contracts.

### Qwen3.5, GDN dependencies and test coverage

- Restore the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B NPU smoke test and its CI entry with a per-test
  timeout. The restored case uses a 1024-token response limit; it is not a
  claim of unrestricted long-response support.
- Keep main's native Qwen3.5 model/loading structure. Disable MegatronAdaptor's
  replacement FLA functions and use training `fla-core==0.5.2` and
  `flash-linear-attention==0.5.2`; retain the matching serving-side causal
  convolution and KV-cache compatibility fixes when rebasing vendor patches.
  Training FLA and the serving image's NPU FLA package remain distinct
  dependencies.
- Carry the platform-independent DeepScaler answer-parsing fixes and their
  regression tests, rather than adding NPU branches to reward calculation.
- Scope Qwen3-30B and Qwen3.5 torch_dist conversion checkpoints with
  `TemporaryDirectory` so each test owns and cleans up its intermediate
  checkpoint. Keep the default conversion/reference-loading coverage.

### Training, recovery, weight transfer and environment

- Follow main's unified training entry point, retained-serving lifecycle,
  trainer recovery, and rollout data/transport/replay interfaces.
- Adapt distributed trainer initialization through the existing NPU provider,
  preserving the common stateful weight-update flow and NPU HCCL/IPC backends.
- Integrate full/delta disk-checkpoint weight updates and the serving-side
  pre-read hook.
- Rebase serving patches onto paired vLLM `8cc9aa5a` and
  vLLM-Ascend `e00cb64a` sources from the Ascend 0.30 base image.
- Extend sampling support with aligned log-probabilities through packed NPU
  output, CPU decoding and streaming responses for score centering/replay.
  Preserve speculative-decoding metrics in terminal chunks.
- Port the shared CPU KV-offload ratio, encoder DP identity/port, and
  multimodal decoder-only changes into the NPU vendor patch.
- Instrument all six weight-transfer HTTP operations, including shutdown,
  with in-flight and duration metrics on both success and failure.
- Build the pinned router wheel with main's health-check patch so its Python
  and Rust components agree with Vime-owned worker health management. Add the
  patched Sunabako arm64 wheel build and document installation dependencies.
- Extend existing transport and serving-control tests. Keep
  `docker/patch/latest/` identical to the synchronized main revision.

## Validation

Current revision and serving bundle:

- All 9 local pre-commit hooks pass.
- Selected CPU/contract groups: **822 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Coverage
  includes transport/replay, score centering, training recovery, disk
  receiver/index, weight-transfer contracts and HTTP operation metrics;
  this is not the full CPU CI suite.
- Both NPU serving patches apply to their frozen source revisions and reproduce
  the deployed source trees.
- Qwen3-4B non-colocate HCCL E2E passes, including training and weight updates.
- Qwen3-30B-A3B E2E passes with the diagnostic `--no-pin-cpu-grads` override:
  torch_dist/reference loading, graph capture, two training steps and three
  IPC weight updates complete; job and test both exit successfully.
- Qwen3-VL-8B and GLM-4.7-Flash (MTP enabled) pass the subsequent local run,
  each completing two training steps and a successful Ray job.

Earlier integration evidence, collected before the serving upgrade:

- Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-30B-A3B (torch_dist/ref-load), Qwen3-VL and GLM-4.7-Flash
  (default MTP) passed local E2E.
- Streaming partial-response continuation passed at `top_p=1.0`: 5 rollouts,
  80 checked training samples, 68 recorded aborted prefixes and 49 samples
  with verified continuation. This validates the recorded prefix/continuation
  data path, not every concurrent-cancellation or offload scenario.
- Qwen3.5 passed the 1024-token case with spawned serving workers and HF-only
  loading. That run bypassed torch_dist conversion/reference loading and is
  not evidence that the default CI configuration passed.

These historical results do not certify the current serving/environment bundle
or a freshly built image.

items.title: [#20236][perf] Hoist beam-search output_token_ids out of the per-beam loop
items.author: yifanQi98
items.summary: is not in, so falls through to the C++ binding, which rebuilds the whole nested list on every access ( is ). reads it once for the loop head and reads it again per beam, so an N-beam response converts the same structure N+1 times.
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

`_handle_response` materializes `output_token_ids` once on the beam-search path and passes it to each `_handle_sequence` call. The optional parameter defaults to `None`, so the other call path retains its fallback behavior. This avoids repeated conversion of the nested beam/token list.

Out-of-tree subclasses that override the private `_handle_sequence` method without accepting the new keyword may fail on beam responses. The reported timing results are author-provided; this review did not verify them.

## QA Engineer Review

The added CPU-only tests cover beam and non-beam responses. They check that `output_token_ids` is read once and that the expected token IDs reach each output. The test file is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`. No test execution result is available here. **Coverage verdict: sufficient** for the changed materialization behavior.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/executor/result.py`: Beam responses now pass one materialized token-ID list to each sequence handler. Verify beam and non-beam outputs, including behavior through the optional-argument fallback.
- `tests/unittest/executor/test_result.py`: Covers one-read behavior and token IDs for beam and non-beam responses. Listed in the CPU CI test list.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`: Adds the executor result unit test to the CPU CI list. This changes test selection only.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

`LlmResult.output_token_ids` is not in `py_result_properties`, so `LlmResult.__getattr__`
falls through to the C++ binding `Result`, which rebuilds the whole `(beams, tokens)` nested list
on every access (`a is b` is `False`). `_handle_response` reads it once for the loop head and
`_handle_sequence` reads it again per beam, so an N-beam response converts the same structure
N+1 times. Each conversion is itself O(beams x tokens), so the redundant work is quadratic in
beam width and also grows with decode length.

This change materializes it once per response in `_handle_response` and passes it into
`_handle_sequence`. The new parameter defaults to `None`, preserving the current behaviour at
the other in-tree call site. Analysis and the access counts behind it are in #20236.

Host-side only, no GPU involved. The patch was applied to `main`'s `result.py` and the
complete `_handle_response` driven against a real C++ binding `Result` / `LlmResult`: 60
interleaved sample pairs per condition, both execution orders, output objects constructed and
released outside the timed region, GC enabled. Medians in ms:

| beams | tokens | stock | patched | saving |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (non-beam) | 3 | 0.0089 | 0.0089 | 95% CI includes zero |
| 1 | 3 | 0.0097 | 0.0094 | 95% CI includes zero |
| 4 | 3 | 0.0209 | 0.0187 | 95% CI includes zero |
| 20 | 3 | 0.097 | 0.070 | -27% |
| 100 | 3 | 0.872 | 0.329 | -62% |
| 300 | 3 | 5.776 | 0.977 | -83% |
| 500 | 3 | 14.94 | 1.65 | **-89%** |
| 500 | 32 | 72.36 | 1.90 | **-97%** |

At 500x3 the paired mean saving is 13.32 ms (bootstrap 95% CI [13.26, 13.39]), replicated at
13.32 / 13.52 / 13.64 ms across three independent processes, 60/60 pairs faster in each. No repeatable, clear performance regression was observed for the
non-beam path or beams=1/4 in these measurements; this does not establish zero overhead. Measured with Python 3.12.7; compiled bindings and remaining dependencies came
from an installed 1.3.0rc29, so this is host-side evidence rather than a full `main` build.

One premise worth stating precisely: `output_token_ids` is **not** read-only at the language
level (the binding is nanobind `.def_rw("output_token_ids", &Result::outputTokenIds)`).
Hoisting is valid because nothing in the response-handling path mutates the matrix between
the loop head and the per-beam reads -- `_handle_sequence` builds a new list per beam via
unpacking, and stop-word trimming operates on each beam's `CompletionOutput`, never on the
incoming matrix.

Deliberately out of scope, to keep this to a single concern: `request_perf_metrics` is also
read per beam through the C++ binding and may be another optimization opportunity. Its
isolated performance cost has not been established by these measurements. Related but
distinct: #20166 vectorizes the worker-side `_prepare_beam_history_cba`, while this change
optimizes the client-side `_handle_response`.

## Test Coverage

New `tests/unittest/executor/test_result.py`, registered in
`tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml` so CI collects it
(`scripts/check_test_list.py --validate` passes). Both tests are `cpu_only`.

- `test_beam_response_materializes_output_token_ids_once` -- drives the real
  `_handle_response` with a real C++ binding `Result` behind a counting forwarder, asserts
  `output_token_ids` is materialized exactly once, and checks every beam's `token_ids`.
  On unpatched `main` it fails with `materialized 9 times for 8 beams` (the N+1 above);
  with this change it passes.
- `test_non_beam_response_materializes_output_token_ids_once` -- same guarantee for the
  single-sequence path, which already read once and must not regress.

Beyond the committed tests, patched and unpatched `main` were compared field by field (every
`CompletionOutput` dataclass field plus result-level state, including `_spec_dec_counters`)
across 93 host-side scenarios using `main`'s actual `result.py` with installed 1.3.0rc29
dependencies: beam widths 2/4/20/100/500 x token lengths 1/3/8/32, beam and
non-beam, log probs on/off, decoder output prefix, streaming flag, END_ID / LENGTH /
CANCELLED / STOP_WORDS with actual stop-word trimming, multi-candidate non-beam
interleaving, empty outer matrix and empty per-beam token lists, and real serialized results
round-tripped through `LlmResult.deserialize()`. All identical. This is strong evidence
rather than a proof over all inputs. The committed test functions' assertions were also
executed directly in that isolated environment (without the pytest runner); full `main`
build and CI validation remain necessary.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
- The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR.


- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

Note on the label item: this change is `api-compatible` (a new keyword parameter with a
default on a private method), but I do not have triage permission to apply the label -- a
maintainer will need to add it. No new dependencies, no ownership change, no architecture
change; the `_handle_sequence` docstring documents the new parameter.

One compatibility caveat worth flagging: `_handle_sequence` is private but not name-mangled,
so an out-of-tree subclass overriding it without accepting the new keyword would break on
the beam path.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6704147][fix] Create KV bounce gather/scatter streams non-blocking
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: NVBug 6704147: two GB200 gpt-oss-120b disaggregated perf cases lost 17-25% throughput after #17390 turned on the overlap scheduler for them. The overlap flip is the trigger.
items.body:
## Description

NVBug 6704147: two GB200 gpt-oss-120b disaggregated perf cases lost 17-25% throughput after
#17390 turned on the overlap scheduler for them. The overlap flip is the trigger. The cause is
in the Python KV bounce buffer, which both configs enable (`kv_cache_bounce_size_mb: 512` with
`transceiver_runtime: PYTHON`).

`VmmBounceTransport` created its gather and scatter streams with `cudaStreamCreate()`. A
stream created that way synchronizes implicitly with the legacy default stream, and the
executor makes the default stream wait for every model forward
(`torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(self.execution_stream)` in `_forward_step`).

- With the overlap scheduler off, the GPU is idle when KV is sent or received, so this costs
  nothing.
- With overlap on, the next forward is almost always queued already, so each gather on the
  ctx worker and each scatter on the gen worker first waits for that forward. On this ctx
  worker a forward is a ~150 ms prefill and gathers are serialized, so KV sends fall behind
  prefill. The gen worker then sits waiting for KV.

This PR creates both streams with `cudaStreamNonBlocking`, as the C++ transfer-agent bounce
already does (`ExecPool.cpp`). The streams need no ordering against the default stream:

- **Send:** `_send_kv_async` runs after `_update_requests` has synchronized on the sampler
  event of the forward that wrote the KV.
- **Receive:** a receive starts only after the KV manager's admission readiness event has
  completed (`prepare_resources` waits on it, or the overlap loop polls it before publishing).
- **Completion:** the gather blocks on its own event, and the scatter worker synchronizes its
  stream before reporting completion.

#19588 moved the perf configs of these cases to the C++ agent bounce
(`agent_bounce_buffer_enable: true`), which is why post-merge CI recovered. The Python bounce
is still what runs whenever `kv_cache_bounce_size_mb` is set without
`agent_bounce_buffer_enable`. On main that is the Kimi K3 disagg examples. On release/1.3 it is
both cases from this bug: release/1.3 has #17390 but not #19588.

### Perf (GB200 oci-hsg, main CI wheel c98b9765d8, `bounce/impl.py` overlaid)

`disagg-e2e-gb200_stress-gpt-oss-120b-fp4_8k1k_ctx1_tp1_gen1_tp4_eplb0_eagle3_ccb-NIXL`,
accuracy step off, same wheel in every arm:

| arm | Total tok/s | gen host stalls > 300 ms | median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python bounce, overlap on (before this PR), 2 reps | 94,157 / 96,083 | 191 | 8.98 |
| **Python bounce, overlap on (this PR), 2 reps** | **116,314 / 119,369** | 3 | 3.09 |
| Python bounce, overlap off | 113,509 | 3 | 5.26 |
| C++ agent bounce, overlap on | 119,408 | 3 | 3.07 |
| C++ agent bounce, overlap off | 114,253 | 3 | 5.31 |

- **Ctx worker:** before this PR it needed 1,662 iterations for 2,560 requests, and 12.8% of
  them scheduled nothing. With this PR: 1,287 iterations and 0.2%, the same as overlap off.
- **Gen worker:** before this PR, 6.3% of active requests were unscheduled per iteration
  (waiting for KV). With this PR: 0.7%.

The bug's other case,
`disagg-e2e-gb200_gpt-oss-120b-fp4_8k1k_con128_ctx1_tp1_gen1_tp4_eplb0_mtp0_ccb-NIXL` (Python
bounce, overlap on), goes from 63,166 to 124,087 Total tok/s. Benchmark duration drops from
186.8 s to 95.1 s, and gen host stalls > 300 ms from 52 to 3.

## Test Coverage

- New `test_transport_streams_do_not_sync_with_default_stream` in
  `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_bounce.py` (already in `l0_a10.yml`, `l0_h100.yml` and
  `l0_cpu.yml`). It asserts that both transport streams are created with
  `cudaStreamNonBlocking` and that `cudaStreamCreate()` is never called.
- Ran `test_bounce.py` in the CI image (main CI wheel c98b9765d8, CPU node). On the current
  `impl.py` the new test fails (84 passed, 1 failed). With this PR's `impl.py`, 85 passed.
- The e2e perf A/B above.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] Follows the TensorRT-LLM coding guidelines.
- [x] Test cases are provided.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## QA Engineer Review
`tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_bounce.py` adds a test for non-blocking stream creation and checks that the blocking stream-creation API is not used. The test covers the stream handles used by the bounce transport. The file is listed in the `l0_h100.yml` and `l0_a10.yml` CI test lists. items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
- Adds an opt-in config flag: `moe_hybridep_enable_custom_allgather` in `TransformerConfig`, default `False`, which also creates a `--moe-hybridep-enable-custom-allgather` command-line flag. It is passed through the token dispatcher and `hybrid_ep_dispatch` into `init_hybrid_ep_buffer`.
- Only enables it on fixed DeepEP builds. DeepEP's version string didn't change with the fix, so the check uses the fact that https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/682 also changed the Python default of `enable_custom_allgather` from `True` to `False`. On an older build, a request to enable it gets a warning and stays on NCCL.

items.author: yuxianq
items.summary: Backport the bounded ragged-Q tensor-map correction from to. Repeated PrimTS context execution motivated the workaround; NVIDIA documents the descriptor correction in its.
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
The vendor pin changes `flashinfer-prims-ts` to the bounded ragged-Q correction. The correction preserves descriptors and loads, and applies only on SM100/SM103 when Q cannot establish a compact prefix of at least 128 KiB. Fixed-Q and sufficiently large compact-Q paths retain their existing descriptors. The private context builder forwards the device through scheduler-probe, contiguous, and paged compilation paths.

The reported measurements show latency tradeoffs: paged BF16 D256 is slower on B200 and B300, and packed FP8 E4M3 D256 is slower on B200. These are warmed wrapper GPU latencies, not end-to-end throughput or tail-latency results. The CI bot and merge-request pipeline reported failures; their causes are not established here.

## QA Engineer Review
The modified unit test adds coverage for packed-query tails with contiguous and paged KV inputs, causal and sliding-window masks, and CUDA graph replay. Boundary and control cases include compact queries around 128 KiB, nonzero Q storage offsets, fixed-shape queries, and graph replay after changing Q, with outputs compared to an independent FP32 reference. The author reports 410 existing-case executions and 26 new cases passing on B200 and B300; these results were not independently verified. No integration test-list entry was found. **Coverage verdict: sufficient** for the described correction’s boundary and control behavior; integration-list applicability was not established for this unit test.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `3rdparty/vendor_sources.lock.yaml` — Updates the `flashinfer-prims-ts` source pin and tree digest. Verify the pinned snapshot contains the intended correction and that vendor-source resolution remains reproducible; the existing patch and other vendor-entry fields are unchanged.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_prims_ts_attention_backend.py` — Adds attention-context tests for packed-Q tails, storage offsets, boundary sizes, fixed-Q control, and CUDA graph replay across KV layouts and masks. No matching entry was found in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/` or the manual-QA lists; this is a unit test, so listing applicability is not established.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Backport the bounded ragged-Q tensor-map correction from [FlashInfer #6482](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6482) to `release/1.3`. Repeated PrimTS context execution motivated the workaround; NVIDIA documents the descriptor correction in its [driver notice](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/tesla-release-notes-615-71-09/index.html#known-issues).

Preserve the original ragged-Q descriptor, coordinates, fill behavior, and kernel loads. On actual SM100/SM103 execution devices, apply the post-encoding correction only when the real Q tensor cannot establish a compact prefix of at least 128 KiB. Large compact Q tensors and the fixed-Q path retain their original descriptors. The change adds no GPU kernel, workspace, or synchronization. No driver-version cutoff is assumed.

This replaces the earlier native-Q implementation in this PR. The branch is rebased onto the PrimTS vendor refresh (#20301): the source pin moves from the refreshed [ae312f7cc172](https://github.com/yuxianq/flashinfer/commit/ae312f7cc1723b06fda5168105ade0f328ee47d8) to [ae3851ab5f95](https://github.com/yuxianq/flashinfer/commit/ae3851ab5f958ba22f154059df5b38321f6369d2), with the existing compatibility patch unchanged. Relative to `ae312f7cc172`, the change adds only the bounded guard and its enable flag, the same source change as FlashInfer #6482; the resource implementation is unchanged. The refreshed source already forwards the actual execution device to the context builder.

## Test Coverage

The existing 41 parameterized cases are preserved. Twenty-six additional cases cover BF16/FP8 E4M3 with supported D128/D256 dimensions, packed/paged KV, compact-Q sizes below/at/above 128 KiB, a contiguous Q view with nonzero storage offset, and fixed-Q control. The new cases check eager execution, CUDA graph replay, and replay after changing Q against an independent FP32 reference.

After the rebase, the added tests pass `k_dtype`/`v_dtype` to the context wrappers, matching the refreshed `plan()` signature. On the rebased head, all 67 cases passed in two ordered sessions on B200 (134 executions, UMD/KMD 615.71.09), including `test_prims_ts_context_wrapper_cuda_graph_replay_with_updated_metadata`. The pushed head differs from the tested commit only in the pinned FlashInfer commit hash; the vendored tree is identical.

Before the rebase:

| GPU | Existing 41 cases, 10 ordered sessions | New boundary/control cases |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| B200 / SM100 | 410 passed | 26 passed |
| B300 / SM103 | 410 passed | 26 passed |

All **872 executions** passed with zero failures, errors or skips. This is 67 parameterized cases per GPU, with the original 41 repeated ten times in session order; it is not 872 unique cases. The 26 new cases make 78 independent-reference comparisons per GPU. Imported module paths/hashes, exact test ordering, and all frozen source hashes were verified before and after execution.

Each pytest process recorded the actual loaded UMD `libcuda.so.615.71.09`; KMD was also 615.71.09. Runtime: TRT-LLM 1.3.0, PyTorch `2.14.0a0+b2c75dd062.nv26.09`, CUDA 13.4, CUTLASS DSL `4.8.0.dev0`. Tests imported the candidate Python source with retained release CI native libraries (build 10743), whose C++ tree matches the pre-rebase baseline. The 19 C++ files that `release/1.3` changed since then (MPI progress thread, EPLB allocator, SM107 FMHA cubins) are not exercised by these tests, and this Python-only change needs no native rebuild.

The added tests are covered by the existing attention-directory entries in `l0_b200.yml` and `l0_b300.yml`.

### Performance

Measured before the rebase. Compared with this PR's previous native-Q implementation (`9c7fc6f81727`), the bounded backport has measurable, small latency tradeoffs. Paged BF16 D256 is slower on both GPUs; FP8 D256 is slower on B200. Small-Q BF16 improves. These costs are retained in the results, not classified as noise.

| GPU | Case | Native-Q µs/call | Bounded µs/call | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B200 | Small packed BF16 D256 | 8.250 | 8.046 | -2.47% |
| B200 | Paged BF16 D256, many short requests | 45.900 | 46.414 | +1.12% |
| B200 | Packed FP8 E4M3 D256 | 7.578 | 7.634 | +0.74% |
| B200 | Fixed BF16 D128 control | 9.010 | 9.010 | approximately 0% |
| B300 | Small packed BF16 D256 | 7.612 | 7.437 | -2.31% |
| B300 | Paged BF16 D256, many short requests | 42.797 | 43.100 | +0.71% |
| B300 | Packed FP8 E4M3 D256 | 7.054 | 7.056 | +0.04% |
| B300 | Fixed BF16 D128 control | 8.072 | 8.072 | -0.01% |

All cases use Hq/Hkv=8/2, causal masking and BF16 output. Small-Q uses Q lengths `[3,27,1]`, KV `[33,59,17]`; paged uses Q `[1,3,17,65]` and KV `[33,33,65,129]`, each repeated 32 times with 32-token pages; FP8 uses two Q=KV=128 requests; fixed uses two Q=3/KV=33 requests.

Each variant ran in an isolated process, in two rounds with reversed order, with 31 CUDA-event samples of a 256-call graph. Values are medians of the two process medians. Both paired rounds show the paged and B200 FP8 slowdowns. The 32 benchmark processes passed 96 independent-reference checks; the bounded candidate accounts for 16 processes/48 checks. Eager-event and warm host-planning measurements were collected separately and are more variable. These are warmed wrapper GPU latencies, not end-to-end serving throughput or tail-latency guarantees.

The descriptor guard is host code; relative to the original release baseline, the device-kernel code is unchanged. Relative to the native-Q control, this backport restores ragged coordinates and descriptor format. Those differences do not by themselves establish the cause of the measured latency increases.

Vendor reconstruction passed offline, against the local committed source, and against the published upstream pin with access required. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Independent source review found no concrete issue. Source hashes are retained before and after GPU validation.

### Reproduction

On the unpatched `release/1.3` base `d661fdbf`, running the existing test file in file order with session repeats reproduced the CI failure at the 68th execution every time, on two B200 nodes and one B300 node: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` in `test_prims_ts_context_wrapper_cuda_graph_replay_with_updated_metadata` (second session). On the same GPUs, containers and UMD/KMD 615.71.09, the pre-rebase PR head passed the same 37-case order 370 times on B200 and 111 times on B300. No failing driver-version baseline or first fixed driver build is claimed. Earlier validation of the native-Q implementation is not counted as validation of this revision.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Description explains the final change and its scope.
- [x] Source and tests follow repository guidance; upstream licenses are preserved.
- [x] Relevant regression tests are included.
- [x] Public wrapper APIs and dependency pins remain unchanged.
- [x] Vendor source and compatibility-patch integrity are verified.
- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

items.title: fix(inference): support batch-invariant Mamba prefix caching
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Previously this combination was rejected, and the batch-invariant mixer skipped publishing intermediate states. Cache complete-chunk FP32 SSM states using the existing extraction path.
items.body:
## What changes

Enable prefix caching for batch-invariant Mamba inference when KV blocks align with the SSM scan chunks. Previously this combination was rejected, and the batch-invariant mixer skipped publishing intermediate states.

Cache complete-chunk FP32 SSM states using the existing extraction path. Restored prefixes start at the same scan boundary as uncached prefill; suffix prefill initializes the partial-tail replay buffers. Keep the FP32-state and non-speculative-decode requirements, and reject misaligned cache block sizes.

Also fix cached suffix scheduling: a 600-token prompt with 512 cached tokens and an 88-token compute budget previously rounded to zero and could wait indefinitely. The scheduler now excludes the cached prefix when applying the compute budget, while returning the full request span.

## Validation

- Seven targeted GPU regressions passed on one GB200 with Transformer Engine 2.19: four graph/chunking combinations plus cache-alignment and scheduler tests.
- Tiny BF16 hybrid model compares generated tokens and log probabilities exactly against uncached eager inference, including reordered batches, aligned and one-token suffixes, warm cache hits, and invalidation after a weight update.
- Standalone all-features probe exercised 18 graph steps and skipped 1,536 cached prefix tokens with exact token/log-probability parity.
- Kernel determinism coverage check passes with the new parity test registered.
- On current main, a broader run passed 90 tests before stopping at two existing TP4/PP4 cases requiring four ranks (this run used one). The four new GPU parity cases passed again.

Local runtime uses NeMo-RL's existing compatibility shim to enable its installed FlashAttention 4 beta. Full-model and multi-GPU reproducibility remain to be validated; these tests do not establish invariance across TP/EP configurations.

Needed by the deterministic GRPO draft https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4723. No dependency pins changed here.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
- `metric_history_floors_ms` adds optional per-metric baseline filtering. A floor excludes earlier records and records with missing or invalid `ts_created`. If no records remain, the metric has no baseline and is not gated.
- Floored metrics ignore stored baselines and recompute from filtered history. They continue to use the stored threshold.
- Gen-only modes apply the floor to all five gen-worker device-step-time statistics. E2E modes remain unfloored.
- Review finding counts and test execution results are unavailable from the supplied evidence.

## QA Engineer Review
- Added `tests/unittest/others/test_perf_regression_history_floor.py`. Its tests cover floor boundaries, timestamp formats and invalid values, per-metric filtering, empty history, stored-baseline handling, regression behavior, pipeline forwarding, and harness wiring.
- Modified `tests/integration/defs/perf/test_perf_sanity.py`. The existing `test_e2e` cases appear in multiple `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/` and `tests/integration/test_lists/qa/` files. No test-list files changed.
- Coverage verdict: **sufficient** for the floor behavior described. Test execution is not confirmed.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `tests/integration/defs/perf/perf_regression_utils.py`: Verify filtering, inclusive floor boundaries, empty-history behavior, stored-baseline bypass, and forwarding through the processing pipeline.
- `tests/integration/defs/perf/test_perf_sanity.py`: Verify gen-only uploads floor all five device-step-time statistics and e2e uploads remain unfloored. Existing `test_e2e` cases are present in CI and manual-QA lists.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_perf_regression_history_floor.py`: Covers floor filtering, edge cases, regression behavior, forwarding, and harness wiring. The integration test lists do not apply to this unit-test file.
- `tests/integration/defs/perf/README_perf_regression_system.md`: Documents the optional floor contract, timestamp filtering, and behavior when no history remains. Verify the documented contract stays aligned with the implementation.
- `tests/integration/defs/perf/README_test_perf_sanity.md`: Documents gen-only floor scope and the unfloored e2e behavior. Verify these rules stay aligned with the harness.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

NVBug 6925906 reports a perf regression on `aggr_upload-gen_only_no_context-gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con4301_ctx12_dep4_gen1_dep8_eplb384_mtp1_ccb-NIXL`: mean gen-worker device step time went from 31.64 to 98.75 ms. This is not a runtime regression. Every post-merge run of the case since 2026-10-01 is flagged only because its baseline still contains rows that were measured under a definition of the metric that no longer applies.

**Why the published number moved.** In this run each of the 8 attention-DP ranks gets ceil(4301/8) = 538 requests, but `max_batch_size` is 512. So every rank decodes in two waves:
- a full-batch wave: ngen = 512 × 2 = 1024, about 98 ms per step
- a tail wave of the remaining 26 requests: ngen = 64, about 31 ms per step

Both waves last about 420 iterations. #19700 (nvbug 6843918) changed which wave the metric describes. Before it, the harness used the modal bucket, so the published value flipped between ~98 and ~31 ms from run to run. After it, the harness always uses the expected full-batch bucket. The bug's "good" point, build 2988 at 31.64 ms, is one of four pre-#19700 runs that happened to land on the 31 ms bucket.

**Why CI keeps flagging it.** The post-merge baseline is the P5 of a 3-day rolling mean over 90 days of history. Those four old ~31 ms rows hold it at 51–67 ms, so all 20 post-merge runs since #19700 (96–101 ms) are flagged. Without a change, that continues until the old rows age out, around 2026-12-24.

**Change.** `process_and_upload_test_results` gains an optional per-metric `ts_created` floor (`metric_history_floors_ms`). It reaches `calculate_baseline_metrics` through `prepare_regressive_test_cases`. A floored metric's baseline uses only history created at or after the floor. A metric with no history left above its floor gets no baseline and is not gated, which is the same rule that already applies to newly added metrics.

`test_perf_sanity.py` floors all five `d_*_gen_worker_per_iter_device_step_time` statistics at the #19700 merge time (`2026-10-01T12:09:03Z`), but only in the gen_only modes. e2e still uses the modal bucket, so its series is continuous and is left alone. Records are not modified, and no OpenSearch writes or manual `b_is_valid` edits are needed.

**Evidence**

GB300 / oci-jhb, 3 interleaved reps per arm. Each arm used its own commit's wheel and harness.

| Arm | Published mean (ms) | ngen=1024 bucket (ms) | Total tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| good `e0448239a5` | 98.36 / 100.34 / 101.59 | 100.10 | 513,178 |
| bad `9bf6b8b9da` | 98.31 / 98.86 / **31.43** | 98.52 | 517,030 |
| ToT `783136904c` | 98.19 / 96.32 / 96.74 | 97.08 | 527,369 |

- The bad commit's third rep reproduced the "good" 31 ms value. Its 64-token bucket had 437 rows against 436 in the full-batch bucket, so the harness picked the short wave.
- On the same bucket the good and bad commits are equal. ToT is 3.0% faster than good.
- I replayed the harness's own baseline code over this case's OpenSearch history. It reproduces all 76 baselines CI printed (mean and median) to within 0.0001 ms.
- With this change, every measured rep above passes the gate against current CI history (mean baseline 97.97 ms). A real 6% slowdown of ToT is still flagged.
- Across all 56 gen_only-mode lanes on main, the change clears 7 lanes that are currently flagged only because of pre-#19700 rows. The 2 con8 lanes that are still flagged are a separate real step on 2026-10-10 (tracked in nvbug 6919428) and are left untouched.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/others/test_perf_regression_history_floor.py` is CPU-only (`cpu_only`) and runs in `l0_cpu` via `unittest/others`. It covers:
- the floor in `calculate_baseline_metrics`: boundary, ms and s epochs, missing or malformed `ts_created`, per-metric scope, and empty-after-floor
- `prepare_regressive_test_cases` and the real `process_and_upload_test_results` pipeline with its OpenSearch seams stubbed
- the harness wiring: the gen_only branch selects the floors, e2e gets none, and the call forwards them
- the floor timestamp sitting between the last pre-#19700 and first post-#19700 uploads

Each wiring and boundary mutant (call site drops the kwarg, gen_only selects no floor, e2e also floored, floor moved, pipeline not forwarding, floor check disabled) fails at least one test. Existing `test_perf_regression_branch.py` still passes.

items.title: [None][fix] Prevent pre-merge image builds from waiting for unplanned wheels
items.author: chzblych
items.summary: Internal and NGC image builds then wait for packages that this pipeline will never produce. [Discussion: Image builds use the plan and trigger type to control wheel downloads and SBSA BOLT optimization.]
items.body:
## Description

### Problem

Selecting `Build-Docker-Images` removes both build branches, but the SBSA release wheel BOLT path can still force a build-stage wheel download. Internal and NGC image builds then wait for packages that this pipeline will never produce.

### Solution

Generate an architecture-specific wheel production plan after final stage selection, including the SBSA Docs skip, and pass it through both image callers with the current artifact path. Reused builds remain producers because their artifacts are copied to that path.

An explicitly absent producer prevents downloading. Pre-merge staging without a producer builds from source with wheel BOLT disabled; post-merge/nightly builds that still require BOLT fail early instead. Existing wheel selection remains in effect when a producer is scheduled. Empty plans preserve legacy caller behavior, with a pre-merge guard. Profile overlay, PLC registry routing, polling, and retries are unchanged.

## Test Coverage

### Validation

- Prior local Groovy checks passed for 13 scheduling scenarios and 80 policy combinations, including Internal/NGC build arguments. Jenkins and Docker operations were mocked; the pipeline code is unchanged since those checks.
- Pre-commit passed on the same pipeline code; `git diff --check` passed on this commit.
- No test files are added. Live Jenkins parameter/CPS behavior and real image builds have not been validated.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Reviewed the repository contribution and PR checklist requirements as applicable.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Dev Engineer Review
The pipeline builds a wheel-production plan after stage selection and passes it with the trigger type to both image-build paths. Reused builds count as producers because they copy artifacts to the current upload path. If the plan marks an architecture as having no producer, wheel preparation skips the download. Pre-merge builds without a confirmed SBSA producer disable wheel BOLT optimization; other triggers fail if BOLT requires a wheel that the plan marks absent. An empty plan preserves legacy availability behavior.

The PR objectives report successful local checks for 13 scheduling scenarios and 80 policy combinations, plus pre-commit and `git diff --check`. Live Jenkins parameter/CPS behavior and real image builds have not been validated. Current review findings were not supplied, so severity counts are unavailable.

## QA Engineer Review
No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `jenkins/BuildDockerImage.groovy`: Verify trigger-type fallback, wheel-plan validation, explicit no-producer behavior, and pre-merge and SBSA release BOLT decisions.
- `jenkins/L0_MergeRequest.groovy`: Verify the plan reflects selected stages and the SBSA Docs skip. Verify both image-build paths receive the plan and the correct trigger type.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: [Rollout] Add experimental deferred exact-KV Ouro decoding
items.author: Camellia86
items.summary: Ouro's deep loops can be grouped across response positions instead of running them immediately after every shallow readout. This adds an inference-only runner that retains loop-two states, batches loops three and four at a fixed deep-readout boundary, and pres…
items.body:
Ouro's deep loops can be grouped across response positions instead of running
them immediately after every shallow readout. This adds an inference-only runner
that retains loop-two states, batches loops three and four at a fixed deep-readout
boundary, and preserves each request's original positions and true per-loop KV.

The example exposes intervals 1/2/4/8 and an eager same-readout reference. It keeps
full-depth prompt prefill, per-answer RNG, selected processed logprobs, raw tokens,
readout depths and stop/length reasons. Unread deep tails are discarded on stop.

Validation:

- 28 CPU tests against independent dense causal equations using the companion
  engine documented by the Ouro recipe: readouts, all committed KV planes, GQA,
  staggered blocks, batch shrink, termination, processed scores and reproducible
  sampling.
- Black, isort, Ruff and diff whitespace checks pass.
- The standalone example's command-line entry point passes its import/help check.

The fixed mixed-readout policy needs quality comparison with native K4. BF16 batch
shapes can change scores and sampled trajectories. This PR does not wire the
experimental policy into GRPO; full-model end-to-end performance and training
probability replay remain separate validation work.

Follow-up to https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/459.

items.title: fix(optimizer): avoid TE state copies in distributed checkpoint metadata
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Avoid temporary copies of GPU optimizer state when DistributedOptimizer saves or restores group metadata with Transformer Engine FusedAdam. Near the GPU memory limit, the existing roundtrip through TE's tensor-state serialization can cause checkpoint resume to…
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Avoid temporary copies of GPU optimizer state when DistributedOptimizer saves or restores group metadata with Transformer Engine FusedAdam. Near the GPU memory limit, the existing roundtrip through TE's tensor-state serialization can cause checkpoint resume to OOM even when the final optimizer state fits.

For the exact TE FusedAdam class on TE 2.18+, initialize missing state directly in its final representation, serialize group metadata without unscaling tensor state, and restore group metadata while preserving existing state buffers. Parameter-state checkpoint loading remains responsible for restoring tensor contents. Older TE, other optimizers, subclasses, and optimizers with registered load hooks retain their existing path. 
## Contribution checks

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6913451][fix] Cut remote MPI session submit_sync wait and launcher stop latency
items.author: trtllm-agent
items.summary: submitsync blocks on poll(SYNCIDLEINTERVAL) instead of sleeping, and the launcher sends the HMAC-signed shutdown with a small pyzmq helper instead of importing the whole package; a CPU-only unit test covers the prompt return.
items.body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: The remote MPI session's launcher path spends avoidable time in two places, which pushes a correct run past the harness's fixed 60 s budget during teardown: submit_sync sleeps 8 s after each empty 0.1 s poll instead of blocking on the response socket, and the launcher stops the MPI Comm server by importing all of tensorrt_llm just to send one shutdown message.
- **Fix**: Cut remote MPI session submit_sync wait and launcher stop latency. submit_sync blocks on poll(SYNC_IDLE_INTERVAL) instead of sleeping, and the launcher sends the HMAC-signed shutdown with a small pyzmq helper instead of importing the whole package; a CPU-only unit test covers the prompt return.
- **Original test**: `bash .repair-bot/reproduce/6913451-c98b9765d85f-1791975185945285784/tot/handoff/drive_task_kwargs.sh`
- Automated fix generated by repair-bot

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6843484][fix] Keep multi-node aggregated perf-sanity jobs in one NVLink domain; cherry-pick #20000 to release/1.3
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: Fixes the perf-sanity failures from NVBugs 6843483, 6843484 and 6843490 that still fail in the latest post-merge (#29). These bugs were filed against post-merge #2987, #2989 and #2990.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes the perf-sanity failures from NVBugs 6843483, 6843484 and 6843490 that still fail in the latest `release/1.3` post-merge (#29).

These bugs were filed against `main` post-merge #2987, #2989 and #2990. Three groups of failures are already fixed and are not part of this PR:
* The `gen_only_no_context` Qwen3-235B cases (`Benchmark output contains N failed requests`, i.e. `No 0 servers available`). Fixed by #19700 / #19965. They pass on `release/1.3` #22–#29 and `main` #2999–#3018.
* The AgentX con1156 hang (`gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-dspark_agentx_con1156`). It is not fixed: it is waived under nvbugs/6877254, which is tracked separately. On `release/1.3` the stage is green only because CI merges `main`'s waive list into the branch's, and the case is skipped.
* The Nemotron-Ultra-V3 disagg `gen_only` timeout, which passes on `release/1.3` #24–#29.

Two root causes remain on `release/1.3`, one per commit.

### 1. Multi-node aggregated perf-sanity stages are not kept inside one NVLink domain

Affected stages:
* `GB200-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-1`
* `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-{1,2}`
* `GB300-32_GPUs-8_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE8-GPU32-Post-Merge-{1,2}`

The cases are `gen_only_no_context` DeepSeek-R1 con4096 dep16, DeepSeek-V4-Pro con666 dep16 / con180 dep32, and GLM-5 con512 dep32. In the bugs they appear as `ncclGinGdakiCreateContext ... failed: 2`, `no new log output for 7201s`, or `CANCELLED by 146504` (the idle-GPU reaper).

**What happens.**
* `runLLMTestlistWithSbatch` adds `--segment=<nodeCount>` only for `Disagg-PerfSanity` and `SingleNvlinkDomain` stages.
* Aggregated multi-node perf-sanity stages (`aggMultiNodeMode`) get no segment, so Slurm can spread one EP16/EP32 job over several NVL72 racks. On oci-hsg, oci-jhb and oci-aga, `topology/block` uses 18-node blocks, one per rack.
* Across racks, `NVLinkOneSided` and `NVLinkTwoSided` fail with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` (MNNVL memory cannot be mapped). The MoE communication factory then falls back to `NcclEP`.
* With `NcclEP` the case crashes in NCCL GIN context creation (`ncclGinGdakiCreateContext ... failed: 2`, `nccl_ep.cc:2130`) or in `NCCL-EP NVFP4 dispatch requires uint8 tokens`. Otherwise it stalls with idle GPUs until the reaper or the 2 h no-output watchdog cancels it.

**Evidence: Slurm nodelist vs. outcome for these 5 stages.** Nodelists come from the stage logs of `release/1.3` #20–#29 and `main` #3009–#3017. Builds whose logs have expired or that hit the #3009 DNS outage are excluded.

| Placement | Runs | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 rack | 12 | 12 | 0 |
| 2+ racks | 48 | 0 | 48 |

* The same case flips with placement: GB200 DeepSeek-R1 con4096 passed on `release/1.3` #22/#23/#24/#29, each time on one rack. It failed on #20/#26/#28, each time on two.
* MoE communication strategy chosen:
  * Passing single-rack run (`release/1.3` #29, `nvl72175-T[06,08-10]`): `NVLinkOneSided` on all ranks, no `via NET` links.
  * Failing two-rack run (`main` #3017, `nvl72138-T[12,15],nvl72057-T[08,11]`): `NVLinkOneSided not available: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE`, then `NcclEP`.
* Control: the `Disagg-PerfSanity` stages, which already pass `--segment`, landed in one rack in 152/152 runs, up to 14 nodes.

**Fix.** `--segment=<nodeCount>` is now also requested in `aggMultiNodeMode`, the same as for `Disagg-PerfSanity` and `SingleNvlinkDomain`. This one-line change in `jenkins/L0_Test.groovy` affects only multi-node stages whose name contains `PerfSanity`; every such stage is ≤ 8 nodes, well under the 18-node block size.

### 2. Cherry-pick #20000: stale disagg rendezvous files and the CI no-output watchdog

Affected stage: `GB300-12_GPUs-3_Nodes-PyTorch-Disagg-PerfSanity-CTX1-NODE1-GPU4-GEN1-NODE2-GPU8-Post-Merge-1`, case `disagg_upload-e2e-gb300_deepseek-r1-fp4_128k8k_con256_ctx1_pp4_gen1_dep8_eplb0_mtp1_ccb-NIXL`.

* On `release/1.3` it has failed in every build in the reports I fetched (#24/#26/#28/#29) with `no new log output for 7201s ... Cancelling it`. In #29, the precheck passed and the benchmark started at 13:04. The job log then stayed at 158,646 bytes until the watchdog cancelled it at 15:09.
* #20000 fixed exactly this on `main`:
  * a heartbeat line in the job log every 10 min during the benchmark;
  * `multi_round` 3 → 2 for this case;
  * clearing stale `hostnames-*` / `benchmark_status.*.txt` before each attempt.
* Since #20000, `main` has uploaded this case in #3012, #3014, #3015 and #3016. `release/1.3` has never uploaded it.
* The cherry-pick applies cleanly. After it, `slurm_launch_draft.sh` and `test_perf_sanity.py` are byte-identical to `main` at #20000, and both case YAMLs are identical to `main`.

## Test Coverage

* Stages fixed by commit 1:
  * `GB200-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-1`
  * `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-1`
  * `GB300-16_GPUs-4_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE4-GPU16-Post-Merge-2`
  * `GB300-32_GPUs-8_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE8-GPU32-Post-Merge-1`
  * `GB300-32_GPUs-8_Nodes-PyTorch-PerfSanity-GEN1-NODE8-GPU32-Post-Merge-2`
* Stage fixed by commit 2:
  * `GB300-12_GPUs-3_Nodes-PyTorch-Disagg-PerfSanity-CTX1-NODE1-GPU4-GEN1-NODE2-GPU8-Post-Merge-1`
* `aggr_upload-gen_only_no_context-gb300_deepseek-r1-fp4_8k1k_con4096_ctx1_dep4_gen1_dep16_eplb0_mtp1_ccb-NIXL` stays waived under nvbugs/6912139 in this PR. It can be unwaived once these stages are green.
* `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

The change updates the cache-transceiver precheck harness, its documentation, tests, and DeepSeek V4 benchmark metadata. It does not change product code.

When no checkpoint directory resolves, the precheck can use a validated `metadata.architecture` hint to resolve `auto` KV cache manager settings. A resolved checkpoint takes precedence, and missing or unregistered model identity still fails closed. The precheck also checks rank agreement and ctx/gen transfer contracts, and records checkpoint-resolution and synthetic-KV-shape status.

The two unit-test files are listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_a10.yml`. The end-to-end test file is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_h100.yml`.
