## Description

Fixes https://nvbugs/6748135 on `main`. This forward-ports release/1.3 PR #19782 (`83d385b5b1`, NVBug 6759214, the same failure).

**Failure.** The disaggregated DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark perf-sanity cases never start their CTX/GEN/DISAGG servers. The cache-transceiver precheck fails on every rank of every instance:

```
RuntimeError("use_kv_cache_manager_v2 is 'auto', but the precheck could not resolve a registered model class from model_dir=None; refusing to assume V1")
CACHE TRANSCEIVER PRECHECK FAILED - the disaggregated test will NOT run
```

**Root cause.** `run_precheck.resolve_model_prefs()` gets the model class only from a staged checkpoint's `config.json`. When no checkpoint directory resolves under `LLM_MODELS_ROOT`, `model_dir` is `None`. The KV-shape path already handles that case (`FALLBACK_KV_SHAPE`), but the manager-version `auto` path raises. The model preference hooks need only the architecture name, so a missing checkpoint does not have to be fatal.

**Fix** (test harness only; no product code). Same diff as #19782:
- `metadata.architecture` is an optional, validated hint, looked up in the model registry. It is used only when no checkpoint directory resolves: a resolved checkpoint always wins, and an unknown hint still fails closed. All 13 DeepSeek V4 disagg configs (perf + perf-sanity) declare `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`.
- Each rank resolves both roles' transfer contract (backend, runtime, manager version, dtype, global KV shape) before it builds a KV manager. All ranks must agree, and the ctx/gen handshake compares the contracts again.
- Every status JSON records `model_dir_resolved` and `synthetic_kv_shape`, so a PASS on a synthetic pool reads as a transport check, not as proof the checkpoint is ready.

**Main adaptation.** #17495 changed main's precheck default to `use_kv_cache_manager_v2=True` (release/1.3 still uses `'auto'`). The only difference from #19782 is one fingerprint-test probe, which uses `False` instead of `True`. The diff equals commit `6ad977dd72b` in mass-merge PR #20232 (identical `git patch-id`). #20232 is `CONFLICTING` with main, and its CI never started (`Pull request not mergeable`), so this bug's fix is filed on its own. If #20232 lands first, this PR becomes a no-op and can be closed.

**Why main still needs it after #17495.** That PR moved the default to `True`, so the `auto` branch no longer fires on today's configs. The underlying gap remains: any config that sets `use_kv_cache_manager_v2: auto` without a staged checkpoint fails the same way. The contract and metadata checks are also missing on main. The QA weekly main run hit this failure 4 times before #17495 (`82f980469f`, `0f4c99e739`, `58fd2d3fc8`, ×2 cases).

## Test Coverage

items.title: [None][fix] Reduce deterministic GVR V2 top-K overflow overhead
items.author: longcheng-nv
items.summary: Fix excessive overhead in deterministic GVR V2 top-K, especially at K=1024 and K=2048. With clustered logits, a few warps receive most of the candidates.
items.body:
<!-- Copyright (c) 2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION. All rights reserved. -->

## Description

Fix excessive overhead in deterministic GVR V2 top-K, especially at **K=1024 and K=2048**. Follow-up to #20100.

With clustered logits, a few warps receive most of the candidates. Their local buffers can overflow even when the shared buffer has enough total space, triggering an expensive scan of the whole row.

This fix:
- Recovers overflowing candidates in parallel using exact per-warp counts.
- Adds candidate-buffer headroom without changing sampling thresholds.
- Removes unused shared-memory allocations and adjusts buffer sizes to limit memory pressure.

## Measured improvement

At BS=512 and N≈131,000, added cost drops from **208–221 µs to 1.05–2.76 µs**.

Each row compares identical input tensors on the same B200, using **nsys + cold L2**. Overhead is relative to the default-path control in each run.

| Model / K | Shape (BS × N) | Kernel time: before → after | Overhead: before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V4 Pro · K=1024 | 512 × 32,771 | 53.01 → 30.23 µs | +83.63% → +6.02% |
| V4 Pro · K=1024 | 512 × 131,075 | 300.57 → 94.25 µs | +225.04% → +1.13% |
| V3.2 · K=2048 | 512 × 32,783 | 63.21 → 33.80 µs | +106.67% → +11.31% |
| V3.2 · K=2048 | 512 × 131,087 | 295.88 → 77.19 µs | +296.63% → +3.71% |

## Final performance across the full grid

**B200 · nsys + cold L2 · 275 captured-logit shapes · all 11 power-of-two batch sizes from 1 to 1024.**

Overhead below is relative to the default path, using `deterministic=True` with per-route output order.

| Model | K | Geometric mean overhead | Maximum added time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash | 512 | +8.94% | +2.63 µs |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro | 1024 | +9.13% | +5.47 µs |
| DeepSeek V3.2 | 2048 | +14.12% | +7.68 µs |

Inputs are model logits captured from random-token prompts, with stored rows reused to form batches.

## Test Coverage

- **Correctness and repeatability:** 275 captured-logit and 84 synthetic shapes passed; 48 shapes were also checked on another GPU.
- **Regression checks:** 54 kernel tests, 24 boundary cases and 45 default-path comparisons passed.
- **Memory and style:** Compute Sanitizer reported 0 device-memory errors; all applicable pre-commit checks passed.

<details>
<summary>Measurement and validation details</summary>

- **Before/after provenance:** before values are from the archived pre-fix snapshot `2807acd470e6`; after values use the final source matching PR commit `358db83774`. Input hashes, GPU identity and timing settings were checked for every comparison.
- **Timing:** CUDA graphs, 5 warmups and 24 repetitions per arm. Two default-path controls and the deterministic arm run in rotated order on the same GPU. The baseline is the mean of the two controls.
- **Cold L2:** a 512 MiB eviction runs before every replay, outside the measured range.
- **Scope:** measurements cover per-route deterministic output; optional canonical ascending-index sorting is excluded. Geometric means weight shapes equally.
- **Regression tests:** the actual kernel sources run through a standalone package shim, without importing the full TensorRT-LLM runtime or repository conftest. Coverage includes clustered scores, large batches, odd valid lengths and misaligned prefill windows.
- **Sanitizer:** device-memory checks remain enabled. API-error reporting is disabled for version-negotiation diagnostics between CUDA 13.3 bindings and the 13.2 driver.

Focused regression command in an installed TensorRT-LLM environment on B200:

```bash
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/test_cute_dsl_gvr_topk_deterministic.py -k clustered
```

</details>

## PR Checklist

- Regression coverage is included and local checks passed.
- API, dependency and ownership changes: none.
- CI results and reviewer approvals are tracked in GitHub checks and reviews.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6770503][test] Remove perf-sanity unit tests on release/1.3
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: https://nvbugs/6770503 is a functional bug in a perf-sanity unit test. Perf sanity is a test script, not product code. [Discussion: The perf-submit tests retain example-module coverage, including concurrency validation.]
items.body:
## Description

https://nvbugs/6770503 is a functional bug in a perf-sanity unit test. #18990 renamed the perf-sanity helpers (`GEN_ONLY_DEVICE_STEP_TIME_METRICS` → `DEVICE_STEP_TIME_METRICS`, …), the helper unit tests still used the old names and broke, and #19129 updated them.

Perf sanity is a test script, not product code. Unit tests on that script don't protect product behavior. They only fail when the script is refactored, as happened here. A real defect in the script shows up as a failure in the perf-sanity stage itself. This PR removes the perf-sanity unit tests from release/1.3.

`tests/unittest/scripts/test_perf_sanity_helpers.py`, the file the bug was filed against, is already gone: #19107 deleted it. This PR removes the perf-sanity unit tests that remain.

**Deleted.** Each file below tests perf-sanity code and nothing else.

| File | What it tested |
|---|---|
| `tests/unittest/others/test_cache_transceiver_precheck_config.py` | `tests/scripts/perf-sanity/cache_transceiver_precheck/precheck_config.py` (also imports `run_precheck.py`) |
| `tests/unittest/others/test_cache_transceiver_precheck_run.py` | `tests/scripts/perf-sanity/cache_transceiver_precheck/run_precheck.py` |
| `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_cache_transceiver_precheck_e2e.py` | End-to-end run of `run_precheck.py` on one GPU |
| `tests/unittest/others/test_perf_regression_branch.py` | `s_branch` handling in `tests/integration/defs/perf/perf_regression_utils.py`, the perf-sanity regression check and OpenSearch upload (#18127) |
| `tests/unittest/others/test_http_utils_fail_fast.py` | The perf-sanity fail-fast path (#16403): the `check_files` / `server_proc` arguments of `wait_for_endpoint_ready`, plus `fail_if_proc_died` and `report_error`. Only `test_perf_sanity.py` and `test_visual_gen_perf_sanity.py` use these. The functional callers (`_test_disagg_serving_multi_nodes.py`, `test_disagg_serving_perf_metrics.py`) call `wait_for_endpoint_ready(url)` without them. |

**Trimmed.** These two files mix in tests of code that isn't perf-sanity, so only the perf-sanity tests are removed.

- `tests/unittest/scripts/test_perf_submit.py`: removes the tests of `jenkins/scripts/perf/submit.py` and `jenkins/scripts/perf/local/submit.py`. Keeps the two tests of `examples/disaggregated/slurm/benchmark/submit.py`, which is an example and not part of perf sanity.
- `tests/unittest/scripts/test_cluster_env.py`: removes the tests of the PerfSanity-only side of `tests/test_common/cluster_env.py`: `get_ucx_tls_cmd`, the stage-name and `supported_gpus` parsing, and the `jenkins/scripts/perf/cluster_env.py` re-export. Keeps the tests of `apply_ucx_env()` and `detect_gpu_type()`, which the multi-node disagg serving tests use (#20114).

**Bookkeeping.**
- The precheck tests are listed by name in `l0_a10.yml` and `l0_h100.yml`, so their entries are removed. Leaving them would point CI at files that no longer exist.
- Their `.test_durations` entries are removed too.
- The precheck `README.md` and a `run_precheck.py` docstring pointed readers at the deleted tests. Those pointers are removed; there are no code changes.

**Kept on purpose.** These tests mention perf sanity but test something else:
- `test_cbts.py`: uses perf-sanity paths as fixtures for CBTS test selection.
- `test_custom_config_registration.py`: tests transformers AutoConfig registration.
- `test_time_breakdown.py`: tests `tensorrt_llm/serve/scripts/time_breakdown`.
- `test_perf_fixed_sequence_length.py`: tests `defs/perf/test_perf.py`, the QA perf suite, not perf sanity.

## Test Coverage

This PR only removes tests.

- The two trimmed files pass when run standalone (without the unittest conftest, which needs a `tensorrt_llm` install): 21 passed in `test_cluster_env.py` + `test_perf_submit.py`.
- `scripts/check_test_list.py --validate` passes (`OK: 1967 unique test entries validated`), and so does `--check-duplicate-waives`.
- `git grep` finds no remaining reference to any deleted file, in test lists or anywhere else in the tree.
- `l0_cpu.yml` collects `unittest/others` and `unittest/scripts` as directories, and `l0_a10.yml` collects `unittest/scripts`, so the remaining tests in those directories keep running.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

## GitHub Bot Help

To see a list of available CI bot commands, please comment `/bot help`.

items.author: yt0428
items.summary: Nemotron-H-Puzzle checkpoints that provide but omit the legacy and fields fail during model initialization. TensorRT-LLM's local inherits the generic, which does not derive these model-specific fields.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Nemotron-H-Puzzle checkpoints that provide `layers_block_type` but omit the legacy `num_hidden_layers` and `hybrid_override_pattern` fields fail during model initialization. TensorRT-LLM's local `NemotronHPuzzleConfig` inherits the generic `PretrainedConfig`, which does not derive these model-specific fields.

Make `NemotronHPuzzleConfig` inherit Transformers' native `NemotronHConfig`, retaining its `nemotron_h_puzzle` model type and local `AutoConfig` registration. This reuses native layer-count and backward-compatible main/MTP pattern handling while preserving Puzzle's per-layer `block_configs`.

Related bug: [NVBug 6787519](https://nvbugs/6787519).

## Test Coverage

Added `tests/unittest/_torch/modeling/test_nemotron_h_puzzle_config.py` with four CPU test cases covering:

- Local `AutoConfig` loading with `trust_remote_code=False` and `True`, derived layer count and main/MTP patterns, and heterogeneous per-layer MoE parameters.
- Configuration save/reload, preserving Puzzle-specific fields and architecture.
- Legacy `hybrid_override_pattern` input compatibility.

The test module is marked `cpu_only` and is covered by the existing `unittest/_torch/modeling` entry in `l0_cpu.yml`.

Local validation against the updated main baseline:

- Isolated execution of the actual production configuration class, helpers and registration with the new test file: **4 passed** with this fix; **4 failed** on the unmodified main configuration.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed; the commit includes DCO sign-off.

The isolated run excludes native model-module initialization and repository-wide test fixtures. Full-package pytest remains pending in an environment with TensorRT-LLM native bindings. GPU end-to-end validation was not rerun for this PR.

- [x] Reviewed the repository checklist. This PR adds regression coverage, introduces no dependencies or LLM API fields, and does not change model identifiers, ownership or the architecture diagram.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6885370][fix] Keep Nemotron-H SSM cache dtype unset
items.author: dominicshanshan
items.summary: <!-- Please explain the issue and the solution in short. [Discussion: For Nemotron and Qwen3 hybrid models, tuning resolves and cache dtypes from the model dtype.]
items.body:
NemotronHConfig from tensorrt_llm._torch.configs (#18042), registered for nemotron_h checkpoints whose hybrid_override_pattern has "-" MLP layers, defaulted mamba_ssm_cache_dtype to "float32". transformers 5.5.4 prefers a registered non-transformers config class over the checkpoint's remote code even with trust_remote_code=True, so dense checkpoints such as NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2, whose config.json does not declare the field, switched from a bf16 to an fp32 SSM state cache.

That doubles the recurrent state per sequence (75.5 MB -> 148.9 MB for Nano-12B-v2). At max_batch_size 512 the V2 Mamba cache then needs 513 x 148,865,024 + 786,432 = 76,368,543,744 bytes, above the ~53 GB H100 quota, and these perf tests fail at executor init with "The V2 Mamba GPU cache quota is too small for live recurrent states and attention pages":

  perf/test_perf.py::test_perf[nemotron_nano_12b_v2-bench-pytorch-bfloat16-input_output_len:128,128]
  perf/test_perf.py::test_perf[nemotron_nano_12b_v2-bench-pytorch-bfloat16-input_output_len:500,2000-con:250]

Leave mamba_ssm_cache_dtype as None when the checkpoint does not declare it, so resolve_auto_ssm_cache_dtype falls back to the model dtype, as it does with the checkpoint's own config and on main (which does not carry #18042). A declared value is still honored, and patterns transformers can represent natively still load through its own NemotronHConfig.

Add a regression test for both cases.

items.title: Add Mixture-of-Kittens MoE backend on main
items.author: FDecaYed
items.summary: MCore supplies routing and owns the expert parameters, optimizer state, and checkpoints; MoK executes dispatch, routed/shared experts, and combine. Ports #6572 and #7289, building on the earlier main adaptation in #7695.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Enable `moe_megakernel_backend=mok` on main. MCore supplies routing and owns the expert parameters, optimizer state, and checkpoints; MoK executes dispatch, routed/shared experts, and combine.

Ports #6572 and #7289, building on the earlier main adaptation in #7695. Related to #5795 and #7756. Uses the MoK revision already installed by #7696.

- Support BF16 and native MXFP8 routed weights, with BF16 shared experts and existing grouped-weight layouts.
- Preserve parameter aliases and their MCore/TE attributes; refresh derived views after device/dtype conversion and checkpoint loading.
- Forward packed-sequence metadata and hash-routing inputs, and use main's precision-aware whole-MoE recomputation.
- Keep optional imports lazy and reject unsupported configurations. Initial support is TP=1/ETP=1 with fused shared experts. A native shared-expert fallback for TP>1 and the shared-output gate from #7391 are follow-ups; the pinned MoK API has neither a routed-only mode nor the gate argument.

## External Dependency

https://github.com/QiZhangNV/mixture-of-kittens/tree/qizhang/mcore-integration 

## Validation

- Standard CI passed on `951fd137d5`, including the MoE and determinism suites and the selected GPT/MoE integration tests.
- 50 MoK configuration/adapter tests and six routing-adapter GPU determinism cases passed. These do not exercise the full Blackwell MoK backend.
- Required formatter/linter checks, syntax checks, and kernel determinism coverage check passed. Advisory mypy is not clean in the local lint environment.
- The patch-coverage check remains below target: the latest commit adds two storage-validation lines that were not exercised.
- Blackwell BF16/MXFP8 kernel execution, distributed EP training, CUDA graph replay, and end-to-end checkpoint resume remain to be validated on this main port.

Draft pending GPU validation. No performance result is claimed.

items.title: Replace IndexedOrder with ExecutionOrder for MFSDP v2
items.author: shjwudp
items.summary: Replace MFSDP v2's with so prefetch can distinguish repeated occurrences of the same module without changing construction-order scheduling behavior. Uniqueness is detected automatically as items are appended.
items.body:
Replace MFSDP v2's `IndexedOrder` with `ExecutionOrder` so prefetch can distinguish repeated occurrences of the same module without changing construction-order scheduling behavior.

Uniqueness is detected automatically as items are appended. A module appearing exactly once selects its unambiguous position by identity, preserving the existing behavior for reordered or repeated demand calls, including VPP grouping. A module appearing multiple times must match the next occurrence at the cursor; mismatches raise without consuming that occurrence. A weak lookup stores each unique index or marks an item as repeated, keeping demand lookup constant-time without retaining modules. Offset-based prefetch lookahead does not advance the cursor.

The diff is limited to the order class replacement, context annotations/construction, the prefetch consumer, and three focused unit tests. VPP schedules, training integration, and pipeline tests match the base branch. There are no reset APIs, per-root maps, or explicit construction/recording modes.

This is the standalone prerequisite for #7998 requested in [the review discussion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7998#discussion_r4262243673). Runtime execution-order recording remains in that follow-up.

Validation:
- Five focused cases across three tests passed against repository source, covering occurrence-specific prefetch under all budgets, unique-call repositioning for VPP grouping, strict repeated-call validation, cursor wrapping, and weak ownership with membership/reverse traversal.
- The original VPP reproduction using the repository's schedule table and context construction passes both forward and reversed-chunk backward demand traces without scheduler changes.
- Ruff, isort, syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local formatting used Black 24; the required Black 26 check and distributed GPU tests remain pending.

items.title: [deps] uv.lock pins nvidia-cudnn-frontend==1.26.0, whose DSA indexer_top_k asserts on odd top-k (DeepSeek-V4)
items.author: linmuchuiyang
items.summary: nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.26.0 vectorises the output store by 2 and asserts for odd: Any real-length sequence hits it (first full-model log-prob pass, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 61 layers); synthetic tests with fixed even lengths do not. Fixed in cudnn-frontend #407 (202…
items.body:
## What happens

Megatron-Core's DSV4 sparse attention calls cuDNN's DSL kernel with `top_k = min(index_topk, sk)` where `sk` is the
compressed KV length of the sequence (`csa_kernels._indexer_topk_core`). nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.26.0 vectorises the output
store by 2 and asserts for odd `top_k`:

```
cudnn/deepseek_sparse_attention/indexer_top_k/_varlen_util.py:962: assert top_k % vecsize_out == 0
```

Any real-length sequence hits it (first full-model log-prob pass, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 61 layers); synthetic tests with fixed
even lengths do not. Fixed in cudnn-frontend #407 (2026-07-20), first release 1.27.0 (2026-08-06); 1.31.0 is current.

## Ask

Bump the lock to `nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.27.0` (`--no-deps`-equivalent: nothing else in the lock moves; verified by
installing 1.27.0 over the 1.26.0 venv and running 61-layer GRPO for 15+ jobs). Also relevant to the DSV4 examples and the
Megatron-Lite DSA docs, which list cudnn-frontend as a critical dependency.

Environment: verl `1d367a4f` (`uv.lock` entry at line ~2509), Megatron-LM `43e45e13`, GB200.
discussion:
Independent reproduction on **H100** (not Blackwell), so this is not architecture-specific. DeepSeek-V4-Pro GRPO, verl `main@45a40312`, vLLM 0.29.0, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2 + Megatron-LM `43e45e13`, `nvidia-cudnn-frontend==1.26.0` from the lock:

```text
ray::WorkerDict.actor_rollout_compute_log_prob()
  File ".../megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py", line 1795, in __call__
  ...
  File ".../cudnn/deepseek_sparse_attention/indexer_top_k/indexer_top_k_varlen_util.py", line 962, in else_block_11
    assert self.top_k % vecsize_out == 0
AssertionError: None
```

It fires in the actor's first `compute_log_prob` forward as soon as a rollout sample shorter than `index_topk` (1024 for Pro) has an odd length, i.e. on essentially any real RL batch. A DeepSeek-V4-**Flash** run on the same stack never hit it (3 steps clean), so Flash-only CI would not catch this.

After bumping the venv to `nvidia-cudnn-frontend==1.27.0` (nothing else changed) the same 64-node Pro job completed 5/5 GRPO steps with rollout/actor log-prob Pearson 0.994–0.995.

items.title: [megatron] optimizer_offload_fraction < 1 crashes at the first update_actor when optimizer_offload=True
items.author: linmuchuiyang
items.summary: The all-CPU form (fraction 1.0) never has a GPU sub-optimizer, which is why it works. Megatron-LM #7232 (HDO materialised twice under the distributed optimizer) is the nearest upstream thread.
items.body:
## What happens

Megatron engine, `actor.megatron.param_offload=True`, `optimizer_offload=True`,
`optim.override_optimizer_config.optimizer_cpu_offload=True`, `overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d=True`:

- `optimizer_offload_fraction=1.0` (default): works (hundreds of steps across runs);
- `optimizer_offload_fraction=0.5`: one `WorkerDict` process dies during the first `update_actor` with no Python traceback
  (Ray `ActorDiedError`, `SYSTEM_ERROR`, "connection error code 2"); host memory is healthy (73 GB RSS per worker, 445 of
  952 GB per node), no `oom_kill`;
- `optimizer_offload_fraction=0.0`: Python traceback

```
  File "verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py", line 1120, in __exit__
  File "verl/workers/engine/base.py", line 323, in _context_switch
  File "verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py", line 694, in to
  File "verl/utils/megatron_utils.py", line 698, in offload_megatron_optimizer
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Reproduced on a 4-layer truncated DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8 nodes, EP16) and on the 61-layer model (64 nodes, PP16/EP16); same
behaviour on both.

## Reading

`offload_megatron_optimizer` / `load_megatron_optimizer` walk `HybridDeviceOptimizer.sub_optimizers` and move every state
tensor to CPU and back; with a fraction < 1 the GPU sub-optimizer (`FusedAdam`) keeps its own device assumptions and the
per-step round trip leaves its state on the wrong device (0.0: the move itself raises; 0.5: the next fused step crashes
natively). The all-CPU form (fraction 1.0) never has a GPU sub-optimizer, which is why it works. Megatron-LM #7232 (HDO
materialised twice under the distributed optimizer) is the nearest upstream thread. I have not isolated the exact tensor;
logs of all three runs are available.

## Ask

Either support fractions < 1 in the offload/onload helpers (skip the GPU sub-optimizer's state, or offload it through
HDO's own d2h/h2d path) or reject `optimizer_offload_fraction < 1` together with `optimizer_offload=True` at config
validation with a clear message. The use case: 61-layer DeepSeek-V4-Pro at 64 nodes has 63 GB of 189 GB GPU memory in use
and 905 of 952 GB host memory, so keeping part of the Adam state on the GPU is the natural lever for a checkpoint save.

Environment: verl `1d367a4f`, Megatron-LM `43e45e13` (+ #4046/#7785), GB200 aarch64.

items.title: [rollout, vllm] MXFP4 refit rejects vLLM's auto-selected Blackwell MoE backend only at the first update_weights, after ~45 min of JIT + autotune
items.author: linmuchuiyang
items.summary: The engine then (a) JIT-compiles (~25 min per node, single-threaded host compiler), (b) autotunes for ~20 min at 2-6 % GPU utilisation, and only at the first weight sync verl raises. On clusters with a GPU-idle watchdog the job is killed before it even get…
items.body:
## What happens

DeepSeek-V4 (MXFP4 experts) on sm_100 with `engine_kwargs.vllm.moe_backend` left unset: vLLM 0.29 picks
`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`. The engine then (a) JIT-compiles `fused_moe_trtllm_sm100` (~25 min per node, single-threaded
host compiler), (b) autotunes `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` for ~20 min at 2-6 % GPU utilisation, and only at the first
weight sync verl raises

```
NotImplementedError: mxfp4 MoE refit does not support Mxfp4MoeBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8;
supported: DEEPGEMM_MXFP4, MARLIN, BATCHED_MARLIN, AITER_MXFP4_BF16
```

(`verl/utils/vllm/vllm_fp4_utils.py::_refittable_mxfp4_backends`). On clusters with a GPU-idle watchdog the job is killed
before it even gets there. The Flash example never sees this because the TRT-LLM path does not exist on H100.

## Proposal

Fail (or auto-select) before the engine is built, not after the first rollout:

1. in `vLLMHttpServer._preprocess_engine_kwargs` (or rollout config validation), when the checkpoint is MXFP4 and the
   platform is sm_100+, require `moe_backend` to be one of the refittable backends and raise a clear error otherwise; or
2. default `moe_backend=marlin` for MXFP4 checkpoints on Blackwell when the user did not set one (what every working run here
   uses), with a log line explaining why; `deep_gemm`, when installed, is the faster refittable alternative.

I can send a PR for either; (2) changes behaviour silently, so I would rather have a maintainer pick.

## Environment

verl `1d367a4f`, vLLM 0.29.0, flashinfer 0.6.18, GB200 (aarch64), DeepSeek-V4-Pro 4-layer truncated model (same code path
for the full model). Related but different: #7978 / #7987 (bf16 TRT-LLM MoE layout).
discussion:
@linmuchuiyang For DeepSeek-V4 in SM100+, please set moe backend to `deep_gemm` explicitly:
```
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.moe_backend=deep_gemm
```

items.title: [megatron] fix: onload the offloaded optimizer before load_checkpoint (resume with optimizer_cpu_offload)
items.author: linmuchuiyang
items.summary: Resuming a Megatron-engine run that uses together with (Megatron, HDO) fails at the first after the resume: or, with Megatron-LM PRs NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#4046 / NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7785 applied, calls but leaves the optimizer where verl parked it after construct…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Resuming a Megatron-engine run that uses `actor.megatron.optimizer_offload=True` together with `optimizer_cpu_offload=True` (Megatron `HybridDeviceOptimizer`, HDO) fails at the first `optimizer.step()` after the resume:

```
KeyError: tensor(...)      # HybridDeviceOptimizer._set_sub_optimizer_grads
```

or, with Megatron-LM PRs NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#4046 / NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7785 applied,

```
RuntimeError: attempting to assign a gradient with device type 'cpu' to a tensor with device type 'cuda'
```

`MegatronEngine.load_checkpoint` calls `load_megatron_model_to_gpu` but leaves the optimizer where verl parked it after construction (fp32 shards on the host). HDO rebuilds its sub-optimizers inside `load_state_dict` and classifies every parameter by `is_cuda`: a shard that is still on the CPU gets no pinned copy and is treated as a CPU-resident parameter; when verl later onloads the optimizer, the CPU sub-optimizer holds a CUDA tensor. #6690 (`pin_memory` failure on the same resume path) is a neighbour of this bug.

Fix: in `load_checkpoint`, call `load_megatron_optimizer(self.optimizer)` when `self._is_offload_optimizer`, before `checkpoint_mananager.load_checkpoint` — symmetric to the model onload that is already there; the existing code offloads it again afterwards. The `KeyError` half of the problem is Megatron-LM's (#4046 / #7785, both open); this change is needed in addition to them.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=resume+optimizer+offload+megatron ; https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=load_megatron_optimizer
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

Not coverable by CI (needs a multi-node Megatron run with CPU-offloaded optimizer and a checkpoint). Validated on GB200 (aarch64), verl `1d367a4f`, Megatron-LM `43e45e13` + #4046/#7785, DeepSeek-V4-Pro:

- 4-layer truncated model, 8 nodes, resume from `global_step_2` (`model+optimizer+extra`): fails as above without the change (two runs, both failure modes), resumes and finishes step 3 with it (rollout/actor Pearson 0.9992);
- 61-layer model, 128 nodes (PP16/EP32), resume with `model+extra`: resumes and finishes step 3 (Pearson 0.9955).

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py` `MegatronEngine.load_checkpoint`: onload the optimizer when it is offloaded, before delegating to the checkpoint manager (10 lines incl. comment).

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply pre-commit checks: not run on my side (no x86 dev environment; 10 lines, within the 120-column limit). Happy to fix anything the CI linter reports.
- [ ] Documentation: not needed.
- [ ] Tests: not feasible in CI (see above).
- [ ] CI request: will post in `ci-request` once a maintainer confirms the approach.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Multi-node vLLM rollout replicas (`data_parallel_size > data_parallel_size_local`) fail at engine start on vLLM ≥ 0.28 with

```
Remote engine 15 must not use --headless in external or hybrid dp lb mode
```

`vLLMHttpServer` starts node 0 as the API server and nodes > 0 with `run_headless`, but passes `data_parallel_start_rank = node_rank * data_parallel_size_local` to **every** node. Since vLLM 0.28, `EngineArgs.create_engine_config` infers hybrid-LB mode when `data_parallel_start_rank is not None and not headless` (still the case on vLLM `main`, `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`), and in hybrid-LB mode the leader rejects headless remote engines. The node-0 server is the internal-LB leader and must not carry a start rank; its local engines start at rank 0 anyway.

This PR only sets `data_parallel_start_rank` for `node_rank > 0`. #6856 covered the pre-0.28 semantics and was closed by a vLLM-side port fix (vllm-project/vllm#49212); this is the 0.28+ follow-up. gpustack, kserve and vllm-ascend made the same change in Sep–Oct 2026.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+data_parallel_start_rank ; https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=headless+hybrid
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

Cannot be covered by CI (needs a replica spanning several nodes). Validated on a GB200 cluster (4 GPUs per node, aarch64), verl `1d367a4f` + vLLM 0.29.0, DeepSeek-V4-Pro with `moe_backend=marlin`:

- without the change: 16 replicas × 16 GPUs (4 nodes each) all fail with the message above within 8 minutes of job start;
- with the change: 8 replicas × 32 GPUs (8 nodes each) load, allocate KV cache, capture CUDA graphs and serve; GRPO runs end to end (rollout/actor log-prob Pearson 0.995), 15+ multi-node runs since, including 128-node runs (16 replicas × 32 GPUs).

Single-node replicas (`data_parallel_size_local == data_parallel_size`) are unaffected: vLLM disables hybrid-LB for that case regardless of the start rank; an 8-node smoke with one replica per node behaves identically before and after.

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py`: move the `data_parallel_start_rank` entry of `dp_args` under `if self.node_rank > 0`, with a comment explaining the vLLM semantics.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply pre-commit checks: not run on my side (no x86 dev environment; the change is 9 lines, within the 120-column limit). Happy to fix anything the CI linter reports.
- [ ] Documentation: not needed (bug fix, no user-facing change).
- [ ] Tests: not feasible in CI — requires a multi-node replica; validation above.
- [ ] CI request: will post in `ci-request` once a maintainer confirms the approach.

items.title: [ckpt, hardware] fix: make checkpoint CPU offload device-agnostic
items.author: kahlun
items.summary: gates FSDP's sharded-state-dict CPU offload on: is evaluated once at import. On any non-CUDA accelerator it is permanently, so the gathered model and optimizer shards stay resident in device memory for the whole window instead of being staged through hos…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`FSDPCheckpointManager` gates FSDP's sharded-state-dict CPU offload on `is_cuda_available`:

```python
state_dict_cfg = ShardedStateDictConfig(offload_to_cpu=True if is_cuda_available else False)
optim_cfg = ShardedOptimStateDictConfig(offload_to_cpu=True if is_cuda_available else False)
```

`is_cuda_available` is `torch.cuda.is_available()` evaluated once at import
(`verl/utils/device.py`). On any non-CUDA accelerator it is permanently `False`, so the gathered
model and optimizer shards stay resident in device memory for the whole `torch.save` window
instead of being staged through host memory. CUDA gets the memory headroom; every other backend
pays for it, with no way to opt in.

This switches the four sites to `is_device_available()` — the platform-abstraction check
(`get_platform().is_available()`) that this same class already uses to decide whether accelerator
RNG state is reachable in `BaseCheckpointManager.get_rng_state`.

Why this is a per-device-class oversight rather than a deliberate CUDA-only choice: the
`offload_to_cpu` lines predate the platform abstraction layer (present at least as of
2026-04-20; `is_device_available` arrived 2026-06-04 in #6086), and the migration to it has been
incremental — #7871 applied the same `is_device_available()` treatment to the Megatron engine's
seed path in September. `offload_to_cpu` is a plain PyTorch FSDP feature with no CUDA-specific
code behind it, so there was never a technical reason to exclude other backends. The measurement
below confirms it works on a non-CUDA backend today.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=offload_to_cpu
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is_device_available
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=offload_to_cpu

  I enumerated every open PR in the repo and checked its changed-file list: **#7286 is the only
  open PR that touches `verl/utils/checkpoint/fsdp_checkpoint_manager.py`.**

  **Not a duplicate of #7286** (`[ckpt] fix: load FSDP checkpoint shards onto CPU instead of the
  saved device`, open). That PR is the closest neighbour — same file, same "treat sharded state
  dicts as CPU-resident" theme — but a disjoint change: it adds `map_location="cpu"` to the three
  `torch.load` calls in `load_checkpoint`, which is wrong on CUDA too and fixes where tensors are
  *revived from disk*. This PR changes the `ShardedStateDictConfig` / `ShardedOptimStateDictConfig`
  gather configs, which is CUDA-privileged by construction and governs where tensors land *during
  the FSDP gather*, on both the save and load paths. The two touch different lines and neither
  subsumes the other; they merge independently in either order. Worth noting for whoever lands the
  second one: together they make the manager's CPU-residency story consistent end to end, which is
  the stated motivation of #7286.

  **Related precedent, not overlapping**: #7871 (merged) added an `is_device_available()` check for
  non-GPU/NPU devices in `verl/workers/engine/megatron/utils.py`. Same class of fix, different
  file; it did not touch the checkpoint managers.

- [x] PR title formatted as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

**Measured on real hardware: 2× Intel Arc Pro B60 (XPU), `torch 2.11.0`, `xccl` backend.**

The standalone repro below wraps an 8-layer 4096-wide model in FSDP across 2 ranks, runs one
`optimizer.step()` so optimizer state exists, then performs the same sharded gather twice —
once with `offload_to_cpu=False` (today's behaviour on XPU) and once with `True` (this patch) —
reporting the resulting tensor device and the peak device memory during each gather:

```
device=xpu world_size=2 free/total=22057000960/25669140480

[offload_to_cpu=False] sample tensor 'net.0.weight' device=xpu:0  peak_device_mem_during_gather=2816.8 MiB  optim_sd_keys=16
[offload_to_cpu=True]  sample tensor 'net.0.weight' device=cpu    peak_device_mem_during_gather=2560.8 MiB  optim_sd_keys=16

RESULT offload_False_device=xpu:0 offload_True_device=cpu
RESULT peak_delta_MiB=256.1
PASS: offload_to_cpu mechanism confirmed functional on this device
```

Two things this establishes:

1. **`offload_to_cpu=True` works correctly on a non-CUDA backend.** The gathered shard lands on
   `cpu` and the optimizer state dict is intact (16 entries, matching the 16 parameters). Nothing
   about this FSDP feature is CUDA-specific, so the current gate is excluding a working code path.
2. **The cost of the current `False` default is real and scales with model size.** 256 MiB of extra
   peak device memory held through the gather, on the order of the per-rank sharded state-dict size
   for this model — i.e. proportional to model/optimizer size, not a fixed overhead. On a card
   already near capacity this is the difference between a checkpoint save that completes and one
   that OOMs, which is the failure mode #7286 describes from the load side.

**On CUDA this patch is a no-op by construction**, which is why no CUDA regression run is included:
`PlatformCUDA.is_available()` is `return torch.cuda.is_available()` — the identical expression the
old module-level `is_cuda_available` captured. The only semantic difference is import-time vs.
call-time evaluation, which cannot differ in practice since CUDA availability is fixed for a
process. On a CPU-only host both spellings yield `False`, so the `*_on_cpu` checkpoint tests are
unaffected.

Lint: `ruff==0.12.2 check` and `ruff format --check` clean (pinned to the repo's
`.pre-commit-config.yaml` rev; note `ruff format` reflows two now-shorter ternaries, included in
the diff).

**Not covered:** `tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp_ckpt.py` — the repo's own end-to-end
`FSDPCheckpointManager` save/load round trip — has not been run with this patch. It needs 2
accelerators and a Qwen2.5 tokenizer, and on XPU additionally a verl image with
`flash_attention_2` available. What is established here is the mechanism and its memory cost on
real XPU silicon, not a full verl checkpoint round trip through the patched manager. That test is
the natural place to settle it if you would like it settled before merging, and I am happy to run
it on the B60s on request.

**Known trade-off, stated explicitly:** this makes non-CUDA backends stage shards through host
memory, so it trades device-memory pressure for host-memory pressure — exactly the trade CUDA has
always made here. On nodes where host RAM is the scarcer resource this is not free. I considered
exposing it as a `checkpoint.offload_to_cpu` config override instead, and deliberately did not:
that adds a user-facing knob to work around what is currently a one-platform exclusion from an
existing default, and the right first step is to make the default consistent across backends. If
maintainers would prefer the knob (either instead of or on top of this), say so and I will follow up
separately.

<details>
<summary>Repro script (2 accelerators, torchrun, no verl import needed)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Repro: FSDP sharded state_dict() offload_to_cpu behavior on XPU vs CUDA.

Run with: torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 repro_offload_to_cpu.py
"""

import argparse
import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.distributed.fsdp import FullyShardedDataParallel as FSDP
from torch.distributed.fsdp import ShardedOptimStateDictConfig, ShardedStateDictConfig, StateDictType


def get_device_module():
    if hasattr(torch, "xpu") and torch.xpu.is_available():
        return "xpu", torch.xpu
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        return "cuda", torch.cuda
    raise RuntimeError("no accelerator available")


class Toy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, hidden=4096, layers=8):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(*[nn.Linear(hidden, hidden) for _ in range(layers)])

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x)


def gather_once(model, optimizer, offload_to_cpu, device_mod, rank):
    device_mod.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    cfg = ShardedStateDictConfig(offload_to_cpu=offload_to_cpu)
    optim_cfg = ShardedOptimStateDictConfig(offload_to_cpu=offload_to_cpu)
    with FSDP.state_dict_type(model, StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT, cfg, optim_cfg):
        model_sd = model.state_dict()
        optim_sd = FSDP.optim_state_dict(model, optimizer)
    dist.barrier()
    peak = device_mod.max_memory_allocated()

    sample_key = next(iter(model_sd))
    sample_tensor = model_sd[sample_key]
    sample_device = getattr(sample_tensor, "device", None)
    if sample_device is None and hasattr(sample_tensor, "local_tensor"):
        sample_device = sample_tensor.local_tensor().device

    if rank == 0:
        print(
            f"[offload_to_cpu={offload_to_cpu}] sample tensor '{sample_key}' device={sample_device} "
            f"peak_device_mem_during_gather={peak / 1024**2:.1f} MiB "
            f"optim_sd_keys={len(optim_sd.get('state', {}))}"
        )
    return sample_device, peak


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--hidden", type=int, default=4096)
    parser.add_argument("--layers", type=int, default=8)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    device_name, device_mod = get_device_module()
    local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    device_mod.set_device(local_rank)
    backend = "xccl" if device_name == "xpu" else "nccl"
    dist.init_process_group(backend=backend)
    rank = dist.get_rank()
    device = torch.device(f"{device_name}:{local_rank}")

    model = Toy(args.hidden, args.layers).to(device)
    model = FSDP(model, device_id=device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-4)

    x = torch.randn(8, args.hidden, device=device)
    loss = model(x).sum()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    dist.barrier()

    if rank == 0:
        free, total = None, None
        try:
            free, total = device_mod.mem_get_info()
        except Exception:
            pass
        print(f"device={device_name} world_size={dist.get_world_size()} free/total={free}/{total}")

    dev_false, peak_false = gather_once(model, optimizer, False, device_mod, rank)
    dev_true, peak_true = gather_once(model, optimizer, True, device_mod, rank)

    if rank == 0:
        print(f"RESULT offload_False_device={dev_false} offload_True_device={dev_true}")
        print(f"RESULT peak_delta_MiB={(peak_false - peak_true) / 1024**2:.1f}")
        assert str(dev_true).startswith("cpu"), "offload_to_cpu=True did not land the shard on cpu"
        assert not str(dev_false).startswith("cpu"), "offload_to_cpu=False unexpectedly landed on cpu"
        print("PASS: offload_to_cpu mechanism confirmed functional on this device")

    dist.barrier()
    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

### API and Usage Example

No API change. No config change. Behaviour change is limited to non-CUDA accelerators, which now
get the same CPU-offload default CUDA already had.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/utils/checkpoint/fsdp_checkpoint_manager.py`:

- Import `is_device_available` instead of `is_cuda_available`.
- `load_checkpoint`: `ShardedStateDictConfig` / `ShardedOptimStateDictConfig` now take
  `offload_to_cpu=is_device_available()`.
- `save_checkpoint`: same for both configs.
- Drops the redundant `True if … else False` wrapper; `ruff format` then reflows the two
  surrounding ternaries onto single lines.

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide
- [x] `ruff` / `ruff-format` clean at the pinned `v0.12.2`
- [x] Docs — no user-facing surface changes, nothing to update
- [ ] Tests — see the Test section for what was measured on 2× B60 and what was not run

items.title: [reward] fix: normalize punctuation around extracted GSM8k answers
items.author: Zh0uHX
items.summary: The GSM8k reward function (, the default scorer for ) compares the raw regex match with the ground truth, so correct answers surrounded by ordinary formatting get 0 reward: Fix: normalize every extracted candidate (drop thousands separators, trailing periods …
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

The GSM8k reward function (`verl/utils/reward_score/gsm8k.py`, the default scorer for `openai/gsm8k`) compares the raw regex match with the ground truth, so **correct answers surrounded by ordinary formatting get 0 reward**:

| Response | Method | Extracted on `main` | Score on `main` | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#### 72.` | strict | `72.` | 0 | 1 |
| `#### $300` | strict | `None` (the regex rejects `$`; the existing `.replace("$", "")` was dead code) | 0 | 1 |
| `#### 18.00` | strict | `18.00` | 0 | 1 |
| `Total is 72.` | flexible | `72.` | 0 | 1 |
| `So she earns 1,000 dollars.` | flexible | `1,000` (strict strips commas, flexible did not) | 0 | 1 |
| `The answer is 42, right, ok` | flexible | `,` | format_score | 1 |
| `No numbers here, really.` | flexible | `,` | format_score | 0 |

Fix: normalize every extracted candidate (drop thousands separators, trailing periods and trailing decimal zeros) and only accept candidates that contain a digit. Every GSM8k ground truth is an integer (checked all 8,792 train and test answers), so dropping trailing decimal zeros cannot turn a wrong answer into a correct one. The `####` marker is still required in strict mode.

### How much this matters on real model outputs

I sampled one response per GSM8k test question (n=1319) with the exact prompt from `examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py`, temperature 1.0 (rollout default), max 1024 new tokens, using MLX on a MacBook. I then scored the same responses with `main` and with this PR:

| Responses | Method | reward=1 on `main` | reward=1 with this PR | 0→1 | 1→0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | strict | 11 (0.8%) | 15 (1.1%) | 4 | 0 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | flexible | 359 (27.2%) | 412 (31.2%) | 53 | 0 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | strict | 164 (12.4%) | 175 (13.3%) | 11 | 0 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | flexible | 701 (53.1%) | 835 (63.3%) | 134 | 0 |

- **flexible**: on `main`, 13–16% of the answers that the fixed scorer accepts got 0 (53/412 for 0.5B, 134/835 for 1.5B). Most of these are a trailing period, a thousands separator or `$X.00`. For 61 (0.5B) and 10 (1.5B) responses, a bare `,` or `...` was extracted as the "answer".
- **strict** (the default path): before RL, only 30–36% of responses use the `####` marker, so the absolute effect is smaller. Still, 11 of the 175 answers that 1.5B gets right under the fixed scorer (6%) were scored 0 on `main` (`#### $29.00`, `#### 6.00`, `#### 25.`). These are the formats a policy produces once it learns the marker, and the reward currently treats them like wrong answers.
- **No response that scored 1 on `main` scores 0 with this PR.** I hand-checked a random sample of the 0→1 flips. All were the model's final answer, except one where flexible's existing "last number in the text" rule picked a number from the question that happened to equal the answer. That behavior is unchanged by this PR.

### Relation to existing PRs (why this is not a duplicate)

Search: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+gsm8k

- #7274 fixes a different bug in the same function: the answer is dropped when it lies outside the 300-character tail window. It does not normalize the extracted string, so every case in the table above still fails with it. Its only overlap with this PR is the leaked loop variable that returns `"."`. To make rebasing easy, this PR leaves the windowing code untouched and puts its tests in a separate file.
- #7789 only makes the extraction method configurable. It does not touch extraction.

### Test

```bash
pytest -q tests/utils/reward_score/test_gsm8k_answer_normalization_on_cpu.py
# 28 passed  (on main: 17 failed; with #7274 applied instead: 16 failed)
pre-commit run --files verl/utils/reward_score/gsm8k.py tests/utils/reward_score/test_gsm8k_answer_normalization_on_cpu.py
# all hooks passed
```

The new test file ends in `_on_cpu.py`, so it runs in `cpu_unit_tests.yml`.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. `extract_solution` / `compute_score` keep their signatures. Only the returned answer string is normalized.

### AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and the evaluation above myself, and can answer questions about the change.

items.title: [rollout, sglang] fix: use SGLang's Triton MoE runner for bf16 rollouts on Blackwell
items.author: wengeezhang
items.summary: Fixes #8229: on Blackwell, a bf16 SGLang rollout of a Qwen3-MoE model crashes at the first weight sync. On compute capability 10.x, SGLang resolves to for unquantized Qwen3-MoE-family checkpoints.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8229: on Blackwell, a bf16 SGLang rollout of a Qwen3-MoE model crashes at the first weight sync.

On compute capability 10.x, SGLang resolves `moe_runner_backend=auto` to `flashinfer_trtllm` for unquantized Qwen3-MoE-family checkpoints. That runner keeps bf16 expert weights in a block layout, and `update_weights_from_tensor` restores the load-time shape only for `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`. The first sync therefore fails in `FusedMoE._load_w13` (`The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (512)`), and the SGLang scheduler exits. Upstream: sgl-project/sglang#27787. It still reproduces on sglang 0.5.20 and 0.5.21; the fixes in sgl-project/sglang#33743 and sgl-project/sglang#44163 are not merged.

This PR has verl ask SGLang for the Triton MoE runner under the same conditions in which SGLang picks `flashinfer_trtllm` on sm100 (its Qwen3-MoE- and DeepSeek-family rules), that is when all of the following hold:
- neither the rollout nor the checkpoint is quantized: `rollout.quantization` is unset and the HF config has no `quantization_config`, which SGLang would detect on its own;
- `engine_kwargs.sglang.moe_runner_backend` is unset or `auto`;
- `engine_kwargs.sglang.moe_a2a_backend` is unset or `none`;
- the GPU is CUDA with compute capability 10.x.

Triton is the runner SGLang's unquantized MoE method falls back to everywhere else, and it takes weight updates. The following keep SGLang's own choice:
- quantized rollouts or checkpoints;
- an a2a backend;
- an explicit runner;
- Hopper and other GPUs;
- ROCm.

The architecture lists are not copied. On other architectures SGLang already lands on Triton, so the default changes nothing there.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. No open issue or PR covers this:
  - [moe_runner_backend](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+moe_runner_backend)
  - [flashinfer_trtllm bf16](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+flashinfer_trtllm+bf16)
  - [_load_w13](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=_load_w13)

  The closest is #7978 (closed), the same failure mode on vLLM's TRT-LLM MoE backend.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

- **CPU unit test, run and then removed at review:** a 16-case test of `default_moe_runner_backend` (each condition above, `engine_kwargs` as an OmegaConf `DictConfig`, ROCm, and capabilities 9.0, 10.0, 10.3, 12.0 and unknown) passed locally: 25 passed together with `test_lora_merge_mode_on_cpu.py`. A maintainer asked to drop it, and `e8080be0` removes it.
- **pre-commit on the changed files:** ruff, ruff format, mypy, license, docstring coverage, device API usage and test structure all pass. `autogen-trainer-cfg` could not run locally because hydra-core is missing there; no config file changes.
- **On 1×B200**, this PR against its base on the same pod with the same config; nothing sets `moe_runner_backend`. Environment: verl main's `uv.lock` (sglang 0.5.20, flashinfer 0.6.18, TE 2.16.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130), Megatron backend, a random 2-layer Qwen3-MoE (8 experts), GSM8K, bf16 SGLang rollout, 4 steps.

  | verl | MoE runner | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | this PR (`8b9ca7df`) | Triton, picked by this PR. Server log: `sglang moe_runner_backend=triton: SGLang's default on Blackwell cannot take bf16 weight updates (sgl-project/sglang#27787); ...` | 4/4 steps, exit 0. rollout_corr/kl by step: 1.8e-4, 6.1e-5, 1.2e-4, 4.3e-5 |
  | base main (`2bc6ac46`) | SGLang's default `flashinfer_trtllm` (the server autotunes `flashinfer::trtllm_bf16_moe`) | Fails at the first weight sync: `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 2` in `FusedMoE._load_w13`, then "Scheduler hit an exception" and exit 1 |

  On that GPU (compute capability 10.0), `default_moe_runner_backend` returns `"triton"` for bf16, `None` for fp8, and `None` when a runner is set explicitly.

  These runs used `8b9ca7df`, before `1d2f5ad5` narrowed the conditions above. The validated case meets every one of them, so the result carries over: a bf16 rollout of an unquantized checkpoint, no a2a backend, runner unset.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. To keep SGLang's own choice on Blackwell, set it explicitly, for example:

```
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.sglang.moe_runner_backend=flashinfer_trtllm
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/rollout/sglang_rollout/utils.py`: new `default_moe_runner_backend(quantization, engine_kwargs, hf_config)`. It returns `"triton"` under the conditions listed above, and `None` otherwise, which keeps SGLang's choice.
- `verl/workers/rollout/sglang_rollout/async_sglang_server.py`: `launch_server` passes the rollout quantization, `engine_kwargs` and the model's HF config, applies the result to the server args, and logs the choice.

The default can be dropped once SGLang restores the layout for `flashinfer_trtllm` itself.

- [x] Apply pre-commit checks (see Test; `autogen-trainer-cfg` needs hydra-core, no config changes here).
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation: not needed, no user-facing option changes.
- [ ] Add unit test(s): none in the final diff; the CPU test was removed at review (see Test).
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.

items.title: [rollout, sglang] bf16 MoE weight sync crashes on Blackwell with SGLang's default MoE runner (flashinfer_trtllm)
items.author: wengeezhang
items.summary: The SGLang scheduler raises in and exits: ### Cause (SGLang) - With, SGLang picks on sm100 for unquantized Qwen3-MoE-family checkpoints. restores the load-time shape before the copy only for.
items.body:
### Problem

On Blackwell (B200, compute capability 10.0), a bf16 SGLang rollout of a Qwen3-MoE model fails at the first weight sync (`on_init_end` → `update_weights`). The SGLang scheduler raises in `FusedMoE._load_w13` and exits:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 2
```

### Cause (SGLang)

- With `moe_runner_backend=auto`, SGLang picks `flashinfer_trtllm` on sm100 for unquantized Qwen3-MoE-family checkpoints ([`arg_groups/model_overrides/qwen3_moe.py` L81–93 at v0.5.20](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/v0.5.20/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/model_overrides/qwen3_moe.py#L81-L93)).
- That runner stores the bf16 expert weights in a block layout. `update_weights_from_tensor` restores the load-time shape before the copy only for `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` ([`unquant.py` L897–910](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/v0.5.20/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py#L897-L910)).
- Upstream report: sgl-project/sglang#27787. It still reproduces on sglang 0.5.20 and 0.5.21, and the fixes (sgl-project/sglang#33743, sgl-project/sglang#44163) are not merged yet.

### Reproduction

- **Setup:** 1×B200 with verl main's `uv.lock` environment: sglang 0.5.20, flashinfer 0.6.18, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Megatron backend.
- **Model and run:** a randomly initialized 2-layer Qwen3-MoE (8 experts, hidden 512, moe_intermediate 256), GSM8K, `rollout.name=sglang`, bf16, 4 steps.
- **Results:**
  - main at b3946294: fails as above at the first weight sync.
  - The same run with `+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.sglang.moe_runner_backend=triton` completes all 4 steps (rollout_corr/kl 5e-5 to 1.6e-4).
  - The same run on Hopper is not affected: SGLang's override above applies on sm100 only.

### Proposal

Until SGLang restores the layout itself, have verl ask SGLang for the Triton MoE runner for unquantized rollouts on compute capability 10.x when `engine_kwargs.sglang.moe_runner_backend` is not set. An explicit setting keeps working as before.

items.title: [algo, trainer, vllm] feat: add ResOPD sparse on-policy distillation
items.author: yph22
items.summary: ResOPD integrates the teacher top-k head and aggregate tail analytically and samples only the within-tail residual, estimating the full-vocabulary reverse-KL gradient. Use an existing synchronous OPD configuration with: See for the complete configuration overr…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add `distillation.distillation_loss.loss_mode=resopd`, implementing [ResOPD: Tail Residualization for Sparse On-Policy Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04882) from the [implementation](https://github.com/InternLM/ResOPD). ResOPD integrates the teacher top-k head and aggregate tail analytically and samples only the within-tail residual, estimating the full-vocabulary reverse-KL gradient.

Use an existing synchronous OPD configuration with:

```yaml
distillation.distillation_loss.loss_mode: resopd
distillation.distillation_loss.topk: 4
distillation.distillation_loss.use_policy_gradient: false
distillation.distillation_loss.use_task_rewards: false
distillation.distillation_loss.loss_max_clamp: null
distillation.distillation_loss.log_prob_min_clamp: null
actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels: false
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_torch_compile: false
```

See `docs/algo/opd.md` for the complete configuration overrides.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched [ResOPD](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+ResOPD), [distillation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+distillation), and tail residual; inspected the related PRs and #6676 discussion.

- #7855 adds coarse **forward** KL with a tail bucket; it does not sample the within-tail residual to estimate full reverse KL.
- #7590 / #7806 implement truncated reverse KL on the **student** top-k support. ResOPD uses teacher top-k plus the actual sampled token and does not require the fixed-token scoring extension in #7806.

### Test

Python 3.12.12, PyTorch 2.10.0, CPU only, one thread:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/trainer/test_resopd_on_cpu.py \
  tests/trainer/test_resopd_integration_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py
# 45 passed

# With the same CPU/thread environment:
python -m pytest tests/workers/test_distillation_topk_symmetry_on_cpu.py -q
# 6 passed
```

Coverage: independent per-action gradient formula and expected full reverse-KL gradient (all five actions, four support sizes, three seeds), teacher detachment, low precision, negative surrogate values, teacher requests, causal response masking, sequence-parallel slicing/padding, and unchanged legacy parser behavior. Teacher RPC and SP ranks are mocked; no model weights are loaded.

All 14 configured pre-commit hooks passed on the changed files, including generated-config verification, Ruff, mypy, license and compilation checks. `git diff --check` and the PR-title validator passed. An AST comparison confirms that `resopd_loss` has identical logic to the authors' release.

An end-to-end GPU training run of this upstream port has not been performed. CPU validation used PyTorch 2.10.0, rather than the current upstream lock's 2.13.0; the repository dependency files are unchanged.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md; checked for duplicate work.
- [x] Added documentation and CPU tests discovered by the existing `*_on_cpu.py` workflow.
- [x] Pre-commit checks on all changed files.
- [x] Reviewed by the ResOPD author; the requested documentation edit is included.
- [x] Maintainer CI authorization, if required.

AI assistance: this port and its tests were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance at the ResOPD author's request.

items.title: [training_utils, cfg] feat: per-stage SkipManager configs for reward/log-probs/values/actor-update/weight-sync
items.author: knlnguyen1802
items.summary: Generalizes the SkipManager protocol from rollout-only to training-loop stages, implementing PR 1 of the RFC in verl-omni#716. Six new stage roles —,,,,, — each individually gated by step lists, cacheable/replayable through the existing protocol, and …
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Generalizes the SkipManager protocol from rollout-only to training-loop stages, implementing PR 1 of the RFC in verl-omni#716 ([SkipManager for every RL pipeline stage](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/issues/716)).

Six new stage roles — `reward`, `old_log_prob`, `ref_log_prob`, `values`, `actor_update`, `weight_sync` — each individually gated by step lists, cacheable/replayable through the existing `BaseSkip` protocol, and all **disabled by default** (zero behavior change when `skip.*` is unset; existing rollout-skip behavior is untouched). Trainer hook sites on the V1 trainer land in a follow-up PR.

- `StageSkipConfig` (`enable/dump_dir/steps/action/ack_debug`) + six `SkipManagerConfig` fields; the dormant `SkipAction.EMPTY` becomes reachable but is validated per role — accepted only by the debug-only `actor_update`/`weight_sync` stages (`reward`/`old_log_prob`/`ref_log_prob`/`values` accept `cache`/`repeat` only)
- `TrainerStageSkip` base (`verl/utils/skip/stage_skip.py`): the cache for one `(role, step)` is the stage's declared batch columns plus the returned metrics, stored under `{dump_dir}/{exp}_{proj}/GBS{gbs}/{step}/{role}/`; handles both `DataProto` and `TensorDict` batches (the V1 / diffusion paths)
- fail-closed conflict assertions in `SkipManager.init`:
  - `skip.old_log_prob` x `algorithm.rollout_correction.bypass_mode` — both replace the old-log-prob recompute pass (bypass reuses rollout log probs, skip replays cached ones), so enabling both is ambiguous
  - `skip.weight_sync` requires `skip.weight_sync.ack_debug=True` — skipping weight sync stalls rollout progress and is debug-only
- `skip/<role>` hit counters (`SkipManager.record_hit` / `SkipManager.summary()`), incremented only on successful short-circuits in `annotate`/`annotate_tq`; validation rollouts keep bypassing skip entirely

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+skip+manager — no open PR generalizes skip beyond rollout; #5838 (adaptive zero-advantage skipping) is a separate effort per the RFC's non-goals; #7708 is the skip-manager docs fix the RFC plans to coordinate with
- [x] Title formatted `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

Extended `tests/utils/test_utils_skip.py` with six test classes: per-role action whitelists (incl. `empty` rejected on metric stages), both conflict assertions through `SkipManager.init`, default-disabled instantiation of all roles, counter record/summary/reset, `annotate` cache round-trips for `DataProto` and `TensorDict` batches (dump pass, then replay pass asserts the method body did not run and metrics/columns are identical), `repeat` fallback, and `empty`-action no-ops.

Run locally (the dev host has no torch, so the pytest additions execute in CI rather than locally):
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` (0.12.2) — clean
- `python -m py_compile` on all changed modules — clean
- `scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh` — all four `_generated_ppo_*.yaml` regenerated, purely additive (+31 lines each, the six skip entries)
- a torch-free harness executing the real modules (config validation, registry, conflict raises through `init`, counters, dump-dir layout, `empty` semantics) — 8/8 assertion groups pass

### API and Usage Example

```yaml
# replay old-log-probs for steps 1-3 from a previous run's cache
skip:
  old_log_prob:
    enable: True
    dump_dir: /path/to/stage_dump
    steps: [1, 2, 3]
    action: cache
  weight_sync:        # debug only: freeze rollout weights
    enable: True
    steps: [1, 2, 3]
    action: empty
    ack_debug: True   # required, otherwise SkipManager.init raises
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/skip/config.py`: `StageSkipConfig` dataclass + six `SkipManagerConfig` fields (the three rollout configs are intentionally left as-is — collapsing them into aliases would either change the rollout `dump_dir` default or leak `ack_debug` into rollout configs)
- `verl/utils/skip/stage_skip.py` (new): `TrainerStageSkip` + `RewardSkip`, `OldLogProbSkip`, `RefLogProbSkip`, `ValuesSkip`, `ActorUpdateSkip`, `WeightSyncSkip`
- `verl/utils/skip/skip_manager.py`: `hit_counters`/`record_hit`/`summary`, `_assert_stage_conflicts`, counter increments at the short-circuit sites
- `verl/trainer/config/ppo_trainer.yaml`: six stage entries in the `skip:` block (+ the four regenerated `_generated_*.yaml`)
- `tests/utils/test_utils_skip.py`: six new test classes

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide
- [x] pre-commit: ruff check/format clean locally and the trainer-config generation verified via the real script (see Test); the full pre-commit suite runs in CI
- [ ] Documentation: skip-manager doc updates land in the docs PR of this stack (coordinated with #7708), not here
- [x] Unit tests added (CI executes them; dev host has no torch — see Test)
- [ ] Slack `ci-request`: will ping once the PR is ready for CI runs

items.title: Fix FP8/FP4 context loss during GDN and KDA recompute
items.author: QiZhangNV
items.summary: When selective recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward.
items.body:
When selective `gdn` recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward. With MXFP8 parameter gathering enabled, this can also cause a missing `main_grad` error.

Use `te_checkpoint` for FP8/FP4 in GDN and KDA to preserve the quantization context, keeping the existing checkpoint path for non-quantized configurations.

Validated with 12 GPU regression cases and a single-node, four-GPU Qwen-style proxy covering MXFP8, NVFP4, and MXFP8 parameter gathering.

Separate RNG configuration finalization from container validation.

items.summary: Adds AMD ROCm (gfx950 / MI350X) support to vime's CI: a ROCm training image, a Buildkite GPU pipeline, and ROCm-adapted vllm-config test variants. All ROCm-specific logic is isolated into ROCm-only files so shared CUDA/runtime code is untouched.
items.body:
## Summary

Adds AMD ROCm (gfx950 / MI350X) support to vime's CI: a ROCm training image, a Buildkite GPU pipeline, and ROCm-adapted vllm-config test variants. All ROCm-specific logic is isolated into ROCm-only files so shared CUDA/runtime code is untouched.

## What's included

**ROCm image — `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`**
Layers vime's training half (TransformerEngine, apex, Megatron-LM, torch_memory_saver, vime) on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`. Based on @indianspeedster's rebuild (#432), plus fixes:
- **`pyarrow==25.0.1`** — the base ships pyarrow 26.0.0, a numpy-2 build that rejects the `numpy==1.26.4` pin Megatron requires at import (breaking Ray serialization + HF `datasets`). 25.0.1 is the newest wheel that imports under numpy 1.26.4 and still satisfies `datasets>=24`.
- **`vllm-generation-health.patch`** applied — provides the `/health_generate` route the rollout health monitor polls (the slim patch set had dropped it).
- Dropped unused `megatron-energon` / `multi-storage-client`; `CMD ["sleep", "infinity"]` so `docker run -d` stays up for `docker exec`.

**ROCm-rebased vLLM patches — `docker/amd_patch/latest/`**
The nightly base needs patches rebased from the shared `docker/patch/latest/` set (the CUDA versions apply without rejects but silently misplace a hunk under `--fuzz`). These live in a **separate ROCm-only directory** (alongside the existing ROCm megatron patches) so the CUDA `docker/Dockerfile`'s shared patches are left byte-identical — **the CUDA image build is unaffected**.

**Buildkite pipeline — `.buildkite/pipeline-rocm.yaml`**
Manual-gated GPU suites on the self-hosted gfx950 (MI355X) queue. Each step sets the ROCm device-visibility env (`RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_{HIP,CUDA,ROCR}_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, stopping Ray from rewriting gpu_lock's HIP pin) and RCCL env (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 / P2P/IB disable`), and normalizes `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to the locked HIP set for non-contiguous GPU allocations.

**Test variants — `tests/*-rocm.py`**
ROCm-adapted vllm-config / mixed-offload suites carrying the ROCm-only flags (`--no-gradient-accumulation-fusion`, vLLM mem-util 0.3, `--update-weight-transport disk` for colocate). Added as standalone `-rocm.py` files so `actor.py` / `command_utils.py` / the base test files aren't modified.

# What does this PR do?

Runs the two Nemotron 3.5 Lightning GB200 functional tests (`..._ep8_dgx_gb200` nightly and `..._ep4_dgx_gb200_1N4G`) and the two Nemotron 3 Super release tests (`nemotron3_super_release_gb200`, `..._gb200_sm`) in `--deterministic-mode`, so CI compares them bit for bit.

Changes in each `model_config.yaml`:

| Change | Reason |
|---|---|
| `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO: 0`, `NCCL_ALGO: Ring`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG: :4096:8` | Deterministic env values; also remove `NON_DETERMINSTIC_RESULTS` |
| `--deterministic-mode: true` | Enables the mode |
| Drop `--cross-entropy-loss-fusion` and `--cross-entropy-fusion-impl` | Deterministic mode rejects fused cross-entropy |

`--attention-backend` and the HybridEP dispatcher are unchanged.

## Testing

Ran each recipe's `MODEL_ARGS` and `ENV_VARS` on GB200 (26.10 rc5 image) with `--mock-data` and a fresh init instead of the Pile data and frozen checkpoint, which are not available on my cluster. Each recipe ran twice:

| Recipe | Nodes | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [1N4G (EP4)](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/nvidia/mbridge-dev-zhiyul?nw=0pkjc1ukr7rk) | 1 | 20/20 iterations, both runs bit-identical |

| [Super 64n](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/adlr/mbridge-dev-zhiyul?nw=eppi14wwbda) | 64 | 20/20 iterations, both runs bit-identical |

Compared at full float32 over all 20 steps: lm loss, mtp_1 loss, mtp_2 loss, num-zeros, grad norm, load-balancing loss.

- HybridEP is listed as not yet verified in the determinism docs. This is evidence at 8 GPUs and 20 steps only.

- `TRITON_CACHE_AUTOTUNING: 1` in all four recipes, and `_run_training.sh` defaults `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` to `$OUTPUT_PATH/triton_cache` when it is 1 (deterministic mode requires a shared cache dir; the image defaults the flag to 1). 1N4G A/B (cold) and a warm rerun, and a 2-node nightly A/B, are bit-identical over 20 iterations on GB200 (mock data). items.title: [hardware, doc] feat: speed up the Qwen3-4B TPU GRPO example (256 concurrent rollouts, micro batch 4, 1024-token buckets)
items.author: jialei777
items.summary: Roughly halves the step time of the Qwen3-4B TPU GRPO example (, added in #8225) with three defaults: - 32 -> 256: vLLM decodes all 32 x 8 rollouts of a batch at once. With 32 concurrent sequences the trainer waited 35-45 s per step in the weight-sync pause f…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Roughly halves the step time of the Qwen3-4B TPU GRPO example (`examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`, added in #8225) with three defaults:

- `MAX_NUM_SEQS` 32 -> 256: vLLM decodes all 32 x 8 rollouts of a batch at once. With 32 concurrent sequences the trainer waited 35-45 s per step in the weight-sync pause for in-flight requests; now ~0.1 s.
- `MICRO_BATCH_SIZE` 1 -> 4, also used for `actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu`: 4 sequences per micro batch in the actor update and the reference log-probs halves the trainer time.
- `pad_to_length=True`, `pad_to_length_bucket=1024` (the reference model inherits them): packed micro batches are padded to 1024-token buckets instead of 256, so the at most 6 shapes all compile in the first step instead of new shapes compiling during training.

Not a duplicate: the only other change to these files was #8225.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+tpu
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

2 TPU v6e-4 slices (4 trainer + 4 rollout chips), GKE spot, image built from `examples/tpu/grpo/Dockerfile`, `verl-hardware-plugin` `main`. Command from `examples/tpu/grpo/README.md` with `TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 TEST_FREQ=100 VAL_BEFORE_TRAIN=False`:

| Per step (s) | `main` (micro batch 1, 32 seqs) | + micro batch 4 | + 256 seqs | This PR (+ 1024-token buckets) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `update_actor` | ~26 | 13-14 (23-38 when compiling) | 11-13 (23-25 when compiling) | 11.7-12.7 (steps 2-10) |
| `ref` | ~5.0 | 2.6-2.9 (7-12 when compiling) | 2.3-2.7 (7-7.5 when compiling) | 2.5-3.0 (steps 2-10) |
| weight-sync pause (`tpu-sync/quiesce`) | 25-35 | 35-43 | 0.03-0.14 | ~0.1 |
| `step`, mean of steps 2-10 | ~72 | 67 | 35.5 | **32.0-32.8** |

- Each run 10/10 steps, reward rising to ~0.55-0.65 by step 10 in all configurations, response lengths unchanged.
- Validation of this branch as committed (no overrides besides `RAY_DATA_HOME`): 10/10 steps, all 20 model compiles in step 1, `update_actor` 11.0-12.1 s and `ref` 2.5-2.9 s from step 3, weight sync ~1.8 s, mean step over steps 2-10 **32.0 s**.
- Tried and not adopted (no gain or slower): `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` (32.2 s), `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85` (32.0 s), 2 batches in flight with `MAX_NUM_SEQS=512` (43.5 s).
- With 256-token buckets, sums of 4 sequences take up to 24 packed lengths, and steps that met a new one paid 10-25 s of compiles (steps 3, 5, 7); with 1024-token buckets every shape compiles in step 1.
- The step is now bound by the rollout (~35-40 s per batch); steps whose batch was already generated take ~17 s.
- Memory fits on 4 trainer chips, but libtpu logs more recoverable `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED ... Fragmentation` allocation retries than at micro batch 1. `MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=1 MAX_NUM_SEQS=32` restores the old rollout and trainer batching.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. `MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=1 MAX_NUM_SEQS=32 bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh` keeps the previous settings.

### Design & Code Changes

- `run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`: `MAX_NUM_SEQS` default 32 -> 256; `MICRO_BATCH_SIZE` default 1 -> 4; `actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu` uses `${MICRO_BATCH_SIZE}` (was 1); `actor_rollout_ref.actor.torchtitan.pad_to_length=True` and `pad_to_length_bucket=1024`.
- `examples/tpu/grpo/README.md`: expected 4B step time ~70 s -> 30-40 s.
- `docs/hardware/multi_chip_support.rst`: list Google TPU v6e with a link to `examples/tpu/grpo` instead of "experimental, under development".
