items.title: [Tracking] Disaggregated inference: remaining limitations and follow-up work
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Requested in so deferred work is not recorded only in documentation or PR threads. This is a tracking issue, not a claim that every item blocks #6675.
items.body:
## Purpose

Track remaining limitations and follow-up work for native and Dynamo disaggregated inference introduced by #6675. Requested in [review](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6675#discussion_r4264024875) so deferred work is not recorded only in documentation or PR threads.

This is a tracking issue, not a claim that every item blocks #6675. Split implementation work into linked issues/PRs and check an item off only when its implementation and validation are complete.

## Unsupported capabilities

- [ ] **KV/SSM registration across suspend/resume and memory relocation.** Both roles currently require `kv_cache_management_mode=persist`; `offload` and `recompute` are rejected. Define pause/drain/rebind ordering, including TMS interactions; refresh transfer registrations and peer metadata whenever backing buffers change, without releasing memory that a remote reader can still access. Test KV and hybrid conv/SSM state on both roles. [Review discussion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6675#discussion_r4258875847).
- [ ] **MoE routing replay across the handoff.** Transfer prompt routing buffers and join them with decode routing data. Setup currently rejects routing replay. Request UID, policy/KV epoch history, eviction history, and final-only ledger/stager writes are already handled; those are not the missing replay feature.
- [ ] **Prompt and top-N log-probabilities.** Transfer the required prompt-side outputs and preserve frontend semantics. Native disaggregation currently rejects these requests; selected generated-token log-probabilities are supported.
- [ ] **Multimodal handoffs.** Define and validate the media/state contract; native disaggregation currently accepts text/token prompts only.
- [ ] **Context-parallel inference shards.** Current shard specifications require `cp=1`; supporting other layouts needs an explicit state-transfer layout and end-to-end validation.
- [ ] **NCCL handoff between independently launched Dynamo workers.** Currently rejected because workers have separate process groups. It requires cross-worker group setup and coordinated receive readiness before sends, including failure handling. Native NCCL handoff within a shared launch is already supported; this restriction does not cover model-parallel or weight-transfer NCCL collectives.

## Design follow-ups

- [ ] **SamplingParams wire-format cleanup.** Separate validated request construction from reconstruction of already-normalized wire data so `__post_init__` cannot reinterpret it. The concrete top-N crash is guarded in #6675; the broader cleanup remains. [Review discussion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6675#discussion_r4254143646).
- [ ] **Evaluate routing decode-eviction recovery back to prefill.** Current recovery reuses the base engine's local recomputation path, with import/recovery coordination; an `EVICT` round trip is an optional follow-up, not required to avoid the previously reported crash. [Review discussion and current behavior](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6675#discussion_r4260904805).

## Deployment and validation follow-ups

- [ ] **External-supervisor recovery integrations.** The termination-confirmation hook and ownership protocol exist. Validate concrete Slurm/Ray/Kubernetes integrations that prove the old adapter and *all* decode ranks have stopped before reclaiming source state, including unreachable-node fencing and coordinator/engine lifecycle coupling. A timeout or replacement worker becoming healthy is not that proof.
- [ ] **Repeatable functional coverage for native and Dynamo serving and RL.** Cover checkpoint-backed Nemotron Nano, multi-rank TP/PP/EP, one-token handoffs, cancellation, cache pressure, refit/epoch transitions, and modern Gym ledger/stager behavior. Targeted unit tests and small-model runs do not establish all of these deployment combinations.
- [ ] **Batch-invariant hybrid recovery comparison.** A longer BF16 recovery run diverged from uninterrupted output, also on the ordinary aggregated recovery baseline. Repeat with a compatible batch-invariant TransformerEngine environment before attributing this to disaggregation. [Results and limitation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6675#discussion_r4260904805).

## Related existing reports

Keep root-cause/fix status in these issues rather than duplicating it here:

- #7835 — one-token handoff and subsequent EP progress.
- #7898 — EP=1 dummy recurrent-state allocation under pressure.

## Usage and current contracts

- [Native usage and limitations](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6d2a8487cb09d6f1a4cd67ef45808466be21a109/docs/mcore-inference-user-guide.md#disaggregated-prefill-and-decode).
- [Dynamo launch and external-recovery contracts](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6d2a8487cb09d6f1a4cd67ef45808466be21a109/megatron/inference/integrations/dynamo/README.md).

items.author: tomlifu
items.summary: With calculatepertokenloss=True and a Python-int token count, TopKRouter.attachandlogloadbalancingloss builds the aux-loss token count with torch.tensor(numlocaltokens, device=...). That copies from pageable host memory, which CUDA graph capture forbids, so pe…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
With calculate_per_token_loss=True and a Python-int token count, TopKRouter.attach_and_log_load_balancing_loss builds the aux-loss token count with torch.tensor(num_local_tokens, device=...). That copies from pageable host memory, which CUDA graph capture forbids, so per-layer CUDA graphs that include moe_router stop at capture with seq_aux_loss and global_aux_loss (a regression from #7046). Fill the count on the device with torch.full instead; the value, dtype and shape are unchanged.

Add TestPerTokenAuxLossCudaGraph, which captures and replays the router with per-token loss for both load-balancing types.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes the TPU GRPO examples in `examples/tpu/grpo/` run on `main` with `verl-hardware-plugin` and makes them reproducible from scratch: a `Dockerfile`, a KubeRay `RayCluster` for 2 TPU v6e-4 slices (8 chips), and a step-by-step README. Only `examples/tpu/grpo/` changes.

Requires verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#51 (torchtitan import fix) and verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#52 (weight sync backends renamed; the scripts use `tpu-sync`).

Why `main` did not run:

1. #8150 imports `LRSchedulersContainer` from `torchtitan.components.optimizer`; the torchtitan build used on TPU (`f880cc73`) only has it in `components.lr_scheduler`, so the TPU engine never registered. Fixed in the plugin (verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#51). Newer torchtitan does not help: its re-layout also removed modules verl's engine needs.
2. #8181 defaults `transfer_queue` `total_storage_size` to `null`, which needs `TransferQueue>=0.1.11`; the image has 0.1.8. The scripts set `transfer_queue.backend.SimpleStorage.total_storage_size=100000`.
3. `run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh` passed `spmd_backend=default` (removed in #8150), set plugin-only torchtitan fields without `+`, and used 32 rollout replicas, which `tpu-sync` rejects.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `examples/tpu` or these errors (searches below).

AI assistance (Jetski, Gemini) was used to debug, write the changes, run the TPU tests and draft this description. The submitter must review every changed line before merging.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+tpu , https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+LRSchedulersContainer , https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+total_storage_size
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

GKE, spot TPU v6e, image built from this `Dockerfile`, plugin verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#52 (includes #51). Jobs submitted with the README's commands on a `RayCluster` from `ray-tpu-v6e4-2slice.yaml`:

| Job | Layout | Script | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6B smoke test | 2x v6e-4 | `run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh` | 5/5 steps, ~9 s/step, weight sync 0.45 s |
| 4B, 5 steps | 2x v6e-4 | `TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=5 TEST_FREQ=5 run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh` | 5/5 steps, GSM8K val acc 0.414 -> 0.523, ~70 s/step |
| 4B, 5 steps | 2x v6e-8 (`NNODES_TRAINER=2 NNODES_ROLLOUT=2`) | same | 5/5 steps, GSM8K val acc 0.414 -> 0.523, ~73 s/step |
| 0.6B with the deprecated `backend=raiden` | 2x v6e-4 | `run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend=raiden` | 5/5 steps, same path, `FutureWarning` printed |

Before this PR, `main` + plugin `main` failed with the `LRSchedulersContainer` ImportError and then the `tq.init()` TypeError. Pre-commit passes on all changed files.

Known issues:

- 4B on 2x v6e-4 runs close to the trainer chips' HBM limit; libtpu logs recoverable `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED ... Fragmentation` allocation retries. 2x v6e-8 has headroom.
- 4B with `tpu-sync` on 2x v6e-8 hung 3 times in `update_actor` in earlier runs and passed in the latest one; looks like an intermittent stall, tracked in verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#52.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. See `examples/tpu/grpo/README.md`:

```bash
docker buildx build -t <IMAGE> --push examples/tpu/grpo
kubectl apply -f examples/tpu/grpo/ray-tpu-v6e4-2slice.yaml
ray job submit --working-dir . --runtime-env-json "$RUNTIME_ENV" -- bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh`: 5-step smoke test, `tpu-sync` weight sync.
- `run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`: 100-step GRPO run with `torch.compile`, splash attention, SimpleFSDP, `DEFER_AND_FUSE`, and `tpu-sync` weight sync.
- Both scripts: 2 single-host v6e-4 slices by default (`NNODES_TRAINER=2 NNODES_ROLLOUT=2` for 2 v6e-8 slices), models and data under `$RAY_DATA_HOME` (default `/data`, the bucket mount), `total_storage_size=100000`.
- `ray-tpu-v6e4-2slice.yaml` (new): `RayCluster` with 1 CPU head pod and 2 TPU v6e-4 slices, a GCS bucket mounted at `/data`; `<IMAGE>`, `<BUCKET>` and `<GSA_EMAIL>` are placeholders.
- `Dockerfile` (new): Ray 2.56, PyTorch 2.13 (CPU) + `torch_tpu`, JAX/`libtpu`, `tpu-sync`, torchtitan `f880cc73`, vLLM 0.29.0 + vllm-torchtpu, verl dependencies.
- `README.md`: prerequisites and 5 steps with every command (code, image, models and data, GKE and Ray cluster, run).

- [ ] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting) (on the changed files).
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs) (`examples/tpu/grpo/README.md`).
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: the examples need a multi-host TPU cluster, which the CI does not have. They were validated manually on TPU v6e (see Test).
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ).
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`. (Not related.)

items.title: fix(gdn2): AUT-2519 require TP×CP head divisibility for GDN2 context parallelism
items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: GDN2 (from main) always splits heads across CP ranks. Dev only counted CP in the head-divisibility check when, and dev's default is. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## Background

FDecaYed's review 5501312260 on #8112 found that dev's config check lets invalid GDN2 context-parallel layouts through. GDN2 (from main) always splits heads across CP ranks. Dev only counted CP in the head-divisibility check when `linear_cp_mode="headwise"`, and dev's default is `"chunkwise"`. So TP1/CP2 with 1 key head and 2 value heads passed validation and then failed at the Q/K split. This was found by reading the source; it was not reproduced on GPU.

## What changed

- `TransformerConfig`: when CP>1, GDN2 key and value head counts must be multiples of TP×CP in both `linear_cp_mode` settings.
- Under CP, GDN2 now raises a clear `ValueError` for `cp_partition_mode="contiguous"` and for `dynamic_context_parallel=True`. This matches the existing headwise-CP limits.
- GDN and KDA behave as before.
- The head-divisibility assert messages now also print `experimental_attention_variant`.
- Docs: added a GDN2 note to the `linear_cp_mode` docstring and to `docs/user-guide/features/context_parallel.md`.
- Tests: added `test_gdn2_head_divisibility_uses_tp_times_cp` (6 CP2 layouts), `test_gdn2_cp_support`, and a `gdn2-contiguous` case.

## Details

- This is dev-only. Main (`fb65908d`) already checks GDN heads against TP×CP for every variant, and main's `TransformerConfig` has no `cp_partition_mode` or `dynamic_context_parallel`.
- The GDN2 GPU tests use 4 key and 8 value heads with at most TP×CP=4, so their layouts are still valid.

## Tested

- Local, on CI image `megatron-lm@sha256:2cbc1243aead…`, whose dependency files are identical to `dev` `c75a269e`:
  - black, isort, ruff and pylint (10.00/10): clean.
  - `test_transformer_config_dynamic_cp.py`: 126 passed, including the 12 new GDN2 cases.
- CI on `e4487716`:
  - CICD Megatron-LM (run 38475067559), Installation Test, Copyright check and the Megatron-Core build passed.
  - 88 check runs succeeded, 7 were skipped and none failed.
  - The `tests/unit_tests/transformer/**/*.py` job ran all 12 new GDN2 cases and they passed.
- `codecov/patch` reports 67.40% of diff lines hit, against an 80% target, even though those 12 cases run every new branch.
  - The same job logged `CoverageWarning: No data was collected`.

items.body:
## what changed

stage dataset index arrays on the same filesystem, replace their final paths after all writes finish, and publish the description last. gpt, blended, and masked datasets use the same save path. cache names, formats, and existing read paths stay unchanged.

fixes #8189.

## why

an interrupted `numpy.save` currently leaves a truncated file that passes the cache hit check on restart. staging keeps incomplete writes away from the final paths. a normal restart rebuilds an incomplete cache, and existing readers keep their original mappings during replacement.

this prevents new torn writes. caches already damaged by earlier runs still need rebuilding. power-loss durability and fast-cache-load synchronization are outside this change.

## validation

- the three new gpt, blended, and bert recovery cases fail on main with a truncated-array error and pass with this change.
- 13 focused checks pass on linux with python 3.12, numpy 1.26.4, and torch 2.8.0a0 using cpu/gloo. these include the existing gpt and cache-preparation checks, including fast loading and deferred mmap. the existing checkpoint-directory fixture was reused. the full gpu test runner remains for ci.
- four separate process-exit scenarios pass, covering interruption during array writes and between replacements, fresh and existing caches, restart with leftover staging directories, and existing mmap readers.
- `tools/autoformat.sh` completed in check mode. black, isort, pylint, and ruff pass. its non-blocking mypy step reports existing type errors and missing imports in the lint environment.

items.title: fix(inference): accumulate the batch-invariant torch MoE combine in fp64 to match training
items.author: YigongQin
items.summary: Make the torch-backend batch-invariant MoE combine accumulate in fp64, matching training's batch-invariant unpermute, so MXFP8 (and torch-backend BF16) MoE layers give bitwise-identical training and generation outputs on tokens with outlier activations. Found …
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Make the torch-backend batch-invariant MoE combine accumulate in fp64, matching training's batch-invariant unpermute, so MXFP8 (and torch-backend BF16) MoE layers give bitwise-identical training and generation outputs on tokens with outlier activations.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none. Found while chasing nonzero train/generation KL in the Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP8 zero-KL RL recipe.

End-to-end verification: [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4683](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4683) (MXFP8 zero train/generation KL recipe, which needs this fix).

Related: [#6521](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6521) (fp64 top-k reduction in the vLLM backend's `_moe_sum`), [#6806](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6806) (training-side mirror of that reduction), [#7302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7302) (MXFP8 batch invariance and the parity test extended here).

## The bug

Under batch-invariant mode, training's `unpermute` (`megatron/core/transformer/moe/batch_invariant.py`) mirrors the inference engine's summation tree. When router probabilities are applied before the combine (gated SwiGLU and the batch-invariant squared-ReLU kernels), it sums each EP rank's expert contributions in **fp64**, then rounds the rank partial to fp32 once. That mirrors the vLLM backend's `_moe_sum(acc_fp64=True)` from #6521.

The torch backend's combine, `_unpermute_tokens_in_expert_order_kernel` (`megatron/core/inference/moe/batch_invariant.py`), summed the same contributions in **fp32**, in local-expert-id order. MXFP8 always runs this kernel, including vLLM-backend MXFP8 layers, which fall back to the mcore path.

fp32 is exact only while a token's contributions on a rank span roughly 16 binades. A typical token stays inside that, so both paths agree. An outlier token can have one dominant expert output (about ±31) next to contributions below 2^-20, which fp32 drops and fp64 keeps. Usually that is invisible after the final BF16 rounding. But when the large terms sum to exactly a BF16 halfway point, the dropped tail decides the rounding direction, and training and generation land one BF16 ULP apart.

## Why the existing test did not catch it

`test_batch_invariant_moe_matches_training` covers the right code path (NVLS dispatcher, `mcore_fused_moe`, the batch-invariant combine) with the wrong data:

- the `NANOV3_BASE` toy layer: hidden 128, 8 experts (2 per rank at EP=4), top-6;
- 17 + rank tokens per rank;
- plain `torch.randn` hidden states.

With Gaussian inputs, every token's expert outputs have similar magnitudes, so the fp32 sum is already exact and order-independent. The two accumulators can only diverge on inputs with a heavy-tailed scale.

## Reproduction (fails on `main`)

`test_batch_invariant_mxfp8_moe_matches_training_with_outlier_tokens` reuses the existing parity test with:

- the Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE shape and router: hidden 2048, FFN 768, 128 experts, top-8, softmax;
- 500 + rank tokens per rank;
- outlier inputs: `randn × exp(randn per token) × exp(0.5·randn per channel)`.

On `main` (4 × GB200, EP=4) it fails on rank 1:

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
Mismatched elements: 5 / 1026048 (0.0%)
Greatest absolute difference: 0.125 at index (457, 0, 685)
Greatest relative difference: 0.00714111328125 at index (457, 0, 1738)
```

Token 457 is an outlier row (input absmax 97.5 against a median row absmax of 10.75). The five elements that differ are its largest outputs, each off by exactly one BF16 ULP:

| column | training | generation |
|---|---|---|
| 333 | −12.125 | −12.0625 |
| 685 | −31.375 | −31.5 |
| 803 | −9.1875 | −9.125 |
| 1738 | −17.5 | −17.375 |
| 1970 | +31.875 | +31.75 |

Localization: a temporary probe (not part of this PR) fed each generation expert kernel's real inputs from this failing forward to its training counterpart. It ran on the real 32 local experts per rank, with training's 32-row padding against generation's 128.
- fc1 quantization, fc1 GEMM, SwiGLU and fc2 GEMM all matched bitwise on all four ranks.
- The fc2 input quantization differed only in the FP8 sign bit, consistent with +0 against −0, and the fc2 GEMM outputs still matched.
- So the experts are identical; the difference came from the combine.

## What changed

- `megatron/core/inference/moe/batch_invariant.py`: `_unpermute_tokens_in_expert_order_kernel` accumulates in fp64 and rounds once to the fp32 rank partial, matching training's `within_rank_fp64` mirror and the vLLM `_moe_sum`. The kernel is batch-invariant-only, so the default path is untouched. Memory traffic is unchanged (BF16 in, fp32 out), and there are at most top-k fp64 adds per element.
- `tests/unit_tests/inference/test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py`:
  - optional `config_overrides`, `base_local_tokens` and `outlier_tokens` arguments on the parity test (defaults keep every existing case unchanged);
  - the `_QWEN3_30B_A3B_MOE` shape;
  - the outlier-token test above;
  - an NVLS symmetric-buffer reset before allocation. Buffers are cached by name and sized on first use, so a larger-hidden case otherwise fails with `symmetric memory init failed [ep_agv_h, ep_rsv]`.

## Validation

4 × GB200, EP=4:

```bash
python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py \
  -k "batch_invariant_moe_matches_training or outlier_tokens"
```

- Before the fix: the outlier test fails (above); the existing cases pass.
- After the fix: all pass: `vllm`, `vllm-clamped`, `torch-mxfp8-swiglu`, `vllm-mxfp8-swiglu` and the new outlier test. Four cases are skipped by environment (no DeepGEMM BF16 kernels; the grouped-tensor case needs cuBLASLt 13.5.1).
- End to end: the NeMo-RL MXFP8 zero-KL recipe in [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4683](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4683) runs synchronous GRPO on Qwen3-30B-A3B. It uses Megatron training and non-colocated Megatron generation on the torch MXFP8 backend, with MXFP8 on every TE linear, on GB200 (2 nodes × 4 GPUs). With this fix in its Megatron-LM tree:
  - the all-MXFP8 nightly (job 988940) and an experts-only MXFP8 variant (job 988570) both ran 5 steps;
  - both recorded `train/gen_kl_error` exactly 0 and `train/token_mult_prob_error` exactly 1 on every step;
  - before the fix, the Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP8 recipe's `gen_kl_error` was nonzero.

  That PR depends on this one.
- Kernel and determinism suites: `test_moe_permute.py` (including `test_batch_invariant_unpermute_is_token_local`) and `test_inference_unpermute_batch_invariant_path_replays` pass (34 passed). `test_inference_default_unpermute_is_the_racy_path` XPASSed; it is the non-batch-invariant negative control and doesn't use the changed kernel.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel, I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` (`megatron/core/inference/moe/batch_invariant.py` is already registered; its replay test passes)
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

items.author: FDecaYed
items.summary: Keep backend/layout/static-CP validation, and test both mode settings against valid and invalid inputs. Unsupported deterministic runtimes and dense indexer backward still fail at their respective wrappers.
items.body:
## Purpose and relationship to the existing ports

Draft main-based companion for #7441, completing its **packed THD/static-CP attention/indexer determinism** coverage. The automated Mirror Dev to Main run for #7441 did not create a mirror: the source PR has no `mirror-to-main` label. The previous packed integration #7921 is closed without merging.

This is intentionally not a second monolithic copy of every #7441 change:

| Area | Main landing path |
| --- | --- |
| Stable Top-K, SBHD forward ordering, attention/indexer backward | #7708 (shared prerequisite, temporarily included here) |
| Packed THD/static CP, padding and forward/replay ordering | This draft, adapted from the two packed commits of #7921 |
| TE operation-fuser grouped-MLP probability gradients | Existing independent #7769; not duplicated here |
| Deterministic router auxiliary-loss guard | Already present on main through its dedicated auxiliary-loss-fusion option |

The branch starts from main `3bb482c487cd447a2b40a3bf076ab14cad514e13` and temporarily carries the three shared #7708 commits. Please land/reconcile #7708 first, then rebase this draft to keep the remaining packed-only diff. Its current scope includes the shared prerequisite so the branch is buildable against main; it does not target a bot `pull-request/*` branch.

## Changes

- Pass explicit deterministic mode through packed indexer Top-K and both packed attention backward paths, preserving default-mode dispatch and static CP process-group plumbing.
- Preserve compressed-first compact key order between no-grad and training forwards, with sink-only padded rows and no mutation of caller-owned index tensors.
- Keep clipped-KL/indexer gradients, global real-token normalization, and deferred CP reductions from the existing port.
- Remove main's now-obsolete blanket rejection of packed deterministic mode. Keep backend/layout/static-CP validation, and test both mode settings against valid and invalid inputs. Unsupported deterministic runtimes and dense indexer backward still fail at their respective wrappers.
- Mark the five parameterized SM100 attention/indexer regression cases for the GB200 lane. On #7708's current CI, H100 skips those cases and the GB200 bucket excludes their unmarked file; this draft explicitly selects them.
- Reconcile the single test-import conflict by retaining both main's `cp_utils` use and the packed port's `packed_sparse_attention` use.

Scratch allocation follows #7708's per-call cuDNN allocation strategy. This does **not** copy #7441's shared device-global workspace cache or resolve the outstanding review on that dev implementation.

## Attribution

Original deterministic DSv4 work: Haochen Yuan (@HaochenYuan), #7441. Stable Top-K/forward-ordering approach: Bo Li (@bobboli), #7169. Main shared and packed adaptations, batch-local indexing and clipped-KL corrections: Yan Xu (@Connor-XY), #7708 / #7706 / #7921. Cherry-picked commits retain original authors, co-author trailers, source SHAs and sign-offs, with signed Deyu Fu adaptation commits.

## Validation on this branch

- `BASE_REF=main CHECK_ONLY=true bash tools/autoformat.sh`: mandatory Black/isort/pylint/ruff checks passed for all nine changed files.
- Kernel determinism coverage checker: passed for all nine changed files; no exemption label or test disabling.
- 39 CPU-adapted exact-source numerical/replay/dispatch cases passed for the shared helpers.
- 10 exact-source CPU packed-wrapper/layout cases passed, including padding preservation, deterministic compaction and the new layout-validation regression.
- Structural check confirms explicit GB200 selection for the five SM100 regression variants.
- `git diff --check` and local signature/sign-off verification passed.

**Validation boundary:** Osaka has no GPU. These isolated CPU probes bypass GPU package/conftest initialization and stub kernel/collective work; they do not certify CUDA, CP1/2/4, graph replay, or the rebased branch's end-to-end numerics. Optional mypy still reports missing training dependencies/existing typing issues and is not certified clean. The earlier GB300 results documented in #7708/#7921 are provenance, not a claim that this new head passed GPU tests.

Keep this PR **draft** pending exact-head GPU CI (including the real packed CP and SM100 cases), reconciliation with #7708, and the required reviews. No performance claim and no whole-recipe determinism certification are made.

items.title: [Nemotron 4 Inference] Support Shortcut MoE Inference Overlap
items.author: susavlsh10
items.summary: Adds opt-in, CUDA graph compatible Shortcut MoE inference overlap for GDP and FlashAttention 2 layers. Serial inference remains the default, and existing training paths are preserved.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds opt-in, CUDA graph compatible Shortcut MoE inference overlap for GDP and FlashAttention 2 layers. Serial inference remains the default, and existing training paths are preserved.

## Overlap schedule

Two CUDA streams execute independent branches:

- **Main:** mixer normalization, projections, GDP/attention, output projection, then shared experts.
- **Shortcut:** routing → NVLS all-gather → token/expert preparation → routed GEMMs → output reduction → NVLS reduce-scatter.

The streams fork from the pair input and join before the final routed/shared output and residual update.

**Prefill/mixed** use the ordinary atomic mixer forward, supporting chunked prefill and existing graph shape selection. **Decode** uses projection/core/post adapters for launch ordering. GDP and FlashAttention run once for the full batch, without kernel splitting. Block CUDA graphs capture both branches and their dependencies.

## Configuration

- `--inference-shortcut-moe-overlap`
- `--inference-shortcut-moe-expert-max-blocks 304`

The expert limit bounds the routed GEMM launch grid to reduce compute interference; it does not reserve SMs. Zero disables the cap. Serial and training ignore it.

items.title: [rollout] guard delta-loader masked copy to model param/buffer storage (part of #7060 known issue)
items.author: Virtuoso461
items.summary: Part of the masked-copy guards known issue in #7060 (also relates to the low-precision scope of #5972 / the 26Q4 roadmap #8186). This ports guard (a) from THUDM/slime#1806: masked semantics now apply only to destinations whose storage belongs to the model's ow…
items.body:
Part of the masked-copy guards known issue in #7060 (also relates to the low-precision scope of #5972 / the 26Q4 roadmap #8186).

## What does this PR do?

**Guard (a):** the delta loader's masked-copy context patched `Tensor.copy_` globally — any same-shape floating `copy_` inside the window (temporaries, scratch tensors, other modules' state) was silently NaN-masked. This ports guard (a) from THUDM/slime#1806: masked semantics now apply **only** to destinations whose storage belongs to the model's own `named_parameters()` / `named_buffers()`, tracked as a sorted `data_ptr` interval index (bisect lookup, no per-call allocation); everything else passes through to the original `copy_`.

## Guard (b) — audit result (follow-up, needs sender-side signalling)

From reading SGLang's current `weight_updater.py`: on the custom-loader path, `end_weight_update` runs `post_load_weights` **only when no load ran** (`run_post_load = not self._session.loaded_weights`, P2P/RDMA case). So for the delta loader, derived tensors (fp8 scales, MoE biases, MLA `w_kc`/`w_vc`) are never recomputed after a masked apply — confirming the known issue. A complete fix needs the sender to flag which flushes require a post-load pass (e.g. a `post_load` bit in `__delta_spec__`) so `apply_delta` can call SGLang's `post_load_weights(model)` after leaving the masked context, without paying quant-recompute cost on every flush. I plan to send that as a follow-up PR against the delta checkpoint engine + loader; happy to take direction from maintainers on the wire-format part.

## Tests

New cases in `tests/checkpoint_engine/test_sglang_loader.py` (CPU-only):
- a foreign same-shape floating tensor copied inside the window goes through the original `copy_` (NaNs land), while the model param is masked — fails on the unpatched loader
- registered buffers are treated as model storage (mask applies)

Existing suite for the loader: 8 passed, no regressions. `_FakeModel` gained minimal `parameters()` / `named_buffers()` so the guard can index it.

items.summary: Clarify the units and arithmetic behind GRPO/PPO train, mini and micro batch sizes. The configured actor and critic values are prompt-equivalent global sizes; the trainers multiply them by before partitioning trajectories across the corresponding data-parallel…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Closes #1524.

Clarify the units and arithmetic behind GRPO/PPO train, mini and micro batch sizes. The configured actor and critic `ppo_mini_batch_size` values are prompt-equivalent global sizes; the trainers multiply them by `rollout.n` before partitioning trajectories across the corresponding data-parallel ranks.

Add the issue's `1024 / 256 / 80 / n=5` worked example, formulas for fixed-size gradient accumulation and optimizer-update counts, and explicit boundaries for dynamic token-budget batching, forward-only log-probability batches, multi-output rollouts, filtering, padding and asynchronous replay.

The explanation is linked from the PPO guide, configuration reference and batch-size FAQ. This changes documentation only: no runtime behavior, defaults, APIs, dependencies or CI configuration change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Queries: [#1524 references](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+1524+in%3Abody), [batch-size documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22batch+size%22+documentation), and [GRPO batch](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+GRPO+batch). No direct implementation was found. Related open PRs #8201, #6025 and #8026 concern mini-batch balancing, multi-output trajectories and batch invariance respectively; their relevant file diffs were inspected and they do not provide this worked unit explanation.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

The human submitter reviewed every changed line and confirmed completing the relevant local testing before submission, as required by `AGENTS.md`.

Automated checks run locally on Linux with Python 3.12.3:

- `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never`: all 14 hooks passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/special_sanity/test_config_docs.py tests/special_sanity/test_check_example_naming.py -q`: 15 passed.
- `git diff --check main`: passed.
- Full Sphinx HTML build completed. The generated example anchor, table and all three cross-page links were inspected programmatically and resolve correctly.
- A local-only verifier independently parsed the documented YAML and confirmed the expected counts: 5,120 rollout trajectories, 1,280 trajectories per global actor mini-batch, 160 per actor DP rank, two micro-batches per optimizer update, four updates for one PPO epoch and eight for two epochs.

The full Sphinx build reports 328 warnings on both the patch and untouched `main` in the same isolated documentation environment. After normalizing checkout paths and shifted source line numbers, the warning content is identical: zero diagnostic lines were added or removed. These include existing duplicate section labels, existing references/highlighting warnings and API autodoc imports unavailable in the isolated docs dependency set; this is not claimed as a warning-free build.

No model downloads, provider calls, GPU/multiprocess training, end-to-end training, complete training dependency installation, or non-Linux platform testing were performed. Those are not needed to exercise this documentation-only change.

### API and Usage Example

No API or configuration behavior changes. The documentation now explains the existing calculation. For the issue's fixed-size example with eight actor data-parallel ranks:

```text
B=1024, n=5, M=256, d=8, m=80, E=1
rollout trajectories = B*n = 5120
global actor mini-batch = M*n = 1280
local actor mini-batch = M*n/d = 160
micro-batches per optimizer update = M*n/(d*m) = 2
actor optimizer updates = (B/M)*E = 4
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Correct the canonical `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n` key and explain that configured PPO mini-batches use prompt-equivalent global units.
- Add a symbol table, formulas, divisibility checks and the original worked example to the GRPO guide.
- Distinguish actor data-parallel size from rollout tensor parallelism or total GPU count.
- Explain that dynamic token-budget micro-batching does not have a fixed micro-batch count and that rollout/reference log-probability micro-batches are forward-only.
- Cross-link the shared explanation from PPO, the configuration reference and FAQ.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used for issue auditing, documentation drafting and validation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the relevant tests, understands the calculation and remains responsible for the contribution.

- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to the CI workflow, or explain why tests are not applicable: no new runtime behavior exists; existing documentation/config sanity tests and the Sphinx build cover the changed files.
- [ ] Once the PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` Slack channel or Feishu group. I do not have access to either channel from this environment, so this has not been represented as completed.
- [x] If related to the `recipe` submodule, update its reference. Not applicable; the submodule is unchanged.

items.title: Add opt-in expert deployment layout exchange to mLite
items.author: lidongdongbuaa
items.summary: It preserves parameter names, shapes and dtypes, including FP8 values and scalar scales. Copy received byte ranges into aligned storage before reconstructing mixed dtypes.
items.body:
Superseded by #8283, a draft rebased onto current `dev`.

- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR. Pending author review; keep this PR as a draft.

# What does this PR do?

Add an opt-in mLite checkpoint primitive that redistributes materialized expert deployment tensors between different EP layouts without gathering the full expert set first. For example, EP2 to EP4 requires selecting one source replica and reaching destinations outside a single two-rank source EP group. The caller provides the exchange group; training ownership and existing export defaults are unchanged.

Fixes #8186. Related context: #7050.

## Changes

- `ExpertLayoutPlan` maps global expert IDs to source holders and all required destination replicas using an explicit ordered process group.
- `exchange_expert_layout_tensors` coordinates bounded collective rounds, including empty or exhausted senders, and exchanges opaque tensor bytes with `all_to_all_single`. It preserves parameter names, shapes and dtypes, including FP8 values and scalar scales.
- Validate source ownership, duplicate names, matching plans/budgets and group order before the corresponding tensor exchange. Copy received byte ranges into aligned storage before reconstructing mixed dtypes.
- Add usage and limitations documentation plus real multi-process CPU/Gloo tests for split/merge layouts, replicas, noncontiguous global ranks, unequal stream lengths and invalid inputs.

The PP broadcast and matching-EP local export implementations discussed in #7050 are outside this PR. This change isolates layout mapping and collective transport from model-specific quantization, ordinary-parameter export and rollout loading; it does not enable a new production path by default.

## Validation

Reapplied to `NVIDIA/Megatron-LM:dev` at `16b41e2fa987c79951d1d848b2f36618d8b7e75c`.

```bash
bash experimental/lite/tests/run_tests.sh \
  experimental/lite/tests/unit/primitive/ckpt/test_expert_layout.py
```

20 passed, no skips, exit 0 on macOS with Python 3.9.6 and PyTorch 2.8.0 (CPU/Gloo). The tests run four processes, plus a four-rank subgroup inside six processes, and compare tensor bytes independently.

items.title: Make partial_grad respect grad_comm_dtype in MFSDPv2
items.author: XiaodaNV
items.summary: used the dtype of the unsharded (bf16 for BF16/MXFP8 models) for the reduce-scatter input, so had no effect in v2. The buffer is now allocated in, falling back to the main-gradient dtype like v1's.
items.body:
## What

`FsdpParameterGroup.allocate_partial_grad_buffer` used the dtype of the unsharded `.grad`
(bf16 for BF16/MXFP8 models) for the reduce-scatter input, so `MixedPrecisionPolicy.grad_comm_dtype`
had no effect in v2. The buffer is now allocated in `grad_comm_dtype`, falling back to the
main-gradient dtype like v1's `ParamAndGradBuffer`. 

## Why

Makes v1 and v2 reduce gradients in the same dtype so they can be compared fairly.

## Test

`tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2/test_grad_comm_dtype.py`: the partial buffer allocated
during backward has the policy dtype (default, bf16 override, no `main_grads_dtype`) and `.grad`
keeps the main-grad dtype. Passed on 4 GPUs.

items.title: [data] fix: re-raise ImportError in overlong prompt filter instead of dropping all rows
items.author: yweiii
items.summary: When an optional dependency is missing (for example for multimodal data), raises inside for every sample. The catch-all in, added in #3814 to drop malformed rows, swallows it and returns, so the filter silently drops the whole dataset.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When an optional dependency is missing (for example `qwen_vl_utils` for multimodal data), `_process_multi_modal_info` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` inside `doc2len` for every sample. The catch-all `except Exception` in `maybe_filter_out_long_prompts`, added in #3814 to drop malformed rows, swallows it and returns `max_prompt_length + 1`, so the filter silently drops the whole dataset. Training then fails much later with an unrelated error:

```
ValueError: num_samples should be a positive integer value, but got num_samples=0
```

A missing package is an environment problem, not malformed data, so this PR re-raises `ImportError` (which covers `ModuleNotFoundError`) in both `doc2len` paths. Malformed rows are still dropped as before.

Related: #6888 moves these two functions to module level (`_filter_prompt_length_with_processor` / `_filter_prompt_length_with_tokenizer`). If it lands first, the same two lines apply there and I'm happy to rebase.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+doc2len
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

Added `test_maybe_filter_out_long_prompts_reraises_import_error` to `tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_on_cpu.py`. It patches `_process_multi_modal_info` to raise `ModuleNotFoundError` and asserts the filter raises `ImportError` instead of returning an empty dataset.

- Before the fix: `Failed: DID NOT RAISE ImportError` (captured output shows `filter dataset len: 0`)
- After the fix: passes, and all 11 tests in the file pass locally

Found while running the CPU dataset tests locally without `qwen_vl_utils` installed: `test_image_rl_data` failed with the `num_samples=0` error above.

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/dataset/rl_dataset.py`: add `except ImportError: raise` before `except Exception` in both `doc2len` closures (processor and tokenizer paths).
- `tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_on_cpu.py`: add the regression test above.

items.title: [dev] mla(perf): Latent CP for Kimi-K3 MLA
items.author: yuzhongw-nvidia
items.summary: For long-context MLA training the CP ring moves full K/V (≈ 0.5 GB per hop at 512K tokens / CP16) and TE's wrapper keeps all P receive buffers alive through the forward. Exchanging the latent cuts the payload 13× and lets each step's buffers die immediately; a…
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
<!-- Add a one line overview of what this PR aims to accomplish. -->

Adds `MLAWithLatentCP`, an experimental MLA self-attention variant whose context parallelism exchanges the **compressed KV latent** (`kv_lora_rank + qk_pos_emb_head_dim` channels, 576 for Kimi-K3) between CP ranks instead of the up-projected K/V. Each ring step re-runs the inherited `linear_kv_up_proj` on the received latent, attends, and merges the partial outputs in fp32; backward re-circulates `(latent, dlatent)` pairs and recomputes the up-projection per step, so no full K/V is ever saved. Core attention calls the public Transformer Engine `fused_attn_fwd/bwd` (cuDNN) or FlashAttention-4 directly, selected by the existing `attention_backend` flag. The existing MLA path is untouched; no TE private function is used.

Enabled by `TransformerConfig.mla_latent_cp=True` (GPT decoder specs and the hybrid stack, MTP included). Supports THD packed/padded input in the zigzag CP layout, causal MLA with RoPE as in `MLASelfAttention` and with the output gate, TP with sequence parallelism, CP=1, dynamic CP (p2p mode), `cp_comm_type` `p2p` / `a2a` / `a2a+p2p` (Ulysses stage over the hierarchical a2a group with the up-projection sliced to the rank's heads), fused weight-gradient accumulation, MXFP8 including quantized parameters. Unsupported combinations are rejected in `TransformerConfig.__post_init__`. Contiguous CP input for MLA depends on #7545 (MLA input-layout conversion); `dev` already rejects `cp_partition_mode=contiguous` with MLA.

## Why

For long-context MLA training the CP ring moves full K/V (≈ 0.5 GB per hop at 512K tokens / CP16) and TE's wrapper keeps all P receive buffers alive through the forward. Exchanging the latent cuts the payload 13× and lets each step's buffers die immediately; attention backends can be called directly (FlashAttention-4 is not reachable through TE's CP ring). The latent approach has a structural cost — K/V must be rebuilt per ring step — which the optimizations below pay back.

## Optimizations (in the order they were added; effects measured on the proxy below)

1. **Latent payload, per-step up-projection recompute**: ring payload 503 MB → 38 MB per hop; peak reserved memory −6.4 GB; structural cost ≈ +1 s recompute and ≈ +2.4 s K/V assembly per step at 16 ring steps.
2. **Direct core-attention calls** (cuDNN via TE's public API, or FA4): TE's private THD correction kernels gone (−0.85 s); FA4's backward is 9–11% faster per launch than cuDNN at these shapes (qk 192 / v 128) → −2.9 s/step vs the cuDNN latent ring. FA4 is only available under CP through this path.
3. **fp32 online-softmax merge** as one fused in-place kernel per step; the final merged output/LSE is reused for every backward step (no per-step correction).
4. **One TP all-gather of the latent before the ring, one reduce-scatter after** instead of per-step SP collectives inside the TE linear: −1.5 s of compute-stream NCCL kernel time.
5. **K/V assembly as one autograd Function** with strided copies in both directions (avoids `cat` with a stride-0 operand and the unvectorised split-backward cat): ≈ −2.3 s of kernel time.
6. **Up-projection parameters as Function inputs**: one `AccumulateGrad` / DDP hook per parameter per microbatch, which dynamic CP and DDP bucket readiness require.
7. **`a2a+p2p` and `a2a`**: latent all-gathered over the a2a group, queries/outputs exchanged tokens↔heads, gathered chunks permuted into the zigzag of the p2p group; the ring runs unchanged with P/A steps on H/A heads. All per-step costs shrink with the step count and the attention kernels work on A× larger problems: 70.5 → 67.6 s ([4,4]).
8. **Head-sliced up-projection in a2a modes**: the TE module projects only the rank's H/A heads through a row slab of its weight (zero-copy view, swapped in by a per-call pre-hook after DDP's parameter all-gather completes); gradients map back to the full weight: −0.9 s at [4,4]; **66.1 s at [8,2]**.
9. **Two-stream forward ring** (TE's `cp_stream` pattern) kept behind `mla_latent_cp_two_stream` (default off): measured neutral at 64K–512K on GB300.

## Results

Kimi-K3 9-layer proxy, packed THD 512K tokens, 64 × GB300 (TP4 + sequence parallel, CP16, EP64, MXFP8, Muon, MTP1, selective recompute + fine-grained offload); step time = mean of 7 iterations after one warm-up iteration, one run per configuration; the old path is the existing `MLASelfAttention` → TE context-parallel attention (cuDNN; TE's ring has no FA4 branch). Per-iteration times of the new path are below the old path's corresponding iterations in every FA4 configuration.

| configuration | step (s) | vs old p2p | TFLOP/s/GPU | peak allocated / reserved (GB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| old path, `p2p` (cuDNN) | 71.01 | — | 833 | 69.0 / 83.5 |
| old path, `a2a+p2p` [4,4] (cuDNN) | 68.36 | −3.7% | 865 | 69.2 / 79.4 |
| old path, `a2a+p2p` [8,2] (cuDNN) | 67.38 | −5.1% | 878 | 69.2 / 78.6 |
| latent CP, `p2p`, cuDNN | 73.43 | +3.4% | 805 | 69.0 / 78.2 |
| latent CP, `p2p`, FA4 | 70.51 | −0.7% | 839 | 69.0 / 77.1 |
| latent CP, `a2a+p2p` [4,4], FA4 | 66.66 | −6.1% | 887 | 69.0 / 77.2 |
| **latent CP, `a2a+p2p` [8,2], FA4** | **66.10** | **−6.9%** | **895** | **69.0 / 77.1** |

`[A, P/A]` = `hierarchical_context_parallel_sizes`. TE's own hierarchical scheme also prefers [8,2]; against that best old configuration the new path is 1.3 s (−1.9%) faster, with 1.5 GB less reserved memory, and faster in every iteration (by 0.6–1.8 s). Peak allocated is reached outside MLA and is unchanged; the reserved and device-used savings (−6.4 GB / −5.4 GB vs the old p2p path, −1.5 GB / −1.7 GB vs old [8,2]) come from freeing ring buffers per step. Pure `a2a` needs heads-per-TP-rank divisible by the CP size (not possible at CP16 with 24 heads); at 64K/CP4 it is the fastest mode (20.64 s vs 20.89 s old).

**Full model.** With the feature squashed onto the Kimi-K3 preview stack and re-measured with same-commit pairs (same container, mock data, GBS 32, MTP1), the gain carries over to the full model:

| model | parallel layout | old path: TE `p2p`, cuDNN | latent CP `a2a+p2p` [8,2], FA4 | Δ step | TFLOP/s/GPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Kimi-K3 full model (93 decoder blocks)**, THD 512K | TP4 PP4 EP64 CP16, 256 × GB300 | 169.2 s | **157.9 s** | **−6.7%** | 715 → **766** |
| 9-layer proxy, THD 512K | TP4 PP1 EP64 CP16, 64 × GB300 | 69.93 ± 0.23 s | **65.50 ± 0.30 s** | **−6.3%** (faster in every paired step) | 846 → **903** |

Peak allocated memory is unchanged on both (164 GB on the full model's first pipeline stage), reserved memory −4.8 GB (full) / −6.4 GB (proxy), and the mock-data loss trajectories are identical to MXFP8 rerun noise. At 64K with CP2 the pure `a2a` mode replaces the ring entirely: 18.8 → 18.5 s/step on real data with parity 2.69e-4.

![Step time and throughput, old TE p2p ring vs latent CP a2a+p2p [8,2] + FA4, 9-layer proxy and full model](37_latent_cp_speedup.png)

**Numerics.** Real-data resume parity (THD 64K, 32 steps, same checkpoint and data) against the old path: max |Δ lm loss| 1.4–1.9e-4 across the modes (`p2p` cuDNN 1.42e-4, `p2p` FA4 1.91e-4, `a2a+p2p` 1.63e-4, `a2a` 1.89e-4), run-to-run floor ≈ 1e-4, no NaN/skipped steps; on the integrated stack `a2a+p2p` [2,2] 2.32e-4 and pure `a2a` (CP2) 2.69e-4, at the proxy's own rerun floor.

**Profile audit (nsys, one step).** Kernels present only in the new path are its own ring ops (fused fp32 merge, padding-row mask, second-chunk index ops, strided K/V copies, fp32 accumulates, a2a split/cat and permutation index ops) and the FA4 kernels; TE's private `thd_*` correction/half-read/reorder kernels and the cuDNN fusion helpers disappear; ≈ 280–290 of ≈ 320–330 shared kernels have identical launch counts, the rest being the per-ring-step up-projection group and NCCL op counts. GPU idle and exposed communication are unchanged across configurations. Host time of the ring per layer-microbatch: 5 / 9 ms (fwd / bwd) at [8,2] vs 24 / 25 ms for the TE wrapper.

Also explored and not included: a latent **all-gather** CP scheme (no ring, two prefix-attention calls per rank). It reaches 69.3 s at 512K but raises peak allocated memory by 24 GB, because every rank rebuilds K/V for the whole sequence and all heads; the code is kept on a side branch.

## Tests

`tests/unit_tests/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/test_mla_latent_cp.py` compares the old and new paths on identical weights, inputs and upstream gradients (outputs and all parameter gradients): TP × CP layouts up to 8 GPUs, packed and padded THD, CP=1, dynamic CP, separate KV norm, MXFP8 with bf16 and quantized parameters (including the head-slab path), fused weight-gradient accumulation, `a2a`/`a2a+p2p` including odd head counts, two-stream mode, FA4-vs-cuDNN; it also exercises the zero-copy half-KV ring step and the a2a permutation directly (CPU) and covers the config/construction/spec guards. On GB300 (TE 2.20 container): 54 passed / 9 skipped on one 4-GPU node (skips are 8-GPU cases), 9 passed on 2 nodes; the MLA/attention/GPT/hybrid regression groups are identical on `dev` with and without this branch.

## Notes for reviewers

- Only `megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/mla_latent_cp.py` (new) plus small gated edits: `TransformerConfig.mla_latent_cp` / `mla_latent_cp_two_stream` (+ validation), the spec swap in `get_gpt_decoder_layer_specs` and `HybridStack.__init__`, and a one-line reset of the hierarchical CP groups in `parallel_state.destroy_model_parallel`.
- FA4 is driven through `flash_attn.cute.interface._flash_attn_fwd/_bwd` (FA4 has no public split API), pinned to `flash_attn_4==4.0.0b11` and SM100+; cuDNN remains the default (`attention_backend=fused`/`auto`).
- Dynamic CP is supported for `p2p`; the `a2a` modes reject it (MCore has no hierarchical variant of the per-microbatch CP groups).
- The measured results come from an internal proxy setup that depends on a preview branch and is not reproducible on `dev` as is; the unit tests are the validation that runs here.

Opened as a draft per the repository rule.

items.title: [MoE] Bound mixed-precision router weighting memory
items.author: bvolpato
items.summary: Unfused multiplies low-precision activations by FP32 router probabilities before casting back. That creates a full FP32 temporary, and the GLU backward graph retains additional activation intermediates.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Unfused `TEGroupedMLP` multiplies low-precision activations by FP32 router probabilities before casting back. That creates a full FP32 temporary, and the GLU backward graph retains additional activation intermediates. Uneven token loads can make these allocations large.

Process large promoted products in row chunks and recompute supported, parameter-free GLU activations during backward. Keep FP32 router probabilities and the original activation rounding. Recomputation keeps the forward CUDA autocast context. Custom activations retain their activation graph, and fused activation implementations are unchanged.

The real Transformer Engine expert path also passed with chunking forced on. CI vetting and the `Run functional tests` label require maintainer access.

items.title: feat(determinism): Accept an empty NCCL_ALGO and Ring,NVLS under --deterministic-mode
items.author: KeitaW
items.summary: Accept under as a request to let NCCL choose the algorithm for each collective, as suggested in #8138. This replaces the opt-in flag proposed in the issue.
items.body:
# What does this PR do?

Accept `NCCL_ALGO=""` under `--deterministic-mode` as a request to let NCCL choose the algorithm for each collective, as suggested in #8138 ([comment](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/8138#issuecomment-6131995489)). This replaces the opt-in flag proposed in the issue.

On main, `--deterministic-mode` fills in `NCCL_ALGO=Ring` when the variable is unset and rejects the empty string, because the token check needs at least one token. With this PR the empty value is kept. PyTorch 2.8 and later write `NCCL_ALGO=^NVLS` under `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` only when the variable is unset, and they count an empty `NCCL_ALGO` as set ([c10/util/env.cpp](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.12.1/c10/util/env.cpp#L51-L66)). NCCL 2.24 and later read no algorithm from the empty string and so exclude none ([tuning.cc, 2.27.7](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.27.7-1/src/graph/tuning.cc#L401-L405)), which leaves the choice to NCCL's cost model and to the tuner plugin, if one is loaded; NCCL 2.23 and earlier enable only Ring and Tree for it (only Ring when CollNet is available), so they do not use NVLS ([tuning.cc, 2.23.4](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.23.4-1/src/graph/tuning.cc#L297-L315)). Rank 0 issues a warning that bit-exact reproducibility then rests on what NCCL selects.

Unset still defaults to `Ring`, `Tree` is still rejected, and `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` stays in `validate_args`. A value of only whitespace is still rejected, now with a message saying why: NCCL 2.24 and later fail to parse it.

As suggested in review ([comment](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8180#issuecomment-6188474175)), `NCCL_ALGO=Ring,NVLS` (in either order) is accepted too. NCCL then chooses between Ring and NVLS for each collective and does not use Tree. A list with `NVLS` must also contain `Ring`, because broadcast and reduce run only with Ring ([tuning.cc L255, 2.27.7](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.27.7-1/src/graph/tuning.cc#L255)). NCCL uses NVLS only for a communicator with more than two GPUs in the node and, without CollNet, only for one that stays within a single node ([nvls.cc L160](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.27.7-1/src/transport/nvls.cc#L160), [tuning.cc L446-L448](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.27.7-1/src/graph/tuning.cc#L446-L448)), so a group that spans nodes, often the data-parallel group, runs Ring. PyTorch leaves the value alone because it is set, and no warning is issued for it.

On Hopper GPUs (compute capability 9) the empty value and any list with `NVLS` are rejected, while `^NVLS` stays accepted. There the result of an NVLS reduction can depend on multicast objects allocated earlier in the process unless the kernel driver and Fabric Manager are 550.144.03 or later in the 550 branch, or 570 or later ([NVIDIA/nccl#2360](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/2360#issuecomment-5705740833)), and Megatron does not check those versions.

After `_initialize_distributed` creates the default process group, a runtime check, `assert_nccl_algo_still_empty`, reads `NCCL_ALGO` through libc and stops the run if an empty value has been replaced, for example by PyTorch's `^NVLS`. In `docs/user-guide/deterministic-training.md`, the `NCCL_ALGO` row lists the empty value and links a new section, "Letting NCCL choose the algorithm", which also covers `Ring,NVLS`, the version boundaries, the Hopper rejection and the runtime check.

The first new test in `tests/unit_tests/training/test_determinism_args.py` covers unset, `""`, `^NVLS`, `Ring,NVLS`, `NVLS,Ring`, `" "`, `Tree` and a bare `NVLS`. Unset becomes `Ring`, the next four are kept, and in these cases the other variables still get their defaults; the last three are rejected with their own messages and leave the environment unchanged. Other tests cover the warning (rank 0 only, and only for the empty value), the Hopper rejection (of `""` and `Ring,NVLS`, before any warning; unset and `^NVLS` still pass) and the runtime check (it raises once libc holds `^NVLS` and ignores an unset value). A GPU test creates a process group under `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` and reads `NCCL_ALGO` through libc: PyTorch writes `^NVLS` for an unset value (this case is skipped below PyTorch 2.8) and leaves `""` alone. With the replay test below, the two files pass on CPU (28 passed, 10 of them existing, and the 3 GPU items skipped) and under `torchrun --nproc_per_node 8` on 8 × H100 (30 passed on every rank, with the replay test skipped on Hopper).

`tests/unit_tests/determinism/correctness/test_nccl_nvls_allreduce.py` replays the pattern of NVIDIA/nccl#2360 under `NCCL_ALGO=Ring,NVLS`: for k = 0 to 3, it creates k other communicators that each run a small AllReduce, then AllReduces a fixed 32 MiB bf16 tensor twice on a new one, and every result must have the same bits on every rank. The input is normal values scaled by 2^e, with e from -8 to 24, chosen to make the sum sensitive to the reduction order even with fp32 accumulation. The unit-test `conftest.py` sets `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0` and `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1`, which NCCL reads once per process, at its first communicator, so rank 0 of the pytest run starts the replay as a separate single-node `torch.distributed.run` job without those two variables. The test is marked `launch_on_gb200`, the marker by which the GB200 unit-test lane selects tests; it is skipped on Hopper, with two GPUs or fewer, and without NVLink multicast, and it has not run in NVIDIA CI yet. On one 8 × B200 node (driver 580.178.04, NCCL 2.27.7), the test passed on its own and after `test_determinism_args.py` in the same pytest session with CI's marker filter: NCCL ran each of the eight 32 MiB AllReduces with NVLS on 24 channels, and all 64 results (8 ranks, 4 histories, 2 repeats) had the same digest, the same in both runs.

On one 8 × H100 node, `pretrain_gpt.py` with `--deterministic-mode` and `NCCL_ALGO=""` (mock data, TP 2, PP 2, DP 2, 20 iterations; NGC PyTorch 25.09 with NCCL 2.27.7) stops at the Hopper check on every rank before `torch.distributed` is initialized. With `NCCL_ALGO` unset, the same run trains, the runtime check is called on every rank, and all 248 TensorBoard scalar values are bit-identical to the same run on main.

On 8 B200 nodes (64 GPUs), `--deterministic-mode` with `NCCL_ALGO=""` reproduced the 8-node opt-in runs from #8138 bit for bit in the three dense layouts (TP 8 with and without the distributed optimizer, and TP 2; seed 1234, 100 steps). These runs used the image of the B200 runs in #8138 (NGC PyTorch 25.09, NCCL 2.27.7, aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1 and its tuner), with this change ported to the Megatron code base of those runs. The logged lm loss, grad norm, params norm and num zeros matched at every step, also on a node set that shares no node with the opt-in runs, and the empty-value runs matched each other across a repeat and a run with every 8-rank block moved one node over. NCCL made the same algorithm and protocol choice for every collective and size as under the opt-in, including NVLS for the 32 MiB TP AllReduce at TP 8 and Tree for the 4- and 8-byte cross-node AllReduces, and the tuner made the same choices.

We then ran this PR's first commit in the same image, with only the Megatron tree replaced: in the three layouts it gave the same bits and the same NCCL and tuner choices as the runs with the ported change, also on a repeat and with every block moved. With `NCCL_ALGO` unset, every collective ran Ring.

With `NCCL_ALGO=Ring,NVLS`, this PR's code in the same image gave the same bits in all three layouts across a repeat and a run with every 8-rank block moved one node over: NCCL ran every 32 MiB TP AllReduce at TP 8 with NVLS and every other collective with Ring, and NCCL and the tuner made the same choices in each pair.

`megatron/training/determinism.py` (add `import ctypes`):

```python
def assert_nccl_algo_still_empty() -> None:
    """No-op unless NCCL_ALGO was set empty. Call after the first NCCL process group.

    PyTorch writes NCCL_ALGO from C++, which ``os.environ`` does not see, so the value is
    read back through libc.
    """
    if os.environ.get("NCCL_ALGO") != "":
        return
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None)
    libc.getenv.restype = ctypes.c_char_p
    libc.getenv.argtypes = [ctypes.c_char_p]
    actual = libc.getenv(b"NCCL_ALGO")
    assert actual == b"", (
        f'NCCL_ALGO was "" but is {actual!r} after process-group creation, so '
        "PyTorch's NVLS exclusion applied anyway. Unset NCCL_ALGO to use the Ring default."
    )
```

`megatron/training/initialize.py`, right after `inprocess_restart.maybe_force_nccl_backend_init(device_id)`
(same indentation):

```python
        if args.deterministic_mode:
            from megatron.training.determinism import assert_nccl_algo_still_empty

            assert_nccl_algo_still_empty()
```

Tests, in `tests/unit_tests/training/test_determinism_args.py` (add `import ctypes`, import
`assert_nccl_algo_still_empty`, and `from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils`):

```python
def test_assert_nccl_algo_still_empty(monkeypatch):
    """Passes while libc still sees "", fails once a C++ write (PyTorch's) changes it."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("NCCL_ALGO", "")  # putenv, so libc agrees with os.environ
    assert_nccl_algo_still_empty()
    ctypes.CDLL(None).setenv(b"NCCL_ALGO", b"^NVLS", 1)  # what PyTorch does in C++
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="NVLS exclusion applied anyway"):
        assert_nccl_algo_still_empty()


@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a CUDA device")
@pytest.mark.parametrize("nccl_algo, expected", [(None, b"^NVLS"), ("", b"")])
def test_pytorch_leaves_empty_nccl_algo_alone(nccl_algo, expected, monkeypatch):
    """Negative control (unset -> PyTorch writes ^NVLS) and the claim this PR relies on ("" is left alone).

    Without the control, the "" case could pass because PyTorch stopped banning NVLS.
    """
    Utils.initialize_distributed()
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None)
    libc.getenv.restype = ctypes.c_char_p
    libc.getenv.argtypes = [ctypes.c_char_p]
    if nccl_algo is None:
        monkeypatch.delenv("NCCL_ALGO", raising=False)
    else:
        monkeypatch.setenv("NCCL_ALGO", nccl_algo)
    try:
        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)  # the autouse fixture restores it
        group = torch.distributed.new_group(list(range(torch.distributed.get_world_size())))
        assert libc.getenv(b"NCCL_ALGO") == expected
        torch.distributed.destroy_process_group(group)
    finally:
        libc.unsetenv(b"NCCL_ALGO")  # PyTorch's C++ write bypasses monkeypatch
```

If it fires, the run would only lose NVLS (a performance loss, not a determinism
one), so a warning would also be defensible, but the assert makes the failure
impossible to miss. It only checks the first process group. I ran the logic of the
first test against the real libc with a stub `torch`; the second test needs a GPU
and I haven't run it.

Thank you so much for the thorough review!

> could `apply_determinism_to_args` fail fast when `NCCL_ALGO=""` on Hopper?

Done in "feat(determinism): Reject an empty NCCL_ALGO on Hopper", with your assert. We changed four things in its message. The versions now read "550.144.03 or later in the 550 branch, or 570 or later (the 560 branch has no fix)", because ">= 550.144.03 (or 570+)" reads as if 560 qualified. "lets NCCL use NVLS" became "lets NCCL 2.24 and later use NVLS", since NCCL 2.23 and earlier don't use NVLS for an empty value. "which is not reproducible" became "which may not be reproducible", because in nccl#2360 repeated runs of one setup are bitwise stable and the result changes with what was allocated earlier in the process. And "Fabric Manager's version cannot be checked here" became "their versions are not checked here", which also covers the kernel driver. A later change could gate on the driver version if Fabric Manager can be assumed to match it; that can't be confirmed from Python, so it isn't part of this PR.

> Could we also check at runtime that `NCCL_ALGO=""` survived, so upstream PyTorch change can't silently bring `^NVLS` back?

Added as you wrote it in "feat(determinism): Check that PyTorch left an empty NCCL_ALGO alone", called in `_initialize_distributed` right after the default process group is created. The GPU test skips its unset case below PyTorch 2.8, because 2.6.0 to 2.7.1 don't write `^NVLS`, and it also calls the check after `new_group`. A new CPU test pins that an unset value is not checked. We ran the file under `torchrun --nproc_per_node 8` on 8 × H100: 24 passed on every rank, including the negative control (unset gets `^NVLS`).

items.title: test: disable git auto-maintenance in swe workspace diff test
items.author: gavinqii
items.summary: Example: https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/38288879812 (job ): The runner has git 2.55. After the test's, git starts auto-maintenance in the background, which creates and then deletes.
items.body:
## Problem

`tests/test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py::test_patch_uses_actual_image_baseline_without_changing_git_index` is flaky on CI. Example: https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/38288879812 (job `agent-test (0, test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py)`):

```
shutil.Error: [('.../agent repo/.git/objects/maintenance.lock', '.../grader repo/.git/objects/maintenance.lock', "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: ...")]
```

The runner has git 2.55. After the test's `git commit`, git starts auto-maintenance in the background, which creates and then deletes `.git/objects/maintenance.lock`. The next line, `shutil.copytree(repo, fresh)`, sometimes lists the lock file and then fails because it's gone before the copy reaches it.

## Fix

Turn off auto-maintenance and auto-gc in the temporary test repo (`maintenance.auto=false`, `gc.auto=0`) right after `git init`. The test only uses this repo as a fixture, so nothing it checks depends on maintenance.

## Testing

Ran `pytest tests/test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py` locally 3 times with the CI agent-test dependency set on Python 3.10; 3/3 passed each run.

items.title: refactor(fsdp): Use DBuffer owner APIs and direct P2P receives
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: Owner gather/scatter duplicates DBuffer metadata in and receives through temporary tensors before copying into destinations. This PR uses the sharded-side DBuffer directly and receives into destination views.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

Owner gather/scatter duplicates DBuffer metadata in `GroupOwnerLayout` and receives through temporary tensors before copying into destinations. This PR uses the sharded-side DBuffer directly and receives into destination views.

Changes:

- Change gather's source and scatter's destination from tensor dictionaries to `DBuffer`; pass `tensor_to_owner` separately:

  ```python
  gather(source: DBuffer, destination: dict[int, torch.Tensor], *, tensor_to_owner: dict[int, int])
  scatter(source: dict[int, torch.Tensor], destination: DBuffer, *, tensor_to_owner: dict[int, int])
  ```

- Remove `GroupOwnerLayout`, its `from_group` constructor, and `select_ge_2d_params`. Callers select participating tensor indices.
- Change `assign_owner_work(layout, mesh, tensor_indices, cost_fn)` to `assign_owner_work(buffer, tensor_indices, cost_fn)`, deriving eligible ranks from the buffer's actual placements instead of assuming `RowAtomic`.
- Remove per-peer receive buffers, gather concatenation, and final receive-buffer copies. Require gather destinations and scatter sources to be contiguous full tensors with matching element counts, dtype, and device. Scatter sends slices as views and receives directly into DBuffer shards.
- Explicitly support one-dimensional sharded meshes, using the actual `RowAtomic`, `BlockAtomic`, or `TensorAtomic` placement. Remove tensor-index sorting and rename the rank-offset ordering helper to `_get_sorted_rank_ranges`.

Tests exercise separate computed-input and scratch DBuffers, all three placements, subgroup global ranks, dictionary traversal order, and preservation of owner-local shards, excluded tensors, and padding.

Owner assignment still operates on one buffer per call. The cross-group API in #7974 and the optimizer caller in #7519 require adaptation to these interfaces.

Validation after rebasing onto `b597bd1fa`:

- Ran `test_owner_planning.py` and `test_gather_scatter.py` through `torch.distributed.run` on two RTX A6000 GPUs: 8 passed and 11 skipped per rank. The skipped cases require three or four ranks.
- Updated the gather/scatter test to use main's extracted `layout_builder` functions.

items.author: guihong-nv

items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
The NanoV3 GB200 EP4 benchmark completes successfully but repeatedly exceeds the +20% throughput improvement ceiling at batch 128. Refresh its stale performance reference from the complete median-throughput row of three fresh GB200 sweeps and restore the recipe's original `mr` scope, which was quarantined in #7916.

Batch-128 throughput changes from **11,512.760738** to **14,234.332897 tokens/sec**. Update its throughput, average/p50/p99 latency, and TPOT together using the original full-precision result. Retain the existing 10% regression tolerance, 20% throughput improvement ceiling, other batch references, and benchmark metadata. Restoring `scope: [mr]` returns the pre-quarantine GitLab selection.

### Validation

Three independent server launches on two GB200 nodes reproduced the same isolated high-side failure against the original reference. Each sweep ran batch sizes 1, 8, 32, and 128 with five warmups and ten timed iterations per batch.

| Sweep | Batch-128 throughput (tok/s) | Change vs old baseline | Average latency (ms) | p99 latency (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 14,218.683365 | +23.50% | 1,137.180562 | 1,209.695876 |
| 2 | 14,248.113662 | +23.76% | 1,134.807123 | 1,193.082603 |
| 3 — selected median throughput | 14,234.332897 | +23.64% | 1,136.289481 | 1,236.761791 |

The selected baseline is the complete batch-128 row from sweep 3, not a mixture of independently selected metric values. The sample throughput coefficient of variation is 0.103%.

Runtime provenance: source `d7157825675a65c2503a061ffd1fffa7886df9b7`; CI image tag `main_73361945` (PyTorch 26.09); ARM64 manifest `sha256:5f37d7e0464e5abab9ec8b22f808d11a81bb23a859f9dfd99a1e4e2d49b98f71`. The runs used four GB200 GPUs, TP=1/PP=1/EP=4, FlashAttention 2, legacy scheduling, NVLS dispatch, GSM8K prompts, and 128 output tokens. W&B upload was disabled. Runtime arguments confirm the same checkpoint and principal model configuration as the historical run.

- The original reference fails exactly one of 20 comparisons in each fresh sweep: batch-128 throughput.
- Replaying the official comparator with the refreshed reference passes **all 60 metric comparisons** across the three fresh sweeps.

items.title: Fuse GDP prefill preparation into the decode prepare kernel
items.author: santhnm2
items.summary: Between the varlen short conv and the chunked recurrence, GDP dynamic-batching prefill split the post-conv activations into value, key and query, folded the Householder copies into the sequence dimension, GQA-expanded query/key, and computed beta = sigmoid(b) …
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Between the varlen short conv and the chunked recurrence, GDP dynamic-batching prefill split the post-conv activations into value, key and query, folded the Householder copies into the sequence dimension, GQA-expanded query/key, and computed beta = sigmoid(b) and g = -exp(A_log) * softplus(a + dt_bias): about 14 copy and elementwise kernels per layer, three of them strided copies of most of the post-conv tensor. For a production-sized hybrid model that is ~148 us of GPU time per GDP layer for a 4096-token step.

Decode already does the same work in one kernel (gdp_decode_prepare). Generalize that kernel and add gdp_prefill_prepare on top of it. The two entry points share the loads, the libdevice math (so both stay bitwise identical to the eager path) and the [n, T*M, H, ...] value/key/beta layout, and differ only where their consumers do:

- decode interleaves query and g onto the Householder copies for the fused recurrent kernel and runs one program per head;
- prefill keeps query and g one per token, as chunk_gated_delta_product_varlen expects, and runs one program per (token, copy) covering every head, because a prefill step carries thousands of tokens.

A constexpr selects the query/g layout and the head-block size selects the grid. The prefill token count is a runtime argument, so prefill lengths do not each compile a kernel; decode keeps its token count (1 plus the draft length) as a compile-time constant. decode_prepare.py becomes prepare.py, holding the kernel and both entry points.

ssm_prefill now runs the varlen conv through a new _prefill_conv helper (the counterpart of _decode_conv) followed by the fused kernel, and the varlen branch moves out of _prepare_qkv, which only training and static batching use.

Tests assert torch.equal against the eager sequence across Householder counts, GQA ratios, dtypes, strided inputs and step sizes up to 4096 tokens, and a determinism replay covers the prefill entry point.
