items.title: Stage request payloads off the dynamic engine loop
items.author: lauradang
items.summary: Runs off the dynamic engine loop, so a slow payload write no longer pauses decoding for every active request. Addresses (Megatron token capture: the TQ media write blocks the engine step).
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Runs `RequestPayloadStager.stage()` off the dynamic engine loop, so a slow payload write no longer pauses decoding for every active request.

Addresses [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4663](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/issues/4663) (Megatron token capture: the TQ media write blocks the engine step).

On `main`, `_send_requests_to_coordinator` calls `payload_stager.stage()` inline for each completed request before sending replies, from the bookkeeping pass of every engine step. When the stager's write is a blocking network round trip, every finished request stalls the engine loop for the duration of its write. NeMo-RL token capture is one such stager: it writes each completed request's token delta (and, with media capture, its pixels) to a TransferQueue store.

Now each stageable completed request gets its own asyncio task:

- `_stage_and_reply` builds the `OffloadedRequestPayload` on the loop thread, runs `stage()` via `asyncio.to_thread`, then sends that request's reply from the loop thread (the ZMQ socket stays single-threaded).
- Each reply still waits for its own write, so `payload_stage_metadata` keeps describing a completed write (stage-before-ack is unchanged). Only the engine stops waiting. This matches what the NeMo-RL vLLM worker already does with the same write.
- Failed and unstaged replies are sent immediately, as before. A stager exception sends the reply unstaged instead of failing the loop.
- Tasks are held in `_staging_tasks`, because the event loop keeps only [weak references to tasks](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task). `shutdown()` drains them before closing the socket and logs how many it waited for.
- The periodic step log reports the staging backlog (`payload staging: in-flight N, peak M`), so a write path that cannot keep up is visible.
- The `RequestPayloadStager` protocol is unchanged, and stagers need no changes.

## Results

NeMo-RL GRPO, Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B on VSTAT video, token capture with media, Megatron inference, 42 steps. Overhead is the extra `exposed_generation` per step for capture on vs. off, paired per step. [W&B overlay of the generation-bound runs](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev?nw=2n1rne2a5x2).

**Generation-bound** (one TP8/EP8 generation replica, on-policy, so generation time is fully exposed):

| | capture on | capture off | extra exposed generation / step |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/4f2asz54) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/puejmm4j) | +3.97 s (mean) / +3.82 s (median) |
| this PR | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/ig3pkhci) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/gukf26yk) | +2.63 s (mean) / +2.95 s (median) |
| this PR + 6 NeMo-RL reassembler workers (instead of 2) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/98g9vssq) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/gukf26yk) | +1.54 s (mean) / +1.56 s (median) |

This PR removes the engine-side share (~1.3 s/step). The rest is on the NeMo-RL consumer side (reassembler queueing, media transfer through the store). That part is shared with the vLLM backend (same pipeline, [vLLM capture-on run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/pjrbikqm)) and is tracked in NeMo-RL.

**Default async layout** (three generation replicas, one step of lookahead): no measurable overhead even on `main`, because generation has spare capacity and hides the write: 35.6 s vs. 36.2 s/step ([on](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/n63nmvq0), [off](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/pszdknot), [overlay](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev?nw=vd6ela6gjmk)).

## Related PRs

Megatron-LM:
- #7015: added the `RequestPayloadStager` / `RequestPromptPreparer` hooks this PR changes how the engine calls.
- #7557: hands compact prompt ids and media tensors to the payload stager (makes media writes large).
- #7598: multimodal prefix stitching used by the same capture path.

NeMo-RL:
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4332](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332): Megatron token capture with media, where this was measured. [Review comment that flagged the in-step write](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332#discussion_r4152142339), [measurements](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332#discussion_r4223398167).
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4129](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4129): Megatron (MInf) token capture through the payload stager.
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4191](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4191): vLLM VLM media capture; its worker already runs the same write off its engine.
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4307](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4307): stages MoE routing indices through the same stager (also benefits).

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: addresses [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4663](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/issues/4663). This PR removes the engine-side stall described there; NeMo-RL picks it up through a Megatron-Bridge bump. The rest of the overhead measured in that issue (reassembler queueing and media transfer, shared with vLLM) is NeMo-RL-side and not changed here.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests (`test_slow_stager_does_not_block_the_engine_loop`, `test_stager_error_keeps_payload_on_the_reply`, `test_drain_waits_for_in_flight_staging`, `test_staging_backlog_is_reported_in_the_step_log`, `test_staging_backlog_log_is_empty_without_a_stager`, `test_drain_logs_the_in_flight_count`, `test_drain_is_silent_when_nothing_is_in_flight`; the existing offload/ledger reply tests now run in an event loop)

- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel ... (N/A)

- [ ] I have added relevant documentation (docstrings only)
- [x] I have run the autoformatter.sh on my PR (black/isort/ruff/pylint clean; mypy is advisory in the script and reports no new errors in the changed code)

- The CPU-runnable tests in `tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py` were run locally: 74 passed vs. 67 on `main`, with identical pre-existing failures/errors (GPU/NCCL-only).

items.title: Pack whole requests into CUDA-graph-gated chunked prefill steps
items.author: santhnm2
items.summary: With --inference-cuda-graph-all-prefills, chunked prefill snapped every newly admitted request to the largest captured-graph boundary within its own remaining length. A request that fits in the step but does not land on a boundary was therefore split, and sinc…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
With --inference-cuda-graph-all-prefills, chunked prefill snapped every newly admitted request to the largest captured-graph boundary within its own remaining length. A request that fits in the step but does not land on a boundary was therefore split, and since a partial admit ends the scheduling loop, every step carried one finishing remainder plus one new partial request. On arc_challenge (~1.7k-token prompts, max_tokens=4096) each engine ran 2-prefill, 2048-token steps while hundreds of requests waited.

Admit the whole remainder when it fits and the batch still matches a captured graph (padding up to the graph's token count), and split only a request that does not fit, at the largest boundary within budget, so steps pack to the largest graph. The decision moves into _cg_chunked_prefill_chunk_size, with unit tests including a scheduler-loop simulation of the old and new packing.

On an 8-node (TP4/EP32) arc_challenge eval, steps went from [2048 tokens] 2 prefills to [4096 tokens] 3-4 prefills, and eval wall time dropped 16% (226 s to 189 s).

items.title: Share one logits buffer across HybridModel block-scope CUDA graphs
items.author: santhnm2
items.summary: A block-scope inference graph keeps its output tensor alive for replay, and graphs are keyed by batch dimensions, so each captured graph pinned its own full-vocabulary logits in the graph pool. With prompt log-probs (every token's logits materialized) that is …
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
A block-scope inference graph keeps its output tensor alive for replay, and graphs are keyed by batch dimensions, so each captured graph pinned its own full-vocabulary logits in the graph pool. With prompt log-probs (every token's logits materialized) that is ~0.5 MiB per token per graph: about 2 GiB per 4096-token prefill graph, and ~36 GiB for the prefill/mixed graphs of a max_tokens=4096 run with --inference-cuda-graph-all-prefills, which ran out of memory during capture.

Copy the logits of graphed dynamic-batching forwards into a single model-owned [1, max_rows, vocab] buffer and return a view of it, where max_rows covers max_tokens and every request's speculative tokens. The buffer is allocated during the eager warmup before the first capture, so it lives outside the graph pool at a fixed address. Reuse across replays is safe because the controller copies the logits into its own buffer on the current stream immediately after the forward (`_dynamic_step_forward_logits`) and never reads the returned tensor again, including under async scheduling; the next replay is ordered after that copy.

items.title: Synchronize ranks before re-initializing model parallel in unit tests
items.author: ilml
items.summary: Fixes the intermittent MoE unit-bucket hang in #7745 by synchronizing all ranks before tears down the existing process groups. initializes model parallel, and (like several other tests) initializes it again in the test body.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Fixes the intermittent MoE unit-bucket hang in #7745 by synchronizing all ranks before `Utils.initialize_model_parallel` tears down the existing process groups.

**Cause**

`Utils.initialize_model_parallel` calls `ps.destroy_model_parallel()` without a barrier. `TestRouterAuxLoss.setup_method` initializes model parallel, and `test_force_balanced_aux_loss` (like several other tests) initializes it again in the test body. A rank that finishes creating the setup's groups early therefore destroys them while slower ranks are still inside Gloo `connectFullMesh` for the last one. Those ranks fail with `Connection closed by peer`, pytest moves them on to the next test, and the remaining ranks wait 30 minutes on Gloo store keys for a group the others never create. The NCCL watchdog timeouts, the launcher restart and the job-limit cancellation in #7745 all follow from that.

The all-rank logs of [run 37393427924](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/37393427924/artifacts/11385665581) show the sequence. Ranks 3–5 fail in `setup_method` with `Connection closed by peer` at 00:53:27.285. By then ranks 0 and 2 have already destroyed those groups and are waiting in the test body's re-initialization; their 30-minute store waits start at 00:53:27.58.

**Fix**

Barrier on the default group (after `torch.cuda.synchronize()`) before destroying the groups, as `Utils.destroy_model_parallel` already does on teardown. The condition is `torch.distributed.is_initialized()`, which is the same on every rank, so the barrier cannot itself desynchronize ranks.

**Testing**

- Standalone reproduction: 8 Gloo processes on CPU repeatedly create an 8-rank group and immediately destroy it, with 3 ms of loopback latency to widen the window. Without a barrier, every rank fails within 18 cycles with the errors seen in CI (`connectFullMesh ... Connection closed`, `DistStoreError: wait timeout ... keys: /default_pg/0//19//cpu//0/2`). With a barrier before the destroy, all 40 cycles complete.
- `tests/unit_tests/test_parallel_state.py` and `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_aux_loss.py` on 2 GPUs with the CI software stack: identical pass/fail sets with and without the change. The failures are cases that need 4–8 ranks.
- The 8-rank cases themselves run only in the H100 MoE bucket. The failure is intermittent, so a green CI run is necessary but not sufficient evidence.

items.title: Stop logging checkpoints as wandb artifacts and keep private args out of the wandb config
items.author: shurkat-nvidia
items.summary: Every save logged the checkpoint as a wandb model artifact holding only a file:// reference to a cluster path, and every load called useartifact on it. Nothing reads these, the references dangle once --save-retain-interval deletes the checkpoint, and each loga…
items.body:
Every save logged the checkpoint as a wandb model artifact holding only a file:// reference to a cluster path, and every load called use_artifact on it. Nothing reads these, the references dangle once --save-retain-interval deletes the checkpoint, and each log_artifact call made wandb re-serialize the run config. Remove wandb_utils and its two call sites.

The wandb config was vars(args) itself, so any private runtime state attached to args (underscore-prefixed attributes) was serialized into the config at setup and again on each config sync, which is expensive when that state is large. Exclude underscore-prefixed attributes.

items.title: Keep prompt log-probs raw under processed_logprobs
items.author: santhnm2
items.summary: Prompt log-probs are now computed from the raw distribution in both s. Under, temperature and top-k/top-p apply only to engine-sampled rows. [Discussion: Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository.]
items.body:
# What does this PR do ?

Prompt log-probs are now computed from the raw distribution in both `logprobs_mode`s. Under `processed_logprobs`, temperature and top-k/top-p apply only to engine-sampled rows.

**Why:** `processed_logprobs` (#5419) exists so RL can recover the behavior policy's probability of each sampled token, for importance-sampling and mismatch corrections. Prompt tokens were never sampled from that distribution. The prefill path still sent every prompt row through the request's sampling transform, which caused two problems:
- prompt scores depended on the request's sampling settings, so they had no stable meaning for scoring workloads like lm-eval loglikelihood;
- any prompt token outside the request's top-k/top-p nucleus got `-inf`. The code already noted this ("prompt rows may keep -inf").

Multi-turn RL doesn't need processed prompt rows either. NeMo RL stitches together each turn's *generated* logprobs and always sets `skip_prompt_log_probs=True`. A later turn's prompt rows would be scored under the current weights, not the ones that sampled those tokens.

**Changes**
- `DynamicInferenceContext.calculate_log_probs_tensors`, prefill branch:
  - `log_softmax` for all rows;
  - processed log-probs only at each request's final (sampled) row;
  - the `-inf` → tempered fallback is applied only to those rows.
  - A partial prefill chunk's final row scores its next prompt token, so it stays raw too.
- Top-N log-probs reuse the same tensor, so prompt top-N is raw as well.
- Decode and only-last-token rows are all sampled rows and are unchanged. Processed mode still rejects speculative decoding.
- Updated docs, the `InferenceConfig.logprobs_mode` docstring, and the CLI help.

**Behavior change:** only for `logprobs_mode='processed_logprobs'` with `skip_prompt_log_probs=False`. Raw mode is unchanged.

**Tests**
- `test_calculate_and_store_log_probs[processed_logprobs]` now expects raw prompt rows and processed sampled rows.
- New `test_processed_log_probs_keep_partial_chunk_row_raw` covers the partial-chunk row.
- These are GPU tests and have not been run yet. A CPU stub check of the new prefill branch passes.

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 1 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/contexts/test_dynamic_context.py \
  -k "calculate_and_store_log_probs or keep_partial_chunk_row_raw"
```

items.title: perf(gdn): gather by the inverse permutation in CP all-to-all backward
items.author: JackRao123
items.summary: / reorder tensors with in three places: - the head-dim pre-permutation, - the THD sequence permutation, - its inverse on the way back. Autograd's backward is an atomic, because it can't assume unique indices.
items.body:
## What
`a2a_cp_to_hp` / `a2a_hp_to_cp` reorder tensors with `index_select` in three places:
- the head-dim pre-permutation,
- the THD sequence permutation,
- its inverse on the way back.

Autograd's `index_select` backward is an atomic `index_add_`, because it can't assume unique indices. All three indices are permutations, so the gradient is just a gather by the inverse permutation. That's much faster and deterministic.

This adds `_PermuteAlongDim`, whose forward is `index_select` by the permutation and whose backward is `index_select` by its inverse, and uses it at the three sites:
- **Head permutation:** the inverse comes from a new cached `_build_head_perm_and_inverse_for_split_sections`. `_build_head_perm_for_split_sections` is unchanged, since tests call it directly.
- **THD sequence permutation:** `_build_thd_cp_a2a_perm` already returns its inverse.
- **`a2a_hp_to_cp`:** rebuilds the forward index from the inverse with one O(n) scatter, so callers' signatures don't change.

## Correctness
For a permutation, the old backward adds each element exactly once into zeros and the new one copies it, so gradients are bit-identical.
- **New test** `tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_gdn_permute_along_dim.py`: asserts exact equality of outputs and gradients against `index_select`, for the head permutation and both directions of the THD permutation, in fp32 and bf16.
- **Existing tests:** `test_gated_delta_net.py` and `test_gated_delta_net_parallel.py` under `torchrun --nproc_per_node 4` (GB300) gave 151 passed / 72 skipped / 0 failed on every rank. On a second box, the full suite hits an NCCL watchdog timeout in `test_parallel_gated_delta_net2_correctness`. The base commit hits the same timeout there without this change, and with this change that test passes on its own (6/6 per rank).

## Performance
Measured on a downstream fork, on a model whose KDA layers use these helpers. 262k tokens on 8x GB300, CP4:
- Forward/backward step: 34.1 s → 28.9 s.
- The profiled `index_add_` cost was 5.5 s per step.
- Peak memory is unchanged.

items.title: fix(dsa): warn once when a selected fused hook falls back
items.author: JackRao123
items.summary: When the configured fused DSA backend declines a hook (,,, ), the caller falls back to the PyTorch reference path. That path is far slower and materializes much larger tensors; the naive top-k builds the full fp32 score tensor.
items.body:
## What
When the configured fused DSA backend declines a hook (`run_fused_qk_topk`, `run_fused_qk_topk_with_loss`, `run_fused_absorbed_sparse_attention`, `run_fused_dsa_attention`), the caller falls back to the PyTorch reference path. That path is far slower and materializes much larger tensors; the naive top-k builds the full `[sq, b, h, sk]` fp32 score tensor.

`_log_declined_hook` logged this at DEBUG on every call, so a run could sit on the reference path with nothing in the logs. This changes it to a WARNING emitted once per (backend, hook, reason).

## Why once
Declines happen on every forward, so a per-call warning would flood the logs. The key keeps distinct reasons visible.

## Testing
- **Unit test:** `test_dsa_kernel_hooks_log_declined_backend` now asserts the message is visible at WARNING level and that a repeat decline doesn't log again. It and `test_dsa_kernel_hooks_dispatch_to_backend` pass on this branch (GB300).
- **Downstream check:** on a downstream fork, a healthy GLM-family DSA run (cuDNN backend, 262k and packed 8x32k) emits no declined warnings, so this doesn't add noise to normal runs.

items.title: fix(distributed): restore FSDP v1 pipeline training and checkpoints
items.author: cuichenx
items.summary: Keep it draft until that dependency is available. Fix Megatron-FSDP v1 mesh construction and checkpoint restart with non-interleaved pipeline parallelism. [Discussion: Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository.]
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

**Depends on #8010 for shared-embedding initialization with meta-device construction.** This PR contains no replacement initialization logic. Keep it draft until that dependency is available.

## What does this PR do?

Fix Megatron-FSDP v1 mesh construction and checkpoint restart with non-interleaved pipeline parallelism.

With eight ranks and PP=2, the mesh helpers reshape all eight ranks using stage-local dimensions whose product is four. Include the outer PP axis in both FSDP and HSDP construction, then select the current stage and expert rank. Existing process-group consistency checks remain in place.

FSDP DTensor checkpointing also bypasses the block `sharded_state_dict()` methods that normally give pipeline layers global names. Two stages can consequently save different weights and Adam moments under the same `decoder.layers.0.*` keys. Add a shared handler that uses each layer's global `layer_number` for model tensors, optimizer state, and optimizer group metadata. Run it after fused-parameter, expert, and MTP processing on save and load, preserving the original tensor aliases for in-place loading. MTP retains its separate namespace.

Precision-aware v1 optimizers put gradients in `decoupled_grad`. Recognize that attribute when reducing shared embeddings across pipeline stages. Empty shards remain `None` for the optimizer, while synchronization retrieves their metadata-bearing buffer tensors so every DP rank participates.

Existing checkpoints affected by stage-local key collisions cannot recover the omitted weights and must be regenerated. The new checkpoint remapping applies only to v1; v2 optimizer keys are already global and must not be renamed again. PP=1 checkpoint names remain unchanged. The existing default missing-weight validation rejects incomplete legacy checkpoints.

## Validation

- Previously passed unchanged coverage: 26 mesh and 16 checkpoint cases on each of eight H100 ranks, plus six Bridge checkpoint tests. Includes PP=1/2/4, uneven stages, CP/EP/TP/ETP and HSDP mesh combinations, and preservation of v2 optimizer keys.
- The revised 96-case embedding-gradient test passed on every rank of an eight-H100 run. Its eager fixture isolates the retained gradient fix across ordinary/decoupled gradients, PP=1/2, TP=1/2, tied/MTP/unshared cases, BF16 wrappers, and verified empty shards. Together with unchanged mesh/checkpoint coverage, 138 Core cases passed per rank.
- Small Lightning with #8010 (`5920bd95`) plus this PR: eight hybrid layers, MTP=2, PP=2/EP=2/TP=1, BF16 compute and FP32 master weights/Adam moments. Three training steps, save at step two, then restart: all saved weights and optimizer tensors restored bitwise exactly on all eight ranks. The next loss (5.374913215637207) and gradient norm (2.875216245651245) match uninterrupted training exactly. After that step, 281/287 complete model/Adam tensors are bitwise equal; all pass rtol=1e-5/atol=1e-6, maximum absolute difference 4.331e-8.
- Full 52-layer Lightning with #8010 plus Core #8159: three forward/backward/optimizer steps completed on eight H100s, PP=2/EP=2/TP=1/CP=1, original widths/128 experts/vocabulary, MTP=2 and synthetic sequence length 256. Loss 12.176648 → 10.490705 → 9.382988, no skipped/NaN iterations; peak allocated memory 69.898 GiB. BF16 Adam moments fit this full-size smoke on one node; checkpoint restart was validated with the smaller FP32-moment run above.
- `tools/autoformat.sh` check mode passed Black/isort/pylint/ruff. Mypy is not installed in the pinned lint group and is optional in that script.

Training probes use function-level patch injection into NeMo 26.08.01, including #8010 and the existing main-branch embedding-gradient handling from #6486. Distributed unit tests use the full proposed Core source based on `cab97ebd1`.

Training probes set `deallocate_pipeline_outputs=False`, since v1's backward hooks return output views rejected by pipeline output deallocation. Coverage is non-interleaved PP; these short synthetic-data tests do not establish convergence or performance.

Focused Core command: `torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 -m pytest tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1/test_fsdp_mesh.py tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1/test_pipeline_checkpoint.py tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1/test_pipeline_embedding_grads.py -q`.

Independent subagent review of the removal and remaining diff completed; no source blockers.

## Contribution checks

- [x] Added distributed unit regressions for mesh group membership, PP=1/2/4 checkpoint round trips, uneven stages, wrapper prefixes, MTP/expert keys, optimizer aliases, legacy checkpoint rejection, and shared embedding gradients with real BF16 wrappers, distinct TP partitions, ordinary/decoupled gradients, actual backward reduction, and verified empty shards.

- [x] Documented behavior and compatibility in the helper docstring and this description.

items.author: jalbericiola
items.summary: It needs pydantic, which is not a declared dependency. Before, an editable install did not map; it was importable only from the repository root. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
# build(rl): ship the megatron.rl packing modules in the wheel

## What this PR does

NeMo RL imports the shared-prefix packing modules from `megatron.rl` (added in
P1). This PR ships them in built wheels and makes non-RL training stop
importing the RL runtime.

Depends on P1.

## Changes

- `pyproject.toml` `py-modules`: built wheels include the `shared_prefix_*`
  modules and `tree_layout` (torch and the standard library only), the lazy
  package `__init__`, and `generation_api`.
  - `generation_api` backs the lazy `megatron.rl.Request` exports. It needs
    pydantic, which is not a declared dependency.
  - The rest of the RL runtime (`rl_utils`, agents, inference, server) needs
    undeclared dependencies and stays out of the wheel.
- Editable installs now map the whole `megatron/rl` directory. Before, an
  editable install did not map `megatron.rl`; it was importable only from the
  repository root. Because of that, `megatron/training/training.py` now
  imports the `megatron.rl` training hooks only for RL runs.
- `.github/workflows/install-test.yml`: the pip job installs a built wheel. A
  new step then imports every shipped packing module (every `py-module` except
  `generation_api`) from the installed package, outside the checkout, and
  checks that `megatron.rl.rl_utils` is not installed. It uses
  `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` and `$RUNNER_TEMP` because the job runs in a container.
- `docker/Dockerfile.ci.dev`, `docker/Dockerfile.ci.lts` and the image build
  inputs (`.github/workflows/_build_ci_container.yml`,
  `populate-build-cache.yml`): the CI images install an editable skeleton of
  the repository, and setuptools refuses a listed `py-module` whose package
  directory is missing (`package directory 'megatron/rl' does not exist`).
  The skeleton now includes `megatron/rl/__init__.py`. This also affected
  #7914 before the split.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `tools/autoformat.sh`: black, isort, pylint and
  ruff (through `tools/autoformat.sh`) now cover the `shared_prefix_*` and
  `tree_layout` modules. `generation_api.py` and `__init__.py` stay outside
  these globs.

## Tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/test_megatron_rl_wheel.py tests/unit_tests/test_training.py
```

- `tests/unit_tests/test_megatron_rl_wheel.py` checks that `py-modules` lists
  exactly the packing modules plus `generation_api`. P1's API-contract test
  imports every packing module with undeclared dependencies blocked.
- `tests/unit_tests/test_training.py::test_megatron_rl_is_imported_only_for_rl_runs`
  checks that importing the training loop does not load the RL runtime.

Result on one GB200 node (torch 2.11, Transformer Engine 2.15, mamba-ssm 2.3.2.post1, causal-conv1d 1.6.2.post1, flash-attn 2.8.1): 16 passed (`test_megatron_rl_wheel.py`, `test_training.py`). A wheel built from this branch contains exactly `megatron/rl/__init__.py`, `generation_api.py`, the seven `shared_prefix_*` modules and `tree_layout.py`; the new CI step imports the eight packing modules from it outside the checkout, and fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` when a shipped module imports an unshipped one (checked by injecting `import megatron.rl.logging`). The CI image's editable skeleton install was reproduced: it fails without `megatron/rl/__init__.py` and succeeds with it. This branch alone on top of main also ran the surrounding regression suites (routers, attention, MTP, Mamba, training, RL) on one and four GPUs. Every failure in those runs also occurs on main in the same container: tests that need more ranks than the run had, and missing APEX extensions.

## Shared-prefix stack

This PR is one of seven that #7914 was split into; #7914 itself is now P6, the
HybridModel integration. Each one needs fewer CODEOWNERS groups and can be
reviewed on its own. Shared-prefix
execution stores a prompt once per star (by default up to 16 completions of the
same group)
and runs those completions against it, instead of repeating the prompt in every
packed row.

| PR | Branch | Reviewer groups | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 #8152 RL packing library | `shared-prefix/p1-rl-packing` | reinforcement-learning | — |
| P2 #8153 MoE multiplicities and recompute context | `shared-prefix/p2-moe-multiplicities` | core, mixture-of-experts | — |
| P3 #8155 MTP loss groups | `shared-prefix/p3-mtp-loss-groups` | core, transformer | — |
| P4 #8156 forest attention and layout | `shared-prefix/p4-forest-attention` | core, transformer | — |
| P5 #8157 Mamba state fork | `shared-prefix/p5-mamba-state-fork` | core, hybrid-model | P4 |
| P6 #7914 HybridModel integration | `shared-prefix/hybrid-kernels-20261006` | core, hybrid-model | P1, P2, P3, P5 |
| P7 #8158 RL packaging | `shared-prefix/p7-rl-packaging` | ci, training | P1 |

P1 to P4 can merge in any order. A dependent branch carries its dependencies'
commits until they merge; review only its last commit.

Without a caller, P2 to P5 do not change existing numerics. Two P2 changes do
apply to every caller, and both keep results unchanged:

- recomputation through `tensor_parallel.checkpoint` and
  `CheckpointWithoutOutput` restores the forward pass's `contextvars` context
  (`te_checkpoint` is unchanged);
- the router GEMM backward skips gradients nobody requested.

P1 changes `megatron.rl` import-time behavior (lazy request types, lazy log
file). P6 is the first PR that wires the feature into a model.

# feat(ssm): add shared-prefix Mamba state forking

## What this PR does

Runs a `MambaLayer` on a shared-prefix layout:

- Each prompt is scanned once, up to its last scan-chunk boundary.
- The convolution and SSM state there are forked, differentiably, into one
  branch per completion.
- Each branch replays the remaining prompt tail (fewer than `chunk_size`
  tokens) and the convolution halo.

Nothing calls this path unless a caller opts in.

Depends on P4 for `megatron/core/shared_prefix_layout.py`.

## Changes

- `mamba_shared_prefix.py`:
  - `forward_mamba_layer_shared_prefix(layer, hidden_states, layout)` runs one
    layer at TP1 or TP>1 with sequence parallelism, and at CP1 or CP>1
    through sequence-to-head collectives.
  - `NRL_SP_MAMBA_IMPL` selects the backend:
    - `ragged_state_fork` (default) pads each branch only to its own chunk
      boundary, so scan work follows the real completion lengths.
    - `state_fork` uses only the public mamba-ssm API and pads every branch to
      its longest sibling.
    - `replay_prefix` rescans the prefix per branch as a parity baseline;
      `packed_recurrence` and `packed_fused` are diagnostic oracles.
      `packed_fused` is a forward-only diagnostic: its backward has never
      been validated, so it is rejected when grad is enabled.
    - The `*_training` variants use the named backend in training and
      `state_fork` in evaluation.
  - `validate_mamba_layer_shared_prefix` is meant to run for every Mamba layer
    before any layer executes. P6 wires that in. It rejects:
    - non-`MambaMixer` mixers and missing gated RMSNorm;
    - a mixer whose TP or CP size differs from the caller's (the error names
      both sizes);
    - the contiguous linear CP layout at CP>1;
    - for the default backend: a non-power-of-two `chunk_size`, a non-default
      SSM state dtype, and missing private kernels. In those cases the error
      names `NRL_SP_MAMBA_IMPL=state_fork` as the manual workaround.
- `mamba_ragged.py`, `mamba_ragged_scan.py`: the ragged forest scan.
  - `mamba_ragged_scan.py` adapts mamba-ssm's `ssd_combined` and
    `ssd_state_passing` kernels (Apache-2.0, covered by the repository
    LICENSE). Only the inter-chunk forest state passing is new.
  - The new ragged gather sums sibling gradients in a fixed FP32 order,
    without atomics.
  - `NRL_SP_MAMBA_SAVE_INTERMEDIATES=1` keeps the FP32 scan intermediates for
    backward instead of recomputing them. It defaults to 0 and is checked at
    the first scan.
- `mamba_forest_replay.py` and `mamba_sequence_packing.py` hold the
  `packed_recurrence` backend; `mamba_branch_layout.py` holds the branch
  packing helpers that `state_fork` and `replay_prefix` use.
- Every shared path passes channel-last input to `causal_conv1d`, whose
  channel-first backward is wrong at some lengths.
- `MambaContextParallel.pre_conv_ssm(..., include_gate=True)`: with
  `include_gate=False` the gate stays TP-local. The default is unchanged.

The new kernels are registered in the determinism manifest.

## Tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_shared_prefix_mamba_numerics.py \
    tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_shared_prefix_mamba_backends.py \
    tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_mamba_branch_layout.py \
    tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_shared_prefix_mamba_kernels.py
```

Result on one GB200 node (torch 2.11, Transformer Engine 2.15, mamba-ssm 2.3.2.post1, causal-conv1d 1.6.2.post1, flash-attn 2.8.1): 423 passed (one GPU). This branch alone on top of main also ran the surrounding regression suites (routers, attention, MTP, Mamba, training, RL) on one and four GPUs. Every failure in those runs also occurs on main in the same container: tests that need more ranks than the run had, and missing APEX extensions.

- `tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_shared_prefix_mamba_numerics.py`: the four
  differentiable backends (`ragged_state_fork`, `state_fork`, `replay_prefix`,
  `packed_recurrence`) against dense rows.
  - Branch lengths are chosen so that the `state_fork` and `replay_prefix`
    convolutions fall in the defective `causal_conv1d` length classes. The
    ragged and packed paths pad every segment to the scan chunk, so they run
    the same parity check without reaching those classes.
  - In FP32 the difference is only summation order, bounded at 5e-5 relative
    L2.
  - In BF16, shared must stay within 1.5 times the dense error against an
    FP32 reference.
  - Evaluation and training forwards must match bit for bit.
  - The `packed_fused` oracle is not tested.
- `tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_shared_prefix_mamba_backends.py`:
  - backend selection and layer validation on CPU;
  - int32 and int64 offsets bitwise;
  - the gather backward against `index_add_`;
  - compile reuse across lengths.
- `tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_mamba_branch_layout.py`: branch pack/merge
  gradients against a slice reference (CPU, FP64, bitwise) and `gradcheck`.
- `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_shared_prefix_mamba_kernels.py`:
  - bit-exact replay of the ragged gather and the forest scan, kernel by
    kernel;
  - replay of the ragged and packed scans with a real `MambaMixer`'s
    parameters;
  - a negative control without `MAMBA_DETERMINISTIC=1`.

  Bit-exact replay needs `MAMBA_DETERMINISTIC=1` for the SSD kernels and
  `CAUSAL_CONV1D_DETERMINISTIC=1` (causal-conv1d >= 1.6.0) for the
  convolution.

These tests run at TP1/CP1. The TP>1, sequence-parallel and CP>1 paths,
including `include_gate=False`, are covered by P6's model-parity tests at
TP2/SP/CP2 and TP1/CP4.

## Notes for reviewers

- The default backend calls private mamba-ssm SSD kernels, validated on
  2.3.2.post1 only.
- Planned follow-up:
  - keep `ragged_state_fork` (default) and `state_fork` (the public-API
    workaround above);
  - remove the other backends;
  - replace `NRL_SP_MAMBA_IMPL` and `NRL_SP_MAMBA_SAVE_INTERMEDIATES` with
    configuration.

## Shared-prefix stack

This PR is one of seven that #7914 was split into; #7914 itself is now P6, the
HybridModel integration. Each one needs fewer CODEOWNERS groups and can be
reviewed on its own. Shared-prefix
execution stores a prompt once per star (by default up to 16 completions of the
same group)
and runs those completions against it, instead of repeating the prompt in every
packed row.

| PR | Branch | Reviewer groups | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 #8152 RL packing library | `shared-prefix/p1-rl-packing` | reinforcement-learning | — |
| P2 #8153 MoE multiplicities and recompute context | `shared-prefix/p2-moe-multiplicities` | core, mixture-of-experts | — |
| P3 #8155 MTP loss groups | `shared-prefix/p3-mtp-loss-groups` | core, transformer | — |
| P4 #8156 forest attention and layout | `shared-prefix/p4-forest-attention` | core, transformer | — |
| P5 #8157 Mamba state fork | `shared-prefix/p5-mamba-state-fork` | core, hybrid-model | P4 |
| P6 #7914 HybridModel integration | `shared-prefix/hybrid-kernels-20261006` | core, hybrid-model | P1, P2, P3, P5 |
| P7 #8158 RL packaging | `shared-prefix/p7-rl-packaging` | ci, training | P1 |

P1 to P4 can merge in any order. A dependent branch carries its dependencies'

items.title: feat(transformer): add shared-prefix forest attention
items.author: jalbericiola
items.summary: Under, which enables, it uses FlashAttention's deterministic backward and a deterministic, so the accumulation order is fixed. When a caller sets it on a, the forest kernel replaces.
items.body:
# feat(transformer): add shared-prefix forest attention

## What this PR does

Adds exact attention over a shared-prefix layout, in which each prompt is
stored once and followed by its completions:

- a prompt token attends the prompt causally;
- a completion token attends the whole prompt and its own completion
  causally, never a sibling completion or another prompt.

RoPE positions restart at the prompt length for each completion. Nothing calls
this attention unless a caller sets the new per-call slot, so existing
attention behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- `megatron/core/shared_prefix_layout.py`: the layout descriptor.
  - `SharedPrefixLayout` describes one star `[prompt, c_1, ..., c_G]`, and
    `SharedPrefixForestLayout` describes several.
  - They provide dense-row indices, positions, CP zigzag ownership and per-row
    token multiplicities, and their `forest` tuples are what the attention
    consumes.
  - They also carry logical (unpadded) completion lengths and the MTP
    loss-group partition, which the HybridModel integration (P6) uses and
    tests.
  - The module sits next to `packed_seq_params.py` because the SSM and model
    code (P5, P6) import it.
- `megatron/core/transformer/shared_prefix_attention.py`:
  - `flash_composed_forest_attention` runs a whole forest in at most two
    FlashAttention varlen passes and merges them by log-sum-exp: a causal
    self pass and a non-causal completion-to-prompt pass.
  - Its backward is exact and accumulates every completion's contribution into
    the shared prompt keys and values in FP32. Under
    `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, which `--deterministic-mode`
    enables, it uses FlashAttention's deterministic backward and a
    deterministic `index_add_`, so the accumulation order is fixed.
  - `flash_composed_forest_attention_cp` runs the same computation on zigzag
    CP shards through sequence-to-head all-to-alls, including replicated GQA
    KV heads.
  - Validation for callers, to run before any layer:
    - `validate_shared_prefix_attention` rejects any module that is not a
      `SelfAttention`, and a `SelfAttention` the forest kernel cannot run: selective core-attention recompute, QK-clip statistics, sliding
      windows, non-vanilla softmax, attention dropout, logit softcapping, TP or
      CP group sizes that differ from the caller's, and uneven CP head splits;
    - `require_shared_prefix_flash_attn` rejects a missing flash-attn or one
      older than 2.7.
- `Attention._shared_prefix_forest`: a class-level per-call slot, `None` by
  default. When a caller sets it on a `SelfAttention`, the forest kernel
  replaces `core_attention`. Attention subclasses that override `forward`, such
  as multi-latent attention, never read it.
  - The branch rejects packed-sequence parameters, external masks or biases,
    non-fp16/bf16 inputs, and inference contexts that reach core attention.
  - It does not check the module settings above itself; callers run
    `validate_shared_prefix_attention` first.

The kernel is registered in the determinism manifest and listed in the op
catalog.

## Tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_shared_prefix_attention.py \

# feat(transformer): normalize MTP loss per packed loss group

## What this PR does

`process_mtp_loss` normalizes the MTP loss by token counts over the whole
packed sequence. When a caller combines several forwards into one (for
example several shared-prefix groups), each original forward had its own
counts. The new `loss_group_lengths` argument restores them.

## Changes

- `process_mtp_loss(..., loss_group_lengths=None)`: CP-local lengths that
  partition the packed sequence into independent loss groups. Each group's
  MTP gradient then equals the gradient of a separate call for that group,
  including the original/rolled token-count correction.
- Precondition: each group must consist of whole packed sequences. Its
  CP-local boundaries must be the physical sequence boundaries
  (`cu_seqlens_q_padded`, or `cu_seqlens_q` when unpadded) divided by the CP
  size. The docstring states this; the code does not check it.
- At CP>1 the argument requires the zigzag CP layout and is rejected with the
  contiguous one. With the contiguous layout, a rank's share of a group depends
  on the rest of the pack, so the per-rank counts would differ from a separate
  call.
- The argument requires `calculate_per_token_loss=True`. Lengths that do not
  partition the CP-local sequence are rejected.
- Without the argument the loss is unchanged.

## Tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_multi_token_prediction_loss_groups.py
```

runs on CPU or GPU:

- one grouped call against one call per group, with and without an MTP input
  mask, to 1e-12 in FP64;
- the per-token weights against their analytic values, on a pack built so that
  every group's correction differs;
- the rejection of the contiguous CP layout.

items.title: perf(dsa): compute indexer scores with the cuDNN kernel
items.author: JackRao123
items.summary: computed indexer scores with a per-head fp32 PyTorch loop:, then, and for each indexer head, all on SIMT rather than tensor cores. It serves two callers: -, whenever a chunk doesn't cover every row or carries explicit lengths: long causal calls that need ch…
items.body:
## What
`_compute_indexer_scores_chunk_with_global_rows` computed indexer scores with a per-head fp32 PyTorch loop: `bmm`, then `relu_`, `mul_` and `add_` for each indexer head, all on SIMT rather than tensor cores. It serves two callers:
- `_indexer_topk_from_score_chunks`, whenever a chunk doesn't cover every row or carries explicit lengths: long causal calls that need chunking, and calls with varlen bounds;
- the full-score varlen branch of `_indexer_topk_bshd`.

This PR computes the scores with `indexer_forward_wrapper` instead, under the same name, and deletes the loop:
- **Plain causal chunks:** pass `q_causal_offsets=row_start`, which is the reference mask (`(row_start + i + 1) // ratio`).
- **Chunks with explicit lengths:** run with the tightest causal offset that covers every row, computed on device with no host sync. The exact per-row prefix is then applied, so masked positions match the reference exactly.

`q_causal_offsets` is available in the pinned `nvidia-cudnn-frontend==1.29.0`.

## Numerics
- **New test** `test_dsa_cudnn_indexer_scores.py`: compares against a direct einsum reference over 9 cases: causal at ratio 1 and 4, unaligned row offsets, pooled bounds, empty rows, non-monotonic lengths, lengths beyond `sk`, packed resets.
- **Result:** the `-inf` mask is identical in every case; max abs diff ≤ 1.2e-4 on scores up to ~300.
- **Environment:** this branch on GB300 with `nvidia-cudnn-frontend==1.29.0`, 9/9 passing.

## Performance
Measured on a downstream fork with a model whose indexer always passes explicit bounds (a 4:1 pooled-key indexer). 262k tokens on 8x GB300, CP4 EP8:
- Forward/backward step: 50.7 s → 32.7 s. The fp32 loop was about 15 s of it.
- Over 6 steps, loss and grad norm match the reference path within run-to-run noise.

Upstream models gain wherever they hit chunked scoring with explicit bounds, long causal calls, or the full-score varlen branch; I haven't benchmarked an upstream model.

# feat(moe): logical token multiplicities and fixed-row router blocks

## What this PR does

In a packed layout one row can stand for several logical tokens. For example,
a shared prompt row stands for one copy of the prompt per completion. This PR
lets the MoE router count such rows correctly for expert-bias updates and makes
its forward routing scores independent of packing. Only
`local_tokens_per_expert` is weighted. Aux losses, z-loss, capacity dropping,
quantile balancing, routing replay and router diagnostics still count physical
rows, and the backward GEMMs are unchanged, so a caller must disable those
features. P6 rejects the loss, dropping, balancing and replay settings; router
diagnostics must be left off by the caller. Without a caller that opts in, routing is
unchanged.

## Changes

- `token_multiplicities` (optional, default `None`) on `TopKRouter.forward`,
  `InferenceTopKRouter.forward`, `TopKRouter.routing`,
  `TopKRouter._apply_expert_bias` and `MoELayer.route`. When set, each row is
  counted that many times in `local_tokens_per_expert`, so expert-bias updates
  match a dense forward. Counts stay exact in the existing int64 buffer.
  - On the default path, routers and routing callables are still called with
    exactly the upstream keywords.
  - Existing callers and replacement `routing` callables therefore keep
    working.
- `RouterInterface.forward` declares the optional argument, and the router
  docstrings describe it: one logical token count per flattened
  sequence-first row.
- `MoELayer._shared_prefix_token_multiplicities`: a per-call slot, `None` by
  default, that a caller sets around one layer call. Only the eager
  `MoELayer.forward` path reads it; paths that call `route()` directly or replay
  a CUDA graph ignore it.
- `moe_utils.router_gating_token_blocks()`: inside this scope the forward
  router GEMM runs over fixed row blocks. A packing change can otherwise select a
  different GEMM reduction, and even FP32 router differences below 2e-6 can
  flip BF16 expert choices.
- `tensor_parallel/random.py`: `CheckpointFunction` and
  `CheckpointWithoutOutput` recompute inside a copy of the forward pass's
  `contextvars` context.
  - CUDA autograd can run backward on an engine thread with different context
    values.
  - Without this change, a forward-scoped setting such as the router block
    scope is lost during recomputation.
  - Tensor observations stay suspended inside the restored context.
  - This applies to every recompute through these two helpers and keeps
    results unchanged. `te_checkpoint`, used with FP8/FP4, is unchanged.
- `RouterGatingLinearFunction.backward` computes only the gradients autograd
  requires. A frozen router still produces the input gradient but skips the
  weight-gradient GEMM, which has no consumer. This applies to every MoE run.

    tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py \
    tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m pytest tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py \
    tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py

Every failure in those runs also occurs on main in the same container: tests that need more ranks than the run had, and missing APEX extensions.

  - the routing signature without multiplicities;
  - exact logical counts;
  - fixed-row blocks against per-block copies;
  - gradients for all seven combinations of trainable input, weight and bias.

# feat(rl): add the shared-prefix packing library

## What this PR does

GRPO samples several completions per prompt, and a packed forward normally
repeats the prompt in every row. This PR adds the planning side of
shared-prefix execution to `megatron.rl`. Rows with the same group ID and
exact prompt tokens are packed into stars. A star stores the prompt once,
followed by up to `MAX_SHARED_PREFIX_BRANCHES` (16) completions. Several
stars can share one packed forward.

Terms:

- **Star**: one prompt followed by its completions, `[prompt, c_1, ..., c_G]`.
- **Forest**: several stars packed into one forward.
- **Dense rows**: the separate sequences `[prompt, c_g]` that a star replaces.

## Changes

- `tree_layout.py`: the parent-linked tree descriptor of a packed unit.
- `shared_prefix_packing.py`: planner rows, exact-prompt matching, star and
  forest layouts, even group subdivision and forest packing.
- `shared_prefix_metadata.py`: group-coherent data-parallel sharding and equal
  real-row execution slots.
- `shared_prefix_tensors.py`: token, position and scatter maps, TP/CP padding
  and zigzag sharding.
- `shared_prefix_alignment.py`: brings every data-parallel replica to a forward
  count the caller has agreed on. It splits execution units at real-row
  boundaries and never adds dummy rows.
- `shared_prefix_dense_bins.py`, `shared_prefix_execution.py`,
  `shared_prefix_cost.py`: dense-bin reconstruction, execution plans and the
  work model.
- `megatron/rl/shared_prefix.md` documents the API and the integration
  contract.

The packing modules depend only on torch and the standard library. They never
import `megatron.core`. NeMo RL (NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4537) is the first consumer.

## Changes to existing `megatron.rl` behavior

`import megatron.rl` becomes lighter:

- The Pydantic request types move from `megatron/rl/__init__.py` to
  `generation_api.py`. The package exports load lazily, and `agent/` and
  `inference/` import the types from the new module. Newly pickled request
  objects therefore name `megatron.rl.generation_api` as their module.
- `logging.py` prints its log directory and opens (truncates) its log file on
  the first `log()` call instead of at import.

## Tests

CPU-only, with no distributed fixtures:

```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest \
    tests/unit_tests/rl/test_shared_prefix*.py tests/unit_tests/rl/test_tree_layout.py
```

This branch alone on top of main also ran the surrounding regression suites (routers, attention, MTP, Mamba, training, RL) on one and four GPUs. Every failure in those runs also occurs on main in the same container: tests that need more ranks than the run had, and missing APEX extensions.

- The tensor property tests run a toy model on planned and materialized
  layouts and check every predicted position against a dense per-row forward.
  The planning property tests push seeded random batches through sharding,
  slot planning, layout planning and alignment, end to end.
- `tests/unit_tests/rl/shared_prefix_oracles.py` holds a quadratic reference
  attention mask built from the tree descriptor, plus a plan-and-materialize
  helper.
- `test_shared_prefix_api_contract.py` pins the symbols and keywords NeMo RL
  calls and checks that the packing modules import without undeclared
  dependencies.

## Notes for reviewers

- Nothing in Megatron-LM calls this library yet. P8 adds a test that checks
  this planner's padding quantum and CP ownership against core execution (P6).
  Wheel packaging of these modules is P7.

items.title: [tool, rollout, perf] feat: add opt-in one-step tool read-ahead
items.author: jiacao-amd
items.summary: It does not establish a general rollout or end-to-end RL training speedup. The current implementation has not demonstrated value on a representative real RL workload, so this draft is being withdrawn.
items.body:
**Closed after an applicability review.** The measured ~16% reduction applies to a constructed linked-record workload with explicit successor IDs and synthetic tool delays. It does not establish a general rollout or end-to-end RL training speedup. The current implementation has not demonstrated value on a representative real RL workload, so this draft is being withdrawn. The implementation and recorded test results are retained for reference.

---

### What does this PR do?

A linked-record tool often returns the exact identifier the model will request next. This PR adds an opt-in `ReadAhead` helper that starts that one immutable read during the next model turn and delivers it only when the model actually requests the matching key. A runnable `ToolAgentLoop` example scopes the reader to a trajectory and cleans up pending HTTP work on completion, failure, or cancellation.

This is a separate direction from #8136's continuation admission burst. That PR is now closed and did not establish an isolated scheduling benefit. This contribution overlaps tool waiting with model work; it does not modify the model, inference kernels, backend scheduling, or default agent loop behavior.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [tool prefetch](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+tool+prefetch+in%3Atitle), [read-ahead](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22read-ahead%22), [speculative tool](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22speculative+tool%22+in%3Atitle), [references to #8136](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8136+in%3Abody). No open PR implementing this tool-read overlap was found. Broad search hits in checkpoint handling are unrelated. There is no originating issue to close.
- [x] Use the required module/type title format.

### Test

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tools/test_read_ahead_on_cpu.py \
  tests/tools/test_function_tool_on_cpu.py \
  tests/tools/test_mixed_tools_on_cpu.py \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_call_tool_on_cpu.py -q
# 61 passed; one existing Ray deprecation warning.

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never
# All 14 hooks passed. Staged hooks also passed after adding the documentation index entry.

git diff --cached --check
# Passed.
```

Six helper cases cover one-step overlap without recursive reads, wrong-key fallback, speculative-failure retry, demanded-failure propagation, and cancellation of both unused and consumed prefetches. Five added example cases use real local HTTP and the existing tool dispatch: concurrent trajectory isolation with read-ahead off/on, and cleanup on normal return, model error, and cancellation. Model turns in these CPU integration cases are scripted; they are not model evaluations. Existing `*_on_cpu.py` discovery includes these tests. The new RST page also parses without warnings.

**Current-commit real-model HTTP E2E:** commit `bde9bde4864ba15c3fd942ce280fb7bc628fc2fb`, full MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL revision `5711b268169967567844e1e560e8a3966da959b1`, eight MI355X GPUs. The committed `ReadAheadAgentLoop` and `ReadRecordTool` were loaded through Hydra and the standard tool registry, using their committed YAML files. The harness uses the real `LLMServerClient` and default Ray load balancer; a Ray adapter forwards actual prompt token IDs to the model server and consumes live SSE output. Record reads go through a real aiohttp service with synthetic immutable linked-record delays of 0.25/0.5/1/2 seconds.

The same server ran **one off → on → off cycle**. Each phase had a four-task smoke, three stable warmups, and three formal 64-trajectory batches: nine formal batches total. Native FCFS, async scheduling disabled, sparse4096 graph settings, model and workload stayed fixed. Each batch used a fresh prefix-cache salt. Model loading and warmup were excluded. The old scheduling PR was not enabled.

| Mode | Three batch completion times (s) | Mean ± sample SD (s) |
|---|---|---|
| Off, before | 31.811044 / 31.616662 / 31.635930 | 31.687879 ± 0.107099 |
| On | 26.452443 / 26.420624 / 26.787237 | 26.553435 ± 0.203103 |
| Off, recheck | 31.579407 / 31.315902 / 31.611394 | 31.502234 ± 0.162159 |

Completion time fell by **16.20% / 15.71%** relative to the two baselines; baseline drift was -0.59%. The last-finishing trajectory's exposed read wait averaged 24.556 → 19.039 → 24.561 seconds, with about 5.510 seconds of overlapping reads when enabled. Its physical reads still took about 24.52 seconds; model service request time averaged 6.498 → 6.960 → 6.497 seconds. The gain comes from overlapping tool waiting and model generation.

**576/576 formal trajectories passed** independent checks of ordered record IDs, full returned values, calculator inputs, and final answers. Every batch made 624 model requests, 496 physical HTTP reads, and 64 calculator calls. Enabled batches reused 432 prefetches, without extra reads. All physical requests retained their injected delays, no unconsumed dependency was crossed, and HTTP tasks, helper tasks, Ray counters, and backend queues were drained. Request and token counts reconcile with server metrics.

| Mode | Generated tokens in the three formal batches |
|---|---|
| Off, before | 18702 / 18536 / 18626 |
| On | 18917 / 18728 / 18862 |
| Off, recheck | 18732 / 18844 / 18748 |

Three further live-model diagnostics passed: turn-limit termination, an injected model transport failure after the first live turn, and caller cancellation. Each canceled the deliberately blocked successor HTTP request and left no pending work. These are separate from the timed batches. Scripted preflight results are also excluded from model-quality and performance results.

Executed commands in the prepared AAC container (environment, launch commands, source and protocol hashes are retained with the results):

```bash
bash "$AAC_TASK_DIR/protocol/continue_one_cycle.sh"
"$AAC_PYTHON" "$AAC_TASK_DIR/protocol/audit_e2e.py" "$AAC_JOB_DIR"
# One cycle and all three diagnostics passed; controller exit code 0.
```

The downloaded raw results were audited again locally with the UV-managed environment; they produced an identical aggregate. All 1,277 frozen source/protocol manifest entries passed checksum verification. No serving-cache writes were observed during timed regions; file timestamps are a proxy, not a full compilation trace. The independent auditor rejected five deliberately corrupted traces covering dependency order, shortened delays, extra reads, wrong values, and pending work.

This validates the current PR HTTP example against a live full model. It is still a deterministic linked-record workload with synthetic service delays and no shared tool-capacity limit. No RL optimizer or weight updates ran, and output tokens were not identical. Three samples per state in one cycle do not establish a general RL or production remote-service speedup.

Operational record: the test was reduced to one cycle during model loading by handing control to a replacement controller in the same container. The original wrapper remained paused; after the replacement exited 0 and the model-stop GPU report showed zero use/memory and no KFD processes, allocation 48534 was intentionally canceled to release it. The parked wrapper’s later GPU-report hook logged a ROCm shared-memory error; the successful pre-cancellation model-stop report and the later error are both preserved. No second or third comparison cycle ran.

The raw results and frozen harness/source archive are retained by the contributor, outside the PR: `job-48534-results.tar.gz`, SHA256 `b3ec030a231b09e6e295a3dc9db8c9570662efb52f2c19f1e9eeffd9fd14eecb`. This fresh E2E result supersedes the earlier dedicated-helper experiment as evidence for the PR implementation; the documentation labels the earlier measurement as historical.

### API and Usage Example

```python
from verl.tools.read_ahead import ReadAhead

reader = ReadAhead(fetch_record, lambda record: record.get("next_record_id"))
try:
    # Call read only when the model requests the key; keep reader across turns.
    result = await reader.read(record_id)
finally:
    await reader.aclose()  # At trajectory end, after demanded reads stop.
```

The example agent/tool YAML files are under `examples/tutorial/agent_loop_get_started/`. Configure an immutable record snapshot URL and select the custom loop, then set its `read_ahead` option to `true` (default `false`). `docs/advance/tool_read_ahead.rst` gives the service contract and rollout overrides.

### Design & Code Changes

- Keep at most one speculative result per trajectory. Derive the next key only from the consumed result; never recursively follow an unconsumed record.
- Reuse only a matching key. Cancel and join mismatches; retry failed speculation on demand; propagate demanded errors.
- Require serial reads, complete operation keys, immutable/read-only data, and cancellation-aware async fetches. The example serializes reads and binds its reader with a per-run context, without storing tasks in serialized outputs.
- Keep cleanup at trajectory scope because ordinary `BaseTool.release` runs after each call. Close the reader before its HTTP session.
- Add documentation, tests, and the 2026 individual-contributor header to the existing license allow-list for the new files.

Related work: [Conveyor](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00059v2), [PASTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18897v3), and [LLMCompiler](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04511v3). This is deterministic one-step lookahead, not a reproduction of learned prediction or joint scheduling. Wrong predictions can waste reads; service-wide admission limits remain the caller's responsibility, and cancelling an HTTP request does not guarantee remote work stops.

- [x] Add documentation and usage example.
- [x] Add tests covered by the existing CPU workflow.
- [ ] Human submitter review of every changed line and independent execution of the relevant tests before requesting review.
- [ ] Request project CI when the draft is ready.

No recipe submodule change is involved.

### AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with research, implementation, tests, the prior experiment, current-commit HTTP E2E validation, and PR preparation. The commit includes attribution trailers. This is a draft for the human submitter's review; it does not attest that the human has reviewed the new lines or independently rerun the tests.

items.title: fix(inference): keep streamed partials aligned with the merged record after eviction
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: The stream stalls, then skips tokens, so the concatenation of deltas no longer equals the final reply. Log probs shift with the tokens. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
**Problem.** With `SamplingParams(streaming=True)`, a request that the dynamic engine evicts under KV pressure, or recomputes on suspend, streams wrong partial frames after it resumes. The stream stalls, then skips tokens, so the concatenation of `ENGINE_REPLY_PARTIAL` deltas no longer equals the final reply (`record.merge()`). Log probs shift with the tokens.

**Root cause.** `_try_send_streaming_partials` keeps a per-request emitted-token offset (`_partial_emit_lengths`) over the whole stream, but slices it into `record[-1].generated_tokens`. `DynamicInferenceRequestRecord.checkpoint()` (eviction and suspend recompute) appends a new segment whose prompt absorbs the earlier generations and whose `generated_tokens` restart at 0. The surviving offset therefore indexes past the start of the new segment.

**Fix.** Index the stream in `record.merge()` coordinates. The total length and the token, log-prob and top-n slices span all checkpoint segments (`_slice_merged_segments`, with no merged copy), and prompt log probs come from the first segment, as in `merge()`. Also bound `new_top_n_logprobs` by `emit_end` like tokens and log probs. Previously, held-back top-n entries were sent early and then sent again.

**Tests.** `test_streaming_partials_continue_across_checkpoint` (CPU; two checkpoints; with and without stop-word holdback; `streaming_interval` 1 and 3) and `TestDynamicInferenceEngine::test_streaming_partials_match_merged_record_after_eviction` (GPU; tiny KV pool forces real evictions; streamed deltas must equal the final request). Both fail on main and pass with this change.

items.title: fix(tau-bench): train on sampled token ids instead of retokenized chat text
items.author: PlanckChang
items.summary: Tau-bench multi-turn RL was training on a retokenized chat-template rendering, not on the tokens SGLang sampled. The loss mask for that rendering was also wrong whenever the template inserted text the model did not generate.
items.body:
## Summary

Tau-bench multi-turn RL was training on a retokenized chat-template rendering, not on the tokens SGLang sampled. The loss mask for that rendering was also wrong whenever the template inserted text the model did not generate.

## What was wrong

Each turn sent the full conversation as text. The sampled token ids were discarded. Training targets came from `apply_chat_template` plus `encode`. BPE does not round-trip, so `encode(decode(ids))` is often a different sequence. Qwen3-style templates can also rewrite earlier `<think>` blocks when a new user turn arrives, so the next inference context and the training tokens diverged.

The assistant span was then labeled with one mask bit per retokenized id:

- The model text had its trailing `<|im_end|>` stripped, and the template appended `<|im_end|>\n` again. That closer and the following newline were all `loss_mask=1`. The newline is not a sampled token.
- From the second assistant turn on, `<|im_start|>assistant` (and a generation prompt such as `<think>\n`) was supposed to be masked. The mask length was `len(encode(prefix))`, measured separately from `encode(prefix + content)`. If BPE merges across that boundary, template tokens fall inside the loss.

Tool and user turns were already `loss_mask=0`. The bug was the assistant span.

## What this does

- Tokenize the first prompt once. Later requests send that exact `input_ids` prefix and `return_logprob=true`.
- Keep SGLang `output_token_logprobs` as the assistant tokens (`loss_mask=1`), including a sampled `<|im_end|>`. Decode them only to parse the tool call.
- Append the chat-template tail after that end token for the tool/user observation and, when the episode continues, the next generation prompt. That tail is `loss_mask=0`. If the sample did not emit the end token, insert one copy and leave it masked.
- Stop the episode when a turn hits the length limit instead of closing a partial assistant message with template tokens.
- Skip transient git lock files when the image-baseline patch test copies a repository. `git maintenance` was removing `objects/maintenance.lock` during `shutil.copytree`.

## Test plan

- [x] `python tests/test_tau_bench_token_delta.py`
- [x] `python tests/test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py`
- [x] Sampled ids that do not survive `encode(decode(ids))` stay intact in the training sequence
- [x] `<|im_start|>assistant`, the newline after `<|im_end|>`, and tool/user text are `loss_mask=0`
- [x] A template end token the model did not sample is inserted once and masked
- [x] A BPE merge across `<|im_end|>` stays in the masked suffix

items.title: refactor(training): migrate TrainingConfig and ValidationConfig
items.author: cuichenx
items.summary: Migrate TrainingConfig and ValidationConfig together, making and authoritative in the shared training loop while preserving existing CLI behavior. Resolve batch-size defaults centrally before constructing training services.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Migrate TrainingConfig and ValidationConfig together, making `cfg.train` and `cfg.validation` authoritative in the shared training loop while preserving existing CLI behavior.

- Read training/evaluation batch sizes, horizons, stopping policies, validation controls, and runtime housekeeping from the run config. Resolve batch-size defaults centrally before constructing training services.
- Keep derived training/evaluation iteration counts on the config; leave runtime progress on its existing owner.
- Update scheduler, dataloader, checkpoint-resume, RL batching, warmup, and dataset-construction consumers. Keep `test_mode` only in TransformerConfig while retaining `--test-mode`.
- Keep inference independent of TrainingConfig: correct pure inference/export startup calls and select compatibility-bootstrap services by container type. Checkpoint conversion can still restore sample metadata without creating a training config.

This targets `main` and does not depend on the distributed-config migration (#7778). No copyright-year changes, unrelated formatting cleanup, or new config-specific test file.

## Issue tracking

Related to #3554 (training-loop consolidation).

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py`
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the formatting and lint checks on my PR

No kernel implementation changes. Scoped changed-test Black/isort and undefined-name checks on changed training code pass. All-files pre-commit reports existing failures in untouched files; those changes are not included.

### Validation

Tested implementation: `bfcc1f5a57fc34b3fa55d523b3a16e8a5d299af6`.

- Two-H100 focused suite: **693 passed per rank**, versus **683 passed per rank** on frozen main `cab97ebd1f2005d7d5aa0dfe48e5f877f1e37f53`. One unchanged four-GPU CP-length test was deselected on both sides.
- GPU kernel-warmup behavioral tests: **16 passed per rank**.
- Real two-GPU GPT fresh training, checkpoint resume, and token-threshold batch-size scheduling passed on both revisions. Logged losses, learning rates, batch/sample counts, gradient norms, and evaluation metrics match exactly; timing is excluded.

The focused suite covers runtime-service ordering, native batch defaults, sample-based horizons, evaluation batching/full validation, dataloaders/cache preparation, checkpoint loading/conversion, and RL batching. Checkpoint tests used the same existing CPU-RNG fixture correction from #7778 on both revisions; that unrelated correction is not included here. The full unit suite and full model matrix were not run.

### Code review

Independent full-diff review completed and findings addressed. This PR remains a draft.

items.title: test: split GDN/GDN2 CI and quarantine flaky GDN2 parallel tests
items.author: balasaajay
items.summary: Split the combined GDN/GDN2 unit-test job into two independently scheduled buckets, with GDN running exclusively on one GB200 x4 runner and GDN2 on H100. The shared module-test bodies move into a non-collected helper.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Split the combined GDN/GDN2 unit-test job into **two independently scheduled buckets**, with GDN running exclusively on one GB200 x4 runner and GDN2 on H100.

| Bucket under `tests/unit_tests/ssm/` | Cases | Platform | GPUs per runner | Environments |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| `test_gated_delta_net.py` — all GDN module, FLA/TE parallel correctness, and remaining checks | 139 | GB200 only | 4 | dev |
| `test_gated_delta_net2.py` — GDN2 module and parallel correctness | 60 (54 selected in dev) | H100 | 8 | lts, dev |

The shared module-test bodies move into a non-collected helper. All **199 cases** retain their assertions, shapes, seeds, TP/CP layouts, fixtures, parameter IDs, and existing skip/internal markers, except for the dev-only GDN2 parallel quarantine below. The GDN padding comparison adopts the established tolerance described below; other numerical bounds are unchanged. GDN2 cases change their file path; GDN retains its original node IDs and gains `launch_on_gb200`. Its TP/CP layouts fit four workers. The original H100 run used all eight ranks, with additional ranks forming data-parallel replicas; moving GDN to four workers changes that replication. Production code is unchanged.

The H100 recipe schedules GDN2 and the GB200 recipe schedules one dedicated GDN bucket. A scoped exclusion in `find_test_cases.py` keeps GDN out of H100 catch-all buckets; existing child-bucket exclusions prevent duplicate GB200 execution. Other tests marked `launch_on_gb200` retain their existing cross-platform behavior. Both buckets use the latest tag and existing per-platform settings. The pinned legacy suite has no GDN tests.

## Measured behavior

The [original combined H100 job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38189023070/job/114618053972) took **55m38s overall**, including **52m17s in pytest**. The GDN-only portion is approximately 32–33 minutes when reconstructed from its logs.

In [run 38284519331](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38284519331), GDN on four GB200 GPUs took **37m48s overall**, including **32m41s in pytest**, with 118 passed and 21 skipped. GDN2 on H100 passed 44 cases and skipped 16 after an NCCL-timeout retry; its job took 45m30s excluding queue time. These observations do not establish a hardware speedup or a reduction in total workflow duration. Separate buckets allow scheduling independently; runner availability, compilation, and retries affect elapsed time.

## GDN padding tolerance

[Run 38305226282](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/38305226282/job/115006737425) exposed a stale tolerance in the shared `test_gpu_forward_thd_padding_correctness[1-False-1-gdn]` case: rank 0 had 19/245,760 output elements outside `atol=rtol=3e-4`, with maximum absolute difference 0.001953125. The other three ranks passed. Relevant source and the container image were unchanged from the prior passing GB200 execution; this was a numerical assertion failure, not a timeout.

Set **only this GDN padded SBHD-versus-THD comparison** to `atol=rtol=5e-3`, matching the [existing standalone padding test](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6ffe9f7326ed325ec2c6ee39558f6de0e80de643/tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_gated_delta_net_padding.py#L33). [PR #6851's validation note](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6851#issuecomment-5455230207) documents intermittent BF16 differences of 0.001953125–0.00390625 and establishes this tolerance for the distinct FLA layouts. The code comment links that precedent. GDN2 keeps its `1e-2` tolerance, and ordinary GDN THD correctness keeps `3e-4`. This aligns duplicate test policy; it does not claim a kernel arithmetic fix.

## Temporary GDN2 parallel quarantine

[Issue #7742](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/7742) tracks intermittent H100 GDN2 hangs across TP4 and CP2 layouts. The latest occurrences exhausted three launcher attempts or GitHub's one-hour job limit. One captured rank stack waits for an Inductor asynchronous backward compilation; the underlying cause remains unresolved.

Mark `test_parallel_gated_delta_net2_correctness` as `flaky_in_dev` in **both** `test_gated_delta_net2.py` and `test_gated_delta_net2_parallel.py`. This temporarily excludes all six parameterizations in each copy from dev CI; the standalone file previously excluded only its two TP4 cases. All six remain eligible in LTS. The other 54 GDN2 module cases and all 139 GDN cases retain their selection behavior. The existing empty-selection handling lets the standalone dev bucket complete successfully.

This contains the known parallel-test stalls; it does not fix the compiler hang. The issue separately records a GDN2 module THD stall, which remains enabled, and the unrelated BF16 GDN padding mismatch addressed above. Re-enable the parallel test after an identified fix passes all six layouts on eight H100 GPUs across repeated cold-cache runs without launcher retries. No compiler setting or timeout is changed here.

## Validation

- The two-bucket implementation previously passed **108 existing CPU tests** covering Testmon mandatory selection and workflow/matrix behavior. Those routing paths are unchanged by the tolerance fix and quarantine.
- Actual before/after pytest collection previously verified **199 → 139 + 60**, with exact mapped node IDs and unchanged effective parameters, fixtures, and existing skip/internal markers, except for the dev-only GDN2 parallel quarantine below. Collection used a temporary architecture-query shim with CUDA unavailable; no GPU fixtures or test bodies executed locally. The tolerance change does not alter collection.
- The padding AST audit verifies the corrected padding method exactly matches the standalone implementation. The shared file's only semantic changes for that fix are the two intended GDN padding tolerance constants. GDN2 and non-padding tolerances remain unchanged.
- Fresh before/after pytest collection for the quarantine preserves all **205 node IDs and their order** across GDN (139), GDN2 (60), and the existing standalone GDN2 parallel file (6). Dev selection excludes exactly the six parallel cases in each GDN2 file; the GDN2 module bucket selects 54 cases, and the standalone bucket selects zero with exit code 0. The LTS marker expression still selects all 205 cases; this checks selection only, not execution in an LTS container. AST checks confirm unchanged test bodies, signatures, and parameter values.
