items.title: [Fix] Adapt release checks to Vime Docker-only builds
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: On current main, checking release 0.4.0 immediately raises, before validating anything. Its stable SGLang-style image/snapshot comparisons also do not describe Vime's pinned Docker build.
items.body:
## Problem

The release checker inherited from Slime unconditionally reads `build_conda.sh`, which Vime intentionally removed. On current main, checking release 0.4.0 immediately raises `FileNotFoundError`, before validating anything. Its stable SGLang-style image/snapshot comparisons also do not describe Vime's pinned Docker build.

## Fix

- Keep package/docs/expected-version and dated Docker-version validation.
- Validate the actual immutable Docker base and dependency commit pins, including consistency between build stages.
- Check copied/applied patches per stage and coverage of the selected patch directory, including Python, Rust, router and conditional ARM SDK patches.
- Remove Conda and nonexistent stable-version assumptions from the release skill. This is a user-approved Vime-native workflow adaptation, not a Slime production-code change.

The script shrinks from 142 to 107 lines. No dependency, Dockerfile, image, package version or training changes.

## Validation

- Before: current-main checker exits 1 with `FileNotFoundError: build_conda.sh`.
- After: `check_release.py --repo . --expected-version 0.4.0` exits 0 and checks all 26 selected patch files.
- `python tests/test_docs_consistency.py`: 14 passed, including mismatched versions, mutable/invalid pins, omitted patch application, absent patch directory, orphan patches and expected-version handling.
- The existing Buildkite CPU command already runs this test file; no new test file or CI registration is needed.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

This is static release preflight, not proof of patch application, Docker compilation or GPU correctness. Those release gates remain separate.

### Release command follow-up
Keep the existing native AMD64/ARM64 `build` + `manifest` flow. The Docker README now replaces the nonexistent `just release` command with the actual two-host build and digest-based publication instructions. Both recipes were checked with `just --dry-run`; no image was built or pushed by this documentation change.

items.title: [reward] fix: handle dict-returning score functions in PrimeRewardManager
items.author: Virtuoso461
items.summary: Fixes #8216 ### What does this PR do? in had no branch for dict results, so dict-returning reward functions (mathdapo, rlla,...) hit, raised, and 's except-all fallback silently zeroed the whole batch.
items.body:
Fixes #8216

### What does this PR do?

`parallel_compute_score_async` in `PrimeRewardManager` had no branch for dict results, so dict-returning reward functions (math_dapo, rlla, ...) hit `float(result[0])`, raised `KeyError: 0`, and `verify()`'s except-all fallback silently zeroed the whole batch.

This adds the same `isinstance(result, dict) -> result["score"]` handling that `NaiveRewardManager` / `BatchRewardManager` / `DAPORewardManager` already have.

### Tests

New `tests/workers/reward_manager/test_prime_on_cpu.py` (CPU-only):
- dict result -> uses "score" key (failed before this fix)
- float / tuple (prime_math style) results unchanged
- failing task still scores 0.0

Full `tests/workers/reward_manager/` suite: 22 passed.

items.title: [Bug] PrimeRewardManager silently scores the whole batch 0.0 when the reward function returns a dict
items.author: Virtuoso461
items.summary: The KeyError is then swallowed by 's fallback, so the entire batch gets reward 0.0 with only a single print line. During RL training this silently destroys the reward signal.
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`PrimeRewardManager` (`verl/workers/reward_manager/prime.py`) crashes the result-processing loop of `parallel_compute_score_async` with `KeyError: 0` whenever the reward function returns a dict such as `{"score": 1.0, "acc": True, "pred": "42"}` — which is exactly what `math_dapo.compute_score`, `rlla.compute_score` and several custom reward functions return (`default_compute_score` passes dicts through unchanged).

The KeyError is then swallowed by `PrimeRewardManager.verify`'s `except Exception` fallback, so **the entire batch gets reward 0.0** with only a single print line (`[Error] Unexpected error during scoring. Setting all as 0. KeyError: 0`). During RL training this silently destroys the reward signal.

For comparison, `NaiveRewardManager`, `BatchRewardManager` and `DAPORewardManager` all have an `isinstance(score, dict) -> score["score"]` branch; only the prime manager is missing it.

### Reproduction

```python
from verl.workers.reward_manager.prime import run_reward_scoring

def dict_score(task, completion, reference, extra_info):
    return {"score": 1.0, "acc": True, "pred": "42"}  # same shape as math_dapo

scores = run_reward_scoring(
    dict_score,
    completions=["the answer is 42"],
    references=["42"],
    tasks=["math_dapo"],
    extra_info=[None],
    num_processes=1,
)
# raises KeyError: 0  (float- and tuple-returning fns like prime_math work fine)
```

### Expected behavior

A dict result should contribute `result["score"]`, matching the naive/batch/dapo managers.

### Environment

verl main @ 2035f58, Linux, Python 3.12, CPU-only reproduction.

items.title: Fuse the Q/K RMSNorm into TE's single-QKV RoPE path
items.author: filaretov
items.summary: This PR lets Megatron-LM's attention take the fused single-QKV RoPE path with per-head Q/K RMSNorm by passing the TE RMSNorm weights into, instead of splitting QKV and running the norm and RoPE separately. It relies on that lets that kernel apply the norm; wi…
items.body:
This PR lets Megatron-LM's attention take the fused single-QKV RoPE path with per-head Q/K RMSNorm by passing the TE RMSNorm weights into `apply_fused_qkv_rotary_pos_emb`, instead of splitting QKV and running the norm and RoPE separately.

It relies on [this TE PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3673) that lets that kernel apply the norm; with an older TE, or with L2Norm/LayerNorm QK-norms, nothing changes and the split path stays.

The tests compare fused vs split attention outputs and gradients on the same layer, and replay forward and backward bit-exactly (registered in the kernel determinism manifest).

items.title: [26.09-alpha] Fix the FC1 size of the fused shared expert with tensor parallel
items.author: michal2409
items.summary: The existing tests set the TP size to 1, so they did not find the problem. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

This is the `26.09-alpha` version of the `main` fix: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8145.
The tag `26.09-alpha.rc2` (`cde318d`) has the bug. MLPerf DeepSeek-V3 images use this tag.

Fix the FC1 `out_features` of `FusedSharedExpertMLP` for tensor parallel (TP) > 1. Then TE can fuse the shared expert MLP.

## The problem

`_make_fused_grouped_swiglu_ops` makes the TE `GroupedLinear` op for FC1 with
`out_features=fc1_weight.size(0) * tp_world_size`. But `fc1_weight` is the local TP shard
(`op.weight0 = fc1_weight`), and `te.pytorch.ops.GroupedLinear` has no TP mode. So the op must use the local size.

With TP > 1, TE does not fuse GroupedLinear + ScaledSwiGLU + GroupedLinear, because
`validate_grouped_mlp_dims` needs `fc1.out_features == 2 * fc2.in_features`.
TE then runs the unfused ops. The unfused `ScaledSwiGLU` needs one scale for each row,
but the shared expert gives one unit scale. The forward pass stops with:

```
transformer_engine/pytorch/csrc/extensions/activation.cpp:367 in function scaled_activation_compute:
Assertion failed: scales_tensor.numel() == rows. scaled activation expects one scale per input row
```

This problem does not occur with TP=1, because then the two sizes are equal.
We found it with DeepSeek-V3 on GB200: TP=2 with sequence parallel, MXFP8,
`use_grouped_gemm_for_shared_expert=True`, and `moe_shared_expert_glu_interleave_size=32`.

## Changes

- Use `out_features=fc1_weight.size(0)` for the FC1 op.
- Remove the `get_pg_size` import, because it has no use now.
- Add `test_make_fused_grouped_swiglu_ops_uses_local_shard_sizes_with_tp`.
  The existing tests set the TP size to 1, so they did not find the problem.

## Tests

- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_shared_experts.py` on `26.09-alpha` with this fix, on one GB200 node
  (4 GPUs): 23 tests pass. `test_shared_expert_forward_backward[2-4-alltoall]` needs 8 GPUs (TP2 x EP4),
  so it cannot run there.
- The new test on `26.09-alpha` without this fix fails with `assert 16 == 8`.
- `black`, `isort`, `ruff`, and `pylint` (versions from `pyproject.toml`) pass on the two changed files.
- End-to-end test with the same change on `26.09-alpha.rc2`:
  - Model: a DeepSeek-V3 proxy with 19 layers and 256 experts.
  - System: 16 GB200 nodes, TP2 PP4 VP4 EP16, MXFP8, full-iteration CUDA graph.
  - Without the fix, warmup step 0 stops with the assertion above.
  - With the fix, 10 training steps and the evaluation complete.
  - The eval loss (9.698) agrees with a run that uses the non-fused shared expert (9.696).

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none. Related: #8024 makes the fused path use the TP group of the module for its collectives.
The two changes do not overlap. A TP > 1 run needs both if `tp_group` is not the global TP group.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] Determinism test for a changed GPU kernel: not applicable, because this PR changes no kernel.
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

items.title: Quantize MLA key and value in TE's fused key/value RoPE kernel
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Fuses MXFP8 key/value quantization into Transformer Engine's MLA RoPE kernel, replacing separate split-quant kernels with a single fused kernel (~100 us vs ~136 us per layer).
items.body:
With MXFP8 attention, fused_apply_mla_rope_for_kv writes the key and value in BF16 and attention reads them back to quantize them. Add use_fused_mla_kv_rope_quant to MLATransformerConfig. With it, in training, when Transformer Engine provides fused_mla_kv_rope_mxfp8 and an MXFP8 recipe with FP8 attention is active, MLA takes the MXFP8 key and value from that kernel, quantizes the RoPE'd query as attention would (or keeps the already quantized query of the fused Q up-projection), and passes the pre-quantized query, key and value to attention through the path the fused Q up-projection uses. The backward is the key/value split RoPE backward. Output and gradients are bitwise identical to the path without the option.

items.title: Take the MTP acceptance argmax from TE's cross entropy
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Eliminates redundant argmax computation in MTP training by reusing the argmax returned from TE's parallel_cross_entropy instead of computing it separately.
items.body:
In training, MTP's acceptance-rate metric finds the argmax of each MTP head's logits with torch.argmax, or a vocab-parallel max and two all-gathers, right after the loss has scanned the same logits for their maximum. TE's parallel_cross_entropy can return that argmax (return_argmax=True).

te_parallel_cross_entropy and te_cross_entropy take return_argmax and return (loss, argmax), with None when TE lacks the option. LanguageModule.compute_language_model_loss takes return_argmax and passes it on when the selected cross entropy accepts it. process_mtp_loss asks for the argmax in training when the loss callable takes return_argmax, and _compute_mtp_acceptance_counts uses it, computing the argmax as before when it is None. The counts are unchanged: TE's index is the first maximum over the full vocabulary, as with torch.argmax.

items.title: Accumulate the embedding weight gradient into main_grad
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Optimizes VocabParallelEmbedding backward to accumulate weight gradients directly into main_grad using ZeroTensor for dummy gradients, eliminating ~1ms overhead per embedding use on large vocabularies.
items.body:
With gradient_accumulation_fusion, VocabParallelEmbedding's backward now adds its weight gradient into main_grad itself, as the linear layers do, and hands autograd a ZeroTensor, so the DDP hook still runs but adds nothing. PyTorch's embedding backward builds a dense [vocab, hidden] gradient that the hook then adds whole, about 1 ms per embedding use for a 129280 x 7168 vocabulary on VR200.

For 3073 to 8192 tokens, Triton kernels add only the rows of the tokens that occur, with the arithmetic of PyTorch's sort-based embedding backward followed by main_grad.add_, so main_grad is bit-identical. Otherwise the backward adds PyTorch's dense gradient into main_grad.

The MXFP8 LM head sets zero_tensor_dummy_wgrad on its weight: with MTP the main and MTP heads use it in one backward pass, and Transformer Engine versions that read the attribute return ZeroTensor dummy weight gradients, whose sum is free.

items.title: Load the MLA query RoPE dims contiguously in the forward kernel
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Optimizes MLA query RoPE forward kernel by replacing stride-2 loads with contiguous loads, reducing runtime from 18.7μs to 11.3μs on VR200 while maintaining bit-identical output.
items.body:
The in-place query RoPE forward (_mla_rope_fwd_inplace_kernel) read the emb_dim RoPE elements of every head with two stride-2 loads, one for the even and one for the odd elements, and with remove_interleaving it wrote them back with two stride-2 stores. It now loads them with one contiguous load and splits the even and odd elements in registers, and writes the remove_interleaving output with one contiguous store. For DeepSeek-V3's query, [4096, 1, 128, 192] in bf16, the kernel takes 11.3 us instead of 18.7 us on VR200.

With the new load the compiler paired the products into FMAs differently, and its pairing also changed with BLOCK_H. The FMAs are now formed explicitly, with the pairings the two-load kernel compiled to, so the output is bit-identical to before at every BLOCK_H the autotuner can choose and no longer depends on BLOCK_H or num_warps. The exception is fp32 q with bf16 cos/sin and inverse=True, where the previous output itself changed with BLOCK_H; it now equals the previous small-BLOCK_H output.

The query replay test now also covers remove_interleaving=True.

items.title: [megatron, training_utils] feat: budget BSHD padded tokens in dynamic batching
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: With, budgets each micro-batch by the sum of its real tokens. On the Megatron BSHD path, however, every micro-batch is stored as tokens: it is padded to its longest sequence (or to the mini-batch max with ) and then aligned for TP/CP/FP8.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

With `use_dynamic_bsz=True`, `rearrange_micro_batches` budgets each micro-batch by the sum of its real tokens. On the Megatron BSHD path (`use_remove_padding=False`), however, every micro-batch is stored as `batch_size * aligned_max_seq_len` tokens: it is padded to its longest sequence (or to the mini-batch max with `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`) and then aligned for TP/CP/FP8. A few short samples next to a long one can therefore exceed `max_token_len_per_gpu` by a large factor.

This PR adds an opt-in `megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model=bshd_padded` that budgets the padded storage the BSHD forward actually allocates. The default stays `token`, so behavior is unchanged unless the option is set.

Related: #5338 proposes length-grouped micro-batches for FSDP. This PR differs in three ways: it targets the Megatron BSHD engine, it uses the exact padded length of `preprocess_bshd_engine` (TP/CP/FP8 alignment and `forced_max_seqlen`), and it reuses the existing DP count sync and within-limit loop of `rearrange_micro_batches` (including `min_num_micro_batch` and VPP divisibility) instead of adding a separate code path. It does not include the token hard cap of #6735, and it does not touch the micro-batch construction changed by #7097.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [bshd dynamic](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+bshd+dynamic), [padded token](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+padded+token), [rearrange_micro_batches](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+rearrange_micro_batches). The closest is #5338 (see above). #7519 and #8127 (MXFP8) change THD alignment and #8208 changes BSHD router replay; they may conflict textually but not semantically.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest \
  tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing_bshd_padded_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_engine_config_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py tests/utils/test_prepare_micro_batches_with_group_size.py \
  tests/special_sanity/test_config_docs.py -q
```

Result: `85 passed, 1 skipped`. The new tests cover:

- `BSHDPadding.num_tokens` equals the tokens allocated by the real `preprocess_bshd_engine` (with stubbed Megatron parallel state) across 36 combinations of TP/CP/FP8, fixed length and sequence length.
- 33+33 tokens with CP=8 cost 96 (aligned), not 66.
- For a mixed short/long batch, the token model packs 16 samples into one micro-batch (16 x 1024 padded tokens), while the padded model isolates the long sample.
- For every micro-batch count from the minimum up to the batch size: the exact count is returned, partitions are non-empty and within budget, and every sample appears exactly once. FP8 padding also stays within budget.
- Budgeting with a fixed length (`pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`), fail-fast on an oversized single sample, rejection of `force_group_size > 1`, unchanged token-path output vs `main` for a fixed input, and CP scaling through `prepare_micro_batches`.
- A 3-rank Gloo DP group with different batch sizes and length distributions: every rank gets the same micro-batch count (the max of the local counts) and every partition stays within the padded budget. An oversized sample on one rank raises on all ranks without hanging.

`tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing.py::test_seqlen_balancing_distributed_params` needs CUDA/NCCL. It is not a CPU test and fails the same way on `main` without CUDA.

Example (64 samples: 60 of 200-2000 tokens and 4 of 14k-16k tokens; TP2/CP4; budget 65536):

| | token model | bshd_padded |
|---|---|---|
| per-micro-batch max length | 2 micro-batches, max 502272 padded tokens | 3 micro-batches, max 65472 |
| `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True` | 2 micro-batches, max 502272 | 16 micro-batches, max 62784 |

Not validated yet: GPU runs with a real Megatron BSHD forward/backward, memory and throughput.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=16384 \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model=bshd_padded \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=False
```

The reference model follows the actor setting. The critic uses `critic.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model`.

```python
from verl.utils.seqlen_balancing import BSHDPadding, rearrange_micro_batches

micro_batches, indices = rearrange_micro_batches(
    batch, max_token_len, dp_group=dp_group, bshd_padding=BSHDPadding(tp_size=2, cp_size=4)
)
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Cost contract: `len(mb) * get_bshd_padded_seq_len(raw_len, len(mb), tp, cp, fp8) <= max_token_len_per_gpu * cp_size`. Here `raw_len` is the micro-batch max, or the mini-batch max when `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`.
- `verl/utils/seqlen_balancing.py`:
  - `get_bshd_padded_seq_len` computes the TP/CP/FP8 alignment and is now shared with `preprocess_bshd_engine`.
  - `BSHDPadding` describes the padding rule.
  - A new partitioner sorts samples by length, cuts greedy contiguous runs under the budget, and splits the most expensive run until the requested count is reached.
  - `rearrange_micro_batches(..., bshd_padding=None)` uses the partitioner for the initial count and inside the existing within-limit loop (`all_reduce MIN`). DP ranks therefore agree on the count, and every partition is checked against the exact padded cost.
  - A single sample whose padded size exceeds the budget fails fast on all ranks through the existing synchronized constraint check.
- `verl/models/mcore/util.py`: `preprocess_bshd_engine` calls the shared alignment helper; behavior is unchanged.
- `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: `prepare_micro_batches` forwards `bshd_padding`.
- `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: builds `BSHDPadding` from the TP/CP world sizes, `tf_config.fp8` and the `forced_max_seqlen` of `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`, and rejects `use_remove_padding=True`.
- Config and docs: `McoreEngineConfig.dynamic_bsz_cost_model` (validated), `engine/megatron.yaml`, `ref/megatron_ref.yaml` (follows the actor), the regenerated `_generated_ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml`, and `docs/perf/perf_tuning.rst`.
- Explicitly rejected combinations: THD (`use_remove_padding=True`, which also covers dynamic CP) and `force_group_size > 1`.
- Known approximations:
  - With FP8 padding the alignment depends on the micro-batch size, so the count may exceed the minimum; partitions always stay within budget.
  - VLM BSHD inputs are aligned without FP8, so the cost is an upper bound on that path.

#### Open questions for reviewers

1. With the default `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`, every micro-batch costs the mini-batch max length, so the count can grow a lot (16 in the example). The docs recommend `False`. Should `bshd_padded` turn it off automatically instead?
2. `bshd_padded` with `use_dynamic_bsz=False` is a documented no-op. Should it raise instead?
3. The option lives in `megatron.*` because only the Megatron BSHD engine needs it, and actor training and log-prob computation share one engine config.

items.title: [trainer, cfg, doc] feat: support custom validation metrics
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: Add a config-driven hook,, that lets users add validation metrics without subclassing the trainer. Built-in validation metrics are grouped only by and use fixed statistics (mean/std/best/worst/maj @N).
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add a config-driven hook, `data.custom_validation_metrics.{path,name}`, that lets users add validation metrics without subclassing the trainer.

Built-in validation metrics are grouped only by `data_source` and use fixed statistics (mean/std/best/worst/maj @N). Metrics split by another per-sample attribute, or metrics that combine several fields, currently require overriding `_val_metrics_update` in a trainer subclass. The new hook is loaded with `load_extern_object`, like `custom_reward_function` and `data.custom_cls`. It covers both the legacy `RayPPOTrainer` and the V1 `PPOTrainer`, and it is disabled by default, so behavior is unchanged unless it is configured.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [custom validation metrics](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+custom+validation+metrics), [_val_metrics_update](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+_val_metrics_update), [process_validation_metrics](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+process_validation_metrics). No open PR adds such a hook. Related PRs with a different scope: #7240 adds a built-in pass@k metric (it touches the same files, so a textual conflict is possible), #8113 adds validation sampling profiles, and #6845 fixes a sparse-key crash.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest \
  tests/trainer/ppo/test_custom_validation_metrics_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_metric_utils_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_import_utils_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/fully_async_policy/test_async_genrm_config_on_cpu.py -q
# 64 passed

# each tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_*_on_cpu.py file, run separately
# 229 passed in total
```

For both trainers, the new `test_custom_validation_metrics_on_cpu.py` calls the real `_val_metrics_update` and checks that:

- built-in metrics are unchanged and the custom metrics are merged;
- the function receives `data_sources` as a `list` and the exact per-sample `reward_extra_infos` dict;
- a disabled hook produces only the built-in metrics;
- a non-dict return value raises `TypeError`, and a key collision with a built-in metric raises `ValueError`;
- invalid configs (missing `name`, missing file, missing attribute, non-callable object) fail at load time;
- constructing `RayPPOTrainer` or the V1 `PPOTrainer` from a composed `ppo_trainer` config with a wrong function name fails during construction.

No GPU or end-to-end run was done. The change only affects validation-metric post-processing and is a no-op when disabled.

### API and Usage Example

```python
# my_metrics.py
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np


def difficulty_metrics(data_sources: list[str], reward_extra_infos: dict[str, list]) -> dict[str, float]:
    acc_by_difficulty = defaultdict(list)
    for difficulty, acc in zip(reward_extra_infos["difficulty"], reward_extra_infos["acc"], strict=True):
        acc_by_difficulty[difficulty].append(acc)
    return {f"val-aux/difficulty/{key}/acc/mean": float(np.mean(vals)) for key, vals in acc_by_difficulty.items()}
```

```bash
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo ... \
  data.custom_validation_metrics.path=/path/to/my_metrics.py \
  data.custom_validation_metrics.name=difficulty_metrics
```

- `data_sources`: the data source of each validation sample.
- `reward_extra_infos`: the same per-sample dict passed to `process_validation_metrics` (`reward`, `acc` and any extra reward fields).
- The returned dict is merged into the validation metrics, and its keys are used verbatim.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/ppo/metric_utils.py`:
  - `load_custom_validation_metrics_fn(data_config)` returns `None` when `path` is unset, raises `ValueError` if `name` is missing, and raises `TypeError` if the object is not callable.
  - `merge_custom_validation_metrics(...)` calls the function, raises `TypeError` on a non-dict result and `ValueError` on a collision with a built-in key.
- `RayPPOTrainer` and the V1 `PPOTrainer` load the function in `__init__`, so a wrong path or name fails at startup instead of after the first validation rollout. The result is merged at the end of `_val_metrics_update`, which also covers the legacy `_merge_validation_results` path.
- `OneStepOffRayTrainer` and `FullyAsyncRollouter` override `__init__` without calling `RayPPOTrainer.__init__` but still use the inherited `_validate`. Each gets one line that loads the function the same way, so validation keeps working and the option is honored.
- `verl/trainer/config/data/legacy_data.yaml` and the regenerated `_generated_*.yaml`: new `custom_validation_metrics: {path: null, name: null}` next to `custom_cls`.
- `docs/examples/config.rst`: new "Customized Validation Metrics" section.

#### Open questions for reviewers

- Should the function also receive `sample_uids` and `sample_turns` (e.g. for per-prompt metrics such as pass@k)? The current `fn(data_sources=..., reward_extra_infos=...)` signature matches an existing user function; more inputs could be added later as optional keyword arguments.
- Should custom keys be namespaced automatically (e.g. a `val-custom/` prefix) instead of being used verbatim with only a collision check?
- Is `data.*` the right place, or would `trainer.*` be preferred?

items.title: [megatron, training_utils] feat: budget BSHD padded tokens in dynamic batching
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: With, budgets each micro-batch by the sum of its real tokens. On the Megatron BSHD path, however, every micro-batch is stored as tokens: it is padded to its longest sequence (or to the mini-batch max with ) and then aligned for TP/CP/FP8.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

With `use_dynamic_bsz=True`, `rearrange_micro_batches` budgets each micro-batch by the sum of its real tokens. On the Megatron BSHD path (`use_remove_padding=False`), however, every micro-batch is stored as `batch_size * aligned_max_seq_len` tokens: it is padded to its longest sequence (or to the mini-batch max with `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`) and then aligned for TP/CP/FP8. A few short samples next to a long one can therefore exceed `max_token_len_per_gpu` by a large factor.

This PR adds an opt-in `megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model=bshd_padded` that budgets the padded storage the BSHD forward actually allocates. The default stays `token`, so behavior is unchanged unless the option is set.

Related: #5338 proposes length-grouped micro-batches for FSDP. This PR differs in three ways: it targets the Megatron BSHD engine, it uses the exact padded length of `preprocess_bshd_engine` (TP/CP/FP8 alignment and `forced_max_seqlen`), and it reuses the existing DP count sync and within-limit loop of `rearrange_micro_batches` (including `min_num_micro_batch` and VPP divisibility) instead of adding a separate code path. It does not include the token hard cap of #6735, and it does not touch the micro-batch construction changed by #7097.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [bshd dynamic](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+bshd+dynamic), [padded token](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+padded+token), [rearrange_micro_batches](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+rearrange_micro_batches). The closest is #5338 (see above). #7519 and #8127 (MXFP8) change THD alignment and #8208 changes BSHD router replay; they may conflict textually but not semantically.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest \
  tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing_bshd_padded_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_engine_config_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py tests/utils/test_prepare_micro_batches_with_group_size.py \
  tests/special_sanity/test_config_docs.py -q
```

Result: `85 passed, 1 skipped`. The new tests cover:

- `BSHDPadding.num_tokens` equals the tokens allocated by the real `preprocess_bshd_engine` (with stubbed Megatron parallel state) across 36 combinations of TP/CP/FP8, fixed length and sequence length.
- 33+33 tokens with CP=8 cost 96 (aligned), not 66.
- For a mixed short/long batch, the token model packs 16 samples into one micro-batch (16 x 1024 padded tokens), while the padded model isolates the long sample.
- For every micro-batch count from the minimum up to the batch size: the exact count is returned, partitions are non-empty and within budget, and every sample appears exactly once. FP8 padding also stays within budget.
- Budgeting with a fixed length (`pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`), fail-fast on an oversized single sample, rejection of `force_group_size > 1`, unchanged token-path output vs `main` for a fixed input, and CP scaling through `prepare_micro_batches`.
- A 3-rank Gloo DP group with different batch sizes and length distributions: every rank gets the same micro-batch count (the max of the local counts) and every partition stays within the padded budget. An oversized sample on one rank raises on all ranks without hanging.

`tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing.py::test_seqlen_balancing_distributed_params` needs CUDA/NCCL. It is not a CPU test and fails the same way on `main` without CUDA.

Example (64 samples: 60 of 200-2000 tokens and 4 of 14k-16k tokens; TP2/CP4; budget 65536):

| | token model | bshd_padded |
|---|---|---|
| per-micro-batch max length | 2 micro-batches, max 502272 padded tokens | 3 micro-batches, max 65472 |
| `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True` | 2 micro-batches, max 502272 | 16 micro-batches, max 62784 |

Not validated yet: GPU runs with a real Megatron BSHD forward/backward, memory and throughput.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=16384 \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model=bshd_padded \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=False
```

The reference model follows the actor setting. The critic uses `critic.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model`.

```python
from verl.utils.seqlen_balancing import BSHDPadding, rearrange_micro_batches

micro_batches, indices = rearrange_micro_batches(
    batch, max_token_len, dp_group=dp_group, bshd_padding=BSHDPadding(tp_size=2, cp_size=4)
)
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Cost contract: `len(mb) * get_bshd_padded_seq_len(raw_len, len(mb), tp, cp, fp8) <= max_token_len_per_gpu * cp_size`. Here `raw_len` is the micro-batch max, or the mini-batch max when `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`.
- `verl/utils/seqlen_balancing.py`:
  - `get_bshd_padded_seq_len` computes the TP/CP/FP8 alignment and is now shared with `preprocess_bshd_engine`.
  - `BSHDPadding` describes the padding rule.
  - A new partitioner sorts samples by length, cuts greedy contiguous runs under the budget, and splits the most expensive run until the requested count is reached.
  - `rearrange_micro_batches(..., bshd_padding=None)` uses the partitioner for the initial count and inside the existing within-limit loop (`all_reduce MIN`). DP ranks therefore agree on the count, and every partition is checked against the exact padded cost.
  - A single sample whose padded size exceeds the budget fails fast on all ranks through the existing synchronized constraint check.
- `verl/models/mcore/util.py`: `preprocess_bshd_engine` calls the shared alignment helper; behavior is unchanged.
- `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: `prepare_micro_batches` forwards `bshd_padding`.
- `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: builds `BSHDPadding` from the TP/CP world sizes, `tf_config.fp8` and the `forced_max_seqlen` of `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`, and rejects `use_remove_padding=True`.
- Config and docs: `McoreEngineConfig.dynamic_bsz_cost_model` (validated), `engine/megatron.yaml`, `ref/megatron_ref.yaml` (follows the actor), the regenerated `_generated_ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml`, and `docs/perf/perf_tuning.rst`.
- Explicitly rejected combinations: THD (`use_remove_padding=True`, which also covers dynamic CP) and `force_group_size > 1`.
- Known approximations:
  - With FP8 padding the alignment depends on the micro-batch size, so the count may exceed the minimum; partitions always stay within budget.
  - VLM BSHD inputs are aligned without FP8, so the cost is an upper bound on that path.

#### Open questions for reviewers

1. With the default `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`, every micro-batch costs the mini-batch max length, so the count can grow a lot (16 in the example). The docs recommend `False`. Should `bshd_padded` turn it off automatically instead?
2. `bshd_padded` with `use_dynamic_bsz=False` is a documented no-op. Should it raise instead?
3. The option lives in `megatron.*` because only the Megatron BSHD engine needs it, and actor training and log-prob computation share one engine config.

items.title: MInf: Let the payload stager defer staging
items.author: tdene
items.summary: Right now, the engine loop has to wait for inside its bookkeeping. If this wait is long, it blocks the engine loop, and the GPU goes idle. [Discussion: Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository.]
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Right now, the engine loop has to wait for `RequestPayloadStager.stage()` inside its bookkeeping. If this wait is long, it blocks the engine loop, and the GPU goes idle.

This matters for NeMo RL's token-level rollout checkpointing. While a checkpoint is being taken, the framework forbids the stager from writing finished requests into its store: the checkpoint records which requests were still in flight, and a terminal write in the meantime would invalidate that record. This blocks the entire engine loop because `RequestPayloadStager.stage()` stops responding.

This PR lets `stage()` return `RequestPayloadStageDeferred` instead. The engine then holds the finished request's reply, neither indexing nor sending it, and offers it to the stager again on every bookkeeping pass; `flush_deferred_stages()` lets the stager trigger a retry from any thread as soon as it may write again. `reset()` refuses while deferred replies are outstanding.

Failed replies are unaffected.

items.title: MInf: Add support for token-level snapshotting
items.author: tdene
items.summary: Gives MInf the ability to snapshot the engine's live state at a token-level granularity, and also to load such a snapshot on a restart. This feature is used for resiliency with RL setups, so that if inference has to be interrupted while there are still live re…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Gives MInf the ability to snapshot the engine's live state at a token-level granularity, and also to load such a snapshot on a restart.

This feature is used for resiliency with RL setups, so that if inference has to be interrupted while there are still live requests in the engine, the engine state can be saved and restored.

For the snapshot side, `DynamicInferenceEngine.snapshot_live_requests()` returns a `LiveRequestSnapshot` dataclass. This can be called by any user of MInf.

For the resume side, the `RequestPromptPreparer` can now provide an encoded `ResumedGeneration`, which the engine reads and honors.

As a side-effect, part of the engine logic had to be refactored to avoid code duplication; `_admit_request` now handles both new requests and resumed requests.

items.title: [trainer, cfg] feat: make old-log-prob entropy diagnostics optional
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: Make the entropy computed during old-log-prob recomputation optional. The PPO and V1 trainers always request when recomputing old log-probs, only to log.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Make the entropy computed during old-log-prob recomputation optional.

The PPO (`RayPPOTrainer`) and V1 trainers always request `calculate_entropy=True` when recomputing old log-probs, only to log `actor/entropy`. The actor update does not use this entropy; it requests its own according to `calculate_entropy` / `entropy_coeff`. Computing it adds an entropy pass over the full vocabulary to every recomputation (for example, the non-fused Megatron path clones the logits for it).

This PR adds `actor_rollout_ref.actor.calculate_old_log_prob_entropy`, which defaults to `true`, so behavior is unchanged by default. When it is `false`, both trainers skip entropy in this stage and omit `actor/entropy` from it. Actor-update entropy and entropy regularization are unaffected, and bypass mode still skips recomputation entirely. This PR does not measure memory or throughput savings.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [old_log_prob entropy](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+old_log_prob+entropy), [calculate_entropy old log prob](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+calculate_entropy+old+log+prob), [optional entropy](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+optional+entropy). No open PR makes this entropy optional. #6519 skips entropy/KL gradients in the actor update when their coefficients are 0, and #5838 skips zero-advantage responses in training. Both touch nearby code with a different scope, so this is not a duplicate.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/test_old_log_prob_entropy_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py -q
```

- With this PR: `28 passed`.
- The same test files against current `main`: `5 failed, 23 passed`.

The tests call the real trainer methods, NestedTensor/padding conversion, entropy aggregation and the log-prob debug metric. Worker and TransferQueue calls use doubles. Coverage includes the default, enabled and disabled settings, zero and non-zero entropy coefficients, unequal response lengths, internal masks, router replay and sum-pi-squared fields, and V1 bypass. They also check that the actor update still requests entropy according to its own config when this stage skips it. A full training loop has not been run.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.actor.calculate_old_log_prob_entropy=false
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/config/actor/actor.yaml`, `verl/workers/config/actor.py` and the generated trainer configs: new field `calculate_old_log_prob_entropy: true`.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py` and `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`: pass the flag as `calculate_entropy`, and only fetch, store and aggregate entropy when it is set.
- `docs/examples/config.rst`: documents the option.

items.title: [trainer] fix: preserve underscored UIDs in V1 replay buffer
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: Keep prompt groups isolated in the V1 when a UID contains underscores. Trajectory keys are, but the replay buffer recovers the UID with. [Discussion: <!-- This is an auto-generated comment: summarize by coderabbit.ai --> <!-- This is an auto-generate]
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Keep prompt groups isolated in the V1 `ReplayBuffer` when a UID contains underscores.

Trajectory keys are `{uid}_{session_id}_{index}`, but the replay buffer recovers the UID with `key.split("_")[0]`. A UID such as `math_00017` maps to `math`. Its trajectories are then missed by sampling (sync mode raises "selected terminal groups with no materializable trajectories"), by DAPO reward classification, by failed-group detection and by clearing. UIDs that share a prefix can also be mixed or cleared together. The default trainer generates UUID4 UIDs (hyphens only), so default runs are not affected. The problem appears with custom or dataset-provided UIDs.

This PR parses the UID from the fixed suffixes (`key.rsplit("_", 2)[0]`) everywhere the buffer maps trajectory keys to groups.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [replay buffer uid](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+replay+buffer+uid), [replay_buffer underscore](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+replay_buffer+underscore). I also checked every open PR that touches `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/replay_buffer.py`:
  - #8203 (draft, BREAKING) replaces `replay_buffer.py` with a `StreamingDataloader` actor and already parses keys with `rsplit("_", 2)` there. This PR is a minimal fix for the current `ReplayBuffer` on `main`. If #8203 lands first, this PR can be closed.
  - #6874 adds a session marker but keeps the same left split, so its parser will need to be reconciled whichever lands first.
  - #6868 and #7415 change dispatch and storage backends, not key parsing.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13, TransferQueue 0.1.11) with a local Ray cluster:

```bash
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_replay_buffer_on_cpu.py -q
```

- With this PR: `54 passed`.
- The same test file against current `main`: `8 failed, 46 passed`.

The tests use real Ray and TransferQueue. They cover clearing groups with shared prefixes, sampling and DAPO reward classification for underscored UIDs, multiple trajectory indices, sync and async materialization, and failed-group detection.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. The key format `{uid}_{session_id}_{index}` is unchanged. The docstring now states that UIDs may contain underscores.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/replay_buffer.py`: new `_trajectory_uid()` helper replaces the seven `key.split("_")[0]` call sites.
- `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_replay_buffer_on_cpu.py`: regressions with underscored and shared-prefix UIDs.

items.title: [algo] fix: pad nested importance weights for distillation PG
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: Fix policy-gradient distillation when rollout importance weights arrive as a NestedTensor. Before calling the PPO policy loss, converts,, advantages and from NestedTensor to padded dense tensors, but passes through unchanged.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix policy-gradient distillation when rollout importance weights arrive as a NestedTensor.

Before calling the PPO policy loss, `distillation_loss()` converts `log_prob`, `old_log_prob`, advantages and `response_mask` from NestedTensor to padded dense tensors, but passes `rollout_is_weights` through unchanged. On the no-padding path the weights stay jagged and the policy loss fails. In the forward pass it raises `ValueError: NestedTensor where_self(...): expected condition to be a jagged layout NestedTensor`, and in backward it raises `NotImplementedError: aten._nested_sum_backward.default`.

This PR pads nested weights with `0.0` before the policy loss, matching the other dense inputs. Padded positions are already excluded by `response_mask`. Dense or absent weights are unchanged.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [distillation nested](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+distillation+nested), [distillation importance weights](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+distillation+importance+weights). I also checked every open PR that touches `verl/trainer/distillation/losses.py`. #8061 passes `forced_max_seqlen`, #7887 handles empty top-k micro-batches, and #6920, #7096, #7855 and others add losses or metrics. None converts `rollout_is_weights`, so this is not a duplicate.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/workers/test_distillation_policy_gradient_on_cpu.py -q
```

- With this PR: `12 passed`.
- The same test file against current `main`: `4 failed, 8 passed`, with the two errors above.

The tests call the real `distillation_loss()`, padding conversion and PPO policy loss. They compare loss values and student gradients against independent dense inputs, and confirm that the teacher receives no gradient. Coverage includes unequal response lengths, non-unit and zero weights, internal masks, dense and absent weights, and both `token-mean` and `seq-mean-token-mean`.

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/distillation/losses.py`: two lines that pad nested `rollout_is_weights` before `policy_loss_fn`.
- `tests/workers/test_distillation_policy_gradient_on_cpu.py`: numerical and gradient regressions.

items.title: [megatron] fix: allow BSHD with inactive MoE router losses
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: Allow the Megatron BSHD path with when no MoE router loss is active. is auto-enabled by Megatron-Bridge at CP>1. [Discussion: <!-- This is an auto-generated comment: summarize by coderabbit.ai --> <!-- This is an auto-generate]
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Allow the Megatron BSHD path (`use_remove_padding=False`) with `calculate_per_token_loss=True` when no MoE router loss is active.

`calculate_per_token_loss=True` is auto-enabled by Megatron-Bridge at CP>1. On the BSHD path the engine currently raises for every model, because verl does not pass a padding mask to the MoE router, so the aux/z loss would be normalized by the padding-inclusive `B*S` while gradients are divided by real tokens. That mismatch only matters when an aux or z loss actually contributes. Dense models, and MoE configs with zero aux coefficients and z-loss disabled, are rejected even though they are unaffected.

This PR moves the check into `validate_bshd_moe_router_loss_compatibility()`. It raises only when an aux routing type (`aux_loss`, `seq_aux_loss`, `global_aux_loss`) has a positive coefficient (scalar or per-type list) or `moe_z_loss_coeff > 0`. Per-token normalization and the rejection of active aux/z losses are unchanged.

No API change. Configs that were already supported behave the same. BSHD with per-token loss is now accepted when MoE aux/z losses are inactive.

items.title: [megatron] fix: align BSHD router replay with model token order
items.author: yellowbee686
items.summary: Fix router replay for the V1 Megatron engine when (BSHD layout). Router replay currently packs routes and the R3 replay mask with the THD helpers: samples are concatenated without per-sample padding.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix router replay for the V1 Megatron engine when `use_remove_padding=False` (BSHD layout).

Router replay currently packs routes and the R3 replay mask with the THD helpers: samples are concatenated without per-sample padding. A BSHD forward instead pads every sample to the micro-batch length (TP/CP/FP8 alignment and `forced_max_seqlen`), and after the sequence-parallel scatter the routers see tokens in sequence-major `[S, B]` order. For micro-batches with more than one sample, R2 records are therefore restored to the wrong positions, and R3 replay applies routes to the wrong tokens.

This PR builds the route and mask tensors with `preprocess_bshd_engine` using the model's padding target, flattens them sequence-major before the scatter, and reverses that order when restoring R2 records. The default THD layout, dynamic CP, contiguous CP and the legacy dense packed path are unchanged. Stored routes stay `int16`, and collectives keep using the existing bit-identical `uint8` view. BSHD aux/z-loss restrictions and dynamic-CP support are out of scope.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [router replay bshd](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+router+replay+bshd), [router replay token order](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+router+replay+token+order). I also checked every open PR that touches `verl/utils/megatron/router_replay_utils.py`. #7524 rebalances the expert assignment of R2 padding rows, and the MXFP8/NVFP4/Kimi/LoRA PRs (#7519, #7971, #8127–#8132, #7866, #7483) edit the file for other features. None changes the BSHD token order, so this is not a duplicate.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/utils/megatron/test_bshd_router_replay_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/megatron/test_router_replay_model_walk_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/engine/megatron/test_router_replay_utils_on_cpu.py -q
```

- With this PR: `13 passed, 1 skipped`.
- The new `test_bshd_router_replay_on_cpu.py` against current `main`: `9 failed, 1 passed`.

The new tests cover the BSHD layout helpers, R2 recording, R3 replay targets and masks, and THD regressions, including four-process Gloo TP/CP collectives. Megatron import surfaces and parallel-state queries are stubbed. A GPU model forward, NCCL, optimizer updates and rollout-captured R3 routes have not been run yet.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. BSHD router replay is enabled with the existing settings plus `actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_remove_padding=False`. The layout notes are added to `examples/router_replay/README.md`.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/megatron/router_replay_utils.py`: `merge_router_topk_indices()` and `set_router_replay_data()` take keyword-only `data_format` and `forced_max_seqlen` arguments. The BSHD branch uses `preprocess_bshd_engine` / `postprocess_bshd_engine` plus a sequence-major flatten/unflatten pair. The THD branch is unchanged.
- `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: computes `data_format` before router replay and passes it, together with `forced_max_seqlen`, to both calls.
- `examples/router_replay/README.md`: documents the BSHD layout and test scope.

items.body:
…rs (#8020)

With logprobs_mode=processed_logprobs (default) the rollout engine returns log-probs renormalized over the top_p/top_k/min_p truncated support, while the actor's old_log_probs are full-vocabulary. The correction ratio old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob therefore carries the truncated mass on every token: sequence-level IS weights collapse below lower bounds and k1 rejection bounds (0.999_1.001, 0.5_2.0) reject every sequence, so the Geo-RS / Seq-MIS presets silently produce zero gradient (issue #8020).

- validate_config now raises an actionable error when rollout_is/rollout_rs correction is combined with a truncated sampler and processed log-probs.
- compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask warns (once per process) when a batch ends up fully rejected or fully zero-weighted.
- compute_is_metrics no longer raises ZeroDivisionError on the ESS metric when IcePop zeroes every weight; it reports ESS 0.0 instead.

items.title: [algo, fsdp, perf] refactor: share support normalization in score centering
items.author: tongyx361
items.summary: When FSDP score centering processes a recorded sampler head, the head-scoring helper and sampled-token CE currently normalize the same vocabulary separately. This follow-up shares head/sample normalization and computes complete-support loss scores directly in …
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When FSDP score centering processes a recorded sampler head, the head-scoring helper and sampled-token CE currently normalize the same vocabulary separately. This follow-up shares head/sample normalization and computes complete-support loss scores directly in the verified support. Unknown/incomplete rows keep the existing recorded-top-k plus full-vocabulary trainer-tail approximation, including its epsilon regularization. Sampling and recording parameters do not change.

Dependency: the automatic alignment and coverage-receipt changes in #8196. This draft is stacked on codex/sc-auto-support-8196, a mirror of the reviewed #8196 feature head; its diff contains only the two performance commits. It will be retargeted/rebased onto main after #8196 merges. This adds a separate full-local-vocabulary FSDP path. #8199 remains the Megatron/TP extension and can continue to use the unchanged general correction-helper APIs. #8020 proposes broader support replay for IS/RS and is outside this optimization.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Checked #8020 and open references to #8010/#8020; [open centering PR search](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+centering) found #8196 and #8199. Neither implements shared FSDP head/sample normalization. This PR depends on #8196 and does not reimplement its feature scope.
- [x] Title uses the repository's module/type format.

### Test

Commands run with the existing uv environment from the performance checkout:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 uv run --active --no-sync pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_shared_scores_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_score_centering_shared_engine_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_score_centering_wiring_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_on_cpu.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run --active --no-sync pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_shared_scores_on_gpu.py
uv run --active --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```

Results: **89 CPU tests passed, 30 CUDA/Triton tests passed, all 14 pre-commit hooks passed**. CUDA tests cover no IS/TIS/IcePop, FP32/BF16, mixed alignment, noncontiguous logits/receipts, sampled/head collisions, entropy/KL consumers and unchanged input logits. Six CPU and six CUDA cases additionally check low-entropy supports with large common logit offsets against an independent FP64 expected-score objective. An independent scorer check passed 18 additional CUDA cases, with max FP32 gradient error 2.98e-8 and no BF16 error on those fixtures.

Additional bounded integration artifacts include 20 tiny-Qwen2 CUDA gates (8 actual model parameter-gradient comparisons, dense/packed B2 with lengths [8,5]) and 4 SP2 gates with actual NCCL/Ulysses gather, 13-to-14 padding and unpadding. These use the actual engine/loss hooks but do not exercise FSDP wrapping or distributed attention. SP2 candidate versus matched legacy-SP parameter-gradient relative L2 was 1.29e-7–1.46e-7 for FP32 and 0.350%–0.373% for BF16. BF16 is not bitwise equivalent because sparse contributions are accumulated in FP32 before a single cast.

Matched loss-pipeline benchmark: H100 80GB, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, BF16, N=4096, V=151936, K=128, 4 warm-ups and 6 ABBA rounds (12 observations per route). The baseline is the #8196 automatic correction helper plus sampled CE; both routes retain identical mass/alignment/tail diagnostics.

| Verified aligned rows | Baseline median ms | Shared median ms | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% | 21.100 | 8.908 | 57.8% |
| 50% | 21.103 | 8.705 | 58.7% |
| 100% | 21.103 | 8.421 | 60.1% |

Peak allocated memory, including identical inputs: 6,236,165,120 -> 3,749,990,400 bytes (5.808 -> 3.492 GiB). Max fixture loss difference 4.47e-8, BF16 logits-gradient max difference 7.63e-6, mass-metric max difference 4.17e-7. The repository benchmark script reproduces the fixture and records source SHA, environment and measurement scope.

This measures synthetic-logits score/loss forward and dense-gradient backward. Model computation, optimizer, rollout, reward, Ray and communication are excluded. A separate public pretrained Qwen3-0.6B matched generated-token update fixture (B1, prompt106+response32, BF16, TIS clamp2, SGD) measured 80.979 -> 80.454 ms with overlapping ranges and unchanged peak memory; that fixture does not establish an actor speedup. Its shared parameter gradients matched an independent FP32 score-domain oracle, while the legacy route differed by 1.37% relative L2. A second bounded B1 fixture uses prompt4064+response32, top-k32/top-p1 and an actual processed support of 32–36 tokens. It measured **126.796 -> 114.068 ms (-10.0%)** over four observations per route, with input/initial-weight-inclusive peak memory **16,957,184,000 -> 14,469,977,088 bytes (-2.316 GiB)**. Loss absolute difference was 1.99e-8 and parameter gradients were finite, but candidate-versus-legacy BF16 parameter-gradient relative L2 was **4.49%** on this very low-entropy fixture. This is one controlled unsharded update fixture, not a distributed actor or an RL-step benchmark.

A separate FP64 score-domain diagnostic on the same fixture construction explains the numerical sensitivity: shared response-logits gradients differed by 0.0263% relative L2 (max absolute 1.49e-8), versus 0.301% for the legacy path. BF16 model-parameter gradients still differed by 3.55% relative L2 from that score reference, compared with 4.69% for legacy; no exact model-gradient equivalence is claimed. The original FP32 absolute-logsumexp oracle was itself sensitive to cancellation at near-zero log-probs and is retained in the artifacts rather than treated as ground truth. A singleton-support variant correctly produces zero shared/oracle gradients and is not counted as an effective model update.

These results do not establish training quality, distributed FSDP acceptance or end-to-end RL performance.

### API and Usage Example

No new user configuration is required. SC still tries verified support alignment first and otherwise uses the configured head/trainer approximation. The FSDP engine supplies its already rolled/SP-sliced sampled labels to the SC logits processor. Callers without sampled labels retain the old correction-helper route, and hooks without shared sampled scores retain the existing CE fallback.

Manual benchmark (run on an idle CUDA device):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run --active --no-sync python benchmarks/benchmark_score_centering.py --output score_centering_benchmark.json
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Share one chunked full-vocabulary forward normalizer across head/sample scoring and detached head-mass diagnostics. Complete rows normalize their loss directly over finite recorded support.
- Avoid full-vocabulary softmax recomputation in backward for complete rows; fallback rows reuse the shared normalizer. CUDA row selection has no GPU-to-host synchronization.
- Accumulate sparse head/sample collisions in FP32 before casting; retain dense vocabulary-sized logits gradients. Keep logits unchanged for entropy/KL and other graph consumers.
- Pass already local prediction labels through FSDP; gather/unpad outputs once in the packed route and preserve the existing dense route.

The full-vocabulary mass diagnostic still requires O(NV) forward work for every row. This change does not turn the model LM head or dense logits-gradient allocation into K-only work. The new helper requires a materialized full local vocabulary and must not be applied directly to an unmaterialized TP shard.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the contribution guide and repository template.
- [x] Run all pre-commit hooks and relevant CPU/CUDA tests.
- [x] Update SC cost documentation and add a manual benchmark.
- [x] New CPU/GPU regression filenames are discovered by the existing unit-test workflows.
- [x] The submitting human confirmed reviewing every changed line and independently running relevant tests.
- [x] Published and read back the exact final head; title, pre-commit, type/docstring coverage, secrets scan, CodeRabbit and CLA checks passed.
- [ ] CPU/GPU main-base workflows are not automatically triggered on this stacked base. Rebase/retarget after #8196 merges, then verify those checks on the resulting head.

AI assistance: implementation, review drafts and local validation were prepared with OpenAI Codex. The human maintainer confirmed reviewing every changed line and independently running relevant tests before publication.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: use current compressed-tensors API for QAT export
items.author: cyanseek
items.summary: FSDP NVFP4 QAT weight export fails with the compressed-tensors versions in the current lockfile (0.17 and 0.18). imports the removed module and calls the removed method when the engine exports rollout weights.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

FSDP NVFP4 QAT weight export fails with the compressed-tensors versions in the current lockfile (0.17 and 0.18). `QATQuantizer` imports the removed `compressors.quantized_compressors.fp4_quantized` module and calls the removed `compress_weight` method when the engine exports rollout weights.

Import the compressor from its public namespace and pass the existing weight, block scale, and global scale through `compress(state_dict, QuantizationScheme)`. Preserve the streamed output names, scale fusion, passthrough weights, and W4A4 input scales.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Checked [NVFP4 compressor PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+NVFP4+compressor) and [QAT compressed-tensors PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+QAT+compressed-tensors). No matching fix found. Closed #6815 concerned an older installation stack; this change targets the current locked dependencies. #6992 concerns W4A8 simulation and #7895 concerns Megatron MXFP4.
- [x] Title follows the module/type convention.

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_qat_quantizer.py -q
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```

On RTX 5090 with PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, the new tests pass with compressed-tensors 0.17.0 and 0.18.0: **12 passed per version**. Unmodified main fails to import the quantizer with both versions.

The regression covers FP32/FP16/BF16 weights, W4A16/W4A4, CPU/GPU destinations, multiple decoder layers, QKV/GateUp scale fusion, zero blocks, excluded weights, exact source preservation, and actual packed-weight decompression against an independent E2M1 rounding reference.

Additional local integration checks use a real two-rank FSDP2 QAT engine and a locally constructed tiny Qwen2. Both dependency versions pass with CPU offload on/off: two training steps, export after each step, all seven projections packed and decompressed, source parameters preserved exactly, and exported weights updated after the next optimizer step. These validate the training/export path; they do not run a vLLM generation workload.

### API and Usage Example

No configuration change. Existing FSDP NVFP4 QAT rollout-weight export uses the current compressor API.

### Checklist Before Submitting

items.title: [Dev] Add identity hyper-connections (iHC)
items.author: jingqiny-99
items.summary: Adds an identity hyper-connections (iHC) variant of mHC behind a new flag, (CLI:; requires ). With the flag on, fixes the residual mixing matrix to the identity instead of the Sinkhorn-projected manifold matrix: - only produces and ( outputs instead of ); and…
items.body:
## Summary

Adds an identity hyper-connections (iHC) variant of mHC behind a new `TransformerConfig` flag, `enable_identity_hyper_connections` (CLI: `--enable-identity-hyper-connections`; requires `--enable-hyper-connections`).

With the flag on, `HyperConnectionModule` fixes the residual mixing matrix `H_res` to the `n x n` identity instead of the Sinkhorn-projected manifold matrix:

- `mapping_proj` only produces `H_pre` and `H_post` (`2n` outputs instead of `n^2 + 2n`); `alpha_res` and the `H_res` part of `bias` are not created.
- The `H_res` projection and the Sinkhorn-Knopp step are skipped entirely; `compute_mappings` materializes a per-token identity `[s, b, n, n]` in the activation dtype.
- The downstream `H_res` / `H_post` / BDA path (`fused_h_res_h_post_bda`, native and fused `h_post_bda` kernels, mHC recompute, CUDA graph plumbing) is unchanged and consumes the identity as-is. Kernel-level shortcuts for the identity case are left for a follow-up.
- With `use_fused_mhc=True`, aggregate and `h_post_bda` stay fused; the projection takes the native path because the fused `proj_rms_compute_h` kernel assumes the mHC output layout.
- mHC and iHC checkpoints are not interchangeable (parameter shapes differ).

The resulting propagation is `x_{l+1} = x_l + H_post^T @ F(H_pre @ x_l)`.

One change outside the module: `TransformerLayerNode.detach` in the fine-grained EP-overlap schedule now records a gradient bridge only for tensors that require grad. It used to hand every detached tensor to `run_backward`, which raises for a tensor without `grad_fn`; the constant iHC `h_res` is exactly that, so `overlap_moe_expert_parallel_comm` would have crashed. For mHC every bridged tensor requires grad, so behaviour there is unchanged (verified below).

## Test plan

New tests:
- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_identity_hyper_connection.py`: config validation, parameter layout (`2n` rows, no `alpha_res`), identity `h_res` in fp32 / bf16, empty-sequence forward/backward, output equals `x_l + H_post^T (F + bias)` stream by stream, iHC matches mHC whose Sinkhorn output is forced to the identity (outputs and gradients), `_forward_with_checkpoint` matches `_forward_normal`, `use_fused_mhc=True` path, `HyperConnectionTransformerLayer` forward/backward with and without `recompute_modules=[mhc]`.
- `tests/unit_tests/a2a_overlap/test_mhc_schedule.py::test_identity_hyper_connections_schedule_matches_eager` (EP=4 alltoall overlap schedule vs eager, with and without mHC recompute), placed last in its class.
- `tests/unit_tests/models/test_hybrid_moe_model.py`: the new field is registered in `GOLDEN_CONFIG`.

Why the iHC tests run under `torch.compiler.set_stance("force_eager")`: the constant `h_res` would otherwise add `requires_grad=False` guard variants to the `torch.compile`'d mHC kernels that every mHC test in the bucket shares (`native_h_post_bda`, `native_h_aggregate`, ...). Several existing eager-vs-schedule / eager-vs-graph comparisons (`test_full_recompute_carries_the_mhc_bridge_gradient`, `test_gpu_mhc_split_replay_matches_eager`) are sensitive to the compile-cache history: they fail when the default recompile limit of 8 is crossed, or a cold compile happens, between their two arms. On an 8x H100 node, clean `dev` fails `test_gpu_mhc_split_replay_matches_eager[True-False-False]` in a process that only runs `test_hyper_connection_recompute.py` before it, so this is pre-existing order sensitivity rather than an iHC regression; the eager stance keeps the cache history seen by those tests identical to `dev`. (An earlier revision of this PR reset the dynamo caches in the iHC teardowns instead; that changed the history and made CI fail the graph-split test, which is how this was found.)

Run on EOS, 8x H100, CI image `mcore-ci-dev`, `run_ci_test.sh --platform h100 --environment dev` (same markers as `cicd-unit-tests-latest`):
- `transformer/test_identity_hyper_connection.py`: 12 passed
- `transformer/test_hyper_connection_recompute.py`: 51 passed
- `a2a_overlap/test_mhc_schedule.py`: 25 passed (clean `dev` baseline on the same node: 23 passed)
- `transformer/test_hyper_connection_recompute.py` + `test_identity_hyper_connection.py` + `test_transformer_layer.py` in one pytest process: 123 passed

`black` / `isort` / `ruff` / `pylint` / copyright check pass against `dev`.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add three identity columns to both training rollout JSONL (from _log_rollout_data) and validation JSONL (from _validate) so offline analysis can:
  * group the n rollouts of each prompt by `uid`, and
  * left-join back to the source parquet by `(data_source, index)`.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: ...
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.
  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

### Test

- `tests/trainer/ppo/test_dump_join_keys_on_cpu.py`: 11 cases covering helper happy path, missing columns, empty batch, length mismatch, mixed input types (ndarray/list), native dtype preservation, uid stringification, collision warning, no-collision merge.
- `python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/test_dump_join_keys_on_cpu.py` passes (11 passed).
- `pre-commit run --files verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_dump_join_keys_on_cpu.py` passes (ruff, mypy, license, docstring, naming).

AI assistance (TRAE CLI) was used to draft the implementation plan and diff. Submitter reviewed every changed line.

### Design & Code Changes

- All three columns piggyback on `reward_extra_infos_dict` to avoid changing the `_dump_generations` signature.
- `uid` is canonicalized via `str()` (training/validation uids are already `str(uuid.uuid4())`); `data_source` and `index` keep native dtype so offline join does not need either side to pre-cast.
- Column collisions with reward-manager output warn + skip (keeping the reward value). Dump is an observability path; it must not be able to halt training.
- Length mismatch between join columns and `n` fails loud inside the `_build_join_keys` helper, bypassing the silent `len(v) == n` filter inside `_write_generations`.
- The validation dump branch uses a local copy of `reward_extra_infos_dict` so the join keys never reach `process_validation_metrics` or the `merged` return path.
- `rl_dataset.py:419` defaults `extra_info["index"]` to 0; datasets that fail to populate `extra_info["index"]` during preprocessing will have index=0 for every sample, which makes join-back infeasible. This is a dataset-provider responsibility and the dump path does not add defensive heuristics for it.
