items.title: [BREAKING][trainer, cfg] feat: stream V1 rollout dispatch through a dataloader actor with session-watermark refill
items.author: Begunner
items.summary: This PR moves V1 prompt dispatch, TransferQueue state tracking and eviction, and replay sampling out of the trainer process into a dedicated Ray actor, (sync) / (async), which replaces. In async modes the actor's coordinator keeps a target number of rollout s…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

This PR moves V1 prompt dispatch, TransferQueue state tracking and eviction, and replay sampling out of the trainer process into a dedicated Ray actor, `StreamingDataloader` (sync) / `StreamingDataloaderAsync` (async), which replaces `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/replay_buffer.py`. In async modes the actor's coordinator keeps a target number of rollout sessions in flight (`watermark_batches`) regardless of what the trainer is doing, replacing the one-shot `num_warmup_batches` warmup, the per-step batch dispatch in `prepare_step`, and the one-for-one eviction refill.

#### Motivation

On `main`, async trainers dispatch `num_warmup_batches` extra batches once at startup, then dispatch one full batch at the start of every step (`prepare_step`) and replace evicted groups one-for-one inside `sample()`. **In-flight concurrency therefore peaks right after each step's dispatch and drains as sessions complete until the next step.** The rollout replicas alternate between being overloaded at the start of a step and sitting mostly idle on the long tail at the end of it.

The [DeepSeek-V4.1 technical report](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/main/DeepSeek_V41_Tech_Report.pdf) (Section 5.2.1, "Asynchronous Post-training Infrastructure") describes the same pattern. Dispatching several extra batches up front and supplementing a full batch after each training iteration, which is what `num_warmup_batches` plus the per-step batch from `prepare_step` amounts to, caused severe oscillations in their training metrics. Their final design caps the number of in-flight samples and uses sample-level dispatch: as soon as the number of newly completed samples reaches the group size of the next prompt, that prompt is dispatched, regardless of which groups the completions came from. They also tried dispatching a new prompt only after a whole GRPO group finished, and dropped it because it stalled on long-tail samples within a group.

This PR follows the sample-level design. A dedicated actor keeps `round(watermark_batches * train_batch_size * rollout.n)` sessions in flight independently of the trainer. On every poll it counts the session slots freed across all groups and dispatches `free_slots // rollout.n` new prompts, so a single long-tail session only holds its own slot rather than blocking a whole prompt.

Keeping rollout busy regardless of the trainer raises the opposite problem in `separate_async`: when rollout outpaces training, finished groups would pile up without bound. Prompt staleness is roughly the number of unconsumed groups divided by `train_batch_size`, so an unbounded pile means unbounded staleness and TransferQueue memory, and under `drop` it wastes generation on groups that are evicted later. A second limit, `max_outstanding_batches` (default `4`), caps dispatched-but-unconsumed groups. The two limits govern different regimes: when rollout is the bottleneck the watermark binds and staleness stays near `watermark_batches`; when the trainer is the bottleneck the cap binds and staleness settles near `max_outstanding_batches`, while the trainer still always finds a full mini-batch. `max_off_policy_threshold` remains a safety net for long-tail groups rather than the steady-state operating point.

### Test
CPU unit tests.

GPU end-to-end:

> TODO: colocate_async + swe-rebench

### API and Usage Example

Async warmup is replaced by a steady-state in-flight target:

```bash
# before
trainer.v1.separate_async.num_warmup_batches=1
# after: keep watermark_batches * train_batch_size * rollout.n sessions in flight,
# and at most max_outstanding_batches * train_batch_size groups dispatched but not yet consumed
trainer.v1.separate_async.watermark_batches=2
trainer.v1.separate_async.max_outstanding_batches=4
```

Custom samplers now subclass the dataloader class for the trainer mode and override sampling hooks; the actor's coordinator keeps owning polling, refill, and request handling:

```python
from verl.trainer.ppo.v1.streaming_dataloader import StreamingDataloaderAsync


class UserCustomDataloader(StreamingDataloaderAsync):
    def _terminal_eviction_reasons(self, global_steps: int, partition_id: str):
        """Return (stale_uids, dapo_uids, failed_uids, dapo_counts) for terminal groups to evict."""
        ...

    def _select_prompt_uids(self, partition_id: str, sampleable_keys: set[str], batch_size: int):
        """Return (selected_uids, partition_snapshot, prompt_global_steps_snapshot)."""
        ...
```

```bash
trainer.v1.sampler.custom_sampler.path=path/to/your/sampler.py
trainer.v1.sampler.custom_sampler.name=UserCustomDataloader
```

### Design & Code Changes

```text
TaskRunnerV1
├── PPOTrainer (sync / colocate_async / separate_async)
│     └── Ray RPC: sample / count_sampleable / wait_sampleable / save_checkpoint / load_checkpoint
└── StreamingDataloader actor
      ├── train StatefulDataLoader + AgentLoopManager (TransferQueue)
      └── asyncio coordinator, one pass at a time:
            poll TQ metadata -> evict terminal groups -> refill prompts -> serve the pending request
```

- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/tq_schema.py` (new): single definition of the TransferQueue key and tag protocol shared by AgentLoop workers, the dataloader actor, the trainer, and `RolloutTqSkip`: prompt keys `{uid}`, session keys `{uid}_{session_id}`, trajectory keys `{uid}_{session_id}_{index}`.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/streaming_dataloader.py` (new, replaces `replay_buffer.py`):
  - Owns the train dataloader and the AgentLoop manager, and registers, polls, evicts, and samples prompt groups.
  - Sync refills only while a request is pending; DAPO evictions add `2k` refill credits bounded by `max_inflight_gen_batches`; `sync_refill_failed_groups` is opt-in.
  - Async keeps `round(watermark_batches * train_batch_size * rollout.n)` sessions in flight; rejected terminal groups no longer trigger a one-for-one replacement because their sessions already freed their slots. Refill is additionally capped by `max_outstanding_batches * train_batch_size` unconsumed groups (in flight plus awaiting sampling); the cap must be at least `watermark_batches`, and a warning is logged when it lets steady-state staleness reach `max_off_policy_threshold`.
  - Validation pauses train polling and refill until the next train request.
  - Async checkpoints save `data.pt` plus a TransferQueue snapshot, and restore reissues pending/running prompts from their stored prompt fields.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/agent_loop_tq.py`:
  - Each session writes a metadata-only `{uid}_{session_id}` key (`running`, then `finished` / `failure` after all its trajectory writes settle), which lets the actor count free session slots.
  - `AgentLoopManagerTQ.generate_sequences` rotates the first worker across calls; streaming refills dispatch a few prompts at a time and would otherwise always land on worker 0.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`, `trainer_colocate_async.py`, `trainer_separate_async.py`:
  - Sampling, warmup, TransferQueue checkpointing, and in-flight reissue move to the actor.
  - `separate_async` step switching queries the actor through `count_sampleable` / `wait_sampleable`.
  - New `trainer.v1.sampler.poll_interval` (default 2.0 s) is also the idle threshold for adaptive switching.
- `verl/trainer/main_ppo.py`: `TaskRunnerV1` creates the actor (custom sampler resolution included), passes it to `fit()`, and kills it on exit.
- Docs: `docs/advance/v1_async_trainer.md`, `docs/extend_guide.rst`, `docs/advance/skip_manager.rst`.

#### Breaking changes

- `trainer.v1.{colocate,separate}_async.num_warmup_batches` is replaced by `watermark_batches` (default `2`), with steady-state rather than one-shot semantics.
- `trainer.v1.sampler.custom_sampler` must subclass `StreamingDataloader` (sync) or `StreamingDataloaderAsync` (async); `verl.trainer.ppo.v1.replay_buffer` is removed.
- Sync trainers without DAPO or `sync_refill_failed_groups` now require `data.gen_batch_size` to be `null`, `1`, or `train_batch_size` (previously any divisor of `train_batch_size`). Async trainers and the exact-refill sync paths keep the existing behavior of overriding other values to `1`.
- Async trainers reject `max_off_policy_strategy=wait` with `max_off_policy_threshold=1`: watermark refill always keeps prompts in flight, so that combination would never become ready.
- `PPOTrainer.fit(agent_loop_manager)` becomes `PPOTrainer.fit(streaming_dataloader)`. `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.agent_loop_manager_class` is still honored, now inside the actor.
- `skip.rollout_tq.enable=True` is rejected by all V1 trainer modes: with other groups in flight, injecting cached trajectories cannot guarantee that the same groups form the sampled batch. The Ascend separate-async e2e no longer enables it.

items.body:
# IMPORTANT

Depends on PR #7449.

This PR is currently based on #7449 HEAD
(`fb5ef6e3ca1cf430920ddc892d0792186c10133e`).

The actual follow-up change in this PR is limited to:
- 4 production lines in `distrib_optimizer.py`
- one restore-boundary regression test

The additional commits/files currently shown in the diff belong to #7449 and
will disappear once this PR is rebased onto main after #7449 lands.

## Problem

After `load_checkpoint()` returns, the restored execution parameters, optimizer
moments, and step counters match the checkpoint, but the public model parameters
can remain stale.

This means the first resumed forward can use parameters that differ from the
restored optimizer execution state.

## Fix

After the HybridDeviceOptimizer state is restored, copy the restored FP32 master
parameters back to the model parameters when `param_update_in_fp32` is enabled.

## Tests

The regression checks the restore boundary before any resumed optimizer update,
then checks the first resumed loss/update and three continuation steps.

Validated on two ranks across:
- precision-aware full CPU offload, BF16
- precision-aware full CPU offload, BF16 + FP32
- precision-aware partial CPU offload, BF16
- precision-aware partial CPU offload, BF16 + FP32
- non-precision-aware partial-offload control

All repaired configurations match the reference.

items.title: [trainer] feat: balance every PPO mini-batch across DP ranks, shuffle on the trainer
items.author: FZYsheep
items.summary: Balances each PPO mini-batch across DP ranks instead of only balancing the whole train batch. However, workers split their local shard into PPO mini-batches sequentially and synchronize gradients after each mini-batch.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Balances each PPO mini-batch across DP ranks instead of only balancing the whole train batch.

### Problem

`trainer.balance_batch` currently reorders samples so that the **total** workload on every DP rank is similar. However, workers split their local shard into PPO mini-batches sequentially and synchronize gradients after each mini-batch. With only whole-batch balancing, the i-th mini-batch can still contain very different total workloads across DP ranks, creating stragglers inside the mini-batch step. This imbalance is further amplified when each DP rank splits its mini-batch into micro-batches of equal count, because one rank may end up processing much longer sequences per micro-batch than another.

### Solution

- Add `get_minibatch_balanced_partitions` to shuffle samples into PPO mini-batches and balance every mini-batch across DP ranks independently.
- Each rank's shard is laid out mini-batch by mini-batch, so the i-th sequential mini-batch on every rank comes from the same balanced global mini-batch.
- The balancing unit is the GCD of the actor and critic global mini-batch sizes (including `rollout.n`), so both models stay balanced.
- When an active actor or critic enables `shuffle` with `ppo_epochs > 1`, workers reshuffle samples inside each DP rank across epochs, which would remix the balanced chunks. In that case we fall back to whole-batch balancing and keep the original worker-side shuffle behavior. Single-epoch shuffle retains per-mini-batch balancing: the trainer shuffles samples before balancing, and worker-side shuffle is disabled for the balanced batch.

### Behavior change

- With multiple PPO epochs and `actor_rollout_ref.actor.shuffle` / `critic.shuffle` enabled on an active model, keep the original worker-side per-epoch shuffle and use whole-batch DP balancing.
- With a single PPO epoch, shuffle is applied by the trainer before per-mini-batch DP balancing; workers preserve the balanced layout.

### V1 ordering for fixed-size micro-batches

Also addresses the [V1 ordering gap raised in review](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8201#issuecomment-6204997497). V1 now matches V0's workload ordering from #3605: sort samples by estimated workload within each rank's share of a balancing unit, then place lighter samples at both ends and heavier samples in the middle. Sorting stays inside the GCD-sized balancing units, preserving every actor and critic PPO mini-batch boundary and each rank's assigned workload.

This additional ordering mainly benefits **fixed micro-batch size** (fixed sample count per micro-batch), when workers preserve the sample order. It groups samples of similar workload, approximately aligns heavier work across DP ranks, and places lighter micro-batches at the beginning and end to reduce pipeline-parallel warm-up/cool-down bubbles. It is a heuristic rather than a guarantee of equal workload at every micro-batch position.

Dynamic micro batching rebuilds the micro-batch groups and, with dynamic workload balancing enabled, already balances and orders the resulting micro-batches. Therefore, the trainer-side sample ordering is not expected to provide a consistent additional speedup on that path. Per-mini-batch DP balancing itself remains useful for both fixed and dynamic micro batching. Worker-side reshuffling can also undo the sample ordering.

The benchmark below measures per-mini-batch DP balancing; it does not isolate the benefit of this newly added V1 ordering.

### Benchmark

Qwen3-30B-A3B, 4 nodes × 8 GPUs = 32 GPUs, sequence-length distribution from a real Qwen 30B-A3B SWE Agentic RL run.

| Config | Strategy | step 60 | step 100 | speedup vs upstream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cp8_128k | upstream verl | 224.9 | 237.9 | 1.00× |
| cp8_128k | per-mini-batch balance (this PR) | 191.9 / 190.5 | 204.7 / 201.8 | 1.17× |
| cp4_64k | upstream verl | 331.3 | 352.9 | 1.00× |
| cp4_64k | per-mini-batch balance (this PR) | 291.9 | 296.3 | 1.14–1.19× |
| pp2cp4_128k | upstream verl | 254.2 | 263.6 | 1.00× |
| pp2cp4_128k | per-mini-batch balance (this PR) | 224.6 | 234.3 | 1.13× |
| cp4_128k | upstream verl | 414.1 | 434.9 | 1.00× |
| cp4_128k | per-mini-batch balance (this PR) | 352.1 | 373.1 | 1.17× |

All four production-like configurations show consistent speedups from balancing each mini-batch across DP ranks.

### Test commands

```bash
PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python python3 -m pytest tests/utils/test_minibatch_balancing_on_cpu.py -xvs
```

Results: 6 passed.

Co-authored-by: Claude

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs with [`balance minibatch`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+balance+minibatch) and [`mini-batch balance`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+mini-batch+balance).
The first query returned only this PR. Related PR #6025 keeps outputs from the same prompt together; #7281 removes scalar tensor dispatch from controller-side balancing. Neither implements per-mini-batch workload balancing across DP ranks.

### Validation

```bash
PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python uv run --no-project python3 -m pytest tests/utils/test_minibatch_balancing_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py -xq
```

Results: 17 passed. The V1 ordering test covers per-mini-batch balancing and whole-batch fallback, checking that each rank's balanced shares are preserved and lighter samples stay at both ends (including odd- and even-sized shares). Existing tests cover shuffle and actor/critic GCD selection. Ruff 0.12.2 lint and format checks passed for the updated test file; `git diff --check` passed.

### AI assistance

OpenAI Codex was used to assist with this change, validation, and PR preparation.

items.title: fix: omit empty MFSDP v2 optimizer shards on all TE versions
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: MFSDP v2 currently retains empty local shards in the optimizer with TE >= 2.18. These entries have no values to update but still create gradient-cast tensors, saved-gradient tuples, and clipping/Adam bookkeeping.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

MFSDP v2 currently retains empty local shards in the optimizer with TE >= 2.18. These entries have no values to update but still create gradient-cast tensors, saved-gradient tuples, and clipping/Adam bookkeeping. Exclude them on every TE version, while preserving group containers on newer TE and the existing empty-group workaround on older TE.

Always clear model-owned gradients as well as optimizer-owned gradients. This is necessary once empty shards are omitted: otherwise the second backward sees a mixture of set and unset gradients in an FSDP parameter group. Preserve the existing CUDA-graph behavior that zeros gradients in place.

## Evidence

A sequential comparison on the same 64 GB300 GPUs ran 128 steps per variant, with 64K context and CP=EP=8. Both MFSDP variants use upstream `main` at `daa007400639a7ed63db6b98b989ad7367c629e4` plus the NT4 training patches, including #7322, early NUMA binding, and unchanged automatic-GC thresholds `(2000, 10, 10)`. Statistics cover steps 51–128; full-GC counts sum all 64 ranks.

| MFSDP variant | Mean step time | Full GC events | Objects promoted per rank per step |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 4.1940 s | 237 | 17,449 |
| Omit empty optimizer entries | 3.9337 s | 109 | 7,961 |

Mean step time improved **6.2%** in this pair. Optimizer entries fell from 4,459 per rank to 668–808, preserving every nonempty shard and the local element counts. The number of tensor-view calls was unchanged. Full collections still affected 44/78 steps versus 35/78 before; the remaining DDP/MFSDP gap is not resolved by this change.

Initial/final main losses were **12.865110 / 7.719327** before and **12.865089 / 7.719135** after. Maximum/mean absolute loss differences over 128 steps were **0.014230 / 0.003239**. Main/MTP losses and gradient norms stayed finite, with zero OOMs or allocation retries on all ranks. These are observed sequential-run differences, not a numerical-equivalence tolerance.

This PR targets current `main` (`e30d863a6`) independently of #7322, so its local-shard check uses the existing DTensor API. The benchmark applied the equivalent filter to #7322's local tensors; it is not a benchmark of otherwise unmodified current main.

## Validation

- Two-GPU `torch.distributed.run` on this PR: **5 tests passed per rank**, covering ten training steps with two microbatches each for ordinary and precision-aware Adam, FusedSGD gradient conversion, and both gradient-clipping modes. The training test now requires actual empty model shards, checks their exclusion from optimizer groups, and checks all model gradients are cleared before every step.
- Two-GPU follow-up on this PR: **3 additional tests passed per rank**, covering FP32/BF16 optimizer checkpoint round trips and full-iteration plus optimizer CUDA graph replay.
- Prior four-GB300 integration on the benchmark source: ten updates in both Adam modes; loss trajectories exactly matched the unsharded reference.
- `tools/autoformat.sh` passed its required checks (Black, isort, pylint, Ruff). Its advisory mypy stage reports typing/missing-stub diagnostics in these files.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Score centering (#8010, #8196) on the Megatron actor. The sampler head log-probs are normalized over the vocab-parallel shards (row max and normalizer all-reduced over the TP group, masked local gather summed, backward local), the heads are split by context parallel like top-k distillation, and the Megatron logits processor runs the hook on the `score_centering` micro-batch flag. The cross entropy gets a copy of the logits under score centering: Megatron-Core shifts fp32 logits in place and the hook re-reads them in backward.

Stacked on #8196; only the last commit is new. No open PR touches score centering on Megatron.

items.title: Add opt-in R3 route-mismatch metric and targeted R3 CI checks
items.author: kar137
items.summary: Rollout routing replay (R3) had no measure of the train/inference routing disagreement it removes and no check that the replay is aligned: the R3 e2e tests only passed --ci-test and the step-0 KL check is skipped under R3, so a replay off by one token or one l…
items.body:
Rollout routing replay (R3) had no measure of the train/inference routing disagreement it removes and no check that the replay is aligned: the R3 e2e tests only passed --ci-test and the step-0 KL check is skipped under R3, so a replay off by one token or one layer still passed CI.

- --log-r3-route-mismatch: during the training forward only, count per MoE layer the real tokens (every token but each sample's last, without CP/TP padding) whose replayed expert set differs from the router's own top-k; all-reduce the counts and log train/r3_route_mismatch, _max, _layer_<i> and _min_tokens. Off by default and R3-only.
- --ci-r3-route-mismatch-threshold: under --ci-test, assert that every MoE layer replayed real tokens and that the worst layer stays under the bound. Both R3 e2e tests pass the metric and a bound.
- RoutingReplay.assert_all_consumed expects backward pops only for the routers activation recompute re-runs, and runs on the R3 path under --ci-test.

items.title: [Training] Avoid copies when gathering contiguous TP row shards
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: Contiguous dimension-0 TP weight shards currently gather into one buffer per rank and then concatenate those buffers into another full tensor. This allocates intermediate storage and copies the gathered weights again.
items.body:
Contiguous dimension-0 TP weight shards currently gather into one buffer per rank and then concatenate those buffers into another full tensor. This allocates intermediate storage and copies the gathered weights again.

Use `dist.all_gather_into_tensor` to write eligible CUDA/NCCL row partitions directly into their final tensor, for both synchronous and asynchronous weight synchronization. The asynchronous path still launches the bucket's collectives before waiting for every handle.

The fast path requires contiguous input, `partition_dim == 0`, `partition_stride == 1` and NCCL. GLU `linear_fc1` weights/biases and the `linear_fc2` dimension fix retain their existing gather/reordering paths, as do CPU, non-NCCL, column, noncontiguous and other-stride inputs. Replicated/duplicated parameters, expert bias, TP1 and expert-group selection retain their existing behavior. The PR contains one commit and changes only the gather implementation and its unit tests.

## Validation

- Complete repository-pinned `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: all nine hooks passed with no source changes.
- CPU regression: **47 passed, 0 failures, 0 skips** (33 new parametrized cases plus 14 existing distributed weight-update cases).
- Real H100 CUDA/NCCL **TP2 and TP4**: each rank passed 61 bitwise output comparisons and 6 identical expected-rejection checks, totaling **402 case/rank checks**. The new collective was verified to activate on eligible inputs.
- Four real AdamW updates per rank followed by bitwise-equal gathered weights and Linear consumer outputs: **24 updated-consumer checks**.

Megatron group accessors use the repository test adapters; tensors, CUDA/NCCL communication and optimizer updates are real. Full RL training, Ray/vLLM serving, AgentX and full-model quality were not tested in this change.

## Component benchmark

NVIDIA H100, Python 3.12.1, PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, NCCL 2.29.7. BF16 tensors; five warmups per arm and eleven alternating AB/BA paired repetitions per configuration. Take maximum synchronized wall time across ranks per call, then median over all repetitions. Extra peak memory is allocated PyTorch tensor storage above retained inputs, not total model/device memory.

| TP | Mode | Tensors × full output MiB each | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | Speedup | Extra peak MiB |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | sync | 1 × 256 | 2.306 | 1.559 | 1.48× | 512 → 256 |
| 2 | async | 4 × 256 | 9.057 | 6.081 | 1.49× | 3072 → 1024 |
| 4 | sync | 1 × 256 | 1.534 | 0.776 | 1.98× | 512 → 256 |
| 4 | async | 4 × 256 | 5.991 | 2.980 | 2.01× | 3072 → 1024 |

The TP4 asynchronous 4 × 256 MiB bucket reduces component wall time from 5.991 ms to 2.980 ms and extra peak tensor storage from 3 GiB to 1 GiB. These figures are not a full-training-throughput claim. The linked evidence includes all 16 size/mode/TP configurations, all paired timing samples, the portable reproduction worker and commands.

[Raw paired measurements and reproduction commands](https://gist.github.com/0z5a/9c371d4a1d08a8569d63268e1a889db7)

Measurements were pinned to development base `6ebe1c605a9cc9b04bdaa1383b66b49b220a6dd5`. This PR is based directly on `0z5a-branch` at `8c8b8e8e908818683b96dbdb2f438ff54cfd6aa0`: its baseline gather code, parameter metadata, test adapters and existing weight-update tests are byte-identical to the measured base. The submitted candidate gather file is byte-identical to the actual tested file (SHA256 `d082fc872ed8d11ed9c6169778838efc4bd5680178247503fd2e12afaadfe77c`). Earlier unsuccessful dependency/preflight/input-assumption attempts were retained and are not counted as passes.

AI assistance: implementation and validation were prepared with OpenAI Codex at the submitter's request, with attribution and DCO sign-off in the commit. Opened as a draft pending the submitter's line-by-line review; no human-review or full-training validation is claimed.

items.title: [fsdp, ckpt] fix: preserve merged LoRA export precision and staged weights
items.author: cyanseek
items.summary: Follow up on #8180: FSDP2 merged-LoRA HF export reuses the rollout generator, which casts FP32 master weights to BF16 before the HF writer applies its export dtype policy. FP16 and FP32 exports therefore lose precision and contain BF16 tensors.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Follow up on #8180: FSDP2 merged-LoRA HF export reuses the rollout generator, which casts FP32 master weights to BF16 before the HF writer applies its export dtype policy. FP16 and FP32 exports therefore lose precision and contain BF16 tensors. Preserve stored precision for the HF callback and let the existing writer apply its dtype policy; rollout retains its BF16 default.

For CPU-offloaded shards, finish host-to-device staging before the merge context can restore the pinned source storage. Otherwise, a consumer retaining the generated tensors can receive restored base weights while the asynchronous copy is still pending. The change retains per-tensor streaming and the existing merge/restore lifecycle.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched [LoRA dtype PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+LoRA+dtype), [LoRA offload PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+LoRA+offload), and [follow-ups to #8180](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8180+in%3Abody). No matching fix found. #8110 changes VeOmni rollout receiver precision; #8046 changes vLLM sleep behavior. Neither fixes this generator's HF dtype or source-storage lifetime.
- [x] Title follows the module/type convention.

### Test

Real 2×RTX 3080 Ti, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, PEFT 0.20.0. Locally constructed tiny Qwen2 with nonzero LoRA; no model download.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/ckpt/test_fsdp_lora_hf_export.py -q
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_fsdp_lora_merge.py -q -k 'qwen2 or collect_merged_lora_params'
python -m pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_fsdp_lora_only_checkpoint_on_cpu.py tests/utils/ckpt/test_lora_custom_object_save_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/rollout_sglang/test_lora_merge_mode_on_cpu.py -q
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```

The final patch passes all 6 regression cases across FP32/FP16/BF16 and CPU offload on/off. The same test on main fails all 4 FP32/FP16 cases on dtype and passes the 2 BF16 controls. It checks saved dtype/weights and HF reload outputs against an independent PEFT merge, tied-weight coverage, exact restoration of training parameters, and BF16 rollout behavior.

Actual FSDPEngine initialization and two training steps also pass with CPU offload on/off, with HF export/reload between the steps. The original engine continues training; HF files are checked as inference exports. A local diagnostic queues `torch.cuda._sleep(200_000_000)` before consuming the merged rollout generator: the dtype-only fix still corrupts 509/1024 q_proj elements, while the complete patch passes.

All 14 repository pre-commit hooks pass on the final patch. Adjacent LoRA GPU tests (8 passed, 4 deselected) and CPU tests (26 passed) ran on the dtype fix before the final staging adjustment; their helper/config paths were unchanged by that last adjustment. No large-model quality or throughput claim is made.

### API and Usage Example

No new configuration. Existing `hf_model` saves respect the checkpoint writer's precision policy for merged LoRA weights.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the contribution guide.
- [x] Full repository pre-commit checks passed on the current patch.
- [x] Documented the internal dtype and staging contracts in the generator.
- [x] Added GPU regression tests automatically discovered by `gpu_unit_tests.yml`.
- [ ] Request CI through the project channel after the PR is ready.
- [x] No recipe submodule change.

items.title: perf(moe): add opt-in torch grouped weight gradients for BF16 experts
items.author: ggboooy
items.summary: On the legacy, separately stored BF16 expert-weight path, grouped dW can launch one cuBLASLt GEMM per expert across internal streams. With 64 local experts, eager submission and gaps between these launches are material at short token counts.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Add an opt-in SM90 BF16 grouped-linear path that uses PyTorch grouped matmul for MoE expert weight gradients while retaining TE grouped GEMM for forward and input gradients. The default remains the original TE implementation.

## Motivation

On the legacy, separately stored BF16 expert-weight path, grouped dW can launch one cuBLASLt GEMM per expert across internal streams. With 64 local experts, eager submission and gaps between these launches are material at short token counts. Computing the ragged-K weight gradients in a grouped operation reduces that overhead.

## Implementation

- Add `moe_use_torch_grouped_wgrad` to `TransformerConfig`; the standard argument factory exposes `--moe-use-torch-grouped-wgrad`.
- Keep the existing TE-owned parameters, expert-parallel attributes, state-dict keys and load hooks. There is no installed-TE patch or process-wide TE monkeypatch.
- Reuse packed activations and build int32 cumulative expert offsets in forward via pinned memory and a nonblocking H2D copy. Each autograd context owns its inputs and offsets.
- Call TE `general_grouped_gemm` for forward/dgrad and `torch.nn.functional.grouped_mm` (or `torch._grouped_mm` on PyTorch 2.9) for dW. Return per-expert views of the new gradient storage, without concatenating expert inputs or copying dW back to another allocation.
- Preserve the original TE path for unsupported dtype, layout, precision, offload, accumulation, distributed-weight and graph configurations.
- Add focused module tests, bit-exact replay tests, determinism-manifest coverage, a standalone benchmark, captured routing-shape fixtures, and documentation.

Enable through MCore:

```python
moe_grouped_gemm=True,
moe_use_torch_grouped_wgrad=True,
params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
bf16=True,
add_bias_linear=False,
gradient_accumulation_fusion=False,
```

## Testing

Tested on the submission checkout based on `736353b7e014`, using PyTorch 2.9.1+cu129 and Transformer Engine 2.19.0 on SM90.

- **Two GPUs: 36 focused tests passed on each rank.** Native-TE output/dgrad/dW comparisons; empty and ragged groups; checkpoint recomputation; multiple outstanding forwards and gradient accumulation; frozen experts; multidimensional inputs and strided upstream gradients; checkpoint parameter names; CLI exposure; and fallback guards.
- Byte-exact forward/backward replay passes with and without side-stream contention. Both the helper and the actual MCore TE wrapper are covered and registered in the determinism manifest.
- **80 single-module benchmark cases passed dispatch and numerical checks.** The observed maximum relative L2 difference in output, dgrad and dW was zero on this fixed random-input set; no universal bitwise-equivalence claim is made.
- Repository `tools/autoformat.sh` check, Black, isort, Pylint, Ruff, Python compilation, `git diff --check`, and the kernel determinism coverage gate pass. The new helper also passes focused mypy with missing external-library stubs ignored.
- The repository script's advisory mypy stage still reports missing TE stubs and existing typing errors in surrounding files; this is not a clean repository-wide mypy result.
- No upstream CI result is available yet.

Focused reproduction:

```bash
torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts="" -q \
  tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_torch_grouped_wgrad.py \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_torch_grouped_wgrad_replay.py \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_te_wrappers.py::TestTEWrappers::test_te_grouped_linear_torch_wgrad_replays
```

The focused suite initializes real process groups through the repository utilities; `--noconftest` avoids unrelated dataset-download fixtures.

## Single-module performance

One SM90 GPU (132 SMs, approximately 80 GiB), BF16, 64 local experts, `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1`, and `NVTE_USE_CUTLASS_GROUPED_GEMM=1` in both arms. FC1 weights are [64, 1024, 2048], FC2 weights are [64, 2048, 512].

The checked-in 80 shapes use actual expert-token counts captured at rank 0 / microbatch 0 from a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B text workload at TP1/PP2/CP4/EP4. Tensor values and weights are newly generated BF16 random values. **The 8K/32K labels describe the source global sequence length; these are isolated module measurements, not distributed training timings.**

Each shape uses five warmup calls per arm followed by ABBA/BAAB ordering, six samples per arm/metric and five calls per sample. The table is the median of per-shape medians over 20 routing distributions. CUDA-event intervals include eager submission gaps, rather than summing kernel active time.

| Global sequence | FC | Metric | TE (ms) | Torch dW (ms) | Speedup |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | FC1 | dW | 0.638 | 0.210 | 3.041x |
| 8,192 | FC1 | Module F+B | 2.346 | 1.534 | 1.529x |
| 8,192 | FC2 | dW | 0.638 | 0.124 | 5.144x |
| 8,192 | FC2 | Module F+B | 2.336 | 1.519 | 1.538x |
| 32,768 | FC1 | dW | 0.666 | 0.502 | 1.327x |

| 32,768 | FC2 | dW | 0.649 | 0.303 | 2.144x |
| 32,768 | FC2 | Module F+B | 2.348 | 1.547 | 1.518x |

- **dW:** packed X/dY and offsets already exist; both paths allocate new BF16 output.
- **Module F+B:** one GroupedLinear forward, dgrad, dW and common gradient clearing; includes the candidate's forward metadata transfer. No SwiGLU, routing, communication, activation recomputation or optimizer update.
- The supported path bypasses the generic quantized TE autograd wrapper, so module-level gains include wrapper overhead as well as dW dispatch. They must not be attributed solely to a faster GEMM kernel.

Benchmark reproduction (no model checkpoint required):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1 NVTE_USE_CUTLASS_GROUPED_GEMM=1 \
  torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=1 tools/benchmark_torch_grouped_wgrad.py \
  --shapes tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/data/torch_grouped_wgrad_shapes.jsonl \
  --output /tmp/torch-grouped-wgrad-benchmark
```

See `docs/developer/torch_grouped_wgrad.md` and the adjacent CSV for the scope and results.

## Limitations

- Eager SM90 BF16, separately stored expert parameters, expert TP/GTP size one, and ordinary autograd gradient accumulation.
- Bias, FP8/FP4, quantization recipes, FP16 autocast, TE debugging, fused main-grad accumulation, delayed wgrad, CPU/activation offload, FSDP, grouped parameters and CUDA graphs retain the original TE path.
- The native TE GroupedTensor/op-fuser path is an alternative and was not benchmarked here; this proposal targets the legacy BF16 expert path.
- No new distributed communication or DeepGEMM integration. No full-model throughput, optimizer-update or convergence claim.

items.author: XiaodaNV
items.summary: Add an unpadded layout for MFSDP v2 RowAtomic/BlockAtomic parameter groups: tensors are packed back to back and rank boundaries snap to the nearest row (32-row block for MXFP8) boundary, giving generally unequal shards with zero padding. Currently, every group…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Add an unpadded layout for MFSDP v2 RowAtomic/BlockAtomic parameter groups: tensors are packed back to back and rank boundaries snap to the nearest row (32-row block for MXFP8) boundary, giving generally unequal shards with zero padding.

Currently, every group is padded to a multiple of `dp_size * LCM(row sizes)` (`* 32` for MXFP8). For groups mixing many row widths this is large: the DeepSeek-V3-shaped dense group measured for #7585 pads 13% at DP=4 and over 80% at DP=16.

Changes:
- `GlobalLayout.build_for_row_atomic_unpadding`: padding-free builder; shards differ by at most one row/block and may be empty.
- `GlobalLayout.validate_for_row_atomic`: checks only that no rank boundary splits a row/block of the tensor it falls in, instead of requiring equal segments and globally aligned offsets. Padded layouts still pass.
- `DBuffer`: the list-based `all_gather`/`reduce_scatter` paths slice per-peer chunks via `GlobalLayout.get_peer_ranges`, so uneven layouts work on multi-axis (HSDP/HFSDP) meshes, not only TensorAtomic on 1-D.
- `QuantizedDBuffer`: scale-plane layouts derive from the unpadded data layout.
- Knob: `fully_shard(uneven_shards=...)`, `DistributedDataParallelConfig.megatron_fsdp_uneven_shards`, `--megatron-fsdp-uneven-shards`. Incompatible with `nccl_ub` (symmetric memory needs equal shards); default behavior is unchanged.

Tests: layout builder/validation, 1-D and 2-D DBuffer round trips, QuantizedDBuffer planes with empty ranks, MXFP8 MLP training parity, SGD/HFSDP parity, adapter flag, all parametrized against the padded default. `tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2` passes on 4xGB200.

items.title: Fix --ckpt-step checkpoint selection bugs
items.author: 0x5t4l1n
items.summary: Fixes three related bugs in handling that cause the wrong checkpoint to be loaded: 1. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes three related bugs in `--ckpt-step` handling that cause the wrong checkpoint to be loaded:

1. **`--ckpt-step 0` silently ignored** — `getattr(args, 'ckpt_step', None)` is used as a truthiness check, so step 0 (falsy) falls through and loads the latest checkpoint instead.

2. **`release=True` not cleared** — When the tracker file records a release checkpoint but the user requests a specific numeric step, the `release` flag remains `True`, causing `get_checkpoint_name` to resolve to the `release/` directory instead of `iter_NNNNNNN/`.

3. **Non-persistent checkpoint silently overrides explicit step** — In `_load_base_checkpoint`, a non-persistent checkpoint at step >= the requested step takes precedence, even when the user explicitly requested a specific persistent checkpoint via `--ckpt-step`.

## Changes

- `get_load_checkpoint_path_by_args`: truthiness → `is not None`, set `release = False`
- `_load_base_checkpoint`: same truthiness fix, same `release = False`, skip non-persistent override when `--ckpt-step` is explicitly set

## Test plan

- [ ] `--ckpt-step 0` now loads step-0 checkpoint instead of latest
- [ ] `--ckpt-step N` with release tracker loads `iter_000000N/` not `release/`
- [ ] `--ckpt-step N` ignores non-persistent checkpoints at step >= N

Fixes #8110

items.title: [data] fix: preserve reasoning content in multi-turn SFT tokenization
items.author: akushonkamen
items.summary: rendered each message in isolation with, but chat templates such as Qwen3 build the block from only when the assistant message is rendered together with its preceding conversation. Per-message rendering therefore silently dropped the reasoning channel: raised…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #7807. `MultiTurnSFTDataset` rendered each message in isolation with `apply_chat_template([message])`, but chat templates such as Qwen3 build the `<think>` block from `reasoning_content` only when the assistant message is rendered together with its preceding conversation. Per-message rendering therefore silently dropped the reasoning channel: `sanity_check()` raised `AssertionError` on reasoning conversations, and with `ignore_input_ids_mismatch=True` the trained sequence never contained any `<think>` section, which teaches the model to put final answers into the reasoning channel.

The fix uses the previously unused `full_message` argument: for conversations that carry a `reasoning_content` field, assistant turns are rendered as part of the conversation prefix (`full_message[:index+1]`), and the tokenized `full_message[:index]` prefix is sliced off to obtain the per-turn increment. Every other turn, and the whole VLM/processor path, keeps the previous per-message rendering, so token sequences stay byte-identical for conversations without `reasoning_content` and for templates without position-dependent rendering.

**Why this is not duplicating an existing PR (per AGENTS.md):** searched open PRs for [`7807`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+7807) (0 hits), [`reasoning_content`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+reasoning_content), and [`MultiTurnSFTDataset`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+MultiTurnSFTDataset). The closest ones are #7322/#7700 (ContinuousTokenBuilder integration, a feature redesign that does not claim #7807) and #8153 (only adds test trajectories for `scripts/chat_template_checker.py`, explicitly not tied to any issue). The issue timeline shows no cross-references. This PR is a minimal bug fix on the current pipeline and does not conflict with those efforts.

**AI assistance disclosure:** this change was developed with the assistance of an AI coding agent. The submitting human reviewed every changed line, ran the duplicate-work checks above, and ran all tests below.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+7807
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+reasoning_content+in%3Atitle%2Cbody
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+MultiTurnSFTDataset
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - Title: `[data] fix: preserve reasoning content in multi-turn SFT tokenization`
  - No breaking API change, so no `[BREAKING]` prefix.

### Test

All commands CPU-only (transformers 5.12.1, torch 2.14.1 CPU, macOS arm64, tokenizers under `~/models/`):

1. New regression test, red on `main`, green with this fix (Qwen3-0.6B):
```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/utils/dataset/test_multiturn_sft_qwen3_reasoning_on_cpu.py
# on main : 1 failed, 1 passed
#           (test_multiturn_sft_qwen3_reasoning_preserved[Qwen3-0.6B] fails with the
#            sanity_check AssertionError reported in #7807)
# with fix: 2 passed
#           (also asserts token-for-token equality with the previous implementation
#            on Qwen2.5-0.5B, i.e. no regression for non-position-dependent templates)
```
2. Existing tests stay green and unchanged:
```bash
python -m pytest -q "tests/utils/dataset/test_multiturn_sft_dataset_on_cpu.py::test_multiturn_sft_dataset" \
                    "tests/utils/dataset/test_multiturn_sft_dataset_on_cpu.py::test_multiturn_sft_dataset_with_chat_template_kwargs"
# 4 passed: Qwen2.5-0.5B (ignore=False), Qwen3-0.6B (ignore=True), Qwen3.5-0.8B (ignore=False), gpt-oss-20b
```
3. Pre-commit hooks on the changed files:
```bash
pre-commit run --files verl/utils/dataset/multiturn_sft_dataset.py tests/utils/dataset/test_multiturn_sft_qwen3_reasoning_on_cpu.py
# all 13 hooks Passed (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, autogen-trainer-cfg, docstring/license/structure checks, compileall)
```

### API and Usage Example

No API or config change. Behavior for a Qwen3 multi-turn conversation whose assistant messages carry `reasoning_content`:

```python
item = dataset[0]  # no longer raises AssertionError from sanity_check
# item["input_ids"] now equals tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
#     whole_conversation, tools=tools, enable_thinking=True)
# tokenizer.decode(item["input_ids"][item["loss_mask"] == 1]) contains
# "<think>reasoning ...</think>\n<tool_call>...</tool_call>" for every assistant turn,
# so ignore_input_ids_mismatch=True is no longer needed for this scenario.
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/dataset/multiturn_sft_dataset.py` (`_process_single_message`): added a gated context-rendering branch (text-only path, `index != 0`, assistant role, conversation contains a truthy `reasoning_content`). It renders `full_message[:index+1]` via verl's `apply_chat_template` wrapper and slices off the tokenized `full_message[:index]` prefix; if the shorter prefix is not a token-level prefix of the longer render, it warns and slices by length (the existing `sanity_check` remains the final sequence oracle). `__getitem__` now passes `tools` ungated and the per-message branch applies the historical `tools if index == 0 else None` gating internally, keeping VLM behavior identical.
- New CPU test `tests/utils/dataset/test_multiturn_sft_qwen3_reasoning_on_cpu.py` (auto-picked-up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`, which globs `**/*.py`).

- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` all passed.
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation: no user-facing API/config change (bug fix only), so no doc update needed.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to the CI workflow: new `*_on_cpu.py` test is covered by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`.
- [ ] CI trigger: this is an external PR, so workflow runs need maintainer approval — could a maintainer please approve the workflows to run? (The Slack invite link is not accessible to me.)
- [x] Not related to the `recipe` submodule.

items.author: Waterpine
items.summary: Optimize MoE inference routing, token dispatch, and expert GEMMs, with correctness and end-to-end performance validation on GB300.:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the tea…
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Optimize MoE inference routing, token dispatch, and expert GEMMs, with correctness and end-to-end performance validation on GB300.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Changes

- Fuse eligible sigmoid/top-k routing and parallelize expert token-alignment table construction
- Apply measured BF16 GEMM configurations to matching GB300 expert shapes, retaining heuristic fallbacks for other configurations
- Reduce NCCL/NVLS dispatch overhead through packed gathers and fused masking, output conversion, and shared-expert addition
- Share ordered TP reductions between batch-invariant (BI) training and inference paths
- Add unit tests and registered bit-exact kernel determinism tests

## Performance

Measured using Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B BF16 and the stakeholder-provided GSM8K HTTP workload on GB300, with four GPUs per node. One-node tests use TP4/EP4; two-node tests use TP4/EP8
- Candidate: 379fc56cd
- Ordinary baseline: unchanged main 442d0183d
- BI baseline: the same main revision with the identical ordered TP correction applied to both baseline and candidate. BI ratios are therefore not relative to unchanged main

Four fresh servers were run in baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline order. Speedup is baseline total batch wall time divided by candidate total batch wall time for equal work.

Each entry reports end-to-end speedup for BS8 / BS32 / BS128, where BS is the number of concurrent requests in each client batch. Values above 1 indicate improvement; values below 1 indicate regression. All formal samples are included in this table.

| Mode | Topology | Output length: 1,024 tokens | Output length: 2,048 tokens | Output length: 4,096 tokens | Output length: 8,192 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary | 1 node, NVLS | 1.1908 / 1.1690 / 1.1454 | 1.1898 / 1.1661 / 1.1629 | 1.1847 / 1.1612 / 1.1694 | 1.1854 / 1.1594 / 1.1677 |
| Ordinary | 2 nodes, NVLS | 1.1844 / 1.1775 / 1.1379 | 1.1896 / 1.1794 / 1.1562 | 1.1900 / 1.1771 / 1.1624 | 1.1808 / 1.1807 / 1.1684 |
| Ordinary | 2 nodes, NCCL | 1.1904 / 1.2023 / 1.1816 | 1.2026 / 1.2116 / 1.1942 | 1.2091 / 1.2030 / 1.1991 | 1.2036 / 1.1917 / 1.2005 |
| BI | 1 node, NVLS | 1.0270 / 1.0371 / 0.9897 | 1.0291 / 1.0434 / 0.9884 | 1.0295 / 1.0437 / 0.9873 | 1.0265 / 1.0411 / 0.9871 |
| BI | 2 nodes, NVLS | 1.0139 / 1.0113 / 1.0210 | 1.0102 / 1.0090 / 1.0219 | 1.0115 / 1.0107 / 1.0212 | 1.0113 / 1.0091 / 1.0212 |


Across these long-output cells, geometric mean throughput improves by approximately 17–20% in ordinary mode and 1–2% in BI mode. These are end-to-end HTTP batch measurements, not isolated kernel speedups or TTFT/ITL measurements.

## Correctness and validation

- Numerical validation covered BS8/32/128 and output lengths 1/1024/2048/4096/8192 on all five supported mode/topology combinations above
- Each comparison covered 2,580,648 generated positions, with zero token differences and zero full-vocabulary BF16 logit-row hash differences. Each row contains 131,072 logits; baseline-repeat controls also passed.
- Ordinary validation used fixed admission; BI validation used dynamic HTTP admission. This does not claim ordinary-mode bitwise equality across arbitrary dynamic schedules
- Targeted unit, distributed, and determinism tests were run. Shared baseline/candidate test outcomes matched, including the two failures below
- Black, isort, Ruff, Pylint, whitespace, and kernel-determinism coverage checks passed. Full upstream CI remains pending.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: None yet. The following follow-up issues have not been opened.

### Known issues and limitations

- Existing BI training/inference mismatch: `test_dynamic_engine_matches_batched_forward_rl` fails on both baseline main and the candidate in the tested environment. Training-style forward and dynamic-inference log probabilities differ. The root cause remains unconfirmed, and this PR does not fix it. Successful baseline/candidate inference comparisons do not establish training/inference parity
- Missing dependency: `test_batch_invariant_prefill_matches_full_forward` fails on both versions because the selected backend requires unavailable DeepGEMM BF16 grouped-GEMM bindings. This path needs a dependency-complete rerun
- Latency spikes: Multi-second host-side stalls occur in both baseline and candidate and remain unresolved. Separate Output Length 1 analyses retain raw results alongside explicitly labeled paired exclusions; filtered results are not tail-latency guarantees. First-use GEMM compilation overhead is a separate remaining issue
- Remaining regressions: BI two-node NVLS/Output Length 1/BS8 measured 0.949×, with both repeated comparisons slower and no multi-second outliers. BI one-node BS128 long outputs measured approximately 1.0–1.3% higher latency. These results remain under investigation and are not dismissed as noise
- Benchmark-client sensitivity: Ordinary one-node NVLS/Output Length 1/BS128 measured 0.923× with the original client. A separate investigation identified connection-pool overhead; an independent client configuration measured 1.039×. That configuration changes the benchmark protocol, is not part of this production-code change, and does not replace the original result.


## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))

items.title: fix(data): preserve empty datasets during prompt length filtering
items.author: GoldArowana
items.summary: An empty JSONL file or a valid slice currently crashes during construction because indexes. Return the original empty list before inspecting the first prompt.
items.body:
An empty JSONL file or a valid `@[0:0]` slice currently crashes during `Dataset(..., max_length=8)` construction because `filter_long_prompt` indexes `origin_samples[0]`. Return the original empty list before inspecting the first prompt.

This preserves existing Dataset/filter semantics: empty input is already accepted with `max_length=None`, and nonempty input may become empty after length filtering. It does not establish that empty data can complete rollout, evaluation, or training; downstream consumers retain their own validation.

Extend the existing registered CPU test with actual temporary JSONL files and a locally constructed Transformers fast tokenizer backed by WordLevel (no model downloads). Cover empty files and empty slices with and without a length limit, an 8-token boundary and 9-token overlong prompt, all-filtered input, empty-list identity with and without a processor, and existing ordering behavior. The file retains `NUM_GPUS = 0`.

Validation on Linux / Python 3.12:
- Before the guard: `python -m pytest tests/test_filter_long_prompt.py tests/test_read_file_slicing.py` — **4 failed, 20 passed; exit 1**, with the expected empty-input IndexErrors.
- After the guard: the same command — **24 passed; exit 0**.
- Official CI-shaped entry: `python tests/test_filter_long_prompt.py` — **14 passed; exit 0**, including after formatting.
- Normal commit ran all applicable repository pre-commit hooks successfully; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent read-only review found no blocking correctness, coverage, or CPU CI issues.

Tests used CPU-only, offline settings: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' SLIME_ACCELERATOR=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-p no:cacheprovider' PYTHONPATH=.`. No GPU, training, rollout service, or weight-download checks were run. This change covers a CPU data-filtering boundary.

Related PRs #2365, #2449, #2126 and #2363 and their discussions were refreshed before publication; their epoch-sampling and multimodal changes do not address this empty-input guard.

AI assistance was used for reproduction, implementation, tests, and an independent review; the reported validation commands were actually executed.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Other inputs continue through the existing eager path. Use explicit FMA and rounded division at the corresponding eager operation boundaries, and record the in-place mutation for autograd.
items.body:
## Problem

`StatelessAdam.step()` launches several pointwise operations and allocates parameter-sized temporary tensors for every update, even though it does not retain Adam moments.

## Change

- Fuse the update into one Triton kernel per parameter for same-shape, contiguous FP32 CUDA parameters and gradients. Other inputs continue through the existing eager path.
- Preserve Adam/AdamW modes, bias correction, maximize, decoupled gradients, learning-rate changes, and empty optimizer state. Use explicit FMA and rounded division at the corresponding eager operation boundaries, and record the in-place mutation for autograd.
- Add single-GPU correctness and temporary-memory coverage, register it in the generated PR workflow, and include the kernel package in wheel installations.

The existing `--use-stateless-adam` configuration selects this path automatically when eligible; no new option is required.

## Validation

On one RTX 5090, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128, and Triton 3.6.0:

```text
PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/test_stateless_adam.py tests/test_stateless_adam_cuda.py -q
43 passed
```

Coverage includes reset-Adam parity, exact eager rounding with coupled-decay cancellation, unchanged gradients, non-contiguous and low-precision fallback, broadcast decoupled gradients, non-default CUDA streams, and autograd mutation tracking. The memory regression fails on the original implementation: a 16 MiB parameter update allocates 32 MiB of temporary tensors; the fused path stays below the 1 MiB threshold.

CPU-only execution passes 6 tests and skips 37 CUDA tests. A wheel built and installed into an isolated directory passes a real CUDA update and stale-graph check outside the source checkout. Black, isort, Ruff, workflow-generation consistency, and `git diff --check` pass.

## Benchmark

Baseline: `58b0878679de339ec7844b45d884a87955a134be`. Hardware/software: one RTX 5090, driver 580.178.04, CUDA 12.8, and the versions above.

Optimizer-only measurements use FP32 parameters and fixed gradients, AdamW with weight decay 0.1 and learning rate 1e-6. After warmup, alternate baseline/fused order over 7 rounds of 30 updates; report median synchronized wall time, including Python and launch overhead.

| Parameter layout | Original | Fused | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| One tensor with 32M elements | 1.038 ms | 0.256 ms | 4.06x |
| 256 tensors with 4096 elements each | 3.293 ms | 2.087 ms | 1.58x |
| Qwen3-0.6B: 310 tensors, 596,049,920 parameters | 12.406 ms | 4.605 ms | 2.69x |

For the Qwen layout, additional peak PyTorch tensor allocation during the optimizer step falls from 1,245,708,288 bytes (1.16 GiB) to zero after warmup. This excludes allocator-reserved memory, CUDA context memory, and compilation.

A Transformers Qwen3-0.6B forward/backward/update benchmark using Slime's optimizer reduces step time from **47.23 ms to 39.20 ms (17.0%)** and peak allocated GPU memory from **5.62 GiB to 5.04 GiB**. It uses FP32 parameters/gradients, BF16 autocast, SDPA, batch size 1, sequence length 256, fixed random tokens, learning rate 1e-5, and weight decay 0.1. Baseline/fused/fused/baseline runs each start from the same checkpoint and seed, with 10 warmup and 30 measured steps. The reported time is the median of the two per-run medians. All four 40-step loss curves match exactly in this configuration.

This is optimizer and model-step validation, not a complete Slime RL run or a task-quality result. Distributed Megatron, CPU offload, other GPUs, and other PyTorch/Triton versions were not exercised.

Prepared with Codex assistance; the results above were measured on the original and final implementations.

items.title: fix(ray): bind trainer CPU affinity to the selected GPU
items.author: DongDongJu
items.summary: Workers with partial or reordered GPU allocations can select one CUDA device but bind their calling thread to another GPU's CPUs: the old affinity path uses global rank modulo GPUs per node as an NVML index. Resolve the already selected CUDA device by its UUID…
items.body:
Workers with partial or reordered GPU allocations can select one CUDA device but bind their calling thread to another GPU's CPUs: the old affinity path uses global rank modulo GPUs per node as an NVML index. 
Resolve the already selected CUDA device by its UUID instead, intersect its preferred CPUs with the thread's existing effective affinity, and read back the applied mask.

Unsupported backends, missing identity/bindings, MIG, empty intersections and NVML/affinity errors remain nonfatal. Successful NVML initialization is always balanced with shutdown. 
The operation stays at the existing initialization site and affects only the calling thread; it does not place other threads or memory.

Validation: the real TrainRayActor constructor/init regression fails on the old path (CUDA GPU 4, but GPU 0's CPU mask) and passes after this patch. All 41 new CPU tests and 29 accelerator/placement tests pass, including direct execution and pytest collection. Black, isort, Ruff and git diff --check pass. 
Registered the test in the CPU CI template and regenerated the workflow.

Read-only inspection confirms distinct NUMA masks for GPUs 0 and 4 on the local eight-GPU host. CUDA/Ray execution, actual training-thread continuity and performance remain unvalidated because no GPU allocation or running Ray runtime was confirmed.
No throughput or memory-locality improvement is claimed.

items.title: [algo, rollout, cfg, doc] feat: automatically align score centering with sampler support
items.author: cr-gao
items.summary: Score centering (#8010) now attempts to align with the actual sampler support automatically. A verified complete-support record selects support-normalized centering and sampled scoring.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Score centering (#8010) now attempts to align with the actual sampler support automatically. A verified complete-support record selects support-normalized centering and sampled scoring. Otherwise the existing recorded top-k plus full-vocabulary trainer-tail approximation is used; the recording budget does not change sampling parameters. The approximation keeps actual sampler head/sample probabilities, includes the existing epsilon tail regularization, and can assign modeled tail mass outside an unknown sampler support.

The new manual score_centering_top_p flag is removed. A provider completeness receipt, rather than configured k values or near-unit head mass, controls per-token selection. Recorded K below an effective finite sampling top-k produces an advisory warning; warning and estimator selection remain independent. Validation and greedy reward-baseline requests do not record heads.

This extends the current score-centering feature rather than duplicating #8020, which proposes broader IS/RS support-size replay. #8199 remains the separate Megatron extension and needs its shared API rebased on the resulting feature head. Dedicated equivalent normalization performance work is separate in #8206, stacked on a mirror of this feature head.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Checked open references to #8010 and #8020 and searched score_centering/topk_log_probs and centering + perf. [Open centering PR search](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+centering) found #8196 and #8199; this updates #8196.
- [x] Title format.

### Test

Additional implementation validation:

- CPU: the focused score-centering, provider, Hydra, metrics, numerics, wiring, agent-loop/TQ and worker-config suite passed 176 tests, with 10 skips and one explicitly deselected pre-existing missing-model-path test. The undeselected worker-config run still reproduces the original missing-model-path failure; it is not counted as passing.
- GPU: six vLLM provider cases passed on H100 with public Qwen3-0.6B revision c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca, including pure top-p, incomplete heads and actual small-batch cutoff ties. After the final provider-integrity changes, five CUDA cases passed: two portable cutoff-tie/provider cases and three deterministic pure-top-p overflow cases covering no IS/TIS/IcePop with an actual sampled token outside the recorded head.
- pre-commit: all 14 hooks passed, including generated configs, mypy, formatting and repository sanity checks.
- Reproduction commands (from the feature checkout, with the installed uv environment):

  ```bash
  uv run --active --no-sync pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_alignment_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_config_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_metrics_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_numerics_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_score_centering_wiring_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_topk_coverage_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_agent_loop_extra_fields_schema_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_agent_loop_tq_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/ --deselect tests/workers/config/test_model_config_on_cpu.py::TestHFModelConfigCPU::test_target_modules_raises_on_invalid_type
  VLLM_TOPK_SUPPORT_MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-0.6B CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run --active --no-sync pytest -q tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_topk_support.py
  uv run --active --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
  ```

  The GPU file now contains nine cases. The existing six-case provider run and later five-case targeted run overlap in the two cutoff-tie tests; this draft does not claim a fresh nine-case run.

- Numerical scope: off-policy dense gradient oracles cover no IS/TIS/IcePop and mixed alignment. Near-zero-tail tests verify finite behavior and record the inherited epsilon approximation error; they do not establish exact mass conservation there.
- These checks do not establish training quality, real actor-update speedup, remote CI, or end-to-end performance of this revision.

Historical validation reported by the original submitter on the original implementation:

- CPU: `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_score_centering_wiring_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_agent_loop_tq_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/` → 102 passed, 11 skipped, 1 failed (`test_model_config_on_cpu::test_target_modules_raises_on_invalid_type`, fails identically on main).

Validation by the original submitter on the current head (19f10e93, RTX PRO 6000, vLLM 0.29.0):

- GPU: `tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_topk_support.py` → 9 passed.
- Fig. 4 (left) analogue with truncation, same setup as #8010 (Qwen3-0.6B on Countdown, fp8 sampler vs bf16 FSDP trainer, REINFORCE, SGD 1e-2, 400 steps, one seed per arm) plus `top_p=0.95, top_k=128, topk_log_probs=128`, no extra flag (the `bypass_pg` arm is the earlier run; its path is unchanged):

  ![score centering top-p Countdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cr-gao/verl/assets/score-centering/score_centering_topp_auto_countdown.png)

  | mode | train acc, last 50 steps | held-out max / final | `ppo_kl` max | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `bypass_pg` | 0.11 | 0.31 / 0.09 | 4.93 | collapses at step 118 |

  Same numbers as the untruncated SC arm in #8010 (0.67 / 0.63 / 0.56) and as the earlier run of this PR with the manual flag (0.65 / 0.64 / 0.59). `sc_support_aligned` = 1.0 and `sc_support_unknown` = 0 at every step, `sc_sampler_tail_mass` ≤ 6e-9, `sc_train_head_mass` 0.981–0.990, 15 s/step (sc) vs 10 s/step (pg).

### API and Usage Example

Enable score_centering on the algorithm and actor correction settings as before, and set rollout.calculate_log_probs=true, logprobs_mode=processed_logprobs and a positive topk_log_probs recording budget. Sampling temperature must be positive for training SC. No second support-mode flag is required. The vLLM provider records response_support_complete, which is transported in prediction-row layout as rollout_support_complete. Old records without receipts remain supported through the approximation.

### Design & Code Changes

- Verify global ranked probability records; reject missing/ragged records, duplicate/out-of-vocabulary ids, inconsistent probabilities and custom-token padding that cannot prove coverage.
- Select aligned or approximate centering per token. Use the same trainer normalization for centering, sampled score and applicable importance weights in each selected domain.
- Preserve the new receipt across partial-resume concatenation, AgentLoop conversion and synthetic padding.
- Expose token-weighted support alignment, unrecorded sampler mass and unknown-coverage diagnostics. Existing head-mass diagnostics remain available.
- Connect the GPU provider test to vLLM CI and preserve greedy reward-baseline/validation separation.

items.title: [megatron] fix: backward through chunked vocab-parallel entropy
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: With the Megatron engine, fails in backward whenever the entropy is part of the graph: applies to chunks that are views of one logits tensor. Its backward subtracts from the saved logits in place and adds back afterwards.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

With the Megatron engine, `entropy_from_logits_with_chunking=True` fails in backward whenever the entropy is part of the graph:

```
RuntimeError: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified by an inplace operation: [torch.cuda.FloatTensor [1, 2048, 131072]], which is output 0 of AsStrided, is at version 4; expected version 2 instead.
```

`vocab_parallel_entropy_with_chunking` applies `_VocabParallelEntropy` to chunks that are views of one logits tensor. Its backward subtracts from the saved logits in place and adds back afterwards. All views share one version counter, so the first chunk's backward invalidates the logits the other chunks saved.

It only shows up when the update forward computes the entropy with chunking, e.g. `entropy_coeff != 0`, or `calculate_entropy=True` in bypass mode (no old-log-prob recompute, so the entropy comes from the update forward; `0 * entropy_loss` still backpropagates). Related: #1970.

Chunks now use an out-of-place backward, which costs one temporary of chunk size. The unchunked path keeps the in-place backward, so its memory use is unchanged.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=entropy+chunking+inplace and https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=vocab_parallel_entropy+inplace+operation (only the closed #1970).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

`tests/special_distributed/test_tensor_dict.py::test_vocab_parallel_entropy` now also backpropagates through the chunked entropy and compares it with the unchunked gradient.

`torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 tests/special_distributed/test_tensor_dict.py` on 4 GPUs (TP2):

- `main` with the new check: all ranks fail with the error above.
- this PR: `test_vocab_parallel_entropy passes`, `test_vocab_parallel_sum_pi_squared passes`.

Found in a Nemotron-H 30B-A3B run at 256K context (Megatron engine, bypass mode, `calculate_entropy=True`, chunked entropy), which crashed on the first update.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/megatron/tensor_parallel.py`: `_VocabParallelEntropy.forward` takes `inplace_backward` (default `True`); the chunked wrapper passes `False`. Backward returns `None` for the extra argument.
- `tests/special_distributed/test_tensor_dict.py`: chunked forward/backward check in the existing entropy test.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change; I reviewed it.

items.title: [fsdp] feat: support R3 router replay
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Wires R3 (rollout router replay) into the plain FSDP engine. The megatron and veomni engines already replay the rollout's MoE routing; the FSDP engine dropped.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Wires R3 (rollout router replay) into the plain FSDP engine. The megatron and veomni engines already replay the rollout's MoE routing; the FSDP engine dropped `routed_experts`.

With `actor.fsdp_config.router_replay.mode=R3` and `rollout.enable_rollout_routing_replay=True`, `FSDPEngineWithLMHead` passes the rollout's top-k expert indices to the model as the forward argument `routed_experts` in `compute_log_prob` and the actor update. The model applies them.

### Design & Code Changes

- `fsdp.yaml`: add `router_replay.mode` (default `disabled`).
- `engine_workers.py`: read the mode for `fsdp` / `fsdp2`, so the existing `enable_routing_replay` flag is set on the batch.
- `fsdp/transformer_impl.py`: `_pack_routed_experts` flattens `routed_experts` in the packed order of `input_ids` and appends the pad suffix. Shape `(1, total_nnz + pad_size, num_layers, topk)`, int64. Rows without a recorded choice are all zero and the model routes them natively (same convention as the veomni controller).
- `veomni/transformer_impl.py`: one line to keep VeOmni on its own replay hook.

Not supported, and rejected with an error instead of ignored: padded inputs (`use_remove_padding=False`), Ulysses SP, a batch without `routed_experts`, a model whose `forward` has no `routed_experts` parameter. R2 is not implemented.

No in-tree Hugging Face model takes `routed_experts` yet; this PR only adds the engine side.

### Test

```
pytest tests/workers/test_fsdp_router_replay_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_router_replay_engine_helpers_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_actor_router_replay_sync_on_cpu.py
22 passed
```

CPU only. Not run end to end on GPU yet.

items.title: [utils] fix: honor tokenizer.json when AutoTokenizer rebuilds the pre-tokenizer
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: now checks that the tokenizer returned by encodes like the it was loaded from and, on mismatch, loads the file as stored. transformers 5 rebuilds some tokenizer classes (e.g.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`hf_tokenizer` now checks that the tokenizer returned by `AutoTokenizer` encodes like the `tokenizer.json` it was loaded from and, on mismatch, loads the file as stored (`PreTrainedTokenizerFast`).

transformers 5 rebuilds some tokenizer classes (e.g. `LlamaTokenizer`) from the class recipe and ignores the pre-tokenizer stored in `tokenizer.json`. For a byte-level BPE vocabulary whose `tokenizer_config.json` names such a class, every space and newline is dropped without any error:

```
"Solve it  step by step.

	x = 3"  ->  "Solveitstepbystep.x=3"
```

Prompts, validation text and decoded responses become run-together text, and no train/rollout consistency check catches it because both sides see the same token ids. Reproduced with transformers 5.5.3, 5.12.0 and 5.17.0.

### Test

`tests/utils/test_hf_tokenizer_on_cpu.py`: a byte-level vocabulary filed under a generic class and under `LlamaTokenizerFast`; ids must equal the raw `tokenizers` encoding and decode back to the text. The Llama case fails without the fix.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. Tokenizers that already reproduce their `tokenizer.json`, and paths without a local `tokenizer.json`, are returned unchanged.

items.title: fix: Defer frozen MFSDP cleanup without input gradients
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: An MFSDP unit owning only frozen weights can still contain a separately sharded trainable child. If the unit's inputs do not require gradients, PyTorch fires its full backward hook when output gradients arrive.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

An MFSDP unit owning only frozen weights can still contain a separately sharded trainable child. If the unit's inputs do not require gradients, PyTorch fires its full backward hook when output gradients arrive. Resharding there frees frozen weights before internal backward consumes them to compute the child's gradients.

For ordinary backward, defer that unit's completion callback until the final autograd callback. Weight cleanup runs after every microbatch; automatic gradient synchronization runs only on the last microbatch, using the existing `microbatch(context, is_last=False)` scope to skip intermediate waits. An ordinary standalone backward still synchronizes automatically.

The combined 1F1B scheduler bypasses the root's autograd completion callback, so it calls `context.post_backward()` after each microbatch's full backward schedule completes. `finish_grad_sync()` only waits for submitted gradient reductions; MCore retains its explicit final synchronization after all backward work, including delayed weight gradients.

Fixes #7823. Trainable units retain their existing parameter-countdown completion timing.

## Validation
