items.title: test: prevent Git maintenance race in SWE workspace fixture
items.author: GoldArowana
items.summary: The SWE workspace-diff fixture commits a temporary repository and immediately copies its live directory. Automatic Git maintenance can remove after enumerates it, causing an unrelated CPU test failure before any workspace-diff assertions run.
items.body:
The SWE workspace-diff fixture commits a temporary repository and immediately copies its live `.git` directory. Automatic Git maintenance can remove `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` after `copytree` enumerates it, causing an unrelated CPU test failure before any workspace-diff assertions run.

Observed upstream evidence: [CPU job log](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/38084962578/job/114309457332) reports `shutil.Error` / missing `maintenance.lock` at the copytree call, with unstaged failing and staged/committed passing. [The report on #2451](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2451#issuecomment-6102325157) identifies it as unrelated to that PR's Qwen3.5 change.

Set repository-local `maintenance.auto=false` immediately after fixture initialization, before its first commit. The two-line, test-only change prevents this fixture from launching automatic maintenance while its object directory is copied. It changes no global Git configuration. All assertions remain intact: unstaged/staged/committed edits, image baseline exclusion, binary patch application, preserved index/HEAD, and resulting file contents. The existing CPU registration and `NUM_GPUS = 0` entry point remain unchanged.

Validation on Linux, Python 3.12.14, pytest 8.3.5 and Git 2.52.0, against main `58b0878679de339ec7844b45d884a87955a134be`:

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' SLIME_ACCELERATOR=cpu
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-p no:cacheprovider'
python tests/test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py
python -m pytest tests/test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py
pre-commit run --files tests/test_agent/test_swe_workspace_diff.py
```

- Direct CPU entry point and pytest: each 3 passed, exit 0.
- Controlled local reproduction used a real temporary Git repository and real automatic maintenance process. A low GC threshold triggered maintenance; a pre-auto-gc hook held it while copying. When copytree reached the lock, releasing the hook let Git remove its own lock, reproducing the same ENOENT. With repository-local `maintenance.auto=false` before the commit, commit and copytree passed without a maintenance hook or lock. The reproduction driver exited 0 after verifying both outcomes.
- Independent read-only review confirmed the exact two-line patch, the real-Git reproduction and preserved assertion coverage. All applicable configured pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed; hooks did not change the validated patch.

The local reproduction deliberately controls timing; it is not a claim of naturally reproducing the upstream intermittent failure. This setting prevents the fixture's automatic maintenance trigger, not externally launched explicit maintenance. Remote CI remains to run. No GPU, training, broad build or paid service was used.

AI assistance: implemented and independently reviewed with OpenAI Codex.

items.title: Add independent projection and sigmoid scaling for latent MoE
items.author: mkhona-nvidia
items.summary: Latent MoE changes expert preactivation scale as latent width changes. Add three independent controls, with defaults that preserve existing computation: -: multiply the hidden-to-latent output by before expert dispatch.
items.body:
Latent MoE changes expert preactivation scale as latent width changes. Add three independent controls, with defaults that preserve existing computation:

- `--moe-latent-projection-scaling`: multiply the hidden-to-latent output by `sqrt(hidden_size / moe_latent_size)` before expert dispatch.
- `--moe-latent-up-projection-scaling`: separately multiply the latent-to-hidden output by the same gain after optional normalization and projection, before shared expert addition.
- `--moe-latent-sigmoid-input-scale KAPPA` (default `1.0`): replace only `sigmoid(gate)` with `sigmoid(kappa * gate)` in routed latent experts.

Both projection gains default to false and remain independent of the sigmoid setting. The sigmoid scale preserves SwiGLU's multiplicative gate factor, the linear branch, and SiTU's gate/linear tanh arguments. Dense/shared experts and router inputs are unaffected. No parameters or checkpoint tensor shapes change; reuse the same settings when loading a checkpoint.

Thread the sigmoid scalar through eager and custom fused SwiGLU, hard-clamped SwiGLU, and SiTU, including biased and router-weighted variants. The manual backward includes the chain-rule factor: SwiGLU uses `sigmoid(kappa*v) * (1 + kappa*v*(1-sigmoid(kappa*v)))`; SiTU preserves its tanh derivative and multiplies the sigmoid derivative term by `kappa`. Router-probability gradients use the same scaled forward activation.

Non-unit sigmoid scales require positive latent width, MoE experts, and gated SiLU; all scales must be finite. TE native activations select the standard activation path for non-unit values. The integrated TE op fuser and inference-optimized MoE kernels reject non-unit values explicitly; use `--bias-activation-fusion` with the standard grouped or sequential expert implementation.

The README documents the computation, initialization dependence, and independent projection/sigmoid/normalization ablations. The up-projection gain is generally unnecessary with latent fan-in-aware initialization. No training-quality improvement or end-to-end variance preservation is assumed.

Validation:
- 142 isolated CPU checks passed using the complete production activation/fusion modules, the production MLP constructor/forward methods, exact new configuration guards, and committed test bodies. GPU compilation and unrelated distributed/configuration infrastructure were stubbed. These compare forward and input/bias/router-probability gradients with an independent eager reference at scales 0.0, 0.5, 1.7 and 1.0, verify dense/shared scoping and the TE native activation fallback, and exercise configuration independence.
- 48 additional FP32/BF16 cases exactly match the pre-change forward and backward at the default scale.
- 72 isolated projection checks cover all four down/up-gain combinations, values and gradients, biases, normalization, latent widths, invalid configurations and shared output addition.
- Added non-unit GPU bit-exact replay cases for activation kernels and complete latent MoE layers, including SiTU with both projection gains. Kernel determinism coverage passed.
- Required `tools/autoformat.sh` checks: Black, isort, Pylint and Ruff passed. Its non-blocking mypy stage reports 73 diagnostics on unchanged lines or missing optional dependencies; none on added lines.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- CUDA/Transformer Engine execution, full distributed unit tests, GPU replay, overlap and CUDA graph capture were not run in this macOS CPU environment and remain for GPU CI.

- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

Issue tracking: no linked issue.

Pre-checks:
- [x] Added relevant unit tests and GPU determinism replay cases.
- [x] Added configuration typing and documentation.
- [x] Ran the prescribed autoformatter checks (mypy diagnostics noted above).
- [ ] GPU/distributed tests and training ablations completed.

Pull request vetters can view their responsibilities [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/vetters).

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/contributors).

Could we also add an independent, user-defined sigmoid-input scale, e.g. `--moe-latent-sigmoid-input-scale`, defaulting to `1.0`?

The down-projection gain scales the entire expert input. We also need the ability to adjust only the sigmoid argument:

$$
\sigma(v)\\rightarrow\\sigma(\kappa v).
$$

This would allow tuning sigmoid sensitivity while leaving the multiplicative branches and SiTU’s tanh arguments unchanged. It should be independent of both projection gains and apply only to routed latent experts.

Please update the fused backward as well, including the $\kappa$ chain-rule factor, and check forward/backward agreement with the unfused reference for a non-unit scale.

items.title: [training_utils, hardware] fix: dispatch log-prob kernels by tensor device
items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: On an Ascend environment with installed, dispatches CPU logits to that NPU-only operator and raises. Installing Flash-Attention causes the equivalent problem because its availability takes priority over the input device.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

On an Ascend environment with `torch_npu.npu_cross_entropy_loss` installed, `logprobs_from_logits()` dispatches CPU logits to that NPU-only operator and raises `NotImplementedError`. Installing Flash-Attention causes the equivalent problem because its availability takes priority over the input device. This already forced the FSDP distillation CPU regression to replace real log-probs with a dummy tensor.

Select optimized cross-entropy using both kernel availability and `logits.device.type`: Flash-Attention for CUDA tensors, native CE for NPU tensors, and the existing PyTorch fallback elsewhere. The CUDA disable switch and `inplace_backward` argument continue to work. Remove the dummy FSDP log-prob stub and verify real numerical outputs in both padding modes.

Minimal failing example on the unmodified Ascend checkout:

```python
import torch
from verl.utils.torch_functional import logprobs_from_logits

logprobs_from_logits(torch.randn(2, 3, 13), torch.randint(13, (2, 3)))
# NotImplementedError: Could not run 'npu::npu_cross_entropy_loss'
# with arguments from the 'CPU' backend.
```

### Duplicate-work check

- [x] Searched [logprobs_from_logits device](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+logprobs_from_logits+device) and [device-aware logprobs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+device-aware+logprobs).
- #3852 restructures/compiles log-probs but retains the same availability-only kernel dispatch in its current diff; it does not fix this device mismatch. #8143 adds fused linear CANN CE in different modules and does not modify this helper.
- [x] Title follows the repository format.

### Test

Local environment: Ascend 910B2, CANN 8.5.2, torch 2.7.1+cpu with torch-npu 2.7.1.post2, Transformers 5.12.1, Python 3.12.0/aarch64.

```bash
python -m pytest -q -s tests/utils/test_logprobs_device_dispatch_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_logprobs_device_dispatch_on_npu.py tests/workers/test_distillation_topk_symmetry_on_cpu.py
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```

Before the fix, **20 failed / 4 passed**: the 18 CPU combinations reach device-only kernels, and the two real FSDP CPU log-prob paths fail against installed torch-npu after removing the dummy stub. A direct call with the real installed NPU operator also reproduces the `NotImplementedError` above.

After the fix, **44 passed**:

- CPU FP32/FP64/BF16 forward and gradients, 2D/strided 3D logits, and each optional-kernel availability combination.
- **18 real NPU cases**: FP32/FP16/BF16 outputs and gradients, native CE and fallback, including the case where Flash-Attention is reported available. The NPU CE operator is executed normally; a call-through spy checks that native CE is selected when available. Largest FP32 absolute errors: outputs **2.39e-7**, gradients **7.46e-8**; tested FP16/BF16 outputs and gradients match their reference exactly.
- Two CUDA **metadata** cases use FakeTensorMode on CPU to check flattening, output shape/device, `inplace_backward=False`, and the disable switch. CUDA hardware/kernel numerics were not run locally.
- Six FSDP distillation regressions, now using real CPU log-probs and checking their numerical values against log-softmax in both padding modes.

All **14** pre-commit hooks passed. The new CPU and NPU files are collected by existing workflows; the real NPU test skips when torch-npu or an NPU is absent. No full RL training or throughput benchmark was run; this PR claims device-correct dispatch, not a speedup or training-quality change.

### Remote CI status

As of 2026-10-11 (Asia/Shanghai), head `37a66fe24ae6d37e7164d39fc95f57eb190932c4` is awaiting maintainer approval to run fork Actions. All 33 workflow runs report `completed / action_required`. The [NPU unit tests run](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/actions/runs/38073663057) has 0 jobs, so upstream NPU CI has not executed. The 44 passing tests and 14 pre-commit checks above are local validations; upstream CI has neither passed nor started running. This approval gate is not a code/test failure.

### API and documentation

No public API or configuration change. The helper docstring now describes the device-aware selection. The optimized implementations and fallback math are unchanged.

items.title: [perf, hardware] fix: flush NPU profiler scopes on exceptions
items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: When an Ascend training stage raises inside, the wrapper skips, and. The failure's traceback can retain the running profiler: its framework operation trace has not been flushed when the exception reaches the caller.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When an Ascend training stage raises inside `NPUProfiler.annotate()`, the wrapper skips `mark_end_range()`, `step()` and `stop()`. The failure's traceback can retain the running profiler: its framework operation trace has not been flushed when the exception reaches the caller. `marked_timer()` similarly leaves its MSTX range open on failure.

Put scope cleanup in `finally` blocks so failing stages and timers close their markers and discrete profiles flush before returning the exception. If a profiler `step()` raises, still attempt `stop()`; continuous profiling also resets its process-level count after cleanup. Continuous stage annotations keep the outer profile running, as on the success path.

### Duplicate-work check

- [x] Searched [mstx exception](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+mstx+exception) and [profiler cleanup](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+profiler+cleanup): no matching open PR before submission.
- #7105 adds mini-batch scheduling in this area. Its current diff still invokes the stage before unguarded cleanup and does not fix these exception paths; this change is independent of scheduling.
- [x] Title follows the repository format.

### Test

Hardware: Ascend 910B2, CANN 8.5.2, torch 2.7.1+cpu with torch-npu 2.7.1.post2, Python 3.12.0/aarch64.

```bash
python -m pytest -q -s tests/utils/test_mstx_exception_cleanup_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_special_mstx_profile.py tests/utils/test_mstx_exception_cleanup_on_npu.py
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```

- Before the fix: all **7** new exception-path CPU tests fail; the new real-NPU regression also fails against a separate unmodified main checkout because the backend is still running after the stage exception.
- After the fix: **26 passed**, including the 18 existing NPU profiler tests and the new real-NPU trace test. All **14** pre-commit hooks pass.

The CPU tests inject stage, marker and profiler-step failures and check exception identity, single stage execution, range closure, backend shutdown and count reset. The NPU test uses the real `DistProfiler` dispatcher and real NPU profiler, retains the backend to expose premature reliance on garbage collection, and verifies:

1. The original stage exception propagates once, with the backend already stopped.
2. The nonempty framework operation trace exists immediately after failure.
3. Parsing that trace yields a complete `update_actor` MSTX interval (`ph="X"`, positive duration) and the real matrix-multiply operation.
4. A subsequent stage succeeds, stops its profile, and writes a second operation trace.

The NPU test runs in a bounded child process and explicitly cleans up a baseline profiler if its assertions fail. It is collected by the existing NPU unit-test workflow; absent torch-npu/device skips it on other runners. The CPU regression file is collected by the existing CPU workflow.

items.title: [model, hardware] fix: preserve Transformers 5 Qwen3-VL-MoE checkpoint layout on NPU
items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: Loading a native Transformers 5 Qwen3-VL-MoE checkpoint on Ascend fails after verl applies its NPU patches. The patch replaces the entire sparse-MoE class with the Transformers 4 implementation, reversing the last two dimensions of the expert parameters.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Loading a native Transformers 5 Qwen3-VL-MoE checkpoint on Ascend fails after verl applies its NPU patches. The patch replaces the entire sparse-MoE class with the Transformers 4 implementation, reversing the last two dimensions of the expert parameters. A small real HF checkpoint reproduces both mismatches:

```text
experts.gate_up_proj: checkpoint [4, 256, 64], patched model [4, 64, 256]
experts.down_proj:    checkpoint [4, 64, 128], patched model [4, 128, 64]
```

`Qwen3VLMoeTextModel.from_pretrained()` raises with `ignore_mismatched_sizes=False`. The same patch also replaces the native top-k router with `nn.Linear`, preventing HF's class-based router-output recording. FSDP calls `apply_npu_fsdp_patches()` before loading the model, so this affects the normal Ascend initialization path.

For the modern API, identified by `Qwen3VLMoeTextTopKRouter`, patch only `Qwen3VLMoeTextExperts.forward`. Reuse the existing Qwen3.5 NPU grouped-matmul implementation: both models have the same expert-forward arguments and `[experts, out_features, in_features]` stored weights. The native constructor, sparse block, router, checkpoint layout and output-recording hooks are preserved. The Transformers 4 branch continues using the existing NPU classes.

The modern contract is visible in the [upstream Transformers implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.12.1/src/transformers/models/qwen3_vl_moe/modeling_qwen3_vl_moe.py).

### Duplicate-work check

- [x] Searched [Qwen3VLMoeTextExperts](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+Qwen3VLMoeTextExperts) and [qwen3_vl_moe npu_patch](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+qwen3_vl_moe+npu_patch): neither returned an open PR before submission.
- #5572 concerns vision positional embedding device placement; this fixes the expert checkpoint and router contracts. The existing Qwen3.5 grouped-matmul implementation is reused rather than reimplemented.
- [x] Title follows the repository format.

### Test

Local hardware: one Ascend 910B2, CANN 8.5.2, torch 2.7.1+cpu with torch-npu 2.7.1.post2, Python 3.12.0/aarch64.

```bash
python -m pytest -q -s tests/models/test_qwen3_vl_moe_npu_patch_on_cpu.py tests/models/test_qwen3_vl_moe_npu_patch.py
```

| Transformers | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 5.12.1 | 7 passed |
| 5.5.3 (current requirements minimum) | 7 passed |
| 4.57.6, CPU schema tests | 1 passed, 1 skipped (modern-router test) |

Before the fix, both CPU regression tests fail against real HF classes; the two-layer native checkpoint also fails `from_pretrained()` with the mismatches above. After the fix, the tests cover strict weight loading, FP16/BF16 outputs, input gradients and every parameter gradient against native HF on the same NPU, top-1/top-2 routing (including empty experts), and native-checkpoint → NPU forward → save → reload. The latter verifies exact parameter equality, bitwise output equality after reload, and `output_router_logits=True` for each layer.

Maximum relative L2 errors across both modern versions and all cases:

| dtype | MoE output | input/parameter gradients |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | 0.468% | 0.970% |
| FP16 | 0.0663% | 0.1014% |

The tests bound elementwise error using dtype epsilon and independently bound relative L2 error. Normalized top-1 router gradients are checked against mathematical zero with an absolute 1e-6 bound. Native CPU/NPU top-k rounding differences are avoided by comparing the MoE implementations on the same device.

`pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: all 14 hooks passed. The NPU regression file is explicitly added to `npu_unit_tests.yml`, whose general test command excludes `tests/models/`; the CPU file is collected by the existing CPU workflow.

Validation uses small real models and real NPU operators. Full 30B/235B RL training and throughput benchmarking were not run; this PR makes no training-quality or speedup claim.

### Remote CI status

As of 2026-10-11 (Asia/Shanghai), head `9be89f0add5cac799972b1f17cc6f99f71aa96cc` is awaiting maintainer approval to run Actions from this fork. items.title: [fsdp] fix: preserve FP32 buffers when casting the model to model_dtype
items.author: li-lizhe
items.summary: converts registered buffers as well as parameters, so floating-point buffers that the model implementation builds in FP32 are rounded to the model dtype. is the visible case: it is constructed in FP32, and rounding it to BF16 is irreversible — a later policy o…
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #8154.

`FSDPEngine._build_module()` ends with a blanket `module.to(torch_dtype)`. `Tensor.to(dtype)` converts registered buffers as well as parameters, so floating-point buffers that the model implementation builds in FP32 are rounded to the model dtype. `RotaryEmbedding.inv_freq` is the visible case: it is constructed in FP32, and rounding it to BF16 is irreversible — a later `buffer_dtype=torch.float32` policy only upcasts the already-rounded values, so the positional encodings (and the resulting per-token log probabilities) change.

This PR casts the floating-point (and complex) **parameters** to `model_dtype` and leaves registered buffers at their construction precision. Integer tensors, meta-initialized parameters and tied `Parameter` identity are unaffected. The helper `verl.utils.torch_dtypes.cast_module_params_to_dtype` is device-agnostic and adds no dependency.

#### Why this is not a duplicate

- Exact issue search: [open PRs mentioning #8154](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8154+in%3Abody) → no other PR.
- Keyword search: [open PRs mentioning `inv_freq`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+inv_freq) → no other PR.
- The only related open PR is #7165, which makes the same cast honor Hugging Face `_keep_in_fp32_modules*`. Qwen3 / Qwen3.5 declare neither list, so their RoPE buffers still lose precision through #7165's unchanged "no keep-list" path. This change keeps every registered buffer at its construction precision and is independent of the keep-list mechanism.

#### AI assistance disclosure

Hermes Agent assisted with the implementation, the tests and the PR drafting. The human submitter reviewed the change and takes responsibility for it. The head commit carries an `Assisted-by: Hermes Agent` trailer.

## Test Plan

New CPU test: `tests/utils/test_cast_module_params_on_cpu.py` (6 cases; picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml` through the `*_on_cpu.py` suffix).

```text
python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_cast_module_params_on_cpu.py
6 passed
```

Run on a CPU-only host with `torch 2.10.0+cpu`, through a minimal `verl` package shim (importing the real `verl` package pulls Ray, which is not installed on that host). Standalone check of the underlying mechanism with the same torch build: the old `module.to(torch.bfloat16)` turns the FP32 `inv_freq`-style buffer into BF16 and changes its values (max frequency error `9.77e-05`), while `cast_module_params_to_dtype(module, torch.bfloat16)` leaves the buffer FP32 and bit-identical, casts FP32 parameters to BF16, and leaves integer tensors untouched.

## Not tested

- No end-to-end FSDP forward with a real checkpoint; the log-probability deltas in #8154 were measured by the reporter on a CUDA host and are not re-measured here.
- Not exercised on NPU or CUDA (the change itself is device-agnostic).

items.title: Reuse the index file handle when creating its memory map
items.author: heartplus
items.summary: When reads metadata from an index header, it opens the file once to read the header and again inside. At large distributed-training scale, the extra open can add unnecessary metadata RPCs on distributed filesystems.
items.body:
When `_IndexReader` reads metadata from an index header, it opens the `.idx` file once to read the header and again inside `numpy.memmap`. At large distributed-training scale, the extra open can add unnecessary metadata RPCs on distributed filesystems.

Create the memory map from the already-open file object inside the same context manager. The Python file object is closed after mapping, while the mapping keeps its existing lifetime and cleanup. The pre-supplied metadata path still opens the index only once.

Validation:
- Local CPU smoke check using the actual `DType` and `_IndexReader` class definitions extracted with AST, real NumPy mappings, and Python audit hooks: header-reading opens decrease from 2 to 1; pre-supplied metadata opens remain at 1.
- Checked both text and multimodal indices, lengths/pointers/document indices/modes, indexed access, mapping cleanup, and invalid header/version rejection.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Full GPU unit tests were not run (no CUDA/container environment on this macOS host). `tools/autoformat.sh` was attempted but stopped because `black` is not installed.
- No distributed-filesystem performance benchmark was run; the measured improvement is the removed file open.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: prevent parameter corruption during FSDP2 CPU offload
items.author: SelfDLer
items.summary: Prevent silent parameter corruption when moving FSDP2 models to CPU with uneven parameter shards. The investigation traced the problem to parameter values changing during CPU offloading, without any forward pass, backward pass, or optimizer update.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent silent parameter corruption when moving FSDP2 models to CPU with uneven parameter shards.

I identified this issue while debugging Qwen3-Omni training and evaluation failures reported in:

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/issues/660
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8039

The observed symptoms included degraded evaluation accuracy in multi-node training. The investigation traced the problem to parameter values changing during CPU offloading, without any forward pass, backward pass, or optimizer update.

This PR uses blocking device-to-CPU transfers in both affected verl paths:

- Runtime offloading through `offload_fsdp2_model_to_cpu`.
- Initialization-time offloading inside `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict`, which reuses the same helper.

This follows the discussion in:
https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/741#issuecomment-6139999835

### Root Cause

`model.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` can leave a device-to-CPU transfer in progress while FSDP2 processes the converted parameter.

For uneven shards, `FSDPModule._apply` calls `FSDPParam.reset_sharded_param`, which may allocate new padded CPU storage and copy the transferred local tensor into it. This CPU copy can read the transfer destination before the asynchronous D2H transfer has completed.

Incorrect values can then persist in the new padded storage. Synchronizing after the entire `model.to()` call returns does not repair values that have already been copied into that storage.

This is not specific to NPU: I reproduced the same failure on CUDA by queuing additional computation before the transfer.

### Design & Code Changes

- Use `model.to("cpu", non_blocking=False)` in `offload_fsdp2_model_to_cpu`, so each transfer completes before FSDP2 can consume its CPU result.
- Route the CPU move in `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict` through that helper with `empty_cache=False`, preserving the initialization path's cache behavior.
- Keep the CPU-to-device helper's `non_blocking=True` argument.
- Update transfer-policy tests to require blocking D2H on both CUDA and NPU.
- Generalize the NPU regression into `test_fsdp2_model_cpu_offload.py`, shared by CUDA and NPU CI. It covers nested FSDP2 modules, large even/uneven weights, and the original small bias vectors.
- Queue warmed-up matrix multiplications on the actual conversion stream and check both default and non-default streams. Change parameter values between trials and check CPU values after synchronization to distinguish persistent corruption from an unfinished transfer.
- Update the CUDA regression so it validates parameter correctness rather than requiring the pinned allocation associated with the previous non-blocking D2H path.

The fix uses existing PyTorch module conversion behavior and does not patch private FSDP2 internals or introduce backend-specific synchronization code.

### Related Work

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7347 enabled non-blocking runtime FSDP2 model transfers for performance. This PR changes the D2H policy to restore correctness. The initialization-time asynchronous CPU move predates #7347 and is covered here as well.
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8057 addresses pinned-memory allocation configuration. It does not establish transfer completion before FSDP2 reads CPU data.
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/741 provides a downstream workaround. This PR addresses the shared verl helpers used by downstream callers.

### Validation

#### Investigation and downstream validation

The standalone reproducer uses two accelerator processes and a nested FSDP2 model with either evenly or unevenly sharded weights. It writes known parameter values, saves an independent blocking CPU reference, and checks exact equality after offloading.

No forward pass, backward pass, or optimizer update is involved.

| Environment | Configuration | Uneven shards: asynchronous D2H followed by synchronization | Other cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NPU: PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post6 | 10 iterations, no additional queued computation | 10/20 rank-trials failed | All passed |
| CUDA: PyTorch 2.11.0, CUDA 13.0 | 50 iterations, 64 queued matrix multiplications before each transfer | 50/100 rank-trials failed | All passed |

The other cases include evenly sharded controls, blocking D2H transfers, and waiting immediately after each individual D2H conversion. Comparisons use `rtol=0` and `atol=0`.

These are aggregate rank-trial counts; they do not establish that every failure occurred on the same rank.

I also verified that the downstream fix resolves the reported issues and allows two-node Qwen3-Omni training to run successfully. The downstream tests and pre-commit checks passed.

These results establish the failure mechanism and validate the downstream workaround. They are separate from validation of the final changes in this verl PR.

#### Regression coverage

The relevant tests cover:

- Transfer policy for runtime and initialization-time CPU offloading.
- Cache-release behavior and buffer placement during initialization.
- Nested FSDP2 modules with even and uneven shards.
- Exact CPU parameter values and device round-trip correctness.
- Queued computation before runtime offloading on default and non-default streams.
- Per-rank failure reporting after the critical transfer window.

The updated CPU transfer-policy tests were run against the previous NPU-only implementation and the revised implementation:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/utils/test_fsdp2_model_transfer_on_cpu.py -k 'not sharded_save'
```

- Before: 4 failed, 9 passed, 1 deselected. All four failures were CUDA D2H policy checks, covering runtime offloading and initialization on both ranks.
- After: 13 passed, 1 deselected.
- The deselected test is the existing two-process CPU snapshot test, which checks a separate save-to-CPU helper.

These tests verify transfer policy and control flow using mocked device transfers. They ran with PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu and imported `verl.utils.fsdp_utils` from the modified checkout. Accelerator numerical correctness is covered by the distributed regressions listed below.

Ruff lint and formatting, Python syntax, workflow YAML parsing, license checks, device-API checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

I ran the revised numerical regression on a single node with two NPUs. It passed for both default and non-default streams:
```bash
env -u DIST_INIT_METHOD \
  PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PYTHONPATH" \
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
  torchrun \
    --nnodes=1 \
    --node_rank=0 \
    --nproc-per-node=2 \
    --rdzv_backend=static \
    --master_addr=127.0.0.1 \
    --master_port=29517 \
    tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_model_cpu_offload.py
```
Result:
```text
FSDP2 npu CPU offload passed: 2 ranks, default and non-default streams
```
This run verified initialization-time offloading, nested FSDP2 modules with even and uneven shards, repeated runtime offloading with queued computation, and exact parameter values on CPU and after restoring to NPU (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`).

Pre-commit checks also passed for this revision.

### Performance Considerations

This change prioritizes parameter correctness over asynchronous D2H overlap.

Blocking D2H can increase host-side waiting and may change whether the resulting CPU storage is pinned. Consequently, keeping `non_blocking=True` in the CPU-to-device helper does not guarantee the same H2D overlap or throughput as before.

The performance impact of this broader verl change has not been quantified. The successful downstream training runs are correctness evidence, not a controlled performance comparison.

### API and Usage

No public API or configuration changes are required.

Existing callers of the two affected helpers automatically receive the corrected D2H behavior.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Read the contribution guide.
- [x] Search for related PRs:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+FSDP2+offload
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+repadding
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+non_blocking
- [x] Continue the existing PR #8187 rather than opening a duplicate.

items.title: [roadmap] verl 26Q4 roadmap
items.author: wuxibin89
items.summary: Q4 2026 roadmap for verl covering low-precision training strategies (FP8/MXFP4/NVFP4), rollout optimizations, and train/rollout quantization alignment.
items.body:
# Model Engine
## Low Precision Training
### Background
**Goals in RL**
- Cheaper rollout and inference-only forwards (ref, teacher, old_log_prob): less memory, less memory traffic, faster GEMM.
- Lower train/rollout mismatch once rollout is quantized: training should see the same quantization as sampling.

**Two routes**
| Route | Training compute | Training speedup | Key issues |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 + QAT | BF16, fake quant (quantize-dequantize + STE) on weight / act / KV in the rollout format | no | quantizer parity with rollout kernels; QAT noise raises gradient variance |
| Real low-precision compute | FP8 / MXFP8 / MXFP4 / NVFP4 GEMMs (e.g. TE), FP32 master weights | yes | rowwise/columnwise copies per format; low-precision FSDP all-gather; train/rollout format alignment |

**Where FP32 master weights live** decides the backend design:
- In the optimizer (Megatron): model holds BF16 or low-precision compute weights, cast once per optimizer step on the
  local shard; easy to keep low-precision params persistent.
- In the model (FSDP2 / VeOmni): model holds sharded FP32 params, cast to compute dtype at every all-gather; any optimizer
  works, high-precision weights always available (checkpoint, weight sync), cast cost repeats per micro-batch.

**Formats**
| Format | Block | Scale | fprop / dgrad see the same W | HW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 per-tensor | tensor | FP32 | yes | Hopper+ |
| FP8 blockwise | A 1x128, W 128x128 | FP32 or pow2 | yes for W (2D block) | Hopper |
| MXFP8 | 1x32 | E8M0 | no (rowwise and columnwise quantized separately) | Blackwell |
| MXFP4 | 1x32 | E8M0 | no | Blackwell (Hopper via FP4->FP8 dequant) |
| NVFP4 | 1x16 + per-tensor FP32 | E4M3 | yes when weight uses 16x16 2D (TE default) | Blackwell |

**DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 reference**
- MXFP4 QAT for routed experts and the indexer QK path; FP32 master -> FP4 -> lossless dequant to FP8 128x128, so
  training reuses the FP8 framework and dgrad uses the same W as fprop (V4 §3.4).
- Real FP4 weights for rollout, ref and teacher forwards (V4 §5.2.1).
- KV cache: FP8 + BF16 RoPE dims (V4 §2.3.4); FP4 main KV cache QAT, SWA KV stays FP8 (V4.1 §2.4.4).
- Comm: BF16 + stochastic rounding for MoE grad sync, all-to-all + local FP32 sum (V4 §3.5.1).
- Batch-invariant / deterministic kernels for bitwise train/infer alignment (V4 §3.3).

### Existing
#### BF16 + QAT
[NVFP4 QAT (Quantization-Aware Training) in verl](https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/low_precision/nvfp4_qat.html)
| Backend | QAT format (training) | Rollout format | Implementation | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSDP | NVFP4 W4A16 (group 16) | NVFP4 W4A16, vLLM `compressed-tensors` | `verl/utils/qat/` | Qwen3-8B-Base, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base |
| Megatron | NVFP4 W4A16 (group 16) | NVFP4 W4A16, vLLM `modelopt` | `verl/utils/modelopt/` | Qwen3-8B-Base, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base |
| VeOmni | FP8 blockwise (W 128x128, A 1x128; linear / KV NoPE / indexer QK / MoE) + FP4 1x32 routed experts | FP8 blockwise + MXFP4 experts, vLLM `Mxfp4MoEMethod` refit | `veomni/ops/qat/`, `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_fp4_utils.py` | [DeepSeek-V4-Flash](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/VeOmni/pull/1089) |

#### Real low-precision compute
[FP8 RL in verl](https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/low_precision/fp8.html)
| Backend | Mode | Training compute | Rollout compute | Implementation | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSDP | rollout-only | BF16 | FP8 blockwise, vLLM / SGLang / TRT-LLM | `{vllm,sglang}/*fp8_utils.py` | Qwen3-8B-Base, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base |
| Megatron | rollout-only | BF16 | FP8 blockwise, vLLM / SGLang / TRT-LLM | same as above | Qwen3-30B-A3B |
| Megatron | E2E | FP8 blockwise via TE (`fp8: hybrid`, `fp8_recipe: blockwise`) + FP8 optimizer | FP8 blockwise, vLLM | Megatron-Bridge + TE | Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-30B-A3B (Hopper); on Blackwell TE runs blockwise as MXFP8 ([#6172](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6172)) |
| VeOmni | - | - | - | - | not supported |

### Q4 Plan
| Priority | Common | Megatron | VeOmni |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | train/rollout quantizer parity | DeepSeek-V4 FP4->FP8 lossless path | DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 QAT E2E |
| P1 | unified recipe config; low-precision inference-only forwards; low-precision comm | Blackwell MXFP8 E2E; Blackwell NVFP4 training | torchao low-precision compute + FSDP2 all-gather; torchao NVFP4/MXFP4 QAT |
| P2 | batch-invariant / deterministic kernels | FP8 optimizer states; MoE W4A8 | Muon + BF16 Newton-Schulz |

#### Common
- [ ] P0 Train/rollout quantizer parity: same quantizer + scale fmt (ue8m0/e4m3), report mismatch KL & rollout throughput
- [ ] P1 Unified low-precision recipe config across FSDP/VeOmni/Megatron/Automodel
  - today: `rollout.quantization`, `megatron.override_transformer_config.fp8*`, `fsdp_config.qat`, `megatron.qat`, veomni `qat_implementation`, automodel `enable_fp8`
  - recipe = train compute fmt + QAT (weight/act/KV fmt, modules) + rollout fmt; fail fast on train/rollout fmt mismatch
- [ ] P1 Batch-invariant / deterministic train+rollout kernels for bitwise alignment

#### Megatron
Route: Megatron-LM + TransformerEngine, master weights in the optimizer.
- Compute weights are BF16, or FP8/MXFP8 with `fp8_param` / `fp8_param_gather`; DistributedOptimizer / Megatron-FSDP
  keep sharded FP32 main params and cast back after each step.
- TE provides the low-precision GEMMs and recipes (per-tensor delayed/current, blockwise, MXFP8, NVFP4) and the
  rowwise/columnwise copies; under MXFP8, Megatron-FSDP gathers rowwise for fprop and columnwise for dgrad.
- QAT goes through modelopt; HF <-> mcore weights and FP8 export go through Megatron-Bridge.
- Fit: large-scale MoE (TP/PP/EP/CP), mature FP8 stack. Cost: new models need mcore / Bridge support.

- [ ] P0 DeepSeek-V4 FP4->FP8 lossless path: FP4 fake quant in FP32 master -> FP8 (128x128) cast, reuse TE blockwise + `fp8_param_gather` (V4 §3.4)
  - 2D 128x128 block => fprop/dgrad use the same W, no re-quant of W^T
  - monitor max/min FP4 sub-block scale ratio per 128x128 block, fallback when lossless condition breaks
- [ ] P1 Blackwell MXFP8 E2E: TE MXFP8 + `fp8_param_gather` + `reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag`
  - resolve train MXFP8 (1x32, fprop/dgrad W differ) vs rollout blockwise 128x128 (DeepGEMM) format mismatch
- [ ] P1 Blackwell NVFP4 training: TE NVFP4 recipe (16x16 2D weight, RHT, SR) + vLLM NVFP4 W4A4 rollout
- [ ] P2 FP8 optimizer states, MoE W4A8 (FP4 x FP8 GEMM)

#### VeOmni
Route: FSDP2 + torchao, master weights in the model.
- Model holds sharded FP32 params; FSDP2 `MixedPrecisionPolicy` casts each shard to BF16 at all-gather; any standard
  optimizer works unchanged.
- QAT is VeOmni's own fake-quant ops (`veomni/ops/qat/`, STE) wired into patchgen-generated HF modeling, which makes
  new models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4) quick to bring up.
- Real low-precision compute is to come from torchao: float8 / MX linear, plus float8 FSDP2 all-gather that quantizes
  the high-precision shard before gather (low-precision comm without persistent low-precision weights).
- Fit: HF-native models, fast model bring-up, flexible recipes. Cost: no low-precision compute yet; current TileLang
  QAT kernels are SM90 + BF16 only.

- [ ] P0 DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 QAT E2E (blocks Model Support: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
- [ ] P1 torchao low-precision compute: float8 (tensorwise/rowwise), MXFP8 on Blackwell
  - low-precision FSDP2 all-gather: quantize sharded high-precision weights before gather (float8 / MXFP8)
- [ ] P1 torchao fake-quant QAT for NVFP4 / MXFP4

## Model Support
- [ ] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- [ ] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
- [ ] GLM-5.3-Flash

# Rollout
## Async rollout
- [ ] P0 Token-level interrupt + persist KV cache / routing across weight switch, no re-prefill on resume
- [ ] P1 Sample-level dispatch: dispatch next prompt once #completed samples >= group size

## Weight refit optimization
- [ ] Delta shard support for quantized `(weight, scale)`
- [ ] NCCL M2N reshard https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8088

## Performance optimization
- Load balance: session-affinity routing for multi-turn agents
- Centralized kv-cache pooling
- kv-cache offload

## Fault tolerance
- [ ] Disaggregate rollout replica restart
- [ ] Disaggregate trainer restart

## Uni-Agent
[Uni-Agent Q4 roadmap](https://github.com/verl-project/uni-agent/issues/191)

# Accelerator support
We will keep enhancing multi-accelerator support: built-in for NVIDIA / Ascend / AMD, and out-of-tree for others via
[verl-hardware-plugin](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin).

## AMD ROCm
- [x] ROCm platform backend [#6702](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/6702), MI300 e2e CI [#6668](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/6668)
- [x] DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO on AMD GPUs [#7050](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7050), on MI355X with QAT / FP8 / BF16 [#8146](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8146)

## Google TPU
- [x] Ray TPU resource discovery [#7849](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7849), SFT with TorchTitan engine [#8098](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8098)
- [x] Plugin: TPU platform [plugin#18](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin/pull/18), TorchTitan TPU engine [plugin#31](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin/pull/31), vLLM rollout on multi-host TPU [plugin#34](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin/pull/34), Raiden P2P weight sync [plugin#37](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin/pull/37)
- [x] GRPO with TorchTitan + vLLM via plugin [#8155](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8155)

# Trainer
- [ ] Deprecate `verl/experimental/fully_async_policy|one_step_off_policy` to verl-recipe
- [ ] Remove V0 trainer `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`

# verl-omni
verl-omni Q4 roadmap: https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/issues/700

items.title: test: register Megatron bindings regression in CPU CI
items.author: GoldArowana
items.summary: The Megatron bindings regression test added in #2453 is missing from the fixed CPU matrix. It also has no direct-execution entry point, so exits successfully without running its assertion, and no declaration, so defaults to eight GPUs.
items.body:
The Megatron bindings regression test added in #2453 is missing from the fixed CPU matrix. It also has no direct-execution entry point, so `python tests/test_reloadable_process_group_megatron_bindings.py` exits successfully without running its assertion, and no `NUM_GPUS` declaration, so `run-ci-changed` defaults to eight GPUs.

This adds the standard pytest entry point and `NUM_GPUS = 0`, registers the existing test beside the other reloadable-process-group CPU tests, and regenerates the workflow with the official generator. The three-file diff adds 13 lines; production code and the critic fixture are untouched.

Validation on Linux, Python 3.12.14, pytest 8.3.5 and official PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu, using `/workspace/slime-cpu-setup/venv/bin/python` as `python`:

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' SLIME_ACCELERATOR=cpu
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export PYTHONPATH=. PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-p no:cacheprovider'
python tests/test_reloadable_process_group_megatron_bindings.py
python -m pytest tests/test_reloadable_process_group_megatron_bindings.py
python .github/workflows/generate_github_workflows.py
pre-commit run --files tests/test_reloadable_process_group_megatron_bindings.py .github/workflows/pr-test.yml.j2 .github/workflows/pr-test.yml
```

- Original direct execution at base `22a89f96835969a47055a659c588f46151f8b07a`: exit 0, no pytest session or assertion execution.
- Updated direct execution and pytest: each 1 passed, exit 0.
- Regression mutation in a temporary source copy: disabled only `_rebind_imported_collectives(replacements)`, retaining torch.distributed wrapping. The child exited normally; all three Megatron binding identity checks became false and the existing assertion failed (1 failed, exit 1).
- Official workflow generation: exit 0. Independent read-only review confirmed generated YAML exactly matches the template and reviewed the mutation evidence.
- All applicable configured pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. The reviewed patch was unchanged by hooks.

The test only spawns a subprocess, supplies fake Megatron bindings, patches function references and compares identities. It creates no process group, invokes no collective and allocates no accelerator tensor. Missing NumPy produced a warning but did not affect the test. This is local CPU coverage evidence; remote CI remains to run. No GPU, training, numerical validation or real Megatron collective validation was performed.

items.title: [dev] misc fixes while bring-up chunk-wise cuda graph
items.author: HaochenYuan
items.summary: Independent fixes collected while developing chunk-wise CUDA graphs (#5258); none depends on that feature. Fixes PP1 + SP + MTP + packed sequences:. [Discussion: /review model=claude mode=strict]
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Independent fixes collected while developing chunk-wise CUDA graphs (#5258); none depends on that feature.

- **Padding mask under SP + MTP** (`gpt_model.py`, `hybrid_model.py`): the decoder gets the sequence-parallel-scattered padding mask, the post-process keeps the caller's full-length mask (MTP rolls it with `input_ids`/`position_ids`; MoE layers re-align it themselves). Fixes PP1 + SP + MTP + packed sequences: `_roll_tensors_packed_seq: All packed CP1 tensors must have the same sequence length`.
- **KDA under CUDA graph capture** (`kda.py`): skip the `torch.equal(cu_seqlens_q, cu_seqlens_kv)` host sync while a stream is capturing, as GDN already does; the boundaries were validated in the eager warm-up.
- **Batch dict aliasing** (`data_schedule.py`): work on a shallow copy of the iterator's batch. The per-rank slicing rebinds entries in place, and replay paths (`RerunDataIterator`, the PagedStashRunner dropless retry) serve the same dict objects again expecting the pre-slice tensors.
- **CUDA context on the recompute thread** (`utils.with_current_cuda_device`, used by `tensor_parallel.checkpoint` and `te_checkpoint`): the recompute runs on the autograd worker thread; kernels launched through the CUDA driver directly (cuTile in the fused mHC kernels) need a current context there, which torch only creates lazily (`Failed to launch cuTile kernel: invalid device context`).
- **HybridModel + `--cross-entropy-fusion-impl linear`**: output layer is `LinearCrossEntropyModule`, same fused linear + CE branch as GPTModel.
- **Fine-grained offload NUMA hint** (`training.py`): a failing `set_ideal_affinity_for_current_gpu` warns per rank instead of aborting (fails when the job's cgroup holds no CPU of the GPU's socket).
- `fp8_utils._get_custom_recipe`: error message as plain string literals (black 26 rewraps the triple-quoted string with trailing blanks in any PR touching the file).

Validation: GB200, 4 ranks. `test_gpt_model.py`, `test_hybrid_model.py`, `test_kda.py`, `test_sequence_packing.py`, `test_random.py`, `test_fp8_utils.py` give the same results as pristine dev (remaining failures are missing MambaSSM and 8-rank-only cases). The PP1+SP+MTP fix was exercised end to end on a DSv3-shaped GPT proxy (TP2 PP1 EP2 SP, THD packing, MTP) in #5258.

items.title: [dev] Share the fused compact DSA indexer workspace across CSA layers
items.author: HaochenYuan
items.summary: Under CUDA graphs the fused compact DSA indexer keeps a persistent workspace per static geometry (MXFP8 q/k quantization destinations, packed scales, candidate offsets) that must be prepared outside capture. Every CSA layer owned its own copy: about 7 Gi…
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Under CUDA graphs the fused compact DSA indexer (`--dsa-kernel-backend cudnn`, `--dsa-indexer-precision mxfp8`) keeps a persistent workspace per static geometry (MXFP8 q/k quantization destinations, packed scales, candidate offsets) that must be prepared outside capture. Every CSA layer owned its own copy: about 7 GiB per rank on DSv4 at 16K tokens per rank.

- All CSA layers built from one `TransformerConfig` now share one workspace per geometry and balanced-indexer slot (`_CompactIndexerWorkspaceStore`, keyed on the config). The layers of a graph run serially on one stream and nothing in the workspace outlives the indexer dispatch that fills it, so sharing only removes duplicates.
- New config field `dsa_compact_indexer_workspace_sharing` (default `True`; `--no-dsa-compact-indexer-workspace-sharing` restores per-layer workspaces), golden-config entry, doc paragraph in `cuda_graph.md`.
- Tests: kernel-level workspace tests (`test_csa_compact_indexer_workspace_sharing.py`) and a contract test in the CSA test class that a workspace prepared by one layer serves the capture of another.

Validation: GB200, 4 ranks: CSA test files 118 passed. DSv4-flash 1M on 128 GPUs with chunk-wise graphs: last-stage NVML memory 173.8 → 149.4 GiB together with linear CE (#5258 validation).

items.title: [dev] chained optimizer fix for cuda graph
items.author: HaochenYuan
items.summary: combined the per-optimizer norms with, a host synchronization that makes the optimizer step uncapturable into a CUDA graph. Keeping the norm as a float32 device tensor instead changes the clip coefficient by one float32 rounding and breaks exact golden va…
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
`ChainedOptimizer.get_grad_norm` combined the per-optimizer norms with `math.sqrt(sum(x**2))`, a host synchronization that makes the optimizer step uncapturable into a CUDA graph (`--optimizer-cuda-graph`). Keeping the norm as a float32 device tensor instead changes the clip coefficient by one float32 rounding and breaks exact golden values of multi-optimizer runs (Muon), as the `gpt3_moe_..._muon` functional test showed.

- `get_grad_norm` now returns `torch.sqrt(sum(x**2).to(torch.float64))`: squares summed in fp32 as before, root in float64 on the device. CUDA's double `sqrt`, like `math.sqrt`, is IEEE correctly rounded, so the value equals the Python-float path bit for bit and no host sync remains.
- `clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32` forms the coefficient in the norm's dtype (float64 → same arithmetic as the Python path) and rounds it once to fp32 before TE's `multi_tensor_scale_tensor`, which reads the scale as `float*`. The fp32 tensor path used by single-optimizer runs is unchanged (`.to(torch.float32)` is a no-op there).
- Tests: the clipped gradients from a float64 device norm equal those from the Python-float path (`torch.equal`, clipped and unclipped branches); the chained float64 norm equals `math.sqrt(float(sum))`.

Validation: 4-GPU A/B of the Muon functional-test configuration (EP4, clip 1.0, deterministic, 20 iterations): loss, grad norm and num-zeros identical to dev on every iteration; DSv4 proxy with `--optimizer-cuda-graph` + chunk-wise graphs captures and replays (no measurable step-time change).

items.title: [ci, fsdp] fix: pin PEFT to 0.20.0 for FSDP1 LoRA compatibility
items.author: MrJVium
items.summary: Pin to in to restore FSDP1 LoRA compatibility. PEFT 0.21.0 introduced a state-dict handling refactor in. [Discussion: <!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai --> The Ascend workflow enables G]
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Pin `peft` to `0.20.0` in `requirements-npu.txt` to restore FSDP1 LoRA compatibility.

PEFT 0.21.0 introduced a state-dict handling refactor in
[huggingface/peft#3490](https://github.com/huggingface/peft/pull/3490).
For nested FSDP1 models, PEFT may fail to match adapter module names against
the FSDP state dict and return an empty LoRA state dict, as tracked in
[huggingface/peft#3876](https://github.com/huggingface/peft/issues/3876).

In the affected verl workflow, the empty state dict is passed to vLLM, which
raises `StopIteration` while accessing the first LoRA module. The receiver
then exits without sending an ACK, causing the sender to hang until the CI
job times out.

The regression was observed in the following Ascend E2E job with PEFT 0.21.2:

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/actions/runs/37787622168/job/113346339988

PEFT 0.20.0 is the latest known working version for this FSDP1 LoRA path.
This pin is intended as a temporary compatibility measure until the upstream
fix for nested `_fsdp_wrapped_module` prefixes is included in a stable PEFT
release.

Related verl PR:

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8152 adds fail-fast validation for
  an empty LoRA state dict. It improves diagnostics but does not restore
  correct adapter state-dict extraction. This PR instead prevents the
  regression by selecting the known-good PEFT version.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Query:
  https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+PEFT+FSDP1+LoRA
- [x] Format the PR title as `[env, fsdp] fix: pin PEFT to 0.20.0 for FSDP1 LoRA compatibility`

### Test

Root-cause evidence from the failed job:

- Installed dependency: `peft==0.21.2`
- `layered_summon` returned an empty LoRA state dict
- vLLM failed in `_create_merged_loras_inplace` with `StopIteration`
- The distributed job subsequently hung waiting for synchronization

Validation to complete before requesting review:

```bash
python -c "import peft; assert peft.__version__ == '0.20.0', peft.__version__"

items.title: [perf] fix: read head_dim from config for Qwen3-VL FLOPS estimation
items.author: kkyyxhll
items.summary: Fixes in to read from the model config instead of deriving it as, which underestimates the FLOPS (and therefore underreports MFU) for Qwen3-VL models whose. Also adds a regression test case for based on the exact config of, a model where the derived value d…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes `_estimate_qwen3_vl_flops` in `verl/utils/flops_counter.py` to read `head_dim` from the model config instead of deriving it as `hidden_size // num_attention_heads`, which underestimates the FLOPS (and therefore underreports MFU) for Qwen3-VL models whose `num_attention_heads * head_dim != hidden_size`.

Also adds a regression test case for `qwen3_vl` based on the exact config of `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, a model where the derived value differs from the true `head_dim` (the existing `qwen3_vl` test uses the 8B model, where `hidden_size // num_attention_heads` happens to equal `head_dim`, so this bug was not exposed).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+qwen3-vl+head_dim
  - Note: #6944 (open) contains the same one-line `head_dim` fix plus an additional ViT merger-token-count correction. This PR was authored independently and only addresses the `head_dim` issue; happy to close it in favor of #6944 if the maintainers prefer to consolidate there.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

All existing golden values are unchanged (13 original cases pass), plus one new case:

```text
$ pytest tests/utils/test_flops_counter.py -q
14 passed in 0.24s
```

The new `qwen3_vl_4b` case uses the exact `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` config (explicit `head_dim=128`) and covers both batch shapes `[512, 1024, 2048]` and `[4096, 4096, 4096]` with image tokens. With the old derivation, `head_dim` would be computed as `2560 // 32 = 80` instead of `128`, underestimating the total FLOPS by ~9-10%.

### API and Usage Example

No API changes — this only corrects an internal estimation detail.

### Design & Code Changes

`_estimate_qwen3_vl_flops` derived `head_dim = hidden_size // num_attention_heads`, but Qwen3-VL sets an explicit `head_dim` in `text_config`:

| Model | hidden_size | num_attention_heads | head_dim | heads × head_dim |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-VL-4B | 2560 | 32 | 128 | 4096 ≠ 2560 |
| Qwen3-VL-32B | 5120 | 64 | 128 | 8192 ≠ 5120 |

This affects two terms:

1. the attention projection FLOPS (`q/k/v/o` linear layers), and
2. the attention score FLOPS `6 * seqlen^2 * num_attn_heads * d_head * num_hidden_layers`.

The fix reads `head_dim` from the config with the same `getattr` fallback pattern already used by `_estimate_qwen3_vl_moe_flops` (and the other estimators):

```python
head_dim = getattr(config.text_config, "head_dim", hidden_size // num_attention_heads)
```

The fallback keeps backward compatibility: `qwen2_vl` and `qwen2_5_vl` share this estimator, do not set `head_dim`, and satisfy `hidden_size == num_attention_heads * head_dim`, so their estimates are unchanged.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always` (not run locally — no verl dev environment available; the change is a single line consistent with existing style, CI will lint)
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). (not needed — no user-facing API/doc change)
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s): extended `tests/utils/test_flops_counter.py` with a `qwen3_vl_4b` case using the official Qwen3-VL-4B config
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in the [verl Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ).
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`. (not applicable)

items.title: [reward] fix: prime_code scores every call-based APPS/TACO task 0
items.author: zhongerdeajie
items.summary: graded every call-based (function-call) APPS/TACO sample 0, even for a correct solution, and additionally gave 0 instead of partial credit under. APPS and TACO publish call-based tests with each input already a list of arguments (e.g.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8174. `prime_code` graded every call-based (function-call) APPS/TACO sample **0, even for a
correct solution**, and additionally gave 0 instead of partial credit under `continuous=True`. Two
defects, two commits:

1. **`testing_util.py` — parse layout (commit 1).** The call-based branch of `run_test` assumed
   LiveCodeBench-style tests: each input is a *string* holding one JSON value per line
   (`inputs.split("\n")` then `json.loads` per line). APPS and TACO publish call-based tests with
   each input already a *list of arguments* (e.g. `"inputs": [[[1,2,3,4,5,6,1], 3]], "outputs": [12]`),
   so `inputs.split` raised `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'split'` inside the
   grading subprocess. `_temp_run` catches it, appends `-1` for every test, and redirects stderr to
   `os.devnull` first — so nothing is logged and the sample just silently scores 0 (exactly the
   "looks like the model failed" symptom from the issue). Fix: decide **per test case** by whether
   the input is a string. Strings are parsed exactly as before (unchanged behavior for existing
   data); anything else is already the argument list and is used as-is, with inputs/outputs
   JSON-encoded only for the truncated metadata.

2. **`prime_code/__init__.py` — keep `fn_name` in per-sample runs (commit 2).** With
   `continuous=True` (what `default_compute_score` uses for `apps`/`taco`/`codecontests`/`codeforces`),
   the per-sample loop rebuilt each test case as
   `{"inputs": [inputs[i]], "outputs": [outputs[i]]}` — dropping `fn_name`. `run_test` therefore
   dispatched call-based samples to the **standard-input** branch, compared captured stdout against
   the expected return value, and every per-sample run failed with `Wrong Answer` / empty output.
   Consequence on main: call-based problems could only ever score through the all-tests-pass fast
   path; any failing test made the continuous score exactly 0 (e.g. 2/3 passing tests → 0.0). This
   affects **both** test layouts and is independent of the layout bug. Fix: propagate `fn_name` to
   the per-sample test cases when present; standard-input problems are untouched.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+prime_code
      — returns #8175 (open, same issue for commit 1), #8022 (open, unrelated counting bug in
      `compute_score`), #8044 (closed, non-continuous path). None of them touches the `fn_name`
      propagation this PR adds as commit 2.
- [x] Title formatted as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` — `[reward] fix: ...`

### Test

New CPU test `tests/utils/reward_score/test_prime_code_call_based_on_cpu.py`
(picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml` via the `_on_cpu.py` suffix):

```
pytest -q tests/utils/reward_score/test_prime_code_call_based_on_cpu.py
```

- on main: `test_call_based_full_reward[apps_list_layout]` fails (correct solution scores 0.0)

items.title: [rollout, vllm] feat: pin each multi-turn session to one vLLM DP rank
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: With a vLLM rollout replica that has (e.g. DP + EP inside one server), each DP engine has its own prefix cache. [Discussion: Thanks, done as suggested: - only forwards; no vLLM/DP logic in the client.]
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

With a vLLM rollout replica that has `data_parallel_size > 1` (e.g. DP + EP inside one server), each DP engine has its own prefix cache. `LLMServerClient` sends every turn under a fresh uuid and no DP rank, so vLLM's internal DP load balancer picks the least-loaded engine per request, and the turns of a multi-turn session land on different DP ranks and miss their prefix cache.

`LLMServerClient` now forwards the sticky caller id as `session_id`. `vLLMHttpServer` turns it into `data_parallel_rank = crc32(session_id) % data_parallel_size` using its own DP size and passes it to `AsyncLLM.generate` (the in-process equivalent of the `X-data-parallel-rank` header vLLM's OpenAI server accepts from routers). `_pd_dispatch` forwards `session_id` to both PD legs, so each server pins with its own DP size. No config; DP == 1 is unchanged, and SGLang / TRT-LLM accept `session_id` as a no-op.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=data_parallel_rank and https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=X-data-parallel-rank (none route requests to a vLLM DP rank).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

Nemotron-H 30B-A3B, SWE-bench Pro multi-turn agent replay on GB200, one DP4/EP4 vLLM server per node: prefix-cache hit rate went from 0.81 to 0.86 and long sessions finished 10-15% faster. In a full RL run with pinning, the cumulative hit rate was 0.93.

### Design & Code Changes

- `llm_server.py`: pass `session_id=request_id` to `server.generate`; the client stays backend-agnostic.
- `vllm_async_server.py`: `_dp_rank_for_session()` (CRC32 is stable across processes, unlike `hash()`; hash pinning ignores engine load, which is fine with many concurrent sessions per replica). `generate()` passes the rank to the engine; `_pd_dispatch()` forwards `session_id` to the prefill and decode legs.
- `async_sglang_server.py`, `trtllm_async_server.py`: accept `session_id` (unused for now).

Replica-level stickiness is unchanged (`GlobalRequestLoadBalancer` still maps a session to one replica); this adds the same stickiness inside a DP > 1 replica.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change; I reviewed it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
discussion:
Thanks, done as suggested:
- `LLMServerClient` only forwards `session_id=request_id`; no vLLM/DP logic in the client.
- `vLLMHttpServer._dp_rank_for_session()` computes the rank from the server's own `data_parallel_size`; `_pd_dispatch` forwards `session_id` to both the prefill and decode legs.
- SGLang and TRT-LLM `generate` accept `session_id` as a no-op.
- Docstring notes that hash pinning ignores engine load.

Agreed on the GRPO `n` samples point; left as is.

items.title: [fsdp, model] Qwen3.5 Ulysses SP: forward matches DP but parameter gradients don't (GDN cp_context backward + engine lm_head grad)
items.author: MaCoredroid
items.summary: With Ulysses sequence parallelism on Qwen3.5-9B (hybrid full attention + Gated DeltaNet), the forward pass matches data parallelism but the parameter gradients do not. Across two independent checks, SP-vs-DP gradient cosine is 0.85–0.96, while the DP-vs-DP noi…
items.body:
### Summary

With Ulysses sequence parallelism on **Qwen3.5-9B** (hybrid full attention + Gated DeltaNet), the **forward pass matches data parallelism but the parameter gradients do not**. Across two independent checks, SP-vs-DP gradient cosine is 0.85–0.96, while the DP-vs-DP noise floor is ≥ 0.9999. Log-prob parity passes (mean |Δlogp| ≈ 0.005), so the problem is easy to miss.

The two checks point to two separate problems:

1. **GDN layers under fla context parallelism (`cp_context`)**: wrong weight gradients in `linear_attn`, the embeddings and early layers.
2. **lm_head weight gradient on the `FSDPEngineWithLMHead` path**: cos 0.68 at 1.39× the reference norm. This does not appear when the head and loss are computed outside verl's engine.

The existing test `tests/special_distributed/test_qwen35_linear_attention_ulysses_sp.py` compares outputs and the gradient w.r.t. the **input hidden states** of one layer. As far as I can tell it doesn't compare the layer's **weight** gradients, which is where the mismatch shows up.

### Environment

- verl `704a9f01` (2026-10-08). There have been no later commits to `models/transformers/qwen3_5.py` or `monkey_patch.py` on `main` as of 2026-10-09. One local patch loads optimizer state only around `optimizer.step`; it is unrelated to forward/backward.
- torch 2.13.0+cu129, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2, transformers 5.12.1
- Qwen3.5-9B, full fine-tune, FSDP2, fp32 master weights, gradient checkpointing, remove-padding, dynamic batch
- GDN under SP via verl's Qwen3.5 monkey patch (fla `cp_context` for GDN, all-to-all for full attention)

### Check 1: verl `TrainingWorker` / `FSDPEngineWithLMHead`

**Setup**

- One real rollout sequence: 1,669 prompt + 65,536 response = 67,205 tokens.
- 4 GPUs, comparing DP=4 (SP=1) against SP=2 / DP=2. Every rank runs exactly one micro-batch holding a copy of the sequence, so both layouts compute the gradient of the same one-sequence loss.
- A second DP run gives the noise floor. No optimizer step is taken.
- Loss: PPO actor loss (vanilla, clip 0.2, dual clip 3, seq-mean-token-mean), low_var_kl 0.001, entropy 0, advantage +1 on every response token. Fused log-prob kernel (torch backend); params and optimizer offloaded.
- Comparison: the FSDP mesh is all 4 ranks in both layouts, so each rank's gradient shard is compared with the same shard from DP run 1.

| vs DP run 1 | all params cos (rel L2) | lm_head cos (norm ratio) | embed_tokens cos | GDN `linear_attn` | full attn | MLP | layer 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP run 2 (noise floor) | 0.99999 (0.005) | 1.0000 (1.000) | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| **SP=2** | **0.958 (0.292)** | **0.682 (1.389)** | 0.882 | 0.979 | 0.992 | 0.997 | 0.890 |

Forward log-probs, SP=2 vs DP: mean |Δ| 0.0051, max 0.24.

### Check 2: standalone FSDP2 trainer using verl's Qwen3.5 Ulysses patch

**Setup**

- One 46.7K-token rollout sequence on 4 GPUs.
- DP (one rank holds the sequence), a second DP run as the noise floor, and Ulysses SP over all 4 ranks.
- Sequence-level (GSPO-style) surrogate loss. The lm_head and loss are computed by the trainer itself, not by verl's engine.

| | all params cos | `linear_attn` | embed_tokens | lm_head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP repeat (noise floor) | 0.99992 | | | |
| **SP=4, verl patch** | **0.851** | 0.79 | 0.67 | 0.999 |
| SP=4, head-parallel GDN (see below) | 0.99991 | | | |

Forward log-probs, SP vs DP: mean |Δ| 0.0057. Results are the same with offload on or off.

### What fixed (1) but not (2)

I replaced the fla context-parallel GDN with a head-parallel GDN: all-to-all from sequence-sharded to head-sharded around the short conv and fla's standard chunk kernel, then back. In check 2 that brings gradients to the noise floor (0.99991, rel L2 0.013). Installed into verl's engine (check 1), it does **not** fix the lm_head gradient (cos 0.684, ratio 1.389), and the overall cosine is no better (0.936). So the engine path seems to have its own lm_head/loss-side issue. A cosine of about 0.68 at roughly √2 the norm would fit some tokens being counted twice and others dropped. I haven't localised it; the next things I would try are disabling the fused log-prob kernel and using an even-length sequence.

### Expected

SP gradients should match DP within the noise floor (cos ≈ 0.9999), as the forward does.

### Workaround

SP=1 with param/optimizer offload for long sequences.

I can share the gradient-check scripts (they build the one-sequence batch, run both layouts and dump per-group / per-layer cosines) if that helps reproduce.
discussion:
Closing this for now. I couldn't reproduce the GDN gradient mismatch in isolation. On a different GPU architecture (RTX 5080, SP=2/4 over gloo, same verl/fla/transformers versions), `qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward` gives parameter gradients matching a full-sequence reference to cos ≥ 0.99998. That holds with long-memory gates, multi-chunk and packed sequences, and activation checkpointing. The original observations came from a full training stack on Hopper GPUs, so the cause is either in the integration or specific to that architecture, and I can't currently isolate which.

One note for the existing test: with random init the GDN state decays within a few tokens, so a gradient check on randomly initialised layers barely exercises cross-rank state. Setting `A_log`/`dt_bias` to long-memory values and comparing weight gradients would make it much more sensitive.

I'll reopen with a minimal repro if I can pin it down.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: copy offloaded shards in fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu
items.author: ZhiliangWu
items.summary: Fix when in the fully async trainer. With offload on, the local shards are already on CPU, so returns a tensor that shares memory with the live shard, not a copy.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix `fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu` when `param_offload=True` in the fully async trainer.

With offload on, the local shards are already on CPU, so `.detach().cpu()` returns a tensor that shares memory with the live shard, not a copy. In `FullyAsyncTrainer._compute_old_log_prob`, `restore_model_from_cpu(1)` then also overwrites the snapshot from `save_model_to_cpu(k)`, and `restore_model_from_cpu(k)` brings back the weights from the start of the sync window instead of the current ones. As a result, every local step trains again from the weights at the start of the window. A sign of this is a PPO ratio of exactly 1, so actor/ppo_kl and actor/pg_clipfrac are exactly 0.

This PR makes a real copy with `.to("cpu", copy=True)`, the same method that the FSDP1 helper `fsdp1_sharded_save_to_cpu` from #7306 uses, and adds a CPU unit test for it.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: [`fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu), [`save_model_to_cpu`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+save_model_to_cpu), [`fully_async offload`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+fully_async+offload), [issues: `fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu)
  - No open or merged PR fixes the FSDP2 case. Related PRs:
    - #7306 (merged) added the FSDP1 snapshot helpers for Decoupled PPO. It did not change `fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu`.
    - #6095 (merged) fixed the Megatron save and offload in this path when `param_offload` is on.
    - #5081 (open) makes these copies non-blocking in `verl/experimental/fully_async_policy/fsdp2_utils.py`, which is no longer on main. Its `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` also returns the live shard when the shard is already on CPU.
