items.title: [hardware, profile] fix: improve existing pytorch profiling to support other pytorch supported device
items.author: kahlun
items.summary: knew exactly one device activity,, and accepted exactly one device keyword,. On an accelerator that is not CUDA there was then no way to record device kernels: the default asks for CUDA, torch logs and the trace holds CPU ops only, while naming the real devi…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`get_torch_profiler` knew exactly one device activity, `ProfilerActivity.CUDA`, and
`TorchProfilerToolConfig` accepted exactly one device keyword, `"cuda"`. On an accelerator that is
not CUDA there was then no way to record device kernels: the default `contents=[]` asks for CUDA,
torch logs `CUDA is not available, disabling CUDA profiling` and the trace holds CPU ops only, while
naming the real device in `contents` fails config validation.

torch exposes one `ProfilerActivity` member per backend it can profile, named after the device type
it profiles, and a single profiler session records exactly one of them. So the active platform's
`device_name` is both the activity to collect and the `contents` keyword that requests it. This PR
resolves it that way instead of hardcoding CUDA, and takes the accepted device keywords from
`torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity` rather than from a verl-maintained list.

**No new `PlatformBase` API** — `device_name` is already an abstract property.

### No change for existing platforms

`PlatformCUDA.device_name` is `"cuda"`, and `PlatformROCm`, `PlatformMetaX` and `PlatformIluvatar`
inherit it (torch exposes HIP as `torch.cuda`), so all four build exactly the same `activities` list
as before. Platforms with no matching member (`npu`, `mlu`, `musa`, `gcu`, `tpu`, `supa`) still get a
CPU-only trace, exactly as they do today when torch disables the unavailable CUDA activity — the
warning explaining it is now verl's, and it names the device.

`xpu`, `hpu` and `mtia` start working with no further verl change and no plugin code.

### Out-of-tree backends whose activity is not named after the device type

`DEVICE_ACTIVITIES` is a module-level `device type -> ProfilerActivity` map, so a backend that needs
a different pairing can add one entry from its plugin:

```python
from verl.utils.profiler.config import DEVICE_ACTIVITIES
DEVICE_ACTIVITIES["mlu"] = torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.PrivateUse1
```

This is deliberately data rather than API: it keeps the mapping out of `PlatformBase` while leaving
privateuse1-based backends a one-line override. In practice those backends all select a vendor
profiler through `global_profiler.tool` instead, which this PR does not touch.

`CPU` and `PrivateUse1` are excluded from the map and `"privateuse1"` is not an accepted `contents`
keyword: CPU activity is collected in every trace regardless of `contents`, and `PrivateUse1` is
torch's slot for an out-of-tree backend rather than a device type any platform reports as its
`device_name`, so accepting it would validate a value that is then silently never recorded.
`"cpu"` remains accepted.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- #7988 proposed the same fix through two optional `PlatformBase` hooks,
  `torch_profiler_activity()` and `torch_profiler_content_name()`. This PR drops both: `device_name`
  already carries the information, which removes the paired-hook invariant between them, removes the
  requirement for every plugin to implement them, and leaves `platform_base.py` untouched.
- `gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state open --search "profiler activity"` — nothing else open
  in this area.

### Test

```bash
pytest tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py
# 50 passed, 18 subtests passed

VERL_PLATFORM=intel     pytest tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py   # 50 passed, 18 subtests
VERL_PLATFORM=cambricon pytest tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py   # 50 passed, 18 subtests

ruff check verl/utils/profiler/config.py verl/utils/profiler/torch_profile.py \
           tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py                        # clean
ruff format --check <same three files>                              # clean
```

New tests:

- `TestDeviceActivityFromPlatform` — a non-CUDA device is recorded and CUDA is *not* added alongside
  it (torch checks CUDA before every other device, so leaving it in would disable device profiling
  altogether); CUDA platforms are unchanged; every entry in `DEVICE_ACTIVITIES` resolves to its own
  activity, so the lookup holds for whatever members a given torch build exposes; a device with no
  member warns; a CUDA-written `contents` run on another accelerator warns and records no device
  activity; `contents` naming only profiler options warns nothing; a CPU platform does not add CPU
  twice.

  The non-CUDA cases take their device from whatever `torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity` the running
  build exposes rather than hardcoding one accelerator, and skip if a build offers none.
- `TestDeviceContentsConfigValidation` — every keyword in `DEVICE_CONTENTS` validates, profiler
  options still validate, an unknown keyword and `"privateuse1"` are both rejected.

Two pre-existing tests (`test_get_torch_profiler`, `test_cpu_activity_added_for_device_only_contents`)
assert the CUDA activity, which until now was hardcoded and so held on any machine. They now patch in
a CUDA platform, stating the assumption they always had — without it they fail when the suite runs on
non-CUDA hardware.

No new e2e CI test: CI has no non-CUDA device. Manually verified end to end on Intel Arc Pro B60
(device kernels present in the chrome trace, which was not the case before this change).

### API and Usage Example

No API change. On a non-CUDA accelerator, the default config now records device kernels:

```yaml
global_profiler:
  tool: torch
  global_tool_config:
    torch:
      contents: []          # records the active platform's device activity, e.g. xpu
      # contents: [xpu]     # equivalent, explicit
      # contents: [stack]   # CPU-only, as requested, no warning
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/profiler/config.py` — `DEVICE_ACTIVITIES` map built from
  `torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.__members__` (keyed by lowercased device type, so the lookup does
  not depend on how torch capitalizes a member); `DEVICE_CONTENTS` derived from it for config
  validation, replacing the hardcoded `["cuda", "cpu", "memory", "shapes", "stack"]`.
- `verl/utils/profiler/torch_profile.py` — `get_torch_profiler` resolves the active platform's
  `device_name` through that map; warns when the platform has no activity, and when `contents` names
  a device activity belonging to a different backend.
- `docs/perf/torch_profiling.md` — documents the device keyword per accelerator.
- `tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py` — as above.

### Checklist

- [x] Searched for similar PRs (see "Why this is not a duplicate").
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.
- [x] `pre-commit` / ruff clean on changed files.
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/perf/torch_profiling.md`).
- [x] New CI-runnable unit tests added.
- [ ] Slack `ci-request` ping if CI needs a nudge.
- [ ] Recipe submodule unchanged (n/a).

items.title: [ci, fsdp] fix: make the FSDP rmpad checkpoint test deterministic and actually verify the load
items.author: MincongZhou
items.summary: Makes actually do the two things it claims to do: run deterministically, and verify that the checkpoint it writes is the checkpoint it loads back. Both defects are in that one file; no production code is touched.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes `tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp_ckpt.py` actually do the two things it claims to do: run deterministically, and verify that the checkpoint it writes is the checkpoint it loads back. Both defects are in that one file; no production code is touched.

**1. The determinism guard was dead code.** The file set `FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC=1` at the bottom of `__main__` (old line 161). flash-attn reads that variable while *its own package* is being imported, and this file's own imports already trigger that (`verl/__init__.py` → `verl/utils/torch_functional.py:35` imports `flash_attn.ops.triton.cross_entropy`). Setting it afterwards had no effect — which is why the bit-exact logits comparison at the end of the test is flaky. This is the same class of bug huggingface/transformers fixed in [64d14ef / #37185](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/commit/64d14ef28dac918e13d833d5a76280ae6c998d35).

**2. The checkpoint round-trip assertion could never fail.** Old line 116 was `saved_state_dict = model.state_dict()`. `state_dict()` does not copy — it hands back the live parameter tensors (FSDP1 flat params / FSDP2 DTensors). By the time the comparison at old lines 133-135 runs (after `load_checkpoint`), `saved_state_dict` *is* the post-load model, so the check compared the model against itself and passed no matter what was restored. The only remaining signal was the flaky logits compare, i.e. the one assertion that could fail was the unreliable one and the reliable-looking one was vacuous.

This matters more now, not less: #7431 moves this test into the blocking `model_rmpad` job, so a verification step that always passes would become a blocking gate that validates nothing.

### Root cause

| # | File:line (before) | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| A | `tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp_ckpt.py:161` | `os.environ["FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC"] = "1"` runs in `__main__`, after `import verl` already imported flash-attn → dead |
| B | `tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp_ckpt.py:116` | `model.state_dict()` aliases live params → the round-trip assertion compares the model with itself → vacuous |

### Design & Code Changes

Four hunks, one file:

1. set `FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC=1` and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` **before** the imports that pull flash-attn in (root-cause fix for A);
2. `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` + `torch.manual_seed(2026)` in `test_fsdp_ckpt` — determinism that does not depend on flash-attn's import order, plus a reproducible draw;
3. snapshot the saved weights **by value** so the round-trip check can actually fail (fix for B);
4. delete the now-duplicated dead `os.environ` line from `__main__`.

An alternative for hunk 1 is to put the two variables in a step-level `env:` block of the two `test_fsdp_ckpt.py` steps in `.github/workflows/model.yml`. That version composes with #7431's restructuring but couples determinism to the workflow rather than to the test, which is why the self-contained version is proposed. Happy to switch if maintainers prefer the workflow-side placement.

### Test

**A — the import-order fix, both directions.** A `sitecustomize` meta-path probe prints the environment at the moment `flash_attn` is first imported, running the file exactly as CI does:

```
# BEFORE (unpatched)
PROBE AT_FA_IMPORT -> FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC=None CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=None
# AFTER (patched)
PROBE AT_FA_IMPORT -> FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC='1' CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=':4096:8'
```

**B — the vacuous assertion, both directions.** 2 ranks, `gloo`, CPU, real `FSDPCheckpointManager` + `apply_fsdp2`, 1-layer Qwen2; the test's exact update → save → step → load sequence, with the on-disk shards then corrupted (`+1.0` on every tensor of every rank):

```
CONTROL (clean checkpoint):
    shipped loop (aliased snapshot)   -> PASSED
    patched loop (real snapshot)      -> PASSED
TREATMENT (checkpoint corrupted +1.0):
    shipped loop (aliased snapshot)   -> PASSED   <-- the bug: it cannot fail
    patched loop (real snapshot)      -> FAILED (Tensor-likes are not equal!)
```

A checkpoint that restores `weights + 1.0` is accepted by the shipped assertion and rejected by the patched one. Working-tree check of the mechanism itself: `model.state_dict()["weight"].data_ptr() == model.weight.data_ptr()` is `True`, and after `model.weight.add_(1.0)` the aliased dict still compares equal to the live weight while a `detach().clone()` snapshot does not.

Runnable checks:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `ruff check --config pyproject.toml tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp_ckpt.py` | `All checks passed!` (identical to the unmodified file) |
| `ruff format --check --config pyproject.toml <file>` | `1 file already formatted` |
| `python -m py_compile <file>` | OK |
| `pytest tests/workers/test_fsdp_gradient_accumulation_sync_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_fsdp_wrap_policy_on_cpu.py -q` | **13 passed** (closest runnable siblings; this patch is test-only, so this is a no-regression check) |
| `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` forward+backward+`AdamW.step()` on the same 1-layer Qwen2 (CPU, fp32, eager) | completes without `RuntimeError` — clears the main risk of hunk 2 |

**Not verified here:** that hunk 1 removes the CUDA flake itself (needs the 8× GPU `model_rmpad` job with `flash_attention_2`), and flash-attn's exact env-var spelling (could not reach `raw.githubusercontent.com` from this environment). CI on this PR is the check for both.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Existing work in this area: [#7431](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/7431) (`Closes #1388`, touches `.github/workflows/model.yml` only) moves this test into the blocking `model_rmpad` job; this PR touches only `tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp_ckpt.py`, so they are complementary rather than overlapping. Query used: `is:pr FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC` / `is:pr fsdp_ckpt test deterministic`.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks: `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on the changed file (the only pre-commit hook that applies to a Python test file).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s): not applicable — this PR *is* a test fix, and it does not add a new test target. The existing test is what becomes meaningful.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel in the verl Slack / Feishu group.

items.title: [hardware, recipe] feat: DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO on ROCm (MI355X) with QAT, FP8 or BF16 training
items.author: PeterYang12
items.summary: Makes DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO run end to end on AMD MI355X with an FP8 rollout, and gives it one recipe with three training modes. Follow-up to #7050 (ROCm enablement) and #7455 / #7470 (Megatron-Bridge path).
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO run end to end on AMD MI355X with an FP8 rollout, and gives it one recipe with three training modes. Follow-up to #7050 (ROCm enablement) and #7455 / #7470 (Megatron-Bridge path). Two commits:

1. **`[docker]` image.** `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4` builds the versions the runs were validated with: Transformer Engine 2.18 (ROCm build: Triton grouped GEMM path that avoids a bf16 grouped-GEMM backward hang on gfx950, float-scale blockwise FP8 GEMM), a libhsa-runtime that returns memory under `expandable_segments` on ROCm 7.2.x, Megatron-LM `fd1121b8f` plus the `deepseek-v4-rocm-support` commits (config-driven FP8 fake quantization, FP8-training alignment options, and the `index_select` gather of the unfused CSA sparse attention that upstream introduced with the reworked SBHD path in NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6400, which this older base predates), Megatron-Bridge 0.5.0 plus a fix that keeps the FP8 weight export on the checkpoint's power-of-two scale grid, and four vLLM 0.26.0 patches applied at build time (NaN guard on the FP8 indexer logits; CuMem wake cache release, vllm#49857; indexer K-cache block-flat layout on gfx950/gfx942, vllm#50455; SwiGLU clamp on the FP8 Triton fused MoE path).
2. **`[recipe]` one script, three modes.** `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh`, `TRAIN_MODE=qat|fp8|bf16`. `qat` is BF16 training with Megatron's FP8 fake quantization (weights on 128x128 power-of-two scales, inputs on 1x128 float scales, straight-through estimator) and an FP8 W8A8 vLLM rollout; `fp8` is Transformer Engine blockwise FP8 training with float activation scales; `bf16` is BF16 training with a BF16 rollout. All modes round the KV latent and the indexer q/k the way the rollout's FP8 KV cache and FP8 indexer do. Everything is a transformer-config override; the only environment variables are the two Transformer Engine kernel selectors.

Why the alignment matters: on ROCm, vLLM quantizes FP8 activations with float scales (amax / 448) while Transformer Engine's blockwise recipe uses powers of two, so the same training code that aligns on NVIDIA (DeepGEMM) does not align here. With the rollout's rounding reproduced in training, `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` at step 1 drops to the BF16-forward level and the train/rollout KL stays flat over 300 steps.

The Megatron-LM and Megatron-Bridge changes live in the author's forks while they are proposed upstream; the Transformer Engine wheel and the libhsa-runtime are published as release assets because no official ROCm package carries those fixes yet.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+deepseek-v4+rocm
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP8 checkpoint), 4 nodes x 8 MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3, GRPO/GSPO on DAPO-Math, validated on AIME-2024 every 10 steps:

| Mode | step-1 `rollout_probs_diff_mean` | step-1 `rollout_corr/kl` | 300 steps | AIME-2024 acc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qat | 0.0096 | 0.0021 | KL 0.0022 -> 0.0029, no NaN/hang | 0.60 -> 0.76 |
| fp8 | 0.0097 | 0.0021 | KL 0.0022 -> 0.0039 | 0.60 -> 0.76 |
| bf16 | 0.0060 | 0.0008 | KL 0.0008 -> 0.0011 | 0.59 -> 0.79 peak |

On the image built from this branch, a 7-layer cut of the model (single node) gives diff / KL of 0.0129 / 0.0068 in `qat` and 0.0130 / 0.0069 in `fp8` over 3 steps, matching the earlier runs. Per step on 32 GPUs: ~490 s (`qat`), ~420 s (`fp8`), ~330 s (`bf16`), of which ~85 s is the weight sync.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4 -t rocm-verl-dsv4 .
# Ray on every node (commands in the script header), then on the head node:
WK=<wandb key> TRAIN_MODE=qat bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh
TRAIN_MODE=fp8 TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=5 bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh trainer.val_before_train=False
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4`: version pins and build-time patches as described; `docker/rocm/patches/vllm-*.patch` carry the upstream reference in their headers.
- `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh`: the recipe; the header documents the modes, the Ray commands and the reference values. The mode only changes a set of `override_transformer_config` keys (`fp8_fake_quant`, `fp8_fake_quant_kv_cache`, `fp8_fake_quant_indexer_qk`, and for `fp8`: `fp8=e4m3 fp8_recipe=blockwise fp8_blockwise_act_pow2_scale=False`), applied to both the actor and the reference policy.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting)
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation: the recipe header is the documentation; happy to add a docs page if preferred.
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s): needs 32 MI355X and the DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint; validated by the runs above.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.

items.title: [draft] [worker, hardware] fix: pin each Ray worker's accelerator in both vis…
items.author: kahlun
items.summary: pins this rank's accelerator only when a variable is set. In the default configuration verl never calls at all, and instead relies on Ray's per-actor visibility mask relabeling devices so that index 0 is this rank's device.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`Worker._setup_env_cuda_visible_devices()` pins this rank's accelerator only when a
`RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_*_VISIBLE_DEVICES` variable is set. In the default configuration verl
never calls `set_device()` at all, and instead relies on Ray's per-actor visibility mask
relabeling devices so that index 0 is this rank's device.

That assumption holds only where the accelerator runtime honors its own visibility mask. Where
it does not, every rank in the job runs on the same physical device. The collision does not
raise a device error — it surfaces as out-of-memory, or as collectives taking paths intended for
ranks that share a device.

This PR resolves the index to pin from Ray's own assignment, in **both** visibility modes,
through a new `PlatformBase.ray_device_index()`:

* the position of Ray's reported id inside the visible-devices mask when one is set;
* the reported id itself when nothing is masked.

A platform whose runtime ignores its own mask overrides the hook. Behavior on a runtime that
honors the mask is unchanged — a masked actor resolves to index 0, which is what the process
defaulted to before.

Two related fixes come with it:

1. **Physical vs. logical ids under a user mask.** With NOSET set and
   `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7`, Ray reports physical id `5` and the current code calls
   `set_device(5)` against a runtime that sees only logical 0–3. That is
   [#7507](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7507); the platform hook fixes it for every
   platform at once, without hardcoding vendor environment-variable names in
   `single_controller`.
2. **A NOSET name that no longer exists.** `ray_noset_visible_devices()` hardcodes a list of
   NOSET variables. Ray derives its NOSET name from the variable it masks, and those get renamed
   — [ray-project/ray#64440](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64440) moved Ray's Intel
   GPU manager from `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` to `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` and deleted the old NOSET
   name — so the hardcoded entry names a variable Ray no longer reads. Derive it the way Ray
   does and let the platform name any others, as the sglang rollout path already does in
   `async_sglang_server.py` and `sglang_pd_replica.py`.

### Why this belongs in core rather than in a hardware plugin

The hardware-plugin guidance is to default to plugin-side patching and reserve core changes for
hardware-agnostic blockers. This is one, on three counts.

**1. The gate is wrong independently of any single vendor.** `if is_ray_noset_visible_devices:`
conditions *whether verl pins at all* on a flag that only describes *who sets the mask*. Those
are different questions. Three vendors have now hit it from three directions:

| Report | Hardware | Symptom | Current workaround |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [#7507](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7507) | Ascend 910B4 | `set_device(5)` → `Invalid device ID` with `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7` | mask-index lookup, `ASCEND_`/`CUDA_` names hardcoded in `single_controller` |
| [#8138](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8138) | Google TPU | Ray's host-level chip id does not index the one-chip visible list | `if device_name == "TPU": local_rank = os.environ["TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS"]` in `single_controller` |
| this PR | Intel Arc Pro B60 | both ranks land on device 0; run dies out of memory | — |

Three different vendor branches in the same three lines of `worker.py` is the shape of a missing
abstraction, not of three vendor bugs.

**2. The vendor-specific half stays out of core.** Core gains only the policy — *resolve the
index from Ray's assignment* — plus one method. The hardware knowledge stays in the platform
class: `PlatformROCm` inherits the CUDA mask variable, `PlatformNPU` names
`ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, and an out-of-tree platform overrides `ray_device_index()` when its
runtime ignores the mask. No vendor branch is added to `single_controller`.

**3. A plugin cannot reach this code path in time.** The only plugin-side route is patching
`Worker._setup_env_cuda_visible_devices`. That method is the **first statement of
`Worker.__init__`**, and a plugin's patches are applied from its platform's `__init__`, which is
itself first triggered by the `get_resource_name()` call *inside that same method*. By the time
the platform object exists, the function that needed patching is already executing. Applying it
earlier means patching at verl import time, before any platform is selected.

That last point is not hypothetical: `PlatformTPU` is a plugin platform, and #8138 still had to
patch core `worker.py` to pin a TPU chip.

### Relationship to #8138, and an offer

`PlatformTPU` in `verl-hardware-plugin` already ships a method for exactly this:

```python
def ray_local_rank_override(self) -> Optional[str]:
    # Ray does not enumerate TPU chips, so the index comes from TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS, which
    # get_worker_env_vars() sets when the worker is created.
    return os.environ.get("TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS", "0")
```

`PlatformBase` on `main` has no such hook and `worker.py` calls no `ray_*` platform method, so
that override is currently dead code — which is why #8138 hardcodes the vendor name in core
instead. `ray_device_index()` is the missing hook.

As written here the hook fires only when Ray reports at least one accelerator id for the
resource, which covers CUDA, ROCm, NPU and XPU but not TPU, where Ray reports none (the TPU
plugin patches Ray's lookup to return `[]` rather than raise, because verl assigns chips itself
through `TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS`). Making the hook return `Optional[int]` and letting it decline would
let it fire on an empty list too, so `PlatformTPU` could own its chip index and #8138's
`if device_name == "TPU"` branch could be dropped. Happy to make that change here, or to adopt
the plugin's existing `ray_local_rank_override` name instead of a new one — whichever maintainers
and the TPU authors prefer. I have no TPU access, so that reading of the TPU path needs their
confirmation.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here:
  [`ray_noset_visible_devices`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+ray_noset_visible_devices),
  [`_setup_env_cuda_visible_devices`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+_setup_env_cuda_visible_devices)
  - [#7507](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7507) (open) maps physical NPU ids to
    logical indices inside the NOSET branch. This PR is a superset: the same mapping through the
    platform layer rather than hardcoded vendor variable names, plus the default non-NOSET mode
    that #7507 leaves untouched. Glad to rebase on it or have it closed in favour of this.
  - [#8138](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8138) (open) adds a TPU branch to the same
    three lines — see the section above. Textual conflict either way round; whichever lands
    first, the other rebases.
  - [#1465](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/1465) (merged) introduced the
    `is_ray_noset_visible_devices` gate this PR removes.
  - [#2967](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/2967) (merged) fixed local-rank binding
    under `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` — the NOSET half of this problem.
  - [#5463](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/5463) (open) removes Ray leakage from the
    base worker interface. This PR adds no new Ray dependency to `single_controller` —
    `ray.get_runtime_context()` is already called here — and moves the device-index decision
    behind a non-Ray platform method, so it should rebase cleanly on that refactor.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

**Unit (`tests/plugin/test_platform_abstraction.py`):** `ray_device_index()` for the
mask-set, mask-unset, non-contiguous-mask and non-indexable-mask (UUID) cases, that a subclass
override is honored, and that `ray_noset_visible_devices()` derives the NOSET name from the
platform's visible-devices variable rather than the hardcoded list. Mock-only, no accelerator
required.

**In-process construction:** `Worker` is also built outside Ray — `SFTTrainer._build_engine()`
builds `TrainingWorker` in-process under torchrun, and
`tests/single_controller/test_get_set_dispatch_collect_cpu.py` constructs `Worker()` directly.
Querying Ray there would start a local Ray instance just to answer, since
`ray.get_runtime_context()` initializes Ray when it is not already running. Guarded with
`ray.is_initialized()` and covered by a test asserting `ray.get_runtime_context` is never called
during in-process construction.

**End-to-end on hardware that exposes the collision:** 2× Intel Arc Pro B60, GRPO on both the
legacy and v1 trainers, FSDP1 and FSDP2, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on GSM8K, vLLM rollout. Before:
both Ray actors report the same physical device UUID and the run dies out of memory. After: two
distinct physical devices at every step including verl's own `create_device_mesh()`, a 6 GB
allocation on rank 0 leaves rank 1's free memory unchanged, world and FSDP-mesh SUM/AVG probes
return correct values, and all four strategy/trainer combinations complete two steps with exit
code 0. The platform involved is out-of-tree, so CI cannot cover this leg.

**No behavior change on in-tree platforms:**

| Mode | Ray reports | Mask read | Resolved index | Before this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ray masks the actor (default) | physical id, e.g. `3` | `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3` | `0` | no pin; process default was `0` — same |
| NOSET, no user mask | `0..N-1` | unset | the id itself | `set_device(id)` — same |
| NOSET + user mask `4,5,6,7` | `5` | `4,5,6,7` | `1` | `set_device(5)` → invalid device — **fixed** (#7507) |
| Mask not indexable (CUDA UUID form) | UUID | UUID list | matched by value | n/a |

ROCm is covered by the CUDA path: `PlatformROCm` subclasses `PlatformCUDA`, Ray's AMD manager
uses `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` or `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and rejects `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` set
without `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, and `_setup_env_cuda_visible_devices()` normalizes HIP→CUDA with
asserted-equal values before the pin — so the id Ray reports is always a member of the mask being
read.

### API and Usage Example

New platform hook with a default implementation; existing platforms need no change:

```python
class PlatformBase(abc.ABC):
    def ray_device_index(self, accelerator_ids: list[str]) -> int:
        """Map the accelerator ids Ray assigned to this actor to a device index to pin."""
```

Thin accessor in `verl/utils/device.py`, following the existing `get_*` pattern:

```python
from verl.utils.device import get_ray_device_index

local_rank = get_ray_device_index(ray.get_runtime_context().get_accelerator_ids()["GPU"])
```

A platform whose runtime does not honor its own visibility mask overrides the hook:

```python
class PlatformXPU(PlatformBase):
    def ray_device_index(self, accelerator_ids: list[str]) -> int:
        # torch-xpu discards ZE_AFFINITY_MASK once its lazy init runs, so every actor still
        # enumerates all devices and xpu:N is physical device N regardless of the mask. Pin the
        # physical id Ray assigned; a mask-relative index would put every rank on xpu:0.
        return int(accelerator_ids[0])
```

No config, CLI or user-facing API changes.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/plugin/platform/platform_base.py` — new `ray_device_index()`. Reads
`visible_devices_envvar()`: if a mask is set, return the position of Ray's id in it; if the id is
not in the mask then the mask is not one we can index into (CUDA's UUID form), and a masked actor
only sees what Ray gave it relabeled from 0, so return 0. If nothing is masked, every device on
the node is visible and the id is the index.

`verl/utils/device.py` — `get_ray_device_index()`, delegating to the active platform.

`verl/single_controller/base/worker.py` — drop the `is_ray_noset_visible_devices` gate
and resolve from Ray's assignment in both modes. Return early when `ray.is_initialized()` is
false, so in-process `Worker` construction neither queries Ray nor starts a local Ray instance.
Skip pinning when Ray assigned this actor no accelerator of this resource type — CPU-only actors
and the driver. As before, the first assigned id is used when an actor holds several.

`verl/utils/ray_utils.py` — `ray_noset_visible_devices()` keeps the existing list for
compatibility and additionally derives `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_{visible_devices_envvar}` the way
Ray does, plus any names the platform reports through `ray_noset_envvars()`. The function has no
in-tree callers left after this change — `worker.py` was the last one, and the sglang paths build
the variable name inline — but it is public and out-of-tree platforms call it, so it is fixed
rather than removed. Glad to drop this hunk if maintainers would rather deprecate the helper.

`tests/plugin/test_platform_abstraction.py` — tests described above.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).

- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.
- [x] Not related to the `recipe` submodule.

items.title: [vllm, hardware] fix: vLLM-Ascend 0.23 sched_yield on ARM hosts and FIA causal mask for genuine decode
items.author: fangweii1
items.summary: Forward-ports two vLLM-Ascend 0.23 NPU compatibility fixes to, adapted to main's refactored structure (originals: #8126, merged into, and #8140): 1. Atlas A2) the vLLM 0.23 scheduler busy-wait with in degrades badly and causes CPU spin.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Forward-ports two vLLM-Ascend 0.23 NPU compatibility fixes to `main`, adapted to main's refactored `apply_npu_vllm_patches()` structure (originals: #8126, merged into `release/v0.8.0`, and #8140):

1. **Disable `sched_yield` on ARM NPU hosts**: on ARM hosts (e.g. Atlas A2) the vLLM 0.23 scheduler busy-wait with `sched_yield` in `vllm.distributed.utils` degrades badly and causes CPU spin. `patch_vllm_ascend_v023_sched_yield()` keeps `USE_SCHED_YIELD` disabled on ARM; other architectures are unchanged.
2. **Only skip the causal mask for genuine decode**: during FULL graph capture vllm-ascend forces `attn_state` to `DecodeOnly`, including mixed prefill-decode graphs and spec-decode verify batches that still need the causal mask. `patch_vllm_ascend_v023_fia_decode_mask()` rewrites `AscendAttentionBackendImpl.full_graph_fia` and `forward_fused_infer_attention` at import time so the mask is skipped (`atten_mask=None`, `sparse_mode=0`) only when `attn_state == DecodeOnly and max_query_len == 1`. It is a no-op when the installed vllm-ascend already contains the fix, and warns + skips on unexpected sources.

Both patches are gated on vLLM 0.23.x and can be dropped once the fixes land in the installed vllm-ascend release.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: this is a forward-port of #8126 and #8140 (both target `release/v0.8.0`); no open PR covers these fixes on `main`.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

- `python -m py_compile verl/utils/vllm/npu_vllm_patch.py` passes.
- `pytest tests/utils/test_npu_vllm_patch_on_cpu.py` passes (1 passed) — the version gate uses `getattr(vllm, "__version__", "0.0.0")` so the test's stub `vllm` module keeps working.
- End-to-end DAPO training (Qwen3-8B, Megatron + vLLM 0.23, 8x Ascend A2 NPU): patches apply cleanly at import time (no skip warnings), training completes with step timings comparable to the pre-patch baseline (step 2-8 avg 48.9s vs 47.2s, within run-to-run variance given RL rollout sampling).

### API and Usage Example

No API change. The patches apply automatically on NPU hosts when vLLM 0.23.x is installed; no user action required.

### Design & Code Changes

Single-file change in `verl/utils/vllm/npu_vllm_patch.py`:

- Add `patch_vllm_ascend_v023_sched_yield()` and `patch_vllm_ascend_v023_fia_decode_mask()`.
- Invoke both from `apply_npu_vllm_patches()`, gated on `0.23.0 <= vllm_version < 0.24.0` (main has no module-level version block, so the check lives inside the refactored entry point).

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply pre-commit checks: not run — pre-commit/ruff is unavailable in the submitter's offline environment; the change follows the surrounding file's style.
- [ ] Documentation: not applicable — internal compatibility patches with no user-facing API change.
- [ ] Add unit/e2e tests to CI: not feasible — requires an ARM NPU host with vLLM 0.23.x; see the Test section.
- [ ] Once ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` Slack channel.
- [ ] `recipe` submodule: not related.

items.title: [hardware, model, cfg, tests] feat: Ascend CANN fused linear cross-entropy
items.author: RitianD
items.summary: Adds Ascend NPU support for fused via CANN / vocab-parallel fused CE APIs, so can run without the CUDA Triton path that overflows UB on 910B. Related open PR falls back to torch fused kernels on Ascend.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds Ascend NPU support for fused `linear_cross_entropy` via CANN / `torch_npu` vocab-parallel fused CE APIs, so `use_fused_kernels=True` can run without the CUDA Triton path that overflows UB on 910B.

Fixes #7950.

Related open PR [#8001](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8001) falls back to torch fused kernels on Ascend. This PR keeps a real fused CE path on NPU (CANN) instead of materializing full logits. Hybrid backward: `dentropy==0` uses CANN CE; `dentropy!=0` (e.g. PPO `entropy_coeff!=0`) uses chunked PyTorch CE+entropy grads aligned with Triton `efficient_entropy`. `use_fused_kernels` is not force-disabled by `entropy_coeff`.

Also fixes a training crash after fused CE: on some NPU builds, `postprocess_thd_engine` / `postprocess_bshd_engine` built jagged NestedTensors from sliced views that still referenced the full packed storage, so `unbind()` failed with `split_with_sizes` mismatch. Sequence slices are now `.contiguous()` before `as_nested_tensor`, and CANN logprobs/entropy are flattened contiguous for `reduction="none"`.

AI assistance was used to implement and iterate on this change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+7950+in%3Abody
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

- CPU: `pytest tests/utils/test_cann_linear_ce_on_cpu.py -q` (policy / gate / chunked CE+H backward helpers; no NPU required)
- NPU (910B / torch_npu with fused linear-CE APIs): `pytest tests/utils/test_cann_linear_ce_on_npu.py -sv` (includes hybrid `dentropy!=0` grad check)
- Enable in training: `actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=True` (works with `entropy_coeff=0` or `!=0`)
- Optional: `VERL_NPU_LCE_BACKEND=auto|cann|triton`, `VERL_NPU_LCE_RETURN_LOGITS=0|1`, `VERL_NPU_LCE_CHUNK_SIZE` (default 2048)
- Training regression: fused actor update after NestedTensor contiguous fix (previously failed in `postprocess_batch_func` / `nt.unbind()`)

### API and Usage Example

```bash
# Launch (NPU)
actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=True
# entropy_coeff may be 0 or non-zero; hybrid backward handles dentropy

# Optional env
export VERL_NPU_LCE_BACKEND=auto   # default: use CANN when APIs exist
# export VERL_NPU_LCE_RETURN_LOGITS=1  # optional metric entropy (less stable on some builds)
# export VERL_NPU_LCE_CHUNK_SIZE=2048  # vocab chunk for hybrid CE+H backward
```

No new Hydra keys. On NPU, `linear_cross_entropy` dispatches to CANN when APIs are available (supports both `npu_*` and older `fused_*` / `*_grad` symbol names).

### Design & Code Changes

- New `verl/utils/kernel/npu/cann_linear_ce.py`: wrap `fused_linear_online_max_sum` + `fused_cross_entropy_loss_with_max_sum` + backward; default memory-saving path (`return_logits=False`); `vocab_end` is half-open `[start, end)`.
- Hybrid backward: CANN CE when `dentropy==0`; chunked PyTorch CE+entropy (`_chunked_ce_entropy_backward`) when `dentropy!=0`.
- `linear_cross_entropy`: on `device.type=="npu"`, prefer CANN; otherwise keep CUDA Triton path unchanged.
- Do not force-disable `use_fused_kernels` when `entropy_coeff!=0` (fused always returns logprobs+entropy; coeff only scales the loss).
- `postprocess_thd_engine` / `postprocess_bshd_engine`: `.contiguous()` on per-sequence slices before `as_nested_tensor` to avoid NPU NestedTensor values/lengths mismatch.
- Tests: CPU policy + chunked CE+H tests; NPU numerical / CE-only and hybrid entropy backward / last-vocab-id regression tests.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: CPU tests use `*_on_cpu.py` naming for the existing CPU unit-test workflow; NPU numerical tests are `*_on_npu.py` for Ascend runners (not wired into a new workflow in this PR).
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)

items.title: fix(data): make val max_samples subsample follow validation_shuffle
items.author: stanleyIl
items.summary: subsampling ran under because reads a single flag from the config that both the train and val datasets share. With the default, the val subsample was random, contradicting and breaking validation reproducibility across restarts.
items.body:
Fixes #7824

## What

`val_max_samples` subsampling ran under `data.shuffle` because `RLHFDataset` reads a single `shuffle` flag from the config that both the train and val datasets share. With the default `legacy_data.yaml` (`shuffle: True`, `validation_shuffle: False`), the val subsample was random, contradicting `validation_shuffle` and breaking validation reproducibility across restarts.

`create_rl_dataset` now maps `data.validation_shuffle` onto the dataset-level `shuffle` flag when `is_train=False`, so the val subsample follows the same flag the val dataloader sampler already uses (`trainer_base.py` / `ray_trainer.py`), and `validation_shuffle=False` yields a deterministic head slice. When `validation_shuffle` is unset, behavior is unchanged (falls back to `data.shuffle`).

## How to check

New CPU test file `tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_validation_shuffle_on_cpu.py` (5 cases: val follows validation_shuffle; train still follows shuffle; fallback when unset; seeded random subsample is reproducible; caller config not mutated).

```
pytest tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_validation_shuffle_on_cpu.py -v  # 5 passed
ruff check && ruff format --check  # clean
```

Verified the core case fails on `main` (subsample is random: `selected 8 random samples out of 64`) and passes with this change (deterministic head slice rows 0-7).

## AI use disclosure (per AGENTS.md)

- The fix and tests were prepared with AI assistance (ZCode, GLM). I have reviewed the full diff line by line and can defend every change.
- Duplicate check done on 2026-10-08: no open PR touches `validation_shuffle` or the `create_rl_dataset` val path. The nearest PR is #7819 (same reporter, fixes the sister issue #7816 by seeding the train `max_samples` rng) — it does not wire `validation_shuffle` into the val subsample; this change is complementary, not overlapping.

Signed-off-by: stanleyIl <stanleyIl@users.noreply.github.com>

items.title: [vllm, hardware] fix: only skip causal mask for genuine decode on vLLM-Ascend 0.23
items.author: fangweii1
items.summary: Skipping the attention mask unconditionally in decode state produces corrupted outputs on those batches. This PR adds a verl-side runtime patch that rewrites and at import time (vllm 0.23.x only) so the causal mask is skipped only for genuine single-…
items.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

On vLLM-Ascend 0.23, `attn_state` is forced to `DecodeOnly` during FULL graph capture, including mixed prefill-decode graphs and spec-decode verify batches, which still need the causal mask. Skipping the attention mask unconditionally in decode state produces corrupted outputs on those batches.

This PR adds a verl-side runtime patch (`verl/utils/vllm/npu_vllm_patch.py`) that rewrites `AscendAttentionBackendImpl.full_graph_fia` and `AscendAttentionBackendImpl.forward_fused_infer_attention` at import time (vllm 0.23.x only) so the causal mask is skipped (`atten_mask=None`, `sparse_mode=0`) only for genuine single-token decode (`attn_state == DecodeOnly and max_query_len == 1`).

Patch properties:
- Source-level replacement applied via `inspect.getsource` + `exec` in the vllm-ascend module namespace, mirroring the upstream fix exactly.
- No-op when the installed vllm-ascend already contains the fix.
- Warns and skips when the installed source does not match the expected releases/v0.23.0 code, so it never breaks startup on other builds.
- Drop this patch once the fix is included in the installed vllm-ascend release.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No API change. On NPU + vllm 0.23 setups, FULL-graph attention now keeps the causal mask for mixed prefill-decode and spec-decode batches.

## How was this patch tested?

- Verified the replacement produces methods bytecode-identical (`co_code` / `co_consts` / `co_names`) to the fixed upstream implementation, tested against both the unpatched base and an already-fixed vllm-ascend checkout (no-op path).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the modified file.
- End-to-end DAPO training run (Qwen3-8B, Megatron + vLLM 0.23 on Ascend 910B) with the patch applied: no patch warnings in the log, training throughput unchanged versus the pre-patch run (~25.7s generate_sequences mean in both).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open verl PRs for `npu_vllm_patch`, `decode mask`, and `vllm-ascend attention`; no existing PR covers this fix.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code CLI); the submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests listed above.

items.title: fix(qwen3.5): average TP-replicated linear-attention gradients across TP
items.author: gavinqii
items.summary: In the Qwen3.5 spec, adds the linear-attention layers ( =, plus ) as a. These parameters are replicated on every tensor-parallel rank, not sharded, but nothing synchronizes their gradients across TP.
items.body:
## Summary

In the Qwen3.5 spec, `slime_plugins/models/qwen3_5.py` adds the linear-attention layers (`linear_attn` = `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet`, plus `input_layernorm`) as a `HuggingfaceAttention`. These parameters are **replicated** on every tensor-parallel rank, not sharded, but nothing synchronizes their gradients across TP.

`hf_attention.py` gathers the sequence-parallel input before these modules, so in exact arithmetic every TP rank computes the same full gradient. In practice the kernels are not bitwise deterministic across ranks. The replicas drift apart a little more every step, so TP ranks end up training slightly different weights, and a distributed checkpoint keeps only one of the copies.

This PR marks these parameters with `average_gradients_across_tp_domain = True`. Megatron's `finalize_model_grads` (`_allreduce_non_tensor_model_parallel_grads`) then averages their gradients across the TP group, so the replicas stay identical. With TP=1 it is a no-op: that path returns early when the TP group size is 1.

## Evidence

A/B on Qwen3.5-9B SFT, 2 nodes × 8 B200, TP=2 / PP=2, 30 training steps, same data and seed. The only difference is the gradient flag. A test-only probe compared each replicated parameter across the 2 TP ranks after every step (all-reduce MAX − MIN):

| step | without this change | with this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (after init) | 0 / 120 params differ | 0 / 120 |
| 2 | 74 / 120 differ, max abs diff 3.1e-5 | 0 / 120 |
| 5 | 82 / 120, max abs 1.2e-4 | 0 / 120 |
| 30 | 85 / 120, max abs 2.4e-4 (max rel 0.19%) | 0 / 120 |

We first saw this in a strict save/restore check that compares per-rank tensor fingerprints (Qwen3.5-35B, TP2). At save time, the source TP ranks already held different values for these replicated weights. The checkpoint stores a single copy, so the restored TP1 no longer matched the source TP1. In a 122B A/B, the extra all-reduce cost +0.24% step time.

These runs used a slime 0.3.0-based build. On `main`, the `Attention` class touched here differs only by a new `name` argument, and the sequence-parallel gather/scatter in `hf_attention.py` is the same. I haven't rerun the A/B on `main`.

## Notes

- `qwen3_next.py` builds its linear attention the same way and may need the same change. I haven't measured it, so it's not included here.
- No new test: reproducing the drift needs a multi-GPU TP run. Happy to add a test if there's a preferred harness for this.
discussion:
Additional evidence, still on a slime 0.3.0-based build (P6 B200, 10 steps each).

**This change on four Qwen3.5 layouts.** The flag is set in `Attention.__init__`, and the probe only measures. Counts are summed over all ranks.

| Layout | replicated params / flagged / differing across TP (step 10) |
|---|---|
| 35B-A3B TP2 PP1 EP8 SP | 300 / 300 / 0 |
| 122B-A10B TP2 PP4 EP8 SP | 360 / 360 / 0 |
| 122B-A10B TP4 PP4 EP8 SP | 2880 / 2880 / 0 |
| 397B-A17B TP2 PP8 VPP2 EP8 SP | 3600 / 3600 / 0 |

**Numerics, 35B-A3B.** Same seed and data: two runs with this change (F1, F2) and one without it (U).

| pair | loss max / mean abs diff | grad_norm max / mean abs diff |
|---|---|---|
| F1 vs F2 (run-to-run noise) | 1.65e-3 / 7.5e-4 | 1.08 / 0.17 |
| F1 vs U | 2.18e-3 / 4.5e-4 | 0.51 / 0.07 |
| F2 vs U | 1.22e-3 / 6.0e-4 | 1.11 / 0.15 |

Without the change, 1656 of 2400 replicated rank-params differ across TP by step 10. With it, none do. Step time is unchanged (72.4 / 71.9 s vs 71.9 s).

**CI.** The only failing check, `test_swe_workspace_diff.py::test_patch_uses_actual_image_baseline_without_changing_git_index[unstaged]`, looks like a flaky race in the test added in #2457. Git's background maintenance removed `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` during `copytree`. The test passes on `main` at the same commit and is unrelated to this change, which only touches `qwen3_5.py`. Could a maintainer re-run it?

Ready for review whenever someone has time.

items.title: fix: put the critic value head on a VLM's language_model
items.author: annika-modal
items.summary: VLM wrappers like delegate to an inner that owns the LM head. The critic's was assigned to the wrapper, so it was never called: the critic returned vocab-sized logits and the first value step failed the assertion in.
items.body:
VLM wrappers like `Qwen3_5VLModel` delegate `forward()` to an inner `language_model` that owns the LM head. The critic's `LinearForLastLayer` was assigned to the wrapper, so it was never called: the critic returned vocab-sized logits and the first value step failed the `logits.size(-1) == 1` assertion in `loss.py`. This attaches the value head to `language_model` when the model has one (custom-provider and spec-provider paths) and looks it up there in `_iter_critic_output_layers`, so post-load reinitialization still finds it. Plain GPT models are unchanged, and the HF loader already skips the 1-output head.

Added a CPU test that builds a critic through the spec-provider path for a VLM-style wrapper and a plain model; the wrapper case fails without the fix. We hit this on Qwen3-VL through Megatron-Bridge in an older slime and fixed it there with the same change (run on 2×H200, PPO with a critic, 3 steps); I haven't run `Qwen3_5VLModel` with a critic on GPU.

items.title: fix: filter_long_prompt crashes on chat-templated multimodal prompts
items.author: annika-modal
items.summary: With, stores the templated string in and the parsed media in. The multimodal branch of re-ran on that string, which expects a list of messages, so any image dataset with (or ) set failed at load time with.
items.body:
With `apply_chat_template`, `Dataset.__init__` stores the templated string in `sample.prompt` and the parsed media in `sample.multimodal_inputs`. The multimodal branch of `filter_long_prompt` re-ran `process_vision_info` on that string, which expects a list of messages, so any image dataset with `--rollout-max-prompt-len` (or `--rollout-max-context-len`) set failed at load time with `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'`. This reuses `sample.multimodal_inputs` instead.

The existing tests stubbed `process_vision_info` to ignore its input, which hid the bug, so I removed that stub and added a test that fails if the filter re-parses the prompt and checks the parsed media reach the processor. I also reproduced the crash and the fix with the real `Dataset` and a Qwen3-VL processor on CPU.

items.title: [rollout, vllm, perf] feat: add bounded resume admission burst
items.author: jiacao-amd
items.summary: When tools return during a multi-turn rollout, their continuation requests can wait behind a large wave of first requests. Add an opt-in router that admits a bounded number of extra continuation/retry requests while keeping base slots available to fresh work.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When tools return during a multi-turn rollout, their continuation requests can
wait behind a large wave of first requests. Add an opt-in router that admits a
bounded number of extra continuation/retry requests while keeping base slots
available to fresh work. vLLM continues to use FCFS.

`ToolAgentLoop` labels requests as fresh, continuation, or retry; partial-rollout
retries refresh that metadata. The router preserves existing sticky,
least-loaded replica routing and records admission counts and wait times.

Queued admissions and release/control RPCs now use separate Ray concurrency
groups. Per-attempt admission IDs make completion idempotent, cancellation
reconciles remote grants, and server removal retires outstanding accounting.
A canceled client retains its slot while backend generation is still running.
Fresh-wave burst defaults to zero, and overdue fresh work stops new burst
admissions. The plugin remains opt-in; no unmeasured backend-pressure
thresholds or automatic tuning are added.

Backend request-priority policies, their configuration fields, SGLang priority
forwarding, and the companion effective-cost admission plugin are removed from
the final diff. The existing explicit vLLM priority path for single-turn
determinism is unchanged. Historical priority experiments remain documented as
evidence for retaining FCFS, without configuration examples for removed APIs.

This updates the existing contribution and replaces closed draft #8135; it does
not introduce a second PR. The earlier duplicate-work checks are recorded at:

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+resume+priority+scheduling
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+agent+loop+priority
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+resume+priority+scheduling

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs; query links are above.
- [x] Use the required module/type title format.

### Test

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_call_tool_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_response_length_cap_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_router_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_routed_experts_on_cpu.py \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_audio_server_contract_on_cpu.py -q
```

81 passed, 2 Ray warnings, 136.95 seconds. A subsequent targeted success/error
matrix passed both cases (2 passed, 44 deselected, 35.43 seconds), including
an additional backend-error case:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/workers/rollout/test_router_on_cpu.py \
  -k cancelled_client_keeps_slot -q
```

Together these runs cover 82 distinct tests. Tests use real local Ray actors for the 1000
queued-acquire saturation limit, remote cancellation, completed-grant races,
and backend completion after client cancellation. Other regression tests
cover stale releases, removed/re-registered servers, fresh-wave gates,
partial-rollout metadata, legacy plugins, and audio/multimodal contracts.

All staged pre-commit hooks passed, including generated-config verification,
mypy, and formatting; no hooks were skipped. The scheduling RST section parses
with five tables and no warnings. The SGLang adapter, rollout configuration
schema, and generated configurations match the base.

Serving measurements use MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL on AMD MI355X, 64 trajectories,
four model turns each, approximately 8K initial prompt tokens, 64 output tokens
per request, pipelined arrivals, and tool waits of 0.25/0.5/1/2 seconds. Warmups
are excluded; formal groups have three hot repetitions and distinct sessions.

| Same-node configuration | Three wall times (s) | Mean +/- sample std (s) |
|---|---|---|
| Single TP4 reference | 16.777641, 16.712037, 16.731432 | 16.740370 +/- 0.033703 |
| Single TP8, FCFS | 12.159869, 12.218751, 12.176857 | 12.185159 +/- 0.030306 |
| Two simultaneous TP4 replicas, FCFS | 9.885591, 9.963323, 9.972187 | 9.940367 +/- 0.047644 |

Two TP4 replicas reduce wall time by 18.42% versus single TP8 using the same
number of GPUs. At admission capacity 64, this workload triggers zero burst
admissions; that gain comes from replica parallelism. The single-TP4 reference
uses the capacity-40, fresh-wave-cap-1, resume-cap-20 router below.

An earlier four-GPU study measured 22.459374 seconds for the original FIFO
baseline and 16.035935 seconds after joint engine/router tuning (-28.60%). This
is a historical comparison from a separate measurement batch; it does not
isolate the contribution of burst admission. Full TTFT, queue, utilization,
preemption, prefix-cache, environment, and rejected-case details are recorded
in `docs/advance/agent_loop.rst`.

These are standalone serving measurements, not a full PPO training run or a
validation of live-trainer replica balance. Expert parallel remains excluded
from the production recommendation because output equivalence is unverified.
The serving measurements above predate the lifecycle fixes in this update.
No GPU rerun was performed for these fixes: read-only cluster inspection found
no immediately available idle burst node, and existing jobs were left intact.
The current implementation still needs a same-engine, same-base-capacity
burst-on/off GPU comparison before extending the workload recommendation.

Burst does not help every workload. In the earlier TP8 capacity-40 active-burst
candidate, wall time was 14.081865 seconds versus 12.188314 seconds for the
capacity-64 FIFO cross-check (+15.54%). Its coefficient of variation was 2.20%,
so it was rejected. Capacity changed as well, so this is evidence against that
configuration, not an isolated measurement of burst cost.

### API and Usage Example

Router YAML for the tested single-TP4 workload:

```yaml
router_class: verl.workers.rollout.router.SoftAdmissionRequestLoadBalancer
max_concurrent_requests: 40
fresh_wave_max_resume_burst_requests: 1
max_resume_burst_requests: 20
fresh_max_wait_seconds: 60
```

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    name: vllm
    scheduling_policy: fcfs
    max_num_seqs: 32
    engine_kwargs:
      vllm:
        max_num_batched_tokens: 32768
        async_scheduling: false
    router_config_path: /path/to/request_router.yaml
```

These settings are workload-specific examples, not new defaults. Without the
router configuration, the existing default load balancer is used.

### Design & Code Changes

The base admission capacity is available to every request. Only continuation
and retry requests can use extra burst slots. The burst target is:

```text
min(current_burst_cap,
    ceil(base_capacity * resume_pressure / total_pressure))
```

Pressure includes queued and in-flight requests. The lower fresh-wave cap
defaults to zero while fresh requests remain queued; explicitly measured
configurations can opt into a small cap. The larger cap applies after the
router fresh queue drains, which means admission, not backend completion.
Overdue fresh work stops new burst admissions; existing requests are not
preempted. The threshold does not promise an end-to-end latency bound.

Each backend attempt receives a unique admission ID, separate from the sticky
trajectory ID. Duplicate and stale releases cannot free another attempt.
Client cancellation cancels a queued Ray acquire and reconciles a grant that
completed first. After backend generation starts, cancellation defers release
to backend completion/failure. Server removal clears its grants, and late
completion cannot affect replacement work; the caller remains responsible for
stopping generation on the removed server.

Ray admission and control methods run in separate concurrency groups, with a
lock protecting shared state and thread-safe waiter delivery. Saturating the
admission group therefore leaves release and server-management RPCs runnable.
No polling or extra RPC is added to the successful request path.

Removing `router_config_path` fully restores the default load balancer.
Setting only `max_resume_burst_requests: 0` still retains base admission limits.
No backend queue/KV-cache thresholds are inferred from request counts; tune
and validate the opt-in configuration using full rollout wall time.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Run all pre-commit hooks on changed files.
- [x] Update documentation and relevant existing CPU tests.
- [ ] Run repository-wide `pre-commit run --all-files` before requesting review.
- [ ] Human submitter review of every line in the updated diff and independent
  relevant test execution before requesting review.
- [ ] Request project CI when the draft is ready.

### AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, benchmarks, and this update.
Commits contain `Co-authored-by` and `Signed-off-by` trailers. The PR remains a
draft for human review; the current update does not claim human review of new
lines or independent human test execution.

items.title: [rollout, vllm, perf] feat: prioritize resumed agent requests
items.author: jiacao-amd
items.summary: Adds opt-in, resume-aware scheduling for multi-turn agent rollouts: - classifies model requests as,, or and records prompt, estimated uncached-token, expected-output, and enqueue metadata. It reserves no idle slots; the burst target returns to zero without r…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds opt-in, resume-aware scheduling for multi-turn agent rollouts:

- `ToolAgentLoop` classifies model requests as `fresh`, `continuation`, or
  `retry` and records prompt, estimated uncached-token, expected-output, and
  enqueue metadata.
- A pluggable priority policy converts lightweight request-cost estimates and
  wait time into vLLM priority values.
- A router plugin keeps a base admission capacity and dynamically admits extra
  continuation/retry requests when resume pressure is present. It reserves no
  idle slots; the burst target returns to zero without resume traffic.
- Partial-rollout retries refresh their request metadata and remaining token
  budget.

All new behavior is disabled by default.

This does not duplicate an existing contribution. Searches performed before
opening this PR found no matching open PR or issue:

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+resume+priority+scheduling
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+agent+loop+priority
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+resume+priority+scheduling

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Query links are included above.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_call_tool_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_response_length_cap_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_router_on_cpu.py -q

59 passed, 2 warnings
```

Staged pre-commit results:

- Ruff: passed
- Ruff format: passed
- mypy: passed
- generated trainer config verification: passed
- documentation, license, device API, DataProto, test-structure, example-name,
  uv/GPU-branch, and Python compile hooks: passed
- The naming hook was skipped because it scans the in-repository `.venv` and
  reports `veRL` inside Ray's installed example. The files changed by this PR
  were checked separately and contain no prohibited spelling.

Prototype agentic serving evaluation used the exact scheduling classes in this
change against patched vLLM/AITER on MI355X, TP8, FP8 KV, 64 sessions x 4 model
turns, 8K initial input, 64 output tokens per turn, and base concurrency 32:

| Policy | Trajectory throughput | Rollout wall time |
|---|---:|---:|
| FIFO | 1.362/s | 46.99 s |
| Effective-cost priority | 1.502/s | 42.61 s |
| Priority + dynamic resume burst | 1.793/s | 35.69 s |

- Combined strategy vs FIFO: +31.66% trajectory throughput, -24.05% wall time.
- Dynamic burst vs the same priority policy: +19.40% throughput, -16.25% wall
  time.
- 256/256 requests completed with zero failures.
- Prefix-cache hit rate remained approximately 74.43%.

The benchmark was a standalone multi-session agentic harness rather than a
complete PPO training run. The final cleanup removes disabled experimental
headroom paths and tightens burst-cap enforcement; the serving evaluation will
be rerun before moving the PR out of draft.

### API and Usage Example

Router YAML:

```yaml
router_class: verl.workers.rollout.router.EffectiveCostAdmissionRequestLoadBalancer
max_concurrent_requests: 32
max_resume_burst_requests: 32
fresh_max_wait_seconds: 60
target_wait_seconds: 26
```

Rollout configuration:

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    name: vllm
    scheduling_policy: priority
    router_config_path: /path/to/request_router.yaml
    multi_turn:
      request_priority_policy: verl.workers.rollout.request_scheduling.EffectiveCostPriorityPolicy
      request_priority_policy_kwargs:
        target_wait_seconds: 26
        cost_per_priority: 256
        max_priority: 64
```

The numeric values are workload-specific tuning examples, not new defaults.

### Design & Code Changes

The cost model is:

```text
estimated_cost =
    prefill_weight * estimated_uncached_tokens
  + decode_weight * expected_output_tokens
    * (1 + prompt_tokens / decode_context_scale)

effective_cost = estimated_cost / (1 + wait_seconds / target_wait_seconds)
```

Lower effective cost maps to higher vLLM priority. Soft aging prevents
indefinite starvation, and an optional fresh-request wait bound is available as
a hard guard.

The dynamic burst target is pressure-derived and capped:

```text
ceil(base_capacity * resume_pressure / total_pressure)
```

Only continuation/retry pressure enables extra admission. Fresh traffic may
use the entire base capacity, so the implementation does not pre-reserve idle
resume slots.

  admission, cancellation, aging, burst behavior, and burst-cap reduction.
- [ ] Request project CI after the draft is ready for review.

### AI assistance

AI assistance was used to implement, test, benchmark, and prepare this change.
The human submitter reviewed the complete diff, understands the implementation,

items.body:
Bumps [trl](https://github.com/huggingface/trl) from 0.27.0 to 1.14.1.
Release notes

Sourced from trl's releases.

v1.14.1

What's Changed

  • Fix the server-mode crash at the first weight sync on vLLM 0.20 to 0.25 by @​albertvillanova in huggingface/trl#7410
  • [Fix] Generate one completion per sample after tool calls in vLLM server mode by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7418
  • Preserve explicit model_init_kwargs in CLI scripts by @​DaoyuanLi2816 in huggingface/trl#7394
  • Honor resume_from_checkpoint in CLI scripts by @​DaoyuanLi2816 in huggingface/trl#7391

Full Changelog: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/compare/v1.14.0...v1.14.1

v1.14.0

Features

trl.losses is gone: DPO, KTO and GRPO stream their own log-probs

[!WARNING] from trl.losses import FusedLinearDPOLoss (or FusedLinearKTOLoss, FusedLinearGRPOLoss, FusedLinearJSDLoss) no longer works. The module introduced in v1.13 has been removed.

v1.13 vendored Liger's chunked_loss into trl.losses as a holding action, not a destination (#7063). The problem it was holding: those classes reimplement each trainer's loss math, so TRL carried two copies of every formula, and copies drift. That drift is where the bugs were. GRPO's grad_norm differed from the default path, KTO ignored the reference model under PEFT, KTO class weights and DPO label_smoothing were silently dropped. Worst of all, under plain DDP the fused path ran the loss on the unwrapped model, so DistributedDataParallel's reducer was never armed and gradients were never all-reduced: every rank silently kept its own.

The fix is to stop reimplementing. All DPO, KTO and GRPO need from the fused path is per-token log-probs of the selected tokens, and TRL already had _ChunkedLogProbFunction for exactly that: it streams the vocabulary with an online logsumexp and recomputes in the backward pass. Each trainer now runs backbone -> _ChunkedLogProbFunction -> its own existing loss code, unchanged. One implementation of each loss, and the memory win is kept, because full logits are still never materialized.

Thirteen restrictions existed only because the loss had been rewritten in a form that could not express those options. Most are gone: DPO with use_liger_kernel=True now accepts mixed loss types, f-divergences and precomputed reference log-probs, and GRPO gains entropy and off-policy masking. Still refused: use_weighting, compute_metrics, a PEFT adapter on lm_head, prompt-learning PEFT, and the MoE auxiliary loss.

Single H100, Qwen3-0.6B, bs=4, seq 512:

config median step peak
v1.13 fused, inline ref 0.2243 s 7.05 GB
v1.14 chunked, inline ref 0.2457 s (+9.5%) 7.05 GB
v1.14 chunked, precompute_ref_log_probs=True 0.1971 s (-12.1%) 4.83 GB (-31%)

The third row is the point: that configuration did not exist before, because the fused path rejected precomputed reference log-probs outright.

use_liger_kernel=True still works and still enables Liger's model kernels through transformers. In DPO, GRPO and KTO it now selects TRL's chunked log-probability path instead of Liger's fused loss.

  • Stream KTO log probabilities by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7075
  • Stream GRPO log probabilities by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7077
  • Move DPO to chunked log probabilities by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7243
  • Drop the fused Liger JSD path from the experimental distillation trainers by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7301
  • Skip frozen chunked log probability gradients by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7076
  • Redirect the KTO liger loss through the distributed wrapper under DDP by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7247
  • Document what use_liger_kernel actually does in each trainer by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7361

A fused Triton logprob + entropy kernel now ships in TRL

The loss head is the only hot path TRL owns: transformers already kernelizes the model internals, and nothing on the Hub covers what happens after the decoder. On one H100 (bf16, V=151936, H=4096, 8192 tokens), selective_log_softmax plus entropy_from_logits cost 12.8 ms and 2.32 GiB over [8, 1024, 151936]. A fused Triton kernel does the same in 0.89 ms, roughly 14x, and lands closer to the fp32 reference than the bf16 path it replaces. GRPO runs this two to four times per step.

It now lives in-tree at trl.kernels and is on by default on CUDA, ROCm and XPU, with the PyTorch implementation as fallback. It was briefly loaded from the Hub; that was reversed because this kernel is pure Triton and compiles at runtime, so the Hub bought nothing while costing a version gate unrelated to whether the kernel works, a download that fails offline, trust_remote_code=True for anyone with kernels installed, a silent except Exception: pass wrapped around all of it, and 13 of 13 tests skipped in CI.

... (truncated)

  • 55aaf50 Fix the server-mode crash at the first weight sync on vLLM 0.20 to 0.25 (#7410)
  • c6a6a16 Release: v1.14 (#7392)
  • cc5bb3f Agree on logged keys across ranks before flushing GRPO and RLOO metrics (#7382)
  • 5469923 Ship the logprob and entropy kernel in trl instead of the Hub (#7363)
