items.title: [7/7] [rollout] feat: audit that training and rollout quantize the same layers
items.author: wengeezhang
items.summary: Audits, at the first weight sync after a training step, that the learner and the rollout engine quantize the same layers, per parameter name. On vLLM the audit asks the live engine.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Audits, at the first weight sync after a training step, that **the learner and the rollout engine quantize the same layers**, per parameter name. On vLLM the audit asks the live engine. On SGLang, the refit loader refuses a sync whose dtypes disagree with the engine's parameters.

This is part 7, the last, of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell). **It is stacked on #8131** (and through it on #8129, #8130, #8127 and #7918):
- until they merge, this diff includes them, and the change of this PR is its last commit;
- it builds on #8131 because the SGLang dtype check shares the loader and its `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK` switch.

| # | PR | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #8127: MXFP8 training + shared TE quantizer | main |
| 2 | #8128: quantized-rollout sentinel | main |
| 3 | #7918: exact MXFP8 exclusion matcher | main |
| 4 | #8129: MXFP8 vLLM rollout | 1, 3 |
| 5 | #8130: MXFP8 SGLang rollout + refit loader | 1 |
| 6 | #8131: post-sync refit self-check | 4, 5 |
| 7 | **this PR**: quantized-layer audit | 6 |

**Why.** "Matched" train/rollout quantization presumes both sides quantize the same layers, but the two sets are decided by unrelated mechanisms:
- training decides implicitly: a TE linear module inside `fp8_autocast` is quantized;
- rollout decides by name: `ignored_layers` and the sync-time name rule.

Nothing checked that they agree, and on B200 they did not. vLLM 0.24's ModelOpt matcher turned the router exclusion `mlp.gate` into an exclusion of the dense `mlp.gate_up_proj`, so 56 of 311 parameters of Qwen3-1.7B were served in BF16 while training ran them in FP8. Nothing else noticed:
- KL stayed at 0.007–0.010, inside the healthy range;
- the self-check's probed layers were fine;
- the configured rule reported 28 of 28 layers in agreement.

Only asking the engine exposed it. #7918 / #8129 fix that matcher; this PR catches the class of fault.

**What.**
- **Trainer side** (`verl/utils/quant_layer_audit.py`). Which decoder layers ran FP8 GEMMs is read from TE's FP8 weight workspaces. The audit wraps the training engine's weight export (`get_per_tensor_param`), which every sync route passes through (the colocated worker, the checkpoint engine, the server-replica path). It compares, per synced parameter name, with the rollout side and gives its verdict when the weight stream ends.
- **Param offload.** The signal survives `param_offload=True`: modules are marked before offload drops the workspace cache. With no signal at all, the audit warns that it cannot run.
- **vLLM.** `quantized_param_names` asks the live engine, through `collective_rpc`, which parameters it holds in FP8. The server now returns the per-worker results.
- **SGLang.** There is no return channel, so the trainer compares with the sync rule. The refit loader then checks, before anything is written, that every incoming linear weight's dtype matches the engine parameter that will receive it. HF names are mapped onto SGLang's fused modules, and a mismatch is refused by name instead of cast silently, e.g. Mixtral's `experts.N.w1/w2/w3`, which the sync rule misses.
- **Switch.** `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=warn` (default) logs disagreements, `=raise` makes them fatal, `=0` disables the audit.

**Evidence on B200** (#7519):
- it caught the fault above (56 of 311 parameters);
- in the healthy runs it agreed with the engine on all 69 and all 18,867 parameters it checked (small MoE; Qwen3-30B-A3B).

**Known limitation.** On SGLang there is no engine query, so the audit judges against the sync-time rule and inherits its errors. On vLLM the engine re-check cannot see a quantized `ParallelLMHead`, so `lm_head` is judged by the configured rule alone. That rule used to count `lm_head` as quantized under FP8 blockwise, which vLLM's FP8 method never does, and reported one spurious disagreement in warn mode; it now leaves `lm_head` unquantized under FP8 (d637e696).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+quantized+layer. No open PR checks train/rollout quantized-layer agreement; this is part 7 of #7519's split.
- [x] PR title formatted as `[rollout] feat: ...`

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_quant_layer_audit_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py -q
# 42 passed
# all MXFP8 CPU tests at this commit:
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py \
  tests/utils/test_quant_layer_audit_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_quant_utils_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_utils_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_vllm_quant_utils_moe_on_cpu.py -q
# 132 passed, 1 skipped
```

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. Environment knobs:
- `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT`: `warn` (default) / `raise` / `0`;
- `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE=1`: traces the hook path.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/quant_layer_audit.py`: training-side report, rollout predicates (vLLM rule, SGLang sync rule), comparison, engine re-check, logging that always reports a verdict or why none was possible.
- `verl/workers/engine_workers.py`: install the auditor on the training engine; ask vLLM for its FP8 parameters after the sync.
- `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: the export hook.
- `verl/utils/megatron_utils.py`: mark modules before offload drops the TE workspace cache.
- `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py`, `vllm_rollout.py`, `vllm_async_server.py`: `quantized_param_names` and the returned `collective_rpc` results.
- `verl/workers/rollout/sglang_rollout/mxfp8_refit_loader.py`: the sync-vs-engine dtype check, run before anything is written.
- `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`: "Quantized-layer audit".
- Tests:
  - `test_quant_layer_audit_on_cpu.py`;
  - the SGLang loader tests for name resolution across fused modules and for the dtype check.

### AI assistance disclosure

Developed with AI assistance. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, ran the B200 experiments reported in #7519, and can defend the change end to end.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`.
- [x] Add unit test(s): CPU tests above; hardware evidence in #7519.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.

items.title: [6/7] [rollout] feat: self-check MXFP8 kernel layouts after every weight sync
items.author: wengeezhang
items.summary: After every MXFP8 weight sync, runs the engine's own kernel on one layer and one MoE expert and compares the result with a dequantized BF16 reference. A stale or mis-laid-out kernel layout raises instead of silently serving garbage.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

After every MXFP8 weight sync, **runs the engine's own kernel on one layer and one MoE expert** and compares the result with a dequantized BF16 reference. A stale or mis-laid-out kernel layout raises instead of silently serving garbage. Works on both vLLM and SGLang.

This is part 6 of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell). **It is stacked on #8129 and #8130** (and through them on #8127 and #7918): until they merge, this diff includes them, and the change of this PR is its last commit.

| # | PR | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #8127: MXFP8 training + shared TE quantizer | main |
| 2 | #8128: quantized-rollout sentinel | main |
| 3 | #7918: exact MXFP8 exclusion matcher | main |
| 4 | #8129: MXFP8 vLLM rollout | 1, 3 |
| 5 | #8130: MXFP8 SGLang rollout + refit loader | 1 |
| 6 | **this PR**: post-sync refit self-check | 4, 5 |
| 7 | #8132: quantized-layer audit | 6 |

**Why.** Both engines rewrite synced weights and scales into kernel-specific layouts after loading: swizzled scales, shuffled or interleaved experts. If a re-derivation is missed, the kernel pairs fresh weights with stale scales, yet:
- every shape and dtype still matches;
- the sync reports success;
- the job exits 0.

Two such faults reached runs on B200:
- **SGLang FlashInfer CUTLASS dense scales:** KL 7.2, accuracy 0.000.
- **vLLM TRT-LLM MXFP8 MoE experts:** a repack that kept shape and dtype escaped the refit cycle. On a small test MoE the KL was only 0.047, below any divergence alarm; only a check that runs the kernel could see it.

**What.**
- **Dense probe.** `verl/utils/mxfp8_refit_check.py` runs the smallest MXFP8 linear layer's own quantized GEMM on a small random input and compares it with a BF16 GEMM on the dequantized canonical weight and scale. The canonical copy is captured after `load_weights` and before the kernel layout is re-derived.
- **MoE probe.** One local expert of the smallest MXFP8 MoE layer is probed the same way: every probe row is routed to it, and the result is compared with a dequantized gated-MLP reference.
- **Threshold.** A relative error above `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL` (default 0.25; `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL` for experts) raises.
- **Unwritten expert scales (SGLang).** Before re-deriving the layout, the loader also checks that the sync wrote every staged expert scale (the staging buffer is pre-filled with the UE8M0 NaN code `0xFF`). It names experts the sync rule missed instead of pairing them with NaN scales.
- `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=0` disables both.

**Evidence on B200** (#7519).
- **Healthy MXFP8 runs:** the probes read 0.026–0.027 (dense) and 0.049–0.052 (expert), five to nine times below the tolerance. No false alarm.
- **The stale TRT-LLM expert layout:** 1.739 at the first sync.
- **Deliberate trip:** with the tolerance lowered to 1e-6, the MoE self-check raised at the first sync, confirming the stop path end to end.
- **Overhead:** on Qwen3-30B-A3B a sync with quantization and the checks takes 4 s longer than a BF16 one, about 1% of a step.

**Where a probe is skipped.** The log states every skip:
- vLLM, expert probe: under expert or data parallelism, and for non-SiLU gates;
- SGLang, expert probe: under expert parallelism, under TP without `reduce_results`, and where the router logits it makes up cannot pin one expert at weight 1 (sigmoid, grouped, biased or custom routing, fused shared experts, a routed scaling factor). The probe runs through the model's own TopK, so it also runs on SGLang's default FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE runner; on 1×B200 with SGLang 0.5.20 it read 0.049–0.054 on every sync and 1.756 when the expert layout was re-derived twice.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+refit+check. No open PR validates kernel layouts after a weight sync; this is part 6 of #7519's split.
- [x] PR title formatted as `[rollout] feat: ...`

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_quant_utils_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py -q
# 35 passed
# all MXFP8 CPU tests at this commit:
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_quant_utils_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_utils_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_quant_utils_moe_on_cpu.py -q
# 105 passed, 1 skipped
```

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. Environment knobs: `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK` (`0` disables), `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL` (default `0.25`), `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL` (default: the linear tolerance).

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/mxfp8_refit_check.py`: UE8M0 dequantization, the dense and MoE-expert references, the assertions and the env switches.
- `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`: snapshot after `load_weights`, probe after the kernel layout is re-derived (`process_quanted_weights_after_loading`); the expert probe calls the weight holder's `forward_modular` / `forward_monolithic`.
- `verl/workers/rollout/sglang_rollout/mxfp8_refit_loader.py`: the same probes after re-processing, and the unwritten-scale check.
- `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`: "Post-sync self-check".
- Tests:
  - `test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py`;
  - the vLLM and SGLang refit tests now also cover the probes passing on a healthy refit, catching a stale dense or expert layout, and their skips.

### AI assistance disclosure

Developed with AI assistance. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, ran the B200 experiments reported in #7519, and can defend the change end to end.

items.title: [5/7] [rollout, sglang] feat: MXFP8 SGLang rollout with a refit loader
items.author: wengeezhang
items.summary: Adds MXFP8 rollout on SGLang: - at every weight sync, the learner's own TE quantizer quantizes the weights on the trainer side before they are streamed, so the sampler serves the learner's FP8 weight grid; - a refit loader re-derives SGLang's kernel-specific s…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds **MXFP8 rollout on SGLang**:
- at every weight sync, the learner's own TE quantizer quantizes the weights on the trainer side before they are streamed, so the sampler serves the learner's FP8 weight grid;
- a **refit loader** re-derives SGLang's kernel-specific scale layouts after each sync. Without it, the FlashInfer and DeepGEMM MXFP8 backends serve garbage after the first sync.

This is part 5 of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell). **It is stacked on #8127**: until that merges, this diff includes it, and the change of this PR is its last commit.

| # | PR | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #8127: MXFP8 training + shared TE quantizer | main |
| 2 | #8128: quantized-rollout sentinel | main |
| 3 | #7918: exact MXFP8 exclusion matcher | main |
| 4 | #8129: MXFP8 vLLM rollout | 1, 3 |
| 5 | **this PR**: MXFP8 SGLang rollout + refit loader | 1 |
| 6 | #8131: post-sync refit self-check | 4, 5 |
| 7 | #8132: quantized-layer audit | 6 |

**Launch and sync.** With `rollout.quantization: mxfp8`, SGLang starts from the BF16 checkpoint with its FP8 method in MXFP8 mode (a `quantization_config` override, no offline conversion). `lm_head` and the token embedding are in `ignored_layers`; SGLang builds MoE routers without a quantization config. `ServerAdapter.update_weights` quantizes with `verl.utils.mxfp8_quant.mxfp8_quantize` (from #8127) before streaming `(weight, weight_scale_inv)`.

**Why the refit loader is needed.** SGLang's FlashInfer CUTLASS / CuTe-DSL and DeepGEMM MXFP8 backends derive a kernel-specific copy of the weight scales at load (`weight_scale_inv_swizzled` / `weight_scale_inv_deepgemm`), and SGLang's weight-update path never rebuilds it. On 2×B200 with SGLang 0.5.12 and `flashinfer_cutlass`:
- generation was garbage from step 0: held-out accuracy 0.000, train–rollout KL 7.2, entropy 10.4 (about uniform over the vocabulary), while the job exited 0;
- with the loader, accuracy went 0.360 → 0.727 in 6 steps and KL matched the Triton path (0.0067).

**What the loader does.**
- **Registration.** `mxfp8_refit_loader.load_and_reprocess` is registered at launch and named as each update's `load_format`.
- **Dense layers.** It loads the tensors the standard way, then re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` on every MXFP8 layer whose *resolved* backend keeps a derived copy. That backend is read from the layer: sglang ≥ 0.5.18 resolves FlashInfer or DeepGEMM by default; on older versions it is `flashinfer_cutlass` only.
- **MoE expert scales.** SGLang rewrites them in place at load, so the loader stages them back to the canonical `[E, N, K/32]` layout for `load_weights` and folds the re-derived layout back into the storage the CUDA graph captured.
- **Rejected backend.** `flashinfer_trtllm` shuffles the weight tensor itself in place and cannot be re-processed idempotently.

**Other changes.**
- **Delta checkpoint engine.** It applies raw BF16 in place and would bypass the weight-sync quantization, so it is now rejected with rollout quantization (fp8 included).
- **GEMM-backend warning.** On sglang < 0.5.18 without an explicit GEMM backend, a launch warning names the flag. Measured with Qwen3-8B on 2×B200, the default Triton MXFP8 GEMM decoded 1.9× slower than BF16 (52 vs. 27 ms per response token); `flashinfer_cutlass` was 1.3× slower (34 ms).

**Evidence on B200** (gsm8k, Qwen3-8B, SGLang 0.5.12, 30 steps; #7519):
- with every decoder linear on the learner's grid, step-1 train–rollout KL is 0.00681;
- over the last 10 steps it is 0.00670, 46% below FP8 tensorwise training with a BF16 sampler;
- no non-finite metric.

**Not validated on hardware:**
- the sglang ≥ 0.5.18 backend resolution (CPU tests only);
- the SGLang MoE path (CPU tests only).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+mxfp8.
  - **#7186** (draft) also adds MXFP8 SGLang rollout, but quantizes with an independent Triton kernel and has no refit loader. This PR quantizes with TE's quantizer, so the sampler holds the learner's grid, and it handles the derived scale layouts.
  - This is part 5 of #7519's split.
- [x] PR title formatted as `[rollout, sglang] feat: ...`

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_utils_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py -q
# 23 passed
# with #8127's tests and the existing preprocess test:
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py \
  tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_utils_on_cpu.py -q
```

items.title: [4/7] [rollout, vllm] feat: MXFP8 vLLM rollout on the learner's weight grid
items.author: wengeezhang
items.summary: Adds MXFP8 rollout on vLLM whose weights are quantized, at every weight sync, by the learner's own TE quantizer. The sampler therefore serves the learner's FP8 weight grid (E4M3 elements, one E8M0 scale per 32-element block), not an independent re-quantization…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds **MXFP8 rollout on vLLM** whose weights are quantized, at every weight sync, by the learner's own TE quantizer. The sampler therefore serves the learner's FP8 weight grid (E4M3 elements, one E8M0 scale per 32-element block), not an independent re-quantization.

This is part 4 of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell). **It is stacked on #8127 and #7918**: until they merge, this diff includes them, and the change of this PR is its last commit.

| # | PR | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #8127: MXFP8 training + shared TE quantizer | main |
| 2 | #8128: quantized-rollout sentinel | main |
| 3 | #7918: exact MXFP8 exclusion matcher | main |
| 4 | **this PR**: MXFP8 vLLM rollout | 1, 3 |
| 5 | #8130: MXFP8 SGLang rollout + refit loader | 1 |
| 6 | #8131: post-sync refit self-check | 4, 5 |
| 7 | #8132: quantized-layer audit | 6 |

**How it works.**
- **Launch.** With `rollout.quantization: mxfp8`, vLLM starts from the BF16 checkpoint with an injected config that it normalizes to `ModelOptMxFp8Config` (weight `fp8_e4m3fn`, `uint8` UE8M0 `weight_scale`, block `[1, 32]`).
- **What stays BF16.** `lm_head`, the token embedding and the MoE routers are in `ignored_layers`.
- **Exclusion matching.** The config is marked for #7918's exact module-path matching, because vLLM 0.24's substring fallback otherwise turns the router entry `mlp.gate` into an exclusion of the dense `mlp.gate_up_proj`.
- **Quantization.** Each sync quantizes the BF16 weights inside the vLLM worker with `verl.utils.mxfp8_quant.mxfp8_quantize` (from #8127).
- **Refits.** They reuse verl's existing FP8 record/stage/reprocess/fold cycle, with the ModelOpt MXFP8 dense and MoE methods registered, so kernel layouts are re-derived into the storage that CUDA graphs captured.
- **Two MoE details:**
  - vLLM 0.24's `ModelOptMxFp8FusedMoE` processes its weights once and returns early afterwards, so the patched hook clears that flag on every refit;
  - `replace_parameter` is also intercepted in the ModelOpt namespace, so the kernel objects rebuilt after a refit point at the live parameters. The same-shape repack record is already in main (#7986).

**Evidence on B200** (full methodology in #7519):
- **Byte check.** At two syncs, layers 0/17/35 × all projections × both TP ranks: the engine's E4M3/E8M0 bytes, the post-processed kernel layouts and the learner's cached FP8 forward weights agree. 0 of ~600 MB differ in every comparison. At the second sync, 14 optimizer updates had changed 0.84% of those FP8 bytes, so a stale sampler would have been caught.
- **Same quantizer.** TE's quantizer and vLLM's own MXFP8 quantizer agree byte for byte on all 252 linear weights of Qwen3-8B.
- **Consistency.** In one engine at fixed weights (Qwen3-8B, learning rate 0, paired prompts), train–rollout KL with an MXFP8 learner falls by:
  - 10.6% [8.6, 12.7] with the qkv/o/down projections on the grid;
  - 16.1% [14.1, 18.1] with every linear on the grid,

  both against a BF16 sampler.
- **MoE.** On Qwen3-30B-A3B (4×B200, TP2 × EP2), verl's FP8-blockwise pipeline, whose sampler rounds onto a different grid, has 2× the KL of this pipeline from step 1 (0.00921 vs. 0.00446). Its generation takes 24% less time than BF16's.
- **Refit fix.** For a TRT-LLM MXFP8 MoE layer whose repack keeps shape and dtype, an expert's output relative error against a dequantized reference was 1.739 after the first sync without the refit record and 0.052 with it.
- **Dense rollout speed.** With every linear on the grid, the difference from BF16 is within the run-to-run spread of two identical BF16 samplers (3.1%).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+mxfp8. #7186 (draft) targets SGLang with an independent Triton quantizer. No open PR adds MXFP8 vLLM rollout. This is part 4 of #7519's split.
- [x] PR title formatted as `[rollout, vllm] feat: ...`

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_quant_utils_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py -q
# 9 passed
# with #8127, #7918 and the existing vLLM MoE refit tests:
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py \
  tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_quant_utils_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_vllm_quant_utils_moe_on_cpu.py -q
# 66 passed, 1 skipped
```

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files.

### API and Usage Example

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref.rollout:
  name: vllm
  quantization: mxfp8
```

Pair it with `fp8_recipe: mxfp8` training (#8127) to put the sampler on the learner's grid. vLLM's Marlin/emulation fallbacks can also serve MXFP8 weights on SM80+ (not exercised on Blackwell, which takes the native path).

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py`: the `mxfp8` launch config and the exact-matching marker.
- `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`:
  - `is_vllm_modelopt_mxfp8_quant`;
  - `quant_weights` quantizes with the TE quantizer and emits `<name>_scale`, the ModelOpt name (blockwise FP8 uses `_scale_inv`); the 2D scale is not squeezed.
- `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_fp8_utils.py`: registers the ModelOpt MXFP8 dense and MoE methods with the refit cycle; clears the MoE once-flag; intercepts `replace_parameter` per quant module.
- `verl/trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml`: lists `mxfp8` among the rollout quantization options.
- Docs:
  - `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`: "MXFP8 Rollout and Train-Inference Consistency";
  - `docs/low_precision/mxfp8_exclusion_patch.md`: verl now marks its generated config.
- Tests:
  - `tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_quant_utils_on_cpu.py`: config detection, quantizer and scale naming, the patched methods surviving a refit, the full refit cycle, the MoE once-flag, the same-shape repack being restaged, the identity backend left alone;
  - `test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py`: the vLLM launch config keeps `lm_head` in BF16.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes both PPO trainers **raise instead of logging** when a quantized rollout is evidently producing garbage. It is a no-op unless `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization` is set, and it applies to the existing FP8 rollout as well as MXFP8.

This is part 2 of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell). It has no dependencies.

| # | PR | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #8127: MXFP8 training + shared TE quantizer | main |
| 2 | **this PR**: quantized-rollout sentinel | main |
| 3 | #7918: exact MXFP8 exclusion matcher | main |
| 4 | #8129: MXFP8 vLLM rollout | 1, 3 |
| 5 | #8130: MXFP8 SGLang rollout + refit loader | 1 |
| 6 | #8131: post-sync refit self-check | 4, 5 |
| 7 | #8132: quantized-layer audit | 6 |

**Why.** Two failures met while validating MXFP8 rollout on 2×B200 were silent: the job exited 0 and every metric kept being logged.
- A quantized `lm_head` made the rollout logits NaN. Sampling never emitted EOS, and reward stayed 0.000 for all 20 steps.
- An engine kept serving kernel scale layouts derived at load after a weight sync. Train–rollout KL read 7.2 (healthy quantized rollouts: 0.001–0.03), entropy approached log(vocab), and every response hit the length cap.

**What.** Both failures show up in the step metrics from step 1. `check_quantized_rollout_metrics` raises if any of these holds:
1. `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` is non-finite while the batch had valid tokens;
2. `rollout_corr/kl` is non-finite or above `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX` (default 1.0);
3. `response_length/clip_ratio` is about 1 on `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_CLIP_STEPS` consecutive steps (default 2).

`VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL=0` disables it.

**Limits.** The sentinel only catches gross failures. A moderate fault stays inside the range of healthy quantized rollouts, so no threshold separates it, e.g.:
- one layer type left unquantized: KL 0.007–0.010;
- a stale MoE expert layout: KL 0.047.

The mechanism checks (#8131, #8132) cover those. On B200, with the truncation trigger set to one step, the sentinel stopped a randomly initialized MoE whose responses all hit the length cap at step 1.

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+quantized+rollout. No open PR adds a run-time guard for quantized rollouts; this is part 2 of #7519's split.
- [x] PR title formatted as `[trainer] feat: ...`

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_quant_sentinel_on_cpu.py -q
# 8 passed
```

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. Environment knobs: `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL` (`0` disables), `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX` (default `1.0`), `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_CLIP_STEPS` (default `2`).

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/quant_sentinel.py`: `QuantizedRolloutSentinel` / `check_quantized_rollout_metrics`, reading metrics the trainers already compute.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`, `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`: one call after the data metrics are computed.

items.author: wengeezhang
items.summary: Adds the MXFP8 training recipe (, Blackwell) to verl's Megatron path, plus the shared Transformer Engine (TE) weight quantizer that the MXFP8 rollout PRs use to put the sampler on the learner's weight grid. This is part 1 of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXF…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds the **MXFP8 training recipe** (`fp8_recipe: mxfp8`, Blackwell) to verl's Megatron path, plus the shared Transformer Engine (TE) weight quantizer that the MXFP8 rollout PRs use to put the sampler on the learner's weight grid.

This is part 1 of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell), which the review asked to break up. It has no dependencies.

| # | PR | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **this PR**: MXFP8 training + shared TE quantizer | main |
| 2 | #8128: quantized-rollout sentinel | main |
| 3 | #7918: exact MXFP8 exclusion matcher | main |
| 4 | #8129: MXFP8 vLLM rollout | 1, 3 |
| 5 | #8130: MXFP8 SGLang rollout + refit loader | 1 |
| 6 | #8131: post-sync refit self-check | 4, 5 |
| 7 | #8132: quantized-layer audit | 6 |

**Training.** `fp8_recipe: mxfp8` already flows through `override_transformer_config`. The one functional gap was THD sequence padding:
- TE's MXFP8 quantizer needs both GEMM dimensions divisible by 32, and the wgrad scale blocks run along the token dimension.
- So packed sequences are padded to `lcm(32, align)` per sequence under MXFP8, using Megatron-Core's own `get_fp8_align_size` (the mapping it applies to its MoE FP8 padding).
- Every other recipe keeps its previous alignment (blockwise: `lcm(16, align)`).

**Shared quantizer.** `verl/utils/mxfp8_quant.py` exposes:
- `mxfp8_quantize`: TE's `MXFP8Quantizer` (E4M3, row-wise 1×32 blocks, compact UE8M0 scales), the function the learner applies to the weight operand of its forward GEMMs;
- `MXFP8_KEEP_HIGH_PRECISION_LAYERS`: keeps `lm_head` and the token embedding in BF16.

Quantizing `lm_head` made the rollout logits NaN on B200: reward stayed 0.000 for 20 steps while the job exited 0.

One guard against misconfiguration: QAT combined with a TE FP8 recipe is rejected at engine init, because the two contracts conflict.

Nothing changes unless an FP8 recipe is configured. End-to-end results for the whole MXFP8 pipeline are in #7519. For this part, MXFP8 training ran in all four B200 settings there with no non-finite metric. Examples:
- held-out gsm8k accuracy 0.9393 vs. 0.9363 for BF16 after 60 steps;
- `update_actor` per-token cost −43%.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+mxfp8. No other open PR adds MXFP8 training on the Megatron path; this is part 1 of #7519's split, not a duplicate of it.
- [x] PR title formatted as `[megatron] feat: ...`

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py -q
# 6 passed
# with the existing preprocess and router-replay tests:
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py \
```

No GPU, real vLLM model startup, or training run was performed.

items.summary: Atlas A2 machines), the vLLM 0.23 scheduler busy-wait with in degrades badly and causes CPU spin in NPU training jobs. This PR adds in, which forces to stay disabled on ARM hosts when the installed vLLM-Ascend stack uses vLLM 0.23.x.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

On ARM hosts (e.g. Atlas A2 machines), the vLLM 0.23 scheduler busy-wait with `sched_yield` in `vllm.distributed.utils` degrades badly and causes CPU spin in NPU training jobs. This PR adds `patch_vllm_ascend_v023_sched_yield()` in `verl/utils/vllm/npu_vllm_patch.py`, which forces `USE_SCHED_YIELD` to stay disabled on ARM hosts when the installed vLLM-Ascend stack uses vLLM 0.23.x. Behavior on non-ARM hosts is unchanged. This patch can be dropped once the fix is included in the installed vllm-ascend release.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+sched_yield — no open PR covers this sched_yield / CPU spin issue.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

No automated test is added: the patched code path only triggers on ARM NPU hosts (e.g. Atlas A2) with vLLM 0.23.x installed, which CPU-based CI cannot cover. Locally verified: `python -m py_compile verl/utils/vllm/npu_vllm_patch.py` passes.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. The patch is applied automatically at import time on NPU hosts when vLLM 0.23.x is installed; no user action is required.

### Design & Code Changes

Single-file change in `verl/utils/vllm/npu_vllm_patch.py` (+24 lines):

- Add `patch_vllm_ascend_v023_sched_yield()`: sets `vllm.distributed.utils.USE_SCHED_YIELD = False` on ARM hosts (keeps the upstream default on other architectures).
- Invoke it from the existing NPU patch block, gated on `0.23.0 <= vllm_version < 0.24.0`.

items.author: brandonrjacobs
items.summary: The coding-agent example constructs directly in three places ( and both graders in ). Using another sandbox provider therefore means patching the example, even though already defines a provider-neutral contract.
items.body:
## Summary

The coding-agent example constructs `E2BSandbox(image)` directly in three places (`generate.boot_agent_sandbox` and both graders in `swe.py`). Using another sandbox provider therefore means patching the example, even though `slime.agent.sandbox.Sandbox` already defines a provider-neutral contract.

This adds a small selector:

- `make_sandbox(image)` builds the class named by `SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_BACKEND`.
- The value is a registered name (`e2b`, the default, so existing setups are unchanged) or the dotted import path of an out-of-tree class that implements `Sandbox`, in the style of the `--custom-*-path` arguments. No provider code is added to slime.
- `generate.py` resolves the backend at import, so a bad value fails the run at startup instead of aborting every sample.

## Changes

- `slime/agent/sandbox.py`: `SANDBOX_BACKENDS`, `sandbox_backend()`, `make_sandbox()`. Standard library only.
- `examples/coding_agent_rl/generate.py`, `swe.py`: the three call sites use `make_sandbox(image)`.
- `tests/test_agent/test_sandbox_backend_selection.py`: default, name normalization, dotted-path loading, and the errors for an unknown name, missing module, or missing attribute. `test_agent_rollout_cpu.py` now monkeypatches `make_sandbox` instead of `E2BSandbox`. The new file is in the `agent-test` CI matrix (template and regenerated workflow).
- Example README (env table, "Porting to a New Sandbox Backend") and launcher (`SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_BACKEND` default and Ray runtime-env passthrough).

## Testing

- `pytest tests/test_agent`: 71 passed, 1 skipped (needs `sglang`). ruff, black, isort and autoflake are clean at the pre-commit pins, and the changed files parse under Python 3.10.
- End to end with an out-of-tree backend selected by import path (a CoreWeave Sandboxes implementation kept outside slime). One SWE-bench Verified instance, `astropy__astropy-12907`, went through the unmodified `boot_agent_sandbox` → `ClaudeCodeHarness.run` → `swe.git_diff` → `swe.run_evaluation` path, with a stand-in model endpoint. The reference patch graded 1.0 and an empty diff 0.0.

Opened as a draft to check the approach. Keeping provider integrations out of tree follows the scope guidance in CONTRIBUTING.md.

items.title: fix(grpo): normalize rewards per query and unique rollout
items.author: huanhuan6666
items.summary: Context compaction can turn one sampled rollout into multiple training rows. currently normalizes the whole batch when the row count differs from.
items.body:
Fixes #2445.

Context compaction can turn one sampled rollout into multiple training rows. `BatchBuilder._post_process_rewards` currently normalizes the whole batch when the row count differs from `rollout_batch_size * n_samples_per_prompt`. This mixes unrelated queries. Grouping rows by query alone also overweights episodes that produce more rows.

This change groups by `Sample.group_index`, computes the mean and optional sample standard deviation over distinct `rollout_id` values within each query, then broadcasts each episode's normalized reward to its rows in their original order. For example, query A with episode rewards `[1, 0]` and query B with `[0, 0]` keep centered rewards `[0.5, -0.5]` and `[0, 0]`, even when episodes are split during compaction.

- Preserve fixed-size positional grouping for legacy generators that omit all query IDs; reject partially missing IDs or detectable ambiguous fan-out.
- Treat missing rollout IDs as independent rows, consistent with `BatchBuilder.convert`.
- Return zero for singleton groups and reject conflicting rewards within an episode. Custom reward postprocessing remains available for segment-specific reward semantics.
- Cover the existing GRPO, GSPO, CISPO and REINFORCE++ baseline normalization modes without changing loss reduction or token masks.

Validation: 86 CPU tests passed, including 27 new reward regressions and the existing trajectory-manager branching, Sample, rollout-data and sample-hook tests. The regression exercises the real `TrajectoryManager -> BatchBuilder.convert -> get_grpo_returns` path with and without compaction. On the unmodified base, 19 of the 27 new cases fail. The new test file is registered in CPU CI; Black 24.3.0, isort 5.13.2, Ruff 0.14.7 and `git diff --check` pass. No GPU training run was performed.

Related work: #2062 already proposes the same query/rollout grouping principle; #2204 addresses explicit query grouping. This is a focused implementation against the current `BatchBuilder`, with native compaction regression coverage and strict handling of ambiguous legacy batches. Both earlier PRs remain unmerged as of this submission preparation.

items.title: [reward] fix: normalize the boxed fallback answer in math_dapo
items.author: KardeniaPoyu
items.summary: In, when a response doesn't contain an line, it falls back to extracting. However, the fallback currently does a raw string comparison against the ground truth.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

In `math_dapo.verify()`, when a response doesn't contain an `Answer:` line, it falls back to extracting `\boxed{}`. However, the fallback currently does a raw string comparison against the ground truth. Meanwhile, the `Answer:` path normalizes both the prediction and the ground truth using `normalize_final_answer()`.

As a result, equivalent answers like `\boxed{1,000}` vs gt `1000`, `\boxed{x = 5}` vs gt `5`, extra spaces, or basic LaTeX symbols get scored as `-1.0`, while writing `Answer: 1,000` gets `+1.0`.

This PR:
1. Normalizes both the extracted boxed answer and the ground truth before comparison in the fallback path.
2. Returns the normalized `box_pred` (consistent with the `Answer:` branch, preventing unnormalized tokens from breaking `maj@N` voting).
3. Preserves strict string matching when `strict_box_verify=True`.

Fixes #8123

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+math_dapo
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=is%3Aissue+math_dapo
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` -> `[reward] fix: normalize the boxed fallback answer in math_dapo`

### Test

Ran CPU unit tests locally:
```bash
pytest tests/utils/reward_score/test_math_dapo_boxed_fallback_on_cpu.py
```
Output: 9 passed in 0.4s (covers equivalent representations, wrong answers, and `strict_box_verify=True`).

Also ran the existing reward score suite:
```bash
pytest tests/utils/reward_score/
```
All passing (excluding pre-existing Windows-specific sandbox tests).

### API and Usage Example

No API changes. The fallback behavior now matches the Minerva `Answer:` normalization:

```python
from verl.utils.reward_score.math_dapo import compute_score

# Before: score = -1.0, pred = '1,000'
# After:  score = +1.0, pred = '1000'
compute_score(r"So the answer is \boxed{1,000}.", "1000")
```

### Design & Code Changes

- In `verl/utils/reward_score/math_dapo.py`:
  - Keep `is_correct_strict_box()` solely for extracting the boxed string.
  - Normalize `box_pred` and `answer` using `normalize_final_answer()`.
  - Compare the normalized values and return the normalized prediction.
- Added `tests/utils/reward_score/test_math_dapo_boxed_fallback_on_cpu.py` with parameterized test cases.

items.title: [Bug] Native-harness compaction breaks episode-level GRPO normalization after trajectory splitting
items.author: huanhuan6666
items.summary: Native-harness context compaction can split one completed rollout episode into multiple training Samples. With the default GRPO reward normalization, those extra rows change the grouping and statistics used for advantages, even though the number of sampled epi…
items.body:
### Summary

Native-harness context compaction can split **one completed rollout episode into multiple training Samples**. With the default GRPO reward normalization, those extra rows change the grouping and statistics used for advantages, even though the number of sampled episodes and their task rewards have not changed.

Reproduced on commit `8c17b676cb57af1d17ee4402e91e9209af84b60b` using the unmodified `TrajectoryManager`, `BatchBuilder`, and `get_grpo_returns` on CPU. Synthetic turns and task scores are used; this is not a full harness/model-server/GPU training run.

### Relationship to #2230

This shares the cross-query normalization fallback described in #2230 and discussed in #2204.

This separate report focuses on the **native-harness episode-to-segment contract** and an additional requirement for a correct fix: the segments of one episode must not become independent observations when computing a query's reward mean/std. Merely replacing the global fallback with per-`group_index` normalization over all rows would still overweight episodes that produce more segments.

### How the native-harness path reaches the problem

1. A harness rewrites its context between model calls, for example through compaction.
2. [`TrajectoryManager.get_trajectory`](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/8c17b676cb57af1d17ee4402e91e9209af84b60b/slime/agent/trajectory.py#L306) exports multiple Samples from that episode. They inherit the episode reward and preserve `group_index` / `rollout_id`.
3. The [rollout manager flattens the nested Samples](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/8c17b676cb57af1d17ee4402e91e9209af84b60b/slime/ray/rollout.py#L371).
4. [`BatchBuilder._post_process_rewards`](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/8c17b676cb57af1d17ee4402e91e9209af84b60b/slime/data/batch_builder.py#L202) compares the flattened row count against `rollout_batch_size * n_samples_per_prompt`. If they differ, it reshapes all rewards into one row and normalizes them together.
5. [`get_grpo_returns`](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/8c17b676cb57af1d17ee4402e91e9209af84b60b/slime/utils/ppo_utils.py#L533) broadcasts those normalized values onto the corresponding response positions; it does not restore query/episode grouping.

The trajectory manager correctly preserves generation contexts and masks in this reproduction. The problem occurs when the resulting segments are interpreted as reward observations during training-data conversion.

### Reproduction

Configuration:

```text
advantage_estimator = grpo
rollout_batch_size = 2
n_samples_per_prompt = 2
rewards_normalization = True
custom_reward_post_process_path = None
```

There are exactly four completed episodes throughout:

| Query | Episode | Task reward | Samples without compaction | Samples with compaction |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | A0 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| A | A1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| B | B0 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| B | B1 | 0 | 1 | 2 |

For the affected episodes, the test records three generations under an append-only history, then a fourth generation under a compacted history. The actual trajectory manager produces two segments. Assertions verify that every generated action is trained exactly once under its original context, with the correct episode IDs and rewards.

The uncompressed control has four training rows. The compacted case has six, ordered as `[A0_segment0, A0_segment1, A1, B0, B1_segment0, B1_segment1]`.

Actual output from `BatchBuilder.convert`:

```text
No compaction; 4 training rows:
  raw rewards:                 [1, 0, 0, 0]
  mean-only normalization:     [0.5, -0.5, 0, 0]
  with std normalization:      [0.707106, -0.707106, 0, 0]

With compaction; 6 training rows:
  raw rewards:                 [1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]
  mean-only normalization:     [0.666667, 0.666667, -0.333333, -0.333333, -0.333333, -0.333333]
  with std normalization:      [1.290992, 1.290992, -0.645496, -0.645496, -0.645496, -0.645496]
```

**Query B has two equally unsuccessful episodes, but all its segments receive negative advantages because another query succeeded.** The script also verifies that these values reach `get_grpo_returns` and the active response positions.

### Expected behavior: statistics over episodes, then broadcast to segments

For the usual episode-level GRPO objective, splitting an existing episode into context-preserving segments should not change that episode's advantage or another query's baseline.

In the compacted example, mean-only normalization should produce:

```text
Query A episode rewards:       [1, 0]
Query A episode advantages:    [0.5, -0.5]
Broadcast onto A's segments:   [0.5, 0.5, -0.5]
Broadcast onto B's segments:   [0, 0, 0]
Combined training-row values:  [0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0, 0, 0]
```

With std normalization, the corresponding values should be approximately `[0.707106, 0.707106, -0.707106, 0, 0, 0]`, matching the uncompressed episode-level statistics.

Importantly, **grouping the six rows by query alone is insufficient**: A's segment rewards become `[1, 1, 0]`, with a mean of `2/3`, instead of the episode-level mean of `1/2`. That would still change the advantages simply because the successful episode was split into more segments. This is an arithmetic consequence of treating segments as independent episodes, not a claim that a particular proposed patch has been tested.

### Possible fix / regression criteria

- Preserve both query identity (`group_index`) and episode identity (`rollout_id`) through conversion.
- For episode-level rewards, compute each query's mean/std over unique original episodes, then broadcast the resulting episode advantage to its training segments.
- Explicitly distinguish segment-level reward semantics if those are supported; do not silently infer episode groups from the flattened row count.
- Add a regression check that splitting an episode leaves every episode's normalized advantage unchanged, with and without std normalization, and that an all-equal-reward query stays at zero regardless of other queries.

The existing per-rollout loss denominator in `BatchBuilder.convert` addresses loss aggregation, but does not repair reward statistics that have already been computed over the wrong observations.

This report concerns the default normalization path with multiple queries and split episodes. It does not claim that raw task reward scoring is incorrect or that all slime configurations are affected.

### Executable CPU reproduction

Tested against the pinned source with PyTorch 2.8.0. This uses actual upstream data-transform functions with synthetic turns and scores; it does **not** launch a harness CLI, model server, Ray cluster, or GPU training job. No training-quality impact is claimed beyond the demonstrated incorrect advantages.

Save the script below as `slime_repro.py` and run it from an installed slime checkout with `python slime_repro.py` (or use `--repo /path/to/slime`). Both the uncompressed control and compacted case are checked, with and without std normalization.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```python
"""Verify native-harness compaction -> Samples -> reward normalization on CPU.

Imports the unmodified upstream TrajectoryManager, BatchBuilder and GRPO-return
function. Model responses and task scores are synthetic; no GPU, harness CLI,
Ray cluster, reward service, or distributed optimizer is launched.
"""

import argparse
import itertools
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--repo', type=Path, default=Path.cwd())
    options = parser.parse_args()
    sys.path.insert(0, str(options.repo))

    from slime.agent.trajectory import TrajectoryManager, TurnRecord
    from slime.data.batch_builder import BatchBuilder
    from slime.observability.rollout_data_utils import validate_rollout_id_annotated
    from slime.utils.ppo_utils import get_grpo_returns
    from slime.utils.types import Sample

    ids = {'Q': 1, 'A1': 11, 'O1': 21, 'A2': 12, 'O2': 22, 'A3': 13, 'O3': 23, 'Z': 99, 'A4': 14}
    names = {token: name for name, token in ids.items()}

    def message(name):
        role = 'assistant' if name.startswith('A') else 'tool' if name.startswith('O') else 'user'
        return {'role': role, 'content': name}

    def episode(group, index, score, compact):
        manager = TrajectoryManager()
        sid = f'query-{group}-episode-{index}'
        generated_context = {}

        def record(prompt, output):
            generated_context[output] = prompt
            manager.record_turn(
                sid,
                prompt_messages=[message(name) for name in prompt],
                response_message=message(output),
                turn=TurnRecord(
                    prompt_ids=[ids[name] for name in prompt],
                    output_ids=[ids[output]], output_log_probs=[-0.1], finish_reason='stop',
                ),
            )

        record(['Q'], 'A1')
        record(['Q', 'A1', 'O1'], 'A2')
        record(['Q', 'A1', 'O1', 'A2', 'O2'], 'A3')
        record(
            ['Q', 'Z', 'A3', 'O3'] if compact else ['Q', 'A1', 'O1', 'A2', 'O2', 'A3', 'O3'],
            'A4',
        )
        samples = manager.get_trajectory(
            sid, base_sample=Sample(index=index, group_index=group, rollout_id=index), reward=score,
        )
        assert len(samples) == (2 if compact else 1)
        trained_counts = Counter()
        for sample in samples:
            tokens = [names[token] for token in sample.tokens]
            mask = [0] * (len(tokens) - sample.response_length) + sample.loss_mask
            for position, (name, trained) in enumerate(zip(tokens, mask, strict=True)):
                if trained:
                    assert tokens[:position] == generated_context[name]
                    trained_counts[name] += 1
            assert sample.group_index == group and sample.rollout_id == index
            assert sample.reward == score
        assert trained_counts == Counter({'A1': 1, 'A2': 1, 'A3': 1, 'A4': 1})
        return samples

    observations = []
    for compact in (False, True):
        # Four complete episodes, two per query. Compact episodes 0 and 3.
        nested = [
            [episode(0, 0, 1.0, compact), episode(0, 1, 0.0, False)],
            [episode(1, 2, 0.0, False), episode(1, 3, 0.0, compact)],
        ]
        validate_rollout_id_annotated(nested)
        # Same flattening operation as RolloutManager._get_rollout_data.
        samples = nested
        while samples and isinstance(samples[0], list):
            samples = list(itertools.chain.from_iterable(samples))

        for use_std in (False, True):
            args = SimpleNamespace(
                custom_reward_post_process_path=None, custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_path=None,
                advantage_estimator='grpo', rewards_normalization=True,
                grpo_std_normalization=use_std, n_samples_per_prompt=2, rollout_batch_size=2, reward_key=None,
            )
            converted = BatchBuilder(args).convert(samples)
            # Same function used by the default Megatron GRPO advantage branch.
            returns = get_grpo_returns(
                torch.tensor(converted['rewards']),
                [torch.zeros(sample.response_length) for sample in samples],
            )
            rows = []
            for sample, raw, normalized, ret in zip(
                samples, converted['raw_reward'], converted['rewards'], returns, strict=True
            ):
                active_advantages = ret[torch.tensor(sample.loss_mask).bool()]
                assert torch.allclose(active_advantages, torch.full_like(active_advantages, normalized))
                if sample.group_index == 1:
                    assert normalized < 0 if compact else normalized == 0
                rows.append({
                    'query': sample.group_index, 'episode': sample.rollout_id,
                    'tokens': [names[token] for token in sample.tokens],
                    'loss_mask': sample.loss_mask, 'raw_reward': raw,
                    'normalized_reward': normalized,
                    'trained_token_advantages': active_advantages.tolist(),
                })
            observations.append({
                'compaction': compact, 'std_normalization': use_std,
                'expected_episode_count': 4, 'actual_training_rows': len(samples),
                'rows': rows,
                'whole_rollout_loss_denominator': converted['rollout_mask_sums'],
            })
            print(f'compact={compact}, std={use_std}, rows={len(samples)}')
            print('  raw:       ', converted['raw_reward'])
            print('  normalized:', [round(value, 6) for value in converted['rewards']])

    report = {
        'commit': subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(options.repo), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(),
        'scope': __doc__,
        'context_and_mask_checks_passed': True,
        'cross_query_normalization_reproduced': True,
        'cases': observations,
    }
    dest = Path(__file__).with_suffix('.results.json')
    dest.write_text(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n')
    print('Confirmed: genuine compaction Samples reach wrong normalization; all context/mask assertions passed.')
    print(dest)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
</details>

items.body:
Implements the opt-in text-scoring path proposed in [RFC #466](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/issues/466).

The external OPD teacher currently returns prompt scores and top candidates that the learner discards. Add `--opd-teacher-scoring per-position` to request only each actual response token's score through vLLM's per-row candidate API. Full context and the learner's loss contract stay the same. The current path remains the default, and image samples retain their existing rendering and scoring flow.

Includes score validation, empty-response handling, CPU tests wired into CI, and English and Chinese usage docs. Requires a teacher with vllm-project/vllm#56984, the V2 runner, and the non-streaming TITO endpoint with `raw_logprobs`.

Validation: 124 relevant CPU tests and pre-commit passed. Qwen3-0.6B scoring and learner loss/gradient checks passed on an RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (bf16, V2 runner, eager mode, prefix caching disabled). The benchmark covers 900 timed requests.

Selected median HTTP scoring times over 12 interleaved rounds:

| Prompt tokens | Response tokens | Concurrency | Current top-1 (ms) | Actual-only (ms) | Per-position (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 16 | 1 | 22.53 | 21.25 | 21.60 |
| 2048 | 512 | 1 | 208.53 | 184.73 | 136.85 |
| 1 | 1 | 4 | 46.54 | 47.17 | 52.12 |
| 2048 | 512 | 4 | 494.69 | 459.45 | 377.80 |

Actual-only uses `prompt_logprobs=0`. Short inputs show no consistent gain. These are request-to-score timings, not training throughput. Cross-batch bf16 differences also occur in the current path and remain in the raw results. Full multi-GPU training and real image-model inference were not run.

Benchmark scripts and raw results are available in [my fork](https://github.com/LinzeShi/vime/blob/acfd5f0b149a4b8f6d9c58a372d2f653bfebd662/benchmarks/opd_teacher_scoring/README.md).

items.title: Support manual Megatron restarts with retained serving
items.author: zhuzilin
items.summary: Allow a failed Megatron training job to restart on the same Ray cluster while retaining healthy SGLang engines, routers, and accepted rollout data. The new trainer can change its parallel layout and replay the batches after the last committed checkpoint withou…
items.body:
## Summary

Allow a failed Megatron training job to restart on the same Ray cluster while retaining healthy SGLang engines, routers, and accepted rollout data. The new trainer can change its parallel layout and replay the batches after the last committed checkpoint without regenerating samples or repeating accepted reward postprocessing.

Replay uses Straw storage (`--rollout-data-transport straw`) or per-rollout debug dumps (`--save-debug-rollout-data` with `{rollout_id}` in the path). Internal serving retention does not require the legacy `--use-fault-tolerance` flag.

The PR also makes recovery ownership explicit, publishes each converted training batch once, fixes restored disk-delta weight updates, and bounds cleanup independently of normal training and storage operations.

## Changes

### Serving and training lifetimes

- Introduce a named, detached `ServingCluster` that owns routers, engines, placement groups, the queue controller, and the weight-update lock. `RolloutManager` borrows those resources and can be replaced independently.
- Fence live training drivers before accepting a successor. Register trainer actors with serving so they can be released even after manager failure.
- Retain serving and replay data after training failure; dispose the session after successful completion. Launchers preserve a running Ray cluster when resubmitting a job.
- Let the driver own attempt cleanup, including rollback when startup fails after attaching to serving. Give an unresponsive manager a bounded opportunity to pause, then release trainers directly through serving. Cleanup failures do not replace the original training exception.
- Dispose manager and serving resources independently, so a custom data source's cleanup error does not skip serving cleanup.

### Checkpoint and replay ownership

- Use queue receipts as the authority for accepted raw and converted batches. Represent conversion as an ordinary queue control task instead of maintaining a second batch-progress ledger.
- Keep the recovery journal responsible for the committed model boundary and the replay window. Reconcile accepted queue results after manager death or a lost RPC reply.
- Separate runtime training completion from durable checkpoint completion. Only a committed model/source checkpoint releases the associated replay pins.
- Bound scheduler progress to buffered and currently collected work; discard finished conversion references instead of retaining an ever-growing delivery history.
- Make checkpoint selection return a configuration copy and a restore plan. Pass checkpoint fields and the serving weight version through an explicit `TrainingResume`; keep long-lived data-source configuration separate from each trainer attempt.
- Preserve the existing journal field representation and all public custom function signatures and return conventions.

### Shared batch publication

- Convert and publish the global training batch once. Send each DP rank a selection over shared tensor records instead of serializing another payload per rank.
- Rebuild selections when training resumes with a different parallel layout. Keep R3/score-centering tensors lazy and reuse accepted converted data.
- Keep custom conversion and reward-postprocessing hooks at the original whole-batch boundary.
- Put asynchronous consumers on their owning data source, with its pause, restore, and close lifecycle, instead of using a module-global worker.

### Engine recovery and weight synchronization

- Bound engine reset and health-check RPCs, unregister failed engines, and terminate their serving children before replacing them.
- Send old weight-update-group reset requests to **all** serving groups before waiting. Prefill and decode can share an NCCL group; waiting for one side before notifying the other can deadlock healthy PD engines.
- On the first disk-delta update after trainer replacement or engine changes, publish the current restored weights as a full baseline. Keep weight versions above earlier publication attempts.
- Restore the DDP gradient-synchronization hook correctly across repeated rollouts with `overlap_grad_reduce`.

### Optimizer state and defaults

- Support recovery with `--use-stateless-adam --no-save-optim`. Save and restore the LR/WD scheduler alongside the model; require RNG state and validate the scheduler sidecar before accepting the checkpoint.
- Continue requiring optimizer state for ordinary Adam. Changes are confined to Slime's Megatron adapter; `/root/Megatron-LM` is unchanged.
- Set both `--rollout-health-check-timeout` and `--rollout-health-check-first-wait` to **600 seconds** by default.
- Add an independent `--rollout-cleanup-timeout`, default **60 seconds**, for exiting an attempt. It does not limit normal data reads, generation, training, or checkpoint writes.
- Update English and Chinese recovery documentation and retain the CPU/GPU recovery suites in the CI matrix.

## Validation

### Regression and fault tests

Lifecycle/configuration validation recorded for commit `8a6406bd`.

The lifecycle/configuration follow-up passed **443 distinct regression cases** across training recovery, argument validation, Straw transport, fully asynchronous/distributed rollout, optional Straw dependencies, engine control, and score centering. Repeated verification runs are not added to this count.

The **12-case real-Ray manager recovery suite** additionally covers:

- Manager death after raw acceptance, conversion acceptance, or recovery-journal persistence.
- Lost conversion replies with a surviving manager.
- Replay and repartitioning with online GC both enabled and disabled.
- Engine reset timeout while retaining healthy peers.
- A live manager that cannot pause, and direct trainer release by the serving owner.
- Joint prefill/decode reset through a barrier that requires both peers to participate.

Tests also check partial-startup rollback, cleanup error propagation, checkpoint selection without mutating requested paths, and unchanged args-based custom data-source construction.

Commands used for the final regression suites:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/tests:/root/Megatron-LM"
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest \
  tests/test_training_recovery.py \
  tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py \
  tests/test_rollout_straw_transport.py \
  tests/test_server_control.py \
  tests/test_fully_async_rollout.py \
  tests/test_optional_straw.py \
  tests/test_score_centering.py \
  tests/test_distributed_rollout.py -q
python tests/test_rollout_manager_recovery.py
```

Existing test files remain registered in `.github/workflows/pr-test.yml.j2`; this follow-up adds cases to those files rather than new matrix entries.

### GPU recovery

Validation used a four-host cluster with **8 H100 GPUs per host** and shared JuiceFS storage.

The original recovery validation passed six GPU scenarios covering disk-delta updates, PD engine failure, object-store fully asynchronous rollout, ordinary Adam with overlapping gradient reduction, dense stateless Adam, and MoE stateless Adam with R3.

The lifecycle/configuration changes were also exercised with:

| Scenario | GPUs | Fault and restart | Checks |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, PD, stateless Adam | 4 | Real training OOM, retained manager, TP 1 → 2 / DP 2 → 1 | Healthy serving processes retained; checkpoint/scheduler restored; accepted samples replayed; subsequent training and saves complete |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, R3, stateless Adam | 8 | Real training OOM plus manager loss, TP 1 → 2 / DP 4 → 2 | Serving retained; samples and routing data replayed; scheduler progress restored; finite gradients and completed training |

Large-MoE recovery uses stateless Adam; ordinary Adam recovery is covered by the dense-model scenarios.

### Batch-publication measurement

Measured Qwen3-30B-A3B on **32 H100s**: 16 training GPUs, 16 serving GPUs, configured serving concurrency 256, 256 samples per rollout, 1,024 generated tokens per sample, four rollouts, and R3 enabled. TP=2, EP=8, DP=8.

| Manager phase | Before | Shared-batch publication |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Whole-batch conversion | 0.00699 s | 0.00641 s |
| Global publication | Not timed separately | 1.92476 s |
| DP partition/publication | 3.09694 s | 0.09642 s |

These are phase means. The DP phase becomes about **32.1× faster** because it builds selections over one published batch. This is **not an end-to-end throughput speedup**; the revised global-publication cost is reported separately. R3 routes were nonempty and fully consumed during the measured training runs.

## Scope and limitations

- Recovery requires resubmitting the job to the same live Ray cluster. This PR does not introduce automatic job retries.
- Losing the serving owner or the whole Ray cluster requires cold startup from a committed checkpoint.
- Keep model, rollout settings, global batch size, session identity, and custom hook configuration unchanged when attaching to retained serving. Supported trainer parallelism and memory settings can change.
- Stateless Adam rebuilds FP32 master parameters from the saved model precision. Parallel-layout changes can also alter RNG behavior; bitwise-identical training after restart is not promised.

items.title: fix: linear-attention gradients are wrong when CP > 1 (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next)
items.author: sdc17
items.summary: Nothing errors out and the loss still goes down, so it is easy to miss, but every CP > 1 run that goes through this code path has been training on wrong gradients since #1748. How wrong: - real layer (fla kernels, bf16), CP=4: the input gradient is off by 9.4%…
items.body:
**Right now, with context parallelism (CP > 1), the linear-attention layers send wrong gradients back to the rest of the network.** This hits the Gated DeltaNet layers of Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next, which go through `HuggingfaceAttention` and make up 3 of every 4 layers in these models. Nothing errors out and the loss still goes down, so it is easy to miss, but every CP > 1 run that goes through this code path has been training on wrong gradients since #1748.

How wrong:

- real `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet` layer (fla kernels, bf16), CP=4: the input gradient is off by 9.4% (0.06% with this PR, i.e. bf16 noise);
- toy causal layer, CP=2 / 4 / 8: off by 74% / 129% / 112% (1e-16 with this PR).

The error is in the gradient each layer hands down to the layers below it, and it is introduced again at every linear-attention layer.

## Why it's wrong

With CP, `HuggingfaceAttention` all-gathers the sequence, every CP rank runs the layer on the whole sequence, and then each rank keeps only its own two zigzag chunks of the output.

Since #1748, the CP all-gather uses `_AllGatherForDuplicatedComputation`, whose backward returns only the local slice of the incoming gradient. That is only right if every rank holds the same gradient. It holds for the SP gather (the scatter after the layer all-gathers the output gradient back), but not for CP: each CP rank only receives the gradient of its own output chunks, so the ranks end up with different input gradients, and the true gradient of a chunk is the sum over all ranks. Keeping only the local slice drops every path through which a chunk affects later chunks that live on other ranks.

## Fix

Use `torch.distributed.nn.functional.all_gather` for the CP gather again (this is what the code did before #1748). Its backward is a reduce-scatter, which is exactly that sum. The SP part of #1748 stays as it is. `_AllGatherForDuplicatedComputation` has no other users, so I removed it.

## How I checked

**CPU repro (gloo, no GPU needed, script below).** A causal toy layer (per-sequence cumsum) goes through the same zigzag layout, reassembly and output slicing as `hf_attention.py`. The numbers are the relative error of the input gradient against the same layer run without CP (1e-16 is float64 round-off, i.e. an exact match):

| CP | Input-gradient error, current code | Input-gradient error, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 74% | 1.4e-16 |
| 4 | 129% | 2.0e-16 |
| 8 | 112% | 3.3e-16 |

**Real layer on GPU.** `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet` with the fla kernels, bf16, random init, packed sequences, CP=4 on 4 GPUs, compared with the same layer without CP:

- input gradient: 9.4% error with the current code, 0.06% with this change (bf16 noise);
- parameter gradients (after summing over CP ranks, as the DP×CP all-reduce does): 0.3% in both cases.

So within a single layer the weight gradients come out right; what's wrong is the gradient handed down, which means the weight gradients of every layer below it are wrong as well.

## About the two failing checks

`cpu-unittest (test_fully_async_rollout.py)` (`No module named 'straw'`) and `cpu-unittest (test_score_centering_transport.py)` fail the same way on main (latest main run: https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/37003384102) and on other open PRs, so they are not caused by this change.

## CPU repro script

```python
# CPU-only repro of the CP input gradient in slime_plugins/models/hf_attention.py.
# A causal toy layer (per-sequence cumsum: every output depends on all earlier inputs, like GDN) is run with the same
# zigzag CP layout, all-gather + reassembly + output slicing as hf_attention.py, and the input gradient is compared
# with a run without CP, once with the current all-gather backward (local slice) and once with
# torch.distributed.nn.functional.all_gather (reduce-scatter).
#   python cp_grad_repro.py
import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.distributed.nn.functional as dist_nn
import torch.multiprocessing as mp


class LocalSliceAllGather(torch.autograd.Function):
    """Same as _AllGatherForDuplicatedComputation in hf_attention.py."""

    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, x, group):
        ctx.rank = dist.get_rank(group=group)
        out = [torch.empty_like(x) for _ in range(dist.get_world_size(group=group))]
        dist.all_gather(out, x.contiguous(), group=group)
        return tuple(out)

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, *grads):
        return grads[ctx.rank], None


def causal_layer(x, cu):
    return torch.cat([torch.cumsum(x[s:e], dim=0) for s, e in zip(cu[:-1], cu[1:])])


def worker(rank, world, port, results):
    os.environ.update(MASTER_ADDR="127.0.0.1", MASTER_PORT=str(port))
    dist.init_process_group("gloo", rank=rank, world_size=world)
    group = dist.group.WORLD
    seqlens = [8 * world, 4 * world, 2 * world]
    cu = [0]
    for n in seqlens:
        cu.append(cu[-1] + n)
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    x = torch.randn(cu[-1], 3, dtype=torch.float64)
    w = torch.randn(cu[-1], 3, dtype=torch.float64)  # loss = sum(w * layer(x))

    xr = x.clone().requires_grad_()
    (w * causal_layer(xr, cu)).sum().backward()
    ref = xr.grad

    # positions this rank owns in the zigzag layout: chunks rank and 2*world-1-rank of every sequence
    loc = []
    for s, e in zip(cu[:-1], cu[1:]):
        c = (e - s) // (2 * world)
        loc += list(range(s + rank * c, s + (rank + 1) * c))
        loc += list(range(s + (2 * world - 1 - rank) * c, s + (2 * world - rank) * c))
    loc = torch.tensor(loc)
    local_cu = [v // world for v in cu]

    errs = {}
    for name in ("current", "fix"):
        xl = x[loc].clone().requires_grad_()
        if name == "current":
            parts = LocalSliceAllGather.apply(xl, group)
        else:  # this PR
            parts = dist_nn.all_gather(xl, group=group)
        whole = []  # reassembly as in hf_attention.py
        for i in range(len(cu) - 1):
            chunk = (cu[i + 1] - cu[i]) // 2 // world
            st, en = local_cu[i], local_cu[i + 1]
            whole += [parts[r][st:st + chunk] for r in range(world)]
            whole += [parts[r][st + chunk:en] for r in range(world)][::-1]
        out = causal_layer(torch.cat(whole), cu)
        pieces = []  # output slicing as in hf_attention.py
        for i in range(len(cu) - 1):
            chunks = torch.chunk(out[cu[i]:cu[i + 1]], 2 * world, dim=0)
            pieces += [chunks[rank], chunks[2 * world - 1 - rank]]
        (w[loc] * torch.cat(pieces)).sum().backward()
        err = torch.tensor([((xl.grad - ref[loc]).norm() / ref[loc].norm()).item()])
        dist.all_reduce(err, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX)
        errs[name] = err.item()
    if rank == 0:
        results[world] = errs
    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    manager = mp.Manager()
    results = manager.dict()
    for i, world in enumerate((2, 4, 8)):
        mp.spawn(worker, args=(world, 29500 + i, results), nprocs=world, join=True)
    for world in (2, 4, 8):
        cur, fix = results[world]["current"], results[world]["fix"]
        print(f"CP={world}: input-gradient error vs no CP: current code {cur:.0%}, this PR {fix:.1e}")
```

items.title: [rollout, trainer] feat: report token-weighted generation staleness
items.author: tongyx361
items.summary: Add optional behavior-version provenance and token-weighted age metrics to fully asynchronous rollout and the v1 trainer. When a response resumes after a weight update, record each nonempty attempt's generation version and token count.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add optional behavior-version provenance and token-weighted age metrics to fully asynchronous rollout and the v1 trainer. When a response resumes after a weight update, record each nonempty attempt's generation version and token count. Report coverage explicitly: missing or inconsistent metadata never becomes age zero. The feature defaults off, preserves sampling and training loss, and performs no additional queue metadata reads when disabled. AI assistance was used.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [focused query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20behavior%20version%20in%3Atitle). No matching open PR was found in the focused search.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Exact extracted branch: `python -m pytest tests/utils/test_behavior_age_metrics_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_behavior_version_segments_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_response_length_cap_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_routed_experts_on_cpu.py -q` — 48 passed. This includes actual async-client abort/empty-abort/resume generation with changing versions, token and budget preservation, malformed/missing provenance, token-weighted aggregation, padding, current-version validation, mixed older queue rows, unrelated-error propagation, and the production trainer metrics collection prefix with zero added reads when disabled. Tests use the extracted checkout and a uv-managed interpreter with CUDA hidden. No full training/GPU acceptance or performance claim is made.

### API and Usage Example

```text
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.collect_behavior_version_metrics=true
```

The default is false. Metrics live under `training/off_policy/`: response/token coverage, token staleness mean/min/max/stale fraction, and cross-version response fraction. Staleness uses the weights for the current update (`global_steps - 1`). Empty coverage omits age statistics.

### Design & Code Changes

Store compact `[generation_version, new_token_count]` segments using existing backend version metadata. Read optional queue fields only when enabled, retrying per row when older rows lack the field. Complete provenance alone contributes to age; all nonpadding consumed responses contribute to coverage denominators. This PR is independent of rollout-attempt metrics and checkpoint persistence.

Training metrics use the consumed batch partition and exclude padding. Token staleness is in model-version units under training/off_policy/token_staleness; provenance coverage and cross-version response fractions are grouped under training/off_policy/behavior_version. Missing records reduce coverage and never count as zero staleness. Validation does not emit these training metrics.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [ ] Apply pre-commit checks on all repository files. All changed-file checks passed.
- [x] Add / Update documentation.

All complete-PR changed-file pre-commit hooks passed. This re-review used AI assistance. Historical experiment evidence above remains historical; no new GPU experiment was run for this re-review.


### Delayed-output provenance correction (2026-10-08)

The vLLM backend now snapshots the weight version after successful admission and returns that version even when the final frontend output arrives after a pause and weight update. Previously an old attempt could read the mutable new version at final delivery and report zero staleness with full coverage. Parked requests capture the version under which they are subsequently admitted, and unknown admitted versions remain uncovered. The backend correction adds no metadata read, synchronization, or sampling change. Add the behavior metrics documentation page to the Async Training toctree, repairing its orphan-document CI failure. These corrections remain within this existing PR.
