items.title: [rollout, trainer] feat: observe partial generation attempts and backend stops
items.author: tongyx361
items.summary: Partial generation can stop and resume multiple times before a trajectory is consumed. Add optional attempt counts and available prefill wall intervals, while retaining raw vLLM finish/stop reasons separately from the client's cumulative response-budget decisi…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Partial generation can stop and resume multiple times before a trajectory is consumed. Add optional attempt counts and available prefill wall intervals, while retaining raw vLLM finish/stop reasons separately from the client's cumulative response-budget decision. A backend EOS at the client budget remains recorded as an EOS even when the client returns `length`.

AI assistance was used to extract and verify this change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [focused query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20finish_reason%20metrics%20in%3Atitle). No matching raw-attempt observation PR was found. Existing [#7906](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7906) changes response truncation; this change does not alter slicing, truncation or clip metrics.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[rollout, trainer] feat: observe partial generation attempts and backend stops`.

### Test

Fresh clean-branch CPU tests: `uv run python -m pytest tests/workers/rollout/test_partial_metrics_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_termination_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_routed_experts_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_response_length_cap_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_submitter_gate_on_cpu.py -q` — **51 passed**, with 18 dependency deprecation warnings.

The suite exercises the real async retry/merge implementation and actual vLLM server methods using a scripted engine: native stops coinciding with the client cap, empty abort/resume, unchanged tokens/logprobs/routes, disabled observation paths, admission rejection, missing timing and aggregation excluding padding. The imported source paths were verified to point to this branch. No GPU engine or distributed training validation was rerun on this branch.

All pre-commit hooks passed on all 16 changed files; all four generated configurations were regenerated and checked. `git diff --check` passed.

### API and Usage Example

Enable with `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.collect_partial_rollout_metrics=true`; the default is `false`. For vLLM timestamp availability, set `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.disable_log_stats=false`.

### Design & Code Changes

Observation is gated independently of retry control and generated data. The client stores attempt summaries and backend termination records in existing trajectory `extra_fields`; the v1 trainer fetches them only when enabled. Counts apply to consumed, nonpadding trajectories and exclude work on evicted trajectories.

Prefill wall intervals use `RequestOutput.metrics.scheduled_ts` and `first_token_ts` when available. These fields and their subtraction were verified in vLLM 0.29 source. Missing, incomplete or invalid timestamps remain unavailable, including aborts before the first token; they are never converted to zero latency. Measured intervals include preemption after scheduling and are not GPU compute time or GPU-hours. Other backends contribute client attempts without fabricating backend timing.

Training observations use the consumed batch partition and exclude padding. response_coverage uses all consumed nonpadding responses; resume fractions use covered responses, and resume-prefill coverage uses recorded resume attempts. Older queue rows without extra_fields are read individually and reduce coverage instead of failing the batch. Summed observed prefill seconds are overlapping request wall intervals, not elapsed batch latency or GPU time.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [ ] Apply all-files pre-commit checks. All hooks passed on all changed files.
- [x] Update the v1 async trainer documentation.
- [x] Add unit tests to the existing CPU test tree; vLLM-specific method tests require an installed vLLM package and use a scripted engine without GPUs.
- [ ] Request CI after human review.

- [ ] Recipe submodule update (not applicable).

### Independent re-review

### Design & Code Changes

Phase synchronization is opt-in and defaults false; the default path adds no device synchronization or phase-clock calls. Local rank wall times follow existing reporting-rank aggregation and are not a global maximum or a measure of GPU-only compute. Optimizer time includes zero_grad. Driver lifecycle intervals may nest inside existing gen/update_weights timers and must not be summed with their parents. No GPU overhead/throughput claim is made. This PR has no weight-export dependency.

Phase durations use timing_s/actor_forward_backward_mean and timing_s/actor_optimizer_mean (and corresponding critic keys); MFU stays under perf/mfu. Durations explicitly average reporting ranks using the Metric aggregation contract, avoiding the legacy reducer interpreting the min substring in timing as a minimum. These are synchronized worker wall intervals; driver lifecycle timers can overlap parent timers and must not be summed with them.

items.title: fix(weight-sync): honor checkpoint shard indexes in disk delta sync
items.author: chaoworks
items.summary: Disk-delta sync can report success while leaving the model's indexed weights unchanged when a checkpoint directory contains unreferenced safetensors files with duplicate tensor names. Both the trainer's baseline reader and the engine's local checkpoint writer …
items.body:
Disk-delta sync can report success while leaving the model's indexed weights unchanged when a checkpoint directory contains unreferenced safetensors files with duplicate tensor names. Both the trainer's baseline reader and the engine's local checkpoint writer scan every safetensors file, so a stale file visited last can override the indexed tensor location. The sender and receiver can agree on that stale file, pass checksum verification, and still leave the weights used for model reload untouched.

Read the shard list from `model.safetensors.index.json` when present, matching the model loader's indexed-file selection. Apply this to the trainer and both SGLang patch bundles. Missing indexed shards fail instead of falling back to stale files; unindexed checkpoints retain the existing behavior.

### Validation

- Added 13 CPU regression cases covering indexed selection, missing shards, unindexed checkpoints, and actual pull/apply round trips for both encodings and both patch bundles. The tests execute the receiver module extracted from each shipped patch.
- On baseline `8c17b676`: **10 failed, 3 passed**. With this change: **13 passed**.
- Additional local H20 probe: four GPUs tested independently × two encodings × two patch bundles. All 16 cases failed before and passed after; each passing case applies three successive BF16 SGD updates and checks reloaded weights and forward outputs with zero tolerance. This is a checkpoint/transport integration probe, not a full SGLang serving or RL run.
- Black, isort, Ruff, `git diff --check`, and `git apply --check` for the modified standalone receiver module in both bundles passed.

Reproduce the committed regression suite with:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_disk_delta_checkpoint_index.py -q
```

Prepared with Codex assistance; validation results above were observed on the actual before/after implementations.

items.title: [rollout, vllm] fix: avoid duplicate LoRA tensor copy after IPC receipt
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Its callback clones each tensor out of the receiver's reused IPC buffer, because vLLM retains the tensors after the callback. then clones the complete adapter again before constructing.
items.body:
## Problem

The LoRA branch of `update_weights_from_ipc` accumulates bucketed tensors
until the adapter is complete. Its callback clones each tensor out of the
receiver's reused IPC buffer, because vLLM retains the tensors after the
callback. `_update_weights` then clones the complete adapter again before
constructing `TensorLoRARequest`. Both copies coexist during loading.

## Change

Keep the callback-owned tensor storages and create only a new mapping for the
request. The copy that protects against IPC-buffer reuse remains unchanged.
This affects only the complete-LoRA path; base weight updates are untouched.

## Duplicate check

No open VERL PR found for this second clone. This is separate from
[#7496](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7496), which fixes delivery
of adapters to disaggregated engines, and from
[#8105](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8105), which forwards a
model's adapter conversion hook after receipt. No model-specific conversion
code is included here.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py -q`
— 7 passed. The added tests simulate a receiver reusing one tensor storage
across two buckets, verify the retained adapter values after that storage is
overwritten, and verify `_update_weights` does not make a second tensor copy.
Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` passed.

This is an ownership and peak-memory fix; no model-output change is intended.
An actual distributed IPC performance measurement is not claimed.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change. This is a draft awaiting human
line-by-line review before it is ready to merge.

items.title: [rollout, vllm] feat: forward model LoRA adapter hooks during tensor sync
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: That bypasses a model's adapter conversion hook used by the on-disk loader. Also, the rollout server currently overwrites an explicit with a value derived only from the training rank.
items.body:
## Problem

VERL's in-memory `TensorLoRARequest` path calls vLLM's tensor loader directly.
That bypasses a model's adapter conversion hook used by the on-disk loader.
Also, the rollout server currently overwrites an explicit
`engine_kwargs.vllm.max_lora_rank` with a value derived only from the training
rank. A serving layout with independent packed factors can require a larger
rank while preserving the same effective LoRA update.

## Change

- If the vLLM model exposes `convert_lora_adapter`, pass that callable to the
  tensor/checkpoint loader. Models without the hook keep the existing path.
- Preserve and round up an explicitly requested serving rank instead of
  overwriting it. Reject an adapter if its converted rank exceeds the engine's
  configured capacity.

The conversion algorithm and model-specific names are **not** in VERL. They
belong to the serving model; see dependent [vLLM #59915](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59915).

## Duplicate check

[#7496](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7496) transfers LoRA
adapters to disaggregated rollout engines. This PR changes how an adapter
already received by the vLLM worker is interpreted and validated; it does not
change the transport protocol or add another transfer phase.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_lora_adapter_hook_on_cpu.py -q`:
  1 passed. The test checks hook forwarding and rejection when converted rank
  exceeds the configured maximum.
- Ruff check/format and `git diff --check`: passed.
- The dependent vLLM change loaded the original PEFT adapter in a six-layer
  fixed-input serving evaluation with eager and default CUDA Graph enabled.
  That result validates the serving hook. Separately, a six-layer CPU fixture
  sent 115 raw PEFT tensors through VERL's `TensorLoRARequest` receiver and
  produced rank 8 / 95 modules; every resulting A/B tensor matched vLLM's
  direct disk loader bit-for-bit.
- Real vLLM receiver smoke test with this VERL wheel and the original adapter:
  one H200, six BF16 layers, two fixed 16-token prompts, two repeats per
  base → adapter → zero-adapter → restored-adapter phase. Both eager and default
  `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA Graph runs completed. Zero-adapter versus base and
  restored-adapter versus original adapter were exactly equal on the measured
  prompt-token logprobs; adapter effect was 0.007614 maximum. Occasional
  same-adapter repeat noise reached 0.000134, so bitwise self-repeat is not
  claimed. This exercises the in-engine receiver but not the trainer sender,
  bucketed IPC, or a full RL training step.

AI assistance was used to prepare the change. This is a draft awaiting human
line-by-line review and trainer-to-rollout IPC validation before it is ready to merge.

items.title: [trainer] fix: compute exact best/worst/maj@k without replacement
items.author: tongyx361
items.summary: Replace validation bootstrap estimates with analytic means and standard deviations over uniformly selected subsets of distinct responses, without replacement. Select uniformly among tied plurality answers, then uniformly among the sampled rows with the selecte…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Replace validation `maj@k` bootstrap estimates with analytic means and standard deviations over uniformly selected subsets of `k` distinct responses, without replacement. Select uniformly among tied plurality answers, then uniformly among the sampled rows with the selected answer. Results no longer depend on response order or the bootstrap seed. For answers `[A, A, B]` with scores `[1, 1, 0]`, `maj@2/mean` is `2/3` and `maj@3/mean` is `1`.

Existing metric names are preserved, but historical values used sampling with replacement and first-occurrence tie/score selection, so they are not directly comparable. This PR now includes existing #8102 as a prerequisite through ordinary merges, preserving its author history. Together they replace validation best/worst/maj@k estimates with exact moments without replacement. #7240 adds a binary pass@k metric and does not implement the majority-vote distribution. #6845 concerns sparse reward-key alignment, a separate behavior.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement, document, and test this change. This draft PR was created at the human submitter's explicit request. Human line-by-line review and independent test confirmation remain pending.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [majority](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+majority), [maj@k](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22maj%40k%22). Related #8102, #7240, and #6845 were inspected and have different scopes. There is no linked issue for this change.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

- `python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/test_metric_utils_on_cpu.py -q` (invoked with uv in an existing test environment): 50 passed and 327 subtests passed, with two existing empty-list mean warnings.
- `pre-commit run --files verl/trainer/ppo/metric_utils.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_metric_utils_on_cpu.py docs/workers/ray_trainer.rst --show-diff-on-failure` (invoked with uv): all hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Tests compare both analytic moments against exhaustive subsets of two-, three-, and four-answer populations for every valid k, including tied winners and different scores within an answer. They cover full-population selection, one answer, input permutation, invalid subset sizes, seed independence through validation integration, and an independent integer-combination hypergeometric calculation for a 1,024-row binary population. The existing CPU workflow discovers this `*_on_cpu.py` test file. Changed-file hooks passed at the current head; refreshed remote CI is pending publication.

Local cold-cache timings for all validation k values: 256 responses / 9 answers took about 39 ms; 1,024 responses / 2 answers took about 1.3 ms; an uneven 528-response / 32-answer population took about 1.4 s. These are illustrative CPU measurements, not throughput guarantees. Subsequent metrics sharing the same sorted answer counts and k reuse cached probabilities.

### API and Usage Example

Existing validation metric names and the k ladder are preserved. The new helper accepts `1 <= subset_size <= len(data)`. `calc_maj_val` now returns the expected score under uniform tie and row selection. Best/worst metrics use the exact rank-mass method from #8102; all three validation metrics now use analytic solutions. The compatibility seed parameter is retained and ignored by these calculations.

```python
from verl.trainer.ppo.metric_utils import majority_vote_metric

data = [{"pred": "A", "val": 1.0}, {"pred": "A", "val": 1.0}, {"pred": "B", "val": 0.0}]
majority_vote_metric(data, 2, "pred", "val")
# (approximately 0.6666667, 0.4714045)
majority_vote_metric(data, 3, "pred", "val")
# (1.0, 0.0)
```

### Design & Code Changes

For a candidate answer selecting m rows, dynamic programming restricts all other answers to at most m rows and tracks their total selected rows and number of ties t. Each valid state contributes a tie weight of `1/(t+1)`. The coefficients follow the multivariate hypergeometric law: products of group binomial coefficients divided by `C(N,k)`. Independent binomial PMFs conditioned on total k provide a common numerical scaling for these coefficients without enumerating subsets.

Answers with equal population counts share a computation. A bounded cache keyed by sorted counts and k allows reuse across score variables and prompts. Full-population, k=1, equal-count, binary-answer, and guaranteed-winner cases have direct calculations.

Conditional on an answer winning, a uniformly chosen sampled row has that answer's full empirical score distribution by exchangeability. Weight the group score moments by answer-winning probabilities and center scores before computing variance. `/std` measures variation of the random majority score, including tie and row selection; it is not an estimator standard error. Existing averaging of per-prompt moments is preserved. The trainer documentation describes the new probability definition and historical comparability.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply pre-commit on all files. All hooks passed for the changed files instead.
- [x] Add / Update the documentation in `docs/workers/ray_trainer.rst`.
- [x] Add unit tests covered by the existing CPU CI workflow.
- [ ] Request CI in the community channel. No external message has been sent.
- [ ] Update the recipe submodule. Not applicable.

### Combined exact-metric verification

The current branch passed 50 CPU tests and 327 subtests, including a joint integration test that fails if best/worst/maj invokes bootstrap, checks permutation and seed independence, and preserves both prerequisite test suites. All three changed-file pre-commit hooks and git diff --check passed. A full-population extreme-finite best/worst regression asserts deterministic endpoints and zero standard deviation without numerical overflow. Both original PR heads and the updated #8102 head remain ancestors; no history was rewritten. AI assistance was used. Human line-by-line review and independent test confirmation remain pending; this existing PR remains a draft.

items.title: [RFC] Reduce OPD teacher scoring overhead in VIME
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: VIME's OPD path requests for the full prompt and response, then keeps the teacher log probability of each actual response token. It does not use the additional top candidate or the prompt-only scores.
items.body:
VIME's OPD path requests `prompt_logprobs=1` for the full prompt and response, then keeps the teacher log probability of each actual response token. It does not use the additional top candidate or the prompt-only scores. This proposal reduces the work needed to obtain those response scores while preserving the existing training objective.

vLLM added per-position candidate scoring in [#56984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56984). VIME can use it to request one actual response token at each scored position. The integration belongs in `vime/rollout/on_policy_distillation.py`; the existing loss and learner data contract stay unchanged.

An initial local comparison supports an opt-in per-position path. It used Qwen3-0.6B, an RTX 4070 Laptop GPU, bfloat16, the V2 runner, eager execution and loopback HTTP. The three paths used identical inputs and `max_tokens=1`. These are median request-to-score times over 12 interleaved rounds with a 512-token prefill budget:

| Prompt tokens | Response tokens | Concurrency | Current top-1 | Actual token only | Per-position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64 | 16 | 1 | 25.80 ms | 24.48 ms | 24.70 ms |
| 512 | 128 | 1 | 64.18 ms | 58.87 ms | 51.22 ms |
| 2048 | 512 | 1 | 204.87 ms | 183.45 ms | 137.83 ms |
| 512 | 2048 | 1 | 211.48 ms | 187.37 ms | 159.12 ms |
| 512 | 2048 | 4 | 503.02 ms | 450.22 ms | 449.76 ms |

The new path improves several longer-input cases beyond `prompt_logprobs=0`, but adds no clear benefit for short inputs or the last configuration above. A second run with a 4096-token prefill budget also improved the longer-input cases. The inputs are fixed text sequences, not sampled training trajectories. The pilot measures HTTP scoring overhead, including serialization and parsing; it does not establish a training speedup or a new default.

The pilot used vLLM `84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a` and model revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, with prefix caching disabled and raw log probabilities. VIME's baseline is `791f101e20db377b28e15f12a00863baaea2605f`. The integration PR will include the reproducible comparison script.

For a prompt of length `P` and a response of length `R`, the per-position request sends the full `P + R` token sequence, `prompt_logprob_start=P-1`, and an `[R, 1]` table containing the actual response token IDs. Its output is decoded into the existing `sample.teacher_log_probs` vector of length `R`. Each value remains the log probability under the teacher's full vocabulary distribution.

The first integration uses an explicit choice of text scoring path. The existing path remains the default and remains available for older teacher servers. Per-position scoring requires a teacher with the merged API, the V2 model runner, and the non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate` endpoint returning raw log probabilities. Missing scores, invalid shapes or unsupported configurations produce a clear error; they do not silently substitute scores or fall back after a failed text request.

Text scoring is the initial optimized path. Image samples retain their existing render, feature alignment and scoring path until the new path has real image coverage. The patch must preserve that behavior. Empty responses produce an empty score vector without a teacher request; invalid response lengths are rejected. No Top-K training objective, new student metadata or loss change is included. `max_tokens=1` remains until the separate upstream scoring-only lifecycle is available.

Across both runs, all five single-request correctness cases matched exactly. All 64 concurrent requests returning old and new scores together also matched exactly. The old path itself changed numerically between single and concurrent batches, so cross-batch bitwise equality is not an acceptance criterion. Shifted-candidate negative controls detected the alignment error. Replaying VIME's existing HTTP and reward hooks also matched the candidate adapter on all five inputs.

The implementation tests will cover malformed responses, empty responses, the legacy path and existing image routing. A short OPD training regression will check that scores reach the learner with the correct lengths and masks. Full training and real image validation have not been run in this pilot; they remain required for the corresponding integration claims.

| Work | Deliverable | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compare all three scoring paths | Initial local comparison complete; retain the benchmark for integration | @LinzeShi |
| Integrate the selected path | Request handling, score parsing and compatibility tests | @LinzeShi |
| Validate training and document usage | Short training regression and configuration guidance | @LinzeShi |

The next step is the opt-in text integration, followed by the training regression. These changes form one focused VIME PR. The existing upstream scoring RFC [#56860](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56860) owns the engine API; this proposal covers its use by VIME.
discussion: Could you take a look at what vLLM lack in terms of OPD?

@aoshen02 I looked into prefix caching for teacher scoring and opened vllm-project/vllm#60366. The idea is to reuse the shared context up to the first scoring position, with prototype results on 1, 2 and 4 GPUs. Could you take a look and add the RFC label?

items.title: [fsdp] fix: select ABC wrapper by module MRO
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: The previous condition also selects that substitute for a PEFT module whose MRO puts before. Its class swap then fails with.
items.body:
## Problem

FSDP2 temporarily substitutes `FSDPModule` while wrapping an `ABC`-first
`nn.Module`. The previous `isinstance(model, ABC)` condition also selects that
substitute for a PEFT module whose MRO puts `nn.Module` before `ABC`. Its class
swap then fails with `TypeError: __class__ assignment: object layout differs`.

## Change

Choose the substitute only when `ABC` actually precedes `nn.Module` in the
module's MRO. The existing behavior for `ABC`-first modules is unchanged.

## Scope and duplicate check

This is a training-side FSDP2 class-layout fix. It does not implement a model
adapter conversion, modify vLLM LoRA loading, or change rollout transport.
[#7749](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7749) addresses general
FSDP2 initialization and a separate recipe, while
[#7165](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7165) addresses FP32-keep
modules; neither fixes the `ABC`/`nn.Module` MRO selection.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/utils/test_fsdp2_peft_wrapping.py -q`
— 6 passed, 2 subtests passed. The new regression test exercises both base
class orders and the actual class swap; it checks restoration after the
context manager exits. `git diff --check` passed.

This fix affects FSDP wrapping, not model output or serving. No model evaluation
is claimed for this isolated change. The combined-stack training results
previously shown in this PR were removed because they do not isolate this fix.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change. The human submitter is
responsible for reviewing every changed line and the reported tests.

items.title: Fix Qwen3.5 image positions in SGLang patch bundles
items.author: 1fanwang
items.summary: Qwen3.5 image rollouts using the pinned SGLang release lose the height and width coordinates of image tokens in the fused rotary path. Text inputs can look normal while image positions are wrong.
items.body:
## Summary

Qwen3.5 image rollouts using the pinned SGLang release lose the height and width coordinates of image tokens in the fused rotary path. Text inputs can look normal while image positions are wrong.

Backport the merged SGLang correction into the stable and latest patch bundles used by Docker and conda. The release CI also runs the upstream kernel and axis-map regressions. The existing on-policy native path is preserved.

Fixes https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/2336.

Upstream correction: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/e635577431cbdfb8ce5fafb0fcd8a4ac074062c6.

## Testing Done

One NVIDIA B300, driver 580.159.04, Python 3.12.6, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, TorchVision 0.26.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0 and CuTe-DSL 4.5.2. The baseline is SGLang 0.5.15.post1 at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/0b3bb0cbe31873994c9f989fddfe2f87ca839fdd.

The reproducer constructs the real Qwen3.5 layer and compares its fused preparation path with its native rotary path using seeded weights.

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contiguous image coordinates | Q/K maximum errors 2.796875 / 3.3125 | Both 0.015625 |
| Strided image coordinates | Q/K maximum errors 2.796875 / 3.3125 | Both 0.015625 |
| Both text layouts | Q/K maximum error 0.015625 | Unchanged |

Before and after:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -s --tb=short test_model_mrope.py
```

Before:

```text
image-contiguous q: max_abs=2.79687500 position_stride=(17, 1)
image-contiguous k: max_abs=3.31250000 position_stride=(17, 1)
image-strided q: max_abs=2.79687500 position_stride=(68, 1)
image-strided k: max_abs=3.31250000 position_stride=(68, 1)
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E   Mismatched elements: 345 / 17408 (2.0%)
E   Greatest absolute difference: 2.796875 at index (12034,) (up to 0.02 allowed)
```

After:

```text
image-contiguous q: max_abs=0.01562500 position_stride=(17, 1)
image-contiguous k: max_abs=0.01562500 position_stride=(17, 1)
image-contiguous v: max_abs=0.00000000 position_stride=(17, 1)
image-contiguous gate: max_abs=0.00000000 position_stride=(17, 1)
image-strided q: max_abs=0.01562500 position_stride=(68, 1)
image-strided k: max_abs=0.01562500 position_stride=(68, 1)
image-strided v: max_abs=0.00000000 position_stride=(68, 1)
image-strided gate: max_abs=0.00000000 position_stride=(68, 1)
```

<details>
<summary>Reproducer source: test_model_mrope.py</summary>

```python
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import torch

from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig
from sglang.srt.configs.qwen3_5 import Qwen3_5Config
from sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state import (
    destroy_distributed_environment,
    destroy_model_parallel,
    init_distributed_environment,
    initialize_model_parallel,
)
from sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention import initialize_dp_attention
from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5 import (
    Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer,
    Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration,
)
from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs, set_global_server_args_for_scheduler


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def layer(
    tmp_path_factory: pytest.TempPathFactory,
) -> Iterator[Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer]:
    torch.cuda.set_device(0)
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    model_path: Path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("qwen35-config")
    config = Qwen3_5Config(
        architectures=[Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.__name__],
        text_config={
            "hidden_size": 1024,
            "intermediate_size": 1536,
            "num_attention_heads": 4,
            "num_key_value_heads": 2,
            "head_dim": 256,
            "num_hidden_layers": 4,
            "full_attention_interval": 4,
            "max_position_embeddings": 512,
            "rms_norm_eps": 1e-6,
            "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25,
            "rope_parameters": {
                "rope_type": "default",
                "rope_theta": 10000,
                "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10],
                "mrope_interleaved": True,
            },
        },
    )
    config.save_pretrained(model_path)
    server_args = ServerArgs(
        model_path=str(model_path), device="cuda", dtype="bfloat16"
    )
    set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(server_args)
    model_config: ModelConfig = ModelConfig.from_server_args(server_args=server_args)
    init_distributed_environment(
        world_size=1,
        rank=0,
        local_rank=0,
        distributed_init_method=(model_path / "process-group").as_uri(),
        backend="nccl",
        timeout=60,
    )
    try:
        initialize_model_parallel()
        initialize_dp_attention(server_args=server_args, model_config=model_config)
        with torch.device("cuda"):
            model_layer = Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer(
                config=config.text_config, layer_id=3
            ).to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        with torch.no_grad():
            for parameter in model_layer.parameters():
                torch.nn.init.normal_(tensor=parameter, mean=0.0, std=0.1)
        yield model_layer
    finally:
        destroy_model_parallel()
        destroy_distributed_environment()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "layout", ["text-1d", "text-3d", "image-contiguous", "image-strided"]
)
@torch.inference_mode()
def test_model_preparation_preserves_rotary_axes(
    layer: Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer, layout: str
) -> None:
    torch.manual_seed(1)
    hidden_states = torch.randn(
        (17, layer.hidden_size), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
    )
    if layout.startswith("text"):
        positions = torch.arange(17, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
        if layout == "text-3d":
            positions = positions.repeat(3, 1)
    else:
        positions = torch.tensor(
            [
                [0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
                [0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
                [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 3, 4, 5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
            ],
            device="cuda",
            dtype=torch.int64,
        )
        if layout == "image-strided":
            buffer = torch.zeros((3, 68), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
            buffer[:, :17].copy_(positions)
            positions = buffer[:, :17]

    expected = layer.forward_prepare_native(
        positions=positions, hidden_states=hidden_states
    )
    actual = layer.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(
        positions=positions, hidden_states=hidden_states
    )
    for name, got, wanted in zip(
        ("q", "k", "v", "gate"), actual, expected, strict=True
    ):
        assert got is not None and wanted is not None
        maximum_error = (
            (got.reshape(-1).float() - wanted.reshape(-1).float()).abs().max()
        )
        print(
            f"{layout} {name}: max_abs={maximum_error.item():.8f} "
            f"position_stride={positions.stride()}",
            flush=True,
        )
    for name, got, wanted in zip(
        ("q", "k", "v", "gate"), actual, expected, strict=True
    ):
        assert got is not None and wanted is not None
        tolerance = 0.02 if name in ("q", "k") else 0.0
        torch.testing.assert_close(
            actual=got.reshape(-1).float(),
            expected=wanted.reshape(-1).float(),
            atol=tolerance,
            rtol=tolerance,
        )
```

</details>

Both fresh Docker and conda patch stages produced the tested correction. Full image/conda environment builds, release CI, pretrained-model evaluation, RL training and other architectures have not run. The existing conda reapply failure occurs before this patch and is unchanged.

items.title: [trainer] fix: compute exact best/worst@k for numeric scores
items.author: tongyx361
items.summary: Compute validation and exactly for arbitrary numeric scores, including negative scores and partial credit. Replace 1000 with-replacement bootstrap iterations with the exact mean and standard deviation of the maximum/minimum over uniformly selected subsets of d…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Compute validation `best@k` and `worst@k` exactly for arbitrary numeric scores, including negative scores and partial credit. Replace 1000 with-replacement bootstrap iterations with the exact mean and standard deviation of the maximum/minimum over uniformly selected subsets of `k` distinct responses.

**Sampling definition changes:** these metrics now use sampling without replacement. Existing metric names and the k ladder remain unchanged, but historical with-replacement values are not directly comparable. For `[0, 0, 0, 1]`, `best@2/mean` is `0.5` and `best@4/mean` is `1.0`, compared with previous with-replacement expectations of `0.4375` and `0.68359375`.

**These are score extrema, not a generic correctness probability.** Four partial-credit scores `[0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1]` yield `best@4/mean = worst@4/mean = 0.1`. No positive-score threshold is introduced. `/std` describes the variation of subset extrema, not the standard error of the estimated expectation; at `k=n`, the means are the observed extrema and both standard deviations are zero.

Related work: credit to @emmericp for #7240's pass@k implementation and its explanation of with-replacement bias. This PR does not duplicate that work: #7240 adds a separate success-probability metric, which requires an explicit binary correctness signal or success predicate; this PR computes first and second moments of existing best/worst metrics for arbitrary scores. For binary correctness scores, `best@k/mean` equals the standard combinatorial pass@k estimate, while the distinction matters for nonbinary scores.

The PR is independent of #7240 and can land first. If #7240 lands afterward, reconcile the shared metric-utils loop and update its assertion that `best@4/mean < 1.0` for `[1, 0, 0, 0]`, since the new value is exactly `1.0`. The success-definition fix in #7240 belongs in that PR. `maj@k` retains its existing with-replacement bootstrap implementation.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement, document, test, and review this change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [bootstrap](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+bootstrap), [best@k](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22best%40k%22), and [worst@k](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22worst%40k%22). Related #7240 was reviewed and has a different scope.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

- `python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/test_metric_utils_on_cpu.py -q`: 44 passed, 23 subtests passed; two existing warnings from the empty-list mean test.
- `pre-commit run --files verl/trainer/ppo/metric_utils.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_metric_utils_on_cpu.py docs/workers/ray_trainer.rst --show-diff-on-failure`: all hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Coverage compares analytic moments against exhaustive subsets, checks binary scores against the combinatorial pass@k formula, duplicate/negative/constant scores, large score offsets, `k=1`, `k=n`, and invalid subset sizes. Integration tests verify seed independence, removal of best/worst bootstrap calls, and unchanged majority-vote bootstrap results. The existing CPU workflow discovers this test file through `*_on_cpu.py`; no workflow change is needed. Independent agent review found and fixed a cancellation issue for widely separated scores; re-review verified the fix and 1,350 randomized cases against exhaustive subsets. No remaining actionable findings. On head `d1bb2be25e95`, remote CPU unit tests, pre-commit, documentation tests, type/docstring coverage, sanity checks, and the title check passed. The full CI suite is not green: some Ascend jobs failed, ROCm jobs were cancelled, and other jobs remain pending; the causes of those outcomes have not been diagnosed here.

### API and Usage Example

The helper returns `[(best_mean, best_std), (worst_mean, worst_std)]` and accepts `1 <= k <= n`. Existing validation keys, per-prompt aggregation, and the k ladder are unchanged.

```python
from verl.trainer.ppo.metric_utils import compute_best_worst_at_k

# Binary scores: best@k mean coincides with the combinatorial pass@k estimate.
compute_best_worst_at_k([0, 0, 0, 1], 2)
# [(0.5, 0.5), (0.0, 0.0)]
compute_best_worst_at_k([0, 0, 0, 1], 4)
# [(1.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0)]

# Partial credit remains a score, rather than being counted as a correct answer.
compute_best_worst_at_k([0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1], 4)
# [(0.1, 0.0), (0.1, 0.0)]
```

### Design & Code Changes

For sorted observations, the maximum's rank-i probability is `C(i-1, k-1) / C(n, k)`. Compute these weights by a downward recurrence starting at `k/n`, then reverse the weights for the minimum. Center scores before calculating variance to avoid subtracting large raw second moments. Duplicate values retain their distinct sample ranks. At `k=n`, both extrema are deterministic and their standard deviations are zero.

Per-prompt moments retain the existing aggregation across prompts. `/std` describes variation of subset extrema, not the standard error of the estimator. The trainer documentation explains this distinction and the change in historical comparability.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Run pre-commit on all files. All hooks were run and passed for the changed files instead.
- [x] Add / Update the documentation in `docs/workers/ray_trainer.rst`.
- [x] Add unit tests covered by the existing CPU CI workflow.
- [ ] Request CI in the community channel. No external message has been sent.
- [ ] Update the recipe submodule. Not applicable.

### Current verification and integration

Full-population best/worst now returns the sorted extrema directly with zero standard deviation, including extreme finite inputs whose differences overflow float64. Current-branch verification: 44 CPU tests and 24 subtests passed; every changed-file pre-commit hook passed. OpenAI Codex assistance was used for this correction. Original contributor attribution and commit history are preserved.

Existing #8104 now includes this PR as a prerequisite through ordinary merges and supplies analytic majority metrics; the combined validation path computes best/worst/maj without bootstrap. The combined exact-metric suite passed 50 tests and 327 subtests. This PR retains its best/worst scope; #8104 remains a draft pending human review. No new PR or GPU experiment was created.

items.title: Add Megatron LoRA support for actor training with dense and MoE models
items.author: Easily2
items.summary: This PR adds opt-in LoRA support for Megatron actor training in slime. It freezes the base model and trains low-rank adapters for supported dense projections, hybrid-attention projections, and MoE shared/routed experts.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds opt-in LoRA support for Megatron actor training in slime.
It freezes the base model and trains low-rank adapters for supported
dense projections, hybrid-attention projections, and MoE shared/routed
experts.

Rollout engines receive effective base-plus-adapter weights through the
existing full-weight synchronization path, without requiring native
adapter support in SGLang.

## Changes

- Add `--use-lora` and configuration for rank, alpha, target modules,
  adapter learning rate, checkpoint loading, and export.
- Inject adapters before Megatron DDP and optimizer construction so
  frozen base parameters are excluded from training.
- Support tensor-parallel linear layers and shared adapters across
  routed experts within each layer.
- Merge adapter deltas during rollout weight synchronization and HF
  export without modifying the frozen base weights in place.
- Use the frozen base model as the reference policy for KL computation.
- Support adapter-only checkpoint loading/export, full training
  checkpoint resume, and merged HF export.
- Add English/Chinese documentation and a Qwen3-30B-A3B LoRA example.

## Guardrails

Validate unsupported combinations at startup, including PPO/critic
training, on-policy distillation, MLA, reference-policy updates,
nonzero LoRA dropout, and native adapter rollout synchronization.

Routed experts share adapter factors within each layer; per-expert
adapters are not supported.

## Validation

- Verified end-to-end LoRA training.
- Verified multi-GPU computation and checkpoint save/load.
- Added unit and integration tests for LoRA configuration, training,
  checkpointing, and weight synchronization.
- Integrated the tests into CI and passed local static and formatting checks.

items.title: [rollout, reward] fix: align padding for asynchronous reward inputs
items.author: zupengwang
items.summary: Fix asynchronous reward inputs for multi-output trajectories with different prompt lengths. currently pads concatenated sequences independently from prompts/responses, so the response boundary in can disagree with.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix asynchronous reward inputs for multi-output trajectories with different prompt lengths. `_compute_score` currently pads concatenated sequences independently from prompts/responses, so the response boundary in `attention_mask` can disagree with `responses`. Default reward managers then decode padding, truncate the final answer, or apply an incorrect DAPO length penalty.

For outputs with `(prompt_len, response_len) = [(3, 5), (9, 2)]`, the final two-token response is treated as length five; with `max_resp_len=7` and a four-token DAPO buffer, this introduces a spurious `-0.5` penalty. This fixes the input contract of the multi-output scoring introduced in #6228. No issue-closing claim is made.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [reward padding](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+reward+padding), [_compute_score padding](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+%22_compute_score%22+padding). Checked open/closed PRs and relevant comments/diffs on 2026-10-03 against main `8718ca30a3f002f93b7c4fd99b9b2506718681bc`. #7580/#6025 address weighting/grouped batching, #7217 validation metadata, and #5506 VLM postprocessing; none of their inspected diffs fixes this boundary.
- [x] Proposed title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`: `[rollout, reward] fix: align padding for asynchronous reward inputs`.

### Test

Linux, Python 3.12.13, frozen CPU uv dependencies. The same final regression yields **7 failed / 5 passed on the unmodified baseline**, and **12 passed with the patch**. Failures are behavior assertions, not import/setup errors. Seven existing adjacent test files yield **53 passed**.

```bash
uv sync --frozen --extra cpu --python 3.12
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  uv run --frozen --all-packages --extra cpu pytest -s -x \
  --asyncio-mode=auto -o 'python_files=*_on_cpu.py' \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_async_reward_padding_on_cpu.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  uv run --frozen --all-packages --extra cpu pytest -q \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_agent_loop_extra_fields_schema_on_cpu.py \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_multimodal_position_ids_on_cpu.py \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_audio_server_contract_on_cpu.py \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_call_tool_on_cpu.py \
  tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_agent_loop_tq_on_cpu.py \
  tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_compute_reward_colocate_on_cpu.py \
  tests/experimental/reward_loop/test_async_token_bucket_on_cpu.py
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never
pre-commit run --files tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_async_reward_padding_on_cpu.py \
  --show-diff-on-failure --color=never
```

All 14 hooks passed, with an explicit additional run for the new untracked test. The adjacent suite was executed using the same uv-created interpreter; the commands above also provide a portable uv entrypoint. An additional rate-limited reward-manager suite had 13 setup errors because its hardcoded local tokenizer fixture was unavailable; those tests are not counted as passed or skipped.

The regression exercises the real TQ postprocessor, reward input producer, Naive/DAPO managers and DisRM preprocessing with a local tokenizer. Only Ray transport and TQ storage writes are replaced. It covers both padding leakage and truncation, tensor/mask/position invariants, tool observations, a genuine token ID zero, precomputed rewards and scorer exceptions. Real backend inference, GPU training and performance are untested; these results are not a remote CI claim.

### API and Usage Example

No public API or configuration changes. Existing multi-output trajectories use a shared prompt/response boundary for asynchronous scoring. Reward functions continue to see tool observations, consistent with the discussion in #6392.

### Design & Code Changes

- In `_compute_score`, reuse `_pad_token_ids` to left-pad prompts and right-pad responses to their respective trajectory maxima before concatenating IDs/masks and computing positions.
- Add CPU regressions and document the padding/length-metadata contract.
- Risk: custom consumers relying on the previous compact concatenated width now receive `max_prompt_len + max_response_len`; extreme length combinations can increase temporary padding. No performance benefit is claimed.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex performed investigation, implementation and local test execution. The human submitter has confirmed review and authorized publication. The test results above were produced by Codex; independent human rerunning has not been confirmed, so this PR remains a draft pending that step. No CLA/DCO attestation is made here.

items.title: [RFC][Rollout] Support vLLM-RLT as a native rollout backend
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: The first milestone is an Ouro GRPO loop with versioned generation, full policy publication and fresh-process resume. Keep the backend change small and independently reviewable.
items.body:
## Goal

Support vLLM-RLT as an optional rollout backend through VIME's standard `train.py` / `RolloutManager`, reusing Megatron training, reward/group handling, checkpointing and physical-weight conversion.

The first milestone is an Ouro GRPO loop with versioned generation, full policy publication and fresh-process resume. Keep the backend change small and independently reviewable.

## Existing work and dependencies

- [Ouro integration #459](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/459) is merged into `0z5a-branch`. It provides the shared-weight provider, recurrent replay, conversion and online engine interactions. Its legacy example manages its own engine; reuse that work when moving lifecycle ownership into the standard control plane.
- [Nanbeige #463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/463) already contains a draft shared backend factory, native Ray engine, publication adapter and standard sample/trace integration. [Huginn #464](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/464) builds on it. This issue tracks backend acceptance and remaining lifecycle coverage alongside those PRs, without duplicating their model implementations.
- Coordinate the public score and weight-update contract with [vLLM-RLT #78](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/vllm-rlt/pull/78). The current integration pins [engine commit `d2a3589`](https://github.com/0z5a/vllm-rlt/tree/d2a358933393f25d74dd2bdd1068a741cd5d9226). Keep profile-specific score names and request/engine settings in one adapter. An accepted pinned companion can be documented as experimental; stable support requires an accepted upstream dependency.

Current staging base: [`0z5a-branch` at `3e56931`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/tree/3e569314a42a3de4aa99340021a4d00ad4e1f431). Draft implementation and legacy recipe results do not establish that the backend acceptance gate below has passed.

## Initial support contract

| Item | First milestone |
| --- | --- |
| Model / objective | Pinned Ouro-1.4B revision; standard online GRPO, no reference/critic/KL |
| Execution | Fixed full depth K=4; positive temperature and full-vocabulary sampling |
| Training layout | TP=PP=CP=1; DP only for explicitly validated world sizes |
| Resources | One native rollout engine with explicit trainer/rollout GPU ownership; initially separate resources |
| Updates | Full physical weights, initial actor publication and committed versions on outputs |
| Lifecycle | Start, ready/health, generate, drain/cancel, update, cooperative close and restart/republication |

Depth 2/3/4 and actual-depth replay regressions retain their own evidence. Colocation/offload, early exit, async generation, CUDA Graphs, PD/NIXL and speculation need separate capability and combination checks. Nanbeige/Huginn, PPO/DPPO/Flow-DPPO, RLTT and broader parallelism are follow-ups rather than prerequisites for the Ouro backend milestone.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Parse `--rollout-backend vllm-rlt` before engine-specific arguments; keep the default vLLM path and optional imports independent of RLT. Unsupported profiles/combinations fail before GPU allocation.
- [ ] Use a small factory and a Ray-owned engine adapter for startup, readiness, generation, request exclusion during updates, and cooperative teardown of this job's resources.
- [ ] Preserve standard `Sample` semantics for tokens, response length, mask, reward, group identity, behavior logprobs and weight versions. Carry a serializable recurrent trace with runtime epoch, committed policy identity, model/tokenizer/engine identities, execution plan, prefill and response-aligned actual depths, sampling/score settings, replay metadata and finish reason.
- [ ] Reuse physical-weight conversion: publish each shared block once, including required embeddings, norms, head and inference gates. Explicitly publish the actor's initial policy before accepting requests.
- [ ] Implement pause → drain/cancel → full manifest/chunks → validation → committed ACK → cache invalidation/version isolation → ready. Incomplete publication blocks generation until a full recovery; do not promise rollback of in-place copies. Same-version retries require the same manifest.
- [ ] Restore actor, optimizer, scheduler, RNG and rollout plan in a fresh process; create a new runtime epoch and republish the restored policy. Add resource release/recovery modes only when their engine contracts are verified.

## Acceptance gate

- [ ] Existing Ouro GRPO correctness is reproducible: shared parameters, score/depth alignment, at least two real optimizer updates, publication and checkpoint/resume.
- [ ] Standard `train.py` / `RolloutManager` runs without `debug-train-only`: v0 rollout → update/publish v1 → v1 rollout → update/publish v2.
- [ ] Default vLLM recipe passes with no RLT installation/import requirement.
- [ ] Mixed-length token/logprob/depth/version traces survive serialization, dump/load, packing and training conversion; incomplete or mixed-policy responses are rejected.
- [ ] Missing tensors, failed chunks and worker timeouts block generation; complete recovery re-enables it. Controlled weight/logit probes verify publication.
- [ ] Old prefix/KV state cannot be reused after a policy change; same-version reuse remains correct.
- [ ] Fresh-process resume matches continuous training state and republishes to a newly initialized engine.
- [ ] Start/close/restart, cancellation and unsupported capability checks preserve resource ownership.

Record complete source/model SHAs, dependencies, GPU placement, seeds, commands, exit codes and uncovered cases. Label evidence `CPU-MOCK`, `GPU-LOCAL`, `MULTI-RANK` or `NOT-RUN`; CPU contract checks do not replace real engine/optimizer acceptance.

Use matched hardware, precision, model, sampling, batch and update counts for performance results. Report startup separately and measure the complete rollout → reward → optimization → publication/checkpoint loop, with contention disclosed.

| Measurement | Baseline | Standard RLT backend | Speedup | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Whole training step | — | — | — | NOT-RUN |
| Rollout / training / publication | — | — | — | NOT-RUN |
| Fresh resume correctness | — | — | N/A | NOT-RUN |

Backend completion means users can select RLT through VIME's standard entry, iterate the correct recurrent policy and recover reliably, with a documented and tested support boundary.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix session grouping for `grpo_vectorized` in the V1 trainer. It currently skips the session-aware path, so rewards copied to intermediate outputs are counted repeatedly in the group mean and standard deviation.

Use each session's final output to compute advantages, then broadcast them to its other outputs, as `grpo` already does.

### Checklist Before Starting

Related #7580 changes loss weighting, and #7473 forwards estimator metadata. Neither fixes this dispatch.

### Test

The regression runs the actual reward-copying postprocessor, with storage writes mocked. Three sessions with rewards `[1, 4, 5]` produce `[1, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5]` in storage. The reward-4 session gets advantage `-0.104031` before the fix and `+0.320256` afterward.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' python -m pytest -q \
  tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_agent_loop_tq_on_cpu.py \
```

items.title: [Bug] Startup health polling can block on an unresponsive server
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach. This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. [Discussion: independent check on main: this no longer reproduces.]
items.body:
### Bug Description

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. The expected behavior is to bound each probe, then check process liveness and retry while the process is alive. The overall startup wait should remain unbounded for slow model loading.

### Steps to Reproduce

On main at `791f101e20db377b28e15f12a00863baaea2605f`, save the script below as `/tmp/reproduce_health_wait.py` and run it from the repository root:

```bash
python /tmp/reproduce_health_wait.py .
```

It extracts the unchanged production function to avoid importing GPU/training dependencies, starts a real silent loopback HTTP server, and supplies a callback that reports the child as exited. This isolates the blocked-probe behavior; it does not simulate a real vLLM process crash.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script (requires requests)</summary>

```python
"""Reproduce the startup wait against a real silent loopback HTTP server."""
import ast
import json
import pathlib
import socketserver
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import requests

root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
revision = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
path = "vime/backends/vllm_utils/vllm_engine.py"
source = (subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", f"{revision}:{path}"], cwd=root, text=True)
          if revision else (root / path).read_text())
node = next(n for n in ast.parse(source).body
            if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "_wait_server_healthy")
namespace = {"requests": requests, "time": time}
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[node], type_ignores=[]), path, "exec"), namespace)
received, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
result = {"liveness_checked": False}


class SilentHandler(socketserver.BaseRequestHandler):
    def handle(self):
        self.request.settimeout(5)
        self.request.recv(4096)
        received.set()
        release.wait(10)


def is_alive():
    result["liveness_checked"] = True
    return False  # Simulate the process monitor reporting an exited child.


def wait_for_health(url):
    try:
        namespace["_wait_server_healthy"](url, is_alive)
    except Exception as exc:
        result["error"] = str(exc)


with socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), SilentHandler) as server:
    server_thread = threading.Thread(target=server.handle_request, daemon=True)
    waiter = threading.Thread(target=wait_for_health,
                              args=(f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}",), daemon=True)
    server_thread.start()
    waiter.start()
    try:
        assert received.wait(5), "health request did not reach the loopback server"
        waiter.join(4)
        result["still_waiting_after_4s"] = waiter.is_alive()
        print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    finally:
        release.set()
        server_thread.join(5)
        waiter.join(5)

```

</details>

### Expected Behavior

The probe times out, allowing the loop to check process liveness and report `Server process terminated unexpectedly.` If the process is still alive, polling continues.

### Actual Behavior

After the four-second observation window:

```json
{"liveness_checked": false, "still_waiting_after_4s": true}
```

Restoring `timeout=3` yields:

```json
{"error": "Server process terminated unexpectedly.", "liveness_checked": true, "still_waiting_after_4s": false}
```

### Environment

- VIME main: `791f101e20db377b28e15f12a00863baaea2605f`
- Linux x86_64 / WSL2, Python 3.12.4, Requests 2.34.2
- CPU-only reproduction; no model, GPU, Ray, vLLM server, or Megatron runtime is needed or exercised.

### Additional Context

#90 intentionally removed the overall startup deadline while keeping a per-probe timeout. #174 subsequently removed that timeout. I will follow up with a focused fix and regression tests.

items.title: [fsdp, model] fix: gather DTensor LM heads for fused kernels
items.author: kolehma8
items.summary: Alternative approach to #8091: explicitly materialize the FSDP2 LM-head weight before entering the Torch, Triton, or Liger fused autograd function. Only the weight is gathered; activations, logits, and labels are not gathered by this change.
items.body:
## Summary

Alternative approach to #8091: explicitly materialize the FSDP2 LM-head weight before entering the Torch, Triton, or Liger fused autograd function. Only the weight is gathered; activations, logits, and labels are not gathered by this change.

This is a **draft for design comparison**, not a claim that explicit gathering is preferable to FSDP-managed execution.

## Related work and duplicate-work check

The issue discussion and open PRs were checked before submission. #8096 addresses the same underlying issue by registering the fused projection as an FSDP forward method on the independently sharded head. #8004 addresses an opt-in FP32-head path.

This draft explores a materially different mechanism: the fused-kernel wrappers accept the existing weight argument, conditionally gather a DTensor into a regular tensor, and rely on DTensor autograd for the head's gradient communication. It does not register a new head forward method or move the head into the root FSDP group. The alternative and its tradeoffs are documented on #8091. These approaches should be evaluated as alternatives, not landed as duplicate fixes.

## Implementation

- Add one shared weight-preparation helper outside `autograd.Function.apply`, preserving the gather/copy autograd graph even when a kernel receives raw tensor pointers.
- Move CPU-offloaded DTensor shards to the activation device before the NCCL gather, and align their compute dtype with the activations. Regular weights already on the correct device retain their identity.
- Use `Partial("avg")` gradient placements across the FSDP/HSDP mesh. A plain `full_tensor()` fixed forward execution but produced incorrect head gradients with rank-distinct inputs in the initial probe.
- Apply preparation to `FusedLinearForPPO` (Torch and Liger) and the Triton `linear_cross_entropy` wrapper.
- Remove premature Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5 materialization so these adapters reach the shared preparation path with the original DTensor.
- Keep the directly gathered, independently wrapped head out of deferred FSDP gradient bookkeeping. DTensor autograd already reduces its gradients each microbatch; deferring the unused FSDP head group otherwise still triggers the reported missing `_unsharded_param` exception. Other layers retain deferred synchronization, and tied/root-owned heads retain their existing FSDP behavior.

## Validation

Tests were run on H200 and B300 pods with Liger-Kernel 0.8.4, Transformers 5.10.4, and CuTe DSL 4.6.0.

| Hardware | PyTorch | Triton | 2-rank FSDP | 4-rank HSDP (2 x 2 mesh) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H200 | 2.9.1.6+cu129 | 3.5.1 | 44 passed, 8 skipped | 44 passed, 8 skipped |
| B300 | 2.11.0.1+cu130 | 3.6.0 | 52 passed | 52 passed |

Counts are distributed cases per invocation, **not multiplied by the number of ranks**. All H200 skips are FP32 Liger cases: the SM90 fused scaled cross-entropy implementation supports BF16 only.

The matrix uses small randomly initialized **real Qwen3 models** and covers Torch/Triton/Liger, tied/untied heads, CPU offload on/off, FP32 master parameters with FP32/BF16 computation, and immediate/deferred synchronization. It compares outputs, every trainable parameter's accumulated gradient, and two momentum-SGD updates with two microbatches per update. Inputs and loss multipliers differ across ranks. Additional cases check regular and sharded CPU/GPU weights, identity preservation, and gradients returning to their original device.

The final reference invokes the **same fused kernel inside the head's normal FSDP forward lifecycle**, isolating materialization and distributed-gradient behavior from kernel arithmetic. Initial supported two-rank cases also passed against an unfused PyTorch reference. The four-rank unfused comparison exposed a Triton FP32 output difference of approximately 0.000893; the final matrix uses the same-kernel reference without relaxing its numerical tolerances.

Commands, with `PYTHON` pointing to the relevant pod's validation interpreter and `PYTHONPATH` including this checkout plus isolated dependency directories:

```bash
export PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1
export VERL_USE_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS=none

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 uv run --no-project --python "$PYTHON" \
  python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 \
  -m pytest -q -ra --tb=short \
  tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_fused_head_gather.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 uv run --no-project --python "$PYTHON" \
  python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 \
  -m pytest -x -q -ra --tb=short \
  tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_fused_head_gather.py

uv run --no-project --python "$PYTHON" python -m pytest -q --tb=short \
  tests/utils/test_experimental_torch_functional_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_fsdp_gradient_accumulation_sync_on_cpu.py
# 21 passed on the H200 pod

uv run --no-project --python "$PYTHON" python -m pytest -q --tb=short \
  tests/models/test_fused_kernels_ulysses_sp_on_cpu.py
# 26 passed on the H200 pod
```

Targeted Ruff checks, formatting checks, and `git diff --check` also passed. The GPU matrix is directly runnable with the commands above; this draft does not add it to a CI runner.

## Tradeoffs and limits

- The fully materialized head weight is retained for kernel backward, rather than being freed and re-gathered through the head's ordinary FSDP lifecycle.
- The head synchronizes gradients **on every microbatch**, even when the rest of the model defers synchronization. This is a correctness tradeoff, not a communication-performance improvement.
- Callers bypassing VeRL's engine and calling `set_requires_gradient_sync(False)` directly must use the new VeRL helper or otherwise preserve the directly gathered head's synchronization.
- No throughput, peak-memory, pretrained-model training, full PPO/GRPO, or full FSDPEngine end-to-end result is claimed. Engine-context and adapter regressions passed; distributed numerical coverage uses Qwen3 rather than every VLM adapter.
- Ascend and composable tensor parallelism are not validated by this draft.

## AI assistance and draft status

GitHub Copilot assisted with implementation, investigation, and test execution under the submitter's direction. The explicit-gather approach and draft submission were requested by the human submitter. Human review of every changed line, reproduction of the relevant tests, and agreement on the alternative design remain requirements before marking this ready for review.

This work is on a separate clone and branch. It does not modify the existing TP/FLSCE branch or PR #7945.

items.title: [fsdp, model] fix: run fused LM heads through FSDP2 hooks
items.author: cyanseek
items.summary: With untied embeddings, FSDP2 shards independently, but fused forwards read its weight from the parent. This bypasses the head's unsharding, mixed precision, CPU offload and backward hooks.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8091. With untied embeddings, FSDP2 shards `lm_head` independently, but fused forwards read its weight from the parent. This bypasses the head's unsharding, mixed precision, CPU offload and backward hooks. A two-GPU Qwen3 reproducer fails with mixed Tensor/DTensor operands (Torch), BF16/FP32 operands (Triton), or CPU weights under offload.

Run the fused projection through an FSDP-registered forward method on the existing head. The head keeps its own sharding group and ordinary logits `forward`; backend selection and label preparation remain unchanged. The dense, Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5 and GLM4V adapters share this entry point.

Related work: closed #7427 instead keeps the fused head in the root FSDP unit. Open #8004 adds an opt-in FP32 head and routes that branch through its head forward, while the default fused path still reads the weight directly. Open #5948 falls back to materialized logits for a sharded Qwen3-VL Torch head; this change retains fused computation and also fixes the default dense and other adapter paths. It does not implement #8090's Triton shape change or #7323's visual-call alignment.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+FSDP+fused
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

On two RTX 5090 GPUs, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Transformers 5.6.1 and Liger 0.8.2:

```bash
python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 -m pytest -xsv --tb=short tests/special_distributed/test_fused_lm_head_fsdp2.py
# 144 passed on each rank (144 distributed cases, not 288 independent tests)
```

The matrix covers six small random model configurations, Torch/Triton/Liger, tied/untied heads, CPU offload on/off, two accumulated micro-batches per update, two updates, and no-grad inference. Outputs, all trainable gradients and updated parameters are compared with both ordinary HF logits and the same fused arithmetic with a root-owned head. The latter uses strict `atol=1e-6` gradient/update checks. Vision models use synthetic image inputs with their vision tower in the root FSDP unit, isolating the independently sharded head from separate HF vision-embedding sharding issues.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_fused_kernels_ulysses_sp_on_cpu.py tests/models/test_fused_lm_head_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_experimental_torch_functional_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_fsdp2_model_transfer_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_fsdp_gradient_accumulation_sync_on_cpu.py
# 46 passed
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never
# all 14 hooks passed
```

Existing two-GPU Ulysses fused-kernel, CPU-offload state_dict and pinned model-transfer tests also passed. A separate local harness also passed all 12 real FSDPEngine configurations (three backends × CPU offload × SP=1/2), including model loading, packed variable-length inputs, activation checkpointing, two accumulated updates, gradient clipping and AdamW. It uses a synthetic token-weighted masked objective; it is not a full PPO/GRPO run. No pretrained large-model training or performance improvement is claimed. The GPU environment used pinned observed versions with uv, not the complete upstream uv.lock GPU environment.


Additional validation of the updated regression matrix:

| Hardware | PyTorch | Transformers | Distributed cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2× RTX 5090 | 2.11.0+cu129 | 5.6.1 | 144 passed |
| 2× RTX 5090 | 2.13.0+cu130 | 5.12.1 | 144 passed |
| 2× RTX 3080 Ti | 2.13.0+cu130 | 5.12.1 | 144 passed |

Each unfused-reference update now starts from the same parameters as the tested model. The same-kernel reference still follows an independent two-update trajectory with strict gradient/update tolerances. The unfused update absolute tolerance is tightened to `1e-4` for both steps. All gradient tolerances and BF16 coverage are retained. The runner uses fail-fast, short tracebacks and reports the update index in numerical assertions.

The PyTorch 2.13 environments use eager attention without FlashAttention; the Torch fused backend uses its existing PyTorch cross-entropy fallback. Triton 3.7.1 and Liger 0.8.2 kernels run directly. All 14 pre-commit hooks passed for the changed test files.
### API and Usage Example

No new user configuration or CLI is required. Existing `use_fused_kernels` configurations use the registered head entry point automatically.

### Design & Code Changes

Register one additional FSDP forward method lazily on independently sharded heads, using PyTorch's public registration API. Keep existing non-FSDP behavior and VLM dtype/DTensor handling inside the projection. Add CPU numerical coverage and the two-GPU regression matrix to the existing distributed test runner.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation and test execution. The human submitter reviewed the change and approved submission.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the contribution guide.
- [x] Apply all pre-commit checks.
- [x] No user-facing configuration or API change requiring a new usage document.
- [x] Add CPU regression coverage and wire the GPU matrix into the existing distributed runner.
- [x] Human submitter reviewed the change and approved submission; the test commands and results are documented above.
- [ ] Request upstream GPU CI in the project's CI channel. No message has been sent by this task.
- [x] The recipe submodule is not involved.

items.title: [rollout] fix: release router allocations after cancelled acquire
items.author: cyanseek
items.summary: Cancelling while the router has allocated a server but has not returned the RPC result leaks the in-flight count: acquisition happens before the generation. This leaves stale load information for routing and can prevent fully-async rebalancing from observing …
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Cancelling `LLMServerClient.generate()` while the router has allocated a server but has not returned the RPC result leaks the in-flight count: acquisition happens before the generation `try/finally`. This leaves stale load information for routing and can prevent fully-async rebalancing from observing zero in-flight requests before its timeout.

Shield the pending acquisition and release a successful late allocation through the existing release helper, while propagating cancellation immediately. This also covers `FullyAsyncLLMServerClient`. It does not abort generation already dispatched to an inference backend.

Related cancellation use cases are described in #6866. This does **not** implement that issue's per-request backend-abort API. Closed #6865 adds dispatch/abort hooks after acquisition; open #5778 batches acquisition/release, and #6940 changes routing. Their inspected diffs do not cover this single-acquire cancellation window.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [acquire](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+acquire), [acquire_server cancellation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+acquire_server+cancel), [6866 references](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+6866+in%3Abody). Checked against main `8718ca30a3f002f93b7c4fd99b9b2506718681bc` on 2026-10-03.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

CPU validation with Python 3.12.13, Ray 2.55.1 and the frozen `cpu` uv environment: **42 passed** across the router, routed-experts and response-length-cap suites. The regression uses a real Ray actor with event-controlled result delivery, and a stub inference actor; it is not a GPU inference or training test. The same final regression with the unchanged base acquisition method fails for both clients: the count remains 2 instead of 1.

The regression checks prompt cancellation, one late release with the original request ID, preservation of another in-flight request, subsequent successful/failed generation, output token/log-prob/version metadata and no-server errors. Existing neighboring tests exercise partial-rollout merging and response caps.

The executed local runner initializes an isolated Ray cluster with 2 CPUs and a 100 MiB object store, runs these three suites and shuts the cluster down. Reproduce the setup after `uv sync --frozen --extra cpu` and activating that environment:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=tests/workers/rollout:. python - <<'PY'
import pytest
import ray

ray.init(address="local", num_cpus=2, include_dashboard=False,
         object_store_memory=100 * 1024**2)
try:
    result = pytest.main([
        "-q",
        "tests/workers/rollout/test_router_on_cpu.py",
        "tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_routed_experts_on_cpu.py",
        "tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_response_length_cap_on_cpu.py",
    ])
finally:
    ray.shutdown()
raise SystemExit(result)
PY
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never
```

All 14 full-repository pre-commit hooks passed, including formatting, mypy, generated trainer configuration and sanity checks. No throughput or training-equivalence claim is made; no GPU backend or distributed training run was performed.

### API and Usage Example

No API/configuration changes. Existing callers may cancel `generate()` while waiting for routing; the successful late allocation is released while the client event loop remains alive. Process death and backend abort are outside this change.

### Design & Code Changes

- Protect the acquisition await from local cancellation; attach cleanup only on the cancellation path.
- Reuse `_release_server` and router-declared fields, preserving plugin behavior.
- Extend the existing CPU router suite and document cancellation semantics.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation and local validation. 

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): all 14 hooks passed.
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit tests to CI: the existing `cpu_unit_tests.yml` discovers `test_router_on_cpu.py` through `*_on_cpu.py`; no workflow change needed.
- [ ] Once ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` Slack channel or Feishu group.
- [ ] If related to the `recipe` submodule, update its reference. Not applicable; no recipe change.
