items.title: fix(rollout): preserve weight versions on stream abort
items.author: Beverly621
items.summary: SGLang already includes in chunk metadata, but returned before recording it. If the HTTP stream is cancelled mid-generation, slime keeps the generated tokens and rollout log-probabilities while remains empty.
items.body:
## Summary

- Record the backend-reported weight version when a streaming chunk adds model tokens, including chunks retained when the request is aborted before a terminal response.
- Keep consecutive chunks from the same version to one `Sample.weight_versions` entry; a zero-token terminal update still adds no version.
- Add CPU regression coverage for aborted-stream provenance, staleness, and oldest-first partial-rollout ordering.

## Problem

`generate_streaming()` appends each SGLang chunk with `update_terminal_info=False` until a `finish_reason` arrives. SGLang already includes `weight_version` in chunk metadata, but `Sample._apply_meta_info()` returned before recording it. If the HTTP stream is cancelled mid-generation, slime keeps the generated tokens and rollout log-probabilities while `weight_versions` remains empty.

| One-token stream, generated by version `2`, aborted before terminal metadata | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Sample.weight_versions` | `[]` | `["2"]` |
| Staleness at current version `3` | unknown | `1` update |
| Oldest-first continuation versus a version `3` group | version `3` group first | version `2` group first |

The empty version is therefore more than missing observability: with staleness-based buffer ordering enabled, a partial trajectory containing older tokens can be scheduled after newer work.

## Fix

Move weight-version recording ahead of the terminal-metadata guard. Record a version only when the chunk contributes tokens, and collapse adjacent identical versions so frequent streaming chunks do not grow the list unnecessarily. Terminal status, prefix-cache accounting, tokens, log-probabilities, and sampling behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- The aborted-stream regression failed on base `main` with `weight_versions == []` and passes with this change.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_sample.py tests/test_streaming_rollout.py tests/test_fully_async_rollout.py tests/test_rollout_buffer_order.py tests/test_queue_sample_codec.py -q` — **83 passed**.
- `pre-commit run --files slime/utils/types.py tests/test_sample.py tests/test_streaming_rollout.py` — all applicable hooks passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

This is a CPU-tested fix for streaming metadata handling;

  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

- Qwen3-30B-A3B
- Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct

6. Forward-output consistency: Compared last-token logits before and after conversion using a GSM8K text sample for Qwen3 and a Geo3K image-text sample for the other models. All comparisons passed with atol=rtol=1e-5.

items.title: fix(data): address optional Straw and trusted top-p validation regressions
items.author: Beverly621
items.summary: Fix two independent CPU regressions present on: an optional Straw import on the object-store path and incomplete validation of new sampled-token metadata against previously validated top-p support. They are separate commits.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix two independent CPU regressions present on `main`: an optional Straw import on the object-store path and incomplete validation of new sampled-token metadata against previously validated top-p support. They are separate commits. Both fixes are included here because the full PR CPU suite runs both affected tests, so either fix alone leaves the other job red.

| Path | Problem on `main` | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object-store rollout without a queue lease | `group_lease()` imports `straw.protocol.Lease` before it checks whether the group has a lease. The no-lease path can fail with `ModuleNotFoundError` even though it does not use Straw. | Return `None` for a no-lease group before importing Straw. Lease-backed groups still construct the same `Lease` after authorization checks. |
| Validated top-p support plus new sampled-token metadata | `TensorRef.validated` proves the stored support was validated earlier, but the fast path also skips comparing a *new* `tokens`/`sampled_logps` pair with that support. | Keep the no-payload-read fast path when no new tokens are supplied. When new tokens are supplied, run the existing bounded support scan and check membership and recorded log-probabilities. |

The original failures are visible in the [base-branch CPU workflow](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/36706056601). They also reproduce on the current `main` used for this update.

## Regression coverage

- Extend `test_optional_straw.py` to call `group_lease()` on an object-store group in a subprocess that blocks Straw imports. This directly covers the no-lease path. The existing dynamic-filter regression also runs in the CI environment without Straw.
- Update the top-p transport regression to use 4,097 rows, crossing the implementation's 4,096-row chunk boundary. It checks continuous, bounded and matching ID/log-probability reads, then rejects a changed sampled token.
- Preserve the metadata-only republication check for validated references when no new sampled tokens are supplied.

The changes do not alter sampling probabilities, queue authorization, or the reference-policy replay fix in #2434.

## Validation

- Rebased on `THUDM/slime:main` (`8c17b676`, including #2434).
- Ran the complete Python 3.10 Linux CPU CI matrix: **77/77 test files passed**. This used the workflow's dependency split: 9 jobs with Straw installed and 68 jobs without Straw.
- Ran `pre-commit run --all-files`: all configured hooks passed.
- Ran `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`: passed.
discussion:
：）👋~
1）For reviewer context, both [#2433](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2433) (Search-R1 docs) and [#2438](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2438) (streaming weight versions) are affected by the two existing main CPU regressions addressed here. 
2）On #2438, these appear as the [fully async rollout](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/37014765204/job/110862814487) and [top-p transport](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/37014765204/job/110862814417) failures.
3）The changes proposed in #2433 and #2438 are separate from these fixes.
Once this PR is merged, I’ll update both branches onto the new main and rerun their CI. I’m keeping the fixes in this PR rather than duplicating them in either branch.

items.title: fix(data): avoid requiring straw without queue leases
items.author: Beverly621
items.summary: Instead, it imported before inspecting the group. On a CPU worker without the optional Straw package, that import raised before the no-lease return could run.
items.body:
## Summary

- Keep the object-store rollout path usable when the optional `straw-queue` package is not installed.
- Import `straw.protocol.Lease` only for groups that actually carry a queue lease.

## Root cause

Dropping a group during fully asynchronous dynamic filtering follows this path:

```text
_generate_rollout_async()
  -> discard_rollout_group()
  -> group_lease()
```

An object-store group has no `_queue_lease`, so `group_lease()` should return `None`. Instead, it imported `straw.protocol.Lease` before inspecting the group. On a CPU worker without the optional Straw package, that import raised `ModuleNotFoundError` before the no-lease return could run. The existing `test_dynamic_filter_drops_groups_and_refills` covers this case and fails in the [base `main` CI job](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/36706056601/job/109856459432) at `slime/data/transport.py:179`.

## Change

Move the import below the no-lease check and the existing consistency check. Groups without a lease now return without importing Straw; groups with a lease still construct the same `Lease` object. This does not change queue authorization or require a new dependency for object-store transport.

## Validation

- Ran the full `tests/test_fully_async_rollout.py` file with Straw imports deliberately blocked, simulating an environment without `straw-queue`: **15 passed**. This includes the previously failing dynamic-filter regression.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The repository's applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

## Related CI failure

The base branch also has an independent top-p validation failure. It is addressed in [#2436](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2436) and is outside this PR's scope.
discussion: Superseded by #2436, which includes this Straw lazy-import fix as a separate commit alongside the independent top-p validation fix. Both previously failing CPU jobs and the full PR Test run now pass on #2436 (commit 07dd1b4c, run https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/36975779068).

items.title: [single_controller] feat: enable FusedWorker in v1 trainer and await async sub-workers
items.author: ETOgaosion
items.summary: Switch worker-group construction in the v1 trainer (and the colocated v0 / separation entry points) from the deprecated WorkerDict container to FusedWorker. The old container is already annotated; this PR makes the v1 path actually use it.
items.body:
> This is the **first PR** of the topology RFC [#7269](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/7269) (Declarative Model-Topology API). It enables the FusedWorker container in the default v1 path as a prerequisite; follow-up PRs will introduce atomic RL workers and the declarative `topology:` placement block.

## What

Switch worker-group construction in the v1 trainer (and the colocated v0 / separation entry points) from the deprecated `create_colocated_worker_cls` WorkerDict container to **FusedWorker** (`create_colocated_worker_cls_fused`). The old container is already annotated `# deprecated, switching to FusedWorker`; this PR makes the v1 path actually use it.

The sub-worker classes and training logic are unchanged — only the container changes.

### Why the async fix is required

The fused router (`FusedWorker._fuw_execute`) is a synchronous method that previously did `return udc_method(...)`. Sub-worker methods such as `update_weights` are `async def`, so this returned a bare, never-awaited coroutine, which Ray fails to serialize:

```
TypeError: cannot pickle 'coroutine' object
RuntimeWarning: coroutine ... was never awaited
```

The router now drives the returned awaitable to completion with the new `run_coroutine_sync` helper (runs directly when no loop is running, otherwise on a short-lived worker thread). Non-async methods are returned unchanged.

## Changes

- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`: use `create_colocated_worker_cls_fused`.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py` and `verl/experimental/separation/ray_trainer.py`: same switch for the colocated v0 / separation paths.
- `verl/single_controller/ray/base.py`: await async sub-worker results inside `_fuw_execute`.
- `verl/utils/ray_utils.py`: add `run_coroutine_sync` (stdlib only).
- `tests/single_controller/test_colocated_workers.py`: add `test_fused_workers` covering the fused container with a sync and an async (`async def`) sub-worker, compared against detached worker groups.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs before opening this:
- #4792 creates one placement group across nodes with IP-based worker sorting.
- #1519 adds TorchRPC as a single-controller backend.
- #7840 introduces backend-neutral Runtime/control contracts.

None switch the default v1 worker-group container to FusedWorker or fix the async-sub-worker routing.

## Tests

- New on-GPU test executed on an 8x A100 node (Python 3.11, Ray 2.58, vLLM 0.29 stack):

```
pytest tests/single_controller/test_colocated_workers.py::test_fused_workers -svx
tests/single_controller/test_colocated_workers.py::test_fused_workers PASSED
1 passed, 1 warning in 24.30s
```

- Before the `run_coroutine_sync` fix, the same test fails with `TypeError: cannot pickle 'coroutine' object` on the async sub-worker, confirming the regression coverage.
- `pre-commit` (ruff / ruff format / mypy / generated-config and doc checks) passes.

> AI-assisted work: I used an AI assistant for drafting and implementation; all changed lines were reviewed and the tests above were run by me.

items.title: fix(ppo): avoid top-p replay for reference logprobs
items.author: Beverly621
items.summary: enabled that replay unconditionally, including when switched to the reference model and called it with. The reference pass was therefore renormalized over support recorded from the actor rollout.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve rollout top-p support replay for actor log-probabilities.
- Compute `ref_log_probs` with the reference model's full-vocabulary normalization, without applying the actor's recorded rollout support.
- Add a focused CPU regression for reference probability mass outside that support.

## Problem

Top-p replay ([#2102](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2102)) aligns trainer actor log-probabilities with the truncated policy used during rollout. `MegatronActor.compute_log_prob()` enabled that replay unconditionally, including when `train_actor()` switched to the reference model and called it with `store_prefix="ref_"`. The reference pass was therefore renormalized over support recorded from the *actor* rollout.

For a sampled token `A`, let the rollout support be `{A, B}` and the replayed actor probability be `q(A) = 0.5`:

| Reference distribution `(A, B, C)` | Full `p_ref(A)` | Replayed `p_ref(A given {A, B})` | Log ratio with full reference | Log ratio with replayed reference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `(0.1, 0.2, 0.7)` | `0.1` | `1/3` | `log(0.5 / 0.1) ≈ 1.609` | `log(0.5 / (1/3)) ≈ 0.405` |
| `(0.2, 0.4, 0.4)` | `0.2` | `1/3` | `log(0.5 / 0.2) ≈ 0.916` | `log(0.5 / (1/3)) ≈ 0.405` |

The two full reference log-probabilities differ, but replay makes them identical because it discards reference probability mass outside the actor's recorded nucleus. This changes the reference term used by the KL penalty.

## Fix

- Add an explicit `use_rollout_top_p_replay` option to `compute_log_prob()`, defaulting to `True` so actor replay retains its existing behavior.
- Pass `False` only for the reference-model log-probability call. Teacher/OPD paths and other sampling behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- The new CPU regression checks that the two reference distributions retain distinct full-vocabulary log-probabilities while actor replay still uses the recorded support.
- 28 relevant CPU top-p/log-probability tests passed locally.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed.
discussion:
CI note: The two failing CPU jobs in [this PR's run](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/36963298390) also fail with the same errors on the current base main (bbba9465) in the [main workflow run](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/actions/runs/36706056601):
- test_dynamic_filter_drops_groups_and_refills: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'straw'.
- test_top_p_validation_checks_shared_support_in_chunks: the same reads=[] assertion failure.

These failures are unrelated to this PR's reference log-probability change.
 The focused regression passes locally, and the other non-skipped checks pass. 
The two base-branch failures are now addressed together in #2436, which passes the full PR test suite.
keeping this PR scoped to reference top-p replay.

items.title: [model] fix: triton fused output shape
items.author: kylemontgomery1
items.summary: When, the Torch backend returns log probabilities and entropy as, while the Triton backend leaves them flattened as. With, this flat output causes an at in.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When `use_fused_kernels=True`, the Torch backend returns log probabilities and entropy as `[B,S]`, while the Triton backend leaves them flattened as `[B*S]`. With `use_remove_padding=False`, this flat output causes an `IndexError` at `output.log_probs.shape[1]` in `FSDPEngineWithLMHead.prepare_model_outputs()` (`verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py`). This PR restores the batch and sequence dimensions in the Transformers Triton forward adapters. Closes https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8089.

- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.fused_kernel_options.impl_backend=triton \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
```

```

items.author: dongha-yoon
items.summary: Adds the Megatron producer for the NCCL M2N checkpoint backend. It exports HF-named tensors from their owning training ranks with global shape, shard geometry, and expert-ownership metadata, avoiding TP/EP tensor-value gathers during conversion.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds the Megatron producer for the NCCL M2N checkpoint backend. It exports HF-named tensors from their owning training ranks with global shape, shard geometry, and expert-ownership metadata, avoiding TP/EP tensor-value gathers during conversion. The backend transfers these weights to the destination-local vLLM receiver introduced in #8087.

This is the final producer step in **#7432 → #7552 → #8087 → this PR**. It builds on the receiver changes from #8087 and the layout/FSDP/backend foundation in #7552.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for similar open PRs on 2026-10-01: [NCCL M2N](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22NCCL+M2N%22), [nccl_m2n](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+nccl_m2n), and [Megatron reshard](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+Megatron+reshard). All result pages for these queries were collected.
- [x] Formatted the title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

**Full-stack validation completed.** The combined NCCL M2N stack was previously validated in a cluster run with the full **Qwen3-32B BF16** model on **160 H100 GPUs across 20 nodes**: 128 trainer GPUs and 32 rollout GPUs, Megatron TP4/PP1/CP1/EP1 with **vanilla MBridge 0.15.1**, and vLLM TP4. Both `nccl_m2n` and the `nccl` baseline completed **two training steps**.

### API and Usage Example

For an existing Megatron/vLLM job, select the checkpoint backend through the existing configuration:

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    checkpoint_engine:
      backend: nccl_m2n
```

The existing Megatron engine setting `vanilla_mbridge` selects the adapter. The backend calls `MegatronEngine.get_per_tensor_param_nccl_m2n()` and uses its local-weight descriptors and rank-layout metadata; users do not invoke a separate export API or set a receiver wire-format flag.

### Design & Code Changes

- Add owner-local weight descriptors and vanilla MBridge conversion for dense weights, fused QKV/gate-up weights, and local expert families.
- Add the Megatron-Bridge adapter with cached conversion tasks, local mapping copies, model-specific post-conversion hooks, complete expert-ownership checks, and preservation of checkpoint scale dtypes.
- Connect the exporter and PP/EP/TP rank metadata to the NCCL M2N backend, checking exported shard coordinates against Megatron's process-group geometry.
- Update the base exporter descriptor contract and recognize `mlp.gate.weight` as a replicated router weight.

items.title: [ckpt, rollout, vllm] feat: load destination-local NCCL M2N weights
items.author: dongha-yoon
items.summary: Adds the vLLM receiver for the NCCL M2N backend's wire format. M2N has already partitioned these tensors for each destination worker, so this path loads them into local parameter storage without applying vLLM's normal TP slicing a second time.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds the vLLM receiver for the NCCL M2N backend's `rank_local_named_tensors` wire format. M2N has already partitioned these tensors for each destination worker, so this path loads them into local parameter storage without applying vLLM's normal TP slicing a second time. It uses the existing CUDA IPC/shared-memory bucket transport and retains the standard `named_tensors` path.

This is the receiver step in **#7432 → #7552 → this PR → #8088**. The preparation uses the current #7552 head as its exact parent; no additional foundation changes sit between that head and this receiver commit. #7552 remains the layout/FSDP/backend prerequisite, and the Megatron producer is a separate follow-up.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for similar open PRs on 2026-10-01: [NCCL M2N](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22NCCL+M2N%22), [rank-local wire format](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22rank_local_named_tensors%22), and [vLLM receiver](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+vllm+receiver). All result pages for these queries were collected.
- [x] Formatted the title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Full-stack validation—Megatron export → NCCL M2N transfer → vLLM destination-local loading and generation—will be reported in the final Megatron producer follow-up after it is completed, with the tested commit, configuration, commands, and logs. GPU/E2E validation of this public stack is currently pending.

### API and Usage Example

The checkpoint backend remains selected through the existing configuration:

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    checkpoint_engine:
      backend: nccl_m2n
```

The backend and adapter carry the wire-format information; users do not set a separate vLLM flag. Internally, `ServerAdapter.update_weights(..., wire_format="rank_local_named_tensors")` forwards `weights_are_tp_sharded=True` to `update_weights_from_ipc()`. Unsupported wire formats are rejected.

This receiver rejects LoRA adapter updates, QAT, and ModelOpt QAT on the TP-local path. Models detected by the existing `is_fp8_model` helper require rollout TP1; this is not a claim of support for every quantization scheme. The code introduces destination-local loader handling; the current Megatron-Bridge producer's rollout TP>1 behavior remains unverified and is not a support claim of this receiver PR.

### Design & Code Changes

- Add a temporary local-loader context for column/row parallel and fused QKV/merged-column parameters. Validate local shapes and restore overwritten parameter attributes when the load context exits.
- Identify vocabulary weights by the vLLM layer type, copy their local rows, and clear destination padding. Patch and restore each shared Parameter object once; this does not deduplicate repeated tied-alias weight updates.
- Forward the rank-local wire contract through the existing IPC update path and activate the loader context only for non-FP8 rank-local parameter updates. FP8 TP1 updates retain the existing quantized loading path.

### AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with source comparison, local port preparation, validation orchestration, and this PR description. The implementation was reviewed by @kaixih and @kwen2501, before being ported upstream. @dongha-yoon is the human submitter responsible for this upstream contribution. The existing authorship and commit messages were preserved.

items.title: [data] fix: correct enable_thinking_default YAML value and loss mask mismatch
items.author: ZhiliangWu
items.summary: Two bugs in cause a mismatch between tokenization and loss masking when the chat template produces different token counts for thinking ON vs OFF. evaluates to, so silently enables thinking mode.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Two bugs in `MultiTurnSFTDataset` cause a mismatch between tokenization and loss masking when the chat template produces different token counts for thinking ON vs OFF.

1. **Wrong YAML type**: `enable_thinking_default: none` in `sft_trainer_engine.yaml` is the string `"none"`, not Python `None`. `bool("none")` evaluates to `True`, so `_process_single_message` silently enables thinking mode.
2. **Loss mask ignores thinking mode**: `extract_system_prompt_and_generation` (which measures the generation prompt length for loss masking) receives `apply_chat_template_kwargs` but never `enable_thinking_default`. It always measures with the template's built-in default, regardless of what `_process_single_message` uses.

Bug 1 triggers bug 2: `_process_single_message` renders with thinking ON, while `extract_system_prompt_and_generation` measures with the template default. When the two modes produce different prefix lengths, template tokens get non-zero loss and are trained on as content.

This PR fixes both:
1. **YAML default**: `none` → `null`, so the value becomes Python `None` and both methods skip passing `enable_thinking`, letting the template's built-in default apply consistently.
2. **Loss mask**: `extract_system_prompt_and_generation` now receives `enable_thinking_default` via `apply_chat_template_kwargs`, matching `_process_single_message`. This prevents the mismatch from reoccurring if a user explicitly sets `enable_thinking_default` to `true` or `false`.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+enable_thinking_default
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.
  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

### Test


### API and Usage Example

No API change. Existing configs work as before. 

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/config/sft_trainer_engine.yaml`: `enable_thinking_default: none` → `null`
- `verl/utils/dataset/multiturn_sft_dataset.py`: pass `enable_thinking_default` to `extract_system_prompt_and_generation` at init, using the same pattern as `_process_single_message`.

### Checklist Before Submitting

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review.

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: ...
- [x] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`.
discussion:
> Thanks for the fix! The YAML change (`none` → `null`) is clearly correct: OmegaConf parses `none` as the string `"none"`, so `bool("none")` silently turned thinking on for every sample. 👍
> 
> However, I think the second change (passing `enable_thinking_default` into `extract_system_prompt_and_generation`) can introduce a **new** loss-mask bug for Qwen3-style templates, so I'd suggest dropping it or reworking it.
> 
> **Why:** `generation_prompt` is computed as the diff between `add_generation_prompt=True` and `False`. However, it's used to mask the prefix of an assistant message rendered **on its own** (`_process_single_message`, `add_generation_prompt=False`). For Qwen3 these two don't match when `enable_thinking=False`:
> 
> * Qwen3 template, `add_generation_prompt` branch:
>   ```
>   {{- '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}
>   {%- if enable_thinking is defined and enable_thinking is false %}
>       {{- '<think>\n\n</think>\n\n' }}
>   {%- endif %}
>   ```
>   
>   
>       
>         
>       
>   
>         
>       
>   
>       
>     
>   With this PR and `enable_thinking_default: false`, `generation_prompt` = `<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`.
> * But a single assistant message rendered alone (`messages=[assistant]`, so `last_query_index == 0` and `loop.index0 > ns.last_query_index` is false) is `<|im_start|>assistant\n{content}<|im_end|>\n`. It has no empty think block.
> * So `loss_mask[: len(self.generation_prompt)] = 0` would zero out the first few tokens (`<think>`, `\n\n`, `</think>`, `\n\n` ≈ 4 tokens) of the **actual answer content**. On current `main` this doesn't happen, because `generation_prompt` is always `<|im_start|>assistant\n` for Qwen3.
> 
> `sanity_check` won't catch it either, since it only compares `input_ids` and doesn't check `loss_mask`.
> 
> There's also a related gap. `enable_thinking` can come per sample from the `enable_thinking_key` column, but this change only uses the global default. Datasets with mixed per-row values would still be inconsistent.
> 
> **Suggestion:**
> 
> 1. Keep the YAML fix. That alone resolves the reported `bool("none")` issue.
> 2. If we want to make the loss mask robust to `enable_thinking`, here are two options:
>    
>    * Compute `generation_prompt` per effective `enable_thinking` value (e.g. cache for `None/True/False`) and pick it in `__getitem__`.
>    * Better: check that the rendered assistant `input_ids` actually start with `generation_prompt` before masking (assert, or mask only the matching common prefix). That way template quirks fail loudly instead of silently masking content.
> 3. Please add a case to `tests/utils/dataset/test_multiturn_sft_dataset_on_cpu.py` that checks the loss mask with `enable_thinking=False` on a Qwen3 tokenizer. The "Test" section of the PR description is currently empty.

Thanks for the detailed review and comments. Indeed the change 2 would result in issues due to the chat-template-inconsistency from Qwen3,  where the `add_generation_prompt=True` path (inference) and the single-message rendering path (training) produce different prefixes. 

Per your suggestions, I dropped that change and would leave a more robust loss masking for another PR.

items.title: [rollout] fix: supply runtime context to agent loop constructors
items.author: yueyiming2009
items.summary: Expose per-rollout runtime metadata to custom agent loops through constructor-supplied, without mixing runtime fields into dataset kwargs. already knows the validation mode and dispatch step, but custom loops have no explicit runtime context.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Expose per-rollout runtime metadata to custom agent loops through constructor-supplied `RolloutContext`, without mixing runtime fields into dataset kwargs.

`AgentLoopWorker._run_agent_loop()` already knows the validation mode and dispatch step, but custom loops have no explicit runtime context. In the TransferQueue path, the batch's `validate` flag is consumed before per-prompt dispatch.

The worker now creates a frozen context for each new agent-loop instance and passes it through Hydra to `AgentLoopBase.__init__`. Custom loops read `self.rollout_context.is_validation` and `.step`. The existing `run(sampling_params, **dataset_fields)` invocation, sampling behavior, and native postprocessing remain unchanged.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for similar work: [validation/agent PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+validation+agent), [RolloutContext PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+RolloutContext), and [rollout_context PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+rollout_context).
- [x] Checked upstream main at `8718ca30a3f002f93b7c4fd99b9b2506718681bc`: runtime context is not provided to custom agent loops.
- [x] This is distinct from [verl-project/verl#7217](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7217), which forwards validation to asynchronous reward computation, and [verl-project/verl#7019](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7019), which addresses postprocessing argument-name collisions.
- [x] Title follows `[rollout] fix: ...`.

### Test

- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest -q tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_agent_loop_validation_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_audio_server_contract_on_cpu.py`: **34 passed**.
- The CPU tests execute production context, base-constructor, and dispatch definitions extracted from source with real Hydra/Pydantic and fake runtime collaborators. They do not initialize Ray, GPUs, or a model.
- Covers training, step-zero and later evaluation, all eight Hydra conversion/recursion combinations, constructor-config precedence, context immutability, unchanged dataset kwargs (including fields named `rollout_context`, `is_validation`, and `step`), direct construction with/without context, custom `run()` without arbitrary kwargs, public export, and concurrent native TransferQueue dispatch with 64 initial evaluation prompts.
- Every dispatched rollout gets a distinct context, and context values remain independent of later trajectory-dictionary mutations.
- Ruff format/check, focused regression-file mypy, changed-file compilation, targeted license checks, documentation timestamp checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Validation used Python 3.12, Hydra 1.3.7, OmegaConf 2.3.0, Pydantic 2.13.5, and pytest 9.1.0. This was not a frozen upstream-lock environment.
- Full all-files pre-commit, heavy runtime-import suites, and GPU end-to-end training were not run.

### API and Usage Example

```python
from verl.experimental.agent_loop import AgentLoopBase, RolloutContext

class CustomAgentLoop(AgentLoopBase):
    async def run(self, sampling_params, **dataset_fields):
        context = self.rollout_context
        if context is None:
            raise RuntimeError("This agent loop requires rollout context.")
        is_validation = context.is_validation
        dispatch_step = context.step
        # Dataset fields and runtime context remain separate.
```

`RolloutContext` is a frozen Pydantic model with `is_validation: bool` and `step: int`. `step` identifies the trainer's dispatch step, not necessarily the behavior-weight version.

The base constructor accepts optional `rollout_context`; direct construction without it retains `None` rather than inferring training mode. Custom constructors should forward this argument or `**kwargs` to the base constructor. Built-in single-turn and tool loops already forward constructor kwargs. Worker dispatch supplies context regardless of trace enablement.

### Design & Code Changes

- Define and export `RolloutContext` alongside the existing agent-loop types. A frozen Pydantic object survives Hydra conversion without requiring changes to the other constructor arguments or a separate wrapper.
- Store the context in `AgentLoopBase` and supply a fresh instance from the worker's authoritative trajectory metadata for each rollout.
- Keep `run()` kwargs untouched: no reserved `validate` dataset key, marker field, or sampling-based inference. Native postprocessing, worker scheduling, and queue publication are unchanged.
- Update API documentation and add CPU regressions under the existing `*_on_cpu.py` CI discovery pattern.
- Register the new regression file's contributor copyright header with the existing license checker.

items.title: [Training][Rollout] Integrate Ouro shared layers and policy updates
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: Rollouts use the companion engine's public generation and transactional full-weight publication contract for local and real prefill/decode engines. The provider replays full-depth prompt prefill and each decode token's actual execution depth, including the las…
items.body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/459/files).

Base: `0z5a-branch` at `791f101e20db377b28e15f12a00863baaea2605f`.

## Purpose

Integrate Ouro's physical shared layers with VIME's existing Megatron GRPO optimizer, loss, distributed checkpoint and HF conversion paths. Rollouts use the companion engine's public generation and transactional full-weight publication contract for local and real prefill/decode engines.

The provider replays full-depth prompt prefill and each decode token's actual execution depth, including the last-exited KV state at deeper planes. Physical parameters retain their checkpoint names across MCore/DDP wrappers; recurrent loops do not duplicate parameter storage. `examples/ouro/run.sh` provides a multi-iteration launch and fresh-process resume recipe.

Target: `0z5a-branch` at `791f101e20db377b28e15f12a00863baaea2605f`. The submitted diff contains the implementation and user recipe: **17 files, 870 additions and 28 deletions**. Added tests, validation harnesses, raw logs and coordination artifacts have been removed. Their results are summarized here.

## Coordination and dependency

Companion [ThinkFlowLab/vllm-rlt#78](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/vllm-rlt/pull/78) remains a draft. Following [Minhao's PR 1 design](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/vllm-rlt/issues/70#issuecomment-5927860064), VIME uses full four-loop prompt prefill, actual decode-depth replay, selected-token processed scores and returned effective seeds. The reduced-prefill prototype is superseded.

The reference currently exposes `log_probs` and per-request `logprobs_mode`. The proposed upstream API uses `logprobs` and engine-level `raw_logprobs`/`processed_logprobs`, with weight publication in PR 2. Adapting to and testing Minhao's exact implementation remain pending availability of that branch.

## Validation

| Check | Thor local engine | Two A100 GPUs, real PD |
|---|---|---|
| Full Ouro-1.4B training and fresh-process resume | Five continuous eager updates vs four graph updates plus resumed fifth: all **272 checkpoint tensors and Adam metadata exact** | Three continuous eager updates vs two graph updates plus resumed third: all **272 exact** |
| Generic HF export | All **269 physical tensors exact** | All **269 physical tensors exact** |
| Training through inference features | Early exit, delayed async and self-speculation each complete two full-model updates | Delayed async, NIXL transfers, committed worker versions and cooperative shutdown |

After porting to the target branch, the mixed-depth probability/recomputed-gradient CPU check and physical-parameter HF round trip pass on the unchanged Thor runtime. Changed Python files pass Ruff, Black and isort checks. Five full-model K=2/3/4/early/delayed cases exactly replay tokens and selected scores from returned entropy seeds.

Actual-depth replay reduces early-exit actor/inference score MAE from 3.622689 to 0.011142; fixed K=4 still has MAE 0.026607. Training/inference score equality is not asserted for the full model.

## Speed comparisons

Full Ouro-1.4B warmed rollout medians, five alternating-order pairs, two prompts, 32 response tokens, temperature 0.9 and fixed seeds; initialization and capture excluded:

| Rollout | Eager (s) | Graphs (s) | Speedup | Time saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| K=2 | 1.0689 | 0.9939 | 1.076× | 7.02% |
| K=3 | 1.5190 | 1.4207 | 1.069× | 6.47% |
| K=4 | 1.9414 | 1.8234 | 1.065× | 6.08% |
| Self-speculative K=4 target / K=2 draft | 1.4952 | 1.3741 | 1.088× | 8.11% |

| Real full-model GRPO component | Eager median (s) | Graph median (s) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Thor rollout | 1.8644 | 1.8612 | 1.002× |
| Thor training | 10.9735 | 11.7205 | 0.936× |
| Thor publication | 0.0287 | 0.0285 | 1.007× |
| Thor whole step | 12.8710 | 13.5940 | 0.947× |
| A100 PD whole step | 62.1185 | 62.2978 | 0.997× |

Thor component medians use matched updates 1–3 at K=3/4/2, four prompts × four samples and 16-token responses. A100 medians include first-use capture and fresh resume under existing GPU contention. Whole-training acceleration and reward convergence are not demonstrated.

The A100 runtime's default UCX GPU IPC probe failed; passing PD runs use command-scoped `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy` with host-staged transport. BF16 bitwise comparisons require matched one-slot batches; differing dynamic batch shapes fail strict parity. TP/PP/CP=1 is required by this recipe.

[Launch, parameter conversion and resume instructions](https://github.com/0z5a/vime/blob/feat/ouro-training-integration/examples/ouro/README.md). Completed task-owned model/checkpoint/export files are cleaned after checks. No process termination, environment updates or lcpu NFS changes were performed.


Historical layer review: [provider #3](https://github.com/0z5a/vime/pull/3/files) → [budget recipe #4](https://github.com/0z5a/vime/pull/4/files) → [public contract/conversion #5](https://github.com/0z5a/vime/pull/5/files). This upstream PR is the consolidated diff against `0z5a-branch`.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: honor engine dtype for mixed precision defaults
items.author: zupengwang
items.summary: Setting currently leaves FSDP compute and autocast in BF16 when is absent, so the FP16 gradient scaler is also omitted. Use the engine's as the default for both an absent and a partial mapping.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8076. Setting `actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.dtype=float16` currently leaves FSDP compute and autocast in BF16 when `mixed_precision.param_dtype` is absent, so the FP16 gradient scaler is also omitted.

Use the engine's `dtype` as the default for both an absent and a partial `mixed_precision` mapping. Explicit `param_dtype` overrides still take precedence; reduction and buffer defaults remain FP32. The existing wrapper, autocast and scaler setup then receives the configured dtype.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [issue reference](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8076+in%3Abody), [FSDP dtype](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+FSDP+dtype), [param_dtype](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+param_dtype).
- [x] Title: `[fsdp] fix: honor engine dtype for mixed precision defaults`.

No open PR addressing this fallback was found in the October 1 pre-publication check. Merged #6150 honors an explicitly configured mixed-precision dtype in autocast; it does not make `engine.dtype` the fallback. Open #8026 concerns batch-invariant kernels, #7165 concerns FP32-preserved modules, and #4275 concerns LoRA sharding groups.

### Test

Remote Linux, one RTX 4090. Base `fbb4b3a8bf636f290c9c59fc346f756849e9c241`; tested head `ba4b3f2d833dafe195ad9dc049d92a6a47b6f9df`.

```bash
uv run --frozen --all-packages --extra cpu pytest -s -x --asyncio-mode=auto \
  tests/workers/test_fsdp_engine_dtype_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_engine_forward_step_detach_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_engine_detach_tree_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_engine_return_model_output_on_cpu.py
# 31 passed; CPU dependencies from uv.lock

python -m pytest tests/workers/test_fsdp_engine_dtype.py -q
# 12 passed; torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1

pre-commit run --files \
  tests/workers/test_fsdp_engine_dtype.py \
  tests/workers/test_fsdp_engine_dtype_on_cpu.py \
  verl/workers/config/engine.py \
  verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py \
  docs/workers/model_engine.rst
# all hooks passed
```

With the new tests on unmodified main: CPU 12 failed / 8 passed; CUDA 6 failed / 6 passed. Failures are dtype mismatches. CUDA tests use native FSDP1/FSDP2 around a tiny model and exercise forward dtype, loss scaling, two backward passes, gradient clipping and a parameter update. They run at world size 1 (FSDP1 NO_SHARD), not a multi-GPU or GRPO convergence test. The CUDA environment reuses existing dependencies and is not the complete locked GPU CI image.

The CPU test filename is collected by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`; the GPU test is collected by `gpu_unit_tests.yml` without changing workflow paths or exclusions.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.dtype=float16 \
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.dtype=float16
```

An explicit `mixed_precision.param_dtype` remains authoritative, including when it differs from `dtype`. `model_dtype` continues to control model initialization.

items.title: [rollout, vllm] feat: add request hooks to vLLMHttpServer.generate
items.author: eteluna
items.summary: Adds two request hooks to, so a server subclass can change a request's sampling parameters and its output without overriding. Admission, pause/resume, and weight-sync coordination stay in.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds two request hooks to `vLLMHttpServer.generate()`, so a server subclass can change a request's sampling parameters and its output without overriding `generate()`. Admission, pause/resume, and weight-sync coordination stay in `generate()`.

This implements the hook option discussed in #7735 ([maintainer comment](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/7735#issuecomment-5884513068)). The motivating user is [verl-project/verl-genrank#4](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-genrank/pull/4), which needs per-request `logprob_token_ids` and the selected-token rows in the output. Today `generate()` keeps only the sampled token's log probability, so verl-genrank overrides the whole method and copies its admission bookkeeping (`_submission_paused`, `_resume_event`, `_admitting`). That copy is already behind main: since `e42d6af6`, the commit verl-genrank pins, `generate()` moved admission into `_park_until_admitted()` and started rejecting late arrivals.

verl-omni also overrides `generate()`. Its pinned verl (`fefb080`) predates the admission gate, so these hooks may help it keep upstream admission when it updates.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. No open PR covers this:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+7735+in%3Abody
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+vLLMHttpServer+hook
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+logprob_token_ids
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Environment: `uv sync --frozen --all-packages --extra vllm` (vllm 0.29.0, torch 2.13.0), on a machine without a GPU.

- `pytest tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_submitter_gate_on_cpu.py`: **16 passed** (12 existing, 4 new).
- With the source change reverted, the three hook tests fail and the default-behavior test passes.
- The full "Run vllm CPU unit tests" list from `vllm.yml`: 97 passed, 5 failed. The 5 failures are all in `TestCliArgsVllmParserRoundTrip` ("Failed to infer device type") and fail the same way on unmodified main, because this machine has no GPU; the CI runner has one.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: passed.
- GPU tests were not run. The change calls an empty hook before `SamplingParams` is built and passes both return values through a hook that returns them unchanged.

### API and Usage Example

```python
class SelectedTokenServer(vLLMHttpServer):
    def _preprocess_sampling_params(self, sampling_params):
        sampling_params["logprob_token_ids"] = sampling_params.pop("selected_token_ids")

    def _postprocess_output(self, output, final_res, sampling_params):
        rows = final_res.outputs[0].logprobs if final_res.outputs else []
        ids = sampling_params.logprob_token_ids
        output.extra_fields["selected_logprobs"] = [[row[t].logprob for t in ids] for row in rows]
        return output
```

The subclass is selected through `vLLMReplica.server_class`, as today.

### Design & Code Changes

Both hooks sit in the existing "Hook methods for subclass overrides" section; their defaults keep the current behavior.

- `_preprocess_sampling_params(sampling_params: dict) -> None`
  - Input: the request's sampling-parameter dict after upstream fills its defaults (`max_tokens` already removed, `logprobs` set to 0 or `None`, `detokenize` defaulted).
  - Order: before `SamplingParams` is built and before `_park_until_admitted()`.
  - Errors: an exception fails the request; it is never admitted, so the admission counter is untouched.
- `_postprocess_output(output, final_res, sampling_params) -> TokenOutput`
  - Input: the `TokenOutput` built by upstream, the engine's `RequestOutput`, and the built `SamplingParams`.
  - Order: after the engine stream ends and the admission counter is released; runs for normal outputs and for requests aborted with empty outputs. Requests rejected at the admission gate return before it.
  - Errors: an exception fails only this request.
  - Hooks should add to `extra_fields` rather than replace it: the PD prefill leg reads `kv_transfer_params` from there.
- With PD disaggregation, each leg calls `generate()` with its own copy of the sampling parameters, so the hooks run once on the prefill server (whose output is discarded) and once on the decode server.
- CI: `test_submitter_gate_on_cpu.py` imports vllm, which the `cpu` extra does not install, so `cpu_unit_tests` skips it and it was not in the vllm workflow's CPU list. This PR adds it to the "Run vllm CPU unit tests" step, which also starts running its 12 existing gate tests.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks.
- [x] Add / Update the documentation: the hooks are documented in their docstrings, as the existing hooks are; no page under `docs/` describes these hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests to the CI workflow (see above).
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.
- [x] Not related to the `recipe` submodule.

AI assistance was used for the implementation, the tests, and this description. I reviewed every changed line.

items.author: dependabot[bot]
items.summary:
Release notes

v1.14.0

Features

trl.losses is gone: DPO, KTO and GRPO stream thei…
items.body:
Bumps [trl](https://github.com/huggingface/trl) from 0.27.0 to 1.14.0.
Release notes

Sourced from trl's releases.

v1.14.0

Features

trl.losses is gone: DPO, KTO and GRPO stream their own log-probs

[!WARNING] from trl.losses import FusedLinearDPOLoss (or FusedLinearKTOLoss, FusedLinearGRPOLoss, FusedLinearJSDLoss) no longer works. The module introduced in v1.13 has been removed.

v1.13 vendored Liger's chunked_loss into trl.losses as a holding action, not a destination (#7063). The problem it was holding: those classes reimplement each trainer's loss math, so TRL carried two copies of every formula, and copies drift. That drift is where the bugs were. GRPO's grad_norm differed from the default path, KTO ignored the reference model under PEFT, KTO class weights and DPO label_smoothing were silently dropped. Worst of all, under plain DDP the fused path ran the loss on the unwrapped model, so DistributedDataParallel's reducer was never armed and gradients were never all-reduced: every rank silently kept its own.

The fix is to stop reimplementing. All DPO, KTO and GRPO need from the fused path is per-token log-probs of the selected tokens, and TRL already had _ChunkedLogProbFunction for exactly that: it streams the vocabulary with an online logsumexp and recomputes in the backward pass. Each trainer now runs backbone -> _ChunkedLogProbFunction -> its own existing loss code, unchanged. One implementation of each loss, and the memory win is kept, because full logits are still never materialized.

Thirteen restrictions existed only because the loss had been rewritten in a form that could not express those options. Most are gone: DPO with use_liger_kernel=True now accepts mixed loss types, f-divergences and precomputed reference log-probs, and GRPO gains entropy and off-policy masking. Still refused: use_weighting, compute_metrics, a PEFT adapter on lm_head, prompt-learning PEFT, and the MoE auxiliary loss.

Single H100, Qwen3-0.6B, bs=4, seq 512:

config median step peak
v1.13 fused, inline ref 0.2243 s 7.05 GB
v1.14 chunked, inline ref 0.2457 s (+9.5%) 7.05 GB
v1.14 chunked, precompute_ref_log_probs=True 0.1971 s (-12.1%) 4.83 GB (-31%)

The third row is the point: that configuration did not exist before, because the fused path rejected precomputed reference log-probs outright.

use_liger_kernel=True still works and still enables Liger's model kernels through transformers. In DPO, GRPO and KTO it now selects TRL's chunked log-probability path instead of Liger's fused loss.

  • Stream KTO log probabilities by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7075
  • Stream GRPO log probabilities by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7077
  • Move DPO to chunked log probabilities by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7243
  • Drop the fused Liger JSD path from the experimental distillation trainers by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7301
  • Skip frozen chunked log probability gradients by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7076
  • Redirect the KTO liger loss through the distributed wrapper under DDP by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7247
  • Document what use_liger_kernel actually does in each trainer by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7361

A fused Triton logprob + entropy kernel now ships in TRL

The loss head is the only hot path TRL owns: transformers already kernelizes the model internals, and nothing on the Hub covers what happens after the decoder. On one H100 (bf16, V=151936, H=4096, 8192 tokens), selective_log_softmax plus entropy_from_logits cost 12.8 ms and 2.32 GiB over [8, 1024, 151936]. A fused Triton kernel does the same in 0.89 ms, roughly 14x, and lands closer to the fp32 reference than the bf16 path it replaces. GRPO runs this two to four times per step.

It now lives in-tree at trl.kernels and is on by default on CUDA, ROCm and XPU, with the PyTorch implementation as fallback. It was briefly loaded from the Hub; that was reversed because this kernel is pure Triton and compiles at runtime, so the Hub bought nothing while costing a version gate unrelated to whether the kernel works, a download that fails offline, trust_remote_code=True for anyone with kernels installed, a silent except Exception: pass wrapped around all of it, and 13 of 13 tests skipped in CI.

  • Use fused kernels for logprobs and entropy by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7253
  • Move TRL loss kernels into TRL by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#7266
  • Ship the logprob and entropy kernel in trl instead of the Hub by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7363

Other

  • Ensure device agnostic for examples/docs/templates by @​kaixuanliu in huggingface/trl#6770
  • AsyncGRPO: PEFT/LoRA support with adapter-only vLLM sync by @​AmineDiro in huggingface/trl#7017
  • Add support for vLLM 0.29.0 by @​qgallouedec in huggingface/trl#7178
  • [GOLD] Recommend LFM2.5 and Gemma 4 students by @​kashif in huggingface/trl#6388

... (truncated)

Commits

  • cc5bb3f Agree on logged keys across ranks before flushing GRPO and RLOO metrics (#7382)
  • 5469923 Ship the logprob and entropy kernel in trl instead of the Hub (#7363)
  • 824726e Add support for vLLM 0.30.0 (#7365)

Bumps [nvidia-modelopt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer) from 0.44.0 to 0.47.0.
Release notes

Sourced from nvidia-modelopt's releases.

ModelOpt 0.47.0 Release

New Features

Quantization

  • ONNX quantization with Autotune now benchmarks placements in the requested runtime precision and retains calibrated INT8/FP8 Q/DQ only when it meets the configured TensorRT speedup threshold (1.02x by default); otherwise it saves the high-precision no-Q/DQ model.

  • Add a Muse Glimmer AutoQuantize recipe that searches language-model MLP projections, self-attention projections, and lm_head over W4A16 NVFP4 Four-Over-Six, FP8, and BF16 fallback at 5.5 effective bits while leaving the vision tower unquantized.

  • Add examples/alpamayo/qad.py, which runs quantization-aware distillation on the quantized Alpamayo checkpoint produced by examples/alpamayo/quantize.py. It distills the quantized VLM against the original FP16 VLM with QADTrainer, supports FSDP2 for multi-GPU runs, and --export reassembles the trained VLM into a full AlpamayoR1 checkpoint that AlpamayoR1.from_pretrained can reload.

  • Add a calibration-free streaming Kimi-K3 converter and checkpoint-mirror recipe for NVFP4 routed experts with input_scale=1.0 and 128x128 block-FP8 KDA/MLA attention weights. The converter operates shard-by-shard on the source checkpoint's packed MXFP4 experts instead of loading the 2.8T model through the in-memory hf_ptq.py path.

  • Add end-to-end PETRv1 and PETRv2 ONNX PTQ examples covering calibration, INT8 and FP8 VoVNet backbone quantization, TensorRT deployment, and accuracy evaluation.

  • Add opt-in FP8 Vision Encoder recipes under the qwen3_vl and qwen3_5 model types. The vision-only recipe keeps the language model and KV cache in high precision; the joint recipe quantizes Vision Encoder and language-model Linears and uses FP8 KV-cache cast. Both quantize primary and deepstack merger Linears where present, while leaving patch embedding and vision-attention BMMs in high precision. Exported checkpoints require an inference runtime that supports quantized Vision Encoder Linears.

  • Add mtq.temporarily_fold_weights for repeated frozen-weight inference and mtq.preserve_quantizer_attributes_context for restoring temporary quantizer property and type changes. Temporary folding snapshots affected fake-quant weights on a configurable device and restores them with their quantizer state; retained pre-quant scales are inactive, while shared weights, shared quantizers, and SequentialQuantizer weights are unsupported.

  • Add the nvfp4_act_headroom calibration algorithm for NVFP4 activation global scales. Instead of setting the global scale from the largest per-block amax seen during calibration (plain max, which leaves no room above it so any larger activation saturates), it anchors the scale to a low percentile of the per-block amax distribution, leaving the rest of the FP8 block-scale range as headroom: amax = max(rho * anchor, upper), where anchor and upper are the per-block amaxes at anchor_percentile (default 1) and upper_percentile (default 99.99; set to 100 to never clip calibration data), and rho (default 16384) is the headroom factor. Applies only to NVFP4 dynamic-block input quantizers; SequentialQuantizer activation quantizers raise. Weight scales are an orthogonal axis selected by a nested weight_scale_algorithm (max by default, or mse / local_hessian), so one recipe can combine a weight calibration with this activation policy in a single pass. Ships modelopt_recipes/general/ptq/nvfp4_act_headroom-kv_fp8_cast.yaml, which mirrors nvfp4_default-kv_fp8_cast with only the calibration algorithm swapped and exports a standard NVFP4 checkpoint.

  • Add PTQ support for Step-3.7 (stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash), whose routed experts were previously left unquantized. Quantize with the new huggingface/step3p7/ptq/nvfp4_experts_only-kv_fp8_cast or huggingface/step3p7/ptq/nvfp4_mlp_only-kv_fp8 recipes rather than the general ones, which select experts by module names Step does not use.

Megatron Framework (M-LM / M-Bridge)

  • Add clamp_kv_cache_scales to export_mcore_gpt_to_hf. Set it to False when exporting a QAT Megatron-Core model to preserve its learned FP8 KV-cache scales; the default retains the existing minimum scale of 1.0.
  • Add SFT-masked data support to examples/megatron_bridge/distill.py: --sft --sft_dataset_root <dir> distills on raw prompt-completion JSONL ({"input", "output"} records) with the loss masked to the response tokens, using Megatron-Bridge's FinetuningDatasetConfig and the model's own HuggingFace tokenizer instead of the pretraining GPTDataset and NullTokenizer.
  • Add per-expert weight quantization for Transformer Engine TEGroupedLinear (fused MoE experts): each expert now has its own weight_quantizer (a GroupedQuantizer holding one TensorQuantizer per expert) with an independent amax, instead of a single shared amax across all experts. Applies to mtq.quantize calibration, HF / Megatron export, and QAD.
  • Add opt-in torch.compile execution for Transformer Engine grouped-linear per-expert weight quantizers while preserving their native checkpoint amax shapes. Set MODELOPT_TEGROUPED_COMPILE_WEIGHT_LOOP=1 before quantized-module conversion; the default path remains eager.
  • Add HuggingFace unified export of quantized Qwen3-VL and Qwen3.5-VL checkpoints (PTQ or QAD) via examples/megatron_bridge/export_quantized_megatron_to_hf.py, Qwen3.5-VL additionally covering GatedDeltaNet linear-attention layers and MoE shared experts. Only the language model is quantized; the vision tower is copied from the source HuggingFace checkpoint.
  • Megatron-Bridge scripts now choose the MoE expert layout automatically from the model config: the faster fused TEGroupedMLP (grouped GEMM) unless the architecture cannot export it to HuggingFace, in which case SequentialMLP keeps the checkpoint exportable and --no_moe_grouped_gemm forces it explicitly. For the affected architectures this changes MoE activation scales from one shared scale to per-expert.

Misc

  • Add modelopt.torch.utils.mlflow.MlflowRunLogger for recording a script run on an MLflow tracking server: the invocation, the ModelOpt version, the run log (captured by teeing stdout/stderr) and any caller-supplied artifacts, with configuration as searchable params. mlflow is an optional dependency, imported only when tracking is enabled.
  • Add --mlflow <tracking-uri> to examples/hf_ptq/hf_ptq.py (MLflow's own MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is honoured too). A tracked run records the invocation, the resolved recipe ($imports expanded), the run log and the quantization summaries, with every command-line argument as a searchable param; failed runs are recorded with their traceback. The experiment defaults to $USER/hf_ptq/<checkpoint basename>-<recipe name or --qformat> and can be overridden with --mlflow_experiment / --mlflow_run_name.
  • Add --mlflow <tracking-uri> to examples/vllm_serve/vllm_serve_fakequant.py (MLflow's own MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is honoured too), so a fake-quant serve records what it quantized and an evaluation of that endpoint can be traced back to a recipe. A tracked run uploads the launcher command, the resolved RECIPE_PATH (or the merged QUANT_CFG/KV_QUANT_CFG when presets are used), the worker log and the quantizer summary; the experiment defaults to $USER/vllm_serve_fakequant/<model basename>-<recipe name or quantization config> and can be overridden with --mlflow-experiment / --mlflow-run-name.

Backward Breaking Changes

  • Migrate the FAR3D ONNX PTQ example to the shared evaluator and ModelOpt containers and quantize_vovnet.py. Only the encoder supports INT8 and FP8; decoder calibration, quantization, and related CLI flags are removed, and the decoder remains in its exported mixed FP16/FP32 precision.
  • Image-text calibration with --calib_with_images now forwards multimodal batches through the complete VLM for all VLM families, so existing non-Nemotron commands may produce different language-model activation ranges and output scales. Recipe-based VLM PTQ also targets the complete VLM: vision modules stay in high precision by default and are quantized only when a model-specific recipe enables them, so custom recipes must explicitly exclude vision modules when required.
  • Move the checkpoint-mirror recipe tier from huggingface/models/<org>/<checkpoint>/ to the top-level models/<org>/<model_id>/, keyed by each recipe's canonical Hugging Face Hub id — so the Step 3.5 Flash recipe moves to models/stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash/ptq/ and the NVIDIA Nemotron recipes gain the NVIDIA- prefix (e.g. models/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16/ptq/nvfp4-mse). Update any saved --recipe paths for these checkpoint recipes accordingly; the per-model_type recipes under huggingface/ are unchanged.
  • Move the Mistral Medium 3.5 checkpoint-mirror recipe from huggingface/models/nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4/ptq/nvfp4-max-calib to models/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B/ptq/nvfp4-max-calib, keying it by the canonical Hugging Face base model. Update any saved --recipe paths to the new location.
  • Remove the --auto_quantize_bits, --auto_quantize_method, --auto_quantize_score_size, --auto_quantize_cost_model and --auto_quantize_active_moe_expert_ratio flags from examples/hf_ptq (deprecated in 0.46). Use an AutoQuantize --recipe from modelopt_recipes/general/auto_quantize/ instead. Those recipes now also splice in the shared base cost_excluded_layers unit, which the removed CLI applied unconditionally, so a VL model keeps its vision tower and MTP layers out of the effective-bits denominator. On a VL model this changes the per-layer cost weights, so an existing --auto_quantize_checkpoint from an earlier release is rejected with "Use a different checkpoint path"; delete or repoint it to re-run the search.
  • Remove the examples/llm_ptq symlink and the examples/vlm_ptq forwarder (both deprecated in 0.46). Use examples/hf_ptq, passing --vlm for vision-language models.
  • Remove the backward-compat --qformat / --quant_cfg short names int8_sq, int8_wo, w4a8_awq, nvfp4_awq, nvfp4_mse, nvfp4_local_hessian, fp8_pb_wo and fp8_pc_pt (deprecated in 0.45). Use the preset basename under modelopt_recipes/configs/ptq/presets/model/ instead: int8_smoothquant, int8_weight_only, w4a8_awq_beta, nvfp4_awq_lite, nvfp4_w4a4_weight_mse_fp8_sweep, nvfp4_w4a4_weight_local_hessian, fp8_2d_blockwise_weight_only and fp8_per_channel_per_token. The modelopt.recipe.presets.QFORMAT_ALIASES table and the aliases argument of load_quant_cfg_choices() are removed along with them.
  • Remove the legacy layerwise bool form, its use_sequential alias, and the top-level layerwise_checkpoint_dir key from calibration algorithm configs (deprecated in 0.45). Use the nested form, e.g. layerwise: {enable: true, checkpoint_dir: /path}. A pre-0.45 modelopt_state carrying either legacy key now fails validation on restore instead of being migrated; re-save it with a 0.45/0.46 release first.
  • Remove in-trainer quantization via QuantizationArguments.quant_cfg / --quant_cfg (deprecated in 0.45); use --recipe. New recipes general/ptq/mxfp4_mlp_weight_only and general/ptq/nvfp4_mlp_weight_only replace MXFP4_MLP_WEIGHT_ONLY_CFG / NVFP4_MLP_WEIGHT_ONLY_CFG in the examples/gpt-oss QAT flow.
  • Remove the QuantizationArgumentsWithConfig alias in modelopt.torch.quantization.plugins.transformers_trainer (deprecated in 0.45). Use QuantizationArguments.
  • Transformer Engine TEGroupedLinear (fused MoE experts) now uses per-expert weight quantization (one amax per expert) instead of a single shared amax, so ModelOpt checkpoints containing quantized TEGroupedLinear modules saved before 0.47 are not compatible with 0.47. Re-run PTQ to regenerate compatible checkpoints.
  • mtq.quantize now raises when a config asks for weight quantization but none of its weight-quantizer patterns match the model, instead of calibrating and exporting a silently unquantized checkpoint ("quant_algo": null). Configs that quantize activations or the KV cache only are unaffected, as are patterns that match and are then disabled by a later entry. If this fires, use the recipe for that architecture under modelopt_recipes/huggingface/<model_type>/ or fix the module patterns. Set MODELOPT_SKIP_WEIGHT_QUANT_CHECK=1 to disable the check process-wide, e.g. for a pipeline-parallel rank whose local stage legitimately has none of the targeted modules.

Deprecations

  • Remove examples/llm_eval/lm_eval_tensorrt_llm.py (the trt-llm model) in favor of the TensorRT-LLM backend shipped by lm-evaluation-harness itself (registered as trtllm, also supports loglikelihood_rolling and pipeline parallelism); lm_eval is pinned to >=0.4.12,<0.5. Replace python lm_eval_tensorrt_llm.py --model trt-llm --model_args tokenizer=<tok>,checkpoint_dir=<ckpt> with python lm_eval_trtllm.py --model trtllm --model_args model=<ckpt>,tokenizer=<tok>, and set tensor_parallel_size and max_input_len explicitly — they default to 1 and 2048, and longer prompts are silently truncated. Use lm_eval_trtllm.py rather than the plain lm_eval CLI: it patches an off-by-one in the backend's _parse_logprobs that otherwise raises KeyError on every loglikelihood task. Loglikelihood tasks additionally require TensorRT-LLM >= 1.3.0rc11; generative tasks are unaffected. examples/hf_ptq/scripts/huggingface_example.sh gains --input (BUILD_MAX_INPUT_LEN, default 4096) to size the evaluation engine's context, and honours a preset LM_EVAL_TP to override the tensor-parallel size.
  • Bump minimum container requirement to nemo:26.08 for the Megatron-Bridge / Megatron-LM optimization features. Megatron-LM quantization still works on nemo:26.06 but will be dropped in a future release.

items.body:
Bumps [transferqueue](https://github.com/Ascend/TransferQueue) from 0.1.10 to 0.1.11.
Release notes

Sourced from transferqueue's releases.

v0.1.11

Highlight

🚀 New Features

  • SSD Offload for SimpleStorage: Add optional node-local SSD offloading to SimpleStorage to reduce long-lived host-memory pressure for workloads with large training samples. Each (field, global index) payload is placed independently according to its serialized size: samples at or above 1 MiB are stored on SSD, while smaller samples remain in host memory. The hybrid store preserves existing PUT, GET, CLEAR, overwrite, capacity, and checkpoint semantics without changing the public API. SSD files are isolated by run and storage unit and cleaned up on clear or graceful shutdown. The feature is disabled by default and can be enabled through backend.SimpleStorage.ssd_offload.enabled with the offload directory configured by backend.SimpleStorage.ssd_offload.path. In the reported two-node NVMe benchmark, SSD-backed E2E throughput remained within approximately 3.7–8.0% of the in-memory path for 1–4 MiB per-field samples. (#162)

🐛 Fixes & Improvements

  • Pooled and Reusable ZMQ Request Sockets: Replace the create-connect-send-receive-close cycle used for every RPC with reusable ZMQSocketPool instances, avoiding repeated TCP/ZMTP handshakes and bounding socket growth under concurrency. Leases are exclusive so replies cannot be consumed by the wrong request, and any socket involved in a timeout, cancellation, or other failed request is discarded rather than returned to the pool. Pools are isolated by role, event loop or thread, and peer address, preventing unsafe socket reuse across execution contexts or after peer relocation. TQ_SOCKET_POOL_SIZE controls the per-peer concurrency and idle-socket cap, with a default of 4. In the reported local 300-way concurrency test, peak sockets decreased from 300 to 4 while elapsed time decreased from 71 ms to 48 ms. (#167)

  • Resilient Storage-Unit Requests and Accept-Queue Hardening: Recover automatically when a storage-unit request is lost in transit instead of failing the entire job after a receive timeout. Timed-out GETs and idempotent PUTs are retried over a fresh connection up to TQ_SIMPLE_STORAGE_MAX_ATTEMPTS times, defaulting to 3; PUTs carrying a user data_parser are intentionally not replayed because the parser may have side effects. The storage ROUTER backlog is also increased from ZMQ's default 100 to 4096 through TQ_STORAGE_ZMQ_BACKLOG, reducing silent request loss when the TCP accept queue is saturated. New arrival counters and an optional TQ_ACCEPT_PROBE_INTERVAL kernel-level accept-queue probe improve diagnosis by distinguishing requests lost before arrival from requests that arrived but did not complete. (#171, #172)

  • Storage Proxy Peer Filtering and Worker Resilience: Prevent arbitrary TCP/ZMQ traffic from reaching and terminating the storage-unit request worker. The storage proxy now forwards only peers using recognized TransferQueue storage-manager or metrics-collector identities. Undecodable frames from an otherwise valid peer are handled inside the worker's error boundary and receive an explicit error response instead of terminating the request loop and leaving future clients blocked until timeout. (#168)

  • Explicit Concurrent-Clear Key-Miss Handling: Introduce StorageKeyNotFoundError, exported from transfer_queue, so callers can distinguish the expected race where kv_clear removes data after metadata has been resolved but before it is fetched. The error type is preserved across the ZMQ request path instead of being flattened into a generic RuntimeError, and this expected concurrent condition is logged at DEBUG rather than ERROR. Other failures, such as requesting an unknown field, continue to surface as errors. Large routing-table dumps in failure logs are also replaced with a compact storage-unit count. (#160)

  • Updated Mooncake CI Coverage and Documentation: Refresh the Mooncake version used by CI and update the project README with the latest project information. (#161, #170, #174)

  • [doc] Update README by @​0oshowero0 in Ascend/TransferQueue#170
  • [perf, fix] Pool and reuse ZMQ request sockets by @​OutstanderWang in Ascend/TransferQueue#167
  • [fix] Retry a lost storage-unit request instead of failing the job by @​adoda in Ascend/TransferQueue#171
  • [chore] Update README by @​0oshowero0 in Ascend/TransferQueue#174
  • [fix] Fix to avoid request dropping in the accept queue by @​OutstanderWang in Ascend/TransferQueue#172
  • [feat] simple storage support ssd offload by @​xupinjie in Ascend/TransferQueue#162
  • [chore] Bump version from 0.1.11.dev0 to 0.1.11 by @​0oshowero0 in Ascend/TransferQueue#177

Release notes

Sourced from vllm's releases.

v0.30.0

Highlights

This release features 762 commits from 315 contributors (104 new)!

  • New models: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (#56214, #56228, #56208) with the whole KV stored in MXFP8 through the FlashMLA V4.1 record on SM100 (#56893), DeepGEMM Mega-mHC (#56962), and async Engram prefetch with Engram DP sharding (#56512); DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (#54566), also on ROCm (#55107) and with LoRA (#55897); GLM-5.3-Flash (#53906) with EPLB (#55119); K2-Horizon (#55063); Cohere Compass (#54774); Bailing V3 VL (#55921); Nanbeige4.2 via the Transformers backend (#56071); and a DeepSeek-V4 CPU backend with AVX512/AMX sparse MLA, indexer, mHC and compressor kernels (#55355).
  • Fast Start: a persistent per-GPU weight-cache daemon holds post-quantized, TP-sharded weights in GPU memory so restarting engines map them over CUDA IPC with --load-format ipc_cache instead of reloading from disk (#54921), now covering FP4 checkpoints (#55465) and multi-node TP (#55468).
  • Watermarking: Gumbel-max watermarked generation and detection with a keyed PRF, per-request opt-out and an example detection endpoint (#54053); dual-key Gumbel-max makes it compatible with speculative decoding (#56122); the Rust frontend forwards the per-request controls (#56338).
  • HiSparse: a host-resident tier for sparse-MLA decode that spills KV pages to pinned host memory under GPU pressure and serves top-k misses from a per-request GPU hot buffer, enabled through HiSparseConnector (#53781), with Prometheus counters (#56061), a host cache shared across TP ranks (#56629), and the attention config inferred from the connector (#57041).
  • Model Runner V2: dual-batch overlap in eager mode (#50945) and with FULL CUDA graphs for microbatched steps (#51700); MTP (#46994) and EAGLE3/DFlash/DSpark (#50514) speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism; adaptive verification for every draft-model speculator through an online acceptance estimator (#52228); gc frozen during graph capture, cutting capture from 12s to 2s and engine init from 28.9s to 8.2s on H200 (#54646); --return-sampling-mask compacted on GPU, fixing an about 2x RL step-time regression (#54901).
  • Qwen3.8-Flash-Next performance: separate prefill and decode QSA indexer kernels (#54513), fused PLE kernels (#54517), FP8 indexer cache (#54890), padded-index skipping in sparse GQA (#54873), fused PLE residual and QSA output gate (#55309), UVA PLE offload and Engram tensor parallelism via --engram-config (#54371), and torch.compile removed from the NVIDIA implementation so FP8 fits on a single GB300 (#55272).
  • Kimi K3 performance: native CUDA AttnRes default on SM100 (#54261), KDA mixed-batch gather/scatter removed (5.2-7.7% E2E throughput, #56159), grouped FP8 MLA cache insertion (4-6x kernel speedup at small batch, #55356), DSV3 low-latency GEMM on strided tensors (12-81% kernel speedup, #54565), overlapped TP8 KDA projections (#54697), FlashInfer KDA kernels (#55364), internal prefix checkpoints with partial prefix caching and speculative decoding (#53614), and symmetric DCP disaggregation for hybrid Mamba models (#55531).
  • Large scale serving: PCP+DCP on sparse-MLA models (#56157), PCP with single-module MTP and replicated DSpark (#56107) and decode-only FULL CUDA graphs (#53867), Elastic EP reusing CUDA graphs across reconfiguration (#54985), an opt-in FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-reduce for NVLink-less boxes (#53576), DeepEP v2 async finalize overlapping shared experts with combine (#52781), Mooncake Store heterogeneous TP sharing (#53129), a KVCR secondary-tier adapter (#53624), and encoder-cache sharing over NIXL (#47941) and Mooncake (#41567).
  • Quantization: targeted online quantization through quantization_config.targets (#51285) and on partially pre-quantized checkpoints from any quant method (#51392), W4A16 DSA with the nvfp4_fp8_ds_mla KV cache (#51724), FlashInfer CuTeDSL NVFP4 W4A16 default over Marlin on SM100/103 (#53014), NVFP4 in the torch linear backend (#53319), per-quantization linear backend overrides (#51204), AutoRound 2/3/5/6/7-bit on CUDA (#52890), and DeepSelect top-k for the DSA sparse indexer (#56464).
  • Breaking changes: scale-out endpoints are opt-in on plain vllm serve via --enable-scale-out, replacing VLLM_ENABLE_SCALE_OUT_ENDPOINTS (#54579, #55176); GPTQ activation ordering (g_idx) removed (#54809); items deprecated for 0.29 removed, including the VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL and VLLM_MM_HASHER_ALGORITHM env vars (#55353); the all Mamba cache mode deprecated (#55041); python -m vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server deprecated in favor of vllm serve --grpc (#56746); YaRN aligned with Transformers so vendor YaRN aliases no longer re-scale max_model_len (#56446).
