items.title: [rollout] fix: make max_num_batched_tokens mutable
items.author: kahlun
items.summary: When and, it raises to: is a, which freezes every field that isn't listed in. isn't in that list, so the self-heal crashes: How to reproduce: set and leave unset.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

#7632 added a self-heal to `vLLMHttpServer._validate_configs()`. When
`enable_chunked_prefill=False` and `max_num_batched_tokens < max_model_len`, it
raises `max_num_batched_tokens` to `max_model_len`:

```python
self.config.max_num_batched_tokens = self.config.max_model_len
```

`RolloutConfig` is a `BaseConfig`, which freezes every field that isn't listed in
`_mutable_fields`. `max_num_batched_tokens` isn't in that list, so the self-heal
crashes:

```
File "verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py", in _validate_configs
    self.config.max_num_batched_tokens = self.config.max_model_len
File "verl/base_config.py", line 37, in __setattr__
dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError: Field 'max_num_batched_tokens' is frozen and cannot be modified
```

**How to reproduce:** set `rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=False` and leave
`rollout.max_model_len` unset. The model's `max_position_embeddings` then fills in
`max_model_len`, and it's bigger than the default `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`
(for example, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct: 32768). With #7632, the vLLM server dies in
`__init__`. Before #7632, vLLM rejected the config instead.

**Why CI didn't catch it:** #7632 also removed `enable_chunked_prefill=False` from
the example scripts and CI jobs. The only script that still sets it
(the torch profiler example) pins `max_model_len` explicitly, so it never hits this
branch.

## Example cli produce the bug on cuda device
```
export DATA_DIR=/root/data

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
    algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
    data.train_files=$DATA_DIR/gsm8k/train.parquet \
    data.val_files=$DATA_DIR/gsm8k/test.parquet \
    data.train_batch_size=16 \
    data.max_prompt_length=512 \
    data.max_response_length=128 \
    data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
    data.truncation=error \
    actor_rollout_ref.model.path=Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=5e-7 \
    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
    +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.attn_implementation=eager \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=8 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
    actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_torch_compile=False \
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.use_torch_compile=False \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=False \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.free_cache_engine=False \
    +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_sleep_mode=False \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.4 \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=2 \
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.param_offload=True \
    algorithm.kl_ctrl.kl_coef=0.001 \
    trainer.critic_warmup=0 \
    trainer.logger=console \
    trainer.project_name=verl_intel_gpu_grpo_e2e \
    trainer.experiment_name=qwen2_5_05b_intel_gpu_grpo \
    trainer.n_gpus_per_node=2 \
    trainer.nnodes=1 \
    trainer.save_freq=-1 \
    trainer.test_freq=-1 \
    trainer.total_epochs=1 \
    +ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_gpus=2 \
    trainer.total_training_steps=2
```

## Fix

Add `max_num_batched_tokens` to `RolloutConfig._mutable_fields`, the same way
`max_model_len` is already mutable. `max_model_len` is back-filled a few lines
earlier in the same `_validate_configs()`.

Why this fix rather than one that avoids mutation:
- `self.config` is a private copy. Each server builds it with
  `omega_conf_to_dataclass()` in `__init__` and adjusts it in
  `_validate_configs()` before anything reads it. Nothing else shares the object,
  so the stale-shared-state problem that freezing guards against doesn't apply here.
- The only other option that keeps the field frozen is to keep the adjusted value
  outside the config and pass it only to the vLLM engine args. Then
  `config.max_num_batched_tokens` would report 8192 while vLLM actually runs with
  32768, which is worse than a controlled mutation.
- `dataclasses.replace()` would run `__post_init__` again on the whole rollout
  config just to change one int.

## Diff

```diff
--- a/verl/workers/config/rollout.py
+++ b/verl/workers/config/rollout.py
@@ -145,6 +145,7 @@ class CheckpointEngineConfig(BaseConfig):
 class RolloutConfig(BaseConfig):
     _mutable_fields = {
         "max_model_len",
+        "max_num_batched_tokens",
         "load_format",
         "engine_kwargs",
         "prompt_length",
```

New file `tests/workers/config/test_rollout_config_on_cpu.py`:

```python
from verl.workers.config.rollout import RolloutConfig


def test_max_num_batched_tokens_raised_when_chunked_prefill_disabled():
    # vLLMHttpServer._validate_configs raises max_num_batched_tokens to max_model_len
    # when chunked prefill is off; that write must not hit the frozen-field guard.
    config = RolloutConfig(name="vllm", enable_chunked_prefill=False, max_num_batched_tokens=8192)
    config.max_model_len = 32768
    config.max_num_batched_tokens = config.max_model_len
    assert config.max_num_batched_tokens == 32768
```

## Test

- [x] `pytest tests/workers/config/test_rollout_config_on_cpu.py`: fails on current
      `main` with `FrozenInstanceError` and passes with this change.

### Checklist Before Submitting
- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).

items.title: [NPU] Default context parallel above 1 to KV all-gather
items.author: CalvinXKY
items.summary: Verified on Qwen3-4B, CP=2, steps 8–9, about 119s/step. selects all-gather; keeps ring attention. [Discussion: <!-- readthedocs-1185709 --> ### Documentation build overview > 📚 📁 Comparing e3eb94bec7795a9f9db7eb]
items.body:
## Summary

- NPU Ring CP (`cp_comm_type=p2p`) calls `aclnnFlashAttentionVarLenScore` and fails with error 161001 when the context-parallel size is greater than 1.
- Default that path to KV all-gather (`CP_COMM_TYPE=all_gather`). Verified on Qwen3-4B, CP=2, steps 8–9, about 119s/step.
- Accept MindSpeed `--context-parallel-algo` and `--ulysses-degree-in-cp`. `kvallgather_cp_algo` selects all-gather; `megatron_cp_algo` keeps ring attention. Ulysses group initialization and a CANN fix for the ring op are not in this change.

KV all-gather holds the full KV on every CP rank, so memory and communication are higher than Ring CP, and compute does not overlap with the all-gather.

Related to #433

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/utils/test_platform_contract.py` covers CP=1 (env unset), CP>1 default `all_gather`, and `megatron_cp_algo` → `p2p`
- [x] The new `docker/npu_patch/megatron.patch` hunk applies on top of `docker/patch/latest/megatron.patch`
- [ ] Rebuild the NPU image, because `megatron.patch` changed, then rerun a CP=2 train

items.title: [rollout] chore: upgrade vllm==0.30.0
items.author: arde171
items.summary: Upgrade the rollout engine pin to the current release: ->, and regenerate so the lock and the pin agree. This follows the same pattern as #7973, which performed the previous bump; this is the next step from 0.29.0.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Upgrade the rollout engine pin to the current release: `vllm==0.29.0` -> `vllm==0.30.0`, and regenerate `uv.lock` so the lock and the pin agree.

This follows the same pattern as #7973 (`[rollout] chore: upgrade vllm==0.29.0/sglang==0.5.20`), which performed the previous bump; this is the next step from 0.29.0.

`vllm 0.30.0`'s PyPI wheel is already a cu130 / torch-2.13 abi3 build, so no source build or wheelhouse routing is required.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here:
      https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+vllm+upgrade
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (checked by CI)
- [x] `{modules}` = `rollout`; `{type}` = `chore`; no `[BREAKING]`

### Test

`uv lock` resolves cleanly against PyPI (exit 0), with `vllm` locked at `0.30.0`.

The lock also moves `nvidia-nccl-cu13 -> 2.30.7`, `triton -> 3.8.0`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl -> 4.7.1`, `nvidia-cudnn-cu13 -> 9.24.0.43` and `quack-kernels -> 0.6.5`. This is not an unrelated refresh: regenerating with `uv lock --upgrade-package vllm` produces the same set, because `vllm 0.30.0` transitively requires those newer versions.

The GPU test jobs run on self-hosted runners that are not exposed to fork PRs (the job queues for 24h and is cancelled), so I have not been able to obtain a CI signal here. Happy to post in the `ci-request` channel, or to run any specific command you want and paste the output.

### API and Usage Example

No API change: this is a dependency pin plus the regenerated lockfile.

### Design & Code Changes

Two files:

- `pyproject.toml`: `vllm==0.29.0` -> `vllm==0.30.0`, plus the adjacent comments that name the version (the flashinfer transitive pin is `==0.6.18.post1` in 0.30; the `transformers` floor comment now refers to 0.30).
- `uv.lock`: regenerated.

I deliberately did **not** touch `setup.py` (`vllm>=0.18.0`, a floor that 0.30 already satisfies), `requirements.txt` (no vllm pin), or `manage_envs.py` (no vllm version) — none of them need changing for this bump.

I also have not ported any rollout code adaptation, because I have no evidence yet that 0.30 requires one: #7973's code changes (`vllm_rollout/weight_update_utils.py`, `models/mcore/patch.py`, `utils/vllm/utils.py`) accompanied the torch 2.11 -> 2.13 bump as well. If you tell me 0.30 needs a specific adaptation, I will add it.

- [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`

items.title: [rollout] feat: expose a server manager replica-size hook
items.author: NancyFyong
items.summary: Extract the existing footprint calculation into. Custom rollout managers can override this method rather than copy, preserving upstream initialization and metrics behavior.
items.body:
### Summary

Extract the existing footprint calculation into `LLMServerManager._get_rollout_replica_world_size()`. Custom rollout managers can override this method rather than copy `_initialize_llm_servers`, preserving upstream initialization and metrics behavior. The default TP/DP/PP and prefill/decode calculations are unchanged.

Requested during [verl-omni #656 review](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/656#discussion_r4118154957), where sequence-parallel replicas currently require a downstream lifecycle override. Replica implementations remain responsible for matching worker slicing and rank mapping to their footprint.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `replica size hook`, `rollout_world_size`, `_initialize_llm_servers`, and `LLMServerManager replica`: [search](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22replica%22+%22hook%22).

[PR #7170](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7170) is related but adds topology validation and shared functions, not an overridable manager hook. This PR adds no topology validation and changes no replica/adapter placement logic; it provides only the downstream extension point. No open PR implementing this hook was found.

### Validation

Base: `fbb4b3a8bf636f290c9c59fc346f756849e9c241`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --asyncio-mode=auto \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_replica_size_hook_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_pd_disaggregation.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_response_length_cap_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_llm_server_routed_experts_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_prometheus_rollout_targets_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_router_on_cpu.py
```

91 passed, 1 skipped. The 17 new tests fail before the extraction and pass after it. Coverage includes default and PD sizes, custom footprints, hybrid/standalone/TRT-LLM initialization, start-rank handling, config identity, launch errors and metrics.

All pre-commit hooks passed over every tracked file, including generated configs, mypy and sanity gates. Git 2.29 does not support the `ls-files --deduplicate` call used by `pre-commit --all-files`; the same file set was passed explicitly:

```python
import subprocess
files = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "-z"]).decode().strip("\0").split("\0")
subprocess.run(["pre-commit", "run", "--show-diff-on-failure", "--files", *files], check=True)
```

CPU tests only; no new GPU support or end-to-end GPU validation is claimed.

### Usage

```python
class DiffusionLLMServerManager(LLMServerManager):
    def _get_rollout_replica_world_size(self):
        return super()._get_rollout_replica_world_size() * self.rollout_config.ulysses_degree
```

This example assumes the downstream replica already uses the same SP footprint for slicing and rank mapping.

### AI assistance

Pi assisted with implementation, tests and PR preparation. The human submitter confirmed that they reviewed every changed line and ran relevant tests before publication.

items.title: [rollout] remove leftover todo ENV, remove SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE environment
items.author: kahlun
items.summary: Removes the unconditional set/ from, plus the now-unused. The unrelated vLLM-module-mocking block in the same function is left untouched.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Removes the unconditional `SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1` set/`del` from `verl/workers/rollout/replica.py::_load_sglang()`, plus the now-unused `import os`.

```diff
 import asyncio
 import logging
-import os
 from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

 def _load_sglang():
-    os.environ["SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE"] = "1"
-
     try:
         import vllm  # noqa: F401
     ...
     from verl.workers.rollout.sglang_rollout.async_sglang_server import SGLangReplica
-
-    del os.environ["SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE"]
     return SGLangReplica
```

The unrelated vLLM-module-mocking block in the same function is left untouched.

## Why?

This flag was added in #3456 (2025-09-16) as a temporary workaround and removed from the code in #3701:

```python
# NOTE: verl driver is cpu only, avoid sglang fp8 quantization import error.
# TODO: remove this once we bump to sglang>=0.5.1
```

Its own removal condition is long met — verl pins `sglang==0.5.20`. Two problems with keeping it:

1. **On CUDA it is a no-op today, but a latent hazard.** Real-CUDA detection dominates, so nothing breaks now — but setting a "CPU" flag on a GPU process relies on sglang never trusting `is_cpu()` at a site CUDA can't override. `cache_move.py` already shows one such site (XPU falls into it); a future one could catch CUDA too.

2. **It breaks the SGLang backend on XPU.** `SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1` is an opt-in "run on CPU" declaration. On an Intel XPU host (x86 CPU) it makes sglang's `is_cpu()` return `True`, which triggers an unguarded CPU-only kernel import in sglang (`cache_move.py` → `from sgl_kernel import copy_all_layer_kv_cache_cpu`) that the XPU `sgl_kernel` build does not export:
   ```
   ImportError: cannot import name 'copy_all_layer_kv_cache_cpu' from 'sgl_kernel'
   ```


Upstream sglang declined to shield callers from this flag (sgl-project/sglang#41141, closed not merged): *"For XPU or CUDA, user doesn't have to set up this flag at all."* Since verl is the caller setting it unconditionally, the fix belongs here.

## High-level design / API

No API change. Pure removal of an internal env-var manipulation.

## Test

Because the flag only affects sglang's import + engine launch inside `_load_sglang()`, testing focused there. All on `sglang==0.5.19` (verl pins 0.5.20, one patch up), single A100, tp=1, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.

**1. Import path, CUDA** — flag removed, `_load_sglang()` imports `SGLangReplica` cleanly:
- GPU visible: OK (`is_cuda=True`, `is_cpu=False`)
- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""` (CPU-only-driver, the scenario the 2025 comment guarded): OK — the original fp8 import error does **not** reproduce.

**2. Real rollout, CUDA** — drove verl's actual path (`_load_sglang()` → `launch_server_process` → real SGLang HTTP server → `/generate`), comparing flag-removed vs flag-restored, interleaved. Warm-run throughput (excluding the one cold first-run, which paid one-time CUDA-graph/autotune/cache costs — `init=41s`, `9.5k tok/s` — on whichever condition ran first):

| condition | warm engine init | warm tok/s | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| flag removed (this PR) | ~35 s | ~13.1k (13087, 13117) | identical, coherent |

items.title: Fix hydra argument-order and invalid config key breaking Ascend multinode GLM5.2 nightly CI
items.author: Copilot
items.summary: The "E2E Ascend RayJob multinode GRPO GLM5.2 Top16 Megatron" nightly job was failing before the training script even reached the RayJob worker setup, due to two bugs in the launch invocation. Hydra's argparse greedily consumes overrides as a single positional …
items.body:
The "E2E Ascend RayJob multinode GRPO GLM5.2 Top16 Megatron" nightly job was failing before the training script even reached the RayJob worker setup, due to two bugs in the launch invocation.

### Argument ordering (`unrecognized arguments`)
`--config-name` was appended via the `EXTRA` array *after* all the `key=value` hydra overrides (`DATA`, `MODEL`, `ACTOR`, `ROLLOUT`, `REF`, `TRAINER`). Hydra's argparse greedily consumes overrides as a single positional block; anything following an optional flag like `--config-name` is treated as unrecognized:
```
main_ppo.py: error: unrecognized arguments: ++ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.env_vars.VERL_VLLM_ASCEND_GLM52_PATCH='1' actor_rollout_ref.nccl_timeout=7200
```
Moved `--config-name='ppo_megatron_trainer'` to be the first argument passed to `main_ppo`, matching the convention already used in `examples/ascend_extras/grpo_trainer/run_glm5_2_megatron.sh`.

### Invalid config override
Fixing the ordering surfaced a second, previously-masked failure:
```
Could not override 'actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.vanilla_mbridge'.
Key 'vanilla_mbridge' is not in struct
```
`vanilla_mbridge` does not exist anywhere in the config schema (only `use_mbridge` is a real field on `McoreEngineConfig`). Removed the stray `actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.vanilla_mbridge=False` override.

### Change
File: `tests/special_npu/nightly_ci_ascend/run_grpo_glm52_top16_megatron_npu_multinode.sh`
```diff
 ACTOR=(
     ...
     actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_mbridge=True
-    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.vanilla_mbridge=False
     actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=False
     ...
 )

 EXTRA=(
-    --config-name='ppo_megatron_trainer'
     "++ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.env_vars.VERL_VLLM_ASCEND_GLM52_PATCH='1'"
     actor_rollout_ref.nccl_timeout=7200
 )

 python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
+    --config-name='ppo_megatron_trainer' \
     "${DATA[@]}" ...
```

items.title: [veomni, ci] fix: upgrade VeOmni APIs and migrate GPU CI to uv
items.author: Luosuu
items.summary: Update the VeOmni engine to its current public parallel-state API, restore VeOmni coverage in the SFT engine comparison suite, and migrate the VeOmni GPU PPO workflow to the shared UV environment. The old engine calls the removed API and passes an ignored keyw…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Update the VeOmni engine to its current public parallel-state API, restore VeOmni coverage in the SFT engine comparison suite, and migrate the VeOmni GPU PPO workflow to the shared UV environment. The old engine calls the removed `init_parallel_state` API and passes an ignored `enable_full_shard` keyword to model parallelization.

- Initialize parallel state directly from `AcceleratorConfig`, preserving DP/HSDP, Ulysses and EP topology, validating the derived DP size, and leaving meshes unnamed to avoid reusing the trainer's `base` entry. There is no legacy initializer fallback.
- Forward `enable_full_shard` as VeOmni's supported `enable_reshard_after_forward` option.
- Pin VeOmni CI and the `veomni-sft` UV source to commit `10a26aca258f91a7af3e698cc0db8c6c51705989`. The published 0.1.12 release predates the config-based initializer; its version number alone is insufficient.
- Re-enable the VeOmni FSDP=4 / Ulysses=2 case in `test_sft_engine_all.sh`, which is used by the SFT LLM and VLM workflows. Both jobs overlay Transformers 5.16.1 with `uv run --with`, matching the pinned VeOmni generated models while keeping the project's shared lock resolution intact. Ascend workflow installs also use Transformers 5.16.1.
- Migrate the VeOmni GPU PPO workflow from the legacy vLLM image and ad-hoc pip installs to `verl:uv.cu130` and `uv run --frozen`. Reuse the locked `vllm`, `fsdp`, `veomni-sft` and `math` extras with the Transformers 5.16.1 overlay for preprocessing, training and expert export. Add dependency-file trigger paths and retain the persistent UV cache.
- Run the PPO entrypoint, profiler checks and Ray workers with matching UV extras/overlay, including direct script launches. Quote the Hydra `py_executable` value so the `==` in the Transformers requirement parses correctly. The NPU path retains the ambient Ascend environment because the shared lock resolves CUDA dependencies.
- Launch SFT workers with `python -m torch.distributed.run`. A base-venv `torchrun` entry point otherwise uses its own interpreter and bypasses the UV Transformers overlay.
- Fix the quoted checkpoint cleanup glob in resume-disabled SFT comparison runs, clear stale artifacts before training and remove partial checkpoints on exit, including after failures.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [current initializer](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+init_parallel_state_from_config), [VeOmni PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+veomni+in%3Atitle), and `gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state open --search "veomni uv"` (no duplicate CI migration found).
- [x] Use the required PR title format.

No other open PR addressing this initialization/resharding fix was found. Related #5598 changes input preparation and attention selection; its diff does not change either the initializer or resharding keyword. #5584 adds quickstart documentation and an example script.

### Test

**80 related CPU cases passed**, including 8 new parallel-state/resharding cases:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/home/tiger/oss_dev/verl-veomni-upgrade \
  /tmp/verl-tinker-veomni-compat-env/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/workers/test_veomni_parallel_init_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_router_replay_engine_helpers_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_packed_pad_to_length_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_engine_forward_step_detach_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_engine_return_model_output_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/config/test_engine_config_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/veomni/test_router_replay_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/veomni/test_moe_param_export_on_cpu.py \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

**Actual SFT script validation passed** on a locally generated tiny Qwen2 model and synthetic multi-turn Parquet data, using the pinned VeOmni commit, Transformers 5.16.1 and Torch 2.10.0+cu129. The following calls ran `tests/special_e2e/sft/run_sft_engine.sh` with `MODEL_PATH`, `DATASET_DIR`, `VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH` and `ckpts_home` set to temporary fixtures:

```bash
BACKEND=fsdp NUM_GPUS=1 SP_SIZE=1 FSDP_SIZE=1 FSDP_STRATEGY=fsdp \
  bash tests/special_e2e/sft/run_sft_engine.sh
BACKEND=veomni NUM_GPUS=8 SP_SIZE=2 FSDP_SIZE=4 FSDP_STRATEGY=fsdp2 \
  bash tests/special_e2e/sft/run_sft_engine.sh
```

Both completed two training steps, validation and checkpoint saving, with dynamic batching and gradient checkpointing enabled. The existing `compare_sft_engine_results.compare_results` assertions passed:

| First-step metric | Single-GPU FSDP baseline | Eight-GPU VeOmni (FSDP=4, Ulysses=2) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loss | 2.7822391987 | 2.7822391987 |
| Gradient norm | 6.6204566956 | 6.6241192818 |

Additional validation:

- A two-GPU actual SFT trainer run passed with Ulysses=2, including validation and checkpoint saving.
- Two-GPU Qwen2 forward/backward/optimizer smoke tests passed for both resharding values.
- A real UV overlay probe started from an environment containing Transformers 5.12.1 and launched two workers through `uv run --active --no-sync --with transformers==5.16.1 bash -c 'python -m torch.distributed.run ...'`. Both workers imported Transformers 5.16.1 and the current VeOmni initializer.
- `uv lock --upgrade-package veomni`, `uv lock --check` and frozen SFT dependency export passed; only VeOmni's source changed in the lockfile.
- `uv export --frozen --extra vllm --extra fsdp --extra veomni-sft --extra math` and the same combo with `uv sync --frozen --dry-run` passed. The exported environment contains the pinned VeOmni git commit, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM 0.29.0, FlashAttention and CuPy.
- A local launch-capture check passed for default GPU, UV opt-out, NPU autodetection and trainer failure (exit 23). It checks workflow/launcher/Ray prefix agreement, Hydra parsing, argument preservation and failure propagation.
- Two actual Ray actors started through `uv run --active --no-sync --with transformers==5.16.1` imported Transformers 5.16.1 and the current VeOmni API. This reused the existing local Torch 2.10 CUDA environment; it does not validate full locked PPO training. The workflow package diagnostic also reported the overlay version correctly.
- Changed workflow YAML files parse successfully. SFT shell syntax checks and all applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- Checkpoint cleanup was verified on success and failure, including stale/partial files, paths with spaces, unchanged files outside the checkpoint directory, and preserved training exit status.

The local GPU fixtures do not establish validation on the full upstream Torch 2.13/CUDA 13 stack, real GSM8K/VLM datasets, or Ascend hardware. The full upstream workflows must validate those configurations.

### API and Usage Example

Existing verl configuration fields are unchanged. VeOmni environments must use the pinned current git revision and Transformers 5.16.1. Older VeOmni initializer APIs are not supported.

- [x] Add CPU regression coverage for parallel topology, validation and resharding.
- [ ] Human review of every changed line and independent execution of relevant tests.
- [ ] Full upstream CI validation.

**AI assistance:** OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests and this description. This remains a draft for human review; human review and independent test execution are pending before marking it ready.

items.title: [rollout, vllm] fix: drop tied-embedding alias in fp8 weight sync
items.author: cr-gao
items.summary: The quantized (fp8) branch of the async weight sync feeds every bucket straight into. For a model with the trainer state dict carries both and its alias, and the two can land in different buckets.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

The quantized (fp8) branch of the async weight sync feeds every bucket straight into `load_quanted_weights`. For a model with `tie_word_embeddings=True` the trainer state dict carries both `model.embed_tokens.weight` and its alias `lm_head.weight`, and the two can land in different buckets. vLLM 0.29 checks skipped aliases per `load_weights` call, so a bucket that carries only the alias fails the check and the first sync aborts:

```
ValueError: 'lm_head.weight' was skipped because it is tied to 'model.embed_tokens.weight' in Qwen3ForCausalLM, but 'model.embed_tokens.weight' was not found in the checkpoint, so the tied weight is uninitialized.
```

The standard (non-quantized) branch already filters the alias through `drop_tied_alias_updates` (#7973); the fp8 branch was left out. This PR applies the same filter there, including the MTP drafter call, and adds a CPU regression test.

Reproduced with Qwen3-0.6B, `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization=fp8`, vLLM 0.29.0: the first weight sync failed before the fix and a 3-step GRPO run completed after it.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+tied+embedding+fp8 and https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+drop_tied_alias_updates (only #7973, which covers the standard branch)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

```
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py -q
# 28 passed (vLLM 0.29.0); the new test fails on main and passes with the fix
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py`: pass `param_updates` through `drop_tied_alias_updates` before `load_quanted_weights` (main model and drafter).
- `tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py`: `test_quantized_sync_drops_tied_alias_updates`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; every changed line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the submitter.

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).

### What does this PR do?

The FP8 end-to-end section of `docs/low_precision/fp8.md` lists `NVTE_FP8_BLOCK_SCALING_FP32_SCALES=1` as a general requirement. It only applies on Hopper.

On Blackwell (SM100+), Transformer Engine has no native block-scaled GEMM. It runs the block-wise recipe through MXFP8 GEMMs, whose E8M0 scales hold only an exponent. So both of its block-quantize kernels assert power-of-two scales on SM100+, and a run with the variable set stops at the first FP8 quantization:

```
transformer_engine/common/transpose/quantize_transpose_vector_blockwise.cu:534 in function quantize_transpose_vector_blockwise:
Assertion failed: pow2_scale. On Blackwell and newer, the FP8 block scaling recipe is emulated with MXFP8, which requires using power of two scaling factors.
```

This is the failure reported in #6172 (8×B200) when following this doc and the verl-recipe FP8 E2E script. This PR marks the variable as Hopper-only and says that on Blackwell it must stay unset; power-of-two scales are the Transformer Engine default. Docs only.

Refs #6172. This does not fix #6172: that issue also reports garbled FP8 rollouts on Blackwell once the variable is removed, and this PR does not address that.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs:
  - [NVTE_FP8_BLOCK_SCALING_FP32_SCALES](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=NVTE_FP8_BLOCK_SCALING_FP32_SCALES)
  - [blockwise Blackwell](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=blockwise+Blackwell)
  - No PR changes this requirement. Related: #6172 (the issue above); #7895 (sets the variable in its DeepSeek-V4 example scripts, does not touch this doc); #7519 (MXFP8 training, does not change this line).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

Documentation-only change.

- `pre-commit run --files docs/low_precision/fp8.md`: all hooks pass, including "Check docs Last updated info".
- Reproduced on 1×B200 (SM 10.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Transformer Engine 2.16.1). `te.Linear` (2048→2048) and `te.GroupedLinear` (4 × 2048→768) ran forward and backward under `Float8BlockScaling(fp8_format=Format.E4M3)` and were compared with a bf16 run of the same module:

| `NVTE_FP8_BLOCK_SCALING_FP32_SCALES` | `te.Linear` out / dgrad / wgrad rel. err | `te.GroupedLinear` out / dgrad / wgrad rel. err |
|---|---|---|
| unset (power-of-two scales) | 0.0377 / 0.0423 / 0.0462 | 0.0376 / 0.0475 / 0.0510 |
| `1` | `RuntimeError`: the `pow2_scale` assertion above | same |

The same modules under `MXFP8BlockScaling` give the same errors as the unset row, with or without the variable.

Source references (Transformer Engine 2.16.1, commit c9877beb):
- `transformer_engine/common/transpose/quantize_transpose_vector_blockwise.cu:533-536` and `transformer_engine/common/transpose/quantize_transpose_square_blockwise.cu:490-493`: `if (sm_arch() >= 100) NVTE_CHECK(pow2_scale, ...)`.
- `transformer_engine/pytorch/csrc/extensions/gemm.cpp:289-300`: "Emulate the FP8 block scaling recipe with MXFP8 on Blackwell and newer as it is not natively supported by cublasLt".
- `transformer_engine/common/swizzle/swizzle_block_scaling.cu:116-118, 205-206`: each FP32 block scale becomes an E8M0 scale by keeping only its exponent byte, `(sf >> 23) & 0xFF`. This is why the scales must be powers of two.

### API and Usage Example

None.

### Design & Code Changes

`docs/low_precision/fp8.md`:
- The requirement line now says that the variable is Hopper-only, why it fails on Blackwell, and what to do there.
- "Last updated" is bumped.

The verl-recipe script `low_precision/run_dapo_qwen3_moe_30b_megatron_fp8e2e.sh` also exports the variable unconditionally. That lives in the recipe repository and can get a matching note separately.

items.title: [trainer, megatron, fsdp] fix: forward-KL topk distillation shape mismatch with pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max
items.author: alwaysyiyu
items.summary: When (introduced in #6901), the student forward pads every micro-batch to the mini-batch's global max seqlen via, but still splits the teacher top-k tensors with without passing. With heterogeneous sequence lengths the teacher is padded to the per-micro-batc…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True` (introduced in #6901), the student forward pads every
micro-batch to the mini-batch's global max seqlen via `forced_max_seqlen`, but
`compute_forward_kl_topk` still splits the teacher top-k tensors with `preprocess_bshd_engine`
**without** passing `forced_max_seqlen`. With heterogeneous sequence lengths the teacher is
padded to the per-micro-batch max instead, so the two shapes diverge and the assertion

```
teacher_topk_log_probs_cp_split.shape[:2] == teacher_topk_ids_cp_split.shape[:2] == student_logits.shape[:2]
```

fails.

This threads the micro-batch's `forced_max_seqlen` (already stored as non-tensor data by the
engine) through `compute_topk_loss` into the BSHD teacher split. It picks up the earlier closed
attempt #7012 (which recomputed the value as `student_logits.shape[1] * cp_size`) and instead uses
the authoritative `forced_max_seqlen` recorded by the engine, matching the student path exactly.

Related: #6901 (introduced the padding), #7012 (prior closed attempt).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+forced_max_seqlen
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `[trainer, megatron, fsdp] fix: forward-KL topk distillation shape mismatch with pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`

### Test

Validated on an Ascend NPU cluster running on-policy distillation (OPD) with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE,
TP=2 CP=2, `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`, and heterogeneous prompt/response lengths. Before the
fix the step aborts with the shape-mismatch assertion above; after the fix the step completes and
`student_logits.shape[:2] == teacher_split.shape[:2]` holds. The THD path and
`pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=False` are unaffected (no `forced_max_seqlen` is stored).

### API and Usage Example

No user-facing API/config change. `compute_forward_kl_topk` gains a backward-compatible
`forced_max_seqlen: int | None = None` parameter (internal), and `compute_topk_loss` reads
`forced_max_seqlen` from the micro-batch's non-tensor data. Callers need no change:

```python
compute_forward_kl_topk(
    student_logits,
    teacher_topk_log_probs,
    teacher_topk_ids,
    config,
    data_format,
    forced_max_seqlen=tu.get_non_tensor_data(data, key="forced_max_seqlen", default=None),
)
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/distillation/losses.py`: read `forced_max_seqlen` from the micro batch and forward it to the distillation loss fn.
- `verl/trainer/distillation/megatron/losses.py`: accept `forced_max_seqlen` and pass it to both `preprocess_bshd_engine` calls in the BSHD branch (THD branch untouched).
- `verl/trainer/distillation/fsdp/losses.py`: accept the parameter for signature parity (unused; FSDP2 does not use `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`).

### What does this PR do?

The MoE weight-loader workaround skips DeepSeekMTP because it is not registered as a supported model. Its predictor also stores layers in a ModuleDict and nests each decoder under mtp_block, so the existing traversal cannot reach its expert parameters.

items.title: Form fully-async batches like molt and add the FlashREINFORCE recipe
items.author: mzopedia
items.summary: FlashREINFORCE's results depend on molt's asynchronous trainer as much as on the loss: how many rollouts are in flight, when finished rollouts become a batch, and how an epoch ends. This PR adds three things: - molt's batch formation for fully-async rollout, a…
items.body:
> **Depends on #2428 and #2429.** This branch contains their commits; the change under review here is the last commit (fe0d6427). It will be rebased once they are merged.

## Summary

FlashREINFORCE's results depend on molt's asynchronous trainer as much as on the loss: how many rollouts are in flight, when finished rollouts become a batch, and how an epoch ends. This PR adds three things:

- molt's batch formation for fully-async rollout, as an opt-in worker;
- the training-side changes that batch formation needs;
- an example that reproduces molt's quick-start recipe.

### Scheduling (opt-in: `--fully-async-pool-size N` selects `PooledRolloutWorker`)

- **Pool:** holds N rollout groups, counting the ones still generating and the finished ones not yet in a batch.
- **Refill:** one prompt per group taken, and only while a batch is being formed; between batches nothing is dispatched.
- **Collection order:** finished groups are taken in a random order fixed at dispatch. molt collects them with `ray.wait`, which returns an arbitrary ready one.
- **`--fully-async-max-queued-batches`** (default 1): how many batches may be formed ahead of training. The trainer frees a slot when it takes a batch, before training on it.
- **Aborts and evaluation:** a group aborted by a weight update is resent at once and keeps its place in the pool, because SGLang holds the request until the engines continue. Batch formation pauses during evaluation.
- **`--fully-async-drain-each-epoch`:** stops refilling once every prompt of the epoch is dispatched, and ends the epoch with a smaller batch. This matches molt's episodes: 1,460 prompts = 11 × 128 + 52.
- **Metrics:** `rollout/fully_async/{queued_batches,pool_finished,epoch_tail,failed_rollouts}`.
- **Transport:** not supported with `--rollout-data-transport straw`, which is rejected at validation.

### Training side

- **Smaller steps:** `BatchBuilder.split_by_dp` trains a rollout with fewer groups than `--global-batch-size` as one smaller step, such as the epoch tail. Such a rollout previously failed the `num_rollouts >= global_batch_size` assertion in `build_dp_schedule`.
- **LR schedule:** the scheduler now advances `--global-batch-size` per update, so a smaller step still counts as one scheduler iteration. Existing configurations are unchanged: every step already had exactly `global_batch_size` groups, so `step_global_batch_size` always equalled it.
- **`--apply-wd-to-all-params`:** removes Megatron's weight-decay exemption for biases and 1-D parameters, giving torch AdamW semantics as in molt.

### `examples/flash_reinforce`

It reproduces molt's quick-start recipe on one 8-GPU node (1 trainer GPU and 7 SGLang engines):

- DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on `sail/Sanity-Test-R1D-1.5B` (1,460 math prompts);
- 12,000 updates of 128 rollouts with 8k-token responses;
- evaluation on AIME 2024/2025 avg@32.

`math_grader.py` is molt's grader (Apache-2.0), vendored with lint-only changes. `KEEP_CHECKPOINTS` prunes old checkpoints. The README lists the metrics to watch and the remaining differences from molt.

## Tests

- `tests/test_fully_async_rollout.py`:
  - the pool refills only while a batch is being formed;
  - finished groups are taken in dispatch-key order;
  - an epoch drains into a smaller last batch, and a tail smaller than the data-parallel size is dropped;
  - an aborted rollout resumes in place, and a failed rollout is dropped and refilled;
  - the dynamic filter applies;
  - batch formation pauses during evaluation;
  - the rollout function takes a formed batch.
- `tests/test_flash_reinforce.py`:
  - parsing of the new options (`--fully-async-*`, `--apply-wd-to-all-params`) and their validation;
  - a rollout smaller than one step is trained as one step.
- `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py`: defaults for the new options in the validation helper.
- `tests/test_qwen2.5_0.5B_flash_reinforce.py` (new, 4 GPUs, added to the e2e matrix): Qwen2.5-0.5B on 20 GSM8K prompts with the full FlashREINFORCE configuration and molt-style batch formation (pool 12, 2 queued batches, epoch drain, weight decay on all parameters). It evaluates before training and while trajectories are in flight, and checks that per-sample rollout data are aligned, weight versions are non-decreasing and gradients are finite.

## Validation

On one node with 8x A100-80GB, in the `slimerl/slime:nightly-dev-20260923a-cu129` image:

- **CPU unit tests:** every file of the `cpu-unittest` matrix (73) passes, run as `python tests/<file>`. As in CI, the straw-marked files use the current `straw-queue` from PyPI.
- **Lint and CI config:** `pre-commit run --all-files` passes, and `pr-test.yml` matches `generate_github_workflows.py`.
- **`test_qwen2.5_0.5B_flash_reinforce.py`** (4 GPUs): passed.

**Recipe run.** The first 1,024 of the recipe's 12,000 updates, with the full schedule (the LR schedule spans 12,000 updates). It ran on this branch before the rebase onto #2426; the only difference under `slime/` is that PR's `QueueDataSource` refactor and staleness definition.

| after update | AIME 2024 avg@32 | AIME 2025 avg@32 | mean | truncated at 8k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.228 | 0.213 | 0.220 | 72% |
| 256 | 0.238 | 0.200 | 0.219 | 70% |
| 512 | 0.252 | 0.213 | 0.232 | 58% |
| 768 | 0.280 | 0.233 | 0.257 | 55% |
| 1,024 | 0.296 | 0.238 | 0.267 | 50% |

Throughout the run:

- `train/ppo_kl` was exactly 0.
- No sequence left the trust region (`tis_seq_reject_frac` = 0), and `tis_binary_kl` was about 1.6e-4, some 30x below δ.
- The gradient norm was about 0.05.
- Samples were about 10 updates stale, and 17–29% of them were generated by more than one weight version.

items.title: [fsdp] feat: make FSDP2 CPU offload pin_memory configurable
items.author: Longwt123
items.summary: Default is, so no existing behavior changes. The naming and the rationale mirror the existing knob, which documents the same "pinning competes with everything else that pins on the node" problem.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`FSDPEngine` hardcodes `CPUOffloadPolicy(pin_memory=True)` whenever FSDP2 CPU offload is active — both for the training engine (`offload_policy=True`) and for the reference engine (`forward_only=True`). The offloaded params/grads are therefore always kept in **pinned host memory**.

Pinned host memory is allocated by the accelerator host allocator (on Ascend: `aclrtMallocHostWithCfg`) and is **not** accounted by the container memory cgroup, nor visible as process RSS / `VmPin`. A large pinned working set can therefore fail to allocate on a busy node even though the container memory limit was never reached, and the failure is a hard error rather than a graceful retry.

This PR adds `FSDPEngineConfig.offload_pin_memory` (default `True`, i.e. exactly the current behavior) and passes it to `CPUOffloadPolicy`, so a memory-constrained node can opt into pageable host memory at the cost of a slower H2D on the offload/onload path.

It also removes the same failure mode from the FSDP-Turbo nightly case (`run_grpo_qwen3_5_2b_fsdp_turbo_npu.sh`). That path builds its offload policy inside the external FSDPTurbo package, which already exposes `FSDPPlanConfig.pin_memory`; the case now sets `turbo_config.distributed.fsdp_plan.pin_memory=false`, so offload stays enabled and only the host memory becomes pageable.

### Motivation / field evidence

Reproduced on an Ascend A3 nightly job (`nightlyCI_grpo_qwen3_5_2b_fsdp_turbo_vllm_ascend`), driver `26.0.rc3`:

```
torch.OutOfMemoryError: allocate_host_memory_slowpath ... CachingHostAllocator.cpp:252
NPU function error: aclrtMallocHostWithCfg, error code is 207001
  -> Memory_Allocation_Failure(EL0004)
  -> rtsMallocHost execution failed, reason=driver error: out of memory
```

Key observations from the node while the job failed:

- The container cgroup was nowhere near its limit (`memory.current` ≈ 1 GiB vs a 800 GiB limit, `memory.failcnt` = 0), and inside the container `VmPin` was `0 kB` — the pinned pages are not charged to the cgroup.
- `MemAvailable` on the node was still ≈ 1.9 TiB; the allocation failed once clean `MemFree` dropped to ~160–200 GiB, because the synchronous host-pinned allocation does not wait for reclaimable page cache.
- The torch-side pin site for this code path is `torch/distributed/fsdp/_fully_shard/_fsdp_param.py`, which calls `padded_sharded_param.pin_memory()` from `_init_sharded_param` (see the traceback below). Whether that pinning happens is decided by the `CPUOffloadPolicy.pin_memory` flag of the policy handed to `fully_shard`.

The failing frames, for reference:

```
.../torch/distributed/fsdp/_fully_shard/_fully_shard.py:226 in fully_shard
    state._fsdp_param_group = FSDPParamGroup(
.../torch/distributed/fsdp/_fully_shard/_fsdp_param_group.py:141 in __init__
    FSDPParam(
.../torch/distributed/fsdp/_fully_shard/_fsdp_param.py:397 in _init_sharded_param
    padded_sharded_param = padded_sharded_param.pin_memory()
```

So on a busy node the only way to make the offload path robust is to be able to stop pinning.

### Why this is not a duplicate

Checked open PRs before submitting (`gh pr list --state open --search "pin_memory"`, `"CPUOffloadPolicy"`, `"offload_policy"`):

- **#7182** (`[fsdp] fix: make ref model CPUOffload configurable instead of hardcoded`) touches the same three files, but with a different axis: it lets users turn the ref model's offload **on/off** (performance motivation — avoid CPU↔GPU transfers when the ref model fits on device). This PR keeps offload enabled and makes the **host memory backing of that offload** selectable (reliability motivation — avoid an unaccounted pinned allocation that can fail on a loaded node). The two are orthogonal and can coexist: with both merged, `ref.fsdp_config.{param_offload, offload_pin_memory}` independently control whether ref params are offloaded and how they are stored on the host.
- **#7342** (`fix(megatron): fall back to non-pinned CPU copy when pin_memory() fails on resume`) and **#7881** hit the same class of problem in the **Megatron** backend (`verl/utils/megatron_utils.py`). This PR deliberately does **not** touch Megatron; the FSDP2 `CPUOffloadPolicy` path is a separate code path.
- **#7804** is about offloading optimizer states around each update; unrelated.

### Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `verl/workers/config/engine.py` | `FSDPEngineConfig.offload_pin_memory: bool = True` + docstring |
| `verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py` | `CPUOffloadPolicy(pin_memory=True)` → `CPUOffloadPolicy(pin_memory=self.engine_config.offload_pin_memory)` |
| `verl/trainer/config/engine/fsdp.yaml` | document/export the new key |
| `verl/trainer/config/_generated_ppo_trainer.yaml` | regenerated (actor / ref / critic blocks) |
| `tests/workers/config/test_engine_config_on_cpu.py` | assert the default |
| `tests/special_npu/nightly_ci_ascend/run_grpo_qwen3_5_2b_fsdp_turbo_npu.sh` | set `turbo_config.distributed.fsdp_plan.pin_memory=false` for actor and ref |

Default is `True`, so no existing behavior changes. The naming and the rationale mirror the existing `BaseEngine.delta_pin_snapshots` knob, which documents the same "pinning competes with everything else that pins on the node" problem.

Usage:

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  actor:
    fsdp_config:
      offload_policy: true
      offload_pin_memory: false   # pageable host memory instead of pinned
  ref:
    fsdp_config:
      offload_pin_memory: false
```

### The two FSDP CPU-offload paths

The same failure has two entry points; both are pinning by default and both are left configurable after this PR:

| Path | Where the policy is built | Knob |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy=fsdp2` | `verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py` | new `FSDPEngineConfig.offload_pin_memory`. Before this PR the flag was hardcoded to `True`, so there was no way to opt out. |
| `strategy=fsdp_turbo` | inside the external FSDPTurbo package (`FSDPTurbo(...)` → `fully_shard(...)`), driven by `FSDPPlanConfig.cpu_offload` / `FSDPPlanConfig.pin_memory` | already existing `turbo_config.distributed.fsdp_plan.pin_memory`; the nightly case in this PR uses it, so no upstream change is needed for that path. |

The sibling FSDP2 nightly case (`run_grpo_qwen3_5_2b_fsdp2_npu.sh`) also runs with `offload_policy=True`, so it can switch to pageable with `offload_pin_memory=False` if it ever hits the same allocation failure.

### Tests

Run locally:

```bash
python -c "import yaml;yaml.safe_load(open('verl/trainer/config/engine/fsdp.yaml'));yaml.safe_load(open('verl/trainer/config/_generated_ppo_trainer.yaml'))"   # OK
python -m py_compile verl/workers/config/engine.py verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py tests/workers/config/test_engine_config_on_cpu.py   # OK
```

`tests/workers/config/test_engine_config_on_cpu.py` covers the new default; it needs a full torch/hydra environment, so I did not execute it in this environment — CI will run it.

Field evidence was collected on Ascend A3 (8×NPU, driver 26.0.rc3): the pinned host allocation failure reproduces reliably while `pin_memory=True` is hardcoded — a reproducer that grows pinned allocations until `aclrtMallocHostWithCfg` returns 207001 fails exactly the same way — and pinned allocations were measured to be invisible to the container cgroup (`memory.current`, `memory.failcnt` and `VmPin` all stay flat). With `offload_pin_memory=True` the FSDP2 code path is byte-for-byte the previous one, so this change cannot regress existing setups; pageable offload trades a slower H2D on the offload/onload path for an allocation that is charged to the cgroup and can be reclaimed.

The nightly script change is a Hydra override of an existing FSDPTurbo config key; it is exercised by the `nightlyCI_grpo_qwen3_5_2b_fsdp_turbo_vllm_ascend` job itself.

### Verification trigger

`nightly_ascend.yml` is schedule-only, so the FSDP-Turbo case could only ever be exercised by the 19:00 UTC cron run of `main` — a change to the case itself could not be validated before merging. This PR adds a path-filtered `pull_request` trigger and lets only the turbo job opt in; the other seven jobs keep their `github.event.schedule` guard, so a pull request runs exactly one job instead of the whole nightly matrix.

This overlaps with #8055, which adds the same trigger for a wider set of paths; whichever lands first, the other should drop its copy.

The intended verification for the changes above is that job: it runs on this PR's own merge commit, so it exercises `pin_memory=false` (FSDP-Turbo path) and the new `offload_pin_memory` default (fsdp2 path) end to end.

### AI assistance

AI assistance (Trae AI) was used to draft this change and the description. The analysis of the failure, the choice of `CPUOffloadPolicy.pin_memory` as the fix point, and the reproduction on the Ascend node were reviewed by the submitting human, who takes responsibility for the change.

items.title: Add FlashREINFORCE: batch-mean advantage and binary-KL trust region
items.author: mzopedia
items.summary: (NVIDIA molt) is critic-free RL with one rollout per prompt, built for asynchronous rollout. It is not a new loss but a combination of four pieces. [Discussion: @zhuzilin Could you help to review this MR?]
items.body:
## Summary

[FlashREINFORCE](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/labs-molt/pull/116) (NVIDIA molt) is critic-free RL with one rollout per prompt, built for asynchronous rollout. It is not a new loss but a combination of four pieces. slime already had two of them; this PR adds the other two.

| Piece | slime |
|---|---|
| Advantage: reward minus the mean reward of the whole rollout batch; no prompt groups, no std normalization, no whitening | **new**: `--advantage-estimator flash_reinforce` |
| REINFORCE gradient with the training forward reused as the old log-probs (PPO ratio exactly 1) | existing: `--num-steps-per-rollout 1`; the objective now defaults to `--pg-loss-type reinforce` for this estimator |
| Sequence-level trust region: every token carries its unclipped importance weight `pi_train / pi_rollout`; a sequence whose mean sampled-token binary KL exceeds δ gets no policy gradient | **new**: `--use-tis --custom-tis-function-path slime.backends.megatron_utils.loss.binary_kl_trust_region_function --tis-binary-kl-threshold 5e-3` |
| Loss: token mean within each sequence, then mean over the sequences of the step | existing default (no `--calculate-per-token-loss`) |

### `flash_reinforce` estimator

`BatchBuilder` subtracts the mean reward of the whole rollout batch, before the data-parallel split, so no collective is needed. `compute_advantages_and_returns` broadcasts the centered reward to every response token, like GRPO. `--disable-rewards-normalization` and `--custom-reward-post-process-path` behave as for the other estimators.

### `binary_kl_trust_region_function`

It plugs into the existing `--custom-tis-function-path` hook and follows molt's `PolicyLoss`:

- The log-ratio is bounded to ±30 before exponentiating, and `p = pi_rollout(y_t)`, `q = pi_train(y_t)` are clamped to `[1e-6, 1 - 1e-6]` for `KL(Bernoulli(p) || Bernoulli(q))`.
- The per-sequence mean runs over loss-mask tokens only. With context parallelism, the per-sequence sums are all-reduced over the CP group; every CP rank joins, including one that holds no token of the micro-batch.
- A rejected sequence keeps its loss mask: its policy-gradient term is zeroed, but it stays in the denominator, and its entropy and KL terms and metrics are unaffected. Non-finite statistics are rejected with finite weights.
- The loss is reweighted only with `--use-tis`, since the hook also runs for `--get-mismatch-metrics`.
- Metrics: `train/tis`, `train/tis_abs`, `train/tis_binary_kl`, `train/tis_seq_reject_frac`.

`--tis-binary-kl-threshold inf` disables the gate: an importance-weighted policy gradient without a trust region, which is molt's ablation.

The FlashREINFORCE section of the usage guide (en/zh) documents the full combination and the options it must not be combined with.

## Behavior changes

None for existing configurations. The new flag is read only by the new callback. Validation rejects a non-positive or NaN threshold, and the default is 5e-3.

## Tests

`tests/test_flash_reinforce.py` (new, added to the CPU unit-test matrix):

- **Centering:** the whole batch is centered without std; prompt groups are ignored; a single-outcome batch gets zero advantages; `--disable-rewards-normalization` and custom post-processing are respected; other estimators are unchanged; the centered reward is broadcast to every token.
- **Arguments:** CLI parsing and validation.
- **Trust region, with cases ported from molt:**
  - a single far-off token rejects the whole sequence, and the gate is two-sided;
  - a close sequence keeps its unclipped weight, and δ = inf disables the gate;
  - masked tokens stay out of the mean, and a sequence without loss tokens is kept;
  - non-finite log-probs are rejected with finite weights;
  - only the offending sequence is rejected;
  - mismatch metrics alone leave the loss untouched.
- **`policy_loss_function`:** gradients match a dense reference, with exactly zero gradient for rejected sequences, and entropy and `ppo_kl` are unaffected by rejection.
- **Context parallelism:** a 2-rank gloo test covers the zigzag and all-gather layouts with and without loss recompute, including a rank that owns no token.

`tests/test_score_centering.py` covers the new default objective. The validation helper in `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` gains the new argument's default.

## Validation

On one node with 8x A100-80GB, in the `slimerl/slime:nightly-dev-20260923a-cu129` image:

- **CPU unit tests:** every file of the `cpu-unittest` matrix (72) passes, run as `python tests/<file>`. As in CI, the straw-marked files use the current `straw-queue` from PyPI.
- **Lint and CI config:** `pre-commit run --all-files` passes, and `pr-test.yml` matches `generate_github_workflows.py`.
- **`test_qwen2.5_0.5B_score_centering.py`** (2 GPUs, top-p 1.0 and 0.95): passed. It exercises the changed default-objective selection.

The end-to-end FlashREINFORCE smoke test and the recipe run depend on the scheduling options of the follow-up PR, so they are reported there.

items.title: Support evaluation in fully-async rollout and harden trajectory continuation
items.author: mzopedia
items.summary: Fully-async rollout already continues in-flight trajectories across weight updates: a weight update pauses the engines, the aborted sample keeps its partial response and rollout log-probs, and resends prompt plus partial response with the remaining token budge…
items.body:
## Summary

Fully-async rollout already continues in-flight trajectories across weight updates: a weight update pauses the engines, the aborted sample keeps its partial response and rollout log-probs, and `generate` resends prompt plus partial response with the remaining token budget. This PR fixes the gaps around that path and lets fully-async rollout evaluate.

- **Evaluation under `generate_rollout_fully_async`** (previously a `ValueError`). It runs on the rollout worker's event loop, next to the in-flight trajectories. `GenerateState`'s semaphore and pacer are bound to that loop, so evaluating through `sglang_rollout.generate_rollout` on a second loop (the workaround via `--eval-function-path`) races with them. Distributed fully-async (`--rollout-data-transport straw`) still rejects evaluation.
- **Group reward models no longer score an incomplete group.** Fully-async requeues a group with an `ABORTED` member and resumes it after the weight update, so `--group-rm` scored such a group twice, first with partial responses.
- **Resumed multimodal samples keep their partial response.** `generate` and `generate_streaming` sent the text prompt for every multimodal sample, dropping what had already been generated. A resumed sample now resends the processor-expanded prompt ids plus the partial response, as multi-turn VLM rollouts already do. Fresh requests are unchanged.
- **`rollout/staleness/multi_version_frac`**: the fraction of samples whose tokens come from more than one weight version, which makes continuation visible.
- **wandb 0.30 compatibility**: `wandb.util.generate_id` was removed, so `init_wandb` crashed whenever the run name gets a random suffix (the default). The suffix is now generated with `secrets` in the same style.

`examples/fully_async/README.md` documents how trajectories continue across weight updates, and how to correct the off-policy tokens (`--use-tis`) or mask them (`--partial-rollout --mask-offpolicy-in-partial-rollout`).

## Behavior changes

- `generate_rollout_fully_async(..., evaluation=True)` evaluates instead of raising (object-store transport).
- The other changes only touch groups with aborted members, resumed multimodal samples and the new metric.

## Tests

- `tests/test_fully_async_rollout.py`:
  - an aborted sample is requeued and continues from its partial response (input ids, remaining `max_new_tokens`, aligned log-probs and loss mask, `weight_versions == ["1", "2"]`, reward computed once);
  - only the aborted member of a group is regenerated;
  - an exhausted budget truncates the sample without a request;
  - the group reward model waits until aborted members finish;
  - a resumed multimodal sample resends its partial response;
  - evaluation runs on the worker's event loop;
  - `multi_version_frac`.
- `tests/test_streaming_rollout.py`: multimodal resume in `generate_streaming`.
- `tests/test_wandb_utils.py` (new, added to the CPU unit-test matrix).

## Validation

On one node with 8x A100-80GB, in the `slimerl/slime:nightly-dev-20260923a-cu129` image:

- **CPU unit tests:** every file of the `cpu-unittest` matrix (72) passes, run as `python tests/<file>`. As in CI, the straw-marked files use the current `straw-queue` from PyPI.
- **Lint and CI config:** `pre-commit run --all-files` passes, and `pr-test.yml` matches `generate_github_workflows.py`.
- **`test_qwen2.5_0.5B_fully_async_short.py`** (4 GPUs, straw transport as in CI): passed.
- **Object-store variant with evaluation:** the same test on the default object-store transport, with 4 rollouts and AIME evaluation every 2 rollouts, passed. It exercises `AsyncRolloutWorker` and evaluation while hundreds of requests are in flight; the upstream test now uses straw, which bypasses that worker.

Multimodal resume is covered by the unit tests only; it was not exercised with a VLM on GPUs.

items.title: [ckpt, trainer, megatron] fix: finalize async checkpoints in RL trainers
items.author: ewan0x79
items.summary: This is a follow-up to #8003 and the. That PR drives Megatron async checkpoint finalization from SFT, but the PPO/GRPO trainers do not advance or drain the queue.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

This is a follow-up to #8003 and the [RL checkpoint gap identified in its
discussion](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8003#issuecomment-5861613027).
That PR drives Megatron async checkpoint finalization from SFT, but the
PPO/GRPO trainers do not advance or drain the queue. An RL save can therefore
return with its completion callback still pending: the resume tracker may not
be published, and the final save may remain unfinished when training exits.

This PR drives finalization at aligned RL training boundaries, drains the
previous save before starting another, and blocks on the final save before
normal exit. Once actor/critic writes and auxiliary state complete, the driver
publishes one shared resume tracker. It also defers old-checkpoint retention
until after tracker publication, preserving the checkpoint selected for resume
while the next save is pending.

This PR is stacked on #8003. Until that PR merges, the diff against
`main` also includes its SFT commit.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for related work: [open Megatron async checkpoint
  PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+Megatron+async+checkpoint+RL)
  and [PRs mentioning #8000](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8000+in%3Abody).
  #8003 covers SFT queue progress; this change covers the RL trainer path it
  does not drive.
- [x] The proposed title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` and
  passes `tests/special_sanity/check_pr_title.py`.

### Test

Focused CPU tests:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/trainer/ppo/test_async_checkpoint_on_cpu.py \
  tests/trainer/ppo/test_async_checkpoint_retention_on_cpu.py
```

Result: 25 passed. The full repository check also passed all 14 hooks:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always
```

It left the worktree clean.

This local subset covers actor/critic completion, deferred tracker publication,
draining before another save, and retention while a new save is pending.
Trainer-entrypoint cases for normal-exit draining are also included in
`tests/trainer/ppo/test_async_checkpoint_integration_on_cpu.py`. The additional
three-step `max_actor_ckpt_to_keep=1` case is in
`tests/trainer/ppo/test_async_checkpoint_retention_on_cpu.py`. Both files match
the existing `cpu_unit_tests` workflow's `*_on_cpu.py` pattern.

For GPU validation, these RL changes were adapted back to verl 0.8. A
three-step Megatron RL run completed; a separate run resumed from its step-3
sharded checkpoint and completed step 4. A fresh-output, three-step run with
`max_actor_ckpt_to_keep=1` also completed: the tracker selected step 3, the
older actor checkpoint directories were pruned, and the step-3 sharded actor
checkpoint remained.

### API and Usage Example

No new user-facing configuration fields are added. With the existing
`checkpoint.async_save=true` setting, RL trainers now complete pending saves
before exit and publish the shared resume tracker only after completion.

### Design & Code Changes

- Forward `finalize_async_checkpointing` through the RL worker/engine path and
  progress it from the PPO/Ray and separation trainers at aligned step
  boundaries, before another save, and at normal exit.
- Coordinate actor/critic completion and auxiliary state on the driver, then
  atomically publish the shared `latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt` tracker.
- Defer role-local retention during a coordinated save. Apply the configured
  limits after publication, with cleanup retryable if it is interrupted.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the PR template.
- [x] Run the prescribed repository-wide pre-commit command: all 14 hooks
  passed, with no file changes.
- [x] Update documentation: `docs/advance/checkpoint.rst` describes the
  coordinated save and deferred retention behavior.
- [x] Add CPU regression tests selected by the existing `cpu_unit_tests`
  workflow. The workflow result is not yet available.
- [ ] Request CI in `ci-request` when the PR is ready for review.
- [x] The `recipe` submodule is not part of this change.

AI assistance was used for this change.

items.title: [megatron] fix: remove inherited MTP layers from reference pipeline parallelism layouts
items.author: lxb007981
items.summary: With an MTP-enabled actor, the reference model inherits its custom pipeline layout, for example: The reference model only computes next-token log probabilities and does not need MTP layers. However, its inherited layout still contains MTP entries, causing a la…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

With an MTP-enabled actor, the reference model inherits its custom pipeline layout, for example:

```
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.pipeline_model_parallel_layout="Et*10|t*12|t*8|t*8|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*4mL"
```

The reference model only computes next-token log probabilities and does not need MTP layers. However, its inherited layout still contains MTP entries, causing a layer-count mismatch during initialization.

Parse the inherited layout in check_mtp_config() and remove MTP entries for the reference model, preserving decoder placement, stage order, and empty stages.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: ...
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Use NVIDIA Megatron-Bridge for model construction and HF weight conversion. Remove the vanilla_mbridge selector, legacy adapter, checkpoint options, and dependency entries; retain the use_mbridge engine setting.  

### Checklist Before Starting

- [ ] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: ...
- [ ] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.

items.title: feat: add LMCache example for KV cache reuse across SGLang restarts
items.author: DongDongJu
items.summary: slime already forwards SGLang's LMCache options, but does not provide an example demonstrating external KV reuse across an engine restart or scoping it to a frozen model. Add a small LMCache MP example using the existing per-model SGLang configuration.
items.body:
slime already forwards SGLang's LMCache options, but does not provide an example demonstrating external KV reuse across an engine restart or scoping it to a frozen model. 
Add a small LMCache MP example using the existing per-model SGLang configuration.

**The intended RL use case is retaining reusable prefixes when a frozen teacher or reference-generation engine restarts without changing its checkpoint.** LMCache stays running while SGLang is relaunched with the same weights and compatible cache layout. 
This can avoid repeated prefill for retained prefixes; it does not restore agent state or establish a training-throughput improvement.

The example explicitly sets `update_weights: false` and enables LMCache only on the reference engine, leaving it disabled on the trainable actor. 
This boundary matters because clearing SGLang's local cache does not establish that its standalone LMCache store has been invalidated after a weight update. 
The README explains checkpoint isolation, version compatibility, and the need for a custom rollout to actually query the frozen model.

A dependency-free smoke script sends requests through `/generate`. Its cold phase requires zero cached tokens. 
After a manual engine restart, its warm phase requires host-cache reuse and zero device-cache hits, so an ordinary local radix-cache hit cannot satisfy the check. 
The manual GPU check lives with the example; the config regression test extends the existing CPU test file.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/utils/test_sglang_config.py -q -p no:cacheprovider --maxfail=1`: **26 passed**, with SGLang 0.5.15.post1 available on the Python path.
- Verified both example models' settings reach `_compute_server_args`: actor LMCache disabled, frozen reference LMCache enabled, and the YAML config path preserved.
- Ruff 0.14.7, Black 24.3.0, isort 5.13.2, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Actual standalone SGLang stop/relaunch with the LMCache process kept alive: cold request **0/2561** cached tokens; first request after restart **2560/2561**, with `device=0` and `host=2560`. LMCache logged retrieval of those 2560 tokens.
- Negative check: repeating the warm phase without another restart failed as expected on the local radix-cache hit.

GPU environment: Qwen3-0.6B BF16, SGLang 0.5.20 at `94602c9`, LMCache 0.5.5, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12, and one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU. The standalone GPU check used disabled CUDA graphs and Triton attention.

The standalone test used a separate, newer SGLang runtime; it does **not** validate launching SGLang 0.5.20 through slime. Configuration tests used slime's Docker-targeted SGLang 0.5.15.post1. A complete multi-model RL run, numerical parity, weight-update invalidation, and throughput gains remain unvalidated.

items.body:
Collect owned LM-head inputs during the existing target forward, with immutable head snapshots and atomic versioned manifests. Original sample/group/rollout identities and causal token/mask positions survive packing; missing rollout provenance stays unknown. Collection is disabled by default.

**Review this feature:** [incremental diff](https://github.com/0z5a/vime/compare/a5b3e0b17f0f406fb9912f1953fb5b9f8447bb64...76ad2be4a1fa2a90fbe3ff4a8ce08f64f1ec4020) (**18 files, +1,157/-13**). Prerequisite: maintenance #460 at `a5b3e0b1`. Target: `0z5a-branch` at `3e569314` (merged #459); head `76ad2be4`. The Files changed tab includes maintenance. #452 is absorbed; old fork review #6 is superseded. Original history is preserved without force-push.

Supported: micro-batch 1, TP=PP=CP=DP=1, no VPP/MTP/MoE, bias-free head, one actor update per publication. Unsupported/skipped target forwards fail before collection. Selected tensors own their storage; a round owns one immutable head. Token/batch/tensor-byte budgets are checked before copying. Empty rounds publish no batch; failure removes only newly owned files. The per-round budget is not an RSS or retention cap.

| Actual validation on the current production tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Contract/collector/metadata/arguments/shared CPU regressions | **217 passed, 0 skipped** |
| A100 full-parameter BF16 Ouro: real generation → target forward → optimizer → full publication | **6 rounds passed**; 1,434,650,624 trainable parameters; nonzero gradients each round |
| Physical serving/target equality | **PASS**: all 269 tensors after every publication and before every generation |
| Reloaded selected-token logits from features + same-version head | **PASS**: max/mean error **0.0/0.0**, repeat noise 0; 16 selected tokens in each of 7 rounds |
| Separate-process restore + seventh real update | **PASS**: model/Adam steps/RNG/cursor restored; generation version 7; fresh artifact namespace |
| Underlying native 3 vs 2 + fresh-process 1 | **PASS**: all 1,074 model/Adam/RNG checkpoint chunks and scheduler exactly equal |
| Maintenance prerequisite vs feature-off; feature-off vs on | **PASS for all 3 pairs**: six complete 1,074-chunk state comparisons, identical real-rollout replay, loss and gradient results |
| Ordinary Qwen actor path | **PENDING**: zero native optimizer updates. Aligned NCCL short check passed; six-round native collector and fresh restore remain queued |
| Maintenance CPU CI follow-up | **PASS locally**: Python 3.11 plugin/agent/utils stages, all 33 upstream-sync CPU files; stale Ouro loader list fixed |
| Formatting / diff checks | **PASS** |
| [CI #1405](https://buildkite.com/vllm/vime-ci/builds/1405) | **PASS automated checks**; GitHub success; Buildkite reports passed and blocked, so manual stages remain unexecuted; no manual rerun |

Ouro: pinned `ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B@574fa66c`, one A100-SXM4-40GB, TP=PP=CP=DP=1, existing Python 3.12.3 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / Ray 2.58.0. No dependency or driver updates. Private checks compare actual serving tensors and reload exported files; extra audit work is excluded from speed runs. The first extended-horizon resume failed; the standard `--use-checkpoint-opt-param-scheduler` option preserved saved scheduler state and the next run passed. Original failed evidence is retained outside Git.

Each row measures one full fixed-replay training/publication step from the same pinned checkpoint. Model initialization and the final checkpoint write are excluded. Collector export is included; extra logit-reconstruction matmuls are excluded. These are collector costs, not online generation throughput. Torch allocated-memory peaks are captured at optimizer completion.

| Pair | Order | Off step (s) | On step (s) | Off/on ratio | On overhead | Response tokens | Export MiB | On train GPU peak GiB |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | off → on | 26.074 | 27.634 | 0.944× | +5.98% | 256 | 192.06 | 32.83 |
