items.title: fix(agent): abort timed-out SGLang requests via router workers
items.author: Arlo-mt
items.summary: When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources. The existing cleanup logic sends: This request returns HTTP 404 and the excepti…
items.body:
## Background

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

## Problem

`sglang_url` points to the SGLang router address, but the router does not expose or forward the `/abort_request` endpoint.

The existing cleanup logic sends:

```text
POST <router>/abort_request
```

This request returns HTTP 404 and the exception is silently ignored. As a result, the original request may continue decoding on the worker even though the client has already timed out. The retry request can then be routed to another DP worker, causing the old request and the retry request to run concurrently.

This leads to:

- Orphaned SGLang requests occupying KV-cache resources
- Duplicate computation after retries
- Multiple DP workers decoding requests from the same logical agent turn
- Longer tail latency and possible additional timeout failures

## Solution

This change adds a small helper, `_abort_sglang_request`, in `slime/agent/adapters/common.py`.

When a request is cancelled or times out:

1. Query the router's `/workers` endpoint.
2. Extract the backend worker URLs.
3. Send `/abort_request` with the original request `rid` to every worker concurrently.
4. Keep the abort request scoped to the specific `rid`; `abort_all` is never used.

Only the worker that owns the request will actually abort it. Requests with other IDs are not affected.

## Scope

- Modify only `slime/agent/adapters/common.py`
- No new dependencies
- No SGLang router changes
- No public API changes
- Preserve support for the current router-based SGLang deployment

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile slime/agent/adapters/common.py`
- `git diff --check`
- Manual async test with a fake router and two fake workers
- Verified that the same `rid` is sent to all backend workers

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix multimodal prompt building for rows without media
items.author: natedemoss
items.summary: I was poking at with a dataset that mixes image rows and plain text rows, and ended up finding three separate problems in. When the media column is nothing goes into that set, the pattern collapses to, and that matches the empty string at every position: One…
items.body:
I was poking at `--multimodal-keys` with a dataset that mixes image rows and plain
text rows, and ended up finding three separate problems in `_build_messages`.

### The prompt gets shattered when a row has no media

The placeholder split builds a regex alternation out of whatever media the row
actually carries. When the media column is `None` nothing goes into that set, the
pattern collapses to `"()"`, and that matches the empty string at every position:

```python
>>> from vime.utils.data import _build_messages
>>> _build_messages({"text": "Describe this image.", "images": None},
...                 "text", True, {"image": "images"})
[{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'D'},
                              {'type': 'text', 'text': 'e'},
                              {'type': 'text', 'text': 's'}, ...]}]
```

One content dict per character. These rows definitely reach here — `filter_long_prompt`
already has an explicit text-only branch for exactly this shape of dataset.

I want to be upfront that this is the least severe of the three. I checked
Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL and GLM-4.1V, and all three render the shattered content to
byte-identical text, so it's wasted work and a fragile representation rather than
corrupted training data. Still worth not doing.

### A typo in `--multimodal-keys` silently drops every image

`MultimodalTypes.get()` returns `None` for a name it doesn't know, and the old code
just skipped those. So `'{"images": "images"}'` — plural, which is an easy thing to
type given the column is usually called `images` — quietly attaches no media at all
and you train text-only against a VLM dataset with nothing in the logs to tell you.

This one I'd call the real bug. I made it raise, and listed the supported types in the
`--multimodal-keys` help text since they weren't written down anywhere.

This is the only behaviour change in the PR that could break a currently-working run,
so shout if you'd rather it stayed a warning.

### Rows already in list-of-dicts form abort the dataset load

If a message's content is already a list, the code deliberately passes it through
("no processing will be done"). But the leftover-media check afterwards doesn't know
that happened, so the row's media has no placeholder to be spent on and the whole
`Dataset` construction dies:

```
message['content'] is a list of dicts, no processing will be done.
AssertionError: Multimodal data count mismatch: 1 more image(s)than '<image>' placeholders in prompt
```

Now it only runs the check when placeholder expansion actually happened. (Also put the
missing space back in that message.)

### Tests

`tests/test_build_messages.py`, wired into the *synchronized upstream CPU tests* job
next to `test_filter_long_prompt.py`. Nine cases: three fail on `main`, the other six
pin the substitution behaviour that should not move.

One asymmetry I left alone and pinned instead: `images: None` leaves the content as a
plain string, `images: []` gives a single text dict. Collapsing `[]` into the no-media
path would be tidier but you'd lose the `Not enough image data` assert when a prompt
has `<image>` and an empty column, which seemed like the more useful behaviour to keep.

### Verification

CPU jobs all pass locally (~740 tests across *plugin contracts*, *upstream sync CPU*,
*utils* and *agent adapter*). `pre-commit` clean.

Two things I couldn't run on my machine, neither touched by this change: the GPU
suites, and `test_glm5_indexer_q_norm` / `test_rollout_metrics` /
`test_rollout_routing_replay_validation`, which need megatron and vllm from the
`vllm/vime:latest` image.

`test_cispo_loss` and `test_policy_loss` fail for me on clean `main` too — Windows box
with no C++ toolchain, so `torch.compile` can't get through `pick_vec_isa`. Unrelated.

---

AI-assisted, per CONTRIBUTING: the diff and tests were written by Claude Opus 5
(Anthropic, via Claude Code) working from my direction, and it's attributed in the
commit trailer. I've reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.
discussion:
I found one remaining mixed-message case at `9574840e4479d328b536fa80b982dec7626a6b90`: the inline-content pass-through works by itself, but adding a plain-text system or assistant turn makes it fail again.

```python
from vime.utils.data import _build_messages

row = {
    "text": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are helpful."},
        {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "image", "image": "a.png"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe it."},
        ]},
    ],
    "images": ["a.png"],
}
_build_messages(row, "text", True, {"image": "images"})
```

This raises `AssertionError: Multimodal data count mismatch: 1 more image(s) than '<image>' placeholders in prompt`. Removing the system message passes. Adding a plain-string assistant turn after the inline user message also fails.

`expanded_any` becomes true for *any* string content, even if that string has no media placeholder, so the unrelated text turn re-enables the leftover check for inline media. This looks like an incomplete edge of the PR's stated pass-through fix, not a claim that this PR introduced the original mismatch bug.

Could the regression coverage include these mixed conversations and define how inline media relates to the row media column? Simply counting only matched placeholders would also need to preserve the existing all-string missing-placeholder validation.

Verified through the real `vime.utils.data` import on this head, Python 3.12.3 / CPU: three focused cases yielded **1 pass / 2 failures**. No import stubs, downloads, GPU training or full-suite claim. This review/reproducer was AI-assisted. I'm leaving implementation with this PR rather than opening a duplicate.

items.body: ## Overview Adds training/inference support for the GLM-4.7-Flash model on Ascend 910B NPU. GLM-4.7-Flash uses DeepSeek-V3-style Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) plus a GLM-style MoE (64 routed experts + 1 shared expert, sigmoid router with expert bias), and supports Multi-Token Prediction (MTP). This PR registers the corresponding megatron bridge, adds the model-argument and run scripts, and fixes an MTP drafter compatibility issue under NPU cudagraph capture. ## Changes ### New bridge plugin - **`vime_plugins/megatron_bridge/glm4moe_lite.py`**: Adds the megatron bridge for `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM`. It subclasses `GLM45Bridge` to reuse its MTP plumbing (`num_nextn_predict_layers` mapping loop, fused-expert handling, etc.) and only overrides `provider_bridge` and `mapping_registry` for the MLA model. MindSpeed TE module types are registered via the public `AutoMapping.register_module_type` API through `_register_mindspeed_te_module_types()`, so weight loading works on NPU without manually patching the container's `param_mapping.py`. Non-MLA branches that are always dead code for this model (`is_mla` / `is_mla_mapping` are always true) have been removed, along with the now-unused `QKVMapping` / `GPTModelProvider` imports. - **`vime_plugins/megatron_bridge/__init__.py`**: Imports and registers the new bridge. ### MTP cudagraph compatibility fix - **`docker/npu_patch/vllm.patch`**: Adds a static patch to vLLM's upstream Glm4MoeLiteMultiTokenPredictorLayer.forward that rewrites the bool-mask index assignment (inputs_embeds[positions == 0] = 0) into the equivalent element-wise torch.where. The original form routes to aclnnNonzeroV2 (a data-dependent-shape op), which fails with stream is captured under NPU cudagraph capture. After the rewrite, the MTP drafter runs under cudagraph on Ascend. The patch is applied at image build time (reconciled at runtime via series.conf), so no runtime hook or env gate is needed. The change is scoped to the GLM MTP class and is a no-op for non-GLM models. ### Run scripts - **`scripts/models/glm4.7-30B-A3B-npu.sh`**: Model argument definitions for GLM-4.7-Flash 30B-A3B (MoE config, MLA q/kv lora rank, qk/v head dim, etc.). - **`scripts/run-glm4.7-30B-A3B-npu.sh`**: NPU training entry script (GRPO, 16 cards on a single node); enables MTP training and vLLM MTP speculative decoding, and sets `VIME_PATCH_GLM_MTP_GRAPH=1`. ## Usage ```bash bash scripts/run-glm4.7-30B-A3B-npu.sh ``` Weight and data paths can be overridden via the `DATA_ROOT` environment variable. ## Testing - GLM-4.7-Flash GRPO training runs through on a single NPU node with 16 cards; weight loading is normal and the reward keeps trending upward. - Whether to enable MTP or not

items.title: docs(examples): fix outdated fan-out and reward semantics in coding_agent_rl README
items.author: JasonFooAGI
items.summary: Docs-only: four lines in, all in the trajectory fan-out / reward description.
items.body:
## What

Docs-only: four lines in `examples/coding_agent_rl/README.md`, all in the trajectory fan-out / reward description.

- Correct the stale "one `Sample` per chain" claim (two places: the adapters bullet and Fan-out Semantics).
- Replace the outdated "reward is split as `reward / K`" with the actual credit path — full reward per Sample, shared `rollout_id` so the loss reducer counts the trajectory once — and restructure Fan-out Semantics as sources → credit → consequence, dropping the now-dangling `K`.
- Add a previously-undocumented note: with fan-out, GRPO reward normalization falls back from per-prompt groups to a batch-wide baseline.

## Why the text had gone stale

- **"one Sample per chain"** — written in the original example PR (#1923); stale since **#2005** (turn-node `TrajectoryManager` refactor), which introduced the `SampleBuilder` drift classification (CLEAN / REALIGN / FORK) and the rewrite-merge, so one chain can yield multiple Samples.
- **"reward is split as `reward / K`"** — accurate when written (#1923: split in `generate.py`'s `_merge_samples`; #2005 kept it as `reward / len(samples)` inside `get_trajectory`); stale since **#2161**, which switched to assigning the full reward to every Sample. (The `rollout_id` half of that sentence was and still is correct.)
- The GRPO note is an addition, not a stale fix — the batch-wide fallback in `_post_process_rewards` was never documented.

Kept the diff minimal; happy to follow up on the rest.

## Testing

Docs-only. Every rewritten statement was checked against the code it describes:
`slime/agent/trajectory.py` (drift classification, rewrite-merge, full-reward assignment, shared `rollout_id`), `slime/ray/rollout.py` (`rollout_mask_sums` per-rollout reducer, `_post_process_rewards` normalization fallback), `examples/coding_agent_rl/swe.py` (1.0/0.0 graders), and `tests/test_agent/test_trajectory_manager_branching.py` (full reward asserted in 2.8/2.9).

items.title: fix(agent): keep agent turns trainable under reasoning_content echo divergence
items.author: JasonFooAGI
items.summary: Over the past half year, preserving reasoning across turns has moved from opt-in to default — and in coding/agent scenarios, to a hard contract. GLM-5's SFT explicitly trains coding agents with preserved thinking blocks; Z.ai enables preserved thinking by …
items.body:
## What

Coding agents disagree on how they echo `reasoning_content` back in later prompts — some echo it verbatim (e.g. Claude Code), some drop it (e.g. [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) through 0.1.0-rc.7 passed it back only on tool-call turns). When the echo diverges from the assistant message the trajectory manager recorded, history matching (dict equality) fails and generated turns silently stop training: short turns are rewrite-merged into routing-only context, long turns fork the trajectory. This PR adds two opt-in env switches covering the two common echo behaviors. Both default to off; the default path's merge/fork decisions and samples are unchanged.

## Motivation

Over the past half year, preserving reasoning across turns has moved from opt-in to default — and in coding/agent scenarios, to a hard contract. GLM-5's SFT explicitly trains coding agents with preserved thinking blocks ([GLM-5 report](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.15763v2)); Z.ai enables preserved thinking by default on its coding endpoint and requires `reasoning_content` to be returned complete and unmodified ([docs](https://docs.z.ai/guides/capabilities/thinking-mode)); Kimi's code and flagship models keep it always-on and likewise require historical `reasoning_content` to be kept as-is ([docs](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-thinking-models)); Anthropic's API hard-requires tool-use turns' thinking blocks (with signatures) to be echoed verbatim; and Qwen3.8's chat template renders prior-turn `reasoning_content` **by default** ([chat_template.jinja](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/chat_template.jinja): `preserve_thinking is undefined or preserve_thinking is true`), whereas Qwen3.5's strips it with no preserve option ([chat_template.jinja](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/blob/851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a/chat_template.jinja)). Both templates read only the `reasoning_content` field — so what the client echoes is exactly what gets rendered. The motivations vendors cite — reasoning continuity, prefix/KV-cache reuse, not re-deriving reasoning per turn — all assume the field survives the client round trip intact. Training should therefore treat reasoning-carrying trajectories as first-class, not as mismatches — and since the deployment-side client's echo behavior is not under our control, the training distribution should also cover the drop case instead of silently demoting those turns.

## Root cause

Two failure modes, one per echo behavior:

1. **Echoing client + OpenAI adapter.** `_build_reply_parts` (slime/agent/adapters/openai.py:211) records a `manager_message` that always omits `reasoning_content` (to match stripping clients). Any turn whose echo carries `reasoning_content` therefore fails to history-match the recorded turn and falls into the rewrite-merge/fork path. (The Anthropic adapter always keeps it and is unaffected.)

2. **Dropping client + a manager message that keeps `reasoning_content`** (Anthropic always; OpenAI with the new switch). The recorded turn carries `reasoning_content`; the replayed echo drops it → dict mismatch → `_try_merge_assistant_rewrite` (slime/agent/trajectory.py:370) rewrite-merges any short generated leaf (response < `fork_threshold`, default 1024), irreversibly destroying its `TurnRecord` and demoting the turn to routing-only context. Cascading across a multi-turn trajectory, only the last turn stays trainable and the trajectory reward concentrates on it.

## Changes

- **`SLIME_AGENT_OPENAI_MANAGER_REASONING`** (default `off`): the OpenAI adapter's recorded `manager_message` keeps `reasoning_content`, so echoing clients history-match again.
- **`SLIME_AGENT_REASONING_FORK_POLICY=reasoning_dropped`** (default `off`): when a replayed echo dropped the recorded `reasoning_content`, the turn forks instead of rewrite-merging, keeping it trainable — regardless of response length and of whether other fields also changed. Only *drops* are carved out: a *rewritten* reasoning falls back to the existing threshold merge/fork logic (a rewritten reasoning is treated as not worth training). The policy is snapshotted once at `TrajectoryManager` construction; unknown values warn and disable. Fork decisions are now tagged in node metadata (`{"fork": {"reason": "reasoning" | "threshold", ...}}`) for attribution.
- Unchanged paths: with both switches off, merge/fork decisions and the resulting samples are identical to before — the only addition is the attribution metadata on tree nodes; the threshold merge logic and the token-level drift classification (`classify_token_drift`, slime/agent/trajectory.py:169) are untouched.
- Docs (en/zh `get_started/agent.md`) and CI registration for the new test file.

## Alternatives considered

- **Train on the server-recorded history instead of the client's echoed history.** Not adopted: it trades the problem for train/serve distribution shift — at serving time the agent rewrites history (in particular dropping old reasoning), and the model would face prompt shapes it was never trained on.

- **Normalize `reasoning_content` before comparing the recorded and echoed messages.** Not adopted: in practice clients either echo verbatim or drop the field; a rewritten reasoning is aberrant, and the existing threshold merge/fork fallback already leaves such turns untrained — the outcome we prefer.

- **Auto-detect whether the client echoes reasoning.** Not adopted: whether to record `reasoning_content` must be decided when the turn is recorded, before the client's next request reveals its echo behavior — detection always lags a turn and can never cover the first. There is also no stable per-client rule to detect: echo behavior varies across turns and releases, invalidating any one-time result.

- **Relax the history-match (dict equality) check — e.g. ignore `reasoning_content` when comparing.** Not adopted: blinding the comparison does not remove the divergence, it pushes it down to token alignment, where the REALIGN fallback silently un-trains earlier turns without attribution and stitches turns with inconsistent views of history into one contradictory sample. The policy instead keeps equality strict as the canary and classifies the mismatch after it fires, rather than hardcoding per-client assumptions about which differences are harmless.

## Testing

CPU unit tests (`NUM_GPUS = 0`, registered in `pr-test.yml`):

```
python -m pytest tests/test_agent/test_trajectory_reasoning_echo.py tests/test_agent/test_adapters.py
# test_trajectory_reasoning_echo.py: 30 passed (new file)
# test_adapters.py: 22 passed, 1 skipped (7 new tests)
```

- New file `tests/test_agent/test_trajectory_reasoning_echo.py`: echo-mode × policy × response-length matrix; rewritten reasoning falls back to the threshold path; policy fork at the threshold boundary; non-reasoning rewrites still merge; already-demoted or child-bearing nodes fork structurally without policy metadata; empty `response_message` defense; env parsing (default off; unknown value warns + disables); policy snapshot at construction; Anthropic multi-turn e2e with a stripping client.
- `tests/test_agent/test_adapters.py`: manager message omits/keeps `reasoning_content` per switch; turns without reasoning are unaffected by the switch; OpenAI multi-turn e2e with an echoing client under both switch states.

End-to-end rollout validation on a single H20 96GB node (rollout only, no training; the PR branch plus read-only instrumentation counters): a 2×2×2×2 matrix over {history rendering: Qwen3.5-style template (strips prior-turn thinking) vs preserve-thinking rendering (Qwen3.8 default)}, {switches off/on}, {fork_threshold 1024/50}, {two coding agents: Claude Code CLI (Anthropic adapter) and [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 0.1.1-rc.2 (OpenAI adapter, full passback)}, against Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 served by SGLang, on a real multi-turn tool-use task suite (sessions run 7–23 turns depending on the harness), temperature 1.0. All 16 conditions completed — and every run returned the same reward, so task success is uninformative here; the differences live entirely in the trajectory data. The matrix was run twice: absolute numbers fluctuate (~±50%, dominated by trajectory-length variance) while every directional conclusion below reproduced. Two extra cells split the switch factor on the deepseek/t38/th1024 configuration: {manager=on, policy=off} and {manager=off, policy=on}.

These are small-scale, single-node, single-task-family runs; we report the mechanism-level outcomes they establish, and they should not be read as representative of large-scale training distributions.

- **Bug reproduced**: with switches off at the default threshold, the full-echo harness's replayed turns mismatched the reasoning-stripped manager message on essentially every turn, and short turns were rewrite-merged into routing-only context — 19 of 20 turns demoted, trainable tokens collapsing to a few hundred per session while task reward stayed identical.
- **Root-cause fix**: with the manager switch on, the mismatch disappears — one compact sample per trajectory, zero merges or forks, the best total-to-trainable token ratio in the matrix (~5:1).
- **Switch split** (direct evidence for the usage guidance): {manager=on, policy=off} is equivalent to both-on (single clean sample, zero merges/forks) — a fully-echoing client needs only the manager switch. {manager=off, policy=on} collapses the same way as both-off, with zero policy forks — the policy cannot engage when the recorded turn carries no `reasoning_content`, so enabling it alone is a false sense of safety.
- **Precise scoping, no false positives**: non-reasoning rewrites (the CLI normalizing a tool call's arguments) still follow the pre-existing threshold logic — merged when short, forked when long — and the policy fired zero times across all 18 cells.
- **Cheaper than the symptomatic alternative**: `fork_threshold=50` also rescues the demoted turns (trainable tokens back to normal), but by forking every mismatched turn — each fork re-emits the shared prefix, inflating training-side sequence tokens by an order of magnitude. The switches remove the mismatch itself instead.
- **Template effect** (motivates the usage note): the stripping template fragments the Anthropic-adapter trajectory at every turn boundary (drift-fork chains; several-fold more training-side sequence tokens for the same trainable content); preserving thinking keeps one sample per root→leaf path.
- **Unchanged layer, now quantified**: even in the best configuration, the pre-existing token-level REALIGN mechanism masked some previously-trained tokens per session (re-tokenization jitter, 0.6–1.4k tokens). This PR does not touch the token layer; this channel exists identically with and without the switches.

Coverage note: the fork policy's carve-out path (`reason=reasoning` fork) was not exercised in these runs — the harness build used here echoes reasoning fully, so no drop occurred. That path is covered by the unit-test matrix above; running it against a selectively-echoing harness (dsh ≤0.1.0-rc.7) is left as a follow-up.

## Compatibility / cost

- Both switches default off: existing-path merge/fork decisions and samples are unchanged (the only addition is fork-reason metadata on tree nodes).
- With dropping clients, enabling the fork policy turns previously merged-away turns into training samples, so sample count and training cost grow (each fork copies the shared prefix). In return, early-turn behavior is actually trained and the trajectory reward stops concentrating on the last turn.

## Usage

- Prefer a chat template that preserves prior-turn thinking ([Qwen3.8's default](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/chat_template.jinja); Qwen3.5 strips it with no preserve option) and an agent that echoes `reasoning_content` back: enable only `SLIME_AGENT_OPENAI_MANAGER_REASONING` for a full history match — no fork policy needed.
- For dropping clients: with the OpenAI adapter enable **both** switches — with only the policy on, the manager message and the dropped echo both omit `reasoning_content`, history still matches, and the loss happens at the token level, out of the policy's reach; with the Anthropic adapter (whose manager message always carries `reasoning_content`) the fork policy alone suffices.
- In the matrix, the cleanest combination was a preserving template + both switches + default threshold (for a purely echoing client the manager switch alone already suffices — the policy simply stays idle; for dropping or unknown clients both are required, manager-only is actively harmful there); if non-reasoning rewrite signals (e.g. tool-call normalization) should also stay trainable, lower `fork_threshold` instead — the policy deliberately does not cover those.
- After enabling, watch sample-count growth and training cost.

Per-switch guidance, including these adapter-specific combinations, is documented in `docs/en/get_started/agent.md` / `docs/zh/get_started/agent.md`.

items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: This made the documented multi-turn examples fail at import/runtime even though the underlying vLLM rollout path was available. For valid complete vLLM responses, the new parser is behaviorally equivalent to the previous inline logic.
items.body:
## Summary

- document Vime's existing agentic rollout, sandbox, and coding-agent workflows in English and Chinese
- centralize parsing of vLLM `token_ids` and token log probabilities
- fix stale SGLang response assumptions in the existing `mem_agent` and `multi_agent` examples
- keep `retool` and `search-r1` excluded after review

## Motivation

The agent examples already depended on a shared vLLM response parser that did not exist, and one still expected SGLang-only response metadata. This made the documented multi-turn examples fail at import/runtime even though the underlying vLLM rollout path was available.

For valid complete vLLM responses, the new parser is behaviorally equivalent to the previous inline logic. It additionally keeps token IDs and log probabilities aligned when content is partial and rejects malformed token ID lists.

## Sync audit

The complete Slime tree at cutoff `41014d1f` and all 243 files touched since the previous cutoff were reviewed. Engine-specific paths were mapped to their vLLM counterparts; remaining absent paths were classified as existing or explicit exclusions. No other shared runtime omission was found.

- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD pytest -q tests/test_vllm_rollout.py` (`36 passed`)

items.title: [CI/Build] Run the CPU tests CI silently skips, and guard against new gaps
items.author: natedemoss
items.summary: goes into synchronized upstream CPU tests, which runs in — it imports, so it needs vLLM present. It fails when a test file is neither referenced by a CI job nor waived in, and when a file CI runs as bare has no entry point.
items.body:
## Problem

CI enumerates test files by hand — one `python tests/<file>.py` line per test in `.buildkite/pipeline.yml`, one `(file, num_gpus, ...)` tuple in `.buildkite/gpu_suites.py`. Nothing walks `tests/`, so a test only runs if its author also wired it into a job. Two failure modes, both of which leave CI green:

1. **The file is never wired in.** Three existing files are in this state today and have never run in CI:
   - `tests/test_qwen3_linear_attention_cu_seqlens.py`
   - `tests/test_chunked_gae.py`
   - `tests/test_rollout_metrics.py`

2. **The CPU job's invocation style fails open.** `python tests/<file>.py` on a module with no `if __name__ == "__main__"` block just imports it: zero `test_*` functions execute and the command exits 0 without asserting anything.

## Changes

- **Wire the unreferenced files into the right jobs.** `test_qwen3_linear_attention_cu_seqlens.py`, `test_chunked_gae.py`, and the new `test_ci_test_coverage.py` go into *plugin contracts & CPU tests* (all three are CPU-safe). `test_rollout_metrics.py` goes into *synchronized upstream CPU tests*, which runs in `vllm/vime:latest` — it imports `vime.ray.rollout`, so it needs vLLM present.
- **Add `__main__` entry points** to the two files the CPU job invokes as bare `python <file>`, matching every other file in that job.
- **Add `tests/test_ci_test_coverage.py`** so neither gap can reopen. It fails when a test file is neither referenced by a CI job nor waived in `NOT_RUN_IN_CI`, and when a file CI runs as bare `python <file>` has no `__main__` entry point. The waiver list is itself checked for staleness (entries must name a file that still exists and that CI still does not run), so it cannot rot.

`NOT_RUN_IN_CI` starts with five entries, each with the reason: the two GLM-5.2 e2e tests whose `run_gate()` is disabled at the source, and three multi-GPU end-to-end runs no `gpu_suites` entry selects.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_ci_test_coverage.py` — 4 passed.
- Confirmed against `main` that the three existing files had zero references anywhere in `.buildkite/`, and that dropping any part of the pipeline change makes the new test fail with the offending file named.
- `ruff check`, `black --check` (24.3.0), and `isort --profile=black` (5.13.2) clean on all touched files; `pipeline.yml` parses.
- `test_chunked_gae.py` takes ~3 min on CPU (noted in a comment in the pipeline) — the 256x128K cases are dominated by the serial `vanilla_gae` reference the parallel scan is checked against. The other additions are fast.

## AI assistance

items.title: Order pipeline weight-update process groups across rollout engines
items.author: chengcuiping
items.summary: The PP sources are Ray actors invoked concurrently. Each rollout-engine actor uses a blocking HTTP call to join a group and processes methods serially. [Discussion: @zhuzilin, could you please take a look at this PR when you have time?]
items.body:
## Problem

In non-colocated full NCCL weight updates with pipeline-parallel training and multiple independent SGLang rollout engines, each PP source creates a custom `slime-pp_<rank>` group containing itself and every engine GPU.

The PP sources are Ray actors invoked concurrently. Each rollout-engine actor uses a blocking HTTP call to join a group and processes methods serially. If engine 0 starts PP0 while engine 1 starts PP1, each group waits for the request queued behind the other engine's blocking call. The existing rollout-engine lock only covers later broadcasts, so it cannot prevent this group-creation cycle.

## Fix

- Have all training ranks execute connect/disconnect phases in global PP-rank order.
- In phase `k`, only the DP=0/TP=0 source for PP rank `k` creates or destroys its device group.
- Use the existing all-training-rank Gloo group to propagate phase failure before advancing.
- Apply a finite group/Ray wait timeout inherited from the distributed timeout and clean partial groups/futures/blocked engine actors fail-stop.
- Clear destroyed local group state before reconnect and release the transfer lock in `finally`.

This adds synchronization only when engines connect or disconnect, not to the normal bucket update path.

## Tests

- The deterministic opposite-arrival regression fails on `a067ce6f` and passes with this change.
- Unit tests cover timeout cancellation/engine cleanup, transfer-lock release, and failed reconnect state.
- Four-A100 deterministic NCCL opposite-order test: 20/20 passed.
- NCCL create/update/destroy stress: 50/50 passed with source/engine checksum agreement.
- Controls: PP=1 with two independent engines 20/20; PP=2 with one TP=2 engine 20/20.
- A no-delay Ray arrival-order probe observed the dangerous opposite order in 8/200 rounds. This is the opportunity rate for that arrival ordering on the test host, not a measured online deadlock rate.
- Production Slime helper plus Ray/NCCL integration: 20 rounds and 40 broadcasts passed with matching checksums.
- Two real SGLang HTTP/model-runner servers plus two Slime PP source actors: both groups connected, both online updates succeeded, both engines advanced to weight version 2, and generation changed identically after the update.
- 27 related CPU tests and ruff, black, isort, compileall, and diff checks passed.

The patched production-helper connect times were 0.121 s for PP0 and 0.115 s for PP1, comparable to 0.113/0.119 s in an earlier 10-round integration run. No meaningful connect-time regression was observed in this test.

## Environment note

The full Slime launcher could not run in the available A100 environment because that environment's installed `sglang-kernel` package contained SM100 but not SM80 common operations. No dependency was changed for this PR. The target path was instead validated successfully with real A100-compatible SGLang HTTP/model runners, Slime PP source actors, NCCL group creation, online weight updates, and functional generation checks.

## Risk

Connect/disconnect now performs one small Gloo all-reduce per PP group. A genuine timeout terminates only the affected rollout-engine actors because a serial actor blocked inside SGLang cannot service a queued cleanup RPC; recovery must recreate those engines. The steady-state weight broadcast path is unchanged apart from ensuring its lock is released on exceptions.

items.title: perf(agent): isolate prompt rendering from event loop
items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: Long full-history prompt rendering blocks the agent adapter's aiohttp event loop. Move the existing call to one adapter-owned worker thread, retaining exact upstream rendering, saved sampled-token prefixes, and safe fallback for changed histories/tool schemas.
items.body:
## Summary

Long full-history prompt rendering blocks the agent adapter's aiohttp event loop. Move the existing `_session_prompt_ids()` call to one adapter-owned worker thread, retaining exact upstream rendering, saved sampled-token prefixes, and safe fallback for changed histories/tool schemas.

The worker bounds submitted running/queued work. Canceled requests retain their executor capacity until physical completion, discard queued jobs, return promptly during admission cancellation, and avoid starting SGLang or recording a trajectory after cancellation. App cleanup drains the worker. Session prefix lists/template options are snapshotted before offload; the live session is used for generation and records only flushed turns.

Bounded recent-window metrics at `GET /debug/adapter_metrics` include prompt length, total prompt-render latency, queue wait, worker utilization, event-loop lag, cancellations and discarded work, with P50/P95/P99 distributions.

Related to #2285.

## Scope

This improves event-loop responsiveness and observability. It preserves upstream full-history rendering and canonical-boundary checks, including original sampled prompt/response token prefixes introduced by #2457. It does not remove the cumulative O(N²) tokenization cost or claim general incremental tokenization. Sampler score-centering/top-p/R3 metadata, output-token validation, and protocol behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest -q tests/test_agent tests/test_grouped_rewards.py`: 169 passed, 2 skipped against main `58b08786`.
- Direct CPU runners: worker tests 12 passed; prompt continuity 14 passed. Real in-memory BPE tests compare synchronous and worker IDs for tool continuation, changed tools and compaction, and assert both full-history and splice-boundary renders run off the event-loop thread.
- Cancellation handoff, repeated cancellation with delayed cleanup, stable session snapshots, capacity ownership, health/metrics responsiveness and executor shutdown regressions passed.
- The upstream sampler replay/token contracts and Responses/Anthropic/Codex harness tests passed.
- Local synthetic continuity workload: 16,250 prompt IDs, 12 renders per mode, identical IDs. Synchronous heartbeat p95/max lag was 47.17/48.64 ms; worker p95/max lag was 0.63/1.09 ms. Total render time was 0.197/0.206 s respectively. These single-host timings show event-loop isolation, not a tokenizer throughput improvement or production guarantee.
- Repository-pinned pre-commit, workflow regeneration, YAML and `git diff --check` passed. Sunabako 8-GPU/35-minute E2E registration, container init/cidfile cleanup, proxy/mount setup and artifacts remain unchanged. GPU E2E execution is not claimed locally.

items.title: fix(opd): temperature-scale SGLang teacher logprobs
items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes, not the matched-temperature objective. Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it …
items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

## Change

- add a first-class `input_logprob_temperature` request option to the bundled SGLang patch, aligned with draft [sgl-project/sglang#36213](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36213)
- keep that option separate from decode sampling and apply it only before input-logprob normalization
- have SGLang acknowledge the applied temperature in response metadata
- request that behavior from OPD and fail closed for non-unit temperatures when an external teacher does not support it
- preserve vanilla SGLang compatibility when `--rollout-temperature=1.0`
- document the `KL(p_T || q_T)` contract
- remove the stale CPU-matrix entry for `test_rollout_validation.py`, which #2322 deleted

## Tests

- [x] OPD payload/compatibility unit tests (`5 passed`)
- [x] release-specific SGLang request/core/acknowledgment tests (`45 passed` on CPU)
- [x] pre-commit hooks on all changed slime files
- [x] new patch applies cleanly to both `v0.5.15.post1` and `latest`, including each directory's `sglang-deterministic.patch` afterward
- [x] Python compilation and shell syntax checks
- [ ] `tests/test_qwen2.5_0.5B_opd_sglang.py` on GPU (`run-ci-megatron`): generation-time `q_T` must equal prompt-rescored `q_T` for the same token

This follows up on #2085 and addresses the SGLang behavior identified in #2319.

items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: TileLang fixed the shared-memory liveness bug in tile-ai/tilelang#2204. Slime's CUDA 12 image still receives TileLang 0.1.9 through the pinned FlashQLA dependency, so a blanket dependency upgrade is not currently compatible with that image.
items.body:
## Summary

- Disable `TL_ENABLE_AGGRESSIVE_SHARED_MEMORY_MERGE` for TileLang versions in the affected range `>=0.1.9.dev0,<0.1.11`.
- Preserve the optimization for pre-regression releases such as 0.1.8 and fixed releases starting at 0.1.11.
- Fail closed for missing, invalid, or TileLang `0.0.dev0` metadata.
- Declare `packaging` as a runtime dependency and add a CPU contract test that imports the real GLM5 backward module with stubbed TileLang versions and inspects the actual JIT pass configuration.

TileLang fixed the shared-memory liveness bug in tile-ai/tilelang#2204. Slime's CUDA 12 image still receives TileLang 0.1.9 through the pinned FlashQLA dependency, so a blanket dependency upgrade is not currently compatible with that image. The version guard keeps the optimization on known-safe versions while applying the documented workaround to the affected compiler releases.

## Tests

- `PYTHONPATH=. python tests/test_glm5_tilelang_sparse_mla_version_guard.py -q` (`12 passed`)

items.title: fix(args): reject unsupported colocated offload sync
items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: Colocated full sync currently uses and CUDA IPC even when is selected. torchmemorysaver-backed offload allocations are not compatible with that PyTorch CUDA IPC serialization path, so this turns a late failure into an actionable startup error.
items.body:
## Summary

- Reject the known-incompatible Megatron configuration that combines colocated local rollout engines, training offload, full weight sync, and the NCCL transport.
- Run the validation after custom YAML overrides, so a dangerous `custom_config` cannot bypass it.
- Keep valid boundaries unchanged: no-offload, zero local rollout GPUs, `debug_train_only`, non-colocated runs, and full+disk sync.
- Point users to the two supported choices: full+disk with a shared `--update-weight-disk-dir`, or `--no-offload-train` when memory permits.

Colocated full sync currently uses `UpdateWeightFromTensor` and CUDA IPC even when `--update-weight-transport=nccl` is selected. torch_memory_saver-backed offload allocations are not compatible with that PyTorch CUDA IPC serialization path, so this turns a late `storage._share_cuda_()` failure into an actionable startup error.

This is the narrow fail-fast stage; it does not claim to add a new non-disk colocated transport.

## Tests

- `PYTHONPATH=. python tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py -q` (`26 passed`)
- The regression matrix covers derived colocate defaults, PPO-forced offload, YAML overrides, explicit no-offload, zero rollout GPUs, debug-train-only, and full+disk.
- Ruff, Black, isort, autoflake, compileall, and `git diff --check` passed.

Refs #2188

items.author: liuhao-labs

items.body:
## Summary

Long masked prompts still produce full `[T, V]` vocabulary logits before Slime selects trainable tokens, causing the projection and fp32 conversion peaks in #2253. Add opt-in `--compact-actor-logits` to project only the `N` loss-masked rows for eligible built-in actor policy/SFT paths.

Critics, custom providers/hooks/losses, MTP, TIS/mismatch metrics, debug capture, rollout log-probs, PPO reward-KL, score centering, MuP scaling, and custom Megatron output processors preserve the full-logit path. The optimization is disabled by default and can be enabled with `--compact-actor-logits` for eligible built-in paths.

Normal forward and combined 1F1B both resolve the model's `_postprocess` method dynamically. The context covers the pipeline schedule call. Model state-dict keys and checkpoint ownership are unchanged.

Fixes #2253.

items.title: perf(rollout): reuse filtered prompt token ids
items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: Max-length filtering already tokenizes every retained text prompt, but default rollout preparation encodes the same rendered prompt again. Reuse those IDs for stock training and evaluation, eliminating the second encoding pass.
items.body:
## Summary

Max-length filtering already tokenizes every retained text prompt, but default rollout preparation encodes the same rendered prompt again. Reuse those IDs for stock training and evaluation, eliminating the second encoding pass.

The cache contains only immutable packed uint32 IDs (4 bytes per token). Deep-copied siblings share the payload and each materializes its own mutable token list on consumption. The cache is excluded from serialization and dataclass reconstruction. Multimodal outputs and custom rollout/generate/data-source contracts remain uncached.

Training is wired through the current `slime.data.data_source` API. Missing rollout configuration disables caching; existing tokens and multimodal processing retain their precedence.

Related to #1111.

## Validation

- 111 local CPU tests passed across filtering, Sample serialization/reconstruction, train/eval cache ownership, buffer/checkpoint behavior, fully async rollout, and plugin contracts.
- Direct CI-style filtering runner: 25 passed.
- Repository-pinned pre-commit checks passed.
- On the original 10,000-prompt in-memory BPE benchmark, second-pass `tokenizer.encode` calls dropped from 10,000 to 0. The immediate same-process comparison for filtering plus preparation was 2.65s versus 0.57s; packed payload size was 8.35 MiB. Timing is workload-dependent.
- The updated GitHub CPU/agent matrix also exercises distributed Ray/Straw fan-out against the current upstream data-source API.
discussion: i checked this before and decided not to add it because re-tokenization especially in text-only case wont add too much latency. theoretically yes we should have this.

Thanks for the context. I measured the retained text-only path before opening this, because the benefit depends on dataset size and prompt length.

On the same local workload (10,000 retained prompts, 2,189,001 prompt token IDs, an in-memory ByteLevel BPE), the current path made one batched tokenization call during filtering plus 10,000 per-sample `encode()` calls during rollout preparation. With this change, the second count is zero.

The immediate same-process comparison was:

- current path: 2.652 s total (0.586 s filter + 2.066 s prepare)
- cached path: 0.571 s total (0.541 s filter + 0.030 s prepare)
- rollout preparation: 98.6% lower, total for the two stages: 78.5% lower

The retained cache payload was 8,756,004 bytes (8.35 MiB) as packed uint32 IDs. It is only created when max-length filtering has already tokenized the prompt, only for retained text prompts on the stock rollout path, and it is consumed before Ray transfer. Multimodal processor outputs and custom rollout/data-source paths remain uncached.

So this is not intended to add tokenization work when filtering is disabled; it only reuses work that has already happened. The exact speedup will vary with tokenizer and prompts, but the invariant improvement is one fewer encoding pass per retained text prompt.

Rebased onto current `main` (`3778dbf`) and preserved the existing implementation unchanged. The stale baseline failure from the removed `test_rollout_validation.py` is no longer part of the new CI run. Local checks passed: `test_filter_long_prompt.py` (22), `test_sample.py` (20), `test_rollout_data_utils.py` (6), plus the repository-pinned format/lint checks. @nanjiangwill, this is ready for another look when convenient.

items.title: fix: distribute routing replay padding across experts
items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: Rollout routing replay appends synthetic expert selections for per-sample, context-parallel, and batch-alignment padding. These rows are loss-masked, but they still pass through MoE expert dispatch and therefore must not concentrate on one expert block or expe…
items.body:
## Summary

Rollout routing replay appends synthetic expert selections for per-sample, context-parallel, and batch-alignment padding. These rows are loss-masked, but they still pass through MoE expert dispatch and therefore must not concentrate on one expert block or expert-parallel rank.

The original fill flattens `[pad, num_layers, topk]` before taking modulo `num_experts`, so a fixed layer advances by `num_layers * topk` and every padding call restarts at zero. Numbering pad rows after CP fixes those aliases, but assigning `((pad_row + layer) * topk + column) % num_experts` still produces contiguous expert IDs. At layer 0 with contiguous expert sharding, 1-5 rows at `topk=8` can activate as few as 1/1/2/2/3 of 8 EP ranks for 128 experts and 1/1/1/1/2 for 256 experts. At EP=32 the corresponding counts are 2/4/6/8/10 ranks for 128 experts and 1/2/3/4/5 for 256 experts.

## Fix

Keep padding marked as `-1` while the per-sample and context-parallel layouts are constructed. After CP slicing is complete, number only the pad rows that remain. For pad-row ordinal `p`, layer `l`, route column `c`, expert-parallel size `P`, top-k `K`, and `Q = num_experts / P` experts per rank, fill:

```
a = p * K + c + l * (P * K)
expert_rank = a % P
local_expert = (a // P) % Q
expert = expert_rank * Q + local_expert
```

This is a rank-first permutation of expert IDs. Every fixed-layer row reaches `min(P, K)` EP ranks, consecutive pad rows give an optimal prefix histogram across ranks, and every `num_experts` assignments visit every expert once. Layer blocks retain the same per-layer EP balance. Sequence parallelism then partitions these already distributed assignments.

The EP size comes from Megatron's initialized `mpu`, which already owns the TP and CP geometry used by this helper. Assignment arithmetic uses `int64` and casts once to the routed-expert payload dtype, avoiding overflow in intermediate products. Non-padding replay data is unchanged.

## Verification

- The production helper is exercised for every 1-5-pad case at 128/256 experts, `topk=8`, and EP=8/32. EP=8 now activates all 8 ranks for every row count; EP=32 activates 8/16/24/32/32 ranks. Every per-layer rank histogram differs by at most one assignment, and all `8 * pad_rows` expert IDs are distinct in these cases.
- Non-padding rows are compared exactly before and after the repair. Multi-row batch-alignment padding continues the same post-CP ordinal sequence.
- Ordinary CP and `allgather_cp` are checked across CP ranks, then reconstructed from sequence-parallel slices to verify that padding is assigned after CP and before SP.
- A synthetic Qwen3-30B-A3B CP=1 layout uses 32 mixed sample token lengths summing to 19,969, TP=4, EP=8, and the default 128x data-padding multiplier. Per-sample padding contributes 32 terminal rows; alignment to `4 * 128 = 512` rows adds 511 more because `19,969 = 39 * 512 + 1`. The resulting pre-SP layout has 20,480 rows, including 543 padding rows and 4,344 synthetic assignments per layer. Upstream's original flattened fill uses 8/128 experts and 1/8 EP ranks with 16.0x expert and 8.0x EP peak/mean. The repaired fill uses 128/128 experts and 8/8 ranks; its expert peak is 34 over a 33.9375 mean (1.001842x), and every EP rank receives exactly 543 assignments (1.0x peak/mean).
- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_accelerator.py tests/test_cp_utils.py`: 18 passed on CPU-only PyTorch.
- The repository's complete pre-commit hook set passes for both changed files.

The quantitative case validates routing metadata mechanics rather than end-to-end training throughput; a multi-GPU Megatron run can be added if maintainers want that integration evidence.

items.title: fix(update-weight): gather legacy TE grouped experts
items.author: primorLee
items.summary: Those parameters therefore lack the tensormodelparallel and partitiondim metadata that slime currently requires before entering its all-gather path. With ETP=2, slime consequently forwards one local shard to SGLang instead of the reconstructed expert tensor.
items.body:
## Summary

- recover expert-TP partition metadata for legacy Megatron TEGroupedLinear parameter names
- gather affected expert shards in both synchronous and batched asynchronous weight-update paths
- keep row-parallel linear_fc2 biases and metadata-marked unrecognized expert parameters replicated
- preserve the original fail-fast behavior for unrelated parameters with completely missing TP metadata
- preserve the existing metadata-driven behavior for current Megatron versions

## Problem

In the Megatron-LM revision reported in #2280, expert TEGroupedLinear modules are explicitly sharded across ETP ranks while Transformer Engine receives parallel_mode=None. Those parameters therefore lack the tensor_model_parallel and partition_dim metadata that slime currently requires before entering its all-gather path.

With ETP=2, slime consequently forwards one local shard to SGLang instead of the reconstructed expert tensor. In the reported Qwen3.5-35B-A3B run, SGLang receives 256 elements where it expects 512 and partially updates the rollout model.

NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#5916 later fixed the missing metadata upstream, but slime images using the earlier revision remain affected.

## Fix

_tp_partition_dim first honors normal Megatron metadata. When that metadata is absent, it uses slime's stable exported TE grouped-expert names to recover only the partitioning that is unambiguous:

- linear_fc1.weightN and linear_fc1.biasN: column-parallel, dimension 0
- linear_fc2.weightN: row-parallel, dimension 1
- linear_fc2.biasN: replicated

The fallback is restricted to .experts.linear_fc[12].(weight|bias)N names. The existing expert-TP world-size check still makes ETP=1 a no-op, and parallel_mode=duplicated remains excluded.

The same helper is used by all_gather_param and all_gather_params_async, so direct and batched online updates make the same decision.

## Validation

- Windows Python 3.12 / PyTorch CPU: 6 passed
- Linux Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13 CPU: 5 passed
- project changed-file pre-commit suite: all hooks passed
- Ruff, Python compilation, and git diff --check: passed

The tests cover legacy fc1/fc2 reconstruction, the replicated row bias, an unrecognized parameter with explicit non-TP metadata, fail-fast behavior for unrelated missing metadata, existing regular-TP metadata, and the asynchronous gather/wait path.

I did not rerun the reported 48-H200 topology. The regression directly verifies the missing shard-to-full-tensor transition, expert-TP group selection, concatenation dimensions, GLU reorder, and both slime update paths.

Closes #2280

items.title: fix(agent): preserve malformed tool-call arguments
items.author: primorLee
items.summary: The OpenAI adapter then serializes that sentinel, so clients receive a different argument string from the one produced by the model. The Anthropic adapter emits the sentinel as a normal executable, even though Anthropic requires an input object and the model …
items.body:
## Summary

- preserve the model-produced tool argument string alongside its parsed mapping
- return the original string unchanged as OpenAI `function.arguments`
- keep the parsed mapping for chat-template replay and trajectory matching
- fail closed in the Anthropic adapter when arguments cannot be represented as an input object
- mark valid non-object JSON arguments as ill-formed instead of emitting invalid tool inputs

## Problem

When SGLang recognizes a tool call but its arguments are malformed JSON, the parser currently replaces the argument text with a `{"_raw_arguments": ...}` sentinel mapping.

The OpenAI adapter then serializes that sentinel, so clients receive a different argument string from the one produced by the model. The Anthropic adapter emits the sentinel as a normal executable `tool_use.input`, even though Anthropic requires an input object and the model output was not valid.

For the model output:

```text
{"cmd": "pytest"
```

current `main` returns:

```text
OpenAI: {"_raw_arguments": "{\"cmd\": \"pytest\""}
Anthropic: tool_use(input={"_raw_arguments": ...})
```

This PR keeps two representations at the parsing boundary: the original wire text and the canonical mapping used for history rendering. OpenAI receives the former unchanged. Anthropic only exposes calls whose arguments are representable as an object; an invalid call becomes a normal non-tool response and the turn remains marked `ill_formed`.

Valid object-valued tool calls and XML fallback calls keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

- full CPU agent suite: `70 passed, 1 skipped`
- changed-file `pre-commit`: case-conflict, private-key, large-file, Ruff, autoflake, isort, and Black hooks passed
- Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed
- focused coverage includes malformed JSON, valid raw formatting, non-object JSON, OpenAI wire preservation, and Anthropic fail-closed behavior

Closes #2299

items.title: feat: DSpark speculative decoding draft model training for RL rollout acceleration
items.author: CalvinXKY
items.summary: Integrates DSpark speculative decoding into vime's RL training pipeline to accelerate rollout generation. DSpark trains a lightweight draft model (Markov heads + attention layers) alongside the policy model, enabling speculative decoding during vLLM rollout wi…
items.body:
## Summary

Integrates DSpark speculative decoding into vime's RL training pipeline to accelerate rollout generation. DSpark trains a lightweight draft model (Markov heads + attention layers) alongside the policy model, enabling speculative decoding during vLLM rollout with ~2.5x throughput improvement.

### Key Changes

**New module: `vime/backends/megatron_utils/dspark/`**
- Draft model architecture: Markov heads, attention layers, hidden state capture
- Training losses: CE + L1 (chunked logsumexp for memory efficiency) + confidence loss
- Weight export to vLLM for speculative decoding during rollout
- TP>1 support with vocab padding/unpadding (all-gather, zero-pad, strip)

**Actor integration (`actor.py`)**
- Draft weight cache/restore lifecycle around sleep/wake_up to prevent GPU OOM
- `synchronize()+empty_cache()` before `torch_memory_saver.pause()` to prevent memory fragmentation crash
- Unified try/except for pause/resume across all DSpark configs

**Weight sync (`update_weight/common.py`, `update_weight_from_distributed.py`, `update_weight_from_tensor.py`)**
- vLLM 0.26.0/0.27.2 compatibility shims: `NCCLTrainerAdapter` with `StatelessProcessGroup` + `trainer_send_weights`
- `create_nccl_trainer` tries vLLM 0.27.2 API first, falls back to 0.26.0 adapter
- `send_custom_weights` sends metadata via Ray before NCCL broadcast
- DSpark draft weight sync via file-based transfer (`load_draft_weights_from_file` through `/collective_rpc` HTTP endpoint)
- No-op `cache_dspark_draft_weights` for non-colocate mode

**vLLM engine (`vllm_engine.py`)**
- Engine router retry + extended timeouts for DSpark weight sync
- spec_accept_rate extraction from `/inference/v1/generate` endpoint
- `load_draft_weights_from_file` method for DSpark draft model weight loading

**CLI arguments (`arguments.py`)**
- 14 new `--dspark-*` flags for draft model config (layers, block_size, num_speculative_tokens, loss weights, etc.)

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests: `tests/test_dspark_unit.py` (model build, forward, loss)
- [x] Phase 2 integration test: `tests/test_dspark_phase2.py` (end-to-end training loop)
- [x] TP=1: Qwen3-4B 200-step GRPO, DSpark ON vs OFF, AIME 2024 eval
- [x] TP=4: Qwen3-4B DSpark training verified (24.87% spec_accept_rate)
- [x] Colocate 20-step test (vLLM 0.26.0, origin/main rebase): spec_accept_rate 32-37%
- [x] Non-colocate 20-step test: spec_accept_rate 33-37%
- [x] Colocate 100-step long run: spec_accept_rate 32-40%, ce_loss 3.27→1.68 (draft model learned)
- [x] vLLM 0.27.2 verification: weight sync (IPC packed + draft file transfer) verified, spec_accept_rate 32-36%, AIME 58.75%
- [ ] CI pipeline validation
- [ ] Multi-model validation (Qwen3-8B, etc.)

## Notes
- Requires vLLM 0.26.0+ (compatible with both 0.26.0 and 0.27.2 via try/except shims)
- vLLM patch needed: add `cos_sin_cache` to `SKIP_TENSORS` in `reload/meta.py` (DSpark draft export has no buffers)
- Pretrained draft model initialization recommended (random init shows ce_loss plateau at ~12)
- vLLM 0.27.2 image (39edbd2ae25a) has TE 2.16.1 kernels incompatible with A800 (SM 8.0) — use vLLM 0.26.0 image for A800 training

items.title: feat(rollout): 为异步 RS 精确补齐 prompt-group batch
items.author: inmnin
items.summary: actor 使用当前 proximal policy 做一次 preflight forward，重新计算 logprob，并执行 sequence/geometric RS admission。 3. coordinator 以完整 prompt group 为原子接纳或拒绝候选。 4.
items.body:
## 摘要

感谢维护 slime。这个 PR 为 disaggregated `train_async.py` 增加一个默认关闭、fail-closed 的
`--rs-batch-refill` 路径，用于在 sequence-level / geometric rejection sampling（RS）之后，按完整
prompt group 精确补齐 optimizer step 的 effective batch。

核心目标不是把异步数据变成 on-policy，也不是承诺无条件提速，而是保证：启用该开关后，每个
optimizer step 要么拿到配置数量的完整、通过 RS admission 的 prompt groups，要么在更新前明确失败；
不会静默用 underfilled batch 更新。

## 背景与问题边界

序列级 / geometric RS 会拒绝训推概率差异过大的 sequence。原始 rollout 的结构 batch 仍然存在，
但 RS 后真正参与梯度计算的有效 sequence 数会波动；按本 PR 采用的 group-atomic 语义，完整且组内所有
sample 均通过 gate 的 prompt group 数也可能不足。当前 actor-side RS 路径不会自动补齐这些有效 group。

这里需要特别说明与 [#657](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/657) 的边界：#657 将 importance sampling
weight 与 rejection sampling mask 解耦；当前 main reducer 的 numerator 使用 modified mask，但 denominator
仍显式使用原始 `rollout_mask_sums`。本 PR 不依赖重新归一化，而是最终只接纳 gate 全部通过、mask 保持
不变的完整 group，并恢复每个 optimizer step 固定的 prompt-group cardinality。

本 PR 选择严格的 group-atomic 语义：组内任一 sample 未通过 admission，则整个 prompt group 都不进入
本次训练。这样不会通过只补单个 sample 改变 GRPO group 的结构。

最直接的补法是在 underfill 后重新生成完整 `rollout_batch_size`。但 long-horizon / tool-use rollout 的
尾部延迟通常很高，整批重跑会生成大量最终不会参与训练的轨迹。这里改为由 coordinator 计算真实缺口，
只为 DP/VPP 可调度性做最小向上取整，然后请求对应数量的 replacement groups。

一个最小例子：`rollout_batch_size=2`，每个 prompt 采 2 个 samples。group A 的两个 samples 都通过，
group B 只有一个 sample 通过。启用本 PR 后，B 会按组拒绝，并只请求 1 个 replacement group；replacement
通过后才以 2 个完整 groups 更新。若达到补采轮次上限仍不足，则在 `optimizer.step` 前失败。

## 实现方案

该功能目前只接入 disaggregated `train_async.py`，执行顺序如下：

1. 首轮只生成配置要求的 `rollout_batch_size`，本层不做投机式超采样。
2. actor 使用当前 proximal policy 做一次 preflight forward，重新计算 logprob，并执行 sequence/geometric
   RS admission。
3. coordinator 以完整 prompt group 为原子接纳或拒绝候选。
4. 根据已接纳 group 数计算缺口，只请求缺少的 replacement target；target 仅向上取整到 DP/VPP 所需的
   最小 group multiple。
5. replacement 使用当前 rollout policy 生成，再执行同样的 actor preflight 和 group admission。
6. 最多执行 `--rs-refill-max-rounds` 轮；达到上限仍不足时，在 selected proximal-logprob cache transfer
   和 optimizer step 之前失败。
7. 最终 training forward 继续应用 TIS，并重新执行、校验与 preflight 一致的 RS gate。

preflight 产生的 proximal logprob 先保存在各 actor rank 的 pinned CPU memory 中。group decision 完成后，
只把最终接纳项通过 Ray 传给 RolloutManager；未接纳缓存立即清理。正式 training forward 仍然正常执行，
最终接纳缓存作为 PPO proximal old policy 使用。该设计减少的是跨 actor/manager 的无用传输和最终驻留，
并没有省掉候选 preflight 或 GPU-to-CPU copy。

除主流程外，本 PR 还包含两个由 refill 调用方式暴露出来、各自有回归测试的兼容性修复：

- SGLang `GenerateState` singleton 提交任务时使用本次 `generate_rollout_async` 的 per-call args，而不是首次
  初始化时缓存的 args；
- global rollout data source 在单次取样跨越 epoch 时可继续补足请求数量。

## 正确性与保护条件

补齐数量不会消除 off-policy。本实现有意把第一版范围收窄到 one-step async：

- 强制 `--update-weights-interval 1`、每个 rollout batch 恰好一个 optimizer step，并继续强制内置 TIS；
- 初始候选只接受 policy staleness `[0, 1]`；
- replacement 的 rollout policy version 必须与本轮 actor preflight version 完全一致；
- sample ID、group ID、rollout ID、policy version、loss mask、response shape 和 proximal cache 都做严格校验；
- cache 与最终训练样本必须双射，缺失、重复或多余项都会在更新前报错；
- preflight 与正式训练会重复执行同一 RS gate，并验证最终 mask 未被中间 hook 修改；
- refill coordination 的 RPC 有显式超时；异常路径会尝试清理 actor cache 和 manager pending state，同时保留
  原始异常；candidate generation 继续使用 rollout backend 自身的 timeout / health-monitor 语义；
- checkpoint 保存边界不会把已经 prefetch、但尚未对应模型更新的数据源状态写入 checkpoint；
- refill 跨越数据集 epoch 时，data source 不会在单次补采中途错误结束。

针对审计中发现的可变参数与无效传输风险，当前版本还增加了以下保护：

- 每次 candidate generation 都向 custom rollout function 及其 sample hooks 传入 `deepcopy(args)`，防止其对
  scalar 或 nested config 的修改泄漏到后续 refill round，进而改变 batching、topology 或采样行为；
- custom rollout logger 同样接收独立的 `deepcopy(args)`；logger/debug saver 前后重新转换 train data，并用
  fingerprint 验证 policy inputs 未变化；
- coordinator 一旦确认 retry budget exhausted，立即报错并进入清理，不再先提取 actor cache 或向 manager
  传输、存储注定不会进入 optimizer step 的 proximal logprob。

为了 fail-closed，参数校验会拒绝尚未证明安全的组合，包括 checkpoint resume、persistent fully-async
queue、token-level RS、external rollout engine、dynamic sampling filter、partial rollout、offload/release、
量化 Megatron、dropout、context parallel、自定义 model provider / Megatron before hooks / TIS / advantage /
loss reducer / train-data converter / reward postprocessor，以及非完整 NCCL 权重同步等。显式
`fp8=false` / `fp4=false` 不会被误拒绝。

## 使用方式

```bash
python train_async.py \
  ... \
  --rs-batch-refill \
  --rs-refill-max-rounds 2 \
  --rs-refill-rpc-timeout-seconds 1800 \
  --rs-refill-max-candidate-cache-bytes 1073741824 \
  --update-weights-interval 1 \
  --use-tis \
  --custom-config-path examples/train_infer_mismatch_helper/mis_refill.yaml
```

`examples/train_infer_mismatch_helper/README.md` 和 `mis_refill.yaml` 已补充完整约束与示例；`train.py`
会明确拒绝该参数，避免误以为 colocated path 已支持。

`--rs-refill-max-candidate-cache-bytes` 限制的是 proximal-logprob tensor payload，不包含 Python container、
Ray object store / transport buffer，也不会预留 CUDA allocator headroom。最终 batch 的 DP-local proximal
logprob shard 仍可能在 training rank 上 materialize，因此 long-response 任务需要额外预留 GPU 显存；文档已
明确这一点。

## 请求量对比（非 GPU benchmark）

下面是直接调用本 PR planner 得到的 coordinator target，对比对象是“underfill 后重新请求完整
64-group batch”的朴素补齐策略。它不是 wall-clock benchmark，也不用于声称端到端必然提速。

配置：`rollout_batch_size=64` groups、`n_samples_per_prompt=8`、DP=8、VPP=2、每个 VPP stage 的
microbatch group size=4，因此最小 refill quantum 为 4 groups。

| 实际缺口（groups） | 本 planner target | 整批重采 target | target 减少 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4 | 64 | 93.75% |
| 5 | 8 | 64 | 87.50% |
| 16 | 16 | 64 | 75.00% |
| 缺口 1..64 的均值 | 34 | 64 | 46.88% |

当前 upstream actor-side RS 的行为是“不恢复有效 group 数”，并不是“整批重采”；上表只比较两种可能的
补齐策略。target 是本层传给 rollout function 的请求量，不等同于底层实际 generation task 数。实际耗时
取决于 RS 拒绝率、长尾 rollout、preflight 成本和训推配比；低拒绝率下，本实现仍增加一次 actor preflight，
因此它首先是 effective-batch 正确性选项，而不是无条件性能优化。

## 可观测性

新增指标覆盖：

- initial / replacement generation time 与 coordinator / preflight time；
- 每轮 candidate、累计 rejected / surplus、accepted groups、gate acceptance rate 和 selection utilization；
- actor candidate cache、aggregate/peak cache、selected transfer、manager retained cache 的字节数与耗时；
- effective trainable tokens、refill path time 和 effective tokens per refill-path second；
- initial policy staleness 与 refill round 数。

这些指标用于真实训练中判断补齐是否值得，而不是在没有 GPU A/B 时替代性能实验。

## 验证

### 仓库 CPU 回归

在最终候选 commit 上，按 `.github/workflows/pr-test.yml.j2` 的 `cpu-unittest` 与 `agent-test` 列表，
对 62 个测试文件逐文件启动独立 pytest 进程，避免文件级 module stub 污染：

```bash
PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 \
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' \
PYTHONPATH="$REPO" \
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <test-file>
```

结果：

| 项目 | 结果 |
|---|---:|
| workflow CPU 测试文件 | 62 / 62 通过 |
| pytest cases | **703 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed/error** |
| 唯一 skip | lean CPU 环境未安装 SGLang，`tests/test_agent/test_adapters.py` 按设计 `pytest.importorskip("sglang")` |
| `test_rs_exact_refill_rollout_manager.py` | 23 passed |

另外完成：

- `pre-commit run --all-files`：全部 hooks 通过；
- 变更 Python 文件 `py_compile`、Ruff、Black 与 `git diff --check`：通过；
- 上表跳过的 adapter 文件另在已安装 SGLang `0.5.12.post1`、隐藏 CUDA 的环境中复跑，
  结果为 `15 passed`；新增的两个 SGLang refill regression 也在该环境中复跑，结果为 `2 passed`；
- 未随 PR 提交、用于真实 A/B 的 runner CPU harness：`113 passed, 3 warnings`。

### 真实 4-GPU 配对 A/B

GPU A/B 在祖先 commit `a420a7c8cd8ccf000540447276aa57e21eef029e` 上完成一次 clean CAL → A → B。
当前 PR HEAD `eba72613258164c5fb6ad54770efe4908a74e77d` 相比该实验 commit 只移动了一个测试文件的
`__main__` guard，以兼容 workflow 的直接脚本入口；生产代码没有变化。
此前受到非实验 GPU 进程干扰的尝试全部作废，没有混入下面的数字。

| 项目 | 固定配置 |
|---|---|
| 模型 | Qwen3-4B，同一 torch-dist checkpoint，实验结束再次逐文件校验 SHA-256 |
| 数据 | `BytedTsinghua-SIA/DAPO-Math-17k` 的固定 12-row 小型 workload：4 个 initial rows（2 个 distinct prompts 各重复一次，用于两个 rollout IDs）+ 8 个 distinct refill reserve rows，共 10 个 distinct prompts；输入 SHA-256 `3d1be7cf...5e8de2` |
| 评测 | `BytedTsinghua-SIA/AIME-2024` 的 30 个 distinct prompts，仅作 integration smoke |
| GPU 拓扑 | 2 张 actor GPU（TP=2）+ 2 张 rollout GPU（两个 TP=1 SGLang engines） |
| batch | 2 prompt groups × 4 samples，GBS=8 |
| 训练 | CAL → A（feature off）→ B（exact refill），各 2 steps，response length=512 |
| 异步约束 | TIS，`--update-weights-interval 1`，固定 seed 与 deterministic inference |

A/B 共享同一个运行时冻结的 RS 配置，SHA-256 都是 `1d4162ee...a8c8`。两者除 B 的
`--rs-batch-refill` 与 A 侧 measurement-only MIS scalar wrapper 外保持一致；归一化命令校验会忽略这两个
预期差异并拒绝其他差异。两步 initial candidate 的 prompt、response、reward、loss mask、rollout logprob、
policy version 和 normalized training content 均在同一 HMAC key 下逐项配对，CAL/A/B 完全一致。
实验 Megatron 环境固定在 revision `3714d81d...2862`，其已知 working-tree patch 也单独归档并绑定
SHA-256 `0f7295e5...1048`；它不是本 PR 的一部分，且 A/B 共用完全相同的环境。

CAL 从同一批自然产生的 stale log-ratio 中选择一个 float32 安全边界：fresh step 拒绝 `0/8`，stale step
拒绝 `1/8`，并通过预设的至少 16 个 float32 ULP 间距检查。冻结配置回放证明 A 与 B
得到逐元素相同的 admission mask，因此不是为 B 单独选择更有利的 gate。

| stale step 指标 | A：feature off | B：exact refill |
|---|---:|---:|
| initial candidate groups / samples | 2 / 8 | 2 / 8 |
| RS 拒绝 | 1 / 8 sequences（12.5%），影响 1 / 2 groups | 1 / 2 groups |
| replacement 请求 | 无 | **1 group / 4 samples** |
| refill rounds | 无 | **1** |
| 累计 scored / rejected / accepted groups | 不补齐 | **3 / 1 / 2** |
| surplus groups | 无 | **0** |
| 最终 train forward 的 low/high RS mask | 有 1 个 sequence 被 mask | **0 / 0** |
| stale-step grad norm | 0.05251 | 0.04387 |

B 的 initial candidate policy version 为 `1`，actor preflight/scoring version 为 `2`，replacement version 也
严格为 `2`；这验证了 replacement 来自当前 policy，而不是重新使用 stale policy。最终 accepted batch 恢复到
2 个完整 groups，且正式 training forward 没有再次拒绝任何 selected sample。A/B fresh step 的 grad norm
也完全一致，均为 `0.0628146231`，进一步验证配对起点。

真实分项计时如下。它们覆盖 generation + coordinator/preflight/refill path，不等同于完整 optimizer step
吞吐：

| B 路径 | fresh step | stale + one-refill step |
|---|---:|---:|
| initial generation | 15.536 s | 14.364 s |
| preflight | 2.036 s | 0.464 s |
| replacement generation | 0 | 14.246 s |
| coordinator | 2.062 s | 14.733 s |
| refill path total | 17.598 s | 29.097 s |
| effective trainable tokens | 4096 | 4096 |
| scored trainable tokens | 4096 | 6144 |

其中 coordinator 是包含 preflight、replacement generation 与 selected-cache transfer 的包容性计时，不能与
这些子项再次相加；`refill path total = initial generation + coordinator`。coordinator 扣除这些已单列子项后，
两步 residual 分别只有 0.017 s 和 0.018 s。stale step 的 actor/manager candidate cache 峰值为 16 KiB、累计候选 payload 为 24 KiB，
远低于配置的 256 MiB 上限。

本次真实缺口为 1 group。exact refill 返回 4 个 replacement sample slots；若在同一轮按完整 2-group batch
盲目补采，则会返回 8 个 slots。因此这里能报告的是 **replacement request slots 减少 50%（8 → 4）**。
这是固定观测轮数下的结构性请求量对比，不是实测的 wall-clock speedup，也不推断底层 dynamic-sampling
attempts 或 generated tokens。相对于 feature-off A，B 在该 stale step 实测增加了 14.246 s replacement
generation，以恢复 exact batch；A 不请求 replacement，仍以包含 1 条被 mask sequence 的 nominal GBS=8
batch 更新。二者训练语义不同，因此不将该耗时差解释为通用性能结论。

phase 级计时中，A 的 compute / teardown 为 107.776 / 6.475 s，B 为 124.420 / 6.603 s。为避免人工选取
GPU 交接窗口污染结果，CAL/A/B 的 resident HOLD 分别为 86.936 / 57.078 / 204.059 s，均单独记录并从
`elapsed_seconds = compute + teardown` 中排除。

其他验收结果：

- CAL/A/B GPU telemetry 分别覆盖 75 / 89 / 102 个四卡 snapshots，error fraction 均为 0；
- AIME smoke：A `0/30`、B `1/30`，两者 truncated ratio 都是 96.67%。因为只有一次采样且 response
  上限为 512，这些数字只证明 eval 管线跑通，**不用于声称质量提升或不掉点**。

这次短程受控实验验证的是 underfill 复现、exact group refill、staleness/version 链、工程开销与失败边界。
它不构成收敛实验，也不支持“端到端训练一定加速”或“off-policy 质量完全无损”的结论。

## 与现有 PR 的关系

- [#657](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/657) 将 IS weight 与 RS mask 解耦；当前 main reducer 的
  numerator 使用 modified mask，而 denominator 仍显式使用原始 `rollout_mask_sums`。本 PR 不依赖改变
  reducer 的归一化语义，而是只保留 gate 全部通过且 mask 不变的完整 group，并补回固定 group cardinality。
- [#2084](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2084) 是开放中的通用 off-policy IS hook，让 correction 可使用
  current policy 与 rollout policy 的比值。本 PR 明确限制为每 rollout 一个 optimizer step、使用内置 TIS，
  并拒绝 custom TIS；两者目标不同，本 PR 不依赖 #2084，也不声称覆盖多步更新的通用 off-policy correction。
- [#2196](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2196) 是开放中的 per-call args 修复，避免
  `GenerateState` singleton 固定使用首次调用的参数。本 PR 因 replacement 必须传独立参数而触及同一问题，
  采用在 task submission 时显式传入本次 args 的方式，并在 RolloutManager 边界 deep-copy custom
  rollout/sample-hook args。如果 #2196 先合入，我会 rebase 并尽量去除或缩小重复改动。
- [#2218](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2218) 是开放中的 generation-stage dynamic-filter granular
  refill / abort 生命周期修复；本 PR 处理的是 rollout 完成后、actor-side RS 才能观察到的 effective-batch
  缺口。两者阶段不同，但**当前版本不能直接叠加启用**：本 PR 为保证 exact candidate set 会拒绝
  `--dynamic-sampling-filter-path`。上面的 planner 请求量也没有计入 #2218 的潜在收益。
- Draft [#2278](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2278) 面向 persistent fully-async queue，增加确定性的
  policy-version lag window 与 stale requeue；[#2279](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2279) 将 fully-async
  policy-version lifecycle 作为较小的基础改动单独提交，本身不加入 staleness rejection。本 PR 第一版显式
  拒绝 persistent fully-async queue，只支持 one-step async 的硬版本约束，因此不替代这两个 PR。

## Checklist

- [x] 主路径默认关闭，仅在显式 `--rs-batch-refill` 时启用
- [x] underfill / retry exhaustion 时不执行 optimizer step
- [x] replacement 按完整 prompt group 原子补齐，并只做 topology 最小向上取整
- [x] 硬 staleness / policy-version / ID / mask / cache 校验
- [x] 最终训练继续应用 TIS；不把 refill 描述为 on-policy
- [x] custom rollout/sample/logger 参数隔离与 observability mutation 检查
- [x] actor / manager cache 上限、RPC 超时和异常清理
- [x] CPU 单测、相关回归、pre-commit 与私有实验 harness 自检通过
- [x] 文档、示例配置、CUDA headroom 说明和运行指标已补充
- [x] 完成目标四卡无外部 GPU 进程混入的真实配对 A/B，并报告真实结果与适用边界

这个改动横跨 actor、RolloutManager、data source 和 async scheduling，代码量较大。我尽量通过 opt-in、
严格参数校验、更新前失败和逐边界回归测试来限制风险。如果维护者希望拆分独立兼容性修复，或调整接口、
指标和命名，我愿意配合修改。感谢审阅。

items.title: feat(megatron): report peak memory for log_probs and actor_train
items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: The OOM traceback alone did not show the phase's high-water mark.
items.body:
## Summary

- `print_memory` samples current allocation only at fixed lifecycle points, so it cannot expose a phase's high-water mark and an OOM can happen before the next report
- add accelerator-aware `report_peak_memory(phase)`: reset peak stats on entry and log peak allocated/reserved memory in a `finally` block, so an OOMing phase still reports its high-water mark
- wrap each executed ref/teacher/actor `log_probs` forward and `actor_train`, composed with the existing timer scopes; a reused or skipped actor forward emits no separate `log_probs` report
- support the allocator APIs exposed by Slime's CUDA/ROCm and MUSA backends; registered accelerators without those APIs continue without peak reporting
- intentionally scope the reset to the current device and require non-nested scopes, because an inner reset would discard an outer phase's peak

Measured on a 128x H100 DeepSeek-V4-Flash run at 262,144-token context: the `finally`-path report attributed a 132k-context `log_probs` OOM to 25 GiB of retained activations. The OOM traceback alone did not show the phase's high-water mark.

## Testing

- `python tests/test_accelerator.py` — 12 passed; covers reset-before-body, exact GB/log formatting, reporting on exceptions without swallowing them, unsupported-accelerator fallback, and CUDA/MUSA capability detection
- `black --line-length 119`, `ruff check`, and `isort --profile=black` pass on all touched files

items.title: docs: add SkyPilot launch tutorial under platform_support
items.author: ishankaul1
items.summary: This adds a tutorial for launching multi-node slime on Kubernetes or cloud instances with — provisioning the nodes, starting the Ray cluster, and submitting the training job from a single YAML — following the same pattern as the AMD tutorial: written and maint…
items.body:
This adds a `platform_support` tutorial for launching multi-node slime on Kubernetes or cloud instances with [SkyPilot](https://github.com/skypilot-org/skypilot) — provisioning the nodes, starting the Ray cluster, and submitting the training job from a single YAML — following the same pattern as the AMD tutorial: written and maintained by us (the SkyPilot maintainers), with slime's core docs unchanged.

It covers the Quick Start's Qwen3-4B GRPO recipe in two forms, both validated end-to-end on a Kubernetes cluster (2 nodes × 4×H100):

- the standard multi-node setup, automating the per-node `ray start` steps from the quick start;
- a disaggregated variant that runs the trainer and SGLang engines as separate gang-scheduled jobs with disk-based weight sync (`--rollout-external-engine-addrs` + `--update-weight-transport disk`).

It links to a full end-to-end agentic RL [example](https://github.com/skypilot-org/skypilot/tree/master/llm/slime) kept working against slime in the SkyPilot repo — per CONTRIBUTING.md's guidance to build such pipelines in separate repositories and reference them.

One note for reviewers: the multi-node YAML passes `--num-gpus-per-node` explicitly. With the default of 8 on 4-GPU nodes we reproduced the colocate engine-mapping issue that #2012 fixes; the flag is the documented workaround and stays correct (redundant) after that PR merges.

Also adds a one-line cross-reference from the quick start's multi-node section to the new page — happy to drop that line if you'd rather keep the quick start minimal.

items.title: fix(rollout): normalize fan-out rewards by trajectory
items.author: sxl1993
items.summary: This change computes the trajectory-level baseline from [1, 0] as 0.5 and broadcasts [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5]. The default reward post-processing path is unchanged. [Discussion: @zhuzilin Please review #2302.]
items.body:
## Summary
- count each unique rollout once in the custom fan-out GRPO baseline
- broadcast the normalized trajectory reward to all emitted samples
- reject inconsistent sibling rewards and handle singleton groups without NaNs

## Motivation
For rewards [1, 1, 1, 0], where the first three samples belong to one rollout, the old hook used a sample-weighted baseline of 0.75. This change computes the trajectory-level baseline from [1, 0] as 0.5 and broadcasts [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5].

The default reward post-processing path is unchanged.

## Test
- added a CPU regression case to tests/test_sample.py
discussion: @zhuzilin Please review #2302. It fixes reward normalization for fan-out GRPO by normalizing per trajectory. The main thing to check is the rollout_id grouping logic.
